11.text: They said, "Yo, Galilee crew—why y'all standin' here lookin' up like that? That same Jesus who just went up to heaven? He comin' back the same way."

12.text: So they dipped back to Jerusalem from the Mount of Olives—a short Sabbath stroll away.

13.text: When they got there, they went up to the room where they was stayin': Peter, James, John, Andrew, Philip, Thomas, Bartholomew, Matthew, James (Alphaeus' son), Simon the Zealot, and Judas (James' son).

14.text: All of them was on one accord—prayin' and seekin' God—along with the women, Mary (Jesus' mama), and His brothers too.

15.text: One day, Peter stood up in the middle of the crew (it was like 120 folks deep) and said,

16.text: "Y'all, the Scripture had to come true. The Holy Spirit said this a long time ago through David—'bout Judas, who guided the ones that snatched up Jesus.

17.text: He used to roll with us and had a piece of this ministry."

18.text: (Side note: Judas used that dirty money to cop a field. Then he fell face-first and his body busted open—guts everywhere.)

19.text: Everybody in Jerusalem heard 'bout it. They even started callin' that field Akel Dama, which means Field of Blood.

20.text: Peter kept goin': "It's written in Psalms: 'Let his home be empty, nobody live there,' and also, 'Let somebody else take his spot.'

21.text: So outta the folks who been walkin' with us the whole time Jesus was movin' in and out—

22.text: from the time John baptized Him up until He got taken up—we need one of them to step up and be a witness to the resurrection with us."

23.text: They nominated two dudes: Joseph (aka Barsabas, also called Justus) and Matthias.

24.text: Then they prayed: "Lord, You the one who sees hearts. Show us which one You chose

25.text: to take this spot in the ministry—the spot Judas abandoned when he went sideways."

26.text: So they cast lots, and Matthias got the pick. He got added to the eleven apostles.

1.text: When the Day of Pentecost finally hit, everybody was together, locked in, same mindset, same spot.

2.text: Outta nowhere, this loud sound came from the sky—like a heavy wind rushin' through—and it filled the whole crib where they was sittin'.

3.text: Then they saw somethin' wild—looked like fire split into tongues, and each flame landed on a person.

4.text: Everybody in there got filled with the Holy Spirit, and they started speakin' different languages, whatever the Spirit gave 'em to say.

5.text: Now in Jerusalem, there were some real devout Jews from all over the world.

6.text: When that sound popped off, the whole crowd showed up, tryna figure out what was goin' on. They was trippin'—everybody heard the crew speakin' their native tongue.

7.text: They was shook. "Wait… ain't these dudes Galileans?

8.text: How they speakin' our languages like they was born in our hoods?"

9.text: "We got Parthians, Medes, Elamites, folks from Mesopotamia, Judea, Cappadocia, Pontus, Asia,

10.text: Phrygia, Pamphylia, Egypt, Libya over by Cyrene, even some cats from Rome—Jews and converts,

11.text: Cretans and Arabs—we all hear 'em talkin' in our own lingo, speakin' on how dope God is."

12.text: The crowd was stunned and confused. "Yo… what is even goin' on here?"

13.text: Some others tried to clown: "Man, they just drunk off that new wine."

14.text: Peter stood up with the Eleven, raised his voice, and said, "Y'all in Judea, everybody in Jerusalem—listen up and catch this.

15.text: We not drunk like y'all think—it's only 9AM!

16.text: What y'all seein' right now? This what the prophet Joel said would happen:

17.text: 'In the last days,' God say, 'I'ma pour out My Spirit on everybody. Your sons and daughters gon' prophesy. Young folk gon' see visions. Old heads gon' dream dreams.

18.text: Even on My servants—men and women—I'ma pour out My Spirit, and they gon' prophesy too.

19.text: I'ma show signs up in the sky, and down here on earth—blood, fire, smoke.

20.text: The sun gon' go dark, the moon gon' turn red, right before that big and powerful day when the Lord shows up.

21.text: And anybody who calls on the name of the Lord? They gon' be saved.'

22.text: Y'all, listen: Jesus of Nazareth—God co-signed Him with miracles, wonders, and signs right in front of y'all.

23.text: Even though it was all part of God's plan, y'all handed Him over to wicked folk, had Him crucified, and killed.

24.text: But God raised Him up—death couldn't hold Him, period.

25.text: David already said about Him: 'I saw the Lord always with me, He right beside me, so I won't trip.

26.text: That's why my heart's lit, and I can't stop praising. Even my body gon' rest in peace.

27.text: You won't leave me in the grave, You ain't gon' let Your Holy One rot.

28.text: You showed me the path to life, and in Your presence, I'm full of joy.'

29.text: Listen y'all—let me keep it a buck about David: he died, was buried, and we still got his grave to this day.

30.text: But he was a prophet, and he knew God promised him that one of his descendants would be the Christ, sittin' on the throne.

31.text: So David was speakin' on Jesus' resurrection—His soul ain't stay in the grave, and His body ain't rot.

32.text: This Jesus? God raised Him up, and all of us saw it go down.

33.text: Now He up at God's right hand, got the Holy Spirit like God promised, and He the one who poured all this out—what y'all hear and see now.

34.text: David ain't go up to heaven himself, but he said: 'The Lord said to my Lord, "Sit right here next to Me

35.text: 'til I make all Your enemies Your footstool."'

36.text: So best believe this, all y'all from Israel: God made this same Jesus—the one y'all crucified—both Lord and Christ."

37.text: When they heard that, it hit deep—they was cut to the heart. They said, "Brothers, what we supposed to do now?"

38.text: Peter said, "Repent—turn your life around—and get baptized in the name of Jesus Christ so your sins can get wiped clean. Then you'll receive the Holy Spirit too.

39.text: This promise ain't just for y'all—it's for your kids and everybody far off, anybody God calls."

40.text: Peter kept preachin', warnin' and pushin' them: "Save yourselves from this wild and crooked generation."

41.text: Folks who caught the word and believed got baptized—and that day, about 3,000 new people joined the crew.

42.text: They stayed solid—learnin' from the apostles, kickin' it together, breakin' bread, and stayin' in prayer.

43.text: Everybody felt the weight of it all—mad signs and wonders was happenin' through the apostles.

44.text: All the believers rolled together and shared everything.

45.text: They sold their stuff and looked out for each other, makin' sure nobody lacked nothin'.

46.text: Every day, they was united—pullin' up to the temple, breakin' bread from house to house, eatin' with joy and simple hearts.

47.text: They praised God and had good vibes with everybody—and the Lord kept addin' new folks to the squad every single day.

1.text: Peter and John was headed to the temple together around 3PM, the usual prayer time.

2.text: There was a man who been lame since birth. Every day, folks would carry him and lay him by the temple gate called Beautiful, so he could ask for money from the people goin' in.

3.text: When he saw Peter and John about to walk in, he hit 'em up for some change.

4.text: Peter looked straight at him, and so did John. Peter said, "Aye, look at us."

5.text: The man focused on 'em, expectin' to get somethin'.

6.text: But Peter said, "Look, I ain't got no silver or gold. But what I do got—I'm givin' it to you. In the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth, get up and walk."

7.text: Peter grabbed his right hand and helped him up—and instantly, his feet and ankles got strong.

8.text: The man jumped up, stood on his own, and started walkin'! Then he rolled with Peter and John into the temple—walkin', jumpin', and praisin' God like crazy.

9.text: Everybody saw him movin' around and givin' God praise.

10.text: Then it clicked—"Wait! Ain't that the dude who used to be beggin' by the Beautiful Gate?" They was straight shook and amazed at what just happened.

11.text: The man who got healed was holdin' on tight to Peter and John, and the whole crowd ran over to 'em in Solomon's Porch, blown away.

12.text: Peter saw the crowd and said, "Y'all Israelites—why y'all actin' surprised? Why y'all lookin' at us like we did this with our own power or because we holier than thou?

13.text: The God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—the God of our ancestors—He the one who lifted up His Servant Jesus. The same Jesus y'all handed over and denied in front of Pilate, even when he wanted to let Him go.

14.text: Y'all straight up rejected the Holy and Righteous One, and asked for a killer instead.

15.text: Y'all killed the Author of life—but God raised Him up, and we all saw it.

16.text: It's through Jesus' name—through faith in His name—that this man was healed. Y'all know him. Y'all seen him. And now he standin' here whole 'cause of that faith Jesus brings."

17.text: "Now look—I know y'all did it outta ignorance. So did your leaders.

18.text: But everything that went down? God already said it was gon' happen through the mouths of the prophets—that the Christ had to suffer. And He made it all come true.

19.text: So now it's time—repent and switch lanes. Get your sins wiped out so times of refreshin' can come from God.

20.text: He gon' send Jesus, the one He already told y'all about—

21.text: but for now, Jesus chillin' in heaven until it's time to restore everything, like God been talkin' about through His prophets since way back.

22.text: Moses told our ancestors, 'God gon' raise up a Prophet like me from among y'all. Listen to Him. Do whatever He says.'

23.text: And anybody who don't listen to that Prophet? They gon' be cut off from the people—period.

24.text: Every prophet—from Samuel on down—been speakin' on these days right here.

25.text: Y'all are the descendants of those prophets. Y'all part of the promise God made with our fathers, when He told Abraham, 'Through your people, all the families on earth gon' be blessed.'

26.text: So God sent Jesus to y'all first, after raisin' Him up. He came to bless y'all—turnin' each one of y'all away from your mess."

1.text: While Peter and John was still preachin' to the people, here come the priests, the temple guards, and the Sadducees, rollin' up on them.

2.text: They was real pressed that Peter and John was teachin' the people and preachin' that Jesus rose from the dead.

3.text: So they snatched them up and threw them in jail 'til the next day, since it was already gettin' late.

4.text: But even with that, a whole bunch of folks who heard the message believed—and the number of men alone hit about five thousand.

5.text: The next day, all the big shots pulled up—rulers, elders, scribes,

6.text: plus Annas the high priest, Caiaphas, John, Alexander, and everybody from the high priest's family.

7.text: They brought Peter and John to the center and asked, "By what power or in whose name did y'all do this?"

8.text: Peter, full of the Holy Spirit, said, "Leaders of the people and elders—

9.text: if y'all put us on trial today 'cause we helped a man who couldn't walk, and you tryna figure out how he got healed,

10.text: then hear this: It's by the name of Jesus Christ of Nazareth—the one y'all crucified, the one God raised up—that this man is standin' here healed.

11.text: Jesus is the stone y'all builders tossed aside, but God made Him the cornerstone.

12.text: And let me tell you—ain't no other name under heaven that can save us. Jesus is the only way."

13.text: When they saw how bold Peter and John was, and realized they ain't have no degrees or special training, they were shocked—and recognized these men had been with Jesus.

14.text: And with the healed man standin' right there, they couldn't say nothin'.

15.text: So they told 'em to step outside while they had a lil' sidebar.

16.text: They was like, "What we gon' do with these dudes? Everybody in Jerusalem saw that miracle. We can't deny it.

17.text: But to keep this from spreadin', let's threaten 'em heavy so they don't talk about Jesus no more."

18.text: They brought them back in and told 'em, "Don't speak or teach in Jesus' name again."

19.text: But Peter and John clapped back, "Y'all think it's right to listen to y'all over God? You decide.

20.text: But as for us, we gotta speak on what we seen and heard."

21.text: So after more threats, they let 'em go—they couldn't find a reason to punish 'em 'cause the people was praisin' God over what happened.

22.text: The man who got healed was over forty, so this wasn't no baby miracle—this was major.

23.text: After they got released, Peter and John went back to the crew and told 'em everything the chief priests and elders said.

24.text: The squad heard it and immediately prayed loud together: "Lord, You the one who made heaven, earth, the sea—everything in it.

25.text: You said through Your servant David: 'Why the nations wildin'? Why the people plottin' nonsense?

26.text: The kings of the earth took their stand, The rulers linked up against the Lord and His Christ.'

27.text: That's exactly what happened. Herod, Pilate, the Gentiles, and even Israel's people came together against Jesus, Your holy Servant who You anointed.

28.text: But all of it was still under Your hand, doin' what You planned from jump.

29.text: So now, Lord—look at their threats, and give us the boldness to keep speakin' Your word.

30.text: Stretch out Your hand and heal! Let signs and wonders pop off in Jesus' name!"

31.text: After they prayed, the spot they was in started shakin'. They was all filled with the Holy Spirit again and started speakin' God's word even bolder.

32.text: All the believers was tight—same heart, same mind. Nobody was claimin' their stuff as just theirs; they shared everything.

33.text: The apostles spoke with power 'bout Jesus risin' from the dead, and God's grace was all over them.

34.text: Nobody among them was lackin'—folks who had land or houses sold 'em and brought the money

35.text: and dropped it at the apostles' feet so they could bless whoever needed it.

36.text: One dude named Joses—apostles called him Barnabas (that mean "Son of Encouragement")—he was a Levite from Cyprus.

37.text: He sold his land, brought the cash, and laid it at the apostles' feet too.

1.text: A man named Ananias and his wife Sapphira sold some property.

2.text: But Ananias kept some of the money for himself, and his wife was in on it. He brought just part of the money and laid it at the apostles' feet like it was the full amount.

3.text: Peter said, "Ananias, why you lettin' Satan get in your heart like that? Why you lyin' to the Holy Spirit and holdin' back part of the money?

4.text: The land was yours. You didn't have to sell it. And even after you sold it, the money was yours to handle. So why fake it? You ain't just lie to people—you lied to God."

5.text: As soon as Ananias heard that, he dropped dead. Everybody who heard about it got shook.

6.text: The young men wrapped him up, carried him out, and buried him.

7.text: About three hours later, his wife came in, not knowin' what happened.

8.text: Peter asked her, "So… y'all sold the land for that amount?" She said, "Yep, that's the price."

9.text: Peter said, "Why y'all both tryna test God's Spirit like this? The same dudes who just buried your husband at the door—they finna carry you out too."

10.text: Boom—she dropped dead on the spot. The young men came in, saw her, picked her up, and buried her next to her man.

11.text: Fear hit the whole church and anybody who heard the story. They knew God was not playin'.

12.text: God was still movin'—the apostles were doin' all kinds of signs and wonders in the streets. The believers were tight, meetin' up at Solomon's Porch.

13.text: The rest of the folks ain't even wanna fake joinin'—but they had major respect for them.

14.text: More and more people—both men and women—started believin' in the Lord.

15.text: Folks was bringin' the sick out to the streets, layin' them on mats and couches, hopin' Peter's shadow might pass by and hit 'em.

16.text: Crowds came from the surrounding towns bringin' the sick and the demonized—and everybody got healed. No exceptions.

17.text: The high priest and the Sadducees crew got mad jealous.

18.text: So they arrested the apostles and threw them in the public jail.

19.text: But that night, an angel of the Lord showed up, opened the jail doors, and said,

20.text: "Go back to the temple and keep preachin' this message of life."

21.text: Early the next morning, they pulled up to the temple and started teachin'. Meanwhile, the high priest and the council gathered up and sent for them at the jail.

22.text: But when the guards got there, they found the jail locked up and the guards still posted—but the cell was empty.

23.text: They ran back and said, "Jail locked, guards in place—but the prisoners gone!"

24.text: The priest crew was shook. "What in the world is goin' on?"

25.text: Then somebody ran up and said, "Yo! The men y'all locked up—they out in the temple, teachin' again!"

26.text: The captain and officers went to grab them—but carefully, 'cause they ain't want the people to stone them.

27.text: They brought the apostles in and stood them before the council. The high priest said,

28.text: "Didn't we tell y'all to stop teachin' in Jesus' name? And look—y'all done filled the whole city with this message and tryna pin this man's death on us!"

29.text: Peter and the apostles said, "We gotta obey God over people.

30.text: The God of our ancestors raised Jesus—the one y'all killed by hangin' Him on a tree.

31.text: But God lifted Him up, gave Him the throne, made Him Prince and Savior, to offer repentance and forgiveness to Israel.

32.text: And we saw it all. We're witnesses. And so is the Holy Spirit, who God gives to those who obey Him."

33.text: When they heard that, they lost it—ready to kill them.

34.text: But then this respected Pharisee named Gamaliel stood up—a teacher of the law that everybody respected. He told them to step outside so he could talk.

35.text: He said, "Y'all better think twice before y'all move on these men.

36.text: Remember Theudas? Claimed he was somebody—had like 400 followers. He died, and his whole movement fell apart.

37.text: Then came Judas of Galilee durin' the census. He pulled a crowd too. He died, and everybody scattered.

38.text: So here's what I'm sayin': Leave these men alone. If what they doin' is just human hype, it'll fall apart.

39.text: But if it's from God? Y'all won't be able to stop it—and you'll find yourself fightin' against God."

40.text: They agreed. Called the apostles back in, beat them, and told them again, "Don't speak in Jesus' name." Then they let them go.

41.text: But the apostles left the council hyped—thankin' God they got to suffer for Jesus' name.

42.text: And they didn't slow down. Every day, in the temple and in folks' houses, they kept on teachin' and preachin' that Jesus is the Christ.

1.text: As the number of disciples kept growin', some tension popped off. The Hellenists (Greek-speaking Jews) started complainin' that their widows was bein' overlooked in the daily food hookup by the Hebrew crew.

2.text: So the twelve apostles gathered everybody up and said, "Look—it ain't right for us to stop preachin' the word just to serve food.

3.text: Let's do this—pick seven brothers from y'all: men with a solid rep, full of the Holy Spirit and wisdom. We'll put them in charge of this work.

4.text: Meanwhile, we gon' stay locked in—prayin' and preachin' the Word."

5.text: That plan hit right with the whole crowd. So they chose Stephen (a man full of faith and the Holy Spirit), Philip, Prochorus, Nicanor, Timon, Parmenas, and Nicolas (a convert from Antioch).

6.text: They brought these seven before the apostles, who prayed over them and laid hands on them.

7.text: And with that, God's word kept spreadin'. The number of disciples blew up in Jerusalem, and even a gang of priests started followin' the faith.

8.text: Stephen, full of power and faith, was out here doin' major signs and wonders among the people.

9.text: But some folks from the Synagogue of the Freedmen (including cats from Cyrene, Alexandria, Cilicia, and Asia) tried to argue with him.

10.text: But they couldn't hang with the wisdom and the Spirit behind how he spoke.

11.text: So they got slick—paid some men to lie and say, "We heard him talkin' reckless about Moses and God."

12.text: They stirred up the crowd, got the elders and scribes involved, and ran up on Stephen, grabbed him, and dragged him in front of the council.

13.text: They even brought in fake witnesses who said, "This dude stay talkin' down on the holy temple and the law.

14.text: He said Jesus of Nazareth gon' tear this place down and flip everything Moses gave us."

15.text: But everybody in the council starin' at him saw somethin' different—his face? Looked like an angel's.

1.text: Then the high priest asked, "Is all this true?"

2.text: Stephen said, "Family, listen up: The God of glory showed up to our forefather Abraham when he was still in Mesopotamia—before he moved to Haran.

3.text: God told him, 'Leave your country and your kinfolk, and I'ma take you somewhere new.'

4.text: So Abraham left the land of the Chaldeans and stayed in Haran for a while. After his daddy died, God moved him into this land right here, where y'all now livin'.

5.text: But He ain't give him none of it to own—not even enough to stand on. Yet God still promised he'd pass it down to his kids—even though Abraham didn't have a single child yet.

6.text: God told him straight: 'Your descendants gon' live as foreigners in another land, be enslaved, and get oppressed for 400 years.

7.text: But I'll judge that nation,' God said, 'and then they gon' come out and worship Me right here.'

8.text: Then God gave Abraham the covenant of circumcision. Abraham had Isaac and circumcised him on the eighth day. Isaac had Jacob. Jacob had the twelve patriarchs."

9.text: "Now the patriarchs got salty over Joseph and sold him into slavery in Egypt. But God had His hand on him.

10.text: He rescued Joseph from all his struggles, gave him wisdom and favor with Pharaoh, who made Joseph ruler over Egypt and his whole house.

11.text: Then came a famine and heavy struggle across Egypt and Canaan, and our people ain't have nothin' to eat.

12.text: But Jacob heard there was grain in Egypt and sent our fathers down there.

13.text: On their second trip, Joseph revealed who he was, and Pharaoh got to know Joseph's family.

14.text: Then Joseph sent for his father Jacob and all his folks—75 people total.

15.text: Jacob moved down to Egypt, and he died there, along with our fathers.

16.text: Later they brought their bodies back to Shechem and buried them in the tomb Abraham had bought from the sons of Hamor."

17.text: "When the time for the promise drew near, the people multiplied in Egypt—

18.text: until a new king came up who ain't know Joseph.

19.text: That king treated our people foul—oppressin' them, makin' 'em throw out their babies to die.

20.text: That's when Moses was born, and God was pleased with him. He stayed in his parents' home for three months.

21.text: When they let him go, Pharaoh's daughter picked him up and raised him as her own son.

22.text: Moses got all the Egyptian education—he was a beast with words and action.

23.text: "When he turned 40, he decided to check on his people, the Israelites.

24.text: He saw one of 'em gettin' beat and stepped in—killed the Egyptian.

25.text: He thought the people would get it—like, 'God usin' me to save y'all.' But they wasn't feelin' it.

26.text: The next day he saw two Israelites fightin' and tried to break it up. 'Y'all brothers—why y'all fightin'?'

27.text: But the one in the wrong pushed him away and said, 'Who made you boss over us?

28.text: You gon' kill me too like you did that Egyptian yesterday?'

29.text: That's when Moses dipped. He ran to Midian and started a new life, had two sons."

30.text: "Forty years later, an angel showed up to him in a flame from a bush out in the wilderness near Mount Sinai.

31.text: Moses saw it and was like, 'What's goin' on?' He walked closer, and God's voice came through.

32.text: 'I'm the God of your fathers—Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.' Moses got scared and didn't even wanna look.

33.text: Then God said, 'Take your shoes off. Where you standin' is holy ground.

34.text: I see what My people in Egypt goin' through. I heard their cries. I'm bout to set them free—and I'm sendin' you back to do it.'"

35.text: "This same Moses they rejected, sayin', 'Who made you our ruler and judge?'—God flipped it and sent him as ruler and deliverer through the angel in the bush.

36.text: He led them out, performin' wild signs and wonders in Egypt, at the Red Sea, and in the wilderness for 40 years."

37.text: "This same Moses said, 'God gon' raise up a Prophet like me from among y'all. Listen to Him.'

38.text: He was with our people and the angel on Mount Sinai, the one who gave us the living words from God.

39.text: But our ancestors ain't wanna listen. They rejected him and started longin' for Egypt in their hearts.

40.text: They told Aaron, 'Make us some gods to go ahead of us. We don't know what happened to Moses.'

41.text: So they made a golden calf, sacrificed to it, and threw a party for this idol they made with their own hands.

42.text: "So God stepped back and let them do what they wanted—worship the stars and false gods. The prophets even wrote: 'Did y'all bring Me sacrifices in the wilderness?

43.text: Nah, y'all carried idols—Moloch and Remphan's star. So I'ma send y'all way out past Babylon.'"

44.text: "Back in the wilderness, our ancestors had the tabernacle—the portable sanctuary God told Moses to build.

45.text: That same setup was passed down and carried into the Promised Land by Joshua when they took over from the Gentiles.

46.text: David had favor with God and wanted to build Him a home,

47.text: but Solomon the one who actually built it.

48.text: Even still—the Most High don't live in temples made by human hands. Like the prophet said:

49.text: 'Heaven's My throne. Earth is My footstool. What kind of house could you build for Me?

50.text: Didn't I make all this with My own hands?'"

51.text: "Y'all hard-headed and spiritually deaf—just like your ancestors. Always fightin' the Holy Spirit.

52.text: Which prophet didn't y'all forefathers harass or kill? They even killed the ones who spoke about the coming of the Righteous One—Jesus—who y'all betrayed and murdered.

53.text: Y'all received God's law straight from angels, and still didn't keep it."

54.text: When they heard all that, they was heated—grittin' their teeth, ready to snap.

55.text: But Stephen, full of the Holy Spirit, looked up and saw God's glory—with Jesus standin' at God's right hand.

56.text: He said, "Look! I see heaven wide open—and the Son of Man standin' at God's right hand!"

57.text: They started yellin', covered their ears, and rushed him all together.

58.text: They dragged him out the city and started stonin' him. The ones throwin' the rocks laid their coats down at the feet of a young man named Saul.

59.text: While they stoned him, Stephen prayed, "Lord Jesus, take my spirit."

60.text: Then he dropped to his knees and shouted, "Lord, don't hold this sin against them!" And with that, he passed away.

1.text: Saul was standin' there co-signin' all of it, watchin' Stephen get stoned. Right after that, persecution popped off heavy against the church in Jerusalem. Everybody scattered through Judea and Samaria—except the apostles.

2.text: Some solid believers buried Stephen, cryin' real tears for him.

3.text: But Saul? He was out here wildin', tearin' through the church. Goin' door to door, draggin' folks out—men and women—throwin' them straight in jail.

4.text: The ones who scattered didn't get silent—they kept spreadin' the Word wherever they landed.

5.text: Philip went down to a city in Samaria and started preachin' Jesus like He was the main event.

6.text: The people locked in—everybody was payin' attention to Philip, especially when they heard and saw the signs he was doin'.

7.text: Demons was gettin' snatched outta folks left and right, screamin' on the way out. And a whole lotta folks who were paralyzed or crippled got healed.

8.text: That whole city was lit with joy.

9.text: Now there was this dude named Simon who had everybody in Samaria shook. Been out there practicin' magic and had folks thinkin' he was somebody major.

10.text: Everybody—from the littlest to the grownest—was like, "This man got the power of God, and not just any power, the Great Power!"

11.text: They been on his hype train for a minute 'cause of all the flashy stuff he been doin'.

12.text: But when Philip came through preachin' the Good News about God's kingdom and Jesus as the King, folks believed him and got baptized—men and women.

13.text: Even Simon got saved and baptized. He stuck real close to Philip, amazed at the signs and miracles goin' down.

14.text: Word got back to Jerusalem that Samaria was now rockin' with God. So the apostles sent Peter and John down there.

15.text: When they got there, they prayed over the folks so they could receive the Holy Spirit.

16.text: 'Cause at that point, the Spirit hadn't touched down yet—they had only been baptized in Jesus' name.

17.text: Peter and John laid hands on 'em, and boom—the Holy Spirit came through.

18.text: Simon saw all that and was like, "Yo, let me get in on that too!" He tried to break them off some money so he could have that hand-layin' power.

19.text: He said, "Give me that same hookup so whoever I lay hands on can get the Spirit too."

20.text: But Peter shut that all the way down: "You and your money can perish together, tryin' to buy what only God gives."

21.text: "You ain't got no part or place in this. Yo' heart not right with God."

22.text: "You need to repent, bruh. Pray and ask the Lord to forgive the mess in your heart."

23.text: "I see what's really up—you bitter and chained up in sin."

24.text: Simon said, "Man, pray for me! I don't want none of that stuff you just said to come true!"

25.text: After Peter and John finished preachin' and reppin' Jesus all over Samaria, they headed back to Jerusalem, stoppin' in different villages to spread the Word.

26.text: Then the angel of the Lord told Philip, "Get up and go down south, on that desert road from Jerusalem to Gaza."

27.text: So he got up and went. He ran into an Ethiopian official—a real important man under the Queen of Ethiopia, Candace. He was her money man, and he had come to Jerusalem to worship.

28.text: Now he was on his way back home, sittin' in his chariot readin' the prophet Isaiah out loud.

29.text: The Spirit told Philip, "Go up to that chariot and stay close."

30.text: Philip ran up and heard him readin' Isaiah. He asked, "You understand what you readin'?"

31.text: Dude said, "How can I, unless somebody breaks it down for me?" Then he invited Philip to come sit with him.

32.text: The scripture he was readin' was: "He was led like a sheep to the slaughter, and just like a lamb silent before the shearin', He ain't open His mouth."

33.text: "In His humiliation, justice was denied Him. Who can talk about His family line? 'Cause His life got cut short from the earth."

34.text: The eunuch asked, "Who the prophet talkin' about—himself or somebody else?"

35.text: Philip started preachin' right from that scripture and broke down Jesus to him.

36.text: As they kept rollin', they came up on some water. The eunuch said, "Look! Water! What's stoppin' me from gettin' baptized?"

37.text: Then Philip said, "If you believe with all your heart, you may." The man answered, "I believe Jesus Christ is the Son of God."

38.text: He told the chariot driver to stop. Both of them—Philip and the eunuch—went down into the water, and Philip baptized him.

39.text: As soon as they came up out that water, the Spirit of the Lord snatched Philip up. The eunuch ain't see him no more, but he went on his way hype and full of joy.

40.text: Philip popped up in Azotus. He went city to city preachin' the gospel until he hit Caesarea.

1.text: Saul was still out here breathin' threats, tryna take out every single disciple of the Lord.

2.text: He asked the high priest for permission slips—letters to the synagogues in Damascus—so if he caught anybody rollin' with Jesus (a.k.a. "The Way"), man or woman, he could cuff 'em up and drag 'em back to Jerusalem.

3.text: But as he was gettin' close to Damascus, outta nowhere, a bright light from heaven flashed all around him.

4.text: He dropped to the ground and heard a voice say, "Saul, Saul—why you tryna fight Me?"

5.text: He said, "Who are You, Lord?" The voice said, "I'm Jesus—the One you out here persecutin'. You ain't gon' win fightin' against Me."

6.text: Shook and trembling, Saul said, "Lord, what you want me to do?" Jesus said, "Get up, go into the city, and you'll be told what's next."

7.text: The men with Saul just stood there—speechless. They heard the voice but didn't see nobody.

8.text: Saul got up, but when he opened his eyes, he couldn't see a thing. So they had to lead him by the hand to Damascus.

9.text: He was blind for three whole days. Ain't eat. Ain't drink.

10.text: Meanwhile, there was a disciple in Damascus named Ananias. The Lord came to him in a vision and said, "Ananias." He said, "Here I am, Lord."

11.text: The Lord said, "Get up, go to Straight Street. Find Judas' house. Ask for a man named Saul from Tarsus. He's prayin' right now.

12.text: I already showed him a vision of you layin' hands on him so he can see again."

13.text: Ananias said, "Lord… You sure? I heard plenty about this man and the damage he's done to your people in Jerusalem.

14.text: And now he got authority to arrest everybody who calls on your name right here in Damascus too!"

15.text: But the Lord said, "Go. He My chosen vessel. He gon' carry My name to Gentiles, kings, and Israel too.

16.text: I'ma show him just how much he gon' suffer for My name."

17.text: So Ananias did what God said. He walked in, laid hands on Saul, and said, "Brother Saul, Jesus—the same One who stopped you on the road—He sent me so you can see again and be filled with the Holy Spirit."

18.text: Right then, somethin' like scales fell off Saul's eyes. He could see again. He stood up and got baptized.

19.text: Then he ate, got his strength back, and kicked it with the disciples in Damascus for a few days.

20.text: Straight up, he started preachin' in the synagogues that Jesus is the Son of God.

21.text: Everybody who heard him was stunned. "Ain't this the dude who was wreckin' the church in Jerusalem? Didn't he come here to snatch up believers and take 'em to the chief priests?"

22.text: But Saul kept gettin' stronger and shuttin' folks down with the truth—provin' that Jesus really is the Christ.

23.text: After a while, some Jews made a plan to kill him.

24.text: But Saul got wind of the setup—they were watchin' the city gates day and night.

25.text: So the disciples snuck him out at night, lettin' him down through a hole in the city wall in a big basket.

26.text: When he got back to Jerusalem, Saul tried to link up with the disciples—but they ain't trust him. They thought he was fakin'.

27.text: But Barnabas stepped in, brought Saul to the apostles, and broke it all down—how Saul saw the Lord, talked to Him, and been preachin' bold in Damascus.

28.text: So then he was able to move in and out with the crew, free and bold.

29.text: He started preachin' heavy to the Greek-speaking Jews, and they tried to kill him too.

30.text: When the fam heard, they got him outta there—took him down to Caesarea, then shipped him out to Tarsus.

31.text: After all that, the churches in Judea, Galilee, and Samaria finally had some peace. They kept growin', walkin' in God's fear, and leanin' on the Holy Spirit's comfort. God was buildin' somethin' strong.

32.text: Meanwhile, Peter was makin' moves all over. He came to Lydda to check on the saints.

33.text: There he found a man named Aeneas—been bedridden eight years, paralyzed.

34.text: Peter told him, "Aeneas, Jesus Christ heals you. Get up and make your bed." And boom—he got up right then.

35.text: Everybody in Lydda and Sharon saw him walkin' again, and they turned to the Lord.

36.text: In Joppa, there was a disciple named Tabitha (aka Dorcas). She was known for servin' and helpin' people.

37.text: But she got sick and died. They washed her body and placed her in the upper room.

38.text: Since Lydda was close, and they heard Peter was there, some disciples sent two men askin' him to come quick.

39.text: Peter went with them. When he got there, they took him upstairs. Widows were cryin', showin' off all the clothes Dorcas made when she was alive.

40.text: Peter put everybody out, got down on his knees, and prayed. Then he turned to the body and said, "Tabitha, get up." She opened her eyes, saw Peter, and sat up.

41.text: He helped her up, called in the saints and widows, and showed 'em she was alive.

42.text: Word got out all over Joppa, and many believed in the Lord.

43.text: Peter stayed in Joppa for a while, chillin' at Simon the tanner's house.

1.text: There was a man named Cornelius in Caesarea, a Roman soldier—high up in the Italian Regiment.

2.text: He feared God for real, him and his whole house. He was generous with the people and stayed prayin' to God.

3.text: Around 3PM, he had a vision—clear as day. An angel of God came through and called him by name: "Cornelius."

4.text: Cornelius got shook and said, "What's goin' on, Lord?" The angel said, "God seen your prayers and your giving. It's like a sweet memorial in front of Him.

5.text: Now send some men to Joppa, and ask for a man named Simon, also called Peter.

6.text: He's stayin' with another dude named Simon—a tanner—over by the sea. He'll tell you what to do."

7.text: When the angel left, Cornelius called two of his household staff and one of his God-fearing soldiers that served close to him.

8.text: He broke down the whole situation to them, then sent them straight to Joppa.

9.text: The next day while they were on their way and getting close to the city, Peter went up on the roof to pray around noon.

10.text: He got real hungry and wanted to eat, but while food was being cooked, he slipped into a vision.

11.text: He saw heaven open and somethin' like a big sheet comin' down, tied at all four corners, floatin' to the ground.

12.text: Inside it was all kinds of four-legged animals, wild creatures, creepy things, and birds.

13.text: Then a voice told him, "Get up, Peter. Kill somethin' and eat."

14.text: But Peter said, "Nah, Lord. I've never ate nothin' unclean or common in my life."

15.text: The voice came back: "What God has cleaned, don't you call dirty."

16.text: This happened three times. Then the sheet disappeared—straight back into heaven.

17.text: While Peter was tryna figure out what that vision meant, Cornelius's crew pulled up to Simon's house and stood outside at the gate.

18.text: They called out askin', "Is Simon, also called Peter, stayin' here?"

19.text: While Peter was still thinkin' on the vision, the Spirit said, "Three men are lookin' for you.

20.text: Get up, go down there, and go with them. Don't question nothin'—I sent 'em."

21.text: So Peter went down and said, "I'm the one y'all lookin' for. Why y'all here?"

22.text: They said, "We from Cornelius, a Roman officer. He's a good dude, fears God, respected by everybody. An angel told him to call for you and hear what you got to say."

23.text: Peter let them in and gave them a place to stay for the night. The next day, he rolled out with them. Some of the believers from Joppa came along too.

24.text: The next day, they got to Caesarea. Cornelius was waitin'—he had gathered his whole crew, family and friends.

25.text: When Peter walked in, Cornelius dropped to his knees and started worshipin' him.

26.text: But Peter pulled him up like, "Nah, man. Get up. I'm just a man too."

27.text: They went inside, and Peter saw a big crowd waitin'.

28.text: He said, "Y'all know it's against our law for a Jew like me to even be chillin' with y'all Gentiles. But God showed me not to call anybody dirty or unworthy.

29.text: So when y'all called, I came without hesitatin'. Now, tell me—why you call me?"

30.text: Cornelius said, "Four days ago, around this same time, I was fastin'. Around 3PM, I was prayin' and this man in bright clothes showed up.

31.text: He said, 'Cornelius, God heard your prayers and saw your generosity.

32.text: Send for Peter in Joppa—he stayin' with Simon the tanner by the sea. He gon' speak to you.'

33.text: So I sent for you right away. And you did good to come. Now we all here, in God's presence, waitin' to hear what the Lord told you to say."

34.text: Then Peter started talkin': "Now I get it—God don't play favorites.

35.text: Anybody from any nation that respects Him and does right is welcome with Him.

36.text: He sent His message to Israel first, bringin' peace through Jesus—who is Lord of everybody.

37.text: Y'all already heard what went down all over Judea—starting in Galilee after John preached baptism.

38.text: God anointed Jesus of Nazareth with the Holy Spirit and power. Jesus went around doin' good and healing folks who were oppressed by the devil, 'cause God was with Him.

39.text: We saw it all—everything He did in the land of the Jews and in Jerusalem. They killed Him by hangin' Him on a cross.

40.text: But God raised Him up on the third day and let Him be seen—

41.text: not by everybody, but by us—His chosen witnesses. We ate and drank with Him after He rose.

42.text: And He told us to preach to the people and say that He's the One God chose to judge the living and the dead.

43.text: All the prophets been sayin' it—whoever believes in Him will get their sins forgiven through His name."

44.text: While Peter was still preachin', the Holy Spirit dropped on everybody in the room who was listenin'.

45.text: The Jewish believers that came with Peter were shook—they couldn't believe God gave the Holy Spirit to the Gentiles too.

46.text: But they heard them speakin' in tongues and praisin' God.

47.text: Then Peter said, "Yo… can anybody stop these folks from gettin' baptized? They got the same Spirit we got."

48.text: So he ordered them to be baptized in Jesus' name. And they asked Peter to stay with them for a few more days.

1.text: Word got back to the apostles and the believers in Judea—Gentiles out here receiving the Word of God too!

2.text: So when Peter came back up to Jerusalem, some of the Jewish believers pressed him hard.

3.text: They said, "Yo, you went into a house full of uncircumcised folks and even ate with them?"

4.text: Peter was like, "Lemme break it down for y'all from the top."

5.text: "I was in Joppa prayin', and I had a vision. I saw something like a big sheet floatin' down from heaven, held up by the corners, and it came right to me.

6.text: I looked real close—inside were all kinds of four-legged animals, wild beasts, crawlies, and birds.

7.text: Then I heard a voice tell me, 'Get up, Peter. Kill somethin' and eat.'

8.text: I said, 'Nah, Lord. I don't eat nothin' that's unclean or common.'

9.text: But the voice clapped back, 'Don't you call dirty what God already cleaned.'

10.text: That happened three times, then the sheet went back up to heaven."

11.text: "And right then—like on cue—three men showed up at the house. They were sent from Caesarea.

12.text: The Spirit told me, 'Go with them and don't second guess it.' Six of the brothers here came with me too, and we all walked up in that man's house."

13.text: "He told us he saw an angel in his crib sayin', 'Send somebody to Joppa to get Simon, aka Peter.

14.text: He gon' tell you and your whole house how to get saved.'"

15.text: "And as soon as I started speakin', the Holy Spirit dropped on them just like it did on us at the beginning.

16.text: That's when I remembered what the Lord said: 'John baptized with water, but y'all gon' be baptized with the Holy Spirit.'

17.text: So if God gave them the same gift He gave us when we believed in the Lord Jesus, who was I to try and block what God was doin'?"

18.text: When the crew heard all that, they fell silent. Then they started praisin' God like, "Wow… so God really gave the Gentiles the chance to repent and get eternal life too!"

19.text: Now after Stephen got killed, the heat turned up, and the believers got scattered. Some of them ended up in Phoenicia, Cyprus, and Antioch—but they was only preachin' to Jews.

20.text: But a few of them, men from Cyprus and Cyrene, came to Antioch and started preachin' Jesus to the Greeks too.

21.text: And God's hand was all over it. A whole bunch of folks believed and turned their lives over to the Lord.

22.text: Word got back to the church in Jerusalem, so they sent Barnabas to go check it out in Antioch.

23.text: When he got there and saw God's grace all over them people, he got hype and encouraged them to keep pushin' with purpose and stay close to the Lord.

24.text: Barnabas was solid—good man, full of the Holy Spirit and faith—and a whole crowd of folks got saved.

25.text: Then Barnabas left Antioch to go find Saul in Tarsus.

26.text: When he found him, he brought him back to Antioch. For a whole year, they stayed with the church there, teachin' crowds of folks. And it was in Antioch that people started callin' the disciples "Christians" for the first time.

27.text: Around that time, some prophets came down from Jerusalem to Antioch.

28.text: One of them—named Agabus—got up and gave a word from the Holy Spirit. He said a huge famine was coming all across the world. (That famine hit during Claudius Caesar's rule.)

29.text: So the disciples, each one giving what they could, decided to send support to the believers in Judea.

30.text: And they followed through—sent it by the hands of Barnabas and Saul, straight to the elders.

1.text: Around this time, King Herod got bold and started goin' after folks in the church.

2.text: He had James, John's brother, killed with a sword—just like that.

3.text: And when he saw that it made the Jewish leaders happy, he went ahead and snatched Peter too. This was during the Feast of Unleavened Bread.

4.text: He had Peter locked up, posted four squads of soldiers on him, and planned to bring him out for public trial after Passover.

5.text: So Peter was locked up, but the church was prayin' hard for him.

6.text: The night before Herod was gonna bring him out, Peter was sleepin', chained up between two guards, and more soldiers were on watch outside.

7.text: Then boom—an angel of the Lord popped up, and the whole cell lit up. The angel nudged Peter, told him, "Get up quick." And the chains just fell off.

8.text: The angel said, "Get dressed. Tie your sandals." Peter did it. Then the angel said, "Put your cloak on and follow me."

9.text: Peter followed, but he thought it was all a dream. Like, "Ain't no way this real."

10.text: They walked past the first and second sets of guards, then came to the iron gate to the city—and that gate opened by itself 👀. They stepped out, hit one street, and the angel dipped.

11.text: Peter snapped out of it like, "Yo, this really happened. The Lord sent His angel and got me outta Herod's hands and away from what they was tryna do."

12.text: He pulled up at Mary's house—John Mark's mama—where folks were still prayin'.

13.text: He knocked on the door, and a girl named Rhoda came to answer.

14.text: She heard Peter's voice and got so hype she ran back to tell the others—but forgot to open the door! 😂

15.text: They said, "Girl, you trippin'." But she kept insisting. So they said, "Must be his angel or somethin'."

16.text: Meanwhile, Peter still knockin'. When they finally opened the door and saw him, they were shook.

17.text: He waved for 'em to chill and told the whole story—how God busted him out. Then he said, "Go tell James and the others," and dipped to lay low somewhere else.

18.text: Next morning, the prison was in chaos. Soldiers were like, "Where he at?!"

19.text: Herod did a full search, couldn't find Peter, and ended up killin' the guards over it. Then he went to chill in Caesarea.

20.text: Now Herod was beefin' with Tyre and Sidon. But they squashed it through his aide Blastus 'cause they needed his food supply.

21.text: On the set day, Herod came out in royal drip, sat on his throne, and gave a whole speech.

22.text: The crowd started wildin': "That ain't a man talkin', that's a god!"

23.text: But Herod didn't give God the glory. So an angel popped him this time. He got struck down, eaten by worms, and died. Nasty way to go.

24.text: But God's Word? It kept spreadin' and growin'.

25.text: When Barnabas and Saul finished their mission in Jerusalem, they headed back and brought John Mark along with them.

1.text: Over in Antioch, the church had some real ones—prophets and teachers like Barnabas, Simeon (aka Niger), Lucius from Cyrene, Manaen (who grew up with Herod), and Saul.

2.text: While they was worshippin' and fasting, the Holy Spirit said, "Aye, set apart Barnabas and Saul—I got a mission for 'em."

3.text: So they fasted, prayed, laid hands on them, and sent them out.

4.text: They left, led by the Holy Spirit, and headed down to Seleucia, then sailed to Cyprus.

5.text: When they got to Salamis, they hit the synagogues first and preached the Word to the Jews. John (aka Mark) came along to help.

6.text: They worked their way across the island and ran into this fake prophet named Bar-Jesus, a Jewish dude into sorcery.

7.text: He was tight with the governor, Sergius Paulus—a smart man who actually wanted to hear God's Word.

8.text: But Bar-Jesus (also called Elymas) tried blockin' it, tryna get in the way of the gospel.

9.text: That's when Saul (now called Paul), filled with the Spirit, locked eyes on him and said,

10.text: "You slick, lyin' fraud—straight up child of the devil, enemy to everything right. You really think you can twist God's plan?

11.text: Nah, God's hand is on you now. You gon' be blind for a minute—won't even see daylight." And boom—dude went blind. Fog hit his eyes and he had to get led around like a lost child.

12.text: When the governor saw that, he believed. He was blown away by the power and truth of what Paul was teachin'.

13.text: Then Paul and crew left Paphos, hit Perga in Pamphylia, but John Mark dipped and went back to Jerusalem.

14.text: The rest of them went on to Antioch in Pisidia and slid into the synagogue on the Sabbath.

15.text: After the readings, the synagogue leaders was like, "Y'all got a word for us?"

16.text: Paul stood up, waved to get their attention, and said: "Listen up, family—Jews and God-fearin' folks:

17.text: God chose our ancestors, lifted us up while we were strangers in Egypt, and brought us out with a strong hand.

18.text: For 40 years He dealt with us in the wilderness (yeah, He had patience).

19.text: Then He cleared out seven nations in Canaan and gave us the land.

20.text: After that, He gave us judges for 450 years—up until Samuel.

21.text: Then the people asked for a king, so He gave 'em Saul.

22.text: But Saul got removed, and David was next. God said, 'I found David, a man after My own heart, who gon' do all I say.'

23.text: From David's family line, God brought us Jesus—the Savior He promised.

24.text: John the Baptist came first, preachin' repentance before Jesus showed up.

25.text: And John was clear: 'Don't get it twisted—I'm not Him. The real One is comin' right after me, and I ain't even worthy to untie His kicks.'

26.text: So to y'all—Abraham's kids and everybody who fears God—this Word of salvation is for you.

27.text: The folks in Jerusalem didn't recognize Jesus, or the prophecies they read every Sabbath. So they fulfilled those prophecies by condemning Him.

28.text: They couldn't even find a reason to execute Him, but still begged Pilate to do it.

29.text: After it all happened just like the Scriptures said, they took Him down from the cross and buried Him.

30.text: But God raised Him from the dead.

31.text: And He didn't just vanish—He appeared for days to those of us who traveled with Him. We saw Him, ate with Him—we testifyin' about it now.

32.text: What we're tellin' y'all is the Good News—God kept His promise.

33.text: He fulfilled it by raisin' Jesus up. Like Psalm 2 says: 'You are My Son. Today I have begotten You.'

34.text: He ain't goin' back to the grave, just like God promised: 'I'll give you the blessings I gave David.'

35.text: And in another Psalm: 'You won't let Your Holy One see decay.'

36.text: David served his time, died, and was buried. His body decayed like everybody else's.

37.text: But Jesus? Raised up. No decay. No rot.

38.text: So know this: through Jesus, we got forgiveness of sins.

39.text: Anyone who believes in Him is cleared of guilt—stuff the law of Moses couldn't do.

40.text: Don't sleep on this. Prophets already warned:

41.text: 'Look, you doubters—y'all gon' see somethin' so wild, you won't believe it even if someone told you upfront.'"

42.text: After the sermon, the Jews were headin' out, and the Gentiles was like, "Y'all gotta come back next Sabbath."

43.text: A lotta Jews and converts followed Paul and Barnabas, and they told 'em, "Stay strong in God's grace."

44.text: Next Sabbath? The whole city showed up.

45.text: But the Jews saw the crowd and got salty. Started talkin' reckless and tryna shut Paul down.

46.text: Paul and Barnabas didn't flinch. They said, "We had to give y'all first dibs on the Word. But y'all rejected it and showed y'all ain't about eternal life. So guess what? We takin' it to the Gentiles.

47.text: God told us: 'I made you a light to the nations—so you can bring salvation everywhere.'"

48.text: The Gentiles heard that and lit up. They praised the Word and believed—everybody who was meant to receive it.

49.text: The gospel spread all over the region.

50.text: But the Jewish leaders stirred up the elite women and men in the city, caused drama, and had Paul and Barnabas kicked out.

51.text: So they dusted their feet off and rolled out to Iconium.

52.text: But the believers? They stayed full of joy and the Holy Spirit.

1.text: Paul and Barnabas pulled up in Iconium, went to the synagogue like usual, and spoke with so much truth and power that a big crowd—both Jews and Greeks—ended up believin'.

2.text: But the Jews who ain't believe started stirrin' up drama. They got in the Gentiles' ears and turned them against the brothers.

3.text: Paul and Barnabas didn't back down—they stayed a while, speakin' boldly about the Lord. God backed up their words too, showin' out with signs and miracles through their hands.

4.text: The city got split. Some folks were ridin' with the Jews, others were team Paul and Barnabas.

5.text: Then some of the Jews and Gentiles, along with their leaders, plotted to jump 'em—tryin' to stone them to death.

6.text: When Paul and Barnabas got word of it, they dipped out to Lystra and Derbe in Lycaonia, hittin' the smaller towns in the area too.

7.text: And they didn't stop—they kept preachin' the gospel everywhere they landed.

8.text: In Lystra, they came across this man who had never walked a day in his life—crippled since birth.

9.text: He was listenin' to Paul preach, and Paul locked eyes on him. He could see the man had real faith to be healed.

10.text: So Paul spoke up loud: "Stand up straight on your feet!" The man jumped up and started walkin' like it was nothin'.

11.text: When the crowd saw that miracle, they wilded out. They started shoutin' in their own language, "The gods came down to us lookin' like men!"

12.text: They called Barnabas "Zeus" and Paul "Hermes" 'cause Paul was the main one talkin'.

13.text: The priest from the temple of Zeus even brought oxen and garlands to the city gates tryna offer sacrifices to Paul and Barnabas.

14.text: When they realized what was goin' on, Paul and Barnabas tore their clothes like, "Nah, y'all trippin'!"

15.text: They ran into the crowd shoutin', "Y'all, why y'all doin' this? We just people, just like you. We here to tell y'all to leave these dead idols alone and turn to the living God—

16.text: the same One who made heaven, earth, sea, and everything in 'em. Back in the day, He let nations do they own thing,

17.text: but even then, He left proof of Himself—like blessin' y'all with rain, good seasons, food, and joy in your lives."

18.text: Even after sayin' all that, it was hard to stop the crowd from goin' ahead with the sacrifice.

19.text: But then some Jews rolled up from Antioch and Iconium and flipped the whole crowd against them. They dragged Paul outta the city and stoned him. Thought he was dead.

20.text: But the disciples circled around him, and next thing you know—Paul stood up. Went right back into the city. Next day, he and Barnabas headed to Derbe.

21.text: They preached the good news in Derbe too, makin' a gang of new disciples. Then they circled back through Lystra, Iconium, and Antioch—

22.text: liftin' up the believers, encouragin' 'em to stay strong in the faith, and remindin' them: "We gotta go through a lot to get into the kingdom of God."

23.text: In every church, they raised up elders—after prayin' and fastin', they placed them in God's hands, trustin' the Lord they believed in.

24.text: Then they kept it movin'—passin' through Pisidia and comin' to Pamphylia.

25.text: They preached again in Perga, then went down to Attalia.

26.text: From there, they sailed back to Antioch—where the church had first sent them out, trustin' God to use them. And now? Mission complete.

27.text: When they got back, they gathered the whole church together and told 'em all God had done through them—how God had opened the door of faith to the Gentiles.

28.text: Paul and Barnabas stayed there for a good while, chillin' with the disciples and pourin' into the people.

1.text: Some folks came down from Judea tellin' the believers, "Y'all ain't really saved unless y'all get circumcised like Moses told us."

2.text: That sparked a whole argument. Paul and Barnabas weren't havin' it. It got heated. So they decided to send Paul, Barnabas, and some others to Jerusalem to bring this up with the apostles and elders.

3.text: On the way there, they passed through Phoenicia and Samaria, tellin' folks how the Gentiles were turnin' to God—and that brought everybody so much joy.

4.text: When they got to Jerusalem, the church family welcomed them in—apostles, elders, all of 'em. Paul and Barnabas shared everything God had done through them.

5.text: But then some believers from the Pharisee crew stood up like, "Nah, they still need to get circumcised and follow Moses' law."

6.text: So the apostles and elders met up to hash it all out.

7.text: After folks debated for a while, Peter stood up and said, "Y'all already know God chose me to be the one to bring the gospel to the Gentiles. And guess what? They believed.

8.text: God, who sees people's hearts, gave them the Holy Spirit just like He did us.

9.text: He didn't treat them any different—He cleaned their hearts through faith.

10.text: So why y'all tryna test God, puttin' a burden on them that we couldn't even handle ourselves?

11.text: We believe we all saved the same way—by the grace of the Lord Jesus, period."

12.text: The room got quiet. Then Paul and Barnabas got up and told all the miracles and signs God was doin' among the Gentiles through them. Folks were listenin'.

13.text: When they finished, James stood up: "Listen, fam.

14.text: Simon (Peter) already told us how God made the first move to bring Gentiles into His people.

15.text: The prophets been sayin' this too. Just like it's written:

16.text: 'I'm comin' back to rebuild David's broken-down house. I'ma fix it up.

17.text: So that everybody else—even Gentiles who call on My name—can seek Me.'

18.text: God been had this plan.

19.text: So here's what I think—we shouldn't make it hard for Gentiles who are turnin' to God.

20.text: Let's just ask them to stay away from idols, sexual sin, meat from strangled animals, and blood.

21.text: Folks been preachin' Moses every Sabbath for generations—they know the basics."

22.text: Everybody—apostles, elders, the whole church—agreed to send some brothers back to Antioch with Paul and Barnabas. They picked Judas (aka Barsabas) and Silas, both respected leaders.

23.text: They sent a letter: "From the apostles, elders, and brothers— To the Gentile believers in Antioch, Syria, and Cilicia: Peace to y'all.

24.text: We heard that some folks came out from us talkin' out the side of their necks, makin' y'all confused and scared, tellin' y'all to get circumcised. We didn't tell them to say that.

25.text: So we all agreed to send some real ones—Barnabas and Paul, our beloved brothers,

26.text: who put their lives on the line for Jesus.

27.text: We sendin' Judas and Silas with them to confirm what we say in person.

28.text: It seemed good to the Holy Spirit—and to us—not to burden y'all with a bunch of rules. Just keep these essentials:

29.text: Don't eat food sacrificed to idols. Don't mess with blood. Don't eat anything strangled. And keep it clean sexually. If you do that, you'll be good. Stay up."

30.text: They left Jerusalem and went to Antioch. Once the church there got the letter, they pulled everybody together and read it out loud.

31.text: The whole squad was hyped—it was encouraging news.

32.text: Judas and Silas, who were prophets too, spoke powerfully to strengthen and uplift the people.

33.text: After some time, they went back with blessings and peace from Antioch to Jerusalem.

34.text: (But Silas felt led to stay a while longer.)

35.text: Paul and Barnabas stayed put too, teachin' and preachin' the Word of the Lord with others in Antioch.

36.text: A little later, Paul told Barnabas, "Let's go back and check on all the cities we preached in—see how everybody doin'."

37.text: Barnabas wanted to bring John Mark with them.

38.text: But Paul wasn't feelin' it—Mark had bailed on them before in Pamphylia, and he didn't wanna take someone who quit on the mission.

39.text: The disagreement got real tense. They ended up partin' ways. Barnabas took Mark and went to Cyprus,

40.text: but Paul chose Silas, and the believers prayed over him, sending him out under God's grace.

41.text: He went through Syria and Cilicia, strengthening the churches along the way.

1.text: Paul pulled up to Derbe and Lystra. That's where he met this young dude named Timothy. His mama was a Jewish believer, but his pops was Greek.

2.text: Folks in both Lystra and Iconium was speakin' highly of Timothy.

3.text: Paul saw somethin' in him and wanted him to roll with them. But first, Paul had him circumcised since the Jews in that area knew Timothy's daddy was Greek.

4.text: As they moved from city to city, they delivered the decisions from the apostles and elders back in Jerusalem—stuff the churches needed to follow.

5.text: All them churches got stronger in the faith, and more and more people was joinin' every day.

6.text: While they was movin' through Phrygia and Galatia, the Holy Spirit told them, "Nah, y'all ain't preachin' in Asia right now."

7.text: When they hit Mysia and tried to go into Bithynia, the Spirit was like, "Nope, not there either."

8.text: So they kept it pushin' to Troas.

9.text: That night, Paul had a vision—a man from Macedonia was beggin' him, "Come help us, bro!"

10.text: Soon as Paul woke up, they knew it was God callin' them to go bring the gospel to Macedonia. No hesitation.

11.text: They sailed from Troas, hit Samothrace, and then landed in Neapolis the next day.

12.text: From there, they slid over to Philippi, a major city in Macedonia. They chilled there for a few days.

13.text: On the Sabbath, they stepped outside the city near the river, where folks usually prayed. They sat down and started choppin' it up with the women there.

14.text: One of them was Lydia, a seller of purple cloth from Thyatira. She feared God, and the Lord opened her heart to really hear what Paul was sayin'.

15.text: After she and her whole household got baptized, she said, "If y'all think I'm really down with the Lord, come stay at my place." And she convinced 'em.

16.text: One day on the way to prayer, they ran into this young girl who was possessed with a spirit that let her tell fortunes. She was makin' bank for her masters.

17.text: She kept followin' Paul and the crew, shoutin', "These men serve the Most High God—they tellin' y'all how to get saved!"

18.text: She did this for days. Finally, Paul got fed up and said to the spirit, "In Jesus' name, come outta her!" And boom—it left her right then and there.

19.text: Her owners got tight when they saw the money flow dry up. They snatched up Paul and Silas and dragged 'em to the town square to face the authorities.

20.text: They told the judges, "These Jewish dudes messin' up the city,

21.text: teachin' illegal stuff that we Romans ain't tryna hear or follow."

22.text: A whole crowd turned on Paul and Silas. The officials had their clothes ripped off and ordered them beat with rods.

23.text: After they got beat bad, they were thrown into jail. The jailer got strict orders to keep 'em locked tight.

24.text: So he threw 'em in the deepest part of the prison and chained up their feet.

25.text: Around midnight, Paul and Silas was singin' hymns and prayin' loud enough for the whole jail to hear.

26.text: Outta nowhere, a huge earthquake hit—the whole spot shook. Every door flew open, and the chains just fell off everybody.

27.text: The jailer woke up, saw the doors wide open, and thought everybody dipped. He pulled out his sword, ready to end it all.

28.text: But Paul shouted, "Don't do it! We all still here!"

29.text: The jailer called for some light, ran in, and dropped to his knees in front of Paul and Silas, shakin'.

30.text: He pulled them out and asked, "What do I gotta do to be saved?"

31.text: They said, "Believe in the Lord Jesus, and you'll be saved—you and your whole fam."

32.text: Then they broke down the Word to him and everybody in his house.

33.text: Right that same hour, he cleaned up their wounds. And just like that, he and his whole household got baptized.

34.text: He brought them to his home, fed them, and was filled with joy 'cause him and his fam believed in God now.

35.text: When the sun came up, the officials sent word: "Let them men go."

36.text: The jailer told Paul, "They said y'all can leave now. Go in peace."

37.text: But Paul was like, "Hold up. They beat us in public without a trial—us Roman citizens—and tossed us in jail. Now they wanna send us off quietly? Nah. They need to come apologize in person."

38.text: The officers went back and told the officials what Paul said. When they heard these dudes were Romans, they got shook.

39.text: They came down, apologized, brought them out, and begged them to please leave town.

40.text: Paul and Silas left the jail and slid over to Lydia's house. They linked up with the believers there, gave them some encouragement, and kept it movin'.

1.text: After leavin' Amphipolis and Apollonia, Paul and them touched down in Thessalonica, where there was a synagogue full of Jews.

2.text: As usual, Paul pulled up in there and for three Sabbaths straight, he broke down Scripture, reasonin' with 'em.

3.text: He was explainin' and provin' that the Messiah had to suffer and rise from the dead. Then he hit 'em with the truth: "That Jesus I been preachin' about? He is the Christ."

4.text: Some folks were feelin' it and believed—especially a gang of devout Greek folks and some powerful women. They started rockin' with Paul and Silas.

5.text: But them jealous Jews? They weren't tryin' to hear none of that. So they linked up with some shady dudes from the block, formed a mob, and turned the whole city upside down. Then they stormed Jason's house tryna snatch up Paul and Silas.

6.text: When they couldn't find 'em, they dragged Jason and some other believers to the city leaders like, "Yo! These troublemakers who been flippin' the world upside down? They here now.

7.text: Jason lettin' 'em stay at his spot. And they all out here actin' like there's another king besides Caesar—talkin' about some Jesus."

8.text: The crowd and the officials started wildin' after that.

9.text: But after makin' Jason and the crew pay some bond money, they let 'em go.

10.text: That night, the squad sent Paul and Silas to Berea. First thing they did when they got there? Hit up the synagogue.

11.text: These Bereans, though? They was built different. Way more open-minded than the folks in Thessalonica. They actually listened and went home to fact-check the Scriptures daily to see if what Paul said was true.

12.text: Because of that, a lot of them believed—both Greek women and men with influence.

13.text: But them haters from Thessalonica found out Paul was preachin' in Berea too, so they pulled up just to stir up trouble again.

14.text: The squad had to send Paul away quick—toward the coast. Silas and Timothy stayed behind.

15.text: Paul's escort took him to Athens, and before they dipped, Paul told 'em, "Tell Silas and Timothy I need them here ASAP."

16.text: While Paul was waitin' in Athens, he was lowkey stressed out. The city was full of idols.

17.text: So he started choppin' it up in the synagogue with Jews and Gentile worshippers, and in the marketplace with whoever would listen.

18.text: Some philosophers—Epicureans and Stoics—ran into him and were like, "What is this dude even talkin' about?" Others said, "He sound like he preachin' about some foreign gods." That's 'cause Paul was goin' hard about Jesus and the resurrection.

19.text: So they took him to the Areopagus, sayin', "Aight bruh, break this new teaching down for us.

20.text: You sayin' stuff we never heard before, and we tryna understand what it means."

21.text: Side note: Them Athenians and foreigners in the city ain't do nothin' but sit around choppin' it up about new ideas all day.

22.text: Paul stood in the middle of the Areopagus like, "Y'all real religious out here—I see it.

23.text: As I was walkin' around lookin' at y'all altars, I peeped one that said: TO THE UNKNOWN GOD. Well guess what? That God y'all don't even know? I'm here to tell you about Him.

24.text: He the one who made the whole world and everything in it. Lord of heaven and earth. He don't need no man-made temple to chill in.

25.text: And He don't need nothin' from us. He the one who give us life, breath, and everything else.

26.text: From one blood, He made all nations and set their times and where they live.

27.text: Why? So folks would reach out, feel after Him, and maybe find Him—though He ain't far from none of us.

28.text: 'Cause in Him we live, move, and exist. Like some of y'all poets said, 'We His offspring.'

29.text: So if we God's kids, why we think God is some statue made of gold or silver or stone? Like He just some art project or man-made idea? Nah.

30.text: Back then, God let that ignorance slide. But now? He callin' everybody, everywhere to repent.

31.text: 'Cause He already set the date to judge the world right. And He gonna do it through the Man He appointed. And He proved it to everybody by raisin' Him from the dead."

32.text: When they heard Paul talkin' resurrection, some folks laughed like, "Boy, if you don't get…" Others were like, "This man lowkey spittin'. We wanna hear more later."

33.text: Paul dipped after that,

34.text: but a few folks linked up with him and believed—like Dionysius the Areopagite, a woman named Damaris, and some others.

1.text: After all that, Paul left Athens and headed to Corinth.

2.text: There, he met a Jewish brother named Aquila, from Pontus, who had just moved from Italy with his wife Priscilla—they left because Claudius had kicked all the Jews outta Rome. Paul linked up with them.

3.text: Since they all worked the same hustle—tentmaking—Paul moved in and worked with them while he preached.

4.text: Every Sabbath, he pulled up at the synagogue and broke the Word down to both Jews and Greeks, tryin' to persuade them.

5.text: When Silas and Timothy came down from Macedonia, Paul turned it all the way up—he was led by the Spirit and started fully testifying to the Jews that Jesus is the Christ.

6.text: But when they rejected him and started disrespectin' the name, Paul dusted off his clothes and said, "That's on y'all now. I did my part. From here on out, I'm takin' this Word to the Gentiles."

7.text: He left and went next door—literally—to a man named Justus, who worshipped God.

8.text: And wouldn't you know it—Crispus, the leader of that same synagogue, believed in the Lord—him and his whole family. A bunch of folks in Corinth started believing and got baptized too.

9.text: One night, the Lord came to Paul in a vision and said, "Don't be scared. Speak up. Don't hold back.

10.text: I got you. Nobody in this city gonna lay a hand on you. I got people here—you don't even know."

11.text: So Paul stayed put for a year and six months, teachin' God's Word steady.

12.text: When Gallio became the governor of Achaia, the Jews got bold again. They united and dragged Paul to court.

13.text: They said, "This man is persuadin' people to worship God in a way that breaks our law."

14.text: Paul was about to speak up for himself, but Gallio cut in like, "Look, if this was about an actual crime or serious wrong, I'd listen.

15.text: But this? Just arguments about words, names, and your own law? That ain't my business. Y'all handle it."

16.text: Then he kicked them out the courtroom.

17.text: And right after that, the crowd grabbed Sosthenes—the synagogue leader—and beat him up in front of the courthouse. Gallio ain't even flinch. Didn't get involved.

18.text: Paul stayed in Corinth a little while longer, then said goodbye to the believers and set sail for Syria, takin' Priscilla and Aquila with him. He had his hair cut off in Cenchrea, 'cause he had taken a vow.

19.text: They stopped in Ephesus. Paul went to the synagogue and reasoned with the Jews again.

20.text: They asked him to stay longer, but he said no.

21.text: He told them, "I gotta hit Jerusalem for the upcoming feast, but God willing, I'll be back." Then he left Ephesus.

22.text: When he landed at Caesarea, he went up to greet the church, then traveled down to Antioch.

23.text: After chillin' there for a bit, Paul hit the road again—through Galatia and Phrygia, strengthening all the believers along the way.

24.text: Meanwhile, a brother named Apollos came to Ephesus. He was a Jewish man from Alexandria—eloquent, smart, and strong in the Scriptures.

25.text: He had been taught about Jesus and was passionate when he spoke—he taught what he knew accurately, but he only knew about John's baptism.

26.text: He started preachin' bold in the synagogue. But when Priscilla and Aquila heard him, they pulled him to the side and broke it down more clearly—taught him the whole way of God.

27.text: When Apollos wanted to go to Achaia, the believers encouraged him and wrote a letter tellin' the folks there to welcome him. When he showed up, he was a huge help to those who had already believed by grace.

28.text: He was no joke—Apollos shut down the Jewish opposition in public, breakin' it down from the Scriptures that Jesus is the Christ.

1.text: While Apollos was out in Corinth, Paul came through the upper regions and touched down in Ephesus. He met some disciples there,

2.text: and asked 'em, "Y'all get the Holy Spirit when y'all believed?" They was like, "Man, we don't even know what that is."

3.text: Paul said, "Okay, then what kinda baptism y'all get?" They said, "John's."

4.text: Paul broke it down: "John baptized folks to get they hearts right—he told 'em to believe in the One comin' after him. That One is Jesus."

5.text: Soon as they heard that, they got baptized in Jesus' name,

6.text: and when Paul laid hands on 'em, the Holy Spirit came through heavy. They started speakin' in tongues and prophesyin'.

7.text: It was about twelve dudes altogether.

8.text: Paul started preachin' bold in the synagogue for three months, tryna convince folks about God's kingdom.

9.text: But some folks got hard-hearted, didn't believe, and started bad-mouthin' the Way in public. So Paul said, "Bet," took the disciples, and started teachin' daily in Tyrannus's lecture hall.

10.text: This went on for two years, and everybody in Asia—Jews and Greeks—got to hear the word about the Lord.

11.text: God started doin' some wild miracles through Paul.

12.text: Like, folks was takin' handkerchiefs and aprons that touched Paul's skin, and just by touchin' sick people, they got healed and demons dipped out.

13.text: Then some Jewish exorcists tried to get in on it, sayin', "We cast you out in the name of that Jesus that Paul talks about."

14.text: These dudes was the seven sons of Sceva, a Jewish high priest.

15.text: But the evil spirit clapped back, "Jesus I know. Paul I recognize. But who is you?"

16.text: Then the man with the demon jumped on all seven of 'em, beat 'em down, and had 'em runnin' out naked and bloody.

17.text: Word spread through Ephesus—Jews and Greeks alike—and folks got shook. Jesus' name got real respected after that.

18.text: Folks who had already believed started comin' forward, confessin' and tellin' what they was into.

19.text: A bunch of folks who used to do magic pulled up with their spell books and set 'em on fire right in front of everybody. Them books was worth 50,000 silver coins.

20.text: The Word of the Lord spread like wildfire and kept winnin'.

21.text: After all that, Paul felt the Spirit nudgin' him. He said, "I'm finna go through Macedonia and Achaia, then hit Jerusalem. And after that? Rome."

22.text: He sent Timothy and Erastus on ahead to Macedonia, but stayed in Asia a lil longer.

23.text: Not too long after that, drama popped off over the Way.

24.text: A dude named Demetrius, who made silver shrines for the goddess Diana, was makin' bank off his idol business.

25.text: He called up his fellow craftsmen and said, "Y'all know our bread come from this hustle.

26.text: But look—this man Paul out here sayin' gods made by hands ain't really gods. And he ain't just sayin' it here in Ephesus—he got folks all over Asia changin' up!"

27.text: "If this keeps up, not only will our business tank, but people gon' stop reverin' Diana—the goddess everybody worships."

28.text: The crowd got real mad and started chantin', "Great is Diana of the Ephesians!"

29.text: The whole city got swept up and rushed into the theater, draggin' Gaius and Aristarchus, Paul's people.

30.text: Paul tried to go in too, but the disciples held him back like, "Nah, bro, not today."

31.text: Even some government officials who rocked with Paul hit him up like, "Don't go in there, they wildin'."

32.text: The whole crowd was confused—folks yellin' different stuff, half of 'em didn't even know why they was there.

33.text: Then some Jews pushed Alexander forward to talk. He tried to calm the crowd,

34.text: but when they realized he was Jewish, they shouted for two whole hours, "Great is Diana of the Ephesians!"

35.text: Finally, the city clerk calmed folks down: "Y'all... everybody know Ephesus guards Diana's temple and her statue from Zeus.
