36.text: Since that's facts, y'all need to chill. Don't act reckless.

37.text: These men ain't robbed the temple or disrespected the goddess.

38.text: If Demetrius and his crew got beef, the courts are open. Go handle that legal-like.

39.text: If it's somethin' else, wait for the proper assembly.

40.text: We outta pocket right now, and Rome might come askin' questions we can't answer."

41.text: Then he shut it all down and dismissed the crowd.

1.text: After all that chaos died down, Paul got the disciples together, gave 'em a big ol' hug, and hit the road for Macedonia.

2.text: He slid through the region, encouragin' the people with deep words. Then he made his way to Greece,

3.text: and stayed there three months. But just when he was 'bout to hop on a boat to Syria, some hatin' Jews plotted on him, so he switched it up and went back through Macedonia.

4.text: He had a whole crew rollin' with him: Sopater from Berea, Aristarchus and Secundus from Thessalonica, Gaius from Derbe, Timothy, and two dudes from Asia—Tychicus and Trophimus.

5.text: They went ahead to Troas and waited on us there,

6.text: while we left Philippi after the Feast of Unleavened Bread, met up with them in five days, and chilled in Troas for a whole week.

7.text: On Sunday, we all got together to break bread. Paul was leavin' the next day, so he preached—and y'all, he kept goin' till midnight.

8.text: The room was lit up with lamps, everybody gathered in this third-floor spot.

9.text: This one young dude named Eutychus was sittin' in the window. He started noddin' off hard, and then BAM—he fell straight out the window from the third floor. Dead.

10.text: Paul ran down, threw himself on the boy and said, "Chill, y'all—he still got life in him."

11.text: Then Paul went back upstairs, ate, talked some more until sunrise (man don't stop), and then finally dipped.

12.text: They brought Eutychus back alive, and everybody was shook—but thankful.

13.text: We went ahead on the boat to Assos, where Paul said he'd meet us—he walked it out instead.

14.text: When he linked back up with us, we boarded and hit Mitylene.

15.text: Next day, we passed Chios, then Samos, stayed a minute in Trogyllium, and then made it to Miletus.

16.text: Paul skipped Ephesus this time—he was on a deadline tryna make it to Jerusalem for Pentecost.

17.text: From Miletus, Paul sent word for the elders in Ephesus to pull up.

18.text: When they got there, he said: "Y'all know how I been livin' since day one—

19.text: I served the Lord humble, with tears, even while folks was out here plottin'.

20.text: I ain't hold back nothin'. I told y'all everything that would help—whether it was out in the streets or inside y'all's homes.

21.text: I told both Jews and Greeks to turn to God and believe in Jesus."

22.text: "Now the Spirit got me headed to Jerusalem, and I don't know what's waiting on me—

23.text: except every city I go, the Holy Spirit keep warnin' me: 'Chains and pain ahead.'

24.text: But I ain't pressed. I just wanna finish my race strong, and do what Jesus told me to—spread the good news of God's grace."

25.text: "Truth is, I know this is goodbye. Ain't none of y'all gon' see me again.

26.text: But I want y'all to know—I ain't got no blood on my hands.

27.text: I gave y'all the whole truth, not just the feel-good parts."

28.text: "So y'all better watch over yourselves and the flock. The Holy Spirit picked y'all to be leaders, to guard God's people—His church, the one He paid for with His own blood.

29.text: 'Cause once I'm gone, some savage wolves gon' pull up and won't care who they hurt.

30.text: Even some of y'all gon' switch up, sayin' wild stuff just to get followers."

31.text: "So stay on alert. Y'all remember—I was out here day and night, cryin' while warnin' folks for three years straight.

32.text: Now I leave y'all in God's hands and in His word, which will build y'all up and give y'all a place with the holy ones.

33.text: I wasn't out here beggin' for y'all's money or clothes.

34.text: Y'all saw me—these hands fed me and my people.

35.text: I was showin' y'all how to grind and help the weak. Remember what Jesus said: 'It's more blessed to give than to receive.'"

36.text: When Paul finished, he dropped to his knees and prayed with 'em all.

37.text: They all cried hard, hugged on him tight, kissed him like family.

38.text: What hit them hardest? He said they'd never see him again. They walked him down to the boat... hearts heavy.

1.text: So after we said our goodbyes, we hit the water and sailed straight to Cos, then the next day to Rhodes, and from there to Patara.

2.text: We found a ship headin' to Phoenicia, hopped on, and kept it movin'.

3.text: We passed Cyprus on our left, made it to Syria, and docked at Tyre so the ship could unload cargo.

4.text: While we was there, we found some disciples and stayed with 'em for a whole week. They kept tellin' Paul through the Spirit, "Don't go to Jerusalem, bruh."

5.text: But once the week was up, we hit the road again. The whole crew—wives, kids and all—walked us out the city. We all got on our knees by the water and prayed together.

6.text: After hugs and goodbyes, we got on the boat. They went back home.

7.text: We finished that leg in Ptolemais, greeted the fam there, and stayed for a day.

8.text: The next day we rolled out to Caesarea and stayed with Philip the Evangelist—yeah, that same Philip from back in the day, one of the Seven.

9.text: Bro had four daughters, all of 'em virgins, and all of 'em prophesying.

10.text: After chillin' there for some days, this prophet named Agabus pulled up from Judea.

11.text: Man grabbed Paul's belt, tied up his own hands and feet with it, and said, "The Holy Spirit say: the dude who owns this belt gon' get bound up like this by the Jews in Jerusalem, and handed over to the Gentiles."

12.text: Soon as we heard that, everybody started beggin' Paul not to go.

13.text: But Paul was like, "Y'all cryin' and breakin' my heart. I ain't just ready to be locked up—I'm ready to die in Jerusalem if it's for Jesus."

14.text: When we saw he wasn't gon' change his mind, we stopped pushin' and just said, "Aight then. Let God's will be done."

15.text: After all that, we packed up and headed to Jerusalem.

16.text: Some of the Caesarea disciples came with us and took us to stay with Mnason from Cyprus—he was one of the OG believers.

17.text: When we got to Jerusalem, the fam welcomed us with open arms.

18.text: The next day, Paul went to go holla at James and the elders.

19.text: He gave the whole rundown—everything God had been doin' among the Gentiles through his ministry.

20.text: They was hyped and praised God. But then they hit Paul with, "Look, bruh… there's mad Jewish believers here, and they real serious about the law.

21.text: Word on the street is you tellin' Jews livin' with Gentiles to forget Moses, stop circumcisin' they kids, and ditch the customs.

22.text: So what we gon' do? Folks already know you in town.

23.text: Here's the move—there's four brothas who done took a vow.

24.text: Go with 'em, get purified too, and cover their expenses so they can do what they need to do. That way, folks will see you still respectin' the law.

25.text: As for the Gentile believers, we already sent word sayin' they don't need to do all that—just stay away from food offered to idols, blood, strangled animals, and sexual sin."

26.text: So Paul did what they said. The next day he purified himself with them and went to the temple, lettin' folks know when the vow time would end and sacrifices would be made for all of them.

27.text: But when the seven days were almost up, some Jews from Asia saw Paul in the temple and started a whole scene.

28.text: "Y'all! This the dude preachin' against our people, our law, and this temple everywhere he go! And now he brought a Greek in here too, defilin' this holy place!"

29.text: (They assumed Paul brought Trophimus in 'cause they saw him earlier in the city.)

30.text: That's all it took. The whole city went wild. Folks grabbed Paul, dragged him out, and slammed the temple doors shut.

31.text: They were tryna kill him when word reached the Roman commander that the city was in chaos.

32.text: He rolled up with some soldiers, and soon as the crowd saw them, they stopped beatin' Paul.

33.text: The commander arrested him, threw on two chains, and started askin', "Who is this man? What he do?"

34.text: But the crowd was yellin' all kinds of different stuff—nobody could give a straight answer. So the commander ordered him to be taken to the barracks.

35.text: The mob was so wild, the soldiers had to carry Paul up the stairs.

36.text: Folks were trailin' behind, shoutin', "GET RID OF HIM!"

37.text: Just as they were about to take him inside, Paul said, "Yo, can I talk to you?" The commander said, "You speak Greek?!

38.text: I thought you was that Egyptian who started that rebellion with 4,000 killers in the wilderness."

39.text: Paul said, "Nah, I'm a Jew from Tarsus in Cilicia—real city, not some backwater place. Please, let me talk to the people."

40.text: The commander gave him the green light. So Paul stood on the steps, waved his hand to quiet everybody down, and once it got real silent, he started speakin' to them in Hebrew.

1.text: "Fam, y'all—brothas and fathers—listen up. I'm 'bout to explain myself."

2.text: Soon as they heard Paul speakin' Hebrew, the whole crowd got real quiet.

3.text: He said, "I'm a Jew, born in Tarsus, raised right here in this city. I studied under Gamaliel, got schooled strict in the Law just like y'all. I was deep in it—on fire for God, just like y'all are now.

4.text: I went hard against this Way—had folks locked up, men and women, even had 'em killed.

5.text: The high priest and the elders can vouch for me—I had papers on me from them, went straight to Damascus to snatch up believers and drag 'em back to Jerusalem for punishment."

6.text: "One day around noon, on my way to Damascus, boom—a light from heaven popped off all around me.

7.text: I hit the ground, and I heard a voice say, 'Saul, Saul, why you comin' for Me?'

8.text: I said, 'Who are You, Lord?' And He said, 'I'm Jesus of Nazareth, the one you been goin' after.'

9.text: The folks with me saw the light too—they was shook—but they ain't hear what He told me.

10.text: So I said, 'What You want me to do, Lord?' He said, 'Get up, go to Damascus. You'll get your orders there.'

11.text: I was blinded by that glory light, so the folks with me had to guide me by hand to Damascus."

12.text: "There was this dude named Ananias, solid brother, respected by all the Jews out there, a man of the law.

13.text: He pulled up on me and said, 'Brother Saul, see again.' And just like that, I could see.

14.text: Then he said, 'The God of our ancestors picked you. He want you to know His will, see the Righteous One, and hear His voice.

15.text: You gon' be His witness, tellin' everybody what you saw and heard.

16.text: So what you waitin' on? Get up, get baptized, get them sins washed off, and call on Jesus' name.'"

17.text: "Later on, I came back to Jerusalem and was prayin' in the temple. I caught a vision.

18.text: Jesus told me straight: 'Get outta here quick. These folks ain't gon' listen to what you say about Me.'

19.text: I said, 'Lord, they know how I was—I had Your people beat down and locked up.

20.text: I was right there when Stephen got stoned, noddin' in approval, holdin' the coats for the killers.'

21.text: But Jesus said, 'Leave. I'm sendin' you far off—to the Gentiles.'"

22.text: That was the last straw. The crowd lost it. "Get rid of him! He don't deserve to breathe!"

23.text: They was shoutin', throwin' off they cloaks, flingin' dust in the air like it was a riot.

24.text: The commander was like, "We gotta get this man inside and find out what's up." He ordered Paul to get whooped till he talked.

25.text: But while they was tyin' him up, Paul turned to the centurion and said, "Yo… y'all really gon' beat a Roman citizen who ain't even been found guilty yet?"

26.text: That made the soldier pause. He ran to the commander: "Sir… we gotta be careful. Dude is Roman."

27.text: The commander pulled up and asked Paul, "Is that true? You Roman?" Paul said, "Yeah."

28.text: The commander said, "Man, it cost me a whole bag to get my citizenship." Paul said, "I ain't pay for mine—I was born with it."

29.text: Soon as they heard that, the squad backed up real quick. Even the commander got nervous—he had Paul chained up not knowin' he was Roman.

30.text: The next day, the commander still ain't know why the Jews was goin' so hard on Paul. So he called in the chief priests and the full council. He had Paul brought in, ready to stand before them all.

1.text: Paul locked eyes with the council and said, "Look, fam—I been movin' right with God this whole time. My conscience clean."

2.text: The high priest Ananias wasn't feelin' that and told somebody nearby, "Smack him in the mouth!"

3.text: Paul snapped, "God gon' smack you, bruh. You a fake wall—lookin' holy on the outside but dirty underneath. You sittin' up here actin' like a judge by the law, but then tellin' folks to hit me against the law?"

4.text: The folks near him said, "Yo! You talkin' reckless to God's high priest?"

5.text: Paul said, "My bad, fam—I ain't know he was the high priest. The Word do say, 'Don't bad-mouth your leaders.' I'll respect that."

6.text: Then Paul peeped game: part of the council was Sadducees, part was Pharisees. So he played it smart and said, "Look, y'all—I'm a Pharisee, son of a Pharisee! I'm on trial today 'cause I believe in the resurrection of the dead!"

7.text: Soon as he said that, the room blew up—Pharisees vs. Sadducees went at it.

8.text: (Sadducees don't believe in resurrection, angels, or spirits—Pharisees believe in all that.)

9.text: Folks was shoutin'. Pharisee scribes even said, "We don't see no wrong in this man! What if he really heard from an angel or somethin'? We betta not be fightin' God."

10.text: It got so wild, the commander was scared they'd tear Paul apart. He had the soldiers rush in, grab Paul, and get him outta there back to the barracks.

11.text: That night, Jesus pulled up on Paul and said, "Keep ya head up, Paul. You repped Me in Jerusalem. Now it's time for you to speak on My name in Rome too."

12.text: Next morning, a crew of Jewish men got together, swearin' on everything—they wasn't eatin' or drinkin' till Paul was dead.

13.text: There was more than forty of 'em in the crew.

14.text: They pulled up on the religious leaders and said, "Look, we made a vow. We not touchin' food 'til Paul's gone.

15.text: Y'all need to hit up the commander, act like y'all wanna question him again. We'll be posted up, ready to end him before he even show up."

16.text: Paul's nephew heard the whole thing and ran to the barracks to tell him.

17.text: Paul told a guard, "Take my nephew to the commander. He got somethin' urgent to say."

18.text: The soldier brought the boy in. "Paul, the prisoner, asked me to bring this young man to you. He got a message."

19.text: The commander took the boy aside and said, "What's good? What you gotta tell me?"

20.text: The boy said, "The Jews plannin' to ask you to bring Paul to the council like they wanna question him again. But it's a setup—they tryna kill him.

21.text: Over forty of 'em out there lyin' in wait. They already swore not to eat or drink 'til he gone. Don't fall for it—they ready and just waitin' on your word."

22.text: The commander nodded, "Bet. Keep this between us—don't tell nobody you told me this."

23.text: Right away, he called two centurions: "We movin' out tonight, 9 PM sharp. Get 200 foot soldiers, 70 on horseback, and 200 spear-holders—we takin' Paul to Caesarea.

24.text: Get the man a horse too. We gon' make sure he get there safe to see Governor Felix."

26.text: "From Claudius Lysias, To His Excellency Governor Felix: Respect.

27.text: The Jews tried to kill this man. I pulled up with my squad and rescued him when I found out he was a Roman citizen.

28.text: I wanted to know why they was mad, so I brought him to their council.

29.text: Turns out, it was all about their religious beef—nothin' worthy of jail or death.

30.text: Then I heard there was a plot to kill him, so I'm sendin' him to you now. His accusers can bring their case to you direct. Peace."

31.text: That night, the soldiers followed orders and took Paul to Antipatris.

32.text: The next day, the foot soldiers went back, but the horsemen kept rollin' with Paul.

33.text: They made it to Caesarea, handed the letter to Felix, and presented Paul.

34.text: Felix read it and asked Paul, "Where you from?" Paul said, "Cilicia."

35.text: Felix said, "Aight. I'll hear your case once your accusers pull up." And just like that, Paul got posted up in Herod's Praetorium.

1.text: A few days later, the high priest Ananias showed up with some elders and a smooth-talking lawyer named Tertullus. They pulled up on Governor Felix ready to throw dirt on Paul's name.

2.text: When they brought Paul in, Tertullus kicked off his lil speech: "Your Excellency, Felix—we been real blessed under your rule. You done brought peace and prosperity, and we appreciate that—fr fr.

3.text: Everywhere we go, folks stay grateful. But I ain't tryna waste your time, so let me keep it short.

5.text: This man right here? A straight menace. A walking disease. Stirring up mess among Jews across the globe. He's the ringleader of them Nazarene folks.

6.text: He even tried to disrespect the temple. We caught him, and we was tryna handle it ourselves with our laws—

7.text: but Commander Lysias busted in heavy-handed, snatched him up from us,

8.text: and told us to bring this whole thing to you. You dig into it, you'll see everything we say is true."

9.text: The rest of the Jews in the room nodded like, "Yup. That's facts."

10.text: Felix gave Paul the signal to speak, and Paul said: "Felix, I know you been in this game a long time, so I'm glad to lay my case out in front of you.

11.text: I only been in Jerusalem for twelve days, and all I did was worship.

12.text: Ain't nobody catch me arguing in the temple, starting no riot in the streets or synagogue.

13.text: They can't prove none of what they say.

14.text: But I'ma keep it 💯—yeah, I follow 'The Way' they call a sect. But I worship the same God our ancestors did, and I believe everything written in the Law and the Prophets.

15.text: Just like them, I believe in the resurrection—of both the righteous and the foul.

16.text: So I stay on point, keepin' my conscience clean before God and people."

17.text: "After some years, I came back to bless my folks—bring 'em gifts, do some offerings.

18.text: That's when some Jews from Asia saw me in the temple. I was purified, minding my business—no crowd, no drama.

19.text: But where they at tho? They supposed to be here if they got a problem.

20.text: Or these dudes here—did they catch me doing wrong?

21.text: Only thing I said in front of the council was, 'I'm on trial today 'cause I believe in the resurrection of the dead.' That's it."

22.text: Felix, who actually knew a lil somethin' about "The Way," didn't rule right away. He said, "I'ma wait for Commander Lysias to get here before I decide."

23.text: In the meantime, he told the guards to hold Paul—but give him some freedom. His people could visit and look out for him.

24.text: A few days later, Felix came back with his wife Drusilla, who was Jewish. He called for Paul to talk about faith in Christ.

25.text: But when Paul started breaking down righteousness, self-control, and that judgment comin', Felix got real uncomfortable. He was like, "Yeah… we good for now. I'll holler at you later."

26.text: Truth is, he was low-key hoping Paul would offer some money to buy his freedom. So he kept calling him up—talkin', waiting, plotting.

27.text: Two whole years passed. Then Porcius Festus took over for Felix. But before he dipped, Felix left Paul locked up—just to keep the Jews happy.

1.text: So after Festus stepped into power in the province, three days later he pulled up to Jerusalem from Caesarea.

2.text: Soon as he got there, the high priest and top Jewish leaders came to him with beef about Paul.

3.text: They begged him to bring Paul back to Jerusalem—tryin' to play slick, 'cause they had folks ready to ambush him on the road and take him out.

4.text: But Festus shut that down quick. He said, "Nah, Paul stayin' in Caesarea. I'll be back there soon anyway."

5.text: He told 'em, "If y'all really got something to say, roll with me down there and make your case in court."

6.text: After kickin' it in Jerusalem for ten-plus days, Festus headed back to Caesarea. The very next day, he sat up in court and called for Paul.

7.text: When Paul came through, the same Jews that followed him down jumped up with a bunch of serious-sounding lies—but couldn't prove a single one.

8.text: Paul stood firm: "I ain't break no Jewish law, I ain't disrespect the temple, and I definitely ain't come for Caesar."

9.text: But Festus, still tryna earn some brownie points with the Jews, asked, "You wanna go to Jerusalem and stand trial there in front of me?"

10.text: Paul said, "Look, I'm already in the right courtroom—Caesar's. This where I should be judged. You know I ain't do nothin' wrong to the Jews.

11.text: If I did something foul, I ain't afraid to die. But if they lyin'? Ain't nobody handin' me over just 'cause they askin. I appeal to Caesar."

12.text: Festus huddled up with his people, then came back and said, "Aight then—you wanna go to Caesar? To Caesar you go."

13.text: A few days later, King Agrippa and his sister Bernice pulled up to Caesarea to give Festus that royal welcome.

14.text: They kicked it for a while, and Festus brought up Paul's situation. He said, "This dude was left locked up by Felix.

15.text: The Jewish leaders tried to get me to sentence him when I was in Jerusalem.

16.text: But I told 'em, 'Nah, that ain't how Romans roll. A man gotta face his accusers and defend himself.'"

17.text: "So the next day we had court. I expected some wild charges, but nah—

18.text: they just started debating some religious stuff and this man Jesus who supposedly died—but Paul sayin' He alive.

20.text: I ain't know how to handle all that, so I asked Paul if he wanted to go to Jerusalem.

21.text: But he was like, 'Nah, I'm takin' this to Caesar.' So I'm holdin' him 'til I can ship him off."

22.text: Then Agrippa said, "I wanna hear him too." Festus was like, "Bet. Tomorrow."

23.text: So the next day, Agrippa and Bernice walked in like royalty, posted up with the military squad and all the VIPs of the city. Festus gave the word, and Paul was brought in.

24.text: Festus addressed the room: "Y'all see this man right here? The Jews—both in Jerusalem and here—been pressin' me to kill him.

25.text: But I ain't found him guilty of nothing worthy of death. And since he appealed to Caesar, I'm sendin' him.

26.text: Problem is, I don't got nothin' solid to write in the report. So I brought him here, especially for you, King Agrippa, to help me figure this out.

27.text: 'Cause let's be real—it'd be wild to send somebody up to Caesar with no real charges written down."

1.text: King Agrippa told Paul, "Aight, go 'head and speak for yourself." Paul raised his hand like, "Bet," and started in:

2.text: "I'm actually glad I get to talk to you today, King Agrippa, 'cause you know all the Jewish stuff—our customs, our drama. So I'ma need you to rock with me for a bit and really listen.

3.text: You know how I been livin'—everybody do. From when I was a kid in Jerusalem, raised Pharisee-style, hardcore with it.

4.text: If they wanna be real, they can tell you: I was deep in it, followin' the strictest path in the game.

5.text: Now I'm standin' here gettin' judged 'cause I still believe in the promise God made to our ancestors.

6.text: That same promise all twelve tribes been hopin' for while servin' God day and night. That's the whole reason they got beef with me.

7.text: But real talk—why is it so wild to believe God can raise the dead?"

8.text: "I used to be the main one goin' against Jesus.

9.text: I locked folks up, had 'em killed, voted against 'em—straight up villain.

10.text: I ran up in synagogues, had people tortured, forced 'em to speak against Jesus. I was mad hateful, chasin' believers way outta town."

11.text: "But one day, while I was on my way to Damascus with official paperwork from the priests—

12.text: Boom. High noon. Outta nowhere, a light from heaven brighter than the sun lit us all up.

13.text: We hit the ground. Then I heard a voice in Hebrew: 'Saul, Saul, why you comin' for Me? You just hurtin' yourself fightin' Me.'

14.text: I was like, 'Who are You, Lord?'

15.text: The voice said, 'I'm Jesus—the One you been tryna cancel.

16.text: Get up. I got plans for you. You gon' be My messenger—tellin' folks what you seen and what I'ma show you.

17.text: I'ma protect you from both your own people and the Gentiles.

18.text: I'm sendin' you to open they eyes. To pull 'em outta darkness, outta Satan's grip, and bring 'em to God. So they can get forgiveness and get a seat at the table with My people—through faith in Me.'"

19.text: "So yeah, King Agrippa, I ain't play God on that. I got right to it.

20.text: Started preachin' in Damascus, then Jerusalem, then Judea, then out to the Gentiles. Tellin' everybody: Repent. Turn to God. Live right.

21.text: That's why they tried to take me out in the temple.

22.text: But God had me. So I'm still here today, speakin' to everybody—rich or poor, known or unknown.

23.text: And all I'm sayin' is what the prophets and Moses said would happen: That the Christ would suffer, rise up first from the dead, and bring light to both Jews and Gentiles."

24.text: Right as Paul was preachin', Festus shouted, "Paul, you done lost your mind! All that book-learnin' got you tweakin'!"

25.text: Paul said, "Nah, Festus. I'm speakin' facts. Real talk.

26.text: The king knows what I'm talkin' about—ain't none of this been in secret. You feel me, King Agrippa?"

27.text: "You believe the prophets, right? I know you do."

28.text: Agrippa hit him with, "Boy... you almost made me a Christian today."

29.text: Paul said, "Man, I wish you and everybody else in here would really get saved—not just almost. Just like me... minus these chains tho."

30.text: After that, the king, the governor, Bernice, and everybody else dipped out.

31.text: They was talkin' like, "Yo, this dude ain't done nothin' wrong."

32.text: Agrippa told Festus, "He coulda walked free... if he ain't ask to go see Caesar."

1.text: Once they made the call to send us to Italy, they handed Paul and some other prisoners over to a Roman officer named Julius, part of the Augustan Regiment.

2.text: We boarded a ship from Adramyttium, headin' out along the coast of Asia. Aristarchus, a brother from Thessalonica, rolled with us too.

3.text: The next day we docked at Sidon. Julius was cool with Paul and let him go see his people so they could take care of him.

4.text: We left there and sailed near Cyprus 'cause the wind was actin' up.

5.text: Then we passed the waters near Cilicia and Pamphylia, and hit Myra, a city in Lycia.

6.text: There, Julius found a ship from Alexandria headed to Italy, and transferred us on board.

7.text: We moved slow for days, barely makin' it past Cnidus. The wind wasn't lettin' us push forward, so we sailed under the coast of Crete, near Salmone.

8.text: It was a rough ride, but we made it to a spot called Fair Havens, close to Lasea.

9.text: By then, we had already spent too much time at sea. It was late in the season and dangerous to sail. So Paul gave 'em a word:

10.text: "Y'all, I feel like if we push ahead, it's gon' be bad—loss of cargo, the ship, maybe even our lives."

11.text: But the centurion listened more to the pilot and the shipowner than to what Paul was sayin'.

12.text: Since Fair Havens wasn't a good place to spend the winter, most of the crew voted to keep sailin' to Phoenix, another port in Crete that faced southwest and northwest, hoping to chill there for the season.

13.text: When a gentle south wind came through, they thought it was a good time to go. So they pulled out, staying close to Crete.

14.text: But not long after, a violent storm called Euroclydon came down like a beast.

15.text: The ship got caught—we couldn't control it—so we just let the wind take us.

16.text: We ducked under the shelter of a little island called Clauda and barely managed to secure the lifeboat.

17.text: Once we got it on board, they tied ropes under the ship to hold it together. They were scared we'd hit the Syrtis Sands, so they lowered the gear and just let the storm push us.

18.text: The next day, the storm beat us down so hard we started throwin' stuff overboard.

19.text: On day three, we tossed the ship's gear ourselves.

20.text: After days with no sun, no stars—just storm after storm—we started thinkin' all hope was gone.

21.text: Nobody had eaten in days. Paul stood up and said, "Y'all shoulda listened to me and stayed in Crete. Then we wouldn't be out here losin' cargo, almost losin' lives.

22.text: But listen—I'm tellin' y'all now, take heart. Ain't nobody gon' die. We'll lose the ship, but not one soul.

23.text: Last night, an angel from the God I serve and belong to stood by me and said:

24.text: 'Paul, don't be scared. You must stand before Caesar. And God's got you covered—He's sparin' everybody sailin' with you.'

25.text: So take heart, y'all. I believe God. It's gon' happen exactly how He told me.

26.text: But we will crash on some island."

27.text: On the fourteenth night, still gettin' tossed around the Adriatic Sea, the sailors started feelin' like land was close.

28.text: They checked the depth—first 120 feet, then a little later, 90 feet.

29.text: They got scared we'd hit rocks, so they dropped four anchors from the back of the ship and prayed for daylight.

30.text: Some of the sailors tried to sneak off in the lifeboat, pretending they were setting anchors from the front.

31.text: But Paul told the centurion and soldiers, "If those men leave this ship, y'all not gon' make it."

32.text: So the soldiers cut the ropes and let the lifeboat drop.

33.text: Just before sunrise, Paul told everybody, "Y'all been fasting for 14 days, scared and not eatin'.

34.text: But I need y'all to eat somethin' now—it's for your survival. Ain't even a hair on your head gon' be lost."

35.text: Then he took bread, gave thanks to God in front of everybody, broke it, and started eatin'.

36.text: That lifted everybody's spirits, and they ate too.

37.text: Altogether, there were 276 people on that ship.

38.text: After they had enough to eat, they lightened the load by throwin' the wheat cargo into the sea.

39.text: When daylight hit, they didn't recognize the land but saw a bay with a beach. So they aimed to run the ship aground there.

40.text: They cut the anchors, let 'em drop, untied the rudder ropes, raised the sail, and aimed for the beach.

41.text: But they hit a spot where two seas came together, and the ship got stuck. The front end jammed up and wouldn't move, and the back end got torn apart by the waves.

42.text: The soldiers wanted to kill the prisoners so none of them could escape.

43.text: But the centurion, tryin' to save Paul, stopped them. He told the ones who could swim to jump in first and make it to land.

44.text: The rest grabbed onto broken pieces of the ship. And just like that, every single one of them made it safely to shore.

1.text: Once we made it out safe, we found out the island was called Malta.

2.text: The locals showed us mad love—built a fire and welcomed everybody, since it was cold and rainin'.

3.text: Paul was helpin'—gathered some sticks for the fire. But as soon as he threw the bundle in, a snake jumped out from the heat and latched on to his hand!

4.text: The islanders saw it hangin' and said, "Oh yeah, this man guilty for real. He survived the sea, but karma—aka 'justice'—still gon' get him."

5.text: But Paul? He just shook that snake off into the fire like it was nothin'. Didn't even flinch.

6.text: They waited, watchin' like, "He 'bout to swell up or drop dead." But after a while with no symptoms, they switched up like folks do—"Oh snap, he must be a god!"

7.text: Not too far from there was the house of a man named Publius, the top dude on the island. He hosted us for three days with real hospitality.

8.text: Turns out, Publius's father was layin' sick with fever and stomach issues. Paul pulled up, prayed, laid hands on him—and he got healed.

9.text: Word spread. Then everybody on the island who was sick came through—and they all got healed too.

10.text: They showed us so much love, honored us in all kinds of ways. When we got ready to leave, they made sure we had everything we needed.

11.text: Three months later, we left on a ship from Alexandria that had wintered there. It had the Twin Brothers carved on the front.

12.text: We stopped at Syracuse and stayed three days.

13.text: From there, we made our way to Rhegium. The next day the south wind kicked in, and we arrived in Puteoli.

14.text: We found some believers there who invited us to stay a whole week. Then we made our way toward Rome.

15.text: When the believers in Rome heard we were comin', they pulled up to meet us at Appii Forum and Three Inns. When Paul saw them, he thanked God and felt encouraged.

16.text: Once we got to Rome, the centurion handed the other prisoners over to the guards, but Paul? He got some freedom—allowed to live by himself with just one soldier watchin' him.

17.text: After three days, Paul called a meeting with the Jewish leaders in Rome. When they came through, he said: "Fam, I didn't do nothin' against our people or traditions, but I still got handed over to the Romans in chains.

18.text: When they investigated, they wanted to let me go—there was no reason to execute me.

19.text: But the Jews kept pushin', so I had to appeal to Caesar. Not to snitch on my people—but to defend myself.

20.text: That's why I called y'all here today. I'm locked up right now, wearin' this chain—for the hope of Israel."

21.text: They told him, "We ain't heard nothin' from Judea about you. Nobody here brought charges.

22.text: But we do wanna hear what you think, 'cause everybody been talkin' wild about this group you represent."

23.text: So they set up a day to come hear Paul out. When they showed up at his spot, Paul broke it all the way down—talked about the kingdom of God, showed how Jesus fulfilled the Law and the Prophets, taught from morning 'til evening.

24.text: Some folks were feelin' it, some were still doubting.

25.text: But when they couldn't agree, Paul hit them with this: "The Holy Spirit told y'all truth through Isaiah when He said:

26.text: 'Go tell the people: You'll listen, but won't really hear. You'll look, but won't really see.

27.text: Their hearts dull, ears closed, eyes shut. They don't wanna turn around and be healed.'"

28.text: "So just know this: God's salvation is goin' to the Gentiles now— and they gon' listen."

29.text: After he said that, the Jews left arguin' among themselves.

30.text: Paul stayed two whole years in his own rented place. The door stayed open—anybody who wanted the truth could pull up.

31.text: He kept preachin' the kingdom of God and teachin' about Jesus Christ, bold and unbothered—nobody stoppin' him.

1.text: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by God's will, and Timothy our brother,

2.text: To the saints and faithful brothers and sisters in Christ who are in Colossae: Grace and peace to y'all from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

3.text: We thank God, the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, and we're always praying for y'all,

4.text: Since we heard about your faith in Christ Jesus and your love for all the saints,

5.text: Because of the hope laid up for y'all in heaven, the hope you heard about before in the word of truth, the gospel,

6.text: Which has come to you, just like it has to the whole world, and it's bearing fruit, just like it's been doing among you since the day you heard and understood the grace of God in truth.

7.text: Just like you learned from Epaphras, our dear fellow servant, who's a faithful minister of Christ on your behalf,

8.text: Who also told us about your love in the Spirit.

9.text: For this reason, since the day we heard it, we don't stop praying for you, and asking that you may be filled with the knowledge of His will, in all wisdom and spiritual understanding;

10.text: So that you may walk worthy of the Lord, fully pleasing Him, bearing fruit in every good work, and growing in the knowledge of God;

11.text: Strengthened with all might, according to His glorious power, for all patience and long-suffering with joy;

12.text: Giving thanks to the Father, who qualified us to share in the inheritance of the saints in the light.

13.text: He has delivered us from the power of darkness and transferred us into the kingdom of the Son of His love,

14.text: In whom we have redemption through His blood, the forgiveness of sins.

15.text: He is the image of the invisible God, the firstborn over all creation.

16.text: For by Him, all things were created in heaven and on earth, visible and invisible, whether thrones, dominions, principalities, or powers. All things were created through Him and for Him.

17.text: And He is before all things, and in Him all things hold together.

18.text: And He is the head of the body, the church, who is the beginning, the firstborn from the dead, so that in everything He may have the preeminence.

19.text: It pleased the Father that in Him all the fullness should dwell,

20.text: And by Him, to reconcile all things to Himself—whether things on earth or things in heaven—making peace through the blood of His cross.

21.text: And y'all, who once were alienated and enemies in your minds by wicked works, He has now reconciled

22.text: In the body of His flesh through death, to present y'all holy, blameless, and above reproach in His sight—

23.text: If indeed you continue in the faith, grounded and steadfast, and aren't moved away from the hope of the gospel you heard, the gospel which was preached to every creature under heaven, of which I, Paul, became a minister.

24.text: Now I rejoice in my sufferings for y'all, and I'm filling up in my flesh what's lacking in the afflictions of Christ, for the sake of His body, which is the church,

25.text: Of which I became a minister according to the stewardship from God that was given to me for you, to fulfill the word of God,

26.text: The mystery that's been hidden for ages and generations, but now has been revealed to His saints.

27.text: To them, God willed to make known what are the riches of the glory of this mystery among the Gentiles: which is Christ in you, the hope of glory.

28.text: Him we preach, warning every person and teaching everyone in all wisdom, so that we may present every person perfect in Christ Jesus.

29.text: For this purpose, I labor, striving according to His working, which works in me mightily.

1.text: Look, I need y'all to understand how much I'm grinding for you and the folks in Laodicea, and all the ones who ain't even met me in person,

2.text: So their hearts get encouraged, being tied up together in love, and getting the full assurance of understanding, the knowledge of the mystery of God, the Father, and Christ,

3.text: In Him, all the treasures of wisdom and knowledge are hidden.

4.text: I'm saying all this so nobody can come at you with smooth talk and trick you with fancy words.

5.text: Even though I'm not there physically, I'm with you in spirit, and I'm happy to see y'all holding it down with good order and staying strong in your faith in Christ.

6.text: So, since you've already received Christ Jesus as Lord, walk in Him,

7.text: Rooted and built up in Him, and solid in the faith like you were taught, overflowing with thanksgiving.

8.text: Watch out! Don't let nobody cheat you with all that philosophy and empty lies, following the traditions of men, following the basic principles of the world, and not Christ.

9.text: For in Him, the fullness of God lives bodily,

10.text: And you are complete in Him, who is the head of all power and authority.

11.text: In Him, you got the real circumcision, not by human hands, but by putting off the body of sin—through the circumcision of Christ,

12.text: You were buried with Him in baptism, and through faith in God, who raised Him from the dead, you were raised with Him,

13.text: And though you were dead in your sins and the uncircumcision of your flesh, He made you alive with Him, forgiving all your sins,

14.text: He wiped out the debt we owed with all the rules that were against us—He took it outta the way and nailed it to the cross.

15.text: He disarmed the powers and authorities, made a public show of them, and triumphed over them on the cross.

16.text: So don't let anyone judge you on what you eat or drink, or if you celebrate a festival, a new moon, or sabbaths,

17.text: These things were just a shadow of what's to come, but the reality is in Christ.

18.text: Don't let anyone cheat you outta your reward, acting all humble and worshiping angels, getting deep into things they never even seen, being all puffed up in their fleshly mind,

19.text: And not holding on to the Head, from whom the whole body—nourished and connected by joints and ligaments—grows with the increase that comes from God.

20.text: If you died with Christ and left the basic rules of this world behind, why are you still acting like you gotta follow man-made rules,

21.text: "Don't touch this, don't taste that, don't handle this,"

22.text: All that stuff is temporary, and it's based on human commandments and teachings.

23.text: These rules might seem wise with all their self-imposed religion, fake humility, and neglect of the body, but they don't do anything to stop the flesh from indulging.

1.text: So, if you were raised with Christ, seek the things that are above, where Christ is, sittin' at God's right hand,

2.text: Set your mind on things above, not on stuff down here.

3.text: You died to your old life, and your life is hidden with Christ in God.

4.text: When Christ, who is our life, shows up, you gon' show up with Him in glory.

5.text: So, put to death the stuff that's all about this earth: fornication, uncleanness, passion, evil desires, and greed, which is idolatry.

6.text: 'Cause of all this mess, the wrath of God is coming for the disobedient,

7.text: And y'all used to walk in these ways when you was living like that.

8.text: But now, y'all need to get rid of all of this: anger, wrath, malice, blasphemy, and filthy language outta your mouth.

9.text: Don't be out here lying to each other, since you've put off the old self with its ways,

10.text: And put on the new self, which is being renewed in knowledge, according to the image of the One who created it,

11.text: Here's the real deal: There ain't no Greek or Jew, circumcised or uncircumcised, barbarian, Scythian, slave, or free—Christ is all, and He's in all of us.

12.text: So, as God's chosen people, holy and loved, put on tender mercy, kindness, humility, meekness, and patience,

13.text: Bear with each other, and forgive each other. If anyone has a complaint, forgive them just like Christ forgave you.

14.text: But above everything, put on love, that's the glue that holds everything together.

15.text: Let God's peace rule in your heart, since you were called to peace in one body, and be thankful.

16.text: Let the word of Christ live richly in you, teaching and encouraging each other with psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs, singing with grace in your hearts to the Lord.

17.text: And whatever you do, whether in word or deed, do it all in the name of the Lord Jesus, giving thanks to God the Father through Him.

18.text: Wives, submit to your husbands, as it's fitting in the Lord.

19.text: Husbands, love your wives and don't be bitter toward them.

20.text: Children, obey your parents in everything, 'cause that pleases the Lord.

21.text: Fathers, don't provoke your kids, or they'll get discouraged.

22.text: Bondservants, obey your masters in everything, not just when they're watching, trying to please people, but with a sincere heart, fearing God.

23.text: Whatever you do, do it with all your heart, as if you're doing it for the Lord, not for men,

24.text: Knowing that from the Lord, you will receive the reward of the inheritance; you're serving the Lord Christ.

25.text: But anyone who does wrong is gonna get what they deserve, and God don't show no partiality.

1.text: Masters, give your bondservants what's just and fair, knowing that you got a Master in heaven too.

2.text: Keep on praying earnestly, always alert in prayer with thanksgiving;

3.text: Meanwhile, pray for us too, that God would open a door for us to spread the word, to speak the mystery of Christ, for which I'm locked up in chains,

4.text: So I can make it clear, like I should.

5.text: Walk in wisdom toward those who ain't saved, making the most of your time,

6.text: Let your speech always be full of grace, with just the right amount of spice, so you'll know how to answer everyone.

7.text: Tychicus, my beloved brother, faithful minister, and fellow servant in the Lord, will fill you in on everything about me.

8.text: I'm sending him to you for this very reason, so he can get the scoop on how you're doing and bring some comfort to your hearts,

9.text: With Onesimus, a faithful and beloved brother, who's one of y'all. They gon' tell you everything going down over here.

10.text: Aristarchus, my fellow prisoner, says "what's up," along with Mark, Barnabas' cousin (about whom you got the instructions: if he comes through, show him love),

11.text: And Jesus, who's called Justus. These are the only fellow workers I got for the kingdom who are from the circumcision, and they've been a comfort to me.

12.text: Epaphras, who's one of y'all, a bondservant of Christ, sends his greetings, always praying hard for y'all, that you stand strong and complete in God's will.

13.text: I can vouch for him—he's got mad love for y'all, and for the people in Laodicea and Hierapolis.

14.text: Luke, the beloved physician, and Demas send their greetings.

15.text: Greet the believers in Laodicea, and Nymphas, and the church in his house.

16.text: When you read this letter, make sure you share it with the church in Laodicea, and read the letter from them too.

17.text: And tell Archippus: "Pay attention to the ministry you received from the Lord, and make sure you finish it."

18.text: This greeting is from me, Paul, with my own hand. Don't forget my chains. Grace be with you. Amen.

1.text: Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ by God's will, To the saints in Ephesus, and all y'all faithful in Christ Jesus:

2.text: Grace and peace to you from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ.

3.text: Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who done blessed us with every spiritual blessing in the heavenly places in Christ,

4.text: Just like He chose us in Him before the foundation of the world, so we could be holy and without blame before Him, all wrapped up in love,

5.text: Having predestined us to be adopted as His sons and daughters through Jesus Christ, according to the good pleasure of His will,

6.text: To the praise of the glory of His grace, by which He made us accepted in the Beloved.

7.text: In Him, we have redemption through His blood, forgiveness for all our mess-ups, according to the riches of His grace,

8.text: Which He made overflow toward us in all wisdom and understanding,

9.text: He revealed to us the mystery of His will, according to His good pleasure, which He set up in Himself,

10.text: That when the time is right, He's gon' gather up all things in Christ—everything, whether in heaven or on earth—everything's gonna come together in Him.

11.text: In Him, we also got an inheritance, predestined according to the purpose of Him who works all things out according to His plan,

12.text: So we who first trusted in Christ would be for the praise of His glory.

13.text: In Him, you also trusted, after you heard the truth—the gospel of your salvation; and after you believed, you were sealed with the Holy Spirit of promise,

14.text: Who is the guarantee of our inheritance, 'til we get what we was promised—redemption for the purchased possession, to the praise of His glory.

15.text: So after I heard about your faith in the Lord Jesus and your love for all the saints,

16.text: I don't stop thanking God for y'all, mentioning you in my prayers:

17.text: That the God of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of glory, may give you the spirit of wisdom and revelation, so you can know Him better,

18.text: That your eyes be opened to see and understand the hope of His calling, the riches of His glory in the inheritance of the saints,

19.text: And the amazing greatness of His power towards us who believe, according to the working of His mighty power,

20.text: Which He showed in Christ when He raised Him from the dead and seated Him at His right hand in the heavenly places,

21.text: Far above all rulers, authorities, powers, and dominion, and above every name that's named, not just in this age, but in the one to come.

22.text: And He put everything under His feet, and gave Him to be the head over everything to the church,

23.text: Which is His body, the fullness of Him who fills all things, everywhere.

1.text: And you, He made alive, when you were dead in your mess-ups and sins,

2.text: You used to walk just like everybody else, following the ways of the world, listening to that prince of the air, the spirit that's still working in those who disobey,

3.text: We all was wildin' too, living in the desires of our flesh, doing what we wanted in our minds, and we was children of wrath by nature, just like everyone else.

4.text: But God, who's rich in mercy, 'cause of His great love for us,

5.text: Even when we was dead in our sins, He made us alive with Christ (by grace, you've been saved),

6.text: And He raised us up together, seated us in heavenly places in Christ Jesus,

7.text: So that in the future, He could show off the greatness of His grace and kindness towards us in Christ Jesus.

8.text: For by grace, you've been saved through faith, and that ain't even your doing—it's God's gift,

9.text: Not by anything you did, so nobody can flex about it.

10.text: We are God's handiwork, created in Christ Jesus to do good works, which God prepared for us to walk in beforehand.

11.text: Remember that you, once Gentiles in the flesh—called "Uncircumcised" by those who got that circumcision done by hands—

12.text: At that time, you were outside, no Christ, no access to the promises of Israel, no hope, and no God in the world.

13.text: But now, in Christ Jesus, you who was once far away, He brought you near by His blood.

14.text: For He is our peace, who made both groups one, and broke down the wall that separated us,

15.text: He did away with that hostility, that law of commandments and rules, and made one new person from the two, making peace,

16.text: And He reconciled both of us to God through the cross, killing that hostility.

17.text: He came and preached peace to y'all who were far away and to those who were close.

18.text: For through Him, we both got access to the Father by the one Spirit.

19.text: So now, you ain't strangers or foreigners no more—you fellow citizens with the saints, members of God's household,

20.text: Built on the foundation of the apostles and prophets, with Jesus Christ Himself as the chief cornerstone,

21.text: In Him, the whole building is fitted together and grows into a holy temple for the Lord,

22.text: And in Him, you also are being built together as a dwelling place for God in the Spirit.

1.text: For this reason, I, Paul, a prisoner of Christ Jesus for y'all Gentiles—

2.text: If you've heard of the grace of God that was given to me for you,

3.text: How He revealed to me the mystery, which I already wrote about briefly,

4.text: That when you read this, you can understand the knowledge I got about the mystery of Christ,

5.text: Which was hidden in other times, but now has been revealed by the Spirit to His holy apostles and prophets:

6.text: That the Gentiles are part of the same body, and they share in His promise in Christ through the gospel,

7.text: I became a minister of this mystery according to the grace of God that was given to me by His power.

8.text: To me, the least of all the saints, this grace was given, so I could preach the unsearchable riches of Christ to the Gentiles,

9.text: And show everyone what the fellowship of this mystery is. It's been hidden from the beginning of time, in God, who created everything through Jesus Christ.

10.text: The point is that now, the wisdom of God might be shown through the church to the powers and rulers in the heavenly places,

11.text: According to the eternal plan He carried out in Christ Jesus, our Lord,

12.text: In Him, we got boldness and access with confidence through faith in Him.

13.text: So, don't get discouraged by my struggles for y'all—this suffering is your glory.

14.text: For this reason, I bow my knees before the Father of our Lord Jesus Christ,

15.text: From whom the whole family in heaven and on earth is named,

16.text: I pray that He may grant you, according to the riches of His glory, strength through His Spirit in your inner self,

17.text: So that Christ may dwell in your hearts through faith; that you, being rooted and grounded in love,

18.text: May be able to understand, along with all the saints, the width, length, depth, and height—

19.text: To know the love of Christ, which is beyond understanding; that you may be filled with all the fullness of God.

20.text: Now to Him who is able to do more than we could ever ask or think, according to the power that works in us,

21.text: To Him be the glory in the church through Christ Jesus, to all generations, forever and ever. Amen.

1.text: So, I'm out here, a prisoner of the Lord, tellin' you: Walk worthy of that call you got,

2.text: With humility, gentleness, patience, and put up with each other in love,

3.text: Try to keep the unity of the Spirit in the bond of peace.

4.text: There's one body, one Spirit, just like you was called in one hope of your calling;

5.text: One Lord, one faith, one baptism;

6.text: One God and Father of all, who is above all, through all, and in all of us.

7.text: But to each one of us, grace was given, based on the measure of Christ's gift.

8.text: That's why He said: "When He ascended on high, He led captivity captive, And gave gifts to men."

9.text: Now, when it says "He ascended"—what does that mean, except that He first descended to the lower parts of the earth?

10.text: The One who descended is the same One who ascended far above all the heavens, so He could fill all things.

11.text: And He gave some to be apostles, some prophets, some evangelists, some pastors, and some teachers,

12.text: For the equipping of the saints to do the work of ministry, to build up the body of Christ,

13.text: Until we all come to the unity of the faith and knowledge of the Son of God, to a perfect man, to the fullness of Christ;

14.text: So we should stop acting like kids, tossed around by every new teaching, tricked by the lies and schemes of others,

15.text: But speak the truth in love, and grow up in every way into Christ, the head—

16.text: From whom the whole body, joined and held together by what every part supplies, does its job and builds up the body in love.

17.text: So here's what I'm sayin', and I'm testifying in the Lord: Stop living like the rest of the Gentiles, in the futility of their thinking,

18.text: They got their minds all darkened, separated from the life of God, because they ain't know the truth, their hearts are blinded,

19.text: They don't feel nothin' no more, so they gone off into all kinds of mess, living in greed and sin.

20.text: But that ain't how you learned Christ,

21.text: If you really heard Him and was taught by Him, 'cause the truth is in Jesus:

22.text: You gotta let go of your old ways, the old man, that corrupts you with lies and lust,

23.text: Be renewed in the spirit of your mind,

24.text: And put on the new man, created to be like God, in true righteousness and holiness.

25.text: So, stop the lying—"Let each one of you speak truth to your neighbor," 'cause we all part of the same body.

26.text: "Be angry, but don't sin"—don't let the sun go down while you're mad,

27.text: And don't give the devil a foothold.

28.text: If you used to steal, stop it—now work hard, doing good stuff with your hands, so you got something to give to someone in need.

29.text: Don't let no nasty talk come out your mouth, only speak what's gonna build people up and help 'em,

30.text: And don't grieve the Holy Spirit, the one who sealed you for the day of redemption.

31.text: Get rid of all bitterness, anger, rage, arguing, and bad-mouthing, along with all the hate,

32.text: Be kind to each other, tenderhearted, forgiving one another, just like God forgave you in Christ.

1.text: So, be imitators of God, like dear children,

2.text: And walk in love, just like Christ loved us and gave Himself for us, an offering and a sacrifice to God that smells sweet.

3.text: But fornication, uncleanness, or greed? Don't even let that be named among you—it ain't right for saints,

4.text: No filthiness, foolish talk, or coarse jokes. That's not fitting—what's fitting is giving thanks.

5.text: You know this for sure: no fornicator, unclean person, or greedy man (who's basically an idol worshiper) has any inheritance in the kingdom of Christ and God.

6.text: Don't let nobody fool you with empty words, 'cause because of that stuff, the wrath of God comes on the disobedient.

7.text: So, don't be part of that.

8.text: Y'all used to be in darkness, but now, you're light in the Lord. Walk like children of the light,

9.text: 'Cause the fruit of the Spirit is all about goodness, righteousness, and truth,

10.text: And finding out what's acceptable to the Lord.

11.text: Don't hang with the unfruitful works of darkness, expose them instead.

12.text: It's even shameful to talk about the stuff they do in secret,

13.text: But everything that's exposed is made visible by the light, 'cause whatever makes it visible is light.

14.text: That's why it says: "Wake up, you who sleep, Rise from the dead, And Christ will give you light."

15.text: So watch how you walk—don't walk like fools, but like wise people,

16.text: Make the most of your time, 'cause the days are evil.

17.text: Don't be unwise, understand what the will of the Lord is,

18.text: And don't be drunk with wine (that leads to wildness), but be filled with the Spirit,

19.text: Speak to each other in psalms, hymns, and spiritual songs, singing and making melody in your heart to the Lord,

20.text: Always giving thanks for everything to God the Father in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ,

21.text: Submit to each other out of respect for God.

22.text: Wives, submit to your husbands as you do to the Lord,

23.text: 'Cause the husband is the head of the wife, just like Christ is the head of the church and the Savior of the body.

24.text: So just like the church is subject to Christ, let wives be to their husbands in everything.

25.text: Husbands, love your wives just like Christ loved the church and gave Himself for her,

26.text: To make her holy, cleansing her with the washing of water by the word,

27.text: So He can present her to Himself, a glorious church, with no spot, wrinkle, or anything wrong, but holy and without blemish.

28.text: So, husbands should love their wives like they love their own bodies; he who loves his wife loves himself.

29.text: Nobody ever hated their own body; they take care of it, just like the Lord takes care of the church.

30.text: We are members of His body, of His flesh, and of His bones.

31.text: "For this reason, a man shall leave his father and mother and be joined to his wife, and the two shall become one flesh."

32.text: This is a great mystery, but I'm talking about Christ and the church.

33.text: So, let every one of you love your wife like you love yourself, and let the wife respect her husband.

1.text: Children, obey your parents in the Lord, 'cause that's the right thing to do.

2.text: "Honor your father and mother," and that's the first commandment with a promise:

3.text: "That it may go well with you, and you may live long on the earth."

4.text: And you, fathers, don't provoke your children to anger, but raise them up in the training and teaching of the Lord.

5.text: Bondservants, be obedient to your masters according to the flesh, with fear and respect, doing it sincerely from the heart, like you're working for Christ,

6.text: Not just when people are watching, trying to please men, but as servants of Christ, doing the will of God from the heart,

7.text: With good intentions, serving like you're serving the Lord, not people,

8.text: Knowing that whatever good anyone does, they'll get it back from the Lord, whether they're a slave or free.

9.text: And you, masters, treat your servants the same way, don't be threatening, 'cause you know your Master is in heaven, and He doesn't play favorites.

10.text: Finally, my people, be strong in the Lord and in the power of His might.

11.text: Put on the full armor of God, so you can stand firm against the devil's tricks,

12.text: 'Cause our fight ain't with people—it's against principalities, powers, rulers of darkness in this world, and spiritual forces of evil in the heavenly places.

13.text: So, put on the full armor of God, so you can stand strong when the evil day comes, and when it's all said and done, you'll still be standing.

14.text: Stand firm, with your waist girded with truth, putting on the breastplate of righteousness,

15.text: And your feet shod with the readiness to spread the gospel of peace;

16.text: Above all, take the shield of faith, with which you can block all the fiery darts from the enemy,

17.text: And take the helmet of salvation, and the sword of the Spirit, which is the word of God,

18.text: Always pray with all kinds of prayer and requests in the Spirit, stay alert with perseverance, and keep praying for all the saints,

19.text: And for me, that I might speak boldly about the gospel,

20.text: I'm in chains, but I'm still an ambassador, and I gotta speak boldly like I'm supposed to.

21.text: But so you know how I'm doing, Tychicus, my beloved brother and faithful minister in the Lord, will let you know everything,

22.text: I sent him to you for that purpose, so you'll know how we're doing and he can comfort your hearts.

23.text: Peace to you, and love with faith, from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ,

24.text: Grace be with everyone who loves our Lord Jesus Christ with a sincere heart. Amen.

1.text: This Paul talkin'—an apostle, but not one made by people or some group of men. Naw, I was sent by Jesus Christ Himself, and God the Father, the one who raised Jesus from the dead.

2.text: And all the brothers with me? They co-signin' this too. To the churches out in Galatia—

3.text: Grace and peace to y'all from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ,

4.text: the One who gave His whole self up for our sins, so He could snatch us out this evil world we livin' in—just like God the Father wanted.

5.text: All glory belong to Him, now and forever. Amen.

6.text: I'm honestly shocked—y'all switched up so fast. Turnin' away from the One who called y'all through the grace of Christ, and runnin' to a whole other gospel?

7.text: Not that it's even another real one—these folks just tryna stir stuff up and twist up the real gospel of Christ.

8.text: Listen, I don't care if it's me, or even some angel floatin' down from heaven—if they preach somethin' different than what we already told y'all? Let them be cursed.

9.text: Matter fact, let me say it again—if anybody preaches somethin' other than what you already heard from us? Let them be cursed, period.

10.text: Who you think I'm tryin' to please—God or people? If I was still out here tryna be a people-pleaser, I couldn't call myself a servant of Christ.

11.text: Let me make this crystal clear, fam: the gospel I preached? It ain't man-made.

12.text: I ain't get this from nobody teachin' me. I didn't go to school for it. I got it straight from Jesus, revealed to me personally.

13.text: Y'all already heard how I used to live—deep in Judaism. I was wildin'. I used to persecute God's church bad—tryna shut it all the way down.

14.text: And I was movin' up fast in the Jewish scene, way ahead of my age group. I was mad committed to all the traditions passed down to me.

15.text: But when God—yeah, the same one who had me set apart from birth—decided to call me through His grace…

16.text: …and let His Son be revealed in me (so I could preach to the Gentiles), I ain't go run and ask nobody for advice.

17.text: I didn't hit up the apostles in Jerusalem right away either. I went out to Arabia first. Then I came back to Damascus.

18.text: Three years later, I finally went to Jerusalem to link up with Peter. I stayed with him for about 15 days.

19.text: I ain't see none of the other apostles—just James, Jesus' brother.

20.text: And just so y'all know—I ain't lyin'. God sees me. I'm tellin' the truth.

21.text: After that, I bounced to Syria and Cilicia.

22.text: The churches in Judea didn't even know me by face yet.

23.text: They just kept hearin' stories like: "Yo, that same dude who used to come for us is now out here preachin' the same faith he tried to shut down."

24.text: And because of that? They gave God all the glory.

1.text: Fourteen years later, I went back up to Jerusalem. I brought Barnabas with me—and I brought Titus too.

2.text: I ain't just go on my own. I went 'cause God told me to. I shared the gospel I been preachin' to the Gentiles—especially with the leaders, behind closed doors, just in case everything I'd done would've ended up pointless.

3.text: But guess what? Even Titus, who's a full-on Greek, wasn't forced to get circumcised.

4.text: This whole issue came up 'cause of some fake brothers who snuck in on purpose to spy on our freedom in Christ. They tryna drag us back into bondage.

5.text: But we ain't fold—not for a second. We didn't give in, so that the truth of the gospel could stay pure for y'all.

6.text: Now, as for those folks who thought they was important—it don't mean nothin' to me. God don't play favorites. They didn't add anything new to what I was preachin'.

7.text: On the flip side, they realized I had been called to preach to the uncircumcised (the Gentiles)—just like Peter was sent to the circumcised (the Jews).

8.text: 'Cause the same God who gave Peter the juice to reach the Jews, gave me that same power to reach the Gentiles.

9.text: And when James, Peter (Cephas), and John—the so-called "pillars"—saw the grace God put on me, they gave me and Barnabas the handshake. Like, "Aight, y'all got the Gentiles, we got the Jews."

10.text: The only thing they asked was that we remember the poor—and I was already on that anyway.

11.text: Now let me tell y'all what went down in Antioch—Peter came through and I had to call him out, face to face, 'cause he was straight-up wrong.

12.text: Before some folks from James showed up, he was cool eatin' with the Gentiles. But when they came? He switched up, pulled back, 'cause he was scared of what the religious folks would say.

13.text: And that same two-faced behavior spread—even the rest of the Jews started actin' funny, and yep… even Barnabas got caught up in it.

14.text: I couldn't sit quiet. I told Peter in front of everybody: "Bruh, you Jewish—but you livin' like a Gentile right now. So why you tryna force Gentiles to live like Jews?"

15.text: We're Jews by birth, not 'Gentile sinners.'

16.text: But even we know this: nobody gets right with God by following the law. We believed in Jesus so we could be made right through faith, not through rule-keeping. 'Cause if law could save us, we'd all be doomed. Ain't nobody justified by law.

17.text: Now if we put our faith in Christ, but we still mess up—does that make Jesus the cause of our sin? No way.

18.text: If I go back to rebuild what I already tore down, that just proves I'm wrong—not Jesus.

19.text: Look, I died to that law life so I could live for God.

20.text: I ain't even the one livin' anymore—Christ is livin' through me now. The life I got now in this body? I live it by faith in Jesus—the One who loved me and gave Himself up for me. That's personal.

21.text: I ain't tossin' God's grace aside. 'Cause if bein' made right with God could come from the law, then Jesus died for nothin'.

1.text: Yo, Galatians, what's wrong with y'all? Who bewitched you to turn away from the truth? You saw Christ crucified in front of you—now you actin' like you don't know what's good?

2.text: Hold up. Let me ask you this: Did you get the Holy Spirit by followin' the law, or by hearing the gospel and believing?

3.text: Are y'all really that foolish? You started out in the Spirit—now you think you gon' finish it off by your own effort? Like that's how growth works?

4.text: You've been through so much already—and you really gon' let that go to waste? You think it was all in vain?

5.text: So the God who gave y'all the Spirit and did miracles among you—was He doin' that 'cause y'all followed the law, or because you believed the gospel?

6.text: Just like Abraham, who believed God—and that faith was counted as righteousness.

7.text: Understand this: the true sons of Abraham ain't just his bloodline, but those who live by faith.

8.text: Scripture told us God would justify the Gentiles by faith way back in Abraham's time. When God said, "In you, all nations will be blessed," He wasn't just talkin' to Jews.

9.text: So those who live by faith are blessed with faithful Abraham.

10.text: But for those who depend on the law? They're under the curse. Why? 'Cause the law says: "Cursed is everyone who doesn't do everything the law says."

11.text: Ain't no way to be justified by the law in God's eyes. It's clear: "The righteous shall live by faith."

12.text: But the law ain't about faith—it's about doing. The law says, "Live by it, or else."

13.text: Christ redeemed us from that curse. He became a curse for us. He took the hit, like the law said: "Cursed is everyone who hangs on a tree." Jesus switched up the game—He got on that cross, so we could get the blessing of Abraham.

14.text: All this happened so the Gentiles could get in on the blessing and receive the Holy Spirit through faith.

15.text: Let me break it down like this: Even if it's just a regular contract, once it's confirmed, nobody can change it. God's promises? Ain't like contracts with people—they're eternal and can't be tampered with.

16.text: Now God made promises to Abraham and his Seed. It wasn't about "seeds" (many) but about one Seed—Jesus. Jesus is the promise that holds everything together.

17.text: Here's the thing: the law came 430 years later, but it don't change the promise God gave before. If the inheritance was based on the law, then it wouldn't be a promise anymore. God gave it to Abraham as a promise.

18.text: If the inheritance comes from followin' the law, then it ain't a promise no more. But God gave it to Abraham as a promise, not by works.

19.text: So what's the purpose of the law then? It came because of sin—to show us we needed a Savior, until the promised Seed (Jesus) came. It was put in place by angels, and Moses was the mediator.

20.text: But a mediator only works for more than one person—God is one.

21.text: Does this mean the law goes against God's promises? Nope. If there was a law that could give life, we'd have been justified by it. The law shows us we all fall short—so we can't do it on our own. We need Jesus.

22.text: The law confined us all under sin, so the promise could be given to those who believe in Jesus.

23.text: Before faith came, we were kept under the law, locked up, waiting for the faith that was about to be revealed.

24.text: The law was our tutor—pointin' us straight to Christ. It taught us that we can't save ourselves. It was a set-up for faith.

25.text: But now that faith has come? We ain't under the tutor no more. We live by faith.

26.text: Y'all are God's sons through faith in Christ Jesus.

27.text: And since all of y'all who've been baptized into Christ have put Him on—y'all wear Him like a new identity.

28.text: There's no more Jew, no more Greek, no more slave, no more free, no more male or female. In Christ—we're all one.

29.text: And if you belong to Christ? Then you are Abraham's seed—heirs to the promise.

1.text: Aight, let me break this down: an heir might be master of everything, but as long as he's a child, he's basically treated the same as a slave. He still gotta listen to the guardians and caretakers 'til it's time for him to take over.

2.text: Same for us—when we were kids, we were stuck under the world's rules, no freedom.

3.text: But when the time was right, God sent His Son, born of a woman, born under the law,

4.text: to redeem us, those trapped under the law, and give us the adoption as sons.

5.text: And now that we're His sons? God sent the Spirit of His Son into our hearts, and now we call out to Him—"Abba, Father!"

6.text: So you ain't a slave no more. You a son. And if you a son, you an heir of God through Christ.

7.text: So, you ain't a slave no more, you a son—and if you a son, you an heir of God through Christ.

8.text: But hold up—back when y'all didn't know God, you were servin' all these false gods, things that ain't even real.

9.text: Now you know God, or better yet, God knows you, so how come y'all wanna go back to that old stuff?

10.text: Y'all wanna be enslaved again to things like days, months, seasons, and years.

11.text: I'm worried for you—did I labor for y'all for nothing?

12.text: Yo, become like me, I became like y'all. We're in this together—you haven't wronged me at all.

13.text: Y'all remember when I came to you—sick—and still preached the gospel to you?

14.text: And my condition? Y'all didn't turn away from me. You treated me like I was Christ Himself.

15.text: What happened to all that love? Y'all even said you'd pluck out your eyes for me if you could.

16.text: So now, I'm your enemy just 'cause I'm speakin' the truth to you?

17.text: These false teachers? They zealously court you—but for the wrong reasons. They tryna cut you off from me, so you can be loyal to them instead.

18.text: But it's good to be zealous for good stuff—not just when I'm around, but always.

19.text: I'm like a momma in labor, tryna give birth to Christ in you. I'm not even sure where y'all stand with this, but I'm still working on it.

20.text: I wish I could be with y'all right now and change my tone, 'cause I'm confused about where y'all at spiritually.

21.text: Aight, let me ask y'all: You who want to go back under the law—do you even understand what the law is about?

22.text: It's written: Abraham had two sons: one by the slave woman, and one by the free woman.

23.text: The one born of the slave woman was born by human effort; the one born of the free woman came by promise.

24.text: This story's a symbol—it's about the two covenants:

25.text: Hagar is Mount Sinai in Arabia—and that corresponds to Jerusalem now, where people are still in bondage.

26.text: But the Jerusalem above—that's free. That's the true mother of us all.

27.text: Just like the Scripture says: "Rejoice, barren woman! Shout out loud, you who've never had kids! The one who was deserted is about to have more children than the one with a husband!"

28.text: We, the ones of promise, just like Isaac—we're not just children of the law, we're children of the promise.

29.text: And just like it was back then, the one born of the flesh (Ishmael) persecuted the one born of the Spirit (Isaac)—that's still happening today.

30.text: But listen to what Scripture says: "Cast out the slave woman and her son, 'cause the son of the slave woman won't inherit with the son of the free woman."

31.text: So, family, we ain't children of the slave woman—we children of the free.

1.text: Aight, listen—stand strong in the freedom Christ gave us. Don't let yourself get caught back up in that old law, that yoke of bondage.

2.text: I'm tellin' y'all straight: if you get circumcised, Christ ain't gonna profit you.

3.text: You still gotta follow every single law, not just one. You can't pick and choose.

4.text: So, if you're tryna be justified by the law, you're cut off from Christ. You've fallen from grace.

5.text: But we, through the Spirit, are waiting for that righteousness by faith.

6.text: Look, in Christ, whether you're circumcised or not, it don't matter. It's all about faith that works through love.

7.text: Y'all were runnin' strong, but who tripped you up from obeying the truth?

8.text: That kind of thinking ain't from God, the One who called you.

9.text: Just like yeast spreads through dough, a little bad doctrine messes up everything.

10.text: But I'm confident in you, that you won't let these distractions mess you up. And whoever keeps trippin' you up? They gon' face judgment.

11.text: If I'm still preachin' circumcision, why am I still being persecuted? If I was about that life, the offense of the cross would've disappeared.

12.text: Honestly, I wish the people messin' with y'all would just cut themselves off.

13.text: You've been called to freedom—don't use that freedom to do whatever your flesh wants. Nah, use that freedom to serve each other in love.

14.text: All the laws, all the rules—they come down to this one thing: "Love your neighbor as yourself."

15.text: But if y'all out here biting and devouring each other, you'll destroy yourselves.

16.text: Here's what I'm sayin'—walk by the Spirit, and you won't give in to the lust of the flesh.

17.text: The flesh and the Spirit warring against each other. They oppose each other. That's why you don't do what you wanna do sometimes.

18.text: But if you're led by the Spirit, you ain't under the law anymore.

19.text: Now, let's talk about the works of the flesh—these are obvious: adultery, fornication, uncleanness, lewdness, idolatry, sorcery, hatred, jealousy, outbursts of wrath, selfish ambition, dissensions, heresies, envy, murders, drunkenness, revelries, and more.

20.text: But here's the fruit of the Spirit—love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness, gentleness, self-control. Against these? No law. This is what God wants.

21.text: Envy, murders, drunkenness, revelries, and all that other mess. I already warned you about this, like I did before—if you out here living like this, you won't inherit the kingdom of God.

22.text: But the fruit of the Spirit is: love, joy, peace, patience, kindness, goodness, faithfulness.

23.text: Gentleness and self-control. Ain't no law against these things.

24.text: Those who belong to Christ have already crucified the flesh—all the desires and passions that come with it.

25.text: If we live by the Spirit, we need to walk in the Spirit.

26.text: Let's not be arrogant or provoke each other. No envy.
