1.text: Ayo, if somebody's caught up in sin, y'all who are spiritually mature, help restore them—but do it with gentleness, watchin' yourself so you don't fall into the same temptation.

2.text: Bear each other's burdens—this is how we fulfill Christ's law: love each other and carry each other's weight.

3.text: If you think you're all that but ain't even really all that, you foolin' yourself.

4.text: Take a moment to examine yourself—then you can be proud of your own work, and not compare yourself to someone else.

5.text: Everybody got their own load to carry—don't be worried about somebody else's weight when you got your own to carry.

6.text: If you're learning from the Word, share the good stuff you got with the person teachin' you.

7.text: Don't be fooled—God ain't a joke. Whatever you put out there, you gon' get back.

8.text: If you out here sowin' into your flesh (your selfish desires), you gon' reap corruption. But if you sow into the Spirit, you gon' get eternal life from the Spirit.

9.text: Don't give up doin' good. In the right season, you gon' reap if you don't quit.

10.text: So as long as you have the chance, do good to everyone—especially to those in the family of faith.

11.text: Look at the big letters I'm writin' to y'all with my own hand. I'm serious about this.

12.text: The ones who wanna look good in front of people—they'll try to make you get circumcised. Why? 'Cause they don't wanna get persecuted for Christ's cross.

13.text: They ain't even keeping the law themselves, but they want y'all to get circumcised just so they can brag about it. That's whack.

14.text: But God forbid that I should boast in anything except the cross of Jesus Christ, by which the world is dead to me, and I'm dead to the world.

15.text: Circumcision or uncircumcision? Don't matter. What matters is being a new creation in Christ.

16.text: So, everybody who lives by this rule—peace and mercy be upon them, and on the Israel of God.

17.text: From now on, don't bother me. I carry the marks of Jesus on my body, so I ain't got time for foolishness.

18.text: May the grace of Jesus be with y'all. Amen.

1.text: God, who spoke to our ancestors in different ways and at different times through the prophets,

2.text: Has now spoken to us through His Son, the One He appointed to inherit everything, through whom He also made the universe.

3.text: The Son is the brightness of God's glory and the exact image of God's being, and He's holding everything together by the power of His word. After He purified our sins, He sat down at the right hand of God's majesty on high.

4.text: He became way better than the angels, 'cause He inherited a name that's more excellent than theirs.

5.text: Which of the angels did God ever say, "You are My Son, today I've begotten You"? And again, "I will be to Him a Father, And He shall be to Me a Son"?

6.text: And when He brings the firstborn into the world, He says, "Let all the angels of God worship Him."

7.text: And of the angels, He says, "He makes His angels spirits and His servants a flame of fire."

8.text: But to the Son, He says, "Your throne, O God, is forever and ever; The scepter of righteousness is the scepter of Your kingdom.

9.text: You loved righteousness and hated wickedness; So God, Your God, anointed You With the oil of joy more than Your companions."

10.text: And, "You, Lord, in the beginning laid the foundation of the earth, And the heavens are the work of Your hands.

11.text: They will pass away, but You stay the same; And they will all wear out like old clothes;

12.text: Like a cloak, You'll fold them up, And they'll be changed. But You are the same, And Your years will never end."

13.text: But to which of the angels did God ever say, "Sit at My right hand, Until I make Your enemies Your footstool"?

14.text: Aren't they all just ministering spirits, sent to serve those who will inherit salvation?

1.text: So, we gotta pay close attention to everything we've heard, don't let it slip away from us.

2.text: If the message given through angels was solid, and every mistake and disobedience got what it deserved,

3.text: How we gonna escape if we neglect this great salvation, which first came from Jesus, and was confirmed to us by those who heard Him,

4.text: With God showing up with signs, wonders, miracles, and gifts of the Holy Spirit, doing what He wills?

5.text: He ain't put the world to come under the control of angels,

6.text: But someone testified somewhere, saying: "What is man that You think about him, Or the son of man that You care for him?

7.text: You made him a little lower than the angels, You crowned him with glory and honor, And put him in charge of everything You made.

8.text: You put all things under his feet." But now, we don't see everything under his feet yet, but we do see Jesus, who was made a little lower than the angels,

9.text: For the suffering of death, crowned with glory and honor, so He could taste death for everyone, by God's grace.

10.text: It was only right for the One who made everything and through whom everything exists, to bring many sons to glory by perfecting their Captain (Jesus) through suffering.

11.text: Both Jesus, who sanctifies, and those who are being sanctified, are one family, which is why He ain't ashamed to call us His brothers and sisters,

12.text: Saying: "I'll declare Your name to My family; I'll sing Your praises among them."

13.text: And again, "I'll put My trust in Him." And again: "Here I am, and the children God gave Me."

14.text: Since the children share in flesh and blood, He also shared in the same stuff, so that through death, He could destroy the one who had power over death—the devil,

15.text: And free those who've been living in fear of death, in bondage their whole lives.

16.text: He didn't come to help angels, but He came to help Abraham's descendants.

17.text: So, He had to be like His brothers and sisters in every way, so He could be a merciful and faithful High Priest, making atonement for the sins of the people.

18.text: And since He suffered and was tempted, He knows how to help those who are tempted.

1.text: So, holy brothers and sisters, you who are partakers in this heavenly calling, consider Jesus, the Apostle and High Priest of our faith,

2.text: Who was faithful to the One who appointed Him, just like Moses was faithful in God's house.

3.text: But Jesus, the One we're talking about, has more glory than Moses, because the One who built the house has more honor than the house itself.

4.text: Every house is built by someone, but God built everything.

5.text: Moses was faithful in God's house as a servant, giving us a testimony of what was to come,

6.text: But Christ is over His own house as a Son, and we are that house, if we hold on tight to our confidence and the rejoicing of the hope firm till the end.

7.text: So, just like the Holy Spirit says: "Today, if you hear His voice,

8.text: Don't harden your hearts like your people did in the rebellion, In the day they were tested in the wilderness,

9.text: Where your ancestors tested Me, tried Me, And saw all the things I did for forty years.

10.text: So I was mad at that generation, And said, 'They always go astray in their hearts, And they don't know My ways.'

11.text: So I swore in My anger, 'They ain't gonna enter My rest.'"

12.text: Watch out, fam, don't let any of you have an evil heart of unbelief, turning away from the living God.

13.text: But keep encouraging each other daily while it's still "today," so none of you get hardened by the deceitfulness of sin.

14.text: We've become partakers of Christ if we hold onto our confidence all the way to the end.

15.text: Just like it says: "Today, if you hear His voice, Don't harden your hearts like they did in the rebellion."

16.text: Who heard and rebelled? Wasn't it everyone who came out of Egypt, led by Moses?

17.text: And who was God mad at for forty years? Wasn't it those who sinned, whose bodies dropped dead in the wilderness?

18.text: And to whom did He swear they wouldn't enter His rest? Only the ones who didn't obey.

19.text: So we see that they couldn't get in because of unbelief.

1.text: Since there's still a promise for us to enter God's rest, we need to be careful and make sure none of us miss out.

2.text: The gospel was preached to us just like it was to them, but the word they heard didn't do them any good 'cause they didn't mix it with faith.

3.text: But we who believe enter that rest, just like He said: "I swore in My anger, 'They ain't gon' enter My rest,'" Even though the works were finished since the world began.

4.text: God said this on the seventh day: "God rested on the seventh day from all His works."

5.text: And again He said: "They ain't gon' enter My rest."

6.text: Since some gotta enter it, and the people who first heard the gospel didn't enter 'cause of their disobedience,

7.text: God set aside a new day, calling it "Today," through David, after a long time: "Today, if you hear His voice, Don't harden your hearts."

8.text: If Joshua had given them rest, God wouldn't be talking about another day.

9.text: So, there's still a rest for the people of God.

10.text: Those who enter God's rest stop doing their works, just like God stopped His.

11.text: So, let's make sure we're diligent to enter that rest, so we don't fall into the same disobedience as those before us.

12.text: The Word of God is alive and powerful, sharper than any two-edged sword. It cuts deep—dividing soul and spirit, joints and marrow. It discerning your thoughts and what's in your heart.

13.text: There's nothing hidden from His sight—everything is open to Him, and we gotta give an account to Him for everything.

14.text: Since we got a great High Priest, who has passed through the heavens, Jesus, the Son of God, let's hold on to our confession.

15.text: We don't have a High Priest who doesn't understand our struggles. He's been through the same temptations we face, but He didn't sin.

16.text: So let's come boldly to the throne of grace, so we can get mercy and find grace to help us when we need it.

1.text: Every high priest, chosen from among men, is put in charge to handle stuff that concerns God, so he can offer gifts and sacrifices for sin.

2.text: He's supposed to have compassion on those who don't know better and are wandering, 'cause he himself gets caught up in weakness too.

3.text: That's why he has to offer sacrifices for his own sins, and for the people's too.

4.text: No one just takes this honor for themselves. Only the ones God calls to it, just like He did for Aaron.

5.text: Christ didn't try to glorify Himself to be High Priest. Nah, it was God who said to Him: "You are My Son, Today I have begotten You."

6.text: He also says in another part: "You are a priest forever According to the order of Melchizedek."

7.text: In His human form, Jesus cried out vehemently, praying and pleading with God, the One who could save Him from death, and God heard Him because He was truly God-fearing.

8.text: Even though He was the Son of God, He still had to learn obedience through everything He suffered.

9.text: And after going through all of that, He was perfected, becoming the author of eternal salvation for everyone who obeys Him,

10.text: And He was called by God as High Priest in the order of Melchizedek.

11.text: We got a lot to say about Melchizedek, but it's hard to explain 'cause y'all aren't really hearing right now.

12.text: By now, y'all should be teaching others, but you still need someone to teach you the basics of God's Word. You're still on that milk, not ready for solid food.

13.text: Anyone who only drinks milk ain't skilled in the word of righteousness—they're just a baby in the faith.

14.text: But if you're grown in the faith, you're eating solid food, meaning you've been through some things and learned how to discern between good and evil. You're not out here getting caught up in every little thing anymore.

1.text: So, let's move beyond the basics of Christ and go on to maturity. We ain't gon' keep going over the same things like repentance from dead works and having faith in God,

2.text: Or talkin' about baptisms, laying on of hands, resurrection of the dead, and eternal judgment.

3.text: We'll do all this if God permits.

4.text: But here's the deal: If someone has been enlightened, tasted the heavenly gift, been filled with the Holy Spirit,

5.text: And has tasted the goodness of God's word and experienced the powers of the world to come,

6.text: But they fall away, it's impossible to bring them back to repentance, because they're crucifying Christ again and putting Him to open shame.

7.text: The earth gets rain, and when it drinks it up, it brings forth good things for those who work it, so it's blessed by God.

8.text: But if it brings thorns and thistles, it gets rejected and is almost cursed—its end is to be burned.

9.text: But we believe in better things for you, things that go with salvation, even though we're saying all this.

10.text: God ain't gon' forget the work you've put in and the love you've shown for His name. You've served the saints, and you're still out here serving.

11.text: We want each one of you to stay diligent and keep your hope strong until the end,

12.text: So you don't get lazy, but follow the examples of those who, through faith and patience, inherit the promises.

13.text: When God made a promise to Abraham, He couldn't swear by anyone greater, so He swore by Himself,

14.text: Saying, "For sure, I will bless you, and I will multiply you."

15.text: After waiting patiently, Abraham received what was promised.

16.text: People swear by something greater than themselves, and when they make an oath, it settles things.

17.text: God wanted to show the heirs of promise just how unchangeable His plans are, so He confirmed His promise with an oath.

18.text: God can't lie, and because of that, we can find strong comfort in His promise, especially those of us who've fled to Him for refuge, holding on to the hope that's in front of us.

19.text: This hope is like an anchor for our souls—steady and secure, and it reaches all the way into God's presence behind the veil.

20.text: Jesus is the forerunner, and He's entered for us, becoming our High Priest forever, according to the order of Melchizedek.

1.text: Now, Melchizedek, the king of Salem and the priest of the Most High God, met Abraham when he was coming back from defeating the kings and blessed him.

2.text: Abraham gave him a tenth of everything, and Melchizedek's name means "king of righteousness," and he's also called the king of peace.

3.text: He didn't have a father or mother, no genealogy, no beginning or end to his life—he was like the Son of God, a priest forever.

4.text: Consider how great this man was, even Abraham, the patriarch, gave him a tenth of the spoils.

5.text: Now, the sons of Levi, who receive the priesthood, are commanded to collect tithes from their people, but Melchizedek, who ain't from their family line, received tithes from Abraham and blessed him, the one who had the promises.

6.text: So, the lesser (Abraham) was blessed by the greater (Melchizedek).

7.text: No debate—the lesser is always blessed by the greater.

8.text: Here, regular men receive tithes, but over there, Melchizedek gets them, and it's testified that he's still alive.

9.text: Even Levi, who's supposed to receive the tithes, paid tithes through Abraham, in a way.

10.text: He was still in Abraham's loins when Melchizedek met him.

11.text: So, if the Levitical priesthood could bring perfection (and under it, the law was given), why would we need another priest like Melchizedek to rise up? Why not just stick to the Aaronic line?

12.text: If the priesthood changes, the law has to change too.

13.text: For the priest we're talking about is from another tribe, the tribe of Judah, and Moses didn't speak about priesthood coming from there.

14.text: It's clear that our Lord came from Judah, and that tribe wasn't ever about priesthood.

15.text: But it's even more clear that, just like Melchizedek, another priest who looks like him has come,

16.text: And He ain't come based on fleshly rules but by the power of an endless life.

17.text: God said to Him: "You are a priest forever, According to the order of Melchizedek."

18.text: The old commandment was canceled 'cause it wasn't doing the job—it was weak and didn't bring perfection.

19.text: But now we got a better hope because of the new priesthood, and it's that hope that brings us closer to God.

20.text: And since Jesus wasn't made a priest just like the others, but He was made a priest with an oath from God Himself,

21.text: He became a surety of a better covenant.

22.text: The old priests had to die off, but Jesus? He lives forever, and His priesthood is unchangeable.

23.text: The old priests couldn't keep going because of death,

24.text: But Jesus, because He lives forever, has a priesthood that doesn't change.

25.text: And because of that, He's able to save to the uttermost everyone who comes to God through Him—He's always interceding for us.

26.text: He's the perfect High Priest for us—holy, harmless, undefiled, separate from sinners, and greater than the heavens.

27.text: Unlike the old high priests, He didn't need to offer sacrifices every day—first for His own sins, then for the people's. He did it once, and He offered up Himself.

28.text: The law appointed men who have weaknesses as high priests, but God's oath appoints the Son, who has been perfected forever.

1.text: Now here's the main thing I'm tryna say: We got us a High Priest who's sitting at the right hand of God's throne in heaven,

2.text: He's the Minister of the true sanctuary, the real tabernacle that God built, not man.

3.text: Every high priest is called to offer gifts and sacrifices. So, this One—Jesus—had to have something to offer too.

4.text: If He was on earth, He wouldn't be a priest, 'cause there are already priests doing the work of offering gifts according to the law,

5.text: They're serving a copy and shadow of what's in heaven—just like Moses was told by God to make the tabernacle according to the pattern He showed him on the mountain.

6.text: But now Jesus has a better ministry. He's the Mediator of a better covenant, built on better promises.

7.text: If the first covenant was perfect, we wouldn't need a new one.

8.text: But God found something wrong with it, so He said: "The days are coming," says the Lord, "When I'm gonna make a new covenant with Israel and Judah,

9.text: Not like the covenant I made with their ancestors when I led them outta Egypt. They didn't keep it, and I disregarded them," says the Lord.

10.text: "This is the covenant I'm gonna make with Israel after those days," says the Lord: "I'm gon' put My laws in their minds, And write them on their hearts. I'll be their God, and they'll be My people.

11.text: Nobody's gon' have to teach their neighbor or tell their brother, 'Know the Lord,' 'Cause everyone's gon' know Me, from the least to the greatest.

12.text: I'm gon' be merciful to their wickedness, And their sins and evil deeds, I ain't gon' remember them no more."

13.text: Since God said, "A new covenant," that means the first one's done. Now what's getting old and outdated is ready to disappear.

1.text: Now, the first covenant had rules for worship and the earthly sanctuary.

2.text: A tabernacle was set up: the first part had the lampstand, the table, and the showbread—that part's called the sanctuary,

3.text: And behind the second veil, there was the Holiest of All—

4.text: This had the golden censer and the ark of the covenant covered in gold, with stuff like the golden pot of manna, Aaron's rod, and the tablets of the covenant.

5.text: Above the ark were the cherubim of glory overshadowing the mercy seat. But yo, we ain't got time to go into all these details right now.

6.text: When all this was set up, the priests always went into the first part of the tabernacle, doing the services,

7.text: But only the high priest went into the second part, and that was only once a year, and not without blood, which he offered for himself and the people's sins done in ignorance.

8.text: The Holy Spirit was showing that the way into the Holiest of All wasn't open as long as the first tabernacle was standing.

9.text: This was a symbol for the present time, where both gifts and sacrifices were offered, but they couldn't really make the person performing the service perfect in their conscience—

10.text: It was all about food, drink, washings, and fleshly rules, until the time when everything would change.

11.text: But Christ came as the High Priest of the better things to come, with a greater and more perfect tabernacle, not made with human hands, that is, not of this creation.

12.text: He didn't come with the blood of goats and calves, but with His own blood, He entered the Most Holy Place once for all, and secured eternal redemption.

13.text: If the blood of bulls, goats, and the ashes of a heifer could sanctify people for the purifying of their flesh,

14.text: How much more will Christ's blood, who through the eternal Spirit, offered Himself without blemish to God, cleanse our consciences from dead works so we can serve the living God?

15.text: And for this reason, He is the Mediator of the new covenant, by means of His death, for the redemption of the sins under the first covenant. Now those who are called can receive the promise of the eternal inheritance.

16.text: For where there's a will, there must also be a death of the one who made the will.

17.text: A will is only in effect once the person is dead, because it doesn't have any power while the testator is still alive.

18.text: That's why even the first covenant wasn't set up without blood.

19.text: When Moses spoke the law to the people, he took the blood of calves and goats, mixed with water, scarlet wool, and hyssop, and sprinkled both the book and all the people,

20.text: Saying, "This is the blood of the covenant which God has commanded you."

21.text: Then he sprinkled the tabernacle and all the ministry vessels with the blood.

22.text: According to the law, almost everything is purified with blood, and without the shedding of blood, there's no forgiveness.

23.text: It was necessary for the earthly copies of heavenly things to be purified with these sacrifices, but the heavenly things themselves need better sacrifices.

24.text: Christ didn't go into the man-made holy places, which are just copies of the real thing. He went into heaven itself to appear in God's presence for us.

25.text: He didn't have to offer Himself over and over, like the high priest does every year with someone else's blood—

26.text: If He did, He would've had to suffer from the beginning of time. But now, at the end of the ages, He came to put away sin by the sacrifice of Himself.

27.text: And just as it's appointed for men to die once, and after that the judgment,

28.text: Christ was offered once to bear the sins of many. And those who are waiting for Him, He will appear a second time, but this time, it won't be about dealing with sin, but for salvation.

1.text: So look, the law was just a shadow of the good stuff to come, not the real deal. These sacrifices they offer every year can't make anyone perfect.

2.text: If they could, they would've stopped offering them, because once people were purified, they wouldn't even be thinking about their sins anymore.

3.text: But every year, these sacrifices just remind them of their sins.

4.text: It's impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.

5.text: So when Christ came into the world, He said: "Sacrifice and offering You didn't want, But You prepared a body for Me.

6.text: You didn't take pleasure in burnt offerings or sin offerings,

7.text: Then I said, 'Here I am, I've come— To do Your will, O God.'"

8.text: Before He said this, He said, "Sacrifice and offering, burnt offerings, and sin offerings, You didn't want or take pleasure in," (which are all the stuff according to the law),

9.text: Then He said, "Here I am to do Your will, O God." So, He takes away the old system to set up the new one.

10.text: By this will we are sanctified through the offering of Jesus Christ's body, once and for all.

11.text: Every priest stands and offers the same sacrifices over and over, but none of them can take away sins.

12.text: But Jesus, after offering Himself as the one sacrifice for all time, sat down at the right hand of God,

13.text: From then on, waiting for His enemies to become His footstool.

14.text: By that one offering, He perfected forever those who are being sanctified.

15.text: And the Holy Spirit also testifies to us, for after He said:

16.text: "This is the covenant I will make with them after those days, says the Lord: I will put My laws in their hearts, and write them on their minds."

17.text: Then He added, "Their sins and lawless deeds, I won't remember anymore."

18.text: And where there's forgiveness of these, there's no more sacrifice for sin.

19.text: So, brothers and sisters, since we have boldness to enter the Most Holy Place by the blood of Jesus,

20.text: By the new and living way He opened for us through the veil, that is, His flesh,

21.text: And since we have a High Priest over the house of God,

22.text: Let's draw near with a true heart and full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience and our bodies washed with pure water.

23.text: Let's hold on tight to the confession of our hope without wavering, 'cause He who promised is faithful.

24.text: And let's think about each other, to stir up love and good works,

25.text: Not skipping out on meeting together, like some do, but encouraging each other—and even more as you see the Day getting closer.

26.text: If we sin willfully after we've received the truth, there's no longer any sacrifice for sins left,

27.text: But a fearful expectation of judgment and fiery anger that will devour those who oppose God.

28.text: Anyone who rejected Moses' law had to die without mercy by the testimony of two or three witnesses.

29.text: How much worse do you think it'll be for someone who has trampled on the Son of God, treated the blood of the covenant like it's nothing, and disrespected the Spirit of grace?

30.text: We know God said, "Vengeance is Mine, I will repay," and He will judge His people.

31.text: It's a fearful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.

32.text: But remember the past, when you first heard the truth, and endured through a hard struggle with sufferings,

33.text: Partly when people made a spectacle of you, with insults and trials,

34.text: And partly when you stood with those who were treated the same way. You had compassion on me in my chains and joyfully accepted the plundering of your stuff, knowing you got a better and lasting possession in heaven.

35.text: So don't throw away your confidence—it has a great reward.

36.text: You need to endure, so that after you've done what God called you to do, you can receive the promise:

37.text: "A little while longer, And He who is coming will come and won't delay.

38.text: But the just shall live by faith; If anyone turns back, My soul has no pleasure in them."

39.text: But we aren't the ones who turn back to destruction; we're the ones who believe to the saving of the soul.

1.text: So, faith is the substance of things we hope for, the evidence of things we ain't seen yet.

2.text: By it, the elders got a good testimony.

3.text: By faith, we understand that God framed the worlds with His word, so the stuff we see wasn't made from what we can see.

4.text: By faith, Abel offered a better sacrifice to God than Cain, and through it, he got recognized as righteous. God testified about his gifts, and even though he's dead, his faith still speaks.

5.text: By faith, Enoch was taken up and didn't see death—he was just gone, 'cause God took him. He had this testimony that he pleased God.

6.text: Without faith, it's impossible to please God. You gotta believe that He is, and that He rewards those who seek Him.

7.text: By faith, Noah, being warned about things that hadn't been seen, built the ark to save his family. By his faith, he condemned the world and became heir of the righteousness that comes from faith.

8.text: By faith, Abraham obeyed when he was called to go out to a place he didn't know, but he knew it would be his inheritance.

9.text: By faith, he lived in the promised land like a foreigner, living in tents with Isaac and Jacob, who were heirs with him of the same promise.

10.text: He was waiting for the city with foundations, whose builder and maker is God.

11.text: By faith, Sarah received strength to conceive a child when she was past the age, 'cause she judged God faithful who made the promise.

12.text: So from one man, and he was basically dead, came descendants as many as the stars and the sand by the seashore—too many to count.

13.text: All these people died in faith, without receiving the promises, but they saw them from far off, were assured of them, embraced them, and confessed that they were just strangers and travelers on this earth.

14.text: They said they were looking for a homeland.

15.text: If they were thinking about the country they left, they could've gone back, but they were after something better, a heavenly country.

16.text: That's why God ain't ashamed to be called their God, 'cause He's got a city prepared for them.

17.text: By faith, Abraham, when tested, offered up Isaac, and he who had received the promises was about to sacrifice his only son,

18.text: Even though God said, "In Isaac your descendants will be called."

19.text: Abraham believed that God could even raise Isaac from the dead, and figuratively, he received him back from the dead.

20.text: By faith, Isaac blessed Jacob and Esau concerning the things to come.

21.text: By faith, Jacob, when he was dying, blessed each of Joseph's sons, and worshiped, leaning on the top of his staff.

22.text: By faith, Joseph, when he was dying, spoke about the departure of the Israelites, and gave instructions about his bones.

23.text: By faith, Moses was hidden for three months by his parents 'cause they saw he was beautiful and weren't afraid of the king's orders.

24.text: By faith, when Moses grew up, he refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter,

25.text: Choosing rather to suffer with the people of God than to enjoy the temporary pleasures of sin.

26.text: He thought the reproach of Christ was more valuable than all the treasures in Egypt, because he was looking forward to the reward.

27.text: By faith, he left Egypt, not afraid of the king's anger, and endured as though he was seeing the Invisible One.

28.text: By faith, he kept the Passover and sprinkled the blood, so the one who destroyed the firstborn wouldn't touch them.

29.text: By faith, they walked through the Red Sea like it was dry land, while the Egyptians drowned when they tried to do the same.

30.text: By faith, the walls of Jericho fell down after the Israelites marched around them for seven days.

31.text: By faith, Rahab, the prostitute, didn't perish with those who didn't believe when she hid the spies and made peace with them.

32.text: What more can I say? I don't have enough time to talk about Gideon, Barak, Samson, Jephthah, David, Samuel, and all the prophets—

33.text: Who through faith conquered kingdoms, worked righteousness, received promises, stopped the mouths of lions,

34.text: Quenched fire, escaped the edge of the sword, were made strong from weakness, became brave in battle, and made their enemies run.

35.text: Women received their dead back to life. Others were tortured, not accepting deliverance, so they could have a better resurrection.

36.text: Some faced mockings, scourgings, and even chains and imprisonment.

37.text: They were stoned, sawed in half, tempted, killed by the sword. They wandered in sheepskins and goatskins, poor and afflicted.

38.text: The world wasn't worthy of them. They lived in deserts, mountains, and caves—these were the faithful.

39.text: All these people, even though they had faith and got a good testimony, didn't receive the promises.

40.text: God had something better for us, so they couldn't be perfected without us.

1.text: So since we got this big ol' crowd of witnesses all around us, let's throw off anything weighin' us down and that sin that keep trippin' us up, and let's keep runnin' this race God set for us,

2.text: keepin' our eyes locked on Jesus, the one who started our faith and the one who gonna finish it. For the joy ahead of him, he went through the cross, brushed off the shame, and now he sittin' at the right hand of God's throne.

3.text: Think about him who took all that pushback from sinners, so you don't get tired and give up.

4.text: In your fight against sin, you ain't resisted to the point of sheddin' blood.

5.text: And you done forgot the word that encourage you like a father talkin' to his child? It say,

6.text: "My child, don't shrug off the Lord's discipline, and don't lose heart when he correct you,

7.text: 'cause the Lord disciplines who he love, and he correct everybody he accept as his child."

8.text: Take hardship as discipline; God treatin' you like his children. What child don't get disciplined by they father?

9.text: If you ain't gettin' disciplined--and everybody get discipline--then you ain't really his, you not true sons and daughters.

10.text: We all had human fathers who disciplined us, and we respected them for it. How much more should we submit to the Father of spirits and live!

11.text: They disciplined us for a little while how they thought was best; but God disciplines us for our good, so we can share in his holiness.

12.text: Discipline don't feel good at the time--it's painful. But later, it bring a harvest of right-livin' and peace to the ones trained by it.

13.text: So strengthen your weak arms and shaky knees.

14.text: "Make straight paths for your feet," so the lame won't get worse, but instead get healed.

15.text: Make every effort to live in peace with everybody and to be holy; without holiness nobody gon' see the Lord.

16.text: Watch out so nobody fall short of God's grace and no bitter root grow up to cause trouble and mess up a bunch of people.

17.text: Make sure nobody livin' sexually immoral, or godless like Esau, who traded away his birthright for one meal.

18.text: After that, you know, when he wanted the blessing, he got turned down. Even though he cried for it, he couldn't undo what he already did.

19.text: You ain't come to a mountain you can touch, burnin' with fire, with darkness, gloom, and storm,

20.text: to a trumpet blast or a voice so strong folks begged not to hear another word,

21.text: 'cause they couldn't handle what was commanded: "If even an animal touch the mountain, it must be stoned to death."

22.text: It was so scary Moses said, "I'm tremblin' with fear."

23.text: But you done come to Mount Zion, the city of the living God, the heavenly Jerusalem. You done come to thousands and thousands of angels in joyful assembly,

24.text: to the church of the firstborn whose names written in heaven. You done come to God, the Judge of all, to the spirits of righteous folks made perfect,

25.text: to Jesus, the mediator of a new covenant, and to the sprinkled blood that speak a better word than the blood of Abel.

26.text: Make sure you don't refuse the one who speak. If they ain't escape when they refused the one warnin' them on earth, how much less we gon' escape if we turn away from the one warnin' us from heaven?

27.text: Back then his voice shook the earth, but now he promised, "One more time I'll shake not just the earth but the heavens too."

28.text: That "one more time" mean what can be shaken--the created stuff--gonna be removed, so what can't be shaken will stay.

29.text: So since we gettin' a kingdom that can't be shaken, let's be grateful and worship God in a way he accept, with reverence and awe, 'cause our God is a consumin' fire.

1.text: Let that brotherly love keep going strong.

2.text: Don't forget to be kind to strangers, 'cause some people have entertained angels without even knowing it.

3.text: Remember those who are in prison, like you're right there with them. And those who are mistreated, 'cause you're also in this body.

4.text: Marriage is honorable for all, and the marriage bed is undefiled—but God will judge fornicators and adulterers.

5.text: Don't be out here chasing after stuff you don't have—be content with what you got. Remember, God said, "I will never leave you or forsake you."

6.text: So we can boldly say, "The Lord is my helper; I won't be afraid. What can man do to me?"

7.text: Remember those who lead you, who taught you the word of God, and follow their faith, considering how their lives ended.

8.text: Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever.

9.text: Don't be caught up in all these weird doctrines. It's good for your heart to be strengthened by grace, not by food laws that ain't helped anyone.

10.text: We got an altar where those who serve the tabernacle ain't allowed to eat.

11.text: The bodies of those animals, whose blood the high priest took into the holy place for sin, are burned outside the camp.

12.text: And just like that, Jesus, to sanctify the people with His own blood, suffered outside the gate.

13.text: So, let's go to Him, outside the camp, and be willing to bear His reproach.

14.text: We don't have a permanent city here, but we're looking for the one to come.

15.text: So, through Jesus, let's keep offering the sacrifice of praise to God—the fruit of our lips, thanking His name.

16.text: But don't forget to do good and share—God is pleased with these sacrifices.

17.text: Obey those who lead you, and be submissive to them, 'cause they're watching out for your souls, and they gotta give an account. Let them do it with joy, not with grief, 'cause that's unprofitable for you.

18.text: Pray for us, 'cause we're sure that we have a good conscience and want to live honorably in everything.

19.text: I'm asking especially that you pray so I can be restored to you quicker.

20.text: Now, may the God of peace, who brought up our Lord Jesus from the dead, that great Shepherd of the sheep, through the blood of the everlasting covenant,

21.text: Make you complete in every good work to do His will, working in you what's pleasing in His sight, through Jesus Christ, to whom be glory forever and ever. Amen.

22.text: I'm asking you, brothers and sisters, to bear with this word of encouragement, 'cause I've written to you in a few words.

23.text: Know that Timothy has been set free, and I'll see you soon if he comes.

24.text: Greet those who lead you, and all the saints. Those from Italy greet you.

25.text: Grace be with you all. Amen.

1.text: This James right here, servin' God and our Lord Jesus Christ. I'm writin' to the twelve tribes that been scattered all over. What's good, fam?

2.text: My people, treat it like a win when life start tryna whoop you from every angle.

3.text: Know this: when your faith get tested, it build up that patience muscle.

4.text: But don't cut the process short—let patience do her full work so you can grow up, be whole, and not miss nothin'.

5.text: If any of y'all ain't got wisdom, go ahead and ask God. He give it out generous, no side-eye, no judgment—and He'll make sure you get it.

6.text: But when you ask, do it with full faith—no doubtin'. 'Cause the one who doubtin' is like a wave tossed around by the wind—real shaky.

7.text: That kinda person shouldn't expect to get anything from the Lord.

8.text: They got two minds and can't keep still in nothin' they do.

9.text: If you broke or low in status, go ahead and brag about how God liftin' you up.

10.text: And if you rich, go ahead and humble yourself, 'cause like flowers in the field, you ain't gon' be around forever.

11.text: Soon as that hot sun come up, the grass shrivel up, the flower fall, and all that beauty gone. Same way the rich gon' fade out in the middle of they hustle.

12.text: Blessed is the one who hang in there through temptation—'cause when they pass the test, they gon' get that crown of life God promised to the ones that love Him.

13.text: Don't nobody say, "God tryna tempt me," 'cause God don't get tempted by evil and He ain't out here temptin' nobody.

14.text: We get tempted when our own wants drag us off and trap us.

15.text: Then them desires get pregnant, and what they birth? Sin. And when sin grow all the way up, it bring death to the party.

16.text: Don't get it twisted, fam.

17.text: Every good and perfect thing we got come straight from the Father of lights. He don't switch up or throw shade.

18.text: He chose to give us new life through the word of truth so we could be like the first of many new creations.

19.text: So hear me out, fam: be quick to listen, slow to talk, and real slow to pop off in anger.

20.text: 'Cause human anger don't produce the kinda righteousness God on.

21.text: Drop all that nasty mess and evil overflowin' in your life. Instead, receive that word God planted in you—it's powerful enough to save your soul.

22.text: Don't just listen to the word and think you good. That's playin' yourself. Do what it say.

23.text: If you just hear it but don't do nothin', you like somebody who look in the mirror—

24.text: Then walk off and forget what they even look like.

25.text: But if you look into God's perfect law that sets you free, and you stick with it—don't just hear it then bounce, but actually do it—you gon' be blessed in what you do.

26.text: If you think you holy but can't control your tongue, you straight up foolin' yourself. Your religion don't mean nothin'.

27.text: Real, pure religion in God's eyes is this: look out for orphans and widows when they strugglin', and keep yourself from gettin' dirtied up by this wild world.

1.text: Fam, if you claimin' to believe in our Lord Jesus Christ—the real MVP, the glory King—then stop showin' favoritism. That don't match up.

2.text: Say a dude walks in with gold rings and drippin' in designer, and then another one pull up lookin' dusty and broke…

3.text: And you treat the flashy one like royalty—"Ayy, take this good seat"—but tell the broke one, "Stand over there," or "Sit down here on the floor by my feet,"

4.text: Ain't you just made yourself the judge, with evil intentions in your heart?

5.text: Listen up, fam: Didn't God choose the ones the world sleep on—the poor—to be rich in faith and to inherit the Kingdom He promised to those who love Him?

6.text: But y'all done disrespected the poor. And ain't it the rich folks that be oppressin' y'all and draggin' you to court?

7.text: Ain't it them that be talkin' wild about the name y'all claim?

8.text: If you really out here livin' that "love your neighbor as yourself" life, like the Scriptures say, then you doin' right.

9.text: But if you show favoritism, you sinnin'. Period. The law gon' call you out as a lawbreaker.

10.text: 'Cause if you follow the whole law but mess up on just one thing, it's like you broke the whole thing.

11.text: The same God who said, "Don't cheat" also said, "Don't kill." So if you ain't out here cheating but you killin', you still outta pocket.

12.text: So talk and act like folks who gon' be judged by the law that sets you free.

13.text: 'Cause if you ain't got mercy for others, don't expect mercy in your judgment. Mercy always wins over judgment.

14.text: What's the point, fam, if somebody say they got faith but don't back it up with action? That kind of faith can't save nobody.

15.text: Suppose one of our own ain't got clothes or food for the day—

16.text: And you say, "Be blessed, stay warm and eat good!" but don't actually help them out…what good is that?

17.text: Same goes for faith. If it don't come with works, it's dead. D-E-A-D.

18.text: Somebody might say, "You got faith, I got works." Aight—show me your faith with no works, and I'll show you mine through what I do.

19.text: You believe there's one God? Cool. Even demons believe that—and they shakin' in their boots.

20.text: But you still tryna act like faith don't need action? Boy, if you don't—faith without works is dead!

21.text: Remember Abraham, our forefather? Wasn't he considered righteous 'cause he put in work—offerin' up Isaac, his own son, on the altar?

22.text: See, his faith and actions were tag-teamin'. His works made his faith complete.

23.text: That's why Scripture says, "Abraham believed God, and it was credited to him as righteousness." And they even called him God's friend.

24.text: So you see, people get right with God by what they do, not just by what they say they believe.

25.text: And don't forget Rahab the harlot—sis showed faith by hidin' the spies and sneakin' them out another way. That was workin' faith, too.

26.text: Just like a body without breath is dead, faith without works is dead, too.

1.text: Look, fam—don't everybody try to be a teacher. Know that teachers get judged harder than most.

2.text: We all mess up in a lotta ways. But if you can control your mouth? You on point. That means you got discipline over your whole body too.

3.text: Think about it—when we put bits in a horse's mouth, we can steer the whole thing wherever we want.

4.text: Same with a ship—big ol' boat, strong winds, but a tiny lil' rudder directs it wherever the captain steerin'.

5.text: That's how the tongue is. It's small, but it talks big! Just takes a lil' spark to set a whole forest on fire.

6.text: That tongue? Straight up fire. It's a whole world of wickedness. It messes up your whole self, burns through your life like wildfire—and hell itself be sparkin' it.

7.text: Humans done tamed all kinds of animals—beasts, birds, reptiles, sea creatures. We got all that on lock.

8.text: But nobody can fully tame the tongue. It's wild, evil, full of deadly venom.

9.text: One minute we usin' it to bless God our Father—and the next, we cussin' folks made in His image.

10.text: Same mouth talkin' blessings and curses? That ain't right, fam. That ain't how it's supposed to be.

11.text: Do a spring shoot out both fresh water and bitter water from the same spot?

12.text: Can a fig tree grow olives? Can a grapevine grow figs? Nah. And the same way, saltwater ain't gon' give you fresh water.

13.text: Who out here think they wise and smart? Then show it by how you live—let your actions be humble and full of wisdom.

14.text: But if you carryin' bitter envy and out-for-self vibes in your heart, don't be out here frontin' and lyin' on the truth.

15.text: That ain't God's kind of wisdom. That's worldly, flesh-driven, and straight-up demonic.

16.text: Wherever you got envy and selfishness, confusion and every kind of mess is right there with it.

17.text: But the wisdom that come from above? It's pure first. Then peace-lovin', gentle, open to correction, full of mercy, heavy on good fruit, no favoritism, no fakin'.

18.text: And the ones who plant peace? They gon' harvest righteousness. Peace grows what's right.

1.text: Where all these beefs and fights y'all got come from? Ain't it from the stuff y'all want so bad inside that it got you fightin' your own self?

2.text: You want what you don't got, so you ready to kill. You jealous, but still can't get what you want. So you fight and war. But you still don't got it—'cause you ain't even askin' God.

3.text: And when you do ask, you don't get it 'cause your motives all jacked up. You just want it for your own pleasure.

4.text: Y'all cheatin' on God like spiritual side pieces! Don't you know bein' tight with the world means you beefin' with God? If you wanna be cool with the world, you just made yourself God's enemy.

5.text: Or you think the Word was playin' when it said, "The Spirit God put in us is jealous for us"?

6.text: But He got grace on grace for us. That's why the Scriptures say: "God stands against the proud, But pours grace on the humble."

7.text: So stop fightin'—submit to God. Push back on the devil and he gon' dip.

8.text: Come close to God and He gon' come close to you. Wash your hands, y'all who been wildin'. Get your heart right, you double-minded folks.

9.text: Cry it out. Mourn. Weep. Stop laughin' like everything funny. Let that joy turn to real repentance.

10.text: Humble yourself in front of the Lord—and He gon' lift you up.

11.text: Don't talk down on each other, fam. If you talk bad about your brother and judge him, you ain't just clownin' him—you clownin' God's law. And if you judge the law, you not obeyin' it… you tryna act like you above it.

12.text: There's only one real Judge and Lawgiver—He the one who can save or destroy. So who are you to be out here judgin' somebody else?

13.text: Look here—you who always say, "We gon' hit this city, post up for a year, stack up some bread and flip it…"

14.text: Y'all don't even know what tomorrow got in store. Your life? It's like steam off a cup—shows up for a second then gone.

15.text: Instead, you oughta be sayin', "If the Lord willin', we'll live and make moves."

16.text: But now y'all braggin' and flexin'. That kinda pride? That's evil.

17.text: So if you know the right thing to do and still don't do it? That's sin—period.

1.text: Aight now, all y'all stackin' money dirty—go ahead and cry, holler even, 'cause misery comin' your way.

2.text: Your money gettin' moldy, your designer clothes got moth bites—ain't nothin' lastin'.

3.text: Your gold and silver rusted up, and that rust gon' testify against you. It's gon' eat you up like fire. All that treasure you stacked? You hoardin' in the last days like there's no judgment comin'.

4.text: The folks who cut your grass and worked your fields? You cheated them. Their unpaid wages out here cryin' out—and God heard 'em loud and clear.

5.text: Y'all been livin' it up, luxury style, fattenin' up like animals before slaughter.

6.text: You judged and killed the innocent—and they ain't even fight back.

7.text: So fam, be patient till the Lord come back. Think about a farmer—he waitin' on that good harvest, gotta hold tight through the early rain and the late rain.

8.text: You do the same. Get your heart solid—Jesus on the way.

9.text: Stop grumblin' 'bout each other, or you gon' get judged too. The Judge already standin' at the door—He right there.

10.text: Look at the prophets, y'all. They went through it while speakin' God's name. They stayed down. Follow that example.

11.text: We call folks blessed when they hold on through the storm. Y'all heard about Job, right? How he kept pushin'? And saw how God flipped it in the end? God don't play about His compassion and mercy.

12.text: And most important—stop swearin' on stuff: no oaths, no "on God," no "on my mama." Just say "yes" or "no." Keep it simple and solid so you don't end up in judgment.

13.text: Anybody goin' through it? Pray. Got joy? Sing about it.

14.text: Somebody sick? Call the church elders. Let 'em pray over you and put oil on you in Jesus' name.

15.text: That kind of prayer—rooted in faith—can heal the sick, and the Lord gon' lift 'em up. If they messed up, they gon' be forgiven too.

16.text: Confess what you've done wrong to each other, and pray for each other, so healing can happen. Real prayer from a righteous one? That joint powerful and effective.

17.text: Elijah was just a regular dude like us—but when he prayed hard for the rain to stop, it ain't rain for 3½ years!

18.text: Then he prayed again—and boom, rain came and the earth started growin' again.

19.text: Listen, fam—if somebody in the crew drifts off from the truth, and you help bring 'em back?

20.text: Just know: you helped save a soul from death and covered up a whole bunch of sins.

1.text: In the beginning was the Word, and the Word was chillin' with God, and the Word was God.

2.text: He was right there with God from the jump.

3.text: Everything that got made was made through Him. Not a single thing came to be without Him.

4.text: In Him was life, and that life was the light for all folks.

5.text: That light shined in the darkness, and the darkness ain't know what to do with it.

6.text: God sent a man named John.

7.text: John came as a witness, so he could speak on the Light, so folks would believe through him.

8.text: He wasn't the Light—he was just here to talk about the Light.

9.text: That Light he talked about? That was the real one, the one that gives light to everybody comin' into the world.

10.text: He was in the world, the world was made through Him, and the world ain't even recognize Him.

11.text: He pulled up to His own people, and they ain't want Him.

12.text: But the ones who did welcome Him—who believed in His name—He gave 'em the right to be God's children.

13.text: They ain't born from blood, or from fleshly desire, or some man's decision—but straight up from God.

14.text: The Word became human and moved into the neighborhood. We saw His glory—the kind only a Father's only Son got—full of grace and truth.

15.text: John talked about Him, shoutin', "This the One I told y'all about! The One who came after me, but ranks higher than me—'cause He existed before I did!"

16.text: From all He got, we all received—grace stacked on top of grace.

17.text: The law came through Moses, but grace and truth showed up through Jesus Christ.

18.text: Nobody ever seen God, but the one and only Son, who's right there close to the Father's heart—He made Him known.

19.text: This right here was John's testimony, when the Jewish leaders sent priests and Levites from Jerusalem to ask him, "Who you?"

20.text: He straight up told 'em, "I ain't the Messiah."

21.text: They said, "Okay, so are you Elijah then?" He said, "Nah, not me." They said, "You the Prophet?" He said, "Nope."

22.text: Then they said, "Well who are you then? We gotta report back. What you sayin' about yourself?"

23.text: He said, "I'm just a voice shoutin' in the wilderness, sayin', 'Get the Lord's path straight,' just like Isaiah said."

24.text: The ones who came to him were from the Pharisees.

25.text: They asked, "So why you baptizin' if you not the Messiah, Elijah, or the Prophet?"

26.text: John said, "I baptize with water. But Somebody standin' right here among y'all, and y'all don't even know Him."

27.text: "He comin' after me, but He way greater. I ain't even worthy to untie His sandals."

28.text: All this went down in Bethany across the Jordan, where John was baptizin'.

29.text: The next day, John saw Jesus comin' and said, "Look! The Lamb of God, the One who takes away the world's sin!"

30.text: "This who I was talkin' about when I said, 'Somebody comin' after me who outranks me—'cause He was here before me.'"

31.text: "I ain't even know who He was at first. But I came baptizin' so He could be revealed to Israel."

32.text: John gave his testimony: "I saw the Spirit come down from heaven like a dove, and He stayed on Him."

33.text: "I ain't know who He was, but the One who sent me to baptize said, 'The one you see the Spirit land on and stay? That's Him—the One who baptizes with the Holy Spirit.'"

34.text: "I saw it for myself. That's the Son of God, no doubt."

35.text: The next day, John was standin' there with two of his disciples.

36.text: He looked at Jesus walkin' by and said, "Look—God's Lamb!"

37.text: When the two disciples heard him say that, they followed Jesus.

38.text: Jesus turned around and saw them followin'. He said, "What y'all want?" They said, "Rabbi"—which means Teacher—"where You stayin'?"

39.text: He said, "Come see for yourself." They went, saw where He was stayin', and chilled with Him that day. It was about 4pm.

40.text: One of the two that heard John and followed Jesus was Andrew, Simon Peter's brother.

41.text: First thing Andrew did was find his brother Simon and say, "We found the Messiah!"—which means the Christ.

42.text: Then he brought Simon to Jesus. Jesus looked him over and said, "You Simon, son of John? From now on, you go by Cephas"—which means Rock.

43.text: The next day, Jesus decided to go to Galilee. He found Philip and said, "Come roll with Me."

44.text: Philip was from Bethsaida, same town as Andrew and Peter.

45.text: Philip found Nathanael and told him, "We found the One Moses wrote about in the law—and the prophets too—Jesus of Nazareth, son of Joseph."

46.text: Nathanael said, "Nazareth? Ain't nothin' good come from there." Philip said, "Come see for yourself."

47.text: Jesus saw Nathanael comin' and said, "Now that's a real Israelite—ain't no cap in him!"

48.text: Nathanael asked, "How You know me?" Jesus said, "I saw you while you was sittin' under the fig tree, before Philip even called you."

49.text: Nathanael said, "Rabbi, You really are the Son of God. You the King of Israel!"

50.text: Jesus said, "You believe 'cause I said I saw you under that tree? You gon' see way more than that."

51.text: Then He said, "For real, I'm tellin' you—you gon' see heaven wide open, and angels goin' up and down on the Son of Man."

1.text: Three days later, there was a wedding in Cana over in Galilee. Jesus' mama was there too.

2.text: Jesus and His disciples got invited to the wedding as well.

3.text: When the wine ran out, Jesus' mama said to Him, "They outta wine."

4.text: Jesus said, "Ma'am, what that gotta do with Me? My time ain't come yet."

5.text: But His mama told the servants, "Whatever He tell y'all to do, just do it."

6.text: There was six big stone water jugs sittin' there—used for Jewish purification rituals. Each one held like twenty to thirty gallons.

7.text: Jesus said, "Fill up the waterpots with water." So they filled 'em all the way up to the top.

8.text: Then He told 'em, "Now scoop some out and take it to the master of the feast." So they did.

9.text: The master of the feast tasted the water that had turned into wine. He ain't know where it came from, but the servants did. The master called the groom over.

10.text: He said, "Man, usually folks bring out the good wine first, and then when folks good and tipsy, they bring out the cheap stuff. But you done saved the good wine for last!"

11.text: This was the first miracle Jesus did, right there in Cana of Galilee. It showed His glory, and His disciples started really believin' in Him.

12.text: After that, Jesus rolled down to Capernaum with His mama, His brothers, and His disciples. They ain't stay long.

13.text: The Jewish Passover was comin' up, so Jesus went up to Jerusalem.

14.text: At the temple, He saw folks sellin' oxen, sheep, and doves, and He saw the money changers doin' business too.

15.text: Jesus made a whip outta cords, and started drivin' everybody out the temple—both people and animals. He flipped the money changers' tables and dumped all their coins out.

16.text: Then He told the dove sellers, "Get this stuff outta here! Don't turn My Father's house into a marketplace!"

17.text: His disciples remembered what the Scriptures said: "Zeal for Your house done ate Me up."

18.text: Then the Jewish leaders said, "What sign You gon' show us to prove You got authority to do all this?"

19.text: Jesus answered, "Tear down this temple, and I'll raise it back up in three days."

20.text: They said, "Man, it took forty-six years to build this temple. You think You can raise it in three days?"

21.text: But Jesus was talkin' about His body as the temple.

22.text: After He rose from the dead, His disciples remembered what He had said. That's when they fully believed the Scripture and His words.

23.text: While He was in Jerusalem for Passover, during the festival, a lotta folks believed in His name when they saw the miracles He was doin'.

24.text: But Jesus ain't put His trust in them, 'cause He knew what people was really about.

25.text: He ain't need nobody to tell Him what was inside folks—He already knew what was in their hearts.

1.text: Now check it out - there was this Pharisee named Nicodemus who was part of the Jewish leadership council.

2.text: This dude came to Jesus at night and said, 'Rabbi, we know you gotta be from God for real because ain't nobody could do these miraculous signs you doing unless God is with them.'

3.text: Jesus hit him back saying, 'Real talk, I'm telling you straight up - can't nobody see God's kingdom unless they get born again.'

4.text: Nicodemus was confused like, 'How somebody supposed to be born when they already old? You can't go back in your mama's womb and get born again!'

5.text: Jesus broke it down, 'Listen close now - ain't nobody getting into God's kingdom unless they born through water and the Spirit.'

6.text: What comes from human nature is human, but what comes from the Spirit is spirit.

7.text: Don't be shocked when I tell you that y'all gotta be born again.

8.text: The wind moves however it wants to. You hear it doing its thing, but you can't tell where it's coming from or where it's heading. That's exactly how it is with everybody born from the Spirit.

9.text: Nicodemus still wasn't getting it, asking, 'How all this supposed to work?'

10.text: Jesus was like, 'You supposed to be teaching Israel, and you don't even understand this?'

11.text: Real talk, we speaking on what we know and seen firsthand, but y'all still ain't trying to hear us.

12.text: If y'all don't believe when I'm talking bout earthly things, how you gonna believe when I start speaking on heavenly business?

13.text: Nobody ever made it to heaven except the One who came down from there - the Son of Man.

14.text: Just like Moses had to lift up that snake in the desert, that's how the Son of Man gotta be lifted up too,

15.text: so everybody who believes in Him can get that eternal life.

16.text: For real, God was showing mad love to the world when He gave up His one and only Son. Now anybody who believes in Him ain't gotta die but they getting eternal life instead.

17.text: See, God ain't send His Son to earth to condemn everybody. Nah, He sent Him to save the world through Him.

18.text: Whoever believes in Him ain't getting condemned. But if you ain't believing, you already condemned cause you ain't put your faith in God's one and only Son.

19.text: Here's the real situation: Light came through to the world, but people was feeling the darkness more than the light cause they was doing dirty.

20.text: Everybody out here doing wrong hates the light and won't come near it, cause they don't want their dirt exposed.

21.text: But people living in truth come to the light so everybody can see that what they doing is God's work.

22.text: After all this went down, Jesus and His crew headed out to the Judean countryside. He stayed there with them for a minute, baptizing folks.

23.text: John was doing his thing too, baptizing at Aenon near Salim cause there was plenty of water there, and people kept coming through to get baptized.

24.text: (This was before they locked John up.)

25.text: Some of John's disciples got into it with a Jewish dude about purification.

26.text: They came to John like, 'Rabbi, you know that dude who was with you on the other side of the Jordan? The one you was cosigning? Well, He out here baptizing now and everybody going to Him instead.'

27.text: John responded, 'Look, nobody can get nothing unless heaven gives it to them.'

28.text: Y'all can back me up on this - I been saying I ain't the Messiah. I'm just the one sent ahead to get things ready.

29.text: The bride belongs to the groom, feel me? The groom's homie just stands by, listening for him, getting hype when he hears the groom's voice. That's the kind of joy I got right now, and it's complete.

30.text: He gotta become more important while I become less important.

31.text: The One who comes from above is above everybody. Whoever's from earth belongs to earth and speaks earth talk. But the One from heaven is above all that.

32.text: He testifying bout what He seen and heard, but hardly nobody trying to accept His testimony.

33.text: Whoever does accept His testimony is cosigning that God is truthful.

34.text: The One God sent speaks God's words, cause God ain't holding back the Spirit when it comes to Him.

35.text: The Father loves the Son and put everything in His hands.

36.text: Whoever believes in the Son got eternal life right now, but whoever ain't trying to hear the Son ain't gonna see life - they just gonna keep catching God's wrath.

1.text: When the Lord heard the Pharisees was talkin' about how Jesus was makin' and baptizin' more disciples than John,

2.text: (even though Jesus Himself wasn't baptizin', His disciples were),

3.text: He left Judea and went back up to Galilee.

4.text: But He had to go through Samaria to get there.

5.text: He pulled up to a town in Samaria called Sychar, close to the land Jacob gave his son Joseph.

6.text: Jacob's well was there, and Jesus, tired from the trip, sat down by the well. It was about noon.

7.text: A Samaritan woman came to get some water. Jesus said, "Can you get Me a drink?"

8.text: His disciples had gone into town to grab some food.

9.text: The Samaritan woman said, "Hold up—you a Jew, and I'm a Samaritan woman. Why you askin' me for a drink?" (Jews ain't mess with Samaritans like that.)

10.text: Jesus said, "If you knew the gift God got for you, and who I am, you'd be askin' Me for water—and I'd give you livin' water."

11.text: She said, "Sir, You ain't got nothin' to draw with, and this well deep. Where You gon' get that livin' water?

12.text: You think You greater than Jacob, our ancestor, who gave us this well? He drank from it, so did his sons and his animals."

13.text: Jesus said, "Anybody who drinks this water gon' be thirsty again.

14.text: But whoever drinks the water I give won't ever be thirsty again. That water gon' turn into a spring inside them—overflowin' with eternal life."

15.text: The woman said, "Sir, give me that water then! So I won't be thirsty or have to come back here."

16.text: Jesus said, "Go get your man and come back."

17.text: She said, "I don't got no man." Jesus said, "You right when you say that.

18.text: You done had five men, and the one you got now ain't your husband. So yeah, you told the truth."

19.text: She said, "Sir… I see You a prophet.

20.text: Our people worshipped on this mountain, but y'all Jews say we gotta worship in Jerusalem."

21.text: Jesus said, "Woman, believe Me—time's comin' when it won't matter if you worship on this mountain or in Jerusalem.

22.text: Y'all worship what you don't know. We worship what we know, 'cause salvation comes through the Jews.

23.text: But the time comin'—matter fact, it's here now—when real worshippers gon' worship the Father in spirit and in truth. That's the kind the Father lookin' for.

24.text: God is Spirit, so if you gon' worship Him, it gotta be in spirit and truth."

25.text: She said, "I know the Messiah's comin'—He's called the Christ. When He gets here, He gon' break it all down."

26.text: Jesus said, "That's Me. The one you talkin' to."

27.text: Just then, His disciples came back. They was shocked He was talkin' to a woman, but nobody asked, "What You want?" or "Why You talkin' to her?"

28.text: She left her water jar and ran back to the city. She told the people,

29.text: "Come see a man who told me everything I ever did. Could He be the Christ?"

30.text: They left the city and went lookin' for Him.

31.text: Meanwhile, His disciples was sayin', "Rabbi, You need to eat something."

32.text: Jesus said, "I got food y'all don't know nothin' about."

33.text: The disciples looked at each other like, "Who brought Him food?"

34.text: Jesus said, "My food is doin' the will of the One who sent Me, and finishin' His work.

35.text: Y'all always say, 'Four more months till harvest,' but I'm tellin' y'all—look around. The fields already ripe.

36.text: The one who harvests gets paid and gathers fruit that lasts forever. So the sower and the reaper both get to celebrate.

37.text: The sayin' true: one person plants, another one harvests.

38.text: I sent y'all to harvest fields y'all ain't work for. Other folks did the grindin', and y'all just steppin' into the blessing."

39.text: A lotta Samaritans from that town believed in Him just off what the woman said: "He told me everything I ever did."

40.text: When the Samaritans came to Him, they begged Him to stay. So He stayed two more days.

41.text: And way more folks believed—this time off Jesus' own words.

42.text: They told the woman, "We believe now not just 'cause of what you said, but 'cause we heard Him ourselves. Now we know He's the Christ, the Savior of the world."

43.text: After them two days, Jesus left and went back to Galilee.

44.text: Jesus had already said, "A prophet don't get no love in his own hometown."

45.text: But when He got to Galilee, the people welcomed Him, 'cause they saw everything He did in Jerusalem during the festival—they was there too.

46.text: He went back to Cana in Galilee, where He turned water into wine. There was this official whose son was sick back in Capernaum.

47.text: When he heard Jesus was back from Judea, he went to Him and begged Him to come heal his son, who was about to die.

48.text: Jesus said, "Y'all won't believe unless you see signs and miracles, huh?"

49.text: The man said, "Sir, please come before my child dies!"

50.text: Jesus told him, "Go on home—your son's alive." The man believed what Jesus said and headed back.

51.text: While he was on his way, his servants met him and said, "Your son is alive!"

52.text: He asked what time the boy got better. They said, "Yesterday, around one in the afternoon, the fever broke."

53.text: The father realized that's the exact time Jesus had said, "Your son lives." And he believed—him and his whole household.

54.text: This was the second miracle Jesus did after comin' back from Judea into Galilee.

1.text: After that, there was a Jewish feast, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.

2.text: In Jerusalem, by the Sheep Gate, there's a pool called Bethesda in Hebrew. It got five porches.

3.text: A whole crowd of sick folks would lay there—blind, lame, and paralyzed—waitin' on the water to move.

4.text: 'Cause at certain times, an angel would come stir up the water. First one in after that? Got healed from whatever they had.

5.text: One man had been sick for thirty-eight years.

6.text: When Jesus saw him layin' there and knew he been in that shape for a long time, He asked, "You tryna get well or nah?"

7.text: The man said, "Sir, I ain't got nobody to help me into the pool when the water gets stirred. Every time I try, somebody beats me to it."

8.text: Jesus told him, "Get up. Pick up your mat and walk."

9.text: Right then, the man got healed. He picked up his mat and started walkin'. And it just so happened that was on the Sabbath day.

10.text: The Jewish leaders told the man who got healed, "Hey, it's the Sabbath. You ain't supposed to be carryin' that mat."

11.text: He said, "The man who healed me is the one who told me, 'Pick up your mat and walk.'"

12.text: They asked, "Who told you that?"

13.text: But the healed man ain't know who it was—Jesus had dipped into the crowd right after.

14.text: Later on, Jesus found him in the temple and said, "Look at you—healed and all. Don't go back to sin, or something worse might come on you."

15.text: The man left and told the Jewish leaders it was Jesus who healed him.

16.text: That's why the Jews started goin' after Jesus and tryna kill Him—'cause He did this on the Sabbath.

17.text: Jesus told 'em, "My Father been workin' non-stop, and I'm workin' too."

18.text: That made 'em even madder. Not only was He breakin' Sabbath rules—they said He was makin' Himself equal with God by callin' God His Father.

19.text: Jesus said, "For real, for real—I'm tellin' y'all—the Son don't do nothin' on His own. He only do what He sees the Father do. Whatever the Father does, the Son do too.

20.text: The Father loves the Son and shows Him everything. And He gon' show even bigger things—just wait, y'all gon' be shook.

21.text: Just like the Father raises the dead and gives 'em life, the Son gives life to whoever He wants.

22.text: The Father ain't judging nobody—He gave that whole job to the Son.

23.text: So everybody gotta honor the Son just like they honor the Father. If you ain't honoring the Son, you ain't honoring the Father who sent Him.

24.text: Listen up—I'm tellin' you the truth: if you hear what I'm sayin' and believe the One who sent Me, you got eternal life. You ain't gotta worry about judgment—you already crossed from death to life.

25.text: Truth is, the time's comin'—matter fact, it's already here—when the dead gon' hear the voice of God's Son, and the ones who listen? Gon' live.

26.text: Just like the Father got life in Himself, He gave the Son that same kinda life.

27.text: And He gave the Son authority to judge too—'cause He the Son of Man.

28.text: Don't get it twisted—time's comin' when everybody in the grave gon' hear His voice,

29.text: and they gon' come out—those who did good things gon' rise up to eternal life, and the ones who did wrong? Gon' rise up to face judgment.

30.text: I don't do nothin' on My own. I judge based on what I hear. And My judgment right—'cause I ain't here to do what I want, but what the One who sent Me wants.

31.text: If I was out here speakin' on My own behalf, y'all wouldn't need to listen.

32.text: But there's Somebody else who speaks for Me, and I know He tellin' the truth.

33.text: Y'all sent folks to John, and he told y'all straight-up truth.

34.text: I don't need no man's validation—but I said all that so y'all might get saved.

35.text: John was like a lit-up lamp, burnin' bright, and for a little while, y'all liked that glow.

36.text: But I got somethin' better than John's testimony—the works the Father gave Me to do. The miracles I'm doin'? They prove the Father sent Me.

37.text: And the Father Himself, who sent Me, already testified 'bout Me. But y'all never heard His voice or seen Him.

38.text: His word don't even live in y'all, 'cause you ain't believe the One He sent.

39.text: Y'all stay searchin' the Scriptures thinkin' they the key to eternal life. But they really talkin' 'bout Me.

40.text: And still—you won't come to Me to get that life.

41.text: I don't need no clout from people.

42.text: But I know y'all—y'all ain't got the love of God in you.

43.text: I came in My Father's name and y'all ain't accept Me. But let somebody else come in they own name? Y'all quick to receive them.

44.text: How you gon' believe when you chasin' praise from each other but ain't seekin' the honor that come from God alone?

45.text: Don't think I'ma be the one to snitch on y'all to the Father. Moses—the one y'all swear by? He already speakin' against y'all.

46.text: If y'all really believed Moses, you'd believe Me—'cause he was talkin' about Me.

47.text: But since y'all don't even believe what he wrote, how you gon' believe what I'm sayin'?

1.text: After all that, Jesus crossed over the Sea of Galilee—also called the Sea of Tiberias.

2.text: A big crowd followed Him 'cause they seen the signs He did when He healed the sick.

3.text: Jesus went up on a mountain and sat down with His disciples.

4.text: The Jewish Passover was gettin' close.

5.text: Jesus looked up, saw a big crowd comin' toward Him, and said to Philip, "Where we gon' buy bread to feed all these folks?"

6.text: He said that to test Philip, 'cause Jesus already knew what He was gon' do.

7.text: Philip said, "Man, even 200 days' worth of money wouldn't be enough to give everybody even a lil piece."

8.text: Then Andrew, Simon Peter's brother, said,

9.text: "There's a boy here with five barley loaves and two small fish—but that ain't nearly enough for all these people."

10.text: Jesus said, "Tell everybody to sit down." There was a lotta grass there, so they sat down—about five thousand men.

11.text: Jesus took the loaves, gave thanks, and passed 'em to the disciples to hand out. Same with the fish—folks ate as much as they wanted.

12.text: When everybody was full, Jesus told His disciples, "Gather up all the leftovers so none of it gets wasted."

13.text: They picked up twelve baskets full of scraps from the five loaves—just from what was left after folks ate.

14.text: When the people saw the miracle Jesus had done, they said, "This gotta be the Prophet we been waitin' for!"

15.text: But when Jesus realized they was about to come snatch Him up and force Him to be king, He slipped away to the mountain by Himself.

16.text: That evenin', His disciples went down to the sea,

17.text: Got in a boat and started headin' toward Capernaum. It was dark, and Jesus hadn't come back yet.

18.text: A strong wind came through and stirred the water up.

19.text: After they rowed about three or four miles, they saw Jesus walkin' on the water, comin' toward the boat—and they got scared.

20.text: But Jesus said, "It's Me. Don't be scared."

21.text: They let Him in the boat, and right then—they hit land, exactly where they was headin'.

22.text: The next day, the crowd that had stayed on the other side of the sea realized there was only one boat, and that Jesus didn't leave in it—His disciples did.

23.text: More boats came in from Tiberias, near where they had eaten the bread after Jesus gave thanks.

24.text: When the crowd saw Jesus and His disciples weren't there, they got in the boats and went to Capernaum to look for Him.

25.text: When they found Him across the sea, they said, "Rabbi, when You get over here?"

26.text: Jesus said, "Truth is, y'all lookin' for Me not 'cause you saw signs, but 'cause you got full off that bread."

27.text: "Don't work for food that spoils—work for the food that gives eternal life. That's what the Son of Man gon' give you. God the Father already stamped Him with approval."

28.text: They said, "What we gotta do to do God's work?"

29.text: Jesus said, "Here's God's work: believe in the One He sent."

30.text: Then they asked, "What sign You gon' do so we can believe You? What You gon' show us?

31.text: Our ancestors ate manna in the desert, like Scripture says: 'He gave them bread from heaven to eat.'"

32.text: Jesus said, "Listen close—Moses ain't give y'all that bread from heaven. My Father gives the real bread from heaven."

33.text: "The bread God gives is the One who comes down from heaven and gives life to the whole world."

34.text: They said, "Lord, give us that bread every day."

35.text: Jesus said, "I am the bread of life. Whoever comes to Me won't ever go hungry. Whoever believes in Me won't ever be thirsty."

36.text: But I already told y'all—y'all seen Me and still don't believe.

37.text: Everybody the Father gives Me gon' come to Me. And anybody that comes to Me? I'll never turn 'em away.

38.text: I ain't come down from heaven to do what I want—I came to do what the One who sent Me wants.

39.text: And this is His will: that I don't lose none of the ones He gave Me, but raise 'em back up on the last day.

40.text: His will is that anybody who sees the Son and believes in Him gets eternal life. I'll raise 'em up on the last day too.

41.text: Then the Jews started complainin' 'cause He said, "I'm the bread that came down from heaven."

42.text: They was like, "Ain't this Jesus, Joseph's boy? We know His mom and dad. How He gon' say He came down from heaven?"

43.text: Jesus said, "Y'all need to stop murmurin' amongst yourselves.

44.text: Nobody can come to Me unless the Father who sent Me draws 'em. And I'll raise that one up on the last day.
