21.text: Peter remembered and said, "Rabbi, look! That fig tree you cursed is dead!"

22.text: Jesus said, "Have faith in God.

23.text: I'm tellin' y'all the truth—if you say to this mountain, 'Move and throw yourself in the sea,' and don't doubt but believe it's gon' happen—it will happen.

24.text: That's why I say, when you pray and ask for somethin', believe like it's already yours—and it'll be yours.

25.text: But when you pray, if you holdin' something against somebody, forgive them, so your Father in heaven can forgive you.

26.text: But if you don't forgive, your Father ain't forgivin' you either."

27.text: They came back to Jerusalem. As Jesus was walkin' in the temple, the chief priests, scribes, and elders rolled up on Him.

28.text: They asked, "Who gave You the right to do all this? Who said You could?"

29.text: Jesus said, "I'ma ask y'all one thing, and if y'all answer Me, I'll tell you where my authority come from.

30.text: John's baptism—was that from heaven or just from man? Tell Me that."

31.text: They huddled up like, "If we say 'heaven,' He gon' ask why we ain't believe John.

32.text: But if we say 'man,' these folks gon' turn on us 'cause they all think John was a real prophet."

33.text: So they played it safe and said, "We don't know." And Jesus said, "Then I ain't tellin' y'all either."

1.text: Jesus started speakin' to them using stories. He said, "A man planted a vineyard, put a fence around it, dug out a place for the wine to drip, built a lookout tower, then rented it out to some workers and dipped out to another country.

2.text: When it was time to harvest, he sent a servant to collect his share of the fruit.

3.text: But the workers grabbed that man, beat him down, and sent him back empty-handed.

4.text: Then he sent another servant. This time, they threw rocks at him, hit him in the head, and treated him like trash.

5.text: The man sent another one, and they straight-up killed him. He kept sendin' more—some got beat down, some got killed.

6.text: Now the man had one left—his son, who he loved dearly. He figured they'd respect his son, so he sent him last.

7.text: But those workers said to each other, 'That's the heir! Let's kill him, and the vineyard gon' be ours.'

8.text: So they grabbed him, killed him, and threw his body out the vineyard.

9.text: "So what y'all think the owner gon' do? He gon' pull up, destroy them wicked workers, and lease the vineyard to somebody else.

10.text: Ain't y'all read this before? 'The stone the builders threw away Done became the cornerstone.

11.text: The Lord did that, And it's wild to see.'"

12.text: They wanted to snatch Jesus up right there, 'cause they knew He was talkin' about them. But they was scared of the crowd, so they dipped off instead.

13.text: Then they sent some Pharisees and Herod's folks to Jesus, tryna trap Him in His words.

14.text: They came up and said, "Teacher, we know You real and don't care about nobody's status. You speak the truth straight from God. So tell us—should we pay taxes to Caesar or not?"

15.text: Jesus peeped their game and said, "Why y'all testin' Me? Bring Me a coin so I can see it."

16.text: They handed Him one. He asked, "Whose face and name on here?" They said, "Caesar's."

17.text: Jesus said, "Then give Caesar what belongs to Caesar—and give God what belongs to God." They ain't know what to say after that.

18.text: Then the Sadducees—who don't believe in resurrection—stepped up and asked Jesus a question.

19.text: "Teacher," they said, "Moses told us if a man dies without kids, his brother gotta marry the widow and give her children in his name.

20.text: Now, there were seven brothers. First one got married, died, no kids.

21.text: Second brother married her, died too, still no kids. Same with the third.

22.text: All seven brothers had her and died without children. Then the woman died too.

23.text: So when everybody comes back to life, whose wife she gon' be? All seven had her."

24.text: Jesus said, "Y'all wrong, and it's 'cause y'all don't know the Scriptures or God's power.

25.text: When folks rise from the dead, they don't get married—they gon' be like angels in heaven.

26.text: And about the dead rising—didn't you read what Moses wrote about the burning bush? God said, 'I'm the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.'

27.text: He ain't the God of the dead—He's God of the living. Y'all real wrong on this one."

28.text: One of the scribes overheard the convo and saw Jesus had great answers. He asked, "Which commandment is the most important of all?"

29.text: Jesus said, "The first one is: 'Hear, O Israel, the Lord our God is one.

30.text: Love the Lord your God with all your heart, all your soul, all your mind, and all your strength.'

31.text: And the second one right behind it is: 'Love your neighbor like you love yourself.' Ain't no commandments greater than these."

32.text: The scribe said, "Facts, Teacher. You spoke real. There's one God, no other.

33.text: Lovin' Him with everything you got—and lovin' your neighbor—that's better than any burnt offering or sacrifice."

34.text: Jesus saw the man had real wisdom and told him, "You not far from God's Kingdom." After that, nobody had the nerve to ask Him nothin' else.

35.text: While teachin' in the temple, Jesus said, "How y'all say the Christ is David's son?

36.text: 'Cause David himself, speakin' by the Spirit, said: 'The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at My right hand Till I put Your enemies under Your feet.'

37.text: If David calls Him 'Lord,' how is He his son?" The crowd was lovin' what Jesus said.

38.text: Jesus kept teachin', "Watch out for them scribes who like to strut around in long robes, lovin' the attention in the streets.

39.text: They want the best seats in the synagogue and the top spots at dinner.

40.text: They be robbin' widows and actin' holy with them long prayers. Trust, they gon' be judged harder."

41.text: Jesus sat across from the temple offering box and watched folks droppin' in their money. The rich were droppin' big stacks.

42.text: But this one poor widow came up and dropped in two little coins—barely anything.

43.text: Jesus called His disciples and said, "Let me tell y'all the truth: That poor woman gave more than everybody else.

44.text: They gave outta their overflow. But she gave everything she had—even the little she was livin' on."

1.text: As Jesus was leavin' the temple, one of His disciples said, "Teacher, look at these big ol' stones and buildings!"

2.text: Jesus said, "You see all this? Ain't a single stone gon' be left sittin' on another. All of it gettin' torn down."

3.text: Later on, while Jesus was chillin' on the Mount of Olives across from the temple, Peter, James, John, and Andrew pulled Him to the side and asked,

4.text: "Tell us, when's all this gon' happen? What signs should we be watchin' for?"

5.text: Jesus started in: "Y'all better watch out and don't let nobody play y'all.

6.text: A lotta folks gon' come in My name talkin' 'I'm Him!' and foolin' folks left and right.

7.text: You gon' hear 'bout wars poppin' off and whispers of more war. Don't panic. That stuff gotta happen, but that ain't the end yet.

8.text: Whole nations gon' beef with each other. Kingdoms too. Earthquakes gon' hit different places, famines gon' pop up. But that's just the beginning—just the labor pains.

9.text: Look, be on guard. They gon' hand y'all over to courts, beat y'all in church, and drag y'all in front of kings 'cause of Me. Y'all gon' be witnesses in front of 'em.

10.text: But first, this gospel gotta be preached everywhere, all across the nations.

11.text: When they snatch y'all up and hand y'all over, don't stress about what to say. Just say whatever the Spirit gives you in that moment—it ain't you talkin', it's the Holy Ghost.

12.text: Folks gon' be turnin' on each other—brother against brother, daddy against child. Kids gon' snitch on parents, get 'em killed.

13.text: Everybody gon' hate y'all 'cause of Me. But whoever sticks it out to the end? They the ones gon' be saved."

14.text: "Now when y'all see that wild mess Daniel talked about—the 'abomination of desolation'—standin' where it don't belong (yeah, reader, I'm talkin' to you), run for the hills if you in Judea.

15.text: If you up on the roof, don't even go inside to grab nothin'.

16.text: If you out in the field, don't run back for your coat.

17.text: Prayers up for pregnant women and moms with babies—it's gon' be hard for them.

18.text: Pray it don't go down in the winter.

19.text: 'Cause those days gon' be hell—worse than anything that's ever happened since God made the world.

20.text: If God ain't cut those days short, nobody would make it. But for the sake of His chosen ones, He shortened it."

21.text: "If somebody tell y'all, 'Hey, Christ over here!' or 'He right there!'—don't believe 'em.

22.text: Fake messiahs and false prophets gon' pop up doin' wild signs and wonders, tryin' to trick even God's chosen, if they could.

23.text: So stay alert! I already told y'all what's comin'."

24.text: "But after all that tribulation, the sun gon' go dark, the moon won't shine,

25.text: the stars gon' fall, and even the powers in heaven gon' shake.

26.text: Then they gon' see the Son of Man comin' through the clouds, flexin' with power and glory.

27.text: He gon' send out angels to round up His chosen from everywhere—from the far ends of earth to the highest place in heaven."

28.text: "Now check this parable out—when a fig tree starts gettin' soft branches and sproutin' leaves, you already know summer almost here.

29.text: Same thing here: when y'all see these signs goin' down, know it's right around the corner.

30.text: I'm tellin' y'all for real—this generation won't pass before all this happens.

31.text: Heaven and earth might fade out, but My words? They stay forever."

32.text: "But when it's all gon' pop off? Nobody knows that day or hour—not the angels, not even the Son—only the Father know.

33.text: So stay woke, watch, and pray. You don't know when it's goin' down.

34.text: It's like a man leavin' the crib and puttin' his folks in charge, each one with a job, and the door guy on lookout.

35.text: So stay ready—you don't know if the boss comin' at night, at midnight, when the rooster crows, or early morning.

36.text: You don't wanna get caught sleepin' when He shows up outta nowhere.

37.text: What I'm tellin' y'all, I'm tellin' everybody: Watch!"

1.text: Two days before Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the chief priests and scribes was plottin' on how they could catch Jesus slippin' and kill Him on the low.

2.text: But they was like, "Not during the feast tho, or folks might wild out and start a riot."

3.text: Jesus was chillin' in Bethany at Simon the leper's spot, sittin' at the table, when this woman came through with a fancy alabaster jar full of expensive spikenard oil. She cracked it open and poured it all over His head.

4.text: Some folks at the table got mad and started whisperin', "Why she wastin' that good-smellin' oil like that?"

5.text: "She coulda sold that for over 300 coins and gave the money to the poor." And they started scoldin' her hard.

6.text: But Jesus shut it down like, "Leave her alone. Why y'all stressin' her? She just did somethin' real beautiful for Me."

7.text: "Poor folks gon' always be around, and y'all can help 'em whenever. But I ain't gon' be here like that forever."

8.text: "She did what she could—anointed My body early, gettin' Me ready for burial."

9.text: "I'ma tell y'all the truth—wherever this gospel gets preached around the world, folks gon' talk about what she did. That's her legacy."

10.text: Then Judas Iscariot—one of Jesus' own crew—went to the chief priests to sell Him out.

11.text: When they heard that, they got hype and promised to pay him. From then on, Judas was lookin' for the right time to hand Jesus over.

12.text: On the first day of Unleavened Bread, when they was sacrificin' the Passover lamb, the disciples asked Jesus, "Where You want us to go and set things up so You can eat the Passover meal?"

13.text: Jesus sent two of them out and said, "Go into the city, and you'll meet a man carryin' a water jug. Follow him."

14.text: "When he go in the house, say to the owner, 'The Teacher said, where the guest room at for Me and My crew to eat the Passover?'"

15.text: "He gon' show y'all a big upstairs room, already set. That's the spot. Get it ready."

16.text: The disciples dipped out, went to the city, and found everything just like Jesus said. So they prepped the Passover meal.

17.text: That evening, Jesus came through with the Twelve.

18.text: While they was sittin' down eatin', Jesus said, "For real, one of y'all sittin' at this table with Me is gon' betray Me."

19.text: They all got shook and sad, and started askin' one by one, "It ain't me, is it?"

20.text: Jesus said, "It's one of the Twelve—one of y'all dippin' bread in the same dish as Me."

21.text: "The Son of Man gon' go just like it was written, but woe to the one who sells Him out. It woulda been better if he ain't even been born."

22.text: While they was eatin', Jesus grabbed some bread, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to them. He said, "Take it. This My body."

23.text: Then He took the cup, gave thanks, passed it around, and they all drank.

24.text: He said, "This My blood—the new covenant—poured out for many."

25.text: "I'ma tell y'all straight—I ain't drinkin' no more wine until I drink it fresh in God's Kingdom."

26.text: After they sang a hymn, they rolled out to the Mount of Olives.

27.text: Jesus told 'em, "Tonight, all y'all gon' fall back 'cause of Me. The Scriptures say, 'I'ma strike the Shepherd, and the sheep gon' scatter.'"

28.text: "But after I rise up, I'll be in Galilee waitin' on y'all."

29.text: Peter said, "Even if everybody else fall off, I ain't goin' nowhere."

30.text: Jesus replied, "Truth is, tonight—before the rooster crows twice—you gon' deny Me three times."

31.text: Peter got loud with it, "Even if I gotta die with You, I won't deny You!" And all the others was sayin' the same thing.

32.text: They pulled up to a place called Gethsemane. Jesus told the rest, "Y'all sit here while I go pray."

33.text: He took Peter, James, and John with Him, and He started feelin' real heavy and troubled.

34.text: He said, "My soul is crushed, y'all… like I'm dyin' inside. Stay here and keep watch."

35.text: He walked a little farther, fell on the ground, and started prayin' that maybe the moment could pass Him by.

36.text: He said, "Abba, Father, You can do anything. Please take this cup from Me. But still—not My will, but Yours."

37.text: Then Jesus came back and caught them sleepin'. He said to Peter, "Simon, you sleepin'? You couldn't stay woke for one hour?"

38.text: "Watch and pray, so you don't fall into temptation. The spirit be down, but the flesh? Weak."

39.text: He left again and prayed, sayin' the same thing.

40.text: When He came back, they was knocked out again—their eyes was heavy. They ain't even know what to say to Him.

41.text: Third time He came back, He said, "Y'all still sleepin' and layin' up? That's enough. Time's up. The Son of Man 'bout to be handed over to some sinners."

42.text: "Get up, let's go. My betrayer right here."

43.text: Right while He was still talkin', Judas—one of the Twelve—rolled up with a whole mob. They had swords and clubs, sent by the chief priests, scribes, and elders.

44.text: Judas had told them ahead of time, "The one I kiss—that's Him. Grab Him and make sure He don't get away."

45.text: He walked up on Jesus, said, "Rabbi! Rabbi!" and kissed Him.

46.text: Then they grabbed Jesus and arrested Him.

47.text: But one of the people standin' there pulled out a sword, swung on the high priest's servant, and sliced off his ear.

48.text: Jesus said, "Y'all really came at Me like I'm some kind of criminal? Swords and clubs and all that?"

49.text: "I was at the temple every day teachin', and y'all ain't touch Me. But all this gotta go down so the Scriptures can come true."

50.text: Then everybody dipped. Left Him by Himself.

51.text: There was a young man followin' Jesus, wearin' nothin' but a linen sheet around his body. When they tried to grab him—

52.text: He slipped out the cloth and ran off naked.

53.text: They took Jesus to the high priest, where all the chief priests, elders, and scribes was already gathered up.

54.text: Peter followed Him from a distance, all the way into the high priest's courtyard. He sat with the servants, warm by the fire.

55.text: The chief priests and whole council was lookin' for something to use against Jesus so they could get Him killed—but they couldn't find nothin'.

56.text: A bunch of folks lied on Him, but their stories ain't match.

57.text: Then some stood up and lied again, sayin',

58.text: "We heard Him say, 'I'll tear down this temple made by hands and in three days build another one not made by hands.'"

59.text: But even then, they couldn't get their lies to line up.

60.text: The high priest stood up in the middle and said, "You not gon' say nothin'? You hear what these folks sayin' about You?"

61.text: But Jesus ain't say a word. He stayed quiet. So the high priest asked again, "Are You the Messiah? The Son of the Blessed One?"

62.text: Jesus said, "I am. And you gon' see the Son of Man sittin' at the right hand of Power, comin' with the clouds of heaven."

63.text: Then the high priest ripped his clothes and said, "We don't need no more witnesses!"

64.text: "Y'all heard that blasphemy. What y'all think?" And they all said, "He deserves to die."

65.text: Then they started spittin' on Him, blindfolded Him, hit Him, and said, "Prophesy!" Even the officers was slappin' Him around.

66.text: Meanwhile, Peter was down in the courtyard. One of the high priest's servant girls came by.

67.text: She saw Peter warm by the fire, looked at him hard, and said, "You was with Jesus of Nazareth too."

68.text: But he denied it: "I don't even know what you talkin' about." Then he stepped out on the porch—and the rooster crowed.

69.text: The same servant girl saw him again and told the folks standin' there, "He one of them."

70.text: He denied it again. Then a little later, the people nearby said to Peter, "You gotta be one of them. You a Galilean—your accent givin' it away."

71.text: Peter started cussin' and swearin', "I don't know this Man y'all talkin' about!"

72.text: The rooster crowed a second time. Then Peter remembered what Jesus told him: "Before the rooster crows twice, you gon' deny Me three times." And when he realized it, he broke down and cried.

1.text: Early in the mornin', the chief priests linked up with the elders, scribes, and the whole council. They tied Jesus up, took Him to Pilate, and handed Him over.

2.text: Pilate asked Him, "You the King of the Jews?" Jesus said, "You said it."

3.text: The chief priests started throwin' all kinds of accusations at Him.

4.text: Pilate asked Him again, "You not gon' say nothin'? You hear all this they sayin' about You?"

5.text: But Jesus ain't say a word, and that had Pilate shook.

6.text: During the festival, Pilate had a tradition—he'd let one prisoner go, whoever the people picked.

7.text: One of the locked-up folks was Barabbas. He was in there with some rebels who caught a body during a riot.

8.text: The crowd pulled up and asked Pilate to do what he usually did.

9.text: Pilate said, "Y'all want me to let go the King of the Jews?"

10.text: He knew the priests was only pushin' for Jesus' death 'cause they was jealous.

11.text: But the chief priests hyped up the crowd to ask for Barabbas instead.

12.text: Pilate asked again, "So what y'all want me to do with this one y'all call King of the Jews?"

13.text: They shouted, "Crucify Him!"

14.text: Pilate said, "Why? What He do wrong?" But they just yelled louder, "Crucify Him!"

15.text: So Pilate, tryna keep the people happy, let Barabbas go. Then he had Jesus beaten and handed Him over to be crucified.

16.text: The soldiers took Jesus into the palace, called the Praetorium, and brought the whole squad together.

17.text: They dressed Him in purple and twisted a crown of thorns, put it on His head.

18.text: They started mockin' Him, sayin', "Hail, King of the Jews!"

19.text: They beat Him on the head with a stick, spit on Him, and fake-worshiped Him, kneelin' down like they was jokin'.

20.text: After all that, they took off the purple robe, put His clothes back on, and dragged Him off to be crucified.

21.text: They made a man named Simon from Cyrene—daddy to Alexander and Rufus—carry Jesus' cross. He was just passin' through from outta town.

22.text: They brought Jesus to a place called Golgotha—means "Place of the Skull."

23.text: They tried to give Him wine mixed with myrrh, but He ain't drink it.

24.text: They nailed Him to the cross and started gamblin' for His clothes to see who'd get what.

25.text: It was the third hour when they crucified Him.

26.text: They put a sign above Him sayin': "THE KING OF THE JEWS."

27.text: They crucified two criminals with Him—one on His right, one on His left.

28.text: So Scripture got fulfilled that said, "He was counted with the lawbreakers."

29.text: Folks walkin' by started talkin' trash, shakin' their heads like, "Ha! You the one who said You'd tear down the temple and rebuild it in three days?"

30.text: "Save Yourself and come down off that cross!"

31.text: The chief priests and scribes joined in the roast: "He saved other folks, but He can't save Himself!"

32.text: "If He really the Christ, the King of Israel, let Him come down from the cross right now. Then we'll believe Him." Even the two dudes on the crosses next to Him was throwin' shade.

33.text: Around noon, darkness covered the whole land until about 3 p.m.

34.text: At 3, Jesus shouted loud, "Eloi, Eloi, lama sabachthani?"—means "My God, My God, why You leave Me hangin'?"

35.text: Some folks nearby was like, "He callin' Elijah!"

36.text: Somebody ran, grabbed a sponge soaked in sour wine, stuck it on a stick, and gave it to Him to sip. They said, "Hold up—let's see if Elijah gon' come save Him."

37.text: Then Jesus cried out one last time and took His last breath.

38.text: The temple curtain tore clean down the middle—from top to bottom.

39.text: The Roman soldier standin' there saw how Jesus died and said, "Man… this really was the Son of God."

40.text: Some women was watchin' from a distance. Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James the Less and Joses, and Salome was there.

41.text: They used to follow Jesus and serve Him when He was in Galilee. A lotta other women came with Him to Jerusalem too.

42.text: That evening, since it was Preparation Day—the day before Sabbath—

43.text: Joseph from Arimathea, a respected council member who was waitin' for God's Kingdom, pulled up with courage and asked Pilate for Jesus' body.

44.text: Pilate was surprised Jesus was already dead. He asked the soldier if that was true.

45.text: Once the centurion confirmed it, Pilate gave Joseph the body.

46.text: Joseph bought some fine linen, took Jesus down, wrapped Him up, and laid Him in a tomb cut outta rock. Then he rolled a big stone in front of the entrance.

47.text: Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of Joses was watchin' where He got laid.

1.text: After the Sabbath was over, Mary Magdalene, Mary the mother of James, and Salome went and bought some spices so they could go anoint Jesus' body.

2.text: Early in the mornin' on the first day of the week, right after sunrise, they pulled up to the tomb.

3.text: On the way there, they was askin' each other, "Who gon' roll that big ol' stone out the way for us?"

4.text: But when they looked up, they saw the stone was already moved—it was huge, too.

5.text: They stepped inside the tomb and saw a young man in a long white robe sittin' on the right side. They got shook.

6.text: But he said, "Don't be scared. Y'all lookin' for Jesus from Nazareth—the One they crucified. He ain't here. He got up! Look where they laid Him."

7.text: "Now go on and tell His disciples—and make sure you tell Peter too—that He's headed to Galilee. Y'all gon' see Him there, just like He told y'all."

8.text: They ran out the tomb, tremblin' and shook. They ain't say nothin' to nobody 'cause they was scared.

9.text: Early on that first day of the week, Jesus showed Himself first to Mary Magdalene—the same one He cast seven demons outta.

10.text: She ran and told His people—the ones still grievin' and cryin'.

11.text: But when they heard He was alive and that she saw Him, they ain't believe her.

12.text: After that, He popped up in a different form to two more of them while they was walkin' out in the countryside.

13.text: They went and told the rest, but the others ain't believe them either.

14.text: Later, Jesus appeared to the Eleven while they was eatin'. He checked 'em for not believin' and for bein' hard-headed about the folks who already told 'em He rose up.

15.text: Then He said, "Go everywhere—around the whole world—and preach this good news to everybody."

16.text: "Whoever believes and gets baptized? They saved. But the ones who don't believe? Condemned."

17.text: "And this how My believers gon' roll: In My name, they gon' cast out demons. They gon' speak new tongues."

18.text: "They gon' handle snakes, drink somethin' deadly and not be hurt. They gon' lay hands on the sick and folks gon' get healed."

19.text: After Jesus finished speakin' to them, He went up to heaven and sat down at God's right hand.

20.text: And they went out preachin' everywhere. The Lord was workin' right beside them, showin' proof of the message with all kinds of signs. Amen.

1.text: This the record of Jesus Christ's family—He the Son of David, the Son of Abraham.

2.text: Abraham had Isaac, Isaac had Jacob, and Jacob had Judah and his brothers.

3.text: Judah had Perez and Zerah with Tamar, Perez had Hezron, and Hezron had Ram.

4.text: Ram had Amminadab, Amminadab had Nahshon, and Nahshon had Salmon.

5.text: Salmon had Boaz with Rahab, Boaz had Obed with Ruth, and Obed had Jesse.

6.text: Jesse had David—the king. David had Solomon with Uriah's wife.

7.text: Solomon had Rehoboam, Rehoboam had Abijah, and Abijah had Asa.

8.text: Asa had Jehoshaphat, Jehoshaphat had Joram, and Joram had Uzziah.

9.text: Uzziah had Jotham, Jotham had Ahaz, and Ahaz had Hezekiah.

10.text: Hezekiah had Manasseh, Manasseh had Amon, and Amon had Josiah.

11.text: Josiah had Jeconiah and his brothers around the time they got taken to Babylon.

12.text: After the exile to Babylon, Jeconiah had Shealtiel, and Shealtiel had Zerubbabel.

13.text: Zerubbabel had Abiud, Abiud had Eliakim, and Eliakim had Azor.

14.text: Azor had Zadok, Zadok had Achim, and Achim had Eliud.

15.text: Eliud had Eleazar, Eleazar had Matthan, and Matthan had Jacob.

16.text: Jacob had Joseph, the husband of Mary—and Mary gave birth to Jesus, who's called the Christ.

17.text: So from Abraham to David was 14 generations, from David to the exile was 14, and from the exile to Christ was another 14.

18.text: This how Jesus the Messiah was born: Mary, His mom, was engaged to Joseph. But before they came together, she got pregnant by the Holy Spirit.

19.text: Joseph, her fiancé, was a good dude. He ain't wanna embarrass her, so he planned to call off the engagement on the low.

20.text: But while he was wrestlin' with it, boom—an angel from the Lord showed up in a dream and said, "Joseph, son of David, don't be scared to take Mary as your wife. What's inside her came from the Holy Spirit.

21.text: She gon' have a son, and you gon' name Him Jesus—'cause He gon' save His people from their sins."

22.text: All this went down to fulfill what the Lord had said through the prophet:

23.text: "Look, the virgin gon' be pregnant and give birth to a son, and they gon' call Him Immanuel"—which means "God with us."

24.text: When Joseph woke up, he did what the angel told him. He married Mary,

25.text: but he didn't sleep with her 'til after she had her firstborn son. And he named Him Jesus.

1.text: After Jesus was born in Bethlehem, back when King Herod was in charge, some wise men from the East showed up in Jerusalem.

2.text: They was askin', "Where the newborn King of the Jews at? We saw His star way out East and came to worship Him."

3.text: Herod heard that and got shook—and the whole city felt the tension too.

4.text: He called in all the chief priests and Bible experts and asked, "Where the Messiah supposed to be born?"

5.text: They told him, "Bethlehem, in Judea—just like the prophet said:

6.text: 'You, Bethlehem in Judah, ain't the least outta all Judah's towns. Outta you gon' come a Ruler who gon' lead My people Israel like a shepherd.'"

7.text: Then Herod pulled the wise men to the side on the low, tryna figure out exactly when the star popped up.

8.text: He told them, "Go find that child real careful. When y'all find Him, come back and let me know, so I can worship Him too." (Yeah, aight.)

9.text: After they left, the same star they saw earlier showed back up and guided them 'til it stopped right over the place where Jesus was.

10.text: When they saw that star, they turned up with serious joy—like, over-the-top rejoicin'.

11.text: They stepped in the house, saw the child with His mama Mary, dropped to their knees, and worshiped Him. Then they opened up their treasure chests and brought out gifts—gold, frankincense, and myrrh.

12.text: But God came through in a dream and told 'em not to go back to Herod. So they dipped back to their country takin' a whole different route.

13.text: Soon as they left, boom—an angel of the Lord showed up in Joseph's dream: "Get up, take the child and His mama, and run to Egypt. Stay there 'til I tell you, 'cause Herod lookin' for the boy and tryna kill Him."

14.text: Joseph got up that night, packed up Mary and baby Jesus, and they headed to Egypt.

15.text: They stayed there until Herod died. That fulfilled what the Lord had said through the prophet: "I called My Son outta Egypt."

16.text: Herod realized the wise men played him—dude was heated. So he sent people to kill every baby boy in Bethlehem and the surrounding area, two years old and under—based on the timeline he got from the wise men.

17.text: That right there fulfilled what the prophet Jeremiah had said:

18.text: "A voice cried out in Ramah, weeping and heartbreak, Rachel cryin' for her kids. She wouldn't be comforted, 'cause they gone."

19.text: After Herod died, the angel of the Lord pulled up again in Joseph's dream while they was still in Egypt.

20.text: He said, "Get up, take the child and His mama, and go back to Israel. The folks who wanted the boy dead—they gone."

21.text: So Joseph got up, took Mary and Jesus, and went back to Israel.

22.text: But when he heard that Herod's son Archelaus was running things in Judea, he got nervous. Then God warned him in another dream, so he switched it up and headed for Galilee.

23.text: They ended up living in a town called Nazareth. That fulfilled the prophets too: "He gon' be called a Nazarene."

1.text: Back in those days, John the Baptist pulled up preachin' in the wilderness of Judea.

2.text: He was hollerin', "Y'all better repent, 'cause the Kingdom of Heaven is right around the corner!"

3.text: This him—the one Isaiah was talkin' 'bout when he said: "A voice shoutin' in the wild: Make the Lord's path ready, Clear the road for Him to come through."

4.text: John had on camel hair with a leather belt, and bruh was munchin' on locusts and wild honey.

5.text: Folks from Jerusalem, all over Judea, and around the Jordan was comin' out to hear him.

6.text: And when they came, they confessed their sins and got baptized by him in the Jordan River.

7.text: But when John saw the Pharisees and Sadducees steppin' up to get baptized, he called 'em out: "Y'all some snakes! Who warned y'all to run from what's comin'?

8.text: If you really tryna repent, show it—live right. Bear fruit that matches the change.

9.text: And don't act like you good just 'cause Abraham your ancestor. I'm tellin' y'all, God can raise up Abraham's kids from these rocks.

10.text: The ax is already sittin' at the root of the trees. Any tree not producing good fruit? It's gettin' chopped down and tossed in the fire."

11.text: "I'm baptizin' y'all with water so you can turn from sin, but somebody way greater than me is comin'. I'm not even worthy to carry His sandals. He gon' baptize y'all with the Holy Spirit and with fire.

12.text: He got His winnowing fork ready—He gon' clean up His threshing floor, gather the wheat in the barn, and burn up the chaff with a fire that don't quit."

13.text: Then Jesus came down from Galilee to the Jordan to get baptized by John.

14.text: But John tried to stop Him: "Wait—I need to get baptized by You, and You comin' to me?"

15.text: But Jesus said, Let it happen for now. We gotta do this to fulfill what's right in God's eyes. So John was like, "Bet," and baptized Him.

16.text: Soon as Jesus came up out that water, the skies opened up, and He saw God's Spirit comin' down like a dove and landin' on Him.

17.text: Then a voice boomed from heaven: "That's My Son right there—the one I love. He bring Me so much joy."

1.text: Then the Spirit led Jesus out into the wilderness, so the devil could test Him.

2.text: He ain't eat nothin' for forty days and forty nights. After that? Yeah, He was hungry hungry.

3.text: So here come the tempter talkin' slick: "If You really the Son of God, go 'head and tell these stones to turn into bread."

4.text: But Jesus clapped back, "Nah, it's written—Man don't live off bread alone, but off every word that come from God's mouth."

5.text: Then the devil took Him to the holy city and posted Him up on the highest point of the temple.

6.text: He said, "If You the Son of God, jump! Ain't it written, 'God gon' tell His angels to look out for You,' and 'They gon' catch You so You don't even stub your toe'?"

7.text: Jesus said, "It's also written: Don't play with the Lord your God."

8.text: So Satan tried one more time—took Jesus to a crazy high mountain and showed Him all the kingdoms of the world and their shine.

9.text: He said, "All this could be Yours if You just bow down and worship me."

10.text: Jesus shut it down: "Get outta here, Satan! It's written—Worship the Lord your God, and serve Him only."

11.text: So the devil dipped, and right then, angels showed up and took care of Jesus.

12.text: When Jesus heard John had got locked up, He headed back to Galilee.

13.text: He left Nazareth and moved to Capernaum, by the sea, in the area of Zebulun and Naphtali.

14.text: This was to fulfill what the prophet Isaiah had said:

15.text: "Land of Zebulun and Naphtali, by the sea, past the Jordan, Galilee where the outsiders live—

16.text: The people sittin' in the dark seen a big light. Those sittin' in the shadow of death, light done broke through."

17.text: From that point on, Jesus started preachin' loud and clear: "Change how you livin'—God's kingdom is right here!"

18.text: Jesus was walkin' by the Sea of Galilee when He spotted two brothers—Simon (also called Peter) and Andrew. They was out there tossin' nets in the water 'cause they were fishermen.

19.text: Jesus told 'em, "Come follow Me, and I'll teach y'all how to catch people instead."

20.text: They dropped they nets right then and followed Him.

21.text: He kept it movin' and saw two more brothers—James and John, sons of Zebedee. They was in the boat with they daddy, fixin' nets. Jesus called them too.

22.text: They ain't even hesitate—left the boat, left they pops, and rolled with Jesus.

23.text: Jesus was all over Galilee, teachin' in the synagogues, preachin' the Good News about the kingdom, and healin' folks from every kind of sickness and disease.

24.text: Word got out quick—folks from Syria and everywhere else started bringin' the sick to Him: folks with diseases, pain, demons, seizures, and folks who couldn't walk. Jesus healed every last one.

25.text: Big crowds followed Him—from Galilee, Decapolis, Jerusalem, Judea, and across the Jordan too.

1.text: When Jesus saw the crowd pull up, He went up on a mountain. After He sat down, His disciples came through.

2.text: Then Jesus started speakin', teachin' them like this:

3.text: "Blessed are the ones who know they need God—'cause heaven already belong to them.

4.text: Blessed are the ones who hurt and grieve—'cause God gon' comfort them.

5.text: Blessed are the humble and gentle—'cause they gon' inherit the whole earth.

6.text: Blessed are the ones who crave righteousness like food and water—'cause they gon' be filled up.

7.text: Blessed are the ones who show mercy—'cause they gon' get mercy too.

8.text: Blessed are the ones with pure hearts—'cause they gon' see God for real.

9.text: Blessed are the peacemakers—'cause they gon' be known as God's children.

10.text: Blessed are the ones gettin' hated on for doin' right—'cause the kingdom of heaven theirs.

11.text: And blessed are y'all when people talk reckless about you, lie on you, and come at you sideways just 'cause you rockin' with Me.

12.text: Don't trip—rejoice! Be hype! Your reward up in heaven gon' be major. They did the same thing to the prophets before y'all."

13.text: "Y'all the salt of the earth. But if salt lose its flavor, what's the point? It ain't good for nothin' but gettin' tossed out and stepped on.

14.text: Y'all the light of the world. A city up on a hill can't be hidden.

15.text: Nobody lights a lamp just to put it under a bucket—they put it on a stand so it can light up the whole room.

16.text: So let your light shine in front of everybody, so they can see your good deeds and give props to your Father in heaven."

17.text: "Don't get it twisted—don't think I came to cancel the Law or the Prophets. I ain't come to erase it—I came to fulfill it.

18.text: Truth is, not even a period or comma from the law gon' fade 'til everything is complete.

19.text: Anybody who breaks the smallest command and teaches others to do the same? They gon' be the least in the kingdom. But the ones who live it and teach it? They gon' be great in the kingdom.

20.text: I'm tellin' y'all: unless your righteousness go beyond that of the Pharisees and law teachers, you not even gettin' in the kingdom."

21.text: "Y'all heard the rule: 'Don't kill nobody. If you do, you face judgment.'

22.text: But I'm tellin' you: if you mad at your brother for no reason, you already in danger. And if you call them names like 'Raca' (basically, 'idiot') or 'Fool,' you headin' toward serious judgment—even hellfire.

23.text: So if you about to bring your offering to God, and you remember your brother got beef with you?

24.text: Leave your gift. Go make it right with them first. Then come back and give your gift.

25.text: If somebody takin' you to court, squash the drama before y'all even get there. 'Cause if not, they might hand you over to the judge, and next thing you know—you in jail.

26.text: I'm tellin' you straight: You not gettin' out until every last penny is paid."

27.text: "Y'all heard it said, 'Don't cheat—don't commit adultery.'

28.text: But I'm sayin': if you look at someone with lust, you already committed adultery in your heart.

29.text: If your right eye got you wildin'—pluck it out. It's better to lose one part than your whole body get tossed in hell.

30.text: If your right hand keep messin' you up—cut it off. Better to lose that than your whole body get thrown into hell."

31.text: "They said, 'If you divorce your wife, give her a certificate.'

32.text: But I'm sayin': if you divorce her for anything other than cheating, you makin' her commit adultery—and whoever marries her? Same deal."

33.text: "Y'all heard: 'Don't swear falsely. Keep your vows to God.'

34.text: But I say: don't swear at all. Not by heaven—it's God's throne.

35.text: Not by earth—that's His footstool. Not by Jerusalem—that's His city.

36.text: Don't even swear on your own head—you can't make a single hair white or black.

37.text: Just say 'Yes' or 'No.' Anything more than that? That's the enemy talkin'."

38.text: "Y'all heard, 'Eye for an eye, tooth for a tooth.'

39.text: But I say: don't clap back on evil folks. If somebody slap you on one cheek, offer the other one too.

40.text: If they sue you for your shirt, give 'em your coat too.

41.text: If they force you to walk a mile, walk two.

42.text: If somebody ask you for somethin', give it. If they try to borrow, don't turn 'em away."

43.text: "Y'all heard, 'Love your neighbor and hate your enemy.'

44.text: But I'm tellin' you: Love your enemies. Bless the ones talkin' crazy. Do good to the ones that hate you. Pray for the ones who use you and persecute you.

45.text: That's how you show you belong to your Father in heaven. He makes the sun rise on both the good and the bad. Sends rain to the righteous and the unrighteous.

46.text: If you only love the folks who love you, what's special about that? Even tax collectors do that.

47.text: And if you only speak to your crew, what makes you different?

48.text: So be mature, be whole—just like your Father in heaven is.

1.text: Don't be out here showin' off your good deeds just to get seen by folks. If you do, don't expect no reward from your Father in heaven.

2.text: When you give to folks in need, don't be blowin' it up like a trumpet like them fake folks in church and on the streets tryna look holy. I'm tellin' you—they already got they reward.

3.text: But when you give, keep it lowkey—don't even let your left hand know what your right hand doin'.

4.text: Do your givin' in secret, and your Father—who sees what's done on the low—He gon' bless you in the open.

5.text: When you pray, don't act like the fakes who love to stand and be seen prayin' on corners and in the synagogues. They already got their lil' applause.

6.text: But when you pray, slide into your room, shut the door, and talk to your Father in secret. He sees you—and He gon' bless you for it.

7.text: And don't be prayin' with long, empty talk like folks who don't know God. They think God hear them just 'cause they sayin' a lot.

8.text: Don't be like them—your Father already know what you need before you even ask.

9.text: So when you pray, say: Our Father in heaven, We honor Your name.

10.text: Let Your kingdom come. Let Your will be done—On earth just like it is in heaven.

11.text: Give us today the bread we need.

12.text: Forgive us our debts, As we forgive the folks who owe us.

13.text: Don't lead us into temptation, But rescue us from the evil one. 'Cause the kingdom, the power, and the glory is Yours—forever. Amen.

14.text: If you forgive people for the wrong they did to you, your Father in heaven gon' forgive you too.

15.text: But if you don't forgive them? Don't expect your Father to forgive your mess either.

16.text: When you fast, don't be walkin' around lookin' sad and pitiful like them hypocrites. They do that so folks will know they fastin'. That's all the reward they gon' get.

17.text: But when you fast, wash your face and oil your head—look normal.

18.text: That way, only your Father in secret sees what's up. And He gon' bless you for real.

19.text: Don't be stackin' up treasure here on earth, where moths and rust ruin stuff and thieves break in.

20.text: Stack up treasure in heaven instead—where it can't get messed up or stolen.

21.text: 'Cause wherever your treasure at? That's where your heart gon' be too.

22.text: The eye is like a lamp for your whole body. If your eye is healthy, your whole body full of light.

23.text: But if your eye bad, your whole body full of darkness. And if the "light" in you is really darkness? That's some deep darkness right there.

24.text: You can't serve two bosses. You gon' hate one and love the other, or be loyal to one and despise the other. You can't serve both God and money.

25.text: That's why I'm sayin': don't stress about your life—what you gon' eat, drink, or wear. Life ain't just about food and clothes.

26.text: Look at the birds—they don't plant or harvest or store up food, but God feeds them. Ain't you more valuable than birds?

27.text: Worryin' ain't gon' add one inch to your height or one minute to your life.

28.text: Why worry about clothes? Look at the flowers out in the field—they don't hustle, but they stay lookin' fly.

29.text: Even Solomon, in all his royal drip, ain't look that good.

30.text: If God dresses wildflowers that only last a day, won't He take care of you? C'mon now, have some faith.

31.text: So don't be out here stressin', sayin', "What we gon' eat?" or "What we gon' wear?"

32.text: That's what folks who don't know God worry about. Your Father already know what you need.

33.text: But seek God's kingdom first. Chase after His righteousness. Everything else you need? He gon' add it to you.

34.text: Don't worry 'bout tomorrow—tomorrow got its own problems. Deal with today. That's enough for now.

1.text: Don't be out here judgin' folks, unless you ready to get judged the same way.

2.text: 'Cause however you judge others? That same energy comin' right back to you.

3.text: Why you stressin' about the little speck in your brother's eye, when you got a whole log in your own?

4.text: How you gon' say, "Let me fix your eye," but you walkin' around with a whole plank blockin' your vision?

5.text: You fake for that! Handle your own mess first—take the plank out your own eye—then you'll be able to help your brother with his.

6.text: Don't throw what's sacred to the dogs. Don't toss your pearls to pigs—they'll just stomp on it, then turn around and come for you.

7.text: Ask—and you'll get it. Seek—and you'll find it. Knock—and that door gon' open.

8.text: Everybody who asks, gets. The one who seeks, finds. And if you knock? Yeah, it's gon' open.

9.text: Which one of y'all would give your child a rock if they asked for bread?

10.text: Or a snake if they asked for fish?

11.text: Y'all flawed, and y'all still know how to give good gifts to your kids. So imagine how much more your heavenly Father gon' give to the ones who ask Him!

12.text: So whatever you want folks to do for you? Do that for them. That right there sums up the Law and the Prophets.

13.text: Get in through the narrow gate—'cause the wide one? That's the easy road, but it leads straight to destruction. And a whole lotta folks walkin' that one.

14.text: But the narrow gate? That's the one that leads to life. It ain't easy, and only a few gon' find it.

15.text: Watch out for fake prophets. They come lookin' innocent like sheep, but inside? They straight-up wolves.

16.text: You gon' know them by their fruit. You ever seen grapes growin' from thorns? Or figs from thistles? Nah.

17.text: Every good tree gives good fruit. Bad trees give bad fruit.

18.text: A good tree can't give bad fruit, and a bad tree can't give good fruit.

19.text: Any tree that don't produce good fruit? It's gettin' chopped down and tossed in the fire.

20.text: So yeah—you'll know them by what they produce.

21.text: Not everybody who hollers "Lord, Lord" is gettin' into heaven. Only the ones who do what God wants.

22.text: Plenty gon' say on judgment day: "Lord, didn't we prophesy in Your name? Didn't we cast out demons and do big miracles in Your name?"

23.text: But I'm gon' tell them straight up: "I never knew you. Move around—you out here doin' wrong."

24.text: So if you hear My words and actually do 'em, you like a wise builder who put his house on solid rock.

25.text: The rain came, the flood hit, the wind blew hard—but that house stood tall, 'cause it had a strong foundation.

26.text: But if you hear My words and ignore 'em? You like a fool who built his house on sand.

27.text: The rain came, floods rushed in, wind smacked it—and boom. That house fell hard. And the fall? Yeah, it was major."

28.text: When Jesus finished preachin' all this, the crowd was shook.

29.text: 'Cause He wasn't talkin' like them teachers they was used to. He spoke with real authority—like He knew what He was talkin' about.

1.text: When Jesus came down from the mountain, a huge crowd followed Him.

2.text: Then a man with leprosy pulled up, bowed low, and said, "Lord, if You want to, You can make me clean."

3.text: Jesus reached out, touched him, and said, "I want to. Be clean." And just like that, the man was healed—leprosy gone.

4.text: Jesus told him, "Don't go tellin' everybody. Just go to the priest, show yourself, and give the offering Moses talked about. That's proof for them."

5.text: When Jesus got to Capernaum, a Roman officer came to Him, beggin'.

6.text: He said, "Lord, my servant at home is paralyzed, in bad shape, sufferin' bad."

7.text: Jesus said, "I'll come heal him."

8.text: But the centurion said, "Lord, I ain't even worthy for You to come in my house. Just say the word and he'll be healed.

9.text: I know how authority works—I got soldiers too. I tell one 'Go' and he go, another 'Come' and he come. I say 'Do this' and it's done."

10.text: When Jesus heard that, He was amazed. He turned to the crowd and said, "Y'all, I ain't seen faith like this—not even in Israel.

11.text: And I'm tellin' you: folks from all over—east, west, everywhere—gon' be chillin' with Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob in heaven.

12.text: But some of the so-called 'chosen ones' gon' get thrown out into the dark—where there's cryin' and teeth grindin'."

13.text: Then He told the centurion, "Go on. You believed—now it's done." And the servant got healed that same hour.

14.text: When Jesus got to Peter's crib, He saw his wife's mama layin' in bed with a fever.

15.text: He touched her hand, the fever dipped, and she got up and started servin' everybody.

16.text: That evening, folks brought Jesus a bunch of demon-possessed people. He cast the demons out with just one word and healed everybody.

17.text: That fulfilled what the prophet Isaiah said: "He took on our weaknesses and carried our sicknesses."

18.text: When Jesus saw the crowd gettin' thick, He said, "Let's dip to the other side."

19.text: One of the religious teachers came up and said, "Teacher, I'll follow You wherever You go."

20.text: Jesus said, "Foxes got holes, birds got nests, but Me? I ain't even got a place to lay My head."

21.text: Another dude said, "Lord, let me bury my father first."

22.text: Jesus told him, "Follow Me. Let the dead handle the dead."

23.text: Jesus got in a boat and His disciples rode with Him.

24.text: Outta nowhere, a wild storm hit the sea—waves was takin' over the boat. But Jesus? Knocked out sleep.

25.text: The disciples ran to Him like, "Lord! Save us—we 'bout to die!"

26.text: Jesus said, "Why y'all so scared? Where's your faith?" Then He got up, told the wind and waves to chill—and just like that, the sea was calm.

27.text: The disciples were shook. They said, "Who is this man? Even the wind and the sea do what He say!"

28.text: When they got to the other side, in the Gergesenes area, two demon-possessed men came out the tombs. These dudes were wild—nobody even walked that road 'cause of them.

29.text: They yelled out, "What You want with us, Son of God? You here to torment us before the set time?"

30.text: Off in the distance, there was a big herd of pigs.

31.text: The demons begged, "If You gon' cast us out, send us into the pigs."

32.text: Jesus said, "Go." Soon as He said that, they jumped out the men and into the pigs. Then the whole herd ran off the cliff and drowned in the water.

33.text: The folks watchin' the pigs ran off, told the town everything—especially about the demon dudes.

34.text: The whole city came out to see Jesus. But when they saw Him, they begged Him to leave their area.

1.text: Jesus got back in the boat, crossed over, and pulled up in His own town.

2.text: Some folks brought Him a man paralyzed and laid out on a mat. When Jesus saw how strong their faith was, He said, "Son, cheer up—your sins are forgiven."

3.text: That made some of the religious folks mad quiet, thinkin' to themselves, "This man blaspheming!"

4.text: But Jesus knew what they was thinkin'. He said, "Why y'all got evil in your hearts?

5.text: What's easier to say—'Your sins are forgiven,' or 'Get up and walk'?

6.text: But to show you I got authority on earth to forgive sins..." He turned to the paralyzed man and said, "Get up, grab your mat, and go home."

7.text: And just like that, the man got up and walked off.

8.text: The crowd was shook and started givin' glory to God, amazed He gave that kind of power to a man.

9.text: As Jesus was movin' along, He saw a dude named Matthew workin' the tax booth. Jesus said, "Follow Me." Matthew got up and did just that.

10.text: Later, Jesus was chillin' at the table in the house, and a bunch of tax collectors and "sinners" came through and sat with Him and His crew.

11.text: When the Pharisees saw all that, they asked Jesus' disciples, "Why your teacher eatin' with folks like that?"

12.text: Jesus heard them and said, "People who healthy don't need a doctor—sick folks do.

13.text: Go learn what this mean: 'I want mercy, not sacrifice.' I didn't come for the ones who think they righteous—I came for the ones who know they messed up."

14.text: Then John's disciples pulled up and asked, "Why do we and the Pharisees fast, but Your crew don't?"

15.text: Jesus said, "Can the wedding guests mourn while the groom still with them? Nah. But one day the groom gon' be taken, and then they gon' fast.

16.text: You don't patch old clothes with new cloth—it just tears up worse.

17.text: And you don't put new wine in old skins. If you do, they'll bust and spill everything. Nah—you put new wine in new skins. That way both stay intact."

18.text: While Jesus was still talkin', a leader came up, bowed down, and said, "My daughter just died. But if You come touch her, she'll live."

19.text: Jesus got up and went with him—and so did His disciples.

20.text: On the way, a woman who'd been bleeding for 12 years came up behind Him and touched His clothes.

21.text: She said to herself, "If I can just touch His robe, I know I'll be healed."

22.text: Jesus turned around, saw her, and said, "Be encouraged, daughter—your faith made you whole." And right then, she got healed.

23.text: When Jesus got to the leader's house, the funeral crowd was already playin' music and cryin' loud.

24.text: He said, "Y'all chill—she not dead, she just sleepin'." They laughed at Him.

25.text: But after He kicked 'em all out, He went in, grabbed the girl's hand—and she got up.

26.text: Word about that miracle spread everywhere.

27.text: As Jesus left, two blind men started followin' Him, shoutin', "Son of David, have mercy on us!"

28.text: When He got in the house, they came inside too. Jesus asked, "Y'all believe I can really do this?" They said, "Yes, Lord."

29.text: Then He touched they eyes and said, "Let it happen based on your faith."

30.text: Their eyes opened just like that. Jesus told 'em, "Keep this on the low."

31.text: But they couldn't keep it quiet—they told everybody.

32.text: As they were leavin', some folks brought Jesus a man who couldn't talk 'cause he had a demon.

33.text: Jesus cast the demon out, and the man started talkin'. The crowd was stunned: "Ain't never seen nothing like this in Israel!"

34.text: But the Pharisees? Haters as usual. They said, "He castin' out demons with demonic power." (Boy, bye.)

35.text: Jesus kept movin'—hittin' up towns and villages, teachin' in synagogues, preachin' that kingdom gospel, and healin' every kind of sickness and disease.

36.text: When He saw the crowd, He was moved deep—'cause they was worn out, lost, and scattered, like sheep with no shepherd.

37.text: He told His disciples, "The harvest out here is huge, but we ain't got enough workers.

38.text: So pray to the Lord of the harvest to send out more laborers to work the field."

1.text: Jesus called His twelve disciples over and gave 'em real power—to cast out demons and heal every kind of sickness and disease.

2.text: Here's who He chose: First, Simon (aka Peter) and his brother Andrew. Then James (Zebedee's son) and John his brother.

3.text: Philip, Bartholomew, Thomas, and Matthew (the tax man). James (son of Alphaeus) and Thaddaeus.

4.text: Simon the Zealot, and Judas Iscariot—the one who later betrayed Him.

5.text: Jesus sent these twelve out and told them, "Don't go to the Gentiles or the Samaritans just yet.

6.text: Go to the lost sheep of Israel first.

7.text: And when you go, preach this: 'The kingdom of heaven is real close.'

8.text: Heal the sick. Raise the dead. Cleanse lepers. Cast out demons. You got all this for free, so give it out for free.

9.text: Don't take no gold, silver, or change in your pockets.

10.text: Don't pack a travel bag, extra clothes, shoes, or even a walking stick. A worker deserves to be taken care of."

11.text: "When you pull up in a town, find somebody solid to stay with. Stay there the whole time.

12.text: When you enter a house, bless it with peace.

13.text: If they down with you, let your peace rest on them. If not? Take that peace back.

14.text: If they don't welcome you or listen, dust your feet off as you leave that spot.

15.text: I'm tellin' you—the judgment gon' hit that place harder than Sodom and Gomorrah."

16.text: "Listen—I'm sendin' y'all out like sheep among wolves. Be wise like snakes but gentle like doves.

17.text: Watch out for people—they gon' drag y'all into courts and beat y'all in synagogues.

18.text: You gon' be brought before kings and governors 'cause of Me, as a witness to them and the Gentiles.

19.text: But don't stress about what to say. When the time comes, God gon' give you the words.

20.text: It ain't even gon' be you talkin'—it'll be the Spirit of your Father speakin' through you."

21.text: "Families gon' turn on each other. Brothers snitchin'. Parents and kids betrayin' one another.

22.text: You gon' be hated by everybody just 'cause you rock with Me. But if you stay down to the end, you gon' be saved.

23.text: When they come for you in one city, bounce to the next. You won't finish hittin' every town before the Son of Man comes."

24.text: "A student ain't above their teacher. A servant ain't above their master.

25.text: It's enough to be like the teacher. If they called Me Beelzebub, what you think they gon' call you?

26.text: Don't be scared of 'em. Everything in the dark gon' come to light."

27.text: "Whatever I whisper in your ear in the dark? Say it loud in the light. Shout it from the rooftops.

28.text: Don't fear people who can kill your body but can't touch your soul. Fear the One who can destroy both in hell.

29.text: Ain't two sparrows sold for a penny? But not one of 'em falls without your Father knowin'.

30.text: God even got the number of hairs on your head counted.

31.text: So don't be scared—you worth way more than sparrows."

32.text: "If you stand up for Me in front of people, I'll stand up for you in front of My Father in heaven.

33.text: But if you act like you don't know Me? I'll say I don't know you either."

34.text: "Don't get it twisted—I ain't come to bring peace. I came to bring a sword.

35.text: I came to shake things up—even in families.

36.text: Sometimes your biggest haters gon' be the ones in your own house.

37.text: If you love your parents or your kids more than Me? You ain't worthy of Me.

38.text: If you ain't willing to pick up your cross and follow Me? You not worthy either.

39.text: Try to save your life, and you'll lose it. But if you lose your life for Me? You'll find it."

40.text: "If they welcome you, they welcome Me. And if they welcome Me, they welcome the One who sent Me.

41.text: If they bless a prophet, they gon' get a prophet's blessing. If they receive a righteous person, they gon' get that righteous reward too.

42.text: And even if someone gives a cup of cold water to My disciple—just 'cause they My disciple—they won't lose their reward."

1.text: After Jesus finished givin' His twelve disciples instructions, He dipped out and started preachin' and teachin' in their cities.

2.text: Meanwhile, John was locked up in prison. When he heard about all the stuff Jesus was doin', he sent two of his people

3.text: To ask Jesus, "Are You the One we been waitin' for, or should we be lookin' for somebody else?"

4.text: Jesus told 'em, "Go back and tell John what you see and hear:

5.text: Blind folks gettin' their sight. People who couldn't walk now up on they feet. Lepers gettin' cleaned. Deaf folks hearin'. Dead folks raisin' up. And the broke and overlooked? They finally hearin' Good News.

6.text: And blessed is the one who don't trip on Me."

7.text: As John's crew walked off, Jesus started speakin' to the crowd about John: "When y'all went out to the wilderness, what you expect to see? A reed blowin' in the wind?

8.text: Or a man rockin' soft, fancy clothes? Nah—folks like that live in palaces.

9.text: So what did y'all really go out to see? A prophet? Yup—and not just any prophet.

10.text: John the Baptist is the one Scripture was talkin' about: 'Look, I'm sendin' My messenger ahead of You. He gon' prepare the way for You.'

11.text: I'm tellin' y'all straight: Ain't nobody born of a woman greater than John. But even the least person in God's kingdom got it better than him.

12.text: Since John stepped on the scene, the kingdom of heaven been under pressure—and it's the bold and relentless that take hold of it.

13.text: All the prophets and the law pointed to this moment—up until John.

14.text: If y'all really ready to receive it—he is Elijah, the one who was supposed to come.

15.text: If you got ears—listen up."

16.text: "So what can I even compare this generation to? Y'all like kids sittin' outside playin', yellin' to each other:

17.text: 'We played a song, but y'all ain't dance. We cried, but y'all ain't mourn.'

18.text: John came through, not eatin' or drinkin', and y'all said, 'He got a demon.'

19.text: I came through eatin' and drinkin', and y'all said, 'Look at Him—a glutton, a drunk, hangin' with tax collectors and sinners.' But wisdom gon' prove itself right by what it produces."

20.text: Then Jesus started callin' out the cities where He did the most miracles—but they still ain't turn to God.

21.text: "Woe to you, Chorazin! Woe to you, Bethsaida! If Tyre and Sidon saw what y'all seen, they would've been repentin' in sackcloth and ashes a long time ago.

22.text: I'm tellin' you—it'll be easier on Tyre and Sidon at judgment time than on y'all.

23.text: And you, Capernaum? You think you all the way up? Nah, you gon' be brought low. If Sodom had seen what y'all seen, it would still be standin'.

24.text: But I'm tellin' you—it'll be better for Sodom than for you on judgment day."

25.text: At that point, Jesus prayed out loud, sayin', "Thank You, Father—Lord of heaven and earth. You kept this hidden from the ones who think they wise and revealed it to the childlike.

26.text: Yes, Father—'cause that's how You wanted it.

27.text: My Father handed everything over to Me. Nobody really knows the Son except the Father. And nobody knows the Father except the Son—and whoever the Son chooses to show Him to.

28.text: So come to Me, all y'all who tired and weighed down—I'll give you rest.

29.text: Take My yoke and learn from Me. I'm gentle and humble, and you'll find real rest for your soul.

30.text: My yoke? It's easy. My burden? Light."

1.text: One Sabbath day, Jesus and His disciples was walkin' through some grainfields. They were hungry, so they started pickin' grain to eat.

2.text: The Pharisees saw it and said, "Look! Your disciples breakin' Sabbath law!"

3.text: But Jesus said, "Y'all ever read what David did when he was hungry—him and his people?

4.text: He went in God's house and ate the holy bread, even though only the priests were allowed to eat it.

5.text: And don't y'all know the Law say priests work on the Sabbath, and they still not guilty?

6.text: But let Me tell you—Someone greater than the temple is right here.

7.text: If y'all really understood what God meant when He said, 'I want mercy, not sacrifice,' you wouldn't be accusin' folks who ain't done nothin' wrong.

8.text: 'Cause the Son of Man is Lord—even over the Sabbath."

9.text: Jesus left there and went to their synagogue.

10.text: A man with a messed-up hand was there. They tried to trap Jesus, askin', "Is it legal to heal on the Sabbath?"

11.text: Jesus said, "If you got one sheep and it fall in a ditch on the Sabbath, you gon' leave it there? Nah, you'll pull it out.

12.text: Ain't a person worth way more than a sheep? So yes—it's right to do good on the Sabbath."

13.text: Then He told the man, "Stretch out your hand." The man did, and it got healed—looked just like the other one.

14.text: The Pharisees left mad and started plottin' how to kill Jesus.

15.text: Jesus knew they was comin' for Him, so He dipped out. But big crowds still followed Him—and He healed every last one.

16.text: He told them not to make it public,

17.text: So the prophecy from Isaiah could be fulfilled:

18.text: "Here go My chosen Servant, the One I love. I'll put My Spirit on Him, and He'll bring justice to the Gentiles.

19.text: He won't argue or be loud in the streets.

20.text: He won't crush the weak or snuff out the barely hangin' on—He'll keep bringin' justice until it wins.

21.text: And even the Gentiles gon' put their hope in His name."

22.text: Somebody brought Jesus a man possessed by a demon—he couldn't see or talk. Jesus healed him, and the man started speakin' and seein'.

23.text: Everybody was amazed and said, "Could this really be the Son of David?"

24.text: But the Pharisees said, "He castin' out demons by Beelzebub, the prince of demons."

25.text: Jesus knew what they were thinkin' and said, "A kingdom divided can't stand.

26.text: If Satan castin' out Satan, he fightin' himself—how his kingdom gon' stand?

27.text: And if I cast demons out by Beelzebub, who your own people cast them out by? Let them judge.

28.text: But if I'm castin' them out by God's Spirit—then the kingdom just pulled up on y'all.

29.text: Ain't nobody robbin' a strong man's house unless they tie him up first. Then they can take what they want.

30.text: If you ain't with Me, you against Me. If you ain't helpin' Me gather, you out here scatterin'."

31.text: "Let Me be clear—every sin and kind of blasphemy can be forgiven. But speakin' against the Holy Spirit? That's the one thing that ain't forgivable.

32.text: Talk trash about Me? You might be forgiven. But talk against the Spirit? That don't get forgiven—not now, not ever."

33.text: "Either the tree good and the fruit good, or the tree bad and the fruit bad. You know the tree by what it grows.

34.text: Y'all snakes! How y'all gon' say anything good when your hearts so foul? What's in the heart comes out the mouth.

35.text: A good heart brings out good things. A bad heart brings out evil.

36.text: And let Me tell y'all—every careless word you say? You gon' answer for it on judgment day.

37.text: By your words, you'll be justified—or condemned."

38.text: Then some of the religious leaders said, "Teacher, give us a sign."

39.text: Jesus said, "This generation so wicked and unfaithful. Always askin' for signs. But the only sign y'all gettin' is the sign of Jonah.

40.text: Just like Jonah was in the belly of the fish for three days and nights, the Son of Man gon' be in the heart of the earth three days and nights.

41.text: The people from Nineveh gon' rise up and call y'all out—'cause they repented when Jonah spoke. And now somebody greater than Jonah is here.

42.text: The Queen of the South gon' rise up and check y'all too—she came from way off just to hear Solomon's wisdom. And y'all got somebody greater than Solomon standin' in front of you."

43.text: "When an evil spirit leaves someone, it be out here wanderin', lookin' for a new place to chill. But if it can't find one,

44.text: It says, 'Let me go back to my old spot.' When it comes back and sees the house cleaned up and empty,

45.text: It brings seven more evil spirits worse than itself, and they all move in. That person ends up worse than before. That's what this generation actin' like."

46.text: While Jesus was still talkin' to the crowd, His mama and brothers showed up outside, tryna get a word with Him.

47.text: Somebody said, "Hey Jesus—Your mama and brothers outside waitin' to talk to You."

48.text: Jesus said, "Who really My mama? Who really My brothers?"

49.text: He pointed to His disciples and said, "Here they go—this My family.

50.text: Anybody who doin' the will of My Father in heaven? That's My brother, sister, and mama."

1.text: That same day, Jesus left the house and went to go sit by the sea.

2.text: A huge crowd pulled up, so He got in a boat and sat down, while everybody else stood on the shore.

3.text: He started teachin' through stories and said, "Look, a farmer went out to plant some seeds.

4.text: Some fell on the road, and birds came and snatched 'em up.

5.text: Some fell on rocky ground where there wasn't much dirt. They grew quick but had no depth.

6.text: The sun came up, scorched 'em, and since they had no roots, they dried up.

7.text: Some landed in thorny patches—the thorns grew up and choked 'em.

8.text: But some fell on good soil and produced a harvest—some a hundred times, some sixty, some thirty.

9.text: If you got ears, listen up!"

10.text: His disciples came and asked, "Why You always talkin' to them in parables?"

11.text: He said, "Because y'all been given access to the mysteries of the kingdom—but they ain't.

12.text: If you got it, you gon' get more. If you don't, even what you got gon' get snatched.

13.text: I speak in parables 'cause they lookin' but ain't really seein', hearin' but don't understand.

14.text: Isaiah already said it would be like this:

15.text: 'These folks' hearts done got hard. Their ears barely work. Their eyes stay closed—'cause if they really saw, heard, and understood, they'd turn around and get healed.'

16.text: But y'all? Y'all blessed. Your eyes see. Your ears hear.

17.text: Truth is, a whole lotta prophets and righteous folks wanted to see what y'all see—and they ain't get to. They wanted to hear this, but they never did."

18.text: "Here's what that sower story means:

19.text: Some folks hear the word about the kingdom but don't understand it. Then the enemy slides in and snatches it away—that's the seed on the road.

20.text: The rocky ground? That's folks who hear the word and get hype real quick—

21.text: But they got no root. So the second life gets hard or folks start hatin' on them for believin'? They fall off.

22.text: Seed in the thorns? That's folks who hear it, but stressin' over life and chasin' money chokes the word—it don't go nowhere.

23.text: But seed on good soil? That's folks who hear the word, understand it, and actually produce fruit—some thirty, some sixty, some a hundredfold."

24.text: "God's kingdom is like a man who planted good seed in his field.

25.text: But while everybody was sleep, his enemy came and planted weeds among the wheat.

26.text: When stuff started growin', the weeds popped up too.

27.text: The workers asked the owner, 'Didn't you plant good seed? Why we got weeds?'

28.text: He said, 'An enemy did this.' They asked, 'You want us to pull 'em up?'

29.text: He said, 'Nah, you might mess up the wheat too.

30.text: Let both grow together. Then at harvest, we'll separate—burn the weeds and store the wheat in the barn.'"

31.text: "The kingdom of heaven is like a mustard seed—a tiny thing someone plants in a field.

32.text: But when it grows, it becomes the biggest plant out there—so big birds post up in its branches."

33.text: "The kingdom is like yeast a woman mixes into flour. It don't look like much at first, but soon the whole batch rises."

34.text: Jesus told the crowd all this in parables. He didn't speak to them without stories.

35.text: That fulfilled what the prophet said: "I'll open My mouth in parables. I'll tell hidden things from the beginning of time."

36.text: Then Jesus dipped with His disciples, and they asked, "Break down that weeds parable."

37.text: He said, "The one plantin' good seed is the Son of Man.

38.text: The field is the world. Good seed? That's the kingdom's people. Weeds? That's the devil's crew.

39.text: The enemy who planted the weeds is Satan. The harvest? That's the end of time. And the workers are angels.

40.text: Just like weeds get gathered and burned, that's how it's gon' go down at the end.

41.text: The Son of Man gon' send angels to gather up every evil thing and everybody livin' lawless.

42.text: They'll get thrown in the fire—there's gon' be weepin' and teeth-grindin'.

43.text: But the righteous? They gon' shine bright like the sun in the kingdom of their Father. If you got ears, listen up!"

44.text: "The kingdom is like a treasure hid in a field. A man finds it, hides it again, and then sells everything he got to buy that field.

45.text: The kingdom is like a merchant huntin' for fine pearls.

46.text: When he finds that one priceless pearl, he sells all he has to buy it.

47.text: It's also like a big fishin' net thrown into the sea, catchin' all kinds of fish.

48.text: When it's full, they pull it up, sort the good into containers, and toss the bad.

49.text: That's how it's gon' be at the end—angels separatin' the wicked from the righteous,

50.text: And tossin' the wicked into the fire. More weepin'. More teeth-grindin'."

51.text: Jesus asked, "Y'all understand all this?" They said, "Yeah, Lord."

52.text: He said, "Then every teacher trained in the kingdom is like a homeowner who brings out treasures—some old, some new."

53.text: When Jesus finished all these parables, He left.

54.text: He went back to His hometown and taught in their synagogue. Folks were shocked and said, "Where He get this wisdom and power from?

55.text: Ain't this the carpenter's son? Ain't Mary His mama? Ain't His brothers James, Joses, Simon, and Judas?

56.text: And His sisters? They all live around here. Where He get all this from?"

57.text: They were offended by Him. But Jesus said, "A prophet ain't honored in his own hood."

58.text: And He didn't do many miracles there—'cause they ain't believe.

1.text: Around that time, Herod the ruler heard all the stuff Jesus was doin'.

2.text: He told his people, "That's John the Baptist! He back from the dead, that's why He got all this power!"

3.text: See, Herod had arrested John, tied him up, and threw him in jail 'cause of Herodias—his brother Philip's wife.

4.text: John had called him out, sayin', "You ain't got no business takin' her as your wife."

5.text: Herod wanted to kill John, but he was scared of the crowd—they saw John as a real prophet.

6.text: But on Herod's birthday, Herodias' daughter came through dancin', and it had Herod wide open.

7.text: He made a promise in front of everybody—said she could ask for whatever she wanted.

8.text: Her mama told her what to say, so the girl said, "I want John the Baptist's head on a platter."

9.text: Herod didn't wanna do it, but he ain't wanna look soft in front of his guests. So he gave the order.

10.text: They went and beheaded John in jail.

11.text: His head got brought out on a platter and handed to the girl, and she gave it to her mama.

12.text: John's disciples came, took his body, and buried it. Then they went and told Jesus what happened.

13.text: When Jesus heard the news, He dipped out by boat to a quiet place by Himself. But the crowd wasn't tryna let Him go—they walked there on foot from all over.

14.text: When Jesus stepped out and saw the big crowd, His heart broke for them. So He started healing their sick.

15.text: By the time it got late, the disciples were like, "Jesus, we in the middle of nowhere. Send these folks to town to get some food."

16.text: But Jesus said, "They ain't gotta go. Y'all feed 'em."

17.text: They said, "All we got is five loaves and two fish."

18.text: Jesus said, "Bring it here."

19.text: He had the crowd sit down on the grass. Then He took the five loaves and two fish, looked up to heaven, blessed it, broke it, and gave it to the disciples. They passed it out to the people.

20.text: Everybody ate and got full. And when it was over, they picked up 12 baskets of leftovers.

21.text: That day, Jesus fed five thousand men—not even counting all the women and kids.

22.text: Right after that, Jesus told the disciples to hop in the boat and go ahead to the other side while He sent the crowd home.

23.text: After the crowd left, Jesus went up on the mountain by Himself to pray. By the time it got dark, He was still up there alone.

24.text: Meanwhile, the boat was way out on the water, gettin' tossed by the waves 'cause the wind was wild.

25.text: Around 3 to 6 a.m., Jesus came walkin' on the water toward them.

26.text: When the disciples saw Him, they freaked out like, "It's a ghost!" and started screamin'.

27.text: But Jesus said, "Calm down, y'all. It's Me—don't be scared."

28.text: Peter said, "Lord, if it's really You, tell me to come to You on the water."

29.text: Jesus said, "Come on." So Peter hopped out the boat and started walkin' on water toward Jesus.

30.text: But when he saw how crazy the wind was, he got shook and started sinkin'. He yelled, "Lord, save me!"

31.text: Jesus grabbed him immediately and said, "You had such little faith. Why'd you doubt?"

32.text: As soon as they got back in the boat, the wind stopped.

33.text: Everybody in the boat bowed down and said, "You really are the Son of God."

34.text: When they got to the other side, they landed in Gennesaret.

35.text: Folks there recognized Jesus quick. They went and told everybody around, and soon sick folks were comin' from everywhere.

36.text: They begged Him, "Let us just touch the edge of Your clothes." And everybody who touched Him got healed completely.

1.text: Some religious folks—Pharisees and scribes straight outta Jerusalem—pulled up on Jesus and said,

2.text: "Why your crew don't follow tradition? They eatin' without washin' their hands!"

3.text: Jesus said, "Why y'all so pressed about tradition when you break God's commandments over it?

4.text: God said, 'Respect your mama and daddy,' and 'If you curse your folks, you supposed to be dealt with.'

5.text: But y'all say, 'If I give my money to God instead of my parents, I'm good.'

6.text: So now you lettin' people skip honorin' their parents for the sake of y'all's tradition. That means God's word ain't even hittin' no more 'cause of y'all.

7.text: Hypocrites! Isaiah was talkin' 'bout y'all when he said:

8.text: 'These people talk good with they mouth, But their hearts? Way far from Me.

9.text: They worship Me for nothin', Teachin' man-made rules like they from God.'"

10.text: Then Jesus turned to the crowd and said, "Listen and understand this—

11.text: It ain't what go in your mouth that makes you dirty. It's what comes out your mouth that shows what's really inside."

12.text: The disciples came to Him like, "Jesus… You know You offended the Pharisees with that, right?"

13.text: Jesus said, "Any plant My Father didn't plant? It's gettin' pulled up.

14.text: Leave them alone. They blind, leadin' blind. Both gon' end up in a ditch."

15.text: Peter said, "Lord, can You break that down for us?"

16.text: Jesus said, "Y'all still don't get it?

17.text: Food goes in, passes through the body—it's temporary.

18.text: But the stuff that comes out your mouth? That's from the heart—and that's what makes you messed up.
