19.text: So then you might ask, "How God still blame folks? Ain't nobody resistin' His will."

20.text: But hold up—who are you to talk back to God? Can what's made talk to the Maker and say, "Why you make me like this?"

21.text: Don't the potter got authority over the clay—to make one pot for honor and another for trash?

22.text: What if God, wantin' to show His wrath and power, put up with folks made for destruction—patiently—

23.text: just so He could show off the riches of His glory to the ones He made for mercy?

24.text: And that's us—not just Jews, but Gentiles too.

25.text: Like He said in Hosea: "I'ma call folks My people who ain't even My people. I'ma call her loved who wasn't loved."

26.text: And, "In the same place they was told, 'Y'all not My people,' they gon' be called sons of the livin' God."

27.text: And Isaiah shouted this about Israel: "Even if Israel's people was as many as sand on the beach, only a remnant gon' be saved."

28.text: "The Lord gon' finish what He started. He gon' wrap it up quick and in righteousness."

29.text: And just like Isaiah said before: "If the Lord of Hosts hadn't left us some folks, we'd be like Sodom and Gomorrah—straight wiped out."

30.text: So what's the takeaway? The Gentiles, who wasn't even chasin' righteousness, got it—because they came through faith.

31.text: But Israel, who been chasin' righteousness through the law, ain't catch it.

32.text: Why? 'Cause they was tryin' to earn it through works—not through faith. And they tripped over the stumbling block.

33.text: Like it's written: "Look, I'm layin' down a stone in Zion—a stone folks gon' trip on. But whoever believes in Him won't be ashamed."

1.text: Family, my heart's desire and my prayer to God for Israel is that they get saved.

2.text: I can testify—they got a real zeal for God, but it ain't grounded in truth.

3.text: They tryna make their own righteousness work, instead of submitting to the righteousness that comes from God.

4.text: But Christ? He the end of all that law-based righteousness—for everybody who believes.

5.text: Moses said, "The one who lives by the law gotta keep every part of it."

6.text: But the righteousness that comes from faith don't talk like that. It don't say, "Who gon' go up to heaven?" (like you gotta bring Christ down),

7.text: or "Who gon' go down to the grave?" (like you gotta raise Christ up).

8.text: What it does say is: "The word is right here—near you. It's in your mouth and in your heart." That's the word of faith we been preachin'.

9.text: So if you say with your mouth, "Jesus is Lord," and believe in your heart that God raised Him from the dead—you will be saved.

10.text: 'Cause with your heart you believe and get made right, and with your mouth you confess and receive salvation.

11.text: Scripture say, "Whoever believes in Him won't be put to shame."

12.text: It don't matter if you Jew or Greek—same Lord over everybody, and He got blessings for all who call on Him.

13.text: "Whoever calls on the name of the Lord gon' be saved." Period.

14.text: But how they gon' call on someone they ain't believe in? And how they gon' believe if they ain't never heard about Him? And how they gon' hear without somebody preachin'?

15.text: And how folks gon' preach unless they been sent? Like the Word says:"How beautiful are the feet of them who bring good news—who preach peace and bring glad tidings of good things."

16.text: But everybody ain't listen to the gospel. Isaiah said, "Lord, who believed what we said?"

17.text: So faith comes from hearin'—and hearin' comes from the Word of Christ.

18.text: But hold up—did they really not hear? Oh they heard:"Their voice went out to the whole earth,Their words to the ends of the world."

19.text: Did Israel really not understand? First Moses said:"I'ma make y'all jealous with a nation that ain't even a nation. I'ma provoke you with some folks who don't even look the part."

20.text: Then Isaiah got bold and said:"I let folks find Me who wasn't even lookin'. I made Myself known to people who ain't even ask for Me."

21.text: But about Israel? God said,"All day long I held out My hands to a hard-headed, rebellious people."

1.text: So let me ask—has God tossed His people out? No way! I'm an Israelite myself—from Abraham's bloodline, from the tribe of Benjamin.

2.text: God ain't abandoned His people who He knew from the jump. Don't you remember what Scripture say 'bout Elijah? He was complainin' to God about Israel:

3.text: "Lord, they killed Your prophets, tore down Your altars, and I'm the only one left. Now they tryna kill me too."

4.text: But God told him, "Nah—I got 7,000 on reserve who ain't bowed to Baal."

5.text: Same thing now—God got a remnant, chosen by grace.

6.text: And if it's by grace, it ain't about works. Otherwise, grace wouldn't even be grace anymore.

7.text: So what's the deal? Israel didn't get what it was lookin' for. But the chosen did. The rest got hardened.

8.text: Just like it's written: "God gave 'em spiritual dullness—Eyes that couldn't see, Ears that couldn't hear—And they still like that to this day."

9.text: And David said: "Let their table trap 'em, Let it be a snare and a payback.

10.text: Let their eyes go blind, And their backs stay bent."

11.text: So again—did they stumble just to fall flat forever? Nope! Their fall opened the door for the Gentiles, to make 'em jealous.

12.text: If their fall brought riches to the world, imagine what their comeback gon' bring. That gon' hit different.

13.text: Now I'm talkin' to my Gentile folks—this is my ministry, and I'm proud of it.

14.text: I'm tryna make my own people jealous so maybe some of them will be saved.

15.text: 'Cause if their rejection brought reconciliation to the world, their acceptance gon' be like life from the dead.

16.text: If the first part of the dough holy, the whole batch holy. If the root's holy, so are the branches.

17.text: Now, some branches got cut off, and you—a wild olive shoot—got grafted in. You now share in that holy root.

18.text: Don't be braggin' like you better than the original branches. Remember—you ain't holdin' the root up. The root holdin' you.

19.text: You might say, "They got cut so I could get in."

20.text: Okay, but they got cut 'cause they ain't believe. And you stand 'cause of faith. So stay humble, not arrogant.

21.text: If God ain't spare the original branches, don't think He won't check you too.

22.text: So take in both sides of God—His kindness and His severity. He was hard on those who fell, but He's been kind to you—as long as you stay in that kindness. Otherwise? You could get cut off too.

23.text: But if they stop their unbelief, God can graft them back in just like that.

24.text: 'Cause if He could graft you—a wild branch—into His tree, how much easier is it to bring the original branches back?

25.text: Look, I don't want y'all to miss this mystery and get full of yourselves—Israel got a partial blindness for now, but it ain't forever. Once the Gentiles come in full…

26.text: All Israel gon' be saved. Like Scripture say: "The Deliverer gon' come from Zion And turn Jacob from all his mess.

27.text: This my promise to them—I'm takin' their sins away."

28.text: Right now, they enemies 'cause of the gospel—for your sake. But when it comes to God's choosing? They still loved because of the forefathers.

29.text: God's gifts and His call ain't never gettin' revoked.

30.text: Just like y'all were once disobedient and now got mercy 'cause they disobeyed,

31.text: Now they disobedient so they can receive mercy through your mercy.

32.text: God allowed everybody to fall short so He could show everybody mercy.

33.text: Ohhh the depths of God's riches, wisdom, and knowledge! His judgments too deep to trace. His ways can't be mapped out.

34.text: "Who really knows God's mind? Who gave Him advice?"

35.text: "Who gave God anything first that He owe them back?"

36.text: Everything came from Him, flows through Him, and exists for Him. To Him be all glory, forever. Amen.

1.text: So look, fam—I'm beggin' you, by God's mercy, give your whole self to Him. Let your body be a living sacrifice—holy and pleasing to God. That's the least you can do.

2.text: Don't let the world squeeze you into its mold. Be transformed—from the inside out—by renewin' your mind. Then you'll know what God really wants: what's good, what's pleasing, and what's perfect.

3.text: By the grace God gave me, I'm tellin' each of y'all—don't think you more than you are. Stay humble. Think real about yourself, based on the faith God gave you.

4.text: Just like a body got many parts, and all the parts do different things—

5.text: same way, we all one body in Christ. And each of us belong to each other. We in this together.

6.text: We all got different gifts, 'cause God gave us different kinds of grace. So use 'em!

7.text: If your gift is servin', then serve. If it's teachin', teach.

8.text: If it's encouragement, encourage. If it's givin', give with no stinginess. If you lead, do it with hustle. If you show mercy, do it with joy.

9.text: Love ain't supposed to be fake. Hate what's evil, hold on tight to what's good.

10.text: Show real love for one another like fam. Be quick to honor others over yourself.

11.text: Don't be lazy—stay lit in the Spirit, servin' the Lord.

12.text: Be joyful when you hope, patient when you hurt, faithful when you pray.

13.text: Share what you got with God's people in need. Always be ready to open your door.

14.text: Bless the folks who come at you—don't curse 'em, bless 'em.

15.text: Celebrate with those who celebratin', cry with those who cryin'.

16.text: Be in sync with each other. Don't act all high and mighty—vibe with the humble. Don't think you the smartest in the room.

17.text: Don't pay evil back with evil. Try to do what's right in front of everybody.

18.text: If it's possible, and it's up to you—live in peace with folks.

19.text: Don't go takin' revenge, fam. Let God handle that. Like Scripture says, "Vengeance is Mine—I'll pay it back," says the Lord.

20.text: Instead: If your enemy hungry, feed 'em. If they thirsty, give 'em something to drink. That'll heat coals on their head—and maybe their heart too.

21.text: Don't let evil beat you. Flip it—overcome evil with good.

1.text: Everybody need to fall in line under the folks in power—'cause ain't no authority unless God allowed it. And the ones that exist? God put 'em in place.

2.text: So if you fight the system, you really fightin' what God set up. And if you do that, judgment comin'.

3.text: Folks in charge ain't supposed to scare people doin' right—they supposed to check folks doin' wrong. You wanna stay outta trouble? Then do right, and they'll respect you.

4.text: 'Cause the one in authority workin' for God to help keep things good. But if you wildin'? You better be scared. That power ain't for show. They carryin' it to deal with evil.

5.text: So yeah, obey—'cause you don't wanna get punished, and so your conscience stay clean.

6.text: That's why you pay taxes too—these folks in office? They full-time in that role, actin' as God's servants.

7.text: So give what's owed: taxes to who you owe taxes, fees to who you owe fees, respect to who's due respect, and honor to who's due honor.

8.text: Don't owe nobody nothin'—except love. That's a debt you always pay. 'Cause if you love your neighbor, you already fulfillin' the law.

9.text: All them commandments—"Don't cheat, don't kill, don't steal, don't lie, don't be greedy"—they all get wrapped up in one line: "Love your neighbor like you love yourself."

10.text: Love don't hurt your neighbor. That's why love is the full expression of the law.

11.text: And on top of all that, know what time it is—it's time to wake up. Salvation's closer now than when we first believed.

12.text: The night almost over. The day about to break. So we need to throw off that darkness and gear up with the armor of light.

13.text: Let's move right—like we out in the daylight. No wild partyin', no drunk nights, no freaky business, no jealousy and drama.

14.text: Instead, put on the Lord Jesus Christ like a whole outfit. And don't leave no room for the flesh to act up with its cravings.

1.text: Welcome folks who still tryna grow in their faith—but don't pull up ready to argue over every little opinion.

2.text: Some folks believe they can eat anything, but others—who not as strong yet—stick to vegetables only.

3.text: If you eat, don't look down on the one who don't. And if you don't eat, don't judge the one who do—'cause God already accepted them.

4.text: Who you think you are judgin' somebody else's servant? That's between them and their Master. And trust, they gon' stand—'cause God able to hold them up.

5.text: One person sees some days as more important than others. Another sees every day the same. Let everybody be solid in their own mind.

6.text: If somebody honors a day, they do it for the Lord. If somebody doesn't, they still doin' that for the Lord too. Same thing with food—whether you eat or don't eat, just give God thanks.

7.text: 'Cause ain't none of us livin' just for ourselves—and we ain't dyin' for ourselves either.

8.text: If we live, it's for the Lord. If we die, it's still for the Lord. Either way—we belong to Him.

9.text: Christ died and rose again so He could be Lord over both the livin' and the dead.

10.text: So why you judgin' your brother? Or why you throwin' shade on your sister? We all gon' stand in front of Christ one day.

11.text: Like Scripture says: "As surely as I live," says the Lord, "Every knee gon' bow to Me, And every tongue gon' confess to God."

12.text: So each of us gotta answer for ourselves to God.

13.text: So let's stop judgin' each other. Instead, make sure you ain't blockin' somebody else's walk—don't trip 'em up or slow 'em down.

14.text: I'm convinced—Jesus showed me—nothin' is unclean in itself. But if someone believes it's unclean, then it's unclean for them.

15.text: If your food messin' with your brother's heart, then you not walkin' in love no more. Don't ruin somebody Jesus died for over what's on your plate.

16.text: Don't let your freedom get talked about like it's evil.

17.text: 'Cause the Kingdom of God ain't about what you eat or drink—it's about righteousness, peace, and joy in the Holy Spirit.

18.text: If you livin' like that? You servin' Christ right, and God and people gon' respect that.

19.text: So let's chase after what brings peace and builds people up.

20.text: Don't tear down what God built just 'cause of some food. Everything might be clean, but it's still wrong if eatin' it trips somebody else up.

21.text: It's better not to eat meat or drink wine or do anything that'll cause your brother or sister to stumble or feel weak.

22.text: Got strong faith? Cool. Keep that between you and God. Blessed is the one who don't feel guilty for what they approve.

23.text: But if somebody doubts and still eats? That's sin for them—'cause they ain't eatin' from faith. And whatever's not from faith… is sin.

1.text: So look—those of us who strong in faith gotta be patient with those who ain't there yet. Don't just please yourself.

2.text: Each of us should try to please our neighbor, doin' good to build them up.

3.text: Even Jesus didn't live to please Himself. Like Scripture say: "The insults people threw at You fell on Me."

4.text: The stuff written in the past was written to teach us. It's supposed to give us patience and comfort through the Scriptures, so we can have hope.

5.text: Now, may the God of patience and comfort give you the same mind, the same heart toward each other, just like Christ Jesus had.

6.text: That way, we all speak the same thing, glorifyin' God with one mind and one voice—our Father, the Lord Jesus Christ.

7.text: So, accept each other just like Christ accepted you—for God's glory.

8.text: Now check this—Jesus came to serve the Jews, to make sure God's promises to the ancestors stay solid.

9.text: And so that the Gentiles could praise God for His mercy, like it's written: "Because of this, I'm gon' praise You among the Gentiles, And sing to Your name."

10.text: Again it's written: "Rejoice, Gentiles, with His people!"

11.text: Again: "Praise the Lord, all you Gentiles, And lift Him up, all you nations!"

12.text: And Isaiah said: "There gon' be a root from Jesse, And He gon' rise to rule over the Gentiles, And the Gentiles gon' put their hope in Him."

13.text: So may the God of hope fill you with all joy and peace as you believe, so that you overflow with hope, all by the power of the Holy Spirit.

14.text: Now, I'm confident about y'all, my people—you full of goodness, full of knowledge, and ready to teach each other.

15.text: But I've been a little bold with some of this stuff, remindin' you, 'cause of the grace God gave me.

16.text: God set me up to be a minister of Jesus Christ to the Gentiles, spreadin' the gospel so that the Gentiles can be accepted, sanctified by the Holy Spirit.

17.text: So yeah, I got reason to be proud in Christ—about the work I've done for God.

18.text: I ain't gon' talk about nothin' Christ didn't do through me, though, in word or deed, to make the Gentiles obey.

19.text: Through signs, wonders, and the power of the Holy Spirit, I've covered a lot of ground—from Jerusalem all the way to Illyricum. I've fully preached the gospel.

20.text: My goal has been to preach the gospel where nobody's preached before—so I won't be buildin' on somebody else's foundation.

21.text: Like it's written: "To folks who ain't heard, they gon' see; And the ones who never heard, they gon' understand."

22.text: That's why I been blocked from comin' to y'all.

23.text: But now, I ain't got no more places left to work in these parts, and I've been tryna come to y'all for years.

24.text: When I head to Spain, I'm gon' stop by y'all. I hope to see you while I'm on my way, and I'm countin' on you to help me get there after I hang with you for a bit.

25.text: But first, I'm headin' to Jerusalem to serve the saints.

26.text: The folks from Macedonia and Achaia decided to help out by sendin' a contribution for the poor saints in Jerusalem.

27.text: It was their honor to give, 'cause if the Gentiles shared in their spiritual blessings, it's only right they share in the material blessings too.

28.text: So when I finish this and seal it with them, I'll be on my way to see y'all, headin' to Spain.

29.text: And I know when I get to you, it's gon' be with the full blessing of the gospel of Christ.

30.text: So, I'm beggin' y'all, fam, through the Lord Jesus Christ and the love of the Spirit, to strive with me in prayer to God for me—

31.text: That I be delivered from the unbelievers in Judea, and that the service I'm doin' in Jerusalem be accepted by the saints.

32.text: So that I can come to y'all with joy, by God's will, and be refreshed by your company.

33.text: Now, may the God of peace be with you all. Amen.

1.text: I'm shoutin' out Phoebe, our sister in Christ. She a real one—servin' with the church in Cenchrea.

2.text: Show her love and welcome her like family. Help her out with anything she need—she been a blessing to many, includin' me.

3.text: Give love to Priscilla and Aquila—my folks who ride for Jesus and for me.

4.text: They risked their lives for me. I'm thankful—and so are all the Gentile churches.

5.text: Show love to the church that meets in their house too. Give a big shoutout to my dude Epaenetus—the first to get saved out in Achaia.

6.text: Greet Mary—sis went hard for the crew.

7.text: Andronicus and Junia? Salute them. They fam and did time with me. Folks respect them as apostles. They was reppin' Christ before I even was.

8.text: Say what's up to Amplias—my guy in the Lord.

9.text: Urbanus, another one of our co-laborers, and Stachys—much love.

10.text: Show love to Apelles—he passed the test in Christ. Say hey to the crew in Aristobulus's house.

11.text: Herodion—what up fam. And the folks from Narcissus's house who follow the Lord.

12.text: Tryphena and Tryphosa—faithful women in the Lord. And Persis? She be goin' in for the Kingdom.

13.text: Greet Rufus, chosen by God, and his mama—she like a mother to me too.

14.text: Say what's up to Asyncritus, Phlegon, Hermas, Patrobas, Hermes, and the whole crew with them.

15.text: Philologus and Julia, Nereus and his sister, Olympas—love to all y'all saints.

16.text: Y'all greet each other with a holy hug or kiss—whatever's holy. The churches of Christ all send their love too.

17.text: I gotta keep it real—watch out for folks who stir up division and go against what you been taught. Stay away from them.

18.text: They not servin' Jesus—they servin' themselves. Real slick with their words, flatterin' folks and leadin' the simple-minded astray.

19.text: People already heard about how obedient y'all are—and I'm proud. But I still want you to be wise when it comes to good… and innocent when it comes to evil.

20.text: And best believe—God, the God of peace, gon' crush Satan under your feet real soon. The grace of our Lord Jesus be with y'all. Amen.

21.text: Timothy—my ride-or-die ministry partner—sends love. So do Lucius, Jason, and Sosipater—my kinfolk.

22.text: I'm Tertius—the one who actually wrote this down for Paul—and I'm sendin' y'all love too, in the Lord.

23.text: Gaius, who's hostin' me and the whole church, sends his love. Erastus, the city treasurer, and Quartus, our brother, say hey.

24.text: The grace of Jesus be with all of y'all. Amen.

25.text: Now to the One who can hold you down and keep you strong by the gospel I preach—Jesus Christ. The mystery that been hidden since forever,

26.text: but now made known through the Scriptures to all nations, just like God commanded—so folks can walk in real faith and obedience—

27.text: To God, the only wise One—all glory through Jesus Christ, forever and ever. Amen.

1.text: Paul, a bondservant of God and an apostle of Jesus Christ, sent to build up the faith of God's people and get them to acknowledge the truth that leads to godliness,

2.text: With the hope of eternal life, which God, who can't lie, promised us before time even started,

3.text: But in His own time, He revealed His Word through preaching, which was entrusted to me by the command of God, our Savior.

4.text: To Titus, my true son in the faith we share: Grace, mercy, and peace from God our Father and the Lord Jesus Christ, our Savior.

5.text: That's why I left you in Crete—to set things straight, fix what's lacking, and appoint elders in every city, just like I told you.

6.text: If a man is blameless, the husband of one wife, having faithful children who aren't out here wildin' or being rebellious,

7.text: A bishop gotta be blameless, a steward of God, not self-willed, quick-tempered, always drunk, violent, or greedy for money.

8.text: He should be hospitable, a lover of good stuff, sober-minded, fair, holy, self-controlled,

9.text: Holding on to the faithful word as he was taught, so that he can teach sound doctrine and correct those who go against it.

10.text: There's a lot of disrespectful people, people talking nonsense and deceiving others, especially those who say they're from the circumcision.

11.text: Their mouths need to be shut, they're messing up whole households, teaching things they shouldn't for the sake of dishonest gain.

12.text: One of them said, "Cretans are always liars, evil beasts, lazy gluttons."

13.text: And that's real talk. So rebuke them sharply so they can get right in the faith.

14.text: Don't pay attention to Jewish fables and the rules men make up that go against the truth.

15.text: To the pure, all things are pure, but to those who are defiled and don't believe, nothing's pure. Even their mind and conscience are messed up.

16.text: They claim to know God, but their actions say otherwise—disobedient and disqualified for any good work.

1.text: But you? Speak the things that line up with sound doctrine:

2.text: Older men should be sober, respectful, self-controlled, strong in faith, in love, and in patience.

3.text: Older women too, should be respectful in how they carry themselves, not gossiping, not out here always drunk, but teaching good things—

4.text: They should be telling the younger women to love their husbands, love their kids,

5.text: Be wise, pure, keep the house in order, be good, and obedient to their husbands—so that the Word of God won't be disrespected.

6.text: Likewise, tell the young men to be sober-minded,

7.text: In everything, show yourself to be a role model of good works—let your teaching show integrity, respect, and uncorruptibility,

8.text: Your speech should be sound, so no one can talk bad about you. When your opponents see how you carry yourself, they'll be ashamed 'cause they won't have nothing evil to say about you.

9.text: Tell bondservants (workers) to be obedient to their bosses, to be pleasing in everything, not talking back,

10.text: Not stealing from them, but showing trustworthiness, so they can make the doctrine of God our Savior look good in everything.

11.text: The grace of God that brings salvation has shown up for all people,

12.text: Teaching us that, if we're gonna live right, we have to say no to ungodliness and worldly desires. We need to live self-controlled, righteous, and godly in this world,

13.text: Looking for the blessed hope—the glorious return of our great God and Savior, Jesus Christ,

14.text: Who gave Himself for us, so He could redeem us from every sinful thing, and make us His special people, excited and ready to do good works.

15.text: Speak these things, encourage people, and correct them with all authority. Don't let anyone disrespect you.

1.text: Remind them to be subject to the rulers and authorities, obey them, and be ready for every good work,

2.text: Don't speak evil of nobody, be peaceful, gentle, and show humility to everyone.

3.text: We used to be just like them—foolish, disobedient, deceived, chasing after all kinds of lusts and pleasures, living in hate and envy, hating each other.

4.text: But when the kindness and love of God our Savior showed up,

5.text: He didn't save us because of anything we did right, but because of His mercy. He saved us through the washing of regeneration and the renewing of the Holy Spirit,

6.text: Who He poured out on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our Savior,

7.text: So that, being justified by His grace, we could become heirs according to the hope of eternal life.

8.text: This is a true saying, and I want you to keep telling them that those who believe in God should be careful to keep doing good works. That's good and beneficial for everyone.

9.text: But stay away from foolish arguments, family trees, fights, and all that drama about the law—it's just useless.

10.text: Reject the person who's always causing division after you've tried to talk to them twice,

11.text: 'Cause you know they're messed up and sinning, self-condemned.

12.text: When I send Artemas or Tychicus to you, be sure to come to me at Nicopolis, 'cause I decided to spend the winter there.

13.text: Send Zenas the lawyer and Apollos on their journey quickly so they don't lack nothing.

14.text: And let our people also learn to do good works, help out with urgent needs, so they're not out here being useless.

15.text: Everyone who's with me sends their greetings. Greet the ones who love us in the faith. Grace be with you all. Amen.

1.text: Adam had Seth, then came Enosh.

2.text: Enosh's fam kept it goin'—Cainan, Mahalalel, then Jared.

3.text: Jared had Enoch, who had Methuselah, then came Lamech.

4.text: Lamech had Noah. Noah had three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

5.text: Japheth's sons? Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.

6.text: Gomer's sons: Ashkenaz, Diphath, and Togarmah.

7.text: Javan's boys: Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Rodanim.

8.text: Ham's sons were Cush, Mizraim, Put, and Canaan.

9.text: Cush had Seba, Havilah, Sabta, Raamah, and Sabtecha. Raamah had Sheba and Dedan.

10.text: Cush had Nimrod too. Bro started makin' a name for himself as a mighty dude on earth.

11.text: Mizraim had all these: Ludim, Anamim, Lehabim, Naphtuhim,

12.text: Pathrusim, Casluhim (Philistines came from them), and Caphtorim.

13.text: Canaan had Sidon, his firstborn, then Heth.

14.text: Plus the Jebusite, Amorite, Girgashite,

15.text: Hivite, Arkite, Sinite,

16.text: Arvadite, Zemarite, and Hamathite.

17.text: Shem had Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud, and Aram. Aram's sons: Uz, Hul, Gether, and Meshech.

18.text: Arphaxad had Shelah, Shelah had Eber.

19.text: Eber had two boys—Peleg (named 'cause the earth got split up when he was born) and his brother Joktan.

20.text: Joktan had Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,

21.text: Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah,

22.text: Ebal, Abimael, Sheba,

23.text: Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab. All them were Joktan's sons.

24.text: Here's the line: Shem, Arphaxad, Shelah,

25.text: Eber, Peleg, Reu,

26.text: Serug, Nahor, Terah,

27.text: Then came Abram—who later got renamed Abraham.

28.text: Abraham had two boys: Isaac and Ishmael.

29.text: Ishmael's sons: Nebajoth (the oldest), then Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,

30.text: Mishma, Dumah, Massa, Hadad, Tema,

31.text: Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah—twelve sons in total.

32.text: Abraham's side woman, Keturah, had Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah. Jokshan had Sheba and Dedan.

33.text: Midian's sons: Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. All of them came from Keturah.

34.text: Isaac had Esau and Jacob (aka Israel).

35.text: Esau had Eliphaz, Reuel, Jeush, Jaalam, and Korah.

36.text: Eliphaz's boys: Teman, Omar, Zephi, Gatam, and Kenaz. Eliphaz and Timna had Amalek too.

37.text: Reuel's sons: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah.

38.text: Seir's sons: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan.

39.text: Lotan had Hori and Homam. His sister was Timna.

40.text: Shobal's sons: Alian, Manahath, Ebal, Shephi, and Onam. Zibeon had Ajah and Anah.

41.text: Anah had Dishon. Dishon had Hamran, Eshban, Ithran, and Cheran.

42.text: Ezer's sons: Bilhan, Zaavan, and Jaakan. Dishan had Uz and Aran.

43.text: Before Israel had kings, Edom already had 'em. First up was Bela, son of Beor. His city? Dinhabah.

44.text: When Bela died, Jobab, son of Zerah from Bozrah, took over.

45.text: Then Jobab died, and Husham from Teman ruled next.

46.text: After Husham, Hadad son of Bedad took over. He's the one who beat Midian in Moab. His city? Avith.

47.text: Then came Samlah from Masrekah after Hadad passed.

48.text: After Samlah died, Saul from Rehoboth by the River stepped in.

49.text: Saul died, and Baal-Hanan, son of Achbor, ruled next.

50.text: Then Hadad took over. His city was Pai. His wife? Mehetabel, daughter of Matred, granddaughter of Mezahab.

51.text: Hadad died too. Then the chiefs of Edom were: Timnah, Aliah, Jetheth,

52.text: Aholibamah, Elah, Pinon,

53.text: Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar,

54.text: Magdiel, and Iram. Those were all the Edomite chiefs.

1.text: These was Jacob's sons—aka Israel: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun,

2.text: Dan, Joseph, Benjamin, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.

3.text: Judah had three sons with a Canaanite woman named Shua's daughter—Er, Onan, and Shelah. But Er, the oldest, did some foul stuff in God's eyes, so God took him out.

4.text: Then Tamar, Judah's daughter-in-law, had twin boys by him—Perez and Zerah. So in total, Judah had five sons.

5.text: Perez had two sons: Hezron and Hamul.

6.text: Zerah had five: Zimri, Ethan, Heman, Calcol, and Dara.

7.text: Carmi had a son named Achar—he the one who brought drama to Israel by takin' what was cursed.

8.text: Ethan had a son named Azariah.

9.text: Hezron's sons? Jerahmeel, Ram, and Chelubai.

10.text: Ram had Amminadab, who had Nahshon—he was a big-time leader for Judah.

11.text: Nahshon had Salma, and Salma had Boaz.

12.text: Boaz had Obed, and Obed had Jesse.

13.text: Jesse's sons: Eliab was the first, Abinadab second, Shimea third,

14.text: Nethanel fourth, Raddai fifth,

15.text: Ozem sixth, and David was number seven.

16.text: Jesse also had daughters—Zeruiah and Abigail. Zeruiah's boys were Abishai, Joab, and Asahel—three solid warriors.

17.text: Abigail had a son named Amasa. His daddy was Jether, an Ishmaelite.

18.text: Caleb (Hezron's son) had kids by his wife Azubah and also Jerioth. Their sons were Jesher, Shobab, and Ardon.

19.text: When Azubah passed, Caleb married Ephrath, and she had Hur.

20.text: Hur had Uri, and Uri had Bezalel.

21.text: Later, Hezron married Machir's daughter (that's Gilead's pops) when he was sixty. She gave birth to Segub.

22.text: Segub had Jair, who ended up with 23 towns in Gilead.

23.text: But Geshur and Aram snatched some of them towns from Jair—Kenath and its hood too. Sixty towns total. All of 'em was part of Machir's fam, Gilead's people.

24.text: When Hezron died in Caleb Ephrathah, his widow Abijah had Ashhur, who became the father of Tekoa.

25.text: Jerahmeel (Hezron's oldest) had these sons: Ram (the oldest), Bunah, Oren, Ozem, and Ahijah.

26.text: He had another wife too, named Atarah. She was Onam's mama.

27.text: Ram's sons were Maaz, Jamin, and Eker.

28.text: Onam's boys were Shammai and Jada. Shammai had Nadab and Abishur.

29.text: Abishur's wife was Abihail. She had Ahban and Molid.

30.text: Nadab had Seled and Appaim. Seled didn't have no kids.

31.text: Appaim had Ishi, Ishi had Sheshan, and Sheshan had Ahlai.

32.text: Jada (Shammai's brother) had Jether and Jonathan. Jether didn't have kids.

33.text: Jonathan's sons were Peleth and Zaza. That's all Jerahmeel's people.

34.text: Now Sheshan ain't have no sons—just daughters. So he gave one of his daughters to his Egyptian servant Jarha.

35.text: They had a son named Attai.

36.text: Attai had Nathan, and Nathan had Zabad.

37.text: Zabad had Ephlal, and Ephlal had Obed.

38.text: Obed had Jehu, and Jehu had Azariah.

39.text: Azariah had Helez, and Helez had Eleasah.

40.text: Eleasah had Sismai, and Sismai had Shallum.

41.text: Shallum had Jekamiah, and Jekamiah had Elishama.

42.text: Caleb (Jerahmeel's brother) had a son named Mesha, who started Ziph's line. He also had Mareshah, father of Hebron.

43.text: Hebron's sons: Korah, Tappuah, Rekem, and Shema.

44.text: Shema had Raham (father of Jorkoam), and Rekem had Shammai.

45.text: Shammai's son was Maon, and Maon was the father of Beth Zur.

46.text: Caleb's side chick Ephah had Haran, Moza, and Gazez. Haran also had Gazez.

47.text: Jahdai had these sons: Regem, Jotham, Geshan, Pelet, Ephah, and Shaaph.

48.text: Another one of Caleb's side chicks, Maachah, had Sheber and Tirhanah.

49.text: She also gave birth to Shaaph (father of Madmannah), and Sheva (father of Machbenah and Gibea). Caleb also had a daughter named Achsah.

50.text: These were Caleb's descendants. Hur (Ephrathah's firstborn) had Shobal, father of Kirjath Jearim,

51.text: Salma, who started Bethlehem, and Hareph, who ran Beth Gader.

52.text: Shobal had sons too: Haroeh and half the fams of Manuhoth.

53.text: Kirjath Jearim had families like the Ithrites, Puthites, Shumathites, and Mishraites. From them came the Zorathites and Eshtaolites.

54.text: Salma's people were from Bethlehem, Netophah, Atroth Beth Joab, half the Manahethites, and the Zorites.

55.text: There was also a group of scribes livin' at Jabez—Tirathites, Shimeathites, and Suchathites. They were Kenites from Hammath, who came from Rechab's fam.

1.text: These the sons David had while he was livin' in Hebron: First was Amnon by Ahinoam from Jezreel. Second was Daniel by Abigail from Carmel.

2.text: Third was Absalom—his mama was Maacah, daughter of Talmai, king of Geshur. Fourth was Adonijah, son of Haggith.

3.text: Fifth was Shephatiah by Abital. Sixth was Ithream by his wife Eglah.

4.text: So six sons came while he was runnin' Hebron, where he ruled for seven years and six months. Then he moved to Jerusalem and reigned there thirty-three more years.

5.text: In Jerusalem, David had more kids: Shimea, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon—those four came from Bathshua, daughter of Ammiel.

6.text: He also had Ibhar, Elishama, and Eliphelet.

7.text: Then came Nogah, Nepheg, and Japhia.

8.text: And Elishama again (yep, another one), Eliada, and another Eliphelet—nine sons total in Jerusalem.

9.text: These were all David's sons, not even countin' the ones from his side chicks. Tamar was their sister.

10.text: Solomon's son was Rehoboam. Then came Abijah, then Asa, then Jehoshaphat.

11.text: Jehoshaphat had Joram. Joram had Ahaziah. Ahaziah had Joash.

12.text: Joash had Amaziah, who had Azariah, who had Jotham.

13.text: Jotham had Ahaz, who had Hezekiah, who had Manasseh.

14.text: Manasseh had Amon, who had Josiah.

15.text: Josiah's sons were: Johanan (firstborn), Jehoiakim (second), Zedekiah (third), and Shallum (fourth).

16.text: Jehoiakim's sons were Jeconiah and Zedekiah.

17.text: Jeconiah's sons: Assir, Shealtiel,

18.text: Malchiram, Pedaiah, Shenazzar, Jecamiah, Hoshama, and Nedabiah.

19.text: Pedaiah had Zerubbabel and Shimei. Zerubbabel's kids were Meshullam, Hananiah, and their sister Shelomith.

20.text: Also: Hashubah, Ohel, Berechiah, Hasadiah, and Jushab-Hesed—five total.

21.text: Hananiah had Pelatiah and Jeshaiah. Then came the sons of Rephaiah, then Arnan, Obadiah, and Shechaniah.

22.text: Shechaniah had a son named Shemaiah. Shemaiah had Hattush, Igal, Bariah, Neariah, and Shaphat—six in all.

23.text: Neariah had Elioenai, Hezekiah, and Azrikam—three sons.

24.text: Elioenai had seven sons: Hodaviah, Eliashib, Pelaiah, Akkub, Johanan, Delaiah, and Anani.

1.text: Judah had these sons: Perez, Hezron, Carmi, Hur, and Shobal.

2.text: Shobal's son Reaiah had Jahath, who had Ahumai and Lahad. That whole crew was the fam of the Zorathites.

3.text: From the fam of Etam: Jezreel, Ishma, and Idbash. Their sister was Hazelelponi.

4.text: Penuel ran Gedor, and Ezer ran Hushah. These were Hur's people—he was Ephrathah's oldest son and the one who started Bethlehem's line.

5.text: Ashhur, the man from Tekoa, had two wives: Helah and Naarah.

6.text: Naarah had Ahuzzam, Hepher, Temeni, and Haahashtari. That was her squad.

7.text: Helah had Zereth, Zohar, and Ethnan.

8.text: Koz had Anub, Zobebah, and the fam of Aharhel, Harum's son.

9.text: Now Jabez stood out from his brothers—his mama named him Jabez 'cause she had a hard labor.

10.text: Jabez prayed to the God of Israel sayin', 'Lord, bless me real good, stretch my territory, keep your hand on me, and don't let no evil cause me or others pain!' And God came through and granted his prayer.

11.text: Chelub, Shuhah's brother, had Mehir, who had Eshton.

12.text: Eshton's line included Beth-Rapha, Paseah, and Tehinnah (he ran Ir-Nahash). That whole crew came from Rechah.

13.text: Kenaz had Othniel and Seraiah. Othniel had Hathath,

14.text: and Meonothai had Ophrah. Seraiah had Joab, who ran Ge Harashim—place where all the craftsmen worked.

15.text: Caleb (Jephunneh's son) had Iru, Elah, and Naam. Elah's son was Kenaz.

16.text: Jehallelel's sons were Ziph, Ziphah, Tiria, and Asarel.

17.text: Ezrah had Jether, Mered, Epher, and Jalon. Mered's wife had Miriam, Shammai, and Ishbah (who started Eshtemoa).

18.text: His other wife Jehudijah gave birth to Jered (who ran Gedor), Heber (who ran Sochoh), and Jekuthiel (who ran Zanoah). They all came from Bithiah, Pharaoh's daughter—she married Mered.

19.text: Hodiah's wife, Naham's sister, had the leaders of Keilah (the Garmite) and Eshtemoa (the Maachathite).

20.text: Shimon's sons were Amnon, Rinnah, Ben-Hanan, and Tilon. Ishi's sons were Zoheth and Ben-Zoheth.

21.text: Shelah, Judah's son, had Er (who ran Lecah), Laadah (who ran Mareshah), and the linen workers in Ashbea's house.

22.text: Also, Jokim, the men from Chozeba, Joash, Saraph (who ruled in Moab), and Jashubi-Lehem. That's old school history right there.

23.text: These were potters and craftsmen who stayed in Netaim and Gederah and worked for the king.

24.text: Simeon's sons: Nemuel, Jamin, Jarib, Zerah, and Shaul.

25.text: Shaul had Shallum, who had Mibsam, who had Mishma.

26.text: Mishma had Hamuel, Hamuel had Zacchur, Zacchur had Shimei.

27.text: Shimei had 16 sons and 6 daughters, but his brothers didn't have big families like Judah's folks.

28.text: They lived in Beersheba, Moladah, and Hazar Shual,

29.text: Bilhah, Ezem, Tolad,

30.text: Bethuel, Hormah, Ziklag,

31.text: Beth Marcaboth, Hazar Susim, Beth Biri, and Shaaraim. These were their cities up 'til David was king.

32.text: They also had villages: Etam, Ain, Rimmon, Tochen, and Ashan—five more towns.

33.text: Plus all the little villages around them, stretchin' out toward Baal. They held it down there and kept their family records straight.

34.text: Some of the leaders were Meshobab, Jamlech, Joshah (son of Amaziah),

35.text: Joel, and Jehu (son of Joshibiah, son of Seraiah, son of Asiel),

36.text: Elioenai, Jaakobah, Jeshohaiah, Asaiah, Adiel, Jesimiel, and Benaiah,

37.text: And Ziza (son of Shiphi, son of Allon, son of Jedaiah, son of Shimri, son of Shemaiah). All these were big names in their clans, and their families multiplied like crazy.

38.text: These heads of families made moves and grew their clan real strong.

39.text: They rolled up to Gedor's entrance on the east side of the valley lookin' for good land to feed their flocks.

40.text: They found a big, peaceful, and fertile area—nice and quiet. The Hamites used to live there.

41.text: Back in King Hezekiah's day, some of these brothers attacked the tents and the Meunites there and wiped them out. They settled in and stayed 'cause the land had plenty of room for their livestock.

42.text: About 500 of them from Simeon's tribe went to Mount Seir, led by Pelatiah, Neariah, Rephaiah, and Uzziel—sons of Ishi.

43.text: They defeated the last of the Amalekites who escaped, and they still livin' there to this day.

1.text: So Reuben was Israel's firstborn, but he messed up big time by sleepin' with his daddy's concubine. That move cost him the birthright—it got handed over to Joseph's sons. So when folks track the family tree, Reuben ain't listed first no more.

2.text: Judah ended up outshining all the brothers and even gave us a king. But technically, the birthright still belonged to Joseph's line.

3.text: Reuben's sons were Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi.

4.text: Joel's line went like this: Shemaiah, then Gog, then Shimei,

5.text: then Micah, Reaiah, Baal,

6.text: and Beerah. Beerah was the leader of the Reubenites, but he got taken captive by Tiglath-Pileser, king of Assyria.

7.text: Here's a few more of Reuben's crew, recorded by family: Jeiel (the chief), Zechariah,

8.text: and Bela (son of Azaz, son of Shema, son of Joel). They lived out in Aroer, stretched out all the way to Nebo and Baal Meon.

9.text: They spread even further east, toward the desert by the Euphrates, 'cause their livestock was deep and needed space.

10.text: Back when Saul was king, they went to war with the Hagrites, won that battle, and took over the land east of Gilead.

11.text: The tribe of Gad lived next door to Reuben's people in Bashan, reachin' all the way to Salcah.

12.text: Joel was their top guy, then Shapham, then Jaanai, then Shaphat—all in Bashan.

13.text: The rest of their family included Michael, Meshullam, Sheba, Jorai, Jachan, Zia, and Eber—seven total.

14.text: They came from Abihail, who came from Huri, who came from Jaroah, Gilead, Michael, Jeshishai, Jahdo, and Buz. Real long line of folks.

15.text: Ahi (son of Abdiel, son of Guni) was the head of their clan.

16.text: Gad's people stayed in Gilead, in Bashan, in the villages around there, and even in the open lands of Sharon.

17.text: All these folks got recorded in the family books back when Jotham ruled Judah and Jeroboam ruled Israel.

18.text: The Reubenites, Gadites, and half of Manasseh's tribe had 44,760 warriors—ready for action with shields, swords, bows, and skills.

19.text: They went to war with the Hagrites and their people—Jetur, Naphish, and Nodab.

20.text: God had their back. They cried out to Him during battle, and He came through. They trusted Him, and He delivered the win.

21.text: They took a crazy amount of livestock: 50,000 camels, 250,000 sheep, 2,000 donkeys—and even captured 100,000 people.

22.text: It was a big win, and a lot of folks died, 'cause the war wasn't just theirs—it was God's. They stayed in that land 'til they got taken into exile.

23.text: The half-tribe of Manasseh lived from Bashan all the way to Baal Hermon, Senir, and Mount Hermon. Their numbers grew heavy.

24.text: The leaders of their families were Epher, Ishi, Eliel, Azriel, Jeremiah, Hodaviah, and Jahdiel—straight-up warriors, well-known, and respected in their bloodlines.

25.text: But they started wildin'—turnin' their backs on the God of their ancestors. They started messin' around with other gods, like the same ones God had kicked out the land.

26.text: So God stirred up the spirit of Pul (aka Tiglath-Pileser, king of Assyria), and he came for 'em. He took the Reubenites, Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh into exile—to Halah, Habor, Hara, and the river of Gozan. And that's where they still at to this day.

1.text: Levi had three sons: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.

2.text: Kohath's sons were Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.

3.text: Amram had Aaron, Moses, and Miriam. Aaron's sons were Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.

4.text: Eleazar had Phinehas, and Phinehas had Abishua.

5.text: Abishua had Bukki, and Bukki had Uzzi.

6.text: Uzzi had Zerahiah, and Zerahiah had Meraioth.

7.text: Meraioth had Amariah, and Amariah had Ahitub.

8.text: Ahitub had Zadok, and Zadok had Ahimaaz.

9.text: Ahimaaz had Azariah, and Azariah had Johanan.

10.text: Johanan had another Azariah—he the one who was priest when Solomon's temple got built in Jerusalem.

11.text: That Azariah had Amariah, and Amariah had Ahitub.

12.text: Ahitub had another Zadok, and that Zadok had Shallum.

13.text: Shallum had Hilkiah, and Hilkiah had another Azariah.

14.text: Azariah had Seraiah, and Seraiah had Jehozadak.

15.text: Jehozadak got taken away into exile when the Lord let Judah and Jerusalem fall into Babylon's hands under Nebuchadnezzar.

16.text: Levi's sons? Still the same three: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.

17.text: Gershon's sons were Libni and Shimei.

18.text: Kohath's sons: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.

19.text: Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. That's how the Levite families broke down by their daddies.

20.text: From Gershon's line: Libni, then Jahath, then Zimmah,

21.text: then Joah, Iddo, Zerah, and Jeatherai.

22.text: Kohath's line: Amminadab, then Korah, then Assir,

23.text: then Elkanah, Ebiasaph, another Assir,

24.text: then Tahath, Uriel, Uzziah, and Shaul.

25.text: Elkanah had Amasai and Ahimoth.

26.text: Then Elkanah's line kept goin': Zophai, Nahath,

27.text: then Eliab, Jeroham, and another Elkanah.

28.text: Samuel's sons: Joel (his oldest) and Abijah (his second).

29.text: Merari's line: Mahli, then Libni, then Shimei, then Uzzah,

30.text: then Shimea, Haggiah, and Asaiah.

31.text: These the men King David picked to lead the worship music after the Ark got settled.

32.text: They handled all the music at the tent of meeting before Solomon built the temple in Jerusalem. They kept doin' their duty just like they were assigned.

33.text: From the Kohathites came Heman the singer. He was the son of Joel, who was the son of Samuel,

34.text: son of Elkanah, son of Jeroham, son of Eliel, son of Toah,

35.text: son of Zuph, son of Elkanah, son of Mahath, son of Amasai,

36.text: son of Elkanah, son of Joel, son of Azariah, son of Zephaniah,

37.text: son of Tahath, son of Assir, son of Ebiasaph, son of Korah,

38.text: son of Izhar, son of Kohath, son of Levi, son of Israel.

39.text: Standin' to his right was his brother Asaph. He was the son of Berachiah, son of Shimea,

40.text: son of Michael, son of Baaseiah, son of Malchijah.

41.text: Ethni's son was Zerah, Zerah's son was Adaiah.

42.text: Adaiah had Ethan, Ethan had Zimmah, Zimmah had Shimei.

43.text: Shimei had Jahath, Jahath had Gershon, and Gershon was Levi's son.

44.text: Merari's fam held it down on the left side. That included Ethan, son of Kishi, son of Abdi, son of Malluch,

45.text: son of Hashabiah, son of Amaziah, son of Hilkiah,

46.text: son of Amzi, son of Bani, son of Shamer,

47.text: son of Mahli, son of Mushi, son of Merari, son of Levi.

48.text: All the other Levite brothers handled everything else in the temple—they were assigned to all kinds of jobs in the house of God.

49.text: Aaron and his sons did the sacrifices—burnt offerings, incense offerings, and all the atonement work in the Most Holy Place, just like God told Moses to set it up.

50.text: Aaron's line was: Eleazar, then Phinehas, then Abishua,

51.text: then Bukki, then Uzzi, then Zerahiah,

52.text: then Meraioth, then Amariah, then Ahitub,

53.text: then Zadok, and finally Ahimaaz.

54.text: These are the places the Levites got to live, handed out by tribe and family. The sons of Aaron (from Kohath's crew) got their land by lot.

55.text: They gave 'em Hebron in Judah, along with the land around it.

56.text: But the fields and villages nearby? Those went to Caleb, son of Jephunneh.

57.text: Aaron's folks got one of the cities of refuge—Hebron. Plus Libnah, Jattir, and Eshtemoa, all with land around 'em.

58.text: Also Hilen, Debir,

59.text: Ashan, and Beth Shemesh—all with their common-lands too.

60.text: From Benjamin's tribe, they got Geba, Alemeth, and Anathoth. That made thirteen cities total for Aaron's fam.

61.text: The rest of Kohath's people got ten cities from half the tribe of Manasseh.

62.text: The Gershonites got thirteen cities spread across Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and the Manasseh territory in Bashan.

63.text: Merari's descendants got twelve cities from Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun.

64.text: The Israelites gave all these cities, along with surrounding lands, to the Levites.

65.text: The Levites got these cities by lot from the tribes of Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin—each named specifically.

66.text: Some of Kohath's descendants got cities in Ephraim's territory.

67.text: They gave them Shechem (a city of refuge) in the hill country of Ephraim, plus Gezer,

69.text: Aijalon, and Gath Rimmon—all with common-lands.

70.text: From half of Manasseh's tribe, they got Aner and Bileam.

71.text: Gershon's line, from that same half-tribe of Manasseh, got Golan in Bashan and Ashtaroth.

76.text: From Naphtali's tribe: Kedesh in Galilee, Hammon, and Kirjathaim.

77.text: From Zebulun's tribe, Merari's remaining fam got Rimmon and Tabor.

78.text: On the east side of the Jordan (across from Jericho), they got land from Reuben's tribe: Bezer in the wilderness, Jahzah,

80.text: From Gad's tribe, they got Ramoth in Gilead, Mahanaim,

81.text: Heshbon, and Jazer—all with their common-lands.

1.text: Issachar had four sons: Tola, Puah, Jashub, and Shimron.

2.text: Tola's sons were Uzzi, Rephaiah, Jeriel, Jahmai, Jibsam, and Shemuel. These were the heads of their daddy's clan—straight warriors. Back in King David's time, Tola's line had 22,600 soldiers deep.

3.text: Uzzi's son was Izrahiah, and Izrahiah had five sons: Michael, Obadiah, Joel, and Ishiah. All of them were leaders.

4.text: Alongside them, their clan had 36,000 soldiers ready for war—'cause they had plenty of wives and kids.

5.text: Across all Issachar's fams, they had 87,000 strong warriors, all recorded by name.

6.text: Benjamin had three sons: Bela, Becher, and Jediael.

7.text: Bela's boys were Ezbon, Uzzi, Uzziel, Jerimoth, and Iri—five total. They led their clans and had 22,034 warriors recorded.

8.text: Becher's sons were Zemirah, Joash, Eliezer, Elioenai, Omri, Jerimoth, Abijah, Anathoth, and Alemeth.

9.text: They were listed as heads of their houses—20,200 mighty soldiers.

10.text: Jediael's son was Bilhan. Bilhan's sons were Jeush, Benjamin, Ehud, Chenaanah, Zethan, Tharshish, and Ahishahar.

11.text: All of Jediael's boys led their clans too—17,200 warriors, ready for battle.

12.text: Shuppim and Huppim were Ir's sons, and Hushim was Aher's son.

13.text: Naphtali had four sons: Jahziel, Guni, Jezer, and Shallum. They were Bilhah's kids.

14.text: Manasseh had kids through a side chick from Syria. She had Machir (father of Gilead), who had Asriel.

15.text: Machir married Maachah (she was Huppim and Shuppim's sister). Gilead's grandson was Zelophehad—he only had daughters.

16.text: Maachah had another son named Peresh. His brother was Sheresh. Sheresh's sons were Ulam and Rakem.

17.text: Ulam's son was Bedan. That whole crew came down from Gilead, son of Machir, son of Manasseh.

18.text: Hammoleketh (Gilead's sister) had Ishhod, Abiezer, and Mahlah.

19.text: Shemida's sons were Ahian, Shechem, Likhi, and Aniam.

20.text: Ephraim had Shuthelah, who had Bered, who had Tahath, who had Eladah, who had another Tahath,

21.text: who had Zabad, who had another Shuthelah. Ezer and Elead—sons of Ephraim—got killed by some men from Gath 'cause they tried to jack their livestock.

22.text: Ephraim was tore up about it and mourned for days. His brothers came to comfort him.

23.text: Then he laid with his wife, and she had a son. He named him Beriah, 'cause that tragedy hit their house hard.

24.text: His daughter Sheerah built Lower and Upper Beth Horon, and Uzzen Sheerah.

25.text: His line continued with Rephah, Resheph, Telah, Tahan,

26.text: Laadan, Ammihud, Elishama,

27.text: Nun, and Joshua.

28.text: They lived in Bethel and its nearby towns. Eastward was Naaran, westward was Gezer and its towns. Also Shechem and Ayyah with their towns.

29.text: Along the edge of Manasseh's border were Beth Shean, Taanach, Megiddo, and Dor—all with their towns. Joseph's descendants held down all that land.

30.text: Asher's sons were Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, Beriah, and their sister Serah.

31.text: Beriah's sons were Heber and Malchiel—Malchiel started Birzaith.

32.text: Heber had Japhlet, Shomer, Hotham, and their sister Shua.

33.text: Japhlet's sons: Pasach, Bimhal, and Ashvath.

34.text: Shemer's sons were Ahi, Rohgah, Jehubbah, and Aram.

35.text: Helem's sons (Shemer's brother) were Zophah, Imna, Shelesh, and Amal.

36.text: Zophah's sons: Suah, Harnepher, Shual, Beri, and Imrah.

37.text: Also Bezer, Hod, Shamma, Shilshah, Jithran, and Beera.

38.text: Jether's sons: Jephunneh, Pispah, and Ara.

39.text: Ulla's sons: Arah, Haniel, and Rizia.

40.text: All these were Asher's descendants—heads of their clans, respected men, warriors, and top leaders. They were registered as battle-ready soldiers—26,000 in total.

1.text: Benjamin had five sons: Bela was his first, Ashbel second, Aharah third,

2.text: Nohah was fourth, and Rapha was fifth.

3.text: Bela's sons were Addar, Gera, Abihud,

4.text: Abishua, Naaman, Ahoah,

5.text: Gera again, Shephuphan, and Huram.

6.text: These were the sons of Ehud. They ran their father's households in Geba and ended up movin' folks to Manahath.

7.text: Naaman, Ahijah, and Gera made that move happen. Gera had Uzza and Ahihud.

8.text: Shaharaim had some kids while he was livin' in Moab. This was after he sent away his wives Hushim and Baara.

9.text: His wife Hodesh had Jobab, Zibia, Mesha, Malcam,

10.text: Jeuz, Sachiah, and Mirmah. All of 'em were heads of their fams.

11.text: With Hushim, he had Abitub and Elpaal.

12.text: Elpaal's sons were Eber, Misham, and Shemed—he the one who built Ono and Lod with its towns.

13.text: Then there were Beriah and Shema. They ran the families in Aijalon and even kicked the Gath people out.

14.text: Other sons of Beriah: Ahio, Shashak, and Jeremoth,

15.text: Zebadiah, Arad, Eder,

16.text: Michael, Ispah, and Joha.

17.text: Elpaal's other sons were Zebadiah, Meshullam, Hizki, Heber,

18.text: Ishmerai, Jizliah, and Jobab.

19.text: Shimei's sons were Jakim, Zichri, Zabdi,

20.text: Elienai, Zillethai, and Eliel,

21.text: Adaiah, Beraiah, and Shimrath.

22.text: Shashak's line had Ishpan, Eber, Eliel,

23.text: Abdon, Zichri, and Hanan,

24.text: Hananiah, Elam, Antothijah,

25.text: Iphdeiah, and Penuel.

26.text: Jeroham's sons were Shamsherai, Shehariah, Athaliah,

27.text: Jaareshiah, Elijah, and Zichri.

28.text: These were all chiefs—heads of their clans, leaders in their day—and they lived in Jerusalem.

29.text: The man from Gibeon lived in Gibeon, and his wife was Maacah.

30.text: His oldest was Abdon, then Zur, Kish, Baal, Nadab,

31.text: Gedor, Ahio, Zecher,

32.text: and Mikloth, who had a son named Shimeah. They lived near their family in Jerusalem.

33.text: Ner had Kish. Kish had Saul. Saul had Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Esh-Baal.

34.text: Jonathan had Merib-Baal, and Merib-Baal had Micah.

35.text: Micah had Pithon, Melech, Tarea, and Ahaz.

36.text: Ahaz had Jehoaddah. Jehoaddah had Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri. Zimri had Moza.

37.text: Moza had Binea, Binea had Raphah, Raphah had Eleasah, and Eleasah had Azel.

38.text: Azel had six sons: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. All them were Azel's boys.

39.text: Azel's brother Eshek had sons too: Ulam (firstborn), Jeush (second), and Eliphelet (third).

40.text: Ulam's sons were straight-up warriors—archers with mad skills. He had a big family: 150 sons and grandsons. All of them were from Benjamin's tribe.

1.text: All of Israel got written down in the family records, and those records got kept in the Book of the Kings of Israel. But Judah? They got sent into exile in Babylon 'cause they wasn't faithful to God.

2.text: The first folks to settle back in their cities and land were Israelites, priests, Levites, and the temple workers called the Nethinim.

3.text: Some of the folks from Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, and Manasseh lived in Jerusalem.

4.text: Like Uthai, son of Ammihud, son of Omri, son of Imri, son of Bani—he came from Perez, Judah's son.

5.text: Then from the Shilonites, Asaiah the firstborn and his sons lived there.

6.text: From Zerah's line: Jeuel and 690 of his kin.

7.text: From Benjamin's line: Sallu son of Meshullam, son of Hodaviah, son of Hassenuah.

8.text: Also Ibneiah son of Jeroham; Elah son of Uzzi, son of Michri; and Meshullam son of Shephatiah, son of Reuel, son of Ibnijah.

9.text: All of them together—956 men, heads of their families.

10.text: The priests included Jedaiah, Jehoiarib, and Jachin.

11.text: Azariah son of Hilkiah, son of Meshullam, son of Zadok, son of Meraioth, son of Ahitub—he was the chief in charge of God's house.

12.text: Then Adaiah son of Jeroham, son of Pashhur, son of Malchijah; Maasai son of Adiel, son of Jahzerah, son of Meshullam, son of Meshillemith, son of Immer.

13.text: Their crew had 1,760 heads of households—real solid, capable men workin' the Lord's house.

14.text: From the Levites: Shemaiah son of Hasshub, son of Azrikam, son of Hashabiah—from Merari's line.

15.text: Also Bakbakkar, Heresh, Galal, and Mattaniah son of Micah, son of Zichri, son of Asaph.

16.text: Obadiah son of Shemaiah, son of Galal, son of Jeduthun; and Berechiah son of Asa, son of Elkanah—he lived among the Netophathite villages.

17.text: Gatekeepers were Shallum, Akkub, Talmon, Ahiman, and their fam—Shallum was the leader.

18.text: Back then, they stood watch at the King's Gate on the east side—Levi's folks handled that job.

19.text: Shallum, son of Kore, son of Ebiasaph, son of Korah, and his family were in charge of guarding the temple entrances—same job their ancestors had back in the day.

20.text: Phinehas, Eleazar's son, had led them in the past—and the Lord had his back.

21.text: Zechariah son of Meshelemiah watched the door of the tabernacle.

22.text: All 212 gatekeepers got recorded in the family books. King David and the prophet Samuel had put them in these trusted positions.

23.text: They and their kids had shifts guarding the Lord's house—the tabernacle doors.

24.text: Gatekeepers were posted in all four directions: east, west, north, and south.

25.text: Their cousins from the villages came through every seven days to take shifts.

26.text: There were four chief gatekeepers—Levites—who had charge over the storage rooms and treasuries of the temple.

27.text: They lived all around God's house, 'cause they were responsible for it and had to unlock the doors each morning.

28.text: Some Levites were in charge of the sacred vessels—they kept count when bringing them in and takin' them out.

29.text: Others handled the furniture, all the temple gear, the flour, wine, oil, incense, and spices.

30.text: Some of the priests even made the special mix for the incense.

31.text: Mattithiah, Shallum's firstborn from the Korahite line, was in charge of what got baked in the pans.

32.text: Some of their Kohathite brothers handled the showbread every Sabbath.

33.text: The singers—heads of the Levite families—lived in the temple rooms. They were on duty day and night and didn't have to do anything else.

34.text: These heads of Levite families were leaders in their time. They lived in Jerusalem.

35.text: Jeiel, the father of Gibeon, lived in Gibeon. His wife's name was Maacah.

36.text: His oldest son was Abdon, then Zur, Kish, Baal, Ner, Nadab,

37.text: Gedor, Ahio, Zechariah, and Mikloth.

38.text: Mikloth had Shimeam. They all lived near their fam in Jerusalem.

39.text: Ner had Kish, Kish had Saul, and Saul had Jonathan, Malchishua, Abinadab, and Esh-Baal.

40.text: Jonathan's son was Merib-Baal, and he had a son named Micah.

41.text: Micah's sons: Pithon, Melech, Tahrea, and Ahaz.

42.text: Ahaz had Jarah. Jarah had Alemeth, Azmaveth, and Zimri. Zimri had Moza.

43.text: Moza had Binea, who had Rephaiah, who had Eleasah, who had Azel.

44.text: Azel had six sons: Azrikam, Bocheru, Ishmael, Sheariah, Obadiah, and Hanan. That's Azel's whole squad.

1.text: The Philistines went to war with Israel, and Israelite soldiers got shook and ran. A bunch of them got killed up on Mount Gilboa.

2.text: The Philistines kept chasin' Saul and his sons. They ended up killin' Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua—Saul's boys.

3.text: The fight was gettin' real heavy around Saul. The archers spotted him, lit him up with arrows, and he got wounded bad.

4.text: Saul told his armorbearer, 'Man, pull out your sword and finish me off before these uncircumcised dudes come through and humiliate me.' But his armorbearer was too scared—he couldn't do it. So Saul took his own sword and fell on it.

5.text: When the armorbearer saw Saul was dead, he did the same—fell on his own sword too.

6.text: That's how Saul, his three sons, and everybody in his household died that day—all gone together.

7.text: When the rest of Israel saw what happened—how Saul and his sons were gone—they dipped. They left their towns, and the Philistines moved right in.

8.text: Next day, the Philistines came back to loot the battlefield and found Saul and his sons laid out on Mount Gilboa.

9.text: They stripped Saul's body, took his head and armor, and sent the news all around Philistia—braggin' in their idol temples and to the public.

10.text: They put Saul's armor in their god's temple and stuck his head up in Dagon's temple like a trophy.

11.text: When the folks from Jabesh Gilead heard what the Philistines did to Saul,

12.text: all their brave men got up, grabbed Saul's body and his sons' bodies, brought them back to Jabesh, buried their bones under a tamarisk tree, and fasted for seven days.

13.text: Saul died 'cause he was unfaithful to the Lord. He didn't do what God said, and even went to a psychic for advice.

14.text: He ain't go to God for direction, so God took him out and handed the kingdom over to David, Jesse's son.

1.text: All of Israel pulled up to Hebron and told David, 'You fam. You one of us—flesh and bone.'

2.text: 'Even back when Saul was king, you were really the one leadin' us out to battle and bringin' us back. The Lord your God already said, "You gon' be the shepherd of My people and rule over Israel."'

3.text: So the elders of Israel came to David at Hebron, and David made a pact with them before God. Then they anointed him king, just like the Lord had said through Samuel.

4.text: David and all of Israel rolled up on Jerusalem (back then it was called Jebus). The Jebusites still lived there.

5.text: The Jebusites told David, 'You ain't gettin' in here!' But David wasn't hearing it—he took the stronghold of Zion anyway. That's what they started callin' the City of David.

6.text: David said, 'Whoever hits them Jebusites first gon' be my right-hand man.' Joab, son of Zeruiah, stepped up first—and boom—he got promoted.

7.text: David moved into that stronghold, and they named it the City of David.

8.text: He built up the whole area around it—from the Millo outward. Joab helped rebuild the rest.

9.text: And David kept leveling up. The Lord of Heaven's Armies was with him.

10.text: These were the top warriors David had—the ones who stood with him strong while he was getting established as king. They helped lock it in, just like God promised.

11.text: Jashobeam, son of a Hachmonite, was head of the captains. He lifted his spear and took out 300 men all by himself—one swing, one moment.

12.text: Next up was Eleazar, son of Dodo the Ahohite—one of the big three.

13.text: He rode with David at Pasdammim when the Philistines pulled up to fight in a barley field. Everybody else dipped.

14.text: But he and David stood their ground right in the middle of that field, held it down, and dropped Philistines left and right. God came through with a major W.

15.text: Three of the top 30 leaders came to David at the rock near the cave of Adullam while the Philistines had set up camp in the Valley of Rephaim.

16.text: David was holed up in a stronghold, and the Philistines had soldiers occupying Bethlehem.

17.text: David, real thirsty, said, 'Man, I wish somebody could get me a sip from that well near the gate of Bethlehem.'

18.text: So the three of them broke through the Philistine lines, got water from that well, and brought it back. But David wouldn't even drink it—he poured it out to the Lord.

19.text: He said, 'I can't drink this—it's like drinkin' the blood of the homies who risked their lives to get it.' So he offered it to God instead. That's the kinda stuff these three mighty men were on.

20.text: Abishai, Joab's brother, led another group of three. He took out 300 men with his spear and earned mad respect.

21.text: He was the most honored among that crew and became their captain—but he still didn't top the original three.

22.text: Then there was Benaiah, son of Jehoiada—from Kabzeel. Dude was built different. Took out two warrior-beasts from Moab, chased down a lion in a snowy pit and killed it.

23.text: He even killed an Egyptian giant, like 7½ feet tall. The man had a spear like a beam. Benaiah came at him with a stick, snatched the spear, and ended him with his own weapon.

24.text: Benaiah made a name for himself with those moves—he stood out.

25.text: He was more honored than the thirty but didn't make the cut for the original three. Still, David put him over his security detail.

26.text: Here's more of David's real ones: Asahel (Joab's brother), Elhanan son of Dodo from Bethlehem,

27.text: Shammoth the Harorite, Helez the Pelonite,

28.text: Ira son of Ikkesh from Tekoa, Abiezer from Anathoth,

29.text: Sibbechai the Hushathite, Ilai the Ahohite,

30.text: Maharai the Netophathite, Heled son of Baanah from Netophath,

31.text: Ithai son of Ribai from Gibeah in Benjamin, Benaiah the Pirathonite,

32.text: Hurai from Gaash Valley, Abiel the Arbathite,

33.text: Azmaveth the Baharumite, Eliahba the Shaalbonite,

34.text: Sons of Hashem the Gizonite, Jonathan son of Shageh the Hararite,

35.text: Ahiam son of Sacar from Harar, Eliphal son of Ur,

36.text: Hepher the Mecherathite, Ahijah the Pelonite,

37.text: Hezro the Carmelite, Naarai son of Ezbai,

38.text: Joel, Nathan's brother, Mibhar son of Hagri,

39.text: Zelek the Ammonite, Naharai the Berothite—Joab's armorbearer,

40.text: Ira the Ithrite, Gareb the Ithrite,

41.text: Uriah the Hittite, Zabad son of Ahlai,

42.text: Adina son of Shiza the Reubenite, chief of the Reubenites—he had thirty with him,

43.text: Hanan son of Maachah, Joshaphat the Mithnite,

44.text: Uzzia the Ashterathite, Shama and Jeiel sons of Hotham the Aroerite,

45.text: Jediael son of Shimri, and his brother Joha the Tizite,

46.text: Eliel the Mahavite, Jeribai and Joshaviah sons of Elnaam, Ithmah the Moabite,

47.text: Eliel, Obed, and Jaasiel the Mezobaite.

1.text: These the real ones who came through to Ziklag to roll with David, back when he was still duckin' Saul. These dudes? Straight warriors, ready to throw hands.

2.text: They could shoot arrows or sling stones with either hand—ambidextrous snipers from the tribe of Benjamin, Saul's own fam.

3.text: The main ones was Ahiezer and Joash, sons of Shemaah from Gibeah. Then there was Jeziel, Pelet (Azmaveth's sons), Berachah, and Jehu from Anathoth.

4.text: Ishmaiah from Gibeon was a beast—one of the top 30, and even led them. Then you got Jeremiah, Jahaziel, Johanan, and Jozabad from Gederath.

5.text: Also Eluzai, Jerimoth, Bealiah, Shemariah, and Shephatiah from Haruph.

6.text: Then came Elkanah, Jisshiah, Azarel, Joezer, and Jashobeam—all from the Korah fam.

7.text: Joelah and Zebadiah, sons of Jeroham from Gedor, pulled up too.

8.text: Some cold-blooded warriors from Gad rolled up on David in the wilderness. These ain't your average dudes—trained to fight, hold a shield, toss a spear, and they looked like lions in the face. They was fast too, like mountain deer.

9.text: Ezer was the top dawg, then Obadiah second, Eliab third,

10.text: Mishmannah fourth, Jeremiah fifth,

11.text: Attai sixth, Eliel seventh,

12.text: Johanan eighth, Elzabad ninth,

13.text: Jeremiah again (tenth), and Machbanai eleventh.

14.text: All them from Gad, some real-deal captains—smallest one could command a hundred, the biggest? A thousand deep.

15.text: They even crossed the Jordan when the water was wild, flooded and all. Didn't matter—they cleared out whole valleys, east and west, no hesitation.

16.text: Some dudes from Benjamin and Judah came through to link up with David at the stronghold.

17.text: David stepped out to meet them like, 'Aight, if y'all here in peace to ride with me, cool, we good. But if y'all schemin' on me, just know I ain't done nobody dirty, and may God judge if y'all on some betrayal type stuff.'

18.text: Then the Spirit hit Amasai, the lead captain, and he said, 'We with you, David! All in, son of Jesse! Peace to you and your folks—'cause your God got your back.' So David welcomed 'em and made 'em squad captains.

19.text: Some cats from Manasseh dipped out on Saul and came to David too. This was when David almost rode with the Philistines but they didn't trust him, thinking he'd flip and help Saul instead.

20.text: When David got back to Ziklag, the ones from Manasseh who joined him were Adnah, Jozabad, Jediael, Michael, another Jozabad, Elihu, and Zillethai—big dawgs, all leading thousands.

21.text: They helped David fight off raiders. These men? Straight warriors, leaders in the battlefield.

22.text: And day by day, more folks kept comin' to help David 'til his army started lookin' like God's own squad—deep and powerful.

23.text: Here's the headcount of troops that came to Hebron to hand the kingdom over to David, just like The Most High said it would go down:

24.text: Judah had 6,800 warriors, strapped with shield and spear.

25.text: Simeon brought 7,100 real ones—fit for war.

26.text: Levi had 4,600.

27.text: With them was Jehoiada, reppin' Aaron's line, with 3,700 soldiers.

28.text: Zadok was there too—young and fierce—and brought 22 leaders from his fam.

29.text: Benjamin, Saul's people, had 3,000. Most of them had still been loyal to Saul's house, but some came through.

30.text: Ephraim showed up 20,800 deep—famous for being brave and strong.

31.text: Half-tribe of Manasseh brought 18,000, already chosen to help crown David.

32.text: Issachar's crew was sharp—they understood the times and knew what Israel needed to do. They had 200 leaders, and their people followed their lead.

33.text: Zebulun had 50,000 seasoned warriors, ready for anything. They ain't fold, stayed in formation.

34.text: Naphtali came with 1,000 captains and 37,000 soldiers with shields and spears.

35.text: Dan brought 28,600 who could move like a unit.

36.text: Asher had 40,000 who could go to war and hold formation.

37.text: From across the Jordan—Reuben, Gad, and the other half of Manasseh came strapped with all kinds of weapons—120,000 strong.

38.text: All these warriors rolled into Hebron with loyal hearts, ready to make David king over all Israel. The whole nation was united behind this move.

39.text: They stayed with David three whole days, feasting and chillin'. Their brothers had already set the table.

40.text: Folks came from as far as Issachar, Zebulun, and Naphtali, bringin' food stacked on donkeys, camels, mules, and oxen—flour, fig cakes, raisin cakes, wine, oil, beef, and sheep. It was a whole celebration—Israel was straight-up joyful.

1.text: David called a meeting with all his top soldiers—thousands, hundreds—and every other leader too.

2.text: Then he told everybody in Israel, 'Aight y'all, if this sound good to y'all and God co-sign it, let's hit up all our people still scattered across the land, plus the priests and Levites chillin' in their towns and fields. Tell 'em to link up with us.'

3.text: 'We need to bring God's Ark back home. We ain't even prayed in front of it since Saul was king.'

4.text: Everybody was like, 'Bet. Let's do it.' Sounded right to the whole crew.

5.text: So David gathered everybody from all over—far as Egypt to the edge of Hamath—to go get the Ark of God from Kirjath Jearim.

6.text: David and all Israel went up to Baalah (aka Kirjath Jearim) in Judah to bring back the Ark of God—the one that's posted between the cherubim, where His name stay holy.

7.text: They put the Ark on a brand-new cart, straight from Abinadab's house. Uzza and Ahio were drivin' that cart.

8.text: David and the whole squad started turnin' up in front of God—singin', goin' in with harps, strings, tambourines, cymbals, and blowin' them trumpets like it was a full-on praise party.

9.text: But when they pulled up near Chidon's threshing floor, the oxen tripped, and Uzza reached out to steady the Ark.

10.text: God got hot real quick. He wasn't playin' about His Ark—struck Uzza down right there for touchin' it. Uzza died on the spot, in front of God.

11.text: David got mad—like real mad—'cause God snapped on Uzza like that. That place been called Perez Uzza ever since, meanin' 'God's outburst on Uzza.'

12.text: David started feelin' some type of way about God that day. He was shook and said, 'How I'm supposed to bring the Ark to my crib now?'

13.text: So David ain't take the Ark into his city. Instead, he had it dropped off at Obed-Edom the Gittite's house.

14.text: The Ark stayed at Obed-Edom's place for three whole months—and God poured out blessings on his whole household and everything he owned.

1.text: Hiram, king of Tyre, hit David up—sent messengers with cedar wood, builders, and carpenters to build him a crib.

2.text: That's when David knew, for real for real, that the Lord had set him up as king over Israel. His kingdom was glowin' up, all 'cause God was lookin' out for His people.

3.text: David got himself some more wives while livin' in Jerusalem, and he had more sons and daughters too.

4.text: Here go the names of the kids he had in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, and Solomon,

5.text: Ibhar, Elishua, and Elpelet,

6.text: Nogah, Nepheg, and Japhia,

7.text: Elishama, Beeliada, and Eliphelet.

8.text: Now when the Philistines heard David was crowned king over all Israel, they pulled up tryin' to catch him slippin'. But David got word and stepped out to meet 'em head-on.

9.text: The Philistines ran up on the Valley of Rephaim, ready to raid.

10.text: David went to God, like, 'Should I go fight 'em? You gon' hand 'em over to me?' And God said, 'Go ahead—I got you. You gon' win this.'

11.text: So they met up at Baal Perazim, and David wrecked 'em there. He said, 'God broke through my enemies like a flood bustin' through!' That's why they called that spot Baal Perazim.

12.text: The Philistines left their fake gods behind when they dipped, and David told his people, 'Burn all that up. We don't need it.' So they torched it.

13.text: But the Philistines came back again, same valley, lookin' for smoke.

14.text: David went to God again, and this time God said, 'Nah, don't hit 'em head-on. Swing around back and wait by the mulberry trees.'

15.text: 'When you hear footsteps movin' through the tops of those trees, that's your cue. Jump out then, 'cause that's Me goin' ahead of you, takin' out the Philistine camp.'

16.text: David followed the play God gave him, and they chased them Philistines all the way from Gibeon to Gezer. They didn't stand a chance.

17.text: After that, David's name rang out everywhere. And the Lord made sure everybody in every nation was shook when they heard his name.

1.text: David built himself some cribs in the City of David. He also set up a special spot—a tent—just for God's Ark.

2.text: Then David said, 'Only the Levites can carry God's Ark. That's who the Lord picked to handle it and serve Him forever.'

3.text: So David called the whole nation to pull up to Jerusalem so they could bring God's Ark to the place he set up.

4.text: Then David gathered the descendants of Aaron and the Levites:

5.text: From Kohath's crew: Uriel was the chief, with 120 of his folks.

6.text: From Merari's line: Asaiah led 220.

7.text: From Gershom's line: Joel had 130 rollin' with him.

8.text: Elizaphan's squad came with Shemaiah leading 200.

9.text: Hebron's family brought 80, with Eliel in charge.

10.text: And Uzziel's people had Amminadab at the front, with 112 behind him.

11.text: David called up Zadok and Abiathar the priests, and them Levite leaders: Uriel, Asaiah, Joel, Shemaiah, Eliel, and Amminadab.

12.text: He told 'em, 'Y'all the heads of the Levite fams. You and your crew gotta purify yourselves, 'cause y'all gon' carry God's Ark to the place I prepped for it.'

13.text: 'Last time we ain't do it right—didn't ask God how to move, and He popped off on us for it.'

14.text: So the priests and Levites got themselves spiritually right to carry the Ark of the Lord God of Israel.

15.text: And just like Moses said, they lifted that Ark up on their shoulders with the poles, doin' it God's way this time.

16.text: David told the Levite leaders, 'Pick out folks to sing and play music—stringed instruments, harps, cymbals—let's make this a joyful noise for real.'

17.text: So the Levites chose Heman (Joel's son), Asaph (son of Berechiah), and Ethan (from Merari's line, son of Kushaiah).

18.text: They also brought in the second string crew: Zechariah, Ben, Jaaziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattithiah, Elipheleh, Mikneiah, plus Obed-Edom and Jeiel as gatekeepers.

19.text: The main singers—Heman, Asaph, and Ethan—were the ones bangin' cymbals made of bronze.

20.text: Zechariah, Aziel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Unni, Eliab, Maaseiah, and Benaiah played strings, tuned to Alamoth style.
