21.text: Mattithiah, Elipheleh, Mikneiah, Obed-Edom, Jeiel, and Azaziah were on harps, tuned to Sheminith style.

22.text: Chenaniah, a Levite leader, was in charge of the music 'cause he was gifted like that.

23.text: Berechiah and Elkanah worked the doors where the Ark was.

24.text: Priests Shebaniah, Joshaphat, Nethanel, Amasai, Zechariah, Benaiah, and Eliezer blew trumpets in front of the Ark. Obed-Edom and Jehiah stayed on doorkeepin' duty.

25.text: David, the elders, and the commanders brought the Ark of the covenant of the Lord up from Obed-Edom's crib, and they were hyped.

26.text: When God helped the Levites carry the Ark, they showed love back—offered seven bulls and seven rams.

27.text: David was rockin' a fine linen robe, just like the Levites, the singers, and Chenaniah the music director. David also had on a linen ephod over it.

28.text: All Israel turned up as they brought the Ark back—shoutin', blowin' horns, blastin' trumpets, crashin' cymbals, and strummin' strings and harps.

29.text: But when the Ark got to the City of David, Michal (Saul's daughter) looked out the window, saw King David dancin' like he ain't care who was watchin'—and she felt some type of way. She was straight-up salty in her heart.

1.text: They brought the Ark of God and set it right in the tent David had pitched just for it. Then they gave burnt offerings and peace offerings in front of the Lord.

2.text: When David finished givin' those offerings, he turned to the people and blessed them in God's name.

3.text: Then he passed out food to everybody in Israel—man and woman. Each person got a loaf of bread, a piece of meat, and a cake made with raisins.

4.text: David picked out some Levites to stay on post in front of the Ark—to remember what God had done, to thank Him, and to praise Him.

5.text: Asaph was lead, then Zechariah, Jeiel, Shemiramoth, Jehiel, Mattithiah, Eliab, Benaiah, and Obed-Edom. Jeiel was on the strings and harps, while Asaph handled the cymbals.

6.text: Benaiah and Jahaziel the priests kept blowin' them trumpets in front of the Ark like clockwork.

7.text: That same day, David handed over this praise song to Asaph and his crew to lead the people in thankin' the Lord:

8.text: 'Give thanks to the Lord! Call on His name! Let everybody know what He's done!'

9.text: 'Sing to Him, lift Him up in your songs. Talk about all His wild and wonderful works.'

10.text: 'Shout out His holy name! Let everybody who's really seekin' God be filled with joy!'

11.text: 'Go lookin' for the Lord and His strength. Don't stop chasin' after His presence!'

12.text: 'Remember all the things He done—His miracles and judgments He laid down.'

13.text: 'Y'all, the children of Israel—His chosen folks, Jacob's fam—don't forget who y'all belong to.'

14.text: 'He the Lord our God, and His judgment reaches across the earth.'

15.text: 'Never forget His covenant—His word stands for a thousand generations.'

16.text: 'The same one He gave Abraham, confirmed it with Isaac,'

17.text: 'And then made it law with Jacob—an eternal promise to Israel.'

18.text: 'He said, "I'ma give y'all the land of Canaan. That's your inheritance, your legacy."'

19.text: 'Even when y'all were just a few folks, wanderin' strangers in that land,'

20.text: 'Bouncin' from country to country, livin' as outsiders,'

21.text: 'God didn't let nobody mess with 'em. He even checked kings to protect His people,'

22.text: 'Sayin', "Don't lay a finger on My chosen ones. Don't harm My prophets."'

23.text: 'Sing to the Lord, whole world! Spread the word—salvation's here and it's daily!'

24.text: 'Tell every nation how glorious He is. Brag on His miracles everywhere.'

25.text: 'The Lord is great and deserves all the praise. Ain't no god above Him.'

26.text: 'Other so-called gods? Just idols. But the Lord? He made the whole universe.'

27.text: 'He got honor and majesty with Him—power and joy live where He is.'

28.text: 'Come on, families of the world—give God the glory He deserves. Show Him His strength.'

29.text: 'Give God the praise due His name. Bring Him an offering and come with respect. Worship Him in the beauty of holiness.'

30.text: 'Shake in His presence, whole earth. The world ain't goin' nowhere—it's locked in place.'

31.text: 'Let the skies turn up, and the earth celebrate! Let the nations say loud: "The Lord runs this!"'

32.text: 'Let the ocean roar and everything in it. Let the fields turn up too—all creation join in.'

33.text: 'Even the trees gon' clap for joy when the Lord shows up—to judge the earth right.'

34.text: 'Give thanks to the Lord, 'cause He's good. His mercy don't ever quit.'

35.text: 'And say this: "Save us, God! You the one who rescues. Bring us back and set us free from these other folks so we can shout thanks to Your name and celebrate Your praise."'

36.text: 'Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, forever and ever!' And everybody said, 'Amen!' and praised the Lord like they meant it.

37.text: David left Asaph and his crew right there in front of the Ark, to keep that worship goin' every day like clockwork.

38.text: Obed-Edom and his 68 fam members were also posted up, includin' his son Jeduthun and Hosah—they handled the gates.

39.text: Zadok the priest and his crew were posted at the Lord's tabernacle up in Gibeon.

40.text: They stayed offerin' burnt offerings every morning and night, just like the Law of the Lord told Israel to do.

41.text: Heman, Jeduthun, and the other chosen ones by name stayed on thanksgiving duty—praising God 'cause His mercy never runs out.

42.text: They had trumpets, cymbals, and all kinds of instruments dedicated to God. Even Jeduthun's sons were out there doin' gate duty.

43.text: Then everybody went home. David went back too—ready to bless his own house.

1.text: One day, while David was chillin' in his crib, he told the prophet Nathan, 'Man, look—I'm out here livin' in this fine cedar house, and God's Ark still sittin' out in a tent.'

2.text: Nathan told him, 'Do what's in your heart, bro. God's got you.'

3.text: But that night, God came to Nathan with a word.

4.text: He said, 'Go tell My servant David, "The Lord says: You ain't the one to build Me a house to live in."'

5.text: 'I ain't lived in no house since I brought Israel out of Egypt. I been movin' from tent to tent, tabernacle to tabernacle.'

6.text: 'Everywhere I've traveled with My people, did I ever tell any of the judges I set up over Israel, "Why ain't y'all built Me a house made of cedar?" Nope.'

7.text: 'So now, tell David this: "The Lord of Heaven's Armies says, I pulled you up from herdin' sheep to lead My people Israel.'

8.text: 'I been with you every step of the way, takin' out all your enemies. I done gave you a name—one that stand strong like the greatest names on earth.'

9.text: 'I'm finna lock in a spot for My people Israel—a place they can call home, no more bouncin' around. No more evil folks runnin' up on 'em like before.'

10.text: 'Ever since I raised up judges, it's been chaos, but I'ma calm all your enemies down. And check this—I'ma build YOU a house.'

11.text: 'When your time's up, and you rest with your ancestors, I'ma raise up one of your sons after you. I'ma make his kingdom solid.'

12.text: 'He the one who's gon' build Me a house. And I'ma lock his throne down forever.'

13.text: 'I'll be his Father, and he'll be My son. I won't pull My mercy from him like I did with the one before you.'

14.text: 'His spot in My house and My kingdom? That's permanent. His throne? Locked in forever.'"'

15.text: Nathan told David every single word of that vision, just like God gave it to him.

16.text: Then King David went in, sat before the Lord, and said, 'Who am I, Lord God? And how'd my family even get this far?'

17.text: 'And on top of that, You talkin' like You got long-term plans for my people? You really treatin' me like royalty, Lord.'

18.text: 'What more can I even say? You know me inside and out. You know what I'm about.'

19.text: 'Lord, You did all this outta love for Your servant, and You chose to show off Your greatness to me.'

20.text: 'There ain't nobody like You, Lord. No other god out here compares. We done heard all this with our own ears.'

21.text: 'And who else got a people like Israel? A whole nation You stepped in to redeem for Yourself—to make Your name famous, to do wild, powerful things by takin' out nations ahead of Your people, the ones You rescued from Egypt.'

22.text: 'You made Israel Your people forever, and You, Lord, became their God.'

23.text: 'So now, Lord, everything You promised about me and my house? Make it official. Do what You said.'

24.text: 'Let it stand, and let Your name shine forever. Let folks say, "The Lord of Heaven's Armies, the God of Israel, is really Israel's God!" And let my house stay planted right in front of You.'

25.text: 'You, my God, let me in on the plan. You said You'd build me a house. That's why I got bold enough to pray like this.'

26.text: 'Lord, You are God. And You said You'd bless me with all this goodness.'

27.text: 'Now that You done blessed my house, it's gon' stay blessed forever—'cause when You bless somethin', it's permanent, Lord.'

1.text: After all that, David ran up on the Philistines, beat 'em down, and took Gath plus all the towns around it from their hands.

2.text: Then he handled Moab too. After that, the Moabites had to fall in line and bring him tribute—they was basically payin' taxes now.

3.text: David also smashed Hadadezer, king of Zobah, all the way to Hamath. That dude was tryna flex power near the Euphrates, but David wasn't havin' it.

4.text: He took 1,000 chariots, 7,000 horsemen, and 20,000 foot soldiers from him. David crippled most of the horses so they couldn't be used in battle, but kept just enough for 100 chariots.

5.text: Then the Syrians from Damascus tried to back Hadadezer up—but David wiped out 22,000 of 'em.

6.text: After that, David set up military posts in Syria of Damascus. They had to fall in line too and bring him tribute. Wherever David went, God had his back.

7.text: David took all the gold shields from Hadadezer's crew and brought them back to Jerusalem.

8.text: From the cities of Tibhath and Chun (Hadadezer's territory), he took a whole lot of bronze. Later, Solomon used that to make the giant bronze Sea, pillars, and other temple pieces.

9.text: When Tou, king of Hamath, heard David had crushed Hadadezer's army, he knew what time it was.

10.text: So he sent his son Hadoram to salute King David and show love—'cause Hadadezer had been beefin' with Tou too. Hadoram came with all kinds of gold, silver, and bronze as gifts.

11.text: David didn't keep that for himself. He dedicated it all to the Lord—just like the silver and gold he got from Edom, Moab, Ammon, the Philistines, and Amalek.

12.text: Meanwhile, Abishai (son of Zeruiah) took out 18,000 Edomites in the Valley of Salt. Straight dominance.

13.text: He also set up garrisons in Edom, and they had to submit too. The whole country was servin' David. And again—God kept coverin' him everywhere he went.

14.text: David ruled over all Israel, and he kept things just—handlin' court cases and makin' sure things were fair for the people.

15.text: Joab (Zeruiah's son) was the commander of the army. Jehoshaphat (son of Ahilud) handled the records.

16.text: Zadok (son of Ahitub) and Abimelech (son of Abiathar) were the priests. Shavsha was the scribe.

17.text: Benaiah (son of Jehoiada) was over the Cherethites and Pelethites (David's elite guards), and David's own sons were high-ranking officials right beside him.

1.text: So after that, Nahash, king of the Ammonites, died, and his son Hanun took the throne.

2.text: David was like, 'I'ma show Hanun some love, since his pops showed me love.' So he sent his people to comfort Hanun after his father passed.

3.text: But the Ammonite princes got in Hanun's ear, like, 'You really think David sent them outta kindness? Man, they spies. They scoping out the land so he can take over.'

4.text: So Hanun disrespected David's crew—shaved their beards off, cut their robes at the booty, and sent them off lookin' crazy.

5.text: Word got back to David, and he sent folks to check on his guys, 'cause they were mad embarrassed. David told 'em, 'Stay at Jericho 'til your beards grow back. Then come home.'

6.text: When the Ammonites realized they messed up and were now on David's hit list, they dropped a whole bag—1,000 talents of silver—to hire help. They brought in chariots and horsemen from Mesopotamia, Syrian Maacah, and Zobah.

7.text: They hired 32,000 chariots, plus the king of Maacah and his army. They all rolled up and camped at Medeba. The Ammonites rolled deep too, leavin' their cities and lining up for battle.

8.text: David heard about it and sent Joab and the whole squad of mighty warriors.

9.text: The Ammonites pulled up and set up right in front of their city gate. The backup kings they hired were out posted in the field.

10.text: When Joab saw he was about to get flanked—enemies in front and behind—he took the elite squad and faced off against the Syrians.

11.text: He gave the rest of the troops to his brother Abishai, who squared up against the Ammonites.

12.text: Joab told him, 'If the Syrians got me stressed, you help me. If the Ammonites start doin' the most, I got you.'

13.text: 'Let's stay solid and ride hard for our people and our cities. Let God handle the rest however He sees fit.'

14.text: Joab and his team stepped up to the Syrians—and they folded, ran off quick.

15.text: When the Ammonites saw their backup flee, they got scared too, dipped back into the city. So Joab took his crew back to Jerusalem.

16.text: When the Syrians realized Israel had worked them, they brought reinforcements from across the river. Shophach, commander of Hadadezer's army, led them.

17.text: David got the memo, pulled together all Israel, crossed the Jordan, and set up battle lines. He was ready.

18.text: When the fight popped off, the Syrians ran again. David killed 7,000 chariot riders and 40,000 foot soldiers. He even took out Shophach, their top general.

19.text: After that loss, Hadadezer's people said, 'Yeah nah, we done.' They made peace with David and became his servants. And the Syrians? They weren't messin' with the Ammonites no more after that.

1.text: It was spring—aka battle season—and Joab led the troops out to wreck Ammonite territory. He rolled up on Rabbah and laid siege to the city. David? He stayed back in Jerusalem. But Joab handled it—he took Rabbah down.

2.text: David came through later, took the crown off the Ammonite king's head—it was heavy, like a whole talent of gold, with precious gems in it. David wore it himself. Then they looted the whole city—took everything valuable.

3.text: He rounded up all the people in the city and put 'em to work with saws, iron picks, and axes. He did the same to every Ammonite city he took. After that, David and the squad headed back to Jerusalem.

4.text: Later, another fight popped off with the Philistines at Gezer. Sibbechai the Hushathite stepped up and killed Sippai, one of the giant's sons. The Philistines had to fall back.

5.text: Another battle broke out, and Elhanan (Jair's son) killed Lahmi, Goliath's brother. Lahmi had a spear shaft thick like a weaver's beam—big dude, but he still got dropped.

6.text: Then another war went down in Gath. There was this dude—huge—six fingers on each hand, six toes on each foot. Twenty-four digits total. He was born from the same giant bloodline.

7.text: He dared to talk trash to Israel, so Jonathan, son of Shimea (David's brother), stepped up and handled him.

8.text: All of these were giant blood from Gath, but they all got taken out by David and his crew.

1.text: Then Satan got in the mix and pushed David to take a census of Israel.

2.text: So David told Joab and the leaders, 'Go count everybody in Israel—from Beersheba to Dan—and bring me the numbers. I wanna know what we workin' with.'

3.text: But Joab pushed back, like, 'May the Lord bless us with a hundred times more people! But my king, ain't they all your people already? Why you tryna do this? It could bring guilt on Israel.'

4.text: But David wasn't tryin' to hear it. He overruled Joab. So Joab did what he was told—traveled all through Israel, then came back to Jerusalem.

5.text: He gave David the headcount: 1.1 million sword-ready soldiers from Israel and 470,000 from Judah.

6.text: But Joab didn't count Levi and Benjamin—he hated this command so much he couldn't bring himself to finish it.

7.text: God wasn't feelin' this move at all. He brought judgment on Israel.

8.text: David cried out, 'God, I messed up bad. That was on me. Please forgive me for doin' such a foolish thing.'

9.text: Then the Lord spoke to Gad, David's prophet.

10.text: 'Go tell David: This is what the Lord says—You got three options. Pick one, and I'll make it happen.'

11.text: Gad came to David and said, 'Here's the Lord's word—

12.text: 'You can choose: three years of famine, or three months gettin' chased down and beat by your enemies, or three days of the Lord's plague across the land—with His angel bringin' destruction. Think it over and let me know what to tell Him.'

13.text: David said, 'Man, I'm torn up. But let me fall into the hands of God, not humans. He's way more merciful.'

14.text: So the Lord sent a plague over Israel. Seventy thousand men died, just like that.

15.text: God even sent an angel to destroy Jerusalem. But then He pulled back and said, 'That's enough. Stop now.' The angel of the Lord was standin' by Ornan the Jebusite's threshing floor.

16.text: David looked up and saw the angel hoverin' between heaven and earth, sword drawn over Jerusalem. He and the elders fell on their faces, rockin' sackcloth in full sorrow.

17.text: David said, 'Lord, this was all me. I'm the one who sinned and called for the census. But these folks—Your people—they didn't do nothin'. Punish me and my family, but not them.'

18.text: Then the angel told Gad to tell David to go build an altar on Ornan's threshing floor.

19.text: So David went, just like God told him through Gad.

20.text: Ornan was out there workin' the wheat when he looked up and saw the angel. His four sons ran and hid, but he kept on workin'.

21.text: When David rolled up, Ornan saw him and dropped to the ground face-first.

22.text: David said, 'Let me buy this threshing floor so I can build an altar to the Lord and stop the plague. I'll pay full price.'

23.text: But Ornan said, 'Nah, my king—take it! Do whatever you need. I'll even give you the oxen for offerings, the tools for wood, and the wheat. It's all yours.'

24.text: But David said, 'Nope. I'm payin' full price. I ain't givin' God a sacrifice that didn't cost me nothin.'

25.text: So David paid Ornan 600 gold shekels for the spot.

26.text: David built an altar there, gave burnt offerings and peace offerings, and called on the Lord. God answered with fire from heaven that hit the altar.

27.text: Then the Lord told the angel to chill, and the angel put the sword back in its sheath.

28.text: When David saw God responded to him at Ornan's place, he kept worshipin' right there.

29.text: At that time, the Lord's tabernacle and Moses' altar were still set up at the high place in Gibeon.

30.text: But David couldn't bring himself to go there—he was shook by that angel and his sword.

1.text: David said, 'This right here—that's the spot for the Lord's house. And that altar? That's where Israel gon' bring the burnt offerings.'

2.text: He called together all the foreigners livin' in Israel and put them to work. He assigned masons to start cuttin' stones for the Lord's temple.

3.text: David stacked up iron for the door nails and the joints, plus a whole heap of bronze too—so much they couldn't even measure it.

4.text: He also stocked up on cedar wood, 'cause the folks from Sidon and Tyre brought a lot of it for him.

5.text: David said, 'Look, Solomon's still young and green, and this house for the Lord gotta be next-level—world famous, straight glory. I'mma do all the prep now.' So David went all in before he died.

6.text: Then David called his son Solomon and gave him the mission—to build a house for the Lord God of Israel.

7.text: He told him, 'Son, I had it in my heart to build a house for God's name.'

8.text: 'But God told me straight up: "You done shed too much blood, fought too many wars. You not the one to build My house—you done got too much blood on your hands."'

9.text: 'But you gon' have a son. He'll be a man of peace, and I'll give him rest from all his enemies. His name gon' be Solomon, and I'ma bring peace and quiet in his time.'

10.text: 'He the one who gon' build My house. I'ma treat him like a son, and he'll be My child. His throne over Israel? I'ma make that forever.'

11.text: 'So now, my son—may the Lord be with you. Walk in what He told you, and build that house for the Lord your God.'

12.text: 'And I pray He give you wisdom and understanding as you lead Israel. Follow God's laws and don't stray.'

13.text: 'You'll succeed if you stay on point with everything the Lord told Moses about Israel. Stay strong. Don't be scared. Don't fall apart.'

14.text: 'Look, I went hard preparing for this—I saved up 100,000 talents of gold, a million talents of silver, and way too much bronze and iron to count. Got you timber and stone too, and you can add more if needed.'

15.text: 'You got workers on deck—woodcutters, stonemasons, and skilled craftsmen of every kind.'

16.text: 'Ain't no shortage of gold, silver, bronze, or iron. So get up, get to work. And may the Lord roll with you while you do it.'

17.text: Then David told all the leaders of Israel, 'Help my son Solomon out.'

18.text: 'Ain't the Lord your God already with y'all? Ain't He given you peace all around? He handed y'all the land and cleared out the people in front of us—y'all know it's God's doing.'

19.text: 'So now, lock in. Chase after the Lord with everything you got. It's time to rise up and build His sanctuary, bring in the Ark of the Covenant, and all the holy items—set it all up in the house that's bein' built for His name.'

1.text: When David got old and was full of years, he made Solomon king over Israel.

2.text: Then he called all the leaders of Israel together, including the priests and Levites.

3.text: They counted all the Levite men age 30 and up—came out to 38,000 total.

4.text: Outta that, 24,000 were put in charge of the Lord's house work, 6,000 were set as officials and judges,

5.text: 4,000 were assigned to watch the gates, and another 4,000 were set to praise the Lord with instruments. David said, 'I made these instruments just for worship.'

6.text: David broke 'em into groups based on Levi's sons: Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.

7.text: From Gershon came Laadan and Shimei.

8.text: Laadan's sons were Jehiel (the oldest), Zetham, and Joel—three total.

9.text: Shimei's sons were Shelomith, Haziel, and Haran—also three. These were the leaders from Laadan's side.

10.text: Shimei had four more sons: Jahath, Zina, Jeush, and Beriah.

11.text: Jahath was the oldest, Zizah was second. Jeush and Beriah didn't have many kids, so they were grouped as one family line.

12.text: Kohath had four sons: Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel.

13.text: Amram's sons were Aaron and Moses. Aaron and his sons were set apart forever to handle the most sacred duties—burnin' incense, serving the Lord, and blessing the people in God's name.

14.text: Moses' sons were still counted as Levites.

15.text: Moses had two sons: Gershon and Eliezer.

16.text: From Gershon came Shebuel, his oldest.

17.text: Eliezer's son Rehabiah was the first. Eliezer had no other sons, but Rehabiah's line grew large.

18.text: Izhar's son was Shelomith, his oldest.

19.text: Hebron's sons were Jeriah (first), Amariah (second), Jahaziel (third), and Jekameam (fourth).

20.text: Uzziel had Michah (first) and Jesshiah (second).

21.text: Merari's sons were Mahli and Mushi. Mahli had Eleazar and Kish.

22.text: Eleazar died without sons—only daughters. So Kish's sons married Eleazar's daughters to keep the line goin'.

23.text: Mushi's sons were Mahli, Eder, and Jeremoth—three total.

24.text: These were the Levite families, listed by their father's houses—heads of the clans, individually counted by name, age 20 and up, all workin' in the service of the Lord's house.

25.text: David said, 'God has given Israel peace. The people can now settle in Jerusalem for good.'

26.text: 'And the Levites no longer need to carry the tabernacle or any of its gear.'

27.text: So by David's last instruction, the Levites were now counted from age 20 and up.

28.text: Their new job was to help Aaron's descendants in the Lord's temple—serving in the courtyards and rooms, cleaning the holy items, and helpin' with the rest of the duties.

29.text: They handled the showbread, the fine flour for grain offerings, unleavened bread, baked goods, pan-fried stuff, and anything measured out.

30.text: Every morning and evening they showed up to thank and praise the Lord.

31.text: They also showed up for every burnt offering on Sabbaths, new moons, and festivals—every time, by schedule, just like the law said.

32.text: They took care of the tent of meeting, the holy place, and backed up the priests—Aaron's family—in all the work for the Lord's house.

1.text: These the breakdowns of Aaron's sons and their priestly duties. Aaron had Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.

2.text: Nadab and Abihu died before their daddy and left no kids. So only Eleazar and Ithamar were left to serve as priests.

3.text: David, along with Zadok (from Eleazar's line) and Ahimelech (from Ithamar's line), set up the service schedules for them.

4.text: Turns out Eleazar's side had more clan leaders than Ithamar's—16 from Eleazar, and 8 from Ithamar.

5.text: So they split them up by casting lots—taking turns—since both families had priests working in the Lord's temple.

6.text: Shemaiah (son of Nethanel), one of the Levites, wrote everything down while King David, the leaders, Zadok, Ahimelech (son of Abiathar), and the heads of the priestly families were all present. They took one lot for Eleazar's line, one for Ithamar's, back and forth.

7.text: 1st lot: Jehoiarib. 2nd: Jedaiah.

8.text: 3rd: Harim. 4th: Seorim.

9.text: 5th: Malchijah. 6th: Mijamin.

10.text: 7th: Hakkoz. 8th: Abijah.

11.text: 9th: Jeshua. 10th: Shecaniah.

12.text: 11th: Eliashib. 12th: Jakim.

13.text: 13th: Huppah. 14th: Jeshebeab.

14.text: 15th: Bilgah. 16th: Immer.

15.text: 17th: Hezir. 18th: Happizzez.

16.text: 19th: Pethahiah. 20th: Jehezekel.

17.text: 21st: Jachin. 22nd: Gamul.

18.text: 23rd: Delaiah. 24th: Maaziah.

19.text: This was their official service schedule for goin' into the Lord's house, based on what Aaron passed down, just like the Lord commanded.

20.text: Other Levite families: from Amram's line—Shubael. From Shubael—Jehdeiah.

21.text: From Rehabiah's line—Isshiah was the first.

22.text: From the Izharites—Shelomoth. From Shelomoth—Jahath.

23.text: Hebron's line: Jeriah was first, Amariah second, Jahaziel third, Jekameam fourth.

24.text: From Uzziel—Michah. From Michah—Shamir.

25.text: Michah's brother Isshiah had a son named Zechariah.

26.text: From Merari's line: sons were Mahli and Mushi. From Jaaziah—Beno.

27.text: Jaaziah's sons were Beno, Shoham, Zaccur, and Ibri.

28.text: From Mahli—Eleazar, but he ain't have any sons.

29.text: From Kish—Kish's son was Jerahmeel.

30.text: Mushi's sons were Mahli, Eder, and Jerimoth. All these were Levite families, grouped by their fathers' houses.

31.text: They cast lots for duties too, just like the priestly families. King David, Zadok, Ahimelech, and all the family heads of the priests and Levites were there. The senior men and the younger ones all got the same treatment.

1.text: David and the army commanders picked out men from Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun's families to handle music ministry. These brothas used harps, stringed instruments, and cymbals to speak God's word through song.

2.text: From Asaph's sons: Zaccur, Joseph, Nethaniah, and Asharelah. They were under their father Asaph's lead, who followed the king's direction while prophesyin' in music.

3.text: From Jeduthun's line: Gedaliah, Zeri, Jeshaiah, Shimei, Hashabiah, and Mattithiah—six sons total. They served under Jeduthun, who used a harp to give thanks and praise to the Lord.

4.text: From Heman's family: Bukkiah, Mattaniah, Uzziel, Shebuel, Jerimoth, Hananiah, Hanani, Eliathah, Giddalti, Romamti-Ezer, Joshbekashah, Mallothi, Hothir, and Mahazioth—14 sons in all.

5.text: These were Heman's kids—he was the king's seer, speakin' God's word through song. God blessed him with 14 sons and 3 daughters to raise the horn of praise.

6.text: All of them served under their fathers in the music ministry at the Lord's house, using cymbals, harps, and strings. Asaph, Jeduthun, and Heman were under the king's authority.

7.text: There were 288 trained musicians in total—experts in songs for the Lord. Every one of them was skilled.

8.text: They cast lots for their rotation, no matter if they were a vet or just startin' out—everybody got their shot.

9.text: The first lot went to Joseph. Second to Gedaliah, along with his sons and brothers—12 in all.

10.text: Third lot: Zaccur and his crew—12 total.

11.text: Fourth: Jizri and his fam—12 strong.

12.text: Fifth: Nethaniah, with 12 of his own.

13.text: Sixth: Bukkiah and his twelve.

14.text: Seventh: Jesharelah and his people—12 deep.

15.text: Eighth: Jeshaiah, him and 12 more.

16.text: Ninth: Mattaniah—12 in his crew.

17.text: Tenth: Shimei and 12 of his folk.

18.text: Eleventh: Azarel with 12 under him.

19.text: Twelfth: Hashabiah and his twelve.

20.text: Thirteenth: Shubael and his group of 12.

21.text: Fourteenth: Mattithiah and his 12.

22.text: Fifteenth: Jeremoth and his 12.

23.text: Sixteenth: Hananiah, rollin' 12 deep.

24.text: Seventeenth: Joshbekashah and 12 in his squad.

25.text: Eighteenth: Hanani and his 12.

26.text: Nineteenth: Mallothi and twelve with him.

27.text: Twentieth: Eliathah and his crew of 12.

28.text: Twenty-first: Hothir and 12 family members.

29.text: Twenty-second: Giddalti and 12 under his name.

30.text: Twenty-third: Mahazioth with 12 in his crew.

31.text: Twenty-fourth: Romamti-Ezer—him and his 12 were the final squad on rotation.

1.text: The gatekeeper squads were organized too. From the Korahite fam, Meshelemiah (son of Kore, from Asaph's line) was posted up.

2.text: Meshelemiah had sons: Zechariah (firstborn), Jediael (second), Zebadiah (third), Jathniel (fourth),

3.text: Elam (fifth), Jehohanan (sixth), and Eliehoenai (seventh).

4.text: Obed-Edom's sons were: Shemaiah (first), Jehozabad (second), Joah (third), Sacar (fourth), Nethanel (fifth),

5.text: Ammiel (sixth), Issachar (seventh), and Peulthai (eighth)—God had blessed his whole fam.

6.text: Shemaiah, Obed-Edom's son, also had sons. They ran their family biz strong, 'cause they were some real ones—solid and wise.

7.text: His boys were Othni, Rephael, Obed, Elzabad—and his brothers Elihu and Semachiah—dudes with skill.

8.text: Everybody in Obed-Edom's crew—sons and brothers—were strong and dependable. Sixty-two men deep.

9.text: Meshelemiah had 18 sons and brothers who could handle the job.

10.text: Hosah (from Merari's people) had sons too. Shimri got made the first, even though he wasn't born first—his dad put him in charge anyway.

11.text: Then came Hilkiah (second), Tebaliah (third), and Zechariah (fourth). Hosah had 13 sons and brothers in total.

12.text: These were the leaders of the gatekeeper groups. They all had jobs to do, just like the rest of the Levites, workin' in the Lord's house.

13.text: They cast lots to see who got posted at which gate—no favoritism, whether they were high or low rank.

14.text: East Gate: Shelemiah. North Gate: his son Zechariah (called a wise advisor).

15.text: South Gate: Obed-Edom. His sons handled the storage rooms.

16.text: West Gate: Shuppim and Hosah. Plus they got the Shallecheth Gate on the hill road—Levites watchin' both sides.

17.text: Each day: six Levites on the east, four on the north, four on the south, and two by two at the storehouse.

18.text: At the Parbar (western complex): four on the road, two more by the building.

19.text: These were the gatekeeper squads from the Korahite and Merarite lines.

20.text: Ahijah (a Levite) managed the treasuries for the Lord's house, including sacred items.

21.text: From Laadan's family (descended from Gershon), the lead guy was Jehieli.

22.text: His sons Zetham and Joel ran the temple's treasure storage.

23.text: More Levites handled sacred duties too: the Amramites, Izharites, Hebronites, and Uzzielites.

24.text: Shebuel (Moses' grandson from Gershom's line) was the top boss over all treasuries.

25.text: His extended fam—Eliezer's descendants: Rehabiah, Jeshaiah, Joram, Zichri, and Shelomith.

26.text: Shelomith and his people oversaw everything David and the army leaders had dedicated to the Lord's house.

27.text: Some of that came from battle spoils they set aside to support temple upkeep.

28.text: Everything Samuel, Saul, Abner, and Joab had dedicated to God was also managed by Shelomith and his crew.

29.text: Chenaniah and his sons (from the Izharite line) were officers and judges handling affairs outside Jerusalem.

30.text: Hashabiah and his brothers (1,700 Hebronites) had the job of managing all the Lord's business—and the king's—west of the Jordan.

31.text: Jerijah was the head of the Hebronites. In David's 40th year as king, they searched the family records and found capable men in Jazer, Gilead.

32.text: They found 2,700 more qualified heads of households, and David appointed them to handle responsibilities for the tribes of Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh. They managed everything tied to God and the king.

1.text: Israel's army was organized by family leaders, captains of thousands and hundreds, and their officers. Each group took turns servin' the king—one division per month, twelve months total. Each division had 24,000 soldiers.

2.text: January squad (first month) was led by Jashobeam, son of Zabdiel. His group had 24,000 men.

3.text: He came from the family line of Perez and was top dog over all the first-month troops.

4.text: February squad (second month) had Dodai the Ahohite in charge. Mikloth helped lead. His group had 24,000.

5.text: March squad (third month) was under Benaiah, son of Jehoiada the priest. He was the chief. His division also had 24,000.

6.text: This Benaiah was one of the mighty thirty and led them too. His son Ammizabad was part of his squad.

7.text: April squad (fourth month) was led by Asahel (Joab's brother), then by Asahel's son Zebadiah after him. Same—24,000 men.

8.text: May squad (fifth month): Shamhuth the Izrahite. Another 24,000 deep.

9.text: June squad (sixth month): Ira, son of Ikkesh from Tekoa. 24,000 soldiers.

10.text: July squad (seventh month): Helez the Pelonite from Ephraim's tribe. Had 24,000 too.

11.text: August squad (eighth month): Sibbechai the Hushathite from the Zarhites. 24,000.

12.text: September squad (ninth month): Abiezer from Anathoth in Benjamin's tribe. 24,000.

13.text: October squad (tenth month): Maharai the Netophathite from the Zarhites. 24,000.

14.text: November squad (eleventh month): Benaiah the Pirathonite from Ephraim's tribe. 24,000 soldiers.

15.text: December squad (twelfth month): Heldai the Netophathite from Othniel's clan. 24,000 as well.

16.text: These were the tribal officers: Reuben: Eliezer, son of Zichri Simeon: Shephatiah, son of Maachah

17.text: Levi: Hashabiah, son of Kemuel Aaron's family: Zadok

18.text: Judah: Elihu, one of David's brothers Issachar: Omri, son of Michael

19.text: Zebulun: Ishmaiah, son of Obadiah Naphtali: Jerimoth, son of Azriel

20.text: Ephraim: Hoshea, son of Azaziah Half-tribe of Manasseh: Joel, son of Pedaiah

21.text: Other half of Manasseh (in Gilead): Iddo, son of Zechariah Benjamin: Jaasiel, son of Abner

22.text: Dan: Azarel, son of Jeroham. These were all the tribal chiefs for Israel.

23.text: David didn't count the men under 20 years old, 'cause the Lord said He'd multiply Israel like the stars.

24.text: Joab (Zeruiah's son) started the count but didn't finish, 'cause God's anger broke out over it. So the final numbers weren't even included in David's official records.

25.text: Azmaveth (son of Adiel) managed the royal treasuries. Jehonathan (son of Uzziah) handled the storage buildings in the cities, fields, villages, and fortresses.

26.text: Ezri (son of Chelub) oversaw the field workers.

27.text: Shimei from Ramah ran the vineyards. Zabdi from Shepham handled the wine supplies.

28.text: Baal-Hanan from Geder looked after olive and sycamore trees in the lowlands. Joash was over the oil storage.

29.text: Shitrai from Sharon took care of the herds in that region. Shaphat (son of Adlai) handled the valley herds.

30.text: Obil the Ishmaelite ran the camels. Jehdeiah from Meronoth was over the donkeys.

31.text: Jaziz the Hagrite handled the flocks. All these were the officials who managed King David's assets.

32.text: David's uncle Jehonathan was a wise counselor and scribe. Jehiel (son of Hachmoni) mentored the king's sons.

33.text: Ahithophel was David's top advisor. Hushai the Archite was his close companion.

34.text: After Ahithophel came Jehoiada (son of Benaiah), then Abiathar. And Joab was still the commander of the whole army.

1.text: David called a big meetin' in Jerusalem. He gathered all the leaders of Israel—tribal officials, army captains over thousands and hundreds, those who managed the king's stuff and his sons' properties, top officials, warriors, and mighty men.

2.text: Then King David stood up and said, 'Listen up, my people. I had it on my heart to build a resting place for the Ark of God's covenant—somewhere fitting for His footstool. I even got everything ready to do it.'

3.text: 'But God told me, "You ain't the one to build My house. You've been in too many wars, spilled too much blood."'

4.text: 'Still, the Lord, God of Israel, chose me—outta my whole family line—to be king over Israel forever. He picked Judah to rule, picked my dad's family from Judah, and then He chose me from among my brothers to be king.'

5.text: 'And outta all my sons (and trust, the Lord gave me plenty), He picked Solomon to sit on the throne of the Lord's kingdom over Israel.'

6.text: 'God told me, "Solomon your son is the one who'll build My house and My courtyards. I picked him to be My son, and I'ma be his Father."'

7.text: '"If he stays faithful to My commands and listens like he should, I'll lock in his kingdom forever."'

8.text: 'So now, in front of all Israel, and before God, make sure y'all keep His commandments. Do what He says so you can keep this land and pass it on to your children forever.'

9.text: 'And you, my son Solomon—get to know the God of your father. Serve Him with all your heart and with a willing mind. He sees the real you. He knows your thoughts before you think 'em. If you seek Him, you'll find Him. But if you walk away, He'll leave you behind.'

10.text: 'So take this serious. God chose you to build His sanctuary. Be strong, and get it done.'

11.text: Then David handed Solomon the full blueprint: the entrance, the rooms, the treasuries, the upstairs rooms, the inner spaces, and the spot for the mercy seat.

12.text: He gave him plans that came straight from the Spirit—how to lay out the temple courts, the rooms around them, the storage for sacred things, and the special treasuries.

13.text: He included instructions for organizing the priests and Levites, all the service jobs in the Lord's house, and all the items they'd use in worship.

14.text: He even gave specific amounts of gold for gold items and silver for silver items—down to the last detail for every single task.

15.text: Gold for each gold lampstand and its lamps, and silver for each silver one—everything was laid out by how it was supposed to be used.

16.text: He provided gold by weight for the tables of showbread, and silver for the silver tables.

17.text: He gave pure gold for the meat forks, bowls, and pitchers. Every golden bowl had its weight marked, and the same for each silver one.

18.text: He even weighed out refined gold for the incense altar and the golden chariot—the cherubim with wings that covered the Ark of the Covenant.

19.text: David said, 'God gave me all of this. Every detail. He showed me everything in writing—this was His hand on me.'

20.text: Then David said to Solomon, 'Be strong. Be bold. And do it. Don't be scared or discouraged, 'cause the Lord—my God—He's with you. He ain't goin' nowhere 'til you finish everything for the Lord's house.'

21.text: 'You got all the priests and Levites set for service. Skilled workers ready to handle all kinds of craftsmanship. Plus the leaders and the people—they all got your back.'

1.text: Then King David told everybody, 'Look, my son Solomon—God's chosen him, but he still young and new to all this. And this job? It's major. We ain't just buildin' a building for folks—it's for the Lord God Himself.'

2.text: So I gave everything I had for God's house—gold for gold stuff, silver for silver things, bronze for bronze work, iron, wood, onyx, decorative stones, colorful gems, precious stones, marble—everything in bulk.

3.text: And because I love God's house, I'm givin' even more from my own stash—my personal treasure of gold and silver—on top of all I already set aside.

4.text: I'm givin' 3,000 talents of gold (from Ophir!) and 7,000 talents of refined silver just to cover the temple walls.

5.text: Gold for gold work, silver for silver work—all for the craftsmen doin' their thing. So… who else ridin' with me? Who gon' dedicate themselves to the Lord today?

6.text: Then the leaders of the clans, the tribal chiefs, army commanders, and officials in charge of the king's work stepped up and gave willingly.

7.text: They gave 5,000 talents and 10,000 darics of gold, 10,000 talents of silver, 18,000 talents of bronze, and 100,000 talents of iron.

8.text: And those who had gems gave 'em straight to the treasury of the Lord's house, handled by Jehiel the Gershonite.

9.text: The people were hype—they gave from the heart. King David saw it and couldn't stop smilin'—he was mad joyful.

10.text: David praised the Lord in front of everybody, sayin': 'Blessed are You, Lord God of Israel, our Father, forever and ever.'

11.text: 'Yours, Lord, is the greatness, the power, the glory, the victory, the majesty. Everything in heaven and earth belongs to You. The kingdom is Yours, Lord, and You sit high above all.'

12.text: 'Wealth and honor? That's all from You. You're the one in charge. You lift folks up, You give strength.'

13.text: 'So now, God, we thank You and lift up Your holy name.'

14.text: 'But really—who am I? Who are we, Lord, that we could even give like this? Everything we got came from You. We just givin' back what's already Yours.'

15.text: 'We're just visitors here—travelers. Just like our ancestors. Our time on earth is short—like a shadow. And we ain't even in control of it.'

16.text: 'Lord, all this stuff we've gathered to build Your house came from You. It's Yours anyway.'

17.text: 'I know You test hearts and love uprightness. I gave all this freely and joyfully. And I see Your people here, givin' with that same joy.'

18.text: 'Lord, God of Abraham, Isaac, and Israel—keep this spirit in Your people forever. Keep their hearts turned toward You.'

19.text: 'Give my son Solomon a heart that sticks with You. Help him follow Your commands and build the temple I prepped for.'

20.text: Then David told the crowd, 'Let's bless the Lord, y'all.' And everybody bowed down and worshipped the Lord and honored the king.

21.text: The next day they made sacrifices—1,000 bulls, 1,000 rams, 1,000 lambs—plus drink offerings and more sacrifices. Israel turned up in praise.

22.text: They ate and drank in God's presence with joy. And they made Solomon king again, anointin' him as leader before the Lord and anointin' Zadok as priest.

23.text: Solomon sat on the Lord's throne, takin' his father David's place as king. He was blessed and backed by all Israel.

24.text: All the leaders, mighty men, and David's sons bowed down and pledged loyalty to Solomon.

25.text: The Lord made Solomon look real royal—next-level glory that no king before him in Israel had ever seen.

26.text: That's how David, son of Jesse, ruled all Israel.

27.text: He reigned 40 years—7 in Hebron, 33 in Jerusalem.

28.text: David died old and full of years, blessings, and respect. And Solomon took the throne.

29.text: Everything David did—from the beginning to the end—is written in the books of Samuel the seer, Nathan the prophet, and Gad the seer.

30.text: That includes his whole reign, his power moves, and all that went down in Israel and the neighboring kingdoms.

1.text: King David was gettin' up there in age, and no matter how many blankets they put on him, bruh just couldn't stay warm.

2.text: So his people was like, 'Aight, we need to find a young woman—a virgin—who can take care of the king, keep him company, and keep him warm at night.'

3.text: So they searched all over Israel for the right girl and found Abishag, a Shunammite, and brought her to David.

4.text: She was real fine, took care of the king, but there wasn't no funny business—David ain't sleep with her.

5.text: Now Adonijah, one of David's sons (his mama was Haggith), started feelin' himself. He was like, 'Ima be king.' So he got himself chariots, horses, and fifty men to run in front of him like he already royalty.

6.text: Thing is, David ain't never really checked Adonijah—never told him no or called him out. Plus, dude was real good lookin' and was born right after Absalom.

7.text: He linked up with Joab (David's military general) and Abiathar the priest, and they both backed him up.

8.text: But Zadok the priest, Benaiah (David's top warrior), Nathan the prophet, and David's real ones ain't rock with Adonijah like that.

9.text: Adonijah threw a whole party near the stone of Zoheleth by En Rogel—sacrificed sheep, oxen, and cattle. He invited all his brothers (David's sons) and even some of the king's crew.

10.text: BUT—he ain't invite Nathan the prophet, Benaiah, the mighty warriors, or Solomon. He knew what he was doin'.

11.text: Nathan, the prophet, pulled up on Bathsheba (Solomon's mama) like, 'Girl, you heard Adonijah out here actin' like he king? And David don't even know about it?'

12.text: Nathan told her, 'Look, if you tryna save your life and Solomon's, I got a plan.'

13.text: 'Go straight to King David and ask, "Didn't you promise me that Solomon would be king? So why Adonijah out here claimin' the throne?"'

14.text: 'And while you still talkin', Ima slide in right after you and back you up.'

15.text: So Bathsheba went to see the king. David was still in bed, old and weak, with Abishag takin' care of him.

16.text: Bathsheba bowed down to the king, and David was like, 'What you need?'

17.text: She said, 'My lord, you promised me in God's name that Solomon would be the next king.'

18.text: 'But now, look! Adonijah crowned himself king, and you don't even know it!'

19.text: 'He threw a huge feast, got Joab, Abiathar, and all your sons over there—but he ain't invite Solomon.'

20.text: 'Everybody in Israel lookin' at you, king. You gotta let them know who's really supposed to take the throne.'

21.text: 'If you don't, when you die, me and Solomon gonna be treated like nobodies—or worse.'

22.text: While Bathsheba was still talkin', Nathan the prophet came in.

23.text: Somebody announced, 'Nathan's here!' and he came in, bowed low before the king.

24.text: Nathan was like, 'My king, did you really say Adonijah should be the next king?'

25.text: 'Cuz he out here throwin' a whole coronation party—sacrificing animals, bringin' all the royal sons and officials, and they all yellin', "Long live King Adonijah!"'

26.text: 'But funny thing is… he ain't invite me, Zadok, Benaiah, or Solomon.'

27.text: 'Did you approve this, my king? Or is this some backdoor power move? Cuz nobody told us.'

28.text: Then King David told his people, 'Bring Bathsheba back in here.'

29.text: David took an oath and said, 'As the Lord lives, who brought me through all my troubles—'

30.text: 'I swear Solomon will be king just like I promised—and it's happening TODAY.'

31.text: Bathsheba bowed and said, 'May my king David live forever!'

32.text: David called for Zadok the priest, Nathan the prophet, and Benaiah and they pulled up.

33.text: David said, 'Y'all take my officials, put Solomon on my royal mule, and ride down to Gihon.'

34.text: 'There, Zadok & Nathan gon' anoint him king. Then blow the horn and shout, "Long live King Solomon!"'

35.text: 'Then bring him back here. He will sit on my throne and rule in my place. This is official!'

36.text: Benaiah was like, 'Amen! And may God make Solomon's throne even greater than yours, my king.'

37.text: Just like the Lord been with my king, may He be with Solomon too, and make his throne even greater than King David's.

38.text: Zadok, Nathan, Benaiah, and David's royal guards put Solomon on David's mule and rode to Gihon.

39.text: Zadok took the oil from the temple and anointed Solomon as king. Then they blew the horn, and the people shouted, 'LONG LIVE KING SOLOMON!'

40.text: The whole city was lit. People playin' flutes, rejoicing—the ground was shaking from all the noise!

41.text: Adonijah and his squad heard the noise while they were eatin'—and Joab was like, 'Uh… why the city sound like it's turnin' up?'

42.text: Then Jonathan (Abiathar's son) pulled up, and Adonijah was like, 'Ayy, you got good news, right?'

43.text: Jonathan said, 'Nope. King David just made Solomon king.'

44.text: 'He sent Zadok, Nathan, Benaiah, and the royal guards with him. They put him on the king's mule, took him to Gihon, and anointed him king.'

45.text: 'Now Solomon sittin' on the throne and everybody celebratin'—that's the noise y'all heard.'

46.text: 'Even David's people went to bless him, sayin' "May God make Solomon's throne greater than David's!" And David bowed in thanks.'

47.text: 'David literally said, "Blessed be the Lord who let me see my son on the throne before I die!"'

48.text: The king also said, 'Praise the Lord, the God of Israel, for He done put someone on my throne today, and I'm still here to see it!'

49.text: When Adonijah's guests heard that, they scattered like roaches when the lights come on.

50.text: Adonijah ran straight to the altar and grabbed the horns, beggin' for mercy.

51.text: They told Solomon, 'Adonijah scared, holdin' the altar, askin' you not to kill him.'

52.text: Solomon said, 'If he proves he's cool, he's safe. But if he try somethin' funny, he's dead.'

53.text: So they brought Adonijah to Solomon, he bowed low, and Solomon said, "Go home."

1.text: David knew his time was almost up, so he called Solomon in for a real talk.

2.text: Son, everybody gotta go one day. I'm headin' that way now. But listen—be strong, step up, and be a real man.

3.text: Follow The Most High. Do what He says. Keep His commandments, His laws, everything written down in Moses' book. If you do that, you gon' prosper wherever you go.

4.text: God made me a promise—if my sons stay true, walk with Him with all they got, there'll always be one of us sittin' on this throne.

5.text: Now, you already know how Joab did me dirty. He killed two of Israel's top commanders—Abner & Amasa—in peacetime, like we was still at war. Dude got blood all over him.

6.text: You wise, son. Handle him. Don't let him grow old in peace.

7.text: But Barzillai's sons? Show them love. Let them eat at your table, 'cause they was solid when I was runnin' from Absalom.

8.text: Now about Shimei—you know, the dude who cursed me out when I was down bad? Yeah, I spared him, but that don't mean you gotta. You smart—you know what to do. Make sure he don't die peacefully.

9.text: Now don't let him slide, 'cause you smart, and you know what needs to be done. Make sure he don't go to his grave in peace—handle that.

10.text: David passed away and was buried in the City of David.

11.text: He ruled 40 years—7 in Hebron, 33 in Jerusalem.

12.text: And now Solomon was officially king, and the throne was locked in.

13.text: Adonijah (the dude who tried to take the throne) pulled up on Bathsheba, Solomon's mama.

14.text: She was like, 'You coming in peace?' and he said, 'Yeah, yeah, I got something to ask you.'

15.text: You know, the kingdom was supposed to be mine. Everybody thought I'd be king. But now it's Solomon's—'cause God gave it to him.

16.text: So now, I just got one little request. Don't say no to me.

17.text: Can you ask Solomon to let me marry Abishag the Shunammite?

18.text: Bathsheba was like, 'Aight, I'll ask him.'

19.text: She went to Solomon, and Solomon stood up, bowed to his mama, then had a seat brought for her next to him.

20.text: She said, 'I got a small favor to ask. Don't say no.'

21.text: She asked, 'Can Adonijah marry Abishag?'

22.text: Solomon snapped. "Oh, so now you asking for the whole kingdom too? Why don't you give him my throne while you at it?! Him, Joab, and Abiathar the priest—all of 'em on the same team!"

23.text: Then Solomon made an oath, 'If Adonijah don't die for this, may God strike me down!'

24.text: As surely as God made me king, Adonijah gon' be dead TODAY.

25.text: So Solomon sent Benaiah, and just like that—Adonijah was gone.

26.text: Solomon told Abiathar the priest, 'Go home to Anathoth. You should be dead, but I won't kill you now since you carried the Ark of God for my father.'

27.text: Abiathar got removed as priest, fulfilling the prophecy against Eli's family.

28.text: When Joab heard what happened, he ran straight to the altar and grabbed the horns, hoping to get mercy.

29.text: Solomon was told, 'Joab's at the altar, holdin' on for dear life.'

30.text: Benaiah went to him and said, 'King said come out.' Joab: "Nah, I'll die right here."

31.text: Solomon was like, 'Then let him die there. Handle him. That way, I won't be responsible for all the innocent blood Joab spilled.'

32.text: God gon' repay him for killin' two good men—Abner & Amasa—for no reason.

33.text: Let their blood fall on Joab, but may peace be on David's family forever.

34.text: So Benaiah took Joab out right there. Buried him in the wilderness.

35.text: Solomon put Benaiah over the army and Zadok as priest—Joab and Abiathar were officially replaced.

36.text: Solomon called for Shimei and told him, 'Build a house in Jerusalem, stay there, and don't leave. If you cross the Kidron Brook, you dead.'

37.text: Shimei agreed: 'Sounds good, king.' And he stayed put for a while.

38.text: For three years, everything was cool.

39.text: But then two of Shimei's servants ran away to Gath. He went after them and brought them back.

40.text: So Shimei got up, saddled his donkey, and rode out to Achish in Gath to go get his slaves. He found them and brought them back home.

41.text: When Solomon heard about it, he called Shimei in.

42.text: Didn't I make you swear not to leave? Didn't I say you'd die if you did?

43.text: Why you ain't listen?

44.text: You know deep down all the dirt you did to my father. Now God is paying you back.

45.text: Meanwhile, I'ma be blessed, and David's throne gon' stay strong forever.

46.text: Then Solomon sent Benaiah, and Shimei was done. The kingdom was now fully established.

1.text: Solomon made a peace deal with Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and married his daughter. He brought her to Jerusalem until he finished buildin' his own palace, God's temple, and the wall around the city.

2.text: Back then, people were still sacrificin' at the high places, 'cause there wasn't a temple built for The Most High yet.

3.text: Solomon loved God and followed the ways of his father David. Only problem? He was still burnin' incense and sacrificin' at the high places.

4.text: One day, Solomon went up to Gibeon, the most important high place, and sacrificed 1,000 burnt offerings on the altar. (Yeah, a THOUSAND. Dude went BIG.)

5.text: That night, God pulled up in Solomon's dream and said: 'Ask me for whatever you want.'

6.text: Solomon said, 'Lord, you always had mercy on my father David, 'cause he was loyal and real with You. And You kept Your promise by puttin' his son (me) on the throne.'

7.text: But Lord, I'm just a kid. I don't know what I'm doin'. You made me king, but this job big!

8.text: Your people are countless, too many to number.

9.text: So what I really need? Give me a wise heart to judge right from wrong. Who else could handle a job this big?

10.text: God was feelin' Solomon's request. He was like, 'Aight, bet.'

11.text: God said, 'Since you asked for wisdom instead of money, long life, or the death of your enemies…'

12.text: 'I got you. You gon' be the wisest king to ever do it—nobody before or after will have wisdom like you.'

13.text: 'But hold up, I'ma also give you what you ain't ask for—riches and honor. Ain't nobody gon' compare to you in your lifetime!'

14.text: 'And if you follow me like David did? I'ma bless you with long life too.'

15.text: Solomon woke up like, 'Yo… was that real?!' Then he went to Jerusalem, sacrificed to God, made peace offerings, and threw a huge feast for his crew.

16.text: One day, two women (who were prostitutes) came to King Solomon to settle a case.

17.text: The first woman said, 'My king, me and this woman live in the same house. I had a baby while she was there.'

18.text: 'Three days later, she had a baby too. We were alone—no witnesses, just us.'

19.text: 'Then one night, her baby died 'cause she accidentally rolled over on him.'

20.text: 'So while I was sleepin', she got up, switched our babies, and left her dead baby next to me.'

21.text: 'When I woke up to feed my baby, I saw he was dead. But when I looked close, I realized—THIS AIN'T MY BABY!'

22.text: Then the second woman snapped back, 'Nah! The live baby is mine, yours is the dead one!' The first woman: 'No, the dead one is yours! Mine is alive!' And they kept goin' back and forth in front of the king.

23.text: Solomon sat back like, 'So y'all both say the baby is yours, huh?'

24.text: 'Aight, BRING ME A SWORD.'

25.text: He told his men, 'Cut the baby in half and give each woman a piece.'

26.text: The real mother panicked and cried out, 'NO! Give her the baby! Don't kill him!' But the other woman? 'Go ahead, cut him in half—neither of us will have him then.'

27.text: Solomon was like, 'Aight, give the baby to the first woman. SHE the real mama.'

28.text: Word got out FAST. Everybody in Israel heard about the king's decision. They were shook 'cause they saw that God gave Solomon next-level wisdom to bring real justice.

1.text: Solomon was runnin' the whole kingdom of Israel. Dude was in charge of everything.

2.text: Here's his top officials: Azariah, son of Zadok, was the priest.

3.text: Elihoreph & Ahijah (Shisha's sons) were the scribes, and Jehoshaphat (Ahilud's son) was the royal historian.

4.text: Benaiah (Jehoiada's son) was over the army. Zadok & Abiathar were the priests.

5.text: Azariah (Nathan's son) was in charge of the governors. Zabud (Nathan's son) was a priest & Solomon's right-hand man.

6.text: Ahishar ran the palace. Adoniram (Abda's son) handled the labor force.

7.text: Solomon had 12 governors across Israel. Each was responsible for supplying food for the king's household one month a year.

8.text: Ben-Hur was over the mountains of Ephraim.

9.text: Ben-Deker ran Makaz, Shaalbim, Beth Shemesh, and Elon Beth Hanan.

10.text: Ben-Hesed was in charge of Arubboth, Sochoh, and all of Hepher.

11.text: Ben-Abinadab controlled the regions of Dor. (He was also married to Solomon's daughter, Taphath.)

12.text: Baana (Ahilud's son) ruled Taanach, Megiddo, and Beth Shean, plus everything near Jezreel.

13.text: Ben-Geber ran Ramoth-Gilead. He controlled 60 walled cities with bronze gates in Bashan.

14.text: Ahinadab (Iddo's son) managed Mahanaim.

15.text: Ahimaaz had Naphtali. (He married Solomon's daughter, Basemath.)

16.text: Baanah (Hushai's son) was over Asher and Aloth.

17.text: Jehoshaphat (Paruah's son) managed Issachar.

18.text: Shimei (Elah's son) handled Benjamin.

19.text: Geber (Uri's son) ran Gilead—covering what used to be the lands of King Sihon (Amorites) & King Og (Bashan). (He was the only governor in that region.)

20.text: Judah & Israel was THRIVIN'—as many people as the sand on the shore. Everybody eatin', drinkin', and livin' good.

21.text: Solomon ruled over everything from the Euphrates to Egypt. All the nations in his territory paid tribute and stayed loyal.

22.text: Dude's daily grocery list? 30 kors of fine flour, 60 kors of meal, 10 fat oxen, 20 pasture oxen, and 100 sheep, plus deer, gazelles, roebucks, and fattened birds.

23.text: Every single day, Solomon's kitchen was STACKED—he had 10 fattened oxen, 20 pasture-fed oxen, 100 sheep, plus deer, gazelles, roebucks, and specially fattened birds.

24.text: He ruled everything from Tiphsah to Gaza. All the kings under him stayed in check, and there was peace all around.

25.text: Judah & Israel lived safely, from Dan to Beersheba. Everybody chillin' under their own fig tree & vine—no worries, no drama.

26.text: Solomon had 40,000 stalls for his chariot horses & 12,000 horsemen.

27.text: Each governor made sure Solomon's table was fully stocked during their month—never ran out of anything.

28.text: They also made sure the horses had what they needed—barley & straw, delivered right on time.

29.text: God gave Solomon crazy wisdom, deep understanding, and a big heart—like the sand on the shore.

30.text: He was smarter than ALL the wise men of the East & Egypt.

31.text: He outshined Ethan the Ezrahite, Heman, Chalcol, and Darda. His reputation spread EVERYWHERE.

32.text: Dude wrote 3,000 proverbs & 1,005 songs. (Yeah, he had bars. 🎤🔥)

33.text: He knew about everything—trees, plants, animals, birds, reptiles, and fish.

34.text: People from ALL nations came to hear him speak—kings sent folks just to soak up his knowledge.

1.text: When Hiram, king of Tyre, heard Solomon got anointed as king after David, he sent his people to congratulate him. Hiram had always rocked with David.

2.text: Solomon sent a message back to Hiram, sayin':

3.text: You already know my father David wanted to build a house for the Lord. But he couldn't—he was too busy fightin' wars on all sides.

4.text: But now, God gave me peace all around. No enemies, no drama—just straight-up rest.

5.text: So now, I'm about to build that house for the Lord, just like He told my father. He said, 'Your son will be the one to build it.' So I'ma make it happen.

6.text: I need you to send me cedar trees from Lebanon. My workers will team up with yours, and I'll pay whatever you ask. 'Cause ain't nobody cut timber like the Sidonians.

7.text: When Hiram heard Solomon's message, he was hype. He said, 'Blessed be the Lord for giving David a wise son to rule over this great people!'

8.text: Hiram sent back a message: 'Bet. I got your request, and I'ma hook you up with all the cedar & cypress logs you need.'

9.text: My workers will cut the wood, send it down to the sea, and float it as rafts to wherever you want. Then you can take it from there. All I ask in return? Feed my people. Give us food for my household, and we're good.

10.text: So Hiram sent Solomon all the cedar & cypress he asked for.

11.text: In exchange, Solomon sent Hiram 20,000 kors of wheat & 20 kors of pressed oil every year. They had a whole food-for-wood trade deal.

12.text: God kept His promise to Solomon, givin' him wisdom. There was peace between Hiram & Solomon, and they made a treaty together.

13.text: Solomon raised a labor force from all Israel—30,000 workers.

14.text: He sent them in shifts: 10,000 at a time—one month workin' in Lebanon, two months back home. Adoniram was in charge of them.

15.text: Besides that, he had 70,000 carriers (the ones haulin' materials) and 80,000 stonecutters (quarrying stone in the mountains).

16.text: And over all of them, there were 3,300 supervisors makin' sure the work got done right.

17.text: Solomon commanded them to cut out massive stones—high-quality, expensive stones—to lay the foundation of the Temple.

18.text: Solomon's builders, Hiram's builders, and the Gebalites all worked together, gettin' the timber and stones ready.

1.text: 480 years after Israel left Egypt, in the fourth year of Solomon's reign, he started buildin' the Lord's temple. It was the month of Ziv (second month of the year).

2.text: The temple measurements? 60 cubits long, 20 cubits wide, 30 cubits high.

3.text: The front porch was 20 cubits wide (same as the temple) and stuck out 10 cubits.

4.text: Solomon had special windows built with slanted frames.

5.text: Solomon built side rooms all around the outside walls of the temple—surroundin' both the main hall & inner sanctuary.

6.text: The lower rooms were 5 cubits wide, the middle rooms 6 cubits, and the top rooms 7 cubits. He made it so the beams didn't have to be drilled into the temple walls.

7.text: Everything was built from pre-cut stone—so no hammers, chisels, or iron tools were heard inside while it was bein' built.

8.text: The entrance to the middle floor was on the right side of the temple. They used stairs to go up to the second and third floors.

9.text: Solomon built the main temple structure and finished it. He put cedar beams and boards for the roof.

10.text: The side chambers were 5 cubits high and attached to the temple with cedar beams.

11.text: Then God spoke to Solomon, sayin':

12.text: About this temple you buildin'—if you follow My laws, keep My commands, and walk in My ways, I'ma keep My promise to your father David.

13.text: I'ma stay with My people Israel. I won't abandon them.

14.text: So Solomon kept buildin' the temple until it was done.

15.text: Inside, he lined the walls with cedar panels from floor to ceiling. He covered the floors with cypress planks.

16.text: The Most Holy Place (inner sanctuary) was 20 cubits deep, covered completely with cedar boards from floor to ceiling.

17.text: The main sanctuary was 40 cubits long.

18.text: Inside the temple was all cedar—carved with flower buds & blossoms. No stone was visible.

19.text: Inside the temple, he set up the Most Holy Place to hold the Ark of the Covenant.

20.text: The inner sanctuary was a perfect cube—20 cubits wide, long, and high. He covered it in pure gold and built an altar of cedar.

21.text: The whole inside of the temple was overlaid with pure gold.

22.text: He didn't miss a spot—everything in the inner sanctuary was covered in gold, including the entire altar.

23.text: Inside the Most Holy Place, Solomon made two massive cherubim out of olive wood—each one was 10 cubits high.

24.text: Each cherub had two wings—5 cubits long on each side, making them 10 cubits from wingtip to wingtip.

25.text: Both cherubim were identical in size and shape—each one was 10 cubits tall.

26.text: Their wings stretched out—one wing touched one wall, the other wing touched the other wall, and their wings met in the middle.

27.text: He placed the cherubim inside the inner room, stretchin' their wings out wide. One wing touched one wall, the other cherub's wing touched the opposite wall, and in the middle, their wings touched each other.

28.text: And of course, he covered them in gold.

29.text: Solomon carved cherubim, palm trees, and flowers all over the temple walls—inside and out.

30.text: Even the floors were covered in gold—everywhere.

31.text: The inner sanctuary had olive wood doors, set into a five-sided doorframe.

32.text: The two doors were carved with cherubim, palm trees, and flowers. Then they were covered in gold.

33.text: The entrance to the main sanctuary had another set of olive wood doorposts.

34.text: The doors were made of cypress—each one had two folding panels.

35.text: Solomon had cherubim, palm trees, and flowers carved into them too—then covered in gold evenly.

36.text: The inner courtyard was built with three rows of cut stone and a row of cedar beams.

37.text: In the fourth year of Solomon's reign, during the month of Ziv, they laid the foundation of the Lord's temple.

38.text: In the eleventh year, during the month of Bul (eighth month), the temple was finally finished—7 years later, exactly how Solomon planned it.

1.text: Took Solomon 13 years to finish buildin' his palace—yeah, longer than the Temple. But when he was done, it was a masterpiece.

2.text: He built the House of the Forest of Lebanon, 100 cubits long, 50 wide, 30 high. It had four rows of cedar pillars and cedar beams across them.

3.text: The roof? Straight-up cedar planks on top of 45 beams, arranged in three rows of 15.

4.text: The windows were in three rows, set directly across from each other.

5.text: All the doorways and posts were squared off, with windows facing each other in three tiers.

6.text: He also built the Hall of Pillars, 50 cubits long, 30 wide—had a front porch with pillars and a canopy.

7.text: Then came the Hall of Judgment—that's where Solomon handled business. He lined it floor to ceiling with cedar.

8.text: His personal house had a courtyard just like this. He even built a special house for Pharaoh's daughter (his wife), styled the same way.

9.text: Every part of these buildings? Made with top-tier stone, cut and polished inside & out—from the foundation all the way to the roof.

10.text: The foundation stones were HUGE—some 10 cubits, some 8 cubits.

11.text: Above that? More perfectly cut stone and cedar wood.

12.text: The great courtyard was surrounded by three rows of cut stone and a row of cedar beams—just like the inner court of the Temple.

13.text: Solomon called up Hiram from Tyre, a top-tier metalworker.

14.text: Dude's mama was from Naphtali, his dad was a skilled bronze worker from Tyre. Hiram was gifted—full of wisdom & skill for working with bronze.

15.text: First, he cast two massive bronze pillars, each 18 cubits tall and 12 cubits around.

16.text: He made two bronze capitals (decorative tops) for the pillars, each 5 cubits high.

17.text: He designed them with seven rows of chainwork for decoration.

18.text: He also put two rows of pomegranates around the capitals—same design for both.

19.text: The capitals were shaped like lilies, 4 cubits tall.

20.text: Each capital had 200 pomegranates arranged in rows all the way around.

21.text: When he set them up at the Temple entrance: The right pillar was named Jachin (meaning 'He establishes') The left pillar was called Boaz (meaning 'In Him is strength')

22.text: The tops were shaped like lilies—and just like that, the pillars were done.

23.text: Hiram made a huge bronze basin called 'The Sea'—10 cubits across, 5 cubits high, 30 cubits around.

24.text: It was decorated with ornamental buds all around—10 per cubit, cast as part of the basin.

25.text: It stood on 12 bronze oxen: 3 facing north, 3 facing west, 3 facing south, 3 facing east. The basin rested on their backs, facing outward.

26.text: It was as thick as a handbreadth and had a rim shaped like a cup or lily blossom. It held 2,000 baths of water.

27.text: Hiram made 10 bronze carts (movable wash basins), each 4 cubits long & wide, 3 cubits high.

28.text: Each cart had decorative panels between the frames.

29.text: On the panels, he carved lions, oxen, & cherubim—with braided wreaths underneath.

30.text: Each cart had four bronze wheels with bronze axles, and decorative supports at each corner.

31.text: The top was shaped like a pedestal, 1 cubit across, with engraved decorations. The side panels were square, not round.

32.text: Under the panels were 4 large wheels, with axles attached to the cart. The wheels were 1.5 cubits high.

33.text: These wheels were crafted like chariot wheels, with bronze spokes, rims, and hubs.

34.text: Each cart had four corner supports, made as part of the cart itself.

35.text: At the very top of the cart was a perfectly round piece (half a cubit high), and more decorative flanges & panels.

36.text: He engraved cherubim, lions, & palm trees all over it, adding decorative wreaths.

37.text: All 10 carts were made exactly the same—same design, size, and shape.

38.text: Then he made 10 bronze lavers (basins), each holding 40 baths of water and measuring 4 cubits across.

39.text: He placed 5 carts on the right side of the Temple, 5 on the left. The giant Bronze Sea was set on the right side, near the southeast corner.

40.text: Hiram also made the lavers, shovels, and bowls for the Temple. He finished all the work Solomon hired him for.

41.text: This included: 2 giant bronze pillars, 2 bowl-shaped capitals for the pillars, 2 decorative networks covering the capitals, 400 bronze pomegranates (200 on each network)

42.text: 400 bronze pomegranates (200 on each network)

43.text: Plus: 10 carts & 10 lavers

44.text: 1 giant Bronze Sea & 12 oxen under it

45.text: He also made bronze pots, shovels, and bowls.

46.text: All this bronze work was cast in clay molds near the Jordan River, between Succoth & Zaretan.

47.text: Solomon didn't even bother weighin' all the bronze—there was too much to count!

48.text: Solomon had all the final Temple pieces made: Gold altar, Gold table for showbread

49.text: 10 pure gold lampstands (5 on each side), plus the gold flowers, lamps, and wick trimmers.

50.text: Everything in the Temple was pure gold—basins, trimmers, bowls, ladles, censers, and even the door hinges!

51.text: Finally, Solomon brought in all the gold, silver, & sacred items David had dedicated and stored them in the Temple treasuries. The work was done.

1.text: Solomon gathered all the elders, tribal leaders, and heads of Israel in Jerusalem. It was time to bring the Ark of the Covenant from the City of David (Zion) to the new temple.

2.text: All the people of Israel pulled up for the Feast of Ethanim (seventh month) to witness this big moment.

3.text: The elders arrived, and the priests carried the Ark.

4.text: They brought up the Ark of the Lord, the Tabernacle, and all the sacred furnishings. The priests and Levites handled it all.

5.text: King Solomon and the entire congregation went all out—they sacrificed so many sheep and oxen that nobody could even keep count.

6.text: The priests brought the Ark into the Most Holy Place, placing it under the wings of the cherubim.

7.text: The cherubim had their wings stretched out, covering the Ark and its poles.

8.text: The poles extended out so you could see their ends from the Holy Place (but not from outside). And they're still there today.

9.text: Inside the Ark? Just the two stone tablets Moses put there at Horeb when the Lord made a covenant with Israel after leading them out of Egypt.

10.text: As soon as the priests left the Holy Place, a cloud filled the Lord's house.

11.text: The cloud was so thick, the priests couldn't even keep ministering—God's presence took over!

12.text: Then Solomon said: 'The Lord said He'd dwell in a dark cloud.'

13.text: I've built You a majestic house—a place for You to stay forever.

14.text: Then he turned around, blessed the crowd, and everyone stood up.

15.text: Solomon spoke: 'Blessed be the Lord God of Israel, who spoke to my father David and now made it happen with His own hands.'

16.text: Since I brought My people out of Egypt, I never picked a city for My temple—but I chose David to lead Israel.

17.text: David wanted to build a temple for God.

18.text: But God told him: 'It's good that you want this, but you won't build it—your son will.'

19.text: That's why I'm here—God kept His word. Now I sit on David's throne, and I built this temple in the Lord's name.

20.text: I made a place for the Ark, where God's covenant with Israel is kept.

21.text: Solomon stood in front of God's altar, spread his hands to heaven, and prayed:

22.text: Lord, there ain't nobody like You! No God in heaven or earth who keeps promises like You!

23.text: You kept Your promise to David, my father. You said it, and You did it.

24.text: Now, God of Israel, keep Your next promise: 'David's sons will sit on the throne, as long as they walk in My ways.'

25.text: Lord, please let this promise be fulfilled!

26.text: But for real… will You actually live on earth? Even the highest heavens can't hold You, let alone this temple!

27.text: Still, please hear my prayer, Lord. Listen when I cry out today.

28.text: Let Your eyes always be on this temple, the place where You said, 'My name will be here.'

29.text: When Your people pray toward this temple, please hear them from heaven and forgive them.

30.text: If someone sins and comes here to swear an oath, judge between the guilty and the innocent.

31.text: When Israel loses a battle because of sin, but then they turn back, confess, and pray at this temple, hear them and restore them.

32.text: Then, Lord, up in heaven, hear their case and make the call—punish the guilty for what they did, and clear the righteous, blessin' them for doin' right.

33.text: If Your people Israel take an L in battle 'cause they messed up and sinned against You, but then realize they was wrong, turn back to You, call on Your name, and pray at this temple,

34.text: Lord, when You hear from heaven, forgive Your people's sins and bring them back to their land—the land You promised their ancestors.

35.text: If the sky dries up and there's no rain 'cause we messed up, and we turn back to You, pray, and confess Your name,

36.text: Then Lord, hear from heaven, forgive us, and show us the right way to live. Send rain on the land You gave us!

37.text: If there's a famine, disease, locusts, mildew, or an enemy attack, or any kind of disaster—whatever the crisis may be,

38.text: If anyone in Israel recognizes their struggle and prays toward this temple,

39.text: Lord, hear from heaven and forgive. Answer according to each person's heart, 'cause You alone know what's inside all of us.

40.text: So that Your people will always fear You and follow You while they live in this land You gave us.

41.text: And Lord, when foreigners come here to pray—people who ain't even from Israel,

42.text: Because they heard about Your great name, power, and mighty hand,

43.text: Hear them from heaven and answer their prayers too!

44.text: Let all the nations know who You are and that this temple carries Your name.

45.text: When Israel goes to fight their enemies, wherever You send them, and they pray toward this city and temple,

46.text: Lord, hear them and make sure they win.

47.text: If they sin against You (and let's be real, nobody's perfect), and You let them get captured by their enemies,

48.text: But they come to their senses while in exile and pray to You, saying, 'We messed up, Lord—we did wrong,'

49.text: If they return to You with all their heart and pray toward their homeland and temple,

50.text: Lord, hear them, forgive them, and give them favor with their captors. Let them have mercy on them.

51.text: 'Cause these folks? They belong to You. You brought them out of Egypt, out of the fire, out of slavery.

52.text: Lord, keep Your eyes and ears open to the prayers of Your servant and Your people.

53.text: You made us Your special people, set apart from everyone else—just like You told Moses when You freed us from Egypt.
