54.text: When Solomon finished this whole prayer and plea, he got up from kneeling before the altar, hands still lifted to heaven.

55.text: He turned and blessed the whole crowd with a loud voice:

56.text: 'Bless the Lord! He gave rest to His people, just like He promised. Not one word of His promise has failed!'

57.text: 'May the Lord be with us like He was with our ancestors—may He never leave or abandon us.

58.text: May He turn our hearts toward Him, so we can walk in His ways and keep His commandments.'

59.text: 'And may this prayer stay close to God's heart day and night, so He always watches over us.

60.text: 'That way, the whole world will know that the Lord is the one and only God!'

61.text: 'So y'all—stay loyal to God. Walk in His ways, keep His commandments, just like you're doing now.'

62.text: Then Solomon and all of Israel made huge sacrifices before the Lord.

63.text: Solomon offered 22,000 bulls and 120,000 sheep—that's how they dedicated the Temple!

64.text: That same day, Solomon consecrated the middle court in front of the temple. They used it to offer burnt sacrifices, grain offerings, and peace offerings—because the bronze altar wasn't big enough!

65.text: They held a massive feast for 14 days straight—all of Israel, from Hamath to the Brook of Egypt, turned up in worship before the Lord!

66.text: On the eighth day, Solomon sent everybody home. The people left joyful and full of gratitude for everything the Lord had done for David and for Israel!

1.text: When Solomon finished buildin' the Lord's temple, his own palace, and everything else he wanted to do,

2.text: The Lord appeared to him again, just like He did back at Gibeon.

3.text: God said, 'I heard your prayer, Solomon. I've made this house holy, put My name here forever—My eyes and My heart gon' be on it always.'

4.text: 'But listen—if you walk before Me like your daddy David did, with integrity and righteousness, keeping My commandments,

5.text: Then I'll keep My promise. Your kingdom will stay in your family forever.'

6.text: 'But if you or your kids turn away from Me, start chasing other gods, worshiping idols,

7.text: I'm kicking y'all out the land I gave you, and this temple I made holy? I'll throw it away like it's nothing. Israel will be a joke among the nations.

8.text: People gon' pass by and say, "Dang, what happened? Why did God do them like this?"

9.text: And folks will answer, "'Cause they turned their backs on the Lord, started messin' with other gods, and forgot the One who brought them out of Egypt."'

10.text: After 20 years of Solomon building the Lord's temple and his palace,

11.text: King Hiram of Tyre (who hooked Solomon up with all that cedar, cypress, and gold) got a gift back—20 cities in Galilee.

12.text: Hiram went to check out his new cities… and he wasn't feelin' 'em.

13.text: He said, 'Bruh, what kinda cities are these? This the best you got, my brother?' He called them Cabul (which basically means 'good for nothing').

14.text: Still, Hiram sent Solomon 120 talents of gold (that's a lot of money).

15.text: Solomon put together a whole workforce to build the Lord's temple, his own palace, the Millo, the wall of Jerusalem, and the cities of Hazor, Megiddo, and Gezer.

16.text: Pharaoh (Solomon's father-in-law) had already conquered Gezer, wiped out the Canaanites there, and gave it as a dowry when Solomon married his daughter.

17.text: So Solomon rebuilt Gezer, along with Lower Beth Horon, Baalath, and Tadmor in Judah.

18.text: He also built storage cities, chariot cities, cavalry cities, and whatever else he wanted in Jerusalem, Lebanon, and his whole kingdom.

19.text: All the cities Solomon had for storage, plus his chariot cities and cavalry cities, and whatever else he felt like buildin'—whether in Jerusalem, Lebanon, or anywhere else in his kingdom.

20.text: Now, about the folks left in the land—the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites—the Israelites hadn't wiped 'em all out.

21.text: So Solomon put them to work as forced labor, and that's how it stayed.

22.text: But he didn't make Israelites slaves. They were his warriors, officers, commanders, and leaders.

23.text: His top officials? 550 men in charge of all the work projects.

24.text: Meanwhile, Pharaoh's daughter moved out of the City of David into her new palace Solomon built for her. Then Solomon finished up work on the Millo.

25.text: Three times a year, Solomon offered sacrifices and burnt offerings on the altar he built for the Lord. He also burned incense. The temple was fully up and running.

26.text: Solomon built a whole fleet of ships at Ezion Geber, near Elath on the Red Sea coast (Edom).

27.text: King Hiram sent his best sailors to work with Solomon's crew—'cause these men knew the sea.

28.text: They sailed to Ophir (a place known for mad wealth) and brought back 420 talents of gold to Solomon.

1.text: When the Queen of Sheba heard about Solomon's fame and wisdom, all tied to the Lord's name, she had to see for herself. So she pulled up to Jerusalem with a whole squad—camels packed with spices, gold, and precious stones—ready to test Solomon with hard questions.

2.text: She came through, sat with Solomon, and asked everything on her mind.

3.text: Solomon had all the answers—there wasn't nothin' too deep or too hard for him to explain.

4.text: When she saw Solomon's wisdom, his palace, the food on his table, how his servants moved, their drip, and even his cupbearers, she was speechless.

5.text: And when she saw how he went up to the Lord's house, she knew she was witnessing something different.

6.text: She told Solomon, "Man, I heard about you in my country, but I ain't believe it till now."

7.text: "They ain't even tell me the half! You way wiser and richer than the stories I heard."

8.text: "Your people are lucky. Your servants are blessed, 'cause they get to be around you and hear your wisdom every day."

9.text: "Blessed be the Lord your God! He was real happy to put you on this throne. 'Cause He loves Israel so much, He made you king to lead with justice and righteousness."

10.text: Then she gave Solomon 120 talents of gold, more spices than anyone had ever brought before, and precious stones.

11.text: Even Hiram's ships brought gold from Ophir, along with a huge shipment of almug wood and more precious stones.

12.text: With that almug wood, Solomon made steps for the temple and his palace, plus harps and stringed instruments for musicians. Nobody had ever seen that much almug wood before.

13.text: King Solomon gave the Queen of Sheba everything she asked for, plus gifts from his royal stash. After that, she and her whole crew went back home.

14.text: Every year, Solomon racked up 666 talents of gold.

15.text: That's not even counting what he got from traders, merchants, Arabian kings, and regional governors.

16.text: Solomon had 200 large shields made outta hammered gold, each one using 600 shekels of gold.

17.text: He also made 300 smaller shields, each one using three minas of gold. He kept them in the House of the Forest of Lebanon.

18.text: Then he built a huge ivory throne and covered it in pure gold.

19.text: The throne had six steps, a rounded back, armrests on both sides, and two lions standing beside the armrests.

20.text: Twelve lions stood on the steps, one on each side. No other kingdom had a throne like that.

21.text: Everything Solomon drank from was gold. Silver? That wasn't even considered valuable in Solomon's time.

22.text: He had merchant ships sailing with Hiram's fleet, bringing in gold, silver, ivory, apes, and monkeys every three years.

23.text: Solomon was richer and wiser than all the kings on earth.

24.text: Everybody wanted to hear his wisdom, since God had blessed him with so much knowledge.

25.text: So every year, people came through bringing silver, gold, robes, armor, spices, horses, and mules—a steady flow of gifts.

26.text: Solomon stacked up chariots and horsemen—1,400 chariots and 12,000 horsemen—stationed in chariot cities and in Jerusalem.

27.text: Silver was everywhere in Jerusalem, as common as stones. Cedar wood was as plentiful as sycamore trees in the lowlands.

28.text: Solomon had horses imported from Egypt and Keveh. His merchants bought them at the going rate.

29.text: A chariot from Egypt cost 600 shekels of silver, and a horse cost 150 shekels. They also exported them to the Hittite and Syrian kings.

1.text: King Solomon had a thing for foreign women—Moabites, Ammonites, Edomites, Sidonians, Hittites, and even Pharaoh's daughter.

2.text: These were the very nations God told Israel not to mix with, sayin', 'They gon' turn y'all hearts away from Me.' But Solomon? He ain't listen—he was in love.

3.text: Bruh had 700 wives (all princesses) and 300 side chicks—and they pulled his heart away from the Lord.

4.text: When Solomon got old, his wives had him worshiping other gods instead of staying loyal to the Lord like his father David.

5.text: Solomon started messin' with Ashtoreth, the Sidonian goddess, and Milcom, the nasty god of the Ammonites.

6.text: Solomon was out here doin' wrong in God's sight. He wasn't ridin' for the Lord like his pops David did.

7.text: He straight up built altars for Chemosh (the Moabite idol) and Molech (the terrible god of the Ammonites)—right outside Jerusalem!

8.text: Not just that—he did the same for all his wives so they could burn incense and sacrifice to their gods.

9.text: The Lord was big mad at Solomon, 'cause Solomon turned his heart away—even after God had appeared to him twice!

10.text: God straight up told Solomon not to chase after other gods, but he did it anyway.

11.text: So the Lord said, 'Since you broke My commands and ain't listen, I'ma snatch the kingdom from you and hand it to one of your own servants.'

12.text: But outta respect for David, I won't do it while you alive—I'ma take it from your son.

13.text: Even then, I won't take everything—your son will keep one tribe for David's sake, and for Jerusalem, My chosen city.

14.text: God raised up an enemy against Solomon—Hadad the Edomite, a royal descendant from Edom.

15.text: Back when David was wipin' out Edom, Joab (David's army commander) had killed every male in the land.

16.text: Joab stayed there six months straight, makin' sure no males were left in Edom.

17.text: Hadad, just a young boy at the time, dipped to Egypt with some of his father's servants.

18.text: They traveled through Midian and Paran, then took some men with 'em and went to Pharaoh, king of Egypt.

19.text: Hadad became tight with Pharaoh, so much so that Pharaoh gave him his wife's sister (Queen Tahpenes' sister) as his wife.

20.text: They had a son, Genubath, who was raised right in Pharaoh's palace alongside the royal kids.

21.text: But when Hadad heard David and Joab were dead, he told Pharaoh, 'Let me go back home.'

22.text: Pharaoh was like, 'Why? Ain't you got everything you need here?' But Hadad was set—he just wanted to go.

23.text: Then God raised up another enemy—Rezon, son of Eliadah. This dude had fled from his king, Hadadezer of Zobah.

24.text: Rezon gathered men and became a gang leader after David had defeated Zobah.

25.text: He went and took over Damascus, set up shop, and stayed beefin' with Israel all Solomon's days.

26.text: Then came Jeroboam, Solomon's servant—a strong dude from the tribe of Ephraim. His mama was a widow named Zeruah.

27.text: This is how he started rebelling: Solomon was rebuilding the Millo and fixing the City of David.

28.text: Jeroboam was a natural leader—Solomon saw his work ethic and put him in charge of the whole labor force from the tribe of Joseph.

29.text: One day, Jeroboam was leavin' Jerusalem when Ahijah the prophet from Shiloh met him in a field.

30.text: Ahijah had a new cloak on—he straight up tore it into twelve pieces.

31.text: Then he told Jeroboam, 'Take ten pieces—'cause the Lord says, "I'ma snatch ten tribes from Solomon's kingdom and give 'em to you."

32.text: Solomon's son will keep one tribe 'cause of David and Jerusalem, My chosen city.

33.text: All this happening 'cause Solomon and the people turned away from Me, worshiping Ashtoreth, Chemosh, and Milcom, instead of following My ways.

34.text: But I ain't gon' take everything from Solomon—I'ma let him rule all his life outta respect for David, My servant.

35.text: But after him, I'ma take the kingdom from his son and give you ten tribes.

36.text: His son will keep one tribe so that David's family always has a presence in Jerusalem.

37.text: Jeroboam, I'ma make you king over whatever your heart desires.

38.text: If you follow My ways, keep My commands like David did, I'ma be with you and build you a lasting kingdom like I did for David.

39.text: I'ma humble David's descendants for this, but not forever.'

40.text: Solomon caught wind of Jeroboam's rebellion and tried to kill him. But Jeroboam ran to Egypt and stayed there until Solomon died.

41.text: The rest of Solomon's story, all his accomplishments and wisdom? They written in the Book of the Acts of Solomon.

42.text: He reigned in Jerusalem for forty years over all Israel.

43.text: Then Solomon died, was buried in the City of David, and his son Rehoboam took the throne.

1.text: Rehoboam rolled up to Shechem, 'cause all Israel was gatherin' there to crown him king.

2.text: Meanwhile, Jeroboam (who was still in Egypt 'cause he ran from Solomon) heard about all this.

3.text: The people sent for Jeroboam. When he got there, him and the whole assembly of Israel came to Rehoboam with a request.

4.text: They said, 'Look, your daddy worked us to the bone. If you ease up on these harsh labor laws, we'll gladly serve you.'

5.text: Rehoboam was like, 'Give me three days to think about it.' So the people bounced.

6.text: First, Rehoboam asked the old heads (Solomon's advisors) what he should do.

7.text: They told him, 'If you ease up and treat them right, they'll be loyal forever.'

8.text: But Rehoboam wasn't feelin' that. Instead, he asked his homeboys—the ones he grew up with.

9.text: He said, 'What y'all think? How should I handle these folks tellin' me to go easy on 'em?'

10.text: His boys hyped him up: 'Man, tell 'em, "If you thought my dad was tough, you ain't seen nothin' yet!"'

11.text: 'My pops used whips, but I'ma hit y'all with scorpions!'

12.text: Three days later, Jeroboam and all the people came back, just like the king told them.

13.text: But Rehoboam ignored the elders' advice and went with the foolishness his boys told him.

14.text: He doubled down: 'My dad was strict? I'ma be stricter. He whipped y'all? I'ma hit harder.'

15.text: Rehoboam ain't realize—this was God's plan all along, just like He told Jeroboam through the prophet Ahijah.

16.text: When the people heard this, they were DONE. They snapped back: 'Man, forget David's family! We got no part in his house! Y'all from Judah? Handle your own business! We out!'

17.text: From that day, Rehoboam only ruled the tribe of Judah—Israel walked away from the dynasty of David.

18.text: Then Rehoboam sent Adoram, his tax collector, to calm things down. Big mistake. The people straight up stoned him to death.

19.text: Rehoboam barely made it out alive—he had to hop in his chariot and run back to Jerusalem.

20.text: Soon as they heard Jeroboam was back, the people made him king over all Israel. Only Judah stayed loyal to Rehoboam.

21.text: Rehoboam wasn't about to let that slide. He gathered 180,000 warriors from Judah and Benjamin to fight Israel and take the kingdom back.

22.text: But then, God sent a message to a prophet named Shemaiah.

23.text: God said, 'Go tell Rehoboam, king of Judah, and all these folks with him…'

24.text: 'STOP. Don't fight your own people. This split is My doing.'

25.text: And they actually listened—Rehoboam and his army went home.

26.text: Meanwhile, Jeroboam was lowkey nervous. He thought, 'Man, if the people keep goin' to Jerusalem to worship at the Lord's temple…'

27.text: 'They gon' start feelin' loyal to Rehoboam again—and they might even kill me to go back to him!'

28.text: So instead of trusting God, he came up with his own plan—he made two golden calves. Then he told the people: 'Y'all don't need to go all the way to Jerusalem! Look, here are your gods that brought y'all outta Egypt!'

29.text: He put one calf in Bethel and the other in Dan, so the people wouldn't go back to Judah to worship.

30.text: Big mistake—this turned into a huge sin 'cause now people were worshiping these fake gods all over the place.

31.text: Jeroboam even made random folks priests—not from the tribe of Levi, like God commanded.

32.text: Then he set up a fake holiday in the eighth month, kinda like the Feast of Tabernacles in Judah.

33.text: On that day, he personally offered sacrifices at Bethel to the golden calf. He made priests and burned incense at the altar.

1.text: One day, a man of God came from Judah to Bethel, just as Jeroboam was standing by the altar, burning incense.

2.text: The prophet shouted, 'Hey, altar! Listen up! The Lord says, a king named Josiah will be born in David's house. One day, he's gonna sacrifice all these fake priests y'all got burnin' incense on you, and human bones gon' be burned here!'

3.text: And to prove it, here's a sign: This altar gon' crack wide open, and the ashes will spill out!'

4.text: Jeroboam was HEATED. He pointed at the prophet and yelled, 'Somebody arrest this man!' But as soon as he stretched his hand out, it shriveled up!

5.text: Then BOOM—the altar split in two, just like the prophet said! Ashes went everywhere.

6.text: Jeroboam panicked. He begged the prophet, 'Please, pray to your God for me! Ask Him to heal my hand!'

7.text: So the prophet prayed, and Jeroboam's hand was healed instantly.

8.text: The king was shook. He told the prophet, 'Come eat with me—I'll hook you up with a reward.'

9.text: But the man of God said, 'Nah, even if you gave me half your palace, I wouldn't go with you. The Lord told me, don't eat, don't drink, and don't go back the way I came.'

10.text: So he left Bethel and took a different route home.

11.text: Meanwhile, an old prophet lived in Bethel. His sons came and told him everything that just went down.

12.text: He asked them, 'Which way did he go?' They told him the direction.

13.text: The old prophet said, 'Saddle my donkey.' So they did, and he took off after the man of God.

14.text: He caught up with him, chillin' under an oak tree. He asked, 'You the man of God from Judah?'

15.text: 'Yeah, that's me,' the prophet said.

16.text: The old man invited him, 'Come eat at my house.'

17.text: The prophet replied, 'Can't do it. The Lord said no food, no drink, and don't go back the same way.'

18.text: But the old man LIED. He said, 'I'm a prophet too, and an angel told me it's fine.'

19.text: So the man of God went with him and ate at his house.

20.text: While they were eatin', the Lord spoke through the old prophet and called the man of God out.

21.text: 'The Lord says, you disobeyed! You ate and drank in the place I told you NOT to!

22.text: So now, you won't even be buried in your family's tomb.'

23.text: After they finished eating, the old prophet saddled up the man of God's donkey.

24.text: But on his way home, a lion jumped out and killed him! His body lay on the road, with the lion and the donkey just standing there.

25.text: Some travelers saw the scene and ran back to town to spread the news.

26.text: The old prophet heard about it and said, 'Welp, that's the man of God. He disobeyed the Lord, and the lion took him out—just like God said.'

27.text: He told his sons, 'Saddle up my donkey.'

28.text: He found the prophet's body on the road. The donkey was still standing there. The lion hadn't eaten the body or killed the donkey.

29.text: He picked up the prophet's body, put it on his donkey, and brought it back home.

30.text: Then he buried him and mourned, saying, 'Man, my brother!'

31.text: Later, he told his sons, 'When I die, bury me next to him.'

32.text: 'Everything he said about the altar in Bethel and the high places WILL come true.'

33.text: Even after all that, Jeroboam STILL didn't turn from his evil ways.

34.text: He kept making random people priests, even though they weren't Levites. If you wanted to be a priest, he'd let you.

35.text: That one decision became his downfall and led to the destruction of his whole dynasty.

1.text: Around that time, Jeroboam's son Abijah got real sick.

2.text: Jeroboam told his wife, 'Look, I need you to go see the prophet Ahijah in Shiloh. But listen, don't let nobody know you my wife. He's the same prophet who told me I'd be king.

3.text: Take ten loaves of bread, some cakes, and honey, and go ask him what's gonna happen to our son.

4.text: So Jeroboam's wife put on a disguise and went to Ahijah's house. But the prophet was already blind from old age.

5.text: But God already told Ahijah, 'Jeroboam's wife is coming, pretending to be somebody else. Here's what you gon' tell her when she asks about her son.'

6.text: As soon as she walked in, Ahijah said, 'Come on in, Jeroboam's wife! Why you tryna pretend? I got bad news for you.

7.text: Go tell Jeroboam, 'The Lord says: I made you king, lifted you up from the people.'

8.text: I took the kingdom from David's family and gave it to you, but you ain't been nothing like David. He followed Me with all his heart, but you? You out here wildin'!

9.text: You did more evil than anybody before you! You made fake gods, idols, and straight up disrespected Me.

10.text: So guess what? Your whole house is getting wiped out. Every last male in Israel who's tied to you is done.

11.text: If they die in the city, dogs will eat 'em. If they die in the field, birds gon' pick 'em clean. The Lord said it, and it's done.'

12.text: Now, go home. Soon as you step foot in the city, your son is gonna die.

13.text: And all Israel will mourn for him, but he's the only one in your family who'll get a proper burial. He's the only one who had any good in him.

14.text: The Lord already picked a new king who's gonna wipe out your whole bloodline.

15.text: Israel gon' be shaken like a reed in the water. God's gon' kick them out of this land and scatter them beyond the river. Why? Because of all these fake gods they keep worshiping.

16.text: And all this is happening because you, Jeroboam, led them into sin.'

17.text: Jeroboam's wife went home to Tirzah, and as soon as she stepped over the threshold, the boy died.

18.text: All of Israel mourned and buried him, just like the prophet said.

19.text: The rest of Jeroboam's story—his wars, his reign—it's all written down in the royal records.

20.text: Jeroboam ruled for 22 years. Then he died, and his son Nadab took the throne.

21.text: Meanwhile, Solomon's son Rehoboam was king over Judah. He was 41 years old when he took the throne and ruled for 17 years in Jerusalem.

22.text: But Judah? They did evil in the Lord's sight. Way worse than their ancestors.

23.text: They built altars, sacred pillars, and idols on every high hill and under every green tree.

24.text: There were male cult prostitutes in the land, and Judah was out here doing the same nasty stuff as the nations God kicked out before them.

25.text: In Rehoboam's 5th year as king, Egypt's king Shishak attacked Jerusalem.

26.text: He raided the temple and the royal palace, taking all the treasures—including Solomon's gold shields!

27.text: So Rehoboam had to replace them with bronze shields. Every time he went to the temple, the guards had to carry them, then lock them back up.

28.text: Ain't no gold left. Just bronze.

29.text: The rest of Rehoboam's rule? It's all in the royal records.

30.text: There was constant beef between him and Jeroboam the whole time.

31.text: Then Rehoboam died, got buried in the City of David, and his son Abijam took over.

1.text: In the 18th year of King Jeroboam's reign, Abijam became king over Judah.

2.text: He ruled for three years in Jerusalem. His mama's name was Maachah, granddaughter of Abishalom.

3.text: But he wasn't loyal to God. Just like his daddy before him, he was out here wildin'.

4.text: But for David's sake, the Lord still kept Judah going and let Abijam's son take the throne after him.

5.text: See, David did right by God his whole life—except that one time with Uriah the Hittite.

6.text: And trust, the beef between Rehoboam and Jeroboam stayed strong all their days.

7.text: Everything else Abijam did? It's all in the royal records. And yeah, he stayed at war with Jeroboam too.

8.text: Then Abijam died, got buried in the City of David, and his son Asa took the throne.

9.text: In Jeroboam's 20th year as king, Asa became king over Judah.

10.text: He ruled for 41 years in Jerusalem. His grandma was Maachah, granddaughter of Abishalom.

11.text: But Asa was different—he did right in the eyes of the Lord, just like his ancestor David.

12.text: He kicked out the male shrine prostitutes and tore down all the idols his ancestors made.

13.text: Even his own grandma, Maachah, had to go! She had an obscene Asherah idol, so Asa snatched it down and burned it by the Brook Kidron.

14.text: Now, he didn't take down every high place, but Asa's heart stayed loyal to the Lord his whole life.

15.text: He also brought back the silver, gold, and sacred items into the house of the Lord.

16.text: Asa and Baasha, king of Israel, were at war the whole time.

17.text: Baasha set up shop in Ramah, blocking trade so nobody could come in or out of Judah.

18.text: So Asa took all the gold and silver left in the Lord's temple and his palace and sent it to Ben-Hadad, king of Syria.

19.text: He told Ben-Hadad, 'Yo, let's make a treaty like our daddies did. I'm sending you a little gift—now break your treaty with Baasha so he'll back off.'

20.text: Ben-Hadad was with it. He sent his army to attack Israel, hitting Ijon, Dan, Abel Beth Maachah, Chinneroth, and all of Naphtali.

21.text: When Baasha got the news, he stopped building Ramah and dipped back to Tirzah.

22.text: Then Asa told all of Judah, 'Go grab the stones and timber from Ramah!' And with those supplies, he built up Geba and Mizpah.

23.text: Everything else Asa did—his cities, his power—it's all in the royal records. But in his old age, his feet got messed up.

24.text: Then Asa died, got buried in the City of David, and his son Jehoshaphat took over.

25.text: Meanwhile, Jeroboam's son Nadab became king over Israel in Asa's 2nd year. He ruled for only 2 years.

26.text: But just like his daddy, he did evil in the Lord's sight and led Israel into sin.

27.text: Then Baasha, son of Ahijah, from the tribe of Issachar, plotted against him. He killed Nadab at Gibbethon, while Nadab was trying to siege the Philistines.

28.text: Baasha took him out in Asa's 3rd year and claimed the throne.

29.text: And just like God warned, Baasha wiped out Jeroboam's whole bloodline. Not one of his descendants survived.

30.text: This all happened because Jeroboam made Israel sin, provoking the Lord's anger.

31.text: Everything else Nadab did? It's in the royal records.

32.text: And yeah, the war between Asa and Baasha kept going strong.

33.text: In Asa's 3rd year, Baasha became king over Israel and ruled from Tirzah for 24 years.

34.text: But he wasn't any better. He did evil and followed in Jeroboam's footsteps, making Israel sin.

1.text: Then the word of the Lord came to Jehu son of Hanani, speaking against Baasha.

2.text: God said, 'I pulled you up out the dust and made you king over My people, but you went and did the same evil Jeroboam did. You led My people into sin and got Me mad.'

3.text: 'So now, I'm wiping out your whole family. You ain't gonna have no legacy—your house gonna be like Jeroboam's.

4.text: If you die in the city, dogs gonna eat you. If you die in the field, birds gonna eat you.

5.text: The rest of Baasha's life? His battles? His power? It's all in the royal records.

6.text: Baasha died, got buried in Tirzah, and his son Elah took over.

7.text: And the Lord made sure Baasha's house got wiped out because of all the evil he did. He provoked God just like Jeroboam.

8.text: In Asa's 26th year as king, Elah became king of Israel and ruled for two years in Tirzah.

9.text: But his own officer, Zimri, who was over half his chariots, plotted against him. Elah was getting wasted in his steward's house in Tirzah.

10.text: Zimri walked in, killed him, and took the throne in Asa's 27th year.

11.text: As soon as Zimri sat on the throne, he killed every last male in Baasha's house. No family, no friends—nobody survived.

12.text: And just like God said through Jehu, Baasha's house was wiped off the map.

13.text: All because Baasha and Elah led Israel into sin, making God furious with their idols.

14.text: Everything else Elah did? It's in the royal records.

15.text: In Asa's 27th year, Zimri ruled Israel for just seven days. Meanwhile, the army was out fighting the Philistines.

16.text: When the soldiers heard that Zimri killed the king, they made their commander, Omri, the new king.

17.text: Omri and the army marched to Tirzah, surrounded it, and prepared to attack.

18.text: When Zimri saw he was done for, he set the king's house on fire—while he was inside. He died in the flames.

19.text: This happened because Zimri followed Jeroboam's sins, making Israel turn against God.

20.text: Everything else Zimri did? It's in the royal records.

21.text: But Israel was divided—half wanted Tibni son of Ginath to be king, and half followed Omri.

22.text: Omri's side won the battle, Tibni died, and Omri ruled Israel.

23.text: In Asa's 31st year, Omri became king over Israel and ruled 12 years. Six of those years he ruled from Tirzah.

24.text: Then he bought a hill from a man named Shemer for two talents of silver. He built a new city there and named it Samaria.

25.text: Omri was even worse than all the kings before him.

26.text: He did exactly what Jeroboam did, leading Israel into sin and making God furious.

27.text: Everything else Omri did? It's in the royal records.

28.text: Then Omri died and was buried in Samaria, and his son Ahab took the throne.

29.text: In Asa's 38th year, Ahab son of Omri became king of Israel. He ruled for 22 years in Samaria.

30.text: Ahab was the most wicked king Israel ever had—even worse than those before him.

31.text: Like it wasn't already bad enough, he married Jezebel, daughter of Ethbaal, king of the Sidonians. Then he started worshipping Baal.

32.text: He built a temple for Baal in Samaria and set up an altar inside it.

33.text: He also made Asherah poles. Ahab did more to anger God than any king before him.

34.text: And in his time, Hiel of Bethel rebuilt Jericho, fulfilling the curse Joshua spoke. He laid its foundation with his firstborn Abiram and set up its gates with his youngest Segub.

1.text: Elijah the Tishbite, from Gilead, told Ahab, 'As sure as God lives, there ain't gonna be no dew or rain for years—unless I say so.'

2.text: Then the Lord spoke to Elijah,

3.text: 'You gotta get outta here. Head east and hide by the Brook Cherith, near the Jordan.'

4.text: 'Drink from the brook. And don't trip, I already told the ravens to bring you food.'

5.text: So Elijah listened to God. He went to the Brook Cherith and stayed there.

6.text: The ravens brought him bread and meat every morning and evening, and he drank from the brook.

7.text: But after a while, the brook dried up—since there was no rain.

8.text: Then the Lord told Elijah,

9.text: 'Get up and go to Zarephath in Sidon. A widow there will take care of you.'

10.text: Elijah arrived at the city gates and saw a widow gathering sticks. He asked her, 'Could you bring me some water?'

11.text: As she was going to get it, he called out again, 'And bring me a little bread too!'

12.text: She said, 'Sir, I barely got anything left. Just a handful of flour and a little oil. I was about to make a last meal for me and my son, then die.'

13.text: Elijah told her, 'Don't be scared. Just do what you said, but make me a small cake first. Then, you and your son can eat after.'

14.text: 'The Lord said your flour and oil ain't gonna run out until He sends rain again!'

15.text: So she did what Elijah said. She, Elijah, and her son had food for days.

16.text: Her flour never ran out, and her oil never dried up—just like God said through Elijah.

17.text: But later, her son got real sick. He got so bad, he stopped breathing.

18.text: The woman told Elijah, 'What you got against me, man of God? You came here just to remind me of my sins and let my son die?!'

19.text: Elijah said, 'Give me your son.' He took him upstairs, laid him on the bed.

20.text: Elijah cried out, 'Lord, really? You brought me here just to take this widow's son?!'

21.text: Then Elijah stretched out on the boy three times and prayed, 'Lord, let this child's soul come back!'

22.text: God heard Elijah, and the boy came back to life.

23.text: Elijah carried the boy downstairs, gave him back to his mother, and said, 'Look, your son is alive!'

24.text: The woman said, 'Now I know for sure you're a man of God, and everything you say from God is the truth!'

1.text: After a long time, God told Elijah, 'Go see Ahab—I'm bout to send rain again.'

2.text: So Elijah went to find Ahab. Meanwhile, Samaria was goin' through a serious famine.

3.text: Now Ahab had a servant named Obadiah, who was in charge of the palace. (And Obadiah feared the Lord big time.

4.text: While Jezebel was out here killing God's prophets, Obadiah hid 100 of them in caves—50 in each cave—and made sure they had bread and water.

5.text: Ahab told Obadiah, 'Go check all the springs and brooks. Maybe we can find enough grass to keep our horses and mules alive.'

6.text: So they split up—Ahab went one way, and Obadiah went another.

7.text: As Obadiah was out searchin', Elijah ran into him. Obadiah saw him and was like, 'Wait…is that really you, Elijah?!'

8.text: Elijah said, 'Yeah, it's me. Go tell Ahab I'm here.'

9.text: Obadiah was like, 'Man, what did I do wrong that you tryna get me killed?!'

10.text: 'Ahab been searchin' for you everywhere! Every kingdom, every nation—and made 'em swear they hadn't seen you.

11.text: And now you want me to just roll up to him and say, "Elijah's here"?!'

12.text: 'As soon as I leave, God gon' snatch you away somewhere. Then when Ahab don't find you, he gon' kill me!'

13.text: 'Ain't you heard what I did? I saved 100 of the Lord's prophets! Hid 'em in caves! Fed them bread and water!'

14.text: 'And now you tellin' me to tell Ahab, "Elijah's here"? He gon' kill me!'

15.text: Elijah said, 'Look, God is my witness—I'ma see Ahab TODAY.'

16.text: So Obadiah went to tell Ahab, and Ahab came out to meet Elijah.

17.text: When Ahab saw him, he said, 'Oh, look who it is—the man causing all this trouble in Israel!'

18.text: Elijah shot back, 'Nah, that's YOU & YOUR FAMILY! Y'all the ones turned away from God and started worshiping Baal!

19.text: 'So here's what you do—bring ALL Israel to meet me on Mount Carmel. And bring 450 prophets of Baal & 400 prophets of Asherah—you know, the ones Jezebel feeds at her table.'

20.text: So Ahab sent word, and all of Israel and the false prophets came to Mount Carmel.

21.text: Elijah stepped up and said, 'How long y'all gon' be stuck between two choices? If the Lord is God, follow Him. If Baal is God, follow him.'

22.text: Elijah said, 'Look, I'm the last prophet left of the Lord. But Baal got 450 prophets.

23.text: 'So let's do this—bring two bulls. Let them choose one, cut it up, put it on wood—but don't set no fire. I'ma do the same thing.

24.text: 'Then y'all call on Baal, and I'ma call on the Lord. The God who sends fire—THAT'S the real God.'

25.text: Elijah told Baal's prophets, 'Y'all go first—there's a lot of y'all. Call on Baal, but don't set no fire.'

26.text: So they called on Baal from morning 'til noon. 'O Baal, hear us!' But no answer. They started jumping around the altar.

27.text: Around noon, Elijah started clownin' them. 'Maybe he's busy? Maybe he's sleep? Maybe he on vacation? Y'all better yell louder!'

28.text: So they started shouting & cutting themselves with knives, like they usually did. Blood was everywhere.

29.text: They kept this up until evening. But still no voice, no answer—nothing.

30.text: Then Elijah said, 'Y'all come over here.' So the people came near, and he rebuilt the Lord's altar that had been torn down.

31.text: He took 12 stones (one for each tribe of Israel).

32.text: With those stones, he built an altar for the Lord, dug a trench around it.

33.text: He put wood down, cut up the bull, laid it out. Then he said, 'Fill four big jugs of water & pour it all over the sacrifice.'

34.text: Then he said, 'Do it again.' They did. Then he said, 'One more time.' And they poured water a third time.

35.text: The water ran everywhere—even filled the trench.

36.text: At evening time, Elijah prayed, 'Lord God of Abraham, Isaac, & Israel, show these people today that YOU are God!'

37.text: 'Let them see Your power & turn back to You!'

38.text: Then—BOOM! Fire fell from heaven—burned up the sacrifice, the wood, the stones, the dust, AND dried up all the water.

39.text: The people fell on their faces and cried out, 'The Lord is God! The Lord is God!'

40.text: Then Elijah said, 'Grab every prophet of Baal! Don't let a single one escape!' So they seized them, and Elijah executed them at the Brook Kishon.

41.text: Elijah told Ahab, 'Go eat & drink—rain is coming!'

42.text: Ahab went up to eat, but Elijah went to the top of Mount Carmel, bowed down, and prayed.

43.text: He told his servant, 'Go look toward the sea.' The servant came back: 'I don't see nothin'.'

44.text: Finally, the servant said, 'I see a tiny cloud, the size of a man's hand.'

45.text: The sky got dark with clouds, the wind picked up, and a heavy rain started pouring. Ahab rode off to Jezreel.

46.text: Then the Spirit of the Lord came upon Elijah, and he outran Ahab's chariot all the way to Jezreel!

1.text: Ahab went and told Jezebel everything Elijah had done—including how he had killed all the prophets of Baal.

2.text: Jezebel sent a message to Elijah: 'By this time tomorrow, I swear I'ma do you just like you did them prophets. If I don't, may the gods punish me even worse!'

3.text: Elijah saw that and was like, 'I gotta get outta here.' He ran for his life, went all the way to Beersheba in Judah, and left his servant there.

4.text: Then Elijah went even further into the wilderness, sat under a tree, and prayed, 'Lord, just take me now. I can't do this no more.'

5.text: He lay down and fell asleep under the tree. But then an angel tapped him and said, 'Get up and eat.'

6.text: Elijah woke up, looked around, and saw a cake baked on hot coals & a jar of water. So he ate, drank, and went back to sleep.

7.text: The angel came back, tapped him again, and said, 'Get up and eat—this journey you on is too much for you.'

8.text: So Elijah got up, ate, drank, and that meal kept him going for 40 days & 40 nights until he got to Mount Horeb, the mountain of God.

9.text: Elijah went into a cave and stayed the night. Then God spoke: 'Elijah, what you doing here?'

10.text: Elijah said, 'Lord, I been working hard for You! But Israel? They broke Your covenant, tore down Your altars, and killed all Your prophets. I'm the last one left—and now they tryna kill me too!'

11.text: God said, 'Go stand on the mountain. I'm about to pass by.' Then came a powerful wind—tearing up mountains & breaking rocks! But God wasn't in the wind. Then an earthquake! But God wasn't in the earthquake.

12.text: Then a fire! But God wasn't in the fire. Then... a small whisper. Elijah heard that whisper, wrapped his cloak around his face, and stepped out the cave.

13.text: Then the voice asked again, 'Elijah, what are you doing here?'

14.text: Elijah repeated, 'Lord, I been workin' hard for You. But Israel betrayed You! They tore down Your altars, killed Your prophets, and now they tryna kill me too.'

15.text: The Lord said, 'Go back the way you came, but this time, head to the Wilderness of Damascus. When you get there, anoint Hazael as king of Syria.'

16.text: 'Then, anoint Jehu as king of Israel.'

17.text: 'Whoever escapes Hazael's sword, Jehu gon' kill. Whoever escapes Jehu's sword, Elisha gon' handle them.'

18.text: 'But listen, you ain't the only one left. I got 7,000 people in Israel who ain't bowed to Baal or kissed him.'

19.text: So Elijah left and found Elisha, who was plowing with 12 yoke of oxen. Elijah walked by him and threw his mantle (cloak) over him.

20.text: Elisha ran after Elijah and said, 'Let me go kiss my parents goodbye, then I'll follow you.' Elijah said, 'Go ahead, but remember what just happened here.'

21.text: So Elisha went back, took his oxen, sacrificed them, and cooked them. He gave the food to the people, then left to follow Elijah and became his servant.

1.text: Ben-Hadad, king of Syria, rolled up with 32 other kings, horses, and chariots. He laid siege to Samaria and declared war on it.

2.text: He sent messengers to Ahab, king of Israel, saying, 'This is what Ben-Hadad says—'

3.text: 'Run me your silver and gold. Your finest wives & kids belong to me now.'

4.text: Ahab responded, 'You got it, my lord and king. Everything I have is yours.'

5.text: But the messengers came back, saying, 'Ben-Hadad says, "Nah, I ain't just talking about your silver & gold. Tomorrow, my men are coming to your palace to take anything they like."'

6.text: 'And they'll search your officials' houses too. If it's valuable, it's ours.'

7.text: Ahab called a meeting with his elders and said, 'Y'all see what's happening? This man wants war! He already took my silver, my gold, my wives, my kids—now he wants everything.'

8.text: The elders & people said, 'Don't listen to him! Don't agree!'

9.text: So Ahab sent messengers back, saying, 'I agreed to your first demand, but this second one? Nope.'

10.text: Ben-Hadad fired back, 'By the gods, I swear there won't be enough dust left of Samaria for my soldiers to pick up in their hands.'

11.text: Ahab hit him with a cold clapback: 'Don't talk like you already won. The man putting his armor on shouldn't brag like the one taking it off after battle.'

12.text: Ben-Hadad was drunk when he got the message. He snapped, 'Get ready! Attack the city!'

13.text: A prophet rolled up to Ahab and said, 'Look at this army. God says, "I'ma give you this win today so you KNOW I'm the Lord."'

14.text: Ahab asked, 'Who's gonna fight this battle?' The prophet said, 'Your young officers.' Ahab asked, 'Who's leading?' The prophet said, 'You.'

15.text: So Ahab rounded up 232 young officers. Then he called the rest of Israel—7,000 soldiers.

16.text: They attacked at noon. Meanwhile, Ben-Hadad and his 32 allied kings? Drunk outta their minds in their tent.

17.text: The young officers marched out first. Ben-Hadad's scouts ran back saying, 'Uh, some men are coming from Samaria!'

18.text: Ben-Hadad, still tipsy, said, 'If they coming in peace, take them alive. If they coming for war, take them alive.'

19.text: The officers charged. The Israelites followed.

20.text: Each soldier handled his opponent, and Syria's army fled. Ben-Hadad hopped on a horse and dipped!

21.text: Ahab came through, wrecked their chariots, killed the cavalry, and left Syria in ruins.

22.text: A prophet told Ahab, 'Get ready. Ben-Hadad will be back next spring.'

23.text: Meanwhile, Syria's officials told Ben-Hadad, 'Listen, Israel's God is a "mountain god." That's why we lost. If we fight on flatland, we'll win.'

24.text: 'Swap out the kings for real commanders and build a bigger army. Fight in the plains next time.'

25.text: Ben-Hadad agreed and started rebuilding.

26.text: The next spring, Syria pulled up to Aphek ready for round 2.

27.text: Israel came too, but they looked like tiny flocks compared to Syria's huge army.

28.text: A man of God came to Ahab and said, 'Because Syria disrespected God, saying He only runs the mountains, He's about to let you WIN so you know who He is.'

29.text: Both armies camped for 7 days. On day 7? They clashed.

30.text: Israel killed 100,000 soldiers in ONE day. The rest ran to Aphek, but then? A WALL collapsed and killed 27,000 more!

31.text: Ben-Hadad's men told him, 'Israelite kings show mercy. Wear sackcloth & ropes. Beg Ahab for your life.'

32.text: They went to Ahab and said, 'Your servant Ben-Hadad is asking to live.' Ahab said, 'Wait… he's alive? He my brother then.'

33.text: The men saw Ahab was open to peace, so they pushed harder: 'Yes, Ben-Hadad is your brother!'

34.text: Ben-Hadad told Ahab, 'I'ma give back the cities my dad took from your dad. You can set up markets in Damascus, just like my dad did in Samaria.' Ahab said, 'Bet. Let's make a treaty.' Then he let him go.

35.text: One of God's prophets told a man, 'Hit me!' But the man refused.

36.text: So the prophet said, 'Because you ain't listen, a lion finna eat you.' Sure enough? Dude got eaten by a lion.

37.text: The prophet found another man and said, 'Hit me!' So the man hit him hard.

38.text: The prophet then disguised himself, covering his wounds with a bandage.

39.text: As Ahab passed by, the prophet yelled, 'King! I was in battle, and a soldier brought me a prisoner, telling me to guard him. If he escaped, I'd owe a fine or my life! But I got distracted… and he ran away!'

40.text: Ahab told him, 'Then that's your problem. You just judged yourself.'

41.text: Then the prophet pulled off his disguise and Ahab realized he was a prophet.

42.text: The prophet said, 'God says—since you let go the man I sentenced to die, YOUR life will go for HIS. Your people will pay for it too.'

43.text: Ahab went home mad & upset.

1.text: After all that went down, Naboth the Jezreelite had a vineyard right next to Ahab's palace in Jezreel.

2.text: Ahab told Naboth, 'Lemme buy your vineyard. I wanna make it a garden since it's close to my palace. I'll give you a better vineyard for it, or cash if you prefer.'

3.text: But Naboth said, 'God forbid I sell my family's land!'

4.text: Ahab went home mad & salty over Naboth's refusal. He threw himself on the bed, turned his face to the wall, and refused to eat.

5.text: Jezebel came in like, 'What's wrong with you? Why you pouting like this?'

6.text: Ahab told her, 'I asked Naboth to sell me his vineyard, even offered to trade him a better one. But he said no.'

7.text: Jezebel rolled her eyes and said, 'Boy, you the king! Get up, eat some food, stop sulking. I'll get you that vineyard.'

8.text: She wrote letters in Ahab's name, sealed them, and sent them to the city leaders.

9.text: The letter said: 'Call a fast, put Naboth at the head of the people—'

10.text: 'Then seat two liars next to him who'll say, "Naboth cursed God & the king!" Then take him outside and stone him to death.'

11.text: The city elders did exactly as Jezebel ordered.

12.text: They called a fast and sat Naboth up front.

13.text: Then two fake witnesses came and accused him of cursing God & the king. So they took him outside and stoned him to death.

14.text: They sent word to Jezebel: 'Naboth is dead.'

15.text: Jezebel told Ahab, 'Get up! Take Naboth's vineyard. He dead now.'

16.text: Ahab, all happy again, went straight down to claim the vineyard.

17.text: God told Elijah: 'Go down to meet Ahab. He's in Naboth's vineyard, taking it for himself.'

18.text: 'Tell him: "So you murdered a man & stole his land too?"'

19.text: 'Then say: "God says—where dogs licked up Naboth's blood, they gon' lick up yours too."'

20.text: Ahab saw Elijah and said, 'Oh great, my enemy found me.' Elijah said, 'Yeah, I found you. Cuz you sold yourself to evil.'

21.text: 'God says—I'm wiping out your family. No sons, no legacy.'

22.text: 'I'ma make your house like Jeroboam's and Baasha's, cuz you made Israel sin.'

23.text: 'Oh, and Jezebel? She gon' get eaten by dogs in Jezreel.'

24.text: 'Anybody from Ahab's family that dies in the city? Dogs eating them. Anybody that dies in the fields? Birds eating them.'

25.text: Ahab was the worst king Israel ever had. Jezebel pushed him to do evil.

26.text: He followed false gods, just like the Amorites God had wiped out.

27.text: When Ahab heard this, he tore his clothes, wore sackcloth, fasted, and humbled himself.

28.text: God told Elijah, 'See how Ahab humbled himself? I won't bring disaster in his lifetime.'

29.text: 'But his son? That's when it's all coming down.'

1.text: Ain't been no war between Syria and Israel for three years.

2.text: But in the third year, Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, went to visit the king of Israel.

3.text: The king of Israel told his crew, "Y'all know Ramoth-Gilead belong to us, right? But we just sittin' here while Syria holdin' it down?"

4.text: So he asked Jehoshaphat, "You ridin' with me to take it back?" Jehoshaphat said, "You already know—me, my people, my horses, all of us, we wit' you."

5.text: But then Jehoshaphat was like, "Hold up, we need to ask the Lord about this first."

6.text: So the king of Israel called together 400 prophets and asked them, "Should I go to war for Ramoth-Gilead, or nah?" They all said, "Go ahead! The Lord gon' hand it to you!"

7.text: But Jehoshaphat wasn't feelin' that, so he asked, "Ain't there at least one real prophet of the Lord we can check with?"

8.text: The king of Israel said, "Yeah, there's Micaiah, son of Imlah. But I don't like him—he never got nothin' good to say about me, always talkin' negative." Jehoshaphat said, "Man, don't talk like that!"

9.text: So the king called for one of his men and said, "Go get Micaiah, now!"

10.text: Meanwhile, both kings—Israel and Judah—were sittin' on their thrones, posted up at the city gate, watchin' as all the prophets kept prophesyin'.

11.text: One prophet, Zedekiah, made some iron horns and said, "The Lord says you gon' charge through the Syrians like this and wipe 'em out!"

12.text: All the prophets kept sayin' the same thing, "Go up to Ramoth-Gilead! The Lord gon' give you the win!"

13.text: The messenger who went to get Micaiah told him, "Look, everybody else already sayin' good things to the king. Just say what they say, aight?"

14.text: But Micaiah said, "Naw, whatever the Lord tells me, that's what I'ma say."

15.text: When he got to the king, the king asked, "Micaiah, should we go to war for Ramoth-Gilead or not?" Micaiah said, "Go 'head and do it. The Lord got you."

16.text: The king snapped, "Bruh, how many times I gotta tell you—only tell me what the Lord really say!"

17.text: Then Micaiah kept it real: "I saw all of Israel out here like lost sheep, no shepherd in sight. And the Lord said, 'They ain't got no leader. Let 'em go back home in peace.'"

18.text: The king of Israel turned to Jehoshaphat, "See? Didn't I tell you? He always got bad news!"

19.text: Micaiah said, "Look, listen to the word of the Lord. I saw the Lord sittin' on His throne, with all heaven standin' by Him, left and right.

20.text: And the Lord said, 'Who gon' convince Ahab to go fight at Ramoth-Gilead so he can die there?' Some said this, some said that.

21.text: Then one spirit stepped up and said, 'I got this. I'ma handle it.'

22.text: The Lord said, 'How?' The spirit said, 'I'ma go be a lying spirit in all his prophets' mouths.' And the Lord said, 'Bet, go do that. You'll succeed.'"

23.text: "So listen up, King. The Lord put a lying spirit in all these prophets of yours. He already planned disaster for you."

24.text: Zedekiah came up and slapped Micaiah across the face, "So what? The spirit of the Lord just skipped over me and jumped on you?"

25.text: Micaiah said, "You gon' find out the day you hide in some back room, scared for your life."

26.text: Then the king of Israel told his men, "Take Micaiah back to the governor and the prince."

27.text: And he said, "Lock him up, give him prison food and water until I come back from this war."

28.text: But Micaiah said, "If you come back alive, then the Lord ain't speak through me." And then he shouted, "Everybody, pay attention to what I'm sayin'!"

29.text: So the kings of Israel and Judah rolled out to Ramoth-Gilead.

30.text: The king of Israel told Jehoshaphat, "I'ma go in disguise, but you wear your royal robes." And he went into battle undercover.

31.text: Meanwhile, the king of Syria told his chariot commanders, "Don't bother with the regular soldiers—just go for the king of Israel!"

32.text: So when they saw Jehoshaphat, they thought he was the king of Israel and went after him. But Jehoshaphat called out,

33.text: And when they saw he wasn't the king of Israel, they backed off.

34.text: Then some random soldier shot an arrow at nothing, but that thing found its way right between Ahab's armor. He told his chariot driver, "Turn around, take me outta here—I'm hit!"

35.text: The battle kept goin' all day, and Ahab was propped up in his chariot, bleeding out. By evening, he died.

36.text: As the sun set, somebody shouted, "Everybody, go home!"

37.text: So the king of Israel died and was brought back to Samaria for burial.

38.text: They washed his chariot by the pool in Samaria, and just like the Lord said, dogs licked up his blood while prostitutes washed there.

39.text: The rest of Ahab's story—his palace, his cities, all of it—is in the book of the kings of Israel.

40.text: Then Ahab died, and his son Ahaziah took over.

41.text: Jehoshaphat, son of Asa, became king of Judah in Ahab's 4th year.

42.text: He was 35 years old when he took the throne and ruled in Jerusalem for 25 years. His mother was Azubah, daughter of Shilhi.

43.text: He followed his father Asa's ways, did right in God's eyes, but didn't remove the high places where folks worshiped.

44.text: Jehoshaphat made peace with Israel's king.

45.text: The rest of his story—his power and war record—is in the book of the kings of Judah.

46.text: He also removed the remaining shrine prostitutes from the land.

47.text: There was no king in Edom, just a governor.

48.text: He tried to send merchant ships to get gold from Ophir, but they wrecked before they even left port.

49.text: Then Ahaziah (Ahab's son) asked Jehoshaphat, "Let's team up and use my guys on your ships." But Jehoshaphat said "Nah."

50.text: Jehoshaphat died, was buried in Jerusalem, and his son Jehoram became king.

51.text: Ahaziah, son of Ahab, became king of Israel in Samaria during Jehoshaphat's 17th year. He ruled for 2 years.

52.text: He did evil like his parents, following Jeroboam's sins and making Israel do wrong.

53.text: He worshiped Baal and made God mad, just like Ahab did.

1.text: There was this man from Ramathaim, up in the hill country of Ephraim. His name was Elkanah, son of Jeroham, grandson of Elihu, great-grandson of Tohu, from the family of Zuph. He was an Ephraimite.

2.text: Elkanah had two wives—one named Hannah, the other named Peninnah. Peninnah had kids, but Hannah ain't have none.

3.text: Every year, Elkanah took his whole family up to Shiloh to worship and bring sacrifices to the Lord Almighty. Now, Eli's sons, Hophni and Phinehas, was working as priests for the Lord at that time.

4.text: Whenever Elkanah made his offering, he would give Peninnah and all her kids their share.

5.text: But when it came to Hannah, he gave her extra 'cause he really loved her, even though the Lord ain't blessed her with no kids.

6.text: But Peninnah? She stayed clownin' Hannah, making her feel real bad 'cause she ain't have no kids.

7.text: This went down every single year when they went up to the Lord's house. Peninnah kept coming at her, making Hannah cry so much she ain't even wanna eat.

8.text: Elkanah, her husband, was like, 'Hannah, why you cryin'? Why you ain't eatin'? Why your heart so heavy? Ain't I better to you than ten sons?'

9.text: One time after they finished eating in Shiloh, Hannah got up. Meanwhile, Eli the priest was chillin' by the entrance of the Lord's temple.

10.text: Hannah was hurting deep in her soul. She started praying hard to the Lord, crying her heart out.

11.text: She made a promise and said, 'Lord Almighty, if you see my struggle, if you remember me and bless me with a son, I promise to give him back to you for his whole life. And no razor gon' touch his head.'

12.text: She kept prayin' for a long time, and Eli was just sittin' there watchin' her mouth move.

13.text: Hannah was prayin' in her heart—her lips was movin', but she ain't say nothin' out loud. So Eli thought she was drunk.

14.text: Eli was like, 'How long you gon' be drunk? Put that wine down!'

15.text: But Hannah said, 'No sir, I ain't drunk. I'm just a woman with a heavy heart, and I been pourin' my soul out to the Lord.'

16.text: 'Please don't think I'm some kinda worthless woman. I been speakin' out of deep pain and frustration.'

17.text: Eli answered, 'Alright then, go in peace. And may the God of Israel give you what you been askin' for.'

18.text: Hannah said, 'Thank you for your kindness!' Then she went back, got herself some food, and wasn't sad no more.

19.text: Early the next morning, Elkanah and his family worshiped the Lord, then headed back home to Ramah. Elkanah slept with Hannah, and the Lord remembered her.

20.text: After some time, Hannah got pregnant and had a son. She named him Samuel, sayin', 'Because I asked the Lord for him.'

21.text: Elkanah went up with his whole household to give their yearly sacrifice and fulfill his vow.

22.text: But Hannah ain't go. She told her husband, 'Let me wait till the child is weaned. Then I'll take him to the Lord's house, and he gon' stay there forever.'

23.text: Elkanah said, 'Do what you think is best. Stay here till you wean him, but let the Lord's will be done.' So Hannah stayed home and nursed her son.

24.text: When she finished weaning him, she took him to the Lord's house in Shiloh. She brought a three-year-old bull, a bunch of flour, and a skin of wine. The boy was still real young.

25.text: They sacrificed the bull and brought Samuel to Eli.

26.text: Hannah told Eli, 'Sir, I swear I'm that woman that was standin' here prayin' to the Lord.'

27.text: 'I was prayin' for this child, and the Lord gave me what I asked for.'

28.text: 'So now I'm givin' him back to the Lord. As long as he live, he belong to the Lord.' And they worshiped the Lord there.

1.text: Then Hannah prayed and said: 'My heart is full of joy in the Lord. He lifted me up! I can laugh in the face of my enemies 'cause I know the Lord saved me.'

2.text: 'Ain't nobody holy like the Lord. Ain't nobody else like Him, and ain't no rock as solid as our God.'

3.text: 'Y'all need to stop talkin' all high and mighty. Quit all that arrogance, 'cause the Lord sees everything and He weighs every action.'

4.text: 'The weapons of the strong are broken, but the ones who was strugglin' now got strength.'

5.text: 'The ones who had everything gotta work just to eat, but the hungry? They full now. The woman who couldn't have kids got seven, but the one with many kids is weak now.'

6.text: 'The Lord brings life, and He takes it away. He puts folks in the grave, and He lifts them up.'

7.text: 'The Lord makes some folks poor and others rich. He humbles some and lifts others up.'

8.text: 'He takes the poor up out the dirt, pulls the beggar up out the ashes, and sets 'em up with princes, giving them a seat at the table. The whole world rests on His foundation.'

9.text: 'The Lord keeps His people safe, but the wicked? They get left in the dark. 'Cause ain't no man can win just by his own strength.'

10.text: 'The Lord gon' shatter His enemies. When He speaks from heaven, they gon' be done for. He judges everybody, from one end of the earth to the other. He gon' give power to His king and lift up the one He chose.'

11.text: After that, Elkanah took his family back home to Ramah, but little Samuel stayed and served the Lord under Eli the priest.

12.text: Now Eli's sons? They was outta pocket. They ain't know the Lord at all.

13.text: Back in the day, priests had this routine—when people brought sacrifices, the priest's servant would come through while the meat was still boiling, holding a three-pronged fork.

14.text: He'd stick the fork into the pot or kettle, and whatever came up, the priest took for himself. That's how they did all the Israelites bringing sacrifices in Shiloh.

15.text: But before the fat was even burned, the priest's servant would tell the person sacrificing, 'Yo, hand over that raw meat for the priest to roast. He ain't takin' no boiled meat—only raw.'

16.text: If somebody said, 'Nah, they gotta burn the fat first, then you can take what you want,' the servant would snap back, 'Nope, gimme that now, or I'll take it by force!'

17.text: These young priests was outta control, and the Lord was not pleased. They was making folks hate bringing offerings to the Lord.

18.text: Meanwhile, little Samuel was servin' the Lord, rockin' his linen priest's robe.

19.text: His mama, Hannah, made him a little coat and brought it to him every year when they came up to offer sacrifices.

20.text: Eli would bless Elkanah and Hannah, saying, 'May the Lord give y'all more kids 'cause of the one you gave back to Him.' Then they'd go back home.

21.text: And the Lord blessed Hannah. She had three more sons and two daughters. Meanwhile, little Samuel was growin' up right in front of the Lord.

22.text: Now Eli was old. He kept hearing 'bout all the shady stuff his sons was doin'—how they was messin' with the women who worked at the entrance of the Lord's tent.

23.text: So he told 'em, 'Why y'all actin' like this? Everybody out here talkin' 'bout how y'all wildin' out.'

24.text: 'This ain't a good look, my sons. Y'all makin' God's people sin! This ain't right.'

25.text: 'If a man sins against another man, God can step in. But if a man sins against the Lord, who gon' step in for him?' But they ain't listen to their daddy, 'cause the Lord had already decided their fate.

26.text: Meanwhile, Samuel kept growin' in stature and was favored by both God and people.

27.text: Then one day, a man of God came to Eli and said, 'This what the Lord says: Didn't I reveal myself to your ancestors back when they was slaves in Egypt?'

28.text: 'Didn't I choose your family to be My priests, to serve at My altar, burn incense, and wear the sacred robe before Me? Didn't I give your family all the sacrifices made by fire?'

29.text: 'So why y'all disrespectin' My offerings? Why you let your sons treat My sacrifices like trash? You put them above Me, getting fat off the best of the offerings.'

30.text: 'So now the Lord, the God of Israel, says this: I did say your family would serve Me forever. But nah, I don't roll like that. If you honor Me, I'll honor you. But if you despise Me, you gon' be ignored.'

31.text: 'Days are coming when I'ma cut off your family line. None of y'all gon' grow old.'

32.text: 'You gon' see disaster in My house. And while Israel gets blessed, y'all gon' be struggling. Your whole family gon' be wiped out.'

33.text: 'I'ma leave one of your descendants alive, but he gon' be struggling, breaking your heart. And the rest of 'em? They gon' die young.'

34.text: 'And this how you know it's real—your two sons, Hophni and Phinehas? They both gon' die on the same day.'

35.text: 'But I'ma raise up a real priest, somebody who follows My heart and does what I want. I'ma make sure his house stands strong, and he gon' serve My anointed one forever.'

36.text: 'And when that happens, anybody left from your family gon' be begging for food, sayin', "Please let me work for you, so I can get a bite to eat."'

1.text: Lil' Samuel was servin' the Lord under Eli. Now back then, the Lord ain't be speakin' much—visions and messages from God was real rare.

2.text: One night, Eli was layin' down in his spot. His eyesight was bad, like real bad—man could barely see no more.

3.text: Samuel was layin' down in the Lord's temple, right where the Ark of God was. The lamp of God was still burnin'.

4.text: Then the Lord called out, 'Samuel!' And Samuel jumped up like, 'Here I am!'

5.text: He ran straight to Eli like, 'I'm here! You called me?' But Eli was like, 'Nah, boy, I ain't call you. Go lay back down.' So Samuel went back to bed.

6.text: Then the Lord called out again, 'Samuel!' So Samuel got up, ran to Eli again, and said, 'I'm here! You called me?' But Eli was like, 'Son, I did not call you. Go lay down.'

7.text: Now Samuel ain't really know the Lord yet, 'cause God ain't spoke to him before.

8.text: Then the Lord called Samuel one more time. Samuel jumped up, ran to Eli, and said, 'I know you called me!' That's when Eli finally realized—oh, this God talkin' to the boy.

9.text: So Eli told him, 'Go lay down again. And if you hear that voice, say, "Speak, Lord, your servant is listenin'."' So Samuel went back to his bed.

10.text: Then the Lord showed up and called just like before, 'Samuel! Samuel!' And Samuel said, 'Speak, Lord. I'm listenin'.'

11.text: Then the Lord said, 'Boy, listen—I'm 'bout to do somethin' in Israel that gon' have everybody's ears ringin'.'

12.text: 'When the time come, I'ma do everything I said I was gon' do to Eli's family—ain't nothin' gettin' left out.'

13.text: 'I already told Eli his family gettin' judged forever, 'cause his sons out here actin' a fool, and he ain't stop 'em.'

14.text: 'Ain't no amount of sacrifices or offerings ever gon' fix this. It's done.'

15.text: Samuel laid there till morning, then got up and opened the temple doors. But he did not wanna tell Eli what he heard.

16.text: Eli called him, 'Samuel, my son!' And Samuel was like, 'I'm here.'

17.text: Eli said, 'What the Lord tell you? Don't you hide nothin' from me. If you do, may God do the same and worse to you!'

18.text: So Samuel told him everything—ain't hold nothin' back. Eli sighed and said, 'Well, it's the Lord. He gon' do what He think is best.'

19.text: Samuel grew up, and the Lord was with him. Everything Samuel spoke? It came true.

20.text: From Dan to Beersheba, everybody in Israel knew Samuel was the Lord's prophet.

21.text: The Lord kept showin' up in Shiloh, speakin' to Samuel and makin' Himself known.

1.text: Samuel's word was spreadin' all over Israel. Meanwhile, Israel's army rolled out to fight the Philistines, settin' up camp at Ebenezer while the Philistines posted up at Aphek.

2.text: When the battle popped off, the Philistines straight-up whooped Israel. They took out about 4,000 soldiers out on the battlefield.

3.text: After takin' that L, the Israelite elders was like, 'Man, why did the Lord let us lose like this? We need to bring the Ark of the Covenant from Shiloh—that gon' help us win!'

4.text: So they sent folks to Shiloh to grab the Ark of the Lord's Covenant, the one that sits between the cherubim. Eli's two shady sons, Hophni and Phinehas, came along with it.

5.text: When the Ark pulled up in the camp, all of Israel went wild—yellin' so loud the ground was shakin'!

6.text: The Philistines heard the ruckus and was like, 'Hold up—what's all that shoutin' about in the Hebrew camp?' Then they realized, 'Oh snap, the Ark of the Lord just pulled up.'

7.text: They got shook. 'Oh no! Their God just showed up in the camp! We ain't never seen nothin' like this before!'

8.text: 'We in trouble now! This the same God that wrecked Egypt with all them plagues!'

9.text: 'Man up, Philistines! If y'all don't fight, y'all gon' end up slaves to these Hebrews just like they been to us. Get it together and fight!'

10.text: And fight they did—and Israel lost bad. Every man ran back home. 30,000 soldiers got wiped out.

11.text: And worst of all? The Ark of God got snatched up. Hophni and Phinehas? Dead.

12.text: Same day, a dude from the tribe of Benjamin sprinted back from the battlefield straight to Shiloh. His clothes was torn, dirt all over his head—he was tore up.

13.text: When he got there, Eli was sittin' by the road, watchin'—his heart was racin' 'cause he was worried about the Ark. Soon as the runner hit town and told the people what happened, the whole city started cryin' out.

14.text: Eli heard the noise and was like, 'What's goin' on?!' The runner rushed over and told him everything.

15.text: Now Eli was 98 years old and practically blind.

16.text: The runner said, 'I just came from the battlefield—I had to run back here today.' Eli asked, 'What happened, son?'

17.text: The man broke it down: 'Israel got washed by the Philistines, it was a massacre. Your two sons? Hophni and Phinehas? They gone. And on top of that, the Ark of God got taken.'

18.text: Soon as he heard about the Ark, Eli fell backward off his seat, snapped his neck, and died—man was old and heavy. He had been judge over Israel for 40 years.

19.text: Meanwhile, Phinehas' wife was pregnant and just about due. Soon as she heard the news—that the Ark was taken, that her father-in-law and her husband was dead—she went into labor right then and there.

20.text: As she was dyin' in labor, the women helpin' her was like, 'Don't worry, you had a son!' But she ain't even respond.

21.text: She named the baby Ichabod and said, 'The glory is gone from Israel!' 'Cause the Ark was taken, and her husband and father-in-law was gone.

22.text: 'Yeah, the glory done left Israel, 'cause the Ark of God got taken.'

1.text: The Philistines took the Ark of God from Ebenezer and hauled it off to Ashdod.

2.text: They brought it into the temple of Dagon, their so-called god, and set it up right next to the statue.

3.text: But when the folks in Ashdod woke up the next morning, Dagon was laid out flat, face-down in front of the Ark of the Lord. So they picked him up and put him back where he was.

4.text: Next morning? Same thing—except this time, Dagon's head and both hands was broken clean off at the threshold. Only thing left standing was his torso.

5.text: That's why to this day, Dagon's priests and his worshippers won't step on that threshold in Ashdod—'cause they know what happened.

6.text: But the Lord wasn't done yet. He put heavy pressure on Ashdod—struck 'em down with nasty tumors all over the city and surrounding areas.

7.text: Folks in Ashdod started freakin' out: 'We gotta get rid of this Ark, 'cause God's hand is straight-up destroyin' us and makin' our god, Dagon, look weak!'

8.text: So they gathered up all the big bosses of the Philistines and asked, 'What we gon' do with this Ark?' They decided, 'Send it to Gath.' So they moved it there.

9.text: But soon as it got to Gath, God went off again—the whole city got hit hard, from the rich folks down to the common folk. Tumors broke out everywhere.

10.text: So they panicked and sent the Ark to Ekron. But soon as it pulled up, the Ekronites flipped out: 'Y'all brought the Ark here to kill us all?!'

11.text: So once again, the Philistine leaders had a meeting and decided, 'Man, get this thing outta here! Send it back to Israel before it wipes us all out!' The whole city was gettin' wrecked, and God's hand was pressin' down hard on 'em.

12.text: Some folks straight-up died, while others was suffering from tumors. The whole city was cryin' out for mercy—their screams went straight up to heaven.

1.text: The Ark of the Lord had been stuck in Philistine territory for seven months.

2.text: The Philistines called in their priests and fortune tellers like, 'Yo, what we supposed to do with this Ark? How we send it back?'

3.text: They told 'em, 'Look, if y'all gon' send the Ark back, don't send it empty-handed. Make sure you bring an offering for the Lord. Maybe then He'll heal y'all and stop messin' y'all up.'

4.text: So they asked, 'Aight, but what kinda offering we supposed to give?' They answered, 'Five golden tumors and five golden rats—one for each Philistine leader, 'cause all y'all got hit by the same plague.'

5.text: 'Make models of the tumors and rats messin' up y'all land, and send 'em as a peace offering to the God of Israel. Maybe He'll chill out and stop wreckin' y'all, your gods, and your land.'

6.text: 'Don't be stubborn like Pharaoh and the Egyptians! Y'all remember what happened to them, right? God showed out, and they had no choice but to let Israel go!'

7.text: 'Now here's what y'all do—get a new cart, take two cows that ain't never been yoked before, and hitch 'em up. Take their calves and keep 'em at home.'

8.text: 'Put the Ark of the Lord on the cart, and put y'all gold offerings in a box next to it. Then let it go, and see what happens.'

9.text: 'If the cows head straight for Beth Shemesh, then we'll know it was the Lord who was punishin' us. But if they don't, then it was all just bad luck.'

10.text: So they did just that—hitched up the two cows, locked up their calves, and sent the Ark on its way.

11.text: They put the Ark of the Lord on the cart, along with the box of golden rats and tumors.

12.text: The cows walked straight down the road to Beth Shemesh, mooin' the whole way. They ain't turn left or right. The Philistine leaders followed behind, watchin' to see what would happen.

13.text: The folks in Beth Shemesh was out in the fields harvesting wheat when they looked up and saw the Ark comin'. They got hype!

14.text: The cart rolled into a field belongin' to a man named Joshua and stopped by a big rock. The Israelites chopped up the wood from the cart and sacrificed the cows as an offering to the Lord.

15.text: The Levites took down the Ark and the gold offerings and set them up on the rock. That day, the people of Beth Shemesh gave offerings and sacrifices to the Lord.

16.text: When the five Philistine leaders saw all this go down, they was like, 'Aight, bet.' And they headed back to Ekron.

17.text: Them golden tumors the Philistines sent as a guilt offering to the Lord? One for Ashdod, Gaza, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron.

18.text: Same with the golden rats—one for every city in Philistine territory, whether big or small. They placed the Ark on a rock in Joshua's field in Beth Shemesh, and that rock still there to this day.

19.text: But some men in Beth Shemesh got curious and peeked inside the Ark. Big mistake. The Lord struck 50,070 of them dead. The people started mournin', 'cause they knew the Lord wasn't playin'.

20.text: They was like, 'Man, who can even stand before the Lord? He too holy! Where we gon' send the Ark now?!'

21.text: So they sent a message to the folks in Kirjath Jearim: 'Yo, the Philistines sent the Ark back. Y'all come get it!'

1.text: So the men of Kirjath Jearim came and took the Ark of the Lord. They brought it to Abinadab's house up on the hill and put his son Eleazar in charge of watching over it.

2.text: That Ark stayed in Kirjath Jearim for twenty years. And in all that time, Israel was cryin' out to the Lord, wantin' to get right with Him.

3.text: Samuel told the whole nation of Israel, 'If y'all really wanna come back to the Lord, then drop them fake gods—get rid of all them idols, especially the Ashtoreths. Y'all need to commit to servin' the Lord only, and He'll save you from the Philistines.'

4.text: So Israel did just that—they threw away their idols to Baal and Ashtoreth, and they only served the Lord.

5.text: Then Samuel said, 'Aight, everybody, meet me at Mizpah. I'ma pray to the Lord for y'all.'

6.text: So they gathered up at Mizpah, poured out water as an offering to God, and fasted that whole day. They admitted, 'Lord, we messed up. We sinned against You.' That day, Samuel acted as their judge.

7.text: When the Philistines heard Israel was all gathered up at Mizpah, their leaders was like, 'Oh, they slippin'—let's go get 'em.' Israel heard the Philistines was comin' and got scared.

8.text: They begged Samuel, 'Please, don't stop prayin' to the Lord for us! Ask Him to save us from the Philistines!'

9.text: So Samuel took a baby lamb and sacrificed it as a burnt offering to the Lord. He cried out to the Lord for Israel, and God answered him.

10.text: Just as Samuel was makin' the sacrifice, the Philistines rolled up ready for war. But the Lord let out a massive thunderclap so loud that it shook the Philistines, throwin' 'em into complete chaos. Israel took 'em down.

11.text: The Israelites chased the Philistines all the way back to Beth Car, tearin' 'em up along the way.

12.text: After the battle, Samuel took a big stone and set it up between Mizpah and Shen. He named it Ebenezer, sayin', 'This far, the Lord has helped us.'

13.text: From that day on, the Philistines stayed down—they ain't dare mess with Israel no more. The Lord kept His hand against them the whole time Samuel was alive.

14.text: Any cities the Philistines had taken got returned to Israel, from Ekron to Gath. Israel also made peace with the Amorites.

15.text: Samuel led and judged Israel for the rest of his life.

16.text: Every year, he made the rounds from Bethel to Gilgal to Mizpah, judging the people in each city.

17.text: But his home base was Ramah, where he also judged Israel. He even built an altar to the Lord there.

1.text: When Samuel got old, he made his sons judges over Israel.

2.text: His firstborn was named Joel, and his second son was Abijah. They was posted up in Beersheba, judging the people.

3.text: But these dudes? They ain't walk like Samuel. They got greedy, takin' bribes, messin' up justice for personal gain.

4.text: So all the elders of Israel pulled up on Samuel at Ramah.

5.text: They told him, 'Look, man, you old now, and your sons ain't doin' right. We need you to give us a king—somebody to rule over us like all the other nations.'

6.text: Samuel ain't like that at all. He took it straight to the Lord in prayer.

7.text: The Lord told Samuel, 'Listen to 'em. They ain't rejecting you, they rejecting Me—they don't want Me running things no more.'

8.text: 'Ain't nothin' new. Ever since I brought 'em outta Egypt, they been turnin' away from Me, runnin' after fake gods. And now they doin' the same thing to you.'

9.text: 'Go ahead and give 'em what they want, but make sure you tell 'em what a king really gon' do to 'em.'

10.text: So Samuel sat the people down and gave them the real about kings.

11.text: He said, 'This what a king gon' be like—he gon' snatch up your sons, make 'em run his chariots, ride his horses, and serve in his army.'

12.text: 'He gon' put some of y'all in charge of thousands, some over fifties, and some just to work his farms and make his weapons.'

13.text: 'He gon' take your daughters to be his perfumers, cooks, and bakers.'

14.text: 'He gon' snatch up the best of your fields, vineyards, and olive groves, and hand 'em over to his own people.'

15.text: 'He gon' tax your grain and grapes, takin' a cut for himself and his staff.'

16.text: 'Your servants, your best workers, your livestock—he gon' put 'em all to work for him.'

17.text: 'He gon' take a tenth of your sheep, and at the end of the day? Y'all gon' be his servants.'

18.text: 'And when that day come, when y'all realize y'all messed up and cry out to the Lord about the king y'all chose? He ain't gon' listen.'

19.text: But the people ain't wanna hear all that. They said, 'Nah! We need a king!'

20.text: 'We wanna be like everybody else, with a king who can lead us and fight our battles!'

21.text: Samuel listened to all their demands, then went back and told the Lord.

22.text: And the Lord said, 'Fine. Give 'em a king.' Then Samuel told the people, 'Aight, everybody go home.'

1.text: There was a man from the tribe of Benjamin named Kish, son of Abiel, grandson of Zeror, great-grandson of Bechorath, from the family of Aphiah. Dude was powerful.
