2.text: Kish had a son named Saul, and let me tell you—this man was fine. Nobody in Israel looked better than him. Plus, he was tall, standing a whole head above everybody else.

3.text: One day, Kish's donkeys went missing, so he told Saul, 'Take one of the servants and go look for them.'

4.text: Saul and his servant searched all over—through the Ephraim hills, through Shalisha, through Shaalim, and even through Benjamin's land—but no donkeys.

5.text: When they got to Zuph, Saul told his servant, 'Man, let's go back. My dad gon' stop worrying about the donkeys and start worrying about us.'

6.text: But the servant was like, 'Hold up—there's a man of God in this city. Everything he says comes true. Maybe he can tell us where to look.'

7.text: Saul was like, 'Aight, but what we gon' give him? We outta food, and we ain't got no gift for the man of God. What we got left?'

8.text: The servant said, 'I got a fourth of a shekel of silver. I'll give it to the man of God so he can tell us where to go.'

9.text: (Back in the day, people used to call prophets seers. If you wanted to hear from God, you'd say, 'Let's go see the seer.')

10.text: Saul was like, 'Bet, let's go.' So they headed into the city to find the man of God.

11.text: As they climbed the hill toward the city, they saw some young women comin' out to draw water. They asked, 'Hey, is the seer around?'

12.text: The women said, 'Yeah, he's up ahead! But y'all better hurry, 'cause he just got here for a big sacrifice at the high place.'

13.text: 'If y'all go now, you'll catch him before he goes up to bless the sacrifice. The people won't eat till he gets there. Go quick, you'll find him!'

14.text: So they went into the city, and boom—Samuel was walking right toward them on his way up to the high place.

15.text: Now, the day before, the Lord had whispered to Samuel,

16.text: 'Tomorrow, around this time, I'ma send you a man from Benjamin. You gon' anoint him as leader over My people Israel. He gon' rescue them from the Philistines, 'cause I heard their cries.'

17.text: When Samuel saw Saul, the Lord said, 'That's him! The one I told you about—he gon' rule over My people.'

18.text: Saul walked up to Samuel at the city gate and said, 'Excuse me, sir—can you tell me where the seer's house is?'

19.text: Samuel said, 'That's me. Come with me up to the high place. You gon' eat with me today, and tomorrow morning, I'ma tell you everything on your heart.'

20.text: 'Oh, and about them donkeys y'all been lookin' for? Don't even worry 'bout it. They been found. But let me ask you this—who do you think all of Israel lookin' to now? Ain't it you and your family?'

21.text: Saul was shocked. 'Me? But I'm from Benjamin, the smallest tribe in Israel! And my family? We ain't nobody special. Why you talkin' to me like this?'

22.text: Samuel took Saul and his servant into the dining hall and gave them the best seat at the table with about thirty guests.

23.text: Then Samuel told the cook, 'Bring out that special piece I set aside for our guest.'

24.text: So the cook brought out the thigh and the best cut and placed it in front of Saul. Samuel said, 'This was saved just for you. Go ahead, eat!' So Saul sat and ate with Samuel that day.

25.text: After dinner, they came back down from the high place into the city. Samuel had a private talk with Saul up on the rooftop.

26.text: The next morning, at sunrise, Samuel called to Saul, 'Wake up! It's time for you to go.' So Saul got up, and they walked out together.

27.text: As they were leavin' the city, Samuel told Saul, 'Send your servant ahead of us.' When the servant left, Samuel said, 'Now, stay here for a minute—I gotta tell you what God has planned for you.'

1.text: Samuel took a flask of oil, poured it on Saul's head, kissed him, and said, 'The Lord just anointed you as the leader over His people.'

2.text: 'When you leave me today, you gon' run into two men near Rachel's tomb in Benjamin, at Zelzah. They gon' tell you, "Yo, them donkeys you was lookin' for? They been found. But now your pops ain't even worried about them—he worried about you instead."'

3.text: 'Then, when you keep going to the great tree at Tabor, you gon' run into three men on their way to worship in Bethel. One got three goats, one got three loaves of bread, and one got a skin of wine.'

4.text: 'They gon' greet you and hand you two loaves of bread. Take it—it's yours.'

5.text: 'Then you gon' reach Gibeah, where the Philistine outpost is. There, you gon' run into some prophets comin' down from the high place, playing instruments—harps, tambourines, flutes—and they gon' be prophesyin'.'

6.text: 'When that happens, the Spirit of the Lord gon' take over you, and you gon' start prophesyin' too. You gon' be a whole new man.'

7.text: 'When all this goes down, do whatever feels right, 'cause God is with you.'

8.text: 'Then go ahead to Gilgal, and I'ma come later to offer burnt offerings and peace offerings. Wait seven days for me to get there and tell you what's next.'

9.text: Soon as Saul turned to leave Samuel, God changed his heart. And just like that, everything Samuel said started happening.

10.text: When Saul and his servant got to the hill, there was a group of prophets. And just like that, the Spirit of God hit Saul, and he started prophesyin' too.

11.text: Everybody who knew Saul before was shocked. They was like, 'Wait… what's goin' on with Kish's son?! Saul's a prophet now?!'

12.text: One dude was like, 'Who even taught these prophets?!' And that's how the saying started: "Is Saul also among the prophets?"

13.text: When Saul finished prophesyin', he went up to the high place.

14.text: Later, Saul's uncle asked him and his servant, 'Where y'all been?' Saul said, 'Lookin' for the donkeys. When we couldn't find 'em, we went to see Samuel.'

15.text: His uncle was like, 'What did Samuel tell y'all?'

16.text: Saul said, 'Oh, he just told us the donkeys was found.' But he ain't say a word about Samuel anointing him as king.

17.text: Samuel called all the people together at Mizpah to meet with the Lord.

18.text: He told them, 'The Lord, the God of Israel, says: I brought y'all out of Egypt. I saved y'all from slavery and from every nation that oppressed y'all.'

19.text: 'But today, y'all rejecting God—the same God who keeps saving you. Y'all said, "Nah, we want a king instead!" So now, line up by tribes and clans so we can pick one.'

20.text: Samuel had all the tribes line up, and the Lord picked the tribe of Benjamin.

21.text: Then He picked the Matri clan from Benjamin. Then, from them, He picked Saul, son of Kish. But when they looked for him, he was nowhere to be found.

22.text: So they asked the Lord, 'Uh… where he at?' And the Lord said, 'He hidin' in the baggage.'

23.text: So they ran and pulled Saul out. And when he stood up, he was taller than everybody else.

24.text: Samuel said, 'Look at him—this is the one God chose! Ain't nobody like him in all of Israel!' And the people went crazy, shoutin', 'Long live the king!'

25.text: Then Samuel explained how the kingdom was supposed to run, wrote it all down in a book, and placed it before the Lord. Then he sent everybody home.

26.text: Saul went back to Gibeah, and some loyal men followed him—men whose hearts God had touched.

27.text: But some haters was like, 'Man, how he supposed to save us?' They disrespected him, ain't bring him no gifts. But Saul? He ain't say nothin'.

1.text: Then Nahash the Ammonite rolled up on Jabesh Gilead, ready to take over. The men of Jabesh was like, 'Aight, let's make a deal—we'll serve you if you let us live.'

2.text: Nahash was like, 'Bet. But on one condition—I'ma gouge out all y'all right eyes to humiliate Israel.'

3.text: The elders of Jabesh was like, 'Hold up! Give us seven days to send out messengers across Israel. If nobody comes to save us, then we'll surrender.'

4.text: So they sent messengers to Gibeah, where Saul was. When the people heard what was goin' down, they all started cryin'.

5.text: Meanwhile, Saul was out in the field workin'. When he came back, he saw everybody weepin' and was like, 'What's goin' on?' So they told him what happened with Jabesh.

6.text: Soon as Saul heard the news, the Spirit of God hit him hard, and he got mad as hell.

7.text: Saul took two oxen, chopped 'em up, and sent the pieces across Israel with a message: 'Anybody who don't come fight with me and Samuel? This what gon' happen to their oxen too!' The Lord put fear in the people, so they all showed up ready to fight.

8.text: When Saul did a headcount at Bezek, he had 300,000 Israelites and 30,000 men from Judah.

9.text: They sent a message back to Jabesh Gilead, sayin', 'Tell your people that by noon tomorrow, help is comin'.' When Jabesh heard that, they got hype.

10.text: So the men of Jabesh told Nahash, 'Aight, we comin' out tomorrow—do whatever you want to us.' (But little did Nahash know, help was already on the way.)

11.text: Next morning, Saul split his army into three groups. They attacked the Ammonite camp before sunrise and kept slaughterin' 'em till the sun was burnin' hot. The ones who survived? They scattered so bad, not even two of 'em was left together.

12.text: After the fight, the people was like, 'Who was it that said, "Saul can't be our king?" Bring 'em here so we can kill 'em.'

13.text: But Saul said, 'Nah, not today. The Lord just gave Israel a huge victory—we ain't killin' nobody today.'

14.text: Then Samuel said, 'Aight, everybody, let's go to Gilgal and officially crown Saul as king.'

15.text: So everybody pulled up to Gilgal, made Saul king before the Lord, offered peace offerings, and had a big celebration. Israel turned up that day.

1.text: Then Samuel told all of Israel, 'Aight, I did what y'all wanted—I gave y'all a king.'

2.text: 'Now look—there he go, y'all king, walkin' ahead of y'all. Meanwhile, I'm old now, got gray hairs, and my sons are with y'all. I been leadin' y'all since I was a kid.'

3.text: 'So tell me—have I ever taken anything from y'all? Anybody's ox? Anybody's donkey? Did I cheat anybody? Did I take bribes to look the other way? If so, let me know—I'll pay it back.'

4.text: The people said, 'Nah, you never cheated us, oppressed us, or took nothin' from nobody.'

5.text: Samuel said, 'Aight, y'all heard that! The Lord and His anointed one are my witnesses today that I ain't do y'all dirty.' They replied, 'Yeah, we witness.'

6.text: Then Samuel told 'em, 'Look, it was the Lord who raised up Moses and Aaron and brought y'all ancestors outta Egypt.'

7.text: 'Now stand still while I run down how the Lord been good to y'all from the very beginning.'

8.text: 'When Jacob's people was stuck in Egypt, they cried out to the Lord, and He sent Moses and Aaron to get 'em out and bring 'em here.'

9.text: 'But soon as they got comfortable, they forgot the Lord. So He let their enemies take over—Sisera, the Philistines, and Moab's king all came through and started oppressin' them.'

10.text: 'Then they cried out again, sayin', "We messed up! We turned away from You and started worshipin' Baal and Ashtoreth. Please save us, and we'll serve You!"'

11.text: 'So the Lord sent y'all Jerubbaal (Gideon), Bedan, Jephthah, and even me to rescue y'all from your enemies. And y'all was safe again.'

12.text: 'But when y'all saw Nahash, king of the Ammonites, comin' for y'all, instead of trustin' God, y'all said, "Nah, we need a king to rule us!" even though God was already your King.'

13.text: 'Well, here he is—the king y'all asked for. The Lord gave him to y'all.'

14.text: 'Now listen—if y'all fear the Lord, serve Him, and obey Him, both you and your king will be straight with God.'

15.text: 'But if y'all don't obey and start wildin' again? The Lord's hand gon' be against y'all, just like He was against y'all ancestors.'

16.text: 'Now watch this—the Lord 'bout to show y'all a sign right now.'

17.text: 'Ain't it wheat harvest season right now? I'ma ask the Lord to send thunder and rain so y'all see just how serious y'all messed up by askin' for a king.'

18.text: Then Samuel prayed, and just like that, God sent thunder and rain. The people got shook and was terrified of the Lord and Samuel.

19.text: They told Samuel, 'Please pray for us! We already messed up so much, and now we added askin' for a king to our sins! Don't let us die!'

20.text: Samuel told 'em, 'Don't be scared. Yeah, y'all messed up, but don't turn away from the Lord. Y'all still gotta serve Him with all your heart.'

21.text: 'And don't start chasin' after nonsense—idols can't help or save y'all. They worthless.'

22.text: 'The Lord ain't gon' give up on y'all, 'cause His name too great. He chose y'all as His people, and that ain't changin'.'

23.text: 'And as for me? I'ma keep prayin' for y'all. I ain't gon' stop, 'cause that would be a sin against the Lord. Plus, I'ma keep teachin' y'all the right way.'

24.text: 'Y'all need to fear the Lord and serve Him for real, with all your heart. Just think about everything He's done for y'all.'

25.text: 'But if y'all keep actin' up and doin' wickedness? Y'all and your king gon' be wiped out.'

1.text: Saul had been king for a year, and by the time he hit his second year, he started picking his army.

2.text: He chose 3,000 soldiers—2,000 stayed with him in Michmash and Bethel, and the other 1,000 was with Jonathan in Gibeah. The rest? He sent 'em home.

3.text: Jonathan took the fight to the Philistine outpost at Geba and won. The Philistines heard 'bout it, and Saul put out a war announcement all over Israel: 'Yo, let every Hebrew hear this!'

4.text: All of Israel heard what happened, and the Philistines was mad. So Israel gathered with Saul at Gilgal, ready for whatever.

5.text: But the Philistines pulled up deep—they had 30,000 chariots, 6,000 horsemen, and troops as many as the sand on the beach. They set up camp at Michmash, east of Beth Aven.

6.text: When Israel saw how deep the Philistines rolled in, they got scared. Some ran and hid in caves, bushes, rocks, pits—wherever they could.

7.text: Others ran across the Jordan River to Gad and Gilead. Meanwhile, Saul was still at Gilgal, and his troops? Shakin' in their boots.

8.text: Saul waited seven days, just like Samuel told him. But when Samuel ain't show up, his troops started scatterin'.

9.text: So Saul said, 'Bring me the burnt offering and peace offering.' Then he did it himself.

10.text: And just as soon as he finished? Samuel showed up. Saul went out to greet him.

11.text: Samuel was like, 'What did you just do?!' Saul said, 'Look, man, I saw my troops leavin' me, you ain't show up on time, and the Philistines were closing in at Michmash—'

12.text: 'So I was like, "I gotta do somethin' before the Philistines attack!" So I forced myself to offer the burnt offering.'

13.text: Samuel shook his head, 'You played yourself. You ain't follow the Lord's orders. If you had, your kingdom would've lasted forever.'

14.text: 'But now? Your kingdom is done. The Lord already picked someone better than you, someone after His own heart, 'cause you ain't listen to Him.'

15.text: Then Samuel left Gilgal and went to Gibeah. Meanwhile, Saul checked his army—only 600 men left.

16.text: Saul, Jonathan, and the soldiers stayed in Gibeah, while the Philistines set up at Michmash.

17.text: Then the Philistine raiders split into three squads—one went toward Ophrah in Shual,

18.text: Another went toward Beth Horon, and the last toward the Valley of Zeboim, near the wilderness.

19.text: Israel had no blacksmiths—Philistines made sure of that. They ain't want the Hebrews makin' swords or spears.

20.text: So anytime an Israelite needed to sharpen a tool—plow, ax, sickle—they had to go to the Philistines.

21.text: And the Philistines charged them for it. Even to sharpen basic tools.

22.text: So when it was time for battle, guess what? Ain't nobody in Israel had a sword or spear—except Saul and Jonathan.

23.text: Meanwhile, the Philistine outpost took position at Michmash.

1.text: One day, Jonathan, Saul's son, told his armor-bearer, 'Ayo, let's go check out the Philistine outpost on the other side.' But he ain't tell his dad.

2.text: Meanwhile, Saul was chillin' on the outskirts of Gibeah, sittin' under a pomegranate tree at Migron with about 600 soldiers.

3.text: Ahijah, the priest from Shiloh, was there too, rockin' the ephod. But nobody knew Jonathan had already dipped.

4.text: To get to the Philistine outpost, Jonathan had to cross a narrow pass between two big ol' rocks—one called Bozez, the other Seneh.

5.text: One rock was facin' north toward Michmash, the other south toward Gibeah.

6.text: Jonathan told his armor-bearer, 'Look, let's go up to these uncircumcised Philistines. Maybe the Lord will help us out. 'Cause with God? It don't matter if we got a whole army or just a few—He can still win.'

7.text: His armor-bearer was like, 'I'm with you all the way. Do whatever you feel is right.'

8.text: Jonathan was like, 'Aight, here's the plan. We gon' step out and let them see us.'

9.text: 'If they tell us, "Stay put, we comin' to y'all," we won't move.'

10.text: 'But if they say, "Come up here," that's our sign that the Lord already gave us the win.'

11.text: So they stepped out, and the Philistines saw 'em. They laughed and said, 'Look at these Hebrews crawlin' out they hidey holes!'

12.text: Then the Philistines yelled, 'Come up here! We got somethin' for y'all!' Jonathan turned to his armor-bearer and said, 'That's our sign! Let's go!'

13.text: So Jonathan climbed up on his hands and knees, with his armor-bearer right behind him. They started droppin' Philistines left and right.

14.text: That first attack? Jonathan and his guy took out 20 men in an area no bigger than half an acre.

15.text: Then the panic hit. In the Philistine camp, in the field—everybody started trippin'. Even the raiders freaked out. Then the ground started shaking. God was messin' with them for real.

16.text: Back in Gibeah, Saul's lookouts saw the Philistine army in full chaos—runnin' everywhere.

17.text: Saul was like, 'Wait… who's missing from our squad?' So they did a roll call and realized Jonathan and his armor-bearer was gone.

18.text: Saul told the priest, 'Bring the Ark of God!' (Back then, the Ark stayed with Israel.)

19.text: But while Saul was talkin' to the priest, the noise from the Philistine camp kept gettin' crazier. So Saul cut him off and said, 'Forget that! Let's go!'

20.text: Saul and his whole squad rushed into the battle, and guess what? The Philistines was fightin' EACH OTHER! Total confusion.

21.text: Even the Israelites who had been with the Philistines before, servin' them? They flipped sides and started fightin' for Saul and Jonathan.

22.text: Same with the Israelites that was hidin' in the mountains. When they saw the Philistines runnin'? They jumped in too!

23.text: That day, the Lord saved Israel, and the battle moved on to Beth Aven.

24.text: Now, the soldiers was struggling, 'cause Saul had made a dumb rule: 'Nobody eats until we finish beatin' our enemies—or else they cursed!'

25.text: They came up to a forest, and honey was drippin' everywhere.

26.text: But because of Saul's rule, nobody touched it, even though they was hungry as ever.

27.text: But Jonathan ain't know about the rule—so he dipped his staff in some honey, ate it, and felt better instantly.

28.text: Somebody told him, 'Bruh, your dad said anybody who eats today is cursed. Now look at us—we all about to pass out!'

29.text: Jonathan was like, 'Man, my dad messed up. Look at me—I ate some honey, and I feel good!'

30.text: 'If we woulda been eatin' today, we coulda whooped the Philistines even harder!'

31.text: By the time they chased the Philistines to Aijalon, the soldiers was dead tired.

32.text: So they rushed to the spoils, killin' sheep, oxen, and calves. But they ate the meat WITH the blood still in it.

33.text: Somebody told Saul, 'Yo, the people sinnin'—they eatin' with the blood!' Saul was like, 'Y'all messed up. Bring me a big stone right now!'

34.text: Then he told the people, 'Bring your animals here and kill 'em properly. Don't be sinnin' like this.' So everybody brought their animals and cooked them right.

35.text: Then Saul built an altar to the Lord—his first one.

36.text: Saul was like, 'Let's chase the Philistines all night and take all their stuff till morning!' The people said, 'Bet.' But the priest was like, 'Uh… shouldn't we ask God first?'

37.text: So Saul asked God, 'Should we chase 'em? You gon' give 'em to us?' But God ain't answer.

38.text: Saul was like, 'Something wrong. Somebody sinned today, and we gotta figure out who.'

39.text: 'I swear, even if it's Jonathan, my son—he gon' die.' But nobody said nothin'.

40.text: Saul said, 'Me and Jonathan on this side, everybody else on that side.' The people was like, 'Do what you gotta do.'

41.text: Then Saul asked God to show the truth, and the lot fell on him and Jonathan.

42.text: So he cast the lot again—this time it landed on Jonathan.

43.text: Saul was like, 'What did you do?!' Jonathan said, 'All I did was eat a lil' honey… so now I gotta die?'

44.text: Saul was serious. 'God help me if I don't kill you today, Jonathan.'

45.text: But the people was like, 'Nah, we ain't lettin' you kill him! Jonathan just helped us win this battle—he was workin' with God today!' So they saved Jonathan's life.

46.text: After that, Saul stopped chasing the Philistines, and they went back home.

47.text: Saul ruled over Israel and fought everybody—Moab, Ammon, Edom, Zobah, and the Philistines. Wherever he went, he caused problems.

48.text: He built up his army, crushed the Amalekites, and saved Israel from its enemies.

49.text: Saul had three sons—Jonathan, Jishui, and Malchishua. His daughters were Merab and Michal.

50.text: His wife was Ahinoam, daughter of Ahimaaz. His army commander? Abner, son of Saul's uncle Ner.

51.text: Saul's daddy was Kish, and Abner's daddy was Ner—both of them was sons of Abiel.

52.text: And every time Saul saw a strong warrior, he snatched him up for his army.

1.text: Samuel told Saul, 'The Lord sent me to anoint you as king over Israel. Now, you gotta listen to Him.'

2.text: 'This what the Lord says: Amalek messed up when they attacked My people back when they was leavin' Egypt.'

3.text: 'So now, I need you to wipe them out completely—every man, woman, child, ox, sheep, camel, and donkey. No survivors.'

4.text: So Saul gathered his troops at Telaim—200,000 foot soldiers plus 10,000 from Judah.

5.text: They rolled up on the Amalekite city and got ready to attack.

6.text: Saul told the Kenites, 'Ayo, y'all better dip before y'all get caught up in this. Y'all showed Israel love when we left Egypt, so I ain't tryna wipe y'all out too.' So the Kenites bounced.

7.text: Then Saul and his army crushed the Amalekites, from Havilah to Shur, near Egypt.

8.text: But instead of killin' everybody, Saul took King Agag alive and killed the rest of the Amalekites.

9.text: But Saul and his people kept all the best livestock—the sheep, oxen, and lambs. They only destroyed the weak stuff.

10.text: Then the Lord spoke to Samuel:

11.text: 'I regret makin' Saul king—he turned his back on Me and ain't do what I said.' Samuel was heartbroken and prayed all night.

12.text: Early next morning, Samuel went to find Saul. But folks told him, 'Yo, Saul set up a monument for himself in Carmel and then left for Gilgal.'

13.text: When Samuel found him, Saul was like, 'Blessed be the Lord! I did exactly what He said!'

14.text: Samuel was like, 'Then why do I hear sheep and oxen right now?'

15.text: Saul tried to cover up: 'Oh, the troops kept the best livestock to sacrifice to the Lord. But don't worry—we destroyed the rest!'

16.text: Samuel cut him off: 'Stop talking! Let me tell you what the Lord told me last night.' Saul was like, 'Go ahead.'

17.text: Samuel said, 'Remember when you was small-time? The Lord still made you king.'

18.text: 'He sent you on a mission—wipe out the Amalekites, no mercy.'

19.text: 'So why you ain't obey? Why you kept the loot and did exactly what God said not to do?'

20.text: Saul tried to justify himself: 'I did obey! I took the troops, destroyed the Amalekites, and only brought back Agag.'

21.text: 'And okay, yeah, we kept the best livestock—but only to sacrifice to God!'

22.text: Samuel said, 'You think God wants sacrifices more than obedience? Nah. Obeying is better than sacrificing.'

23.text: 'Rebellion is just like witchcraft, and stubbornness is as bad as idolatry. Since you rejected the Lord's word? He just rejected you as king.'

24.text: Saul finally admitted, 'I messed up. I was scared of the people, so I did what they wanted instead of obeying God.'

25.text: 'Please forgive me! Come with me so I can worship the Lord!'

26.text: But Samuel said, 'Nah. You rejected the Lord, now He rejected you as king.'

27.text: Samuel turned to leave, but Saul grabbed his robe—and it tore!

28.text: Samuel turned back and said, 'Just like that, the Lord has torn the kingdom from you today. He already picked someone better than you.'

29.text: 'And don't think He gon' change His mind. God ain't human—He don't backtrack.'

30.text: Saul was desperate: 'I know I messed up! But at least honor me in front of the people! Come with me so I can worship the Lord!'

31.text: So Samuel went with him, and Saul worshiped.

32.text: Then Samuel said, 'Bring me King Agag.' Agag showed up all nervous, thinkin', 'Maybe they'll let me live.'

33.text: But Samuel said, 'Your sword made women childless? Now your mama gon' be childless too.' Then Samuel hacked Agag to pieces in Gilgal.

34.text: Then Samuel went back to Ramah, and Saul went to Gibeah.

35.text: Samuel never saw Saul again after that, but he still mourned for him. And the Lord regretted makin' Saul king.

1.text: The Lord told Samuel, 'How long you gon' sit here cryin' over Saul? I already rejected him as king. Get up, fill your horn with oil, and go to Jesse in Bethlehem—I already picked one of his sons to be king.'

2.text: Samuel was like, 'How I'ma do that? If Saul hears about it, he gon' kill me.' But the Lord said, 'Take a young cow with you and say you comin' to offer a sacrifice.'

3.text: 'Invite Jesse to the sacrifice, and I'ma tell you exactly who to anoint.'

4.text: Samuel did what God told him and went to Bethlehem. When the town elders saw him, they got shook and asked, 'Yo, you comin' in peace?'

5.text: Samuel said, 'Yeah, don't trip—I'm here to offer a sacrifice to the Lord. Get y'all selves ready and come with me.' Then he had Jesse and his sons get prepared for the sacrifice too.

6.text: When Samuel saw Eliab, he thought, 'Oh yeah, this gotta be the Lord's chosen one.'

7.text: But the Lord told Samuel, 'Nah, don't go off looks or height. I already rejected him. Humans look at the outside, but I look at the heart.'

8.text: Then Jesse brought up Abinadab, but Samuel said, 'Nope, not him either.'

9.text: Then Jesse brought up Shammah, but Samuel was like, 'Nah, not him either.'

10.text: Jesse ran through seven sons, but Samuel was like, 'The Lord ain't picked none of these.'

11.text: Samuel asked Jesse, 'You got any more sons?' Jesse said, 'Yeah, but he the youngest—he out watchin' the sheep.' Samuel said, 'Go get him. We ain't sittin' down 'til he gets here.'

12.text: So Jesse sent for him. David pulled up—he was young, handsome, and had bright eyes. The Lord said, 'That's the one. Get up and anoint him.'

13.text: So Samuel took his horn of oil and anointed David in front of his brothers. From that day on, the Spirit of the Lord was with David strong. Then Samuel left for Ramah.

14.text: Meanwhile, the Spirit of the Lord left Saul, and an evil spirit from the Lord started messin' with him.

15.text: Saul's servants told him, 'Yo, we can tell something is off with you—this spirit from God got you all messed up.'

16.text: 'Let us find somebody who can play the harp real good. Whenever that spirit comes on you, he'll play, and you'll feel better.'

17.text: Saul said, 'Find me somebody good at playin' and bring him to me.'

18.text: One of the servants said, 'I know a dude. Jesse's son, David—he play real good, plus he brave, smart, and good lookin'—and the Lord is with him.'

19.text: So Saul sent messengers to Jesse, sayin', 'Send me David, your son—the one with the sheep.'

20.text: Jesse sent David to Saul with a donkey loaded with bread, wine, and a goat.

21.text: David came to Saul, stood before him, and Saul took a real liking to him—made him his armor-bearer.

22.text: Saul sent word back to Jesse, 'Let David stay with me—he cool with me.'

23.text: And whenever that evil spirit came on Saul, David would play his harp, and Saul would feel better—the spirit would leave him alone.

1.text: The Philistines gathered their army at Sochoh, a town in Judah, and camped between Sochoh and Azekah, in Ephes Dammim.

2.text: Saul and the Israelite army set up in the Valley of Elah, lining up against the Philistines.

3.text: The Philistines were on one mountain, the Israelites on another mountain, with a valley in between.

4.text: Then their champion stepped out—Goliath from Gath. This dude was huge—over nine feet tall.

5.text: He had a bronze helmet, a coat of armor that weighed 125 pounds.

6.text: Bronze armor on his legs, a huge javelin slung on his back.

7.text: His spear was massive, and the spearhead alone weighed 15 pounds. A shield-bearer walked ahead of him.

8.text: Goliath stepped forward and called out to Israel: 'Why y'all even tryna fight? Ain't I a Philistine? Ain't y'all just Saul's servants? Pick one man to fight me!'

9.text: 'If he kills me, we'll be y'all's slaves. But if I kill him, y'all gon' be our slaves.'

10.text: 'I challenge y'all today—send somebody out! Let's do this!'

11.text: Saul and all of Israel heard Goliath's words and was shook—straight-up terrified.

12.text: David was the youngest son of Jesse, an old man from Bethlehem, Judah.

13.text: Jesse's three oldest sons had already gone to war with Saul—Eliab, Abinadab, and Shammah.

14.text: David was the youngest—his three brothers followed Saul,

15.text: But David still went back and forth between Saul and home to take care of his father's sheep in Bethlehem.

16.text: For 40 days, Goliath came out every morning and evening to challenge Israel.

17.text: One day, Jesse told David, 'Take this grain and bread to your brothers at the camp.'

18.text: 'Also, take these ten cheeses to the commander. Check on your brothers and bring back word.'

19.text: Saul and the army was in the Valley of Elah, facing off against the Philistines.

20.text: David got up early, left the sheep with a caretaker, packed up the food, and headed to the camp.

21.text: By the time he got there, the armies were lined up, getting ready to fight.

22.text: David dropped off the supplies with the keeper and ran up to greet his brothers.

23.text: While he was talking, Goliath showed up again, saying the same challenge as before—and David heard him.

24.text: As soon as the Israelite soldiers saw Goliath, they ran in fear.

25.text: They told David, 'You seen this dude?! He's disrespecting Israel! The king said whoever kills him gets money, his daughter, and tax-free living!'

26.text: David was like, 'Wait, what's the reward? And who this uncircumcised Philistine think he is disrespecting God's army?!'

27.text: The soldiers repeated the same reward.

28.text: David's oldest brother, Eliab, heard him talking and got mad: 'Why you even here? Who watchin' them few sheep? I know you just tryna be nosy.'

29.text: David said, 'What did I do now? I'm just askin' a question!'

30.text: Then he turned to somebody else and asked again, and got the same answer.

31.text: When Saul heard David was talkin' like this, he sent for him.

32.text: David told Saul, 'Ain't nobody gotta be scared—I'll fight him!'

33.text: Saul was like, 'Boy, you can't fight him—you just a kid! He been a warrior since birth.'

34.text: David said, 'I take care of my daddy's sheep. When a lion or bear came, I handled it.'

35.text: 'I chased it down, snatched the lamb back, and if it came at me, I grabbed it by the beard and killed it.'

36.text: 'I done killed lions and bears—this Philistine ain't no different. He been disrespectin' God's army, and he gon' get handled.'

37.text: 'The Lord saved me from the lion and the bear—He gon' save me from this Philistine too.' Saul said, 'Go ahead then. May the Lord be with you.'

38.text: Saul tried to put his armor on David—gave him a helmet, a coat of armor.

39.text: David strapped on Saul's sword, tried to walk, then said, 'Nah, I can't do this—I ain't used to it.' So he took it off.

40.text: Instead, he grabbed his staff, picked up five smooth stones, put 'em in his shepherd's bag, and had his sling ready.

41.text: Goliath walked toward David, with his shield-bearer in front of him.

42.text: When Goliath saw David, he laughed. 'This the best y'all got?! A lil' pretty boy?!'

43.text: He said, 'What am I, a dog?! You comin' at me with a stick?!' Then he cursed David by his gods.

44.text: Goliath said, 'Come here! I'ma feed your body to the birds and wild animals!'

45.text: David said, 'You come at me with swords and spears, but I come at you in the name of the Lord!'

46.text: 'Today, the Lord gon' hand you over to me—I'ma knock you down, cut your head off, and feed your army's bodies to the birds and beasts!'

47.text: 'Then everybody gon' know God don't need weapons to save—this battle belongs to the Lord!'

48.text: Goliath stepped forward—David ran toward him!

49.text: David reached in his bag, pulled out a stone, and slung it—BOOM! The stone sank into Goliath's forehead and he fell face-first into the ground.

50.text: David killed Goliath with a sling and a stone—no sword needed.

51.text: Then David ran up, took Goliath's own sword, finished him off, and cut his head clean off. When the Philistines saw their champion was dead, they ran!

52.text: Israel and Judah chased them down all the way to Ekron, killin' them as they ran.

53.text: After the chase, Israel plundered the Philistine camp.

54.text: David took Goliath's head to Jerusalem, but kept his armor in his tent.

55.text: When Saul saw David step up against Goliath, he asked his army commander, Abner, 'Who's this kid's daddy?' Abner said, 'I don't know.'

56.text: Saul said, 'Find out who his father is.'

57.text: When David came back with Goliath's head, Abner took him to Saul.

58.text: Saul asked, 'Who's your father, young man?' David said, 'Jesse, from Bethlehem.'

1.text: After David finished talkin' to Saul, Jonathan's spirit was tied to David's—he loved him like a brother.

2.text: Saul kept David with him, wouldn't even let him go back home.

3.text: Jonathan and David made a covenant, 'cause Jonathan loved David like his own soul.

4.text: Jonathan took off his royal robe and gave it to David—along with his armor, sword, bow, and belt.

5.text: David did whatever Saul asked, and he did it well. So Saul put him in charge of the army. Everybody respected him, including Saul's servants.

6.text: One day, when David came back from fightin' the Philistines, all the women came out the cities singing and dancing for Saul, playin' tambourines and music.

7.text: But listen to what they was singin': 'Saul killed his thousands, But David killed his ten-thousands!'

8.text: Saul was heated. He was like, 'Hold up—y'all givin' David ten-thousands, but only givin' me thousands?! What's next? He takin' the throne too?!'

9.text: From that day on, Saul kept his eye on David—he wasn't feelin' him no more.

10.text: The next day, that evil spirit from the Lord came back on Saul, and he started actin' crazy in the house.

11.text: Saul grabbed his spear and threw it at David, tryna pin him to the wall. But David dodged him—twice.

12.text: Saul started getting scared of David 'cause he could see the Lord was with David—but not with him no more.

13.text: So Saul sent David away and made him a commander over 1,000 soldiers.

14.text: David was smart and successful in everything he did, 'cause the Lord was with him.

15.text: When Saul saw how well David was doin', he got even more scared.

16.text: But all of Israel and Judah loved David, 'cause he was always out in the field with them.

17.text: Then Saul told David, 'Aight, I'ma give you my oldest daughter, Merab. Just keep fightin' the Lord's battles.' But in his heart, Saul was hopin' David would die in battle.

18.text: David was humble about it: 'Who am I? Why should I be the king's son-in-law? My family ain't nobody special.'

19.text: But when it was time to marry Merab, Saul gave her to some other dude, Adriel.

20.text: But Saul's other daughter, Michal, had a thing for David. And when Saul heard about it? He was happy.

21.text: Saul thought, 'Aha! She gon' be a trap for him—the Philistines will take him out!' So Saul told David, 'Aight, now you really gon' be my son-in-law.'

22.text: Saul even told his servants, 'Go tell David on the low that the king really likes you, and so do his servants. You should become his son-in-law.'

23.text: But when they told David, he said, 'Y'all think I can just marry the king's daughter like that? I'm broke!'

24.text: Saul's servants took his words back to him.

25.text: So Saul told them, 'Tell David he don't need no dowry—just bring me 100 Philistine foreskins as revenge on my enemies.' (Saul was hopin' David would die tryin' to get them.)

26.text: When David heard the offer, he was like, 'Bet.' He was cool with it.

27.text: So David and his men went out and killed 200 Philistines—brought back double the foreskins to Saul. Then Saul gave him Michal as his wife.

28.text: Now Saul saw for sure that the Lord was with David—and that Michal really loved him.

29.text: Saul got even more scared of David—from that day on, he saw him as his enemy.

30.text: Whenever the Philistine rulers went to war, David was always more successful than Saul's other officers. His name just kept growin'.

1.text: Saul straight up told Jonathan and his servants that he wanted David dead. But Jonathan wasn't havin' it—he loved David like a brother.

2.text: Jonathan warned David, 'My father tryna kill you. Go hide somewhere 'til morning, and I'ma talk to him. I'll let you know what's up.'

3.text: 'I'ma go out there, talk to my dad in the field near you, and see where his head at. Whatever he say, I'ma tell you.'

4.text: Jonathan spoke up for David to his father Saul: 'Look, don't be wildin'—David ain't did nothin' to you. Matter fact, he been nothin' but good to you.'

5.text: 'He put his life on the line to take down Goliath, and God used him to save Israel. You saw it yourself—you was happy! So why you tryna kill an innocent man for no reason?'

6.text: Saul actually listened to Jonathan and swore, 'As the Lord lives, I won't kill him.'

7.text: Jonathan went back to David, told him what happened, and brought him back to Saul. For a while, everything was cool again.

8.text: Another war popped off, and David went out and handled the Philistines again, takin' 'em down bad.

9.text: But then, that evil spirit from the Lord came back on Saul while he was sittin' in the house, spear in hand. David was playin' the harp like usual.

10.text: Then Saul threw his spear at David again, tryna pin him to the wall! But David dodged and got outta there that night.

11.text: Saul sent men to watch David's house and kill him in the morning. But Michal, David's wife, warned him: 'If you don't leave tonight, you dead by tomorrow morning.'

12.text: So Michal helped David escape through a window—he ran for his life.

13.text: Then she took an idol, laid it in the bed, covered it with blankets, and put some goat hair on the pillow to make it look like David.

14.text: When Saul's men came to grab David, she told them, 'He sick.'

15.text: Saul was like, 'I don't care—bring him to me in the bed, I'ma kill him myself.'

16.text: When the men went in, they found the fake David in the bed.

17.text: Saul snapped on Michal, 'Why you lie for him?! You helped my enemy escape!' Michal said, 'He told me he'd kill me if I ain't help him!'

18.text: David ran straight to Samuel in Ramah and told him everything Saul was tryna do. They stayed in Naioth.

19.text: Saul found out David was at Naioth and sent men to grab him.

20.text: But when Saul's men got there, they saw Samuel and the prophets prophesying. Then the Spirit of God hit Saul's men, and they started prophesyin' too!

21.text: Saul heard about it and sent another group—same thing happened. Then he sent a third group—same thing!

22.text: Finally, Saul went himself to find David. When he got to the big well in Sechu, he asked, 'Where Samuel and David at?' Somebody said, 'They at Naioth in Ramah.'

23.text: Saul headed to Naioth, but before he even got there, the Spirit of God hit him too! He started prophesyin' the whole way there!

24.text: By the time he got to Samuel, Saul was stripped down, prophesyin' in the middle of everybody. He was laid out naked all day and night. That's why folks started sayin', 'Dang, is Saul a prophet too now?!'

1.text: David ran from Naioth in Ramah and went straight to Jonathan like, 'Yo, what did I do?! Why your dad tryna kill me?'

2.text: Jonathan was like, 'Nah, that ain't happenin'! My dad don't do nothing without tellin' me first. He wouldn't keep this from me.'

3.text: David swore on it: 'Bruh, your pops knows we tight—he ain't gon' tell you 'cause he don't want you stressin'. But I promise you, I'm one step from death.'

4.text: Jonathan said, 'Whatever you need, I got you.'

5.text: David told him, 'Tomorrow the king expectin' me at dinner. Let me hide in the field 'til the third night.'

6.text: 'If your dad asks where I'm at, tell him I went home to Bethlehem for a family sacrifice.'

7.text: 'If he cool with that, I'm safe. But if he flips out, that means he tryna kill me.'

8.text: 'Look, we in a covenant before the Lord. If I'm guilty of somethin', just kill me yourself—but don't hand me over to your father.'

9.text: Jonathan was like, 'Man, don't say that! If I knew my father was tryna kill you, you think I wouldn't tell you?!'

10.text: David asked, 'How I'ma know what he say? Who gon' tell me?'

11.text: Jonathan was like, 'Come on, let's go outside.' So they stepped into the field.

12.text: Jonathan said, 'God be my witness. After I talk to my dad tomorrow or the next day, if he still cool with you, I'ma tell you.'

13.text: 'But if he tryna kill you, I swear I'ma warn you so you can escape. May the Lord be with you like He was with my father.'

14.text: 'And when you become king, don't forget about me.'

15.text: 'Even when God wipes out all your enemies, don't cut off my family.'

16.text: Jonathan made a covenant with David, saying, 'May God punish David's enemies.'

17.text: Jonathan had David swear again—'cause he loved him like his own soul.

18.text: Then Jonathan told David, 'Tomorrow's the New Moon feast—your absence gon' be noticed.'

19.text: 'In three days, go back to the hiding spot near the Stone of Ezel.'

20.text: 'I'ma shoot three arrows like I'm target practicin'.'

21.text: 'If I tell the boy, "The arrows are close by," you good—come back.'

22.text: 'But if I say, "The arrows are farther!" that means you gotta run, 'cause God sendin' you away.'

23.text: 'And remember—this pact is forever between us before the Lord.'

24.text: David hid in the field, and when the New Moon feast started, Saul was in his usual seat.

25.text: Jonathan stood next to him, Abner was beside Saul—but David's seat was empty.

26.text: Saul ain't say nothin' the first day, thinkin', 'Maybe David unclean.'

27.text: The next day, when David was still missing, Saul asked Jonathan, 'Why ain't Jesse's son come eat?'

28.text: Jonathan said, 'David asked to go home to Bethlehem.'

29.text: 'He told me his family was havin' a sacrifice, and his brother wanted him there. So I let him go.'

30.text: Saul LOST IT on Jonathan: 'You son of a rebellious woman! You really ridin' for Jesse's son?! You shamin' yourself and your mama!'

31.text: 'As long as David alive, you ain't never gon' be king! Now go get him so I can kill him!'

32.text: Jonathan snapped back: 'Why he gotta die?! What did he even do?!'

33.text: Saul threw his spear at his own son! That's when Jonathan knew—his dad was dead serious about killin' David.

34.text: Jonathan stormed away from the table, mad as hell, and didn't eat that day—he was hurt over how his dad treated David.

35.text: The next morning, Jonathan went to the field with a young servant, as planned.

36.text: He shot the arrow, then told the boy, 'Run and find it!'

37.text: As the boy ran, Jonathan yelled, 'Ain't the arrow farther than you?!'

38.text: Then he shouted, 'Hurry up! Don't wait!' (That was David's cue to run.)

39.text: The boy had no clue what was happenin'—only Jonathan and David knew.

40.text: Jonathan gave his bow and arrows to the boy and told him, 'Take these back to the city.'

41.text: As soon as the boy left, David came out of hiding. He bowed before Jonathan three times, crying.

42.text: Jonathan told David, 'Go in peace. We both swore before the Lord—this bond lasts forever, between us and our kids.'

43.text: Then David left, and Jonathan went back to the city.

1.text: David rolled up to Nob and met with Ahimelech, the priest. Ahimelech was lookin' nervous and asked, 'Why you out here by yourself? Where yo' people at?'

2.text: David lied and said, 'The king sent me on a secret mission. Ain't nobody supposed to know about it. My crew meetin' me somewhere else.'

3.text: 'But listen—you got any food? Just give me five loaves of bread, or whatever you got.'

4.text: Ahimelech was like, 'Ain't no regular bread here, only the holy bread—but I'll give it to you if y'all been stayin' away from women.'

5.text: David said, 'We been clean—ain't been with no women in three days. Besides, this bread just regular now, even though it started as holy.'

6.text: So Ahimelech gave him the holy bread, 'cause that was the only bread they had left—the showbread from the Lord's table.

7.text: But check this—one of Saul's men was there too. His name was Doeg the Edomite, head of Saul's shepherds. And he was watchin'.

8.text: David asked Ahimelech, 'You got a spear or sword? I ain't got no weapon 'cause the king's business was urgent.'

9.text: Ahimelech was like, 'Only thing here is Goliath's sword—the same one you took when you killed him. It's behind the ephod, wrapped in a cloth. You can take it if you want.'

10.text: David said, 'Ain't no sword like that one. Gimme that.' Then he grabbed it and got outta there fast.

11.text: David ran to Gath and showed up at King Achish's palace. But Achish's servants was whisperin', 'Ain't this David, the king of Israel? Ain't he the one they sing about?'

12.text: David heard what they was sayin' and got shook—he knew this wasn't a safe place.

13.text: So he started actin' crazy—scratchin' on doors, droolin' all over his beard like he lost his mind.

14.text: Achish looked at his servants and said, 'Y'all really brought me a madman?!'

15.text: 'I got enough crazy people around me—why y'all bring him here? Get him outta my house!'

1.text: David left there and hid out in the cave of Adullam. When his brothers and his father's people heard about it, they went to meet him.

2.text: Folks who was down bad—broke, in debt, or just fed up with life—started gatherin' around David. He became their leader, and soon he had about 400 men ridin' with him.

3.text: Then David went to Mizpah in Moab and told the king of Moab, 'Please let my parents stay with you 'til I figure out what God wants me to do.'

4.text: So David left his parents there in Moab, and they stayed as long as he was in hiding.

5.text: Then the prophet Gad came and told David, 'Don't stay here—go back to Judah.' So David left and went to the forest of Hereth.

6.text: Meanwhile, Saul heard where David and his men were hidin'. He was chillin' in Gibeah, sittin' under a tamarisk tree, spear in hand, surrounded by his servants.

7.text: Saul told them, 'Listen up, Benjamites! Y'all really think this son of Jesse gon' hook y'all up with land and promotions?'

8.text: 'All of y'all conspirin' against me! Ain't nobody told me Jonathan made a deal with David. Ain't nobody ridin' for me! Y'all lettin' David set up on me like this!'

9.text: Then Doeg the Edomite (the same dude that saw David at Nob) spoke up: 'I saw David in Nob with Ahimelech, the priest.'

10.text: 'Ahimelech prayed to God for him, gave him food, and even gave him Goliath's sword!'

11.text: Saul called for Ahimelech and his whole priestly family from Nob. They all pulled up before the king.

12.text: Saul looked at Ahimelech and said, 'Yo, son of Ahitub, you hear me?!' Ahimelech answered, 'Yes, my king?'

13.text: Saul snapped, 'Why you helpin' David?! You gave him food, a weapon, and even prayed to God for him! Now he plottin' on me!'

14.text: Ahimelech tried to explain, 'But wait, ain't David your most loyal soldier? Your son-in-law? A man you trust to lead your armies?'

15.text: 'And this ain't even the first time I prayed for him! I ain't know nothin' about no plot against you!'

16.text: Saul wasn't tryin' to hear it. 'Nah, you gon' die, you and your whole family!'

17.text: Then Saul told his guards, 'Kill the Lord's priests! They ridin' with David and didn't tell me!' But his men refused to touch the priests.

18.text: So Saul turned to Doeg: 'You do it!' Doeg slaughtered 85 priests that day—all of them wearing priestly robes.

19.text: Then Doeg went to Nob and killed everybody—men, women, kids, even babies. He wiped out oxen, donkeys, and sheep too.

20.text: But one priest survived—Abiathar, son of Ahimelech. He ran and found David.

21.text: Abiathar told David what happened—how Saul had killed all the priests.

22.text: David sighed, 'Man… I knew it! When I saw Doeg that day, I knew he was gon' tell Saul. This my fault.'

23.text: 'Stay with me. Don't be scared. Saul want me dead too, so you safer with me than anywhere else.'

1.text: Some folks came and told David, 'Yo, the Philistines out here wildin' on Keilah, robbing their grain and messing up the city!'

2.text: David went straight to God and asked, 'Should I go handle these Philistines?' And the Lord told him, 'Go ahead and take 'em down. Save Keilah.'

3.text: But David's men weren't feeling it. They said, 'Bruh, we already shook just being in Judah. Now you tryna take us to fight Philistine armies in Keilah?'

4.text: So David went back to God for confirmation. And the Lord told him again, 'Go down to Keilah. I got you. You will win.'

5.text: So David and his crew rolled up, fought the Philistines, put them down with a major blow, and took all their livestock. David saved Keilah, just like God said.

6.text: When Abiathar, the son of Ahimelech, escaped and linked up with David in Keilah, he brought the ephod with him.

7.text: Word got to Saul that David was in Keilah, and Saul got hype. He said, 'God done put him right in my hands! He locked himself in a city with gates and bars. Easy win.'

8.text: So Saul gathered his army and got ready to roll down to Keilah to trap David and his men.

9.text: But David got wind of Saul's plan. He told Abiathar the priest, 'Bring the ephod over here. We need to ask God something real quick.'

10.text: Then David prayed, 'Lord, I heard Saul is coming to tear this city up just to get to me.'

11.text: 'Will the people of Keilah turn me in? Is Saul really coming like they say?' And the Lord answered, 'Yeah, he coming.'

12.text: Then David asked, 'But will the people of Keilah give me up to Saul?' And the Lord said, 'Yeah, they will.'

13.text: So David and his 600 men got up outta there quick and went wherever they could. When Saul heard David had escaped, he called off the attack.

14.text: David and his crew stayed hidden in the wilderness, moving through the mountains of Ziph. Saul was on the hunt every day, but God made sure Saul never caught him.

15.text: David knew Saul was out there trying to kill him, so he kept low in the forests of Ziph.

16.text: Then Jonathan, Saul's son, pulled up to David and gave him some real talk, reminding him that God got him.

17.text: Jonathan told David, 'Don't trip. My father ain't gonna find you. You gonna be king of Israel, and I'll be right there beside you. Even my dad knows that!'

18.text: So the two of them made another covenant before the Lord. Then Jonathan went back home, and David stayed in the woods.

19.text: Then some dudes from Ziph ran to Saul in Gibeah and said, 'Yo, David hiding in our woods, up in the strongholds on the hill of Hachilah, south of Jeshimon.'

20.text: 'Come down here, king, just like you been wanting. We'll make sure you get him.'

21.text: Saul was feeling himself and said, 'Bless y'all for looking out for me! Y'all really got my back.'

22.text: 'Now go double-check where he at. Find out his hiding spots. I hear he real slick and hard to catch.'

23.text: 'Look everywhere he might be hiding. Then come back and tell me, and I'll roll out with y'all. If he's anywhere in Judah, I'll find him!'

24.text: So the Ziphites left to go track David, while Saul was still making plans. Meanwhile, David and his men were hiding deep in the Wilderness of Maon.

25.text: Saul and his men went searching for David, and when David got word, he dipped down to a big rock in the Wilderness of Maon.

26.text: Saul's army was on one side of the mountain, and David's men were on the other. Saul was closing in, about to trap David completely.

27.text: But just then, a messenger ran up to Saul saying, 'Yo! Hurry back! The Philistines are attacking the land!'

28.text: So Saul had to break off the chase and go fight the Philistines instead. That's why they named that place the Rock of Escape.

29.text: After that, David left and stayed in the strongholds at En-Gedi.

1.text: After Saul finished dealin' with the Philistines, somebody came up to him like, 'Yo, David hidin' in the Wilderness of En Gedi.'

2.text: Saul grabbed 3,000 of his best soldiers and went out to find David and his men near the Rocks of the Wild Goats.

3.text: On the way, Saul stopped by some sheep pens where there was a cave. He went inside to handle his business—but David and his men was already deep inside that cave!

4.text: David's men whispered, 'Ayo, this it! God done put Saul in your hands! Do whatever you wanna do to him!' David snuck up and cut off a piece of Saul's robe—real quiet.

5.text: But soon as he did it, David started feelin' guilty.

6.text: He told his men, 'I can't do Saul like that. He's still the Lord's anointed—I can't raise my hand against him.'

7.text: So David shut his men down—wouldn't let them touch Saul. Saul finished up, left the cave, and went on his way.

8.text: Then David stepped out the cave and called after Saul: 'My king!' When Saul turned around, David bowed low.

9.text: David asked, 'Why you listenin' to folks sayin' I'm out to get you?'

10.text: 'You just saw with your own eyes—God put you in my hands today. Some of my guys told me to kill you, but I didn't!'

11.text: 'Look, I even cut off a piece of your robe! If I wanted you dead, you'd be dead!'

12.text: 'Let God judge between us. I ain't out for revenge, but I'll let God handle it.'

13.text: 'Like the old saying goes, "Evil people do evil things." But I ain't one of 'em.'

14.text: 'Why you chasin' me, king? I'm nobody. I'm just a flea, a stray dog.'

15.text: 'Let God handle this. Let Him judge me right.'

16.text: When David finished talkin', Saul was shook. He started cryin'.

17.text: Saul told David, 'You a better man than me. You treated me good, but I been tryna do you dirty.'

18.text: 'Today, you coulda killed me, but you let me live. Who does that to an enemy?'

19.text: 'May the Lord bless you for sparin' me today.'

20.text: 'I know now—you gon' be king for sure. God already settin' you up for the throne.'

21.text: 'Just promise me one thing—don't wipe out my family after I'm gone. Keep my name alive.'

22.text: David swore to Saul, then Saul went back home, but David and his men stayed in the stronghold.

1.text: Samuel died, and all of Israel mourned for him. They buried him in Ramah, his hometown. David moved on to the Wilderness of Paran.

2.text: There was a rich man in Maon named Nabal. He had 3,000 sheep and 1,000 goats, and he was out in Carmel shearin' his sheep.

3.text: His wife, Abigail, was smart and beautiful—but Nabal was rude and reckless. He was from Caleb's family.

4.text: David heard Nabal was shearin' his sheep while he was out in the wilderness.

5.text: So David sent ten of his men to greet Nabal in his name.

6.text: They told Nabal, 'Peace to you, your house, and everything you got!'

7.text: 'We know you got your sheep shearers workin'—just so you know, we never messed with them. We never stole from them while they was out in Carmel.'

8.text: 'Ask your men—they'll tell you. Since today's a feast day, could you spare somethin' for us?'

9.text: David's men told Nabal the message, then waited for his response.

10.text: Nabal snapped, 'Who David think he is? Who this son of Jesse? These days, servants runnin' away from their masters left and right.'

11.text: 'You think I'm just gon' give my food, water, and meat to some random men I don't even know?'

12.text: David's men turned around and went back, tellin' him everything Nabal said.

13.text: David was HOT. He told his men, 'Strap up!' 400 men geared up, while 200 stayed behind to guard their supplies.

14.text: One of Nabal's servants ran to Abigail and told her what went down.

15.text: 'Look, David's men been nothin' but good to us. They never harmed us or stole from us. They actually protected us while we was in the fields.'

16.text: 'They was like a wall around us, day and night, while we took care of the sheep.'

17.text: 'Ma'am, you gotta do somethin'—David is comin' for us. Nabal don't listen to nobody. He reckless.'

18.text: Abigail didn't waste no time. She packed up 200 loaves of bread, two skins of wine, five dressed sheep, roasted grain, 100 raisin clusters, and 200 fig cakes—loaded it all on donkeys.

19.text: She sent her servants ahead of her, tellin' 'em, 'Go on, I'll catch up.' She didn't tell Nabal.

20.text: As Abigail rode up on a donkey, she saw David and his men comin' her way.

21.text: David had just been ventin', 'I protected everything this fool owned, and this how he repays me?!'

22.text: 'May God do worse to me if by morning, every man in Nabal's house ain't dead.'

23.text: When Abigail saw David, she jumped off her donkey, fell on her face, and bowed before him.

24.text: She said, 'My lord, blame me! Please listen to me.'

25.text: 'Please don't take Nabal serious—his name means "fool," and he act just like it! I ain't see your men when they came.'

26.text: 'The Lord stopped you from doin' somethin' you'd regret. Let all your enemies be like Nabal.'

27.text: 'Take this gift I brought for your men.'

28.text: 'Please forgive my husband's foolishness. God got big plans for you, David! You fight His battles, and you stay righteous.'

29.text: 'Somebody tryna kill you, but your life is in God's hands. Your enemies? He gon' sling 'em away like a rock from a sling.'

30.text: 'When God makes you king over Israel, this moment won't haunt you.'

31.text: 'You ain't gotta regret killin' innocent people outta anger. When that time comes, remember me.'

32.text: David took a deep breath, 'Blessed be the Lord for sendin' you to me today!'

33.text: 'Bless you for keepin' me from killin' outta anger!'

34.text: 'If you ain't come, by morning Nabal's house would've been wiped out.'

35.text: David accepted her gift and said, 'Go in peace—I heard you out.'

36.text: Abigail went home, and Nabal was in there drunk off his mind, throwin' a feast like he was a king.

37.text: She ain't tell him nothin' 'til the next morning. When he sobered up, she told him everything.

38.text: Soon as he heard it, his heart gave out. He turned stiff like stone. Ten days later, the Lord struck him, and he died.

39.text: David heard Nabal was dead and said, 'Praise the Lord for avengin' me! He stopped me from doin' evil and paid Nabal back Himself.'

40.text: Then David sent messengers to Abigail, askin' her to be his wife.

41.text: She bowed low and said, 'I'd be honored to be David's servant—even just to wash his men's feet.'

42.text: She got on her donkey with her five maids, went with David's messengers, and became his wife.

43.text: David also married Ahinoam from Jezreel, so he had two wives now.

44.text: Meanwhile, Saul took Michal, David's first wife, and gave her to another man named Palti.

1.text: The Ziphites ran up to Saul again, tellin' him, 'David hidin' in the Hill of Hachilah, across from Jeshimon.'

2.text: Saul grabbed 3,000 of his best soldiers and rolled out to the Wilderness of Ziph to find David.

3.text: Saul set up camp at Hachilah by the road, but David stayed out in the wilderness. When David heard Saul was comin', he sent spies to confirm it.

4.text: David sent out his spies and got confirmation—yep, Saul really out here lookin' for him again.

5.text: David went to check out Saul's camp and saw where Saul and his general, Abner, were sleepin'. Saul was in the middle, surrounded by his men.

6.text: David turned to his crew and said, 'Who ridin' with me into Saul's camp?' Abishai (Joab's brother) stepped up, 'I got you.'

7.text: That night, David and Abishai snuck into the camp. Saul was knocked out, his spear stuck in the ground by his head, and his army was sleepin' all around him.

8.text: Abishai whispered, 'Ayo, God really put your enemy in your hands! Let me run this spear through him—one hit, I promise.'

9.text: David shook his head, 'Nah, we ain't touchin' God's anointed.'

10.text: 'God gon' handle him—either he gon' die naturally, or he gon' die in battle.'

11.text: 'We ain't doin' it. Just grab his spear and his water jug, and let's go.'

12.text: David snatched the spear and jug, and they dipped. Nobody saw them, 'cause God put everybody into a deep sleep.

13.text: David got to the top of a hill, far enough away, and shouted down at Saul's camp.

14.text: David yelled at Abner, 'Ayo, Abner! You ain't gon' answer me?!' Abner woke up and shouted back, 'Who dat callin' out to the king?!'

15.text: David clowned him, 'Bruh, ain't you supposed to be Saul's top guy? How you let somebody walk right up on the king like that?!'

16.text: 'You failed, man. Somebody coulda killed your king tonight. You deserve to die for that. Look, where Saul's spear and water jug at?'

17.text: Saul recognized David's voice and said, 'Is that you, my son David?'

18.text: David said, 'Yeah, it's me. But why you still out here chasin' me? What did I do?!'

19.text: 'If God sent you after me, then fine. But if people hyped you up, then may God curse them, 'cause they makin' me run from my home, like I don't even belong to God's people.'

20.text: 'Why you treatin' me like I'm a nobody? Like I'm some flea you tryna squash? Like a partridge you tryna hunt in the mountains?'

21.text: Saul broke down, 'I messed up. Come back, David. I ain't gon' try to hurt you no more. You spared my life today. I was a fool.'

22.text: David held up Saul's spear, 'Here it is. Send one of your guys to come get it.'

23.text: 'God gon' reward people who do right. He put you in my hands, but I refused to touch His anointed.'

24.text: 'Just like I spared your life today, I hope God looks out for me too.'

25.text: Saul blessed David, 'You gon' do great things and win big.' Then Saul went home, and David went his own way.

1.text: David was thinkin' to himself, 'Man, one day Saul gon' catch me. Best move is to dip to Philistine territory. Then Saul gon' give up tryna find me.'

2.text: So David took his 600 men and went to Gath, to stay with King Achish, son of Maoch.

3.text: David and his crew lived in Gath with Achish—each man with his family. David had his two wives: Ahinoam from Jezreel and Abigail, Nabal's widow.

4.text: When Saul heard David was in Gath, he stopped lookin' for him.

5.text: David told Achish, 'If I got favor with you, let me live in one of the country towns. Ain't no reason for me to be in the royal city with you.'

6.text: So Achish gave David the town of Ziklag—and from then on, Ziklag belonged to the kings of Judah.

7.text: David stayed in Philistine land for a year and four months.

8.text: David and his men went out raiding the Geshurites, Girzites, and Amalekites—the folks who lived in that land before Israel came.

9.text: Every time David attacked, he left nobody alive—men or women. He took their sheep, cattle, donkeys, camels, and clothes, then went back to Achish.

10.text: Achish would ask, 'Where y'all raid today?' David would lie and say, 'We hit parts of Judah, Jerahmeel, or the Kenites.'

11.text: David made sure not to leave any survivors, so nobody could run back and tell Achish the truth.

12.text: Achish trusted David, thinkin', 'Man, he really turned on Israel. He stuck with me now.'

1.text: The Philistines got their armies ready for war against Israel, and King Achish told David, 'You already know you and your men gotta roll with me into battle.'

2.text: David told Achish, 'You already know what I'm capable of.' Achish said, 'Bet. I'm makin' you my top bodyguard for life.'

3.text: By now, Samuel was dead, and all of Israel mourned and buried him in Ramah. Meanwhile, Saul had kicked out all the mediums and spiritists.

4.text: The Philistines set up camp at Shunem, so Saul gathered his army at Gilboa.

5.text: When Saul saw how deep the Philistines' army was, he got shook—his heart was poundin'.

6.text: He tried askin' God what to do, but the Lord wasn't answerin'—no dreams, no Urim, no prophets.

7.text: So Saul told his servants, 'Find me a woman that can talk to spirits, so I can ask her what to do.' His men told him, 'There's a medium in En Dor.'

8.text: Saul disguised himself, put on regular clothes, and took two men with him. They rolled up to the woman at night, and Saul said, 'I need you to bring up a spirit for me.'

9.text: But the woman was like, 'You know Saul banned all the mediums. You tryna set me up to get killed?!'

10.text: Saul swore to her, 'I promise on the Lord's name, you won't be punished for this.'

11.text: She asked, 'Who you want me to bring up?' Saul said, 'Samuel.'

12.text: Soon as she saw Samuel, she screamed and said, 'Wait a minute—you Saul! You tricked me!'

13.text: Saul told her, 'Don't be scared. What you see?' She said, 'I see a spirit comin' up from the ground.'

14.text: Saul asked, 'What he look like?' She said, 'An old man wearin' a robe.' Saul knew it was Samuel, so he bowed down.

15.text: Samuel was not happy: 'Why you botherin' me?! Why you draggin' me back up?!' Saul answered, 'Man, I'm stressed out! The Philistines at war with me, God left me, and I ain't gettin' no answers. I need you to tell me what to do!'

16.text: Samuel was like, 'If God left you and turned against you, why you askin' me?'

17.text: 'Didn't I tell you before? The Lord already took the kingdom from you and gave it to David.'

18.text: 'This happenin' 'cause you ain't listen when God told you to wipe out Amalek.'

19.text: 'And now, the Lord gon' hand over Israel to the Philistines. By this time tomorrow, you and your sons gon' be dead.'

20.text: Saul collapsed, straight-up laid out on the floor—terrified and weak from not eatin' all day.

21.text: The woman walked over to Saul, saw how shook he was, and said, 'Look, I did what you asked, even though it coulda got me killed.'

22.text: 'Now do what I tell you—eat some food so you got the strength to leave.'

23.text: Saul refused: 'I ain't eatin'.' But his men and the woman kept pushin' him, so he finally sat up.

24.text: The woman had a fat calf at the house, so she hurried up and killed it, made some fresh bread, and cooked a meal.

25.text: She served it to Saul and his men, they ate, and then they left that same night.

1.text: The Philistine army lined up at Aphek, and Israel camped at Jezreel.

2.text: As the Philistine lords marched their troops, David and his men were at the back with Achish.

3.text: The Philistine commanders looked at David and asked Achish, 'Bruh, why are these Hebrews here?!'

4.text: Achish defended David, 'Man, this David—Saul's old guy. He been rollin' with me for years, never caused problems.'

5.text: But the Philistine leaders got mad, 'Send him back! What if he flips on us mid-battle? He tryna win Saul back. Ain't this the same dude they sang about?'

6.text: Achish pulled David aside and said, 'Look, I trust you, but the other lords ain't rockin' with you. You gotta go back.'

7.text: 'I don't want no issues, so go in peace.'

8.text: David was confused, 'What I do wrong? I been loyal. Why can't I fight for you?'

9.text: Achish sighed, 'Man, I see you as an angel from God, but the Philistine leaders don't trust you.'

10.text: 'So get up early, you and your men, and head back at sunrise.'

11.text: David and his crew left early in the morning to return to Philistine land, while the Philistines marched on to Jezreel.

1.text: Three days later, David and his crew pulled up to Ziklag, only to see the Amalekites had run through, raided the south, and torched Ziklag.

2.text: They took all the women and everybody in the city—young and old. They ain't kill nobody, but they kidnapped them all and dipped.

3.text: So when David and his men got back, they saw Ziklag straight up burned down, and their wives, sons, and daughters were gone.

4.text: David and all his people broke down crying, weeping till they ain't have no more tears left.

5.text: Both of David's wives—Ahinoam from Jezreel and Abigail, Nabal's widow from Carmel—had been taken too.

6.text: David was real stressed 'cause his own men was talking about stoning him. Everybody was grieving hard over their families being gone. But David found his strength in the Lord his God.

7.text: David told Abiathar, the priest and son of Ahimelech, 'Aye, bring me the ephod.' So Abiathar brought it over to him.

8.text: Then David asked the Lord, 'Should I go after them? Will I catch them?' And the Lord said, 'Go get 'em! You gon' catch up, and you gon' get everything back!'

9.text: So David set out with his 600 men. When they got to the Brook Besor, some of them had to stay back.

10.text: David kept pushing forward with 400 men, while 200 stayed behind 'cause they was too tired to cross the brook.

11.text: They ran into some Egyptian out in the field and brought him to David. They gave him some bread, and he ate. Then they gave him some water.

12.text: They hooked him up with a fig cake and two clusters of raisins. After he ate, he got his strength back, 'cause he ain't had food or water for three days and nights.

13.text: David asked him, 'Who you with? Where you from?' And he said, 'I'm Egyptian, a servant of an Amalekite. My master left me behind three days ago 'cause I got sick.'

14.text: 'We raided the south side of the Cherethites, hit up Judah, and burnt Ziklag down.'

15.text: David asked him, 'Can you take me to them?' The man said, 'Swear to God you won't kill me or send me back to my master, and I'll show you where they at.'

16.text: So he led them down, and there the Amalekites were—chillin', feasting, drinking, and dancing with all the loot they stole from the Philistines and Judah.

17.text: David and his men ran up on them at dusk and fought them all night and all the next day. Ain't nobody get away except 400 young men who hopped on camels and fled.

18.text: David got everything back that the Amalekites took, even his two wives.

19.text: Not a single thing was missing—young or old, sons or daughters, anything they took. David recovered everything.

20.text: Then he took all their flocks and herds. His men gathered them up and said, 'This David's loot now!'

21.text: David got back to the 200 men who had stayed behind at the Brook Besor. They came out to meet him and the rest of the crew. David greeted them warmly.

22.text: But some of the rougher dudes in David's group said, 'They ain't ride out with us, so they don't get none of the loot! Just give 'em back their wives and kids and send them on their way.'

23.text: David said, 'Nah, fam. We not about to do that. The Lord blessed us and kept us safe, letting us take out the enemy that came for us.'

24.text: 'Matter fact, the ones who stayed with the supplies deserve a share just like the ones who fought. Everybody eats!'

25.text: From that day on, that became the rule in Israel—whoever holds it down at home gets the same reward as those on the battlefield.

26.text: When David got back to Ziklag, he sent part of the loot to the elders of Judah—his peoples—saying, 'Here's a gift from the Lord's enemies.'

27.text: He sent some to Bethel, to Ramoth in the South, and to Jattir,

28.text: To Aroer, Siphmoth, and Eshtemoa,

29.text: To Rachal, the cities of the Jerahmeelites, and the cities of the Kenites,

30.text: To Hormah, Borashan, and Athach,

31.text: To Hebron, and all the places where David and his men used to run through.

1.text: The Philistines went to war with Israel, and Israel's army couldn't hang. They turned and ran, but a lot of them got dropped right there on Mount Gilboa.

2.text: The Philistines was on Saul and his sons heavy, and they ended up killing Jonathan, Abinadab, and Malchishua—Saul's boys.

3.text: The battle got real bad for Saul. Some archers spotted him and lit him up, leaving him badly wounded.

4.text: Saul turned to his armor-bearer and said, 'Man, just finish me off before these uncircumcised fools get to me and do me dirty.' But his armor-bearer was too shook to do it. So Saul took his own sword and fell on it.

5.text: When the armor-bearer saw Saul was dead, he did the same thing—fell on his own sword and died right there with him.

6.text: So that day, Saul, his three sons, his armor-bearer, and all his men got wiped out together.

7.text: When the Israelites across the valley and beyond the Jordan saw their army retreating and heard that Saul and his sons were dead, they straight up abandoned their towns. The Philistines rolled in and took over.

8.text: The next day, the Philistines came through to loot the dead bodies. That's when they found Saul and his sons lying there on Mount Gilboa.

9.text: They cut off Saul's head, stripped his armor, and sent the news all over Philistine territory—bragging about it in their idol temples and among their people.

10.text: They put his armor in the temple of their goddess Ashtoreth and took his body, fastening it to the wall in Beth Shan.

11.text: When the people of Jabesh-Gilead heard what had happened to Saul,

12.text: Their strongest warriors got up that night, traveled all the way to Beth Shan, and took Saul and his sons' bodies down from the wall. They brought them back to Jabesh and burned them there.

13.text: Then they buried the bones under a tamarisk tree in Jabesh and mourned for seven days, fasting the whole time.

1.text: Solomon, David's son, got solid in his role as king. The Lord his God was with him heavy, and God lifted him up real high in the eyes of the people.

2.text: He hollered at all of Israel—the generals over thousands and hundreds, the judges, and all the big-name folks from the tribes and families.

3.text: Then Solomon and the whole squad went to the high place in Gibeon. That's where the tent of meeting—the one Moses built in the wilderness—was still standing.

4.text: But David had already brought the Ark of God up from Kiriath-Jearim to Jerusalem, where he had set up a special tent for it.

5.text: Now the bronze altar that Bezalel (the son of Uri, son of Hur) made, that was still up front at the Tabernacle. So Solomon and the whole crowd went there to seek God.

6.text: Solomon stepped up to the bronze altar in front of the Lord's tabernacle and sacrificed a thousand burnt offerings on it. That's some next-level worship.

7.text: That night, God pulled up on Solomon in a dream and said, 'Go ahead, ask for whatever you want—I got you.'

8.text: Solomon said, 'Lord, you really showed love to my pops, David. And now you done made me king in his place.'

9.text: 'So now, Lord God, please make good on the promise you made to David, 'cause you done made me king over a people that can't even be counted—like dust on the ground!'

10.text: 'I need wisdom and know-how, God. Help me lead your people right. 'Cause who else could handle a crew this big and important?'

11.text: God said, 'You know what, since you ain't ask for money, fame, revenge, or a long life—but you asked for wisdom and knowledge to lead my people right? I got you.'

12.text: 'I'ma give you that wisdom and knowledge. But on top of that, I'ma throw in the riches, wealth, and honor too—more than any king before you or after you will ever have.'

13.text: Then Solomon left Gibeon—the place of worship—and went back to Jerusalem to start reigning full-time as king of Israel.

14.text: He started collecting chariots and horses—1,400 chariots and 12,000 horsemen. He kept 'em posted in the chariot cities and some in Jerusalem right by him.

15.text: Solomon had silver and gold all over Jerusalem—it was like having pebbles in the street. And he had cedar trees stacked like regular sycamores in the lowlands.

16.text: Dude had horses brought in from Egypt and Keveh, with the royal dealers buyin' them at market price like it was nothing.

17.text: A chariot from Egypt ran you 600 shekels of silver, and a horse? 150. Solomon's crew was running export deals too—flipping chariots and horses to kings of the Hittites and Syria.

1.text: Solomon had his mind made up—he was gon' build a temple to rep the name of the Lord, and a royal crib for himself too.

2.text: He picked out 70,000 workers to carry the heavy stuff, 80,000 stonecutters to get the rock out the mountains, and 3,600 supervisors to keep everything in check.

3.text: Solomon hit up Hiram, the king of Tyre, sayin', 'Just like you came through for my daddy David with them cedar logs for his house, I need you to come through for me too.'

4.text: 'I'm buildin' a temple in the name of the Lord my God. It's gon' be where we burn sweet incense for Him, keep the showbread on deck, and offer up burnt sacrifices—every morning, every night, on the Sabbaths, New Moons, and all the Lord's holy days. This ain't no one-time thing—this forever for Israel.'

5.text: 'This temple I'm buildin'? It's gon' be somethin' serious, 'cause our God bigger and greater than any other out there.'

6.text: 'But for real, who can even build a house for God? Not even heaven or the heavens beyond heaven can hold Him. So who am I to think I can build Him a place—except just to offer sacrifices?'

7.text: 'So do me a favor—send me somebody who knows what they doin'. I'm talkin' a master craftsman, good with gold, silver, bronze, and iron, who can also work with purple, crimson, and blue fabrics. Somebody who knows how to do engravings and work alongside the skilled brothers my pops, David, already set up in Judah and Jerusalem.'

8.text: 'And send cedar, cypress, and algum wood from Lebanon, 'cause your people know how to chop timber like nobody else. My folks gon' work with your folks on this.'

9.text: 'We need a whole lotta wood, 'cause this temple I'm about to build? It's gon' be grand and straight-up jaw-dropping.'
