3.text: First year, first month of his reign, Hezekiah opened up the doors of the temple and fixed them.

4.text: Then he gathered the priests and Levites and brought them to the East Square.

5.text: He told them, "Listen up, y'all. Get yourselves right. Get this temple right. Clean out all the junk that's piled up in God's house."

6.text: "Our ancestors straight-up abandoned the Lord. Turned their backs on Him. Shut the doors, blew out the lamps, quit burning incense, stopped making offerings—like they just walked away from everything."

7.text: "That's why the Lord's anger hit Judah and Jerusalem so hard. That's why we've been mocked, attacked, and dragged into exile."

8.text: "Look around—our people, our families—we've been takin' losses."

9.text: "But now I'm ready to make a covenant with the Lord, so His anger can turn away from us."

10.text: "My sons, don't slack off now. The Lord picked y'all to stand in front of Him, serve Him, and keep the incense burning."

11.text: Then the Levites rose up: Mahath and Joel from the Kohathites; Kish and Azariah from the Merarites; Joah and Eden from the Gershonites;

12.text: Shimri and Jeiel from Elizaphan's family; Zechariah and Mattaniah from Asaph's line;

13.text: Jehiel and Shimei from Heman's crew; Shemaiah and Uzziel from Jeduthun's line.

14.text: They called their people together, purified themselves, and went to clean out the Lord's temple just like Hezekiah said.

15.text: The priests went deep inside the temple, gathered up all the filth and trash, brought it out to the courtyard, and the Levites took it all to the Brook Kidron.

16.text: They started purifying the temple on the first day of the first month. By the eighth day they hit the outer area. It took eight more days to finish everything. By the sixteenth day, it was done.

17.text: Then they came back to Hezekiah and said, "We cleaned it all—the temple, the altar, the table of showbread, and all the items.

18.text: We even restored the stuff Ahaz trashed during his reign. It's all been purified and set up at the altar now."

19.text: "Also, all the stuff King Ahaz threw out back when he was wildin'? We got it all cleaned up and ready again. Everything's been purified and now it's sittin' right there in front of the Lord's altar."

20.text: Early the next morning, Hezekiah gathered the city officials and headed to the temple.

21.text: They brought seven bulls, seven rams, seven lambs, and seven goats as a sin offering—for the nation, the temple, and all of Judah. He told the priests to offer them to the Lord.

22.text: They killed the bulls, the priests took the blood and sprinkled it on the altar. Same with the rams. Same with the lambs.

23.text: Then they brought the goats for the sin offering, laid hands on them—symbolic transfer of sin.

24.text: The priests killed the goats, sprinkled the blood on the altar to make atonement for all Israel—because Hezekiah said, "This offering ain't just for Judah—it's for the whole people."

25.text: Then he posted up the Levites in the temple with cymbals, harps, and stringed instruments—just like David, Gad the prophet, and Nathan had ordered based on God's command.

26.text: The Levites got on the instruments, and the priests stood ready with the trumpets.

27.text: When the burnt offering started, the worship started. Trumpets blasted. Songs played. All of it was for the Lord.

28.text: The crowd worshiped, singers sang, trumpeters blew—it kept goin' until the offering was done.

29.text: When it ended, the king and everybody bowed down and worshiped.

30.text: Hezekiah and the leaders told the Levites to sing songs from David and Asaph. They sang with joy and bowed their heads low in reverence.

31.text: Hezekiah said, "Now that y'all've rededicated yourselves, bring your sacrifices and thank offerings." So the people pulled up with everything—they brought what was on their hearts to give.

32.text: The numbers? 70 bulls, 100 rams, 200 lambs—all for burnt offerings.

33.text: Plus 600 bulls and 3,000 sheep for consecration.

34.text: There weren't enough priests to handle it all, so the Levites—who were more on point—jumped in to help until the rest of the priests got sanctified.

35.text: There were so many offerings—burnt, peace, drink offerings—the temple was full and active again.

36.text: Hezekiah and the people were rejoicing. God had moved the people's hearts fast—it all came together quicker than anyone expected.

1.text: Hezekiah sent word to all of Israel and Judah—he even wrote letters to Ephraim and Manasseh—inviting everybody to come to the Lord's house in Jerusalem and keep the Passover to the God of Israel.

2.text: The king, his leaders, and the whole assembly had agreed to push Passover to the second month.

3.text: They couldn't keep it at the regular time 'cause not enough priests had gotten themselves ready, and the people hadn't gathered yet.

4.text: But the plan sounded good to the king and everybody else.

5.text: So they sent out a call from Beersheba to Dan—"Y'all come to Jerusalem and celebrate Passover like we're supposed to. It's been way too long since it was done right."

6.text: Messengers ran across the land with the king's letter. It said, "Israel—come back to the Lord, the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. If you return, He'll receive those of you who escaped Assyria's grip."

7.text: "Don't be like your fathers and relatives who disrespected God. Look where that got them—ruined."

8.text: "Don't be stubborn like they were. Surrender to the Lord. Come back into His sanctuary, the one He set apart forever. Serve Him, and maybe He'll turn His anger away."

9.text: "If y'all come back to the Lord, He'll show mercy to your families, even the ones in captivity. He's full of grace—if you reach for Him, He won't turn His back."

10.text: The runners went through Ephraim, Manasseh, all the way to Zebulun—but a lotta folks just laughed and clowned them.

11.text: Still, some people from Asher, Manasseh, and Zebulun humbled themselves and made their way to Jerusalem.

12.text: Meanwhile, God worked on Judah's heart, giving them unity to follow the king's word and the Lord's command.

13.text: A massive crowd gathered in Jerusalem for the Feast of Unleavened Bread in the second month.

14.text: First thing they did? Tore down every altar they could find in the city—smashed the incense spots and dumped it all in the Brook Kidron.

15.text: Then they killed the Passover lambs on the 14th day of the second month. The priests and Levites felt convicted, got themselves right, and brought burnt offerings to the temple.

16.text: The priests took their spots like Moses had instructed, and the Levites handed them the blood to sprinkle on the altar.

17.text: A lot of the people weren't ritually clean, so the Levites had to step in and handle the lambs on their behalf.

18.text: Folks from Ephraim, Manasseh, Issachar, and Zebulun hadn't purified themselves properly, but they still showed up to seek God and eat the Passover.

19.text: Hezekiah prayed, "Lord, forgive everyone who came with a sincere heart—even if they ain't fully clean."

20.text: And God heard that prayer—and healed the people.

21.text: Everybody kept the feast for seven days, full of joy. The Levites and priests praised the Lord daily, singing loud with instruments.

22.text: Hezekiah spoke life into the Levites who were teachin' God's Word, and they all ate together, offered peace offerings, and confessed their sins out loud to the God of their ancestors.

23.text: Then the people said, "Let's run it back!" They kept the feast for another seven days—with even more joy.

24.text: Hezekiah gave the crowd 1,000 bulls and 7,000 sheep. The leaders added 1,000 bulls and 10,000 sheep. A whole crew of priests purified themselves and joined in.

25.text: The entire crew—Judah, the priests, the Levites, Israelites from outta town, foreigners living in Judah—everybody was rejoicing together.

26.text: There hadn't been a celebration like that in Jerusalem since Solomon, son of David, was king. This was historic joy.

27.text: The priests and Levites stood up and blessed the people. Their voices were heard. Their prayers went straight to heaven—God's holy place.

1.text: After all that worship and celebration, everybody who came out from Israel went back to their towns—but not before they smashed every idol and altar they could find. From Judah and Benjamin to Ephraim and Manasseh, they tore down sacred pillars, chopped down wooden images, and wrecked the high places. Once the cleanup was done, everybody headed home.

2.text: Hezekiah set up the priest and Levite crews again, assigning them by their divisions—each one with specific roles: burn offerings, peace offerings, praise, and thanksgiving at the gates of the temple.

3.text: The king also gave from his own stash for the daily sacrifices—morning and evening—and for the Sabbaths, new moons, and other feast days, just like it says in the Law of the Lord.

4.text: He told the folks in Jerusalem to make sure the priests and Levites were taken care of, so they could focus fully on God's law.

5.text: As soon as the word spread, the people responded. They started bringing firstfruits—grain, wine, oil, honey, everything they harvested—and they gave tithes off it all.

6.text: Folks from both Israel and Judah, wherever they lived, brought in their tithes of oxen, sheep, and everything else they had dedicated to God. It was so much, it stacked up in heaps.

7.text: They started bringing it in around the third month, and by the seventh month, they were still piling it up.

8.text: When Hezekiah and the leaders saw all the stacks, they praised God and blessed the people.

9.text: Hezekiah asked the priests and Levites, "What's up with all these heaps?"

10.text: Azariah the high priest (from Zadok's line) told him, "Ever since the people started giving, we've had more than enough to eat—and this overflow? That's just the extra. The Lord really blessed His people."

11.text: So Hezekiah had them build storage rooms in the temple, and they got it done.

12.text: The people faithfully brought in their offerings, tithes, and dedicated items. Cononiah the Levite was in charge, with his brother Shimei as his right hand.

13.text: Under them were a crew of faithful managers: Jehiel, Azaziah, Nahath, Asahel, Jerimoth, Jozabad, Eliel, Ismachiah, Mahath, and Benaiah. All of them followed Hezekiah's and Azariah's orders.

14.text: Kore (son of Imnah the Levite) was the gatekeeper on the east side. He was in charge of the freewill offerings, and made sure everything got distributed properly.

15.text: Under him were Eden, Miniamin, Jeshua, Shemaiah, Amariah, and Shecaniah—faithful workers in the priestly towns. They handed out shares to all the priests, no matter their rank.

16.text: They gave out daily portions to every male from age 3 and up who was registered to serve in the Lord's house,

17.text: including all the priests and Levites, based on their divisions and duties, from age 20 and up.

18.text: Everyone in the records—their kids, wives, sons, and daughters—got taken care of too, because they had been faithful and set apart for God.

19.text: Even in the priestly towns out in the countryside, there were men assigned by name to make sure every male Levite and priest got what they were due.

20.text: Hezekiah held it down all over Judah. He stayed true to what was good, right, and real in God's eyes.

21.text: Everything he did—whether in the temple, the law, or keeping God's commands—he did it with his whole heart. That's why he prospered.

1.text: After Hezekiah did all that right and faithful stuff, Sennacherib, king of Assyria, came for Judah. He set up camp outside the fortified cities, tryin' to snatch them for himself.

2.text: When Hezekiah saw Sennacherib's army posted up with plans to attack Jerusalem,

3.text: he met with his leaders and commanders and said, "Let's cut off all the water sources outside the city." And they helped him make it happen.

4.text: A whole crew came together and stopped up the springs and the stream that ran through the land. They said, "Why should the king of Assyria roll up and find plenty of water?"

5.text: Hezekiah got to work—he rebuilt the broken parts of the wall, built towers, added another outer wall, repaired the Millo in the City of David, and stocked up on weapons and shields.

6.text: Then he appointed captains over the people, gathered everybody in the city square, and told them,

7.text: "Be strong and brave! Don't trip over the king of Assyria or his whole army. We got more on our side than he got on his."

8.text: "He rollin' with human power—but we got the Lord our God with us. He's fightin' our battles." The people felt fired up after Hezekiah's words.

9.text: While Sennacherib was still busy takin' Lachish, he sent messengers to Hezekiah and everybody in Jerusalem.

10.text: They said, "What y'all think y'all doin' stayin' locked up in Jerusalem? Y'all really trust Hezekiah when he says, 'The Lord will deliver us'?"

11.text: "You gon' sit there hungry and thirsty waitin' on this so-called rescue? Hezekiah's got y'all fooled."

12.text: "Didn't that same Hezekiah tear down the high places and altars, and say y'all could only worship at one altar?"

13.text: "Y'all must not know what me and my people did to all the other nations. Their gods couldn't save them from me—

14.text: what makes you think your God gon' do any better?"

15.text: "Don't let Hezekiah gas you. No god has been able to stop me yet—and your God ain't gon' be the first."

16.text: His crew kept trash talkin' the Lord and dissin' Hezekiah too.

17.text: Sennacherib even wrote letters talkin' reckless: "Your God can't save you no more than all them other gods saved their people."

18.text: Then they shouted threats in Hebrew at the folks on the wall—tryin' to scare them into givin' up.

19.text: They talked about the God of Jerusalem like He was just another fake idol made by human hands.

20.text: Hezekiah and the prophet Isaiah cried out to God in prayer.

21.text: And the Lord answered—He sent an angel who wiped out every strong warrior, commander, and officer in the Assyrian army. Sennacherib had to pack up and head home ashamed. And when he got back to his temple, some of his own sons killed him right there.

22.text: So the Lord saved Hezekiah and Jerusalem from Sennacherib and anyone else who tried them. God had their back on all sides.

23.text: Folks from everywhere brought gifts to God in Jerusalem and gifts to King Hezekiah. After that, he was respected by all the nations.

24.text: Later, Hezekiah got sick—real close to death. He prayed, and God spoke to him and gave him a sign.

25.text: But Hezekiah didn't give God the praise He deserved. Pride crept in, and wrath started buildin' over Judah and Jerusalem.

26.text: But then Hezekiah and the people humbled themselves, and the Lord's judgment didn't fall during his time.

27.text: Hezekiah had wealth and honor stacked up. He built treasuries for gold, silver, gems, spices, shields—everything valuable.

28.text: He built storehouses for crops, wine, and oil, and barns for livestock and flocks.

29.text: He even built himself some cities. Dude had property everywhere. God really blessed him.

30.text: He also re-routed water from the Upper Gihon spring through a tunnel into Jerusalem. Hezekiah stayed winnin'.

31.text: But when Babylon sent messengers to check out the miracle that happened in the land, God pulled back for a moment—to test Hezekiah's heart and see what was really inside.

32.text: Everything else Hezekiah did—his faith, his record—it's all written in Isaiah's visions and in the kings' chronicles.

33.text: When he died, they buried him in the royal tombs with David's descendants. All of Judah and Jerusalem showed him love when he passed. Then his son Manasseh became king.

1.text: Manasseh was just 12 when he became king, and he ruled for 55 years in Jerusalem.

2.text: But he was wild—he did evil in the Lord's eyes, copying the same nasty stuff the nations before Israel were doing.

3.text: He brought back the high places his father Hezekiah had torn down, built altars for Baal, made Asherah poles, and worshiped the stars and planets.

4.text: Dude even built altars inside the Lord's temple—the very place God said, "My name gon' stay in Jerusalem forever."

5.text: He set up altars to the stars in both temple courtyards.

6.text: He burned his own sons in fire in the Valley of Hinnom. He was deep in sorcery, witchcraft, mediums, and talking to spirits—straight evil, and God was not pleased.

7.text: He even put an idol he made inside God's temple—the same temple where God told David and Solomon, "This is My spot. My name stays here forever if y'all obey Me."

8.text: God said He'd keep Israel planted in their land if they stuck to His laws—but Manasseh led Judah to wild out harder than the nations God had already destroyed.

9.text: Manasseh dragged Judah and Jerusalem into more sin than the pagan nations ever did.

10.text: God tried to speak to Manasseh and the people, but they wasn't listening.

11.text: So God let the Assyrian army run up on them. They caught Manasseh with hooks, chained him up in bronze shackles, and dragged him to Babylon.

12.text: While he was locked up, Manasseh finally humbled himself and begged the God of his ancestors for help.

13.text: He prayed, and God actually listened. God brought him back to Jerusalem and restored him as king. That's when Manasseh finally realized the Lord was the true God.

14.text: After that, Manasseh built up a wall outside the City of David, all the way to the Fish Gate, and made it tall. He put commanders in all Judah's fortified cities.

15.text: He got rid of all the foreign gods, the idol he had set up in the Lord's temple, and the altars he had built in Jerusalem. He threw them out the city.

16.text: Then he repaired the altar of the Lord and started offering peace and thank offerings again. He ordered Judah to worship the Lord, the God of Israel.

17.text: The people still used the high places—but now they were using them for the Lord instead of idols.

18.text: Everything else Manasseh did—his story, his prayers, and the prophecies spoken to him—was recorded in the book of Israel's kings.

19.text: His prayer, how God listened, his sins, and where he built the idols before he got humble—it's all written in the book of Hozai.

20.text: Manasseh died and was buried in his own house. His son Amon took the throne after him.

21.text: Amon was 22 when he became king, and he only reigned for two years in Jerusalem.

22.text: He did evil too—just like his dad before the change. He kept serving the same idols Manasseh had made.

23.text: But unlike his father, Amon didn't humble himself. He just kept getting worse and worse.

24.text: His own servants plotted and killed him right in his house.

25.text: But the people of the land rose up, executed the conspirators, and put Amon's son Josiah on the throne.

1.text: Josiah was just 8 years old when he became king, and he ruled for 31 years in Jerusalem.

2.text: He did what was right in the Lord's eyes, just like David. He stayed focused—didn't veer left or right.

3.text: In the 8th year of his reign—still a youngin—he started seriously seekin' God. By year 12, he was on a mission. He tore down every high place, idol, and altar in Judah and Jerusalem.

4.text: He smashed the Baal altars right in front of him. Cut down the incense spots, broke the wooden, carved, and molded images to dust, and scattered it over the graves of the folks who used 'em.

5.text: He even burned the bones of those idol priests on their own altars—cleansing Judah and Jerusalem from top to bottom.

6.text: And he didn't stop there—he did the same in Manasseh, Ephraim, Simeon, Naphtali, and all around—swingin' axes.

7.text: After crushin' altars and images all across Israel, he came back to Jerusalem.

8.text: In the 18th year of his reign, after cleaning up the land and the temple, Josiah sent Shaphan, Maaseiah the city governor, and Joah the record keeper to fix up the Lord's temple.

9.text: They gave the money collected from the Levites at the temple—donations from all over: Manasseh, Ephraim, the remnant of Israel, Judah, Benjamin, and back in Jerusalem.

10.text: The funds went straight to the supervisors and then to the workers rebuilding and restoring God's house.

11.text: Craftsmen and builders used it to buy stone and timber for repairs, since the kings before had let things fall apart.

12.text: The workers were faithful. Overseers from the Levites—Jahath, Obadiah, Zechariah, Meshullam—kept things moving.

13.text: Other Levites, skilled in music, handled logistics, supervision, and admin work. Scribes, officers, gatekeepers—everyone had a role.

14.text: While they were handling the money, Hilkiah the priest found the Book of the Law from Moses.

15.text: He told Shaphan, "Yo, I found the Book of the Law in the temple!" and handed it to him.

16.text: Shaphan brought it to the king and said, "Everything you told us to do, we're doing.

17.text: The money's been collected and handed off properly."

18.text: Then he added, "Hilkiah gave me this book," and started reading it out loud.

19.text: When Josiah heard the words of the Law, he tore his clothes—he knew they'd fallen way off.

20.text: He told Hilkiah, Ahikam, Abdon, Shaphan, and Asaiah,

21.text: "Go talk to the Lord for me and the rest of the people. We messed up. God's anger is real 'cause our ancestors didn't follow His Word."

22.text: So they went to Huldah the prophetess—wife of Shallum, keeper of the wardrobe. She lived in Jerusalem's Second Quarter. They told her everything.

23.text: She said, "This is what God says:

24.text: 'I'm about to bring disaster on this place and everybody in it. Everything you read in that book is comin'.'

25.text: 'They turned away from Me, burned incense to fake gods, made Me furious. My anger is comin' and it ain't stoppin.'"

26.text: "'But for the king of Judah—tell him this:

27.text: Since your heart was soft and you humbled yourself, tore your clothes, and cried out to Me when you heard My words, I heard you too,' says the Lord.

28.text: 'I'ma let you die in peace. You won't have to see the destruction with your own eyes.'" So they brought that message back to Josiah.

29.text: Josiah gathered all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.

30.text: Then he went up to the temple with all the people—priests, Levites, everybody. And he read the entire Book of the Covenant out loud so everyone could hear it.

31.text: Standing in front of the crowd, the king made a public promise to God: "I'm gonna follow the Lord with all my heart and soul. I'm keepin' everything written in this book."

32.text: He made everybody in Jerusalem and Benjamin commit to that same covenant. And they followed through—serving the God of their ancestors.

33.text: Josiah wiped out all the idol worship from the entire land that belonged to Israel. He made sure everybody stayed faithful to the Lord as long as he lived.

1.text: Josiah threw a massive Passover for the Lord in Jerusalem. They killed the lambs on the 14th day of the first month.

2.text: He set the priests up in their proper roles and encouraged them to stay strong in serving the Lord's house.

3.text: Then he told the Levites—those who taught the people and were dedicated to God—"Put the ark back in the temple Solomon built. Y'all don't need to carry it anymore. Focus on serving the Lord and His people now."

4.text: "Get ready by your family groups and divisions, just like David and Solomon laid out."

5.text: "Take your place in the temple and help the lay people line up by their family divisions too."

6.text: "Kill the Passover offerings, consecrate yourselves, and help your brothers follow God's Word just like Moses commanded."

7.text: Josiah gave out 30,000 lambs and young goats, plus 3,000 cattle—all from his own stash—for everyone there to use in the Passover.

8.text: His officials also gave generously to the people, priests, and Levites. Hilkiah, Zechariah, and Jehiel gave 2,600 animals and 300 cattle to the priests.

9.text: The Levite leaders—Conaniah, Shemaiah, Nethanel, Hashabiah, Jeiel, and Jozabad—gave 5,000 lambs and 500 cattle to their fellow Levites.

10.text: Everything was ready. The priests were in their positions, the Levites in their divisions, just like Josiah said.

11.text: They slaughtered the lambs, the priests sprinkled the blood, and the Levites handled the skinning.

12.text: The burnt offerings were handed out to the families so they could present them to the Lord—same for the cattle.

13.text: They roasted the lambs just like the law says. The other holy offerings were boiled or cooked, then quickly handed out to the people.

14.text: After all that, the Levites took care of food for themselves and for the priests—'cause the priests had been sacrificing all day and into the night.

15.text: The singers (Asaph's descendants) stayed in their spots, just like David, Asaph, Heman, and Jeduthun had commanded. The gatekeepers stayed at their gates too, since the Levites made sure they were fed.

16.text: The whole Passover and the burnt offerings were done in one day—just like Josiah ordered.

17.text: Everyone who came—Israelites and Judahites—kept Passover and the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven full days.

18.text: That Passover hit different—hadn't been one like it since Samuel's time. Not one king before Josiah had done it like this, with everyone involved.

19.text: And this all went down in Josiah's 18th year as king.

20.text: After all this, when Josiah had finished fixing up the temple, Egypt's king Necho came to fight at Carchemish near the Euphrates. Josiah tried to meet him in battle.

21.text: But Necho sent a message: "Yo, I ain't got beef with you, Judah. I'm on assignment from God to handle another enemy. Don't get in my way—you might end up fighting God Himself."

22.text: But Josiah wouldn't listen. He disguised himself and still went out to fight at Megiddo. He ignored the warning that came straight from God.

23.text: Archers hit Josiah. He told his servants, "I'm hurt bad. Get me outta here."

24.text: They took him from his chariot to another one and rushed him back to Jerusalem. He died and was buried in his family's tomb. The whole nation mourned hard for him.

25.text: The prophet Jeremiah even wrote a whole lament for Josiah. Singers still talk about it when they sing sad songs in Israel—it became a tradition, and it's all written down in the book of Laments.

26.text: Everything Josiah did—his good heart, his dedication to God's law—

27.text: All his actions from beginning to end are recorded in the Book of the Kings of Israel and Judah.

1.text: After Josiah died, the people put his son Jehoahaz on the throne in Jerusalem.

2.text: He was 23 when he became king, but only lasted three months.

3.text: The king of Egypt came through, took him off the throne, and charged the land a heavy tax—100 talents of silver and 1 talent of gold.

4.text: Then Egypt made Jehoahaz's brother Eliakim king and changed his name to Jehoiakim. Meanwhile, Jehoahaz got taken back to Egypt.

5.text: Jehoiakim was 25 when he took over, and he ruled 11 years in Jerusalem. But he did evil in God's eyes.

6.text: Nebuchadnezzar from Babylon came for him—put him in chains and planned to drag him to Babylon.

7.text: Nebuchadnezzar also took some of the sacred items from God's temple and stored them in his own temple in Babylon.

8.text: The rest of Jehoiakim's messy reign is written in the book of the kings. Then his son Jehoiachin took the throne.

9.text: Jehoiachin was just 8 years old when he became king, and he ruled for 3 months and 10 days. He also did evil in God's sight.

10.text: When the new year came, Nebuchadnezzar summoned him, took him and the temple treasures to Babylon, and made Zedekiah king in his place.

11.text: Zedekiah was 21 when he became king and ruled for 11 years in Jerusalem.

12.text: But he did evil too—and didn't listen to the prophet Jeremiah, who was speaking straight from the Lord.

13.text: He even rebelled against Nebuchadnezzar after swearing an oath in God's name. Zedekiah stayed hard-headed and refused to turn back to God.

14.text: The leaders and the people kept spiraling deeper into sin, copying the filthy ways of the nations. They trashed God's temple, the very place He had made holy.

15.text: God kept sending messengers to warn them—early and often—'cause He cared for His people and His temple.

16.text: But they mocked the messengers, ignored the warnings, and laughed at the prophets—until God's anger hit a point of no return.

17.text: So He let the king of Babylon (the Chaldeans) come in and wreck shop. They killed young men in the temple itself, didn't spare anyone—old or young, strong or weak. God handed them all over.

18.text: The Babylonians took every treasure from God's temple, the king's palace, and the leaders. Everything got hauled off to Babylon.

19.text: They burned the temple down, tore down Jerusalem's walls, set the palaces on fire, and destroyed everything valuable.

20.text: Anyone who survived the massacre got taken to Babylon to be servants until Persia rose up.

21.text: This fulfilled what God told Jeremiah—the land finally got its rest. It lay desolate for 70 years to make up for all the ignored Sabbaths.

22.text: In Cyrus's first year as king of Persia, the Lord stirred up his spirit to fulfill Jeremiah's prophecy. Cyrus made an official proclamation across his kingdom, even wrote it down:

23.text: "This is what Cyrus king of Persia says: The Lord God of heaven has given me all the kingdoms of the earth. He told me to build Him a house in Jerusalem, in Judah. So who among y'all belongs to Him? May the Lord be with you—go on up!"

1.text: After Ahab died, Moab got bold and stopped paying tribute to Israel. They was like, 'We out.'

2.text: Meanwhile, Ahaziah—Ahab's son—fell through the upstairs railing in Samaria and got hurt bad. So he sent some messengers out, like, 'Go ask Baal-Zebub, that god over in Ekron, if I'm gonna make it through this.'

3.text: But the angel of the Lord came to Elijah the Tishbite and told him, 'Ayo, get up and intercept them messengers from the king of Samaria. Tell 'em: "For real? Ain't no God in Israel? That's why y'all running to Baal-Zebub?"'

4.text: 'Well, here's the word from The Most High: You ain't getting up off that bed. You finna die right there.' Then Elijah just dipped.

5.text: The messengers turned right back around, and when they got to Ahaziah, he was like, 'Y'all back quick. What happened?'

6.text: They told him, 'Some dude ran up on us and said, "Turn back to the king and tell him: The Most High said, 'So you really out here acting like there ain't no God in Israel? That's why you asking Baal-Zebub? Welp, you ain't leaving that bed—you finna die.'"'

7.text: Ahaziah was like, 'Who? What this dude look like that told y'all this?'

8.text: They said, 'He was wild-looking, hairy, with a leather belt around his waist.' And the king was like, 'Ah, that's Elijah the Tishbite. I should've known.'

9.text: So the king sent a captain with fifty men to go get Elijah. They rolled up and found him chilling on top of a hill. The captain was like, 'Yo, man of God, the king said, "Come down from there!"'

10.text: Elijah hit 'em with, 'Oh, I'm a man of God? Aight. If that's true, then let fire come down from heaven and burn y'all up.' And boom—fire dropped from the sky and wiped them all out.

11.text: So the king sent another fifty soldiers with a captain. They came up and said, 'Man of God, the king said, "Come down here right now!"'

12.text: Elijah was like, 'Oh, I'm a man of God? Bet. If that's the case, let fire come down from heaven and burn y'all up too.' And once again—fire dropped and took 'em all out.

13.text: Then the king sent a third squad, but this captain was smarter. He walked up, dropped to his knees, and pleaded, 'Man of God, please, don't do us like the last two groups. We don't want no smoke—literally.'

14.text: 'Look, we already seen fire come down and take out the last two squads. But please, let us live, man. We just following orders.'

15.text: Then the angel of the Lord told Elijah, 'Go with him, don't trip. You good.' So Elijah got up and went with the captain to see the king.

16.text: When he got there, he told Ahaziah straight up, 'Look, The Most High said: "Since you decided to check in with Baal-Zebub instead of Me, you ain't getting up from that bed. You finna die."'

17.text: And just like that, Ahaziah died—exactly how The Most High said through Elijah. Since he ain't have no sons, his brother Jehoram took over in his place, in the second year of Jehoram, king of Judah.

18.text: Everything else Ahaziah did? If you wanna know, go check the official records—the Book of the Chronicles of the Kings of Israel.

1.text: When the Lord was 'bout to take Elijah up to heaven in a whirlwind, Elijah and Elisha was walking from Gilgal.

2.text: Elijah told Elisha, 'Aye, stay here. The Lord told me to go to Bethel.' But Elisha wasn't having it. He said, 'Nah, as sure as the Lord lives and you alive, I ain't leaving you.' So they kept it moving to Bethel.

3.text: At Bethel, the prophets-in-training came up to Elisha and was like, 'Yo, you know the Lord taking your master away today, right?' Elisha was like, 'Yeah, I know. Chill with all that.'

4.text: Elijah told him again, 'Stay here, Elisha. The Lord told me to go to Jericho.' But Elisha said, 'Nah, I ain't leaving you.' So they went on to Jericho.

5.text: Then the prophets at Jericho pulled up on Elisha and told him the same thing, 'You know Elijah getting taken today, right?' And Elisha was like, 'Yeah, I know. Be quiet.'

6.text: Elijah told him one more time, 'Stay here, the Lord sent me to the Jordan.' But Elisha was locked in. He said, 'As long as the Lord lives and you alive, I ain't leaving you.' So they kept it pushing.

7.text: Fifty of the prophets stood at a distance, watching as Elijah and Elisha stood by the Jordan River.

8.text: Elijah took off his cloak, rolled it up, and smacked the water with it. The water split in two, and they walked across on dry ground.

9.text: After they got to the other side, Elijah turned to Elisha and said, 'Aight, what you want me to do for you before I get taken up?' Elisha said, 'Let me get a double portion of your spirit.'

10.text: Elijah was like, 'Man, you asking for a tough one. But if you see me when I go, then it's yours. If not, then nah.'

11.text: As they was walking and talking, outta nowhere, a chariot of fire with horses of fire pulled up, split them apart, and Elijah got swooped up to heaven in a whirlwind.

12.text: Elisha saw it and shouted, 'My father, my father! The chariots and horsemen of Israel!' And just like that, Elijah was gone. Elisha tore his clothes in two out of grief.

13.text: Then he picked up Elijah's cloak that had fallen and walked back to the Jordan River.

14.text: He took the cloak, smacked the water, and said, 'Where's the Lord, the God of Elijah?' And boom—the water split just like before, and he walked across.

15.text: When the prophets from Jericho saw this, they was like, 'Yo, Elijah's spirit is on Elisha now.' They came up, bowed down, and showed respect.

16.text: The prophets told Elisha, 'Look, we got fifty strong men here. Let 'em go look for Elijah. Maybe the Lord picked him up and dropped him on a mountain or in a valley somewhere.' But Elisha was like, 'Nah, don't do that.'

17.text: They kept pressuring him 'til he got tired of hearing it and said, 'Fine, go ahead.' They sent the fifty men to search for three days, but they ain't find nothing.

18.text: When they came back, Elisha was still chilling in Jericho. He hit 'em with, 'I told y'all not to go, but y'all don't listen.'

19.text: Then the people of Jericho told Elisha, 'Look, the city's nice and all, but the water's bad and the land ain't producing crops.'

20.text: Elisha said, 'Bring me a new bowl with some salt in it.' So they did.

21.text: Then he went to the water source, threw the salt in, and said, 'The Lord says: I just healed this water—no more death or drought from it.'

22.text: And just like that, the water stayed clean from then on, just like Elisha said.

23.text: Elisha left Jericho and went to Bethel. While he was walking, some wild kids ran up on him, clowning him like, 'Go on up, baldy! Get up outta here, baldy!'

24.text: Elisha turned around, looked at them, and called down a curse in the name of the Lord. Next thing you know, two she-bears ran out the woods and tore up forty-two of them kids.

25.text: After that, Elisha went on to Mount Carmel, then back to Samaria.

1.text: Jehoram, Ahab's son, took over as king of Israel in Samaria during Jehoshaphat's 18th year ruling Judah. He held the throne for 12 years.

2.text: Now, he was on some evil stuff, but he wasn't as bad as his mama and daddy. At least he got rid of that Baal statue his father put up.

3.text: But don't get it twisted—he still kept up Jeroboam's mess, the same sins that had Israel out here wildin'. He ain't turn away from that.

4.text: Now, Mesha, the king of Moab, was in the sheep business. Every year, he had to pay the king of Israel 100,000 lambs and the wool from 100,000 rams.

5.text: But soon as Ahab died, Moab was like, 'Nah, we ain't doing that no more,' and they straight-up rebelled against Israel.

6.text: So Jehoram left Samaria and called up all Israel to get ready for war.

7.text: Then he hit up Jehoshaphat, king of Judah, like, 'Ayo, Moab trippin'. They rebelling against me. You riding with me or what?'

8.text: Jehoshaphat said, 'I got you. My people, your people. My horses, your horses. Which way we rolling up?'

9.text: Jehoram said, 'We going through the Wilderness of Edom.' So the kings of Israel, Judah, and Edom all linked up and started marching. But after seven days in the desert, they ran out of water for the army and their animals.

10.text: Jehoram panicked, 'Man, the Lord set us up! He brought all three of us kings out here just to hand us over to Moab!'

11.text: Jehoshaphat was like, 'Hold up, ain't no prophet of the Lord around? We need to check in with Him first.'

12.text: One of Jehoram's servants said, 'Yeah, Elisha, son of Shaphat, is here. He used to be Elijah's right-hand man.'

13.text: Jehoshaphat said, 'Say less. He got the word of the Lord.' So all three kings went to see Elisha.

14.text: Elisha looked at Jehoram and was like, 'Bruh, what you want with me? Go ask your daddy's prophets. Go ask your mama's prophets.'

15.text: Jehoram said, 'Nah, this serious. The Lord brought us here, and now it's looking like He 'bout to let Moab take us out.'

16.text: Elisha said, 'Listen, if it wasn't for King Jehoshaphat standing right here, I wouldn't even give you the time of day.'

17.text: 'But since he's here, get me a musician.' When the music started playing, the Spirit of the Lord came over Elisha.

18.text: Elisha said, 'Here's what the Lord says: Dig a bunch of ditches in this valley.'

19.text: 'You ain't gon' see no wind, no rain, but somehow, this valley gon' fill up with water. You, your army, and all your animals gon' drink plenty.'

20.text: 'And oh yeah, that's light work for the Lord. He also gon' hand Moab over to y'all.'

21.text: 'Y'all gon' run through their cities, take down all their good land, cut down all their trees, and clog up their wells with rocks. Ain't gon' be nothing left when y'all done.'

22.text: The next morning, right when the grain offering was being made, water came rushing in from Edom, flooding the land.

23.text: Meanwhile, the Moabites heard that the kings were rolling up on them, so every man old enough to hold a sword got posted up at the border.

24.text: When they woke up in the morning, the sun was shining on the water, making it look red like blood.

25.text: They said, 'Yo! Them kings must've turned on each other! They done wiped themselves out. Let's go take what's left!'

26.text: So they ran up to Israel's camp, thinking it was all good—until Israel popped out and ambushed them. The Moabites tried to run, but Israel chased them down, wiping them out.

27.text: They destroyed Moab's cities, threw rocks all over the land, clogged up all the wells, and cut down the trees. Only the stronghold at Kir Haraseth was left standing, but even that got surrounded and attacked.

28.text: When the king of Moab saw that he was getting worked, he took 700 of his best soldiers and tried to break through to the king of Edom. But they couldn't.

29.text: In a desperate move, he sacrificed his own firstborn son—the one who was supposed to be king after him—right there on the wall.

30.text: That move sent shockwaves through Israel, and they was like, 'Yeah… we out.' So they packed up and went back home.

1.text: One day, a widow of one of the prophets' followers ran up on Elisha crying. She said, 'My husband—your servant—died, and you know he was a God-fearing man. But now, the bill collectors coming to take my two sons as slaves to pay off the debt.'

2.text: Elisha said, 'What you want me to do? Tell me, what you got in your house?' She said, 'I got nothing but this little jar of oil.'

3.text: Elisha said, 'Aight, go borrow as many empty jars as you can from your neighbors—don't hold back, get a whole lot of 'em.'

4.text: 'Then go in the house with your sons, shut the door, and start pouring that oil into the jars. When one fills up, set it to the side.'

5.text: She did exactly what he said—shut the door, and her sons kept bringing jars while she kept pouring.

6.text: When all the jars were full, she told her son, 'Bring me another one.' But he said, 'That's it, we out of jars.' And just like that, the oil stopped flowing.

7.text: She ran back to Elisha and told him what happened. He said, 'Now go sell all that oil, pay your debt, and live off the rest with your sons.'

8.text: One day, Elisha was in Shunem, where a well-off woman lived. She saw him passing through and insisted he stop by for a meal. From then on, every time he was in town, he ate at her place.

9.text: She told her husband, 'Babe, I'm telling you, this man is holy. He's always coming through here.'

10.text: 'Let's build him a little room upstairs—put a bed, a table, a chair, and a lamp in there—so whenever he comes by, he got somewhere to stay.'

11.text: One day, Elisha was chilling in that room, lying down, and he called his servant Gehazi.

12.text: He told Gehazi, 'Go get that Shunammite woman.' She came and stood before him.

13.text: Elisha told Gehazi, 'Tell her, "Look, you've done all this for us. What can we do for you? You want me to put in a good word with the king or the army commander?"'

14.text: But she said, 'I'm good, I got everything I need among my people.'

15.text: Elisha turned to Gehazi, 'So what can we do for her?' Gehazi said, 'Well, she don't got no kids, and her husband is old.'

16.text: Elisha said, 'Call her back.' She came and stood in the doorway. Elisha said, 'This time next year, you gonna be holding a son.'

17.text: She said, 'No, man of God, don't play with me like that.' But sure enough, she got pregnant and had a son just like Elisha said.

18.text: The boy grew up, and one day he went out to his dad in the field with the workers.

19.text: He started crying, 'My head! My head!' His dad told a servant, 'Take him to his mama.'

20.text: The servant carried the boy home to his mother. He sat in her lap till noon, then he died.

21.text: She took him upstairs, laid him on Elisha's bed, shut the door, and left.

22.text: She called her husband and said, 'Send me a servant and a donkey. I need to go see the man of God real quick.'

23.text: Her husband said, 'Why today? It ain't the Sabbath or a festival.' She just said, 'It's all good.'

24.text: She saddled the donkey and told the servant, 'Let's ride. Don't slow down unless I say so.'

25.text: She pulled up to Mount Carmel, where Elisha was. When Elisha saw her coming, he told Gehazi, 'Look, the Shunammite woman coming!'

26.text: 'Run over and ask her if she, her husband, and her son are good.' She said, 'We good.'

27.text: But when she got to Elisha, she grabbed his feet. Gehazi tried to push her off, but Elisha said, 'Chill, she's deeply troubled. The Lord ain't showed me what's wrong yet.'

28.text: She said, 'Did I ask for a son? Didn't I tell you not to get my hopes up?'

29.text: Elisha told Gehazi, 'Get ready, take my staff, and go. If you see anybody, don't stop to talk—just go lay my staff on the boy.'

30.text: But the boy's mama said, 'I ain't leaving unless you come too.' So Elisha went with her.

31.text: Gehazi got there first, laid the staff on the boy, but nothing happened. He ran back and told Elisha, 'He's still dead.'

32.text: When Elisha got to the house, the boy was lying there, dead.

33.text: Elisha shut the door, just him and the boy, and prayed to the Lord.

34.text: He stretched out over the boy—mouth to mouth, eyes to eyes, hands to hands. The boy's body started warming up.

35.text: Elisha got up, paced around, then stretched out over him again. Suddenly, the boy sneezed seven times and opened his eyes.

36.text: Elisha told Gehazi, 'Call his mama.' She came in, and Elisha said, 'Pick up your son.'

37.text: She fell at his feet, bowed in thanks, then scooped up her son and left.

38.text: Elisha went back to Gilgal, and there was a famine in the land. The prophets-in-training were sitting around, and Elisha told his servant, 'Put on a big pot and make some stew.'

39.text: One of them went out to pick herbs, but he grabbed some wild gourds too. He didn't know what they were, but he cut them up and threw them in the stew.

40.text: When they started eating, they panicked, 'Man of God, there's poison in this pot! We can't eat this!'

41.text: Elisha said, 'Bring me some flour.' He threw it in the pot and said, 'Now serve it.' And just like that, the stew was good to eat.

42.text: One day, a man from Baal Shalisha brought Elisha twenty loaves of barley bread and fresh grain.

43.text: Elisha told his servant, 'Feed it to the people.' The servant said, 'What? This little bit for 100 men?'

44.text: Elisha said, 'Do it. The Lord says they'll eat and have leftovers.' And sure enough, they all ate, and there was some left.

1.text: Naaman was that dude—commander of the Syrian army, respected by his king 'cause the Lord had given him big wins. He was a real warrior, but he had leprosy.

2.text: One time, the Syrians raided Israel and snatched up a young girl. She ended up working for Naaman's wife.

3.text: One day, she told her mistress, 'Man, if only my master could go see the prophet in Samaria, he'd get healed for sure!'

4.text: Naaman went straight to the king and told him what the girl said.

5.text: The king of Syria said, 'Aight, go ahead. I'll send a letter to the king of Israel for you.' So Naaman took off, bringing ten talents of silver, six thousand shekels of gold, and ten fresh outfits.

6.text: When he got to the king of Israel, he handed him the letter, which said, 'I'm sending my guy Naaman to you. Heal him of his leprosy.'

7.text: When the king of Israel read that, he tore his clothes, like, 'What kinda setup is this?! You think I'm God? I can't heal nobody! This man tryna start beef with me!'

8.text: Elisha heard the king was stressing and sent a message: 'Why you tearing your clothes? Send him my way. He gon' learn today that there's a real prophet in Israel.'

9.text: So Naaman rolled up to Elisha's crib with his whole squad—horses, chariots, everything.

10.text: But instead of coming out, Elisha sent a messenger: 'Go wash yourself in the Jordan River seven times. Your skin gon' be brand new.'

11.text: Naaman got mad. 'Hold up, I thought this prophet was gon' come out, call on the Lord, wave his hand over me, and boom—I'm healed!'

12.text: 'Ain't the rivers in Damascus better than this dirty Jordan River? I coulda washed at home!' So he stormed off, big mad.

13.text: But his servants stepped in like, 'Boss, if he told you to do something difficult, you woulda done it, right? This is easy—just wash and be clean.'

14.text: Naaman thought about it, went down to the Jordan, dipped in seven times just like Elisha said—and boom! His skin was smooth like a newborn baby.

15.text: He went back to Elisha with his crew, stood before him, and said, 'Now I know—ain't no other God in the whole world except in Israel. Please take this gift from me.'

16.text: But Elisha said, 'Nah, as surely as the Lord lives, I ain't taking nothing.' And no matter how much Naaman insisted, Elisha wasn't budging.

17.text: So Naaman said, 'Alright then, can I at least take some dirt back with me? From now on, I ain't worshiping no other gods, only the Lord.'

18.text: 'But one thing—when my king takes me to the temple of Rimmon and I gotta bow with him, I hope the Lord understands.'

19.text: Elisha said, 'Go in peace.' So Naaman headed out.

20.text: Now Gehazi, Elisha's servant, was watching all this go down and was thinking, 'Man, my master just let this Syrian slide without taking anything? Nope, I'm about to go get me something.'

21.text: So Gehazi ran after Naaman. When Naaman saw him coming, he got down from his chariot and said, 'Everything good?'

22.text: Gehazi said, 'Yeah, yeah, all good. My master just sent me to tell you that two young prophets just showed up from the hills of Ephraim. Can you hook 'em up with a talent of silver and two fresh outfits?'

23.text: Naaman said, 'Take two talents!' He even had two of his guys carry the silver and clothes ahead for Gehazi.

24.text: When they got to Gehazi's spot, he took the stuff, hid it in his house, and sent the men away.

25.text: Then he went back to Elisha like nothing happened. Elisha said, 'Where you been, Gehazi?' Gehazi said, 'Nowhere, I ain't go nowhere.'

26.text: Elisha looked at him, 'Bruh, you think I ain't see you when Naaman hopped off his chariot to meet you? You really think this was the time to be out here collecting money and clothes, talking about buying olive groves, vineyards, sheep, cattle, and servants?'

27.text: 'Since you wanted to chase that money, Naaman's leprosy finna stick to you and your family forever.' And just like that, Gehazi walked out of there looking white as snow—leprosy all over him.

1.text: The prophets-in-training came to Elisha like, 'Yo, this spot we staying in? It's way too small.'

2.text: 'Let's go to the Jordan, everybody grab some wood, and we'll build a bigger place.'

3.text: One of them said, 'Elisha, you rolling with us?'

4.text: Elisha said, 'Yeah, I got y'all.' So they all headed to the Jordan and started chopping trees.

5.text: But while one of them was chopping, the ax head flew off and fell into the river. He panicked, 'Oh no! That wasn't even mine—I borrowed it!'

6.text: Elisha said, 'Where it drop at?' The guy pointed, so Elisha cut a stick, threw it in the water, and—boom—the iron ax head floated up.

7.text: 'Go ahead, grab it,' Elisha said. The guy reached in and pulled it out.

8.text: Meanwhile, the king of Syria was plotting war against Israel. He told his crew, 'We setting up camp right here.'

9.text: But Elisha got a message from God and told the king of Israel, 'Don't go near that spot—the Syrians waiting on you there.'

10.text: So Israel's king listened and dodged the trap. And this didn't happen just once or twice—it kept happening.

11.text: The king of Syria got fed up. He called his men, 'Aight, who snitching? Which one of y'all working for Israel?'

12.text: One of his servants said, 'Ain't nobody snitching, my king. It's that prophet Elisha—he be knowing everything, even what you say in your bedroom.'

13.text: The king said, 'Find out where he at. I'm sending troops to grab him.' Somebody came back saying, 'He in Dothan.'

14.text: So the king sent horses, chariots, and a whole army. They pulled up at night and surrounded the city.

15.text: Elisha's servant woke up, stepped outside, and saw the army everywhere. He ran back in like, 'Master! What we gon' do?!'

16.text: Elisha said, 'Chill, don't be scared. We got more on our side than they got on theirs.'

17.text: Then Elisha prayed, 'Lord, open his eyes so he can really see.' The Lord did, and the servant saw chariots of fire and heavenly warriors all over the mountain, surrounding Elisha.

18.text: When the Syrian army started closing in, Elisha prayed again, 'Lord, hit 'em with blindness.' And just like that, they all went blind.

19.text: Elisha walked up to them like, 'Y'all in the wrong spot. Lemme take y'all to the man you looking for.' Then he led them straight to Samaria.

20.text: When they got there, Elisha prayed, 'Lord, open their eyes now.' They looked around and realized—uh oh—they were right in the middle of Israel's territory.

21.text: The king of Israel saw them and asked Elisha, 'Should I kill 'em? Say the word, I'll take 'em out!'

22.text: Elisha said, 'Nah, we don't do prisoners like that. Feed 'em, give 'em water, then send 'em back home.'

23.text: So the king made a big feast for them. After they ate and drank, they went back to Syria, and after that, the Syrian raiders stopped messing with Israel.

24.text: Later on, King Ben-Hadad of Syria got his whole army together and laid siege to Samaria, cutting off supplies.

25.text: It got so bad that a donkey's head was selling for eighty silver coins, and people were even buying bird poop for food.

26.text: One day, as the king of Israel was walking on the city wall, a woman yelled, 'Help me, my lord, O king!'

27.text: He said, 'If the Lord ain't helping you, how am I supposed to? Ain't no food in the fields or the vineyards.'

28.text: 'What's wrong?' he asked. She said, 'This woman told me, "Let's eat your son today, and we'll eat mine tomorrow."'

29.text: 'So yesterday, we cooked my son and ate him. But today, when I told her it was her turn, she went and hid her son!'

30.text: When the king heard that, he tore his clothes in grief. As he walked along the wall, people saw that under his robe, he was wearing sackcloth—showing how bad things had gotten.

31.text: The king got mad and said, 'May God do worse to me if Elisha still got his head by the end of today!'

32.text: Elisha was chilling at home with some elders when he said, 'Look, the king's son of a murderer just sent somebody to kill me. When he gets here, shut the door. His master gon' be right behind him.'

33.text: Right as he finished talking, the king's messenger showed up, and the king himself came in after him. He said, 'This disaster came straight from the Lord—why should I wait on Him any longer?'

1.text: Elisha said, 'Listen up, this what the Lord says: By this time tomorrow, you gon' be able to buy fine flour and barley dirt cheap right at the city gate in Samaria.'

2.text: One of the king's officers, who was leaning on him, scoffed and said, 'Man, even if the Lord opened up windows in heaven, that couldn't happen!' Elisha looked at him and said, 'Oh, you gon' see it with your own eyes—but you ain't gon' get to eat none of it.'

3.text: Now outside the city gate, there were four men with leprosy. They looked at each other and said, 'Bruh, why we just sitting here waiting to die?'

4.text: 'If we go in the city, we starve. If we stay here, we starve. Might as well roll up to the Syrian camp and surrender. If they let us live, cool. If they kill us, we was gon' die anyway.'

5.text: So at twilight, they got up and walked to the Syrian camp. But when they got there—nobody was there.

6.text: See, the Lord had made the Syrians hear what sounded like a whole army—chariots, horses, and soldiers. They got scared and said, 'Yo, Israel must've hired the Hittites and Egyptians to ambush us!'

7.text: So they panicked and ran for their lives, leaving everything—tents, horses, donkeys—all still set up.

8.text: When the lepers got to the camp, they went inside one tent, ate good, drank up, grabbed some silver, gold, and clothes, then went and hid it. Then they hit another tent and did the same.

9.text: But then they was like, 'Yo, we wrong for this. This is good news, and we just keeping it to ourselves? If we wait till morning, we might get in trouble. Let's go tell the king's people now.'

10.text: So they ran back to the city, told the gatekeepers, 'We went to the Syrian camp—nobody there! Just horses, donkeys, and all their tents left behind!'

11.text: The gatekeepers spread the word, and soon the whole palace knew.

12.text: But the king was suspicious. He said, 'I bet this a trap. They know we starving, so they hiding, waiting for us to come out so they can rush in and take the city.'

13.text: One of his officers said, 'Look, let's send some men with a few horses to check it out. Worst case, they die like the rest of us starving in here, but at least we'll know what's up.'

14.text: So they took two chariots with horses and sent them out toward the Syrian camp.

15.text: They followed the trail all the way to the Jordan River. The road was littered with clothes and weapons the Syrians had dropped while running for their lives. So they went back and told the king.

16.text: Then everybody in the city rushed out and looted the Syrian camp. And just like Elisha said, flour and barley was selling for cheap at the gate.

17.text: Now remember that officer who doubted Elisha? The king had put him in charge of the city gate, but when the people rushed out, they trampled him to death.

18.text: So just like Elisha had prophesied, the food was sold for the price he said.

19.text: And just like Elisha told that officer—'You gon' see it, but you ain't gon' eat none of it'—

20.text: That's exactly what happened. He saw it with his own eyes, but the people ran him over at the gate, and he died.

1.text: Elisha told the woman whose son he had brought back to life, 'Look, you and your family need to pack up and leave. The Lord about to send a famine on this land for seven years.'

2.text: So she listened to the man of God, took her people, and went to live in Philistine territory for those seven years.

3.text: After the seven years were up, she came back to Israel and went to the king to ask for her house and land back.

4.text: Now at the same time, the king was talking with Gehazi, Elisha's old servant, asking him, 'Tell me some of the crazy miracles Elisha did.'

5.text: And just as Gehazi was telling the king about how Elisha brought somebody back to life, the woman walked in, asking for her land back. Gehazi was like, 'My king, speak of the devil—this the woman right here! And that's her son Elisha brought back to life!'

6.text: The king asked her about it, and she confirmed everything. So he appointed an officer and told him, 'Give her back everything she lost—including all the money her land made while she was gone.'

7.text: Elisha went to Damascus, where Ben-Hadad, the king of Syria, was sick. Word got around that the man of God was in town.

8.text: So the king told Hazael, 'Take some gifts and go ask Elisha if I'm gonna recover from this sickness.'

9.text: Hazael packed up all kinds of stuff—forty camel-loads worth of gifts—and went to Elisha. He said, 'Your boy Ben-Hadad, king of Syria, sent me to ask if he gonna make it.'

10.text: Elisha said, 'Go ahead and tell him he'll recover, but in reality, the Lord showed me he gonna die.'

11.text: Elisha just stared at Hazael for a while, until Hazael started feeling uncomfortable. Then Elisha started crying.

12.text: Hazael was like, 'Why you crying, man?' Elisha said, 'Because I know the evil you about to do to Israel—burning cities, killing young men, smashing babies, and ripping open pregnant women.'

13.text: Hazael was like, 'What? Me? I ain't nobody important. How I'm supposed to do all that?' Elisha said, 'The Lord showed me—you gon' be king of Syria.'

14.text: Hazael left and went back to Ben-Hadad. The king asked, 'What Elisha say?' Hazael said, 'Oh, he said you gon' be alright.'

15.text: But the next day, Hazael took a thick cloth, soaked it in water, and smothered Ben-Hadad till he died. Then Hazael took the throne.

16.text: Back in Judah, during the fifth year of Joram (Ahab's son) ruling over Israel, Jehoshaphat's son Jehoram became king of Judah.

17.text: He was 32 years old when he took the throne, and he ruled in Jerusalem for eight years.

18.text: But he was out here wildin' like the kings of Israel, 'cause he married Ahab's daughter. He was doing evil just like the rest of Ahab's family.

19.text: Even so, the Lord didn't wipe Judah out, 'cause He made a promise to David to keep his family line going forever.

20.text: During Jehoram's reign, Edom got tired of being under Judah and set up their own king.

21.text: So Jehoram rolled up with his chariots, attacked them at night, and tried to hold them down—but his army ended up running back home.

22.text: And from that day forward, Edom stayed independent from Judah. Around the same time, Libnah also broke free.

23.text: Everything else Jehoram did? It's written in the chronicles of the kings of Judah.

24.text: Then Jehoram died and was buried with his ancestors in the City of David. His son Ahaziah took over after him.

25.text: In the twelfth year of Joram (Ahab's son) ruling Israel, Jehoram's son Ahaziah became king of Judah.

26.text: Ahaziah was 22 years old when he started ruling, but he only lasted one year in Jerusalem. His mama was Athaliah, granddaughter of Omri, king of Israel.

27.text: Ahaziah followed the same wicked ways as Ahab's family, since he was connected to them by marriage. He did evil just like them.

28.text: Ahaziah teamed up with Joram, Ahab's son, to fight against Hazael, the king of Syria, at Ramoth Gilead. But the Syrians injured Joram in battle.

29.text: Joram went back to Jezreel to heal from his wounds, and Ahaziah went down to visit him since he was hurt.

1.text: Elisha called up one of his young prophets and said, 'Get ready, grab this oil, and go to Ramoth Gilead.'

2.text: 'When you get there, find Jehu—son of Jehoshaphat, grandson of Nimshi. Pull him aside from his crew and take him to a private room.'

3.text: 'Then pour this oil on his head and tell him, "The Lord says: I anoint you king over Israel." After that, open the door and run—don't stick around!'

4.text: So the young prophet went to Ramoth Gilead.

5.text: When he got there, the army officers were chilling. He said, 'Commander, I got a word for you.' Jehu said, 'Which one of us?' The prophet said, 'You, Commander.'

6.text: So Jehu got up, went inside, and the prophet poured the oil on his head, saying, 'The Lord says: I'm making you king over Israel.'

7.text: 'You gotta wipe out Ahab's whole house to avenge the blood of my servants and prophets that Jezebel killed.'

8.text: 'Ahab's whole family getting cut off—slave and free, don't matter.'

9.text: 'His house finna be just like Jeroboam's and Baasha's—wiped out.'

10.text: 'And Jezebel? Dogs gon' eat her body in Jezreel, and nobody gon' bury her.' Then the prophet opened the door and ran off.

11.text: Jehu came back out, and his people asked, 'Bruh, what did that crazy dude want?' Jehu said, 'Y'all know how prophets talk.'

12.text: They said, 'Stop playing, tell us the truth!' So Jehu said, 'He told me the Lord said, "I anoint you king over Israel."'

13.text: Right then, they took their cloaks, laid them on the steps for Jehu, blew their trumpets, and shouted, 'Jehu is king!'

14.text: So Jehu started plotting against Joram. Now Joram had been at Ramoth Gilead, defending Israel against Hazael, king of Syria.

15.text: But he got wounded and went to Jezreel to recover. Jehu told his people, 'If y'all with me, don't let anybody leave the city to warn Jezreel.'

16.text: Then Jehu hopped in his chariot and headed straight for Jezreel, where Joram was recovering. Ahaziah, king of Judah, was also there visiting Joram.

17.text: A watchman on the tower in Jezreel saw Jehu's squad coming and told Joram. Joram said, 'Send a rider to ask if it's peace.'

18.text: The rider went out and asked, 'The king says: Is everything good?' Jehu said, 'What you worried about peace for? Fall in behind me.' The watchman reported, 'He met them, but he ain't coming back.'

19.text: Joram sent another rider. Same thing happened—he didn't come back.

20.text: The watchman said, 'Yo, this driving look wild—it gotta be Jehu. He drives crazy!'

21.text: Joram said, 'Get my chariot ready.' He and Ahaziah rode out to meet Jehu at Naboth's old field.

22.text: Joram asked, 'Jehu, we good?' Jehu said, 'Ain't no peace while your mama Jezebel out here with all her witchcraft and mess.'

23.text: Joram turned his chariot to run and yelled, 'Ahaziah, it's a setup!'

24.text: Jehu pulled his bow back full strength and shot Joram in the back—the arrow went straight through his heart. He collapsed in his chariot.

25.text: Jehu told his captain, 'Throw his body in Naboth's field. Remember how we was with Ahab when God said he'd pay him back for what he did to Naboth?'

26.text: 'Well, here's that payback. Toss him in that field, just like God said.'

27.text: Ahaziah saw this and took off toward Beth-Haggan. Jehu said, 'Shoot him too!' They hit him near Gur, but he kept running till he reached Megiddo, where he died.

28.text: His servants took him back to Jerusalem and buried him with his ancestors in the City of David.

29.text: Ahaziah had become king of Judah in Joram's eleventh year of ruling Israel.

30.text: When Jehu pulled up in Jezreel, Jezebel heard about it. She did her makeup, fixed her hair, and looked out the window.

31.text: When Jehu came through the gate, she said, 'So you coming in peace, Zimri? You know, the one who killed his master?'

32.text: Jehu looked up at the window and said, 'Who rolling with me?' Two or three eunuchs looked out.

33.text: Jehu said, 'Throw her down.' And they did. Her blood splattered on the wall, on the horses, and Jehu ran over her with his chariot.

34.text: Jehu went inside, ate, drank, then said, 'Alright, go bury her. She was a king's daughter.'

35.text: But when they went out to bury her, all they found was her skull, feet, and hands.

36.text: They came back and told Jehu, and he said, 'Welp, guess that's just like what Elijah prophesied—dogs ate Jezebel in Jezreel.'

37.text: 'Now she ain't even got a proper grave—just some scraps left in the dirt, like trash.'

1.text: Now Ahab had seventy sons in Samaria. Jehu wrote letters and sent them to the leaders in Jezreel, the elders, and the folks raising Ahab's sons.

2.text: 'Y'all got chariots, horses, weapons, and a whole fortified city. Pick the best son of Ahab, put him on the throne, and fight for his family.'

3.text: But they got shook and said, 'Man, two kings couldn't stand up to Jehu. What we supposed to do?'

4.text: So the palace manager, city officials, elders, and the guardians of Ahab's sons sent Jehu a message: 'We your servants. We'll do whatever you say, but we ain't making anybody king. Just tell us what you want.'

5.text: Jehu sent another letter: 'If y'all really with me, take the heads of Ahab's sons and bring them to me in Jezreel by this time tomorrow.'

6.text: Now Ahab's seventy sons were being raised by the city's leaders, so when they got Jehu's message, they took all seventy, killed them, put their heads in baskets, and sent them to Jezreel.

7.text: A messenger came to Jehu and said, 'Boss, they brought the heads.' Jehu said, 'Pile them up at the city gate 'til morning.'

8.text: The next morning, Jehu went out and said to the people, 'Y'all see this? Yeah, I took out my master, but who killed all these?'

9.text: 'Now y'all know—everything the Lord said about Ahab's house is coming true. This is exactly what He promised through Elijah.'

10.text: Then Jehu wiped out everybody left from Ahab's house in Jezreel—his officials, friends, and priests—nobody was spared.

11.text: Jehu left for Samaria. On the way, he stopped at Beth Eked of the Shepherds.

12.text: There, he ran into the relatives of Ahaziah, king of Judah. He asked, 'Who y'all?'

13.text: They said, 'We Ahaziah's brothers. We just came to visit the king's sons and the queen mother's family.'

14.text: Jehu said, 'Take them alive!' They grabbed all forty-two men and killed them at the well of Beth Eked. None survived.

15.text: As Jehu was leaving, he ran into Jehonadab, son of Rechab. Jehu greeted him and asked, 'You down with me like I'm down with you?'

16.text: Jehonadab said, 'Yeah, I'm with you.' Jehu said, 'Then come with me. See how serious I am about the Lord.' So he got in Jehu's chariot.

17.text: When they got to Samaria, Jehu killed off the rest of Ahab's family—every last one of them—just like the Lord said through Elijah.

18.text: Then Jehu gathered everybody and said, 'Ahab served Baal a little, but me? I'ma take it to another level.'

19.text: 'So go call every Baal prophet, priest, and follower. I got a big sacrifice planned for Baal. If you miss it, you ain't living.' But Jehu was finessing—he was really setting them up.

20.text: He ordered, 'Announce a special service for Baal.' And they did.

21.text: Jehu sent word across Israel, and every single Baal worshiper showed up. The temple was packed.

22.text: He told the temple manager, 'Bring out the special robes for Baal's people.' And they handed them out.

23.text: Then Jehu and Jehonadab went into the temple and said, 'Make sure ain't no servants of the Lord in here—only Baal's people.'

24.text: Once the sacrifices started, Jehu had eighty men waiting outside. He told them, 'If y'all let even one person escape, your life for theirs.'

25.text: As soon as the offering was done, Jehu said, 'Lock the doors. Kill them all.' His men rushed in, took them out with swords, and tossed the bodies outside.

26.text: Then they went into the inner temple, pulled down the sacred pillars, and burned them.

27.text: They tore down Baal's temple and turned it into a garbage dump. It's been like that ever since.

28.text: And that's how Jehu wiped Baal worship out of Israel.

29.text: But even after all that, Jehu still kept the golden calf idols in Bethel and Dan—the same ones Jeroboam set up that led Israel into sin.

30.text: The Lord told Jehu, 'You did good wiping out Ahab's house like I wanted, so your family will rule Israel for four generations.'

31.text: But Jehu didn't fully follow the Lord. He still let Israel run wild in Jeroboam's sins.

32.text: Around this time, the Lord started taking pieces of Israel away, and King Hazael of Syria took over a bunch of land.

33.text: From the Jordan eastward—Gilead, Gad, Reuben, Manasseh—he took it all, from Aroer to Bashan.

34.text: Everything else Jehu did—his victories, his battles—it's all written in the book of the kings of Israel.

35.text: Then Jehu died and was buried in Samaria. His son Jehoahaz took over the throne.

36.text: Jehu ruled Israel from Samaria for twenty-eight years.

1.text: When Athaliah, Ahaziah's mama, saw her son was dead, she went full villain mode and started wiping out the whole royal family.

2.text: But Jehosheba, daughter of King Joram and Ahaziah's sister, wasn't having it. She snatched up Joash, Ahaziah's baby boy, and hid him with his nurse in a bedroom so Athaliah couldn't find him.

3.text: She kept him hidden in the Lord's temple for six years while Athaliah ran the kingdom.

4.text: In the seventh year, Jehoiada the priest called up the military captains, the royal guards, and the temple security. He brought them into the temple, made them swear an oath, then showed them the king's son.

5.text: He gave them orders: 'Alright, one-third of y'all guard the king's house.'

6.text: 'Another third, y'all post up at the Gate of Sur. The last third, hold down the gate behind the escorts. Don't let nobody through.'

7.text: 'The rest of y'all, the ones off duty on the Sabbath? Y'all staying in the Lord's house, keeping guard over the king.'

8.text: 'Surround the king from all sides, weapons ready. If anybody tries to come at him—take them out. Stay close to the king when he moves.'

9.text: The captains did exactly what Jehoiada told them. They brought their men on and off duty and met up at the temple.

10.text: Jehoiada handed out weapons—shields and spears from King David's old stash in the temple.

11.text: The guards lined up, fully armed, from one side of the temple to the other, surrounding the king.

12.text: Then they brought Joash out, put the crown on him, gave him the royal scroll, and anointed him king. Everybody started clapping, shouting, 'Long live the king!'

13.text: Athaliah heard all the noise from the temple, so she pulled up to see what was going on.

14.text: She looked and saw the new king standing by the pillar, just like tradition. The officials and trumpeters were celebrating, and the people were hype. Athaliah lost it, tore her clothes, and screamed, 'Treason! Treason!'

15.text: Jehoiada, keeping it cool, told the military captains, 'Get her outta here and handle anybody who tries to back her up.' He made sure they didn't kill her in the Lord's temple.

16.text: So they grabbed her, dragged her through the Horse Gate to the palace, and that's where they took her out.

17.text: Then Jehoiada made a covenant between the Lord, the king, and the people, making sure everybody was locked in to serving the Lord.

18.text: Then the people rushed Baal's temple, tore it down, smashed the altars, broke up all the idols, and killed Baal's priest, Mattan, right there at the altar. Jehoiada put new officers in charge of the Lord's house.

19.text: Jehoiada, the military captains, the royal guards, and all the people led Joash from the Lord's house to the palace. He walked through the escort gate and sat on the throne.

20.text: The people cheered, the city calmed down, and just like that—Athaliah was gone.

21.text: Joash was only seven years old when he became king.

1.text: In Jehu's seventh year as king, Jehoash became king of Judah. He ruled for forty years in Jerusalem. His mama was Zibiah from Beersheba.

2.text: Jehoash did right by the Lord as long as Jehoiada the priest was guiding him.

3.text: But one problem—he ain't take down the high places. Folks was still out here burning incense and making sacrifices up there instead of at the Lord's temple.

4.text: One day, Jehoash told the priests, 'Listen, all the money coming into the temple—the census tax, donations, and whatever folks give from their heart—'

5.text: 'Y'all take that and use it to fix up the temple wherever it's falling apart.'

6.text: But fast forward to Jehoash's twenty-third year as king—the priests still ain't fix the temple.

7.text: So Jehoash called Jehoiada and the other priests and said, 'Why y'all ain't done the repairs yet? From now on, stop collecting money for yourselves. Use it to fix the temple like I said.'

8.text: The priests agreed—they would stop collecting money, and they wouldn't be in charge of the repairs anymore.

9.text: Then Jehoiada the priest got a chest, drilled a hole in the top, and put it by the altar, near the entrance of the Lord's house. Every time someone brought money to the temple, the priests put it in the chest.

10.text: When the chest got full, the king's scribe and the high priest would come, bag up the money, and count it.

11.text: They gave the money to the overseers, who then paid the workers—carpenters, builders, masons, stonecutters—anybody fixing up the Lord's house.

12.text: They used the money for materials too—wood, cut stone, and everything needed to restore the temple.

13.text: But none of that money went toward making silver bowls, lamp trimmers, sprinkling bowls, trumpets, or any other gold and silver items for the temple.

14.text: It all went straight to the workers to get the temple repairs done.

15.text: They ain't even make the workers give receipts—everybody handling the money was solid and trustworthy.

16.text: However, the money from guilt offerings and sin offerings wasn't put in the chest—that was strictly for the priests.

17.text: Then Hazael, king of Syria, rolled up on Gath, took the city, and then set his sights on Jerusalem.

18.text: Jehoash, instead of fighting, took all the holy things dedicated by past kings—Jehoshaphat, Jehoram, and Ahaziah—plus his own, and all the gold from the temple and the royal treasury. He sent it as a payoff to Hazael, and Hazael left Jerusalem alone.

19.text: Everything else Joash did? It's all written in the book of the kings of Judah.

20.text: But in the end, some of his own servants plotted against him and assassinated him at the house of Millo on the way to Silla.

21.text: The ones who killed him were Jozachar, son of Shimeath, and Jehozabad, son of Shomer. Joash died, they buried him in the City of David, and his son Amaziah took over as king.

1.text: In the twenty-third year of Joash, king of Judah, Jehoahaz, son of Jehu, became king of Israel in Samaria. He ruled for seventeen years.

2.text: But he was out here wildin'—doing evil just like Jeroboam, who led Israel into sin. He ain't change a thing.

3.text: So the Lord got fed up and let Hazael, king of Syria, and his son Ben-Hadad keep Israel under their thumb for years.

4.text: Eventually, Jehoahaz begged the Lord for help, and the Lord listened, 'cause He saw how bad Israel was suffering under Syria.

5.text: So the Lord sent a deliverer who helped Israel escape Syria's grip. They started living in their own homes again, just like before.

6.text: But even after all that, they still ain't clean up their act. They kept following Jeroboam's ways and even left that wooden idol standing in Samaria.

7.text: By the time Jehoahaz was done, his army was almost wiped out—just fifty horsemen, ten chariots, and ten thousand foot soldiers left. The king of Syria had crushed them like dust.

8.text: Everything else Jehoahaz did? It's written in the book of the kings of Israel.

9.text: Then he died, they buried him in Samaria, and his son Joash took over.

10.text: In the thirty-seventh year of Joash, king of Judah, Jehoash, son of Jehoahaz, became king of Israel. He ruled in Samaria for sixteen years.

11.text: But he was no better—same old evil, same sins as Jeroboam, keeping Israel on the wrong path.

12.text: Everything else Joash did—including his beef with Amaziah, king of Judah—it's all written in the book of the kings of Israel.

13.text: Then Joash died, was buried in Samaria with the other kings, and his son Jeroboam took the throne.

14.text: Elisha got sick with the illness that would take him out. King Joash of Israel came to see him, crying, 'My father, my father! The chariots and horsemen of Israel!'

15.text: Elisha told him, 'Grab a bow and some arrows.' So Joash did.

16.text: 'Now, put your hand on the bow,' Elisha said. Joash did, and Elisha put his hands over the king's hands.

17.text: 'Open the east window,' Elisha said, and Joash opened it. Then Elisha said, 'Shoot!' Joash let the arrow fly. Elisha said, 'That's the Lord's arrow of victory! You gon' take down Syria at Aphek until they're done for.'

18.text: Then Elisha said, 'Grab some more arrows and hit the ground.' Joash struck the ground three times, then stopped.

19.text: Elisha got mad. 'Man, you should've hit it five or six times! Then you would've completely destroyed Syria! But now? You only gon' beat them three times.'

20.text: Then Elisha died, and they buried him. The following spring, raiders from Moab invaded the land.
