21.text: Some Israelites were burying a man when they spotted the raiders. They panicked and tossed the body into Elisha's tomb. Soon as the body hit Elisha's bones, the man came back to life and stood up!

22.text: Hazael, king of Syria, kept Israel struggling all through Jehoahaz's reign.

23.text: But the Lord, still faithful to His promise to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, had mercy on Israel. He ain't wipe them out or abandon them yet.

24.text: Then Hazael died, and his son Ben-Hadad took over.

25.text: Joash, son of Jehoahaz, went to war against Ben-Hadad and took back the cities Syria had stolen from his father. Three times Joash defeated him and reclaimed Israel's land.

1.text: In the second year of Joash, son of Jehoahaz, ruling Israel, Amaziah, son of Joash, became king of Judah.

2.text: He was 25 when he took the throne, and he ruled in Jerusalem for 29 years. His mama was Jehoaddan from Jerusalem.

3.text: Amaziah did what was right in the Lord's eyes, but he wasn't on David's level. He followed in his daddy Joash's footsteps.

4.text: But he ain't take down the high places, so folks were still out here burning incense and making sacrifices in the wrong spots.

5.text: Once Amaziah had solid control over the kingdom, he handled business—he executed the servants who assassinated his father.

6.text: But he didn't kill their kids, 'cause the law of Moses said, 'Parents don't get punished for their kids' sins, and kids don't get punished for their parents' sins—everybody gets judged for their own mess.'

7.text: Amaziah pulled up on Edom, wiped out 10,000 men in the Valley of Salt, took the city of Sela, and renamed it Joktheel—that name still sticks to this day.

8.text: Then Amaziah sent a message to Jehoash, king of Israel: 'Let's run it. Meet me on the battlefield.'

9.text: Jehoash sent a response: 'Listen, a little thistle in Lebanon told a mighty cedar tree, "Give your daughter to my son," but then a wild animal came through and stomped that thistle out.'

10.text: 'Yeah, you beat Edom, and now you feeling yourself. Stay home, man. Don't start something you can't finish, or you and Judah gonna take an L.'

11.text: But Amaziah wasn't listening. So Jehoash, king of Israel, came through, and they met at Beth Shemesh, which belonged to Judah.

12.text: Judah got whooped bad—everybody ran back home.

13.text: Jehoash even captured Amaziah at Beth Shemesh, then went to Jerusalem, broke down 400 cubits of the city wall—from the Ephraim Gate to the Corner Gate.

14.text: He ransacked the Lord's temple, cleaned out the royal treasury, took hostages, and then went back to Samaria.

15.text: Everything else Jehoash did—his power, his battle with Amaziah—it's written in the book of the kings of Israel.

16.text: Then Jehoash died and was buried in Samaria with the kings of Israel. His son Jeroboam took the throne.

17.text: Amaziah, son of Joash, king of Judah, lived 15 more years after Jehoash died.

18.text: Everything else Amaziah did is recorded in the book of the kings of Judah.

19.text: But his own people plotted against him in Jerusalem, so he ran to Lachish. They sent men after him, and he was killed there.

20.text: They brought his body back on horses and buried him in Jerusalem with his ancestors in the City of David.

21.text: Then the people of Judah took his son Azariah, who was just 16, and made him king in his place.

22.text: Azariah rebuilt Elath and brought it back under Judah's control after his father was gone.

23.text: In the fifteenth year of Amaziah ruling Judah, Jeroboam, son of Joash, became king of Israel in Samaria. He ruled for 41 years.

24.text: But he was on the same mess—doing evil, keeping Israel locked in Jeroboam's sins.

25.text: Still, he managed to restore Israel's borders from Hamath to the Dead Sea, just like the Lord had promised through His prophet Jonah, son of Amittai from Gath-Hepher.

26.text: The Lord saw how bad Israel was struggling—everybody was suffering, slave and free, and they had no help.

27.text: But the Lord wasn't ready to erase Israel from the map yet, so He used Jeroboam to keep them afloat.

28.text: Everything else Jeroboam did—his power, his wars, and how he took back Damascus and Hamath for Israel—it's all recorded in the book of the kings of Israel.

29.text: Then Jeroboam died and was buried with the kings of Israel. His son Zechariah took the throne.

1.text: In the twenty-seventh year of Jeroboam, king of Israel, Azariah, son of Amaziah, became king of Judah.

2.text: He was sixteen when he took the throne and ruled for fifty-two years in Jerusalem. His mama was Jecholiah from Jerusalem.

3.text: He did right by the Lord, just like his father Amaziah did.

4.text: But just like before, the high places were still up. People were still out here burning incense and making sacrifices where they shouldn't.

5.text: Then the Lord struck Azariah with leprosy, and he had it for the rest of his life. He had to live in isolation, and his son Jotham ran things in his place.

6.text: Everything else Azariah did? It's all written in the book of the kings of Judah.

7.text: Then he died, they buried him in the City of David, and his son Jotham took the throne.

8.text: In the thirty-eighth year of Azariah ruling Judah, Zechariah, son of Jeroboam, became king of Israel in Samaria. He only lasted six months.

9.text: And yeah, he did evil just like his ancestors. He kept Israel deep in Jeroboam's sins.

10.text: Then Shallum, son of Jabesh, plotted against him, killed him in public, and took the throne.

11.text: Everything else Zechariah did? It's in the book of the kings of Israel.

12.text: And just like the Lord told Jehu—'Your family will rule for four generations'—that's exactly what happened.

13.text: Shallum, son of Jabesh, became king in the thirty-ninth year of Uzziah (Azariah), king of Judah. He ruled in Samaria for… one whole month.

14.text: Then Menahem, son of Gadi, came up from Tirzah, stormed into Samaria, killed Shallum, and took over.

15.text: Everything else Shallum did? That's in the book of the kings of Israel.

16.text: After that, Menahem went back to Tirzah and attacked Tiphsah. Since they ain't surrender, he destroyed the whole city—and for real, he was ruthless. He even killed all the pregnant women.

17.text: In the thirty-ninth year of Azariah's reign, Menahem, son of Gadi, became king of Israel. He ruled for ten years in Samaria.

18.text: But yeah, same story—he did evil, stuck with Jeroboam's sins, and didn't change a thing.

19.text: Then Pul, king of Assyria, came rolling up. Instead of fighting, Menahem gave him a thousand talents of silver to back off and let him keep his throne.

20.text: To get the money, Menahem taxed the rich folks in Israel—every wealthy man had to cough up fifty shekels of silver to pay off Assyria. After that, Pul left.

21.text: Everything else Menahem did? It's in the book of the kings of Israel.

22.text: Then he died, and his son Pekahiah took the throne.

23.text: In the fiftieth year of Azariah ruling Judah, Pekahiah, son of Menahem, became king of Israel in Samaria. He lasted two years.

24.text: And yup, he did evil too—just like Jeroboam, keeping Israel stuck in sin.

25.text: Then one of his own officers, Pekah, son of Remaliah, plotted against him. He rolled up on Pekahiah in the palace, killed him, and took over.

26.text: Everything else Pekahiah did? That's in the book of the kings of Israel.

27.text: In the fifty-second year of Azariah ruling Judah, Pekah, son of Remaliah, took the throne in Israel. He ruled for twenty years in Samaria.

28.text: But just like everybody before him, he did evil and never stepped away from Jeroboam's sins.

29.text: During Pekah's reign, Tiglath-Pileser, king of Assyria, invaded and took a bunch of cities—Ijon, Abel Beth Maachah, Janoah, Kedesh, Hazor, Gilead, Galilee—basically, all of Naphtali's land. Then he deported the people to Assyria.

30.text: Then Hoshea, son of Elah, plotted against Pekah, killed him, and took the throne in Jotham's twentieth year ruling Judah.

31.text: Everything else Pekah did? It's in the book of the kings of Israel.

32.text: In the second year of Pekah ruling Israel, Jotham, son of Uzziah (Azariah), became king of Judah.

33.text: He was twenty-five when he took the throne, and he ruled for sixteen years in Jerusalem. His mama was Jerusha, daughter of Zadok.

34.text: He did right by the Lord, just like his father Uzziah did.

35.text: But again, the high places were still up. People kept sacrificing and burning incense there. Jotham did, however, build the Upper Gate of the Lord's house.

36.text: Everything else Jotham did? That's in the book of the kings of Judah.

37.text: During his reign, the Lord let Rezin, king of Syria, and Pekah, son of Remaliah, start trouble with Judah.

38.text: Then Jotham died, was buried with his ancestors in the City of David, and his son Ahaz took the throne.

1.text: In the seventeenth year of Pekah, son of Remaliah, ruling Israel, Ahaz, son of Jotham, became king of Judah.

2.text: Ahaz was 20 when he took the throne, and he ruled for 16 years in Jerusalem. But he wasn't on the right path—he ain't do what was right in the Lord's eyes like his ancestor David did.

3.text: Instead, he followed the ways of Israel's kings. He even sacrificed his own son in fire, doing the same wicked stuff as the nations God had kicked out before Israel moved in.

4.text: He was out here burning incense and making sacrifices on the high places, up in the hills, and under every green tree.

5.text: Then Rezin, king of Syria, and Pekah, son of Remaliah, king of Israel, rolled up on Jerusalem, ready for war. They surrounded Ahaz but couldn't take him down.

6.text: At the same time, Rezin took over Elath for Syria, kicked out the people of Judah, and now the Edomites live there to this day.

7.text: So Ahaz panicked and sent messengers to Tiglath-Pileser, king of Assyria, saying, 'I'm your servant, your son—come help me! These kings of Syria and Israel are ganging up on me!'

8.text: Then Ahaz took all the silver and gold from the Lord's temple and the royal palace and sent it as a gift to the king of Assyria.

9.text: Assyria took the money and went to war for him. They attacked Damascus, captured it, took the people as captives to Kir, and killed King Rezin.

10.text: After that, Ahaz went to Damascus to meet Tiglath-Pileser, king of Assyria. While he was there, he saw an altar he liked.

11.text: So he sent the blueprint back to Urijah the priest, telling him to build one just like it.

12.text: Urijah wasted no time—before Ahaz even got back, the new altar was ready.

13.text: When Ahaz returned, he went straight to the altar, made some offerings, and poured out a drink offering.

14.text: Then he took the bronze altar from the Lord's temple, moved it from its proper place, and put it on the north side of the new altar he made.

15.text: Ahaz told Urijah, 'From now on, this new altar is where we do all the offerings—morning burnt offerings, evening grain offerings, sacrifices for the king and the people, drink offerings—everything. And sprinkle all the blood here. That old bronze altar? I'll use that when I need guidance.'

16.text: And Urijah the priest? He just went along with everything Ahaz told him to do.

17.text: Then King Ahaz stripped the gold panels off the carts, took the lavers off them, and removed the bronze Sea from the oxen it stood on, putting it on a stone pavement instead.

18.text: He also tore down the special Sabbath entrance that had been built in the Lord's temple, along with the royal entrance—just to impress the king of Assyria.

19.text: Everything else Ahaz did? It's all written in the book of the kings of Judah.

20.text: Then Ahaz died, was buried in the City of David, and his son Hezekiah took the throne.

1.text: In the twelfth year of Ahaz ruling Judah, Hoshea, son of Elah, became king of Israel in Samaria. He ruled for nine years.

2.text: He was on that same evil path, but not as bad as the kings before him.

3.text: Shalmaneser, king of Assyria, rolled up on him, and Hoshea had to start paying tribute money to stay in power.

4.text: But then Assyria found out Hoshea was playing both sides—he sent messages to So, king of Egypt, trying to make a deal and stopped paying tribute to Assyria. So the king of Assyria wasn't having it—he arrested Hoshea and threw him in prison.

5.text: After that, the king of Assyria marched through Israel, laid siege to Samaria, and surrounded it for three years.

6.text: By Hoshea's ninth year as king, Assyria finally took Samaria and exiled Israel, sending them to Halah, the Habor River, and cities in Medea.

7.text: This all happened 'cause Israel kept sinning against the Lord—the same God who pulled them out of Egypt and freed them from Pharaoh. But instead of staying loyal, they started fearing other gods.

8.text: They copied the ways of the nations God had driven out before them, and they followed the corrupt kings of Israel.

9.text: They thought they could do shady stuff in secret, but God saw everything. They built altars everywhere—from small villages to big cities.

10.text: They set up sacred pillars and idol statues on every high hill and under every green tree.

11.text: They burned incense on those altars just like the pagan nations before them—disrespecting God and making Him angry.

12.text: They worshiped idols, even though God had straight-up told them, 'Don't do this!'

13.text: Over and over, the Lord sent prophets and seers, warning Israel and Judah: 'Turn away from your wicked ways! Follow My commandments! Stick to the laws I gave your ancestors!'

14.text: But they were stubborn, just like their ancestors who refused to trust in God.

15.text: They rejected His laws, broke His covenant, ignored His warnings, and chased after idols. They followed the ways of the surrounding nations, even though God told them not to.

16.text: They completely abandoned the Lord's commandments, made two golden calves, built an idol pole, and started worshiping the sun, moon, stars, and all the false gods.

17.text: They even sacrificed their own kids in fire, practiced witchcraft, and got into sorcery—fully selling out to evil, making God furious.

18.text: So the Lord had enough. He wiped Israel off the map, leaving only Judah.

19.text: But even Judah wasn't acting right—they were following the same corrupt ways as Israel.

20.text: So God rejected the whole nation of Israel, let them get attacked, looted, and finally exiled.

21.text: It all started when Israel broke away from the house of David and made Jeroboam king. He led them away from God, setting them up for destruction.

22.text: Israel kept walking in Jeroboam's sins, never turning back.

23.text: So the Lord finally followed through on His warnings. He had Israel taken out of their land and sent to Assyria—where they still are to this day.

24.text: Then the king of Assyria brought in new people—Babylonians, Cuthites, Avvites, Hamathites, and Sepharvites—to settle in Samaria and take Israel's place.

25.text: But at first, they didn't fear the Lord. So God sent lions among them, and the lions started killing people.

26.text: The new settlers freaked out and told the king of Assyria, 'Look, the people you sent here don't know how to worship the God of this land. That's why lions are attacking them!'

27.text: So the king ordered, 'Send back one of the Israelite priests we captured. Let him teach them how to worship the God of this land.'

28.text: So a priest came back, settled in Bethel, and started teaching them the ways of the Lord.

29.text: But even with that, every group still kept worshiping their own gods, setting up idols in the high places across Samaria.

30.text: The Babylonians made Succoth Benoth. The Cuthites made Nergal. The Hamathites made Ashima.

31.text: The Avvites worshiped Nibhaz and Tartak. And the Sepharvites went as far as burning their kids in fire as sacrifices to Adrammelech and Anammelech, their gods.

32.text: Yeah, they feared the Lord, but at the same time, they still appointed their own priests to serve at the shrines in high places.

33.text: Basically, they were double-dipping—they claimed to respect the Lord but kept serving their own gods, doing things like the nations before them.

34.text: And to this day, they still stuck in their old ways. They don't really fear the Lord or follow His laws and commandments—the same ones He gave Jacob, whom He named Israel.

35.text: God made a covenant with them, saying, 'Don't fear other gods, don't bow down to them, don't serve them, and don't sacrifice to them.'

36.text: 'Fear the Lord—the One who brought you out of Egypt with power. Worship Him and offer sacrifices only to Him.'

37.text: 'Follow His laws, commands, and rules forever. Don't fear other gods.'

38.text: 'And don't forget this covenant I made with y'all. Stick with the Lord, and He'll protect you from your enemies.'

39.text: But they ain't listen. They just kept doing things their own way.

40.text: So, even though they feared the Lord, they still followed their old idolatrous ways.

41.text: And to this very day, their descendants keep doing what their ancestors did—trying to mix worshiping the Lord with serving idols.

1.text: In the third year of Hoshea, son of Elah, ruling over Israel, Hezekiah, son of Ahaz, became king of Judah.

2.text: He was 25 when he took the throne, and he ruled for 29 years in Jerusalem. His mama was Abi, daughter of Zechariah.

3.text: Hezekiah did right by the Lord, following the ways of his ancestor David.

4.text: He tore down all the high places, smashed the sacred pillars, cut down the idol poles, and even destroyed that old bronze snake Moses made—'cause folks had started worshiping it like an idol and calling it Nehushtan.

5.text: Hezekiah trusted in the Lord like no other king before or after him.

6.text: He stayed locked in with the Lord, never straying from His commandments.

7.text: Because of that, the Lord had his back—Hezekiah succeeded in everything he did. He even broke free from the king of Assyria and refused to serve him.

8.text: He pulled up on the Philistines, crushed them all the way to Gaza, taking out both small villages and fortified cities.

9.text: In Hezekiah's fourth year as king—this was Hoshea's seventh year ruling Israel—Shalmaneser, king of Assyria, came for Samaria and laid siege to it.

10.text: Three years later, in Hezekiah's sixth year, Assyria finally took Samaria.

11.text: The king of Assyria deported Israel, sending them off to Halah, the Habor River, and cities in Medea.

12.text: This happened 'cause Israel ain't listen to the Lord. They broke His covenant, ignored Moses' laws, and refused to obey.

13.text: Fast forward to Hezekiah's fourteenth year—Sennacherib, king of Assyria, came through and took over all the fortified cities of Judah.

14.text: Hezekiah sent word to the king of Assyria at Lachish: 'My bad. I messed up. Just tell me what you want, and I'll pay up.' Sennacherib demanded 300 talents of silver and 30 talents of gold.

15.text: So Hezekiah emptied out all the silver from the Lord's temple and the royal treasury.

16.text: He even stripped the gold off the temple doors and pillars that he himself had covered in gold—and sent it all to the king of Assyria.

17.text: Then the king of Assyria sent his top officials—the Tartan, the Rabsaris, and the Rabshakeh—with a huge army to Jerusalem. They pulled up to the aqueduct by the highway leading to the Fuller's Field.

18.text: When they got there, they called for the king. Hezekiah's team—Eliakim (palace overseer), Shebna (the scribe), and Joah (the recorder)—came out to meet them.

19.text: The Rabshakeh said, 'Tell Hezekiah: The great king of Assyria got a question—why you acting so bold?'

20.text: 'You talking like you got some kind of military strategy, but that's just talk. Who you really trusting in that got you thinking you can rebel against me?'

21.text: 'Oh, I see. You putting your faith in Egypt? Man, Egypt is like a broken stick—lean on them, and they'll stab you in the hand. That's Pharaoh for you!'

22.text: 'Or maybe you saying, "We trust in the Lord." Ain't Hezekiah the same one who tore down all those altars and said y'all could only worship in Jerusalem?'

23.text: 'Tell you what—make a deal with my master, the king of Assyria. I'll even give you 2,000 horses… if y'all got enough riders to put on them!'

24.text: 'You can't even take on my lowest-ranking officer, but you think Egypt's chariots and horsemen gon' save you?'

25.text: 'Matter of fact, you think I'm here on my own? The Lord Himself told me to come destroy this place!'

26.text: Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah said to the Rabshakeh, 'Yo, can you speak in Aramaic? We understand it. No need to talk in Hebrew where everybody can hear.'

27.text: But the Rabshakeh laughed and said, 'Nah, I'm talking to everybody—y'all and the people sitting on the walls who about to suffer, starving and drinking their own waste.'

28.text: Then he stepped forward and shouted in Hebrew, 'Listen up, everybody! Hear what the great king of Assyria has to say!'

29.text: 'Don't let Hezekiah fool you—he can't save you!'

30.text: 'Don't let him trick you into trusting the Lord, saying, "The Lord will deliver us, and we won't fall to the king of Assyria."'

31.text: 'Here's what you should do—make peace with me, bring me a gift, and come out. Then every one of y'all can eat from your own vine, drink from your own well, and live good.'

32.text: 'Soon enough, I'll take you to a new land, just like yours—good food, vineyards, olive trees, and honey. You'll live, not die! But don't listen to Hezekiah when he tells you, "The Lord will save us."'

33.text: 'Ain't no god ever saved their people from me! Not Hamath, not Arpad, not Sepharvaim, Hena, or Ivah!'

34.text: 'Even Samaria fell to me! What makes y'all think your God gon' save Jerusalem?'

35.text: The people ain't say a word, 'cause Hezekiah had already told them, 'Don't respond.'

36.text: Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah went back to Hezekiah with their clothes torn and told him everything the Rabshakeh said.

37.text: Then Eliakim (son of Hilkiah, the palace overseer), Shebna (the scribe), and Joah (son of Asaph, the recorder) went back to Hezekiah, clothes ripped in grief, and told him everything the Rabshakeh had said.

1.text: When King Hezekiah heard all this, he tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and went straight to the Lord's temple.

2.text: Then he sent Eliakim (his chief of staff), Shebna (his scribe), and the senior priests—all dressed in sackcloth—to go see the prophet Isaiah, son of Amoz.

3.text: They told Isaiah, 'Hezekiah says today is a straight-up disaster—like a woman in labor who ain't got the strength to push.'

4.text: 'Maybe the Lord heard all that trash talk from the Rabshakeh—how he was sent by the Assyrian king to diss the living God. Maybe the Lord will put him in check. So please, pray for the small remnant that's left.'

5.text: When Hezekiah's officials got to Isaiah,

6.text: Isaiah told them, 'Go tell your king this is what the Lord says: "Don't trip over what you just heard—all that mess from Assyria's men blaspheming Me."'

7.text: 'I'm about to send a spirit to stir things up—he's gonna hear a rumor, run back to his own land, and get taken out with the sword over there.'

8.text: Meanwhile, the Rabshakeh got word that his king was fighting in Libnah, 'cause he had left Lachish.

9.text: Then Assyria's king heard that Tirhakah, king of Ethiopia, was coming for him. So he sent another message to Hezekiah:

10.text: 'Tell Hezekiah, king of Judah: Don't let that God you believe in fool you into thinking Jerusalem won't fall into my hands.'

11.text: 'You heard what me and my ancestors did to all those other nations—completely wiped 'em out. You think you're the exception?'

12.text: 'Where were the gods of Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, or Eden in Telassar? They couldn't stop us.'

13.text: 'Where's the king of Hamath? The king of Arpad? The kings of Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivah? Gone.'

14.text: When Hezekiah got the letter, he read it, then went straight to the temple, spread it out before the Lord, and prayed.

15.text: Hezekiah said, 'Lord, God of Israel, You sit between the cherubim. You alone are God over every kingdom on earth. You made heaven and earth.'

16.text: 'Open Your ears, Lord—hear this. Open Your eyes, Lord—see what's happening. Listen to what Sennacherib is saying about You, the living God.'

17.text: 'Yeah, it's true—the Assyrians wiped out those nations.'

18.text: 'But their gods weren't real. Just wood and stone, made by human hands. Of course they burned them.'

19.text: 'But now, Lord our God, I'm asking You—save us from this man. Show all the kingdoms of the earth that You alone are God.'

20.text: Then Isaiah, son of Amoz, sent this message to Hezekiah: 'The Lord says: Because you prayed about Sennacherib, king of Assyria, I heard you.'

21.text: 'Here's My response:'

22.text: 'Daughter Zion laughs at you, Assyria.'

23.text: 'You really thought you could insult the Holy One of Israel?'

24.text: 'You bragged about climbing mountains, cutting down mighty trees, and drinking foreign waters like you run the world.'

25.text: 'But did you not know? I planned this long ago! You only did what I allowed—turning strong cities into rubble.'

26.text: 'That's why their people were weak—like grass in the field, barely growing before they got stomped out.'

27.text: 'I know where you live. I see what you do. And I know your arrogance against Me.'

28.text: 'Because you raged against Me, your pride has reached My ears. So guess what? I'm putting My hook in your nose, My bridle in your mouth, and sending you right back the way you came.'

29.text: 'And here's a sign for Judah: This year, you'll eat what grows naturally. Next year, same thing. But in the third year, you'll plant and harvest, grow vineyards, and feast.'

30.text: 'The remnant left in Judah will take root and flourish.'

31.text: 'Because from Jerusalem, a remnant will rise again. The zeal of the Lord will make it happen.'

32.text: 'As for the king of Assyria? He won't step foot in this city. He won't even shoot an arrow here.'

33.text: 'The same road he came on, he's leaving on. He's not touching this city.'

34.text: 'Because I, the Lord, will defend it—for My own sake and for My servant David's sake.'

35.text: That night, the angel of the Lord went into the Assyrian camp and wiped out 185,000 soldiers. The next morning, the survivors woke up to nothing but dead bodies.

36.text: So Sennacherib, king of Assyria, packed up and went back home to Nineveh.

37.text: While he was worshiping in the temple of his god, Nisroch, his own sons—Adrammelech and Sharezer—snuck up and killed him with a sword. Then they escaped to Ararat, and Esarhaddon, his son, took over the throne.

1.text: Around that time, Hezekiah got real sick—like, on his deathbed. The prophet Isaiah, son of Amoz, came to him and said, 'The Lord says: Get your affairs in order. You about to die, you ain't gon' make it.'

2.text: Hezekiah turned to the wall and started praying hard to the Lord.

3.text: 'Lord, please remember how I been walking in Your truth with a loyal heart, doing right in Your eyes.' Then Hezekiah broke down crying.

4.text: Before Isaiah even made it out the palace, the Lord hit him with another message.

5.text: 'Go back and tell Hezekiah, the leader of My people: The Lord, the God of David, your ancestor, says—"I heard your prayer, I saw your tears. I got you. You gon' be healed. In three days, you'll be back at My temple."'

6.text: 'I'm adding 15 more years to your life. And on top of that, I'm saving you and this city from the king of Assyria. I'll defend this place for My sake and for David's sake.'

7.text: Then Isaiah said, 'Get a lump of figs.' They brought it, put it on Hezekiah's boil, and just like that, he got better.

8.text: Hezekiah asked Isaiah, 'What sign is the Lord gon' give me to prove I'll be healed and back in the temple in three days?'

9.text: Isaiah said, 'Alright, this is the sign from the Lord—do you want the shadow on the sundial to move forward ten steps or back ten steps?'

10.text: Hezekiah said, 'Man, it's too easy for the shadow to go forward. Make it go back ten steps instead.'

11.text: So Isaiah prayed, and the Lord made the shadow move back ten steps on the sundial of Ahaz.

12.text: Later, Berodach-Baladan, son of Baladan, king of Babylon, sent Hezekiah letters and a gift 'cause he heard Hezekiah had been sick.

13.text: Hezekiah welcomed them in and started showing off—gave them a full tour of his treasure house: all the silver, gold, spices, fine oils, his entire armory—everything. He left nothing out.

14.text: Then Isaiah came to Hezekiah and asked, 'Who were those men? Where they from?'

15.text: Hezekiah said, 'They came from Babylon—a faraway place.'

16.text: Isaiah asked, 'What all did they see?' Hezekiah said, 'Everything. I showed them all my treasures. I didn't hold back anything.'

17.text: Then Isaiah hit him with a word from the Lord: 'Listen up—days are coming when everything in your palace, all the wealth your ancestors stored up, will be carried off to Babylon. Nothing will be left.'

18.text: 'Even some of your own sons—your descendants—gon' be taken as captives, made into eunuchs in the king of Babylon's palace.'

19.text: Hezekiah said, 'Well… at least the Lord's word is good.' He was thinking, 'At least things gon' stay peaceful while I'm still alive.'

20.text: Everything else Hezekiah did—all his power, how he built the water tunnel to bring water into the city—it's all written in the book of the kings of Judah.

21.text: Then Hezekiah died and was buried with his ancestors. His son Manasseh took over the throne.

1.text: Manasseh was just 12 years old when he became king, and he ruled for 55 years in Jerusalem. His mama was Hephzibah.

2.text: But he was wild—he did evil just like the nations God kicked out before Israel moved in.

3.text: He brought back all the high places his daddy Hezekiah had torn down. He built altars for Baal, made an Asherah pole like Ahab had done, and started worshiping the sun, moon, and stars.

4.text: On top of that, he built altars inside the Lord's own temple—the place where God had said, 'This is My spot in Jerusalem.'

5.text: He even put altars for the stars in both courtyards of the Lord's house.

6.text: And it gets worse—Manasseh sacrificed his own son in fire, got deep into witchcraft, sorcery, fortune-telling, and was consulting psychics and mediums. Straight-up disrespecting the Lord.

7.text: Dude even put a carved idol of Asherah inside the Lord's temple—the same place where God told David and Solomon, 'I chose this city out of all Israel. My name stays here forever.'

8.text: 'I promised I wouldn't kick Israel off their land—as long as they followed My commands, like Moses told them.'

9.text: But Manasseh had them out here acting worse than the nations God had destroyed before them.

10.text: The Lord sent prophets with a message.

11.text: 'Manasseh, king of Judah, has done straight-up evil—worse than even the Amorites before him. And he led Judah into sin too.'

12.text: 'So here's what's coming—Judah and Jerusalem are about to get hit so bad that just hearing about it will make people's ears ring.'

13.text: 'I'm about to judge Jerusalem the same way I did Samaria and Ahab's house. I'm wiping this city clean—like wiping a plate, turning it upside down.'

14.text: 'I'm done with y'all. I'm letting your enemies take over, and y'all gonna be looted and carried off.'

15.text: 'This been a long time coming—Israel been acting up since the day I freed them from Egypt.'

16.text: Manasseh wasn't just leading people into sin—he had innocent people killed left and right, till Jerusalem was soaked in blood from one end to the other.

17.text: Everything else he did? It's in the book of the kings of Judah.

18.text: Then Manasseh died and was buried in his own garden—the Garden of Uzza. His son Amon took the throne next.

19.text: Amon was 22 when he became king, and he ruled for just two years in Jerusalem. His mama was Meshullemeth, daughter of Haruz from Jotbah.

20.text: He was no better than his daddy—evil in the Lord's eyes.

21.text: He followed Manasseh's ways, worshiping the same idols.

22.text: He completely turned his back on the Lord and refused to walk in His ways.

23.text: Then his own servants plotted against him and assassinated him in his palace.

24.text: But the people of Judah weren't having that—they executed everyone who was part of the conspiracy and made Amon's son Josiah king.

25.text: Everything else Amon did? It's in the book of the kings of Judah.

26.text: They buried him in his tomb in the Garden of Uzza, and then Josiah took the throne.

1.text: Josiah was just 8 years old when he became king, and he ruled for 31 years in Jerusalem. His mama was Jedidah, daughter of Adaiah from Bozkath.

2.text: He did right by the Lord, following in the ways of his ancestor David. He stayed solid—never strayed left or right.

3.text: In the 18th year of Josiah's reign, he sent Shaphan the scribe—son of Azaliah, grandson of Meshullam—to the temple with a message.

4.text: 'Go see Hilkiah, the high priest, and tell him to count all the money that's been collected at the Lord's house—the money the doorkeepers gathered from the people.'

5.text: 'Then give that money to the workers—the folks repairing the temple. Make sure the overseers hand it out to the carpenters, builders, and masons.'

6.text: 'Use it to buy timber and cut stone to fix up the Lord's house.'

7.text: 'Oh, and don't worry about making them report back on spending. These guys are trustworthy.'

8.text: Then Hilkiah the high priest told Shaphan, 'Yo, I found the Book of the Law in the Lord's house!' He handed it to Shaphan, and Shaphan started reading it.

9.text: Shaphan went back to the king and said, 'We handled the money from the temple and gave it to the workers overseeing the repairs.'

10.text: Then he added, 'By the way, Hilkiah the priest gave me this book.' And he started reading it to the king.

11.text: As soon as Josiah heard the words from the Book of the Law, he tore his clothes in distress.

12.text: Then he told Hilkiah, Ahikam (son of Shaphan), Achbor (son of Michaiah), Shaphan the scribe, and Asaiah (one of his officials),

13.text: 'Go ask the Lord what this means for me, for the people, and for all Judah. The Lord's anger must be huge, 'cause our ancestors straight-up ignored this book. They didn't do what's written in it.'

14.text: So Hilkiah, Ahikam, Achbor, Shaphan, and Asaiah went to see Huldah, the prophetess—the wife of Shallum (son of Tikvah, grandson of Harhas), the wardrobe keeper. She lived in Jerusalem's Second Quarter.

15.text: Huldah told them, 'The Lord God of Israel says this—go tell the king who sent you:'

16.text: 'The Lord says: I'm about to bring disaster on this place and its people—everything written in that book the king just heard.'

17.text: 'Why? 'Cause they turned their backs on Me, burned incense to other gods, and made Me furious with all their idol-worshiping ways. My anger against this place is set—I ain't holding it back.'

18.text: 'But for King Josiah, who sent y'all to ask about Me—tell him this:'

19.text: 'Since your heart was humble, and you truly listened when you heard My warning about this place becoming cursed and desolate—since you tore your clothes and cried out to Me—I heard you.'

20.text: 'So here's what I'm gonna do—I'll let you live out your days in peace. You won't have to see the disaster I'm bringing to this place.' So the officials took that message back to the king.

1.text: King Josiah gathered all the elders of Judah and Jerusalem.

2.text: Then he and all the people—priests, prophets, everybody from the richest to the poorest—went to the Lord's temple. And right there, Josiah read every word from the Book of the Covenant that had been found in the temple.

3.text: Then the king stood by the pillar and made a promise before the Lord—to follow Him, keep His commandments, and live by everything written in the book. And the people stood with him on that promise.

4.text: Josiah ordered Hilkiah the high priest, the assistant priests, and the temple guards to take everything made for Baal, Asherah, and the stars out of the Lord's house. He burned them outside Jerusalem in the fields of Kidron, then took the ashes to Bethel.

5.text: He got rid of all those fake priests—the ones past kings had put in place to burn incense at the high places in Judah and Jerusalem. That included the ones burning incense to Baal, the sun, the moon, the constellations, and all the stars.

6.text: He even took the Asherah pole out of the Lord's house, burned it by the Brook Kidron, ground it to dust, and scattered the ashes over the graves of common folks.

7.text: Then he tore down the temple booths where the cult prostitutes were staying—those places where women wove cloth for the Asherah idol.

8.text: Josiah brought all the priests back from Judah's cities and shut down the high places, from Geba to Beersheba, where priests had been burning incense. He also destroyed the high places by the city gates—like the one at the entrance of Joshua's gate, the former governor of the city.

9.text: Even though these priests weren't allowed to serve at the Lord's altar in Jerusalem, they could still eat unleavened bread with the others.

10.text: Josiah shut down Topheth in the Valley of Hinnom so that nobody could burn their sons or daughters as sacrifices to Molech anymore.

11.text: He removed the horses that the kings of Judah had dedicated to the sun. They were kept near the entrance of the Lord's temple, by the room of Nathan-Melech (a royal official). Then Josiah burned the chariots of the sun.

12.text: He tore down the altars on the roof of Ahaz's upper chamber that past kings of Judah had built, plus the ones Manasseh had built in the temple courts. He crushed them to dust and dumped the remains in the Brook Kidron.

13.text: Then he destroyed the high places east of Jerusalem on the south side of the Mount of Corruption. These were the spots Solomon had built for Ashtoreth (the Sidonian idol), Chemosh (the Moabite god), and Milcom (the Ammonite idol).

14.text: Josiah smashed the sacred pillars, cut down the Asherah poles, and covered the places with human bones to make them unclean.

15.text: Even the altar at Bethel—the one Jeroboam, son of Nebat, had set up to lead Israel into sin—Josiah tore it down. He burned the high place, crushed it to dust, and burned the Asherah pole there too.

16.text: As Josiah looked around, he saw some tombs on the hill, had the bones dug up, and burned them on the altar to defile it—just like the man of God had prophesied years before.

17.text: Then Josiah asked, 'What's that gravestone over there?' The people said, 'That's the tomb of the man of God who prophesied what you just did to this altar.'

18.text: Josiah said, 'Leave him be. Don't touch his bones.' So they left his bones, along with the bones of the prophet from Samaria.

19.text: Josiah wiped out all the shrines in Samaria that past Israelite kings had built to provoke God. He destroyed them just like he did in Bethel.

20.text: Then he executed all the pagan priests in Samaria and burned their bones on the altars. After that, he went back to Jerusalem.

21.text: Josiah told all the people, 'We celebrating the Passover for the Lord, just like it says in the Book of the Covenant.'

22.text: A Passover like this hadn't been celebrated since the time of the judges—not even under the kings of Israel or Judah.

23.text: But in the 18th year of Josiah's reign, he made sure the Passover was properly celebrated in Jerusalem.

24.text: Josiah also removed all the psychics, fortune tellers, household idols, and any detestable thing in Judah and Jerusalem. He made sure to follow everything written in the Book of the Law that Hilkiah the priest had found in the Lord's temple.

25.text: No king before Josiah had ever turned to the Lord with his whole heart, soul, and strength like he did—following the Law of Moses completely. And no king after him did either.

26.text: But even with all that, the Lord's anger against Judah was still hot—because of all the evil Manasseh had done before.

27.text: The Lord said, 'Judah's getting the same treatment as Israel. I'm removing them from My sight and rejecting this city, Jerusalem—the place I chose for My name to dwell.'

28.text: Everything else Josiah did? It's all written in the book of the kings of Judah.

29.text: During Josiah's reign, Pharaoh Necho of Egypt marched to the Euphrates River to help the king of Assyria. Josiah went out to fight him, but Necho killed him at Megiddo.

30.text: Josiah's servants carried his body in a chariot back to Jerusalem and buried him in his own tomb. Then the people took his son, Jehoahaz, anointed him, and made him king.

31.text: Jehoahaz was 23 when he became king, but he only lasted three months in Jerusalem. His mama was Hamutal, daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah.

32.text: And like his ancestors, he did evil in the Lord's sight.

33.text: Then Pharaoh Necho locked him up at Riblah in Hamath so he couldn't rule in Jerusalem. And he put Judah under a heavy tax—100 talents of silver and 1 talent of gold.

34.text: Necho then replaced Jehoahaz with his brother Eliakim, son of Josiah, and changed his name to Jehoiakim. Meanwhile, he took Jehoahaz to Egypt, where he died.

35.text: Jehoiakim paid the silver and gold to Pharaoh by taxing the people—each person had to pay their share according to the king's demands.

36.text: Jehoiakim was 25 when he became king, and he ruled for 11 years in Jerusalem. His mama was Zebudah, daughter of Pedaiah from Rumah.

37.text: And just like his ancestors, he did evil in the Lord's sight.

1.text: During Jehoiakim's reign, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, came through, and Jehoiakim had no choice but to serve him for three years. But then, Jehoiakim got bold and rebelled.

2.text: So the Lord sent raiders—Chaldeans, Syrians, Moabites, and Ammonites—straight at Judah to tear it apart, just like He warned through His prophets.

3.text: This was all part of God's judgment. Judah was getting removed from His sight because of the sins of Manasseh—dude had done too much wrong.

4.text: Especially for all the innocent blood he shed. He filled Jerusalem with it, and the Lord wasn't letting that slide.

5.text: Everything else Jehoiakim did? It's all written in the book of the kings of Judah.

6.text: Then Jehoiakim died, and his son Jehoiachin took over.

7.text: Meanwhile, the king of Egypt stayed out of it, 'cause the king of Babylon had already taken all his land—from the Brook of Egypt to the Euphrates River.

8.text: Jehoiachin was 18 when he became king, but he only ruled for three months in Jerusalem. His mama was Nehushta, daughter of Elnathan from Jerusalem.

9.text: And just like his daddy, he did evil in the Lord's sight.

10.text: Around that time, Babylon's army came up against Jerusalem and laid siege to the city.

11.text: Then Nebuchadnezzar himself showed up while his men were surrounding the city.

12.text: So Jehoiachin, his mama, his officials, his commanders, and his officers all surrendered to Nebuchadnezzar. In the eighth year of Nebuchadnezzar's reign, he took Jehoiachin prisoner.

13.text: Babylon's king looted everything—he emptied out the Lord's temple and the royal treasury. He even cut apart all the gold items Solomon had made for the temple, just like the Lord had warned.

14.text: Then he exiled the entire city—captains, warriors, 10,000 captives, plus all the craftsmen and metalworkers. Only the poorest folks got left behind.

15.text: Jehoiachin, his mama, his wives, his officials, and the upper-class citizens were all taken to Babylon.

16.text: Nebuchadnezzar also took 7,000 elite soldiers and 1,000 skilled workers—anybody fit for war—into captivity.

17.text: Then the king of Babylon made Mattaniah (Jehoiachin's uncle) the new king and changed his name to Zedekiah.

18.text: Zedekiah was 21 when he became king, and he ruled for 11 years in Jerusalem. His mama was Hamutal, daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah.

19.text: But he wasn't any better—he did evil, just like Jehoiakim.

20.text: At this point, God's anger was fully on Jerusalem and Judah. He finally cast them out of His presence. But even after all that, Zedekiah still tried to rebel against Babylon.

1.text: In the ninth year of Zedekiah's reign, on the tenth day of the tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, and his whole army came through and surrounded Jerusalem. They built a siege wall all around it.

2.text: The city stayed under siege until the eleventh year of Zedekiah's reign.

3.text: By the ninth day of the fourth month, the famine was so bad there was no food left for the people.

4.text: Then the city walls got breached. That night, Judah's warriors tried to escape through the gate near the king's garden, even though Babylon's army had the whole city surrounded. Zedekiah took off through the plains.

5.text: But Babylon's army chased him down and caught him in the plains of Jericho. His whole army scattered.

6.text: They captured Zedekiah and took him to Nebuchadnezzar at Riblah, where they handed down judgment on him.

7.text: Right in front of Zedekiah, they killed his sons. Then they blinded him, put him in chains, and hauled him off to Babylon.

8.text: On the seventh day of the fifth month, in the nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar's reign, Nebuzaradan, the captain of the Babylonian guard, came to Jerusalem.

9.text: He burned down the Lord's temple, the king's palace, and every important building in Jerusalem.

10.text: Then the Babylonian army tore down the city walls.

11.text: Nebuzaradan took into captivity the rest of the people who were still in the city, including those who had already surrendered to Babylon.

12.text: But he left behind some of the poorest folks to work the vineyards and fields.

13.text: Babylon's army broke apart the bronze pillars, the carts, and the massive bronze basin (the 'Sea') in the Lord's temple and took all the bronze back to Babylon.

14.text: They also took the pots, shovels, trimmers, spoons, and all the bronze tools the priests used for worship.

15.text: Anything made of gold or silver—firepans, basins, you name it—Nebuzaradan took it all.

16.text: The sheer amount of bronze in the two pillars, the Sea, and the carts Solomon had made for the temple was massive.

17.text: Each pillar was 27 feet tall, with a 4.5-foot-high bronze capital on top, decorated with bronze pomegranates woven into a network. Both pillars were the same.

18.text: Nebuzaradan also arrested Seraiah the chief priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and three temple guards.

19.text: He took the city's army commander, five of the king's closest officials still in the city, the chief recruiting officer, and 60 other men who were still in Jerusalem.

20.text: Nebuzaradan rounded them up and took them to Nebuchadnezzar at Riblah.

21.text: There, the king of Babylon had them all executed. And just like that, Judah was officially taken into captivity.

22.text: Nebuchadnezzar put Gedaliah, son of Ahikam (son of Shaphan), in charge of the people left in Judah.

23.text: When Judah's army commanders and their men heard Babylon had made Gedaliah governor, they went to meet him at Mizpah: Ishmael (son of Nethaniah), Johanan (son of Kareah), Seraiah (son of Tanhumeth), Jaazaniah, and others.

24.text: Gedaliah told them, 'Don't be scared of serving Babylon. Stay in the land, serve the king of Babylon, and things will go well for y'all.'

25.text: But in the seventh month, Ishmael (son of Nethaniah, from the royal family) and ten men with him assassinated Gedaliah, along with the Jews and Babylonians who were with him at Mizpah.

26.text: After that, everyone—rich and poor, along with Judah's army leaders—fled to Egypt, scared of what Babylon might do next.

27.text: In the thirty-seventh year of Jehoiachin's captivity, on the twenty-seventh day of the twelfth month, Evil-Merodach, king of Babylon, took the throne and decided to free Jehoiachin.

28.text: He treated him kindly and gave him a better position than the other captive kings in Babylon.

29.text: Jehoiachin changed out of his prison clothes and ate at the king's table regularly for the rest of his life.

30.text: And for the rest of his days, the king of Babylon made sure Jehoiachin got a daily allowance of food.

1.text: After Saul died, David had just come back from fighting the Amalekites and had been chillin' in Ziklag for two days.

2.text: On the third day, a man came from Saul's camp, lookin' rough—clothes torn, dust all over him. He fell to the ground in front of David.

3.text: David asked, 'Where you from?' The man said, 'I made it out of Israel's camp alive.'

4.text: David asked, 'What happened? Tell me everything.' The man said, 'Israel got wiped out. A lot of people got killed. Saul and Jonathan are dead.'

5.text: David asked, 'How you know for sure that Saul and Jonathan are dead?'

6.text: The man said, 'I was on Mount Gilboa, and I saw Saul leanin' on his spear with enemy chariots and soldiers closin' in on him.'

7.text: He looked back and saw me, called me over. I said, 'Here I am.'

8.text: Saul asked, 'Who you wit'?' and I told him, 'I'm an Amalekite.'

9.text: Then he said, 'Kill me. I'm barely holdin' on, and I don't wanna go out like this.'

10.text: So I did it. I put him out his misery 'cause I knew he wasn't gon' make it. Then I took his crown and his bracelet, and I brought 'em to you.

11.text: David tore his clothes in grief, and all his men did too.

12.text: They mourned, cried, and fasted till sundown, grieving over Saul, Jonathan, and all the fallen Israelites.

13.text: David asked the young man, 'Where you from again?' He said, 'I'm an Amalekite, born to a foreigner.'

14.text: David snapped, 'You wasn't scared to kill the Lord's anointed?!'

15.text: Then David told one of his men, 'Handle him.' And they took him out.

16.text: David told the young man, 'You brought this on yourself. You said with your own mouth that you killed the Lord's anointed.'

17.text: David wrote a song for Saul and Jonathan, mourning their deaths.

18.text: He told Judah to learn it, callin' it The Song of the Bow. (It was written in The Book of Jasher.)

19.text: The glory of Israel is gone, fallen on the heights! How the mighty have fallen!

20.text: Don't let the Philistines in Gath hear it! Don't spread the news in Ashkelon, or their women will celebrate.

21.text: May Mount Gilboa never see rain again—Saul's shield was tossed away there, no longer anointed with oil.

22.text: Jonathan's bow stayed sharp, Saul's sword never missed.

23.text: Saul and Jonathan—beloved in life, inseparable in death. Faster than eagles, stronger than lions!

24.text: Daughters of Israel, cry for Saul! He gave y'all luxury and gold.

25.text: How the mighty have fallen! Jonathan—killed on the battlefield.

26.text: I'm hurtin' for you, my brother Jonathan. Your love was real, deeper than a woman's love.

27.text: How the mighty have fallen! Weapons of war gone.

1.text: After all that went down, David asked The Most High, 'Should I go up to one of Judah's cities?' And The Most High said, 'Yeah, go up.' David asked, 'Where exactly?' And He said, 'Hebron.'

2.text: So David packed up and went to Hebron, takin' both his wives—Ahinoam from Jezreel and Abigail, the widow of Nabal from Carmel.

3.text: David also brought all his people who was rollin' with him, and they moved their families into the towns around Hebron.

4.text: Then the men of Judah came through and made David king over Judah. They also told him, 'Yo, the men of Jabesh-Gilead the ones who buried Saul.'

5.text: David sent a message to them, sayin', 'Y'all blessed by The Most High for what y'all did—showin' love to Saul and givin' him a proper burial.'

6.text: 'May The Most High show y'all love and truth for that. And I'ma do right by y'all too, 'cause y'all handled that like real ones.'

7.text: 'So be strong, stand tall. Saul is gone, but Judah made me king now.'

8.text: But Abner, son of Ner—who was Saul's top general—took Saul's son Ishbosheth and moved him to Mahanaim.

9.text: Then he made him king over Gilead, Ashurites, Jezreel, Ephraim, Benjamin—basically all of Israel.

10.text: Ishbosheth was 40 years old when he started ruling over Israel. He only lasted two years. Meanwhile, Judah was ridin' with David.

11.text: David reigned over Judah from Hebron for seven years and six months.

12.text: One day, Abner and Ishbosheth's crew left Mahanaim and pulled up to Gibeon.

13.text: Joab, Zeruiah's son, and David's crew pulled up too. They met at the pool of Gibeon—sittin' on opposite sides, just starin' at each other.

14.text: Abner was like, 'Let's have some of these young dudes get up and scrap for us.' Joab was like, 'Bet. Let's do it.'

15.text: So twelve of Ishbosheth's guys from Benjamin and twelve of David's squad got up.

16.text: They squared up, grabbed each other, and straight-up stabbed each other at the same time. They all dropped dead. That's why they called that place 'The Field of Sharp Swords' in Gibeon.

17.text: After that, a wild fight broke out, and David's crew beat Ishbosheth's squad down.

18.text: Now Joab, Abishai, and Asahel—three brothers—were out there. Asahel was quick, dude ran like a gazelle.

19.text: He chased after Abner, not switchin' lanes or slowin' down, locked in on him.

20.text: Abner looked back and said, 'Yo, that you, Asahel?' Asahel was like, 'Yeah, it's me.'

21.text: Abner told him, 'Fall back, bro. Go take somebody else's gear.' But Asahel wasn't lettin' up.

22.text: Abner said again, 'Bruh, stop! I don't wanna kill you. I can't face your brother Joab if I do.'

23.text: But Asahel didn't listen. So Abner hit him with the back end of his spear, right in the gut. Spear went straight through, and dude dropped on the spot. Everybody who saw him dead like that just stopped in their tracks.

24.text: Joab and Abishai kept chasin' Abner till sundown. They caught up with him near Giah, on the way to the Gibeon desert.

25.text: The Benjamites regrouped behind Abner, formed up, and took their stand on a hill.

26.text: Abner called out to Joab, 'Bruh, how long we gon' do this? You know it's only gon' end bad. Call your people off.'

27.text: Joab said, 'Man, if you ain't say nothin', my guys would've chased y'all till morning.'

28.text: Then Joab blew the horn, and everybody stopped fightin'. No more chasin', no more beefin'.

29.text: Abner and his men walked all night, crossed the Jordan, and made it back to Mahanaim.

30.text: Joab stopped the chase, regrouped his people, and counted up—nineteen of his men and Asahel were dead.

31.text: But they took out 360 men from Abner's squad.

32.text: They picked up Asahel's body and buried him in Bethlehem. Then Joab and his crew marched all night and made it back to Hebron by sunrise.

1.text: That war between Saul's people and David's people dragged on for a long time. But David kept gettin' stronger, while Saul's house kept fallin' off.

2.text: While in Hebron, David had some sons. His firstborn was Amnon, by Ahinoam from Jezreel.

3.text: His second was Chileab, by Abigail—Nabal's widow from Carmel. Third was Absalom, son of Maacah, Talmai's daughter, the king of Geshur.

4.text: Fourth was Adonijah, son of Haggith. Fifth was Shephatiah, son of Abital.

5.text: Sixth was Ithream, by Eglah, another one of David's wives. All these kids was born while David was in Hebron.

6.text: During the war between Saul's house and David's, Abner was out here tryin' to secure his spot in Saul's camp.

7.text: Now, Saul had a concubine named Rizpah, daughter of Aiah. Ishbosheth came at Abner like, 'Why you messin' with my father's woman?'

8.text: That set Abner off. He said, 'Bruh, you really think I'm out here playin' games? I been holdin' it down for your daddy's house, his people, and his friends. I could've flipped on you anytime, but I didn't. And you gon' come at me over this?'

9.text: 'Man, may God deal with me if I don't do what He promised David—'

10.text: 'Move this whole kingdom from Saul's people to David's, from Dan to Beersheba.'

11.text: Ishbosheth ain't say nothin' after that 'cause he knew Abner wasn't one to play with.

12.text: So Abner sent messengers to David like, 'Aye, who really runnin' this land? Let's make a deal, and I'ma bring all Israel over to you.'

13.text: David was like, 'Bet, we can do that. But first, I need you to bring Michal, Saul's daughter, when you come to see me.'

14.text: David also sent word to Ishbosheth, sayin', 'Run me my wife Michal—I put in work for her, paid for her with Philistine foreskins.'

15.text: So Ishbosheth made her husband, Paltiel, give her up.

16.text: Dude was heartbroken, followed her cryin' all the way to Bahurim, till Abner turned around and said, 'Man, go home.' And he did.

17.text: Abner started talkin' to the Israelite elders, sayin', 'Y'all been wantin' David as king for a minute.'

18.text: 'Well, it's time! The Most High already said David is the one who's gonna save Israel from the Philistines and all our enemies.'

19.text: He also hollered at the tribe of Benjamin, then went down to Hebron to talk to David about all this.

20.text: Abner pulled up to Hebron with twenty of his people. David threw a big feast for them.

21.text: Then Abner told David, 'I'ma bring all of Israel to you, so you can rule over everything like you always wanted.' David let Abner leave in peace.

22.text: Right after that, Joab and David's men came back from a raid, bringin' a whole lot of loot. Abner wasn't there 'cause David had already sent him off in peace.

23.text: When Joab got back, folks told him, 'Yo, Abner came to the king, and David let him leave on good terms.'

24.text: Joab was heated. He went straight to David like, 'Bruh, what did you just do?! Abner was just here, and you let him leave?'

25.text: 'You know Abner only came to spy on you, right? He just tryna peep your moves!'

26.text: Joab left David and secretly sent messengers to bring Abner back, but David ain't know about it.

27.text: When Abner got back to Hebron, Joab pulled him to the side like, 'Let's talk in private.' Then he straight-up stabbed him in the gut—killed him right there, tryna get revenge for his brother Asahel.

28.text: When David heard about it, he said, 'I ain't got nothin' to do with this. My kingdom clean from this murder forever.'

29.text: 'Let that blood be on Joab and his whole family! May his house always have somebody sick, broke, crippled, or dyin' by the sword.'

30.text: Joab and his brother Abishai did Abner like that 'cause he had killed their brother Asahel back at Gibeon.

31.text: David told Joab and all his men, 'Tear your clothes, throw on sackcloth, and mourn for Abner.' Then he followed behind the coffin.

32.text: They buried Abner in Hebron. David stood at the grave cryin', and everybody else wept too.

33.text: Then David sang a funeral song for Abner: 'Did Abner really have to go out like that?'

34.text: 'He wasn't bound up, he wasn't chained, yet he fell like somebody who got done dirty by thugs.'

35.text: Later, people tried to get David to eat while it was still daytime, but he swore, 'Man, may God deal with me if I eat before the sun goes down!'

36.text: The people saw this and respected David even more, 'cause he always did right by folks.

37.text: That day, everybody in Israel realized that David had nothin' to do with Abner's murder.

38.text: David told his people, 'Y'all see this? A real one just got taken out today in Israel.'

39.text: 'I may be king, but I feel powerless against these sons of Zeruiah—they reckless. The Most High gon' deal with them accordingly.'

1.text: When Saul's son, Ishbosheth, heard Abner got murked in Hebron, he straight-up lost his nerve. The whole nation of Israel was shook.

2.text: Now Ishbosheth had two dudes under him—military captains—Baanah and Rechab. They was sons of Rimmon, a Beerothite from the tribe of Benjamin.

3.text: Side note: The Beerothites had dipped to Gittaim a while back and been livin' there ever since.

4.text: Also, Saul's grandson, Mephibosheth—Jonathan's son—was crippled. When he was five, the news came that Saul and Jonathan was dead. His nurse tried to run with him, but she dropped him, and dude ended up lame for life.

5.text: So Rechab and Baanah pulled up at Ishbosheth's crib in the middle of the day, while he was laid up takin' a nap.

6.text: They rolled up inside like they was just there to grab some wheat, but instead, they stabbed him in the stomach. Then they took off.

7.text: After they got in his house, saw him laid up in bed, they straight-up killed him, chopped off his head, and dipped out, movin' all night across the plains.

8.text: They took Ishbosheth's head to David at Hebron, talkin' 'bout, 'Yo, King, look at this! This here is the head of Saul's son—the same dude who was tryna take you out. The Most High just avenged you today!'

9.text: But David looked at them and said, 'As The Most High lives—the one who got me through all my struggles—'

10.text: 'Let me remind y'all—when that other dude thought he was bringin' me good news about Saul dyin', thinkin' I was finna reward him, what happened? I had him executed on sight in Ziklag.'

11.text: 'So if I did that to him, what y'all think gon' happen to y'all? Y'all done killed a man in his own house, while he was laid up in bed. Y'all really thought I was finna celebrate this?'

12.text: David ain't waste no time. He told his men, 'Handle that.' And they did—Rechab and Baanah got executed on the spot. They even cut off their hands and feet, then hung 'em up by the pool in Hebron. But they took Ishbosheth's head and buried it in Abner's tomb in Hebron.

1.text: All the tribes of Israel pulled up to David at Hebron and said, 'Look, we family—we your flesh and blood.'

2.text: 'Even when Saul was king, you was the one leadin' us in battle. And The Most High already told you, "You gon' be the one to lead my people and rule over Israel."'

3.text: So all the elders of Israel came through to Hebron, and David made a covenant with them before The Most High. They anointed him king over all Israel.

4.text: David was 30 when he became king, and he reigned for 40 years.

5.text: He ruled Judah from Hebron for seven years and six months, then ruled all Israel and Judah from Jerusalem for thirty-three years.

6.text: David and his squad rolled up to Jerusalem to face the Jebusites—the folks livin' there. The Jebusites was talkin' trash, sayin', 'Man, you ain't gettin' in here. Even our blind and lame could hold you off!'

7.text: But David wasn't havin' it—he took over the stronghold of Zion, which became the City of David.

8.text: That day, David said, 'Whoever climbs up through the water tunnel and takes out these Jebusites—the so-called "lame and blind" that I can't stand—he gon' be the new commander.' That's why folks say, 'The blind and the lame can't come up in here.'

9.text: David moved into the stronghold and called it the City of David. Then he built up the area, starting from the Millo and working inward.

10.text: David kept rising up, and The Most High, the Lord of Heaven's Armies, was with him.

11.text: Hiram, king of Tyre, sent messengers to David, along with cedar wood, carpenters, and stonemasons. They built David a palace.

12.text: David realized that The Most High had established him as king over Israel and was lifting him up for the sake of His people.

13.text: David took more concubines and wives in Jerusalem after leavin' Hebron, and he had more sons and daughters.

14.text: These the names of his kids born in Jerusalem: Shammua, Shobab, Nathan, Solomon,

15.text: Ibhar, Elishua, Nepheg, Japhia,

16.text: Elishama, Eliada, and Eliphelet.

17.text: When the Philistines heard David got crowned king over Israel, they all went out lookin' for him. But David got word and dipped down to his stronghold.

18.text: The Philistines spread out across the Valley of Rephaim, tryna set up shop.

19.text: David checked in with The Most High, askin', 'Should I run up on these Philistines? You gon' put 'em in my hands?'

20.text: The Most High told him, 'Go ahead, I got you—you gon' take 'em down.' So David pulled up to Baal Perazim, wrecked 'em, and said, 'The Most High broke through my enemies like floodwaters!' That's why they called it Baal Perazim (which means 'Breakthrough Spot').

21.text: The Philistines ran off so quick, they left their idols behind. David and his crew scooped 'em up.

22.text: But them Philistines wasn't done. They regrouped and posted up in the Valley of Rephaim again.

23.text: David checked in with The Most High again, and this time, God said, 'Don't attack straight on. Go around behind 'em and hit 'em near the mulberry trees.'

24.text: 'When you hear the sound of soldiers marchin' on top of them trees, that's your cue—move fast, 'cause that's Me goin' ahead of you to take out the Philistine camp.'

25.text: David did exactly what The Most High said, and he pushed the Philistines all the way back from Geba to Gezer.

1.text: David rounded up 30,000 of Israel's top men and got 'em all together.

2.text: Then he and his squad rolled out from Baale Judah to go bring back the Ark of God—the one called by The Most High's Name, the Lord of Heaven's Armies, who stays between the cherubim.

3.text: They put the Ark of God on a brand-new cart and took it out of Abinadab's house on the hill. Uzzah and Ahio—Abinadab's sons—was drivin' that cart.

4.text: Ahio was up front, leadin' the way while they took the Ark out.

5.text: David and all of Israel was out there jammin'—playin' music for The Most High with harps, lyres, tambourines, rattles, and cymbals. Straight-up celebration mode.

6.text: But when they got to Nachon's threshing floor, the oxen tripped. Uzzah reached out to grab the Ark and keep it from fallin'.

7.text: That made The Most High furious. Uzzah got struck right then and there for disrespectin' the Ark. He dropped dead on the spot, right next to the Ark of God.

8.text: David was mad about it—real heated. He named that spot Perez Uzzah, and that's what it's still called.

9.text: But after that, David got shook. He was like, 'Man, how we supposed to bring this Ark to me?'

10.text: So instead of takin' it straight to the City of David, David sent it to the house of Obed-Edom the Gittite.

11.text: The Ark stayed at Obed-Edom's house for three months, and The Most High blessed him and his whole family for keepin' it.

12.text: Somebody told David, 'Yo, The Most High been blessin' Obed-Edom big time 'cause of the Ark!' So David was like, 'Bet!' and went to bring the Ark to the City of David—this time, with pure joy.

13.text: After they carried the Ark six steps, David stopped and offered up some sacrifices—oxen and fattened sheep.

14.text: Then David broke out dancin'—hard—before The Most High. Dude was gettin' it, wearin' his linen ephod.

15.text: David and all of Israel brought the Ark back with shouts and trumpet blasts—full-blown praise session.

16.text: As the Ark rolled into the City of David, Michal—Saul's daughter—was peepin' through the window. She saw David leaping and spinnin' like crazy before The Most High, and she started lookin' down on him.

17.text: They brought the Ark in and set it up in the tent David had made for it. Then David gave burnt offerings and peace offerings to The Most High.

18.text: Once David was done with all that, he blessed the people in The Most High's Name.

19.text: Then he gave out food to everybody—a loaf of bread, some meat, and a raisin cake to every man and woman. After that, folks went home.

20.text: When David got home to bless his own household, Michal came at him. She was like, 'Wow, look at the king of Israel today—out here embarrassin' himself in front of all the servant girls, actin' like some common street dude.'

21.text: David clapped back, 'I was dancin' for The Most High, the same one who chose me over your daddy and his whole family, makin' me ruler over Israel. So yeah, I'ma praise Him!'

22.text: 'Matter fact, I'ma go even harder than this next time. You might think I look foolish, but those same servant girls you talkin' about? They gon' respect me for it.'

23.text: And just like that, Michal—Saul's daughter—never had kids for the rest of her life.

1.text: So David was chillin' in his palace, finally at peace 'cause The Most High had shut down all his enemies.

2.text: Then he told the prophet Nathan, 'Look, I'm livin' in this fly crib made of cedar wood, but The Most High's Ark still sittin' in a tent.'

3.text: Nathan told him, 'Go 'head and do what's on your heart, 'cause The Most High is with you.'

4.text: But that same night, The Most High came to Nathan with a word.

5.text: 'Go tell my servant David: "So you think you gon' build a house for me to live in?"'

6.text: 'I been movin' from place to place since Egypt, stayin' in a tent this whole time.'

7.text: 'Did I ever tell any of the leaders I put in charge, 'Yo, why ain't y'all built me a cedar house yet?' Nope.'

8.text: 'So here's what you tell David: "I pulled you out the sheep fields, took you from watchin' flocks to rulin' Israel."'

9.text: 'I been with you everywhere you went, knocked down all your enemies, and made your name great—like the biggest names on Earth.'

10.text: 'I'ma set up a home for my people Israel, where they can stay without evil folks messin' with them like before.'

11.text: 'Since back when I put judges over Israel, I been givin' you peace from your enemies. But now, The Most High sayin' He gon' build YOU a house.'

12.text: 'When your time comes and you rest with your ancestors, I'ma raise up one of your own sons to take your place, and I'ma establish his kingdom.'

13.text: 'He gon' build a house for My name, and I'ma make sure his kingdom last forever.'

14.text: 'I'ma be his Father, and he gon' be my son. If he mess up, I'ma check him like a father do, with discipline from people.'

15.text: 'But I ain't never takin' my love away from him like I did Saul, the one I removed for you.'

16.text: 'Your house, your kingdom, and your throne gon' last forever in My sight.'

17.text: Nathan told David everything The Most High had said, straight up.

18.text: Then David went and sat before The Most High, sayin', 'Who am I, Lord? Who is my family, that You done brought me this far?'

19.text: 'And You tellin' me this is just the beginning? You plannin' all this for my future too?'

20.text: 'What else can I even say? You already know me inside and out.'

21.text: 'You did all this, not for me, but for Your word's sake—to make sure Your servant really understands.'

22.text: 'That's why You're so great, Lord! Ain't nobody like You. No other god can compare to what we been told about You.'

23.text: 'What other nation got a story like ours? You picked Israel as Your people, went and rescued us Yourself, and made a name for Yourself with all the wild, powerful things You did!'

24.text: 'You made Israel Your people forever, and You, Lord, became our God.'

25.text: 'So now, Lord, everything You promised about me and my family? Make it happen. Let it stand forever.'

26.text: 'Let Your name be lifted up forever, so folks will say, "The Lord Almighty is God over Israel!" Let my house stand strong before You.'

27.text: ''Cause You, Lord, told me You would build me a house. That's why I'm comin' to You with this prayer.'

28.text: 'Lord, You are God, and everything You say is true. And You promised this goodness to Your servant.'

29.text: 'So please, bless my house, let it stand forever before You. 'Cause when You bless somethin', Lord, it stays blessed forever.'

1.text: After all that, David ran up on the Philistines, put 'em in their place, and took Metheg Ammah from their hands.

2.text: Then he handled Moab—made them get down on the ground, lined 'em up, and measured 'em out. Two lines meant death, one line meant they could live. From that day on, Moab had to serve David and pay up.

3.text: David also went after Hadadezer, son of Rehob, king of Zobah, 'cause he was tryna take back his land near the Euphrates River.

4.text: David took 1,000 chariots, 700 horsemen, and 20,000 foot soldiers from him. He hamstrung most of the chariot horses but kept enough for 100 chariots.

5.text: Then the Syrians from Damascus came through to help Hadadezer, but David wasn't havin' it—he killed 22,000 of them.

6.text: David set up military outposts in Syria, and the Syrians had to start paying tribute. No matter where David went, The Most High had his back.

7.text: He took all the golden shields from Hadadezer's crew and brought 'em back to Jerusalem.

8.text: He also took a whole lot of bronze from Betah and Berothai, cities that belonged to Hadadezer.

9.text: When Toi, king of Hamath, heard that David had wiped out Hadadezer's whole army, he saw the writing on the wall.

10.text: So Toi sent his son Joram to roll up on David with gifts—silver, gold, and bronze. He came through to bless David, 'cause Toi and Hadadezer had beef for a long time.

11.text: David didn't keep none of it for himself—he dedicated all the gold and silver to The Most High, just like he did with all the loot from the nations he conquered.

12.text: This included Syria, Moab, Ammon, the Philistines, Amalek, and the stuff he took from Hadadezer.

13.text: David got real famous after he came back from droppin' 18,000 Syrians in the Valley of Salt.

14.text: He also set up garrisons in Edom, puttin' his people everywhere. The Edomites had no choice but to serve David. The Most High kept him winnin' no matter what.

15.text: David ruled over all of Israel, makin' sure things was fair and just for everybody.

16.text: Joab, son of Zeruiah, was in charge of the army. Jehoshaphat, son of Ahilud, handled the records.

17.text: Zadok, son of Ahitub, and Ahimelech, son of Abiathar, were the priests. Seraiah was the scribe.

18.text: Benaiah, son of Jehoiada, ran the Cherethites and Pelethites (David's personal security). And David's own sons were top officials in his administration.

1.text: One day, David was like, 'Is there anybody left from Saul's family? I wanna show 'em some love for Jonathan's sake.'

2.text: They found a servant from Saul's house named Ziba and brought him to David. The king asked, 'You Ziba?' Ziba said, 'Yeah, that's me!'

3.text: Then David asked, 'Ain't nobody else left from Saul's family that I can bless the way The Most High would?' Ziba said, 'Well… there's one—Jonathan's son, Mephibosheth. But he crippled in both feet.'

4.text: David asked, 'Where he at?' Ziba said, 'He stayin' in Lo Debar, at the house of Machir, son of Ammiel.'

5.text: So David sent his people to go get Mephibosheth from Machir's house in Lo Debar.

6.text: When Mephibosheth, son of Jonathan (and grandson of Saul), showed up, he fell on his face in front of David. David said, 'Mephibosheth?' And he answered, 'Yes, I'm here, your humble servant.'

7.text: David told him, 'Aye, don't be scared. I got nothin' but love for you 'cause of your father Jonathan. I'ma give you back all your granddaddy Saul's land, and from now on, you gon' eat at my table like family.'

8.text: Mephibosheth bowed and said, 'Why you even lookin' out for me? I ain't nothin' but a dead dog to you.'

9.text: Then David called Ziba and said, 'Listen, I just gave Mephibosheth everything that used to belong to Saul and his family.'

10.text: 'So you, your sons, and your servants gon' work the land for him, bring in the crops, and make sure he got food. But Mephibosheth himself? He gon' eat at my table every day, just like one of my own sons.' (Ziba, by the way, had 15 sons and 20 servants.)

11.text: Ziba said, 'King, whatever you say—I'ma do it.' Then David repeated, 'Mephibosheth gon' eat at my table, same as my own sons.'

12.text: Now Mephibosheth had a son named Micha, and everybody in Ziba's house now worked for him.

13.text: Mephibosheth moved to Jerusalem, and from then on, he ate at the king's table every day. And yeah—he was still crippled in both feet.

1.text: Sometime later, the king of Ammon died, and his son Hanun took over.

2.text: David was like, 'I'ma show Hanun some love 'cause his pops, Nahash, looked out for me.' So David sent some of his men to send condolences about his father.

3.text: But the Ammonite princes got in Hanun's ear, sayin', 'You really think David sent his people to honor your father? Nah, bruh. He sent 'em to spy on us, check out the city, and plot against us.'

4.text: So Hanun humiliated them—shaved off half their beards, cut their robes at the waist (exposin' their behinds), and sent 'em off lookin' crazy.

5.text: When David heard about it, he sent word to his men, tellin' them, 'Stay in Jericho till y'all beards grow back, then come home.' 'Cause they was real embarrassed.

6.text: The Ammonites realized they had seriously messed up with David, so they hired some backup—20,000 Syrian foot soldiers from Beth Rehob & Zoba, plus 1,000 men from Maacah, and 12,000 from Ish-Tob.

7.text: When David got the news, he sent Joab and his elite troops out to handle business.

8.text: The Ammonites lined up outside their city gates, ready to fight, while their Syrian backup was posted out in the open field.

9.text: Joab saw they had enemies in front and behind, so he split the army. He took Israel's best soldiers to fight the Syrians.

10.text: Then he put the rest under his brother Abishai, so they could hold it down against the Ammonites.

11.text: Joab told Abishai, 'Aye, if the Syrians come too hard, you got my back. And if the Ammonites get the upper hand on you, I got you.'

12.text: 'Stay strong, fam. Let's fight for our people and for God's cities. And whatever happens, The Most High gon' do what He do.'

13.text: Joab and his soldiers charged the Syrians, and the Syrians straight ran for their lives.

14.text: When the Ammonites saw their backup running scared, they took off too—ran back inside their city. So Joab and his crew left and went back to Jerusalem.

15.text: But the Syrians ain't take the L lightly. They regrouped for round two.

16.text: Hadadezer called in reinforcements from beyond the Euphrates River, and his commander Shobach led the army to a place called Helam.

17.text: David heard what was goin' down, so he gathered all of Israel, crossed the Jordan River, and met the Syrians head-on at Helam.

18.text: The Syrians lost bad—they tried to run, but David's army caught 'em. David killed 700 charioteers and 40,000 horsemen, plus took out their top general, Shobach, right there on the battlefield.

19.text: When the other kings under Hadadezer saw they ain't stand a chance, they made peace with David and started servin' him. From then on, the Syrians were too scared to help the Ammonites ever again.

1.text: It was springtime—the season when kings usually went out to battle. David sent Joab, his servants, and all of Israel to handle the Ammonites and siege Rabbah, but David stayed back in Jerusalem.

2.text: One evening, David got up from his bed, walked around on the rooftop of his palace, and spotted a woman bathing. She was fine as can be.

3.text: David got curious and asked about her. Somebody told him, 'That's Bathsheba, daughter of Eliam—Uriah the Hittite's wife.'
