4.text: But David sent for her anyway. She came through, and he slept with her. After that, she went back home.

5.text: A little while later, she sent word to David: 'I'm pregnant.'

6.text: So David hit up Joab: 'Send Uriah the Hittite to me.' Joab sent him over.

7.text: When Uriah arrived, David played it cool—asked him how Joab was doin', how the battle was goin'.

8.text: Then David told Uriah, 'Go home, clean up, relax.' David even sent a gift to his house after him.

9.text: But Uriah didn't go home. Instead, he slept outside with the palace guards.

10.text: David got the report: 'Uriah ain't go home.' So he asked, 'Bruh, you just came from the battlefield. Why didn't you go home?'

11.text: Uriah said, 'The Ark, Israel, and Judah are all in tents. Joab and the soldiers are in the field fightin'—how I'ma go home, eat, drink, and be with my wife? I ain't doin' it, King, not while my brothers at war.'

12.text: David told him, 'Stay here another day, then I'll send you back.' So Uriah stayed in Jerusalem.

13.text: That night, David invited him to dinner and got him drunk. But even after that, Uriah still didn't go home—he slept outside with the guards again.

14.text: By morning, David had enough. He wrote a letter to Joab and had Uriah deliver his own death sentence.

15.text: The letter said: 'Put Uriah on the front lines where the battle is the worst, then pull back so he gets killed.'

16.text: Joab followed orders—he put Uriah in the heat of the battle, right where the toughest warriors were.

17.text: And just like that, the enemy came out strong, some of David's men got killed, and Uriah the Hittite died, too.

18.text: Joab sent a messenger to report the battle news back to David.

19.text: He told the messenger, 'After you tell the king everything, if he gets mad about us fightin' too close to the city walls…'

20.text: And if he brings up how Abimelech got killed by a woman who dropped a millstone on him in Thebez, just tell him: "Uriah the Hittite is dead, too."

21.text: The messenger went to David and gave him the full report.

22.text: He said, 'The enemy came out strong, we pushed them back to the city gate…'

23.text: But they hit us with arrows from the walls. Some of your soldiers died, and… Uriah the Hittite is dead, too.'

24.text: David told the messenger, 'Tell Joab not to stress. War takes people out—one way or another. Keep pushin' against the city and take it down.' Then he told the messenger to hype Joab up.

25.text: When Bathsheba heard her husband Uriah was dead, she mourned for him.

26.text: After her mourning period was over, David sent for her, brought her to the palace, married her, and she had a son.

27.text: But The Most High was NOT pleased with what David had done.

1.text: The Most High sent Nathan to David. Nathan pulled up and told him a story: 'There were two men in a city—one was rich, the other was poor.'

2.text: 'The rich man had plenty—flocks and herds for days.'

3.text: 'The poor man? He only had one little lamb that he raised with love. The lamb ate from his plate, drank from his cup, and even slept in his arms—like a daughter to him.'

4.text: 'Then one day, a traveler came to visit the rich man. But instead of using his own sheep, he took the poor man's lamb, killed it, and served it up for dinner.'

5.text: David got heated when he heard this. He said, 'Whoever did this deserves to DIE!'

6.text: 'And on top of that, he gotta pay back four times what he took, 'cause he had no mercy!'

7.text: Nathan looked at David and said, 'YOU that man. The Most High says: "I made you king over Israel, saved you from Saul's hands,"

8.text: 'I gave you power, wealth, and wives, and if that wasn't enough, I would've given you more.'

9.text: 'But you disrespected My commands, took Uriah's wife, and had him killed in battle.'

10.text: 'So from now on, your family gon' deal with the sword nonstop, 'cause you disrespected Me and took Uriah's wife.'

11.text: 'And guess what? Trouble gon' rise from your own house. I'ma take your wives and give 'em to another man, and he gon' sleep with 'em out in the open.'

12.text: 'You did your dirt in secret, but I'ma expose you in front of everybody!'

13.text: David finally broke down: 'I messed up. I sinned against The Most High.'

14.text: Nathan said, 'The Most High already put your sin away—you won't die. But since you did this, and folks gon' use it to slander The Most High, your child will die.'

15.text: Then Nathan left, and soon after, The Most High struck Bathsheba's child with sickness.

16.text: David begged The Most High for the child's life. He fasted, laid on the ground all night, prayin'.

17.text: His people tried to get him up, but he wouldn't move—wouldn't even eat.

18.text: On the seventh day, the child died. But David's servants were scared to tell him, thinkin' he might hurt himself.

19.text: But David peeped the whispers and asked, 'The child gone, ain't he?' They answered, 'Yeah, he gone.'

20.text: So David got up, washed up, put on fresh clothes, went to The Most High's house, worshiped, then went home and asked for food.

21.text: His servants were confused: 'When the child was sick, you wouldn't eat, but now that he's dead, you eatin'?'

22.text: David said, 'While he was alive, I prayed and fasted, hopin' The Most High might show mercy.'

23.text: 'But now that he's gone, why fast? I can't bring him back. One day, I'ma go where he is, but he ain't comin' back to me.'

24.text: Later, David comforted Bathsheba, they slept together, and she had another son—Solomon.

25.text: The Most High loved Solomon, so He sent Nathan to name him Jedidiah (which means "loved by The Most High").

26.text: Meanwhile, Joab was fightin' in Rabbah against the Ammonites and had taken the royal city.

27.text: He sent word to David, sayin', 'I took over their water supply.'

28.text: 'Bring the rest of the army, take the city, or they might start callin' it my city instead of yours.'

29.text: So David gathered his forces, pulled up on Rabbah, and took it.

30.text: He took the king's crown, which weighed about 75 pounds of gold and had precious stones in it, and put it on his own head. Then he looted the city big time.

31.text: He put the Ammonite people to work with saws, iron picks, and axes, makin' them work in brick factories. He did this to all the Ammonite cities. Then David and his crew went back to Jerusalem.

1.text: David's son Absalom had a beautiful sister named Tamar, and his half-brother Amnon was obsessed with her.

2.text: Amnon was so pressed that he made himself sick over Tamar, 'cause she was a virgin and it wasn't right for him to mess with her.

3.text: But Amnon had a slick cousin named Jonadab, son of David's brother Shimeah. Jonadab was real sneaky.

4.text: Jonadab asked him, 'Bruh, you the king's son, why you lookin' so down every day? What's up?'

5.text: Amnon told him, 'I'm in love with Tamar—Absalom's sister.'

6.text: Jonadab gave him a dirty plan: 'Act like you sick, lay in bed, and when your dad comes, tell him to send Tamar to cook for you.'

7.text: So David sent for Tamar, tellin' her, 'Go to Amnon's house and fix him some food.'

8.text: Tamar went to Amnon's crib, where he was laid up. She made the food in front of him and baked the cakes.

9.text: But when she brought the food, Amnon refused to eat. He told everyone, 'Get out.' They all left.

10.text: Then Amnon told Tamar, 'Bring the food to my bedroom, I wanna eat from your hand.'

11.text: As soon as she got close, he grabbed her and said, "Come sleep with me, sis."

12.text: Tamar was like, 'No, my brother! This is wrong—this kinda stuff shouldn't happen in Israel!'

13.text: 'Where would I go with this shame? And you—you'd be just another fool! Please, just ask the king, he won't hold me back from you!'

14.text: But Amnon didn't listen. He was stronger than her, so he forced himself on her.

15.text: Then, outta nowhere, he started hatin' her—hated her more than he ever claimed to love her. He told her, 'Get up and get out.'

16.text: Tamar begged him, 'Sending me away is worse than what you already did!'

17.text: But Amnon didn't care. He called his servant and said, 'Throw this woman out and lock the door.'

18.text: Tamar was wearing a royal robe, like all the king's virgin daughters. But the servant put her out and locked the door behind her.

19.text: Tamar put ashes on her head, ripped her robe, put her hands on her head, and walked away crying her heart out.

20.text: Absalom saw her and said, 'Did Amnon do this to you? Look, sis, don't say anything right now. Just stay here with me.'

21.text: When King David heard what happened, he was furious.

22.text: But Absalom never said a word to Amnon—good or bad. But deep down, he hated him for what he did to Tamar.

23.text: Two years later, Absalom threw a big feast for the sheepshearers near Ephraim. He invited all the king's sons.

24.text: Absalom told his father, 'Come celebrate with us! You and all your servants.'

25.text: David was like, 'Nah, if we all go, it'll be too much. But thanks for the invite, son.'

26.text: Then Absalom said, 'Well, at least let Amnon come.'

27.text: David was suspicious, 'Why you want Amnon to go?' But Absalom kept askin', so he finally let all his sons go, including Amnon.

28.text: Absalom had already planned it. He told his servants, 'Wait 'til Amnon gets drunk, then when I say the word—kill him. Don't be scared, just do what I say!'

29.text: So as soon as Amnon was lit, Absalom's servants killed him on the spot. The rest of the king's sons jumped on their mules and got outta there.

30.text: As they were ridin' back, David got fake news: 'Absalom killed all your sons—none of them made it!'

31.text: David tore his clothes and fell to the ground in grief. His servants did the same.

32.text: But Jonadab, the sneaky cousin, told David, 'Nah, it ain't all your sons—just Amnon. Absalom been plottin' this since the day Amnon violated Tamar.'

33.text: 'So don't panic—only Amnon is dead.'

34.text: Meanwhile, Absalom fled. And as he ran, a lookout saw a group of men coming down the road.

35.text: Jonadab told the king, 'See? Your sons are alive, just like I said.'

36.text: As soon as they arrived, they broke down crying. David and his servants cried even harder.

37.text: But Absalom escaped to Geshur, to his grandfather Talmai, king of Geshur. And David mourned for Amnon every day.

38.text: Absalom stayed in Geshur for three years.

39.text: David missed Absalom but had made peace with Amnon being gone.

1.text: Joab, son of Zeruiah, peeped that David was still thinking about Absalom.

2.text: So Joab went to Tekoa, found a wise woman, and told her, 'Act like you been mourning for a long time. Put on your sad clothes, don't wear no oil, and go talk to the king.'

3.text: 'Tell him this story I'ma give you.' And Joab coached her on what to say.

4.text: The woman went to David, fell on her face, and cried out, 'Help me, O king!'

5.text: David asked, 'What's wrong?' She said, 'I'm a widow. My husband is gone.'

6.text: 'I had two sons—they got into it in the field, nobody was there to break it up, and one killed the other.'

7.text: 'Now the whole family wanna execute my only son, sayin' he gotta pay for his brother's death. If they do that, they wipin' out my husband's legacy completely.'

8.text: David told her, 'Go home, I'ma handle it.'

9.text: But the woman said, 'If anybody got a problem, let the blame be on me and my family—not you.'

10.text: David reassured her, 'If anybody says somethin', bring 'em to me—I won't let them touch you.'

11.text: She pushed further, 'Swear to The Most High that you won't let the avenger of blood come for my son.'

12.text: David swore, 'As The Most High lives, not one hair on your son's head will fall.'

13.text: Then she hit David with the real message: 'So why you treatin' your own banished son like this? You just ruled in my favor, but you won't bring Absalom home?'

14.text: 'We all gonna die one day, like spilled water you can't scoop back up. But The Most High finds a way to bring folks back, instead of throwin' 'em away.'

15.text: 'That's why I came to you today—I was scared, hopin' the king would hear me out.'

16.text: 'I know the king got wisdom from The Most High, so I trust you gon' do what's right.'

17.text: 'Your servant believes that my lord the king gon' make the right call—'cause you got wisdom like an angel of God, always knowin' what's good and what's bad. May The Most High be with you!'

18.text: David looked at her and said, 'Tell me the truth—did Joab put you up to this?'

19.text: She smiled and said, 'You got me, king. Joab told me what to say, but you saw right through it.'

20.text: 'He did it to get you to see the bigger picture. But you wise, king—you always know what's goin' on.'

21.text: David sighed and told Joab, 'Alright, go bring Absalom back.'

22.text: Joab bowed down, thanked David, and said, 'I know now that I got favor with you, king.'

23.text: So Joab went to Geshur and brought Absalom back to Jerusalem.

24.text: But David said, 'He can come back, but he ain't gonna see my face.' So Absalom stayed in his house and didn't see the king.

25.text: Absalom was the finest dude in Israel—from head to toe, not a flaw on him.

26.text: His hair was legendary—dude only cut it once a year 'cause it got too heavy. When he did, it weighed about five pounds!

27.text: Absalom had three sons and a daughter named Tamar, who was beautiful just like her aunt.

28.text: Absalom lived in Jerusalem for two years but still hadn't seen David.

29.text: He sent for Joab to talk to the king, but Joab ignored him. He sent for him again, and Joab still didn't come.

30.text: So Absalom told his servants, 'Joab's field is next to mine, right? He got some barley? Go burn it down.'

31.text: Joab finally pulled up, mad as ever: 'Bruh, why you burnin' my field?!'

32.text: Absalom said, 'Cause I told you to come and you ignored me! Why'd I even leave Geshur if my father ain't gon' see me? If I did something wrong, let him kill me.'

33.text: So Joab told the king what Absalom said. David finally called for Absalom. Absalom came in, bowed before the king, and David kissed him.

1.text: After a while, Absalom started flexin'—he got himself chariots, horses, and fifty men runnin' ahead of him.

2.text: Every morning, he'd post up near the city gate, waitin' for folks comin' to see the king about legal matters.

3.text: When people pulled up, he'd be like, 'Where you from?' They'd tell him their tribe, and Absalom would say, 'Man, you got a solid case, but too bad the king ain't got nobody to hear you.'

4.text: Then he'd hit 'em with, "If I was judge, I'd make sure everybody got justice!"

5.text: Anytime someone came to bow to him, he'd grab 'em and hug 'em like family.

6.text: Little by little, he stole the hearts of the people—gettin' them on his side instead of David's.

7.text: After four years, Absalom told David, 'Let me go to Hebron and fulfill a vow I made to The Most High.'

8.text: 'Back when I was in Geshur, I promised that if The Most High brought me back to Jerusalem, I'd serve Him.'

9.text: David told him, 'Alright, go in peace.' So Absalom left for Hebron.

10.text: But this was all a setup. Absalom sent spies to all the tribes of Israel, tellin' them, 'When you hear the trumpet blow, tell everybody, "Absalom is king in Hebron!"'

11.text: He took 200 men from Jerusalem with him, but they didn't know what was goin' on.

12.text: Then he called Ahithophel, David's top adviser, to join him. The conspiracy kept growing, and more people started backin' Absalom.

13.text: A messenger ran to David, sayin', 'The people ridin' with Absalom now!'

14.text: David told his men, 'We gotta GO! If we stay here, we won't make it. Absalom finna roll up on us quick, and he gon' wipe out the whole city.'

15.text: David's servants told him, 'Whatever you say, King—we wit' you.'

16.text: David and his whole household left, but he left ten of his concubines behind to take care of the palace.

17.text: They stopped at the last house before leavin' the city,

18.text: David's whole squad marched past him—the Cherethites, Pelethites, and 600 Gittites from Gath.

19.text: David looked at Ittai the Gittite and said, 'Bruh, you a foreigner. Why you ridin' with me? Go back to Absalom.'

20.text: 'You just got here yesterday—no need to get caught up in this. Go back and be safe.'

21.text: Ittai said, 'Nah, King. Wherever you go, I go—life or death.'

22.text: David nodded and said, 'Alright, come on then.' So Ittai, his men, and their families crossed the Kidron Valley.

23.text: Everybody was cryin' as David and his people crossed over, headin' toward the wilderness.

24.text: Zadok the priest and the Levites brought the Ark of God, but David told 'em, 'Take it back to the city.'

25.text: 'If The Most High wants me back, He'll bring me back. If not, let His will be done.'

26.text: Then he told Zadok, 'Stay in the city and keep watch. If anything pops off, send word through your sons, Ahimaaz and Jonathan.'

27.text: So Zadok and Abiathar took the Ark back to Jerusalem.

28.text: David and his people kept movin' into the wilderness.

29.text: So Zadok and Abiathar did what David said—they took the Ark of God back to Jerusalem and stayed put.

30.text: David climbed the Mount of Olives, cryin', barefoot, and with his head covered. Everybody with him did the same.

31.text: Then he got bad news: "Ahithophel is ridin' with Absalom." David prayed, 'Lord, turn Ahithophel's advice into nonsense!'

32.text: At the top of the mountain, David saw Hushai the Archite, his robe torn, dust on his head—he was mournin' too.

33.text: David told him, 'If you come with me, you just gon' slow us down.'

34.text: 'But if you go back to Absalom and act like you his servant, you can mess up Ahithophel's advice for me.'

35.text: Zadok and Abiathar the priests gon' be there too—whatever you hear, tell them.

36.text: Then they'll send word to me through their sons, Ahimaaz and Jonathan.

37.text: So Hushai went back to Jerusalem, just as Absalom rolled into the city.

1.text: As David got past the top of the mountain, Ziba, Mephibosheth's servant, pulled up with two saddled donkeys loaded with 200 loaves of bread, 100 clusters of raisins, 100 summer fruits, and a skin of wine.

2.text: David asked, 'What's all this for?'

3.text: Ziba said, 'The donkeys for your people to ride, the food for your soldiers, and the wine for anybody who gets weak in the wilderness.'

4.text: David asked, 'Where's Mephibosheth?'

5.text: Ziba lied and said, 'He stayed in Jerusalem talkin' 'bout "Today, Israel gon' give me back my granddaddy Saul's kingdom."'

6.text: David told Ziba, 'Aight, everything that belonged to Mephibosheth is now yours.'

7.text: Ziba bowed low and said, 'Thank you, my king!'

8.text: When David got to Bahurim, a man from Saul's family, Shimei son of Gera, came out cursin' him non-stop.

9.text: Dude was throwin' rocks at David and his men, even though David's soldiers surrounded him.

10.text: Shimei yelled, 'Get outta here, you murderer! You dirty man!'

11.text: 'The Most High is gettin' you back for all the blood you spilled in Saul's house! You took his throne, and now your own son is takin' yours. You gettin' what you deserve!'

12.text: Abishai, Joab's brother, got mad and told David, 'Why this dead dog talkin' to you like this? Let me go take his head off.'

13.text: But David said, 'Nah, let him talk. If The Most High let him curse me, who am I to stop him?'

14.text: 'My own son tryna kill me—this man just talkin'. Maybe The Most High seein' my pain and gon' bless me for this instead.'

15.text: Shimei kept cursin', throwin' rocks, and kickin' up dust as David walked by.

16.text: David and his people got tired and finally stopped to rest.

17.text: Meanwhile, Absalom rolled up in Jerusalem with his squad, and Ahithophel was with him.

18.text: Then Hushai, David's friend, pulled up to Absalom and said, "Long live the king! Long live the king!"

19.text: Absalom side-eyed him and said, 'So this how you do your boy David? Ain't you supposed to be ridin' with him?'

20.text: Hushai played along and said, 'Nah, I roll with whoever The Most High and Israel chooses. If that's you, then I'm wit' you.'

21.text: Absalom turned to Ahithophel and said, "What's the move? What should we do?"

22.text: Ahithophel told him, "Go sleep with your father's concubines—the ones he left behind to watch the palace. If you do that, all of Israel will know you and your father ain't never gon' make up. Then everybody that follows you will be even more solid."

23.text: So they set up a tent on the palace roof, and Absalom went in and slept with David's concubines—out in the open, for all of Israel to see.

24.text: Everybody listened to Ahithophel like his advice came straight from God. Both David and Absalom had relied on his counsel.

1.text: Ahithophel told Absalom, 'Let me pick 12,000 men and chase after David tonight.'

2.text: 'We gon' catch him while he's tired and weak, put fear in him, and make his people scatter. Then I'ma kill only the king.'

3.text: 'After that, everybody else gon' come back to you, and this whole thing will be over.'

4.text: Absalom and his advisors liked the plan—it sounded solid.

5.text: But Absalom said, 'Call Hushai, too—I wanna hear what he think.'

6.text: When Hushai came, Absalom told him, 'Ahithophel say we should attack David now. You agree, or you got a better idea?'

7.text: Hushai said, 'Nah, Ahithophel wrong on this one.'

8.text: 'You know your father and his men—they warriors. Right now, they mad as a mama bear that lost her cubs.'

9.text: 'David ain't stupid. He already hidin' somewhere—he ain't sittin' out in the open.'

10.text: 'And if your first attack don't go right, people gon' panic and say, "David's men are slaughterin' Absalom's troops!"'

11.text: 'So here's my advice—get ALL of Israel, from Dan to Beersheba—an army so big it look like sand on the beach. Then you lead the charge yourself.'

12.text: 'Wherever David tryna hide, we gon' flood him like morning dew, and won't leave a single one of them alive.'

13.text: 'And if he in a city, we gon' drag that whole city into the river 'til not even a stone is left.'

14.text: Absalom and his men chose Hushai's advice over Ahithophel's—'cause The Most High had already planned to mess up Ahithophel's wisdom to bring Absalom down.

15.text: Hushai ran to Zadok and Abiathar the priests and told them everything—both Ahithophel's plan and his own advice.

16.text: 'Y'all gotta send word to David fast—tell him to cross the river tonight, or he and his men are done for!'

17.text: Jonathan and Ahimaaz were at En Rogel, hidin', waitin' on a message. A servant girl came and passed them the word so they wouldn't get caught.

18.text: But somebody saw them and snitched to Absalom! So they took off and hid at a man's house in Bahurim—they jumped in a well in his courtyard.

19.text: His wife covered the well with cloth and spread grain over it, makin' it look normal.

20.text: Absalom's men showed up and asked, "Where's Jonathan and Ahimaaz?"

21.text: The woman played it smooth and said, "They already left—crossed the river."

22.text: As soon as Absalom's men left, Jonathan and Ahimaaz crawled out the well, ran to David, and told him, "You gotta cross the river NOW—Ahithophel wants you dead."

23.text: David and his whole crew crossed the Jordan by sunrise—nobody got left behind.

24.text: When Ahithophel saw that Absalom ignored his advice, he knew it was over for him.

25.text: He went home, put his affairs in order, then hung himself. They buried him in his father's tomb.

26.text: David made it to Mahanaim, while Absalom and his army crossed the Jordan and set up camp in Gilead.

27.text: Absalom replaced Joab with Amasa as commander of the army.

28.text: Meanwhile, David's people started getting supplies. Shobi from Ammon, Machir from Lo Debar, and Barzillai the Gileadite pulled up with beds, pots, wheat, barley, beans, lentils, honey, sheep, and cheese.

29.text: They told David, "We know y'all tired, hungry, and thirsty out here in the wilderness—eat up."

1.text: David took count of his people, set up commanders over thousands and hundreds, gettin' them organized.

2.text: He split them into three groups—one under Joab, one under Abishai (Joab's brother), and one under Ittai the Gittite. David said, 'I'ma go out there with y'all.'

3.text: But the soldiers said, "Nah, King. You too important. If we run, they won't care. Even if half of us die, they still won't care. But you worth 10,000 of us. It's better if you stay back and help from the city."

4.text: David agreed and stood at the gate while his people marched out in groups.

5.text: Before they left, David told Joab, Abishai, and Ittai, "Look, deal gently with my son Absalom, for my sake." Everybody heard him say it.

6.text: The battle went down in the forest of Ephraim.

7.text: David's army crushed Absalom's men, takin' out 20,000 soldiers.

8.text: The battle was everywhere, and the forest itself took out more men than the sword did!

9.text: Then Absalom ran into David's soldiers. He was ridin' a mule, and as he passed under a big oak tree, his hair got caught in the branches!

10.text: His mule kept runnin', but he was stuck there, dangling between heaven and earth.

11.text: One of David's men saw it and ran to tell Joab.

12.text: Joab was like, 'You saw him and didn't kill him?! I would've given you ten pieces of silver and a belt!'

13.text: The man said, 'Man, even if you gave me a thousand silver pieces, I wouldn't touch the king's son. We all heard what the king said—nobody lay a hand on Absalom.'

14.text: Joab said, "I ain't got time for this." Then he grabbed three spears and drove them straight into Absalom's heart while he was still hangin' there alive.

15.text: Then ten of Joab's young men came through and finished Absalom off.

16.text: Joab blew the trumpet, tellin' David's army to stop chasin' Israel.

17.text: They threw Absalom's body in a big pit in the forest and stacked up a huge pile of stones over him. Everybody else ran back home.

18.text: Absalom had built a monument for himself in the King's Valley, 'cause he ain't have a son to carry on his name. That spot still called Absalom's Monument today.

19.text: Ahimaaz, son of Zadok, told Joab, "Let me run and tell the king the good news—The Most High gave him victory today!"

20.text: Joab said, "Nah, not today. The king's son is dead—you don't wanna be the one to tell him that."

21.text: Then he told a Cushite servant, "You go tell him." The Cushite bowed and ran.

22.text: Ahimaaz still wanted to go, so he begged Joab, "Please, let me run too!"

23.text: Joab was like, "Why? You got no good news." But Ahimaaz insisted, so Joab finally said, "Fine, go ahead." Ahimaaz ran the long way but still outran the Cushite!

24.text: David was sittin' at the city gate. His watchman climbed up, saw a man runnin' alone, and shouted down to the king.

25.text: David said, "If he runnin' solo, he bringin' news."

26.text: Then the watchman saw another man runnin' and told David.

27.text: The watchman was like, "That first runner look like Ahimaaz!"

28.text: Ahimaaz got there first, bowed before David, and said, "King, The Most High gave you victory today!"

29.text: David cut straight to the chase: "Is my son Absalom okay?"

30.text: Ahimaaz dodged the question: "I saw a big commotion, but I don't know what happened."

31.text: Then the Cushite came and told David, "Good news, King! The Most High got rid of your enemies today!"

32.text: David asked again, "But what about my son Absalom? Is he safe?"

33.text: The Cushite said, "May all your enemies end up like him."

34.text: David was crushed. He went up to his room cryin' and sayin', "My son, Absalom! My son, my son Absalom! If only I had died instead of you! My son, my son!"

1.text: Somebody told Joab, 'The king still cryin' over Absalom.'

2.text: What should've been a day of victory turned into a sad day 'cause everybody heard that David was grieving his son.

3.text: Instead of celebratin', David's people snuck back into the city like they was ashamed, like they just lost a battle.

4.text: Meanwhile, David had his face covered, cryin' loud, 'My son Absalom! My son, my son!'

5.text: Joab stormed in and told David, 'Man, you trippin'! You out here disrespectin' the same people who just saved your life, your family, and your kingdom.'

6.text: 'It's like you love your enemies and hate your own people! You makin' it real clear—if Absalom was still alive and all of us was dead, that woulda made you happy!'

7.text: 'Now get up, go out there, and speak to your people! If you don't, I swear ain't nobody gonna be left by tomorrow! And trust me, that would be worse than any L you ever took.'

8.text: So David wiped his face, got up, and sat by the gate. When the people heard, they came through to see him.

9.text: All over Israel, people was arguin'— 'David saved us from the Philistines and all our enemies, but he ran when Absalom came for him.'

10.text: 'Now Absalom dead, but nobody sayin' nothin' about bringin' David back?'

11.text: David sent word to Zadok and Abiathar the priests, tellin' them to holler at the elders of Judah: 'Why y'all the last ones to invite me back when all Israel already want me home?'

12.text: 'Y'all my own flesh and blood! Why y'all movin' slow on this?'

13.text: David told them to tell Amasa (the guy Absalom put in charge), 'You family too! May God deal with me if I don't make you commander over the army instead of Joab.'

14.text: That move got Judah's heart back on David's side, and they sent him a message: 'Come back, King!'

15.text: So David started headin' back to Jerusalem, and the tribe of Judah met him at Gilgal to escort him across the Jordan.

16.text: Shimei (the dude that cursed David out last time) rushed down to meet him with 1,000 Benjamites.

17.text: Ziba (Saul's servant) showed up too, bringin' his 15 sons and 20 servants.

18.text: They hurried across the river to help the king's household cross.

19.text: Shimei fell on his face in front of David and said, 'King, please don't hold my past against me!'

20.text: 'I know I messed up, but I'm the first one here to welcome you back!'

21.text: Abishai wasn't feelin' it: 'Shouldn't Shimei be put to death? He cursed the Lord's anointed!'

22.text: But David shut that down: 'Man, what am I gon' do with y'all, Zeruiah's sons? Today ain't a day for killin'—I'm back as king!'

23.text: Then David told Shimei, 'You ain't gon' die.' And he made an oath on it.

24.text: Mephibosheth, Saul's grandson, finally showed up. He looked rough—hadn't taken care of his feet, beard, or clothes since David left.

25.text: David asked, 'Why you ain't come with me, Mephibosheth?'

26.text: Mephibosheth said, 'King, my servant lied on me! I told him to saddle up my donkey so I could ride with you, but he left me behind 'cause I'm crippled.

27.text: 'Then he went and lied to you about me, but you like an angel of God, so do whatever you think is right.'

28.text: 'My whole family was as good as dead, but you let me eat at your table. I ain't got the right to ask for nothin' more.'

29.text: David cut him off: 'Enough talk. You and Ziba split the land.'

30.text: But Mephibosheth said, 'Let him have it all. I'm just happy you home, King.'

31.text: Barzillai the Gileadite came through, escortin' David across the river.

32.text: Dude was 80 years old and had taken care of David while he was on the run.

33.text: David told him, 'Come to Jerusalem with me, I'll take care of you.'

34.text: But Barzillai said, 'Man, I'm old. What I'ma do in Jerusalem?'

35.text: 'I can't taste food right, I can't hear music, I don't need nothin' extra. Why burden you?'

36.text: 'I'll go with you just a little, but then let me go back home. I wanna die in my own city, near my parents' grave.'

37.text: 'But take Chimham instead—let him serve you. Do for him whatever you see fit.'

38.text: David agreed: 'Alright, Chimham can roll with me. I'll look out for him just like you asked.'

39.text: Then David crossed over, kissed Barzillai, blessed him, and Barzillai went back home.

40.text: David went on to Gilgal with Chimham. Judah escorted him, but only half of Israel showed up.

41.text: Then the Israelites came at David, mad: 'Why Judah bring you back without us? We part of Israel too!'

42.text: Judah clapped back: 'King David is family! Why y'all mad? We ain't get no gifts from him!'

43.text: Then Israel fired back: 'We got ten shares in the kingdom—we got more claim to David than y'all! But y'all ignored us and brought him back without askin' us first!'

44.text: The argument got heated—Judah's men spoke even fiercer than Israel's.

1.text: A troublemaker named Sheba, son of Bichri, a Benjamite, stood up and blew his trumpet, sayin': 'Forget David! We ain't got no part in Jesse's son. Every man, back to your tents, Israel!'

2.text: All of Israel dipped and followed Sheba, but the men of Judah stayed loyal to David.

3.text: When David got back to Jerusalem, he took his ten concubines, put them in seclusion, and took care of them, but he never slept with them again. They lived like widows for the rest of their lives.

4.text: David told Amasa, 'Round up Judah's army in three days and report back.'

5.text: But Amasa was takin' too long, so David told Abishai, 'Sheba might be a bigger problem than Absalom. Take my best men and stop him before he hides in a fortified city.

6.text: Joab's men, the Cherethites, Pelethites, and David's warriors rolled out to track Sheba down.

7.text: At Gibeon, Amasa finally showed up. Joab, dressed in his battle gear, stepped forward.

8.text: Joab walked up to Amasa like, 'How you doin', bro?' Then grabbed his beard like he was about to kiss him.

9.text: But Amasa ain't see the dagger in Joab's other hand—Joab stabbed him in the stomach, and his guts spilled out.

10.text: One of Joab's men shouted, 'If you ridin' with Joab and King David, let's go!'

11.text: But Amasa's body was just lyin' there, and people kept stoppin' when they saw it.

12.text: So they dragged him to the side of the road and threw a cloth over him. After that, everybody followed Joab to chase down Sheba.

13.text: Sheba traveled through all the tribes, then ended up in Abel of Beth Maachah.

14.text: Joab's army caught up and surrounded the city, buildin' a siege mound against the walls.

15.text: Then a wise woman inside the city called out, 'Somebody get Joab! I need to talk to him.'

16.text: Joab stepped up, and she asked, 'You Joab?' He said, 'Yeah, that's me.'

17.text: She told him, 'Look, our city got a reputation for bein' peaceful and wise.

18.text: 'We ain't tryin' to fight, but you about to destroy us—God's own people. Why?'

19.text: Joab said, 'Nah, I ain't tryna destroy y'all.

20.text: 'We just want one man—Sheba, son of Bichri. He rebelled against King David. Give him up, and we out.'

21.text: The woman went to the city leaders, they grabbed Sheba, cut off his head, and tossed it over the wall to Joab.

22.text: Joab blew his trumpet, called off the siege, and his men went back home.

23.text: Joab was back as commander of Israel's army.

24.text: Benaiah ran the Cherethites and Pelethites.

25.text: Adoram was in charge of taxes.

26.text: Jehoshaphat was the royal historian.

27.text: Sheva was the scribe.

28.text: Zadok and Abiathar were the priests.

29.text: Ira the Jairite was David's chief minister.

1.text: A famine hit the land for three straight years, so David asked The Most High what was up. The Lord said, 'It's 'cause of Saul and his bloodstained house—he tried to wipe out the Gibeonites.'

2.text: David called up the Gibeonites to make things right. They weren't Israelites but leftovers from the Amorites, and back in the day, Israel had promised to protect them. But Saul had broken that promise, tryna wipe them out to look good for Israel and Judah.

3.text: David asked them, 'What can I do to fix this? How can I make peace so The Most High blesses the land again?'

4.text: The Gibeonites told him, 'We don't want no silver or gold from Saul's house, and we ain't askin' for anybody in Israel to be killed.'

5.text: But they did want justice. 'Saul tried to wipe us out, so we want seven of his descendants. We'll execute them in Gibeah, Saul's hometown.'

6.text: David agreed.

7.text: But he spared Mephibosheth, Jonathan's son, 'cause of the promise he made to Jonathan.

8.text: Instead, he took two sons of Rizpah (Saul's concubine) and five sons of Michal (Saul's daughter) and handed them over.

9.text: The Gibeonites executed them, hangin' them on a hill before The Most High. They were all killed at the beginning of the barley harvest.

10.text: Rizpah, heartbroken, spread out sackcloth on a rock and guarded the bodies, keepin' birds from touchin' them by day and wild animals away at night.

11.text: When David heard about Rizpah's devotion, he was moved.

12.text: He went and got the bones of Saul and Jonathan from Jabesh Gilead—where the Philistines had left them hangin' after they killed Saul in battle.

13.text: Then David gathered up the bones of those who had been executed and buried them properly.

14.text: They buried Saul and Jonathan in their family tomb in Zelah, in the land of Benjamin. After that, The Most High lifted the famine and answered Israel's prayers.

15.text: The Philistines went to war with Israel again, and David went out to fight—but he got tired fast.

16.text: Ishbi-Benob, one of the giants, saw his chance to kill David. His spear weighed 300 shekels (7.5 pounds), and he had a fresh new sword ready to take David out.

17.text: But Abishai (Joab's brother) jumped in, saved David, and killed the Philistine. After that, David's men told him, 'King, you ain't fightin' no more. If you die, the lamp of Israel goes out.'

18.text: Later, another battle broke out at Gob. Sibbechai the Hushathite killed Saph, another Philistine giant.

19.text: Then another fight happened at Gob. Elhanan from Bethlehem took out Goliath's brother—the one whose spear shaft was thick like a weaver's beam.

20.text: And yet again, there was war at Gath, where they faced a giant with six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot—24 digits in total.

21.text: This dude was talkin' reckless, but Jonathan (David's nephew) killed him on sight.

22.text: All four of these giants from Gath got taken out by David and his men.

1.text: David sang this song to The Most High on the day He saved him from all his enemies, including Saul.

2.text: The Lord my rock, my fortress, my way out.

3.text: The God who got my back, the one I put my trust in. My shield, my savior, my stronghold, my safe place. The one who keeps me from harm.

4.text: When I call on The Most High, the one worthy of all praise, I know I'm safe from my enemies.

5.text: Man, death had me surrounded, like waves tryna pull me under.

6.text: I was at my lowest, feelin' trapped, like the grave was closin' in on me.

7.text: But I cried out to The Most High, called on Him in my trouble. He heard me loud and clear from His throne!

8.text: The earth started shakin', the heavens trembled—God was mad!

9.text: Smoke came out His nostrils, fire from His mouth—He was fired up.

10.text: He bent the heavens and came down, darkness under His feet.

11.text: Ridin' on a cherub, flyin' through on the wind.

12.text: He wrapped Himself in darkness, thick clouds all around Him.

13.text: But His brightness still broke through—fire sparkin' from His presence.

14.text: The Most High thundered from the heavens, His voice shook everything!

15.text: He shot His arrows, scatterin' my enemies, sent lightning bolts chasin' 'em down.

16.text: The seas split open, the whole world was laid bare at His rebuke, when He breathed His mighty breath.

17.text: He reached down, grabbed me, and pulled me outta deep waters.

18.text: Saved me from my enemies, from folks way stronger than me.

19.text: They came at me when I was down bad, but The Most High held me up.

20.text: He brought me into a wide-open space, 'cause He got love for me.

21.text: The Most High blessed me 'cause I walked right, 'cause I kept my hands clean.

22.text: I stayed on His path, I ain't turn my back on Him.

23.text: His commands stayed in front of me, and I didn't ignore 'em.

24.text: I kept myself right before Him, I tried to live clean.

25.text: So He blessed me 'cause I stayed faithful, 'cause He saw my heart.

26.text: If you merciful, He gon' show you mercy. If you walk right, He gon' deal with you right.

27.text: If you pure, He gon' be pure with you. But if you shady, He gon' outthink you.

28.text: He lifts up the humble, but He brings down the proud.

29.text: You, Lord, my lamp—You bring light to my darkness.

30.text: With You, I can run through an army, I can jump over walls.

31.text: God's way is perfect, His word never fails. He protects everybody who trusts Him.

32.text: Ain't no god but The Most High, ain't no rock like Him.

33.text: God my strength, my power, the one who makes my path straight.

34.text: He make my feet swift like a deer's, puttin' me on high ground.

35.text: He trains me for battle, makes me strong enough to bend a bronze bow.

36.text: He covers me with His shield of salvation, His care for me lifts me up.

37.text: He made space for me to move, so I ain't trip up.

38.text: I chased my enemies down and wiped 'em out—I ain't stop 'til they were gone.

39.text: I crushed 'em, knocked 'em down, and they couldn't get back up.

40.text: You gave me strength for battle, made my enemies fall at my feet.

41.text: You put their necks under me, and I stomped out those who hated me.

42.text: They cried for help, but nobody saved them. Even The Most High ain't answer them.

43.text: I beat 'em down like dust, stomped 'em out like dirt in the streets.

44.text: You rescued me from my own people's drama and made me ruler over nations.

45.text: Foreigners bowed before me, as soon as they heard my name.

46.text: They lost all courage, hid away like scared men.

47.text: The Most High lives! Blessed be my Rock! Let my God be lifted high!

48.text: He's the one who avenges me, puttin' nations under my rule.

49.text: He saved me from my enemies, lifted me above those who hated me.

50.text: So I'ma thank You, Lord, and sing Your praises to the whole world.

51.text: You my strong tower, showin' mercy to me and my descendants forever.

1.text: These the last words of David, son of Jesse—the man God lifted up, the one He anointed, the songwriter of Israel.

2.text: The Spirit of The Most High spoke through me, and His words stayed on my tongue.

3.text: The God of Israel, the Rock of Israel, told me: 'The one who leads gotta lead with justice, ruling with respect for The Most High.'

4.text: That kind of ruler shines like the sunrise after a storm, like fresh grass growing after the rain.

5.text: Even though my family ain't perfect, God still locked me into a forever promise, securing everything I need. That's my salvation, that's my hope—ain't no way He won't keep blessing me.

6.text: But them rebels? They like thorn bushes—too wild to be grabbed by hand.

7.text: You gotta deal with them using iron and spears, 'cause they gonna end up burned up where they stand.

8.text: These the names of David's top warriors: Josheb-Basshebeth (aka Adino the Eznite), was top of the list—he took out 800 men in one fight.

9.text: Next was Eleazar, son of Dodo—one of the top three warriors. When the Philistines pulled up and Israel's army ran, he stayed.

10.text: He fought so long his hand cramped up around his sword. The Most High gave him victory that day, and when the battle was done, the people only came back to grab the loot.

11.text: Then there was Shammah. The Philistines came trying to take over a field full of lentils, and everybody ran—except him.

12.text: He stood his ground right in the middle of that field, fought 'em off, and The Most High gave him the win.

13.text: One time, three of David's top warriors came down to see him when the Philistines had a camp set up in Bethlehem.

14.text: David was posted up in his stronghold while the Philistines were controlling Bethlehem.

15.text: David sighed and said, 'Man, I'd love some water from that well in Bethlehem by the gate.'

16.text: His three warriors broke through enemy lines, got that water, and brought it back to him.

17.text: But David wouldn't drink it—he poured it out as an offering to The Most High. He said, 'I can't drink this—it's like drinking the blood of the men who risked their lives for it.'

18.text: Abishai, Joab's brother, led another group—he took out 300 men with his spear.

19.text: He was the most respected of that group, but he still wasn't one of the original three.

20.text: Benaiah, son of Jehoiada, was another warrior. He killed two fierce Moabite fighters and even fought a lion in a pit—on a snowy day at that.

21.text: He also fought a giant Egyptian. The Egyptian had a spear, but Benaiah snatched it and killed him with his own weapon.

22.text: Because of this, Benaiah became well-known.

23.text: He was respected more than most, but still not on the level of the top three. David put him in charge of his personal guard.

24.text: Asahel, Joab's brother, was one of the thirty. Elhanan, son of Dodo, was from Bethlehem.

25.text: Shammah the Harodite and Elika the Harodite.

26.text: Helez the Paltite and Ira, son of Ikkesh, from Tekoa.

27.text: Abiezer from Anathoth and Mebunnai the Hushathite.

28.text: Zalmon the Ahohite and Maharai the Netophathite.

29.text: Heleb, son of Baanah, from Netophah. Ittai, son of Ribai, from Gibeah in Benjamin.

30.text: Benaiah the Pirathonite and Hiddai from the brooks of Gaash.

31.text: Abi-Albon the Arbathite and Azmaveth the Barhumite.

32.text: Eliahba the Shaalbonite, one of the sons of Jashen, and Jonathan.

33.text: Shammah the Hararite and Ahiam, son of Sharar, the Hararite.

34.text: Eliphelet, son of Ahasbai, from Maacah, and Eliam, son of Ahithophel, from Giloh.

35.text: Hezrai the Carmelite and Paarai the Arbite.

36.text: Igal, son of Nathan, from Zobah, and Bani the Gadite.

37.text: Zelek the Ammonite and Naharai from Beeroth, Joab's armor-bearer.

38.text: Ira the Ithrite and Gareb the Ithrite.

39.text: Uriah the Hittite. Altogether, 37 mighty warriors.

1.text: The Most High was mad at Israel again, so He let David get caught up in his own thinking. David said, 'Go count everybody in Israel and Judah.'

2.text: David told Joab, his army commander, 'Go through all the tribes, from Dan to Beersheba, and get me the numbers.'

3.text: But Joab wasn't feelin' it. 'May The Most High bless Israel with more people than the stars if He wants, but why you wanna do this, King?'

4.text: David wasn't tryna hear it. So Joab and his officers went out to count the people.

5.text: They traveled the land, crossed the Jordan, camped in Aroer, and hit up the towns in Gad and Jazer.

6.text: Then they went through Gilead, Tahtim Hodshi, Dan Jaan, and around to Sidon.

7.text: They came to the stronghold of Tyre, checked in on all the Hivites and Canaanites, then went south to Judah, all the way to Beersheba.

8.text: After nine months and twenty days of counting, they made it back to Jerusalem.

9.text: Joab handed David the numbers: 800,000 warriors in Israel, 500,000 in Judah.

10.text: Soon as the numbers came in, David's heart hit him hard. 'Man, I really messed up. The Most High, please forgive me—I did something real foolish.'

11.text: The next morning, The Most High sent a word to the prophet Gad, David's seer.

12.text: 'Tell David he got three choices—pick one.'

13.text: So Gad told David, 'You want seven years of famine, three months of runnin' from your enemies, or three days of a deadly plague? Think on it.'

14.text: David was shook. 'I can't pick… but I'd rather fall into The Most High's hands than man's, 'cause God got mercy.'

15.text: The Most High sent a plague that lasted three days, and 70,000 people died from Dan to Beersheba.

16.text: The angel of The Most High stretched his hand over Jerusalem, ready to destroy it—but The Most High stopped him. 'That's enough. Pull back.' The angel stood by the threshing floor of Araunah the Jebusite.

17.text: David saw the angel and cried out, 'I'm the one who sinned, not them! Let the punishment be on me and my family.'

18.text: Gad came to David and told him, 'Go to Araunah's threshing floor and build an altar there.'

19.text: David did exactly what The Most High commanded.

20.text: Araunah looked up and saw the king and his servants coming. He bowed low before David, face to the ground.

21.text: Araunah asked, 'Why you here, King?'

22.text: David said, 'I need to buy this land to build an altar, so The Most High will take this plague off the people.'

23.text: Araunah was like, 'Take whatever you need! Use my oxen for sacrifices, my wood for the fire—everything's yours!'

24.text: But David said, 'Nah, I gotta pay for it. I can't offer The Most High something that cost me nothing.'

25.text: So David bought the threshing floor and the oxen for fifty shekels of silver. Then he built an altar, made offerings, and prayed. The Most High answered, and the plague stopped.

1.text: These the words of Amos—a regular dude from Tekoa who used to watch sheep—He saw this vision from the Lord 'bout Israel, back when Uzziah was king of Judah and Jeroboam (son of Joash) was king of Israel—two years before that big earthquake shook everything.

2.text: He said: "The Lord roarin' from Zion, His voice thunderin' outta Jerusalem. Shepherd fields turnin' sad, and Mount Carmel? Witherin' dry."

3.text: This what the Lord say: "I done let Damascus slide three times… but that fourth one? Nah, it's a wrap. They went too far when they crushed Gilead like grain—used iron tools, no mercy.

4.text: So I'ma send fire to Hazael's house. It's gon' burn down Ben-Hadad's palaces.

5.text: I'ma break down the gate in Damascus, wipe out the folks chillin' in the Valley of Aven, and knock down the ruler in Beth Eden. Syria's people? They goin' into exile in Kir," says the Lord.

6.text: The Lord said: "Gaza done messed up three times—and the fourth time was it. They took a whole group of captives and sold 'em off to Edom.

7.text: So I'ma light Gaza's wall up in flames. The fire gon' eat up all their fancy buildings.

8.text: I'ma silence Ashdod's people, shut down the king in Ashkelon. My hand gon' hit Ekron too. And the rest of the Philistines? Gone," says the Lord God.

9.text: The Lord said: "Tyre got three strikes… and then one more. They sold folks out to Edom too, broke a sacred bond, forgot that brotherhood ain't just a word.

10.text: So I'ma send fire on Tyre's walls. Them palaces? Gone in the blaze."

11.text: The Lord said: "Edom? You on the list too. You chased your brother with a sword, showed no mercy, held onto your hate like it was a trophy, kept that grudge burning forever.

12.text: So I'ma drop fire on Teman, and it's gon' eat up Bozrah too."

13.text: The Lord said: "Ammon? You wild for this. Three strikes plus one. Y'all ripped open pregnant women in Gilead—just to stretch your borders.

14.text: So I'ma burn down the walls of Rabbah, and that fire gon' hit hard—right in the middle of war cries, with a storm like a whirlwind tearing through.

15.text: Their king and all his royal boys? They all goin' into captivity," says the Lord.

1.text: This what the Lord say: "Moab? You crossed a line too. Three strikes, then four. You burned the bones of Edom's king, grinded 'em down like he was nothin' but dust.

2.text: So I'ma set Moab on fire. Kerioth's palaces? Gone. Moab gon' fall with screams and trumpet blasts.

3.text: I'ma wipe out their judges, and all them princes? They fall with 'em," says the Lord.

4.text: The Lord said: "Judah… yeah, I got y'all number too. Three sins, four sins—I ain't holdin' back no more. Y'all disrespected My law, straight-up ignored My commandments. Y'all followin' lies that been passed down like they tradition.

5.text: So I'ma send fire on Judah, and it's gon' burn through Jerusalem's palaces."

6.text: This what the Lord say: "Israel—yeah, y'all too. Three strikes wasn't enough—y'all did four and more. You sell out righteous folk for money. Sell out the poor for a pair of sandals like they cheap.

7.text: Y'all trample the dust on the heads of the poor, twistin' justice outta shape. Then you got men and they daddies sleepin' with the same woman—defilin' My name like it don't mean nothin'.

8.text: Y'all lay down at altars on clothes you took from folks who owe you, then drink wine you got off unjust fines—in My house at that!

9.text: "Y'all forgot who cleared the path for you? I'm the One who took down the Amorites—they was tall like cedar trees and strong like oaks. But I chopped down they fruit and dug up they roots.

10.text: I brought y'all up outta Egypt. Led you forty years through that wilderness, gave you the Amorites' land like it was yours.

11.text: I even raised up your sons to be prophets. Had some of y'all young men dedicated as Nazirites. Ain't that true, Israel?" says the Lord.

12.text: "Instead of honoring that, y'all gave them Nazirites wine, and told My prophets: 'Shut up. Don't speak.'

13.text: So now? I'm feelin' the weight of y'all mess like a wagon overloaded with grain.

14.text: The fast ones? They ain't gettin' away. The strong? They won't find no power. The mighty? Can't even save themselves.

15.text: Archers gon' drop they bows. The quick ones ain't fast enough. Even the horse riders can't escape.

16.text: The bravest warriors? They gon' run away butt-naked when the day hits," says the Lord.

1.text: Listen up to what the Lord sayin', Israel—yeah, I'm talkin' to the whole fam I brought outta Egypt.

2.text: Y'all the only ones I picked outta all the families on earth. That's exactly why I gotta check y'all for y'all sins.

3.text: Two folks can't walk together unless they on the same page, right?

4.text: A lion don't roar in the woods if he ain't caught nothin'. A young lion ain't gon' growl in his den if he empty.

5.text: A bird don't fall in a trap unless a trap's been set. And traps don't snap shut for no reason.

6.text: If a warning horn blows in the city, folks gon' panic, right? If disaster hits a city, don't you think God had His hand in it?

7.text: Look—God don't do nothin' unless He tell His prophets what's comin' first.

8.text: The lion already roared—how you not scared? The Lord done spoke—how can I not speak what He told me?

9.text: Go ahead—announce this in the big houses of Ashdod and Egypt. Tell 'em to pull up and watch what's goin' down on the hills of Samaria. It's chaos in the streets. People gettin' done dirty on every corner.

10.text: These folks don't even know how to do right no more, says the Lord. All they know is how to stash up violence and stolen goods in their cribs.

11.text: So this what God say: "An enemy gon' surround your land. They gon' drain you of your strength, and they gon' rob your mansions clean."

12.text: And the Lord says this too: "Just like a shepherd tryin' to snatch a couple legs or an ear outta a lion's mouth, that's how little gon' be left of y'all in Samaria—just them chillin' on the edge of the bed or couch."

13.text: Hear this and speak out against Jacob's house, says the Lord God, the Commander of everything:

14.text: "On the day I check Israel for all they mess, I'ma also shut down Bethel's altars. The horns on them altars? Snapped off and hittin' the dirt."

15.text: "I'ma destroy them winter homes and summer homes, all them ivory cribs gon' be gone, and them big ol' fancy houses? That's the end of all that," says the Lord.

1.text: Listen here, you bougie women of Bashan, livin' high up in Samaria—the ones who oppress the poor, crush the ones in need, and stay tellin' your men, "Bring me somethin' to sip on!"

2.text: The Lord God swore on His holiness: "Look, the days comin' where y'all gon' be dragged away with fishhooks—you and your kids too.

3.text: Y'all gon' be pushed out through busted-up walls, each one marchin' straight out, and thrown into Harmon," says the Lord.

4.text: "Go ahead, keep showin' up to Bethel—just to sin more. Hit Gilgal too—keep stackin' up them transgressions. Bring your sacrifices every morning, your tithes every three days like you somebody.

5.text: Make a big show outta your 'thanksgiving offerings'—with yeast in it. Announce your little 'freewill gifts' real loud—'cause y'all love performin'," says the Lord God.

6.text: "I made sure y'all felt hunger—empty mouths, no bread in sight. Still… y'all didn't come back to Me," says the Lord.

7.text: "I stopped the rain three months before harvest. Some cities got showers, others got nothin'. Whole towns had to travel just to find water—but even then? Still didn't return to Me," says the Lord.

8.text: "So two or three cities had to go wanderin' to another town just to find water—but even then, they ain't get enough to satisfy 'em. Still, y'all didn't come back to Me," says the Lord.

9.text: "I hit your gardens with blight. Mildew ate up the vineyards, the figs, the olives. Locusts snatched up the rest—still, y'all ain't come back," says the Lord.

10.text: "I hit y'all with plagues like I did Egypt. Your young men got taken out in battle, horses too—your camps stank to high heaven—and still… y'all ain't come back," says the Lord.

11.text: "I shook some of y'all like Sodom and Gomorrah—left you barely makin' it out like a log pulled from a fire. Still… y'all ain't come back to Me," says the Lord.

12.text: "So here's what's next, Israel—since I gotta do all this to get your attention… prepare to meet your God, Israel!"

13.text: 'Cause look—He's the one who shaped the mountains, breathed wind into the world, reads thoughts before you even say 'em, turns the sunrise into dark, and steps high on the earth like He own it. That's the Lord God of Heaven's Armies. That's His name.

1.text: Listen to this word I'm speakin' against y'all—yeah, it's a whole funeral cry, House of Israel:

2.text: "The daughter of Israel done fell flat. She ain't gettin' back up. She laid out in her land, and ain't nobody comin' to help her rise."

3.text: The Lord God says: "A city that used to send out a thousand? Only a hundred gon' come back. And a city that sent out a hundred? Only ten gon' survive."

4.text: This what the Lord say to Israel: "Come find Me—and live.

5.text: But don't go runnin' to Bethel. Don't try to slide through Gilgal. Don't even think about passin' through Beersheba. Gilgal gettin' locked up. Bethel? It's finished."

6.text: "Seek the Lord and live—before He shows up like a wildfire on Joseph's house and burns it to the ground—and ain't nobody in Bethel able to put it out."

7.text: Y'all the type to flip justice into bitterness, and toss righteousness out like trash.

8.text: He the One who made the stars—Pleiades and Orion. Turns death-dark nights into bright mornin's, and flips the day dark like it's midnight. He pulls ocean water up and pours it out all over the earth. The Lord is His name.

9.text: He rains destruction on the powerful, tearin' down strongholds like they made of paper.

10.text: Y'all can't stand folks who tell the truth in public. Anybody who speaks up straight? You hate them.

11.text: That's why, since you trample the poor and hit 'em with grain taxes—even though y'all livin' in fancy cut-stone houses, you won't be livin' in 'em long. You planted vineyards, but you won't get a single sip.

12.text: I see all y'all dirt. Yeah, all of it: You mistreat good people, take bribes like it's normal, and block justice from the folks who need it most.

13.text: That's why the wise ones keep quiet—'cause this whole time is wicked and heavy.

14.text: Chase good, not evil—so you can live. Then maybe the Lord God of Heaven's Armies will actually be with y'all like you say He is.

15.text: Hate what's evil. Love what's good. Let justice show up at the city gates. Maybe then God'll show mercy to what's left of Joseph's people.

16.text: The Lord God of Hosts says this: It's gon' be cryin' in every street, folks yellin' "Oh no! Oh no!" in every hood. They gon' call in farmers to mourn, and professional wailers to do what they do.

17.text: Even in the vineyards where folks usually celebrate? Tears everywhere. 'Cause I'm passin' through, says the Lord.

18.text: Y'all talkin' like y'all want the Day of the Lord. But why? What good is it gon' do you? It's gon' be all darkness, not light.

19.text: Like somebody runnin' from a lion—only to get jumped by a bear. Or thinkin' they safe at home, leanin' on the wall—and then a snake bites 'em.

20.text: Yeah, the Day of the Lord ain't light—it's deep dark. Ain't a glimmer of brightness in it.

21.text: "I hate your feast days. I can't stand your religious meetups.

22.text: All them burnt offerings and grain gifts? I ain't touchin' 'em. Your peace offerings? Nah."

23.text: "Turn off that noise you call worship music. I don't wanna hear your instruments singin'.

24.text: What I do wanna hear? Justice rollin' like a river. Righteousness flowin' like a strong stream."

25.text: "Y'all really think y'all brought Me sacrifices back in the wilderness for forty years, Israel? Nah.

26.text: Y'all was carryin' Sikkuth—y'all own little king idol. Holdin' up Chiun, your handmade stars and gods. Idols y'all put together your own selves."

27.text: "That's why I'ma send y'all into exile—way past Damascus," says the Lord—the One they call the God of Heaven's Armies.

1.text: Woe to y'all sittin' pretty in Zion, actin' safe in Samaria. You high-ranking folks in the top nation, the ones everybody runnin' to for answers.

2.text: Go look at Calneh. Slide through Hamath. Take a trip down to Gath in Philistia. Y'all think y'all better than them? Y'all think your land go further than theirs?

3.text: Woe to the ones pushin' judgment day far off, but bringin' violence closer with every move.

4.text: Y'all loungin' on ivory beds, stretchin' out on couches like y'all royalty. Feastin' on lamb chops and stall-fed veal like it's a cookout every day.

5.text: Strummin' on harps with nothin' but vibes, makin' new instruments like David—but no depth.

6.text: Sippin' wine outta bowls (not cups), oilin' up with the finest scents—but y'all don't shed one tear for what Joseph's people goin' through.

7.text: That's why y'all gon' be the first ones taken when the judgment hits. All y'all reclinin' at banquets? Y'all up next to go.

8.text: The Lord God swore on His own name—the Commander of Heaven's Armies said: "I can't stand the pride of Jacob. I hate these palaces y'all livin' in. That whole city? It's gettin' handed over. Everything in it."

9.text: When it goes down, even if ten folks hide out in one house—they all gon' die.

10.text: And when a relative comes through with the person assigned to cremate, and they carryin' out the bodies, they gon' ask the last person inside, "Anybody left?" And that person gon' whisper, "Nah." And they'll say, "Shhh! Don't even mention God's name right now."

11.text: The Lord commandin' it: The big houses? Smashed to bits. The small ones? Splintered too.

12.text: Do horses run on cliffs? Do folks plow rocks with oxen? Nope. But y'all flipped justice into poison, and righteousness into something bitter.

13.text: Y'all boastin' about Lo Debar like it's a big win. Y'all braggin', "Didn't we snatch Karnaim by our own strength?"

14.text: "I'ma raise up a whole nation against y'all," says the Lord, Commander of Heaven's Armies. "And they gon' press y'all hard—from the entrance of Hamath all the way to the valley of Arabah."

1.text: The Lord God gave me a vision: I saw Him callin' up a swarm of locusts right after the king took his cut of the crops—so this was the last harvest for regular folks.

2.text: When the locusts finished eatin' everything green, I cried out: "Lord God, please forgive! Jacob (Israel) can't take this—he too small!"

3.text: And the Lord changed His mind. "Aight. This one ain't gon' happen," said the Lord.

4.text: Then the Lord gave me another vision: He called for judgment by fire. That fire went deep—burned all the underground water and scorched the land.

5.text: So I cried again: "Lord God, please stop! Jacob too small—he can't survive this!"

6.text: And the Lord changed His mind again. "This one too—ain't gon' happen," said the Lord.

7.text: Then I saw the Lord standin' on a straight wall, holdin' a plumb line in His hand.

8.text: He asked me, "Amos, what you see?" I said, "A plumb line." Then the Lord said: "I'm settin' this plumb line right in the middle of My people, Israel. I ain't gon' overlook they mess no more.

9.text: Them high places of Isaac? Gon' be abandoned. Them temples in Israel? Wrecked. And I'ma bring the sword against Jeroboam's house."

10.text: Then Amaziah, the priest at Bethel, ran to King Jeroboam talkin' slick: "Yo, Amos out here stirrin' up rebellion in the kingdom. People can't handle what he preachin'—it's too much."

11.text: "He sayin' Jeroboam gon' die by the sword and Israel gon' be dragged out their own land."

12.text: Amaziah pulled up on Amos like: "Look here, prophet-man—go back to Judah where you from. Make your money and preach over there.

13.text: But don't come back prophesyin' at Bethel. This here's the king's sanctuary—royal property."

14.text: Amos clapped back: "Man, I wasn't even a prophet. Ain't come from no line of prophets. I was out here takin' care of sheep and sycamore trees.

15.text: But the Lord found me while I was mindin' my business in the field, and He told me, 'Go speak to My people, Israel.'"

16.text: "So listen up— You told me to stop prophesyin' and not to speak against Israel? Cool. But here's what God got to say:"

17.text: "Your wife gon' end up sellin' herself in the streets. Your sons and daughters? Killed by the sword. Your land? Divided and sold off. You? Gon' die in some unclean foreign place. And Israel? Yeah, they definitely gettin' snatched out they land."

1.text: The Lord God gave me another vision: I saw a basket full of summer fruit.

2.text: God said, "Amos, what you see?" I said, "A basket of summer fruit." Then the Lord said: "Exactly. Just like that fruit is ripe, so is Israel. Their time is up. I ain't gon' overlook they mess no more."

3.text: "In that day, the songs in the temple? Gon' be funeral cries. Bodies everywhere—folk gettin' tossed out in silence like trash," says the Lord God.

4.text: "Listen up, y'all who crush the needy and keep the poor from ever gettin' ahead—

5.text: Y'all be sayin', 'Man, when the New Moon festival over so we can get back to sellin'? When Sabbath done so we can get back to grindin'? Let's rig the weights, shrink the product, raise the prices...

6.text: sell folks into debt slavery for a few coins, and even push spoiled wheat just to keep profitin'?'"

7.text: The Lord swore on the pride of Jacob: "I promise, I ain't gon' forget a single thing y'all done."

8.text: "Don't you think the land should quake for this? Ain't everybody in it gon' mourn? It'll rise and fall like the Nile—swelling, flooding, then pulling back."

9.text: "On that day," says the Lord God, "I'll make the sun set at noon. Middle of the day, whole sky go black.

10.text: Y'all parties gon' turn into funerals, songs into cries, sackcloth on your waist, shaved heads in grief. Y'all gon' mourn like you just lost your only child. And by the end? It's gon' be a day y'all never forget—and not in a good way."

11.text: "Days comin'," says the Lord, "when I'll send a famine to the land. Not a hunger for food. Not a thirst for water. But folks gon' be starvin' to hear a word from Me.

12.text: They gon' roam coast to coast, run from north to east, lookin' high and low for the Word of the Lord—but they ain't gon' find it."

13.text: "In that day, even the pretty young girls and strong young men gon' pass out from spiritual thirst.

14.text: The ones who swear by them false gods in Samaria, who say, 'As your god lives, O Dan!' or, 'Long live the way of Beersheba!' Yeah—they all gon' fall and not get back up."

1.text: I saw the Lord standin' by the altar, and He said: "Hit them pillars so hard the whole foundation shakes. Let the roof fall in on their heads. And the ones that make it out? I'ma finish them with the sword. Ain't nobody runnin'. Ain't nobody hidin'. Ain't nobody safe."

2.text: "If they dig way down in hell? I'ma snatch 'em up. If they climb all the way up to heaven? I'ma bring 'em down.

3.text: Hide on top of Mount Carmel? I'm comin' for 'em. Dive to the bottom of the ocean? I'ma send a sea monster to bite 'em.

4.text: Try to blend in with the captives? The sword still gon' find 'em. I'm watchin' 'em—not for good, but for judgment."

5.text: The Lord God of Heaven's Armies— He just touch the earth and it melts. Folks mourn everywhere. The land rise and fall like the Nile.

6.text: He got skyscraper layers in the sky, and He laid the earth's foundation deep. He calls water out the sea and floods the land with it. The Lord is His name.

7.text: "Y'all think y'all special, Israel? Ain't y'all the same as the Ethiopians to Me?" says the Lord. "I brought y'all outta Egypt, yeah... But didn't I also bring the Philistines outta Caphtor? And the Syrians outta Kir?"

8.text: "I see that sinful kingdom. And I'ma wipe it off the face of the earth. But I ain't gon' completely destroy the whole house of Jacob," says the Lord.

9.text: "I'ma sift Israel through the nations like a farmer sifts grain. And not one lil' kernel of the faithful gon' be lost.

10.text: But the sinners—the arrogant ones talkin' 'ain't nothin' bad gon' happen to us'? They gon' die by the sword."

11.text: "But in that day, I'ma rebuild David's house that fell apart. I'ma fix what's broke, raise up what's ruined, and bring it back like the good old days.

12.text: And My people gon' take over what's left of Edom and all the nations that bear My name," says the Lord who's really doin' all this.

13.text: "Listen—days comin' where the plowman gon' catch up with the reaper, and the grape stomper gon' run into the seed sower. Mountains gon' be drippin' wine, and hills gon' flow with it."

14.text: "I'ma bring My people back. They gon' rebuild the ruined cities and move in. They gon' plant vineyards and drink from 'em. Grow gardens and eat they own fruit."

15.text: "And when I plant 'em this time? They ain't gettin' pulled up again. They gon' stay in the land I gave 'em," says the Lord your God.

1.text: In the third year Jehoiakim was king in Judah, King Nebuchadnezzar of Babylon came through and put Jerusalem under siege.

2.text: God let Jehoiakim get taken, along with some of the sacred stuff from God's temple. Nebuchadnezzar took all that back to Babylon—to Shinar—and dropped it off in his god's treasure house.

3.text: Then the king told his right-hand man, Ashpenaz—the dude in charge of all the eunuchs—to go round up some young Israelites. Not just any kids though—he wanted some from royal blood and noble families.

4.text: They had to be fine, flawless, smart as a whip, quick on the uptake, and polished enough to serve in the king's palace. Basically, top-tier. And they had to be ready to learn Babylon's language and culture.

5.text: The king even set them up with a daily meal plan—his own rich food and wine. They were gon' train for three years, and after that, step into the royal service.

6.text: Outta all the Judah boys, there were four standouts: Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah.

7.text: But of course, they tried to rename them: Daniel became Belteshazzar, Hananiah became Shadrach, Mishael became Meshach, and Azariah became Abed-Nego.

8.text: But Daniel? He made up his mind—he wasn't gon' get caught up in all that. No king's fancy food, no royal wine. He didn't wanna defile himself. So he asked the chief eunuch if he could opt out.

9.text: Now God had already made the chief eunuch vibe with Daniel, so he liked him.

10.text: But the eunuch was like, "Man, I feel you, but I'm scared. If y'all start lookin' weak and raggedy, the king gon' come for my neck—literally."

11.text: So Daniel slid over to the steward—the dude the eunuch put in charge of him, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah—and pitched a plan.

12.text: "Look," he said, "give us just veggies and water for ten days. No meat, no wine. Just test it out."

13.text: "After the ten days, check how we look compared to the others eating that royal menu. Then make your call."

14.text: The steward agreed. Ran the trial for ten days.

15.text: And by the end of it? They looked healthier and fuller than all the others.

16.text: So the steward switched up the program. No more royal food or wine for them—just the veggies they asked for.

17.text: And God came through. Gave all four of them mad wisdom and knowledge. Daniel even got insight into visions and dreams.

18.text: When the three years were up, the king called 'em in. The chief eunuch brought them before Nebuchadnezzar.

19.text: The king talked to each of them, but nobody stood out like Daniel, Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah. They were different. So the king kept them close.

20.text: Anytime the king needed advice, wisdom, or understanding, he went to them. And every time, they were ten times better than the magicians and astrologers in his whole kingdom.

21.text: And Daniel? He stayed serving all the way until King Cyrus pulled up on the throne.

1.text: So in year two of Nebuchadnezzar's reign, bruh started havin' dreams—real wild ones. His spirit was shook, and he couldn't sleep no more.

2.text: So he called up all his magicians, astrologers, sorcerers, and Chaldean know-it-alls. He needed somebody to tell him what he dreamed and what it meant.

3.text: He said, "Y'all, I had a dream that got me twisted—I need to know what it was."

4.text: The Chaldeans answered him in Aramaic, "Long live the king! Just tell us what you dreamed, and we'll break it down for you."

5.text: But the king was like, "Nah—I ain't playin'. If y'all can't tell me the dream and what it means, I'm cuttin' y'all to pieces and turning your houses into ash piles."

6.text: "But if you do tell me both the dream and its meaning, I'll hook y'all up with gifts, rewards, and big respect. Now tell me what I dreamed and what it means."

7.text: They tried again: "King, just tell us the dream first—we'll handle the interpretation."

8.text: But Nebuchadnezzar was fed up. "I see what y'all tryna do—stallin'. Y'all just buyin' time 'cause y'all know I ain't changin' my mind."

9.text: "If y'all don't tell me the dream, then I already know y'all just gon' lie to me till things blow over. Tell me the dream first—then I'll know y'all ain't just makin' up the meaning."

10.text: The Chaldeans replied, "Ain't no human on earth can do what you ask! No king, no ruler, nobody ever asked something like this before."

11.text: "This thing you ask is too deep. Only the gods could answer that—and they don't live here with us flesh-and-blood folks."

12.text: That sent the king into full rage mode. He ordered all the wise men in Babylon to be executed.

13.text: The decree dropped quick, and they started hunting folks down—including Daniel and his crew.

14.text: But Daniel kept his cool. He hollered at Arioch—the captain of the king's guard—with wisdom and tact.

15.text: "Yo, Arioch, why the king poppin' off like this? What's the rush?"

16.text: After Arioch broke it down, Daniel went and requested some time from the king to figure out the dream and its meaning.

17.text: Then he rushed home and told his boys—Hananiah, Mishael, and Azariah—what was goin' down.

18.text: He asked them to pray hard and seek mercy from the God of heaven, so they wouldn't die with the rest of Babylon's wise men.

19.text: That night, God showed Daniel the dream in a vision. And Daniel immediately praised the God of heaven.

20.text: Daniel said, "Blessed be God's name forever and ever, He got all the wisdom and the power.

21.text: He flips seasons and kings, Gives wisdom to the wise And knowledge to those that seek Him.

22.text: He reveals deep, hidden things; He sees through the dark, And He shines light right through it.

23.text: Thank You, God of my ancestors, You gave me wisdom and strength. You answered our prayers— Now I know what the king saw!"

24.text: Daniel went straight to Arioch and said, "Don't kill the wise men. Take me to the king—I got what he's lookin' for."

25.text: Arioch rushed Daniel in and said, "King, I found someone from the Judah captives who can break down your dream."

26.text: The king asked Daniel (aka Belteshazzar), "Can you really tell me what I dreamed and what it means?"

27.text: Daniel said, "Look—ain't no magician, astrologer, or psychic on earth who could pull this off."

28.text: "But there is a God in heaven who reveals secrets. He's showin' you, O king, what's gon' happen later on. Here's what you saw:

29.text: "While you were lying in bed, thinkin' 'bout the future, God pulled back the curtain and gave you the preview."

30.text: "And He ain't show me this 'cause I'm smarter than anyone else. It's so we could explain it to you, and you'd understand what's been stirrin' in your heart."

31.text: "You saw a giant statue—huge and shiny. It was wild. Just awe-inspiring."

32.text: "The head was gold, chest and arms were silver, belly and thighs bronze."

33.text: "Its legs were iron, but the feet were a mix—part iron, part clay."

34.text: "Then outta nowhere, a stone—cut out without human hands—came through and smashed the statue at the feet."

35.text: "Everything—the iron, clay, bronze, silver, gold—crumbled like dust in the wind. The wind blew it all away. But that stone? It turned into a mountain and filled the whole earth."

36.text: "That was your dream. Now here's what it means…"

37.text: "You, O king, are a king of kings. God gave you this kingdom, all that power, and glory."

38.text: "He gave you rule over everybody and everything—humans, animals, birds. You're the head of gold."

39.text: "But after you, another kingdom will rise—less glorious. Then a third kingdom, made of bronze, will take over and rule the earth."

40.text: "After that, a fourth one—strong like iron. Iron crushes everything, and that's how this kingdom will be—breaking all that came before it."

41.text: "Now the feet and toes you saw, made of iron and clay? That means the kingdom gon' be divided. Still strong, but unstable."

42.text: "Some parts solid, some fragile. It's mixed like iron and clay—they don't stick together."

43.text: "And that's how this empire will be—trying to unify through alliances and mixing peoples, but it won't hold."

44.text: "But in the middle of all that, God gon' set up His own kingdom. It'll never be destroyed. It won't get handed off to nobody else. It's gon' crush every other kingdom and last forever."

45.text: "Just like that stone you saw smashing everything, that's God telling you what's coming. It's real. It's locked in."

46.text: Then King Nebuchadnezzar hit the floor—face down before Daniel. Had folks bring incense and offerings to honor him.

47.text: He said, "Yo, your God is the real deal—the God of gods, the Lord of kings, the One who actually reveals mysteries."

48.text: Then he put Daniel on! Gave him gifts, made him ruler over the whole province of Babylon, and head boss over all the wise men.
