49.text: And Daniel looked out for his boys too—got Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-Nego promoted over the province while he himself stayed posted at the king's gate.

1.text: So King Nebuchadnezzar got real bold—he built a gold statue 90 feet tall and 9 feet wide. Set it up out in the plain of Dura in Babylon like it was the new hot thing.

2.text: He sent out invites to everybody in charge—governors, judges, treasurers, politicians, counselors, mayors, and all the big shots—to come through for the dedication ceremony of this gold statue he put up.

3.text: And sure enough, all of 'em showed up and stood in front of the golden idol King Neb set up, tryna act impressed.

4.text: Then a loud-voiced hype man stepped up and said, "Listen up! This message for everybody—no matter where you from or what language you speak.

5.text: When you hear the beat drop—horns, flutes, harps, all that—you better bow down and worship this gold statue the king made.

6.text: If you don't? You goin' in the fire. Not tomorrow. Not later. Immediately."

7.text: So the music hit, and all the people—no matter where they from—fell out and worshiped that gold image like sheep.

8.text: But not everybody was with it. Some Chaldeans ran they messy selves to the king and started snitchin'.

9.text: "O king, live forever," they said, all fake respectful.

10.text: "Didn't you make a decree that anybody who hears the music gotta bow down and worship your statue?

11.text: And if they don't, they supposed to get thrown into the fire—like right away?

12.text: Well, sir… these three Hebrew boys—Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-Nego—the ones you gave top jobs to in Babylon? Yeah, they not doin' it. They don't care about your gods or your statue."

13.text: Nebuchadnezzar lost it—mad mad. He ordered those three brought to him immediately.

14.text: "Is it true?" he asked them. "Y'all ain't serving my gods or bowin' to my gold image?"

15.text: "Look—I'll give you one more chance. Music bout to play, and if y'all just fall down and worship it, cool. But if not, y'all gettin' tossed in that furnace. And tell me—what god gonna save y'all then?"

16.text: Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-Nego kept it 100. "We don't even need to respond to that, King.

17.text: Our God can save us from the fire, and from you too."

18.text: "But even if He don't—we still ain't bowin'. Period."

19.text: That really set Nebuchadnezzar off. He was heated, literally and figuratively. He told 'em to crank the furnace seven times hotter than usual.

20.text: Then he picked the strongest soldiers in his squad to tie them up and toss 'em in.

21.text: They bound up the three men—still wearing their coats, pants, turbans and all—and threw them in.

22.text: The furnace was so hot, it burned up the soldiers just for gettin' close.

23.text: And Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-Nego? They fell into the flames—fully tied up.

24.text: But then Nebuchadnezzar jumped up. "Wait—ain't we throw three men in that fire?"

25.text: "Yes, King, just three." "Well LOOK," the king said. "I see four men walkin' around in the fire—loose—and they ain't hurt. And that fourth one? He look divine—like the Son of God."

26.text: So Nebuchadnezzar went up to the mouth of the furnace and shouted, "Shadrach! Meshach! Abed-Nego! Servants of the Most High God—come out here!" They stepped out the fire like it was nothing.

27.text: All the royal officials came running and saw that the fire ain't do a thing to them—not a hair singed, no clothes burned, not even a whiff of smoke.

28.text: Then the king had to give props: "Blessed be the God of Shadrach, Meshach, and Abed-Nego! He sent His angel and saved them because they trusted Him. They defied my command and risked everything to stay loyal to their God."

29.text: "So I'm making a new rule—anybody who talks reckless about their God? Off with them! And their house? Ashes. Ain't no god out here who can rescue like this one."

30.text: And then, like the story couldn't get any better, the king gave them an even higher promotion in Babylon.

1.text: King Nebuchadnezzar sent this out to everybody — all the people, every nation and language across the whole earth: "Peace and blessings to y'all."

2.text: "I gotta let y'all know what the Most High God done did for me — all the signs and miracles He worked out."

3.text: "His signs? Off the chain. His wonders? Powerful. His kingdom last forever, and He always runnin' things — every generation."

4.text: I was chillin' in my palace, feelin' real good.

5.text: Then boom — I had this dream that shook me. I was shook in my sleep, my mind all over the place.

6.text: So I sent out a message to bring in all the wise folk in Babylon so they could break down the dream for me.

7.text: The magicians, astrologers, fortune tellers — all of 'em came. I told 'em the dream, but none of them could tell me what it meant.

8.text: Then Daniel pulled up (y'all know, the one they call Belteshazzar, named after one of my gods — but he got the Spirit of the Holy God in him). I told him the dream too.

9.text: I said, "Belteshazzar, chief over all these magicians — I know you got God's Spirit in you, and no mystery stress you out. Help me out with this vision."

10.text: "Here's what I saw while I was layin' in bed: There was this big tree in the middle of the earth — real tall."

11.text: "It kept growin', got super strong. So tall it touched the sky and everybody on earth could see it."

12.text: "The leaves were beautiful, it had a ton of fruit, and it fed everybody. Wild animals rested under it, birds lived in its branches — everything needed that tree."

13.text: "Then I saw in my dream a 'watcher' — a holy one — come down from heaven."

14.text: "He yelled out loud: 'Cut the tree down! Chop off the branches, strip the leaves, scatter the fruit! Let the animals and birds dip out.'"

15.text: "'But don't touch the stump — leave it in the ground, lock it down with iron and bronze. Let it stay in the grass, and let the dew fall on it. Let him eat grass like the animals.'"

16.text: "'Change his heart from human to animal. Let seven seasons pass over him.'"

17.text: "'This is what the holy ones decided — so everybody will know the Most High run this. He pick who He want to be in charge, even folks y'all wouldn't expect.'"

18.text: "That's what I dreamed. Now, Belteshazzar, break it down for me. The rest of these wise men ain't got it, but I know you do — 'cause the Spirit of the Holy God stay with you."

19.text: Daniel (aka Belteshazzar) stood there quiet, shook for a minute, thinkin' hard. The king said, "Don't let this dream trip you up." Daniel said, "King… I wish this dream was about your enemies and not you."

20.text: "That big tree you saw, growin' tall and strong, reachin' the sky, seen all over the world…"

21.text: "With beautiful leaves, mad fruit, animals chillin' underneath, and birds livin' in the branches…"

22.text: "That's you, King. You done grown strong and powerful. Your greatness touches the heavens, and your rule reach everywhere."

23.text: "But then you saw that holy one come down sayin': 'Chop the tree down, leave the stump, let the dew hit it, let it live like an animal till seven seasons go by.'"

24.text: "That's what's about to happen to you, King. This is what the Most High got planned."

25.text: "You gon' be kicked out from around people. You gon' live like the animals, eat grass like cows. Dew gon' be your shower. This gon' go on for seven seasons — till you realize the Most High is in charge of kings, and He picks who runs things."

26.text: "But the stump stayin' in the ground? That means your kingdom gon' still be yours — once you learn that Heaven is the one who really got the power."

27.text: "So here's my advice, King: do right. Cut out the sin. Show love to the poor. Maybe then your peace will last a little longer."

28.text: And yeah — all this came true for King Nebuchadnezzar.

29.text: A whole year later, he was strollin' around his palace in Babylon, feelin' himself.

30.text: He said, "Ain't this the fly kingdom I built with my own power? All this is mine — for my glory and fame."

31.text: While the words was still comin' out his mouth — BOOM — a voice came down from heaven sayin', "Yo, Nebuchadnezzar! Your kingdom gone!"

32.text: "You ain't gon' be around people no more. You bout to be out here with the animals, eatin' grass. This gon' last seven seasons till you get it through your head: the Most High runs everything."

33.text: That same hour it happened. He got kicked out, ate grass like an ox, his body stayed wet from the dew, hair got long like eagle feathers, nails like bird claws.

34.text: But after that time passed, I, Nebuchadnezzar, looked up to heaven — and my mind came back. I praised the Most High, honored the One who lives forever. His kingdom? Eternal. His rule? Ain't nobody takin' that from Him.

35.text: Everybody on earth? Ain't nothin' compared to Him. He do what He want, both in heaven and down here. Ain't nobody stoppin' Him or questionin' His moves.

36.text: My mind came back, and so did my kingdom — and even more honor than before. My people came back to me, and I got my throne again, plus extra glory.

37.text: So now I, Nebuchadnezzar, praise, lift up, and honor the King of heaven. Everything He do is right. All His ways are just. And He know how to bring down anybody who's too proud.

1.text: King Belshazzar threw a huge turn-up for a thousand of his people, drinkin' wine right in front of all of 'em.

2.text: While he was sippin', Belshazzar told 'em to go grab them gold and silver cups his daddy Nebuchadnezzar stole from God's temple in Jerusalem, so him, his boys, his wives, and his side chicks could drink outta 'em.

3.text: So they brought them sacred cups from God's temple in Jerusalem, and the king, his folks, his wives, and his side pieces all drank outta 'em.

4.text: They was sippin' wine, hypin' up fake gods made of gold, silver, bronze, iron, wood, and stone.

5.text: Right then, a hand popped up outta nowhere. Just the fingers. And it started writin' on the wall, near the lamp, in the king's palace. The king saw that hand movin' and writin'.

6.text: His whole face switched up—he was shook. His thoughts had him spiralin', hips got weak, and his knees was knockin' together like drums.

7.text: He screamed for the astrologers, Chaldeans, and fortune-tellers to come through. Then he said, "Whoever can read this mess on the wall and tell me what it mean, I'ma hook you up with purple clothes, gold chain, and make you third in charge around here."

8.text: All them "wise men" showed up, but none of 'em could read the writing or tell the king what it meant.

9.text: That made Belshazzar panic even more—his face got ghostly pale, and his squad didn't know what to say.

10.text: The queen heard what was goin' down and pulled up to the party. She said, "Long live the king! Chill, don't let this mess rattle you or mess up your face.

11.text: There's a dude in your kingdom who got God's Spirit in him. Back in your daddy's day, he was known for bein' full of light, deep wisdom, and understanding—like the gods themselves. King Nebuchadnezzar, your daddy, made him the head over all the magicians, astrologers, and wise folks.

12.text: This man, Daniel—aka Belteshazzar—he got that excellent vibe, knowledge, skill for readin' dreams, crackin' riddles, and explainin' wild stuff. Call Daniel in, and he'll break it down for you."

13.text: So they brought Daniel in front of the king. The king asked, "You that Daniel, one of them exiles from Judah that my daddy brought here?

14.text: I done heard about you—how you got God's Spirit in you, and how you got light, wisdom, and deep understanding.

15.text: My crew—the wise men and astrologers—they couldn't break this thing down for me.

16.text: But I heard you the one who can interpret and explain deep mysteries. If you can read this writing and tell me what it mean, I'ma give you a purple robe, a gold chain, and make you third in charge."

17.text: Daniel said, "You can keep them gifts, or give 'em to somebody else. But I'll still read what's on the wall and tell you what it mean.

18.text: Look king, the Most High God gave your daddy Nebuchadnezzar all his power, status, honor, and shine.

19.text: And 'cause of that, all the folks from every nation and language was scared of him. He killed who he wanted, let live who he wanted, raised up who he wanted, and brought down who he wanted.

20.text: But when he got too full of himself, all prideful and arrogant, God snatched the throne from him and stripped him of all that glory.

21.text: He got kicked out like a wild animal. He lost his mind, lived with donkeys, ate grass like oxen, and stayed drenched in dew 'til he learned that the Most High God runs the kingdom game and puts who He wants on the throne.

22.text: But you, Belshazzar—you knew all this, and still didn't humble yourself.

23.text: Matter fact, you went against the Lord of heaven. You had the nerve to drink wine outta His temple cups, you and your crew, your wives, and your side chicks. Y'all gave props to gods made outta silver, gold, bronze, iron, wood, and stone—gods that can't see, hear, or think. But the real God, the one holdin' your breath and controllin' your path? You ain't even acknowledge Him.

24.text: That's why He sent that hand to write what you saw.

25.text: Here's what it said: MENE, MENE, TEKEL, UPHARSIN.

26.text: MENE mean: God done numbered your days as king—it's a wrap.

27.text: TEKEL mean: You been weighed on God's scales, and you came up short.

28.text: PERES mean: Your kingdom's gettin' split up and handed to the Medes and Persians."

29.text: Then Belshazzar kept his word—he gave Daniel the purple fit, put a gold chain on him, and announced that Daniel was now third in command.

30.text: That same night, Belshazzar, king of Babylon, got killed.

31.text: And Darius the Mede came in and took over the kingdom. Dude was 62 years old.

1.text: King Darius thought it was a good idea to put 120 officials over the whole kingdom.

2.text: Over them, he picked three top bosses—Daniel was one of 'em—to make sure them officials ain't mess up or steal so the king ain't lose nothin'.

3.text: Daniel stood out from the rest, 'cause he had that favor on him—an excellent spirit. The king was even thinkin' 'bout puttin' him in charge of the whole thing.

4.text: So the other bosses and officials tried to dig up some dirt on Daniel, tryin' to catch him slippin' in his job. But he was solid—faithful, no mistakes, no funny business.

5.text: They said, "Ain't no way we gon' catch him doin' wrong unless it's got somethin' to do with how he serves his God."

6.text: So all them officials and bosses pulled up on the king and said, "O King Darius, long live the king!

7.text: Look, everybody on your team—bosses, counselors, and all—agree that we should make a new law: for 30 days, nobody can pray to no god or person except you. If they do, throw 'em in the lion's den.

8.text: Go ahead and write it down, king, and seal it—'cause the law of the Medes and Persians can't be changed."

9.text: So King Darius signed off on the law, just like that.

10.text: When Daniel heard the law was signed, he went home. He went upstairs, windows open toward Jerusalem, dropped to his knees three times a day like he always did, and prayed and thanked God.

11.text: Them haters was watchin'—they caught Daniel prayin' and askin' God for help.

12.text: They ran back to the king and said, "Didn't you sign a law sayin' for 30 days nobody can pray to anybody but you, or else they get tossed to the lions?" The king said, "Yeah, that's right. Law of the Medes and Persians. No changes."

13.text: They said, "Well, that dude Daniel—the one you brought from Judah? He don't care nothin' 'bout you or your law. He still prayin' three times a day."

14.text: When the king heard that, he was sick about it. He liked Daniel and spent the whole day tryna figure out a way to save him.

15.text: But the crew came back and pressed him: "You know the law, king. Once you make it, it can't be changed."

16.text: So the king gave in. He told 'em to grab Daniel and throw him in the lions' den. But he told Daniel, "The God you always serve—He gon' rescue you."

17.text: They rolled a big stone over the entrance and the king sealed it with his ring—and with his officials' rings too—so nobody could undo it.

18.text: That night, the king went home but didn't eat, didn't listen to no music, and couldn't even sleep.

19.text: Real early the next morning, he rushed out to the lions' den.

20.text: When he got close, he cried out, hurt and worried. "Daniel! Servant of the living God! Did your God—the one you always serve—save you from the lions?"

21.text: Daniel said, "Long live the king!

22.text: My God sent His angel and shut the lions' mouths. They ain't touch me, 'cause I was innocent in His eyes. And I ain't do nothin' wrong to you, either."

23.text: The king was hype. He told them to pull Daniel up out the pit. And Daniel ain't have a scratch on him—'cause he had real faith in his God.

24.text: Then the king ordered the men who tried to snitch on Daniel to be thrown in the lions' den—along with their kids and wives. Before they could even hit the ground, the lions tore 'em up, broke all they bones.

25.text: Then King Darius wrote this letter: "To everybody in the world—every people, nation, and language: Peace to y'all.

26.text: I'm makin' a new rule: In every part of my kingdom, everybody need to show mad respect and fear for the God of Daniel. He the livin' God, He steady and don't switch up. His kingdom ain't goin' nowhere, And He run things forever.

27.text: He saves and rescues, He show out with miracles in heaven and earth. He the One who saved Daniel from them lions."

28.text: So Daniel stayed blessed and kept on thrivin' through the rest of Darius' reign and even when Cyrus the Persian took over.

1.text: In the first year of King Belshazzar's reign in Babylon, Daniel had this wild dream while he was sleepin'. He woke up, wrote it down, and made sure to keep the main points.

2.text: Daniel said, "In my dream that night, I saw the four winds from heaven stirrin' up the big sea.

3.text: Then four crazy lookin' beasts rose up out the sea. Each one looked different from the last.

4.text: The first one looked like a lion but had eagle wings. As I watched, the wings got snatched off. Then it stood up on two feet like a man, and it was given a man's heart.

5.text: Then came the second beast, lookin' like a big ol' bear. It was leaned up on one side, and had three ribs in its mouth like it just finished eatin'. Folks told it, 'Get up and eat even more flesh!'

6.text: After that, I saw a third beast that looked like a leopard. It had four bird wings on its back and four heads. Dominion—like rulership—was given to it.

7.text: Then I saw a fourth beast in another vision that night. Man, this one was terrifying—looked wild and strong, had iron teeth, and was crushin', smashin', and stompin' on whatever was left. It didn't look like nothin' that came before it. It had ten horns.

8.text: While I was thinkin' about them horns, another little horn came up in the middle of 'em, and three of the original horns got snatched out to make room. This new horn had eyes like a man and a mouth that stayed talkin' big talk.

9.text: I watched till thrones got set up, And the Ancient of Days sat down. His fit was white like snow, Hair like pure wool. His throne was straight flames, With wheels burnin' fire.

10.text: A river of fire flowed out from Him. Thousands upon thousands served Him. Millions stood in front of Him. Court was in session, And the books got opened.

11.text: I kept watchin' 'cause that loud-mouth horn was still talkin' wild. Then the beast got killed, and its body got tossed in the fire.

12.text: The other beasts had their power taken too, but they got to live a lil' longer for a set time.

13.text: Then I saw in my dream at night, One like the Son of Man ridin' on the clouds. He came up to the Ancient of Days, And they brought Him near.

14.text: He was handed full dominion, glory, and a kingdom, So that everybody—people from every nation and language—would serve Him. His kingdom gon' last forever, Never gonna pass away or get destroyed.

15.text: Daniel said, "I was torn up on the inside—my spirit was shook. That dream had me messed up.

16.text: So I went up to one of them standin' there and asked what all this meant. He broke it down for me.

17.text: He said, 'Them four beasts? That's four kings gon' rise up from the earth.

18.text: But the people of the Most High—His real ones—gon' get the kingdom and hold it down forever. Ain't nobody takin' it back.'

19.text: But I had to know more 'bout that fourth beast— The one that ain't look like the rest, So mean and powerful, With iron teeth and bronze claws, That devoured, crushed, and stomped everything.

20.text: I needed answers about them ten horns on its head And the one little horn that came up and knocked three down. That little horn had eyes, a loud mouth, and was lookin' real bold.

21.text: I saw that horn makin' war with God's people— And it was actually winnin' for a minute.

22.text: But then the Ancient of Days stepped in, Judged in favor of the saints, And it was finally time for God's people to take over.

23.text: Here's what he said: 'That fourth beast? It's a fourth kingdom that gon' rise up on the earth. It ain't like none before it. It's gon' eat up the whole world, Smash and crush everything in its way.

24.text: The ten horns? That's ten kings from that kingdom. Then another king gon' come after them— He gon' be different, And take down three kings.

25.text: He gon' run his mouth against the Most High, Oppress God's people, And try to change the times and the laws. God's people gon' be under his hand For a time, times, and half a time.

26.text: But then court gon' sit, And they gon' strip his power And destroy him for good.

27.text: After that, the whole kingdom, the power, Everything under heaven Gon' belong to the saints—God's people. His kingdom lasts forever, And every ruler gon' bow down and obey Him.'

28.text: That's where the vision ended. But me? I was real disturbed— My face went pale, And I kept the whole thing to myself.

1.text: In the third year of King Belshazzar's rule, I—Daniel—had another vision. This one came after the first dream I had.

2.text: In the vision, I saw myself in Shushan, the fortress city in the province of Elam. I was standin' by the Ulai River.

3.text: I looked up and saw a ram standin' by the river. It had two horns, both tall, but one was taller than the other—and the taller one came up last.

4.text: The ram was pushin' west, north, and south. Ain't no beast could stand against him. Nobody could rescue from his grip. He did whatever he wanted and got real powerful with it.

5.text: While I was still tryin' to figure it out, a male goat came outta the west, movin' across the whole earth like it was flyin', not even touchin' the ground. It had one big horn between its eyes.

6.text: It ran straight at that ram with the two horns I saw earlier—comin' full speed with serious power.

7.text: It went at the ram with rage, broke both its horns, and the ram ain't have no strength to fight back. The goat slammed him to the ground and stomped him out. Nobody could save the ram.

8.text: The goat got real powerful after that, but right when it was at its peak, the big horn broke off. Then four new horns popped up where that one was, pointin' in all directions.

9.text: Outta one of them four horns, a small horn came up. It started growin' real big toward the south, the east, and even toward the Beautiful Land.

10.text: This little horn got bold—like reachin' up to heaven. It threw down some of the heavenly hosts and some stars and stomped on 'em.

11.text: It even had the nerve to try and act higher than the Prince of the army of heaven. It shut down the daily sacrifices and messed up the temple spot.

12.text: Because folks was wildin' in sin, God let this horn take control, stop the daily offerings, and drag the truth through the mud. And it was successful at it—for a minute.

13.text: Then I heard one holy one talkin', and another one asked, "How long is this mess gonna go on? The daily sacrifices bein' stopped, the holy place and the people gettin' stomped on?"

14.text: The answer came back: "2,300 evenings and mornings. After that, the sanctuary gon' get cleaned up."

15.text: After I saw all this, I was tryna figure out what it meant. Then outta nowhere, someone lookin' like a man showed up.

16.text: I heard a voice callin' from between the Ulai River banks, "Gabriel, break this down for him. Help him understand."

17.text: Gabriel came toward me, and I got so scared I fell face-first to the ground. But he said, "Chill, son of man. This vision is talkin' about the end times."

18.text: While he was speakin', I blacked out—face in the dirt. But he touched me and helped me stand up.

19.text: He said, "I'ma tell you what's gonna go down at the end of all this chaos. It's gonna happen at the time God already set.

20.text: That ram you saw with the two horns? That's the kings of Media and Persia.

21.text: The goat? That's Greece. The big horn between its eyes? That's the first king.

22.text: That horn got broken, and four others rose up in its place. That means four kingdoms will rise from the same empire, but none of them will have the same kind of power.

23.text: Later on, when sin hits its peak, A bold, slick king gon' show up.

24.text: He gon' be powerful—but it won't be his own strength. He gon' cause destruction, He gon' succeed, And he gon' take down the strong and even God's chosen ones.

25.text: He gon' be all about deception, Think he all that in his own heart, Mess up a whole lot of folks while they chillin'. He gon' even try to step to the Prince of princes— But he gon' get taken down, and it won't be by no human hands.

26.text: What you saw in the vision—the one about evenings and mornings—it's true. But lock it down. This for the future, a long time from now."

27.text: I, Daniel, passed out after all that. I was sick for days. But I eventually got up and went back to work for the king. Still, I couldn't stop thinkin' about the vision. I ain't tell nobody, 'cause they wouldn't get it.

1.text: In the first year of Darius—son of Ahasuerus, a Mede by blood—when he got made king over the Babylonian territory,

2.text: I, Daniel, was readin' the scriptures and realized from the prophet Jeremiah that God had said Jerusalem was gon' be desolate for seventy years.

3.text: So I turned my attention to God—prayin', cryin' out, fastin', wearin' sackcloth, and sittin' in ashes.

4.text: I prayed to the Lord my God and confessed, sayin', "Lord, You great and awesome! You keep Your promises and show mercy to the ones who love You and follow Your commandments.

5.text: But we messed up bad—we sinned, acted foul, did what we wanted, rebelled, and straight-up ignored Your instructions and judgments.

6.text: We ain't listen to Your prophets, who spoke in Your name to our kings, our leaders, our parents, and everybody else in the land.

7.text: Lord, You always right, but us? We ashamed—everybody: Judah, Jerusalem, all Israel, whether they close or scattered all over the place. We all in this mess 'cause we turned our back on You.

8.text: We ashamed, Lord—our kings, leaders, and ancestors—'cause we sinned against You.

9.text: But You, Lord our God, got mercy and forgiveness, even when we rebelled.

10.text: We didn't obey Your voice or walk in Your ways like You told us through the prophets.

11.text: All of Israel turned away from Your law and refused to listen. That's why we under the curse You warned us about in the Law of Moses—'cause we sinned against You.

12.text: You kept Your word and brought disaster on us and on our leaders. What happened to Jerusalem? Ain't nobody ever seen destruction like that.

13.text: Just like Moses wrote, all this disaster came down on us—but we still ain't turn to You, Lord, or tried to understand what's real.

14.text: So You let it happen, 'cause You always do what's right—even when we don't listen.

15.text: And now, Lord our God—You the one who brought Your people outta Egypt with a mighty hand and made a name for Yourself that still stands—we done messed up and acted wicked.

16.text: Lord, please, based on Your righteousness, turn Your anger away from Jerusalem, Your holy mountain. Our sins and the sins of our ancestors made us and Your city look bad to the nations around us.

17.text: So now, our God, hear Your servant prayin' and cryin' out. For Your sake, shine Your face on Your ruined sanctuary.

18.text: Lord, open Your ears and eyes—see what we goin' through. We ain't bring our prayers to You 'cause we earned anything, but 'cause You got mad mercy.

19.text: Lord, please hear us! Please forgive! Please act! Don't wait no more—for Your own name's sake—'cause this city and Your people belong to You!"

20.text: While I was still prayin'—confessin' my sins and my people's sins, and askin' God to show mercy on His holy mountain—

21.text: While I was still talkin', Gabriel—the same one I seen in the last vision—came flyin' up to me right around the evening sacrifice time.

22.text: He came and said, "Daniel, I'm here to help you understand what's really goin' on.

23.text: As soon as you started prayin', the word went out—and I'm here 'cause you highly favored. So listen close and try to get this vision."

24.text: "God already marked out seventy weeks for your people and your holy city:– To shut down sin,– To put an end to guilt,– To make things right with God,– To bring in everlasting righteousness,– To lock up vision and prophecy,– And to anoint the Most Holy One.

25.text: So know this and understand: From the moment the order goes out to rebuild Jerusalem until the Prince—the Messiah—comes, it'll be seven weeks and sixty-two more weeks. The streets and walls will be rebuilt, even while times stay rough.

26.text: After those sixty-two weeks, the Messiah gon' be cut off—and not for Himself. Then a ruler will come with his people and destroy the city and the temple. It's gon' end like a flood—war and destruction already set to come.

27.text: That ruler gon' confirm a deal with many for one week. But halfway through, he gon' stop the sacrifices and offerings. He gon' do some foul stuff, real disrespectful—set up something nasty and desolate—until God brings the final judgment down on him."

1.text: In the third year of King Cyrus of Persia, I—Daniel, who they also call Belteshazzar—got a vision. The message was real, and it was about some stuff that was gon' take a long time to go down. But I understood it.

2.text: At that time, I had been in deep mourning for three straight weeks.

3.text: I wasn't eatin' no good food—no meat, no wine, not even lotion on my skin—nothin' pleasant touched me the whole time.

4.text: On the twenty-fourth day of the first month, I was chillin' by the Tigris River.

5.text: I looked up and saw a man—dressed in linen with a gold belt from Uphaz around his waist.

6.text: His body looked like a gemstone, his face was flashin' like lightning, his eyes were like fire, arms and legs like polished bronze, and his voice? Sounded like a whole crowd talkin' at once.

7.text: I was the only one who actually saw the vision. The people with me couldn't see it, but they got hit with a wave of fear and dipped out real quick to hide.

8.text: So I was left alone, seein' this heavy vision. My strength vanished, my face went pale, and I had nothin' left in me.

9.text: I heard him talkin' though, and the sound of his voice knocked me straight out—I fell face-first to the ground in a deep sleep.

10.text: Then outta nowhere, a hand touched me and set me trembling on my knees and hands.

11.text: He said, "Daniel, you're deeply loved. Pay attention to what I'm sayin' and stand up—I was sent here for you." And while he talked, I stood up, still shakin'.

12.text: He said, "Don't be scared, Daniel. From the very first day you set your heart to understand and humbled yourself before God, He heard you. That's why I'm here.

13.text: But I got held up—the spiritual prince over Persia blocked me for 21 days. Then Michael, one of the top warriors of heaven, came to help me, 'cause I was stuck fightin' with the kings of Persia.

14.text: Now I'm here to break it down for you—what's gonna happen to your people later on. This vision is about the future."

15.text: While he was talkin', I couldn't even look up—I was speechless, starin' at the ground.

16.text: Then someone who looked human touched my lips. I finally spoke and said, "My lord, this vision got me overwhelmed—I got no strength left.

17.text: How can I even talk to you right now? I'm weak, breathin' heavy, barely holdin' on."

18.text: Then the one who looked like a man touched me again—and I felt stronger.

19.text: He said, "Don't trip, you deeply loved. Peace to you. Be strong, real strong!" As he talked, strength came back to me. I said, "Go ahead and speak—I'm good now. You gave me strength."

20.text: He said, "You know why I came, right? Now I gotta go back and fight that prince of Persia. And after that, the prince of Greece gon' show up.

21.text: But I'ma tell you what's written in the Book of Truth. Ain't nobody ridin' with me in this fight except Michael—your heavenly protector."

1.text: Back in the first year of Darius the Mede, I—yeah, me—stood up to back him up and give him strength.

2.text: Now listen up, I'ma tell you straight: Three more kings gon' rise in Persia, and then a fourth one—way richer than all of them—gon' use his wealth and power to stir up everybody against Greece.

3.text: Then a powerful king gon' pop up, takin' over everything, doin' whatever he wanna do.

4.text: But right when he get strong, his kingdom gon' get broken up and spread out in four directions. It won't go to his kids, and it won't be as strong as before. It's gon' get taken and given to others.

5.text: The king of the South gon' get strong, and one of his boys gon' get even stronger and end up runnin' the show with a heavy hand.

6.text: After some time, they'll try to link up—one of the Southern king's daughters gon' marry the Northern king to keep the peace. But it won't last. She gon' lose power, he gon' fall too, and the whole setup gon' collapse, includin' the people who tried to hold it all together.

7.text: But one of her folks gon' rise up and come with an army. He gon' storm the North, tear it up, and take the W.

8.text: He'll snatch their gods, gold, silver, and valuables, and haul it all back to Egypt. He gon' outlive the Northern king, too.

9.text: Eventually the king of the North gon' try to come back at the South, but he gon' end up retreatin' to his own turf.

10.text: But his sons ain't gon' let it slide. They gon' raise a massive army and charge through, makin' moves. Then one of 'em gon' come back to his stronghold and stir things up.

11.text: The king of the South gon' get heated and go to war against him. The Northern king gon' pull up with a huge army, but the South gon' beat him and wipe out a whole bunch of his folks.

12.text: But after that, the Southern king gon' get cocky and think he up, but it won't last—he won't be able to hold on to it.

13.text: 'Cause the Northern king gon' come back with an even bigger army and better gear, and after a few years, he gon' be back on the attack.

14.text: During all this chaos, some folks—including violent ones from your own people—gon' rise up against the South, thinkin' they fulfillin' prophecy. But they gon' get dropped.

15.text: The king of the North gon' come through, build siege ramps, and take a fortified city. The South's troops won't be able to hold him back—not even their best soldiers.

16.text: Whoever comes at him, he'll do whatever he want. Nobody can stop him. He even gon' take over the Beautiful Land (that's Israel), and bring serious destruction with him.

17.text: He gon' try to lock in full control of the kingdom by sendin' in his daughter—thinkin' she gon' help him win. But she won't be loyal, and the plan gon' flop.

18.text: Then he gon' set his sights on the coastlands and take over a bunch of them. But some leader gon' push back and embarrass him, and he gon' fall back.

19.text: After that, he'll try to focus on home base, but he gon' trip, fall, and disappear—nobody'll be able to save him.

20.text: Somebody else gon' take his place and raise taxes across the land. But he won't last long—he'll be taken out quietly, not even in battle.

21.text: After him, a shady dude gon' sneak in—he ain't even royalty like that. He gon' come in smooth, take over with manipulation and schemes.

22.text: Folks gon' fall like a flood before him—including the "prince of the covenant."

23.text: After makin' fake alliances, he gon' turn sneaky and rise up with just a small crew.

24.text: He gon' roll up on rich spots like it's nothin', doin' stuff his ancestors never did—spreading out the loot to win people over, settin' traps against strongholds. But it won't last forever.

25.text: Then he gon' get bold and go at the king of the South with a huge army. The South gon' respond with a mighty army too, but he gon' get betrayed.

26.text: His own people—the ones eatin' at his table—gon' set him up. His army gon' get wiped, and many gon' die.

27.text: Both kings gon' be sittin' at the same table, straight lyin' to each other, schemin', but none of it gon' work out, 'cause God already set the end time.

28.text: On his way home, the Northern king gon' be mad at God's covenant people, stir up drama, then head back to his land.

29.text: At the set time, he gon' come back at the South, but it won't go like it did before.

30.text: Ships from Cyprus gon' push back on him. He gon' take it personal, rage out on God's people, and cause even more damage.

31.text: He'll send troops to mess up the temple, stop the daily offerings, and set up the "abomination of desolation."

32.text: He'll use slick talk to corrupt folks who already wildin'. But the real ones—those who know their God—gon' stay strong and do big things.

33.text: Wise folks gon' teach others, even though they gon' be hunted, burned, locked up, and robbed for a while.

34.text: When they fall, they'll get a little help—but some fake folks gon' join the movement for clout.

35.text: Even some of the wise gon' fall so they can be refined and purified, 'cause the final time ain't here yet—it's still on God's schedule.

36.text: Then this king gon' do whatever he want. He gon' boost himself above every god and talk crazy against the God of gods. He gon' prosper until God's wrath finishes up, 'cause what God say is gon' happen.

37.text: He won't care 'bout the gods of his ancestors, won't be interested in women, won't respect any god—he think he above all that.

38.text: But instead, he gon' worship war and power, honor a foreign god nobody ever heard of, and throw money and treasures at it.

39.text: He gon' push that god's agenda, give certain folks power, and divide land for a check.

40.text: At the end time, the king of the South gon' pull up on him—but the king of the North gon' come like a hurricane, with chariots, horses, and a whole navy. He gon' blow through countries.

41.text: He'll hit the Glorious Land (Israel), and take down a bunch of nations. But Edom, Moab, and the Ammonites gon' escape.

42.text: He gon' take over all kinds of lands—even Egypt won't be safe.

43.text: He gon' control all Egypt's money and treasures. Libya and Ethiopia gon' be right behind him.

44.text: But then he gon' get shook by news from the east and north. He gon' go out wildin', ready to destroy and kill.

45.text: He'll pitch his royal tents between the sea and God's holy mountain—but that's where his run ends. Nobody gon' help him.

1.text: Around that time, Michael—the big angel who watches over your people—gon' step in. It's gon' be a time of trouble like the world ain't never seen before. But your people—the ones whose names in the Book—they gon' be saved.

2.text: A whole bunch of folks who been sleepin' in the dirt gon' wake up— Some to eternal life, Others to shame and eternal disgrace.

3.text: The wise ones gon' shine bright, Like the stars up in the sky. And the ones who helped folks get right with God? They gon' shine forever too.

4.text: But you, Daniel? Close up this vision. Seal the book 'til the end times. Folks gon' be runnin' all over, And knowledge gon' be on a whole new level.

5.text: Then I looked up and saw two more people—one standin' on each side of the river.

6.text: One of them asked the man dressed in linen who was floatin' above the water, "How long 'til all this stuff goes down?"

7.text: I heard the man in linen raise both hands to heaven and swear by the One who lives forever, "It's gon' last a time, times, and half a time. When God's people look completely broken, That's when all this gon' finally wrap up."

8.text: I heard it, but I ain't really get it. So I asked, "Sir, how's all this gon' end?"

9.text: He said, "Go 'head, Daniel. The words are locked down 'til the end time.

10.text: A lotta folks gon' get purified, cleaned up, and made right. But the wicked? They gon' keep wildin'. They won't get it—but the wise will understand."

11.text: "From the day the daily sacrifices get stopped And that nasty abomination gets put in place, You count 1,290 days.

12.text: But blessed is the one who waits it out and makes it to day 1,335.

13.text: And you, Daniel—go on and rest. You gon' rise up and get your reward at the very end."

1.text: Aight, so these the words Moses told all Israel while they was still on this side of the Jordan, out in the wilderness, in the valley near Suph, between Paran, Tophel, Laban, Hazeroth, and Dizahab.

2.text: From Horeb to Kadesh Barnea, if you walk straight, it's just an eleven-day trip by way of Mount Seir.

3.text: But check this—it wasn't till the fortieth year, in the eleventh month, on the first day of the month, that Moses finally spoke on everything the Lord told him to tell Israel.

4.text: This was after they took down Sihon, the Amorite king in Heshbon, and Og, the king of Bashan, who ruled in Ashtaroth and Edrei.

5.text: So now, Moses was on this side of the Jordan, in Moab, breaking everything down and explaining the Law, saying:

6.text: The Lord our God told us at Horeb: "Aight y'all, y'all been camped out at this mountain long enough."

7.text: It's time to pack up and move out—head to the hill country of the Amorites, hit up all the lands around there: the valley, the mountains, the lowlands, the desert, and the coast—Canaanite land, all the way up to Lebanon, to the big River Euphrates.

8.text: Look, I already set the land up for y'all! Go ahead, take what's yours—this the same land I promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying I'd give it to them and their kids after them.

9.text: Then I told y'all back then: 'Look, I can't handle all y'all by myself no more.'

10.text: The Lord your God has multiplied y'all—look at you now! You as many as the stars in the sky.

11.text: And I pray the Lord, the God of your fathers, make y'all even a thousand times bigger and bless y'all just like He promised.

12.text: But for real, how I'm supposed to handle all y'all issues, complaints, and drama by myself?

13.text: So here's what we gon' do: Y'all pick some wise, understanding, and knowledgeable folks from your tribes, and I'll put them in charge.

14.text: And y'all was like, "Yeah, that sound like a solid plan."

15.text: So I picked out leaders from y'all's tribes—some over thousands, some over hundreds, fifties, and tens—plus other officials to keep things in order.

16.text: Then I told them judges: "Listen up—when folks come to y'all with problems, be fair. Don't matter if it's between family or an outsider, judge it right."

17.text: Ain't no favoritism in justice—rich or poor, everybody gets a fair shot. And don't be scared of nobody, 'cause God is the real Judge. If a case too tough, bring it to me, and I'll handle it.

18.text: And that's when I laid out everything y'all needed to do.

19.text: So we left Horeb and rolled through that big, scary wilderness, just like God told us to. Then we got to Kadesh Barnea.

20.text: And I told y'all, "Aight, we here. These the Amorite mountains—this the land God is giving us."

21.text: Look, God already set this up for us! Go take it! Don't be scared, don't get shook!

22.text: But then y'all came to me saying, "Hold up, let's send some dudes ahead first to scope out the land and let us know the best way to roll up in there."

23.text: I thought it was a good idea, so I picked twelve men, one from each tribe.

24.text: They went up, checked the land, and came back with a report from the Valley of Eshcol.

25.text: They even brought some fruit back and said, "Yo, this land is good! This exactly what God promised us!"

26.text: But y'all ain't wanna hear it. Instead, y'all straight up rebelled against God's order.

27.text: Y'all started complaining in your tents, talking about, "God don't love us! He brought us outta Egypt just to get us wiped out by the Amorites!"

28.text: Y'all was shook, saying, "The people there way bigger and taller than us! The cities are huge with walls up to the sky! We even saw the Anakim giants there!"

29.text: Then I told y'all, "Stop being scared! Don't trip!"

30.text: God Himself gon' fight for y'all, just like He did back in Egypt.

31.text: Y'all seen how God took care of us in the wilderness—He was carrying us like a father carries his kid all the way to this place.

32.text: But even after all that, y'all still ain't trust the Lord your God.

33.text: He was leading y'all the whole time—showing y'all the way in a fire by night and a cloud by day.

34.text: So when God heard y'all acting like this, He was heated and made a promise, saying:

35.text: "Ain't none of this evil generation gon' step foot in that good land I promised y'all's ancestors—"

36.text: —Except Caleb! He gon' get his share, 'cause he followed God with his whole heart.

37.text: Even I ain't getting in, 'cause of y'all.

38.text: But Joshua? He gon' lead y'all in, so encourage him, 'cause he got the job now.

39.text: And y'all's kids, the same ones y'all thought would be victims? They the ones that gon' inherit the land.

40.text: But as for y'all? Turn around. Head back toward the Red Sea.

41.text: Then y'all tried to flip it, saying, "We messed up! We gon' go fight just like God said!" So y'all grabbed y'all weapons, ready to roll up the mountain.

42.text: But the Lord said to me, "Tell them not to go. I ain't with them, and they gon' lose."

43.text: I told y'all, but y'all ain't listen. Instead, y'all ran up in there, thinking y'all could handle it anyway.

44.text: And what happened? The Amorites came out swinging like a swarm of bees, chasing y'all from Seir all the way to Hormah.

45.text: Y'all came back crying to God, but He wasn't listening.

46.text: And that's how y'all ended up stuck in Kadesh for a long time.

1.text: Then we turned back and headed into the wilderness, toward the Red Sea route, just like the Lord told me. We kept circling around Mount Seir for a long time.

2.text: Then the Lord came through and told me:

3.text: 'Aight, y'all been going in circles around this mountain long enough—turn north now.'

4.text: 'Tell the people: "Y'all about to pass through the land of Esau's descendants—y'all's own relatives—who live in Seir. They gon' be shook when they see y'all rolling up, so be careful."'

5.text: 'Don't start nothing with them, 'cause I ain't giving y'all none of their land—not even a single footstep. I gave Mount Seir to Esau's people, that's their inheritance.'

6.text: 'If y'all need food, buy it. If y'all thirsty, buy water. Pay for what you take.'

7.text: 'The Lord your God been blessing y'all this whole time. He see the struggle y'all been through, trekking through this big ol' wilderness. For forty years, He been right there with y'all, and y'all ain't lacked a thing.'

8.text: So when we left Esau's people in Seir, we stayed off their main road, passing by Elath and Ezion Geber, and then we went toward the Moab wilderness.

9.text: Then the Lord told me: 'Don't mess with Moab or pick no fights with them. I ain't giving you none of their land, 'cause I gave Ar to Lot's descendants to keep.'

10.text: (Back in the day, the Emim used to live there—they was huge like the Anakim.)

11.text: (People used to call them giants, same as the Anakim, but the Moabites called them Emim.)

12.text: (The Horites used to live in Seir too, but Esau's descendants ran them out and took their land, just like Israel later did with the land the Lord gave them.)

13.text: Then the Lord told us: 'Aight, get up and cross the Valley of Zered.' So we did.

14.text: From Kadesh Barnea to the time we finally crossed Zered, 38 years passed—enough time for that whole generation of warriors to die off, just like the Lord said would happen.

15.text: God's hand was against them the whole time, wiping them out from the camp, till they was all gone.

16.text: And when the last of them was gone,

17.text: The Lord spoke to me again, saying:

18.text: 'Today, y'all gon' cross over Ar, the edge of Moab.'

19.text: 'When y'all get near Ammon, don't mess with them or try to take their land. I ain't giving y'all none of it, 'cause I already gave it to Lot's descendants.'

20.text: (That land used to belong to the Zamzummim, another group of giants like the Anakim.)

21.text: (They was big, many, and strong, but the Lord wiped them out so Ammon's people could take the land.)

22.text: (Same thing He did for Esau's descendants in Seir, taking out the Horites so they could settle there.)

23.text: (Even the Avim, who lived near Gaza, got taken out by the Caphtorim who moved in after them.)

24.text: Then the Lord told us: 'Get up, get moving, and cross the Arnon River. Look, I already handed over Sihon, king of the Amorites in Heshbon, to y'all. Go take his land—go to war!'

25.text: 'Starting today, every nation under heaven gon' hear about y'all and be scared. They gon' be shook just hearing y'all coming.'

26.text: So I sent messengers from Kedemoth wilderness to King Sihon of Heshbon, trying to keep the peace.

27.text: I told him: 'Let us pass through your land. We ain't gon' touch nothing, just sticking to the road.'

28.text: 'We'll buy food and water—just let us walk through on foot.'

29.text: 'That's what Esau's people in Seir and the Moabites in Ar did for us, so we just tryna get across to the land the Lord our God giving us.'

30.text: But Sihon wasn't having it. The Lord made his spirit stubborn, and he refused to let us pass, 'cause God had already planned to hand him over to us.

31.text: Then the Lord told me: 'Look, I already started giving Sihon's land to you. Go take it—it's yours now.'

32.text: So Sihon came out with his whole army, ready to fight us at Jahaz.

33.text: But the Lord our God gave him to us—we took him down along with his sons and all his people.

34.text: We took all his cities and wiped them out completely—men, women, kids—nobody was left.

35.text: Only thing we kept was the livestock and the spoils from the cities we conquered.

36.text: From Aroer (on the banks of the Arnon River) all the way to Gilead, no city was strong enough to stop us. The Lord handed them all over to us.

37.text: But we stayed clear of the Ammonite land—the Jabbok River, the hill country, and anywhere else the Lord told us not to go.

1.text: Then we headed up the road to Bashan, and Og, king of Bashan, came out with his whole crew, ready to throw hands at Edrei.

2.text: But the Lord told me: 'Don't even trip. I already gave him and his whole army to you—same way I did with Sihon, king of the Amorites in Heshbon. Handle him just like you handled Sihon.'

3.text: So the Lord our God delivered Og into our hands, along with his people, and we fought till none of them was left standing.

4.text: We took all his cities—not a single one was left. Sixty cities, the whole Argob region, the whole kingdom of Og in Bashan.

5.text: These wasn't no small villages either—every city had high walls, gates, and strong bars. Plus, there was a whole bunch of smaller towns.

6.text: We completely wiped them out, just like we did to Sihon, king of Heshbon. Every man, woman, and child—gone.

7.text: But we kept all the livestock and the goods from the cities for ourselves.

8.text: So at that time, we took the whole land from the two Amorite kings on this side of the Jordan—from the Arnon River up to Mount Hermon.

9.text: (The Sidonians call Mount Hermon Sirion, and the Amorites call it Senir.)

10.text: We took all the cities in the plains, all of Gilead, all of Bashan, up to Salcah and Edrei, which were in Og's kingdom.

11.text: Og was the last of the giants. His bed? Made of iron. You can still see it in Rabbah of Ammon. It was 9 cubits long and 4 cubits wide—that's over 13 feet long!

12.text: So at that time, we split up the land: From Aroer, near the Arnon River, to half of Gilead and its cities—I gave it to the Reubenites and Gadites.

13.text: The rest of Gilead, plus all of Bashan, Og's old kingdom, I gave to half the tribe of Manasseh. (This whole area, Argob and Bashan, was known as the land of giants.)

14.text: Jair, son of Manasseh, took all of Argob up to the borders of Geshur and Maacah. He renamed Bashan after himself—Havoth Jair—and that's what they still call it.

15.text: I gave Gilead to Machir.

16.text: To the Reubenites and Gadites, I gave land from Gilead to the Arnon River (the middle of the river was the border), and up to the Jabbok River, which bordered Ammon.

17.text: Their land included the Jordan Valley, from Chinnereth (Sea of Galilee) down to the Salt Sea, all the way to the slopes of Pisgah.

18.text: Then I told y'all: 'The Lord your God gave y'all this land to keep. But all y'all strong fighters need to cross over armed and ready to fight alongside your Israelite brothers.'

19.text: 'Your wives, kids, and livestock (and I know y'all got a lot of livestock) can stay behind in the cities I gave y'all.'

20.text: 'But once the Lord gives them rest and they got their own land across the Jordan, then y'all can go back to your own land.'

21.text: Then I told Joshua: 'You saw with your own eyes what the Lord did to these two kings. That's exactly what He gon' do to every kingdom you about to face.'

22.text: 'Don't be scared of them—the Lord your God is fighting for you.'

23.text: Then I begged the Lord at that time, saying:

24.text: 'Lord God, You already been showing Your power to me. Ain't no other god in heaven or earth that can do what You do.'

25.text: 'Please, let me cross over and see the good land on the other side of the Jordan—the mountains and Lebanon.'

26.text: 'But the Lord was mad at me because of y'all, and He ain't wanna hear it. He told me, "That's enough! Don't bring this up again."'

27.text: 'Go up to the top of Pisgah and look around—north, south, east, west—but you ain't crossing this Jordan.'

28.text: 'Instead, put Joshua in charge, encourage him, and strengthen him, 'cause he gon' lead these people into the land and help them take it.'

29.text: So we stayed in the valley near Beth Peor.

1.text: Aight, listen up, Israel—pay attention to these rules and judgments I'm teaching y'all, so y'all can live and go take the land the Lord, the God of your ancestors, is giving you.

2.text: Don't add nothing to what I'm telling you, and don't take nothing away. Just follow the commands the Lord your God gave you.

3.text: Y'all saw with your own eyes what the Lord did at Baal Peor—how He wiped out all the men who followed that false god.

4.text: But y'all who stayed loyal to the Lord your God? Y'all still standing today.

5.text: I gave y'all these laws and rules, straight from the Lord my God, so y'all can follow them in the land y'all about to take.

6.text: Stick to them carefully—'cause when other nations hear about these laws, they gon' say, 'Dang, this is a wise and understanding nation!'

7.text: What other nation got a God this close to them? Whenever we call on the Lord, He right there!

8.text: And what other nation got laws this fair like the ones I'm giving y'all today?

9.text: So be real careful—don't forget what y'all seen. Keep it in your heart forever, and teach it to your kids and grandkids.

10.text: Remember when y'all stood before the Lord at Mount Horeb? He told me, 'Gather the people, I'ma speak to them so they learn to fear Me and teach their kids to do the same.'

11.text: Y'all came to the mountain, and it was burning with fire all the way up to the sky—covered in dark clouds and smoke.

12.text: Then the Lord spoke outta the fire. Y'all heard His voice, but y'all ain't see no form—just His words.

13.text: He gave y'all His covenant, the Ten Commandments, and wrote them on two stone tablets.

14.text: And the Lord told me to teach y'all these laws, so y'all can follow them once y'all take the land.

15.text: So listen—be real careful. Y'all ain't see no physical form when God spoke to y'all out the fire at Horeb.

16.text: Don't go acting up and making idols of any kind—no statues of men, women, animals, or birds.

17.text: No statues of anything walking the earth or birds flying in the sky.

18.text: No statues of anything crawling or any fish in the water.

19.text: And don't go looking up at the sun, moon, or stars and thinking you gotta worship them. The Lord put them up there for everybody, not just y'all.

20.text: But y'all different—the Lord pulled y'all outta Egypt (that iron furnace) to be His own people.

21.text: Now, the Lord was mad at me 'cause of y'all, and He swore I ain't crossing the Jordan to the good land He's giving y'all.

22.text: I gotta stay here and die, but y'all gon' cross over and take the land.

23.text: So be careful—don't forget the Lord's covenant and don't go making idols, 'cause He already told y'all not to do that.

24.text: The Lord your God is a consuming fire—He's jealous and won't share y'all with no fake gods.

25.text: If y'all start acting up after y'all settle in the land—making idols and doing what's evil—

26.text: I'm telling y'all right now: Heaven and earth are my witnesses—y'all ain't gon' last in this land. Y'all gon' be destroyed.

27.text: The Lord gon' scatter y'all to other nations, and only a few of y'all gon' be left where He sends you.

28.text: There, y'all gon' be stuck worshiping fake gods—nothing but wood and stone that can't see, hear, eat, or smell.

29.text: But if y'all start looking for the Lord with your whole heart and soul, y'all gon' find Him.

30.text: When trouble hits and all this happens in the future, if y'all turn back to the Lord and listen to Him—

31.text: He gon' be merciful. He won't abandon you, He won't destroy you, and He won't forget the covenant He made with your ancestors.

32.text: Look back through history—from the time God made humans to now—has anything like this ever happened?

33.text: Have any other people heard God's voice from fire like y'all did—and survived?

34.text: Has any god ever come through and snatched a whole nation outta another one—using miracles, signs, war, power, and fear—like the Lord did for y'all in Egypt?

35.text: God showed y'all this so y'all know He alone is God—ain't nobody else like Him.

36.text: He let y'all hear His voice from the sky so y'all could learn, and He showed y'all His fire on earth—His words came from the flames.

37.text: 'Cause He loved y'all's ancestors, He chose y'all, freed y'all from Egypt with His own power,

38.text: And He drove out stronger nations ahead of y'all, just to give y'all their land as an inheritance—just like He promised.

39.text: So today, y'all better understand this: The Lord alone is God—up in heaven and down on earth—ain't nobody else.

40.text: So keep His laws and commands, so things go well for you and your kids, and y'all live long in the land the Lord is giving y'all forever.

41.text: Then Moses set apart three cities on this side of the Jordan, toward the sunrise.

42.text: These cities were safe zones for anyone who accidentally killed someone without meaning to—so they could escape and live.

43.text: Bezer (for Reuben's tribe), Ramoth in Gilead (for Gad's tribe), and Golan in Bashan (for Manasseh's tribe).

44.text: This is the law Moses gave to Israel—

45.text: The commands, testimonies, and rules he told them after they left Egypt.

46.text: He gave these laws on this side of the Jordan, near Beth Peor, in the land they took from Sihon, king of the Amorites, who ruled in Heshbon. Israel had defeated him after leaving Egypt.

47.text: They also took land from Og, king of Bashan—two Amorite kings east of the Jordan, where the sun rises.

48.text: From Aroer (near the Arnon River) to Mount Hermon,

49.text: And all the land east of the Jordan down to the Sea of the Arabah, below the Pisgah hills.

1.text: Then Moses called all Israel together and said: 'Listen up, Israel! These the rules and laws I'm laying down today. Learn them and make sure y'all follow them!'

2.text: The Lord our God made a covenant with us back at Mount Horeb.

3.text: This wasn't just for our ancestors—it's for us, the ones alive right now.

4.text: The Lord spoke directly to y'all, face to face, from the fire on the mountain.

5.text: I had to stand between y'all and the Lord back then, 'cause y'all was too scared to go up the mountain. And this what He said:

6.text: I am the Lord your God, the One who brought y'all outta Egypt, outta slavery.

7.text: Y'all bet not put no other gods before Me.

8.text: Don't go making any idols—no statues, no images of anything in the sky, on the ground, or in the water.

9.text: Don't bow down to them, don't serve them. I'm a jealous God, and I hold people accountable for their sins—even three and four generations down for the ones who hate Me.

10.text: But for those who love Me and keep My commands, I show mercy for a thousand generations.

11.text: Don't be out here using the Lord's name carelessly. The Lord ain't gon' let that slide.

12.text: Keep the Sabbath day holy, just like the Lord told you.

13.text: Do all your work in six days.

14.text: But on the seventh day, it's the Lord's rest day. That mean no working—not you, not your kids, not your workers, not even your animals or any outsiders in your land. Everybody rests.

15.text: And don't forget—y'all used to be slaves in Egypt, and the Lord freed y'all with His mighty power. That's why He told y'all to keep the Sabbath.

16.text: Respect your father and mother, just like the Lord commanded, so you can live long and blessed in the land He's giving you.

17.text: Don't murder.

18.text: Don't cheat on your spouse.

19.text: Don't steal.

20.text: Don't lie on your neighbor in court.

21.text: Don't be out here lusting after your neighbor's wife. Don't be jealous of their house, land, servants, ox, donkey, or anything that belongs to them.

22.text: That's what the Lord told y'all straight from the fire, the clouds, and the darkness—in a loud voice. He didn't add nothing else. Then He wrote them on two stone tablets and gave them to me.

23.text: When y'all heard God's voice out the fire and smoke, and saw the mountain blazing, all the tribe leaders and elders came to me.

24.text: Y'all said: 'The Lord really showed up today! We heard His voice and survived!'

25.text: But if this fire keeps burning, we gon' die! If we hear God's voice again, we ain't gon' make it.

26.text: Ain't no human ever heard God speak outta fire like we just did and lived. Who else has experienced this?

27.text: Moses, you go talk to Him. Listen to what He say, then come back and tell us. We'll listen and do whatever He says.

28.text: The Lord heard what y'all said and told me: 'I heard them loud and clear, and honestly, they right.'

29.text: I just wish they would always have this kind of heart—to fear Me and keep My commandments, so things will go well for them and their kids forever.

30.text: Now, go tell them: 'Go back to y'all's tents.'

31.text: But you, Moses, stay here with Me. I'ma give you all the commandments, laws, and rules so you can teach them how to live in the land I'm giving them.

32.text: So listen—do exactly what the Lord told y'all. Don't turn left or right.

33.text: Walk in the path the Lord set, so you can live long, be blessed, and stay in the land He's giving y'all.

1.text: Aight, listen up—this the commandment, these the rules and laws the Lord your God told me to teach y'all, so y'all can follow them once y'all step into this new land.

2.text: You gotta respect the Lord, keeping all His commands—you, your kids, and your grandkids—for as long as y'all live. Do that, and y'all gon' live long and prosper.

3.text: So listen, Israel! Follow what He said, so things go well for y'all. The Lord promised your ancestors He'd make y'all multiply big time and give y'all a land flowing with milk and honey.

4.text: Listen up, Israel! The Lord our God is the one and only God!

5.text: Love the Lord your God with all your heart, all your soul, and all your strength.

6.text: Keep these words I'm giving you deep in your heart.

7.text: Teach them to your kids—talk about them at home, on the road, when you lay down, and when you get up.

8.text: Tie them to your hands, keep them in front of your eyes like a reminder.

9.text: Write them on your doorposts and gates—make sure His words stay in your face.

10.text: Now when the Lord your God brings you into this promised land—the one He promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—He gon' give y'all big, beautiful cities that y'all ain't even build.

11.text: Y'all gon' get houses full of good stuff y'all ain't put there, wells y'all ain't dig, vineyards and olive trees y'all ain't plant. And when y'all eat and get full—

12.text: Be careful! Don't forget the Lord who brought y'all out of Egypt, out of slavery.

13.text: Respect the Lord and serve Him only—when y'all make promises, let it be in His name.

14.text: Don't chase after other gods—them false gods the people around you worship.

15.text: The Lord your God is jealous—if y'all start acting up, His anger gon' come down hard and wipe y'all off the face of the earth.

16.text: Don't be out here testing the Lord like y'all did back at Massah.

17.text: Stick to the Lord's commands—follow His rules and laws like He told you.

18.text: Do what's right in the Lord's eyes, so things go well for you, and you can take the good land He promised your ancestors.

19.text: The Lord gon' clear out your enemies so y'all can settle in the land—just like He said.

20.text: One day, your kid gon' ask, 'What all these laws, rules, and judgments mean? Why God tell us to follow them?'

21.text: Tell them: 'We used to be slaves in Egypt, but the Lord brought us out with a mighty hand.'

22.text: 'He hit Egypt with signs and wonders, put Pharaoh and his whole house through it—and we saw it all with our own eyes.'

23.text: 'Then He brought us out so He could bring us in—to give us this land He promised our ancestors.'

24.text: 'That's why the Lord told us to keep these commands—so we'd stay blessed, stay safe, and stay alive.'

25.text: 'And if we stay on track, following all His commands, that's what makes us righteous in God's eyes.'

1.text: When the Lord your God brings y'all into this land He's giving you, He gon' clear out a bunch of nations before y'all—Hittites, Girgashites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites—seven nations that's bigger and stronger than y'all.

2.text: And when the Lord your God hands them over to you, y'all gotta take them down completely. Don't make no deals with them, and don't be out here showing mercy.

3.text: Don't marry into their families—don't give your daughters to their sons, and don't take their daughters for your sons.

4.text: 'Cause if you do, they gon' pull your kids away from Me and make them worship other gods. That's gon' set off God's anger, and He gon' wipe y'all out quick.

5.text: This how you handle them—tear down their altars, smash their sacred pillars, cut down their idol poles, and burn up their carved images.

6.text: Y'all are a set-apart people—holy to the Lord your God. He chose y'all to be His own special treasure, outta everybody else on the earth.

7.text: He ain't pick y'all 'cause y'all was the biggest nation—y'all was actually the smallest.

8.text: But He loved y'all, and He kept the promise He made to your ancestors. That's why He brought y'all out of Egypt, with a mighty hand, and set y'all free from Pharaoh.

9.text: So know this—the Lord your God is real. He keeps His word and shows love for a thousand generations to those who love Him and follow His commands.

10.text: But if somebody hates Him, He gon' pay them back to their face and destroy them. He ain't gon' hold back.

11.text: So stick to His commands, His laws, and His rules—do what He said today.

12.text: If y'all listen and obey these commands, the Lord your God gon' keep His covenant with you, just like He promised your ancestors.

13.text: He gon' love you, bless you, and make you multiply. He gon' bless your kids, your crops, your grain, your wine, your oil, your animals—all of it in the land He's giving y'all.

14.text: Y'all gon' be blessed more than any other nation—won't be no barren men or women, and even your animals gon' reproduce.

15.text: The Lord gon' keep y'all healthy—He ain't gon' put none of those terrible diseases from Egypt on you. But He gon' hit your enemies with them instead.

16.text: The Lord gon' hand your enemies over to you, and y'all gotta take them out. Don't feel sorry for them, and don't mess with their gods, 'cause that's just gon' trap you.

17.text: Now, if y'all start thinking, 'Man, these nations way stronger than us—how we supposed to defeat them?'

18.text: Don't be scared. Just remember what the Lord your God did to Pharaoh and all of Egypt.

19.text: Remember the crazy signs and wonders, the plagues, and how God brought y'all out with power. That's exactly what He gon' do to all these nations y'all worried about.

20.text: The Lord gon' send hornets after them until the ones who try to hide get wiped out.

21.text: Don't be shook—the Lord your God is mighty and powerful and He's right there with you.

22.text: The Lord gon' clear them out little by little—He ain't gon' do it all at once, 'cause if He did, the wild animals might overrun the land before y'all settle in.

23.text: But don't worry—He gon' deliver them into your hands and make sure they get completely destroyed.

24.text: He gon' hand their kings over to you, and you gon' wipe out their whole legacy—nobody gon' be able to stand against y'all.

25.text: Burn up their idols and destroy their false gods. And don't try to keep the silver or gold on them, 'cause that's just gon' trap you—it's disgusting to the Lord.

26.text: Don't bring none of that cursed stuff into your house, or you gon' be cursed just like it. Destroy it completely—hate it, reject it, and get rid of it, 'cause it ain't nothing but trouble.

1.text: Every single command I'm giving y'all today? Make sure you follow it, so you can live, grow, and take over the land the Lord promised your ancestors.

2.text: And don't forget—the Lord your God led y'all through the wilderness for 40 years to humble y'all and test what's really in your hearts. He wanted to see if y'all would stay loyal to His commandments or not.

3.text: He made y'all go hungry, then fed y'all manna—something neither y'all nor your ancestors ever seen before. He did that to teach y'all that man don't live by bread alone, but by every word that comes from the Lord.

4.text: Think about it—y'all clothes never wore out, and your feet ain't swell up after 40 years of walking!

5.text: So understand this—just like a father disciplines his son, that's how the Lord your God corrects y'all.

6.text: That's why y'all gotta stay faithful, keep His commandments, walk in His ways, and respect Him.

7.text: The Lord your God is about to take y'all into a good land—a land with streams, fountains, and fresh water flowing from the valleys and hills.

8.text: A land filled with wheat, barley, grapevines, fig trees, pomegranates, olive oil, and honey—

9.text: A land where food ain't ever gon' run out. Y'all ain't gon' be lacking nothing. The land even got iron in the rocks and copper in the hills.

10.text: So when y'all eat good and get full, don't forget to bless the Lord for the good land He gave you.

11.text: Be careful! Don't forget the Lord your God by ignoring His commands, rules, and laws that I'm giving y'all today.

12.text: 'Cause when y'all eat good, build nice houses, and settle down,

13.text: And when your animals, money, and everything else starts multiplying,

14.text: Watch yourself! Don't get prideful and forget the Lord—the One who brought y'all out of Egypt, outta slavery.

15.text: He led y'all through that dangerous desert, full of poisonous snakes, scorpions, and dry land with no water. And He brought water outta a rock just to keep y'all alive.

16.text: He fed y'all manna in the wilderness—something y'all's ancestors ain't ever seen before—to humble and test y'all, so He could bless y'all in the end.

17.text: But don't get it twisted—don't start thinking, 'I did this myself. My strength and hustle got me all this wealth.'

18.text: Nah, remember the Lord your God—He's the one who gives y'all the power to get wealth, to keep His promise to your ancestors, just like He said.

19.text: If y'all forget the Lord and start following other gods, worshiping and serving them, I'm telling y'all right now—y'all gon' be wiped out.

20.text: Just like the nations the Lord destroys before y'all, that's exactly how y'all gon' go down if y'all don't listen to the Lord your God.

1.text: Listen up, Israel! Y'all about to cross the Jordan today and take land from nations bigger and stronger than you—cities with walls that reach the sky.

2.text: The people there? Tall and powerful—the Anakim. Y'all already heard folks say, 'Ain't nobody messing with the Anakim!'

3.text: But understand this—the Lord your God is going ahead of y'all like a consuming fire. He gon' wipe them out, knock them down, and y'all gon' take them out quick, just like He said.

4.text: But don't get cocky after the Lord pushes them out—don't be out here saying, 'It's 'cause I'm so righteous that God gave me this land.' Nah, it ain't about you. It's 'cause them nations wicked.

5.text: It's not 'cause y'all so righteous or pure-hearted. It's 'cause these nations wilding out so bad that the Lord gotta remove them. Plus, He keeping His promise to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

6.text: So get this straight—the Lord ain't giving y'all this land 'cause y'all so holy. Y'all been hard-headed since day one!

7.text: Don't forget how y'all kept making the Lord mad all through the wilderness. Since y'all left Egypt, y'all been rebelling against Him.

8.text: At Horeb, y'all made the Lord so mad He almost wiped y'all out.

9.text: I went up the mountain to get the stone tablets—the covenant the Lord made with y'all. I was up there 40 days and nights, no food, no water.

10.text: Then the Lord gave me two stone tablets written by His own hand—everything He told y'all from the fire on the mountain.

11.text: After 40 days, He gave me the tablets—the very covenant between y'all and Him.

12.text: Then the Lord told me, 'Hurry up! Get down there—your people done messed up big time. They already turned from My ways and made an idol.'

13.text: The Lord also said, 'I've been watching these folks—they hard-headed.'

14.text: 'Moses, step aside and let Me wipe them out. I'ma erase them from history and start over with you, making a nation bigger and better than them.'

15.text: So I went down the mountain, carrying the two stone tablets in my hands, and the mountain was still on fire.

16.text: When I saw what y'all did—y'all made a golden calf, turned from God real quick—

17.text: I threw the tablets down and broke them right in front of y'all.

18.text: Then I fell on my face before the Lord, just like the first time—40 days and nights, no food, no water, begging Him not to destroy y'all for your sins.

19.text: I was scared of how mad the Lord was—He was ready to wipe y'all out. But He listened to me that time too.

20.text: The Lord was even about to take out Aaron—but I prayed for him too.

21.text: Then I burned that golden calf, smashed it, ground it up to dust, and threw the dust in the river.

22.text: And let's not act like that was the only time y'all made God mad. At Taberah, Massah, and Kibroth Hattaavah, y'all did the same thing!

23.text: And at Kadesh Barnea, when the Lord said, 'Go take the land I'm giving you,' y'all refused. Y'all didn't trust Him, didn't listen—straight-up rebelled.

24.text: Since I first met y'all, y'all been rebelling.

25.text: So I fell on my face before the Lord for 40 days and nights, 'cause He said He was about to wipe y'all out.

26.text: I begged Him, 'Lord, don't destroy the people You saved with Your mighty power. They belong to You.'

27.text: 'Remember Your servants—Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. Don't focus on how stubborn and sinful these people are.'

28.text: 'If You destroy them, Egypt gon' say, "God couldn't finish what He started, so He just wiped them out in the wilderness."'

29.text: 'But Lord, they Your people. You brought them out with Your mighty power and Your strong arm.'

1.text: Then the Lord told me, 'Cut out two more stone tablets, just like the first ones, and bring 'em up the mountain. Also, make a wooden chest to hold them.'

2.text: 'I'm gon' write the same words on these new tablets that was on the ones you broke. Then you gon' put them inside the ark.'

3.text: So I made an ark outta acacia wood, cut two stone tablets like the first ones, and climbed back up the mountain with them in my hands.

4.text: And just like before, the Lord wrote the Ten Commandments on them—same words He spoke to y'all from the fire on the mountain that day y'all gathered. Then He gave them to me.

5.text: I came down the mountain, put the tablets inside the ark I made, just like the Lord told me, and they still there.

6.text: (Now, after that, the Israelites moved from Bene Jaakan to Moserah, where Aaron died and was buried. His son Eleazar took over as high priest.)

7.text: (From there, we traveled to Gudgodah, then to Jotbathah, a place with rivers of water.)

8.text: (It was during that time that the Lord set the Levites apart—they the ones who carry the ark of the covenant, serve before the Lord, and bless people in His name, and they still do it today.)

9.text: (That's why the Levites ain't got no land like the other tribes—their inheritance is the Lord Himself, just like He promised.)

10.text: Just like before, I stayed up on the mountain for 40 days and 40 nights. The Lord heard me again and decided not to destroy y'all.

11.text: Then He told me, 'Get up and lead the people forward, so they can take the land I swore to give their ancestors.'

12.text: Aight, Israel, what's the Lord really asking from y'all? Just this—fear Him, walk in His ways, love Him, and serve Him with all your heart and soul.

13.text: Follow His commands and rules, 'cause they ain't just for Him—they for your own good.

14.text: Look, everything belongs to the Lord—heaven, the highest heavens, and the whole earth.
