15.text: But even with all that, He chose y'all's ancestors and set His love on them. And now, He picked y'all, their descendants, to be His own special people.

16.text: So stop being so stubborn—circumcise your hearts! Get rid of that hard-headedness.

17.text: The Lord your God is the realest of all—King of kings, Lord of lords. He's mighty, awesome, and He don't play favorites or take bribes.

18.text: He makes sure orphans and widows get justice. He loves foreigners and makes sure they got food and clothes.

19.text: So y'all gotta love the foreigners too, 'cause y'all was foreigners in Egypt once.

20.text: Fear the Lord, serve Him, stick close to Him, and swear by His name only.

21.text: He's the One you should praise—your God, the One who did all these amazing things y'all saw with your own eyes.

22.text: Your ancestors went down to Egypt as just 70 people, and now look at y'all—the Lord done multiplied y'all like the stars in the sky.

1.text: So love the Lord your God, and keep His rules, laws, and commands—not just sometimes, but always.

2.text: Listen, I ain't talking to y'all's kids—the ones who ain't seen firsthand how the Lord disciplines, how powerful He is, and how He moves with a mighty hand.

3.text: They ain't see the miracles He pulled off in Egypt—how He shut Pharaoh down and flipped Egypt upside down.

4.text: They ain't see how He drowned the Egyptian army—horses, chariots, everything—in the Red Sea when they was chasing y'all. That army? Still gone to this day.

5.text: They ain't live through how God kept y'all in the wilderness till y'all got here.

6.text: Or how He handled Dathan and Abiram—y'all remember? The earth straight up opened its mouth and swallowed them, their families, their tents, and everything they owned right in front of everybody.

7.text: But y'all? Y'all saw all this with your own eyes.

8.text: So keep every command I'm giving y'all today, so y'all can stay strong, take the land, and actually hold on to it.

9.text: Do this, and y'all gon' live long in the land the Lord promised your ancestors—a land flowing with milk and honey.

10.text: This land ain't like Egypt, where y'all had to work the ground, water it by hand, and struggle like it was a backyard garden.

11.text: Nah, this land got hills and valleys—it gets water straight from the heavens.

12.text: God Himself watches over this land from the start of the year to the very end.

13.text: So if y'all truly obey what I'm telling you—love the Lord, serve Him with all your heart and soul—

14.text: He gon' send rain in its season—early rain, late rain—so y'all can grow grain, grapes, and olives.

15.text: He gon' make sure the fields stay full of grass for y'all's animals, and y'all gon' have plenty to eat.

16.text: Watch yourselves! Don't let your hearts get twisted and start chasing other gods and worshiping them.

17.text: If y'all do, the Lord gon' shut the heavens up, no rain gon' fall, the land gon' dry up, and y'all gon' be wiped out quick from this good land He gave you.

18.text: Keep these words locked in your heart and soul. Tie them on your hands, wear them like a badge on your forehead.

19.text: Teach them to your kids—talk about them at home, on the road, when you wake up, and when you go to bed.

20.text: Write them on your doorposts and gates—keep them in front of you at all times.

21.text: Do this, and y'all and y'all's kids gon' live long in the land the Lord promised, as long as the sky is over the earth.

22.text: If y'all faithfully keep all these commands—love the Lord, walk in His ways, stay close to Him—

23.text: Then the Lord gon' drive out every nation in front of you, even the ones that look bigger and badder than y'all.

24.text: Everywhere y'all step? That's yours. From the desert to Lebanon, from the Euphrates River to the Western Sea—it's all y'all's territory.

25.text: Ain't nobody gon' be able to stand against y'all. The Lord gon' make sure everybody fears you wherever y'all step—just like He promised.

26.text: Look, I'm laying out two choices for y'all today—a blessing and a curse.

27.text: The blessing comes if y'all obey the Lord's commands I'm giving you today.

28.text: The curse happens if y'all ignore His commands and start chasing other gods y'all don't even know.

29.text: When the Lord brings y'all into this land, y'all gon' declare the blessing on Mount Gerizim and the curse on Mount Ebal.

30.text: These mountains are on the other side of the Jordan, in Canaan, where the sun sets, near Gilgal by the great oak trees of Moreh.

31.text: Y'all about to cross the Jordan and take the land the Lord is giving y'all. And once y'all got it, y'all gon' settle in it.

32.text: But listen, y'all better follow all the laws and rules I'm setting in front of y'all today.

1.text: These the rules and laws y'all gotta follow once y'all step into the land the Lord, the God of your ancestors, is giving y'all. Stick to them as long as you live.

2.text: Y'all gotta completely destroy all the places where the nations before y'all used to worship their false gods—on the mountains, hills, and under shady trees.

3.text: Tear down their altars, smash their pillars, burn up their wooden idols, cut down their statues, and wipe out their names from history.

4.text: Don't worship the Lord like they worship their gods. That ain't how He want it.

5.text: Instead, look for the place the Lord chooses from among y'all's tribes—the spot where He puts His name. That's where y'all need to go.

6.text: Bring y'all's burnt offerings, sacrifices, tithes, special offerings, freewill gifts, and firstborn livestock there.

7.text: Celebrate in the Lord's presence—you, your family, everybody—because of the blessings He gave y'all.

8.text: Don't do whatever you feel like, like y'all been doing out here in the wilderness.

9.text: 'Cause right now, y'all ain't reached the peace and inheritance the Lord got waiting for y'all.

10.text: But once y'all cross the Jordan, settle in the land the Lord is giving you, and He gives y'all rest from y'all's enemies so y'all can live safely—

11.text: Then He gon' choose a place for His name to dwell, and that's where y'all gotta bring y'all's offerings, tithes, and special gifts.

12.text: And that's where y'all gon' rejoice before the Lord—you, your kids, your servants, and even the Levites, 'cause they ain't got no land like the rest of y'all.

13.text: Don't just offer sacrifices anywhere you see fit.

14.text: Only offer them where the Lord tells you, in the place He chooses from one of y'all's tribes.

15.text: Now, you can eat meat wherever you live, however much you want, as long as the Lord blesses you with it—clean and unclean folks alike can eat it, just like y'all eat gazelle and deer.

16.text: But don't eat the blood—pour it out on the ground like water.

17.text: Don't eat your tithes at home—whether it's grain, wine, oil, or the firstborn of your flock. And don't eat your vowed and freewill offerings there either.

18.text: Eat those in the Lord's presence at the place He chooses—you, your family, your servants, and the Levites. Celebrate the blessings He gave you.

19.text: And don't forget the Levites! Take care of them as long as you in the land.

20.text: When the Lord expands your borders like He promised and you get a craving for some meat, go ahead and eat as much as you want.

21.text: If the place the Lord chose is too far, you can slaughter animals from your own flock at home and eat all you want.

22.text: Same way you eat gazelle and deer, you can eat this—clean or unclean folks alike.

23.text: But don't eat the blood, 'cause the blood is life.

24.text: Pour it out on the ground like water.

25.text: Don't eat it, so things go well for you and your kids when you do what's right in the Lord's eyes.

26.text: But when it comes to the holy offerings and vows, take those to the place the Lord chooses.

27.text: Offer the sacrifices on the Lord's altar, pour the blood on it, and then eat the meat.

28.text: Follow these commands carefully, so things go well for you and your kids forever when you do what's right in the Lord's sight.

29.text: When the Lord drives out the nations before you, and y'all take their land and settle in it—

30.text: Don't get caught up in their ways! Don't start wondering, 'How did these folks worship their gods? Maybe we should do the same?'

31.text: No! Don't worship the Lord like they worship their false gods, 'cause they did disgusting things He hates—they even burned their own kids as sacrifices.

32.text: Stick to what I commanded y'all. Don't add to it, and don't take nothing away.

1.text: If a so-called prophet or dreamer pops up and starts showing signs or wonders—

2.text: And even if what they predict comes true, but then they say, 'Let's go worship other gods that you ain't never known before'—

3.text: Don't listen to them! The Lord your God is just testing you, trying to see if you really love Him with all your heart and soul.

4.text: Stick with the Lord—respect Him, follow His commands, listen to His voice, and serve Him with all you got.

5.text: That so-called prophet or dreamer gotta go. Put them to death, 'cause they tried to lead you away from the Lord, the same God who brought you out of Egypt and freed you from slavery. Get rid of that evil among y'all.

6.text: Even if it's your own brother, your son, daughter, wife, or closest friend, and they secretly try to get you to worship other gods—

7.text: Whether it's gods from nearby nations or far away lands that neither you nor your ancestors ever knew about—

8.text: Don't listen to them! Don't try to protect them, don't cover for them, and don't show them mercy.

9.text: They gotta be put to death, and you gotta be the first one to do it, followed by the rest of the people.

10.text: Stone them until they die, because they tried to pull y'all away from the Lord, the same God who saved you from Egypt.

11.text: This gon' make the rest of Israel take note and think twice before trying that foolishness again.

12.text: If y'all hear rumors that in one of the cities the Lord gave y'all, some folks been saying—

13.text: 'A few shady people started convincing others to go serve other gods that we ain't never known'—

14.text: Y'all better investigate! Check the facts, ask questions, and make sure the story is true.

15.text: If it turns out that they really did pull people into idol worship, then you gotta wipe that city out completely.

16.text: Gather all its stuff into the middle of the street, then burn the whole place down as an offering to the Lord. Leave it in ruins—forever.

17.text: Don't keep nothin' from that city! If y'all handle business, the Lord will turn away His anger, show y'all mercy, and bless y'all even more, just like He promised.

18.text: But you gotta stay obedient, listening to the Lord and keeping all His commands, doing what's right in His eyes.

1.text: Y'all are God's children—so don't be out here cutting yourselves or shaving your heads for the dead like the other nations do.

2.text: The Lord set y'all apart—y'all His chosen people, His special treasure out of everybody on earth.

3.text: Don't eat nothing nasty or detestable.

4.text: Here's what's good to eat: ox, sheep, goat,

5.text: Deer, gazelle, roe deer, wild goat, mountain goat, antelope, and mountain sheep.

6.text: If an animal got split hooves and chews cud, y'all can eat it.

7.text: But some animals chew cud but don't have split hooves—like the camel, rabbit, and rock hyrax—don't eat them! They unclean to y'all.

8.text: Same with pigs—yeah, they got split hooves, but they don't chew cud. Don't eat them, don't even touch their dead bodies.

9.text: In the water, only eat fish with fins and scales.

10.text: Anything that don't got fins and scales? That's nasty, don't eat it.

11.text: All clean birds are good to eat.

12.text: But don't eat these: eagles, vultures, buzzards,

13.text: Kites, falcons, ravens,

14.text: Ostriches, owls, seagulls, hawks,

15.text: More owls, jackdaws, vultures, fisher owls,

16.text: Storks, herons, hoopoes, and bats.

17.text: Any insect that flies and crawls? Nope. Don't eat that either.

18.text: But all the clean birds? Y'all can eat those.

19.text: Don't eat anything that died by itself. You can give it to a foreigner, but y'all set apart for the Lord.

20.text: And don't be out here boiling a baby goat in its mama's milk.

21.text: Don't eat anything that died naturally. You can give it to foreigners or sell it to strangers, but y'all are a holy people to the Lord your God.

22.text: Make sure you tithe—set aside a tenth of your crops every year.

23.text: Take it to the place the Lord chooses—bring your grain, wine, oil, and firstborn animals and eat before Him. This way, y'all always remember to respect the Lord.

24.text: Now, if the place is too far and you can't carry all that—

25.text: Sell it, take the money, and go to the Lord's chosen place.

26.text: Then buy whatever you want—oxen, sheep, wine, strong drink—whatever your heart wants. Eat before the Lord and celebrate with your family.

27.text: And don't forget the Levites, 'cause they ain't got no land like y'all do.

28.text: Every third year, take a tenth of your harvest and store it up in your town.

29.text: The Levites, foreigners, orphans, and widows—anybody who ain't got land—can come and eat till they full. Then the Lord gon' bless all the work you do.

1.text: Every seven years, y'all gotta cancel debts.

2.text: Here's how it works—if you lent somebody something, you gotta let it go. Don't go chasing them down for it, 'cause this is the Lord's release.

3.text: Foreigners? You can still collect from them, but when it comes to your own people, wipe the debt clean.

4.text: If everybody doing right, ain't gon' be no poor folks among y'all anyway, 'cause the Lord gon' bless you big time in the land He's giving you.

5.text: But that's only if y'all actually listen to the Lord and follow His commands carefully.

6.text: If you do, the Lord gon' bless you just like He promised—y'all gon' be lenders, not borrowers. Y'all gon' rule over nations, but ain't nobody gon' rule over you.

7.text: If there's somebody struggling in your community, don't be cold-hearted or stingy with them.

8.text: Open your hand and help them out—give them what they need.

9.text: And don't start thinking, 'Man, the seventh year almost here, I ain't tryna lend them nothing just for the debt to get canceled.' That kind of thinking is wicked. If you let them suffer, they gon' cry out to the Lord, and that's gon' be on you.

10.text: Be generous, and don't be mad about it. When you do, the Lord gon' bless all your work and everything you touch.

11.text: Truth is, there's always gon' be poor folks. That's why I'm telling y'all—always be ready to help your people.

12.text: If one of your own people, a Hebrew man or woman, works as a servant for six years, in the seventh year, they go free.

13.text: And when they leave, don't send them off empty-handed.

14.text: Hook them up with stuff from your flock, your crops, and your wine—give them some of the blessings the Lord gave you.

15.text: Remember, y'all was slaves in Egypt before the Lord freed you. That's why I'm telling y'all to do this.

16.text: But if your servant says, 'I don't wanna leave—I love it here, y'all treat me like family'—

17.text: Then you take an awl (a sharp tool) and pierce their ear at the door, making it official. They gon' stay with you for life. Same goes for female servants.

18.text: And don't trip about letting them go, 'cause they worked for you twice as hard as a hired worker for six years. The Lord gon' bless you for doing right.

19.text: All firstborn male animals from your herd and flock? Set them apart for the Lord. Don't work your firstborn ox, and don't shear your firstborn sheep.

20.text: Take it to the place the Lord chooses, and eat it with your family before the Lord every year.

21.text: But if the animal got a defect—if it's lame, blind, or messed up in any way—don't sacrifice it.

22.text: Instead, y'all can eat it at home—clean or unclean folks alike—just like you would with deer or gazelle.

23.text: But don't eat the blood—pour it out on the ground like water.

1.text: When the month of Abib comes around, keep the Passover for the Lord your God, 'cause that's when He brought y'all out of Egypt at night.

2.text: Sacrifice the Passover from your flock and herd at the place the Lord chooses to put His name.

3.text: Don't eat leavened bread with it. For seven days, eat unleavened bread—the bread of struggle—'cause y'all left Egypt in a hurry. This way, y'all always remember the day the Lord brought y'all out.

4.text: No leaven should be found anywhere in your land for seven days. And don't let any of the Passover meat from the first night stay till morning.

5.text: You can't just sacrifice the Passover anywhere in your land.

6.text: You gotta do it at the place the Lord chooses at twilight, right when the sun is going down—just like when y'all left Egypt.

7.text: Roast the meat and eat it at the Lord's chosen place. Then, in the morning, go back to your tents.

8.text: For six days, eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day, have a sacred assembly to the Lord. No work on that day.

9.text: Start counting seven weeks from the time you start harvesting your crops.

10.text: Then celebrate the Feast of Weeks, bringing a freewill offering according to how much the Lord has blessed you.

11.text: Rejoice before the Lord! You, your kids, your servants, the Levites, foreigners, orphans, and widows—everybody needs to celebrate at the place the Lord chooses.

12.text: And don't forget—y'all used to be slaves in Egypt. So make sure you obey these rules.

13.text: For seven days, celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles after you finish harvesting your crops and making your wine.

14.text: Rejoice! You, your kids, your servants, the Levites, the foreigners, the orphans, and the widows—everybody joins in!

15.text: Keep this sacred feast for seven days at the place the Lord chooses, 'cause He gon' bless your harvest and all the work you do. So go ahead and celebrate hard.

16.text: Three times a year, every man gotta show up before the Lord at the place He chooses—for the Feast of Unleavened Bread, the Feast of Weeks, and the Feast of Tabernacles. And don't show up empty-handed.

17.text: Everybody should bring an offering, giving whatever they can, based on how much the Lord has blessed them.

18.text: Set up judges and officials in every city the Lord gives you, and make sure they judge fairly.

19.text: Don't twist justice—don't play favorites or take bribes, 'cause bribes blind even the wise and mess up fair rulings.

20.text: Stick to real justice, so y'all can live long and hold on to the land the Lord is giving you.

21.text: Don't plant no trees as idols near the Lord's altar.

22.text: And don't set up sacred pillars—the Lord hates those things.

1.text: Don't offer no janky sacrifices—if an animal got a defect or any blemish, don't bring it to the Lord. That's disrespectful to Him.

2.text: If somebody in your community—man or woman—starts wildin' out, breaking the Lord's covenant—

3.text: If they start worshiping other gods, like the sun, the moon, or the stars—things the Lord ain't never told them to follow—

4.text: And word gets out about it, y'all better look into it carefully. If it turns out to be true and that kind of evil really went down in Israel—

5.text: Then that person gotta go. Take them out to the gates and stone them to death.

6.text: Don't execute nobody off one person's word. You need at least two or three witnesses to confirm it.

7.text: The witnesses gotta be the first ones to throw the stones, then everybody else joins in. That way, y'all remove the evil from among you.

8.text: If y'all got a case that's too complicated—whether it's about murder, legal disputes, or punishments—and y'all can't figure it out,

9.text: Then take it to the priests and judges at the place the Lord chooses. Let them make the call.

10.text: Whatever they decide, follow it exactly—don't do your own thing.

11.text: Stick to the judgment they give you. Don't stray left or right—just do what they say.

12.text: If somebody refuses to listen to the priest or the judge, that person gotta die. Y'all gotta get rid of that arrogance in Israel.

13.text: When the people see this, they gon' learn their lesson and stop trying to act above the law.

14.text: When y'all finally settle in the land the Lord is giving you and y'all say, 'We want a king like the other nations,'

15.text: Then make sure it's a king the Lord chooses. He gotta be one of your own—don't put some foreigner in charge over you.

16.text: The king can't be out here stacking up horses, especially not from Egypt, 'cause the Lord already told y'all, "Don't go back there."

17.text: He can't be stacking up wives either, 'cause that'll pull his heart away from the Lord. And he better not be hoarding gold and silver for himself.

18.text: When he becomes king, he needs to write out a copy of this law straight from the priests.

19.text: He gotta keep that law with him and read it every day, so he learns to respect the Lord and follow all His commands.

20.text: This gon' keep him humble—so he don't start thinking he better than his people or start twisting the law to his own benefit. If he follows it, he and his family gon' stay in power for a long time.

1.text: The priests and Levites—the whole tribe of Levi—ain't got no land inheritance like the rest of Israel. They live off the offerings made to the Lord.

2.text: They don't get no land to own, 'cause the Lord Himself is their inheritance, just like He promised.

3.text: This what belongs to the priests from the sacrifices the people bring—whether it's a bull or a sheep—they get the shoulder, the cheeks, and the stomach.

4.text: They also get the firstfruits of y'all's grain, wine, oil, and the first cut of sheep's wool.

5.text: The Lord picked them specifically to serve in His name—them and their descendants—forever.

6.text: If a Levite moves from his hometown and comes to the place the Lord chooses, wanting to serve—

7.text: He can serve just like the other Levites who are already there standing before the Lord.

8.text: He gets an equal share, besides any money he gets from selling his personal property.

9.text: When y'all get into the land the Lord is giving y'all, don't be out here copying the nasty ways of these other nations.

10.text: Don't let nobody be out here sacrificing their kids in fire, practicing witchcraft, sorcery, reading omens, or fortune-telling.

11.text: No spells, no calling on spirits, no mediums, no trying to talk to the dead.

12.text: Anybody who does these things is disgusting to the Lord. That's why He getting rid of these nations before y'all.

13.text: Y'all gotta be different—fully committed to the Lord.

14.text: These other nations out here listening to fortune-tellers and sorcerers—but the Lord ain't set that up for y'all.

15.text: The Lord your God gon' raise up a prophet like me—somebody from among y'all's own people. Y'all need to listen to him.

16.text: This the same thing y'all asked for back at Mount Horeb, when y'all said, 'We can't handle hearing God's voice directly or seeing His fire—we'll die!'

17.text: The Lord said, "They right about that."

18.text: So He gon' raise up a prophet, just like Moses, from y'all's own people. He gon' put His words in that prophet's mouth, and the prophet gon' speak exactly what God commands.

19.text: Anybody who refuses to listen to the words God speaks through that prophet? They gon' answer to God Himself.

20.text: But if some fake prophet comes out here talking like the Lord told him something when He didn't, or if they speak in the name of other gods—that prophet gotta die.

21.text: If y'all wondering, "How do we know if God really spoke through this prophet?"

22.text: It's simple—if what they say don't happen, then God ain't say it. That prophet just running their mouth, and y'all ain't gotta be scared of them.

1.text: When the Lord your God clears out these nations and gives you their land, and y'all settle down in their cities and houses—

2.text: Set aside three cities in the middle of the land the Lord is giving you.

3.text: Build good roads leading to them and divide the land into three sections, so anybody who needs to escape can get there quick.

4.text: Here's how it works—if somebody accidentally kills their neighbor without meaning to, they can run to one of these cities and be safe.

5.text: Like if two folks go out to the woods to chop trees, and one swings an axe but the head flies off and hits the other person, killing them—that wasn't on purpose.

6.text: The person who caused it needs a safe place to run before the victim's family comes after them for revenge. Otherwise, in their anger, they might kill them even though it wasn't murder.

7.text: That's why I'm telling y'all—set up three cities for this.

8.text: If the Lord expands y'all's territory like He promised and gives you more land—

9.text: And if y'all stay obedient to His commands, loving the Lord and walking in His ways—then y'all need to add three more cities to the first three.

10.text: That way, innocent blood won't be shed in the land the Lord is giving you, and y'all won't be guilty of murder.

11.text: But if somebody actually hates their neighbor, sets them up, kills them, and then tries to run to a city of refuge—

12.text: The elders from their hometown need to go get them and hand them over to the victim's family.

13.text: No mercy—y'all gotta get rid of the guilt of murder in Israel so everything stays right.

14.text: Don't go moving your neighbor's property markers that were set by the ancestors. The Lord is giving y'all this land—respect the boundaries.

15.text: One witness ain't enough to convict somebody of a crime. You need at least two or three witnesses to prove it.

16.text: If somebody comes forward lying on someone else, trying to frame them—

17.text: Both of them need to stand before the Lord, in front of the priests and judges.

18.text: The judges gotta investigate carefully, and if they find out the witness was lying—

19.text: Then that liar gets the same punishment they was tryna put on the innocent person. That's how y'all keep evil out of the community.

20.text: Everybody else gon' hear about it and think twice before lying on somebody again.

21.text: No pity. If the crime is serious, the punishment gotta match—life for life, eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.

1.text: When y'all go to war and see the enemy got more soldiers, horses, and chariots than you—don't be scared! The Lord your God is with you, the same one who brought y'all out of Egypt.

2.text: Before the battle starts, the priest gon' come up and talk to the people.

3.text: He gon' say: 'Listen up, Israel! Today y'all facing the enemy. Don't get weak-hearted, don't be scared, don't panic.

4.text: The Lord your God is right there with y'all— He gon' fight for you and give you the victory!'

5.text: Then the officers gon' step up and ask the people, "Anybody just built a new house and ain't had time to dedicate it? Go back home—don't die in battle and let somebody else enjoy your house."

6.text: "Anybody plant a vineyard but ain't got to eat from it yet? Go home—don't die and let another man eat your crops."

7.text: "Anybody engaged to a woman but ain't married her yet? Go home—don't die in battle and let another man take your wife."

8.text: Then they gon' ask, "Anybody scared? If so, go back home so you don't discourage the others."

9.text: After that, they gon' set up captains to lead the army into battle.

10.text: When y'all roll up on a city to fight, first offer them a chance for peace.

11.text: If they accept, don't destroy them. They gon' live under you and serve y'all.

12.text: But if they don't wanna make peace and wanna fight instead—then go ahead and besiege the city.

13.text: When the Lord hands the city over to you, take out all the men with the sword.

14.text: But the women, kids, animals, and everything else in the city? That's y'all's to keep. Take the plunder the Lord is giving you.

15.text: This is what y'all do for cities that ain't part of the land God is giving you—the ones far away.

16.text: But for the cities in the land the Lord is giving you? Don't leave nothing breathing.

17.text: Wipe out the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites—just like the Lord told you.

18.text: If y'all leave them alive, they gon' teach y'all their evil ways, leading y'all into sin against the Lord.

19.text: When y'all at war for a long time, don't go cutting down the city's fruit trees. Those trees give food—they ain't your enemy.

20.text: But if a tree don't give food? You can cut those down to build weapons and siege ramps until the city falls.

1.text: If somebody gets killed and left out in a field, and nobody knows who did it—

2.text: The elders and judges gotta go out and measure the distance from the body to the closest cities.

3.text: Whichever city is closest to the crime scene, its elders gotta take a young cow that's never been worked or used for plowing.

4.text: They gotta take it down to a valley with flowing water—somewhere that ain't been farmed—and break its neck there.

5.text: Then the priests (Levites) come through, 'cause they the ones God picked to handle blessings and settle disputes.

6.text: After that, the elders of the closest city gotta wash their hands over the dead cow's body.

7.text: And they gotta say, "We ain't spill this blood, and we ain't see who did."

8.text: "Lord, forgive us—your people, Israel. We innocent. Don't hold us accountable for this." Then the Lord gon' clear them of guilt.

9.text: That's how y'all keep the land clean from innocent blood—by doing what's right in God's eyes.

10.text: When y'all go to war, and the Lord hands the enemy over to you—

11.text: If you see a beautiful woman among the captives and wanna marry her—

12.text: Bring her home, let her shave her head and trim her nails.

13.text: Give her a full month to grieve for her parents. After that, she becomes your wife.

14.text: But if later you change your mind, you gotta let her go free. Don't sell her or treat her like a slave, 'cause you already humbled her.

15.text: If a man got two wives, and he loves one more than the other, but the unloved wife gives birth to his firstborn—

16.text: When he splits his inheritance, he can't ignore the true firstborn just 'cause his mama ain't his favorite.

17.text: He gotta give the firstborn son his rightful double portion, 'cause that's his first strength. That's just how the rules go.

18.text: If a man got a stubborn, rebellious son who won't listen to his parents, even after they discipline him—

19.text: His parents gotta take him to the city elders at the city gate.

20.text: And they gotta say, "This our son—he's rebellious, don't listen, greedy, and a drunk."

21.text: Then the men of the city gotta stone him to death. That's how y'all get rid of evil and make sure everybody else gets the message.

22.text: If somebody commits a crime that deserves the death penalty, and they get executed and hung on a tree—

23.text: Don't leave their body up overnight. Bury them the same day, so the land don't get cursed. A person hung on a tree is cursed by God.

1.text: If you see your brother's ox or sheep wandering off, don't just ignore it— go get it and bring it back to him.

2.text: If you don't know who it belongs to, take care of it at your house until he comes looking for it. Then give it back.

3.text: Same thing goes for his donkey, his clothes, or anything else he lost. Don't act like you ain't see it.

4.text: If you see your brother's donkey or ox struggling and fallen, don't just walk away—help him lift it back up.

5.text: A woman shouldn't be out here wearing men's clothes, and a man shouldn't be out here dressing like a woman. The Lord ain't rocking with that.

6.text: If you find a bird's nest—whether in a tree or on the ground—with the mama sitting on her eggs or babies, don't take the mama with them.

7.text: Let the mama go and take only the babies. That way, you'll be blessed and live long.

8.text: If you build a house, make sure you put a safety railing around the roof, so you don't bring guilt on yourself if somebody falls off.

9.text: Don't plant different kinds of seeds in your vineyard— it'll mess up your crops and ruin the harvest.

10.text: Don't plow with an ox and a donkey tied together— that ain't right.

11.text: Don't wear clothes made of mixed fabrics— like wool and linen together.

12.text: Make sure your clothes got tassels on the four corners—that's how y'all stay reminded of God's laws.

13.text: If a man marries a woman, but then decides he don't want her anymore, claiming she wasn't a virgin—

14.text: And he spreads rumors about her, bringing shame to her name—

15.text: Then her parents gotta bring proof of her virginity to the city elders at the gate.

16.text: Her father has to say, 'I gave my daughter to this man, and now he tryna ruin her name.'

17.text: Then they show the proof, and the elders gotta punish the man.

18.text: He gotta pay her father 100 shekels of silver for bringing shame on an innocent woman, and he can't ever divorce her.

19.text: They'll fine him a hundred pieces of silver and give it to the girl's father, 'cause he put dirt on a virgin of Israel's name. Plus, she gotta stay his wife—he can't ever divorce her as long as he live.

20.text: But if it turns out he was telling the truth, and she wasn't a virgin—

21.text: Then she gets taken to her father's house, and the men of the city stone her to death—because she played the harlot in her father's house. That's how y'all get rid of evil.

22.text: If a man sleeps with another man's wife, both of them gotta die. Get rid of the evil from Israel.

23.text: If a man sleeps with a virgin who's engaged, and they do it in the city—

24.text: Both of them gotta be stoned. The man 'cause he disrespected another man's wife, and the woman 'cause she ain't cry out for help.

25.text: But if it happens in the countryside, only the man dies—

26.text: The woman ain't done nothing wrong. She was attacked and couldn't call for help.

27.text: It's like when somebody attacks and kills their neighbor—the woman in the field was just minding her business. She screamed, but wasn't nobody around to help her.

28.text: If a man sleeps with a virgin who ain't engaged, and they get caught—

29.text: He gotta pay her father 50 shekels and marry her. He can't ever divorce her.

30.text: A man must not sleep with his father's wife or dishonor his father's bed.

1.text: Anybody who's been castrated or mutilated can't be part of the Lord's assembly.

2.text: A child born outside of marriage can't be in the Lord's assembly—even up to ten generations later.

3.text: No Ammonite or Moabite can join the Lord's assembly—not even ten generations down the line.

4.text: Why? 'Cause when y'all came out of Egypt, they ain't offer y'all food or water. Instead, they hired Balaam, son of Beor, to put a curse on y'all.

5.text: But God flipped the script! He ain't listen to Balaam—instead, He turned the curse into a blessing, 'cause the Lord loves y'all.

6.text: Don't ever seek peace or prosperity from the Ammonites or Moabites. Forever.

7.text: But don't hate the Edomites— they family. And don't hate the Egyptians, 'cause y'all were foreigners in their land once.

8.text: By the third generation, their kids can enter the Lord's assembly.

9.text: When y'all at war, stay clean— don't mess with anything wicked.

10.text: If somebody gets unclean overnight, he gotta go outside the camp and stay out till the evening.

11.text: At sunset, he can wash up and come back in.

12.text: Have a designated bathroom area outside the camp.

13.text: Keep a shovel with you, dig a hole, and cover your waste.

14.text: Why? 'Cause the Lord walks among y'all, fighting for you. Keep the camp holy, so He don't turn away.

15.text: If a slave escapes and comes to you, don't send them back to their master.

16.text: Let them live free wherever they choose— don't oppress them.

17.text: No Israelite woman should be a temple prostitute, and no Israelite man should be out here selling himself either.

18.text: Don't bring prostitute money or dirty earnings into the Lord's house. The Lord don't accept dirty money.

19.text: Don't charge interest on loans to your fellow Israelite— not on money, food, or anything else.

20.text: You can charge interest to foreigners, but not your own people. If you obey, the Lord will bless you in the land He's giving you.

21.text: If you make a vow to the Lord, don't play around—pay it fast. He gon' hold you to it, and if you delay, that's a sin.

22.text: If you don't make a vow, you ain't sinning. But if you say it, you better do it.

23.text: If it comes out your mouth, keep your word— you made that promise voluntarily to the Lord.

24.text: If you walk into your neighbor's vineyard, you can eat some grapes, but don't take none to go.

25.text: If you go through their grain field, you can pluck some heads to eat, but don't use a sickle to start harvesting their crops.

1.text: If a man marries a woman but later decides she ain't what he wants—because he found something in her that ain't right—he can write her a divorce paper, hand it to her, and send her out.

2.text: If she leaves, remarries, and becomes another man's wife,

3.text: And if that second husband also divorces her or dies,

4.text: She can't go back to her first husband. That's nasty in the Lord's eyes, and y'all ain't tryna bring sin on the land He gave you.

5.text: If a man just got married, he ain't gotta go to war or take on major responsibilities for a whole year. He needs to stay home and make his wife happy.

6.text: Don't take a man's millstone (the thing he grinds his grain with) as a loan guarantee. That's like taking his whole livelihood.

7.text: If somebody kidnaps a fellow Israelite, mistreats them, or sells them into slavery, that person gotta die. Y'all gotta get rid of that kind of evil.

8.text: If there's a disease outbreak like leprosy, follow whatever instructions the priests give you. They know what they doing.

9.text: Remember what happened to Miriam when she caught that disease on the way out of Egypt!

10.text: If you lend somebody something, don't barge into their house to get your collateral.

11.text: Wait outside and let them bring it to you.

12.text: If the borrower is struggling, don't keep his pledge overnight.

13.text: Give it back before the sun sets so he can sleep in peace. That's the righteous thing to do in the Lord's eyes.

14.text: Don't cheat or mistreat a poor worker— whether they Israelite or a foreigner living in your land.

15.text: Pay them their wages every day, before the sun goes down. They need that money to survive, and if they cry out to God, He gon' come for you.

16.text: Parents won't be punished for their kids' sins, and kids won't be punished for their parents' sins. Everybody is responsible for their own wrongdoing.

17.text: Don't cheat a foreigner or an orphan, and don't take a widow's last bit of clothing as collateral.

18.text: Remember—y'all used to be slaves in Egypt, and God rescued y'all. That's why He commands y'all to be fair.

19.text: If you forget a bundle of wheat in the field during harvest, don't go back for it. Leave it for the foreigners, orphans, and widows—God gon' bless you for it.

20.text: When you harvest your olive trees, don't go over them a second time. Leave what's left for those in need.

21.text: Same thing with your grapevines—don't pick them clean. Leave some for the poor.

22.text: And don't forget—you used to be slaves in Egypt. That's why God commands you to do this.

1.text: If two men got a dispute and take it to court, the judges gotta decide the case— justifying the innocent and condemning the guilty.

2.text: If the guilty man deserves a beating, the judge will have him lay down and be whipped according to how bad his crime was.

3.text: But don't give him more than 40 lashes, or else he'll be humiliated in front of everybody.

4.text: Don't muzzle an ox while it's working, treading out grain. Let it eat while it works.

5.text: If two brothers live together and one dies without a son, his widow can't marry outside the family. His brother must marry her and take care of her.

6.text: The first son they have will carry the dead brother's name so his legacy don't disappear in Israel.

7.text: But if the brother refuses to marry her, she gotta go to the city elders and say, 'My husband's brother won't keep the family name going.'

8.text: The elders will call him out and talk to him, but if he still refuses—

9.text: The widow will remove his sandal, spit in his face, and say, 'This what happens to a man who won't build up his brother's house.'

10.text: From then on, his family gon' be called, 'The house of the man who got his sandal removed.'

11.text: If two men fighting, and the wife of one jumps in to grab the other man's privates to stop the fight—

12.text: She gotta lose her hand. No mercy on that.

13.text: Don't keep dishonest scales in your bag— one heavy and one light to cheat people.

14.text: Don't keep different measures in your house— one big and one small.

15.text: Use honest and fair weights and measures, so you can live long in the land the Lord is giving you.

16.text: Anybody who cheats like that is disgusting to the Lord.

17.text: Remember what Amalek did when y'all were leaving Egypt.

18.text: They ambushed y'all from behind, attacking the weak and weary— and they ain't respect God.

19.text: So when the Lord gives y'all peace in the land, wipe out Amalek's memory forever. Don't forget this.

1.text: When y'all finally settle in the land the Lord is giving you, take possession and make it home.

2.text: Then gather the first crops from what the land produces, put them in a basket, and take them to the place the Lord chooses for His name to dwell.

3.text: Go to the priest on duty and say, 'I'm here to declare before the Lord that I made it to the land He promised our ancestors.'

4.text: The priest gon' take your basket and place it before the altar of the Lord.

5.text: Then you gotta say before the Lord: 'My ancestor was a wandering Aramean who barely made it. He went to Egypt with just a few folks, but over time, we became a mighty nation.

6.text: But the Egyptians treated us bad— they oppressed us and made us slaves.

7.text: So we cried out to the Lord, and He heard us—He saw our suffering and struggle.

8.text: Then He brought us out with power— using signs, wonders, and a mighty hand.

9.text: Now He brought us to this land, a place flowing with milk and honey.

10.text: So here I am, bringing the firstfruits of the land You gave me.

11.text: Place it before the Lord and worship. Celebrate the blessings He gave you—you, the Levites, and the foreigners among you.

12.text: Every third year—the year of tithing— set aside your tithe and make sure the Levites, foreigners, orphans, and widows get what they need so they can eat and be full.

13.text: Then say before the Lord, 'I have given away the holy tithe as You commanded—to the Levite, the foreigner, the orphan, and the widow. I ain't held back.

14.text: I ain't touched it while mourning, used it improperly, or given any for the dead. I obeyed Your commands, Lord.

15.text: Look down from heaven, Your holy place, and bless Israel and the land You gave us— the land flowing with milk and honey, just like You promised.

16.text: Today, the Lord is commanding y'all to follow His laws and rules. So y'all need to be serious and obey with all your heart and soul.

17.text: Today, y'all declared that the Lord is your God, and that y'all gon' walk in His ways, keep His commands, and obey His voice.

18.text: And today, the Lord declared that y'all are His special people, just like He promised—as long as y'all keep His commandments.

19.text: He gon' set y'all above all nations, giving y'all praise, fame, and honor. Y'all gon' be His holy people, just like He said.

1.text: Moses and the elders told the people: 'Keep all these commandments I'm giving y'all today.'

2.text: When y'all cross the Jordan into the land the Lord is giving you, set up large stones and cover them with lime.

3.text: Write all the words of this law on them once you cross over into the land the Lord promised—a land flowing with milk and honey.

4.text: After crossing the Jordan, put these stones on Mount Ebal and coat them with lime, just like I told y'all.

5.text: Build an altar to the Lord on Mount Ebal using uncut stones. No iron tools should touch them.

6.text: Use whole stones to build the altar and offer burnt sacrifices to the Lord.

7.text: Make peace offerings, eat there, and celebrate before the Lord.

8.text: Write these laws out clearly on the stones.

9.text: Then Moses and the Levite priests spoke to Israel: 'Listen up! Today y'all officially the Lord's people.'

10.text: So obey Him, follow His commands, and keep all His laws I'm giving y'all today.

11.text: That same day, Moses gave the people these instructions:

12.text: When y'all cross over, these tribes gon' stand on Mount Gerizim to bless the people: Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Joseph, and Benjamin.

13.text: And these tribes gon' stand on Mount Ebal to pronounce curses: Reuben, Gad, Asher, Zebulun, Dan, and Naphtali.

14.text: Then the Levites gon' speak loud and clear to all of Israel:

15.text: 'Cursed is the one who makes idols in secret— false gods, hand-crafted, and disgusting to the Lord.' And everybody says, "Amen!"

16.text: 'Cursed is the one who disrespects their mama or daddy.' And everybody says, "Amen!"

17.text: 'Cursed is the one who moves their neighbor's property line.' And everybody says, "Amen!"

18.text: 'Cursed is the one who misleads blind folks, making them lose their way.' And everybody says, "Amen!"

19.text: 'Cursed is the one who twists justice against foreigners, orphans, and widows.' And everybody says, "Amen!"

20.text: 'Cursed is the one who sleeps with his father's wife, disrespecting his father's bed.' And everybody says, "Amen!"

21.text: 'Cursed is the one who has sex with animals.' And everybody says, "Amen!"

22.text: 'Cursed is the one who sleeps with his sister—whether they got the same father or mother.' And everybody says, "Amen!"

23.text: 'Cursed is the one who sleeps with his mother-in-law.' And everybody says, "Amen!"

24.text: 'Cursed is the one who attacks their neighbor in secret.' And everybody says, "Amen!"

25.text: 'Cursed is the one who takes bribes to kill an innocent person.' And everybody says, "Amen!"

26.text: 'Cursed is the one who don't uphold all these laws and live by them.' And everybody says, "Amen!"

1.text: If y'all fully obey the Lord, doing everything He commands, He gon' lift y'all up above all the nations on earth.

2.text: All these blessings gon' come on y'all and overtake y'all, just for listening to the Lord's voice.

3.text: Blessed in the city, blessed in the country.

4.text: Your kids gon' be blessed, your crops gon' be blessed, your livestock gon' multiply.

5.text: Your food supply—your basket and your kneading bowl— gon' be full and blessed.

6.text: Blessed when you come in, blessed when you go out.

7.text: The Lord gon' make your enemies scatter. They might come at you one way, but they gon' run away in seven different directions.

8.text: God gon' bless your storehouses and everything you put your hands on. He gon' bless the land He's giving you.

9.text: He gon' set y'all apart as His holy people, as long as y'all follow His commands and walk in His ways.

10.text: Everybody gon' see that y'all belong to the Lord, and they gon' be scared of y'all.

11.text: The Lord gon' overflow your blessings— your kids, your animals, and your land gon' produce plenty.

12.text: He gon' open up the heavens for y'all, sending rain at the right time and blessing everything you do. Y'all gon' lend to nations but never borrow.

13.text: God gon' make you the head, not the tail. You gon' be on top, not underneath—but only if you listen and obey.

14.text: Don't stray to the left or right. Don't go chasing after other gods—stay on the path He gave you.

15.text: But if y'all ignore the Lord's voice and refuse to follow His commands, these curses gon' come on y'all and overtake you.

16.text: Cursed in the city, cursed in the country.

17.text: Cursed food supply—your basket and your kneading bowl gon' be empty.

18.text: Cursed kids, cursed land, cursed livestock—everything gon' struggle.

19.text: Cursed when you come in, cursed when you go out.

20.text: The Lord gon' send confusion and destruction in everything you do, 'til you completely fail, all because you turned away from Him.

21.text: Disease gon' stick to you 'til it wipes you out. You ain't even gon' make it to the land you tryna possess.

22.text: He gon' hit you with fevers, inflammation, drought, scorching heat, and mildew— these things ain't gon' stop 'til you done.

23.text: The sky gon' be like bronze over your head, and the ground gon' be like iron. No rain, no harvest.

24.text: Instead of rain, dust and ashes gon' fall from the sky 'til you completely destroyed.

25.text: Your enemies gon' tear you up. You'll run at them one way, but end up fleeing in seven different directions. All the nations gon' look at you like a joke.

26.text: Your dead bodies gon' be food for birds and wild animals— and ain't nobody gon' be there to chase them off.

27.text: God gon' hit you with boils like He did in Egypt— sores, rashes, infections that can't be healed.

28.text: He gon' strike you with madness, blindness, and total confusion.

29.text: In the middle of the day, you gon' be stumbling around like it's midnight. Nothing you try gon' work out, and people gon' rob and oppress you nonstop, with nobody to help.

30.text: You gon' get engaged to a woman, but another man gon' sleep with her. You'll build a house, but never live in it. You'll plant a vineyard, but won't get to enjoy the grapes.

31.text: Your ox gon' be taken and slaughtered right in front of you, but you won't get to eat none of it. Your donkey gon' be snatched away and never returned. Your sheep gon' be handed over to your enemies, and ain't nobody gon' save them.

32.text: Your sons and daughters gon' be taken by another nation, and you gon' be helpless, watching them go. Your eyes gon' fail from crying all day, but you won't have the strength to stop it.

33.text: A nation you don't even know gon' eat all your crops and take everything you worked for. You gon' be oppressed and crushed nonstop.

34.text: It's gon' drive you crazy seeing all this happen.

35.text: The Lord gon' hit you with painful boils, from your feet to your head, and ain't no healing from it.

36.text: He gon' take you and your king and send y'all to a land you never knew. There, y'all gon' be forced to worship false gods—wood and stone.

37.text: People gon' look at y'all like a joke, a proverb, a lesson—everywhere the Lord scatters you.

38.text: You gon' plant plenty of seeds, but barely harvest anything— 'cause locusts gon' eat up your crops.

39.text: You gon' plant vineyards and take care of them, but you ain't drinking no wine— 'cause worms gon' eat the grapes.

40.text: You'll have olive trees everywhere, but you ain't using that oil— 'cause the olives gon' fall off before they ripen.

41.text: You'll have sons and daughters, but they ain't staying with you— 'cause they gon' be taken into captivity.

42.text: Locusts gon' eat up every tree and crop in your land.

43.text: The foreigners living among y'all gon' keep rising higher and higher, while you keep falling lower and lower.

44.text: They gon' be lending to you, but you won't lend to them. They gon' be the head, and you gon' be the tail.

45.text: Every one of these curses gon' come after you, chase you down, and overtake you 'til you destroyed— all because you ain't listen to the Lord or follow His commands.

46.text: These curses gon' be a sign and a warning for you and your descendants forever.

47.text: Since you ain't serve the Lord with joy when He blessed you with everything—

48.text: Now you gon' serve your enemies, in hunger, thirst, and poverty. They gon' put a yoke of iron on your neck 'til you completely destroyed.

49.text: The Lord gon' bring a nation against you from far away— flying in fast like an eagle. They gon' speak a language you don't understand.

50.text: They ain't gon' care about your elders, and they ain't gon' have mercy on your children.

51.text: They gon' take everything—your livestock, your crops— 'til you got nothing left. They gon' wipe you out.

52.text: They gon' trap you inside your own cities, tearing down all the walls you thought would protect you. They gon' besiege you everywhere in the land the Lord gave you.

53.text: You gon' be so desperate, you'll eat your own children— the sons and daughters the Lord gave you. That's how bad the siege gon' be.

54.text: The softest, most refined man among you gon' turn cold, even toward his own family.

55.text: He won't share food with his own wife and kids, 'cause he barely got enough for himself.

56.text: Even the most delicate woman, who wouldn't even step on the ground barefoot, gon' turn against her own husband, son, and daughter.

57.text: She gon' secretly eat her own newborns and the afterbirth, just to survive. That's how bad the siege gon' get.

58.text: If y'all don't take this law seriously, if y'all don't respect the Lord's great and powerful name—

59.text: The Lord gon' hit y'all and your descendants with plagues— terrible, long-lasting diseases.

60.text: He gon' bring back all the sicknesses of Egypt, the ones y'all feared the most, and they gon' stick to you.

61.text: Every sickness and plague— even the ones not written in this Book of the Law— the Lord gon' hit you with them 'til you completely destroyed.

62.text: Y'all used to be as numerous as the stars in the sky, but now? Y'all gon' be reduced to just a few. All 'cause y'all ain't listen to the Lord.

63.text: Just like He used to take joy in blessing y'all and making y'all multiply, now He gon' take joy in wiping y'all out. He gon' pluck y'all right off the land He gave you.

64.text: The Lord gon' scatter y'all all over the earth— from one end to the other. Wherever you go, you gon' be forced to serve other gods, gods of wood and stone that neither you nor your ancestors ever knew.

65.text: Ain't gon' be no peace for you anywhere. No rest, no stability. The Lord gon' fill your heart with fear, your eyes with sorrow, and your soul with deep anxiety.

66.text: You gon' be living on edge, never knowing if you gon' survive the next day. Fear gon' haunt you day and night.

67.text: Every morning, you gon' wish it was nighttime. Every night, you gon' wish it was morning. That's how scared and broken y'all gon' be.

68.text: The Lord gon' send y'all back to Egypt in ships— even though He said y'all would never go back that way. And there, y'all gon' be put up for sale as slaves to your enemies— but ain't nobody even gon' want to buy you.

1.text: These are the words of the covenant the Lord told Moses to make with Israel in Moab— this is on top of the one He made at Mount Horeb.

2.text: Moses gathered everybody and said: 'Y'all saw with your own eyes everything the Lord did in Egypt—how He took down Pharaoh, his officials, and his whole land.

3.text: Y'all saw the great trials, the signs, and the wonders.

4.text: But even now, the Lord ain't given y'all the understanding, eyes to see, or ears to hear what it all really means.

5.text: I led y'all in this wilderness for 40 years— and guess what? Your clothes ain't wear out, and neither did your sandals.

6.text: Y'all ain't had bread to eat or wine to drink, so y'all would know that I am the Lord your God.

7.text: When y'all got here, Sihon (king of Heshbon) and Og (king of Bashan) came to fight— but we beat them.

8.text: We took their land and gave it to Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh's tribe.

9.text: So keep this covenant and obey it, so y'all can prosper in everything y'all do.

10.text: Today, all of y'all stand before the Lord— your leaders, elders, officers, all the men of Israel,

11.text: Your kids, your wives, and even the foreigners among y'all— from the ones chopping wood to the ones fetching water.

12.text: This is so y'all can enter into this covenant with the Lord today, the agreement He's making with y'all.

13.text: He's making y'all His people today, just like He promised your ancestors—Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

14.text: This covenant ain't just for y'all standing here today—

15.text: It's for future generations too, the ones who ain't even here yet.

16.text: Y'all remember living in Egypt, and how we passed through other nations on the way here.

17.text: Y'all saw their nasty idols— statues made of wood, stone, silver, and gold.

18.text: So don't let anybody among y'all—man, woman, family, or tribe— turn away from the Lord today to follow these false gods.

19.text: Don't let nobody hear these warnings and think, 'I'll be fine, I'm gon' do what I want.' That's like a drunk fool thinking he safe like a sober man.

20.text: The Lord ain't gon' let that slide. His anger gon' burn against that person, and every curse in this book gon' fall on them.

21.text: The Lord gon' separate them from the whole nation and hit them with all the curses written in this Book of the Law.

22.text: In the future, when your kids and foreigners come through and see the disaster and sickness in this land—

23.text: When they see the land burned up with sulfur and salt, with nothing growing— just like what happened to Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim when the Lord destroyed them—

24.text: They gon' ask, 'Why did the Lord do all this? Why is He so angry?'

25.text: And people gon' answer, 'Cause they broke the Lord's covenant, the one He made with them when He freed them from Egypt.

26.text: Instead of worshiping Him, they chased after false gods— ones they ain't never known, ones the Lord never gave them.

27.text: So the Lord's anger burned against the land, bringing down every curse written in this book.

28.text: He uprooted them from their land in His anger and threw them into another country— and that's where they at now.

29.text: The secret things belong to the Lord, but what He reveals? That's for us and our children forever, so we can follow His law.

1.text: One day, when all these blessings and curses I told y'all about come true, and y'all remember them while living in whatever nation the Lord sent you to—

2.text: If y'all turn back to the Lord, listen to His voice, and follow His commands— you and your kids, with all your heart and soul—

3.text: Then the Lord gon' bring y'all back from captivity. He gon' have mercy on y'all and gather y'all from every nation where He scattered you.

4.text: Even if some of y'all are at the farthest corner of the earth, the Lord gon' bring y'all back.

5.text: He gon' bring y'all back to the land He promised your ancestors, and you gon' take possession of it. He gon' bless you even more than your fathers.

6.text: The Lord gon' change your heart and the hearts of your descendants, so y'all can love Him with all your heart and soul, and truly live.

7.text: And all those curses? The Lord gon' put them on your enemies instead—on the ones who hated and oppressed you.

8.text: Then y'all gon' obey the Lord again, following all His commands like He told you to.

9.text: The Lord gon' bless everything you do— your kids, your livestock, your crops. He gon' take joy in blessing you, just like He did your ancestors.

10.text: But that's only if y'all listen to His voice, keep His commandments, and turn back to Him with all your heart and soul.

11.text: This command I'm giving you ain't hard to understand. It ain't some deep mystery.

12.text: It ain't up in heaven, so you don't gotta ask, 'Who gon' go up there and bring it down so we can hear it and do it?'

13.text: It ain't across the ocean either, so you don't gotta ask, 'Who gon' go get it and bring it back so we can hear and do it?'

14.text: Nah, the word is right here— in your mouth and in your heart—so you can live by it.

15.text: Today, I'm laying it out for y'all— life and good, or death and evil. The choice is yours.

16.text: If you love the Lord, walk in His ways, and keep His commands, then y'all gon' live, multiply, and be blessed in the land you about to take over.

17.text: But if you turn away, refuse to listen, and start worshiping other gods—

18.text: I'm telling you right now—you gon' be destroyed. You ain't gon' last long in the land across the Jordan.

19.text: I'm calling heaven and earth as witnesses today: I put life and death, blessings and curses in front of y'all. So choose life, so you and your kids can live!

20.text: Love the Lord, listen to His voice, and stay close to Him. He is your life and the key to your future. That's how y'all gon' live long in the land He promised to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

1.text: Moses went and spoke these words to all Israel:

2.text: 'I'm 120 years old today. I can't move like I used to, and the Lord already told me, "You ain't crossing this Jordan."

3.text: But the Lord gon' go before y'all. He gon' wipe out these nations, and y'all gon' take their land. Joshua gon' lead y'all across, just like the Lord said.

4.text: The Lord gon' do to these nations just like He did to Sihon and Og, the Amorite kings—He destroyed them completely.

5.text: He gon' hand them over to y'all, and y'all gotta handle them just like I commanded.

6.text: Be strong and courageous. Don't be scared of them. The Lord your God is with you—He ain't never gon' leave you or forsake you.

7.text: Then Moses called Joshua in front of everybody and told him, 'Be strong and courageous! You gotta lead these people into the land the Lord promised their ancestors.

8.text: The Lord Himself is going ahead of you. He gon' be with you—He won't abandon you. Don't be scared or discouraged!

9.text: Moses wrote down the law and gave it to the priests, the Levites who carried the Ark of the Covenant, and to the elders of Israel.

10.text: He commanded them, 'Every seven years, during the Year of Release, at the Feast of Tabernacles—

11.text: When all of Israel gathers before the Lord, y'all gotta read this law out loud to everybody.

12.text: Gather the men, women, kids, and even the foreigners living among y'all, so they can hear, learn, and respect the Lord's commands.

13.text: Even the next generation—who ain't heard this before—needs to learn to fear the Lord while y'all live in the land y'all about to take over.'

14.text: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Your time is almost up. Call Joshua, and both of y'all come to the Tabernacle so I can officially appoint him.'

15.text: The Lord showed up at the Tabernacle in a pillar of cloud, standing above the entrance.

16.text: Then the Lord told Moses, 'You about to die, and after you gone, these people gon' turn their backs on Me. They gon' start worshiping other gods in the new land, breaking My covenant.'

17.text: That's gon' make Me angry. I'm gon' turn My back on them and let them get destroyed. They gon' suffer so bad, they gon' say, "Is this happening 'cause God ain't with us no more?"

18.text: But I ain't gon' listen to them, 'cause they gon' be deep in sin, chasing after other gods.

19.text: So write down this song and teach it to Israel. Let it be a witness against them.

20.text: When I bless them with the land of milk and honey, and they get comfortable, they gon' forget Me and start worshiping false gods.

21.text: When disasters hit them, this song gon' be a reminder. Their descendants ain't gon' forget it, 'cause I already know how they act—even before they step foot in the land.

22.text: So Moses wrote the song that same day and taught it to Israel.

23.text: Then the Lord gave Joshua his orders: 'Be strong and courageous! You gon' lead Israel into the land I promised, and I'm gon' be with you.'

24.text: When Moses finished writing all the words of this law,

25.text: He told the Levites who carried the Ark of the Covenant—

26.text: 'Take this Book of the Law and put it beside the Ark. Let it be a witness against y'all.

27.text: I already know how rebellious y'all are. If y'all act this way while I'm still alive, what y'all gon' do after I'm gone?

28.text: Gather all the elders and officials. I got some final words to say, and I'm calling heaven and earth as my witnesses.

29.text: I already know what's gon' happen after I die. Y'all gon' turn away from the Lord and do evil, making Him angry. Y'all gon' bring disaster on yourselves in the future.

30.text: Then Moses stood before all of Israel and spoke the words of the song from beginning to end.

1.text: Listen up, heavens, 'cause I'm 'bout to speak! Earth, pay attention to my words!

2.text: Let my teachings fall like rain, my words settle like morning dew—like showers watering the grass.

3.text: I'm lifting up the Lord's name— give Him the honor He deserves!

4.text: He's the Rock—His work is flawless! Everything He does is just, He's a God of truth, no corruption in Him.

5.text: But these people done messed themselves up. They ain't acting like His children—they a twisted, messed-up generation.

6.text: How y'all gon' treat the Lord like this? Acting foolish and ungrateful! Ain't He your Father, the One who bought you? He made you and set you up!

7.text: Think back to the old days, remember what happened generations ago. Ask your elders, they'll tell you what's up.

8.text: When the Most High divided the land among the nations, when He spread out the sons of Adam, He set up the boundaries based on His chosen people, Israel.

9.text: But Israel? That's God's special portion. Jacob is His own inheritance.

10.text: He found them in a dry, wild place— a desert full of chaos. He surrounded them, taught them, kept them safe like they were His most prized possession.

11.text: Like an eagle watching over its babies, hovering, carrying them on its wings—

12.text: That's how the Lord led Israel— no false gods, just Him.

13.text: He lifted them up to high places, blessed them with the best food—honey from rocks, oil from stone.

14.text: Milk from cattle, the finest meats, the best wheat, and the richest wine.

15.text: But Jeshurun (Israel) got too comfortable. They got fat, thick, and lazy—then turned their back on God. They forgot who made them!

16.text: They made God jealous by worshiping false gods, doing disgusting things that made Him angry.

17.text: They started sacrificing to demons, not the true God— to gods they never knew, new gods their ancestors never heard of.

18.text: They forgot about the Rock who made them. They ignored the God who gave them life.

19.text: When the Lord saw this, He had enough. He rejected them, 'cause they made Him angry.

20.text: He said, 'I'm gon' turn My back on them. Let's see how they end up. They a messed-up generation—ain't got no loyalty.

21.text: They made Me jealous with fake gods, so I'ma make them jealous with a people who ain't even a real nation. They made Me angry, so I'ma use a foolish people to make them mad.

22.text: My anger burns like a fire, reaching all the way to hell. It's gon' consume the earth and burn the mountains to their foundations.

23.text: I'ma send disaster after disaster on them. I got arrows, and I'ma use 'em all.

24.text: They gon' waste away from hunger, be eaten up by disease, and torn apart by wild animals and deadly snakes.

25.text: The sword gon' strike 'em down outside, and inside they gon' be full of terror—young and old, babies and the elderly, nobody spared.

26.text: I could've said, 'I'ma wipe them out completely, erase them from history.'

27.text: But I held back, 'cause I ain't tryna let their enemies get cocky. I ain't want them thinking, 'We did this ourselves, not the Lord.'

28.text: Israel acting like they ain't got no sense, no wisdom at all.

29.text: If only they were wise enough to understand what's coming, to think about how this all gon' end.

30.text: Ain't no way one enemy chases a thousand of y'all, and two run off ten thousand—unless the Lord let it happen.

31.text: Their gods ain't nothing like our God. Even our enemies can see that!

32.text: They ain't nothing but the vine of Sodom, growing from the fields of Gomorrah. Their grapes are poison, their fruit is bitter.

33.text: Their wine is snake venom, straight-up deadly.

34.text: Y'all don't think I see all this? I got it stored up, waiting for the right time.

35.text: Vengeance is Mine! Payback coming, and when they slip, it's gon' be bad. Their disaster coming quick!

36.text: The Lord gon' judge His people, but He gon' have compassion when He sees they completely powerless, no one left to fight.

37.text: Then He gon' ask, 'Where them fake gods at now? The ones y'all was trusting in?

38.text: Where the gods that took y'all's offerings? The ones y'all poured drink offerings for? Tell them to help y'all now!

39.text: But now y'all see—I'm the only God. Ain't no one else but Me. I got the power to kill and bring life, to wound and heal. Ain't nobody who can escape My hands.

40.text: I lift My hand to heaven and swear— I live forever!

41.text: When I sharpen My sword for judgment, I'ma pay back every enemy that hated Me.

42.text: My arrows gon' be drunk off blood, and My sword gon' devour flesh—even from the enemy leaders.

43.text: Rejoice, nations! 'Cause the Lord gon' take revenge for His people. He gon' punish His enemies and restore His land and His people.

44.text: Moses and Joshua son of Nun stood before the people and spoke every word of this song.

45.text: When Moses finished,

46.text: He told them, 'Take these words seriously. Teach them to your children. Make sure they live by them.

47.text: This ain't just some empty words— this is y'all's life! Obey them, and y'all gon' live long in the land y'all 'bout to take over.

48.text: That same day, the Lord spoke to Moses.

49.text: He said, 'Go up Mount Nebo, in the land of Moab, across from Jericho. Look at the land of Canaan—I'm giving it to Israel.

50.text: Then you gon' die up there and join your ancestors, just like Aaron died on Mount Hor.

51.text: This is 'cause you disrespected Me at Meribah Kadesh, in the Wilderness of Zin. You ain't honor Me in front of the people.

52.text: You gon' see the land, but you ain't stepping foot in it. That's the land I'm giving to Israel.

1.text: This is the blessing Moses, the man of God, gave Israel before he passed.

2.text: He said, 'The Lord showed up at Sinai, shined His light from Seir, came strong from Mount Paran, rolling deep with ten thousand angels. His right hand held a fiery law for His people.

3.text: He loves His people! All His followers in His hands, sitting at His feet, learning from Him.

4.text: Moses gave us God's law, our inheritance as the people of Jacob.

5.text: He was King over Israel (Jeshurun) when all the leaders and tribes gathered together.

6.text: Reuben, may your tribe survive, and don't let your numbers get too low.

7.text: For Judah: 'Lord, hear Judah's voice! Bring him back to his people. Let him have strength in his hands, and help him against his enemies.'

8.text: For Levi: 'Lord, let the Urim and Thummim stay with Your holy one—the one You tested at Massah and Meribah.

9.text: Levi stood firm, even against family— they put God first, kept His word, and stayed true to the covenant.

10.text: They gon' teach Jacob and Israel Your laws. They'll burn incense before You and bring offerings to Your altar.

11.text: Lord, bless Levi's work, accept what he does for You. Strike down anyone who rises against him!

12.text: For Benjamin: 'The one the Lord loves gon' live safe with Him. The Lord gon' shelter him all day long, carrying him on His shoulders.'

13.text: For Joseph: 'His land gon' be blessed by the Lord— heaven's dew, deep underground waters.

14.text: The best crops from the sun, and the best harvest every season.

15.text: The richest land from ancient mountains, the finest treasures from everlasting hills.

16.text: Everything good from the earth, along with God's favor. Let this blessing fall on Joseph, the one set apart from his brothers.

17.text: He's strong like a firstborn bull, with horns like a wild ox. With them, he gon' push nations all the way to the ends of the earth. That's Ephraim's ten thousands and Manasseh's thousands.'

18.text: For Zebulun and Issachar: 'Zebulun, be joyful when you go out! Issachar, be blessed in your tents!'

19.text: They gon' call nations to worship, offering righteous sacrifices. They'll enjoy the riches of the seas and treasures buried in the sand.

20.text: For Gad: 'Bless the one who expands Gad's land! He's fierce like a lion, ripping through arms and skulls.

21.text: Gad claimed his territory early, got land reserved for leaders. He led the people and carried out God's justice.

22.text: For Dan: 'Dan is like a young lion, leaping from Bashan to strike.'

23.text: For Naphtali: 'Naphtali is full of God's favor, overflowing with blessings! Take possession of the west and the south.'

24.text: For Asher: 'Asher is blessed above all his brothers. His people love him, and he walks in oil (wealth and prosperity).

25.text: His feet gon' be as strong as iron and bronze. His strength gon' last as long as his days.

26.text: Ain't nobody like the God of Israel! He rides through the heavens to help you, soaring on the clouds in glory.

27.text: The eternal God is your safe place. His everlasting arms hold you up. He gon' push out your enemies and tell you to destroy them.

28.text: Israel gon' live in safety, with Jacob's descendants flourishing in a land of grain and wine. The skies gon' drop dew on them.

29.text: You blessed, Israel! Ain't nobody like you— saved by the Lord, protected by His shield, victorious by His sword. Your enemies gon' bow before you, and you gon' stomp on their strongholds.

1.text: Moses climbed up from the plains of Moab to Mount Nebo, all the way to the top of Pisgah, across from Jericho. The Lord showed him the whole land—Gilead all the way to Dan,

2.text: Naphtali, Ephraim, Manasseh, and all of Judah, reaching the Western Sea.

3.text: He showed him the South, the plains, the Valley of Jericho (the city of palm trees), and all the way to Zoar.

4.text: Then the Lord told him, 'This the land I promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob, saying I'd give it to their descendants. I'm letting you see it with your own eyes, but you ain't crossing over.

5.text: So Moses, the Lord's servant, died right there in Moab, just like the Lord said.

6.text: The Lord Himself buried Moses in a valley in Moab, across from Beth Peor, but nobody knows exactly where his grave is to this day.

7.text: Moses was 120 years old when he died, but his eyesight was still sharp, and he still had his strength.

8.text: The Israelites mourned for Moses for 30 days in the plains of Moab. Then the time of grieving was over.

9.text: Joshua, son of Nun, was full of wisdom, 'cause Moses had laid hands on him. So the Israelites listened to him and did what the Lord commanded through Moses.

10.text: Ain't never been another prophet in Israel like Moses— the one the Lord spoke to face to face.

11.text: He did signs and wonders in Egypt, in front of Pharaoh, his officials, and all his people.

12.text: With God's mighty power, Moses did things that shook the world— miracles that left Israel in awe.

1.text: These the words of the Preacher. Son of David. King in Jerusalem.

2.text: "Vanity of vanities," he said. "Ain't nothin' but smoke. All of it—just smoke."

3.text: What's the real gain from all this grindin'? All this sweat under the sun?

4.text: Generations come and go. Folks die. Babies get born. But the earth? She just keep spinnin'.

5.text: The sun rises, then drops. Then hurries right back to do the same thing again.

6.text: The wind do laps—south, then north, then around again. Spinnin' on repeat.

7.text: All the rivers pour into the sea, But the sea never fills up. The water goes back, starts over, and does it again.

8.text: Everything is exhaustin'. We don't even got words for it all. The eye ain't never satisfied with what it sees. The ear always tryna hear somethin' new.

9.text: What's been done? Gon' be done again. Ain't nothin' new under the sun.

10.text: You might think, "This brand new right here!" But nah—it already happened before, long before us.

11.text: And we don't even remember what went down back then. And the folks who come after us? They won't remember us either.

12.text: I was king in Jerusalem—yeah, me.

13.text: I made it my mission to learn it all. To figure out this whole life thing. But truth is? God gave humans a burden— We out here chasin' answers, but it's heavy.

14.text: I seen all kinds of work go down under the sun. And honestly? It's all chasin' the wind. Pointless.

15.text: What's bent can't be straightened. And what's missin'? You can't even count it.

16.text: I told myself, "Look how much I've accomplished. Look how wise I've become— Wiser than anybody before me in this city." I studied it all. Knowledge. Deep thoughts.

17.text: Then I said, "Let me get into madness too. Foolishness. Wild stuff." Guess what? Same thing. Wind chasing.

18.text: The more you know, the more it hurts. Knowledge bring grief. Wisdom don't always heal—it cuts.

1.text: I told myself, "Let's try joy. Let's chase pleasure. Let's see what that do." But honestly? That was pointless too.

2.text: I laughed at laughter. I looked at pleasure and said, "What it really doing for me though?"

3.text: So I tested myself with wine. I still kept some wisdom, but I wanted to see what life felt like livin' loose. Tried to figure out what actually makes life worth it while I'm down here.

4.text: I built houses. I planted vineyards for myself.

5.text: I made gardens, orchards—had fruit trees everywhere.

6.text: I built my own irrigation systems. Pools to water all those trees I planted.

7.text: I got servants. Male and female. Even had kids born into my house.

8.text: I stacked silver, gold, and treasure from everywhere. Got choirs. Got bands. All the entertainment I could dream of.

9.text: I leveled up—higher than anybody before me in Jerusalem. And I still kept my wisdom.

10.text: Anything my eyes wanted? I took it. I never told my heart "no." I enjoyed the grind. That was my reward—just the work itself.

11.text: But when I stood back and looked at everything I built with my hands? It still felt like tryna catch the wind. Nothing really hit. No real profit under the sun.

12.text: So I started thinkin': "What's the point of being wise? Or being reckless?" Even the next king ain't gon' do nothin' new.

13.text: Yeah, wisdom better than foolishness—like light better than darkness.

14.text: A wise man sees ahead. A fool stumbles blind. But guess what? They both still die.

15.text: So I told myself, "If I'ma die just like a fool, what all this wisdom for?" This too? Pointless.

16.text: 'Cause nobody gon' remember either of us. Wise or fool—we all get forgotten eventually. Death don't care how smart you was.

17.text: I started hatin' life. All this work under the sun was heavy. It all felt like chasing air.
