18.text: And I hated everything I worked for. Why? 'Cause I gotta leave it to the one who comes after me.

19.text: And who knows if he gon' be smart… or a fool? Either way, he gettin' everything I built. That's wild. That's vanity too.

20.text: I gave up. I felt hopeless about all the years I poured into this grind.

21.text: You could work smart, work hard, work wise… and still leave everything to somebody who ain't put in a second. That's not just pointless—that's foul.

22.text: What do we even get from all this labor? All this late-night stress?

23.text: 'Cause even after work, your heart don't rest. All your days heavy. That too? Pointless.

24.text: You know what's best? Eat. Drink. Enjoy the good that comes from your grind. That joy? That's a gift from God.

25.text: Who can enjoy anything more than me? (And I still couldn't without Him.)

26.text: God gives wisdom, knowledge, and joy to the one who walks right with Him. But the sinner? He just out here workin'… stackin'… just to hand it off to somebody who actually pleases God. That too? Smoke. Wind. Dust in the hands.

1.text: Everything got its time. There's a season for every single thing under heaven.

2.text: A time to be born, and a time to die. A time to plant, and a time to pull it up.

3.text: A time to take down, and a time to build back. A time to kill, and a time to heal.

4.text: A time to cry, and a time to laugh. A time to mourn, and a time to hit your two-step.

5.text: A time to throw things out, And a time to pick stuff up. A time to hug, And a time to keep your distance.

6.text: A time to chase after somethin', And a time to let it go. A time to hold on, And a time to toss it out.

7.text: A time to rip things apart, And a time to stitch it back up. A time to hush, And a time to speak your truth.

8.text: A time to love, and a time to hate. A time for war, and a time for peace.

9.text: So what we really gain from all this grind?

10.text: I've seen the weight God gave us—the work we carry under the sun.

11.text: But hear this: He made everything beautiful… in its own time. And He planted eternity in our hearts. But still—we can't fully grasp what He doin' from start to finish.

12.text: I know this much: Ain't nothin' better than to live with joy, And do right while you got breath.

13.text: Eat good. Drink good. Enjoy what your labor brings. That right there? That's God's gift to you.

14.text: Whatever God does? It lasts. Ain't nothin' you can add to it. Ain't nothin' you can take away. He do it so folks will respect Him.

15.text: What's happenin' now? Been happened before. What's comin'? Already came. God gon' pull receipts from the past too.

16.text: I looked at the courtrooms—supposed to be just. But wickedness was sittin' in the judgment seat. Same thing in the church—iniquity where righteousness should be.

17.text: But I told myself: God got His time. He gon' judge everybody—the good and the wicked. Time for all things. Time for all works.

18.text: And I realized, God lets us see ourselves real raw— Like we ain't all that different from animals.

19.text: 'Cause what happens to us? Happens to them too. We all breathe. We all die. Ain't no special advantage. All of it? Still vanity.

20.text: We all made from dust. And guess what? We all goin' back to it.

21.text: Who really knows what happens to the spirit of a man after he dies? Does it rise? And what about animals? Do they stay low? We don't know.

22.text: So I figured this: The best thing you can do is enjoy the work you do. That's your slice of the pie. 'Cause who knows what's gon' happen after you gone?

1.text: I looked around again and saw all the oppression under the sun. Saw the tears of the oppressed—but no comforter. The oppressors got the power, but the victims? No one to hold them, no one to hear them.

2.text: I said, "Honestly? The dead might be better off than the living."

3.text: But even better than both? The one who ain't even been born— Ain't had to witness all this evil go down.

4.text: I saw how folks work hard, get skill, build somethin'— and next thing? Their neighbor hatin'. All that? Just wind. Ain't no real fulfillment in that.

5.text: The fool just sits with folded arms— and ends up eatin' his own life away.

6.text: Better to have one handful and peace of mind than two handfuls with stress, noise, and empty hustle.

7.text: Then I looked again and saw more vanity under the sun.

8.text: A man grindin' alone. No son, no brother. Still workin' like he got somethin' to prove. He never stops to ask: "Who am I doin' this for?" No joy. No rest. Just accumulation. That's not just vanity—it's a tragedy.

9.text: Two are better than one—'cause they get more done together.

10.text: If one fall, the other can help 'em up. But if you fall alone? Ain't nobody reachin' for you.

11.text: If two lie down together, they stay warm. But one by himself? He gon' freeze.

12.text: One might get jumped. But two can fight back. And a three-strand cord? That don't break easy.

13.text: Better a broke but wise young man than a stubborn old king who won't take advice no more.

14.text: That young man might've been in jail, might've been broke, but now he wearin' the crown.

15.text: I saw everybody ridin' for the new prince. He the people's favorite.

16.text: Crowds cheered for him. Everybody was on his side. But years later? New folks showed up… and they ain't care about him either. That too? Just wind. Just vanity.

1.text: Step careful when you show up in God's house. Don't come in loud with performin'— Come close to listen. That's better than runnin' your mouth like a fool, 'cause fools don't even know they doin' wrong.

2.text: Don't speak too fast in God's face. Let your heart slow down before your mouth runs off. He in heaven. You on earth. So keep your words short and solid.

3.text: All that dreamin'? That comes from a lot of stress. But too many words? That's how fools sound.

4.text: If you make a vow to God—don't play with it. Don't stall. Don't lie. God don't get joy from fools. Do what you said you'd do.

5.text: It's better to not make a promise at all than to promise and not come through.

6.text: Don't let your mouth write a check your life can't cash. Don't try to blame the angel later and say, "My bad, I ain't mean it." Why make God mad and watch all your work fall apart?

7.text: Talk too much. Dream too much. That's just more vanity. What matters? Fear God.

8.text: If you see the poor bein' crushed and justice gettin' flipped in courtrooms— don't act shocked. There's always a higher-up watchin' the one below him, and even they get watched by somebody higher.

9.text: But still—at the end of the day, the whole system runs off the land. Even the king eat from the same harvest.

10.text: If you in love with silver, you'll never have enough. Same with riches— it'll never feel like plenty. That, too? Just more smoke.

11.text: When you got more, more folks show up tryin' to eat off you. So what do you really gain, besides lookin' at your stuff and keepin' score?

12.text: The one who works hard sleeps well— whether his belly full or not. But the rich man? He stay up at night, wrestlin' with his abundance.

13.text: I seen a hard truth under the sun: Wealth held too tight ends up hurtin' the one who hoards it.

14.text: Sometimes money vanish overnight— bad business, bad luck. And when he finally got a child? Ain't nothin' left to give.

15.text: You come in this world naked. You leavin' the same way. Can't take nothin' you earned with you.

16.text: That's the harsh part— you leave with nothin', just like you came. All that grindin'? What was it for? Just tryna catch wind.

17.text: Folks live like that—eatin' in the dark, full of sadness, sickness, and anger. That's all they got to show.

18.text: But here's what I have seen: It's good to eat, drink, and enjoy what your work gives you. Enjoy your portion. That's what God gave you.

19.text: If God blessed you with wealth and the power to enjoy it, take that joy in your labor— that's the real gift.

20.text: When you live like that? You ain't stuck tryna rewind your past. God keep your heart busy with joy.

1.text: I seen somethin' heavy under the sun. It's not rare either—it happens to folks all the time.

2.text: A man blessed with money, success, and respect— He got everything he could ever want. But God ain't give him the power to enjoy it. Some stranger end up eatin' off what he built. That's smoke. That's a cruel pain.

3.text: Say a man got a hundred kids and lives a long, long life— But his soul still ain't full, and nobody even buries him proper? I'm tellin' you… a stillborn baby got it better than him.

4.text: That baby came and left in silence. No spotlight. No pain. Just peace.

5.text: It never saw the sun, never knew struggle— and it got more rest than that man ever will.

6.text: Even if he lived two thousand years… If he never experienced goodness? What's the point? Ain't we all headed to the same ground?

7.text: All that work we do? Just to eat. But the soul? The soul stay hungry.

8.text: What does the wise man really gain over a fool? What edge does the poor man got— even if he know how to move smart through life?

9.text: Better to enjoy what's right in front of you than to keep chasin' fantasies you can't catch. That too? Just graspin' at wind.

10.text: We already been named. We humans. We dust. And we can't go up against the One who's bigger than all of us.

11.text: The more we talk, the more we chase, the more we want— the more empty it all feels. So what's the real benefit?

12.text: Who really knows what's good for us down here, livin' this short, shadowy life? And who can tell us what's comin' after we gone?

1.text: A good name hit harder than perfume. And honestly? The day you die can mean more than the day you was born.

2.text: It's better to go to a funeral than a party— 'cause that's where we all end up. The living? They need that reminder.

3.text: Sadness? It can grow you more than laughter ever will. Pain teaches.

4.text: A wise heart sits in the heaviness. Fools stay chasin' a good time, missin' the lesson.

5.text: Better to get checked by someone wise than be serenaded by fools.

6.text: That loud, empty laughter? It's like dry sticks poppin' in a fire—no substance. Just noise. That too? Vanity.

7.text: Oppression can mess with a wise man's mind. Bribes? They'll rot your heart from the inside.

8.text: The end of a thing? Usually better than the start. And patience? That's stronger than pride.

9.text: Don't be so quick to snap. Anger love to live in a fool's chest.

10.text: Don't sit around sayin', "Back in the day was better." That kind of talk don't come from wisdom.

11.text: Wisdom with money? Now that's power. Both protect you, but one'll feed your soul.

12.text: Money can guard your life. But wisdom? Wisdom gives it meaning.

13.text: Think about what God does— You can't straighten what He made crooked.

14.text: When life's good? Rejoice. But when it's hard? Pause and reflect. God made both seasons, so you'd remember you don't control the future.

15.text: I seen it all: Good people dying too soon, Wicked folks livin' long and loud. It don't always make sense.

16.text: Don't overdo it tryna be "holier-than-thou." You'll burn yourself out.

17.text: But don't wild out either— You'll wreck your life early actin' reckless.

18.text: Hold both truths. Fear God, and He'll help you walk the line.

19.text: Wisdom make one person stronger than a whole city council.

20.text: Ain't nobody perfect. Everybody got sin on them.

21.text: Don't get caught up in every little thing folks say— You might hear stuff that'll hurt you.

22.text: 'Cause let's be real… You done said some wild stuff too.

23.text: I tested all this by wisdom. Said I'd figure it all out. But truth? It was too deep.

24.text: That thing out there? Far off. Buried deep. Ain't nobody fully cracked the code.

25.text: I chased after it though. Tried to understand life, tried to see what's wise, what's foolish, and what's just plain crazy.

26.text: And I found this one thing: A woman whose heart was traps and chains— She more bitter than death. If you walk right with God, you'll avoid her. But if you wildin'? She'll snatch your soul.

27.text: "I kept tryin' to piece it all together," says the Preacher. "One piece at a time."

28.text: "But I still ain't found the full answer. Out of a thousand men, maybe one got it. But among women? I ain't found one yet."

29.text: What I do know? God made us upright. We the ones who ran off schemin'— Tryna rewrite the rules and outsmart the Creator.

1.text: Who got insight like the wise? Who really know how to break things down? Wisdom make your face light up. It soften that hard look life gave you.

2.text: I'm sayin' this: Obey the king's orders. You made a vow to God—honor that.

3.text: Don't storm out the room. And don't stand up for evil just 'cause you mad. That king? He gon' do what he wanna do.

4.text: When the king speak, his word carry weight. Ain't nobody gon' ask him, "What you think you doin'?"

5.text: If you obey, you stay safe. And a wise one knows when to move and how to move.

6.text: Every situation got a time and a way to handle it. But let's be real—life still be hard.

7.text: We don't know the future. We don't even know when it'll hit. Nobody got the date stamped.

8.text: You can't hold your breath in when death come. You can't call time-out when it's your moment. And evil? It won't save the ones already locked into it.

9.text: I seen all this play out. I been studyin' how people move under the sun. Sometimes one man rules over another, and all it bring? Is harm.

10.text: I seen wicked folks get buried, And yeah, they used to show up at the temple, but now? Nobody remembers 'em. That too? Just more smoke.

11.text: When people don't get punished quick, they get bold with their evil. They think they safe.

12.text: But even if a sinner gets away with it a hundred times, I still know this: It'll go well for those who fear God.

13.text: But the wicked? They won't last. Their days will blow by like shadows, 'cause they don't fear the One in charge.

14.text: I seen some real twisted stuff: Righteous folks suffer like they were wicked. And wicked folks livin' like they holy. That don't sit right. That's vanity too.

15.text: So I say this: Enjoy what you can. Eat, drink, laugh. That's the one thing that stay with you while you grind through this life God gave you.

16.text: I tried to understand it all. Tried to study every move under the sun. Stayed up late. No sleep. Just thinkin'.

17.text: But even with all that? I realized—man can't figure out what God doin'. You can work, research, analyze… You still won't catch it all. Even the wise? They try… but they still can't fully wrap their heads around His ways.

1.text: I sat with all this in my heart, tryin' to figure it out—righteous folks, wise folks, what they do—all of 'em still in God's hands. And truth is? You can't look at what's happenin' and know if God mad or pleased.

2.text: 'Cause the same stuff happen to everybody. Good folk, bad folk. Churchgoers, wild ones. Folks who honor vows and folks who break 'em. Same outcome.

3.text: That's what's wrong with this whole thing: Everybody end up the same. People wild out while they alive—hearts full of madness—then boom. They gone.

4.text: But as long as you breathin'? There's still hope. Better to be a live dog than a dead lion.

5.text: The livin' know they gon' die. But the dead? They don't know nothin'. They can't earn nothin'. Nobody remember 'em.

6.text: Their love, their hate, their envy—it all faded. Ain't no comin' back to fix nothin'. Their part in this life is done.

7.text: So go 'head. Eat your bread with joy. Drink your wine with a glad heart. God already checked off your name.

8.text: Dress like you got peace. Keep oil on your head—look like somebody who know joy.

9.text: Love your partner. Enjoy life with the one you love—even in this short, unpredictable life God gave you. That love? That's part of your reward. That joy? That's the return on your grind.

10.text: Whatever your hands find to do—do it with all you got. 'Cause once you dead? Ain't no more plans, no hustle, no wisdom, no nothin'. The grave don't take ambition.

11.text: I looked again and saw: The fastest don't always win the race. The strongest don't always win the fight. Smart folks don't always get paid. Skilled folks don't always get favor. 'Cause time and chance hit us all.

12.text: You don't know your time. Just like fish caught up in a net, or birds caught in a trap—people get snatched up too, with no warning.

13.text: I saw some next-level wisdom once—and it stuck with me.

14.text: Small city. Not many people. Big king came through, built up traps all around it.

15.text: But in that city? One poor wise man. And by his wisdom? He saved the whole place. But guess what? Nobody remembered him.

16.text: So yeah… wisdom better than strength. But the world? It don't listen to the poor man's wisdom. They ignore his voice.

17.text: But even so? The quiet words of the wise hit harder than loud talk from fools in power.

18.text: Wisdom beat weapons. But one reckless fool? He can mess up everything good.

1.text: Dead flies make expensive perfume stink. Same way, one foolish move can mess up a whole rep of wisdom and honor.

2.text: A wise man's heart? Steady and sure. A fool's? All over the place—left, reckless, wrong.

3.text: Even when a fool tryna walk straight, his lack of wisdom show. He broadcastin' his ignorance loud and proud.

4.text: If your boss blow up on you, don't dip too quick. Sometimes holdin' your post is the smartest way to cool a hothead.

5.text: I seen somethin' wild under the sun—A ruler out here makin bad calls.

6.text: Fools sittin' high up in honor, while folks with real sense be overlooked and underpaid.

7.text: I seen servants ridin' horses, while royalty was walkin' like peasants. Whole thing felt backward.

8.text: Dig a hole for somebody else? You might be the one that fall in it. Break through a wall carelessly? You might get bit by what's hidin' behind it.

9.text: Workin' hard got its risks too—stonework can cut you, wood split wrong can hurt you.

10.text: Try to chop with a dull axe? You gon' sweat more. But sharpen it—use wisdom—and you'll get more done with less effort.

11.text: If a snake bite before the charm gets spoken, the charmer ain't useful. Same goes for a big talker who ain't got timing.

12.text: Wise folks speak life and grace. Fools? They get swallowed by their own mouth.

13.text: They start talkin' nonsense, and by the end, it's full-blown madness.

14.text: Fools love to overtalk—Like they know what's comin' tomorrow. Nobody knows the future like that.

15.text: All that runnin' in circles? They wear themselves out. They so lost, they can't even find their way to the city.

16.text: Woe to a land when the king act like a lil boy, and the leaders stay feastin' too early in the day—drunk before noon.

17.text: But blessed is the land with a noble king, and leaders who eat at the right time—for strength, not for turnin' up.

18.text: Sit around too long? The house gon' fall apart. The roof gon' leak. Things decay when hands don't move.

19.text: Folks throw parties to laugh. Wine get folks loose. But money? Money talk.

20.text: Don't badmouth the king—even in your head. Don't trash the rich—even in your bedroom. 'Cause you never know who's listenin'… A bird might catch your words and carry your secret across the sky.

1.text: Go 'head and toss your bread out there—even on the waters. You might not see it today, but it'll come back to you later.

2.text: Don't hold back what you got. Share with seven—nah, go on and bless eight. You don't know what's comin' to shake the world next.

3.text: When the clouds heavy, they gon' pour. When a tree falls, it ain't gettin' back up. It is where it lands. That's just how life be.

4.text: If you sittin' around waitin' for perfect weather, you'll never plant nothin'. If you scared of clouds, you ain't never gon' harvest.

5.text: Just like you can't trace the wind or explain how bones form in a baby's womb, you ain't gon' figure out how God work. He run all this.

6.text: So plant your seed in the morning. Don't sit on your hands come nightfall. You don't know what gon' hit—this one might work, that one might work, or both might blow up big.

7.text: Light hit different. Sunshine on your face? That's joy.

8.text: And if you get to live long, enjoy them years, every one. But don't forget—dark days still comin'. And they last a while. All of this? Still just a vapor.

9.text: Young blood, enjoy your youth. Laugh, dance, love—do your thing. Follow your heart, chase what you see. But just know: God keep receipts. You gon' have to answer for all of it.

10.text: So don't let your heart get bitter, and don't let your flesh run wild. 'Cause childhood and youth? They quick. They gone before you know it.

1.text: Remember your Creator while you still got energy. Before them hard days hit, and the years roll in where you say, "I ain't feelin' this no more."

2.text: Before your light start dimmin'—sun, moon, and stars don't shine the same, and the clouds keep comin' even after the storm.

3.text: When your arms shake like old gateposts, and your legs ain't holdin' you up no more. When your teeth few and far between, and your eyes can't see through the window like they used to.

4.text: When your ears ain't sharp, and the music sound faded. When you up at dawn from the smallest noise, but not even your favorite song moves you.

5.text: When you scared of steps, and the street feel like danger. When your hair turn white like almond blossoms, your step light like a grasshopper, and you just ain't got that desire no more. 'Cause at that point? Man go to his eternal rest—and the mourners walk the streets behind him.

6.text: Remember Him before the silver cord snap, before the golden bowl fall and break, before the jar crack at the spring, and the pulley shatter at the well.

7.text: 'Cause the dust gon' return to the ground where it came from, and the spirit? She gon' float back to God, the One who gave her.

8.text: "Vanity of vanities," the Preacher says—"All of this? It's just vapor."

9.text: And just so you know—the Preacher ain't just deep, he was wise. He taught folks. Broke things down. Put truth in order, wrapped it in words that hit right.

10.text: He searched for the realest way to say things—and every line he dropped? It was solid. No fluff. Just facts.

11.text: Wise words poke you like a cattle prod—they sting so you move. And the ones who know? They build steady like nails from one good Shepherd.

12.text: And listen, my child—don't get caught tryna read every book or chase every scroll. You'll wear yourself out. Too much study don't guarantee peace.

13.text: So here it is: The conclusion of the whole matter: Fear God. Keep His commandments. That's the whole job. That's the assignment.

14.text: 'Cause God gon' bring every deed to the light—even the secret ones. Good or bad—He gon' see it through.

1.text: This all went down back in the days of King Ahasuerus—the same king who ruled over 127 provinces from India all the way to Ethiopia.

2.text: Back then, he was sittin' on his throne in the palace at Shushan, holdin' it down.

3.text: In the third year of his reign, he threw a big feast for all his officials and servants. All the powerful folks from Persia and Media showed up—the nobles and provincial leaders too.

4.text: He was flexin'—showin' off how rich he was and how majestic everything looked. That man kept it goin' for 180 days straight.

5.text: After that, he hosted another feast for everybody in Shushan, from the highest to the lowest, right in the courtyard of the palace garden. That one lasted 7 days.

6.text: The spot was decked out with white and blue curtains, tied with fancy linen cords hangin' on silver rods and marble columns. The couches? Made of gold and silver, sittin' on a floor that looked like a whole art piece—alabaster, turquoise, and black and white marble.

7.text: They was servin' drinks in gold cups—each one different from the next. And the royal wine? Flowin' heavy, like the king had no limits.

8.text: The king said nobody was required to drink if they ain't want to. He told his staff, 'Let folks sip how they want.'

9.text: Queen Vashti? She had her own thing goin' on. She was throwin' a feast for the women in the king's royal palace.

10.text: On the seventh day, after the king had a lil' too much wine and was feelin' real good, he told his seven eunuchs—Mehuman, Biztha, Harbona, Bigtha, Abagtha, Zethar, and Carcas—

11.text: 'Go get Queen Vashti. Tell her to come through wearin' her crown so everybody can see how fine she is.' He really wanted to show her off.

12.text: But Vashti wasn't goin'. She straight up said no to the king's command. That made the king furious—he was heated.

13.text: So he called up the wise men who were known for knowin' the law and how things worked in the kingdom.

14.text: These were his go-to guys: Carshena, Shethar, Admatha, Tarshish, Meres, Marsena, and Memucan—the top seven princes of Persia and Media, who had VIP access to the king.

15.text: 'So what we supposed to do with Queen Vashti?' the king asked. 'She broke the royal order. What's the move according to the law?'

16.text: Memucan stood up and said, 'This ain't just about the king. Vashti just disrespected everybody—the princes, the people, the whole kingdom.'

17.text: 'Word gon' get out that the queen told the king no, and women everywhere gon' start gettin' bold, disrespectin' their men too.'

18.text: 'By tonight, all the noble women in Persia and Media gon' be tellin' their husbands what Vashti did. This thing gon' spread, and the whole kingdom gon' be outta order.'

19.text: 'If the king down with it, he should drop a royal decree—put it in writing so it can't be changed: Vashti can't come before the king no more. And her royal spot? Give that to someone better.'

20.text: 'Once the word gets out across the whole empire—and it's a big one—all the wives gon' respect their husbands, whether they big time or low key.'

21.text: The king and the princes liked what Memucan said. So the king did just that.

22.text: He sent letters out to every province, in their own language and writing, sayin' that every man should run his own house and speak his people's language.

1.text: After all that went down, and the king finally cooled off, he started thinkin' about Vashti—what she did and what had been decided about her.

2.text: His attendants came through like, 'Let's go find some fine young virgins for the king.'

3.text: 'Have officers in every province gather up all the baddest young virgins and bring 'em to Shushan, to the women's quarters. Put 'em under Hegai, the king's eunuch in charge of the ladies. Give 'em all the spa treatments they need.'

4.text: 'Then whichever girl the king likes most—she can take Vashti's place as queen.' This idea sounded real good to the king, so he went ahead with it.

5.text: Now in Shushan, there was this Jewish man named Mordecai, son of Jair, son of Shimei, son of Kish—a Benjamite.

6.text: Kish had been taken from Jerusalem back when Jeconiah was king of Judah, and Nebuchadnezzar from Babylon scooped everybody up.

7.text: Mordecai was raisin' his cousin Hadassah—aka Esther—'cause she ain't have no mom or dad. The girl was fine and had a good heart. When her parents passed, Mordecai took her in like his own daughter.

8.text: So when the king's order got out and all the young women were gathered at Shushan under Hegai's care, Esther got caught up in that too. They brought her to the palace, right into Hegai's hands.

9.text: And Esther? She instantly stood out. Hegai liked her vibe, so he gave her the hookup—extra beauty products, special food, seven handpicked maids from the palace, and moved her into the best room in the women's section.

10.text: Esther ain't tell nobody she was Jewish or about her family. Mordecai had told her to keep that on the low.

11.text: And every single day, Mordecai would be walkin' back and forth outside the women's court, tryna get updates on how Esther was doin'.

12.text: Now the way this worked, each girl had to go through a whole year of beauty prep before she could even see the king—six months with myrrh oil, and six months with perfumes and all kinds of treatments.

13.text: After that, each girl got to bring whatever she wanted with her from the women's house to the king's place.

14.text: She'd spend the night with the king, but in the morning, she had to go to a different section where the concubines stayed, under Shaashgaz, the eunuch in charge of them. She wouldn't see the king again unless he asked for her by name.

15.text: When it was Esther's turn—she was the daughter of Abihail, Mordecai's uncle, who raised her—she ain't ask for nothin' extra. She just trusted what Hegai, the eunuch, suggested. And everybody who saw her? Fell in love with her instantly.

16.text: So they brought Esther to the king in his palace, in the tenth month (Tebeth), during the seventh year of his reign.

17.text: And the king? Man, he was gone. He loved Esther more than all the other women. She had that favor on her. So he put the crown on her head and made her queen instead of Vashti.

18.text: Then the king threw a huge party—The Feast of Esther—for all his officials and servants. He declared a holiday across the provinces and started blessin' folks with royal gifts.

19.text: Later on, when the virgins got gathered up again, Mordecai was sittin' at the king's gate.

20.text: Esther still hadn't told anybody she was Jewish or who her people were—just like Mordecai told her. She always listened to him, just like when she was growin' up.

21.text: Now one day while Mordecai was chillin' at the king's gate, he overheard two of the king's eunuchs—Bigthan and Teresh—plottin'. They were mad and tryna take the king out.

22.text: Mordecai found out and told Queen Esther. She went and told the king, makin' sure to say it came from Mordecai.

23.text: They looked into it, and yup—it was true. So they had both of those men hanged on the gallows. And it all got written down in the official royal records right in front of the king.

1.text: After all that, King Ahasuerus gave Haman—a descendant of Hammedatha the Agagite—a big promotion. Put him above all the other princes and leaders.

2.text: Everybody workin' at the king's gate bowed down to Haman like they was told. But Mordecai? Nah, he wasn't goin'. He ain't bow and he ain't show Haman no honor.

3.text: So the king's servants at the gate pressed Mordecai like, 'Why you disobeyin' the king's orders?'

4.text: They kept botherin' him about it, day after day, and he still wasn't budgin'. He told 'em straight up, 'I'm a Jew.' So they went and snitched to Haman to see if Mordecai's stance was really legit.

5.text: When Haman saw with his own eyes that Mordecai wasn't bowin' or showin' no respect, he got tight—dude was furious.

6.text: But he ain't wanna just deal with Mordecai alone. Once he found out Mordecai's people were Jewish, he set his sights on all of 'em. Haman was plottin' to wipe out every Jew in the whole kingdom.

7.text: In the first month, Nisan, of King Ahasuerus' twelfth year, they rolled dice (they called it 'Pur') to figure out the date for this evil plan. The lot landed on the twelfth month—Adar.

8.text: Then Haman went to the king like, 'There's a group of people scattered all over your kingdom. They different. They don't live like everybody else and they don't follow your rules. They a problem, for real.'

9.text: 'If it's cool with you, let's write up a law to get rid of 'em. I'll drop ten thousand talents of silver on whoever handle it and make sure it ends up in your treasury.'

10.text: The king took off his ring—the one with the royal seal—and gave it to Haman, son of Hammedatha the Agagite. That man was the Jews' #1 enemy.

11.text: Then the king told Haman, 'The money and the people—do what you want. It's in your hands now.'

12.text: On the thirteenth day of the first month, the royal scribes got to work. They wrote up Haman's orders and sent 'em to the king's governors, leaders, and officials in every province. The letter was written in every language and sealed with the king's ring.

13.text: The letters went out fast—sent by couriers across the kingdom—sayin' to kill, destroy, and wipe out every Jew, no matter the age, from kids to elders, women too. It was all supposed to go down in one day: the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, Adar. And they could take whatever the Jews owned too.

14.text: Copies of the order were posted in every province so the people could get ready. That day was comin', and everybody had to know.

15.text: The couriers took off, movin' fast by the king's command. The decree was also announced in Shushan. Meanwhile, the king and Haman sat down drinkin' like it was nothin'. But the whole city of Shushan? Confused and shook.

1.text: When Mordecai heard everything that had gone down, he tore his clothes, threw on some sackcloth and ashes, and went out into the city cryin' loud and deep from the gut.

2.text: He walked all the way up to the king's gate, but couldn't go in, 'cause you ain't allowed inside the gate rockin' sackcloth.

3.text: Everywhere the king's decree showed up, the Jews were in full mourning. Folks was fastin', cryin', hollerin', laid out in sackcloth and ashes.

4.text: Esther's girls and eunuchs came and told her what was up, and it messed her up bad. She sent fresh clothes to Mordecai, tryna get him out that sackcloth—but he said nah, he wasn't takin' 'em.

5.text: So Esther called for Hathach, one of the king's eunuchs assigned to her, and told him to go find out what was really goin' on with Mordecai.

6.text: Hathach went out to meet Mordecai in the city square, right outside the king's gate.

7.text: Mordecai broke it all down for him—everything that happened and how Haman promised to drop big money into the king's account to wipe out the Jews.

8.text: He even gave Hathach a copy of the order posted in Shushan that said the Jews were gettin' destroyed. He told him, 'Show this to Esther. Make sure she gets it. Tell her she gotta go to the king and beg for her people.'

9.text: Hathach came back and told Esther exactly what Mordecai said.

10.text: Then Esther sent a message back to Mordecai through Hathach.

11.text: 'Everybody knows—man or woman—if you walk up in the king's inner court without bein' called, you dead. That's the law. Unless he stretches out that golden scepter. And me? I ain't been called in thirty days.'

12.text: So they took that message back to Mordecai.

13.text: Mordecai replied, 'Don't get it twisted—just 'cause you in the palace don't mean you safe. You not gon' escape what's comin' to the rest of us.'

14.text: 'If you keep quiet right now, help gon' come from somewhere else, but you and your fam? Y'all gon' be gone. But maybe—just maybe—you was made queen for this exact moment.'

15.text: Then Esther sent back her answer to Mordecai.

16.text: 'Tell all the Jews in Shushan to fast for me. No food, no drink—for three whole days and nights. Me and my girls gon' do the same. Then I'ma go see the king—even though it's against the law. And if I die… I die.'

17.text: So Mordecai left and did everything Esther told him to do.

1.text: On the third day, Esther got dressed in her royal fit and went to stand in the inner court of the king's palace, right across from where the king was sittin' on his throne, facin' the entrance.

2.text: When the king saw Queen Esther standin' there, she caught his eye—he was feelin' her. He reached out the golden scepter in his hand toward her. Esther stepped up and touched the tip of it.

3.text: The king said, 'What's up, Queen Esther? What you want? Whatever you ask—up to half the kingdom—I got you.'

4.text: Esther said, 'If it's cool with you, I'd love for you and Haman to come to a banquet I put together for y'all—today.'

5.text: The king said, 'Bet. Go get Haman right now so we can do what Esther said.' So both the king and Haman rolled through to the banquet Esther had set up.

6.text: While they sipped wine, the king asked again, 'Alright Esther, what's your ask? What's your request? Whatever it is—even up to half the kingdom—it's yours.'

7.text: Esther said, 'Okay, here's what I'm askin'—'

8.text: 'If I'm really in your good graces, and you're willin' to hear me out and make it happen, then come back tomorrow to another banquet I'm preparin' for you and Haman. Then I'll tell you exactly what I want.'

9.text: Haman left that day feelin' himself—real happy, real proud. But when he saw Mordecai sittin' at the king's gate not standin' up, not even flinchin', all that joy turned into rage.

10.text: Still, he held it together. Went home, called up his people and his wife Zeresh to vent.

11.text: He started braggin'—talkin' about how rich he was, how many kids he had, how the king kept promotin' him and puttin' him above everybody else in the kingdom.

12.text: Then he said, 'And on top of all that, Queen Esther ain't invite nobody but me to dine with her and the king. And guess what—she invited me again tomorrow.'

13.text: 'But none of it even hits right as long as I gotta see Mordecai the Jew sittin' there like he don't see me.'

14.text: His wife Zeresh and his friends told him, 'You know what? Build a gallows—make it fifty cubits high. First thing in the morning, ask the king to hang Mordecai on it. Then go enjoy that banquet with the king.' That idea sounded perfect to Haman. So he had the gallows built.

1.text: That night, the king couldn't sleep. So he told somebody to bring him the book of records—the royal chronicles—and they started readin' it out loud to him.

2.text: That's when they came across the part where Mordecai had snitched on Bigthana and Teresh—two of the king's eunuchs who guarded the doors. They had been plottin' to kill the king.

3.text: The king said, 'Wait—did we ever do anything to honor Mordecai for that?' The servants said, 'Nah, not a thing.'

4.text: The king said, 'Who's out there in the court right now?' At that exact moment, Haman had just walked into the outer court, ready to suggest hangin' Mordecai on the gallows he built.

5.text: The servants said, 'Haman's out there standin' in the court.' The king said, 'Bring him in.'

6.text: Haman came in, and the king asked, 'What should be done for the man the king wants to honor?' Now Haman? He was in his own head like, 'Who else would the king wanna honor but me?'

7.text: So Haman answered, 'For the man the king wanna honor—'

8.text: 'Bring out a royal robe the king himself has worn, and a horse the king's actually ridden—with the royal crest on its head.'

9.text: 'Then pick one of the king's top officials to dress him up and put him on that horse. Parade him through the city square, shoutin', "This what's done for the man the king wanna honor!"'

10.text: The king said, 'Bet. Go do all that—for Mordecai the Jew who sits at the gate. Don't skip nothin' you just said.'

11.text: So Haman had to grab the robe and the horse, dress Mordecai up, and walk him through the city square yellin', 'This how the king honors somebody!'

12.text: After that, Mordecai just went back to sittin' at the king's gate. But Haman? He ran home with his head down, grievin' hard.

13.text: He told Zeresh and all his friends everything that happened. His crew and his wife were like, 'If Mordecai's one of them Jews, and you already slippin', it's a wrap. You not gon' win this. You definitely gon' fall.'

14.text: While they were still talkin', the king's eunuchs showed up and rushed Haman off to the banquet Esther had prepared.

1.text: So the king and Haman pulled up to eat with Queen Esther.

2.text: On the second day, while they was sippin' wine, the king asked again, 'What you want, Queen Esther? Whatever your request is—even up to half the kingdom—I'ma make it happen.'

3.text: Queen Esther said, 'If I got favor with you, and if you really rock with me, then please—spare my life. And spare my people too. That's what I'm beggin' for.'

4.text: 'Me and my people—we been sold out. Somebody out here tryin' to destroy us, kill us off completely. If it was just about bein' sold into slavery, I wouldn't have said nothin'. But this right here? This ain't something the king should just take as a loss.'

5.text: King Ahasuerus snapped: 'Who did this?! Where he at?! Who got the nerve to pull somethin' like this?!'

6.text: Esther said, 'It's him—the enemy is this evil Haman!' And just like that, Haman's whole face dropped—he was shook in front of the king and queen.

7.text: The king got up, heated, and stormed out into the palace garden. Haman stayed behind beggin' Queen Esther for his life. He knew the king had already decided his fate, and it wasn't lookin' good.

8.text: When the king came back from the garden, he walked in and saw Haman fallin' all over the couch where Esther was sittin'. The king said, 'Oh, so now you tryna come at the queen too? Right here in my house?!' As soon as those words left his mouth, the guards came through and covered Haman's face.

9.text: Then Harbonah, one of the king's eunuchs, spoke up: 'Ayo king—look! There's a gallows fifty cubits high standin' at Haman's house. He built it for Mordecai—the same one who saved your life.' The king said, 'Hang him on it.'

10.text: So they hanged Haman on the very gallows he built for Mordecai. After that, the king finally cooled off.

1.text: That same day, King Ahasuerus gave Queen Esther everything that used to belong to Haman, the Jews' enemy. And Mordecai got brought before the king 'cause Esther had finally told him how they was related.

2.text: The king took off his signet ring—the one he had taken from Haman—and gave it to Mordecai. Then Esther made Mordecai the boss over everything that used to be Haman's.

3.text: But Esther wasn't done. She fell at the king's feet, cryin', beggin' him to shut down Haman's evil plan—the one he made to wipe out the Jews.

4.text: The king stretched out that golden scepter toward her again. So Esther got up and stood before him.

5.text: She said, 'If it pleases the king, and if I still got favor in your eyes, and if this feels right to you—please cancel out those letters Haman wrote. The ones that ordered my people—the Jews—to be destroyed in every province.'

6.text: 'How can I just stand by and watch my people go through that? I can't sit back while they get wiped out.'

7.text: Then King Ahasuerus told Esther and Mordecai, 'Look, I already gave you Haman's house. And we hung him up 'cause he tried to lay hands on the Jews.'

8.text: 'Now y'all go write whatever you want to protect your people. Write it in my name, seal it with my ring—'cause once something's written in the king's name and sealed, it can't be taken back.'

9.text: So the royal scribes got called in that same day—in the third month, Sivan, on the twenty-third day. Mordecai dictated the letter to the Jews, all the governors, princes, and leaders from India to Ethiopia—127 provinces. They wrote it in every language and script, including the Jews' own.

10.text: Mordecai wrote it in King Ahasuerus' name, sealed it with the king's ring, and sent it out fast on royal horses bred for speed.

11.text: The letters gave the Jews permission to link up and defend themselves—to fight back, kill, and destroy anybody who came for them, no matter the age or gender—and they could take the enemies' goods too.

12.text: It was all set to go down on one day—the thirteenth day of the twelfth month, Adar—across every province of the king's empire.

13.text: Copies of the new law got posted everywhere so the Jews could get ready to clap back and handle anybody comin' for them.

14.text: The royal messengers hopped on them fast horses and flew out with the orders, movin' quick 'cause the king ain't play about it. The decree was also put up in Shushan.

15.text: Mordecai came out from the king's presence lookin' like royalty—rockin' blue and white threads, a big gold crown, and a fine linen and purple robe. And Shushan? The whole city turned up.

16.text: The Jews were lit—full of joy, honor, and celebration.

17.text: In every city and province where the king's new order hit, the Jews threw feasts, celebrated hard, and had holidays. And a whole bunch of other folks started claimin' they were Jews too—'cause now they were scared of 'em.

1.text: In the twelfth month, the month of Adar, on the thirteenth day, the day came when the king's command and Haman's decree were supposed to go down. The enemies of the Jews thought they had it in the bag—but it flipped. The Jews rose up and handled those who hated them.

2.text: The Jews came together in their cities across all the provinces of King Ahasuerus to defend themselves and put hands on anyone tryna harm them. And nobody could stand against them—everybody was shook.

3.text: All the king's officials, satraps, governors, and workers were helpin' the Jews now—'cause they was scared of Mordecai.

4.text: Mordecai was big time now. He had clout in the palace and was known all over. Dude just kept risin'.

5.text: So the Jews came out swingin'—takin' down every single enemy with swords, no mercy, no hesitation. They did what they had to do to those who hated them.

6.text: In Shushan, the Jews killed five hundred men.

7.text: They also took out Parshandatha, Dalphon, Aspatha,

8.text: Poratha, Adalia, Aridatha,

9.text: Parmashta, Arisai, Aridai, and Vajezatha—

10.text: The ten sons of Haman, the son of Hammedatha, the Jews' enemy. But they ain't touch nobody's stuff—they left the plunder alone.

11.text: That same day, word got back to the king about how many folks got handled in Shushan.

12.text: The king told Esther, 'The Jews killed five hundred men here in Shushan, plus Haman's ten sons. Imagine what they did everywhere else! So what you want now, Queen Esther? You got it.'

13.text: Esther said, 'If it's alright with you, let the Jews in Shushan run it back tomorrow just like today. And hang Haman's ten sons on the gallows too.'

14.text: The king said, 'Do it.' So they issued the order in Shushan and hanged all ten of Haman's sons.

15.text: The Jews in Shushan linked up again on the fourteenth day of Adar and took out three hundred more men. Still didn't touch the plunder.

16.text: Across the rest of the empire, the other Jews defended themselves, found peace from their enemies, and took out seventy-five thousand folks—but still didn't lay a finger on the loot.

17.text: That all happened on the thirteenth day of Adar. On the fourteenth, they chilled, threw a feast, and celebrated.

18.text: But the Jews in Shushan fought on both the thirteenth and fourteenth, so they rested and partied on the fifteenth.

19.text: That's why the Jews in small towns, in unwalled villages, celebrate the fourteenth of Adar with joy, food, and gift-givin'.

20.text: Mordecai wrote everything down and sent letters to Jews all over—from the closest to the farthest provinces.

21.text: He told them to lock in those two days every year—the fourteenth and fifteenth of Adar—as days to celebrate.

22.text: They were the days when the Jews caught a break, when their sorrow turned into joy, and their pain turned into a holiday. Days to feast, celebrate, send gifts to each other, and bless the poor.

23.text: The Jews agreed to it and made it official—just like Mordecai wrote.

24.text: See, Haman the Agagite—enemy of the Jews—had plotted to wipe 'em out and had cast Pur (the lot) to destroy them completely.

25.text: But when Esther came to the king, he flipped the script and ordered that Haman's own evil plan fall back on him—and had him and his sons hanged.

26.text: That's why they called it Purim, after the word Pur. Because of what went down, what they saw, and how it all turned out.

27.text: The Jews made it law for themselves, their kids, and anyone who joined them—these two days had to be celebrated every year, without fail.

28.text: Every generation, every family, every province, every city—Purim had to be remembered. Nobody could let this tradition die out.

29.text: Queen Esther, daughter of Abihail, and Mordecai the Jew wrote another letter to seal the deal on Purim with full authority.

30.text: Mordecai sent out peace-filled, truth-telling letters to all 127 provinces in the kingdom.

31.text: He confirmed the Purim celebration on its set days, just like he and Esther had laid it out—along with the traditions around fasting and grieving.

32.text: Esther's decree made everything official, and it got written down in the records.

1.text: King Ahasuerus laid down taxes across the whole land—even the islands out in the sea.

2.text: Everything that king did—his power, his strength, and how high he elevated Mordecai—it's all written down in the royal history books of Media and Persia.

3.text: Mordecai the Jew was second-in-command right under King Ahasuerus. He was a real one—respected by the Jews, loved by the people. He stayed lookin' out for his folks and always spoke peace over his people.

1.text: These the names of Jacob's sons—the ones that moved to Egypt wit' him, each one bringing they whole fam.

2.text: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah,

3.text: Issachar, Zebulun, Benjamin,

4.text: Dan, Naphtali, Gad, and Asher.

5.text: Altogether, Jacob had seventy descendants in Egypt, including Joseph, who was already out there handling business.

6.text: Over time, Joseph and all his brothers passed away, ending that whole generation.

7.text: But their kids? Man, they multiplied like crazy, had a whole bunch of babies and grandbabies. The Israelites got so deep and strong they started filling up the whole land.

8.text: Then one day, a new Pharaoh came up in Egypt, and he ain't know nothing 'bout Joseph or what he did.

9.text: He told his people, 'Look, these Israelites? They outnumber us now and they stronger too.'

10.text: 'We gotta do something before they grow even bigger. If a war pop off, they gon' link up with our enemies, fight against us, and dip out this country.'

11.text: So the Egyptians made 'em slaves, put some ruthless bosses over them, tryna break their spirits with hard work. Made 'em build up the cities of Pithom and Rameses just to store Pharaoh's supplies.

12.text: But the crazier the Egyptians treated 'em, the more they kept growing and spreading. Egypt got real nervous.

13.text: So they worked the Israelites even harder, with no mercy at all.

14.text: Made life miserable for 'em—forced 'em to mix mortar, make bricks, work the fields, just straight-up ruthless with the demands.

15.text: Then Pharaoh, Egypt's king, called up two Hebrew midwives, Shiphrah and Puah.

16.text: He told 'em, 'When y'all help the Hebrew women give birth, watch close. If it's a boy, kill him. If it's a girl, let her live.'

17.text: But the midwives feared God, so they ain't listen to Pharaoh—they let the baby boys live too.

18.text: Pharaoh pulled them up and said, 'Why y'all let these boys live? What's up with that?'

19.text: They told him, 'The Hebrew women ain't like Egyptian women—they strong! They be popping them babies out fast, before we even get there.'

20.text: So God took care of the midwives, and the Israelites just kept multiplying, getting stronger and stronger.

21.text: Since the midwives feared God, He blessed them with families of their own.

22.text: Then Pharaoh took it to the next level—he told all his people, 'Every newborn Hebrew boy? Toss him in the Nile River. But y'all can let the girls live.'

1.text: Around this time, a man and woman from the tribe of Levi got married.

2.text: The woman got pregnant and had a son. When she saw how special he was, she hid him for three months.

3.text: But when she couldn't hide him no more, she got a basket made of papyrus reeds, sealed it up with tar and pitch, put the baby inside, and placed it in the reeds along the Nile River bank.

4.text: His sister stood at a distance, watching to see what would happen to him.

5.text: Pharaoh's daughter came down to the river to take a bath, while her attendants walked along the bank. She noticed the basket in the reeds and sent one of her maids to go get it.

6.text: She opened it up and saw the baby inside—he was crying, and she felt sorry for him. She said, 'This gotta be one of the Hebrew babies.'

7.text: Then the baby's sister stepped up and said, 'You want me to go find a Hebrew woman to nurse him for you?'

8.text: 'Yes, go!' the princess said. So the girl went and got the baby's mother.

9.text: Pharaoh's daughter told her, 'Take this baby and nurse him for me. I'll pay you for it.' So the woman took her son back home and nursed him.

10.text: When the boy got older, his mother brought him back to Pharaoh's daughter, who adopted him as her own. She named him Moses, saying, 'I lifted him out the water.'

11.text: Years later, when Moses was grown, he went out to see his people—the Hebrews—and saw how hard they was being worked. While he was out there, he saw an Egyptian beating one of his Hebrew brothers.

12.text: Moses looked around to make sure nobody was watching, then killed the Egyptian and hid his body in the sand.

13.text: The next day, Moses went back out and saw two Hebrew men fighting. He said to the one in the wrong, 'Bruh, why you beating up your own brother?'

14.text: The man said, 'Who put you in charge? You our prince now? You gon' kill me like you killed that Egyptian yesterday?'

15.text: Moses got scared, thinking, 'Dang, people know what I did.' Sure enough, Pharaoh heard about it and tried to kill Moses. But Moses ran away to Midian and stayed there.

16.text: When Moses got to Midian, he sat down next to a well. The priest of Midian had seven daughters who came to draw water for their father's flock, just like they always did.

17.text: But some other shepherds came through and tried to push them out the way. Moses wasn't having it—he jumped up, helped the girls, and made sure their flock got watered.

18.text: When the girls got back home to their father, Reuel, he said, 'Y'all back early today! What happened?'

19.text: They told him, 'An Egyptian helped us out! He ran off the shepherds and then watered our flock for us.'

20.text: 'Where he at then?' Reuel asked. 'Why'd y'all leave him out there? Go invite him to dinner!'

21.text: Moses accepted the invite and ended up staying with them. After a while, Reuel gave him his daughter Zipporah as his wife.

22.text: Later on, she had a son, and Moses named him Gershom, saying, 'I been a foreigner in a land that ain't mine.'

23.text: Years went by, and the Pharaoh who wanted Moses dead finally died. But the Israelites was still suffering under slavery, crying out for help. Their cries went up to God.

24.text: God heard their pain and remembered His promise to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.

25.text: He looked down on Israel and knew—it was time to move.

1.text: One day, Moses was out tending the flock of his father-in-law, Jethro, the priest of Midian. He led the flock deep into the wilderness and came up to Sinai, God's mountain.

2.text: Outta nowhere, an angel of the Lord showed up in a blazing fire right in the middle of a bush. Moses looked, and he was shook—'cause even though the bush was on fire, it wasn't burning up!

3.text: Moses was like, 'Man, this wild! Why this bush ain't burning up? I gotta go check this out.'

4.text: When the Lord saw Moses getting closer, He called out from the bush, 'Moses! Moses!'

5.text: Moses answered, 'Here I am!'

6.text: God said, 'Don't come no closer. Take off your sandals, 'cause you standin' on holy ground.'

7.text: Then He said, 'I'm the God of your ancestors—the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob.' Soon as Moses heard that, he covered his face, 'cause he was scared to even look at God.

8.text: Then the Lord said, 'I seen what's happening to my people in Egypt. I heard they cries from all this oppression. Yeah, I know exactly what they goin' through.'

9.text: 'So I'm steppin' in to rescue 'em from Egypt and bring 'em to their own land—a land rich and full, flowin' with milk and honey. The same land where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites live now.'

10.text: 'Listen up, the cries of my people have reached me, and I see how bad the Egyptians treat 'em. So now, I'm sendin' you, Moses, to Pharaoh. You gon' lead my people, Israel, outta Egypt.'

11.text: But Moses was like, 'Wait, who am I to be standin' in front of Pharaoh? Who am I to be leadin' Israel outta Egypt?'

12.text: God told him, 'Don't even trip—I'ma be right there with you. And here's how you'll know I'm the one sendin' you: When you bring my people outta Egypt, y'all gon' worship me right here on this mountain.'

13.text: Moses said, 'Alright, but if I go tell the Israelites, "The God of your ancestors sent me," they gon' ask me, "What's His name?" What should I tell 'em?'

14.text: God said, 'Tell 'em this—"I Am Who I Am." That's what you tell the Israelites: "I Am sent me to you."'

15.text: Then God added, 'Tell 'em this too: "Yahweh, the God of your ancestors—the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—sent me to you. This my name forever. This the name y'all gon' remember for all generations."'

16.text: 'Now go, gather all the elders of Israel and tell 'em, "Yahweh, the God of our ancestors—Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—showed up to me. He told me He's been watching and He knows exactly how Egypt been treating us."'

17.text: 'Then tell 'em, "God promised He gon' rescue us from Egypt and take us to a land flowing with milk and honey—the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites."'

18.text: 'The elders gon' listen to you. Then you and them need to go to the king of Egypt and tell him, "The Lord, the God of the Hebrews, showed up to us. Let us take a three-day trip into the wilderness so we can worship Him and offer sacrifices."'

19.text: 'But listen, Pharaoh ain't lettin' y'all go easy. He ain't gon' budge unless a mighty hand forces him.'

20.text: 'So I'ma raise my hand, hit Egypt with all kinds of miracles and wonders. And after that? Pharaoh gon' have no choice but to let y'all go.'

21.text: 'And check this—I'ma make sure the Egyptians look at y'all with favor before y'all leave. They gon' give y'all gifts, so y'all won't walk out empty-handed.'

22.text: 'Every Hebrew woman gon' ask her Egyptian neighbor for silver, gold, and fine clothes. Y'all gon' put 'em on your sons and daughters—straight up taking back what was stolen. Y'all gon' walk out of Egypt with their wealth in hand.'

1.text: But Moses was still trippin'. He said, 'What if they don't believe me? What if they don't listen? What if they say, "The Lord ain't appear to you"?'

2.text: Then the Lord said, 'What's that in your hand?'

3.text: Moses looked and said, 'A shepherd's staff.'

4.text: 'Throw it on the ground,' the Lord said. Moses threw it down, and boom—it turned into a snake! Moses jumped back real quick.

5.text: Then the Lord said, 'Reach out and grab its tail.' Moses hesitated, then reached out and grabbed it, and just like that—it turned back into a staff in his hand.

6.text: 'Do this sign,' the Lord told him. 'Then they'll believe that the God of their ancestors—the God of Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—really sent you.'

7.text: Then the Lord said, 'Now, put your hand inside your cloak.' So Moses did it, and when he pulled it out, his hand was all messed up—white as snow, covered in disease.

8.text: 'Now put it back inside your cloak,' God said. Moses did, and when he pulled it out again, it was back to normal.

9.text: 'If they don't believe the first sign, they'll believe the second one. But if they still don't listen, take some water from the Nile, pour it out on dry ground, and watch it turn to blood.'

10.text: Moses started makin' excuses again, 'Lord, I ain't good with words. Never been. Even now, after You talkin' to me, I still get tongue-tied and trip over my words.'

11.text: The Lord said, 'Who made the mouth? Who decides if folks can talk or not, hear or not, see or not? Ain't it Me, the Lord?'

12.text: 'Now go! I'ma be with you while you speak, and I'ma tell you exactly what to say.'

13.text: But Moses still wasn't feelin' it. 'Lord, please! Just send somebody else!'

14.text: Now God was gettin' frustrated. 'Alright then, what about your brother Aaron? He speaks well. Look, he already on his way to meet you, and he gon' be happy to see you.'

15.text: 'You gon' tell him what to say, and I'ma be with both of y'all as you speak. I'ma teach you exactly what to do.'

16.text: 'Aaron gon' be your spokesman to the people. He gon' speak for you, and you gon' be like a representative of God to him, tellin' him what to say.'

17.text: 'And don't forget that staff—take it with you, 'cause you gon' need it to perform these miracles.'

18.text: Moses went back home to his father-in-law, Jethro, and said, 'Let me go back to Egypt to check on my people. I don't even know if they still alive.'

19.text: Jethro told him, 'Go in peace.'

20.text: Before Moses left Midian, the Lord spoke to him again: 'Go back to Egypt. The folks that wanted you dead? They all gone now.'

21.text: So Moses packed up, put his wife and kids on a donkey, and started heading to Egypt. In his hand? That staff of God.

22.text: Then the Lord told Moses, 'When you get back to Egypt, go to Pharaoh and do all the miracles I gave you power to do. But listen—he ain't gon' listen, 'cause I'ma make his heart stubborn.'

23.text: 'Then you tell him, "This is what the Lord says: Israel is my firstborn son. I told you, 'Let my son go, so he can worship me.' But since you refused, now I'ma take your firstborn son."'

24.text: While Moses and his family were stopped for the night, the Lord rolled up on him, ready to take him out.

25.text: But Zipporah, his wife, grabbed a flint knife, circumcised their son on the spot, and touched Moses' feet with the skin. She said, 'Now you a bridegroom of blood to me.'

26.text: (She was talkin' 'bout circumcision.) After that, the Lord backed off and left Moses alone.

27.text: Meanwhile, the Lord told Aaron, 'Go meet your brother in the wilderness.' So Aaron went and met Moses at the mountain of God, and they hugged it out.

28.text: Moses told Aaron everything the Lord said and showed him all the miracles they had to perform.

29.text: Then Moses and Aaron went back to Egypt and called all the elders of Israel together.

30.text: Aaron told them everything the Lord told Moses, and Moses performed the miracles right in front of them.

31.text: The people believed! And when they heard the Lord had seen their struggle and was about to free them, they bowed down and worshiped.

1.text: After Moses and Aaron spoke with Israel's leaders, they went to Pharaoh and said, 'This what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: Let my people go so they can hold a festival for me in the wilderness.'

2.text: Pharaoh snapped back, 'Oh, for real? And who this Lord y'all talkin' about? Why should I listen to Him and let Israel go? I don't know no Lord, and I ain't lettin' Israel go nowhere.'

3.text: But Moses and Aaron stood their ground, 'The God of the Hebrews met with us. We need to take a three-day trip into the wilderness to offer sacrifices to Him. If we don't, He gon' send a plague or bring the sword down on us.'

4.text: Pharaoh shook his head, 'Moses, Aaron, why y'all out here distracting these people from their work? Get back to it!'

5.text: 'Look, there's too many of y'all in this land, and now you tryna slow 'em down? Nah, get back to work!'

6.text: That same day, Pharaoh gave an order to the Egyptian slave drivers and the Israelite foremen.

7.text: 'Aye, stop givin' them straw for their bricks. Make 'em go get it theyself!'

8.text: 'But don't let up on the number of bricks they gotta make. Keep the quota the same. These folks lazy. That's why they out here talkin' 'bout, "Let us go worship our God."'

9.text: 'Make 'em work harder! Load 'em up till they too tired to listen to them lies.'

10.text: So the slave drivers and foremen went out and told the people, 'This what Pharaoh says: Y'all ain't gettin' no more straw.'

11.text: 'Go find it yourselves wherever you can, but you still gotta make the same amount of bricks!'

12.text: So the people scattered all over Egypt, tryna find anything they could use instead of straw.

13.text: Meanwhile, the Egyptian slave drivers kept pressing 'em, 'Y'all better hit that daily brick quota just like before, even without straw!'

14.text: Then they started beating the Israelite foremen they put in charge of the work crews. 'Why y'all ain't hit your brick numbers yesterday or today?!'

15.text: So the Israelite foremen went straight to Pharaoh and begged him, 'Please, don't treat us like this!'

16.text: 'We ain't gettin' no straw, but they still tellin' us, "Make bricks!" We gettin' beat, but this ain't even on us! Your own people the ones messin' up!'

17.text: But Pharaoh snapped, 'Nah, y'all just lazy! Lazy! That's why y'all keep askin' to go worship the Lord.'

18.text: 'Now get back to work! Ain't no straw comin', but y'all still gotta hit that full quota!'

19.text: The Israelite foremen walked outta there knowin' they was in serious trouble after Pharaoh told 'em, 'Don't reduce the number of bricks.'

20.text: As soon as they left Pharaoh's court, they ran into Moses and Aaron, who were waitin' outside.

21.text: They told them, 'Man, may the Lord judge y'all for this! Y'all done made us look bad in front of Pharaoh and his crew. Now they got a reason to kill us!'

22.text: Then Moses went back to the Lord and said, 'Lord, why You let this happen to Your people? Why You even send me?'

23.text: 'Ever since I went to Pharaoh like You told me, he been even more brutal to Your people. And You ain't done nothin' to rescue 'em!'

1.text: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Aight, now you about to see what I'ma do to Pharaoh. When he feel the power of My strong hand, he gon' let y'all go. Matter fact, he gon' be the one forcing y'all to leave!'

2.text: Then God said to Moses, 'I am Yahweh—the Lord.'

3.text: 'I showed up to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob as El-Shaddai—God Almighty—but I ain't reveal My name, Yahweh, to them.'

4.text: 'I made a covenant with them, and under that agreement, I promised to give them the land of Canaan, where they was living as foreigners.'

5.text: 'Best believe, I done heard the cries of My people in Egypt. They groanin' under slavery, and trust—I ain't forgot My promise to them.'

6.text: 'So tell Israel this: I am the Lord. I'ma free y'all from oppression, rescue y'all from slavery, and redeem y'all with My powerful hand and great acts of judgment.'

7.text: 'I'ma make y'all My people, and I'ma be your God. Then y'all gon' know that I am the Lord, y'all's God, the One who freed y'all from Egyptian oppression.'

8.text: 'I'ma bring y'all into the land I swore to Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob. I'ma give it to y'all as y'all own inheritance. I am the Lord!'

9.text: Moses went and told the Israelites what the Lord said, but they ain't even wanna hear it no more. They was too broke down from all the suffering and harsh slavery.

10.text: Then the Lord told Moses,

11.text: 'Go back to Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, and tell him to let My people leave his land.'

12.text: But Moses said, 'Lord, even my own people won't listen to me no more. How I'm supposed to make Pharaoh listen? I ain't even good at talkin'!'

13.text: But the Lord ain't let Moses off the hook. He gave orders to both Moses and Aaron about how they was gon' lead Israel outta Egypt, and what to say to Pharaoh.

14.text: Here go some of the ancestors of Israel's clans: Reuben, Israel's oldest son, had sons—Hanoch, Pallu, Hezron, and Carmi. Their descendants became the clans of Reuben.

15.text: The sons of Simeon were Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jakin, Zohar, and Shaul (whose mama was a Canaanite). Their descendants became the clans of Simeon.

16.text: These the descendants of Levi, written down in their family records: Levi's sons were Gershon, Kohath, and Merari. Levi lived 137 years.

17.text: The descendants of Gershon included Libni and Shimei, and their clans.

18.text: The descendants of Kohath included Amram, Izhar, Hebron, and Uzziel. Kohath lived 133 years.

19.text: The descendants of Merari included Mahli and Mushi. These was the Levite clans, listed in their family records.

20.text: Amram married his aunt Jochebed, and they had two sons—Aaron and Moses. Amram lived 137 years.

21.text: Izhar's sons were Korah, Nepheg, and Zicri.

22.text: Uzziel's sons were Mishael, Elzaphan, and Sithri.

23.text: Aaron married Elisheba, daughter of Amminadab and sister of Nahshon. They had sons—Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar.

24.text: Korah's sons were Assir, Elkanah, and Abiasaph. Their descendants became the clans of Korah.

25.text: Eleazar, son of Aaron, married a daughter of Putiel, and they had a son named Phinehas. These were the ancestors of the Levite families, listed by clans.

26.text: This Aaron and Moses in the list are the same ones the Lord told, 'Lead My people out of Egypt like an army.'

27.text: They the same ones who spoke to Pharaoh, the king of Egypt, about bringing Israel outta slavery.

28.text: When the Lord spoke to Moses in Egypt,

29.text: He told him, 'I am the Lord! Go tell Pharaoh everything I tell you.'

30.text: But Moses argued back, 'Lord, I can't do this! I don't talk right! Why would Pharaoh even listen to me?'

1.text: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Listen up. I'ma make you seem like God to Pharaoh, and Aaron gon' be your prophet.'

2.text: 'You tell Aaron everything I command you, and he gon' tell Pharaoh to let My people go.'

3.text: 'But I'ma make Pharaoh's heart stubborn so I can drop all My miracles and wonders across Egypt.'

4.text: 'Even then, Pharaoh ain't gon' listen. So I'ma hit Egypt hard. Then I'ma step in, bring My people—Israel—outta Egypt with serious judgment.'

5.text: 'And when I flex My power and bring Israel out, Egypt gon' know exactly who I am—the Lord.'

6.text: So Moses and Aaron did exactly what the Lord told 'em to do.

7.text: Moses was 80 years old, and Aaron was 83 when they rolled up on Pharaoh.

8.text: Then the Lord told Moses and Aaron,

9.text: 'Pharaoh gon' ask y'all to prove yourselves with a miracle. When he does, tell Aaron to throw his staff down in front of Pharaoh—it's gon' turn into a snake.'

10.text: So Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and did exactly what the Lord said. Aaron threw down his staff in front of Pharaoh and his officials, and—boom!—it turned into a snake!

11.text: Then Pharaoh called up his wise men, sorcerers, and magicians, and they did the same thing using their magic.

12.text: They threw down their staffs, and they turned into snakes too! But then Aaron's staff ate up all their staffs.

13.text: Still, Pharaoh wasn't fazed. His heart stayed hard, and just like the Lord said, he ain't listen.

14.text: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Pharaoh still got his heart locked up—he ain't tryna let the people go.'

15.text: 'So tomorrow morning, go meet him at the Nile River when he goin' down there. Take that staff that turned into a snake with you.'

16.text: 'Then tell him, "The Lord, the God of the Hebrews, sent me to tell you: Let My people go so they can worship Me in the wilderness. But you ain't listen."'

17.text: 'So now, this what the Lord says: "I'ma show you who I am. Watch—I'ma strike the Nile with this staff, and the whole river gon' turn to blood."'

18.text: 'The fish in it gon' die, the river gon' stink, and the Egyptians ain't gon' be able to drink from it.'

19.text: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Tell Aaron to lift up his staff and stretch it over all the waters of Egypt—the rivers, canals, ponds, and reservoirs. Turn all of it to blood, even the water sittin' in wooden bowls and stone pots.'

20.text: So Moses and Aaron did just what the Lord commanded. While Pharaoh and his officials watched, Aaron raised his staff and hit the Nile—and just like that, the whole river turned to blood!

21.text: The fish died, the river stank, and the Egyptians couldn't drink from it. Blood was everywhere in Egypt.

22.text: But Pharaoh's magicians did the same thing with their tricks, so Pharaoh's heart stayed hard. He refused to listen to Moses and Aaron, just like the Lord had said.

23.text: Pharaoh just went back to his palace like it was nothin'. Didn't even let it bother him.

24.text: Meanwhile, the Egyptians had to start digging along the riverbank just to find drinking water, 'cause the Nile was useless.

25.text: This plague lasted a whole seven days from when the Lord hit the Nile.

1.text: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Go back to Pharaoh and tell him, "This what the Lord says: Let My people go so they can worship Me."'

2.text: 'If you don't, I'ma send a plague of frogs all over your land.'

3.text: 'The Nile gon' be crawling with frogs—they comin' up out the river into your palace, your bedroom, even on your bed! They gon' be in your officials' houses, your people's houses, even hoppin' in y'all's ovens and kneading bowls.'

4.text: 'Frogs gon' be all over you, your people, and your officials—ain't no escaping 'em.'

5.text: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Tell Aaron to raise his staff over all the waters of Egypt—rivers, canals, and ponds—and bring up frogs all over the land.'

6.text: So Aaron stretched out his hand over the waters, and just like that—frogs swarmed everywhere, covering Egypt!

7.text: But Pharaoh's magicians pulled the same trick with their magic—they brought up more frogs too!

8.text: Then Pharaoh called Moses and Aaron, beggin', 'Yo, ask the Lord to take these frogs away from me and my people! If you do, I'ma let y'all go worship the Lord.'

9.text: Moses said, 'Alright, you tell me when you want me to pray for you, your officials, and your people so the frogs bounce out and stay only in the Nile.'

10.text: 'Tomorrow,' Pharaoh said. Moses replied, 'Bet. Just like you said. Then you'll know ain't nobody like the Lord our God.'

11.text: 'The frogs gon' be gone from you, your houses, your officials, and your people. They only gon' stay in the Nile.'

12.text: So Moses and Aaron left Pharaoh's palace, and Moses cried out to the Lord about the frogs.

13.text: And the Lord did exactly what Moses asked—frogs in the houses, courtyards, and fields all dropped dead.

14.text: The Egyptians piled 'em up into big ol' heaps, and the whole land started smelling rank.

15.text: But soon as Pharaoh saw relief, he went right back to being stubborn. He ain't listen to Moses and Aaron, just like the Lord said he wouldn't.

16.text: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Tell Aaron to raise his staff and strike the ground—the dust gon' turn into gnats all over Egypt.'

17.text: So Moses and Aaron did exactly what the Lord said. Aaron hit the ground with his staff, and boom—gnats swarmed the whole land, coverin' up the Egyptians and their animals. The dust all over Egypt turned into gnats.

18.text: Pharaoh's magicians tried to pull the same move, but this time they failed. Gnats was all over everybody—people and animals alike.

19.text: The magicians went to Pharaoh and said, 'Yo, this the finger of God!' But Pharaoh's heart stayed hard. He still wouldn't listen, just like the Lord predicted.

20.text: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Get up early and go block Pharaoh when he head to the river. Tell him, "This what the Lord says: Let My people go so they can worship Me."'

21.text: 'If you don't, I'ma send swarms of flies all over you, your officials, your people, and your houses. The whole land gon' be crawling with flies.'

22.text: 'But this time, I'ma do something different—I'ma spare Goshen, where My people live. No flies gon' be there. Then you'll know I'm the Lord, right here in the middle of Egypt.'

23.text: 'I'ma make it real clear—there's a difference between My people and yours. This miracle happenin' tomorrow.'

24.text: And the Lord did just that. Swarms of flies flooded Pharaoh's palace, his officials' houses—flies everywhere. The whole land of Egypt was straight-up chaotic.

25.text: Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron and said, 'Aight! Go ahead and sacrifice to your God—but do it here in Egypt.'

26.text: Moses said, 'Nah, that ain't gon' work. The Egyptians don't mess with the sacrifices we make to the Lord. If we do that here where they can see us, they gon' stone us!'

27.text: 'We need to take a three-day trip into the wilderness to offer sacrifices to the Lord, just like He told us to.'

28.text: Pharaoh said, 'Aight, fine. Y'all can go sacrifice in the wilderness, just don't go too far. But hurry up and pray for me.'

29.text: Moses said, 'Aight, soon as I leave, I'ma pray to the Lord, and by tomorrow all the flies gon' be gone from you, your officials, and your people. But Pharaoh, I'm warning you—don't play us again and refuse to let us go worship the Lord.'

30.text: So Moses left Pharaoh's palace and prayed to the Lord.

31.text: And the Lord did exactly what Moses asked—every last fly disappeared from Pharaoh, his officials, and his people. Not a single one left.

32.text: But guess what? Pharaoh turned stubborn again. He refused to let the people go.

1.text: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Go back to Pharaoh and tell him, "This what the Lord, the God of the Hebrews, says: Let My people go so they can worship Me."'

2.text: 'If you keep holdin' on to them and won't let 'em go…'

3.text: 'Then My hand gon' strike all your livestock—your horses, donkeys, camels, cattle, sheep, and goats—with a deadly plague.'

4.text: 'But I'ma make sure there's a difference between Israel's animals and Egypt's animals. Not a single one of theirs gon' die!'

5.text: 'The Lord already set the time—tomorrow, this plague comin' down on Egypt.'

6.text: And just like that, the next morning, all the Egyptian livestock died—but not a single Israelite animal was lost.

7.text: Pharaoh sent his officials to check, and sure enough, not one of Israel's animals was dead! But Pharaoh? He still kept his heart hard and wouldn't let the people go.

8.text: Then the Lord told Moses and Aaron, 'Scoop up some soot from a brick kiln, and Moses, toss it in the air while Pharaoh watchin'.'

9.text: 'That ash gon' turn into fine dust spreadin' over Egypt, and next thing you know, boils gon' break out all over people and animals.'

10.text: So they took soot from a kiln and went before Pharaoh. Moses threw it in the air, and boils broke out all over the people and animals alike.

11.text: Even Pharaoh's magicians couldn't stand up, 'cause they was covered in boils just like the rest of Egypt.

12.text: But the Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart, and just like He told Moses before, Pharaoh refused to listen.

13.text: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Get up early in the morning, go stand in Pharaoh's way, and tell him: "This what the Lord, the God of the Hebrews, says: Let My people go so they can worship Me."'

14.text: 'If you don't, I'ma send more plagues on you, your officials, and your people. Then y'all gon' know ain't nobody like Me in all the earth.'

15.text: 'By now, I coulda wiped y'all off the face of the earth with one plague.'

16.text: 'But I let you live for a reason—to show My power and make sure My name gets known all over the world.'

17.text: 'But you still out here actin' like you runnin' things and won't let My people go.'

18.text: 'So tomorrow around this time, I'ma send a hailstorm worse than anything Egypt ever seen.'
