19.text: 'Go on and tell your people—bring in the livestock and servants from the fields. Anybody still outside when the hail comes gon' be wiped out.'

20.text: Some of Pharaoh's officials actually feared what the Lord said, so they hurried to get their servants and animals inside.

21.text: But the ones who ain't care left their people and livestock out in the open.

22.text: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Lift up your hand toward the sky so hail can fall all over Egypt—on the people, the livestock, and all the plants in the fields.'

23.text: So Moses lifted his staff up to the sky, and the Lord sent thunder and hail. Lightning flashed everywhere. A massive storm hit Egypt like never before.

24.text: A hailstorm like this had never been seen in all of Egypt's history. It was heavy hail mixed with constant lightning.

25.text: Everything out in the open—people, animals, and plants—got struck down. Even the trees got wrecked.

26.text: Only place where no hail fell? Goshen—where God's people, Israel, lived.

27.text: Then Pharaoh sent for Moses and Aaron, talkin' 'bout, 'Aight, I messed up this time. The Lord is right, and me and my people? We dead wrong.'

28.text: 'Please ask the Lord to stop this terrifying thunder and hail! I'll let y'all go, no need to stay any longer!'

29.text: Moses said, 'Aight. Soon as I leave the city, I'ma lift my hands up and pray. The thunder and hail gon' stop, and then you gon' know the earth belongs to the Lord.'

30.text: 'But I already know—you and your officials still don't fear the Lord for real.'

31.text: (The flax and barley crops got wrecked 'cause they was already growing.)

32.text: (But the wheat and emmer wheat was spared since they hadn't sprouted yet.)

33.text: So Moses left Pharaoh's court, went out the city, and lifted his hands up to the Lord. The thunder, hail, and downpour stopped instantly.

34.text: But soon as Pharaoh saw the storm was over, he went right back to his old ways—him and his officials sinned again and stayed stubborn.

35.text: Pharaoh's heart stayed hard. He still wouldn't let the Israelites go, just like the Lord told Moses he wouldn't.

1.text: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Go back to Pharaoh and tell him again what I said. I done made him and his officials stubborn just so I can show out with My miracles.'

2.text: 'And I did this so you can tell your kids and grandkids how I clowned the Egyptians, showin' My power—so you know I'm the Lord.'

3.text: So Moses and Aaron went to Pharaoh and said, 'This what the Lord, the God of the Hebrews, says: How long you gon' keep refusin' to humble yourself? Let My people go so they can worship Me.'

4.text: 'If you don't, listen up—tomorrow, I'ma send a swarm of locusts across this whole country.'

5.text: 'They gon' be everywhere, so thick you won't even see the ground. They gon' eat up whatever's left after that hailstorm, even all the trees in the fields.'

6.text: 'They gon' overrun your palace, your officials' houses, and all the homes in Egypt. Ain't nobody ever seen a plague like this in the history of Egypt!' And with that, Moses turned and walked out.

7.text: Pharaoh's officials turned to him like, 'How long you gon' let this man ruin us? Just let them men go worship the Lord their God! You don't see Egypt already in shambles?!'

8.text: So Pharaoh had Moses and Aaron brought back in and said, 'Alright, go worship the Lord your God. But who exactly tryna go?'

9.text: Moses said, 'All of us—young and old, sons and daughters, plus our flocks and herds. We all need to go worship the Lord together.'

10.text: Pharaoh shot back, 'The Lord betta be with y'all if I let you take your little ones! I see right through you—y'all got some evil plan!'

11.text: 'Never! Only the men can go worship, since that's what you asked for.' And Pharaoh had them thrown out the palace.

12.text: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Raise your hand over Egypt to bring on the locusts. Let 'em cover the land and eat whatever's left from the hail.'

13.text: So Moses lifted his staff, and the Lord sent an east wind over Egypt all day and all night. By morning, the locusts had arrived.

14.text: They swarmed the whole land, covering every inch of Egypt. It was the worst locust plague in history—ain't never been one like it since.

15.text: The locusts covered everything, darkening the land. They ate every last plant and all the fruit left on the trees after the hailstorm. Not a single leaf was left in all of Egypt.

16.text: Pharaoh quickly called for Moses and Aaron and said, 'I messed up. I sinned against the Lord your God and against you.'

17.text: 'Please forgive me this one time and pray to the Lord your God to take this death away from me!'

18.text: So Moses left Pharaoh's court and pleaded with the Lord.

19.text: The Lord shifted the wind, and a strong west wind blew the locusts into the Red Sea. Not a single locust remained in Egypt.

20.text: But the Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart again, and he still wouldn't let the people go.

21.text: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Lift your hand toward the sky, and Egypt gon' be covered in a darkness so thick you can feel it.'

22.text: So Moses raised his hand, and darkness fell over Egypt for three whole days.

23.text: Ain't nobody could see each other, and folks just sat still the whole time. But in Goshen, where Israel lived, there was still light.

24.text: Finally, Pharaoh called for Moses and said, 'Fine! Y'all can go worship the Lord. Take your little ones, too—but leave your flocks and herds behind.'

25.text: Moses said, 'Nah, Pharaoh, you gotta give us animals for sacrifices and burnt offerings to the Lord our God.'

26.text: 'All our livestock comin' with us—ain't leavin' a single hoof behind. We don't know what we gotta sacrifice 'til we get there.'

27.text: But the Lord hardened Pharaoh's heart again, and he still refused to let them go.

28.text: Pharaoh snapped, 'Get out my face! I'm warning you—don't ever come back here again! The day you see me again, you gon' die!'

29.text: Moses said, 'Bet. You right. I ain't ever gon' see your face again.'

1.text: Then the Lord told Moses, 'I'ma hit Pharaoh and Egypt with one last blow. After that, Pharaoh gon' let y'all go. Matter fact, he gon' be so ready to get rid of y'all, he gon' force y'all out.'

2.text: 'Tell all the Israelite men and women to ask their Egyptian neighbors for gold and silver jewelry.'

3.text: (The Lord had already made the Egyptians look at Israel real different—showin' 'em favor. And Moses? Man, he was seen as a big deal in Egypt, respected by Pharaoh's officials and the people.)

4.text: Then Moses told Pharaoh, 'This what the Lord says: At midnight tonight, I'ma pass through Egypt.'

5.text: 'Every firstborn son in Egypt gon' die—from Pharaoh's oldest son, sittin' on the throne, to the firstborn of the lowest servant girl grinding flour. Even the firstborn of the livestock ain't gon' make it.'

6.text: 'It's gon' be a cry through Egypt so loud, so painful, ain't never been one like it before and won't ever be one like it again.'

7.text: 'But over in Israel? Not even a dog gon' be barkin'. That's when y'all gon' see clear as day—the Lord makes a difference between Egypt and Israel.'

8.text: 'All your officials, Pharaoh, gon' run to me, beggin', "Please, leave! Hurry up! Take everybody with you!" And then I'ma go!' And with that, Moses stormed out, mad as hell.

9.text: (Now the Lord had already told Moses before, 'Pharaoh ain't gon' listen, but that just means I'ma do even more mighty miracles in Egypt.')

10.text: Moses and Aaron had already performed these miracles right in Pharaoh's face, but the Lord kept his heart hard, so he still wouldn't let Israel leave.

1.text: While the Israelites was still in Egypt, the Lord gave Moses and Aaron these instructions.

2.text: 'From now on, this month right here gon' be the first month of the year for y'all.'

3.text: 'Tell the whole community of Israel: on the tenth day of this month, every family gotta pick out a lamb or young goat for sacrifice—one animal per household.'

4.text: 'If a family too small to eat a whole animal, they need to link up with their neighbors. Make sure the portions match how much each family can eat.'

5.text: 'The animal y'all pick gotta be a one-year-old male, whether it's a sheep or goat—no defects allowed.'

6.text: 'Take good care of this animal until the evening of the fourteenth day of the first month. That's when the whole community of Israel gotta come together and slaughter their lamb or goat at twilight.'

7.text: 'Then y'all gotta take some of the blood and smear it on the sides and top of the doorframes of the houses where y'all gon' eat the meal.'

8.text: 'That same night, roast the meat over a fire and eat it with bitter herbs and flatbread with no yeast.'

9.text: 'Don't eat none of it raw or boiled. The whole thing—head, legs, and inside parts—gotta be roasted over the fire.'

10.text: 'And don't leave nothin' until morning. If there's any leftovers, burn it up before the sun come up.'

11.text: 'Now here's how y'all gotta eat it: be dressed and ready, got your sandals on, and hold your walking stick. Eat it quick, 'cause this right here is the Lord's Passover.'

12.text: 'That night, I'ma pass through Egypt and take out every firstborn son—from Pharaoh's son on the throne to the son of the lowest servant girl. Even the firstborn of the animals ain't safe.'

13.text: 'But when I see the blood on y'all doorframes, I'ma pass over that house. This plague of death ain't gon' touch y'all when I come through Egypt.'

14.text: 'Y'all gotta remember this day. Every year, from generation to generation, y'all gotta celebrate it as a festival to honor the Lord. This a law forever.'

15.text: 'For seven days, eat bread with no yeast. On the first day, clear out every bit of yeast from y'all houses. If somebody eat bread with yeast in it during these seven days, they out the Israelite community.'

16.text: 'On the first and seventh day, hold a holy assembly. Ain't no work allowed on these days—except cookin' food.'

17.text: 'Celebrate the Festival of Unleavened Bread 'cause this gon' remind y'all how I brought y'all outta Egypt on this day. This law right here? It's permanent—celebrate it every year.'

18.text: 'From the evening of the fourteenth day to the twenty-first day of this first month, eat only unleavened bread.'

19.text: 'For seven days, don't let no yeast be found in y'all houses. If anybody eats somethin' with yeast in it, they out the Israelite community—don't matter if they native-born or foreign.'

20.text: 'During these days, y'all can't eat nothin' with yeast. Wherever y'all stayin', only eat unleavened bread.'

21.text: Then Moses called all Israel's elders together and said, 'Go on and pick a lamb or young goat for each family and slaughter the Passover animal.'

22.text: 'Drain the blood into a basin. Take some hyssop branches, dip it in the blood, and brush it on the top and sides of the doorframes. And nobody can step outside 'til morning.'

23.text: 'The Lord gon' pass through Egypt to strike down the firstborns, but when He sees the blood on y'all doorframes, He gon' pass over y'all houses. He won't let the death angel touch y'all.'

24.text: 'Y'all better remember these instructions. This a permanent law for y'all and y'all kids.'

25.text: 'When y'all get to the land the Lord promised y'all, keep doin' this ceremony.'

26.text: 'And when y'all kids ask, "Why we doin' this?"'

27.text: 'Tell 'em, "This the Passover sacrifice to the Lord, 'cause He passed over Israelite houses in Egypt. He struck down the Egyptians but spared us!"' Then everybody bowed down and worshiped.

28.text: So the Israelites did everything exactly how the Lord told Moses and Aaron.

29.text: That night, at midnight, the Lord struck every firstborn son in Egypt—from Pharaoh's son on the throne to the firstborn of prisoners in the dungeon. Even the firstborn of their animals was killed.

30.text: Pharaoh, his officials, and all the Egyptians woke up in shock. Loud wailing was heard all over Egypt. Every house had somebody dead.

31.text: That night, Pharaoh called for Moses and Aaron. 'Get out! Take the rest of your people with you! Go worship the Lord like y'all said!'

32.text: 'Take your animals, too! Just leave! But… bless me before y'all go.'

33.text: All the Egyptians begged Israel to leave quickly, 'cause they was scared everybody in Egypt was gon' die.

34.text: The Israelites grabbed their bread dough before it had yeast, wrapped their kneading boards in their cloaks, and carried 'em on their shoulders.

35.text: The people of Israel did exactly what Moses told them. They asked the Egyptians for silver, gold, and clothes.

36.text: The Lord made the Egyptians favor the Israelites, so they gave 'em whatever they asked for. Israel left Egypt rich!

37.text: That night, Israel left Rameses and started for Succoth—600,000 men plus women and children!

38.text: Some non-Israelites tagged along, too, plus a whole lotta livestock.

39.text: They made flatbread 'cause they ain't had time to let their dough rise before they was forced to leave.

40.text: The Israelites had lived in Egypt for 430 years.

41.text: And on the last day of that 430th year, the Lord's people left Egypt just like He promised.

42.text: That night, the Lord was keepin' watch as His people left Egypt. So every generation gotta commemorate this night—this the Lord's night!

43.text: Then the Lord told Moses and Aaron, 'These are the rules for Passover: No outsiders can eat the meal.'

44.text: 'But if a slave gets circumcised, he can eat it.'

45.text: 'Temporary workers and visitors? Nah, they can't eat it.'

46.text: 'Each Passover lamb gotta be eaten in one house. Don't take the meat outside. Don't break its bones.'

47.text: 'The whole Israelite community gotta celebrate Passover.'

48.text: 'If foreigners wanna celebrate, all their males gotta be circumcised first. Then they can join like they was native-born.'

49.text: 'Same law applies to everybody—native-born and foreigners who live with y'all.'

50.text: So the Israelites followed every command from the Lord to Moses and Aaron.

51.text: And on that very day, the Lord brought all His people outta Egypt like an army!

1.text: Then the Lord told Moses,

2.text: 'Every firstborn child and firstborn animal in Israel? They mine. Dedicate 'em to me, 'cause they belong to me.'

3.text: So Moses told the people, 'Y'all better remember this day forever—the day the Lord brought y'all outta Egypt, outta slavery, with his mighty power. (And don't be eatin' no bread with yeast, either.)'

4.text: 'On this very day, in the spring month of Abib, the Lord set y'all free.'

5.text: 'When the Lord brings y'all into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Hivites, and Jebusites—the land flowin' with milk and honey that He promised to your ancestors—y'all gotta celebrate this event every year.'

6.text: 'For seven days, eat bread without yeast, and on the seventh day, hold a big ol' feast to the Lord.'

7.text: 'For the whole week, no yeast should be in your food. Matter fact, don't even let no yeast be in your land during this time.'

8.text: 'And when y'all kids ask why we do this, tell 'em, "I'm celebratin' what the Lord did for me when He brought me outta Egypt."'

9.text: 'This festival right here? It's gon' be a reminder for y'all, like a mark on your hand or forehead, so you always remember to keep God's laws. 'Cause with His strong hand, the Lord brought y'all outta Egypt.'

10.text: 'So make sure y'all do this every year, at the time the Lord set.'

11.text: 'Now, when the Lord keeps His promise and brings y'all into the land where the Canaanites live,'

12.text: 'Y'all gotta give every firstborn son and every firstborn male animal to the Lord, 'cause they belong to Him.'

13.text: 'If you got a firstborn donkey, you gotta buy it back with a lamb or goat. But if you don't buy it back, you gotta break its neck. And every firstborn son? You gotta buy him back.'

14.text: 'Later on, when your kids ask, "Why we doin' all this?" tell 'em, "The Lord brought us outta Egypt with His strong hand."'

15.text: 'Since Pharaoh ain't wanna let us go, the Lord took out every firstborn male in Egypt—both humans and animals. That's why we sacrifice the firstborn males to the Lord, but we buy back our firstborn sons.'

16.text: 'And just like before, this ceremony gon' be a reminder—like a mark on your hand or forehead—of how strong the Lord's hand was when He freed us from Egypt.'

17.text: Now when Pharaoh finally let the people go, God ain't take 'em on the main road through Philistine land, even though it was the shortest route. God said, 'If they run into a battle, they might get scared and run back to Egypt.'

18.text: So God took 'em the long way, through the wilderness, toward the Red Sea. The Israelites left lookin' like an army, ready for battle.

19.text: And Moses made sure to grab Joseph's bones, 'cause Joseph had told Israel's sons, 'God gon' come through for y'all one day. And when He do, take my bones outta Egypt with you.'

20.text: The Israelites left Succoth and set up camp in Etham, on the edge of the wilderness.

21.text: The Lord Himself led the way. During the day, He was a pillar of cloud to guide 'em, and at night, He was a pillar of fire to give 'em light. That way, they could travel day or night.

22.text: And the Lord never left them—that cloud stayed in front of 'em by day, and that fire kept burning at night.

1.text: Then the Lord told Moses,

2.text: 'Tell the Israelites to turn around and camp near Pi-hahiroth, between Migdol and the sea. Set up right across from Baal-zephon, by the shore.'

3.text: 'Pharaoh gon' think, 'These folks lost! They trapped in the wilderness!'

4.text: 'And once again, I'ma harden Pharaoh's heart so he chase after y'all. But I got a plan—to show out through Pharaoh and his whole army, so everybody in Egypt gon' know I'm the Lord.' So the Israelites set up camp just like they was told.

5.text: Word got back to Pharaoh that the Israelites dipped, and he and his officials was big mad. 'What did we just do? We let our slaves go!'

6.text: So Pharaoh had his chariot prepared, and he called up his troops.

7.text: He rolled out with 600 of his best chariots, plus all the other chariots in Egypt, each one with its own commander.

8.text: The Lord made Pharaoh's heart stubborn, so he took off after the Israelites, who had left Egypt with their fists raised—knowin' they was free.

9.text: Pharaoh and his army rolled up on 'em—all his horses, chariots, and soldiers. They caught the Israelites camped out by the sea, near Pi-hahiroth, across from Baal-zephon.

10.text: When Pharaoh got close, the Israelites looked up and freaked out. The Egyptians was pullin' up fast, so they cried out to the Lord.

11.text: They told Moses, 'Man, why you bring us out here to die in the wilderness?! Ain't enough graves in Egypt for us?! Why you do us like this?!'

12.text: 'Ain't we tell you back in Egypt to leave us alone? We said, 'Let us stay slaves in Egypt—better than dyin' out here!'

13.text: But Moses told 'em, 'Don't be scared! Just stand still and watch how the Lord gon' rescue you today. These Egyptians? You ain't never gon' see 'em again!'

14.text: 'The Lord Himself gon' fight for you. Just stay cool.'

15.text: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Why you cryin' to me? Tell the people to move!'

16.text: 'Lift up your staff, stretch out your hand over the sea, and split the waters. The Israelites gon' walk through on dry ground.'

17.text: 'I'ma harden the Egyptians' hearts so they chase y'all in. But I'ma show out through Pharaoh, his army, his chariots, and his charioteers.'

18.text: 'When I do this, all Egypt gon' know I'm the Lord.'

19.text: Then the angel of God that was leadin' the Israelites moved to the back of the camp. The pillar of cloud moved back with him.

20.text: The cloud came between the Egyptians and the Israelites. Darkness fell over the Egyptians, but the Israelites still had light. So the two sides ain't get close to each other all night.

21.text: Then Moses raised his hand over the sea, and the Lord sent a strong east wind all night, splitting the sea and making the seabed dry land.

22.text: The Israelites walked through the middle of the sea on dry ground, with walls of water standin' on both sides!

23.text: Then Pharaoh's army—his horses, chariots, and charioteers—chased 'em right into the middle of the sea.

24.text: But just before sunrise, the Lord looked down at the Egyptian army from the pillar of fire and cloud—and threw 'em into confusion!

25.text: He jammed up their chariot wheels, so they was strugglin' to drive. The Egyptians started yelling, 'Let's get outta here! The Lord fightin' for them!'

26.text: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Raise your hand over the sea again. The waters gon' rush back and cover the Egyptians, their chariots, and charioteers.'

27.text: As the sun came up, Moses lifted his hand, and the waters crashed back into place. The Egyptians tried to run, but the Lord drowned 'em all.

28.text: The whole army that had chased the Israelites into the sea? Gone. Not a single one survived.

29.text: But the Israelites? They walked through on dry ground, with walls of water still standin' beside them.

30.text: That's how the Lord rescued Israel from the Egyptians that day. The Israelites saw the Egyptians' bodies wash up on the shore.

31.text: When they saw the mighty power the Lord flexed against Egypt, they was in awe. They put their faith in the Lord and trusted Moses as His servant.

1.text: Then Moses and the Israelites broke out in song, singin' to the Lord: 'I'ma sing to the Lord, 'Cause He done showed out! He tossed Pharaoh's horses & riders Straight into the sea!'

2.text: 'The Lord my strength, my song, My victory come from Him! This my God—best believe I'ma praise Him, My folks' God, and I'ma lift Him up!'

3.text: 'The Lord? Oh, He a warrior. His name? Yahweh!'

4.text: 'Pharaoh's chariots and army? Yeah, He flung 'em into the sea. His top officers? They sank in the Red Sea like bricks.'

5.text: 'Deep waters rushed over 'em, They dropped like a stone.'

6.text: 'Your right hand, Lord? Powerful! Your right hand, Lord? Crushed the enemy!'

7.text: 'You in full majesty mode, Takin' down anybody who step up. Your fire of fury? Burn 'em up like dry grass.'

8.text: 'One breath from You? The waters stacked up! Waves stood tall like walls, The sea turned solid in the middle.'

9.text: 'The enemy was talkin' big, Sayin', 'We 'bout to chase 'em down! We 'bout to take 'em out and split up their stuff! We 'bout to pull swords on 'em!'

10.text: 'But then You breathed, Lord, And the waters crashed down. They sank like lead weights in the sea.'

11.text: 'Lord, who like You among the gods? Ain't nobody got Your holiness, Your glory, Or the power You showin' off!'

12.text: 'You lifted Your right hand, And the earth swallowed our enemies.'

13.text: 'With unbreakable love, You lead Your people, The ones You saved! With Your power, You guide 'em home.'

14.text: 'Other nations hear about this and start shakin'. Folks in Philistia got fear in they hearts.'

15.text: 'Leaders in Edom shook, The nobles in Moab got no courage left. Canaanites? They straight-up terrified.'

16.text: 'They froze up in fear, Scared stiff 'til Your people pass by, Lord. Until Your chosen ones walk through.'

17.text: 'You gon' bring 'em home And plant 'em in Your holy place, The spot You set aside for Yourself, The sanctuary You built, Lord.'

18.text: 'The Lord gon' reign forever—no end to this!'

19.text: When Pharaoh's army came chargin' in—horses, chariots, and all— The Lord brought the sea down on 'em. But the Israelites? They walked through on dry land!

20.text: Then Miriam the prophet, Aaron's sister, grabbed a tambourine And led all the women in music & dance.

21.text: Miriam sang: 'Sing to the Lord, 'Cause He done showed out! He flung Pharaoh's horses & riders Straight into the sea!'

22.text: Moses led the Israelites away from the Red Sea And into the Shur wilderness. They traveled three days— No water in sight.

23.text: Then they found an oasis at Marah, But the water? Too bitter to drink. That's why they called it Marah (means 'bitter').

24.text: So the people got mad, Turned on Moses: 'What we 'posed to drink, huh?!'

25.text: Moses called out to the Lord, And the Lord showed him a piece of wood. Moses threw it in the water— Water turned fresh. That's when the Lord laid out a test for His people.

26.text: He told 'em: 'Listen close. If y'all really follow me, If y'all do what's right, Obey what I say— I ain't gon' hit you with none of the diseases I sent to Egypt. 'Cause I'm the Lord who heals you.'

27.text: After Marah, the Israelites moved on to Elim— A place with 12 fresh springs and 70 palm trees. So they set up camp right by the water.

1.text: So the whole Israelite crew packed up from Elim and headed out into the wilderness of Sin—somewhere between Elim and Mount Sinai. They got there on the fifteenth day of the second month, just a month after leavin' Egypt.

2.text: But look—same old thing. The whole crew startin' to complain again 'bout Moses & Aaron.

3.text: 'Man, if only the Lord had just let us die in Egypt!' they moaned. 'We was sittin' there full, eatin' meat and bread for days. Now y'all done brought us out here in the wilderness to starve!'

4.text: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Bet. I'm 'bout to rain down food from the sky. Y'all can pick up as much as you need for the day. But this right here a test—to see if they gon' listen to what I say.'

5.text: 'On the sixth day, they gotta gather up double the amount so they got enough to last.'

6.text: So Moses & Aaron told the whole crew, 'By tonight, y'all gon' realize it was the Lord who brought y'all outta Egypt.'

7.text: 'And in the morning, y'all gon' see His glory—'cause He heard y'all complainin'. But let's be real—y'all ain't complainin' 'bout us. Y'all complainin' 'bout Him.'

8.text: Then Moses added, 'The Lord gon' drop meat for y'all in the evening and bread in the morning—'cause He heard all y'all complaints. But again, let's be clear—y'all ain't mad at us. Y'all mad at the Lord.'

9.text: Then Moses told Aaron, 'Tell everybody, pull up & stand before the Lord. He heard y'all fussin'.'

10.text: And just like that, as Aaron was talkin', they looked out at the wilderness, and boom—God's glory was right there in the cloud.

11.text: Then the Lord told Moses:

12.text: 'I done heard 'em fussin' long enough. Go tell 'em—tonight, they gon' eat meat, and in the morning, they gon' get all the bread they want. Then they'll finally get it—I am the Lord.'

13.text: That evening, a whole swarm of quail flew in and covered the camp. Then by morning, dew covered the ground.

14.text: And when the dew dried up, there was this flaky stuff all over the place, like frost on the ground.

15.text: The Israelites was like, 'What is this?'—they ain't know what it was. Moses told 'em, 'This the food the Lord gave y'all to eat.'

16.text: 'And here's the rule—get what you need, two quarts per person, per tent.'

17.text: So everybody went out to gather it—some got a lot, some only a little.

18.text: But when they measured it out, everybody had just enough. Nobody had too much or too little.

19.text: Then Moses told 'em, 'Don't keep none till the mornin'!'

20.text: But some ain't listen—tried to keep some overnight. By mornin'? It was full of maggots & stinkin'. Moses was big mad.

21.text: So from then on, they gathered it every morning, just what they needed. But when the sun got hot, anything left on the ground melted away.

22.text: On the sixth day, they picked up twice as much—four quarts per person. All the leaders came to Moses like, 'Yo, what's this about?'

23.text: Moses told 'em, 'This what the Lord say—Tomorrow's the Sabbath. Ain't no food comin', so cook what you need today and set the rest aside for tomorrow.'

24.text: So they put some up for later—and this time it ain't rot or stink.

25.text: Moses said, 'See? Eat it today. It's the Lord's Sabbath. Ain't gon' be nothin' on the ground today.'

26.text: 'Six days y'all can gather food, but on the seventh day, ain't gon' be nothin' there.'

27.text: Still, some of 'em tried to go out on the Sabbath to get food—they found nothin'.

28.text: Then the Lord was like, 'How long y'all gon' keep ignorin' what I say?'

29.text: 'Y'all need to understand—this Sabbath is My gift to y'all. That's why I gave y'all twice the food on the sixth day. Stay home! Ain't no need to go out on the seventh day.'

30.text: So the people finally got it and stayed home on the Sabbath.

31.text: The Israelites called the food manna. It was white, lookin' like coriander seeds, and it tasted like honey biscuits.

32.text: Moses said, 'The Lord want y'all to keep some of this, so later generations can see the food He gave us when He brought us outta Egypt.'

33.text: Then Moses told Aaron, 'Take a jar, fill it with two quarts of manna, and keep it in a sacred place before the Lord.'

34.text: So Aaron did just that. Eventually, he put it in the Ark of the Covenant, right in front of the stone tablets of God's law.

35.text: The Israelites ate manna for 40 years, until they reached the land of Canaan.

36.text: The measurement they used—an omer—was about two quarts.

1.text: The whole Israelite crew followed the Lord's command, movin' from spot to spot through the wilderness of Sin. Eventually, they camped at Rephidim, but ain't no water out there to drink.

2.text: So, like always, the people started pressin' Moses again. 'We need water! Give us somethin' to drink!' they demanded. Moses snapped back, 'Man, calm down! Why y'all always fussin' at me? And why y'all keep testin' the Lord?'

3.text: But these folks was mad thirsty, so they kept arguin' with Moses. 'Man, why you even bring us outta Egypt? Tryin' to kill us, our kids, and all our animals with thirst?!'

4.text: So Moses straight up cried out to the Lord, 'What am I supposed to do with these people?! They 'bout ready to stone me!'

5.text: The Lord said, 'Aight, here's what you gon' do—step up in front of everybody, take that staff you used when you struck the Nile, and grab some of the elders to roll with you.'

6.text: 'I'ma be right there standin' on the rock at Mount Sinai. You gon' hit that rock, and water gon' come bustin' out so everybody can drink.' Moses did exactly what the Lord said, and water came gushin' out while the elders watched.

7.text: Moses named that place Massah (which means 'test') and Meribah (which means 'arguin'')—'cause the Israelites stayed arguin' with Moses and testin' the Lord, askin', 'Is God even here with us or not?'

8.text: While the Israelites was still at Rephidim, the Amalekites rolled up and attacked them.

9.text: Moses told Joshua, 'Pick some dudes to roll out and fight Amalek for us. Tomorrow, I'ma be up on the hill holdin' the staff of God.'

10.text: So Joshua did what Moses said and got his squad ready to fight. Meanwhile, Moses, Aaron, and Hur climbed up on a hill.

11.text: Check this—as long as Moses held up his staff, the Israelites was doin' good. But whenever he dropped his hands, the Amalekites started winnin' the fight.

12.text: Moses' arms got tired, and he couldn't hold 'em up no more. So Aaron and Hur grabbed a stone for him to sit on, then they held up his arms, one on each side. His hands stayed steady all the way till sunset.

13.text: Joshua and his squad straight up crushed the Amalekites in battle.

14.text: After the fight, the Lord told Moses, 'Write this down so folks don't forget. Read it to Joshua—I'ma erase the memory of Amalek from the earth.'

15.text: Moses built an altar and called it Yahweh-Nissi (which means 'The Lord is my banner').

16.text: Then he said, 'These folks came for the Lord's people, so now God gon' be at war with Amalek forever.'

1.text: Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, who was the priest of Midian, heard all 'bout what God had done for Moses and the Israelites. Especially how the Lord brought 'em up outta Egypt.

2.text: Moses had sent his wife, Zipporah, and his two sons back to Jethro, and Jethro had been lookin' after them.

3.text: (Moses' first son was Gershom, 'cause Moses said, 'I been a foreigner in a land that ain't mine.'

4.text: His second son was Eliezer, 'cause Moses said, 'The God of my ancestors had my back and saved me from Pharaoh's sword.')

5.text: Jethro, Moses' father-in-law, came to visit Moses out in the wilderness, bringing Zipporah and the two boys with him. They pulled up near the mountain of God.

6.text: Jethro sent Moses a message: 'Yo, I'm on my way to see you. I got your wife and kids with me.'

7.text: Moses went out to meet him, bowed low, and gave him a kiss of respect. They chopped it up, asked how each other was doing, then went into Moses' tent.

8.text: Moses broke it all down for Jethro—how the Lord took down Pharaoh, how He came through for Israel, and all the hardships they faced on the way. He told him how the Lord kept rescuing them.

9.text: Jethro was hyped when he heard all the good things the Lord had done for Israel, especially how He saved them from Egypt.

10.text: Jethro said, 'Praise the Lord! He really came through for y'all, snatchin' y'all outta Pharaoh's grip and outta Egypt's control.'

11.text: 'Now I know for sure that the Lord is the realest—greater than any other god! He put Egypt in check for all that oppression they was on.'

12.text: Then Jethro brought a burnt offering and sacrifices for God. Aaron and the elders of Israel came through and joined him for a sacrificial meal in God's presence.

13.text: The next day, Moses sat down to judge the people's problems. From morning 'til evening, folks lined up waiting on him.

14.text: When Jethro saw what was goin' down, he was like, 'Bruh, what is you doin'?! Why you tryna handle all this alone while everybody just stand around all day?'

15.text: Moses said, 'They come to me to get a ruling from God.'

16.text: 'Whenever folks got beef, they come to me. I settle it, tell 'em what God says, and teach 'em His laws and ways.'

17.text: Jethro said, 'Bruh, this ain't it.'

18.text: 'You gon' burn out, and the people too! This is way too much for one man to handle.'

19.text: 'Listen to me, I'ma put you on game—and may God be with you. You still gon' represent the people before God and bring their problems to Him.

20.text: 'Teach them God's laws, show them the way to live, and how to do right.'

21.text: 'But here's what you gotta do—pick out some solid men. Get some capable, honest dudes who fear God and don't take bribes. Put 'em over groups of 1,000, 100, 50, and 10.'

22.text: 'Let them handle the everyday disputes, but the big cases come to you. That way, you ain't doin' all the heavy liftin' alone.'

23.text: 'If you do this, and God cosigns it, you gon' last longer, and the people gon' be straight.'

24.text: Moses listened to Jethro's advice and put the plan in motion.

25.text: He picked out capable men, put 'em over groups, and made 'em leaders.

26.text: They started handling disputes on the daily, only bringing the serious ones to Moses.

27.text: After all that, Moses said goodbye to his father-in-law, and Jethro headed back home.

1.text: Two months after leavin' Egypt, the Israelites pulled up in the Sinai wilderness.

2.text: They left Rephidim, moved through the desert, and set up camp at the foot of Mount Sinai.

3.text: Moses climbed up the mountain to meet God. The Lord called out, 'Moses, tell the people of Israel this:'

4.text: 'Y'all saw what I did to the Egyptians. I carried y'all like eagles and brought you straight to me.'

5.text: 'Now, if y'all listen to me and keep this agreement, y'all gon' be my special treasure—set apart from every other nation. Everything in the world is mine, but y'all different.'

6.text: 'Y'all gon' be a kingdom of priests, a holy nation. That's what you tell Israel.'

7.text: Moses came down, gathered the elders, and told 'em what God said.

8.text: The people all said, 'We down for whatever the Lord says.' So Moses went back and told the Lord their answer.

9.text: Then the Lord told Moses, 'I'ma pull up in a thick cloud so the people can hear me talk to you. That way, they'll always trust what you say.'

10.text: Then the Lord said, 'Go prep the people. Get 'em clean today and tomorrow—have 'em wash their clothes.'

11.text: 'Tell 'em to be ready on the third day, 'cause that's when I'ma show up on Mount Sinai.'

12.text: 'Mark off a boundary around the mountain. Tell the people, "Don't cross this line! Don't even touch the mountain!" Anybody who does gon' die.'

13.text: 'Don't let nobody touch them—stone 'em or shoot 'em with arrows. But when y'all hear the ram's horn blow long, that's the cue—then folks can come up.'

14.text: So Moses went down, told the people to get right, and they washed their clothes.

15.text: He told them, 'Get ready for the third day, and don't be messin' around with your spouses until then.'

16.text: Early on the third day, thunder shook the sky, lightning flashed, and a thick cloud covered the mountain. A loud ram's horn blasted, and the people started trembling.

17.text: Moses led the people out the camp to meet God, and they stood at the base of Mount Sinai.

18.text: The whole mountain was covered in smoke 'cause the Lord came down in fire. The smoke shot up like from a brick oven, and the whole mountain was shakin'.

19.text: The ram's horn kept blasting louder and louder. Moses spoke, and God answered in thunder.

20.text: The Lord came down on top of Sinai and called Moses up. So Moses climbed up.

21.text: The Lord said, 'Go back down and warn the people—tell 'em not to try and sneak up to see me, or they gon' die.'

22.text: 'Even the priests that come close need to clean themselves up first. Otherwise, I'ma handle them too.'

23.text: Moses was like, 'Lord, we already set the boundary. You told me to mark off the mountain as holy.'

24.text: But the Lord said, 'Go get Aaron and bring him back up. But nobody else, not even the priests, better try to come up here, or they gon' be done for.'

25.text: So Moses went down, told the people exactly what God said.

1.text: Then God spoke up and gave 'em these rules:

2.text: 'I'm the Lord your God, the one who broke y'all outta Egypt, took y'all outta slavery.'

3.text: 'Ain't nobody else supposed to be your god but me.'

4.text: 'Don't be out here makin' idols, statues, or images of anything in the sky, on earth, or in the sea. None of that.'

5.text: 'Don't bow down to them or worship them 'cause I'm a jealous God. I ain't toleratin' y'all cheatin' on me with other gods. Mess up, and it ain't just you—it's gon' hit your kids too, all the way down to the third and fourth generation if y'all reject me.'

6.text: 'But stay loyal to me, follow my commands, and I'll bless a thousand generations of your people.'

7.text: 'Don't play with my name. Don't be out here uselessly swearin' on me. I ain't lettin' that slide.'

8.text: 'Keep the Sabbath holy—that's my day.'

9.text: 'Y'all got six days to handle business, to do all your regular work.'

10.text: 'But the seventh day? That's my day. No work. That goes for you, your kids, your workers, your animals— even the foreigners in your land.'

11.text: 'I made everything in six days—the sky, the earth, the sea—and I rested on the seventh. So I blessed the Sabbath and made it special.'

12.text: 'Honor your mama and daddy so you can live long in the land I'm givin' you.'

13.text: 'Don't kill nobody.'

14.text: 'Don't cheat on your spouse.'

15.text: 'Don't steal.'

16.text: 'Don't lie on people—especially in court.'

17.text: 'Don't be jealous of your neighbor's stuff—not their house, not their spouse, not their workers, not their animals— don't lust after nothin' that ain't yours.'

18.text: When the people saw the lightning, heard the thunder, and the loud blast of the ram's horn, and saw the smoke on the mountain, they were shook. They stood back, trembling.

19.text: They told Moses, 'You talk to us, we'll listen. But we ain't tryin' to hear from God directly, we gon' die if we do!'

20.text: Moses told 'em, 'Y'all chill. Don't be scared. God just came to test y'all so y'all respect him enough not to sin.'

21.text: While the people kept their distance, Moses stepped into the thick cloud where God was.

22.text: Then the Lord spoke to Moses, 'Tell the people—Y'all saw me speak from heaven.'

23.text: 'So don't even think about makin' idols, not gold, not silver, nothin' to compete with me. I ain't sharing my shine.'

24.text: 'Build an altar from the ground, offer your sacrifices—burnt offerings, peace offerings, your sheep, goats, and cattle. Build it where I make my name known, and I'ma bless you.'

25.text: 'If you use stones for my altar, don't cut 'em with tools—that messes it up.'

26.text: 'And don't build no steps to my altar. We ain't tryna have nobody peepin' up under your robe.'

1.text: 'These the rules you gotta tell Israel.'

2.text: 'If you buy a Hebrew servant, he only workin' six years. On year seven, let 'em go free—he ain't gotta pay nothin' for it.'

3.text: 'If he came in single, he leave single. If he got a wife, she walkin' free with him.'

4.text: 'Now, if his master gave him a wife, and they had kids, then only he gets free. The wife and kids still belong to the master.'

5.text: 'But if the servant say, 'I love my master, my wife, and my kids—I ain't tryin' to leave,'

6.text: 'Then his master gotta take him before God. Then he gotta pierce his ear against the doorpost, and from then on, that man servin' for life.'

7.text: 'If a man sells his daughter as a servant, she ain't leavin' in year seven like the men do.'

8.text: 'If she don't please the master who bought her, he gotta let her be bought back. But he can't sell her to foreigners—that's foul since he already broke the deal.'

9.text: 'If the master set her up to marry his son, he gotta treat her like a daughter.'

10.text: 'If he marry her then take another wife, he still gotta give her food, clothes, and love.'

11.text: 'If he don't do those three things, she walkin' free, no payment needed.'

12.text: 'Anybody that kills somebody on purpose? They gotta die too.'

13.text: 'But if it was an accident, then I'ma make a safe place for 'em to run to.'

14.text: 'Now, if somebody planned it out, they gon' die—don't matter if they run to my altar or not.'

15.text: 'If somebody hit their mama or daddy, they gotta die.'

16.text: 'Kidnappers? If they caught with the victim, or if they already sold them, they gon' die too.'

17.text: 'If you curse ya mama or daddy, guess what? Death.'

18.text: 'If two men get into it, and one hit the other with a rock or a fist, but he don't die—'

19.text: 'If he get better later and can walk again, even with a cane, the dude that hit him ain't gettin' punished—but he gotta pay for them lost wages till the man get back on his feet.'

20.text: 'If a master beat his servant and they die on the spot, that master gotta be punished.'

21.text: 'But if the servant recover after a day or two, the master ain't gettin' punished—that's still his property.'

22.text: 'If two men fightin', and they accidentally hit a pregnant woman so she gives birth too soon—if the baby ain't hurt, the man payin' whatever the husband demand.'

23.text: 'But if somebody die, then it's life for life.'

24.text: 'Eye for eye, tooth for tooth, hand for hand, foot for foot.'

25.text: 'Burn for burn, wound for wound, bruise for bruise.'

26.text: 'If a master hit a servant and they lose an eye, that servant gotta be freed as payback.'

27.text: 'If a master knock out a tooth, the servant walkin' free as compensation.'

28.text: 'If an ox kills somebody, that ox gotta be stoned, and nobody eatin' the meat. But the owner ain't responsible.'

29.text: 'BUT, if that ox was known for wildin', and the owner didn't stop it—and it killed somebody, then both the ox and the owner gotta die.'

30.text: 'Unless the victim's family wanna take money instead, then the owner can buy his life back.'

31.text: 'Same rule apply if it kills a kid.'

32.text: 'If an ox kills a slave, the owner gotta pay thirty silver coins to the slave's master, and the ox still gets stoned.'

33.text: 'If somebody digs a pit and leaves it uncovered, and an ox or donkey falls in—'

34.text: 'Then the pit owner gotta pay the animal's owner, but they keep the dead animal.'

35.text: 'If one person's ox kills another person's ox, then they gotta sell the live one and split the money, and they split the dead animal too.'

36.text: 'But if the ox was known for goring, and the owner ain't stop it, then he payin' full price, but he keeps the dead ox.'

1.text: 'If somebody steal an ox or a sheep, then kill it or sell it, that thief gotta pay back five oxen for every ox they took, and four sheep for every sheep they stole.'

2.text: 'If a thief break into a house at night and get killed, the one who killed 'em ain't guilty of murder.'

3.text: 'But if it happen in daylight, then the one who killed 'em guilty of murder. If the thief get caught, they gotta pay back what they stole. If they ain't got the money, they gon' be sold as a servant to pay it off.'

4.text: 'If somebody steal an ox, donkey, or sheep, and they still got it, then they payin' back double.'

5.text: 'If somebody's animal wander into another man's field and start eatin' up crops, the owner of the animal gotta pay up with the best of their own crops.'

6.text: 'If you burnin' bushes and the fire get loose and burn somebody's crops, the one who started it gotta pay for all the damage.'

7.text: 'If somebody leave money or goods with a neighbor for safekeeping, and it get stolen, if the thief get caught, they payin' back double.'

8.text: 'But if the thief ain't caught, the neighbor gotta go before God, and God gon' judge if they guilty or not.'

9.text: 'If two people arguin' over who own somethin'—like an ox, donkey, or clothes—God gon' decide who guilty. Whoever wrong gotta pay back double.'

10.text: 'If somebody leave an animal with a neighbor and it die or disappear, and nobody saw what happened—'

11.text: 'Then the neighbor gotta swear before God they ain't steal it. If they ain't guilty, no payment required.'

12.text: 'But if it was stolen, then the neighbor gotta pay back the owner.'

13.text: 'If a wild animal killed it, then they just gotta show proof—they ain't gotta pay nothin'.'

14.text: 'If somebody borrow an animal, and it die or get hurt while the owner ain't around, they gotta pay for it.'

15.text: 'But if the owner was there, they ain't gotta pay. If the animal was rented, the rental fee covers the loss.'

16.text: 'If a man sleep with a virgin that ain't engaged, he gotta marry her and pay the bride price.'

17.text: 'If her daddy say no, the man still gotta pay like he would if he was marryin' her.'

18.text: 'A witch? Don't let them live.'

19.text: 'Anybody lay with an animal? They dyin'.'

20.text: 'Anybody worship another god other than the Lord? They gon' be destroyed.'

21.text: 'Don't mistreat foreigners. Remember, y'all was foreigners in Egypt. Treat them right.'

22.text: 'Don't exploit no widows or orphans.'

23.text: 'If you do 'em wrong and they cry out to Me, I will hear 'em.'

24.text: 'And if I hear 'em cry, my anger gon' blaze, and I'ma kill you with the sword. Then yo' wives gon' be widows and yo' kids gon' be orphans.'

25.text: 'If you lend money to somebody broke, don't charge interest like a loan shark.'

26.text: 'If you take somebody's coat as security for a loan, give it back before the sun set.'

27.text: 'That's the only blanket they got—how they gon' sleep without it? If they cry to Me, I will hear, 'cause I'm merciful.'

28.text: 'Don't dishonor God or curse your leaders.'

29.text: 'When you give me offerings, don't hold back from the first of your harvest and wine.'

30.text: 'Give me your firstborn sons, too.'

31.text: 'Y'all belong to Me, so don't eat no animal that been torn up by wild beasts—throw that to the dogs.'

1.text: 'Don't be spreadin' no false rumors, and don't team up with evil folks to lie in court.'

2.text: 'Don't just go along with the crowd when they doin' wrong. If you called to testify, don't twist the truth just 'cause everybody else sayin' somethin' different.'

3.text: 'And don't change up your story just 'cause somebody poor—tell the truth, no matter what.'

4.text: 'If you see your enemy's ox or donkey that ran off, take it back to 'em.'

5.text: 'If you see somebody you don't like strugglin' 'cause their donkey collapsed, don't just keep it pushin'—help 'em out.'

6.text: 'In court, don't cheat a poor person out of justice. Fair is fair.'

7.text: 'Don't accuse nobody falsely or sentence an innocent person to death, 'cause I don't clear guilty folks.'

8.text: 'Don't take no bribes, 'cause that money will make you blind to the truth and mess up even an honest person's judgment.'

9.text: 'Don't be out here oppressin' foreigners. Y'all know what it's like to be foreigners, 'cause y'all was foreigners in Egypt. Treat them right.'

10.text: 'Work your land for six years, grow your crops and harvest 'em—'

11.text: 'But on the seventh year, let the land rest so the poor folks can get what they need, and whatever's left, let the wild animals have it.'

12.text: 'Y'all work six days a week, but on the seventh day, y'all rest—that way, yo' ox and donkey get a break, and so do yo' workers and foreigners.'

13.text: 'Listen real close to everything I'm tellin' y'all—don't call on no other gods, don't even say their names.'

14.text: 'Y'all gotta celebrate three festivals for Me every year.'

15.text: 'First, celebrate the Festival of Unleavened Bread. For seven days, eat bread with no yeast, just like I told y'all. This happen every spring, the same time y'all left Egypt. Don't come to Me empty-handed.'

16.text: 'Second, celebrate the Festival of Harvest—that's when you bring Me the first of what you grew.'

17.text: 'Then, celebrate the Final Harvest Festival at the end of the season when you gather everything up. Three times a year, every man in Israel gotta show up before the Lord.'

18.text: 'Don't offer sacrifices with bread that got yeast in it, and don't leave no fat from the festival offerings overnight. Clean it up.'

19.text: 'When y'all harvest crops, bring the best of what you got to the house of the Lord. And don't be cookin' no young goat in its mama's milk.'

20.text: 'Look, I'm sendin' an angel ahead of y'all to keep y'all safe on the journey and bring y'all to the place I promised.'

21.text: 'Listen up—do what he say and don't go against him. He ain't gon' tolerate y'all actin' up, 'cause he reppin' Me.'

22.text: 'But if y'all listen to him and do what I say, I'll be against anybody that's against you. I got y'all.'

23.text: 'My angel gon' lead y'all to the land where the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hivites, and Jebusites live. I'ma wipe them out.'

24.text: 'But don't mess with their gods, don't worship 'em, don't copy their ways—y'all gotta destroy all that mess.'

25.text: 'Y'all serve Me, the Lord, and I'ma bless y'all with food and water, and I'ma keep y'all healthy.'

26.text: 'Nobody gon' miscarry or be infertile in the land, and I'ma make sure y'all live long full lives.'

27.text: 'I'ma send fear ahead of y'all—gonna make all these other folks panic before y'all even show up.'

28.text: 'I'ma run out the Hivites, Canaanites, and Hittites before y'all even touch the land. They gon' clear out.'

29.text: 'But not too fast—if I run 'em out all at once, the land gon' be too empty, and wild animals gon' take over.'

30.text: 'I'ma push 'em out little by little till y'all got enough people to fill the land.'

31.text: 'Y'all boundaries gon' stretch from the Red Sea to the Mediterranean, and from the desert to the Euphrates River. I'ma hand them folks over to y'all, and y'all gon' drive 'em out.'

32.text: 'Don't make no treaties with them or their gods. No deals.'

33.text: 'Don't let 'em stay in yo' land, 'cause they gon' turn y'all away from Me. If y'all serve their gods, y'all gon' get caught up in idolatry, and it's gon' be a trap.'

1.text: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Aight, come up here to Me, and bring Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and seventy elders of Israel. But listen—y'all gotta worship from a distance.'

2.text: 'Only Moses can come close to Me. The rest of 'em? They gotta stay back. And nobody else better try climbin' this mountain.'

3.text: So Moses went down and told the people everything the Lord said—all the rules and commands. And the people, all together, said, 'We gon' do everything the Lord said. No cap!'

4.text: Then Moses wrote it all down. Early the next morning, he built an altar at the foot of the mountain. He also set up twelve stone pillars, one for each tribe of Israel.

5.text: Then he told some young Israelite men to offer burnt sacrifices and peace offerings—bulls for the Lord.

6.text: Moses took half the blood and put it in bowls. The other half? He splattered it on the altar.

7.text: Then he grabbed the Book of the Covenant and read it out loud to the people. Once again, they responded, 'We gon' do everything the Lord said. We gon' obey!'

8.text: Then Moses took the blood and splattered it over the people, sayin', 'Look, this blood seals the covenant the Lord made with y'all through these commands.'

9.text: Then Moses, Aaron, Nadab, Abihu, and the seventy elders of Israel went up the mountain.

10.text: And they saw God—for real. Under His feet, there was somethin' like blue lapis lazuli—clear as the sky. Straight heavenly.

11.text: Even though they looked at God, He didn't strike 'em down. Matter fact, they sat there eatin' and drinkin' right in His presence!

12.text: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Come up higher. Stay here. I'ma give you stone tablets with all My commands, so you can teach the people.

13.text: So Moses and his assistant Joshua got ready, and Moses started climbin' up Mount Sinai.

14.text: Moses told the elders, 'Y'all wait here 'til we get back. If anybody got a problem while I'm gone, Aaron and Hur got this.'

15.text: Then Moses went up the mountain, and a thick cloud covered it.

16.text: The glory of the Lord came down on Mount Sinai, and the cloud covered it for six days. On the seventh day, the Lord called Moses from inside the cloud.

17.text: From the Israelites' perspective, the glory of the Lord at the top of the mountain looked like a raging fire.

18.text: Then Moses walked into the cloud as he climbed higher up the mountain. He stayed up there for forty days and forty nights.

1.text: Then the Lord told Moses,

2.text: 'Tell the people of Israel to bring Me sacred offerings. Only take contributions from folks who really wanna give from the heart.

3.text: 'Here's what y'all can bring: Gold, silver, and bronze.

4.text: Blue, purple, and scarlet thread, fine linen, and goats' hair;

5.text: Ram skins dyed red, badger skins, and acacia wood;

6.text: Oil for the light, and spices for the anointing oil and for the sweet incense;

7.text: Onyx stones, and stones to be set in the ephod and in the breastplate.

8.text: Tell the people to build Me a holy sanctuary so I can stay with them.

9.text: Make sure the Tabernacle and everything in it is built exactly how I show you.

10.text: Tell the people to make an Ark outta acacia wood. It gotta be 45 inches long, 27 inches wide, and 27 inches high.

11.text: Overlay it inside and out with pure gold and run a gold molding all around it.

12.text: Cast four gold rings and attach 'em to its feet—two rings on each side.

13.text: Make some poles outta acacia wood and cover 'em with gold.

14.text: Slide them poles into the rings so y'all can carry the Ark.

15.text: Do NOT take them poles out. Leave them in place.

16.text: Once it's done, put inside the Ark the stone tablets with the covenant terms I'ma give you.

17.text: Then make the Ark's cover—the mercy seat—outta pure gold. 45 inches long, 27 inches wide.

18.text: Make two cherubim outta hammered gold. Put 'em on both ends of the atonement cover.

19.text: Mold the cherubim onto the cover as one solid piece.

20.text: These cherubim gotta face each other and look down on the atonement cover. Their wings gotta spread over it, protectin' it.

21.text: Inside the Ark, put the stone tablets with the covenant terms I give you. Then put the atonement cover on top.

22.text: That's where I'll meet you—above the atonement cover, between the gold cherubim that hover over the Ark. From there, I'ma give you My instructions for the people.

23.text: Make a table outta acacia wood. 36 inches long, 18 inches wide, 27 inches high.

24.text: Overlay it with pure gold and run a gold molding around it.

25.text: Make a 3-inch border all around it and run a gold molding along the border.

26.text: Put four gold rings on the table, one at each corner by the legs.

27.text: Attach the rings near the border to hold the poles for carrying it.

28.text: Make the poles outta acacia wood, cover 'em with gold, so you can carry the table.

29.text: Make special containers outta pure gold—bowls, ladles, pitchers, and jars for pourin' out offerings.

30.text: Always keep the Bread of the Presence on the table before Me.

31.text: Make a lampstand outta pure hammered gold—one whole piece with the base, stem, cups, buds, and petals.

32.text: It should have six branches comin' out the sides—three on each side.

33.text: Each branch should have three lamp cups shaped like almond blossoms, with buds and petals.

34.text: The center stem should have four lamp cups, also shaped like almond blossoms.

35.text: Put an almond bud under each pair of branches where they extend from the stem.

36.text: The whole thing gotta be one solid piece of pure gold, hammered out.

37.text: Then make seven lamps for the stand, set 'em up so they shine forward.

38.text: Make the lamp snuffers and trays outta pure gold too.

39.text: You'll need 75 pounds of pure gold for the lampstand and all its accessories.

40.text: Follow every detail I showed you here on the mountain. No improvisin'!

1.text: Make the Tabernacle from ten curtains of finely woven linen. Decorate 'em with blue, purple, and scarlet thread, with skillfully embroidered cherubim.

2.text: Each curtain gotta be the same size—42 feet long and 6 feet wide.

3.text: Join five of 'em together to make one long curtain, then join the other five into a second long curtain.

4.text: Put loops of blue yarn along the edge of the last curtain in each set.

5.text: Fifty loops should go along the edge of one curtain, and another fifty loops along the edge of the other curtain.

6.text: Then make fifty gold clasps and use 'em to fasten the long curtains together. That way, the Tabernacle will be one solid piece.

7.text: Make eleven curtains of goat-hair cloth to serve as the tent covering for the Tabernacle.

8.text: Each curtain gotta be the same size—45 feet long and 6 feet wide.

9.text: Join five curtains together to make one long curtain, and do the same with the other six. Let three feet from the second set hang over the front of the sacred tent.

10.text: Make fifty loops on one edge of each large curtain.

11.text: Then make fifty bronze clasps, and fasten the loops together so the tent covering is one solid piece.

12.text: The extra three feet of the tent covering should hang over the back of the Tabernacle.

13.text: Eighteen inches of remaining material should hang down over each side so the Tabernacle is fully covered.

14.text: Top it off with a protective layer of tanned ram skins and fine goatskin leather.

15.text: For the Tabernacle's framework, use acacia wood to make frames.

16.text: Each frame should be 15 feet high and 27 inches wide.

17.text: Put two pegs under each frame to keep 'em stable.

18.text: Make twenty frames for the south side of the Tabernacle.

19.text: Then make forty silver bases—two under each frame—so the pegs fit in solid.

20.text: For the north side, do the same thing: twenty frames

21.text: And forty silver bases—two under each frame.

22.text: For the back (west side), make six frames.

23.text: And add two extra frames for the rear corners.

24.text: The corner frames should be matched at the bottom and firmly connected at the top by a single ring.

25.text: So, all together, there'll be eight frames at the rear, set in sixteen silver bases—two bases per frame.

26.text: Make crossbars outta acacia wood to link the frames together—five for the north side

27.text: And five for the south side, plus five for the back (west side).

28.text: The middle crossbar should run the full length of the Tabernacle, halfway up the frames.

29.text: Overlay the frames with gold, and make gold rings to hold the crossbars. Then cover the crossbars with gold too.

30.text: Set up the Tabernacle exactly like the pattern I showed you on the mountain.

31.text: Make a special curtain for inside the Tabernacle, woven from fine linen with blue, purple, and scarlet thread, decorated with embroidered cherubim.

32.text: Hang it on gold hooks attached to four acacia wood posts, which should be overlaid with gold and set in silver bases.

33.text: Hang the inner curtain from the clasps and put the Ark of the Covenant behind it. This curtain separates the Holy Place from the Most Holy Place.

34.text: Then put the Ark's cover—the Mercy Seat—on top of the Ark inside the Most Holy Place.

35.text: Set the table outside the inner curtain on the north side, and the lampstand across from it on the south side.

36.text: Make another curtain for the entrance of the Tabernacle. It should be finely woven linen with exquisite embroidery in blue, purple, and scarlet thread.

37.text: Craft five acacia wood posts, overlay 'em with gold, and hang the curtain from 'em using gold hooks. Then cast five bronze bases for the posts.

1.text: Take some acacia wood and build a square altar—7.5 feet wide, 7.5 feet long, and 4.5 feet high.

2.text: Make horns for each of its four corners, all one piece with the altar. Then overlay the whole thing with bronze.

3.text: Make ash buckets, shovels, basins, meat forks, and firepans—all outta bronze.

4.text: Make a bronze grating for it, and attach four bronze rings at its four corners.

5.text: Put the grating halfway down the side of the altar, right under the ledge.

6.text: For carrying the altar, make some poles from acacia wood, and overlay 'em with bronze.

7.text: Slide those poles through the rings on both sides of the altar.

8.text: The altar gotta be hollow, made from wooden planks. Follow the exact instructions I gave you on the mountain.

9.text: Build a courtyard for the Tabernacle, enclosed by curtains made of fine woven linen. On the south side, make the curtains 150 feet long.

10.text: Hold 'em up with twenty posts set in twenty bronze bases. Hang the curtains with silver hooks and rings.

11.text: Do the same thing on the north side—150 feet of curtains, held up by twenty posts set in bronze bases with silver hooks and rings.

12.text: For the west end, the curtains should be 75 feet long, supported by ten posts set in ten bases.

13.text: The east end—the front of the courtyard—should also be 75 feet long.

14.text: The entrance will be on the east end, flanked by two curtains. The curtain on the right side should be 22.5 feet long, held up by three posts with three bases.

15.text: The curtain on the left side should also be 22.5 feet long, supported by three posts with three bases.

16.text: For the entrance curtain, make it 30 feet long, woven from fine linen with beautiful embroidery in blue, purple, and scarlet thread. Support it with four posts, each set in its own base.

17.text: All the courtyard posts should have silver rings and hooks and bronze bases.

18.text: The whole courtyard should be 150 feet long, 75 feet wide, and 7.5 feet high. The walls should be woven linen, and the bases should be bronze.

19.text: All the articles used in Tabernacle rituals—even the tent pegs holding up the Tabernacle and courtyard curtains—must be made of bronze.

20.text: Tell the people to bring you pure pressed olive oil to keep the lamps burning all night.

21.text: The lampstand should be inside the Tabernacle, in front of the inner curtain that covers the Ark of the Covenant. Aaron and his sons gotta keep the lamps burning in God's presence all night long. This rule never changes—it's for every generation of Israel.

1.text: Tell your brother Aaron and his sons—Nadab, Abihu, Eleazar, and Ithamar—to step apart from everybody else so they can serve as my priests.

2.text: Make some fresh, holy garments for Aaron—something glorious and beautiful.

3.text: I already put skill and wisdom in certain artisans, so tell them to make priestly garments that'll show Aaron's been set apart for my work.

4.text: These are the garments they gotta make: a chestpiece, an ephod, a robe, a patterned tunic, a turban, and a sash. They making these for Aaron and his sons to wear when they serve me.

5.text: Use fine linen, gold thread, and blue, purple, and scarlet yarn.

6.text: Make the ephod outta fine linen and skillfully embroider it with gold, blue, purple, and scarlet thread.

7.text: It's two pieces—front and back—joined at the shoulders.

8.text: The sash should match—woven linen embroidered with gold, blue, purple, and scarlet.

9.text: Get two onyx stones and engrave the names of Israel's tribes on 'em.

10.text: Six names on each stone, in the birth order of Jacob's sons.

11.text: Engrave them like a jeweler engraves a seal, then mount them in gold settings.

12.text: Fasten these two stones on the shoulders of the ephod—so every time Aaron steps up, he represents Israel.

13.text: Make some gold settings.

14.text: Braid two cords of pure gold and attach them to the gold settings on the shoulders.

15.text: Make a chestpiece—a special decision piece—that matches the ephod. Use woven linen, embroidered with gold, blue, purple, and scarlet thread.

16.text: Make it one piece, folded into a square, about 9 inches on each side.

17.text: Mount four rows of gemstones on it. First row: red carnelian, pale-green peridot, and an emerald.

18.text: Second row: turquoise, lapis lazuli, and a white moonstone.

19.text: Third row: orange jacinth, agate, and a purple amethyst.

20.text: Fourth row: blue-green beryl, onyx, and green jasper. Set them all in gold filigree.

21.text: Each stone represents a tribe of Israel, with their name engraved like a seal.

22.text: To attach the chestpiece, make braided cords of pure gold.

23.text: Make two gold rings and attach them to the top corners of the chestpiece.

24.text: Tie the gold cords to those two rings.

25.text: Tie the other ends to the gold settings on the shoulders of the ephod.

26.text: Make two more gold rings and attach 'em to the inside edges of the chestpiece, right next to the ephod.

27.text: Then make two more gold rings on the front of the ephod, below the shoulders, above where the sash ties up.

28.text: Attach the bottom rings of the chestpiece to the ephod's rings with blue cords, keeping it secure.

29.text: So whenever Aaron goes into the Holy Place, he got Israel's names over his heart—a reminder he's reppin' them before the Lord.

30.text: Slide the Urim and Thummim into the chestpiece so they stay over Aaron's heart—that's how he'll seek the Lord's decisions for Israel.

31.text: Make a robe for the ephod, from a single piece of blue cloth.

32.text: Put a reinforced collar in the middle so it won't tear.

33.text: Make pomegranates out of blue, purple, and scarlet yarn, and put them on the hem of the robe, with gold bells between them.

34.text: Gold bells, pomegranates, gold bells, pomegranates—all around the hem.

35.text: Aaron gotta wear this robe whenever he steps before the Lord. The bells will ring, letting folks know he's moving in and out the Holy Place—so he don't drop dead.

36.text: Now make a gold medallion, and engrave it like a seal: 'Holy to the Lord.'

37.text: Tie it with a blue cord to the front of Aaron's turban, where it stays.

38.text: Aaron gotta wear it on his forehead, so he can take on Israel's guilt when they bring their sacred offerings. That way, the Lord will accept the people's sacrifices.

39.text: Weave Aaron's patterned tunic from fine linen. Make his turban from linen, and embroider his sash with colors.

40.text: For Aaron's sons, make tunics, sashes, and head coverings—they should look glorious and beautiful.

41.text: Put them on your brother Aaron and his sons, anoint 'em and ordain 'em. Consecrate them so they can serve as priests.

42.text: Make some linen undergarments for them to wear next to their skin—from their hips to their thighs.

43.text: They must wear these every time they step into the Tabernacle or come near the altar. Otherwise, they'll die from guilt. This law never changes—it's forever for Aaron and his sons.

1.text: Here's how you set apart Aaron and his sons to serve me as priests: Bring a young bull and two perfect rams.

2.text: Then make some bread, thin cakes, and wafers—all without yeast—and mix 'em with olive oil.

3.text: Put 'em in a basket, and bring 'em to the Tabernacle, along with the bull and the two rams.

4.text: Bring Aaron and his sons to the entrance of the Tabernacle and wash 'em with water.

5.text: Put Aaron's priestly robes on him—the tunic, robe, ephod, and chestpiece—then wrap the decorative sash around him.

6.text: Put the turban on his head and fasten the sacred medallion on it.

7.text: Take the anointing oil and pour it over his head. That's how you set him apart.

8.text: Next, bring in Aaron's sons, and put their tunics on 'em.

9.text: Tie their sashes around their waists and put on their head coverings. The priesthood belongs to them forever—this is how you ordain them.

10.text: Bring the young bull to the entrance of the Tabernacle, and Aaron and his sons will lay their hands on its head.

11.text: Then slaughter the bull in the Lord's presence at the entrance of the Tabernacle.

12.text: Take some of its blood, put it on the horns of the altar, and pour out the rest at the base of the altar.

13.text: Gather up the fat from the organs, the liver lobe, and the kidneys, then burn it all on the altar.

14.text: But take the rest of the bull—its hide, meat, and dung— and burn it outside the camp as a sin offering.

15.text: Now bring one of the rams, and Aaron and his sons will lay their hands on its head.

16.text: Slaughter the ram, and splatter its blood on all sides of the altar.

17.text: Cut it into pieces, wash the organs and legs, and set 'em next to the head and body pieces.

18.text: Then burn the entire ram on the altar. This is a burnt offering to the Lord—a pleasing aroma, a special gift.

19.text: Now bring the other ram, and Aaron and his sons will lay their hands on its head.

20.text: Slaughter it, then take some of its blood and put it on the right earlobe, right thumb, and right big toe of Aaron and his sons. Splatter the rest on all sides of the altar.

21.text: Take some of the blood from the altar and some anointing oil, and sprinkle it on Aaron, his sons, and their garments. That's how you set them apart as holy.

22.text: Since this is the ordination ram, take its fat, fat tail, fat from the organs, the liver lobe, the kidneys, and the right thigh.

23.text: Take one loaf, one thin cake, and one wafer from the basket of unleavened bread before the Lord.

24.text: Put all these in Aaron and his sons' hands, and have them lift them up as a special offering to the Lord.

25.text: Then take the bread and meat and burn them on the altar with the burnt offering—a pleasing aroma to the Lord.

26.text: Take the breast of Aaron's ordination ram, lift it up before the Lord, and then keep it as your portion.

27.text: Set aside the breast and thigh of Aaron's ordination ram—they belong to Aaron and his sons.

28.text: From now on, whenever Israel brings a peace offering, a portion belongs to Aaron and his descendants—this is a sacred offering forever.

29.text: Aaron's sacred garments must be passed down to his descendants, so they wear 'em when they get anointed and ordained.

30.text: Whoever becomes high priest after Aaron must wear these for seven days when they minister in the Holy Place.

31.text: Take the ordination ram, and boil its meat in a sacred place.

32.text: Aaron and his sons will eat this meat with the bread from the ordination basket.

33.text: Nobody else can eat it—this is their sacred portion.

34.text: If any of the meat or bread is left by morning, burn it—nobody can eat it.

35.text: Ordain Aaron and his sons for seven days, just like this.

36.text: Each day, sacrifice a young bull as a sin offering to purify them before the Lord.

37.text: Consecrate the altar for seven days. After that, it'll be completely holy, and whatever touches it will become holy.

38.text: Each day, offer two lambs, one in the morning, one in the evening.

39.text: One in the morning, one in the evening—every single day.

40.text: With each lamb, bring two quarts of flour, mixed with a quart of olive oil, plus a quart of wine as a drink offering.

41.text: Do the same thing in the evening—this is a pleasing aroma to the Lord.

42.text: This must be a permanent daily offering for generations to come.

43.text: I'll meet with Israel right there, and my presence will make the place holy.

44.text: I will consecrate the Tabernacle, the altar, Aaron, and his sons so they can serve me as priests.

45.text: Then I will live among the Israelites and be their God.

46.text: They will know I am the Lord who brought them out of Egypt, just so I could live among them. I am the Lord their God.

1.text: Make another altar outta acacia wood for burnin' incense.

2.text: Make it 18 inches square & 36 inches tall, with horns on the corners, all carved from the same piece of wood.

3.text: Overlay it with gold—the top, sides, and horns—and put a gold molding around it.

4.text: Make two gold rings, attach 'em on opposite sides below the molding to hold the carrying poles.

5.text: Make the poles from acacia wood, and overlay them with gold.

6.text: Put the altar right outside the inner curtain, in front of the Ark's cover—the place of atonement—where I'll meet with you.

7.text: Every morning, when Aaron fixes the lamps, he gotta burn fragrant incense on this altar.

8.text: And every evening, when he lights the lamps, he gotta burn incense again—this is a permanent rule for all generations.

9.text: Don't burn any unholy incense on this altar—no burnt offerings, grain offerings, or drink offerings either.

10.text: Once a year, Aaron gotta purify the altar by smearing its horns with the blood from the atonement offering. This a regular, annual thing for generations 'cause this is the Lord's most holy altar.

11.text: Then the Lord told Moses,

12.text: Every time y'all take a census, each man gotta pay a ransom for himself to the Lord. That way, no plague will hit the people when y'all count 'em.

13.text: Every person who gets counted gotta pay a small silver offering—that's half a shekel (based on the sanctuary's scale, which equals twenty gerahs.)

14.text: Anybody 20 years and older gotta bring this offering to the Lord.

15.text: Don't matter if you rich or poor—everybody pays the same amount to purify their lives before God.

16.text: Take this ransom money and use it for the upkeep of the Tabernacle. This offering will remind the Lord of His people and will purify their lives.

17.text: Then the Lord told Moses,

18.text: Make a bronze washbasin with a bronze stand. Put it between the Tabernacle and the altar, and fill it up with water.

19.text: Aaron and his sons gotta wash their hands and feet there before entering.

20.text: If they don't wash up before coming into the Lord's presence or offering a sacrifice, they gonna die!

21.text: This rule ain't changing—Aaron and his sons gotta wash up every time from generation to generation.

22.text: Then the Lord told Moses,

23.text: Gather these top-tier spices: 12½ pounds of pure myrrh, 6¼ pounds of fragrant cinnamon, 6¼ pounds of fragrant calamus, 12½ pounds of cassia, One gallon of olive oil.

24.text: And grab 12 and a half pounds of cassia—using the sanctuary shekel for weight. Oh, and don't forget to get a full gallon of olive oil too.

25.text: Blend 'em together like a skilled incense maker to create a holy anointing oil.

26.text: Use this oil to anoint the Tabernacle, the Ark of the Covenant,

27.text: The table and all its utensils, the lampstand and all its accessories, the incense altar,

28.text: The altar of burnt offering and its utensils, and the washbasin with its stand.

29.text: Consecrate them all—make 'em holy so that anything that touches them becomes holy too.

30.text: Anoint Aaron and his sons too—set 'em apart to serve as priests.

31.text: Tell Israel: 'This holy anointing oil is for the Lord alone, forever.

32.text: Don't use it on just anybody. Don't copy this recipe. It's holy, so treat it holy.

33.text: Anybody who makes this oil for personal use or puts it on someone who ain't a priest must be cut off from the people.

34.text: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Gather these fragrant spices: Resin droplets, Mollusk shell, Galbanum, Pure frankincense (weighed out equally)'

35.text: Mix 'em up like a pro incense maker, sprinkle it with salt, and make it a pure & holy incense.

36.text: Grind some up into a fine powder and put it in front of the Ark inside the Tabernacle where I meet with you.

37.text: Don't use this formula for anything else—it's reserved for the Lord alone.

38.text: Anyone who makes this incense for personal use must be cut off from the community.

1.text: Then the Lord told Moses,

2.text: 'Look, I picked Bezalel, son of Uri, grandson of Hur, from the tribe of Judah.

3.text: I done filled him up with my Spirit, gave him wisdom, skills, & expertise in all kinds of craftsmanship.

4.text: He a master craftsman—knows how to work with gold, silver, & bronze.

5.text: He's skilled in engraving, mounting gemstones, & carving wood—dude got skills in every craft.

6.text: I also picked Oholiab, son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan, to be his assistant.

7.text: And I done blessed all the gifted craftsmen so they can build everything I told you to make: The Tabernacle, The Ark of the Covenant, The Ark's cover—the place of atonement, All the Tabernacle's furniture

8.text: The table & its utensils, The pure gold lampstand & all its accessories, The incense altar

9.text: The altar for burnt offerings & its utensils, The washbasin & its stand

10.text: The priestly garments—Aaron's sacred outfit & his sons' clothes for serving as priests

11.text: The anointing oil, The fragrant incense for the Holy Place. These craftsmen gon' make everything just like I commanded you.'

12.text: Then the Lord gave Moses another set of instructions:

13.text: 'Tell the people of Israel: Be real careful to keep my Sabbath day—'cause the Sabbath is a sign of my covenant with y'all from generation to generation. It's here so y'all can know I'm the Lord who makes you holy.

14.text: Keep the Sabbath day holy—anybody who disrespects it gotta die. If somebody works on that day, they cut off from the community.

15.text: Y'all got six days every week for work, but the seventh day gotta be a Sabbath—a day fully dedicated to the Lord. Anybody who works on that day gotta be put to death.
