16.text: The people of Israel gotta keep the Sabbath, passing it down from generation to generation. It's a covenant law forever.

17.text: This is a permanent sign between me & Israel. 'Cause in six days, the Lord made heaven & earth, but on the seventh day, I chilled & got refreshed.'

18.text: When the Lord finished talking with Moses on Mount Sinai, He gave him two stone tablets—inscribed with the terms of the covenant, written by God's own finger.

1.text: The people started trippin' when they saw Moses takin' too long to come down from the mountain. So they ran up on Aaron and said, 'Yo, make us some gods that can lead us! We dunno what happened to Moses, the dude that brought us outta Egypt.'

2.text: So Aaron was like, 'Aight, take the gold rings from y'all wives, sons, and daughters, and bring 'em to me.'

3.text: Everybody took off their gold earrings and brought them to Aaron.

4.text: He melted the gold down, shaped it into a calf, and when they saw it, they started shouting, 'O Israel, these the gods that brought us outta Egypt!'

5.text: Aaron saw how hyped they was, so he built an altar in front of the calf and announced, 'Tomorrow, we havin' a festival for the Lord!'

6.text: Next morning, the people got up early, made sacrifices, feasted, got drunk, and started wildin' out.

7.text: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Get down there—quick! Your people, the ones you brought outta Egypt, already actin' up!'

8.text: They turned away from me so fast! They melted down gold, made a calf, and now they bowin' down to it, makin' sacrifices, and sayin', 'These are your gods, Israel, the ones that brought you outta Egypt!'

9.text: Then the Lord said, 'Man, I see just how stubborn these people are.'

10.text: 'Now step aside, so I can let my anger loose and wipe 'em all out. Then I'ma start over with you, Moses.'

11.text: But Moses started pleadin' with the Lord, 'Lord, why you so mad at your people, the ones you brought outta Egypt with your power and your strong hand?'

12.text: 'You really gon' let the Egyptians say, "Look at their God—rescued 'em just to wipe 'em out in the mountains!"? Please chill on this anger, Lord, and don't do this to your people!'

13.text: 'Remember Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—you swore to them that you'd make their descendants countless like the stars in the sky, and you'd give them this land forever.'

14.text: So the Lord changed His mind and didn't bring the disaster He threatened on His people.

15.text: Then Moses went down the mountain, holdin' the two stone tablets—the ones God Himself wrote on front & back.

16.text: These weren't just any tablets—they were God's own work, with His words written by His own hand.

17.text: When Joshua heard the noise from the camp, he said, 'Moses, sound like a war goin' on down there!'

18.text: But Moses said, 'Nah, that ain't the sound of victory or defeat—that's celebration.'

19.text: When they got close, Moses saw the golden calf and people dancin' around it—he got heated, threw the stone tablets, and smashed 'em at the mountain's base.

20.text: Then he took the calf, burned it down, crushed it into powder, dumped it in the water, and made everybody drink it.

21.text: Then he turned to Aaron: 'Bruh, what did these people do to you to make you help 'em sin like this?'

22.text: Aaron said, 'Man, chill, you know how these folks stay actin' up.'

23.text: 'They came to me sayin', "Make us some gods to lead us since we dunno what happened to Moses."'

24.text: 'So I told 'em, "Whoever got gold, take it off." They brought it to me, I threw it in the fire, and out came this calf!'

25.text: Moses saw how Aaron let the people go wild, and how their enemies were laughin' at 'em.

26.text: So he stood at the camp entrance and shouted, 'Who rockin' with the Lord, come stand with me!' And all the Levites gathered around him.

27.text: Moses told 'em, 'This is what the Lord says—strap up and go through the camp, takin' out whoever—brothers, friends, neighbors—don't matter.'

28.text: The Levites followed Moses' command, and that day about 3,000 people got put down.

29.text: Then Moses told 'em, 'Today y'all proved y'all stand with the Lord—even though it meant killin' y'all own kin. And today, y'all earned a blessing.'

30.text: Next day, Moses told the people, 'Y'all really messed up bad, but I'ma go back up the mountain—maybe I can beg for forgiveness.'

31.text: So Moses went back up to the Lord and said, 'Lord, these people really did you dirty—they made gods of gold for themselves!'

32.text: 'But if you just forgive them… if not, then just erase my name too.'

33.text: But the Lord said, 'Nah, I only erase the names of those who sinned against me.'

34.text: 'Now lead the people to the place I told you about. My angel gon' lead the way, but when the time comes, I will make them answer for what they did.'

35.text: Then the Lord sent a plague on the people 'cause of the golden calf Aaron made.

1.text: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Aight, get movin'—you and these people you brought outta Egypt. Head to the land I promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob when I told them, "I'ma give this land to your descendants."'

2.text: I'ma send an angel ahead of you to clear out the Canaanites, Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.

3.text: Go up to the land flowin' with milk and honey—but I ain't goin' with y'all, 'cause y'all too stubborn and hardheaded. If I roll with you, I'ma end up wipin' y'all out on the way.

4.text: When the people heard this harsh word, they started mourning and stopped flexin' with their jewelry and fine clothes.

5.text: The Lord told Moses to tell them, 'Y'all stubborn and rebellious—if I roll with y'all, even for a second, I'd wipe y'all out. So take off them chains, bracelets, and fancy robes while I figure out what I'ma do with y'all.'

6.text: So from Mount Sinai on, the Israelites ain't rock no jewelry or fancy clothes no more.

7.text: Moses had a habit—he'd take the Tent of Meeting and set it outside the camp, far off. Anybody who needed to holla at the Lord had to go outside the camp to that tent.

8.text: Whenever Moses went to the Tent of Meeting, everybody got up and stood in front of their own tents, watchin' him till he went inside.

9.text: As soon as Moses stepped in, the pillar of cloud would come down and hover at the entrance, and the Lord would talk to Moses.

10.text: When the people saw the cloud chillin' at the entrance, they would stand up and bow in front of their own tents.

11.text: Inside the Tent of Meeting, the Lord would speak to Moses face to face, like somebody talkin' to their homie. Afterward, Moses would go back to the camp, but his assistant Joshua, son of Nun, stayed in the tent.

12.text: One day, Moses told the Lord, 'You been tellin' me, "Lead these people to the land," but you ain't told me who you sendin' with me. You also said, "I know you by name, and I got favor on you."

13.text: So if that's real, Lord, let me understand your ways more, so I can keep walkin' in your favor. And don't forget—this nation is YOUR people.

14.text: The Lord replied, 'Aight, I'ma go with you personally, and I'ma give you rest. Everything gon' be fine.'

15.text: Then Moses said, 'Lord, if you ain't rollin' with us, don't make us leave this place.'

16.text: 'How else anybody gon' know we your people, that you rock with us? Your presence is what makes us different from everybody else on earth!'

17.text: The Lord replied, 'Aight, Moses, I'ma do what you ask, 'cause I got favor on you, and I know you by name.'

18.text: Then Moses said, 'Aight, Lord, let me see your glory!'

19.text: The Lord replied, 'Aight, I'ma let all my goodness pass before you, and I'ma call out my name—Yahweh. I show mercy to whoever I choose and compassion to whoever I choose.'

20.text: 'But you can't look straight at my face, 'cause nobody can see me and live.'

21.text: Then the Lord said, 'Look, stand over here on this rock.'

22.text: 'When my glorious presence passes by, I'ma hide you in the crevice of the rock and cover you with my hand till I'm gone.'

23.text: 'Then I'ma move my hand, and you can see my back, but you ain't gon' see my face.'

1.text: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Aight, carve out two stone tablets, just like the ones you broke. I'ma write down the same words that was on the first set.'

2.text: Be ready by morning to climb Mount Sinai and come meet me at the top.

3.text: Ain't nobody else allowed to come with you—not a soul. Matter fact, don't even let the livestock graze near the mountain.

4.text: So Moses did what God said—chiseled out two stone tablets, got up early in the morning, and climbed Mount Sinai with the tablets in hand.

5.text: Then the Lord came down in a cloud, stood there with Moses, and called out His own name—Yahweh.

6.text: The Lord passed in front of Moses, calling out: 'Yahweh! The Lord! The God of compassion and mercy! I'm slow to anger, full of love, and faithful.

7.text: 'I show unfailing love to a thousand generations. I forgive sin, rebellion, and iniquity, but I don't let the guilty slide. I hold folks accountable, even down to their kids and grandkids.'

8.text: Moses immediately fell on his face and worshiped.

9.text: Then Moses said, 'Lord, if I really got favor with you, please stay with us. Yeah, we hardheaded and rebellious, but please forgive us and claim us as yours.'

10.text: The Lord replied, 'Listen up—I'ma make a covenant with you. I'ma do miracles so wild that no nation has ever seen before. Everybody gon' witness my power.'

11.text: 'Follow everything I command you today. I'ma go ahead of you and push out the Amorites, Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.

12.text: But don't make no treaties with the people in the land. They'll lead you into their mess and trap you.

13.text: Instead, tear down their altars, smash their pillars, and cut down them Asherah poles.

14.text: You must worship no other gods, 'cause the Lord's name is Jealous—and He don't play about His people.

15.text: Don't make a deal with them folks, 'cause they out here chasing other gods and making sacrifices. They'll invite you to join in, and you gon' go with 'em.

16.text: Then y'all gon' start marrying their daughters, and they gon' pull your sons into their false worship.

17.text: Don't be out here making no metal gods for yourself.

18.text: You must celebrate the Festival of Unleavened Bread. For seven days, eat bread without yeast, just like I told you. Do this every year in early spring 'cause that's when I freed y'all from Egypt.

19.text: Every firstborn belongs to me—human or animal.

20.text: If you got a firstborn donkey, you gotta redeem it with a lamb. If you don't, then break its neck. But all firstborn sons must be redeemed.

21.text: You got six days to work, but on the seventh day, stop—even when it's planting and harvest season.

22.text: Celebrate the Festival of Harvest when y'all bring the first crops. And celebrate the Festival of Final Harvest when everything is gathered up.

23.text: Every man in Israel gotta appear before the Lord three times a year.

24.text: I'ma drive out your enemies and expand your land, and ain't nobody gon' mess with your territory while y'all worship me.

25.text: Don't offer my sacrifice with bread that got yeast in it. And don't keep no Passover meat overnight.

26.text: Bring the best of your first harvest to the Lord's house.

27.text: Then the Lord told Moses, 'Write all this down—this is the covenant I'm making with you and Israel.'

28.text: Moses stayed up there forty days and nights, no food, no water. The Lord wrote down the Ten Commandments on the tablets.

29.text: When Moses came down, holding the stone tablets, he ain't even know his face was glowing 'cause he been talking to the Lord.

30.text: When Aaron and the people saw his face shining, they got shook and didn't wanna come close.

31.text: But Moses called them over. Aaron and the leaders came first, and Moses spoke with them.

32.text: Then all the Israelites came, and Moses gave them all the instructions the Lord had told him.

33.text: Afterwards, Moses put on a veil to cover his face.

34.text: But whenever he went to talk to the Lord, he'd take off the veil till he came back.

35.text: Then he'd give the people God's instructions, and they'd see his face still glowing. So he'd put the veil back on till the next time he went to talk with the Lord.

1.text: Then Moses pulled up on the whole Israelite crew and told 'em, 'Aight y'all, listen up—this what the Lord commanded.'

2.text: 'Y'all got six days to handle your business and do all your work. But on the seventh day, that's the Sabbath—a holy day set aside for the Lord. Anybody who works that day? They gotta be put to death.'

3.text: 'Matter fact, don't even light a fire in ya crib on the Sabbath.'

4.text: Moses kept goin': 'This what the Lord commands y'all to do.

5.text: Everybody whose heart feel moved, bring an offering for the Lord.'

6.text: 'Here's what y'all need to bring: gold, silver, bronze,'

7.text: 'Blue, purple, and scarlet thread, fine linen, and goat hair for makin' cloth.'

8.text: 'Tanned ram skins, fine goatskin leather, and acacia wood.'

9.text: 'Olive oil for the lamps, spices for the anointing oil, and some good-smellin' incense.'

10.text: 'Onyx stones and other gems to be set in the ephod and priest's chestpiece.'

11.text: 'Now, all y'all skilled craftsmen—get ready to build everything the Lord commanded!'

12.text: 'That means the Tabernacle, its tent, covering, clasps, frames, crossbars, posts, and bases.'

13.text: 'The Ark of the Covenant and its carrying poles, plus the atonement cover that go on top of it.'

14.text: 'The inner curtain to shield the Ark.'

15.text: 'The table, its carrying poles, all the utensils, and the Bread of the Presence.'

16.text: 'The lampstand with all its accessories, the lamp cups, and the olive oil for keepin' it lit.'

17.text: 'The incense altar and its carrying poles, the anointing oil, the fragrant incense, and the curtain for the entrance of the Tabernacle.'

18.text: 'The altar of burnt offerings, its bronze grating, all its utensils, and the washbasin with its stand.'

19.text: 'The curtains for the courtyard walls, the posts and bases, and the entrance curtain to the courtyard.'

20.text: 'All the tent pegs for the Tabernacle and courtyard, plus all the ropes. Oh, and don't forget:'

21.text: 'The freshly stitched garments for the priests to wear in the Holy Place—Aaron's sacred clothes and the ones his sons gotta wear while they minister.'

22.text: After Moses finished speaking, everybody headed back to their tents.

23.text: Then everybody whose heart felt stirred came through with their offerings. Folks brought all the materials needed for the Tabernacle, the priestly garments, and all the rituals.

24.text: Men and women, whoever felt moved, pulled up with their gold—brooches, earrings, rings, necklaces—you name it. Everything was given to the Lord.

25.text: If folks had blue, purple, and scarlet thread, fine linen, goat hair, tanned ram skins, or fine leather, they brought it.

26.text: Anybody with silver and bronze? They gave it for the Lord. Those with acacia wood brought it too.

27.text: All the women skilled in sewing and spinning got to work, preppin' blue, purple, and scarlet thread, plus fine linen cloth.

28.text: All the women who knew how to spin goat hair into yarn jumped in too.

29.text: The leaders pulled up with onyx stones and special gemstones for the ephod and the priest's chestpiece.

30.text: They also brought spices and olive oil for the lights, anointing oil, and fragrant incense.

31.text: Basically, every man and woman who had it in their heart to give towards the Lord's work brought their gifts willingly. That's how they contributed to the Lord.

32.text: Then Moses told the people, 'Look, the Lord done picked out Bezalel son of Uri, grandson of Hur, from the tribe of Judah.'

33.text: 'The Lord filled him up with the Holy Spirit, giving him mad wisdom, skill, and talent for all kinds of crafts.

34.text: That boy a master craftsman—expert in gold, silver, and bronze work.'

35.text: 'He's skilled in engraving, gem-setting, wood-carving, and basically any creative work.'

36.text: 'But Bezalel ain't the only one—Oholiab, son of Ahisamach from the tribe of Dan, got that same anointing too. Plus, the Lord gave them the ability to teach others.'

37.text: 'God gave 'em special skills—engraving, designing, embroidering blue, purple, and scarlet thread on fine linen—and weaving. These dudes got the gift for craftsmanship and designing.'

1.text: The Lord gave Bezalel, Oholiab, and the rest of the skilled craftsmen wisdom and ability to do the work needed to build up the Lord's sanctuary. They gotta construct and furnish the Tabernacle just like the Lord commanded.

2.text: So Moses called up Bezalel, Oholiab, and all the skilled folks the Lord blessed who was eager to work.

3.text: Moses handed them all the materials the Israelites brought as offerings for the sanctuary. But the people kept bringing more gifts every morning.

4.text: Finally, the craftsmen stopped working and went to Moses.

5.text: They said, 'Look, the people brought more than enough to get this job done just like the Lord commanded.'

6.text: So Moses gave the order and spread the word through the camp: 'Aight y'all, stop bringing gifts. We good!'

7.text: The offerings they got was more than enough to finish the whole project.

8.text: The skilled craftsmen made ten curtains of fine linen, decorated with blue, purple, and scarlet thread, embroidered with cherubim.

9.text: All ten curtains was the same size—42 feet long & 6 feet wide.

10.text: They linked five curtains together to make one long piece, then did the same for the other five.

11.text: He made fifty loops of blue yarn along the edge of the last curtain in each set.

12.text: The fifty loops on one side lined up perfectly with the fifty loops on the other side.

13.text: Then he made fifty gold clasps to fasten the curtains together, making the Tabernacle one continuous piece.

14.text: He made eleven curtains of goat-hair cloth to serve as a tent covering for the Tabernacle.

15.text: Each of these eleven curtains was 45 feet long & 6 feet wide.

16.text: He joined five curtains together for one long piece and six curtains for another.

17.text: Fifty loops were made along the edges of each big curtain.

18.text: Then he made fifty bronze clasps to fasten 'em together, making one solid covering.

19.text: To top it off, he made a layer of tanned ram skins and a fine goatskin leather cover.

20.text: Bezalel built the frames of acacia wood.

21.text: Each frame stood 15 feet tall & 27 inches wide.

22.text: Each frame had two pegs at the bottom, and all of them was built the same way.

23.text: He made twenty frames for the south side of the Tabernacle.

24.text: He also made forty silver bases—two bases per frame to hold 'em in place.

25.text: For the north side, he made twenty more frames.

26.text: He made forty silver bases for them too—two per frame.

27.text: He made six frames for the rear (west side) of the Tabernacle.

28.text: Then he made two extra corner frames for reinforcement.

29.text: These corner frames was built as one solid unit, attached at the top & bottom with a single ring.

30.text: So in the back, the Tabernacle had eight frames set in sixteen silver bases—two per frame.

31.text: Then he made crossbars from acacia wood to link the frames—five for each side.

32.text: Five went on the north side, five on the south, and five on the rear side (west).

33.text: He made the middle crossbar to run from one end to the other.

34.text: All the frames was covered in gold, with gold rings to hold the crossbars.

35.text: Inside the Tabernacle, he made a special curtain of fine linen, embroidered with cherubim using blue, purple, and scarlet thread.

36.text: To hold it up, he made four acacia posts with gold hooks, set in silver bases.

37.text: For the entrance curtain, he made it from fine linen and embroidered it with designs in blue, purple, and scarlet thread.

38.text: This curtain hung on gold hooks, attached to five acacia posts, with gold tops and bronze bases.

1.text: Then Bezalel made the Ark of the Covenant out of acacia wood—a sacred chest 45 inches long, 27 inches wide, and 27 inches high.

2.text: He coated it inside and out with pure gold and put a gold trim around the edges.

3.text: Then he cast four gold rings and attached them to its four feet—two rings on each side.

4.text: He made poles from acacia wood and covered them in gold.

5.text: Then he slid the poles into the rings on the sides of the Ark, so it could be carried.

6.text: Next, he made the Ark's cover—aka the atonement cover—from pure gold, 45 inches long and 27 inches wide.

7.text: He sculpted two cherubim from hammered gold and put them on opposite ends of the atonement cover.

8.text: The cherubim were molded as one piece with the cover, their wings spread out over it.

9.text: They faced each other and looked down at the atonement cover, with their wings covering it protectively.

10.text: Then Bezalel made the table from acacia wood—36 inches long, 18 inches wide, and 27 inches high.

11.text: He covered it in pure gold and added a gold trim around the edges.

12.text: He decorated it with a 3-inch border and put gold molding around it.

13.text: Then he cast four gold rings and attached them at the four corners near the legs.

14.text: The rings were placed near the border, so they could hold the carrying poles.

15.text: He made the poles from acacia wood and covered them with gold.

16.text: Then he made special containers for the table—bowls, ladles, jars, and pitchers—all from pure gold, to be used for liquid offerings.

17.text: Then Bezalel made the lampstand from pure, hammered gold—a single piece including the base, center stem, lamp cups, buds, and petals.

18.text: The lampstand had six branches—three on each side.

19.text: Each of the six branches had three lamp cups, shaped like almond blossoms, with buds and petals.

20.text: The center stem had four lamp cups, also shaped like almond blossoms, complete with buds and petals.

21.text: There was an almond bud under each pair of branches, all made from one piece.

22.text: Everything—the almond buds, branches, and center stem—was crafted as a single piece from hammered pure gold.

23.text: He also made seven lamps for the lampstand, plus lamp snuffers and trays—all from pure gold.

24.text: The whole lampstand and its accessories were made from 75 pounds of pure gold.

25.text: Then Bezalel made the incense altar from acacia wood—18 inches square and 36 inches high—with horns carved from the same piece.

26.text: He coated the top, sides, and horns in pure gold and added a gold molding around the whole thing.

27.text: Then he made two gold rings and attached them on opposite sides below the gold molding—these were for the carrying poles.

28.text: He made poles from acacia wood and covered them in gold.

29.text: Then he made the sacred anointing oil and the fragrant incense, using the techniques of a skilled incense maker.

1.text: Then Bezalel built the altar for burnt offerings out of acacia wood—a square altar, 7.5 feet wide, 7.5 feet long, and 4.5 feet high.

2.text: He carved horns on each of the four corners, making them one solid piece with the altar, then coated the whole thing in bronze.

3.text: He made all the altar tools out of bronze—the ash buckets, shovels, basins, meat forks, and firepans.

4.text: Then he made a bronze grating and put it halfway down the side of the altar, under the ledge.

5.text: He cast four rings and attached them to the corners of the bronze grating to hold the carrying poles.

6.text: He made the poles from acacia wood and coated them with bronze.

7.text: Then he slid the poles through the rings on the sides of the altar, so it could be carried easily.

8.text: The altar was hollow, made out of wooden planks.

9.text: Then Bezalel made the bronze washbasin and its stand from bronze mirrors donated by the women who served at the entrance of the Tabernacle.

10.text: Then Bezalel built the courtyard around the Tabernacle, enclosing it with curtains made of fine woven linen. The south side curtains were 150 feet long.

11.text: He set up twenty posts, each one securely placed in a bronze base. He hung the curtains with silver hooks and rings.

12.text: He built the north side the same way—150 feet of curtains hung on twenty posts with bronze bases, silver hooks, and rings.

13.text: The west side of the courtyard was 75 feet long, supported by ten posts in ten bases, hung with silver hooks and rings.

14.text: The east side—the front entrance—was also 75 feet long.

15.text: The courtyard entrance had two curtains, one on each side. The right-side curtain was 22.5 feet long, supported by three posts in three bases.

16.text: The left-side curtain was also 22.5 feet long, supported by three posts in three bases.

17.text: All the curtains in the courtyard were made of fine woven linen.

18.text: Each post had a bronze base, with silver hooks and rings. The tops of the posts were covered in silver, and the curtain rings were also silver.

19.text: He made the entrance curtain for the courtyard out of fine woven linen and embroidered it with blue, purple, and scarlet thread.

20.text: The entrance curtain was 30 feet long and 7.5 feet high, just like the other courtyard walls.

21.text: It was held up by four posts, each set into its own bronze base. The tops of the posts were covered in silver, and the hooks and rings were silver too.

22.text: All the tent pegs used for the Tabernacle and courtyard were made of bronze.

23.text: This is the inventory list for everything used in building the Tabernacle of the Covenant. The Levites put it together, following Moses' instructions, and Ithamar (Aaron's son) was in charge of keeping records.

24.text: Bezalel, son of Uri (grandson of Hur), from the tribe of Judah, made everything the Lord commanded Moses.

25.text: Oholiab, son of Ahisamach, from the tribe of Dan, was his assistant—a skilled engraver, designer, and embroiderer in blue, purple, and scarlet thread on fine linen.

26.text: The people donated 2,193 pounds of gold for the Tabernacle, measured by the sanctuary shekel.

27.text: The whole Israelite community donated 7,545 pounds of silver, also measured by the sanctuary shekel.

28.text: This silver came from the tax collected from each man counted in the census—one beka per person (half a shekel, measured by the sanctuary shekel). It was collected from 603,550 men, all 20 years or older.

29.text: A total of 7,500 pounds of silver was used for the 100 bases of the sanctuary walls and the inner curtain posts—75 pounds per base.

30.text: The remaining 45 pounds of silver was used for hooks, rings, and silver overlays for the post tops.

31.text: The people also brought 5,310 pounds of bronze as a special offering.

32.text: This bronze was used to cast the bases for the posts at the entrance of the Tabernacle and to make the bronze altar with its grating and utensils.

33.text: Bronze was also used for the bases of the courtyard posts, the bases of the entrance curtain posts, and all the tent pegs for the Tabernacle and courtyard.

1.text: The skilled craftsmen made the sacred garments from blue, purple, and scarlet cloth—these were the special clothes Aaron wore when he worked in the Holy Place, just like the Lord told Moses.

2.text: Bezalel made the ephod from fine linen and embroidered it with gold, blue, purple, and scarlet thread.

3.text: He made gold thread by hammering out thin sheets of gold, cutting them into fine strands, and weaving them into the fabric with the blue, purple, and scarlet thread.

4.text: The ephod had two parts, one in the front and one in the back, joined together at the shoulders.

5.text: The decorative sash was made from the same material—fine linen, embroidered with gold, blue, purple, and scarlet thread, just like the Lord commanded Moses.

6.text: They mounted two onyx stones in gold settings and engraved them with the names of the twelve tribes of Israel, just like a jeweler engraves a seal.

7.text: They attached these stones to the shoulder pieces of the ephod, as a reminder that the priest represents Israel whenever he comes before the Lord. Everything was done just like the Lord told Moses.

8.text: Bezalel made the chestpiece with great skill, to match the ephod, using fine linen embroidered with gold, blue, purple, and scarlet thread.

9.text: The chestpiece was made as one single piece of fabric, folded to form a pouch, measuring 9 inches square.

10.text: He mounted four rows of gemstones on it. The first row had a red carnelian, a pale-green peridot, and an emerald.

11.text: The second row had a turquoise, a lapis lazuli, and a white moonstone.

12.text: The third row had an orange jacinth, an agate, and a purple amethyst.

13.text: The fourth row had a blue-green beryl, an onyx, and a green jasper.

14.text: Each stone represented one of the twelve tribes of Israel, and their names were engraved like a seal.

15.text: To attach the chestpiece to the ephod, they made braided cords of pure gold.

16.text: They also made two settings of gold filigree and two gold rings, attaching them to the top corners of the chestpiece.

17.text: They tied the gold cords to the rings on the chestpiece.

18.text: The other ends of the gold cords were tied to the gold settings on the shoulder-pieces of the ephod.

19.text: They made two more gold rings and attached them to the inside edges of the chestpiece, next to the ephod.

20.text: Then they made two more gold rings and attached them to the front of the ephod, just below the shoulder-pieces, above the decorative sash.

21.text: They attached the bottom rings of the chestpiece to the rings on the ephod with blue cords. This way, the chestpiece stayed securely in place. Everything was done just like the Lord told Moses.

22.text: Bezalel made the robe that went with the ephod from one solid piece of blue woven cloth.

23.text: The robe had a hole for Aaron's head, reinforced with a woven collar so it wouldn't tear.

24.text: They decorated the hem of the robe with pomegranates made from blue, purple, and scarlet yarn.

25.text: They made gold bells and placed them between the pomegranates along the hem of the robe.

26.text: The bells and pomegranates alternated all around the hem. This robe was worn whenever Aaron ministered before the Lord, just like the Lord commanded Moses.

27.text: They made tunics for Aaron and his sons from fine linen cloth.

28.text: They made the turban and special head coverings from fine linen. The undergarments were also made from finely woven linen.

29.text: They made the sashes from fine linen, embroidered with blue, purple, and scarlet thread, just like the Lord commanded Moses.

30.text: Finally, they made the sacred medallion—the badge of holiness—out of pure gold.

31.text: They engraved it like a seal with the words: "Holy to the Lord."

32.text: They attached the medallion to Aaron's turban with a blue cord, just like the Lord commanded Moses.

33.text: Finally, the Tabernacle was finished. The Israelites did everything exactly the way the Lord commanded Moses.

34.text: They brought everything to Moses: The sacred tent with all its furnishings, clasps, frames, crossbars, posts, and bases. The tent coverings of tanned ram skins and fine goatskin leather. The inner curtain to shield the Ark.

35.text: The Ark of the Covenant and its carrying poles.

36.text: The Ark's cover—the place of atonement.

37.text: The table and all its utensils.

38.text: The Bread of the Presence.

39.text: The pure gold lampstand with its symmetrical lamp cups, accessories, and olive oil for lighting.

40.text: The gold altar.

41.text: The anointing oil and fragrant incense.

42.text: The curtain for the entrance of the sacred tent.

43.text: The bronze altar, the bronze grating, its carrying poles and utensils.

44.text: The washbasin with its stand.

45.text: The curtains for the walls of the courtyard.

46.text: The posts and their bases.

47.text: The curtain for the entrance to the courtyard.

48.text: The ropes and tent pegs.

49.text: All the furnishings used for worship in the Tabernacle.

50.text: The beautifully stitched garments for the priests to wear while serving in the Holy Place—including the sacred garments for Aaron the priest and his sons.

51.text: So the people of Israel followed all the Lord's instructions to Moses.

52.text: Then Moses inspected everything, and when he saw that it had all been done exactly as the Lord commanded, he blessed them.

1.text: Then the Lord spoke to Moses, saying,

2.text: "On the first day of the new year, set up the Tabernacle."

3.text: "Put the Ark of the Covenant inside, and hang up the inner curtain to enclose the Ark inside the Most Holy Place."

4.text: "Bring in the table, arrange the utensils, and set up the lampstand with the lamps."

5.text: "Place the gold incense altar in front of the Ark of the Covenant, then hang the curtain at the entrance of the Tabernacle."

6.text: "Put the altar of burnt offering in front of the Tabernacle entrance."

7.text: "Set the washbasin between the Tabernacle and the altar, and fill it up with water."

8.text: "Then set up the courtyard all around the outside of the tent, and hang the curtain for the courtyard entrance."

9.text: "Take the anointing oil and anoint the Tabernacle and everything inside to set them apart as holy."

10.text: "Anoint the altar of burnt offering and all its utensils to consecrate them. Then the altar will become completely holy."

11.text: "Anoint the washbasin and its stand, and set them apart as holy."

12.text: "Bring Aaron and his sons to the Tabernacle entrance, and wash them with water."

13.text: "Dress Aaron in his priestly garments, anoint him, and consecrate him to serve as priest."

14.text: "Then bring his sons, dress them in their tunics,"

15.text: "Anoint them just like their father, so they too may serve as priests. With this anointing, the priesthood will be set apart for Aaron's family forever."

16.text: Moses did everything exactly the way the Lord commanded.

17.text: So, on the first day of the first month, in the second year, the Tabernacle was set up.

18.text: Moses set down the bases, raised up the frames, attached the crossbars, and set up the posts.

19.text: Then he spread out the coverings over the Tabernacle and put on the protective layers, just as the Lord had commanded.

20.text: He took the stone tablets with the covenant terms and put them inside the Ark of the Covenant.

21.text: Then he brought the Ark into the Tabernacle and hung the inner curtain, shielding it from view, just as the Lord commanded.

22.text: Moses put the table in the Tabernacle, on the north side outside the inner curtain.

23.text: He arranged the Bread of the Presence on the table before the Lord, just as the Lord commanded.

24.text: He set up the lampstand across from the table, on the south side of the Holy Place.

25.text: Then he lit the lamps in the Lord's presence, just like the Lord commanded.

26.text: He placed the gold incense altar inside the Tabernacle, in front of the inner curtain.

27.text: Then he burned fragrant incense on it, just like the Lord commanded.

28.text: He hung up the curtain at the entrance of the Tabernacle.

29.text: Moses placed the altar of burnt offering near the Tabernacle entrance.

30.text: Then he put the washbasin between the Tabernacle and the altar, filling it with water for the priests to wash themselves.

31.text: Moses, Aaron, and Aaron's sons washed their hands and feet from the washbasin.

32.text: Whenever they approached the altar or entered the Tabernacle, they washed themselves, just like the Lord commanded Moses.

33.text: Then he hung the curtains around the courtyard and put up the curtain at the entrance. At last, Moses finished the work.

34.text: Then the cloud covered the Tabernacle, and the glory of the Lord filled the whole place.

35.text: Moses couldn't enter the Tabernacle, because the cloud had settled over it, and the Lord's glory filled it up.

36.text: Whenever the cloud lifted from the Tabernacle, the people of Israel would set out and continue their journey.

37.text: But if the cloud didn't rise, they stayed where they were until it did.

38.text: The cloud of the Lord hovered over the Tabernacle by day, and at night it glowed like fire so that all the Israelites could see it. This continued throughout all their journeys.

1.text: It was year thirty for me, fourth month, fifth day—I was chillin' with the other exiles by the Chebar River, when boom! The heavens cracked open and I saw somethin' straight divine.

2.text: This was in year five since King Jehoiachin got snatched up. Mark that down.

3.text: That's when the word of the Lord came through loud and clear to me—Ezekiel, a priest, son of Buzi. We was in Babylonian land, by that same river. And right there, God laid His hand heavy on me.

4.text: I looked up—and whoa! A whirlwind came rushin' out the north. A big storm cloud, on fire from the inside, light shootin' out like it was burnin' gold, bright and wild in every direction.

5.text: In the middle of all that fire? Four strange-lookin' creatures. They had a human form… but they was definitely not human.

6.text: Each one had four faces and four wings.

7.text: Their legs was straight like poles, feet like calf hooves—but they shined like polished bronze. Straight gleamin'.

8.text: Under them wings? Human hands on all four sides. And every single one of these creatures had faces and wings.

9.text: Their wings touched each other—like they moved in sync. They ain't turn when they walked either. Nah, they moved straight ahead, like they was on assignment.

10.text: Now, these faces? Wild. Each had four: A human face upfront, A lion face on the right, An ox face on the left, And an eagle face on the back.

11.text: Their wings stretched up—two of 'em touched each other, two covered their bodies like cloaks.

12.text: And when they moved? They followed the Spirit. No hesitation, no detours. Just… straight where the Spirit said go.

13.text: These beings looked like they was made of fire—like coals glowin' and torches dancin'. Lightning flashed out from 'em, and they darted back and forth like bolts of light. Blink and you'd miss it.

14.text: They was movin' like ZOOM!—just a flash.

15.text: I peeped the ground near each creature and saw a wheel beside each one. And these wheels? Nah, not regular. They was something else.

16.text: The wheels looked like shimmering beryl stone. All four had the same setup—like a wheel inside another wheel, interlocked but free.

17.text: When they moved, they could shift in any direction, but still never turned. Just rolled wherever the Spirit said go.

18.text: The rims? So tall, they was intimidating. And the rims had eyes all around—watchin' everything. Every angle. Nothing got past 'em.

19.text: When the creatures moved, the wheels moved too. When they lifted up, the wheels lifted too.

20.text: Wherever the Spirit wanted to go, they went—and the wheels followed, because the Spirit of the creatures was in the wheels.

21.text: If the creatures moved, the wheels moved. If the creatures stopped, the wheels stopped. They was connected deep, spiritually synced.

22.text: Above their heads was somethin' like a dome—a vault of crystal, shiny and awe-inspiring, stretched out like the sky.

23.text: Underneath that dome, their wings spread out—two wings each touchin' another creature, two coverin' their own bodies.

24.text: When they flew, it sounded like roaring water, like God Himself was speakin'. Loud like an army rushin'. But when they stopped, the wings dropped silent.

25.text: Then I heard a voice—from above the dome that was over their heads.

26.text: And above that dome? A throne. It looked like it was carved from sapphire. And sittin' on that throne? A figure—a Man, high and lifted.

27.text: From the waist up, He glowed like molten metal, fire swirlin' all around. From the waist down? Fire again, with brilliance shootin' out like the sun.

28.text: The whole thing lit up like a rainbow on a rainy day—that's what the glory of the Lord looked like. When I saw it, I hit the ground. Face to the dirt. Couldn't even speak. And then I heard a voice… talkin' to me.

1.text: Then He told me, "Get up, son of man. Stand on your feet—I got somethin' to say to you."

2.text: Soon as He spoke, the Spirit filled me up and stood me upright. I could hear His voice, clear as day.

3.text: He said, "Listen up, son of man. I'm sendin' you to Israel—yeah, the whole nation. They wildin'. They been rebelled against Me for generations. This ain't new—they mama and daddy been actin' up too.

4.text: These folks hardheaded and got no shame. But I'm still sendin' you. And you gon' tell them straight up, 'This what the Lord God said.'

5.text: Whether they wanna listen or not—'cause trust, they some rebellious folks—they gon' know a real prophet done stepped in the room.

6.text: Now you, son of man, don't be scared of 'em. Don't let their words or their threats shake you. Even if you feel like you livin' in a field full of thorns, or chillin' with scorpions—still, don't be shook. Don't let they mean mugs or side-eyes faze you. They rebellious, yeah—but I still need you to speak.

7.text: You gon' say exactly what I tell you. Don't matter if they listen or not. Say it anyway. They need to hear it.

8.text: But listen—you, son of man, don't be like them. Don't rebel like they do. Open your mouth and eat what I give you."

9.text: Then I looked up—and saw a hand reachin' out to me. In it? A scroll. Like a heavenly book.

10.text: He opened it in front of me. Both sides was full of words—front and back. But it wasn't no happy story. Nah—it was full of sorrow, pain, and warnings. Grief on every line.

1.text: Then He told me, "Son of man, eat what I'm givin' you. This scroll right here—consume it. Then go speak to Israel."

2.text: So I opened my mouth, and He fed me that scroll Himself.

3.text: He said, "Fill your belly, son. Let this Word get down in your soul." I ate it, and no lie—it tasted sweet, like honey on my tongue.

4.text: Then He said, "Now go. Take these words I just gave you and speak 'em to Israel.

5.text: I ain't sendin' you to folks speakin' a foreign tongue or some language you can't decode. Nah—I'm sendin' you to your own people.

6.text: If I had sent you to another nation with unfamiliar speech, they'd probably listen. They would've paid attention.

7.text: But not Israel. They stubborn, hardheaded, and spiritually deaf. They don't listen to Me, so they won't listen to you either.

8.text: But don't trip—I made your face just as strong as theirs. Matter fact, stronger. Your forehead tougher than theirs.

9.text: I gave you a head like flint—like stone that can't be cracked. So don't be scared of they looks, don't be shook by they attitude. They still rebellious, but you built for this."

10.text: Then He told me, "Son of man, take all these words to heart. Lock 'em in. Listen close.

11.text: Then get up, go to your people in exile, and tell 'em, 'This what the Lord God said'—whether they down to listen or not."

12.text: Right then the Spirit lifted me up. And behind me I heard this loud voice like thunder yellin', "Blessed be the glory of the Lord from where He reigns!"

13.text: I also heard the sound of wings—the ones from them creatures—all clappin' together, and the wheels right next to 'em rumblin'. It was loud, like a storm hittin'.

14.text: The Spirit carried me off, and I was heated. Heart heavy, bitter spirit. But God's hand was holdin' me the whole way.

15.text: I got to Tel Abib, where the exiles stayed by the Chebar River. I sat with them in silence—shocked, overwhelmed—for seven whole days.

16.text: After them seven days, God spoke again:

17.text: "Son of man, I'm makin' you a watchman over Israel. That means you gotta listen when I speak, and then warn the people straight up.

18.text: If I say, 'This wicked person gon' die,' and you don't say nothin'—don't warn 'em, don't tell 'em to turn from their mess—they'll die in their sin. But you? I'll hold you accountable for that blood.

19.text: But if you do warn them and they still choose evil, they'll die in their own sin. But you? You off the hook. You did your part.

20.text: Now if a righteous person flips and starts wildin', and I put a trap in their path and you don't speak up? They gon' die too. And everything good they ever did? Wiped clean. And guess what? I'm holdin' you responsible.

21.text: But if you warn that righteous person not to slip up, and they listen? They gon' live. And you? You saved your own soul by speakin' up."

22.text: Then God's hand pressed on me again. He said, "Get up. Go out into the open plains—I got somethin' to tell you there."

23.text: So I went. And sure enough, the same glory I saw back at the Chebar River showed up again, heavy and radiant. I fell on my face.

24.text: Then the Spirit picked me up, stood me on my feet, and spoke: "Go home, Ezekiel. Shut yourself in the house.

25.text: Look—they gon' try to tie you up, bind you with ropes so you can't move around or speak freely.

26.text: I'm gon' shut your mouth for a time. Your tongue? It'll stick to the roof of your mouth. You won't be able to call 'em out or correct 'em—even though they rebellious.

27.text: But when I give you the cue, I'll open your mouth again. And you gon' say, 'This what the Lord God says.' Whoever wanna listen, let 'em listen. Whoever don't, that's on them. They a rebellious house, through and through."

1.text: God said, "Alright, son of man, it's time for a visual. Grab a clay tablet, lay it in front of you, and draw the city of Jerusalem on it.

2.text: Then set the scene—build up siege walls, stack up dirt mounds like you ready for war, post up army camps, and place battering rams all around. Show how the enemy gon' pull up on Jerusalem.

3.text: And take an iron plate—set it like a wall between you and the city. Lock your gaze on it. Face it like it's personal. That's the message: this city under siege, and it ain't no way out. That right there gon' be a sign for all Israel."

4.text: "Now here's where it gets heavy—lay on your left side. Symbolically take on all the mess, all the guilt, all the sin of Israel. You gon' hold it.

5.text: I'm giving you 390 days—one day for each year they been wildin'. That's how long you gon' lay there, takin' on their foolishness.

6.text: When that's done, flip to your right side. Now you hold Judah's sin—forty days. One day per year. Same deal.

7.text: The whole time, keep your face locked on that Jerusalem setup. Arm bare. Ready to prophesy against it like a one-man army.

8.text: And just so you don't get slick and flip sides early—I'ma hold you in place. You ain't movin' till the time is up."

9.text: "Now, for your food: gather wheat, barley, beans, lentils, millet, and spelt. Mix 'em all together in one pot and make bread out of it. That's what you gon' eat for those 390 days.

10.text: But it ain't a feast. You eat 20 shekels of it a day—rationed out. Small bites, spread thin.

11.text: Same with your water—measure it out. One-sixth of a hin. Sip slow, because that's all you got.

12.text: And this gon' shock the people: bake that bread like a barley cake, but use human waste for fuel. Yeah, let 'em see you cookin' with that. This gon' show how foul it's gon' be when they exiled."

13.text: Then God said, "This how the Israelites gon' eat—defiled food, in foreign lands, far from home. That's the consequence."

14.text: I said, "Lord God! Please! I've never defiled myself like that—not ever. I don't eat roadkill or animals torn up by beasts. I don't touch unclean food. I've kept it clean since I was a kid."

15.text: And God, full of mercy, said, "Alright. I'll let you use cow dung instead of human waste. Bake your bread over that."

16.text: Then He hit me with another word: "Son of man, I'ma cut off the food supply in Jerusalem. Folks gon' weigh out bread in fear. Gon' drink water with trembling hands.

17.text: They'll be lookin' at each other confused, sick with worry, wastin' away from their sin. They gon' know this is judgment. And it's real."

1.text: God said, "Alright, son of man, grab a sharp sword—use it like clippers. Shave your head and beard clean off. Then pull out some scales and divide up that hair. This ain't for style—this symbolic.

2.text: Burn one-third of it in the city when the siege ends. Take another third and slash it up with a sword around the city. And the last third? Toss it in the wind—I'ma send swords chasin' after it.

3.text: Now take a small handful, just a remnant, and tuck it in your clothes—right in the hem.

4.text: But then, even from that little bit, pull some out again and toss it in the fire. Burn it. Because from that fire? Flames gon' spread through all Israel."

5.text: "This what the Lord God says: This is Jerusalem. I put her right in the center of the nations—surrounded by everybody else.

6.text: But instead of leadin' right, she wilded out worse than the nations around her. Disrespected My rules. Ignored My commands. Acted like she ain't know Me at all.

7.text: So because y'all broke My laws even harder than the heathens? Didn't even try to act right? Not even on their level?

8.text: I, the Lord, am comin' against you. I'm bout to make an example outta you in front of everybody.

9.text: What I'm about to do to y'all? Never been done before. And I won't do it again. That's how deep y'all in it.

10.text: Fathers gon' eat their sons. Sons gon' eat their fathers. This ain't no metaphor. Judgment gon' hit that hard. And whoever survives? I'm scatterin' you to the wind."

11.text: "As surely as I live," says the Lord God, "because y'all defiled My sanctuary—brought in filth, idols, and nasty habits—I'ma cut you down. I ain't sparin' nobody. No mercy.

12.text: One-third of y'all gon' die from disease and starvation. One-third gon' get dropped by the sword. And the last third? Y'all gon' be scattered, but I'ma still have swords followin' you.

13.text: That's how My anger gon' cool off. My fury gon' be spent. They'll know I'm the Lord when I unleash all this in full force.

14.text: I'ma leave your city lookin' like a wasteland—an embarrassment to every nation walkin' by. Straight shame.

15.text: Folks gon' look at what happened to you and shake their heads. Gon' talk about it like a horror story. Lesson learned, example made. I said it. The Lord.

16.text: When I send famine your way—deadly arrows of destruction—they gon' hit. Bread supply? Gone. Starvin' gon' be the norm.

17.text: And on top of that? Wild animals gon' take y'all kids. Plagues and bloodshed gon' sweep through the streets. And the sword? It's still comin'. I, the Lord, have spoken."

1.text: The word of the Lord came to me again, sayin':

2.text: "Son of man, turn your face toward the mountains of Israel and start speakin' against 'em.

3.text: Tell the mountains, the hills, the valleys, the ravines—'Yo, listen up! This what the Lord God say: I'm comin' through with the sword. And I'm about to tear down every single one of y'all's high places.'

4.text: All them altars you built? Gon'. The incense spots? Crushed. And the folks who bowed down there? They bodies gon' be layin' face-down in front of them fake gods they loved so much.

5.text: I'ma throw y'all corpses down in front of them same idols. Scattered bones all around the altars. No honor. No peace.

6.text: Every place y'all lived gon' be wrecked. Cities? Gone. High places? Desolate. Altars smashed. Idols broken. Incense spots burned out. And everything y'all made with your hands? Abolished.

7.text: Dead bodies everywhere. In the middle of all this? Y'all gon' finally know I'm the Lord."

8.text: "But I ain't wiping everybody out. I'ma leave a remnant. A few of y'all gon' make it out alive, scattered in other countries, far from home.

9.text: And while y'all sittin' in them foreign lands, some of y'all gon' remember Me. Y'all gon' realize how y'all broke My heart with that adulterous spirit—chasin' every idol that caught your eye. Y'all stepped out on Me. When it hit you? Y'all gon' hate what you did. Sick of yourselves for all the nasty things y'all was doin'.

10.text: And when that happens, y'all gon' know I wasn't just talkin' to talk. I meant every word of that judgment I said was comin'."

11.text: "Now go on, son of man—pound your fists. Stomp your feet. Let the people feel the weight of this word. Say, 'Woe to all the disgusting sins Israel's out here doin'! They gon' die by sword, by famine, and by disease.'

12.text: Don't matter where they at—far off? Disease gon' catch 'em. Close by? Sword gon' slice 'em. Trapped inside the city? Starvation gon' eat 'em alive. That's how I'm lettin' My anger out."

13.text: "Then y'all gon' know I ain't playin'. Y'all gon' see the dead bodies laid out by their idols, by the altars, on every hilltop, every mountaintop, under every leafy tree, under every big ol' oak—anywhere they thought was a good place to burn sweet incense to fake gods.

14.text: I'ma stretch My hand against y'all and make the whole land desolate. Wiped clean. Worse than the wasteland by Diblah. Everywhere they used to live? Ghost town. Then they'll know—I am the Lord."

1.text: The word of the Lord came to me again:

2.text: "Son of man, speak this to Israel: 'It's the end. You hear Me? The end. It's hittin' every corner of this land.

3.text: The end is knockin' on your door now. And I ain't holdin' back no more—My anger comin' full force. I'm gon' judge you based on your actions, And pay you back for all the dirty things you done.

4.text: Don't expect mercy. Don't expect a pass. I'm givin' you exactly what you earned. Your sins gon' rise up in your own face, And then you gon' know—I'm the Lord."

5.text: "This what the Lord God say: Disaster. One big, unstoppable disaster. Look—it's already here.

6.text: The end done arrived. Time's up. Ain't no delay. It's dawning right now, and it's all comin' down.

7.text: Doom is here, y'all. This ain't no time for celebrations in the hills. This a day of trouble, not joy.

8.text: My fury comin' down on you heavy. I'm emptyin' My anger all the way out. You gon' be judged, and paid in full for your wicked ways.

9.text: Don't expect Me to flinch or feel sorry. I'm not blinkin'. I'm not lookin away. Your mess is comin' back on you—and I'm the One bringin' it. Then you gon' know who I am. I'm the One who strikes."

10.text: "Look—the day's here. Doom's already movin'. Arrogance blossomed, pride popped off, And now? Violence got a whole baton in its hand like a relay runner.

11.text: Wickedness is struttin' through the city like it run things. But ain't nobody safe. Not one person, not one crew, not one family. And don't expect tears—ain't nobody cryin' over this.

12.text: The time is now. The day is close. Don't get hype if you just bought somethin'. Don't mourn if you just sold somethin'. God's wrath comin' for everybody.

13.text: And don't think you gon' get your stuff back, even if you still alive. This vision applies to everybody. Ain't no exceptions. And if you been livin' foul, Ain't nothin' gon' give you strength now."

14.text: "They blowin' trumpets like they ready for battle, But nobody movin'. God's wrath done froze the whole squad.

15.text: Outside, the sword gon' cut folks down. Inside? Starvation and sickness gon' take the rest. Field or city—it don't matter. Death everywhere.

16.text: Whoever makes it out alive? They gon' run to the mountains, weepin' like doves, Each one cryin' over how dirty they've been.

17.text: Every hand gon' be limp. Every knee gon' feel like jelly. No strength, no courage, just fear.

18.text: Sackcloth on their bodies, Terror on their faces, Shame on every head, And bald patches where grief done snatched their pride."

19.text: "They gon' throw silver in the streets, Gold like it's trash. All that money? Can't save 'em. It won't feed their souls, won't fill their stomachs. Greed was the very trap that took 'em out.

20.text: They took the beauty I gave 'em and turned it into idols. Turned My blessings into blasphemy. So now? It's garbage to Me.

21.text: I'ma let foreigners come take all of it. Evil folks gon' raid it. And when they touch it? It's defiled.

22.text: I'm turnin' My face away. They gon' invade My sacred space, Even the most secret places. Robbers gon' stroll in and ruin everything."

23.text: "Start makin' chains. This land soaked in blood. The whole city overflowin' with violence.

24.text: So I'ma bring in the worst of the nations. They takin' over houses, And I'ma shut down the pride of the strong. Even the sacred spots gon' be desecrated.

25.text: Destruction is here. They gon' look for peace—but it won't exist.

26.text: Disaster after disaster. Rumors on top of rumors. They gon' run to prophets—nothin'. The priests? Don't have no law left. The elders? Ain't got no advice.

27.text: The king gon' mourn, The prince gon' be numb with shock, And the people? Shakin' in fear. I'm gon' judge them exactly how they lived. They reapin' what they sowed. And then—then—they gon' know: I am the Lord."

1.text: It was year six, month six, day five—I was sittin' in the crib, chillin' with some of the elders of Judah, when boom—the hand of the Lord God came down on me heavy.

2.text: I looked up and saw what looked like a man made of fire—waist down, full flame; waist up, glowing like amber, shinin' like glory.

3.text: Then He reached out—looked like a hand—and grabbed me by a lock of my hair. The Spirit lifted me between heaven and earth and dropped me off in a vision, right in Jerusalem, at the entrance of the inner court's north gate—where that scandalous "idol of jealousy" was sittin', makin' God mad on sight.

4.text: But even with all that, the glory of the God of Israel was still there—just like I saw back in the plains.

5.text: He said, "Son of man, look up toward the north." So I looked—and boom, there it was. That same idol of jealousy sittin' at the entrance, bold and disrespectful.

6.text: He said, "You see this mess? This what Israel out here doin' in My own house—things so foul they drivin' Me away from My own sanctuary. But hold up—keep watchin'. It gets worse."

7.text: He took me to the outer court. I saw a hole in the wall.

8.text: He said, "Dig in." So I dug through the wall—there was a door behind it.

9.text: He said, "Go in and look at the filth they tryna hide."

10.text: I stepped in and saw it—walls covered with every creepy, filthy creature you could think of. Nasty animals and idol drawings everywhere—this was Israel's hidden idol gallery.

11.text: And standing right there? Seventy elders of Israel. All up in it. Burning incense. One of 'em—Jaazaniah, son of Shaphan—was leadin' the whole vibe. Cloud of smoke rising like it was holy, but it was pure abomination.

12.text: God said, "You see this? These so-called leaders think I don't see them. They actin' like I done left the land, so now they worshipin' in the dark—each one got his own private idol room. Secret sins on display."

13.text: Then He said, "Come on, it gets worse."

14.text: He brought me to the north gate of the Lord's house again—and what I see? Women sittin' there cryin' for Tammuz, some false god from the streets. Heartbreakin', but not for Me—for that idol.

15.text: He said, "You see this? You ain't seen nothin' yet."

16.text: Then He took me inside the inner court—right by the temple porch. And there were about twenty-five men. But get this—they had their backs to the temple of the Lord and they was facin' east, bowin' down to the sun. Turned their back on God, literally.

17.text: He said, "You see this, son of man? You think this some light offense? These folks out here doin' the most—disrespectin' Me in My own house, floodin' the land with violence, and still tryna provoke Me. They even got the nerve to do this little 'branch to the nose' gesture—like they makin' fun of Me!"

18.text: "So I'ma act. And I ain't holdin' back. I ain't sparin' nobody, and I ain't listenin' to no fake tears. They could scream loud as they want—I'm not hearin' 'em."

1.text: Then I heard Him call out with a booming voice: "Bring the enforcers. The ones responsible for this city—each one need to show up strapped, weapon in hand."

2.text: And just like that, six men came walkin' from the upper gate that faces north. Every one of them had a battle-ax in hand, ready for business. But one of 'em stood out—dressed in linen, lookin' clean. He had a scribe's kit on his hip, like he was takin' names. They all rolled up and posted by the bronze altar.

3.text: Then the glory of the God of Israel lifted up from between the cherubim and moved to the entrance of the temple. And God spoke to the man in linen with the writing gear:

4.text: "Go through the city—walk through Jerusalem—and mark the foreheads of everyone who mourns and cries over the nasty, evil stuff goin' on. The ones still grievin' over sin? Mark 'em."

5.text: Then He turned to the other six and said, "Now y'all follow right behind him. And when you do—wipe everybody else out. Don't hesitate. Don't show pity.

6.text: Old men, young men, women, kids—all of 'em. If they don't got that mark, take 'em out. But don't you dare touch anyone with the mark. Start at My house. Start at the sanctuary." So they began right there—with the elders, the so-called leaders, who were in front of the temple.

7.text: God said, "Y'all see what they turned My house into? Fill these courts with the bodies. Let this place feel the weight of what's been done. Now go out and finish it in the city." And they did.

8.text: While all this was happening, I was left there, shook and alone. I fell on my face and cried out, "Lord God… is You really about to wipe out everybody that's left? Even the few that's still here in Jerusalem? Is this it?"

9.text: He said, "Listen, Ezekiel. The sin in Israel and Judah? It's off the charts. The land is soaked in blood. The city is full of twisted, violent acts. And the people? They bold with it. They say, 'God don't see us. He gone. Ain't nobody watchin.'"

10.text: But Me? I ain't sparin' nobody. I'm not lookin' away. I'm givin' everybody exactly what they deserve."

11.text: Then, right on time, the man in linen—the one with the inkhorn—came back and said, "It's done. I did everything You told me to."

1.text: I looked up—and there it was again. Above the heads of the cherubim, in that glowing space, sat something like a throne. Looked like deep sapphire, royal and radiant.

2.text: Then God spoke to the man in linen: "Go in between the wheels, under the cherubim. Scoop up them hot coals from between 'em and scatter the fire all over the city." And he did—walked in right as I watched.

3.text: The cherubim were standin' on the south side of the temple when the linen-clothed man stepped in, and suddenly, whoosh!—a thick cloud filled the inner court.

4.text: The glory of the Lord rose up from the cherubim's position and paused right at the temple door. The whole place got hazy—thick with smoke and light. That glory hit different. Even the outer court was lit up with the presence of the Lord.

5.text: And the sound? The wings of them cherubim flappin' echoed through the courts—loud like the voice of the Almighty Himself.

6.text: Then it happened. God gave the command again: "Grab fire from the wheels between the cherubim." The man in linen stepped up next to the wheels.

7.text: One of the cherubim reached into the fire, pulled out a burning coal, and dropped it in the linen man's hands. He took it and dipped.

8.text: And under their wings, the cherubim had hands—human-looking hands, hidden beneath the glory.

9.text: Then I looked at the wheels—four of 'em, one for each cherub. Shimmering like beryl stone. But again—this wasn't your average wheel setup.

10.text: All four looked exactly the same: like a wheel inside another wheel—interlocking, multidimensional, supernatural.

11.text: When they moved, they didn't turn or curve—they went straight ahead in whichever direction the cherub's face was pointing.

12.text: Their whole bodies—backs, hands, wings, even the wheels—covered in eyes. They was seein' everything. Every angle. Nothing missed.

13.text: And I heard the name for them: "Wheel."

14.text: Each cherub had four faces: A cherub face, A human face, A lion's face, And an eagle's face.

15.text: The cherubim lifted off the ground—same heavenly beings I saw by the River Chebar. Ain't no doubt.

16.text: When they moved, the wheels moved too. When they rose up, the wheels rose right with 'em. They stayed in sync—one spirit in all of them.

17.text: When the cherubim paused, the wheels paused. When they lifted, the wheels lifted too. They was linked deep, spiritually.

18.text: Then the glory of the Lord moved again. It lifted from the temple entrance and hovered above the cherubim.

19.text: And the cherubim spread their wings and rose from the earth—right in front of me. The wheels rolled right with them. They stopped at the east gate of the Lord's house. And there, above them, rested the glory of the God of Israel.

20.text: I recognized them. These were the same beings I saw in that wild vision by the Chebar River. No doubt—they were cherubim.

21.text: Each had four faces. Each had four wings. And under the wings? Human hands again.

22.text: The faces looked exactly like the ones I saw by the river. No changes. Same presence. Same glory. And just like before—they moved straight ahead. No turning, no hesitation. Just holy purpose.

1.text: Then the Spirit picked me up again and took me to the East Gate of the Lord's house—the one that faces east. And there, standin' at the gate, was twenty-five men. Two names stood out: Jaazaniah son of Azzur and Pelatiah son of Benaiah—these dudes had status, princes of the people.

2.text: God said, "Son of man, see them? These the ones cookin' up evil schemes and givin' foul advice in this city.

3.text: They walkin' around sayin', 'It ain't time to build nothin'. This city's the pot, and we the good meat.' They think they safe in the stew—untouchable in the middle."

4.text: God said, "Prophesy against 'em, son. Go ahead, speak My Word."

5.text: Then the Spirit of the Lord dropped on me heavy and said, "Speak up, Ezekiel! This what the Lord says: Y'all been talkin' slick, but I know exactly what's in y'all heads.

6.text: Y'all done stacked bodies in these streets. The blood of the innocent cryin' out from every corner.

7.text: So here's what I say: Those bodies? They the meat. This city? Yeah, it's the pot. But you—you the ones gettin' pulled out and judged.

8.text: You scared of the sword? Cool. 'Cause that's exactly what's comin' for you.

9.text: I'ma pull you out this city and hand you over to strangers. Judgment gon' hit you hard.

10.text: You gon' die by the sword—outside the city, at the border of Israel. Then you'll finally realize I am the Lord.

11.text: Nah, this city ain't gon' protect you like no caldron. You ain't the prize meat. You gon' be judged at the border, and it'll be too late.

12.text: Why? 'Cause you ain't walked in My ways. You ain't kept My standards. You out here actin' like the world around you. So now you gon' feel what that lifestyle brings."

13.text: While I was speakin' this word, Pelatiah—yep, the leader—dropped dead on the spot. I fell on my face, cryin' loud: "Lord God! You gon' wipe out everybody that's left? Ain't gon' be no remnant?"

14.text: Then the Word of the Lord came again:

15.text: "Son of man, your people—the ones in exile, the outcasts, the ones the folks in Jerusalem wrote off—they say, 'Y'all far from the Lord now. This land belong to us.'

16.text: But tell 'em this: Even though I scattered y'all, Even though y'all in foreign lands, I've been a sanctuary to you out there—a holy place in the middle of captivity.

17.text: And now I'm sayin': I'ma bring y'all back. I'ma gather you from the nations, bring you home to the land of Israel.

18.text: And when y'all get back? You gon' clean house. Tear down the idols. Get rid of all that nasty, fake worship.

19.text: Then I'ma do a heart transplant. Give you one heart. Put a new spirit in you. Take out that cold, stone heart… and give you a soft heart that can actually feel Me again.

20.text: You gon' walk in My ways, live by My laws, and keep it real. You'll be My people. And I'll be your God.

21.text: But for the ones still chasin' idols and filth? They gon' get what's comin' to them. I ain't forget." That's what the Lord God said.

22.text: Then the cherubim lifted their wings again—wheels rollin' with 'em—and the glory of the God of Israel was hoverin' right above.

23.text: God's glory rose up from the city… and stood over the mountain to the east. God left the temple.

24.text: The Spirit lifted me and brought me back to Babylon, to the exiles—just like that. The vision ended, and I was back in real time.

25.text: Then I opened my mouth and told the exiles everything God showed me.

1.text: The word of the Lord came to me, again:

2.text: "Son of man, you livin' right in the middle of a rebellious house. They got eyes, but won't see. They got ears, but don't hear. Hardheaded. Blind on purpose.

3.text: So here's what you gon' do—pack up your stuff like somebody gettin' taken into exile. Do it in broad daylight, so everybody see you movin'. Go from your spot to another place. Maybe, just maybe, they'll get the message.

4.text: Drag your stuff out during the day so they see it. Then at night, go out again—like someone bein' forced out they home.

5.text: Dig through the wall while they watch. Crawl out through the hole with your baggage. Make a scene—they need to feel this.

6.text: Carry your bag on your shoulder as the sun goin' down. Cover your face—like you don't even wanna look at the land no more. This whole act? It's a sign. A message for the people of Israel."

7.text: So I did what He said. In the daylight, I packed my things like an exile. That night, I dug through the wall with my hands, carried my stuff out on my shoulder at twilight—all in front of them.

8.text: The next morning, God spoke again:

9.text: "Son of man, I know they askin' you, 'What you doin'? What's all this?'

10.text: Tell them: This here? It's a word from the Lord. It's about the prince in Jerusalem and everybody else still in the city.

11.text: Tell 'em: 'I'm a living sign. What I just did? It's what's gon' happen to them—they headed into captivity.'

12.text: And that prince? He gon' carry his stuff on his shoulder too, sneak out at night. He gon' dig through the wall and try to escape with his face covered—ashamed, scared, tryin' not to look down.

13.text: But I'ma catch him. My net gon' trap him. I'll take him to Babylon, but he won't see it—though he gon' die there.

14.text: All his boys, all his soldiers? I'm scatterin' 'em like dust. And I'm still comin' with the sword right behind 'em.

15.text: Then they'll know who I am—when I scatter 'em across the nations and drop 'em off in foreign lands.

16.text: But I'll let a few survive. Just a remnant—spared from famine, disease, and violence. And they gon' talk about what they did, gon' confess it in front of the nations. Then they'll know I am the Lord."

17.text: God kept talkin':

18.text: "Son of man, now eat your food like you're scared—hands shakin', breath unsteady. Drink your water like you nervous and stressed out.

19.text: Tell the people: This is what the Lord says to Jerusalem and Israel—'Y'all gon' eat bread with anxiety and drink water in fear. Why? Because the land's about to be emptied out. The violence of the people done cursed the place.'

20.text: The cities? Gon'. The land? Desolate. And y'all gon' know who I am when it's done."

21.text: Then God said again:

22.text: "Son of man, they got a saying in Israel: 'These visions take forever. Nothing ever really happens.'

23.text: Tell them: 'God said—that little saying is done. Y'all ain't gon' use it no more.' Instead, say: 'The time is now. Every word and every vision is comin' to pass.'

24.text: Ain't gon' be no more false visions. No more hype prophets sellin' sweet lies.

25.text: I'm the Lord. When I speak, it happens. No more delays. This generation gon' see it with their own eyes."

26.text: God wasn't done:

27.text: "Son of man, they still tryna play it off, sayin', 'These prophecies ain't for us. That's way in the future.'

28.text: Tell them: 'God said—ain't nothin' I said gon' be postponed. It's gon' happen now. I said it, and I'ma do it.'"

1.text: The word of the Lord came to me again:

2.text: "Son of man, I need you to prophesy against the prophets of Israel—the ones runnin' their mouths like they speakin' for Me but really just speakin' from their own little hearts. Tell 'em: 'This the Word of the Lord.'

3.text: The Lord God says: Woe to these foolish prophets—chasin' their own feelings like it's the Spirit... talkin' like they seen somethin' when they ain't seen a thing!

4.text: Y'all prophets are like foxes in the desert—slick, sneaky, and ain't helpin' nobody.

5.text: Y'all didn't step into the broken places. You ain't built no walls to protect My people. You ain't preppin' them for battle on the Day of the Lord.

6.text: Instead, you out here talkin' loud with empty visions. Lyin' in My name like, 'The Lord says...' But I never sent you. Y'all out here hopin' your lie gon' come true.

7.text: But let's be real—y'all ain't seen nothin'. Y'all makin' it up. You keep throwin' My name on your own imagination. I didn't say a word."

8.text: "So because of that—because y'all spittin' nonsense and droppin' false visions—I'm comin' for you," says the Lord.

9.text: "My hand is against y'all fake prophets who out here makin' up lies. You won't be part of My people. Your names ain't goin' in the roll book. You ain't settin' foot in My land. And then? You'll know I'm the Lord God."

10.text: "Y'all been slick with it. Tellin' My people, 'Peace is comin'!' when peace ain't even on the menu. You build weak walls—phony foundations—and then cover it with cheap plaster, like that's gon' hold.

11.text: So go tell the ones plasterin' over these lies: That wall gon' fall. Storms comin', heavy rain, hail, winds that'll tear the whole thing down.

12.text: And when it crumbles? They gon' ask, 'Where's that plaster you was braggin' about?'"

13.text: "I'm sendin' a storm full of fury. Rain, hail, wind—My anger unleashed.

14.text: That wall y'all covered with spiritual nonsense? I'm breakin' it down to the foundation. And when it falls, y'all fall with it. Then you'll know—I'm the Lord.

15.text: I'll make it known—I'm settin' fire to the wall and the ones who lied to build it.

16.text: Y'all prophets that keep talkin' about peace in Jerusalem when I never said that? Yeah—they gone too."

17.text: "Son of man, now turn toward the daughters of your people—the ones out here usin' fake spiritualism, pretendin' to prophesy.

18.text: Tell 'em: 'Woe to y'all women who out here sewing up little charms, tyin' spells on people, throwin' veils over folks like you got mystical powers—hunting souls like prey. Y'all savin' your own necks while trappin' innocent folks.'

19.text: You sell Me out over a slice of bread and a handful of grain. Killin' off folks that should've lived, and protectin' folks that should've been judged—All with lies. Lies My people actually believe."

20.text: "So I'm sayin this: I'm comin' for your little charms—the ones you use to trap souls like birds. I'ma rip them off and let My people go free.

21.text: I'ma tear off them veils, too. You ain't gon' have My people in your grip no more. They ain't gon' be your victims. And then you'll know I'm the Lord."

22.text: "You out here hurtin' the righteous with your lies—they heart broken and confused, and I didn't send that pain. Meanwhile, you hypin' up the wicked, givin' them false comfort so they don't turn around and get saved.

23.text: So now it's over. No more fake visions. No more hoodoo divinations. I'ma snatch My people out y'all hands. And when I do? You gon' know—I am the Lord."

1.text: Some of the elders of Israel came and sat down in front of me like they wanted a word.

2.text: Then the Lord spoke to me, real direct:

3.text: "Son of man, these men got idols—not on a shelf, but in their hearts. They done set up things that make 'em stumble into sin. And now they wanna ask Me for a word? You think I'ma let 'em treat Me like some fortune teller when their hearts already full of betrayal?"

4.text: "Go tell 'em this: 'This what the Lord says: If anybody from Israel got idols buried in their heart and still tryna come inquire of Me? I'ma answer them alright—but through the weight of those very idols they clingin' to.

5.text: I'm about to grab the heart of Israel—because they done ran far from Me, caught up in false gods and side pieces."

6.text: "So go ahead and tell the house of Israel: Repent. Turn from them idols. Turn your face away from all the mess you've been entertainin'.

7.text: 'Cause if anybody—Israelite or foreigner—pulls away from Me and sets up idols in their heart, then tries to come to the prophet lookin' for a word from the Lord? Nah. I ain't usin' the prophet. I'ma deal with him Myself.

8.text: I'ma set My face against him. Make him a cautionary tale, a walking proverb. Cut him off from My people—then they'll know who I am."

9.text: "And if the prophet gets swayed and speaks something? I allowed it—to expose him. But don't get it twisted—I'ma stretch My hand against that prophet too.

10.text: Both of 'em—the one askin' and the one prophesyin'—gon' be held accountable. Same judgment, same guilt.

11.text: So maybe then My people will stop strayin', stop trashin' My name, and finally walk right—so I can be their God, and they can be Mine."

12.text: Then the word of the Lord came to me again:

13.text: "Son of man, when a land straight-up betrays Me—over and over—I step in. I'll shut down their food supply, send famine, and remove life—man and beast alike.

14.text: And let Me be clear: even if Noah, Daniel, and Job were livin' there, they could only save themselves. Their righteousness ain't stretchin' to nobody else."

15.text: "If I let wild animals roam the streets and run folks off the land, even then—Noah, Daniel, and Job could only save themselves. No sons. No daughters.

16.text: They'd walk out, but the land? Still desolate.

17.text: If I send a sword through the land, sayin', 'Go ahead, cut down everything'—same thing. Only them three righteous men would make it out.

18.text: No kids. No crew. Just them.

19.text: Or if I let disease hit like a plague—people droppin', judgment fallin'—Noah, Daniel, and Job? Still wouldn't save nobody but themselves.

20.text: I mean it. They'd survive 'cause of their walk—but not even their own family would be spared."

21.text: "So what y'all think gon' happen when I drop all four judgments on Jerusalem? Sword, famine, wild beasts, and disease—all at once? Ain't nothin' gon' be left. Man or animal.

22.text: But... I'll still leave a remnant. A few sons and daughters gon' make it out. And when they show up to you, when you see how they live and what they've been through, you'll understand.
