23.text: They'll help you realize that I ain't just wildin' out. Everything I did—I had a reason. You'll see it with your own eyes."

1.text: Then the word of the Lord came to me:

2.text: "Son of man, let Me ask you this—What makes vine wood so special? What makes it better than any other tree in the forest?

3.text: Can you use vine wood to build somethin'? Can you even make a peg outta it to hang a pot on?

4.text: Nah. It's soft, twisted, fragile. So what happens? It gets tossed in the fire for fuel. It burns from both ends, and the middle gets scorched too. Tell Me—what's left that's useful?

5.text: Even when it was whole, you couldn't make nothin' out of it. So how much more useless is it once it's been through the fire?

6.text: "This is what the Lord God says: Just like that useless vine wood you throw in the fire, that's how I'm handin' over the people of Jerusalem.

7.text: I've turned My face against them. They might escape one fire, but they gon' land in another. And when that happens, they'll know—I am the Lord.

8.text: I'm makin' the land desolate. Why? 'Cause they won't stop bein' unfaithful. They just keep breakin' the covenant, keep pushin Me away. That's what the Lord God said."

1.text: The word of the Lord hit me again:

2.text: "Son of man, let Jerusalem know just how filthy her sins really are.

3.text: Say this to her: 'This what the Lord God says to Jerusalem: You was born in Canaan land—your daddy was an Amorite and your mama was a Hittite.

4.text: When you came out the womb, nobody even cared. Your umbilical cord wasn't cut. You weren't washed off. Nobody rubbed you with salt or wrapped you up warm. You were just—

5.text: Tossed out like trash in an open field, left to die. No one pitied you. Nobody had compassion. They looked at you and said, 'Ew, throw that away.'

6.text: But I came by and saw you, baby girl, squirming in your own blood. And I said, 'Live.' Yeah, even in your mess, I told you twice: LIVE.

7.text: Then I raised you up like a wildflower in the field. You grew tall and strong. Your body matured, your hair came in—But you was still naked and bare.

8.text: I came back again and saw you. This time, you were grown—it was time for love. So I spread My robe over you and covered your shame. I made a covenant with you. I claimed you as Mine, says the Lord God.

9.text: I washed you clean. Got all the blood off you. Anointed you with oil.

10.text: I dressed you in embroidered clothes, gave you shoes made from the best leather. Wrapped you in fine linen and silk.

11.text: I hooked you up with bracelets, a chain for your neck,

12.text: a jewel in your nose, earrings for your ears, and a beautiful crown for your head.

13.text: Girl, you were dripping—gold, silver, fine linen, silk, embroidered threads. You ate the best—flour, honey, and oil. You were gorgeous, royalty even.

14.text: Word got out. Nations were talking about you. You were flawless—because of MY glory that I placed on you," says the Lord God.

15.text: "But you? You started feelin' yourself. You trusted your own beauty. Turned your fame into a hustle—you started hoein'.

16.text: You took the clothes I gave you and built shrines on the high places—then laid down with whoever walked by. Disgusting.

17.text: You used the gold and silver I gave you, melted it down into male images—then did nasty things with 'em.

18.text: You burned incense to those fake gods using MY oil. Wrapped them in MY garments.

19.text: You set MY food in front of them like it was a peace offering. The same food I fed you. The same honey, oil, flour. And yep, that's how it went down," says the Lord God.

20.text: "Worse than that—you took MY kids, the sons and daughters you birthed for ME, and burned them alive as sacrifices.

21.text: You killed My babies, passed them through the fire. And for what? For them?

22.text: And after all that filth, you never stopped to remember when I found you—naked, bleeding, helpless in your own blood.

23.text: "Then—after all that mess—Woe, woe to you!" says the Lord God.

24.text: You built shrines on every corner.

25.text: Set up shop at the top of every street. You made yourself cheap. You let anyone in. You turned your beauty into shame.

26.text: You gave yourself to Egypt too—your neighbors with the strong bodies. But you ain't stop there. You was out here doing the most.

27.text: So I stepped in. I pulled back My blessings. Let the Philistines—who don't even know Me—see your wild ways and get disgusted.

28.text: Then you turned to Assyria. You was never satisfied. Still out here giving yourself away.

29.text: You even reached all the way out to Chaldea—land of traders. But even they couldn't fill that empty space.

30.text: How sick is your heart?" says the Lord God. "You act like a bold-faced harlot—no shame, no brakes."

31.text: "You ain't even like the other sex workers—at least they got paid. You gave it up for free—built shrines, set up shop on every street.

32.text: You straight-up cheated like a wife who don't want her man. You welcomed strangers instead of staying loyal.

33.text: Most prostitutes get paid. But YOU paid your lovers. You hired men to sleep with you.

34.text: You flipped the whole game. Ain't nobody chasing you—you chasing them. You paying them. You ain't getting nothing back."

35.text: "So now, O harlot, listen up:

36.text: This is what the Lord God says: Because you threw yourself around, stripped yourself in public, and shed the blood of My children—because of all your nasty idols—

37.text: I'ma gather all your lovers—old flames and new ones, the ones you loved and even the ones you hated—bring 'em all together, and expose your nakedness in front of them.

38.text: I'ma judge you like I do women who cheat or murder—judgment gon' hit you with blood, fury, and jealousy.

39.text: I'ma hand you over. They gon' tear down your shrines, break your idols, snatch your jewels, rip your clothes—leave you naked and bare.

40.text: They gon' form a mob, stone you, and slice you down with swords.

41.text: They gon' burn your house down, make a public example out of you. Your lil' side hustle of harlotry? It's over. No more lovers, no more payin' for attention.

42.text: Then, and only then, will My anger be satisfied. My jealousy gon' cool down. I'll be done.

43.text: But know this: Because you forgot your beginnings, and made Me mad with all your drama, I'ma pay you back. You gon' feel every bit of what you did," says the Lord God.

44.text: "Everybody gon' say this about you: 'Like mother, like daughter.'

45.text: You just like your mama—didn't love your man, didn't love your kids. Your sisters just as wild. Your people? Amorites and Hittites.

46.text: Big sister Samaria lives up north. Little sister Sodom down south.

47.text: You ain't just walk in their mess—you ran past them. You outdid 'em in wickedness.

48.text: As I live," says the Lord God, "Sodom ain't even do what you and your girls have done.

49.text: Sodom's sin was pride, greed, and laziness. They didn't help the poor or needy.

50.text: They were arrogant and did foul things in My face. So I wiped 'em out.

51.text: Samaria only did HALF of what you've done. You made them look righteous by comparison.

52.text: So since you love to judge your sisters—carry your own shame now. You worse than both of them."

53.text: "One day I'ma restore their fortunes—Sodom, Samaria, and even yours, Jerusalem.

54.text: And when that day comes, you gon' be ashamed. 'Cause the very ones you looked down on? I'ma bring them back up next to you.

55.text: They gon' rise again. And so will you and your daughters—but not 'cause of anything you did.

56.text: Back when you were on top, Sodom was a joke to you. But now? Look at you.

57.text: The people you used to shame—the Syrians, the Philistines—they mockin' you now.

58.text: You reaping what you sowed," says the Lord.

59.text: "You broke the covenant. So now I'ma deal with you."

60.text: "But still... I remember the promise I made to you when you were young. And I'ma make a new covenant—an everlasting one.

61.text: You gon' remember everything you did and hang your head low. And when I bring your sisters back into the fold, you'll see they've become daughters to you—not by your covenant, but by Mine.

62.text: I'ma re-establish the covenant. And you gon' know—I am the Lord.

63.text: You gon' be so ashamed, you won't even be able to speak. But I'll cover it all. I'll make atonement for everything you did," says the Lord God.

1.text: Then God hit Ezekiel with another Word.

2.text: "Son of man, I need you to drop a riddle on Israel—a parable, somethin' with layers. Tell the people:

3.text: 'This what the Lord God says: There was this big ol' eagle—wings wide, feathers long, colors poppin'. He flew over to Lebanon, pulled the top branch off a tall cedar.

4.text: He clipped the newest little twig from the top, took it to a land full of hustle and trade, and planted it in the middle of the merchant city.

5.text: But that ain't all—he grabbed some seed from the land, planted it in rich soil, close to water, like he was setting up a willow tree to flourish.

6.text: That seed turned into a vine—low to the ground, real spread out. It grew, but it stayed facing the eagle, like it knew who gave it life. Branches came out. Shoots popped up.

7.text: But then, another eagle rolled up—big wings, feathers everywhere. And guess what? That vine? It bent toward this new eagle. Stretched out its branches like, 'Come water me too!' Even though it was already planted in good soil, plenty of water, ready to bear fruit and grow strong.

8.text: The setup was perfect—this vine had everything. It was supposed to thrive. But…"

9.text: "Say to them: This is what the Lord God says: 'You think that vine gon' make it? Thrive? Really?

10.text: Nope. The first eagle gon' yank it up by the roots. Chop off the fruit. Leaves gon' wither. And it ain't even gon' take much—no army needed.

11.text: It was planted, sure. But it ain't gon' survive. As soon as that dry east wind blows? It's a wrap. Withered. Gone. In the same spot it was planted.'"

12.text: Then the Lord said, "Ezekiel, tell these hard-headed people what this really means:

13.text: That first eagle? That's the king of Babylon. He came to Jerusalem, snatched the king and his top men, and dragged them back to Babylon.

14.text: He made a deal with one of the royal kids— put him under oath, made him promise to stay loyal. He even stripped the land of the strong ones, just to keep that kingdom humble and dependent.

15.text: The plan was: stay in line, follow the covenant, and the kingdom could survive.

16.text: But what happened? That dude broke the covenant. Sent folks to Egypt tryna get horses and backup.

17.text: Tried to double-cross Babylon.

18.text: You think that gon' work? You think you can break a promise and still win? Nah.

19.text: As surely as I live," says the Lord God, "He gon' die in Babylon—the same place of the king he betrayed.

20.text: And don't expect Pharaoh to save him. His army won't mean a thing when Babylon builds up siege walls and cuts off everything.

21.text: He broke his word. Signed the deal and still acted shady. So now? He ain't getting away."

22.text: "This is what the Lord God says: 'Since he played Me, since he broke the covenant he made under My name, I'm gon' pay him back.

23.text: I'ma catch him in My net. He gon' be trapped, tried, and judged in Babylon for the mess he made—against Me.

24.text: His people? His crew? His soldiers? They either gon' get cut down by the sword or scattered in every direction.

25.text: And THEN they'll know—I'm the Lord. I said it. I meant it."

26.text: "But don't get it twisted," says the Lord God. "I'ma take another branch from that same cedar— the highest part, the top twig— and I'ma plant it on a high mountain in Israel.

27.text: That little twig gon' grow. It'll become a majestic cedar. Birds from everywhere gon' come nest in its shade.

28.text: And when it happens, all the trees in the field gon' realize this:

29.text: I'm the One who humbles the tall trees and lifts up the low ones. I dry up green trees and make the dry ones flourish.

30.text: I, the Lord, spoke it. And best believe—I did it."

1.text: The Lord came to Ezekiel again with a word.

2.text: "Yo, what's up with y'all repeating this line in Israel: 'The fathers ate sour grapes, and now the kids got that bitter taste?' Like they the ones sufferin' for what Daddy did?

3.text: Nah, that's dead," says the Lord God. "Y'all ain't gon' say that no more in My house.

4.text: Listen close—every soul belongs to Me. Daddy's soul, son's soul, grandbaby's soul—they all Mine. And the soul that sins? That's the one that's gon' die.

5.text: Let's say a man out here doin' right. He walkin' in truth, showin' justice.

6.text: He don't be out on them idol hills, don't bow to false gods, don't sleep with his neighbor's wife, and don't cross lines with a woman on her cycle.

7.text: He don't take from nobody, he gives back what he borrowed, don't strong-arm folks, feeds the hungry, and keeps the poor warm.

8.text: He don't charge no interest, don't scam folks, but settles beefs fair and square. He follows My laws and lives right.

9.text: That man? He good. He gon' live. I said it. Period.

10.text: Now let's say this righteous man got a son who wildin' out— stealin', killin', doin' dirt.

11.text: He out here messin' with idols, sleepin' with other men's wives,

12.text: oppressing the poor, robbing folks, keepin' what ain't his, prayin' to false gods, livin' foul.

13.text: He out here chargin' folks interest on loans, stackin' off the weak. He think he gon' live? Nah. He gon' die. His blood on him. Don't look at daddy—he made his own mess.

14.text: Now flip it again—this wild son got a kid too. That kid watches everything his daddy did and says, "Nah, I ain't goin' out like that."

15.text: He ain't prayin' to idols, ain't messin' around sexually,

16.text: ain't robbin', ain't oppressin', feeds folks, clothes folks, ain't scamming nobody.

17.text: He lives right, judges fair, follows God's ways— he ain't gon' die for what his daddy did. He gon' live.

18.text: But daddy? Yeah, he gon' die for his own evil— robbin' folks, doin' dirty, hurtin' people. He earned that judgment.

19.text: Y'all be like, "Why the son don't carry his daddy's guilt?"

20.text: 'Cause he ain't do the dirt! He chose right. So he lives.

21.text: "The one who sins is the one who dies." Nobody else payin' your tab. Each person stands for their own actions. Righteousness is on the righteous. Wickedness? Same.

22.text: But peep this: If somebody livin' foul makes a real turn— starts followin' My ways, livin' right— he gon' live. His past won't even be brought up. I ain't keepin' score like that.

23.text: That righteousness gon' cover him. Why? 'Cause I ain't out here rootin' for folks to die in sin. I want people to change and live.

24.text: Now don't get it twisted— If a righteous person flips and starts wildin', does all the wrong stuff the wicked do, he not gon' get credit for what he used to do.

25.text: He gon' die too.

26.text: Y'all steady sayin', "God's not bein' fair." But let's keep it real—who really ain't fair? It ain't Me—it's y'all.

27.text: If the good man turns bad and dies for it, that's on him.

28.text: But if the wicked man turns good, lives right, he saves himself.

29.text: He looked at his life, made the switch, and now he gon' live.

30.text: So again—y'all gon' say I'm unfair? Check yourself. I'm fair. Y'all just don't like the consequences.

31.text: So here's what it is, Israel: I'ma judge everybody based on what they do.

32.text: Repent. Turn from your sin. Don't let it destroy you.

33.text: Get rid of that mess. Let it go. Get a new heart, a new spirit. Why you tryna die out here??

34.text: I ain't got no joy in watching people destroy themselves. That's not My vibe.

35.text: So turn. And live.

1.text: God told Ezekiel: "Go ahead and sing a sad song for the princes of Israel."

2.text: Say this: Your mama? She was like a fierce lioness. She raised her cubs right in the middle of the pride.

3.text: One of her cubs grew up strong— he turned into a young lion, learned how to hunt, and started takin' people down.

4.text: But the nations caught wind of him. They threw a trap, caught him, and dragged him down to Egypt in chains.

5.text: When mama lion saw her hope was dead and gone, she raised up another cub—turned him into a lion too.

6.text: This one roamed free with the others, got bold, became a killer too, learned how to snatch prey, and devoured men just like the first.

7.text: He tore through quiet towns, left cities in ruins. The whole land was shook from the sound of his roar.

8.text: So all the surrounding nations came for him. They threw nets all around him and trapped him in their pit.

9.text: He was caged up with chains, shipped off to Babylon, dragged away in nets, so his roar would never be heard again in Israel.

10.text: Then God said: Your mama was like a vine, rooted deep, flourishing by the water. She was fruitful, strong, her branches tall. She grew rulers from her line.

11.text: Her branches were like scepters—strong and royal. She stood tall, outshining all the rest. You couldn't miss her—she was powerful.

12.text: But rage came for her. She got ripped up and tossed to the dirt. The hot winds dried her fruit. Her strongest limbs snapped and died. Fire ate up what was left.

13.text: Now she's been replanted in a dry, desert place. No water. No strength. No life.

14.text: And from her own broken pieces, a fire sparked and burned everything she had left. All the fruit, all the power, gone. No more strong branches. No more royalty. Nothing left to rule.

15.text: This was a lamentation— and it still is.

1.text: It was the seventh year, fifth month, tenth day. Some of Israel's elders came to sit and hear from God, tryin' to act holy.

2.text: Then the word of the Lord hit Ezekiel hard.

3.text: "Son of man, these elders really came to question Me? Tell them this: 'As surely as I live,' says the Lord God, 'I ain't answering y'all. I'm not here for your games.'

4.text: Go ahead and judge them, Ezekiel. Read them. Expose everything their ancestors did wrong.

5.text: "Tell 'em: This what God says—'The day I picked y'all, the day I showed up in Egypt and made y'all a promise, I said, "I'm the Lord your God."

6.text: I promised to bring y'all outta Egypt into a beautiful land—milk and honey flowin', top-tier real estate.

7.text: I told y'all, "Toss out all them nasty idols, stop defiling yourselves with Egyptian mess. I'm the Lord."

8.text: But y'all didn't listen. Kept your idols. Kept wildin'. So I almost snapped and wrecked y'all in Egypt.

9.text: But I didn't—for the sake of My name. Didn't want the Egyptians clownin' Me for bringin' y'all out only to destroy you.

10.text: "So I led y'all into the wilderness.

11.text: I gave y'all My laws, showed you how to live right.

12.text: Gave you Sabbaths too—signs that we were locked in.

13.text: But even in the wilderness, y'all broke every rule. Didn't care. Disrespected My Sabbaths. I was ready to go off. But again, I held back—for My name's sake.

14.text: But again, I held back—for My name's sake, so I ain't look shady to the other nations.

15.text: I even swore: 'Y'all not entering the promised land.' Why? 'Cause you chose idols over Me.

16.text: Why? 'Cause they ain't care about My laws, didn't walk right, and kept disrespectin' the Sabbath. Their hearts stayed stuck on idols.

17.text: Still, I didn't finish y'all. Mercy held Me back.

18.text: "Then I talked to your kids: 'Don't follow your parents' mess. Don't be like them.

19.text: I'm your God—walk with Me.

20.text: Honor the Sabbath. Know I'm the one who got y'all.'

21.text: But guess what? The children rebelled too. Didn't follow My laws. Played in the same dirt.

22.text: I could've lit it all up—but for My name's sake, I showed restraint.

23.text: I told 'em: 'You gonna get scattered to the nations.'

24.text: Why? 'Cause y'all threw My laws in the trash and went back to your idols.

25.text: "So I let y'all follow bogus rules—rules that couldn't even save you.

26.text: I let y'all go so far, you even sacrificed your own kids. Sick stuff. That's what y'all chose instead of Me."

27.text: "Tell Israel: Y'all stayed unfaithful, even after I brought you into the land I promised.

28.text: You saw them hills and trees? Ran straight up there to do idol worship like you ain't learned nothin'.

29.text: I asked, 'What is this Bamah spot y'all keep runnin' to?' And the name stuck."

30.text: "So tell 'em this: Are y'all really still doing your ancestors' nasty mess? Burning your kids in fire?

31.text: Even now y'all defile yourselves with these idols and got the nerve to try to talk to Me? I ain't havin' it.

32.text: And y'all say, 'We wanna be like the other nations, worshiping wood and stone'? Not on My watch."

33.text: "As surely as I live," says the Lord, "I'ma rule over y'all with a strong hand—even if I gotta come in hot.

34.text: I'm bringing you out the nations where you've been scattered. I'm gathering y'all up.

35.text: Then I'mma meet you in the wilderness, face to face, like I did with your ancestors after Egypt.

36.text: I'm putting y'all through it again—testing hearts.

37.text: I'll check you like sheep, count you, and bring you back into covenant with Me.

38.text: But the rebels? The ones still wildin'? They not coming back to the land. They'll know I'm the Lord real quick."

39.text: "House of Israel, go ahead—keep playin' with your idols if that's what you want. But don't bring that fake worship around Me. Stop disrespecting My name."

40.text: "One day, up on My holy mountain, the whole house of Israel will finally serve Me right.

41.text: I'll accept your offerings. I'll accept y'all again. I'll bring you home and the world will see y'all belong to Me.

42.text: Then you'll know I'm the Lord—when I deliver on My promise and bring y'all back to the land.

43.text: And you gon' remember everything you did—and be ashamed of how far you fell.

44.text: But I'm doing this not 'cause you earned it, but because My name's on the line," says the Lord God.

45.text: Then God told Ezekiel:

46.text: "Turn toward the south. Prophesy against it. Tell the forest this:

47.text: 'God said: I'm about to set a fire. Green trees, dead trees—every last one gon' burn.

48.text: The whole world will know I lit it, and no one can put it out.' "

49.text: Ezekiel said, "Lord, they think I'm just speakin' in parables. They don't get how real this is."

1.text: The word of the Lord came to Ezekiel,

2.text: "Son of man, turn and face Jerusalem. Speak out against the Temple. Prophesy against all Israel.

3.text: Tell them, 'This is what God says: I'm comin' for you. I'm drawin' My sword and I ain't sparing nobody—righteous or wicked.

4.text: Since both gon' get cut, this sword is comin' for everybody—from the south to the north.

5.text: I want everybody to know: this blade came from Me—and once it's out the sheath, it ain't goin' back.'"

6.text: "Sigh deep, son of man. Like your heart done shattered. Let them see the pain all over your face.

7.text: When they ask, 'Why you sighin'?' say, 'Because what's comin' gon' break every heart, make hands drop, kill spirits, and leave folks knees bucklin' like water. It's comin'. It's real.'"

8.text: The Lord kept speakin':

9.text: "Say this: A sword, a sword—sharpened and polished.

10.text: Sharpened for mass destruction. Polished to flash in the light. Y'all wanna laugh now? This blade ain't sparin' royalty or rebels.

11.text: It's prepped to be held. This sword is locked and loaded—straight into the killer's hands."

12.text: "Cry out loud, Ezekiel. Wail. It's comin' for My people—princes included. They about to feel terror. Strike your thigh, 'cause what's comin' gon' hurt."

13.text: "This sword is a test. And even the royal scepter can't stand against it. Ain't nobody exempt."

14.text: "Clap your hands, Ezekiel! Call for triple destruction. This sword gon' hit twice as hard, and it's targetin' the powerful, even in their private chambers.

15.text: I've posted it at every city gate. It's gonna break hearts and trip folks up. It shines for slaughter.

16.text: Right hand, left hand—cut wherever it gotta cut.

17.text: I'll be clappin' too—and when I'm done, My fury gon' rest. I said what I said."

18.text: Then God gave Ezekiel more direction:

19.text: "Draw a map. Two paths. One sword. One land. Mark one road goin' to Rabbah (Ammon's capital), the other to Jerusalem.

20.text: Make it clear—Rabbah or fortified Jerusalem.

21.text: The king of Babylon's at the crossroads, throwin' bones, consulting idols, readin' livers.

22.text: The signs gon' tell him: 'Attack Jerusalem.' Battering rams. War cries. Walls and towers under siege.

23.text: The folks in Jerusalem gon' say, 'That's fake divination.' But nah—they forgot they broke covenant. Now they gettin' dealt with."

24.text: "So this is what the Lord says: Because y'all sins are front and center now, because you've been exposed, You gon' get handled."

25.text: "And you, wicked prince of Israel—your time's up. Your evil reign ends now.

26.text: God says: Take off the crown. The old way is done. I'm flippin' everything—low will rise, high will fall.

27.text: Overthrown. Overthrown. Overthrown! It's finished… until the real one shows up—the one who got the right to rule. I'm givin' it to Him."

28.text: "Ezekiel, now prophesy about the Ammonites. Yeah, they laughed when Israel fell—but they ain't safe either.

29.text: While y'all sittin' around listenin' to fake prophets and lies, y'all forgot—judgment don't skip nobody. The sword's comin' for your neck too."

30.text: "The sword goes back in the sheath now—but not 'cause y'all safe. I'll judge you where you came from, where you were born.

31.text: I'm breathin' fire. Pourin' out wrath. You gon' fall into the hands of violent men—experts in destruction.

32.text: You gon' burn. Your blood gon' stain the land. And when it's over, won't nobody remember you. I, the Lord, said it."

1.text: The word of the Lord hit Ezekiel again.

2.text: "Son of man, are you ready to judge this bloody city? Then do it. Put all her mess on blast—every disgusting, triflin' thing she done.

3.text: Tell her: 'This is what God says—You shed blood right in your own streets. You set up them raggedy idols and stay defilin' yourself.

4.text: You guilty. Bloody hands and nasty idols. You countin' down your final days, and now everybody laughin' at you. Nations clownin' you hard.

5.text: Both the ones close by and the ones far off hear the noise in your streets—and they call you messy and reckless.'"

6.text: "Every prince in Israel got blood on their hands.

7.text: Y'all disrespectin' yo mama and daddy. You mistreat foreigners, crush orphans and widows.

8.text: You done stopped carin' about My holy things. You wildin' on the Sabbaths.

9.text: Y'all runnin' your mouth, snitchin' and spreadin' lies that get folks killed.

10.text: You got folks sleepin' with their own daddy's wives, or messin' with women on their cycle.

11.text: Some of y'all creepin' with your neighbor's wife. Some out here sleepin' with their daughter-in-law. Others are out here touchin' they own sister. Sick.

12.text: You takin' bribes, rippin' off your people, runnin' up interest, extortin' folks, and you done forgot Me," says the Lord.

13.text: "Look here—I'm fed up. Beat my fist at y'all dirty money and all this bloodshed.

14.text: You really think you got the strength to face Me when I come down on you? Nah. I said it, and I'm doin' it.

15.text: I'ma scatter y'all in all directions, and I'ma scrape the filth off you in front of everybody.

16.text: You gon' embarrass yourself in front of the whole world. Then you'll know who I am—for real."

17.text: Then God said again,

18.text: "Son of man, Israel ain't no silver—they straight dross. They nothin' but bronze, tin, iron, and lead sittin' in a furnace. Burned out.

19.text: I'ma bring y'all into Jerusalem and melt you down.

20.text: Just like scrap metal thrown in the fire—silver, bronze, iron, all of it—I'ma blow on you with My wrath. You gon' feel the heat.

21.text: I'ma gather y'all, breathe fire on you, and melt you where you stand.

22.text: You gon' boil like silver, and know that it was Me who turned up the heat."

23.text: Then God came back again and said,

24.text: "Ezekiel, say this: 'This land ain't even been washed clean. No rain. Just dry and filthy during My wrath.'

25.text: The prophets in the land? Lions. Rippin' people apart. Robbin' homes. Makin' widows everywhere.

26.text: The priests? Don't even care what's holy or what ain't. Don't teach nobody right from wrong. Don't even honor the Sabbath. And because of that? I get disrespected daily.

27.text: The princes? Wolves. Huntin' people down just to get rich.

28.text: And the prophets? Still lyin'. Tellin' fake visions, makin' up what they think I said. I ain't say none of that!

29.text: And the people? Oppressin' folks, robbin' each other, abusin' the poor and the immigrant. Coldhearted.

30.text: I looked for just one person—one righteous soul who would stand in the gap for the land. Just one who'd build a wall and pray. But I couldn't find nobody.

31.text: So I poured out My anger. Set the place on fire. Gave them exactly what they earned. I, the Lord, said it—and I meant every word."

1.text: The word of the Lord came to me again:

2.text: "Son of man, there were two women, daughters of the same mother.

3.text: They got wild in Egypt when they was young. That's where they first let men touch them, where they first got felt up.

4.text: The older one was named Oholah—that's Samaria. Her sister was Oholibah—that's Jerusalem. They became mine, and they had sons and daughters.

5.text: But Oholah played the ho while she was still mine. She went crazy for her lovers, them Assyrians—warriors all of 'em,

6.text: Dressed in purple, governors and commanders, all of 'em fine young men, cavalry officers mounted on horses.

7.text: She gave herself to all the finest Assyrian men and defiled herself with all their idols, whoever she lusted after.

8.text: She didn't stop the ho stuff she started in Egypt, where men slept with her, felt up her young body, and poured their lust all over her.

9.text: So I handed her over to her lovers, them Assyrians she was so crazy about.

10.text: They stripped her naked, took her sons and daughters, and killed her with the sword. She became infamous among women, and they executed judgment on her.

11.text: Her sister Oholibah saw this, but she got even more reckless with her lust, even worse than her sister.

12.text: She went crazy for the Assyrians too—governors and commanders, warriors in full gear, cavalry officers mounted on horses, all of 'em fine young men.

13.text: I saw she was defiled; both sisters went down the same path.

14.text: But Oholibah took it even further. She saw men carved on walls, images of Chaldeans drawn in bright red,

15.text: With belts around their waists and flowing turbans on their heads, all looking like Babylonian officers from Chaldea, the land of their birth.

16.text: As soon as she saw them, she went wild for them and sent messengers to them in Chaldea.

17.text: The Babylonians came to her, to her bed of love, and defiled her with their lust. After they defiled her, she turned away from them in disgust.

18.text: When she flaunted her promiscuity and exposed her nakedness, I turned away from her in disgust, just like I turned from her sister.

19.text: Yet she kept on with her ho ways, remembering how she was a ho in Egypt.

20.text: She lusted after lovers with genitals like donkeys and emissions like horses.

21.text: So you longed for the lewdness of your youth, when the Egyptians handled your breasts and pressed your young nipples.

22.text: Therefore, Oholibah, this is what the Lord God says: I'm gonna stir up your lovers against you, the ones you turned away from in disgust, and bring them against you from every side—

23.text: The Babylonians and all the Chaldeans, Pekod, Shoa, and Koa, and all the Assyrians with them, desirable young men, all of them governors and commanders, officers and men of renown, all mounted on horses.

24.text: They'll come against you with weapons, chariots and wagons, and with a host of peoples. They'll set themselves against you on every side with large and small shields and helmets. I'll turn the judgment over to them, and they'll judge you by their standards.

25.text: I'll direct my jealous anger against you, and they'll deal with you in fury. They'll cut off your nose and ears, and your survivors will fall by the sword. They'll take your sons and daughters, and your survivors will be consumed by fire.

26.text: They'll strip you of your clothes and take your beautiful jewelry.

27.text: So I'll put an end to your lewdness and your prostitution started in Egypt. You won't look longingly at these things or remember Egypt anymore.

28.text: For this is what the Lord God says: I'm about to deliver you into the hands of those you hate, those you turned away from in disgust.

29.text: They'll deal with you hatefully, take all you worked for, and leave you naked and bare. The shame of your promiscuity will be exposed, both your lewdness and your ho ways.

30.text: These things will happen to you because you played the ho with the nations and defiled yourself with their idols.

31.text: You walked in your sister's footsteps, so I'll put her cup into your hand.

32.text: This is what the Lord God says: You'll drink your sister's cup, which is deep and wide. You'll be laughed at and ridiculed; the cup holds so much.

33.text: You'll be filled with drunkenness and sorrow, a cup of horror and desolation, the cup of your sister Samaria.

34.text: You'll drink it and drain it dry; you'll dash it to pieces and tear at your breasts. I have spoken, declares the Lord God.

35.text: Therefore this is what the Lord God says: Because you've forgotten me and cast me behind your back, you must bear the consequences of your lewdness and prostitution.

36.text: The Lord said to me: Son of man, will you judge Oholah and Oholibah? Then confront them with their detestable practices,

37.text: For they've committed adultery, and blood is on their hands. They committed adultery with their idols and even sacrificed their children, whom they bore to me, as food for them.

38.text: They've also done this to me: They defiled my sanctuary on the same day and profaned my Sabbaths.

39.text: On the same day they slaughtered their children for their idols, they entered my sanctuary and profaned it. That's what they did in my house.

40.text: They even sent for men who came from far away, and when they arrived, you bathed yourself for them, painted your eyes, and put on your jewelry.

41.text: You sat on an elegant couch, with a table set before it on which you had placed my incense and my oil.

42.text: The noise of a carefree crowd was around her; drunkards were brought in from the desert along with common men, who put bracelets on their wrists and beautiful crowns on their heads.

43.text: Then I said about the one worn out by adultery, 'Now they will engage in prostitution with her, and she with them.'

44.text: And they slept with her. As one sleeps with a prostitute, so they slept with those lewd women, Oholah and Oholibah.

45.text: But righteous men will judge them with the punishment of adulteresses and the punishment of women who shed blood, because they are adulteresses and blood is on their hands.

46.text: This is what the Lord God says: Bring a mob against them and give them over to terror and plunder.

47.text: The mob will stone them and cut them down with their swords; they'll kill their sons and daughters and burn down their houses.

48.text: So I'll put an end to lewdness in the land, and all women will be warned not to imitate your lewdness.

49.text: You'll suffer the penalty for your lewdness and bear the consequences of your sins of idolatry. Then you'll know that I am the Lord God.

1.text: On the tenth day of the tenth month, ninth year of exile, God came to Ezekiel like,

2.text: "Son of man, mark this date. It's official—Babylon just laid siege to Jerusalem today. Write that down.

3.text: Now go tell that hardheaded house a lil parable: 'God said— Put a pot on the stove. Fill it up with water.

4.text: Throw in some prime cuts—thigh, shoulder, all the good meat.

5.text: Pick the best from the flock. Stack the bones like firewood. Get that thing boilin'. Let it simmer.'

6.text: But here's what God really sayin': 'Woe to that bloody city—Jerusalem. It's like a dirty pot full of scum. No matter how much you stir it, the mess won't go away.

7.text: Blood's been spilled right in the open, not even hidden. Ain't nobody tryin' to bury the bodies.

8.text: I let it stay on the surface to stir up My fury—no covering, no excuses.'"

9.text: "So now I'm sayin again," God says: 'Woe to that bloody city! I'ma build this fire high.

10.text: Stack the wood. Let it blaze. Cook everything down till it's burnt. Let the bones turn black.

11.text: Then set that empty pot on the coals till the bronze glows red— til the filth melts off and that nasty scum's gone.

12.text: Y'all been wearin Me out with all these lies, still holdin' on to your dirt. Let that fire purify what y'all won't let go of.'

13.text: 'Your filth is deep-rooted. I tried to cleanse you—but you refused. So I ain't tryna wash you no more. I'ma let My fury run its course.

14.text: I said what I said, and I ain't takin' it back. You gon' get judged by your own actions and your own deeds. That's on Me. I'm the Lord.'"

15.text: Then God came to Ezekiel with a hard word:

16.text: "Son of man, I'm takin' your wife—the love of your life—in one moment. But don't mourn. Don't cry.

17.text: Stay silent. No funeral wailing. Keep your head wrapped. Put your shoes on. Don't eat nobody's comfort food."

18.text: So Ezekiel obeyed. In the morning he gave the message, and by that evening, his wife passed. And the next morning, he didn't shed a tear. Just did what God said.

19.text: The people were like, "Wait—what does all this mean? Why you actin' like this?"

20.text: Ezekiel said, "God told me—

21.text: 'Tell Israel: I'm about to desecrate what y'all hold dear—My temple. Y'all boast in it. Y'all call it your pride and joy. But I'ma take it. Just like that. And your sons and daughters gon' fall by the sword.

22.text: And just like I ain't mourned, you won't mourn either. No head coverings off, no sympathy meals.

23.text: Y'all gon' wear your turbans, keep your sandals on, and suffer quietly— not from grief over death, but from the weight of your sin.'

24.text: Ezekiel is your sign. What happened to me is what's gonna happen to y'all. When it goes down, then y'all will finally know—I'm the Lord."

25.text: "And you, son of man," God said, "On the day I take everything from them—their stronghold, their joy, their pride, their children—

26.text: someone who escapes the horror will come and tell you what happened.

27.text: And that day, I'ma let you speak freely again. You won't be mute no more. You'll be My sign. And they'll know exactly who I am."

1.text: The Lord came to Ezekiel and said,

2.text: "Turn and speak to them Ammonites.

3.text: Tell 'em this straight from Me: Y'all had the nerve to say 'Aha!' when My temple got wrecked, when Israel got wiped out, when Judah got hauled off in chains? Oh bet.

4.text: Because of that petty disrespect, I'm lettin' the folks from the East come through and take everything. They gon' set up camp in y'all land, live off your food, drink your milk, and do what they want.

5.text: I'ma turn your capital, Rabbah, into a camel garage, and all Ammon gon' be a pasture for sheep. Then y'all gon' know—I run this."

6.text: "Since you couldn't keep your hands to yourself—clappin', stompin', and celebratin' Judah's downfall like it was your win—

7.text: I'ma stretch My hand out against you, too. You about to be plundered, cut off, wiped out. Ain't nobody even gon' remember y'all like that no more. Then you'll know—I'm the Lord."

8.text: "And Moab, I ain't forget y'all either. You sat back sayin', 'Judah just like the rest of us now.'

9.text: So I'ma tear down your fancy cities—Beth Jeshimoth, Baal Meon, Kirjathaim—gone.

10.text: The same Easterners wreckin' Ammon? They takin' your land too. I'ma erase Ammon's name and let Moab watch it happen.

11.text: When I'm done judging y'all, you'll know who I am."

12.text: "Edom, you got way too comfortable swingin' back at Judah like this was some personal beef. You came at them with vengeance like you had somethin' to prove.

13.text: Now I'ma come for you—wipe out folks from Teman to Dedan. Y'all gon' be empty. No man, no beast.

14.text: And just so you feel it proper, I'ma let Israel be the one to run it back on you. My wrath, My fury—through them. Then you'll really know this ain't revenge—it's judgment."

15.text: "Philistines, y'all been salty for generations. That grudge you been holdin' turned into violence. You wanted to see Israel destroyed just 'cause you got old beef.

16.text: Well, now I'm bringin' the smoke. I'ma stretch out My hand and cut y'all off. Cherethites? Gone. That last lil' group of seacoast dwellers? Burnt out.

17.text: My rebuke ain't gon' be light—it's gon' be loud, fierce, and final. And when it hit, everybody gon' know—I AM the Lord."

1.text: It was the eleventh year, first day of the month, when the word from the Lord hit me again.

2.text: "Son of man, go on and check Tyre. They been talkin' slick, sayin', 'Aha! Look at Jerusalem, the gateway for all them folks—busted down. Now it's all mine. I'm finna get rich off her downfall.'"

3.text: God said, "Aight Tyre, bet. I'm comin' for you. I'm sendin' wave after wave of nations to hit you—just like the ocean hit the shore nonstop."

4.text: "They gon' tear down your walls, knock down your towers. I'ma scrape you bare—clean like a rock top with nothin' on it."

5.text: "You gon' be nothin' but a spot to dry fishnets out in the sea. I said it. It's gon' happen. You about to be free game for any nation that want a piece."

6.text: "All them little towns you got in the fields? Sword. Dead. Then folks will know—I'm the Lord."

7.text: "Here's what I'ma do," says the Lord. "I'm bringin' Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, king of kings. He comin' down from the north with an army so deep—horses, chariots, troops for days."

8.text: "Them daughter towns? Gone. He comin' with a siege—gonna build up walls, pile up dirt, come at you hard."

9.text: "He'll aim battering rams right at your walls, and axes finna swing till your towers fall flat."

10.text: "So many horses, the dirt they kick up gon' black out the sun. Your walls gon' be shakin' when he roll in, gates bustin' wide open like it's already over."

11.text: "He gon' stomp through your streets like they nothin'. People cut down left and right. All your big strong statues? Crashin'."

12.text: "They gon' rob you blind—take all your gold, all your goods, tear down your pretty houses. Then throw all that rubble—wood, stone, dirt—right into the sea."

13.text: "And them songs y'all love to play? Done. No harps. No music. Silence."

14.text: "I'ma make you flat like bare rock. Folks just gon' spread nets on you. You won't ever be rebuilt. I said it. Period."

15.text: "Listen, Tyre—when you fall, it's gon' shake the whole coastline. When your people scream, when blood get spilled, even the distant cities gon' feel it."

16.text: "All the sea captains and coastal bosses gon' step down from they thrones, toss off they designer fits, and throw on fear like clothes. They gon' sit in the dirt, shakin' nonstop, watchin' your downfall in disbelief."

17.text: "Then they gon' cry about you like this: 'Dang! Tyre gone? You used to run the sea—big name, big game, scarin' everybody. Now look at you—finished.'"

18.text: "Them coastlands gon' be spooked when you fall. Even the oceanfront cities gon' be shook by your exit."

19.text: "When I turn you into a ghost town, buried underwater, drowned in the deep like Atlantis,

20.text: I'ma drop you down with the dead—old ghosts in the pit, people long gone. You gon' be stuck down there, deep in the shadows where nobody lives. You ain't ever comin' back. Meanwhile, I'ma shine My glory in the land of the living."

21.text: "I'm makin' you a whole horror story. Folks might go lookin' for you, but you ain't gon' be found. You done," says the Lord God.

1.text: Then the word of the Lord came to me again.

2.text: "Son of man, I need you to sing a funeral song for Tyre."

3.text: Say this to Tyre, the port city sittin' out at sea, trading with all the coastlands: "The Lord God says—'Tyre, you out here braggin' talkin' 'I'm flawless, I'm fine, I'm all that.'"

4.text: "You sittin' way out in the ocean, and your builders done had you lookin' like a supermodel ship."

5.text: "They used the flyest fir trees from Mount Senir for your boards. Pulled a strong cedar from Lebanon for your mast."

6.text: "Oars? They carved those outta oaks from Bashan. Ashurite craftsmen decked your planks in ivory from Cyprus. Bougie."

7.text: "You had Egyptian linen embroidered on your sails. Blue and purple from Elishah wrapped around you like couture."

8.text: "Sidon and Arvad? They was your crew, rowin' for you. Your pilots? Straight scholars—sharp folk from your own city."

9.text: "The old heads and pros from Gebal? They patched you up tight. Every ship out there, with they whole crew, came through just to buy your goods."

10.text: "You had Persian, Lydian, and Libyan soldiers up in your army, suited up with shields and helmets. They made you look real important."

11.text: "Men from Arvad kept guard on your walls, Gammad soldiers held down your towers. Their shields? Posted up like trophies. Made you look polished."

12.text: "Tarshish was one of your main buyers—traded silver, iron, tin, and lead for your luxury goods."

13.text: "Javan, Tubal, and Meshech? They out here exchanging bronze and even human lives for your merchandise. Yeah, human trafficking."

14.text: "Togarmah sent you horses, war stallions, and mules."

15.text: "Dedan came with ivory tusks and ebony wood. You was real high-end."

16.text: "Syria dropped emeralds, purple cloth, embroidery, linen, coral, and rubies on you for your stuff."

17.text: "Even Judah and Israel came with wheat, millet, honey, oil, and balm."

18.text: "Damascus paid big for your goods too. Luxury items, wine from Helbon, clean white wool—they had tabs with you."

19.text: "Dan and Javan came back and forth, bringin' iron, cassia, and fragrant cane."

20.text: "Dedan sold you saddle blankets, fancy riding gear."

21.text: "Arabia and all the Kedar princes brought lambs, rams, and goats for trade—constant customers."

22.text: "Sheba and Raamah? They came with top-shelf spices, rare jewels, and gold."

23.text: "Haran, Canneh, Eden, Sheba's market cities, Assyria, Chilmad—all in your rotation."

24.text: "They sold you premium threads—purple, embroidery, chestfuls of fly garments, colorful rope, all stacked up in your stalls."

25.text: "The ships of Tarshish hauled your inventory everywhere. You were full, flashy, and floatin' proud out in the sea."

26.text: "But your own rowers steered you into dangerous waters. Then boom—an east wind snapped you in half, right in the ocean."

27.text: "Your whole squad—merchants, warriors, seamen, builders, everybody—you and your cargo? All gone. Drownin' the same day you sank."

28.text: "Even the coastlands gon' shake when your pilots start screamin' out in panic."

29.text: "Every sailor, every deckhand, every captain? They gon' abandon ship and stand on shore, watchin' it all go down."

30.text: "They gon' cry out loud for you, throw dust on their heads, roll around in ash like it's a full-on funeral."

31.text: "They'll shave their heads bald, wear sackcloth, and cry till their hearts break—straight ugly cryin'."

32.text: "They gon' chant this over you: 'Who else got taken out like Tyre? A city that sank right in the sea?'"

33.text: "You used to feed whole nations, Tyre. Rich folks and royalty stayed ballin' off your hustle."

34.text: "But now you lay broken in the deep. All that money, all that crew—gone."

35.text: "The island people watchin' in shock. Their kings? Shook, pale-faced, scared."

36.text: "Traders from all over gon' hiss when they hear about you. You'll be a ghost story now—no comeback, no rebuild, just gone forever."

1.text: Then God hit me with another word.

2.text: "Son of man, go talk to the prince of Tyre and say: 'This what the Lord God say— You got real full of yourself. You out here claimin', 'I'm a god. I sit on a divine throne, chillin' in the middle of the sea.' But nah, bruh, you just a man. You not God, even if your heart swears you one."

3.text: "You think you slicker than Daniel, huh? Ain't no secret you can't figure out, huh?"

4.text: "Yeah, you smart. You got strategy. You ran up a bag—gold, silver, vaults full. A whole empire off your trading game."

5.text: "But now that you rich, your head too big. You really think all that wealth make you untouchable?"

6.text: "So here's what the Lord God say: Since your heart out here actin' like it's divine…"

7.text: "I'ma bring in outsiders, some real ruthless folk. They comin' for your pretty little empire, Slicin' through all that wisdom you proud of. They gon' make you look dusty."

8.text: "You gon' fall hard— Straight into the pit. You gon' die like them other bodies floatin' in the sea."

9.text: "You still gon' talk tough to the one who killin' you? Still think you divine when your life on the line? Nah, you gon' be real human then."

10.text: "You gon' die like a stranger, unclean, By the hand of some foreigners. I said it. That's that."

11.text: Then God gave me another message.

12.text: "Son of man, sing this funeral song for the king of Tyre. Say: 'This what the Lord God says— You was the whole package— Wise, beautiful, flawless. Top-tier."

13.text: "You was in Eden, back in God's own garden. You had on every precious stone— Sardius, topaz, diamonds, beryl, onyx, jasper, sapphires, turquoise, emeralds, and gold. Even your jewelry had music in it. Custom made from day one."

14.text: "You was a cherub—God's own appointed one— posted up on God's mountain, strolling around fire like it was light work."

15.text: "You was perfect, from birth, Until that dirt crept in."

16.text: "Your hustle got too wild. You stayed movin' product, but all that traffic brought violence. So you sinned. God said, 'Out!' You ain't holy no more. I kicked you off the mountain and out the fire."

17.text: "Your ego got fed off your beauty. You let pride ruin your wisdom. So I snatched you down, threw you in front of kings, so everybody could see your downfall."

18.text: "You messed up the sacred spaces, with all your shady business. So I lit a fire from inside you— Burned you to ashes right there, right in front of everybody."

19.text: "Folks who used to roll with you? They shook. They ain't even know what to say. You a horror story now. You done. No reboot, no resurrection."

20.text: Then God gave me another word:

21.text: "Son of man, now turn to Sidon and speak against her."

22.text: "Tell Sidon: 'Look, I'm comin' for you,' says the Lord God. 'I'ma show out right in your city. When I drop judgment, you gon' know who I am.'"

23.text: "I'm bringin' disease. Blood in the streets. Bodies fallin' left and right. Swords comin' from every angle. You gon' know—I am the Lord."

24.text: "And Israel? Y'all ain't gon' be bothered no more by folks like Sidon—no more thorns in your side. Everybody gon' finally know I'm God."

25.text: "Here's what else the Lord God says: When I bring My people—Israel— back from all the places they were scattered, and show My glory through them in front of the whole world…"

26.text: "They gon' live safe again. Build houses. Plant vineyards. Feel secure. While I serve judgment to all the nations that hated on 'em. And they gon' finally know: I am the Lord their God."

1.text: On the twelfth day of the tenth month, in the tenth year, God gave me a word.

2.text: "Son of man, turn and face Pharaoh, king of Egypt. Speak against him and the whole land of Egypt."

3.text: "Say this to him: This what the Lord God say— 'I'm comin' for you, Pharaoh. You big sea monster, layin' up in your rivers, Actin' like you own the Nile. You walk around talkin' bout, 'This my river! I made it myself!'"

4.text: "Nah, I'm finna hook you in the jaw. Drag you out the water with all them fish hangin' off you. Y'all stuck together in pride, now y'all stuck together in judgment."

5.text: "I'm tossin' you into the desert, You and your little fishy crew. Y'all gon' dry out in the field— No one pickin' y'all up, no burial. Y'all just gon' be food for wild animals and vultures."

6.text: "Then Egypt gon' know I'm God. Y'all was supposed to be support for Israel, But you was flimsy, like a reed."

7.text: "When Israel tried to lean on you, You snapped. You messed up their shoulders. You made 'em stumble and break down even worse."

8.text: "So here's what the Lord God say: I'm sendin' a sword your way. Everything breathin'? Gotta go."

9.text: "Egypt gon' be nothing but ruins. Why? 'Cause Pharaoh ran his mouth sayin', 'I made this river myself.'"

10.text: "So yeah, I'm against you AND your river. Egypt gon' be empty and ruined from top to bottom— From Migdol to Syene, all the way to Ethiopia's border."

11.text: "Ain't nobody walkin' through it. No humans, no animals. It's gon' be a ghost town for forty years."

12.text: "Egypt gon' sit in the middle of all the other wastelands. Their cities? Wiped out like the rest. For forty years, I'ma scatter the Egyptians all over the world."

13.text: "But after that," says the Lord God, "When the forty years is up, I'ma bring Egypt back. I'ma let 'em return to Pathros— Back to where they started. But they not gon' be the same."

14.text: "They gon' be humbled. They'll be the least of the kingdoms now. Ain't never gon' rise up like they used to."

15.text: "They'll never be a superpower again. I'ma make sure of that. They done ruling over folks."

16.text: "And Israel? Y'all won't be lookin' to Egypt no more for backup. That relationship gon' remind you of how y'all turned on Me. But once it's all said and done— You'll know I'm the Lord God."

17.text: Fast forward to the twenty-seventh year, first month, first day— God dropped another word.

18.text: "Son of man, Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon? He went all out on Tyre. His army worked till they was bald and bruised— And after all that, they ain't get nothin' out of it. No reward. No plunder."

19.text: "So this what the Lord God say: I'ma give Egypt to Nebuchadnezzar. He gon' take all their riches, Get paid back in full for the effort he put in for Me."

20.text: "Egypt is his paycheck. That war wasn't just his—it was My will, And he put in work."

21.text: "And in that day? I'ma raise up strength in Israel again. I'ma loosen your lips, Ezekiel, So you can speak again among the people. And they gon' know— I am the Lord."

1.text: God spoke to me again.

2.text: "Son of man, I need you to prophesy. Say this: This what the Lord God says— 'Cry out loud, y'all! The day of reckoning comin'!'"

3.text: "'That day right around the corner— The Day of the Lord is near. It's gon' be dark like storm clouds. It's judgment time for the nations.'"

4.text: "'A sword is comin' for Egypt, And Ethiopia gon' feel the pain too. Folks gon' be slain in Egypt, Their wealth snatched, And their whole foundation shattered.'"

5.text: "'Ethiopia, Libya, Lydia, all them mixed-up folks, Chub and everybody ridin' with Egypt— They all gon' fall by the sword too.'"

6.text: This what the Lord says: "The ones who hold Egypt up? They droppin' too. That arrogant power Egypt got? It's comin' down hard. From Migdol to Syene—everybody gettin' touched."

7.text: "Egypt gon' be sittin' in ruins, Just like all them other wrecked countries. Her cities gon' look like ghost towns."

8.text: "Then they gon' know I'm the Lord— When I light Egypt on fire And wipe out all her little helpers."

9.text: "I'ma send messengers in ships that day, They gon' make them carefree Ethiopians panic. The same kind of fear Egypt feel? They gon' feel it too— It's definitely goin' down."

10.text: This what the Lord God says: "I'ma shut Egypt down. And I'ma use Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, to do it."

11.text: "Him and his people— They some cold-blooded warriors. They comin' to destroy Egypt. They drawin' swords And leavin' bodies everywhere."

12.text: "I'ma dry up the rivers, And sell the land off to evil folks. Foreigners gon' wreck it all— The land, the people, the cities. I'm the one sayin' it—don't get it twisted."

13.text: The Lord says this too: "I'ma destroy all them fake gods. I'ma shut down all them idols in Noph. Ain't gon' be no more rulers in Egypt— I'ma send fear through the whole land."

14.text: "Pathros? Wasteland. Zoan? Set on fire. No? Judgment comin'."

15.text: "Sin, the fortress of Egypt? I'ma pour My wrath there. No? Overcrowded no more— They gettin' cut down."

16.text: "Fire's comin' through the whole land. Sin gon' cry out in agony, No gon' be split open, Noph gon' be shook every single day."

17.text: "Young men in Aven and Pi Beseth? Killed in the streets. Them cities? Goin' into captivity."

18.text: "Even Tehaphnehes gon' lose its light. I'ma break the stronghold there. Egypt's pride? Gone. A cloud of sorrow gon' cover her, And her daughters gon' be taken captive."

19.text: "All this judgment I'm bringin'? Egypt gon' know— I'm the Lord."

20.text: On the seventh day of the first month, eleventh year—God dropped another word on me.

21.text: "Son of man, Pharaoh's arm? Yeah, I broke that. And it ain't even wrapped up or splinted. He too weak now to even hold a sword."

22.text: "So this what the Lord God say: 'I'm against Pharaoh. I'ma break both his arms— The strong one AND the one already messed up. He won't be holdin' no sword after that.'"

23.text: "I'ma scatter the Egyptians all over the map. Spread 'em out in every direction."

24.text: "But Babylon? I'ma strengthen him. I'ma put My sword in his hand. Pharaoh? Still weak—he gon' groan like a man Takin' his last breath on the battlefield."

25.text: "The king of Babylon gon' rise. Pharaoh gon' fall. And when they see My sword In Babylon's hand, And he pointin' it straight at Egypt— They gon' know I'm the Lord."

26.text: "I said it before, I'ma say it again— I'ma scatter the Egyptians. Send 'em runnin' in every direction. Then they'll know— I Am the Lord."

1.text: In the eleventh year, third month, first day, God came with another word.

2.text: "Son of man, speak to Pharaoh, king of Egypt, and his whole crew: 'Who you think you matchin' in greatness?'"

3.text: "Let's talk about Assyria— That joint was like a cedar in Lebanon: Tall, fine branches, thick shade, Towerin' up high into the clouds."

4.text: "It was them deep waters that made it grow, Underground streams kept liftin' it up. Water flowed all around where it was planted, And lil' streams shot out to feed other trees in the field."

5.text: "That's why it grew taller than every other tree. Branches stretched far, Soakin' up all that water, Spreadin' wide."

6.text: "Birds nested in its branches, Wild animals chilled underneath, And all kinds of nations took shelter in its shade."

7.text: "It looked beautiful— Tall, wide, strong— Roots dipped into the deep waters."

8.text: "No cedar in Eden could even stand next to it. Fir trees? Nah. Chestnut trees? Not even close. No tree in God's garden could match its beauty."

9.text: "I made it dope with them long branches. Even the trees in Eden got jealous."

10.text: So here's what God says: "Since it got proud 'cause it stood so tall, And its heart swelled with pride,

11.text: I handed it over to a boss nation— Somebody ruthless. He chopped it down for all its evil ways."

12.text: "Foreign nations—mean ones— Came in and tore it apart. Branches fell in the mountains, Limbs got scattered in valleys and rivers. Everybody ran from under its shade— They ain't stick around."

13.text: "All that's left? Birds pickin' at what's left, Beasts crawlin' through the ruins."

14.text: "I did this to show: No tree planted by the water Should get too high and mighty again. Ain't none of them trees reachin' for the clouds anymore. 'Cause they all gon' end up the same— Dead. Laid out underground, With the rest of humankind, Down in the Pit."

15.text: God said: "When that tree fell, Even the underworld mourned. I made the waters stop flowin'. Lebanon cried over it, All the trees drooped in sadness."

16.text: "Whole nations trembled when it hit the ground. I threw it down to hell With all the others headed for the Pit. Even the trees of Eden—the finest ones— Felt some type of way, Like, 'Dang, even that tree ain't make it?'"

17.text: "That tree went to the grave With the ones killed by the sword. All the folks that once stood strong in its shadow— They in the dirt now too."

18.text: "So Pharaoh—let Me ask you this: Which tree in Eden do you really think you're like? Big, bad, glorious? Guess what— You goin' down just like they did. You and your whole squad Gon' be laid out with the rest of 'em, Down in the dirt, Uncircumcised, Cut down by the sword. That's Pharaoh and all his people." –The Lord God said it.

1.text: In the twelfth year, twelfth month, first day, God pulled up on me again with a word.

2.text: "Son of man, go ahead and write Pharaoh's eulogy. Say this: 'You thought you was a young lion out here with the nations? Nah, you was more like a sea monster— Stirrin' up the waters, Kickin' up mud, Foulin' everything you touched.'"

3.text: "This what God says: 'I'm throwin' a net over you, Whole crowd of folks gon' help Me drag you out.'"

4.text: "I'm leavin' you out in the open field, Birds pickin' at you, Wild animals feasting on you."

5.text: "Your body gon' be laid out on the mountains, Valleys filled with your flesh."

6.text: "Yo blood gon' run so deep, It'll water the land, Even fill up dry riverbeds."

7.text: "When I shut your light off, The sky gon' go dark. Stars won't shine, Sun gon' hide, Moon gon' stay out the picture."

8.text: "All the heavenly lights gon' dim on your land— Whole place gon' be in the dark."

9.text: "I'ma shake folks' hearts all over the world, When they hear about your downfall— Places that ain't never even heard of you before."

10.text: "Kings gon' be shook. Hands shakin', Faces pale, Scared for their lives when they see My sword swingin'."

11.text: "God said, 'The king of Babylon comin' with that blade.'"

12.text: "He got a savage army— Most feared outta all the nations— They gon' run through Egypt, Leave nothin' standin'."

13.text: "Even the animals by the Nile? Gone. No more muddy feet, no more trampled banks."

14.text: "I'ma let the waters calm again— Flowin' smooth like oil."

15.text: "When I wipe Egypt out, When the cities empty and silent, Then they gon' know: I'm the Lord."

16.text: "This the funeral song they gon' sing. Daughters from all over gon' be cryin' for Egypt— Mournin' her and her whole crew."

17.text: Two weeks later, same year— God spoke again:

18.text: "Son of man, cry out for Egypt's whole crew. Tell 'em they about to join the other dead nations, Down in the Pit."

19.text: "You thought you were beautiful? Go ahead—lay down with the rest of the uncircumcised."

20.text: "You gon' die like the rest, Sword takin' you and everybody with you."

21.text: "Even the mighty warriors in hell gon' notice you: 'There go Pharaoh—he down here with the rest of us.'"

22.text: "Assyria's already down here, Graves all around her, Everybody slain by the sword."

23.text: "She deep down in the Pit, Company all around, They brought terror to the world— Now they just bones."

24.text: "Elam's there too— Same thing: Fell by the sword, Uncircumcised, Now they sittin' in shame underground."

25.text: "Whole crew laid out together, Dead and disgraced. They scared folks when they were alive, But now they buried with the rest of the shameful."

26.text: "Meshech and Tubal—yeah, they here too. Bodies everywhere. Uncircumcised, dead by the sword. They were out there flexin', Now just more bones in the dark."

27.text: "They don't even get buried with honor. Their swords under their heads, But guilt still on they bones— Terror don't make you holy."

28.text: "Pharaoh, you right there with 'em. Laid out with the rest of the slain, Same sword that got them gon' get you too."

29.text: "Edom? Yup. Kings, princes—all of 'em. Once thought they were strong, Now they laid up with the uncircumcised in the Pit."

30.text: "Even the princes of the north— And the Sidonians— They brought terror too, But now they just another name on the dead list."

31.text: "Pharaoh gon' see all them other fallen kingdoms And feel a weird kinda comfort: 'Least I ain't fall alone.' But you still fallen though."

32.text: "I let folks fear My name while y'all were alive. Now Pharaoh and his whole crew Gon' lay right there with the rest of the dead, Uncircumcised, Cut down by the sword. That's how this ends." –God said it. Period.

1.text: God came through with another word.

2.text: "Son of man, go tell your people this: If I send trouble—like war or judgment— And the people post up a watchman from their own block,

3.text: And that watchman see danger comin', If he blow the trumpet and warn everybody,

4.text: Then if somebody hear it but ignore it— That's on them. If they get caught up, Their blood ain't on nobody but themself.

5.text: They heard the warning and still didn't move. They brought that on they own head. But if they listened? They woulda saved they own life.

6.text: Now if that same watchman see danger And keep quiet? Don't say nothin'? And somebody die 'cause they ain't get the heads-up? Yeah, they still gon' die in they sin— But I'm holdin' that watchman responsible. That's blood on his hands."

7.text: "So look, son of man—I made you that watchman. I talk, you better speak up. Tell the people what I said."

8.text: "If I say, 'Wicked man, you gon' die,' And you say nothin'? They gon' die in sin, But you gon' have to answer for that."

9.text: "But if you do warn them, And they still don't change? They'll die in their mess— But you? You good. You did your part."

10.text: "Now tell Israel this: Y'all always crying, 'Our sins too heavy! We dying out here—how we gon' live?'

11.text: Tell 'em: 'I ain't out here rootin' for death,' says the Lord. 'I don't want nobody out here dyin' in sin. I want y'all to change and live. Turn around! Turn around! Why y'all out here tryna die, Israel?'"

12.text: "Now break this down for 'em, son of man: Just 'cause you been righteous don't mean you untouchable If you turn around and wild out. Same way—if you been wicked, But switch up and do right, You ain't gotta fall with the past."

13.text: "If I tell the righteous, 'You good,' But they start trippin'? That past righteousness don't count no more. They gon' die in what they doin' now."

14.text: "But if I say, 'You gon' die,' And that wicked one turn they life around—"

15.text: "Return what they stole, Do right by folks, Follow the law and stop the sin— That person gon' live."

16.text: "None of that old dirt gon' count against them. They turned around. They did right. They gon' live."

17.text: "But your people be sayin': 'God not bein' fair!' Nah, they the ones bein' shady."

18.text: "If somebody do right but then turn to evil— They gon' die for it."

19.text: "But if somebody was wildin' out, And they get they act together— They gon' live."

20.text: "Y'all still wanna say I'm unfair? I'm judging everybody by what they do. Ain't no favorites."

21.text: Twelfth year of captivity. Tenth month. Fifth day. Somebody who escaped from Jerusalem ran up to me: "Yo… the city gone. It's taken."

22.text: But God already had me the night before— Opened my mouth again. So when that man showed up, I was finally able to speak again.

23.text: Then God dropped another word on me:

24.text: "Them folks who still chillin' in the ruins talkin' like, 'Abraham was one man and got the land— We plenty—we for sure get to keep it.'"

25.text: "Tell 'em this from Me: 'Y'all still out here eatin' bloody meat, Still lookin' to idols, Still killin' folks. Y'all think y'all deserve this land?'"

26.text: "Y'all trust in violence. Y'all dirty with sin. Y'all sleepin' with each other's wives. You really think you supposed to own this place?"

27.text: "Tell 'em: Everybody in the ruins? Sword gon' get 'em. Those out in the fields? Beasts gon' eat 'em. In caves and hideouts? Disease gon' find 'em."

28.text: "I'ma make this land quiet—real quiet. Y'all pride? Done. Mountains empty. Nobody walkin' through."

29.text: "When I turn it into a wasteland, Y'all gon' know— I am the Lord."

30.text: "Son of man, lemme tell you what's really goin' on: They talkin' about you behind closed doors. On the low they be like, 'Hey, come listen to this prophet. He be speakin' the word.'"

31.text: "They show up like fans, Sit down like they My people, Act real churchy… But they don't do nothin' I say. They all talk—hearts still chasin' money and self."

32.text: "To them, you just entertainment. Like some R&B singer with a pretty voice and nice beat. They vibe with the sound… But they don't move on the message."

33.text: "But when all this really happen— And it will— They gon' know: A prophet was talkin' to 'em the whole time."

1.text: God came with another word for me.

2.text: "Son of man, speak out against these so-called shepherds in Israel. Tell them: 'The Lord God got somethin' to say to y'all: Y'all supposed to be feedin' the flock, but instead y'all feedin' yourselves. Shame on you.'"

3.text: "Y'all eat good, rockin' the wool, livin' off the fat sheep— But ain't givin' nothing back to the ones you supposed to be takin' care of."

4.text: "Y'all ain't helped the weak. Ain't healed the sick. Ain't bandaged the broken. Ain't went after the ones that ran off or got lost. All y'all do is flex power and treat people cold."

5.text: "So the sheep ran off—scattered everywhere— And the wild beasts ate 'em up, 'Cause they ain't had nobody watchin' over them."

6.text: "My people out here lost, Wanderin' through mountains and high places, Spread all over the earth… And ain't nobody even lookin' for them."

7.text: "So listen up, you fake shepherds—God got a word."

8.text: "'I swear on My name,' says the Lord, 'Since y'all let My sheep become prey for every wild thing, And y'all didn't even try to find them— Just kept lookin' out for yourselves—'"

9.text: "'I got somethin' for y'all.'"

10.text: "'I'm comin' for y'all. I'm takin' My sheep out y'all hands. Y'all ain't gon' be able to eat off them no more. I'ma rescue My people from y'all mouths— Y'all won't be snackin' off their backs ever again.'"

11.text: "I'm tellin' y'all straight up," says the Lord, "I'm bout to go get My sheep Myself. I ain't waitin' on nobody no more."

12.text: "Like a real shepherd go find his scattered sheep— That's what I'm gon' do. I'm pullin' them out the dark clouds and confusion where they got lost."

13.text: "I'ma bring them back from all over the world, And I'm takin' them home to their land. They gon' eat good in the valleys and hills of Israel."

14.text: "They gon' have real food, Restin' in peace, Chillin' on mountaintop pastures. No more scraps."

15.text: "I, the Lord, gon' feed them Myself, And let them finally lay down and rest."

16.text: "I'm comin' for the lost ones. I'm bringin' back the ones who ran off. I'm patchin' up the wounded. Strengthenin' the sick. But the proud, the greedy? I'm comin' with judgment. They gettin' humbled."

17.text: "And now to y'all, My flock," says the Lord, "I'ma deal with y'all too. I'm gon' separate sheep from sheep—rams from goats."

18.text: "Y'all fat sheep done ate up the best grass And trampled the rest. You drink clean water And muddy up what's left for everybody else?"

19.text: "My other sheep gotta eat what y'all stepped on And drink the dirty leftovers. That ain't right."

20.text: "So I'ma step in," says the Lord. "I'm gon' judge between the fat and the skinny sheep."

21.text: "Y'all bullies pushin' folks with y'all sides and horns, Shovin' the weak ones out the way, Scatterin' the ones who need help."

22.text: "But I'ma save My flock. Ain't nobody gon' be prey no more. I'm holdin' everybody accountable."

23.text: "I'ma raise up one Shepherd for them— My servant David. He gon' feed them right. He gon' lead them how they supposed to be led."

24.text: "And I, the Lord, will be their God, And David gon' be their prince. I said what I said."

25.text: "I'm makin' a peace deal with them. No more wild animals tearin' them up. They gon' be safe in the wilderness, Sleepin' sound in the woods."

26.text: "I'ma bless them and everything around 'em. Rain gon' fall when it's supposed to. It's gon' be rain full of blessing."

27.text: "The trees gon' bear fruit. The land gon' give harvest. They gon' live safe and free."

28.text: "No more fear of enemies. No more beasts tearin' through. Just peace, safety, and freedom."

29.text: "I'ma plant a garden of fame for them— They'll be fed, respected, And won't be embarrassed by outsiders ever again."

30.text: "They gon' know I'm with them. No more guessin'. I'm their God, and they My people."

31.text: "Y'all My flock. The flock of My pasture. You just people, But I'm God. And I got y'all."

1.text: Then God came to me again with a word.

2.text: "Son of man, turn your face toward Mount Seir and speak this word over it."

3.text: "Tell it straight: The Lord God say, 'Mount Seir, I'm comin' for you. I'm stretchin' out My hand, and you gon' be left in ruins.'"

4.text: "Your cities? Gone. Your name? Wiped out. Then you gon' know—I'm the Lord."

5.text: "Why? 'Cause you been hatin' on Israel since forever. You shed blood like it was nothin', Especially when they were already down bad, Right when they was just tryna get back up."

6.text: "So hear Me when I say this," says the Lord God: "You loved blood? Cool. Now blood gon' chase you. I'm preparin' blood for you, And it won't stop comin'."

7.text: "Mount Seir gon' be desolate—real quiet, Ain't nobody comin' or goin'."

8.text: "Your mountains? Full of bodies. Your hills, your valleys, your low places? Covered in folk laid out by the sword."

9.text: "You gon' be permanently desolate. Ain't no one tryna move back there. Then you'll know—I am the Lord."

10.text: "You said in your heart, 'Both Israel and Judah? Yeah, we takin' that. It's ours now.' Like God ain't still up in there."

11.text: "So guess what," says the Lord, "I'ma pay you back with that same energy— That hate you had? That envy you moved in? Yeah, you gon' feel it. And My people gon' see who I really am When I judge you."

12.text: "You'll know I'm the Lord, 'Cause I heard every foul word you spit About the mountains of Israel. You was like, 'They done. That land ours now.'"

13.text: "You ran your mouth on Me, Talkin' bold like you run things. I heard everything."

14.text: "The whole world gon' throw a party When I leave you empty and cold."

15.text: "You was laughin' when My people lost everything— When their land was destroyed. Now I'ma flip the script. Mount Seir? You gettin' that treatment. You and all of Edom. And after that? You'll know who I am."

1.text: God told me, "Son of man, speak up to the mountains of Israel and say, 'Y'all better listen to what the Lord say.'"

2.text: This what the Lord God said: "Since your enemies had the nerve to shout, 'Aha! Them hills and heights we been wantin'? They ours now!'"

3.text: Go ahead and prophesy. Say: "Because folks came through, tore you up, took over from every side, and now all these nations run they mouths about you…"

4.text: So hear Me, mountains, hills, rivers, valleys, ruins, and deserted cities that everybody's been jokin' about and robbin'—this the word of the Lord.

5.text: I'm hot with jealousy for y'all. Edom and all the other nations took what's Mine with evil hearts and greedy hands—like it was free for the takin'.

6.text: So speak on it: Tell the land of Israel, 'God mad. He jealous. And yeah, He saw y'all carryin' the weight of everybody's shade.'

7.text: That's why I, the Lord, swear: them other nations gon' get clowned too. They gon' feel what shame really is.

8.text: But you? Mountains of Israel? You gon' grow again. Branches gon' shoot out, fruit gon' show up—for My people, Israel, 'cause they comin' home.

9.text: I'm with y'all now. I'm turnin' back toward you. Y'all gon' be worked, planted, and made beautiful.

10.text: I'ma multiply folks on you—all of Israel. The cities gon' be full again. The ruins? Rebuilt.

11.text: People, animals—everything gon' grow. Y'all gon' have more than you did before. And that's how you'll know I'm the Lord.

12.text: I'ma bring My people home to walk this land again. It's theirs now. You belong to them, not to loss.

13.text: The Lord said: "They used to say y'all chew up your own people and keep the nation from growin'…"

14.text: But that's over. No more eatin' up folks. No more takin' children or futures. That's done.

15.text: I won't let folks talk down on you no more. Ain't no more shame, no more disrespect. And no more stumblin' blocks in your own house."

16.text: Then God came to me with another word.

17.text: "Son of man, when Israel lived in their land, they messed it up with their ways. I saw it—dirty like a woman on her cycle, unclean through and through.

18.text: I got angry. Real angry. They spilled blood and worshipped idols. So I poured out My judgment.

19.text: I scattered them. Sent them all over the map. Judged 'em based on how they acted.

20.text: But even in exile, they embarrassed Me. People pointed and said, 'Ain't that God's people? Why He let 'em get kicked out like that?'

21.text: Still, I cared about My name. Yeah, they dragged it, but I ain't lettin' My name go out like that forever."

22.text: So tell Israel: "I ain't doin' this for you," says the Lord. "I'm cleanin' y'all up for My name's sake—'cause y'all been messin' it up everywhere y'all went."

23.text: "I'm about to make My name big again. The same name y'all profaned. But when I show out through y'all, The nations gon' know who I am."

24.text: "I'm bringin' y'all back—outta every land, every corner. Back to the place I gave your people."

25.text: "I'm gon' wash y'all clean. Y'all been filthy with idols and foolishness— But I'm rinsin' all that off."

26.text: "I'ma give you a brand new heart— One that's soft, not stone cold. And I'ma put a whole new spirit in you."

27.text: "My Spirit gon' live in you, And help you walk how I told y'all to walk. You'll finally live right."

28.text: "Then you gon' live in the land I promised your ancestors. You'll be My people. I'll be your God."

29.text: "I'ma save y'all from all that grime. Your crops gon' grow. Famine? Nah—we not doin' that again."

30.text: "Your trees gon' bear fruit. Your fields gon' flourish. Ain't no nation gon' clown y'all for bein' broke ever again."

31.text: "When all this hit, Y'all gon' look back and realize how triflin' y'all were— And it's gon' break your heart."
