32.text: "Let Me make it clear again: I ain't doin' this 'cause y'all earned it. I'm doin' it so the world knows I'm God. Y'all should be ashamed, for real."

33.text: "But on that day I clean y'all up? Cities rebuilt. Ruins restored. It's up."

34.text: "That wasteland folks used to laugh at? It gon' look like Eden. People gon' walk by and say, 'Wait… wasn't this a dump? Now it's thrivin'?'"

35.text: "Ruins gon' become neighborhoods. Barren places gon' bloom."

36.text: "And all them other nations nearby? They gon' know I'm the one who flipped the script. I planted what was dead. I rebuilt what was lost."

37.text: "I'ma let y'all ask Me for this, too. And I'ma do it. I'ma multiply your people like a flock."

38.text: "Like the sacred flocks that filled Jerusalem on feast days, That's how your cities gon' look—full and alive again. And then? Everybody gon' know I'm the Lord."

1.text: The hand of the Lord came and scooped me up. His Spirit dropped me right in the middle of a valley full of dry bones.

2.text: He had me walk through it—bone after bone, scattered everywhere. And lemme tell you, they was real dry.

3.text: Then He asked, "Son of man, you think these bones can live again?" I said, "Lord… only You know that."

4.text: Then He said, "Speak to these bones. Say, 'Dry bones, listen to what the Lord gotta say!'"

5.text: "This is what God says to these bones: 'I'ma breathe life into y'all. Y'all gon' live again.'"

6.text: "I'ma hook the muscles back up, cover you with skin, and breathe into you—and you gon' come back to life. Then y'all gon' know I'm the Lord."

7.text: So I did what He said—I prophesied. And while I was speakin', I heard a rumblin', bones clickin' and clackin' back together—bone to bone.

8.text: Then I saw muscles form on 'em, skin coverin' 'em—but they still wasn't breathin'. No life just yet.

9.text: God said, "Now speak to the breath, son of man. Call it from all four winds. Tell it to come breathe on these dead ones so they can live."

10.text: I did what He said—and breath came in. They stood up on they feet, strong and ready. A whole army, lookin' like they never missed a beat.

11.text: Then God told me, "These bones? They Israel. They say, 'We dried up. Hope gone. We cut off.'"

12.text: "So tell 'em this: 'I'm about to open y'all graves, bring you back up, and take you home to Israel.'"

13.text: "When I open them graves and raise y'all up, then y'all gon' know it's Me—I'm the Lord."

14.text: "I'ma put My Spirit in you, and you gon' live. I'ma plant y'all right back in your land. And everybody gon' know I'm the one who said it—and did it."

15.text: God spoke to me again.

16.text: He said, "Son of man, grab a stick and write on it: 'Judah and the people rollin' with him.' Then grab another stick and write: 'Joseph—Ephraim—and all his crew.'"

17.text: "Now put them two sticks together in your hand, like they one stick."

18.text: When folks ask, 'Yo, what this mean?'

19.text: Say, "God said He takin' Joseph's stick and Judah's stick, and He puttin' 'em together. One people. One hand. One God."

20.text: "Hold them sticks up so they can see it."

21.text: Then say, "This what God said: I'm bringin' My people back from all them places they got scattered to."

22.text: "I'ma make 'em one nation. No more North and South. No more split. One king gon' rule all of 'em."

23.text: "They ain't gon' mess with idols no more. No nasty stuff. No foolishness. I'ma clean 'em up. They gon' be My people, and I'ma be their God."

24.text: "David My servant gon' be their king—one shepherd for everybody. They gon' live right, follow My Word, and do what I said."

25.text: "They gon' live in the land I gave Jacob. They kids, and they kids' kids, gon' stay there forever. David still gon' be prince over 'em forever too."

26.text: "I'ma make a peace deal with 'em. A forever covenant. I'ma multiply them, bless them, and plant My holy house right in the middle of 'em—forever."

27.text: "I'll be with them, livin' with them. They'll be My people. I'll be their God."

28.text: "Then the nations gon' know I'm the one who made Israel holy, when My presence is right there with 'em. Not once in a while—forevermore."

1.text: The word of the Lord came to me again.

2.text: "Son of man, turn your face toward Gog from the land of Magog—the big dog prince over Rosh, Meshech, and Tubal—and call him out."

3.text: "Tell him this what God said: 'Gog, I'm comin' for you. Yeah, you. Prince of Rosh, Meshech, and Tubal.'"

4.text: "I'ma turn you around, drag you out with hooks in your jaw. You and your whole army—on horses, geared up in armor, shields, swords, the whole nine."

5.text: "Persia, Ethiopia, and Libya rollin' with you—all of 'em strapped and suited."

6.text: "Gomer and Togarmah bringin' their crews from the north too. You got a whole squad deep behind you."

7.text: "Get ready. Arm up. You and your whole camp. Be on standby."

8.text: "After a long while, you gon' show up. In the last days, you gon' come into the land of My people—the ones I brought back from war and exile. That land used to be empty, but now it's full again. They livin' peaceful."

9.text: "You gon' ride in like a storm, deep and heavy, like a cloud coverin' the land—your whole army with you."

10.text: God says, "When that day come, you gon' start thinkin' slick. Evil gon' start bubbling in your mind."

11.text: "You'll be like, 'I'm bout to hit these folks livin' in peace. No gates, no walls—they wide open.'"

12.text: "You tryna run up and rob 'em, snatch what they got. These the same folks I gathered from all over, who rebuilt the land and settlin' in, finally blessed with stuff again."

13.text: "Even Sheba, Dedan, Tarshish, and all their lil homies gon' say, 'Oh, you came to loot, huh? Tryna snatch gold, silver, cattle and goods?'"

14.text: "So son of man, speak this to Gog: When My people chillin' and livin' safe, don't act like you ain't know."

15.text: "You gon' ride down from the deep north—Gog and all your people—on horses, lookin' like an unstoppable force."

16.text: "You gon' storm Israel like a cloud in the end times. But guess what? I'm the one bringin' you there, so when I handle you, the world gon' know who I am."

17.text: "Ain't you the one I told the prophets about way back? They said somebody like you was comin'… and here you go."

18.text: "And when you touch down in Israel? That's when My fury gon' show up."

19.text: "I'm jealous for My people, and My anger burn hot. That day gon' shake the earth—a massive earthquake in Israel."

20.text: "Everything gon' feel it: fish in the sea, birds in the sky, animals, bugs, and every single person on earth. Mountains fallin', cliffs crumblin', every wall breakin' down."

21.text: "I'ma make chaos hit your camp. Folks gon' turn on each other—every man tryna survive, even if it mean stabbin' his brother."

22.text: "I'ma drop judgment on you: plague, bloodshed, heavy rain, hail, fire, and brimstone straight from the heavens."

23.text: "I'ma make sure the world see My greatness, feel My holiness. And when I'm done? All the nations gon' know: I AM the Lord."

1.text: "Alright now, son of man—go speak on Gog again. Tell him what the Lord God say: 'I'm still on your head, Gog—ruler of Rosh, Meshech, and Tubal.'"

2.text: "I'm gon' drag you back from way up north and set you right in front of My people on Israel's mountains."

3.text: "Then I'ma slap that bow right out yo' left hand, and your arrows? They hittin' the dirt outta your right."

4.text: "You gon' fall, right there on them mountains—your whole squad with you. I'm feedin' y'all to the birds and wild animals like a feast."

5.text: "Ain't gon' be no burial. Y'all gon' die in the open field. Why? Cuz I said so," says the Lord.

6.text: "Oh and I ain't just stoppin' with you—I'm sendin' fire to Magog and all them chillin' in safety on them coastlines. When I'm done, everybody gon' know I'm the Lord."

7.text: "My holy name? Yeah, I'm gon' make it ring loud in Israel again. They ain't gon' mess with My name no more. And the nations? They gon' recognize I'm the Holy One in Israel."

8.text: "It's goin' down. Best believe it. I said it, and it's already in motion."

9.text: "Folks in Israel gon' come out and burn all y'all leftover weapons—shields, bows, spears, whatever—using it for firewood for seven years."

10.text: "They won't even need to chop trees no more. Just burn the weapons of war. And the same folks who got robbed? They gon' be the ones doin' the robbin' now," says the Lord.

11.text: "On that day, I'ma give Gog a gravesite in Israel—a valley east of the sea. It's gon' block the road 'cause that's where his whole crew get buried. They gon' call it Hamon Gog Valley."

12.text: "Israel gon' be buryin' bodies for seven straight months just to clean the land."

13.text: "Everybody gon' take part in it, and that act alone? That's gon' give 'em some clout when I show out and get My glory," says the Lord.

14.text: "They even gon' hire folks just to do clean-up duty—lookin' for bones and settin' markers."

15.text: "When the crew find a bone, they'll flag it till the bury team come scoop it up and drop it in Hamon Gog Valley."

16.text: "Even the city nearby gon' be called Hamonah. That land gon' be clean after that."

17.text: "And you, son of man, tell the birds and beasts this: 'Y'all better pull up. I got a feast for y'all—God's own barbecue on Israel's mountains.'"

18.text: "Feast on the mighty ones, drink blood of earth's top dogs—rams, lambs, bulls, goats—all them fattened up in Bashan."

19.text: "Eat till you stuffed, drink till you gone off it—it's God's sacrifice, and it's all laid out."

20.text: "Horses, riders, soldiers, war men—you gon' be full off all them. This My table," says the Lord God.

21.text: "Then I'ma flex My glory across the nations. Everybody gon' witness the judgment I drop and know I did that."

22.text: "From that day forward, Israel gon' know—I am their God."

23.text: "Even the Gentiles gon' understand why Israel got dragged into exile. It wasn't random—it was cuz they was unfaithful. So I hid My face, let their enemies handle them."

24.text: "I dealt with them based on their dirt. I ain't sugarcoated nothin'."

25.text: "But now? I'ma bring back Jacob's people. I'm showin' mercy on all of Israel. I'm protecting My holy name."

26.text: "Yeah, they carried their shame and all that betrayal when they lived comfy and forgot Me—but I'm still gon' step in."

27.text: "I'ma gather 'em from all the lands I scattered 'em to. I'ma pull up in glory in front of all them other nations."

28.text: "That's when they gon' know I'm really their God—the One who sent 'em into exile, and the One who brought 'em home. Not a single one left behind."

29.text: "And I ain't hidin' My face no more. I'm pourin' out My Spirit on Israel. That's on Me," says the Lord God.

1.text: "25 years deep in exile, start of the year, tenth day of the month—14 years after Jerusalem fell—God pulled up on me again. Same day, His hand was on me heavy."

2.text: "In a vision, God took me back to Israel. He placed me on a real high mountain. Down south on that mountain? I saw somethin' that looked like a city."

3.text: "He brought me closer, and there was this man—glowin' like bronze. Had a measuring stick and linen tape in his hand. Bro posted up right at the gate."

4.text: "He told me, 'Son of man, open your eyes and ears. Pay close attention to everything I'm about to show you. You ain't here by accident—I brought you here to go back and tell Israel what's what.'"

5.text: "I saw a wall all the way around the outer edge of the temple. That man's stick was six cubits long (each cubit was a little longer than usual). He measured the wall—one rod high, one rod thick."

6.text: "Then we walked to the east gate. He went up the steps and measured the front part—one rod wide. Same on both sides."

7.text: "Each little side room in the gate was one rod by one rod. Five cubits in between 'em. That front part of the gate inside? One rod."

8.text: "He measured that inner vestibule too—one rod deep."

9.text: "That front vestibule space? Eight cubits. The gateposts? Two cubits. The entryway was inside the gate structure."

10.text: "East gate had three side rooms on each side—same size. Gateposts matched too."

11.text: "He measured the entrance—ten cubits wide. Full gate length? Thirteen cubits."

12.text: "There was a buffer zone in front of the rooms—one cubit on both sides. The side rooms themselves? Six cubits each."

13.text: "He checked the width from roof to roof of the opposite rooms—25 cubits wide. Doors facing each other directly."

14.text: "He measured the gateposts—60 cubits high. The whole court around the gate extended up to them."

15.text: "From the start of the outer gate to the start of the inner gate's vestibule? 50 cubits."

16.text: "I saw window openings around all the gate rooms and archways, shaped at an angle. Same with the vestibules—windows all around inside. And they carved palm trees on each gatepost."

17.text: "He brought me into the outer courtyard. All around it were rooms and a pavement floor. 30 rooms opened up to that walkway."

18.text: "The walkway ran next to the gates—same length as the gates. That was the lower pavement area."

19.text: "Then he measured the space from the outer gate front to the front of the inner court wall—100 cubits across, both toward the east and the north."

20.text: "We went to the north gate in the outer court. He measured its length and width."

21.text: "Three rooms on each side, plus gateposts and arches—same measurements as the east gate. Gate was 50 cubits long, 25 wide."

22.text: "Windows and palm tree carvings matched the east gate too. Seven steps led up to it. Archway right in front."

23.text: "There was a gate to the inner court straight across from this one—just like the east gate. Distance between gates? 100 cubits."

24.text: "Then we hit the south side. There was a gate there too, facing south. He measured the gateposts and arches—same layout."

25.text: "Windows all around, just like the others. Gate was 50 cubits long, 25 wide."

26.text: "Seven steps led up to this one too, with the archway in front. Palm tree carvings on each post—left and right."

27.text: "Another gate to the inner court, also facing south. Distance from gate to gate? 100 cubits."

28.text: "Now we entered the inner court through the south gate. He measured that too—same specs as the outer gates."

29.text: "Rooms, posts, arches—all measured the same. Windows all around. Length was 50 cubits, width was 25."

30.text: "The archways stretched 25 cubits long, five cubits wide—all around."

31.text: "These inner arches faced the outer court. Palm trees on the gateposts again. This one had eight steps going up."

32.text: "He took me to the inner east gate next. Same measurements."

33.text: "Rooms, posts, arches—same style. Windows all around. Gate was 50 long, 25 wide."

34.text: "Arches faced the outer court. Palm tree carvings again. Eight steps led up."

35.text: "Then we moved to the north inner gate. Measured just like the rest."

36.text: "Rooms, gateposts, arches—all had windows. 50 cubits long, 25 wide."

37.text: "Gateposts faced the outer court. Palm trees on both sides. Eight steps up."

38.text: "There was a room at the gatepost where they washed the burnt offerings."

39.text: "Inside the vestibule were four tables—two on each side—to kill the burnt, sin, and guilt offerings."

40.text: "As you walked toward the north gate entry, there were two more tables. And two more on the other side—same setup."

41.text: "So that's four on one side, four on the other—eight total for slaughterin' the sacrifices."

42.text: "There were also four stone tables, each 1.5 cubits square and one cubit high. That's where they laid the tools for cutting the meat."

43.text: "Hooks were attached inside—one hand wide—all the way around. And the meat? It sat right on the tables."

44.text: "Outside the inner gate, in the inner court, were two rooms for the singers—one on the south side of the north gate, the other on the north side of the south gate."

45.text: "Dude said, 'This south-facing room? That's for the priests over the temple.'"

46.text: "'And the north-facing room? That's for the priests who serve at the altar—Zadok's sons, from Levi's crew, the only ones allowed to step close to God.'"

47.text: "He measured the inner courtyard—100 cubits long, 100 cubits wide. It was a perfect square. The altar sat right in front of the temple."

48.text: "Then we pulled up to the temple porch. He measured the side posts—five cubits on each side. Gateway was three cubits wide on both sides."

49.text: "The porch itself was 20 cubits long, 11 cubits wide. Steps led up to it, and on each side of the doorway stood a pillar."

1.text: Then we stepped inside the main sanctuary. He measured the doorposts—six cubits thick on both sides. That's the width of the holy setup right there.

2.text: The doorway itself? Ten cubits wide. Each side wall of the entrance was five cubits thick. Whole room was 40 cubits long, 20 wide.

3.text: He went deeper and checked the next doorway—posts were two cubits thick. Entrance stood six cubits tall, and the doorway itself was seven cubits wide.

4.text: He measured the next room—20 cubits long and 20 wide, behind the main sanctuary. He looked at me and said, 'This right here? This the Most Holy Place.'

5.text: He checked the outer wall of the temple—six cubits thick. All around it, there were side rooms, each four cubits wide.

6.text: There were three levels of side rooms stacked on top of each other—30 rooms per level. The rooms sat on little ledges built into the temple wall. They ain't attach directly to the main wall, just rested on support ledges.

7.text: Each level went up like stairs—the higher up you went, the wider the rooms got 'cause of how the walls stepped out. The middle level led you from bottom to top.

8.text: I noticed the whole temple sat up on a platform. Foundation under the side rooms was six cubits tall—one full measuring rod.

9.text: The outer wall around the side rooms was five cubits thick. Then there was still a little space left around the edge of the temple—like a narrow terrace.

10.text: There was a 20 cubit-wide gap between that and the outer wall chambers, running all around the temple.

11.text: The side rooms had doors that opened into the terrace—one door facing north, one south. That terrace was five cubits wide all the way around.

12.text: Behind the temple, on the west end, there was a separate building. It was 70 cubits wide, walls five cubits thick, and it stretched 90 cubits long.

13.text: He measured the main temple—100 cubits long. Then the courtyard and that back building with its walls? Another 100 cubits.

14.text: Even the front of the temple, facing east with that courtyard? 100 cubits wide.

15.text: He checked the building out back that faced the courtyard, with its side porches—100 cubits. Same for the inner sanctuary and porch area.

16.text: Everything had doorposts and carved window frames. All around—three levels of galleries opposite the thresholds. Wood paneling ran from the floor all the way up to the windows—and yeah, the windows were covered.

17.text: From the top of the doors to the inner rooms, and on every single wall inside and out, everything was measured and set just right.

18.text: The place was decked out with carved cherubim and palm trees. One palm tree between each pair of cherubs. Every cherub had two faces.

19.text: One face looked like a man facing a palm, the other looked like a young lion, facing the other palm. That same design wrapped all the way around the temple.

20.text: From the floor to the top of the doorway, cherubim and palm trees covered the sanctuary walls.

21.text: The doorposts to the sanctuary were square-shaped, just like the front of the holy spot. All of it matched.

22.text: There was a wooden altar—three cubits high, two cubits long. Corners, length, and sides all made from wood. He told me, 'This the table that sits before the Lord.'

23.text: The temple and the Most Holy Place each had a set of double doors.

24.text: Each door had two folding panels—two panels per door, one set on each side.

25.text: Just like the walls, those doors had cherubim and palm trees carved in. And there was a wood canopy stretched over the porch area outside.

26.text: Window frames were beveled, and palm trees were on both sides of the porch—on the side rooms and up on the canopy too.

1.text: Then he took me back out to the outer court—on the north side—and brought me to some rooms sittin' across from the courtyard that separates the holy from the common. These rooms faced north, right near that other building.

2.text: These rooms were 100 cubits long and 50 cubits wide, with a door facing the north.

3.text: They sat opposite the inner court that was 20 cubits wide, and also across from the outer court pavement. You had stacked galleries—three levels high—one in front of the other.

4.text: Out front was a walkway 10 cubits wide, with a little one cubit space in between. All the doors faced north.

5.text: But up top? The upper rooms were smaller 'cause them gallery ledges cut into the space more than they did for the bottom and middle levels.

6.text: Since these rooms had three levels but no support pillars like the ones in the courts, the upper floor had to shrink in from the ground up.

7.text: There was a wall running in front of the rooms, parallel to 'em, facing the outer court—50 cubits long.

8.text: So the outer-facing rooms were 50 cubits long, while the ones facing the temple stretched 100 cubits.

9.text: There was an entrance to the lower rooms on the east side—you'd walk in from the outer court.

10.text: Now there were also rooms built right into the thickness of the outer wall on the east side—same placement as the north ones, opposite the separated courtyard and building.

11.text: These rooms had the same setup—same length and width, same look, same entrances and exits. They mirrored the ones to the north.

12.text: Just like the rooms that faced south, these had a doorway in front of the walkway, lined up with the eastern wall.

13.text: Then he broke it down for me: 'These north and south rooms, across from the sacred courtyard? That's where the priests go to eat the most holy offerings.'

14.text: 'They gon' store the grain offerings, sin offerings, and guilt offerings in there—it's sacred space. When the priests go in, they can't just walk back out into the outer court wearing them holy garments. Nah—they gotta change outta that sacred gear before stepping out to deal with the people.'

15.text: After he finished measuring the inside of the temple, he took me back out through the east gate. Now he was measuring the whole area all the way around.

16.text: East side? 500 rods.

17.text: North side? 500 rods.

18.text: South side? 500 rods.

19.text: Then he wrapped around to the west—yep, 500 rods there too.

20.text: He measured all four sides. And surrounding everything was a big wall—500 cubits by 500 cubits—set up to separate what's holy from what ain't.

1.text: After that, he brought me back to the east-facing gate.

2.text: And boom—here come the glory of the God of Israel, rollin' in from the east. His voice? Sounded like a whole ocean movin'. The earth lit up with His presence.

3.text: It hit me like the same vision I saw when I first came to announce judgment on the city. Same vibe I caught by the River Chebar. I hit the ground—face down.

4.text: God's glory entered the temple straight through that east gate.

5.text: The Spirit scooped me up and dropped me in the inner court. And just like that—the whole temple was flooded with the glory of the Lord.

6.text: Then I heard Him speakin' to me from inside the temple, and the man was still standin' next to me.

7.text: He said, 'Son of man, this right here? This My throne. My footstool. This where I'm settin' up shop, livin' with My people Israel—forever. Ain't gon' be no more disrespectin' My name. No kings, no folks, nobody draggin' My name through the mud with their little side gods and shady worship.'

8.text: 'They had the nerve to build their front doors right next to Mine, only a wall in between. They dirtied My holy name with all the mess they did. That's why I had to come down on 'em.'

9.text: 'But now? They need to toss all that foolishness and them dead kings outta My sight. Then I'll come dwell with them for good.'

10.text: 'Son of man, show the people what this temple look like. Let it hit 'em in the heart. If they feel shame for how they been livin', that's a start.'

11.text: 'If they really bout that repentance life, then show 'em every detail—how it's built, the ins and outs, all the rules, every line of the blueprint. Write it down in front of 'em so they can follow it for real.'

12.text: 'This the main rule: The whole mountaintop around the temple? It's extra holy. Don't get it twisted—this ain't regular ground. This the law of the temple.'

13.text: 'Now let's talk altar. Here go the measurements, using a long cubit (a regular cubit plus a handbreadth): The base is one cubit high and one cubit wide, with a little ledge—one span—around it.'

14.text: 'From the base to the first ledge is two cubits. That ledge? One cubit wide. Then from there to the next ledge is four cubits, and that one's also one cubit wide.'

15.text: 'The main altar top (the hearth) is four cubits tall. It got four horns reachin' up from the corners.'

16.text: 'The hearth itself is a perfect square—twelve cubits by twelve.'

17.text: 'The ledge around it is fourteen cubits long and wide. There's a rim around that—half a cubit high—and the base of the altar is one cubit all the way around. Steps goin' up face the east.'

18.text: Then He told me, 'Son of man, this what the Lord God says: Here go the rules for the altar once it's built and ready to use for burnt offerings and blood rituals.'

19.text: 'First, give a young bull to the Zadokite priests from Levi's tribe—the ones allowed to approach Me. That bull gon' be the sin offering.'

20.text: 'Take some of its blood, put it on the four horns of the altar, the corners of the ledge, and the rim all around it. That's how you cleanse and cover it.'

21.text: 'Then burn the bull at the designated spot outside the temple—but still inside holy grounds.'

22.text: 'Day two? Bring a goat with no blemishes for another sin offering. Cleanse the altar same way you did on day one.'

23.text: 'After that's done, bring in a young bull and a flawless ram.'

24.text: 'Put 'em before Me, throw salt on 'em, and offer them up as burnt offerings. Salt mean covenant—don't forget that.'

25.text: 'For seven straight days, y'all gon' bring a goat daily for a sin offering. Same with a bull and a ram—both spotless.'

26.text: 'Seven days straight they gon' purify that altar, atone for it, and make it holy.'

27.text: 'Then on the eighth day and from then on, the priests can offer burnt offerings and peace offerings for the people on that altar. And I'll receive y'all with open arms,' says the Lord God.

1.text: Then He brought me back to the outer gate of the sanctuary—the one that faces east—but guess what? It was shut tight.

2.text: And the Lord said, 'Leave it shut. Don't open it. Ain't nobody walkin' through it, 'cause the God of Israel already came through there. That gate been touched by glory—it stay closed.'

3.text: Now the prince? He got privilege. Since he's the prince, he can come sit inside the gate and eat bread in front of the Lord. But he gotta come in through the vestibule and leave the same way.

4.text: He brought me through the north gate to the front of the temple. And boom—God's glory was floodin' the place again. I hit the ground, face to the floor.

5.text: Then the Lord said, 'Listen close, son of man. Watch everything. Hear everything. I'm about to break down all the laws and rules for My house. Pay attention to who gets to come in and who gotta stay out.'

6.text: Go speak to these rebellious folks in Israel. Tell 'em: 'God said, enough with all the nasty stuff y'all been doin' in My house!'

7.text: 'Y'all brought in outsiders—uncircumcised in heart and body—folks who don't even respect Me—and let them come into My sanctuary and disrespect it. Gave 'em access to My table like it was nothin'. Y'all broke My covenant behind that foolishness.'

8.text: 'You didn't guard My sacred things. You let other folks handle My temple like it was just a job. Nah.'

9.text: 'From now on, no outsider—nobody with an uncircumcised heart or flesh—can enter My sanctuary. I don't care if they livin' in Israel or not.'

10.text: 'Now about them Levites who dipped out on Me when the people fell off, chasin' after idols—they gon' carry that guilt.'

11.text: 'I'll still let 'em serve in the temple—like security guards and assistants. They can handle sacrifices and help the people, but that's it.'

12.text: 'They stood with the people in their idol worship and helped lead them into sin. So I swore an oath—they gon' be held accountable.'

13.text: 'They not allowed to come close to Me, not as priests. They ain't touchin' My holy things or steppin' into the Most Holy Place. They gon' carry their shame.'

14.text: 'But I'll still let 'em manage temple duties—just not the sacred stuff.'

15.text: 'But the priests from the line of Zadok? They stayed loyal when everybody else fell off. They gon' be the ones that come close to Me. They gon' handle My fat and blood offerings.'

16.text: 'They can enter My sanctuary, step to My table, and carry out My commands.'

17.text: 'When they enter the inner court, they gotta wear linen—no wool, nothing hot or sweaty.'

18.text: 'Linen turbans, linen pants. No sweat-stained gear in My presence.'

19.text: 'When they step back out to the people in the outer court, they gotta change outta them holy clothes—leave them in the sacred rooms—and put on regular clothes. Ain't nobody supposed to catch a blessing just by brushing up against their ministry clothes.'

20.text: 'They can't shave their heads bald, but they can't let it grow wild either. Keep it neat, trimmed up.'

21.text: 'No wine when they come into the inner court. Stay sober before Me.'

22.text: 'They can't marry just anybody. No divorced women, no random widows. Only virgins from Israel or widows of other priests.'

23.text: 'They gon' teach My people what's holy and what ain't. Show 'em what's clean and unclean.'

24.text: 'When there's drama, they gon' be the ones to judge it—by My standards, not their own. They gon' hold it down on the Sabbaths and all My feast days too.'

25.text: 'They can't go near dead bodies and risk defilement—unless it's immediate family: mom, dad, child, brother, or an unmarried sister.'

26.text: 'Even then, after they touch death, they gotta wait seven days to get clean again.'

27.text: 'And when they come back to serve in the sanctuary? They gotta bring a sin offering. That's protocol,' says the Lord God.

28.text: 'Now let's talk inheritance. They ain't gettin' land like the rest of Israel. Why? 'Cause I'm their inheritance. I'm their portion.'

29.text: 'They get to eat the grain offerings, sin offerings, and guilt offerings. All the stuff dedicated to Me? It belongs to them.'

30.text: 'They get the best of all firstfruits and every kind of offering. You even gotta give 'em the first scoop of your flour to bless your house.'

31.text: 'But they ain't touchin' nothin' that died on its own or got ripped up by wild animals. That's off-limits.'

1.text: Now when y'all split the land for inheritance, set aside a district just for the Lord—a holy spot. It should be 25,000 cubits long and 10,000 wide. That whole area gon' be sacred.

2.text: Inside that space, there's a square for the sanctuary—500 by 500 rods—with 50 cubits of open space around it.

3.text: That whole district gon' be measured out: 25,000 long, 10,000 wide. Right there's where the sanctuary gon' sit—the Most Holy Place.

4.text: That holy section belong to the priests—the ones who serve up close to God. They'll live there, build their homes there, and take care of the sanctuary.

5.text: Then another 25,000 by 10,000 section go to the Levites, who handle temple work. They'll have 20 rooms in their spot.

6.text: Next to the holy district, give the city a section—5,000 cubits wide, 25,000 long. That's for all the people of Israel.

7.text: The prince gon' get land too—one side on the west, the other on the east of the holy district and city. His land stretch all the way across, from the west border to the east.

8.text: That land gon' be his territory. And My princes? They ain't gon' oppress My people no more. Let Israel live in peace, each tribe in their own part.

9.text: 'Enough of the nonsense, O princes of Israel!' says the Lord God. 'Cut out the violence, stop robbin' folks. Do right. Live righteous. And quit stealin' land from My people.'

10.text: 'Use honest scales, honest measurements—no funny business.'

11.text: 'The ephah and the bath should match—each one a tenth of a homer. Don't play games with the math.'

12.text: 'A shekel is 20 gerahs. Your money system? 20, 25, and 15 shekels add up to a mina.'

13.text: 'Here's what y'all owe the Lord: from every homer of wheat and barley, give one-sixth of an ephah.'

14.text: 'For oil, give one-tenth of a bath from every kor (that's ten baths or one homer).'

15.text: 'From every flock of 200 in the best pastures, give one lamb. That's for the grain, burnt, and peace offerings—to cover y'all,' says the Lord God.

16.text: 'Everybody in the land gotta give this offering for the prince.'

17.text: 'And the prince? He's responsible for the burnt offerings, grain offerings, and drink offerings at the feasts, New Moons, Sabbaths, and all Israel's special days. He's the one who brings the sacrifices to make things right with God for the people.'

18.text: 'In the first month, on the first day, get a young bull with no flaws and purify the sanctuary.'

19.text: 'The priest will take some of that bull's blood and smear it on the temple doorposts, the altar corners, and the inner gateposts.'

20.text: 'Do the same thing again on the seventh day of that month—for anybody who sinned without knowin' or slipped up. That's how you cleanse the temple.'

21.text: 'On the fourteenth day of the first month, keep the Passover—seven-day feast, unleavened bread only.'

22.text: 'The prince gon' offer a bull as a sin offering—for himself and for everybody else in the land.'

23.text: 'Then each of the seven days, he gon' bring seven bulls and seven rams—no blemish—for burnt offerings. And each day, a goat too, for sin.'

24.text: 'He also brings a grain offering—one ephah for each bull, one ephah for each ram, and a hin of oil with each ephah.'

25.text: 'Then in the seventh month, on the fifteenth day, for the big feast? Same routine. Seven days straight. Sin offerings, burnt offerings, grain, oil—all of it lined up right.'

1.text: God said, "Alright, listen. That inner courtyard gate that faces east? Keep it locked up six days out the week. But come Sabbath or New Moon? Open that thing up."

2.text: "The prince gon' roll in from the outer entrance and stand by the gatepost. The priests gon' do their thing—burnt offerings, peace offerings. He gon' worship from the threshold, then dip. Gate stays open till sundown."

3.text: "Same for the people—they gon' pull up at that eastern gate and worship too on Sabbaths and New Moons."

4.text: "On the Sabbath, the prince gotta bring six flawless lambs and one perfect ram for the burnt offering."

5.text: "He also gotta bring a grain offering—one ephah for the ram, and as much as he wanna give for the lambs. Plus a splash of oil—one hin per ephah."

6.text: "On New Moon days, he better show up with a flawless young bull, six lambs, and one ram—all without blemish."

7.text: "Same deal—one ephah for the bull, one for the ram, as much grain as he wants for the lambs, and a hin of oil for each ephah."

8.text: "When the prince comes in, he gotta use the vestibule route—and leave the same way he came in."

9.text: "Now when the people come through for the feast days, if you enter from the north gate, you gotta leave out the south gate. And vice versa. Don't leave the same way you came in."

10.text: "And when the folks come in and go out, the prince gon' move with them—same entrance, same exit."

11.text: "At these special feast days, the grain game stays the same: one ephah for a bull, one for a ram, as much as he wants for the lambs, and that hin of oil per ephah."

12.text: "Now if the prince wanna pull up with a voluntary burnt or peace offering? Let him. Open that east gate for him like it's Sabbath. Once he done and walks out, close that gate behind him."

13.text: "Every single morning, bring a flawless one-year-old lamb to the Lord as a burnt offering. No skips."

14.text: "With it, make a grain offering every morning—one-sixth of an ephah, moistened with one-third hin of oil. That's a daily devotion. No excuses."

15.text: "The lamb, the grain, and the oil—all that? Every morning like clockwork. That's how you honor the Lord daily."

16.text: "Now if the prince wanna bless his sons with a piece of his inheritance? That's cool. It's theirs for keeps."

17.text: "But if he gifts land to a servant? That's a lease. It's theirs until the Year of Freedom. Then it goes back to the prince. His sons still keep their part though."

18.text: "And he better not be out here snatchin' other folks' land either. He gotta bless his own kids from his own stash. Ain't no pushing people out they homes."

19.text: Then he took me through this entrance on the side of the gate—led me into the priests' private area that faced north. There was a special spot at the far west end.

20.text: He told me, "This is the spot where priests cook up the guilt offerings and sin offerings. They also bake the grain here. They can't bring that food out to the outer court or else folks gon' get sanctified the wrong way."

21.text: Then he walked me through the outer court. We did a lap around the four corners, and each corner had its own little court.

22.text: Every corner court was forty cubits long, thirty cubits wide—all uniform, same measurements.

23.text: These spots had stone rows lining the edges. And under the stones? Fire pits—ready for cookin'.

24.text: And he said, "These here? These are the temple kitchens. The workers gon' boil and cook the people's sacrifices right here."

1.text: Then he took me back to the temple door—and look, water was flowin' from under the front entrance, headin' east. Since the temple faced east, the water came from under the right side of the temple, south of the altar.

2.text: He took me out through the north gate and brought me around to the east gate—and sure enough, water was pourin' out the right side.

3.text: Then the man stepped out eastward, measuring line in hand. He walked 1,000 cubits and had me walk through the water—it was up to my ankles.

4.text: He measured another 1,000, brought me through again—now it hit my knees. Measured another 1,000—it came up to my waist.

5.text: Another 1,000, and now the water was deep. Too deep to walk across. I'd have to swim—this was a full-blown river now.

6.text: He looked at me and said, 'Son of man, you peep this?' Then he walked me back to the riverbank.

7.text: When I got back, I saw trees—lots of 'em—growing on both sides of the river.

8.text: Then he said, 'This water flows down to the east, into the valley, and eventually into the sea. And when it hits the sea? The water in there gets healed.'

9.text: 'Every living thing that touches that river gon' live. A whole lotta fish gon' be in there too, 'cause them waters get healed. Wherever that river flows, life follows.'

10.text: 'Fishermen gon' set up from En Gedi to En Eglaim—nets stretched out everywhere. Fish gon' be just like the ones in the Mediterranean—plentiful, all kinds.'

11.text: 'But the swampy spots and the marshes? Nah, they won't get healed. They stay salty.'

12.text: 'But along both sides of that river? You gon' see trees that feed you. Leaves never fade. Fruit never stop. Every month, new fruit show up—'cause the water flowin' from the temple fuels 'em. The fruit gon' feed folks, and the leaves? They gon' be medicine.'

13.text: Then the Lord said: 'Here's how y'all gon' divide the land among the twelve tribes. Joseph? He get two portions.'

14.text: 'Y'all gon' get equal shares. I swore to your ancestors I'd give 'em this land—and now it's yours.'

15.text: Here's the north border: Start at the Mediterranean (Great Sea), go by Hethlon, to Zedad,

16.text: Then Hamath, Berothah, Sibraim (between Damascus and Hamath), then down to Hazar Hatticon, near Hauran.

17.text: From the sea to Hazar Enan, by Damascus' border, and into Hamath territory. That's your northern line.

18.text: East side? Run it from Hauran to Damascus, through Gilead, along the Jordan, to the eastern side of the Dead Sea.

19.text: South side? From Tamar to Meribah's waters near Kadesh, along the brook to the Great Sea.

20.text: West side? Straight down the Mediterranean, from the southern border up to the edge near Hamath.

21.text: 'That's the land. Divide it up among the tribes of Israel.'

22.text: 'And don't forget the foreigners who livin' among y'all and raising kids here—they count too. Treat 'em like native-born. They get inheritance just like everybody else.'

23.text: 'Wherever a foreigner settles—give them land in that tribe's portion. That's what I said,' says the Lord God.

1.text: Alright, here go the names of the tribes and how the land gon' be split. From the north border—startin' at that road to Hethlon, near Hamath, all the way to Hazar Enan by Damascus—you got Dan. They get land from east to west.

2.text: Right under Dan? Asher's portion, stretchin' east to west.

3.text: Under Asher? Naphtali, same setup—east to west.

4.text: Next up: Manasseh, east to west.

5.text: Then Ephraim's section, right below Manasseh, east to west.

6.text: Reuben follows, same line—east to west.

7.text: Then Judah gets theirs, from east to west too.

8.text: Now under Judah, we hit that special zone—the holy district. Same width as the others, 25,000 cubits long. This area got the sanctuary dead in the middle.

9.text: This sacred district you set aside for the Lord? It's 25,000 long, 10,000 wide.

10.text: This area go to the priests—the holy ones from Zadok's line. 25,000 cubits north and south, 10,000 east and west. God's sanctuary sit right in the middle.

11.text: These priests stayed true. They ain't fall off when Israel did. They held it down when the Levites didn't. So they get this holy ground.

12.text: Their land gon' be the holiest piece, right next to the Levites' section.

13.text: Levites get their own chunk—same size: 25,000 long, 10,000 wide.

14.text: And listen—they can't sell it, swap it, or give it away. That's the Lord's best, and it stays that way.

15.text: The leftover 5,000 in width next to the 25,000 length? That's city land—homes, open space, community life. City go in the center.

16.text: The city dimensions: 4,500 cubits north, south, east, and west.

17.text: Each side gets a buffer of 250 cubits of green space.

18.text: The rest of the land, 10,000 cubits east and west alongside the holy district, gon' be farmland to feed the city workers.

19.text: And the workers? They come from all the tribes of Israel. It's a community effort.

20.text: So the whole zone—holy district plus city space—is 25,000 by 25,000 cubits. One big square for the Lord and His people.

21.text: Everything else? That's for the prince—on both sides of the holy and city district. East to west, adjacent to the tribes. The sanctuary still at the heart of it all.

22.text: Between Judah and Benjamin's borders, the land belongs to the prince—outside the city and Levites' parts.

23.text: Now the rest of the tribes, from east to west—Benjamin's up first.

24.text: Below him is Simeon's section.

25.text: Then Issachar's.

26.text: Then Zebulun's.

27.text: Then Gad's, stretchin' all the way down.

28.text: Gad's border reaches from Tamar to Meribah by Kadesh, down the brook to the Great Sea. That's the south end.

29.text: This the land y'all gon' divide by lot. These the official pieces each tribe gets, says the Lord God.

30.text: These the city exits. North side? 4,500 cubits long.

31.text: Three gates on the north: one for Reuben, one for Judah, one for Levi.

32.text: East side? 4,500 cubits. Gates for Joseph, Benjamin, and Dan.

33.text: South side? Same length. Gates for Simeon, Issachar, and Zebulun.

34.text: West side? 4,500 cubits. Gates for Gad, Asher, and Naphtali.

35.text: All around, the city perimeter? 18,000 cubits. And from that day forward, the city gon' be called—THE LORD IS THERE.

1.text: So in the very first year Cyrus was king over Persia, the Lord stirred somethin' in his spirit—just like Jeremiah said would happen. Cyrus made a big public announcement across the land and even wrote it down.

2.text: This what King Cyrus of Persia said: 'The Lord God of heaven done gave me all the kingdoms on earth, and He told me to build Him a house in Jerusalem, in Judah.'

3.text: 'So who among y'all belong to His people? If your God with you, go head and roll out to Jerusalem in Judah and rebuild the Lord's house—the God of Israel. That's the real God, and His house in Jerusalem.'

4.text: 'And if y'all ain't goin' but still live around here, help the ones who are. Give 'em silver, gold, goods, animals—whatever. And don't forget the freewill offerings for God's house in Jerusalem.'

5.text: Then the leaders of Judah and Benjamin, plus the priests and Levites—everybody who felt God moving in their heart—got up and said, 'Bet. We gon' go build the Lord's house in Jerusalem.'

6.text: The people around them didn't just stand by—they showed love. Gave 'em silver, gold, goods, livestock, and valuable gifts. And on top of that, some folks just gave because they wanted to.

7.text: King Cyrus even brought out all the stuff that used to be in God's house—the ones Nebuchadnezzar stole from Jerusalem and put up in his false god's temple.

8.text: Cyrus had his treasurer, Mithredath, hand over everything to a dude named Sheshbazzar, who was the prince of Judah.

9.text: Here's what they counted out: thirty gold plates, a thousand silver plates, twenty-nine knives,

10.text: thirty gold bowls, four hundred and ten silver bowls (all kinds), and a thousand other things.

11.text: Altogether, it was 5,400 gold and silver items. Sheshbazzar took all that with him when he and the exiles dipped outta Babylon and headed back to Jerusalem.

1.text: Now look—these the folks from the province who came back home after gettin' snatched up in captivity. Nebuchadnezzar, the king of Babylon, had deported 'em, but they made their way back to Jerusalem and Judah, each one to their own hometown.

2.text: They came up with Zerubbabel—Jeshua, Nehemiah, Seraiah, Reelaiah, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispar, Bigvai, Rehum, and Baanah led the way. Now here go the roll call of the Israelites who returned:

3.text: From the fam of Parosh—2,172.

4.text: From the fam of Shephatiah—372.

5.text: From the fam of Arah—775.

6.text: From the fam of Pahath-Moab (descendants of Jeshua and Joab)—2,812.

7.text: From the fam of Elam—1,254.

8.text: From the fam of Zattu—945.

9.text: From the fam of Zaccai—760.

10.text: From the fam of Bani—642.

11.text: From the fam of Bebai—623.

12.text: From the fam of Azgad—1,222.

13.text: From the fam of Adonikam—666.

14.text: From the fam of Bigvai—2,056.

15.text: From the fam of Adin—454.

16.text: From the fam of Ater, the ones linked to Hezekiah—98.

17.text: From the fam of Bezai—323.

18.text: From the fam of Jorah—112.

19.text: From the fam of Hashum—223.

20.text: From the fam of Gibbar—95.

21.text: From Bethlehem—123.

22.text: From Netophah—56.

23.text: From Anathoth—128.

24.text: From Azmaveth—42.

25.text: From Kirjath Arim, Chephirah, and Beeroth—743.

26.text: From Ramah and Geba—621.

27.text: From Michmas—122.

28.text: From Bethel and Ai—223.

29.text: From Nebo—52.

30.text: From Magbish—156.

31.text: From that other Elam group—1,254.

32.text: From Harim—320.

33.text: From Lod, Hadid, and Ono—725.

34.text: From Jericho—345.

35.text: And from Senaah—3,630 deep.

36.text: Here go the priests: sons of Jedaiah from the line of Jeshua—973.

37.text: Sons of Immer—1,052.

38.text: Sons of Pashhur—1,247.

39.text: Sons of Harim—1,017.

40.text: Now the Levites: sons of Jeshua and Kadmiel, from Hodaviah's folks—74.

41.text: Singers: sons of Asaph—128.

42.text: Gatekeepers: sons of Shallum, Ater, Talmon, Akkub, Hatita, and Shobai—139 in total.

43.text: The Temple workers (a.k.a. Nethinim): sons of Ziha, Hasupha, Tabbaoth,

44.text: Keros, Siaha, Padon,

45.text: Lebanah, Hagabah, Akkub,

46.text: Hagab, Shalmai, Hanan,

47.text: Giddel, Gahar, Reaiah,

48.text: Rezin, Nekoda, Gazzam,

49.text: Uzza, Paseah, Besai,

50.text: Asnah, Meunim, Nephusim,

51.text: Bakbuk, Hakupha, Harhur,

52.text: Bazluth, Mehida, Harsha,

53.text: Barkos, Sisera, Tamah,

54.text: Neziah, and Hatipha.

55.text: Now the folks who served Solomon back in the day: sons of Sotai, Sophereth, Peruda,

56.text: Jaala, Darkon, Giddel,

57.text: Shephatiah, Hattil, Pochereth of Zebaim, and Ami.

58.text: Altogether, the Temple workers and Solomon's servants came out to 392.

59.text: Some folks pulled up from Tel Melah, Tel Harsha, Cherub, Addan, and Immer—but they ain't have no receipts. Couldn't prove who they people were or if they was really Israelites.

60.text: These included the sons of Delaiah, Tobiah, and Nekoda—652 total.

61.text: Even some priestly families had that problem: sons of Habaiah, sons of Koz, and the sons of Barzillai (who married into that Gileadite Barzillai fam and took the name).

62.text: They tried to find themselves in the records, but came up short—so they got cut off from priest duties 'cause they couldn't prove they was legit.

63.text: The governor told 'em they wasn't allowed to eat the sacred priest food until a priest could check in with God using the Urim and Thummim (holy tools for guidance).

64.text: All the people who came back added up to 42,360.

65.text: Not counting their crew—they had 7,337 male and female servants. Oh, and 200 singers—men and women.

66.text: They came through with 736 horses, 245 mules,

68.text: Some of the heads of the family lines, when they got back to the Lord's house in Jerusalem, gave freely to help rebuild it.

69.text: They dropped 61,000 gold coins, 5,000 silver minas, and 100 sets of priest robes into the treasury—whatever they could spare.

70.text: So the priests, Levites, some of the people, singers, gatekeepers, and Temple workers settled in their towns. All of Israel got back to living in their own cities.

1.text: When the seventh month rolled around and everybody was settled in their cities, the people came together like one big family in Jerusalem.

2.text: Then Jeshua, son of Jozadak, and his priest fam, along with Zerubbabel, son of Shealtiel, and his crew, got up and rebuilt the altar of the God of Israel. They had to bring the burnt offerings like Moses laid out in the Law.

3.text: Even though they were nervous 'cause of the folks from the other nations around 'em, they still set the altar back in place and started offering burnt sacrifices—every morning and every evening, just like clockwork.

4.text: They kept the Feast of Tabernacles too, just like the Scriptures said. Brought those daily offerings, exactly how it was supposed to be done each day.

5.text: After that, they kept up with the regular burnt offerings, the ones for the new moons, the special feasts the Lord set aside, and any freewill offerings folks wanted to give. They wasn't missing nothin'.

6.text: From the first day of that seventh month, they started offering burnt sacrifices to the Lord—even though the temple's foundation hadn't even been laid yet.

7.text: They put money in the hands of the masons and carpenters, and gave food, drinks, and oil to the folks in Sidon and Tyre so they could ship cedar logs from Lebanon down to Joppa. They had the green light from King Cyrus of Persia.

8.text: By the second month of the second year after they got back to God's house in Jerusalem, Zerubbabel, Jeshua, the priests, the Levites, and everybody who came outta exile started the work. They picked Levites 20 years and up to run things at the Lord's house.

9.text: Jeshua and his fam, Kadmiel and his fam, plus the sons of Judah and the crew from Henadad's family—all of 'em Levites—stepped up together to lead the rebuild.

10.text: When the builders finally laid the foundation of the Lord's temple, the priests showed up in their robes with trumpets, and the Levites from Asaph's line had cymbals. They praised the Lord just like King David had set up back in the day.

11.text: They sang back and forth to each other, giving God thanks and shouting praise: 'He's good! His mercy don't ever run out when it come to Israel!' Everybody turned up—loud shoutin', full praise—'cause the foundation was finally laid.

12.text: But some of the old heads—the priests, Levites, and elders—who remembered the first temple? They started cryin' loud when they saw this new one's foundation. Still, a lot of folks were shoutin' with joy at the same time.

13.text: It got so wild, you couldn't even tell who was cryin' and who was celebratin'. The sound was so loud, folks could hear it way off in the distance.

1.text: When the enemies of Judah and Benjamin heard that the folks who came back from exile were rebuilding the temple of the Lord God of Israel, they started schemin'.

2.text: They rolled up on Zerubbabel and the family heads and said, 'Let us help y'all build! We worship your God too—we been offering sacrifices to Him ever since King Esarhaddon of Assyria brought us here.'

3.text: But Zerubbabel, Jeshua, and the rest of Israel's leaders were like, 'Nah—we got this. Y'all not helpin' us build the house for our God. King Cyrus of Persia gave us the assignment, so we doin' it ourselves.'

4.text: After that, the locals did everything they could to discourage the people of Judah—had 'em stressed out and shook while tryin' to build.

5.text: They even hired lawyers and advisors to block the project, tryna mess it up from Cyrus' time all the way through King Darius' reign.

6.text: During King Ahasuerus' reign, early on, they wrote up a whole complaint against the people of Judah and Jerusalem.

7.text: Later, during the days of Artaxerxes, Bishlam, Mithredath, Tabel, and their crew wrote to the king. The letter was in Aramaic, and they made sure it got translated properly.

8.text: Rehum the governor and Shimshai the secretary wrote a letter straight up against Jerusalem to King Artaxerxes.

9.text: It came from Rehum, Shimshai, and the rest of their clique—folks from Dinah, Apharsath, Tarpel, Persia, Erech, Babylon, Shushan, Dehav, Elam—basically all the nations that Osnapper had relocated to Samaria and the region beyond the River.

10.text: All them people were part of the mix, brought over by that big-shot Osnapper who had moved a whole bunch of nations into the area.

11.text: Here's a copy of what they wrote: 'To King Artaxerxes—peace and blessings from your loyal folks out here beyond the River.'

12.text: 'Let it be known, King: them Jews you sent back here? They settin' up shop in Jerusalem, that rebellious and wicked city. They buildin' it up again—walls and foundations included.'

13.text: 'You should know—if they finish this city and them walls go up, they won't be payin' no taxes, tributes, or customs. Your pockets gon' feel it, Your Majesty.'

14.text: 'Since we got love for the palace and don't wanna see the king take an L, we figured we better speak up and put you on game.'

15.text: 'Check the history books from your ancestors—you'll see this city been on some rebellious stuff, stirrin' up problems for kings and regions. That's why it got destroyed in the first place.'

16.text: 'So just so you know, if this place gets rebuilt and the walls go up, you ain't gon' have no control left out here beyond the River.'

17.text: King Artaxerxes sent back a response: 'To Rehum the governor, Shimshai the secretary, and all y'all folks livin' out in Samaria and beyond the River—peace.'

18.text: 'That letter y'all sent? I read it loud and clear.'

19.text: 'I had my people dig into the records, and yep—it's true. This city got a whole track record of rebellion, trouble, and starting uprisings against kings.'

20.text: 'Back in the day, strong kings ruled from Jerusalem. They ran the whole region beyond the River, and people used to pay them taxes and tributes.'

21.text: 'So here's the order—shut that whole rebuild down. Don't let 'em lift another brick till I say otherwise.'

22.text: 'Make sure this happens quick. Why let this mess grow and come back to bite the throne?'

23.text: Soon as Rehum, Shimshai, and their folks read the king's letter, they rushed down to Jerusalem and rolled up on the Jews with force. Shut it down, hard.

24.text: So the work on God's house in Jerusalem stopped. It stayed on pause until the second year of King Darius of Persia.

1.text: Then the prophets Haggai and Zechariah (son of Iddo) spoke out to the Jews in Judah and Jerusalem, givin' them a word straight from the God of Israel who was still watchin' over them.

2.text: So Zerubbabel (son of Shealtiel) and Jeshua (son of Jozadak) got up and started buildin' God's house again in Jerusalem. And the prophets? They was right there with 'em, holdin' it down and helpin' out.

3.text: But at that same time, Tattenai—the governor from across the River—showed up with Shethar-Boznai and their crew. They pulled up askin': 'Who told y'all to start buildin' this temple and fixin' up these walls?'

4.text: So we gave 'em the names of the men leadin' the project, lettin' 'em know who was really puttin' in work.

5.text: But God had His eyes on the elders of the Jews, so they didn't get shut down right away. They had to wait for word to go back to King Darius—and for a response to come back.

6.text: Here's a copy of the letter Tattenai sent to King Darius, with Shethar-Boznai and all the other Persian officials from the region beyond the River co-signin' it.

7.text: They wrote: 'To King Darius—peace and respect.'

8.text: 'We need to let you know, we went over to Judea and checked out the temple of the great God. They buildin' it strong—usin' big stones and timber for the walls. And they ain't slackin'—the work movin' fast and steady in their hands.'

9.text: 'We asked the elders: "Who gave y'all permission to build this temple and finish the walls?"'

10.text: 'We also asked for the names of the men in charge, so we could write it all down and let you know exactly who's behind this.'

11.text: 'Here's what they told us: "We servants of the God of heaven and earth. We rebuildin' the temple that was here long ago—the one a great king of Israel built and finished."'

12.text: '"But our ancestors made God mad—real mad—so He let Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon (a Chaldean), take us down. He tore the temple up and took the people into captivity."'

13.text: '"But in the first year Cyrus became king over Babylon, he gave the go-ahead to rebuild God's house."'

14.text: '"And the gold and silver stuff from the temple that Nebuchadnezzar had stolen—Cyrus gave that back too. He handed it over to a man named Sheshbazzar, who he put in charge as governor."'

15.text: '"Cyrus told him: 'Take all these items, head back to Jerusalem, and rebuild the temple on its old spot.'"'

16.text: '"So Sheshbazzar came through, laid the foundation, and started the build. They been workin' on it ever since, but it ain't finished yet."'

17.text: 'So if the king cool with it, we ask that you search the archives up in Babylon to see if King Cyrus really gave that order. Then let us know what the king wanna do next.'

1.text: So King Darius put out an order, and they started searchin' through the records stored with the treasures in Babylon.

2.text: They found a scroll in the palace at Achmetha, up in the province of Media, and this what it said:

3.text: 'In the first year of King Cyrus, he gave this decree: The temple of God in Jerusalem gotta be rebuilt—the place where they give sacrifices. Set the foundation strong. It should be 60 cubits high and 60 wide.'

4.text: 'Use three layers of big stone blocks and one layer of fresh timber. And don't worry about the money—it's comin' from the king's own funds.'

5.text: 'Also, bring back the gold and silver items Nebuchadnezzar stole from the temple in Jerusalem. Take 'em back to their rightful spots in the house of God.'

6.text: So now, Tattenai, governor across the River, Shethar-Boznai, and y'all crew—fall back. Don't mess with 'em.

7.text: Let the governor of the Jews and the elders handle they business. Let 'em build God's house right there where it belongs.

8.text: I'm also makin' a new decree: Help these elders out! Fund it with tax money from your region across the River. No delays, pay up!

9.text: Whatever they need—young bulls, rams, lambs for sacrifices, wheat, salt, wine, oil—whatever the priests ask for, give it to 'em every day, no excuses.

10.text: So they can keep the sacrifices goin' and pray for me and my sons too. I need that blessing.

11.text: And let me be clear—if anybody tries to change this order, snatch wood from their house, stand it up, and hang 'em on it. Then turn their whole crib into a pile of trash.

12.text: May the same God who lives in that temple tear down any king or nation that tries to stop or destroy this house. I, Darius, said it. Don't play—get it done.

13.text: So Tattenai, Shethar-Boznai, and their folks followed every word King Darius said. They ain't drag they feet.

14.text: The Jewish elders kept on buildin', encouraged by the words of Haggai and Zechariah. They finished the temple just like God told 'em to—plus the commands from Cyrus, Darius, and Artaxerxes.

15.text: They wrapped it up on the third day of the month Adar, in year six of King Darius' rule.

16.text: Everybody who came back from exile—the Israelites, the priests, the Levites—celebrated the temple's dedication with pure joy.

17.text: They offered a hundred bulls, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs, and twelve male goats for sin offerings—one goat for each tribe of Israel.

18.text: They got the priests and Levites back into their proper roles to serve in God's house, just like Moses laid out.

19.text: The returnees kept the Passover on the 14th day of the first month.

20.text: The priests and Levites had purified themselves—all of 'em was clean. They sacrificed the Passover lambs for the whole crew, the priests, and themselves.

21.text: The Israelites who came back from exile ate together with everybody who had turned away from the nastiness of the surrounding nations and came to seek the Lord, the God of Israel.

22.text: Then they kept the Feast of Unleavened Bread for seven whole days—full of joy. The Lord made 'em glad and even moved the heart of the king of Assyria to support the work they was doin' for the house of God, the God of Israel.

1.text: After all that, during the reign of King Artaxerxes of Persia, a man named Ezra showed up—son of Seraiah, grandson of Azariah, great-grandson of Hilkiah,

2.text: descendant of Shallum, Zadok, and Ahitub,

3.text: from the line of Amariah, Azariah, and Meraioth,

4.text: then Zerahiah, Uzzi, Bukki,

5.text: son of Abishua, son of Phinehas, son of Eleazar, son of Aaron—the high priest himself.

6.text: Ezra came from Babylon, and he was cold with it—knew the Law of Moses front to back, the Law God gave to Israel. The king gave Ezra whatever he asked for, 'cause God had His hand all over him.

7.text: Some Israelites, along with priests, Levites, singers, gatekeepers, and temple workers came with Ezra in the seventh year of King Artaxerxes' reign.

8.text: Ezra got to Jerusalem in the fifth month of that same seventh year.

9.text: He left Babylon on the first day of the first month, and showed up in Jerusalem by the first day of the fifth—'cause God's hand was still on him.

10.text: Ezra came prepared. His heart was locked in to learn God's Law, live it out, and teach it to the people—statutes and all.

11.text: This right here is a copy of the letter King Artaxerxes gave to Ezra, the priest and Law scholar—an expert in the commandments of the Lord and His rules for Israel:

12.text: 'Artaxerxes, king of kings, to Ezra the priest and Law scribe of the God of heaven—peace and blessings.'

13.text: 'I'm making it official: any of the Israelites, priests, or Levites who wanna roll with you back to Jerusalem—let 'em go.'

14.text: 'You goin' out on royal business—you and my seven advisors. Y'all check up on Judah and Jerusalem, according to the Law of your God that you carry.'

15.text: 'And you gon' take the silver and gold we're givin' freely to the God of Israel, whose house is in Jerusalem.'

16.text: 'Plus, whatever silver and gold you gather up in Babylon—along with the freewill offerings from the people and priests—bring that too. It's all for God's house.'

17.text: 'Use that money wisely—buy bulls, rams, and lambs with their grain and drink offerings, and present 'em on God's altar in Jerusalem.'

18.text: 'And whatever else you and your crew feel led to do with the leftover money—do it according to your God's will.'

19.text: 'Also, all the sacred articles for temple use—make sure they get delivered to God's house in full.'

20.text: 'If you need anything else for the temple, take care of it with funds from the king's treasury.'

21.text: 'I, King Artaxerxes, now declare to all my treasurers beyond the River—whatever Ezra the priest asks for, give it to him, and don't slack.'

22.text: 'Up to 100 talents of silver, 100 kors of wheat, 100 baths of wine and oil, and unlimited salt—no cap.'

23.text: 'Do whatever the God of heaven commands. We not tryin' to catch no wrath from Him—especially not on me or my sons.'

24.text: 'And just so y'all know—no taxes, tribute, or customs can be charged on any priest, Levite, singer, gatekeeper, temple servant, or temple worker. Don't even try it.'

25.text: 'Ezra, based on the wisdom your God gave you, appoint judges and leaders for all the people beyond the River—everybody who knows the Law. And for those who don't? Teach 'em.'

26.text: 'Whoever refuses to follow God's Law—or the king's—handle that. Give 'em what they got comin': death, exile, property taken, or jail. Handle business quick.'

27.text: Bless the Lord, God of our ancestors! He put it on the king's heart to upgrade God's house in Jerusalem.

28.text: God showed me so much favor in front of the king, his advisors, and all the royal bosses—I was encouraged, 'cause the Lord had His hand on me. So I rounded up some top men from Israel to roll with me.

1.text: These the family heads and genealogies of the folks that came up with me from Babylon during the time of King Artaxerxes:

2.text: From Phinehas' line: Gershom. From Ithamar's: Daniel. From David's: Hattush.

3.text: From Shecaniah's people—descendants of Parosh: Zechariah, rollin' deep with 150 men.

4.text: From Pahath-Moab's family: Eliehoenai son of Zerahiah, and 200 men.

5.text: From Shecaniah's line: Ben-Jahaziel and 300 men.

6.text: From Adin's fam: Ebed son of Jonathan, with 50 men.

7.text: From Elam: Jeshaiah son of Athaliah, with 70 men.

8.text: From Shephatiah's crew: Zebadiah son of Michael, with 80 men.

9.text: From Joab's family: Obadiah son of Jehiel, with 218 men.

10.text: From Shelomith's people: Ben-Josiphiah, and 160 men.

11.text: From Bebai's folks: Zechariah son of Bebai, and 28 men.

12.text: From Azgad's family: Johanan son of Hakkatan, and 110 men.

13.text: From Adonikam's last crew: Eliphelet, Jeiel, and Shemaiah—with 60 men.

14.text: From Bigvai's people: Uthai and Zabbud—with 70 men.

15.text: I gathered the squad by the river that flows to Ahava, and we camped there for three days. I looked around and noticed—no Levites showed up.

16.text: So I sent for Eliezer, Ariel, Shemaiah, Elnathan, Jarib, another Elnathan, Nathan, Zechariah, and Meshullam—some leaders—and also Joiarib and Elnathan (again), who had sense.

17.text: I gave 'em instructions to go talk to Iddo, the head man at Casiphia, and tell him and his temple servants to send us folks to help out with God's house.

18.text: Thanks to God's favor, they sent us a wise man—Sherebiah, from the line of Mahli, who was from Levi, son of Israel—along with his sons and brothers, 18 men.

19.text: Then came Hashabiah and Jeshaiah from the sons of Merari, with their kin—20 more men.

20.text: And 220 temple servants (Nethinim), the same ones King David and the leaders had assigned to help the Levites. They was all listed by name.

21.text: Then I called a fast by the river of Ahava, so we could humble ourselves before God and ask Him to guide us, our kids, and all our stuff safely.

22.text: I didn't wanna ask the king for soldiers or bodyguards on the way, 'cause we had already told him, 'God looks out for those who seek Him, but His power and anger hit hard on the ones who don't.'

23.text: So we fasted and prayed—and God came through for us.

24.text: I chose 12 priests to handle the goods—Sherebiah, Hashabiah, and 10 of their brothers.

25.text: I weighed out the silver, gold, and articles for God's house—offerings from the king, his officials, and the Israelites who had showed up.

26.text: I put in their hands: 650 talents of silver, 100 silver items weighin' another 100 talents, and 100 talents of gold.

27.text: Also 20 gold bowls worth a thousand coins, and two polished bronze items that shined like gold.

28.text: I told 'em, 'Y'all and these items are holy to the Lord. This silver and gold is a freewill gift to the God of our ancestors.'

29.text: 'Guard it all real careful until y'all weigh it again in front of the leaders, priests, Levites, and heads of Israel's families when we get to Jerusalem, inside God's house.'

30.text: So the priests and Levites took the goods by weight, ready to deliver it to God's house in Jerusalem.

31.text: We left the river Ahava on the twelfth day of the first month, headin' to Jerusalem. God had His hand on us, and we didn't get jumped by enemies or ambushes along the way.

32.text: We made it to Jerusalem and chilled for three days.

33.text: On day four, everything—silver, gold, and all the items—was weighed at God's house. Meremoth son of Uriah the priest handled it, along with Eleazar son of Phinehas. Jozabad (son of Jeshua) and Noadiah (son of Binnui), both Levites, were with them.

34.text: Everything was counted and weighed properly. It all got recorded that same day.

35.text: The ones who came outta captivity gave burnt offerings to the God of Israel: 12 bulls for the 12 tribes, 96 rams, 77 lambs, and 12 male goats as a sin offering. They offered all of it to the Lord.

36.text: Then we handed over the king's orders to his officials and the local governors across the River. They gave us their support—and backed God's house too.

1.text: After all that got handled, the leaders came to me talkin' 'bout, 'Ezra, the people of Israel—including the priests and Levites—ain't been keepin' they distance from the folks in these other lands. They out here messin' with the same detestable ways of the Canaanites, Hittites, Perizzites, Jebusites, Ammonites, Moabites, Egyptians, and Amorites.'

2.text: 'They even married their daughters and let their sons do the same—so now the holy line, the chosen seed, all mixed up with the other nations. And worst part? It's the leaders and top folks who started this mess.'

3.text: When I heard that, I straight up tore my robe and tunic, yanked out hair from my head and beard, and just sat there—shook.

4.text: Everybody who still feared the words of the God of Israel came and sat with me, 'cause of how wild the exiles had gone. I just sat there stunned until the evening sacrifice.

5.text: When it was time for the evening sacrifice, I got up from my grieving, clothes still torn, dropped to my knees, and stretched out my hands to the Lord my God.

6.text: I said, 'God… I can't even lift my head. I'm ashamed and embarrassed to come to You like this. Our sins? They so deep, they over our heads. Our guilt reachin' all the way to the heavens.'

7.text: 'Since way back—our ancestors' time till now—we been messin' up. That's why we, our kings, and our priests got handed over to other nations. We faced the sword, got taken into exile, got robbed, and straight humiliated—just like today.'

8.text: 'But now, for just a moment, You done showed us grace, Lord. You let a small remnant survive, gave us a little stake in Your holy place, and brought some light back into our eyes. Gave us a lil' life even while we still in chains.'

9.text: 'Yeah, we was slaves, but You ain't forget about us. You touched the hearts of the Persian kings to show us favor—let us rebuild Your house, fix what was broken, and even put up a wall in Judah and Jerusalem.'

10.text: 'But now, God… what can we even say? We've been breakin' Your commandments again.'

11.text: 'The ones You gave through Your prophets sayin': "The land y'all goin' into is messed up—it's spiritually dirty from one end to the other because of the nasty ways of the folks already there."'

12.text: 'You told us: "Don't let your daughters marry their sons or your sons marry their daughters. Don't go seekin' their peace or blessings. That way, you'll stay strong, enjoy the land's goodness, and leave it to your children as an inheritance forever."'

13.text: 'After everything You've let happen to us 'cause of our mess—and even then You went easy on us and still gave us a chance like this—'

14.text: 'Should we really break Your rules again? Go mixin' with the same people doin' the stuff You hate? Wouldn't You be right to wipe us out completely—no remnant, no survivors?'

15.text: 'Lord God of Israel, You always do right. That's why we still here as a small leftover group. But we guilty. And honestly? We can't even stand in front of You like this.'

1.text: While Ezra was down on his knees prayin', cryin', and confessin' in front of God's house, a huge crowd showed up—men, women, and kids from all over Israel. Everybody was cryin' their eyes out.

2.text: Then Shechaniah, son of Jehiel (from Elam's fam), spoke up: 'We messed up, man. We married women from the surrounding nations, and that ain't what God wanted. But even after this, there's still hope for Israel.'

3.text: 'So let's make a deal with God right now. We gon' send away these foreign wives and their kids—do it just like you and all who fear God's commandments are sayin', and let's do it by the Law.'

4.text: 'Ezra, this your lane. Stand up and handle it. We got your back—be strong and go do it.'

5.text: So Ezra stood up and made the leaders—priests, Levites, and all Israel—swear they would follow through. And they all took that oath.

6.text: Ezra left God's house and went to Jehohanan's room (he was Eliashib's son). He didn't eat or drink nothin'—he was in deep grief over how the exiles had turned their backs on God.

7.text: Then they sent out word all across Judah and Jerusalem, tellin' everybody from the exile crew to show up in Jerusalem.

8.text: Anybody who ain't show up in three days? They were gettin' cut off—property taken, and they wouldn't be part of the community anymore.

9.text: So everybody from Judah and Benjamin pulled up in three days. It was the 20th day of the ninth month. They were all sittin' in the open square near God's house, shakin' from the situation—and from the heavy rain.

10.text: Ezra stood up and said, 'Y'all crossed the line. You took foreign wives and added to Israel's guilt.'

11.text: 'So now—own up to it. Confess to the Lord, the God of your ancestors. Do what He says. Separate yourselves from the people of this land—and from those wives.'

12.text: The whole assembly shouted back, 'Yes, sir! You right—we gon' do it just like you said!'

13.text: 'But there's a lotta us, and it's pourin' rain out here. This ain't a one-day fix—too many of us are involved.'

14.text: 'Let our leaders step up for the whole group, and let the guilty men in each town come at scheduled times with their elders and judges, until God's anger calms down.'

15.text: Only Jonathan son of Asahel and Jahaziah son of Tikvah disagreed—and Meshullam and Shabbethai the Levite backed 'em up.

16.text: But the rest of the exiles followed through. Ezra the priest selected family heads, one from each house, listed by name. They started sittin' down to handle it on the first day of the tenth month.

17.text: And by the first day of the first month, they were done talkin' with every man who had married a foreign wife.

18.text: From the priests: From Jeshua (son of Jozadak) and his brothers—Maaseiah, Eliezer, Jarib, and Gedaliah.

19.text: They promised to send their wives away, and offered a ram from the flock for their guilt.

20.text: From Immer's line: Hanani and Zebadiah.

21.text: From Harim's: Maaseiah, Elijah, Shemaiah, Jehiel, and Uzziah.

22.text: From Pashhur's: Elioenai, Maaseiah, Ishmael, Nethanel, Jozabad, and Elasah.

23.text: From the Levites: Jozabad, Shimei, Kelaiah (aka Kelita), Pethahiah, Judah, and Eliezer.

24.text: From the singers: Eliashib. From the gatekeepers: Shallum, Telem, and Uri.

25.text: Parosh's family: Ramiah, Jeziah, Malchiah, Mijamin, Eleazar, Malchijah, and Benaiah.

26.text: Elam's: Mattaniah, Zechariah, Jehiel, Abdi, Jeremoth, and Eliah.

27.text: Zattu's: Elioenai, Eliashib, Mattaniah, Jeremoth, Zabad, and Aziza.

28.text: Bebai's: Jehohanan, Hananiah, Zabbai, and Athlai.

29.text: Bani's: Meshullam, Malluch, Adaiah, Jashub, Sheal, and Ramoth.

30.text: Pahath-Moab's: Adna, Chelal, Benaiah, Maaseiah, Mattaniah, Bezalel, Binnui, and Manasseh.

31.text: Harim's: Eliezer, Ishijah, Malchijah, Shemaiah, Shimeon,

32.text: Benjamin, Malluch, and Shemariah.

33.text: Hashum's: Mattenai, Mattattah, Zabad, Eliphelet, Jeremai, Manasseh, and Shimei.

34.text: Bani's: Maadai, Amram, Uel,

35.text: Benaiah, Bedeiah, Cheluh,

36.text: Vaniah, Meremoth, Eliashib,

37.text: Mattaniah, Mattenai, Jaasai,

38.text: Bani, Binnui, Shimei,

39.text: Shelemiah, Nathan, Adaiah,

40.text: Machnadebai, Shashai, Sharai,

41.text: Azarel, Shelemiah, Shemariah,

42.text: Shallum, Amariah, and Joseph.

43.text: From Nebo's fam: Jeiel, Mattithiah, Zabad, Zebina, Jaddai, Joel, and Benaiah.

44.text: All these men had taken foreign wives—and some of those wives had given them children.

1.text: Aight, so way back at the very start, The Most High set the whole universe in motion—sky up top, land down low.

2.text: But it wasn't put together yet, just a big empty space, dark and deep. Water was everywhere, and The Plug—The Most High's Spirit—was already movin' through it, getting things ready.

3.text: Then The Most High was like, 'Let there be some light up in here.' And boom—light came through.

4.text: He peeped the light and was like, 'Yeah, this solid.' So He split the light from the darkness, keepin' 'em separate.

5.text: He called the light Day and the darkness Night. That was day one.

6.text: Then The Most High was like, 'Aight, let's put some space between all this water.'

7.text: So He set up a sky dome, keepin' the waters up top apart from the waters down low. That's exactly how it went down.
