8.text: And The Most High called the sky dome Up Top. That was day two.

9.text: Then He was like, 'Ayo, let's pull all this water to one spot so the dry land can show up.' And just like that, land appeared.

10.text: He called the dry ground Earth and the big waters Seas. And when He checked it out, He was like, 'Yeah, that's solid.'

11.text: Then He said, 'Let the earth start producing—grass, plants with seeds, trees with fruit that got seeds inside 'em.' And it happened just like that.

12.text: The land started growin' green—plants sprouting up, trees poppin' off fruit, everything workin' just how He planned. And when He saw it, He was like, 'Yeah, that's solid.'

13.text: That was day three.

14.text: Then The Most High was like, 'Aight, let's put some lights up in the sky so folks can tell time—days, seasons, and years.'

15.text: They gon' be lights in the sky to shine on the earth.' And that's what happened.

16.text: The Most High made two big lights—the bigger one to run the day and the smaller one to run the night. He made the stars too.

17.text: He put all these lights up in the sky to shine on the earth,

18.text: to run the day and night, and to separate light from darkness. The Most High looked at it and was like, 'Yeah, that's good.'

19.text: That was day four.

20.text: Then The Most High said, 'Let the water be full of living things, and let birds fly above the earth across the sky.'

21.text: So The Most High made the big sea creatures, all the living things that move and fill the water, and every kind of bird. He looked at it and was like, 'Yeah, that's good.'

22.text: The Most High blessed them and said, 'Have lots of babies and fill up the water in the seas, and let the birds multiply on earth.'

23.text: That was day five.

24.text: Then The Most High said, 'Let the land produce living creatures—livestock, creatures that move low to the ground, and wild animals.' And that's what happened.

25.text: The Most High made all types of wild animals, livestock, and everything that crawls on the ground. He looked at it and was like, 'Yeah, that's good.'

26.text: Then The Most High said, 'Let's make humans in our image, like us. They gon' be in charge of the fish in the sea, the birds in the sky, the livestock, all the wild animals, and everything that crawls on the ground.'

27.text: So The Most High created humans to be like Him. He made them to reflect His image. He created them male and female.

28.text: Then The Most High blessed them and said, 'Have lots of babies and fill up the earth. Take charge of it! Be in charge of the fish in the sea, the birds in the sky, and all the animals that move on the ground.'

29.text: Then The Most High said, 'Look, I'm giving you every seed-bearing plant on earth and every tree that has fruit with seeds in it. They'll be your food.

30.text: And I'm giving all the green plants as food for all the wild animals, all the birds in the sky, and all the creatures that crawl on the ground—everything that has the breath of life in it.' And that's what happened.

31.text: The Most High looked at everything He had made, and He was like, 'Yeah, this real good.' That was day six.

1.text: Aight, so by now, everything was set—the skies, the land, the seas, all done.

2.text: On the seventh day, The Most High wrapped it up. He was done with all the work He had put in.

3.text: So He mad blessed that seventh day, made it special, 'cause that's the day He kicked back after finishing everything.

4.text: Aight, so here's how everything went down when The Most High put earth and sky together.

5.text: Back then, there weren't no bushes, no plants growin' yet 'cause The Most High hadn't sent rain and there wasn't nobody around to work the land.

6.text: But underground streams started bubbling up, keeping the ground fresh.

7.text: Then The Most High got His hands dirty—He formed a man straight out the soil. And then? He breathed life into him, and just like that, the man came alive.

8.text: The Most High set up a garden in a place called Eden, and He put the man there to live.

9.text: He made all kinds of trees grow - beautiful ones, fruit-bearing ones, anything good to eat. But right in the middle? There were two special trees - one gave eternal life, and the other? That one gave knowledge of good and evil.

10.text: A river flowed from Eden, keeping the garden fresh. After that, it split into four streams.

11.text: The first was called Pishon, running through Havilah, where gold was found.

12.text: That land also had some real good perfumes and onyx stones.

13.text: The second was Gihon, wrapping around Cush.

14.text: The third, Tigris, flowed near Assyria, and the fourth was Euphrates.

15.text: The Most High put the man in the garden to take care of it and enjoy the place.

16.text: And He told him straight up, 'Look, you can eat from ANY tree in here—'

17.text: 'EXCEPT one—the tree of knowledge of good and evil. If you touch that one, you gon' die, straight up.'

18.text: Then The Most High was like, 'Aight, this man shouldn't be alone. He need somebody rollin' with him.'

19.text: So He started forming all kinds of animals—wild ones, birds, livestock—and brought 'em to the man to see what he'd name 'em.

20.text: The man named all the creatures, but none of 'em was really a match for him.

21.text: So The Most High put him into a deep sleep. And while he was out, He took one of his ribs and closed him back up.

22.text: Then He took that rib and crafted a woman out of it. And when He brought her to the man—

23.text: The man was like, 'Ayy, this one right here? She just like me—bone of my bone, flesh of my flesh! I'm callin' her Woman 'cause she came from man.'

24.text: That's why a man leaves his parents and joins his wife, and the two become one whole unit.

25.text: Back then, they was both naked—the man and the woman—but they wasn't even trippin' about it.

1.text: Now, the serpent? Oh, he was slick—smooth talker, sharp mind—more cunning than any other creature in the garden. One day, he rolled up on the woman and was like, 'Yo, did The Most High really say y'all can't eat from NONE of these trees?'

2.text: The woman was like, 'Nah, we can eat from the trees in the garden—'

3.text: EXCEPT for one. The Most High said, 'Don't touch that one in the middle, or you gon' die.'

4.text: The serpent scoffed, 'Girl, you ain't gon' die for real.'

5.text: 'The Most High just know that if you eat from that tree, you gon' wake up for real—you gon' see things like Him, knowin' the difference between good and evil.'

6.text: The woman looked at that tree again. The fruit was lookin' real good, and the idea of knowin' things like The Most High? That was tempting. So, she reached out, plucked the fruit, and took a bite. Then she handed some to her man, and he ate too.

7.text: The second they did? Everything changed. Their eyes opened wide, and suddenly, they realized—'Oh snap… we naked!' So, they grabbed some fig leaves, stitched 'em together, and tried to cover up.

8.text: Later that day, they heard The Most High rollin' through the garden in the cool of the evening. They panicked and hid behind some trees.

9.text: The Most High called out, 'Ayy, where y'all at?'

10.text: The man was like, 'I heard You comin', and I got scared 'cause I was naked. So, I hid.'

11.text: The Most High was like, 'Wait… who told you that you was naked? You ain't been eatin' off that tree I told you not to touch, have you?'

12.text: The man tried to shift blame: 'Look, that woman You gave me? She the one who handed me the fruit, so I ate it.'

13.text: The Most High turned to the woman: 'Ayo, what's this you done did?' She was like, 'The serpent! He tricked me, so I ate it.'

14.text: The Most High looked at the serpent and was like, 'Oh, you think you slick? Aight, from now on, you cursed more than ANY creature—You gon' crawl on your belly for the rest of your days. Dust is all you ever gon' eat.'

15.text: 'You and the woman? Y'all beefin' forever. Your offspring and hers always gon' be at war. Her seed? One day, He gon' crush your head, but you gon' strike His heel.'

16.text: Then He turned to the woman: 'Now, childbirth? It's gon' hurt. Raising kids? That's gon' stretch you. And your husband? You gon' want him, but he gon' be the one callin' the shots.'

17.text: Then He looked at the man: 'You listened to your wife instead of Me? Aight, now the ground is cursed 'cause of you. Growin' food? That's gon' be hard work. You gon' sweat for everything you eat. And at the end? You gon' go right back to the dirt I made you from.'

18.text: The ground gon' start actin' up—thorns and weeds gon' pop up everywhere, but you still gotta work it to get your food.

19.text: You gon' have to hustle hard, sweatin' just to eat, 'til the day you go back to the dirt you came from. 'Cause real talk, you was made from dust, and one day, you gon' be dust again.

20.text: The man named his wife Eve, 'cause she would be the mother of all the living.

21.text: The Most High made them some real clothes—animal skins—and covered them up.

22.text: Then The Most High was like, 'Look, they done ate from the knowledge tree. They out here thinkin' they gods now. We can't let 'em touch the Tree of Life too and live forever in this mess.'

23.text: So The Most High kicked them out of Eden and put them outside the garden to work the ground.

24.text: Then He posted some cherubim (heavenly guards) at the entrance, with flaming swords, making sure they never found their way back in.

1.text: Adam and Eve got together, and Eve got pregnant. She gave birth to a son and was like, 'With The Most High’s help, I got me a man-child!' She named him Cain.

2.text: Later, she had another son—Abel. Cain was a farmer, workin’ the land, and Abel was a shepherd, takin’ care of sheep.

3.text: One day, Cain brought an offering to The Most High, some of the crops he had grown.

4.text: But Abel? He brought his best—the finest, fattest of his flock. And The Most High looked on Abel’s offering with favor.

5.text: But Cain’s? He wasn’t feelin’ it. Cain caught an attitude, got heated real quick.

6.text: The Most High was like, 'Ayo Cain, why you mad? Why you got your face twisted up?'

7.text: 'Look, if you do right, won’t you be good? But if you mess up? Sin is crouchin’ at the door, just waitin’ on you—but you gotta rule over it.'

8.text: But Cain wasn’t tryin’ to hear all that. He told Abel, 'Yo, let’s go out to the field.' And when they got there? Cain jumped him and killed him.

9.text: Later, The Most High pulled up and was like, 'Cain, where’s your brother at?' Cain shrugged, 'Man, I dunno. Am I supposed to be watchin’ him?'

10.text: The Most High was like, 'Ayo, what did you do?! Listen! Your brother’s blood is callin’ out to Me from the ground!'

11.text: 'Now you cursed. The very ground that drank your brother’s blood? It ain’t gon’ work for you no more.'

12.text: 'You can plant all you want, but the soil ain’t gon’ produce for you. You gon’ be wanderin’ around, no home, no rest.'

13.text: Cain panicked, 'This punishment too much! I can’t handle it!'

14.text: 'Now I gotta leave, and You gon’ hide Your face from me! Anybody who finds me gon’ try to kill me!'

15.text: The Most High was like, 'Nah, ain’t nobody touchin’ you. Anybody who tries to take you out? They gon’ get hit seven times worse.' Then The Most High put a mark on Cain to make sure nobody messed with him.

16.text: So Cain left The Most High’s presence and ended up livin’ in the land of Nod, east of Eden.

17.text: Cain had a wife, and she gave birth to Enoch. Cain built a city and named it after his son.

18.text: Enoch’s family line: Irad, Mehujael, Methushael, Lamech.

19.text: Lamech had two wives—one named Adah, the other Zillah.

20.text: Adah’s son was Jabal—the first dude to live in tents and raise livestock.

21.text: His brother Jubal? The first musician, playin’ harps and flutes.

22.text: Zillah’s son was Tubal-Cain—he was the first metalworker, makin’ tools and weapons. His sister was Naamah.

23.text: One day, Lamech told his wives: 'Listen up, Adah and Zillah—y’all hear me? I killed a man for tryin’ me, a young dude for messin’ with me.'

24.text: 'If Cain gets avenged seven times, Lamech gon’ get avenged seventy-seven times!'

25.text: Meanwhile, Adam and Eve had another son and named him Seth, ‘cause Eve was like, 'The Most High gave me another son in place of Abel, since Cain took him out.'

26.text: Seth had a son named Enosh. And from that time on, folks started callin’ on The Most High by name.

1.text: Aight, so this the family history of Adam—the first man The Most High made, in His own image.

2.text: He made 'em male and female, blessed 'em, and called 'em human from the jump.

3.text: When Adam was 130 years old, he had a son just like him, in his own image. He named him Seth.

4.text: After Seth was born, Adam lived 800 more years and had more sons and daughters.

5.text: Adam lived a total of 930 years, then he passed on.

6.text: Seth was 105 when he had Enosh.

7.text: After that, he lived 807 years and had more kids.

8.text: Seth's total life? 912 years. Then he was gone.

9.text: Enosh was 90 when he had Kenan.

10.text: Then he lived 815 more years, had more kids.

11.text: Enosh's total? 905 years, then he was gone.

12.text: Kenan was 70 when he had Mahalalel.

13.text: Then he lived 840 more years, had more kids.

14.text: Kenan lived 910 years, then he passed.

15.text: Mahalalel was 65 when he had Jared.

16.text: Then he lived 830 more years, had more kids.

17.text: Mahalalel lived 895 years, then he passed.

18.text: Jared was 162 when he had Enoch.

19.text: Then he lived 800 more years, had more kids.

20.text: Jared's total? 962 years, then he passed.

21.text: Enoch was 65 when he had Methuselah.

22.text: After that, he walked close with The Most High for 300 more years and had more kids.

23.text: Enoch lived a total of 365 years.

24.text: Then one day, The Most High just took him—gone, just like that.

25.text: Methuselah was 187 when he had Lamech.

26.text: Then he lived 782 more years, had more kids.

27.text: Methuselah's total? 969 years—the longest ever—then he passed.

28.text: Lamech was 182 when he had a son.

29.text: He named him Noah and said, 'This boy gon' bring us comfort—help us through this hard work, all the struggle we got 'cause of the curse on the ground.'

30.text: Then he lived 595 more years, had more kids.

31.text: Lamech lived 777 years, then he passed.

32.text: Noah was 500 years old when he had Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

1.text: As time went on, more and more people started spreadin' across the earth, and daughters were born.

2.text: Some heavenly beings, called the sons of The Most High, saw that these women were fine, so they took whoever they wanted as wives.

3.text: But The Most High was like, 'Aight, I ain't gon' let My Spirit keep puttin' up with humans forever. They just straight flesh. I'ma cap their years at 120.'

4.text: During that time, there were some giant warriors known as the Nephilim. These were the offspring of the heavenly sons and human women—some real legends back in the day.

5.text: But The Most High saw that humans were wildin' out—their hearts were full of evil, always thinkin' up some messed-up stuff.

6.text: And it grieved Him deep—He regretted makin' people in the first place.

7.text: So He was like, 'You know what? I'ma wipe 'em all out—humans, animals, everything. This ain't it.'

8.text: But one man stood out—Noah. The Most High looked on him with favor.

9.text: Noah was a real one—righteous, walked tight with The Most High in a world full of wickedness.

10.text: He had three sons: Shem, Ham, and Japheth.

11.text: The whole world was wrecked with violence, and The Most High saw it was corrupt to the core.

12.text: Everywhere He looked, folks was dirty—livin' foul.

13.text: So He told Noah, 'Look, I gotta end this. The world is too wicked, full of violence—I'ma wipe it all out.'

14.text: 'So here's what I want you to do: Build yourself a big ol' boat—an ark. Use gopher wood, and waterproof it inside and out.

15.text: Here's the size: 450 feet long, 75 feet wide, 45 feet high.

16.text: Put a roof on it, leave a 18-inch opening for ventilation, and build three decks—bottom, middle, and top.

17.text: 'I'm bringin' a massive flood to wipe out everything that breathes—everything gon' be gone.

18.text: 'But you? I got a covenant with you. You, your wife, your sons, and their wives gon' get in that ark and be safe.'

19.text: 'And bring a pair of every animal—male and female—onto the ark to keep 'em alive.'

20.text: Birds, land animals, little critters—two of each kind comin' to you.

21.text: 'Oh, and don't forget food—you gotta store up enough for your family and all these animals.'

22.text: And Noah? He did everything exactly like The Most High told him.

1.text: Then The Most High told Noah, 'Aight, it's time. You and your whole family—get inside the ark. You the only one out here livin' right.'

2.text: 'Take seven pairs of every clean animal—male and female. And one pair of every unclean animal.'

3.text: 'Take seven pairs of every bird, too, so they can keep multiplyin' on the earth.'

4.text: 'In seven days, it's gon' start rainin'—forty days and forty nights. I'ma wipe out everything I made.'

5.text: And Noah? He did everything just like The Most High told him.

6.text: He was 600 years old when the flood started.

7.text: So Noah, his wife, his sons, and their wives got inside the ark to stay safe from the flood.

8.text: Animals came two by two—clean ones, unclean ones, birds, all kinds of creatures.

9.text: They entered just like The Most High commanded Noah. Then, the door was sealed shut.

10.text: After seven days, the flood hit the earth.

11.text: It was Noah's 600th year, the 17th day of the 2nd month, when the deep waters burst from underground, and the skies opened up.

12.text: Rain poured down for forty days and forty nights.

13.text: On that very day, Noah and his whole family—his wife, his sons Shem, Ham, Japheth, and their wives—got inside the ark.

14.text: Along with them were every wild animal, livestock, little critters, and every bird.

15.text: They all came to Noah and entered the ark just like The Most High commanded.

16.text: Once everyone was inside, The Most High Himself shut the door.

17.text: For forty days straight, the floodwaters rose up, lifting the ark off the ground.

18.text: The waters kept gettin' higher and higher, but the ark floated above it all.

19.text: Soon, even the tallest mountains were covered.

20.text: The water rose 23 feet above the highest peaks.

21.text: Every living thing on land died—humans, animals, little critters, and birds.

22.text: If it had the breath of life in its lungs, it was gone.

23.text: Everything got wiped out—only Noah and the crew on the ark survived.

24.text: The flood covered the earth for 150 days.

1.text: But The Most High ain't forget about Noah, his family, or all the animals on the ark. He sent a strong wind across the earth, and the floodwaters started goin' down.

2.text: The underground springs stopped flowing, and the rain from the sky cut off.

3.text: Little by little, the water kept goin' down. After 150 days, the flood finally started to dry up.

4.text: On the 17th day of the 7th month, the ark came to rest on the mountains of Ararat.

5.text: The water kept receding, and by the 1st day of the 10th month, the mountaintops started showin' up.

6.text: After 40 more days, Noah opened a window in the ark.

7.text: He sent out a raven to see if the water had dried up. The raven kept flyin' back and forth but didn't settle anywhere.

8.text: Then he sent out a dove to check if there was dry land.

9.text: But the dove couldn't find a place to land, so it came back. Noah reached out, took it back inside the ark.

10.text: Seven days later, he sent out the dove again.

11.text: This time, it came back with a fresh olive leaf in its beak! That's how Noah knew the land was startin' to dry up.

12.text: He waited seven more days, then sent the dove out again—and this time, it ain't come back.

13.text: By Noah's 601st year, on the 1st day of the 1st month, the floodwaters were gone. Noah removed the ark's cover and saw the land was dryin' up.

14.text: By the 27th day of the 2nd month, the earth was completely dry.

15.text: Then The Most High told Noah,

16.text: 'Alright, it's time. You, your wife, your sons, and their wives—step out the ark.'

17.text: 'Bring out all the animals, too—so they can multiply, spread out, and fill the earth again.'

18.text: So Noah and his family walked out of the ark,

19.text: And all the animals, birds, and little critters rolled out too.

20.text: First thing Noah did? He built an altar for The Most High and offered sacrifices from the clean animals and birds.

21.text: The Most High was pleased with Noah's offering and said to Himself, 'I ain't ever gon' curse the ground again because of humans, even though their hearts stay on some foolishness. I ain't ever gon' wipe out everything like that again.'

22.text: 'From now on, as long as the earth remains—planting and harvest, cold and heat, summer and winter, day and night—they all gon' keep goin'.'

1.text: Then The Most High blessed Noah and his sons and told 'em, 'Go on now, be fruitful and multiply. Fill up the whole earth.'

2.text: 'From now on, every animal—beasts, birds, sea creatures—all gon' be shook of you. They in your hands now.'

3.text: 'Everything that moves—animals, fish—y'all can eat 'em now. Just like plants, they food for you.'

4.text: 'But listen, don't eat no meat that still got blood in it—that's where the life is.'

5.text: 'And don't be out here takin' lives—human blood? That's sacred. Anybody who takes a life, I'ma hold 'em accountable.'

6.text: 'Whoever sheds human blood? They blood gon' be shed too. 'Cause humans were made in My image.'

7.text: 'So go on now, be fruitful, multiply, spread out, and live on the earth.'

8.text: Then The Most High told Noah and his sons,

9.text: 'Listen, I'm makin' a covenant—a forever agreement—with y'all and all your descendants.'

10.text: 'This covenant ain't just with you, but with every living thing too—birds, animals, all the creatures that came out this ark.'

11.text: 'And here's My promise: I ain't never gon' destroy the whole earth with a flood again. Never.'

12.text: Then The Most High said, 'I'm leavin' y'all a sign of this covenant—something that'll remind you forever.'

13.text: 'I put My rainbow in the clouds—whenever y'all see it, know that this is My promise to the world.'

14.text: 'Every time rain comes down and that rainbow shows up, just know—'

15.text: 'I remember My covenant. I ain't ever gon' flood the whole world again.'

16.text: 'That rainbow? That's a forever sign.'

17.text: 'Every time you see it, remember what I promised.'

18.text: Noah's sons—Shem, Ham, and Japheth—left the ark and started their families. Ham was the father of Canaan.

19.text: From these three, the whole earth got populated.

20.text: One day, Noah—now a farmer—planted a vineyard.

21.text: He had some of that wine, got too faded, and ended up passed out naked in his tent.

22.text: Ham, Canaan's father, saw his dad laid out naked and ran to go tell his brothers.

23.text: But Shem and Japheth? They grabbed a robe, walked in backwards, and covered their father up—didn't even look at him.

24.text: When Noah woke up and found out what Ham did,

25.text: He said, 'Canaan? You cursed! You gon' be a servant to your brothers.'

26.text: Then he blessed Shem, sayin', 'May The Most High bless Shem, and let Canaan serve him.'

27.text: 'May The Most High expand Japheth's territory, let him dwell in Shem's tents—and let Canaan serve him too.'

28.text: Noah lived 350 more years after the flood.

29.text: He lived a total of 950 years, then he passed on.

1.text: Aight, so here's the family line of Noah's sons—Shem, Ham, and Japheth—after the flood.

2.text: Japheth's sons: Gomer, Magog, Madai, Javan, Tubal, Meshech, and Tiras.

3.text: Gomer's sons: Ashkenaz, Riphath, and Togarmah.

4.text: Javan's sons: Elishah, Tarshish, Kittim, and Dodanim.

5.text: From these came the coastland nations, each with their own land, language, and tribe.

6.text: Ham's sons: Cush, Mizraim (Egypt), Put, and Canaan.

7.text: Cush's sons: Seba, Havilah, Sabtah, Raamah, and Sabteca. Raamah's sons: Sheba and Dedan.

8.text: Cush had a son named Nimrod, who became a mighty warrior on the earth.

9.text: He was a legendary hunter, tight with The Most High, and people used to say, 'Like Nimrod, the mighty hunter before The Most High.'

10.text: His kingdom started with Babel, Erech, Akkad, and Calneh in Shinar (Babylonia).

11.text: From there, he went to Assyria and built Nineveh, Rehoboth-Ir, Calah,

12.text: And Resen, a big city between Nineveh and Calah.

13.text: Mizraim's descendants included the Ludites, Anamites, Lehabites, Naphtuhites,

14.text: Pathrusites, Casluhites, and Caphtorites (who later became the Philistines).

15.text: Canaan's firstborn was Sidon, followed by Heth (the Hittites).

16.text: Then came the Jebusites, Amorites, Girgashites,

17.text: Hivites, Arkites, Sinites,

18.text: Arvadites, Zemarites, and Hamathites. Eventually, the Canaanite clans spread out.

19.text: Their land stretched from Sidon to Gerar (near Gaza) and all the way to Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, and Zeboiim, near Lasha.

20.text: These were Ham's descendants, spread out with their lands, languages, and tribes.

21.text: Shem, the older brother of Japheth, was the father of all the sons of Eber (where the Hebrews come from).

22.text: Shem's sons: Elam, Asshur, Arphaxad, Lud, and Aram.

23.text: Aram's sons: Uz, Hul, Gether, and Mash.

24.text: Arphaxad had Shelah, and Shelah had Eber.

25.text: Eber had two sons—Peleg and Joktan. Peleg got his name because in his time, the earth got divided.

26.text: Joktan's sons: Almodad, Sheleph, Hazarmaveth, Jerah,

27.text: Hadoram, Uzal, Diklah,

28.text: Obal, Abimael, Sheba,

29.text: Ophir, Havilah, and Jobab—all of them were Joktan's descendants.

30.text: They lived from Mesha to Sephar, in the eastern mountains.

31.text: These were Shem's descendants, spread out by their lands, tribes, and languages.

32.text: All these families came from Noah's sons. From them, nations spread across the earth after the flood.

1.text: Back in the day, everybody spoke the same language and used the same words.

2.text: As people moved east, they found a plain in Shinar (Babylonia) and settled there.

3.text: They started talkin': 'Ayy, let's make some bricks and bake 'em hard.' So instead of using stone, they built with bricks and tar.

4.text: Then they was like, 'Aight, let's build us a city with a tower that reach up to the heavens. We gon' make a name for ourselves so we don't get scattered all over.'

5.text: The Most High came down to check out the city and the tower they were buildin'.

6.text: He was like, 'Look at these folks—all speakin' the same language, workin' together. If they doin' this now, ain't no tellin' what else they'll try.'

7.text: 'Let's go down there and mix up their language, so they can't understand each other no more.'

8.text: So The Most High scattered them all over the earth, and they had to stop buildin' the city.

9.text: That's why the place got called Babel, 'cause that's where The Most High confused the languages and spread the people all over the world.

10.text: Aight, so here's Shem's family line: When Shem was 100 years old, he had Arphaxad, two years after the flood.

11.text: After that, Shem lived 500 more years and had more kids.

12.text: Arphaxad was 35 when he had Shelah.

13.text: After that, he lived 403 more years, had more kids.

14.text: Shelah was 30 when he had Eber.

15.text: Then he lived 403 more years, had more kids.

16.text: Eber was 34 when he had Peleg.

17.text: Then he lived 430 more years, had more kids.

18.text: Peleg was 30 when he had Reu.

19.text: Then he lived 209 more years, had more kids.

20.text: Reu was 32 when he had Serug.

21.text: Then he lived 207 more years, had more kids.

22.text: Serug was 30 when he had Nahor.

23.text: Then he lived 200 more years, had more kids.

24.text: Nahor was 29 when he had Terah.

25.text: Then he lived 119 more years, had more kids.

26.text: When Terah was 70, he had Abram (Abraham), Nahor, and Haran.

27.text: Here's Terah's family: Haran was the father of Lot.

28.text: But Haran died early, back in Ur of the Chaldeans, while his father Terah was still alive.

29.text: Abram married Sarai, and Nahor married Milcah (Haran's daughter).

30.text: But Sarai couldn't have kids.

31.text: Terah took Abram, Sarai, and Lot, and they left Ur, headin' for Canaan. But when they got to Haran, they stayed there instead.

32.text: Terah lived 205 years, then he passed away in Haran.

1.text: Then The Most High told Abram, 'Aight, pack up and leave—your country, your family, your father's house. Go to the land I'ma show you.'

2.text: 'I'ma make you into a great nation, bless you, and make your name great—you gon' be a blessing.'

3.text: 'I'ma bless those who bless you, and anybody who come at you sideways? They gon' get cursed. Through you, all the families on earth gon' be blessed.'

4.text: So Abram listened and left, just like The Most High told him. He was 75 years old when he left Haran.

5.text: He took his wife Sarai, his nephew Lot, all their possessions, and the people they had in Haran, and they set out for Canaan.

6.text: They traveled through the land and stopped at Shechem, near the big oak tree at Moreh. Back then, Canaanites still lived there.

7.text: The Most High appeared to Abram and said, 'I'ma give this land to your descendants.' Abram built an altar right there to honor The Most High.

8.text: From there, he moved to the hill country east of Bethel, set up camp, built another altar, and called on The Most High's name.

9.text: Then he kept traveling south toward the Negev desert.

10.text: A famine hit the land, so Abram had to go down to Egypt to ride it out.

11.text: As they got close, he told Sarai, 'Look, you fine as ever—'

12.text: 'When the Egyptians see you, they gon' say, 'That's his wife!' and they gon' kill me just to take you.'

13.text: 'So just say you my sister, so I don't get killed and we both make it through this.'

14.text: When they got to Egypt, the Egyptians saw how fine Sarai was.

15.text: Even Pharaoh's officials noticed and went to tell him. So Pharaoh took Sarai into his palace.

16.text: And since he thought she was just Abram's sister, he hooked Abram up—gave him sheep, cattle, donkeys, servants, and camels.

17.text: But The Most High sent serious plagues on Pharaoh and his household because of Sarai.

18.text: Pharaoh called Abram and was like, 'Yo, what is this?! Why didn't you tell me she was your wife?!'

19.text: 'Why you lie and say she your sister? I almost took her as mine! Bruh, here—take your wife and get out!'

20.text: Then Pharaoh's men escorted them out—Abram, Sarai, and everything they had.

1.text: So Abram left Egypt with his wife, Lot, and everything they had, heading back toward the Negev.

2.text: By this time, Abram was stacked with riches—he had gold, silver, and livestock.

3.text: He traveled back through the land, stopping at the places he had camped before,

4.text: Until he reached Bethel, where he had built an altar to The Most High earlier. And there, he called on The Most High again.

5.text: Lot, who was traveling with Abram, also had flocks, herds, and tents.

6.text: But the land couldn't support both of them living together—it was too crowded with all their possessions.

7.text: Their workers started beefin'—Abram's herdsmen and Lot's herdsmen kept arguing. And on top of that, the Canaanites and Perizzites were still living in the land.

8.text: So Abram told Lot, 'Look, we family—we ain't gotta be out here fightin'.'

9.text: 'The whole land is open. If you go left, I'ma go right. If you go right, I'ma go left. You choose first.'

10.text: Lot looked around and saw the Jordan Valley was lush, well-watered, and lookin' real good—like Eden or Egypt.

11.text: So he chose the whole Jordan Valley for himself and moved eastward. That's how they separated.

12.text: Abram stayed in Canaan, while Lot set up camp near Sodom.

13.text: But Sodom's people? They were wicked—straight up foul—and livin' against The Most High.

14.text: After Lot left, The Most High told Abram, 'Look around—north, south, east, and west.'

15.text: 'Everything you see? I'ma give it to you and your descendants—forever.'

16.text: 'I'ma make your family so big, you won't even be able to count 'em—like the dust of the earth.'

17.text: 'Go on, walk through the land—it's yours.'

18.text: So Abram moved to Hebron and settled near the great oak trees at Mamre. There, he built another altar to The Most High.

1.text: During this time, a war popped off—King Amraphel of Shinar, King Arioch of Ellasar, King Kedorlaomer of Elam, and King Tidal of Goiim

2.text: Went up against the kings of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, Zeboiim, and Bela (Zoar).

3.text: These five kings had all set up camp in the Valley of Siddim (where the Dead Sea is now).

4.text: For 12 years, they had been under King Kedorlaomer's rule, but in the 13th year, they rebelled.

5.text: In the 14th year, Kedorlaomer and his kings rolled up and started takin' over territories—they defeated the Rephaites, Zuzites, and Emites in different lands.

6.text: They even wiped out the Horites in the hill country of Seir and pushed all the way to El Paran near the desert.

7.text: Then they turned back, hit up Kadesh, and wrecked the Amalekites and Amorites.

8.text: That's when the kings of Sodom, Gomorrah, Admah, Zeboiim, and Bela pulled up to fight Kedorlaomer and his squad in the Valley of Siddim.

9.text: But Kedorlaomer and his crew were too strong, and they ran through them.

10.text: When the kings of Sodom and Gomorrah tried to escape, they fell into tar pits, and the rest ran into the hills.

11.text: The enemy kings raided Sodom and Gomorrah, took everything—food, riches, possessions—and bounced.

12.text: They even took Lot, Abram's nephew, and all his stuff since he was living in Sodom.

13.text: A survivor ran and told Abram, who was chillin' by the great trees of Mamre the Amorite. Mamre and his brothers Eshcol and Aner were tight with Abram.

14.text: When Abram heard that Lot got captured, he gathered 318 trained men from his household and went after them all the way to Dan.

15.text: That night, Abram and his men split up, attacked, and took 'em down. They chased them all the way to Hobah, north of Damascus.

16.text: Abram rescued Lot, got back all the stolen goods, and freed the people who were taken.

17.text: After Abram came back from defeating Kedorlaomer and his kings, the King of Sodom came out to meet him in the Valley of Shaveh (King's Valley).

18.text: Then Melchizedek, King of Salem, who was also a priest of The Most High, brought out bread and wine.

19.text: He blessed Abram, saying: 'Blessed be Abram by The Most High, Creator of heaven and earth!'

20.text: 'And praise be to The Most High, who handed your enemies over to you.' Then Abram gave him a tenth of everything he had recovered.

21.text: The King of Sodom told Abram, 'Look, just give me my people back—you can keep all the stuff you recovered.'

22.text: But Abram said, 'Nah, I made a vow to The Most High, Creator of heaven and earth—'

23.text: 'I ain't takin' nothin' from you—not even a thread or a sandal strap—so you can't ever say, 'I made Abram rich.''

24.text: 'The only ones who get a share of this are my allies—Aner, Eshcol, and Mamre. Let them take what's theirs.'

1.text: After all that went down, The Most High spoke to Abram in a vision: 'Don't be scared, Abram. I got you. I'm your shield, and your reward gon' be great.'

2.text: But Abram was like, 'Most High, what's the point? I still don't have a son, and when I die, everything I own gon' go to my servant Eliezer of Damascus.'

3.text: He continued, 'You ain't given me no kids, so a servant in my house gon' be my heir.'

4.text: But The Most High responded, 'Nah, your heir ain't gon' be no servant. You gon' have your own son, from your own body.'

5.text: Then He took Abram outside and said, 'Look up at the sky. Count the stars—if you even can. That's how many descendants you gon' have.'

6.text: And Abram? He believed The Most High, and because of that faith, The Most High counted him as righteous.

7.text: Then The Most High told him, 'I'm the one who brought you out of Ur of the Chaldeans to give you this land.'

8.text: But Abram was like, 'Most High, how I know for sure I'ma get this land?'

9.text: The Most High said, 'Bring me a three-year-old cow, a three-year-old goat, a three-year-old ram, a dove, and a young pigeon.'

10.text: Abram brought all these animals, cut them in half, and laid the halves opposite each other, except the birds.

11.text: Then some vultures tried to swoop down, but Abram chased them away.

12.text: As the sun was setting, Abram fell into a deep sleep, and a terrifying darkness came over him.

13.text: Then The Most High said, 'Know this for sure—your descendants gon' be strangers in a land that ain't theirs. They gon' be enslaved and mistreated for 400 years.'

14.text: 'But I'ma judge the nation that enslaves them, and afterward, they gon' leave with great wealth.'

15.text: 'As for you? You gon' live a long life and die in peace.'

16.text: 'Your descendants gon' come back here in the fourth generation, 'cause the sin of the Amorites ain't hit its peak yet.'

17.text: When the sun went down and it was dark, a smoking firepot and a flaming torch passed between the animal pieces.

18.text: That day, The Most High made a covenant with Abram, sayin', 'I'ma give this land to your descendants—from the river of Egypt to the Euphrates.'

19.text: 'The land of the Kenites, Kenizzites, Kadmonites,'

20.text: 'Hittites, Perizzites, Rephaites,'

21.text: 'Amorites, Canaanites, Girgashites, and Jebusites.'

1.text: Now, Abram's wife Sarai hadn't been able to have kids. But she had an Egyptian servant named Hagar.

2.text: So Sarai told Abram, 'Look, The Most High ain't let me have no kids, so go ahead and sleep with my servant. Maybe I can have a family through her.' Abram listened to Sarai.

3.text: After 10 years in Canaan, Sarai took Hagar and gave her to Abram as his wife.

4.text: Abram slept with Hagar, and she got pregnant. But once she knew she was pregnant, she started actin' different—lookin' down on Sarai.

5.text: Sarai got mad and told Abram, 'This your fault! I gave my servant to you, and now she actin' like she better than me. The Most High gon' judge between us.'

6.text: But Abram was like, 'Look, she your servant—do what you gotta do.' So Sarai treated Hagar so bad that Hagar ran away.

7.text: The angel of The Most High found Hagar by a spring in the desert, on the way to Shur.

8.text: He said, 'Hagar, Sarai's servant, where you comin' from and where you goin'?' She said, 'I'm runnin' away from Sarai.'

9.text: The angel told her, 'Go back and submit to her.'

10.text: Then he said, 'I'ma bless you—I'ma give you so many descendants, they can't even be counted.'

11.text: The angel told her, 'You pregnant, and you gon' have a son. Name him Ishmael, 'cause The Most High heard your cry.'

12.text: 'Your son gon' be wild—fightin' everybody, and everybody fightin' him. But he gon' hold his own.'

13.text: Then Hagar said, 'You really the God who sees me.' She called Him El-Roi (The God Who Sees).

14.text: That's why the well she was at got named Beer-lahai-roi (Well of the Living One Who Sees Me). It's still there between Kadesh and Bered.

15.text: Hagar went back and had Abram's son, and Abram named him Ishmael.

16.text: Abram was 86 years old when Ishmael was born.

1.text: When Abram was 99 years old, The Most High appeared to him and said, 'I'm The Almighty—walk with Me and live right.'

2.text: 'I'ma make a covenant with you and multiply you greatly.'

3.text: Abram fell face down, and The Most High kept talkin':

4.text: 'Look, My covenant is with you—you gon' be the father of many nations.'

5.text: 'Your name ain't Abram no more—it's Abraham, 'cause I made you the father of many nations.'

6.text: 'I'ma make you real fruitful—nations and kings gon' come from your line.'

7.text: 'This covenant is forever—for you and all your descendants.'

8.text: 'I'ma give you and your people this land—Canaan—it's yours forever. And I'ma be y'all's God.'

9.text: Then The Most High told Abraham, 'You gotta keep this covenant—you and all your descendants.'

10.text: 'Every male among you must be circumcised—it's the sign of My covenant.'

11.text: 'Do it on the eighth day after a baby boy is born.'

12.text: 'Every male—born in your house or even servants you bought—must be circumcised.'

13.text: 'This gon' be an everlasting covenant.'

14.text: 'Any man who ain't circumcised? He breakin' My covenant, and he gotta be cut off from the people.'

15.text: Then The Most High told Abraham, 'Your wife Sarai? Her name ain't Sarai no more—it's Sarah.'

16.text: 'I'ma bless her, and she gon' give you a son. Nations and kings gon' come from her.'

17.text: Abraham fell face down and laughed, thinking, 'A hundred-year-old man? A ninety-year-old woman? Having a baby?!'

18.text: Then he said, 'What about Ishmael? Can't he just be the one?'

19.text: But The Most High was like, 'Nah, your wife Sarah gon' give you a son, and you gon' name him Isaac. I'ma establish My covenant with him.'

20.text: 'As for Ishmael? I heard you—I'ma bless him too. He gon' have twelve rulers come from his line, and I'ma make him into a great nation.'

21.text: 'But My covenant? That's with Isaac, the son Sarah gon' have next year.'

22.text: When The Most High finished talkin', He left Abraham.

23.text: That same day, Abraham circumcised himself, his son Ishmael, and every male in his household.

24.text: He was 99 years old when he got circumcised.

25.text: Ishmael was 13 years old when he got circumcised.

26.text: That same day, all the men in Abraham's house got circumcised.

27.text: Every male—whether born in Abraham's house or bought as a servant—was circumcised that day.

1.text: The Most High appeared to Abraham near the great trees of Mamre while he was chillin' outside his tent in the heat of the day.

2.text: He looked up and saw three men standing nearby. As soon as he saw them, he ran up, bowed low,

3.text: And said, 'My Lord, if I got favor with You, don't pass me by.'

4.text: 'Let me get y'all some water to wash your feet. Rest up under this tree.'

5.text: 'Lemme get y'all some food to recharge, then y'all can keep going.' They said, 'Aight, do as you say.'

6.text: Abraham rushed to Sarah and said, 'Hurry up and make some fresh bread!'

7.text: Then he ran to his herd, picked a good calf, and had his servant cook it up.

8.text: He brought them curds, milk, and the cooked meat and stood by while they ate under the tree.

9.text: Then they asked, 'Where's Sarah?' He said, 'She inside the tent.'

10.text: One of them said, 'Aight, next year around this time, Sarah gon' have a son.' Sarah was eavesdropping from inside the tent.

11.text: Now, Abraham and Sarah were old, and Sarah had been past childbearing age.

12.text: So when she heard it, she laughed to herself like, 'Me? A baby? At this age?'

13.text: The Most High said to Abraham, 'Why Sarah laughin'? She think I can't do this?'

14.text: 'Ain't nothin' too hard for The Most High. Next year, she gon' have a son.'

15.text: Sarah tried to play it off, 'I ain't laugh.' But The Most High was like, 'Nah, you laughed.'

16.text: The men got up to leave, lookin' toward Sodom, and Abraham walked with them.

17.text: The Most High said, 'Should I hide what I'm about to do from Abraham?'

18.text: 'He gon' be a great nation, and all nations gon' be blessed through him.'

19.text: 'I chose him to teach his descendants to live right and follow My ways.'

20.text: Then The Most High said, 'Sodom and Gomorrah wildin' out. Their sin is outta control.'

21.text: 'I'ma go down there and see for Myself.'

22.text: The men turned toward Sodom, but Abraham stood there talkin' to The Most High.

23.text: He said, 'Lord, You gon' destroy the righteous with the wicked?'

24.text: 'What if there's 50 righteous folks in the city? You gon' wipe 'em out too?'

25.text: 'That ain't like You! Won't the Judge of the whole earth do right?'

26.text: The Most High said, 'If I find 50 righteous people in Sodom, I'ma spare the whole city.'

27.text: Abraham kept goin', 'What if it's 45?' The Most High said, 'I won't destroy it for 45.'

28.text: 'What about 40?' – 'I won't do it for 40.'

29.text: '30?' – 'Nah, I won't destroy it.'

30.text: 'What about 20?' – 'Still won't do it.'

31.text: 'Okay, Lord, last one—what if there's 10?' – 'For 10, I won't destroy it.'

32.text: Then The Most High left when He finished talking with Abraham.

33.text: And Abraham went back home.

1.text: That evening, two angels pulled up to Sodom, and Lot was chillin' at the city gate. Soon as he saw them, he got up and bowed low.

2.text: Lot said, 'Y'all, come through my house. Wash up, get some rest, then y'all can be on your way in the morning.'

3.text: At first, they was like, 'Nah, we good outside.' But Lot wasn't having that, so they went with him. He cooked a big meal, and they ate.

4.text: Before they could even turn in for the night, the men of Sodom—young and old—rolled up and surrounded Lot's house.

5.text: They shouted, 'Where the men at that came through? Bring 'em out so we can have our way with 'em!'

6.text: Lot ran outside, shut the door behind him,

7.text: And said, 'Please, my brothers, don't do this wicked thing!'

8.text: 'Look, I got two daughters who never been with no man. Y'all can take them instead. Just don't touch these men, they under my protection.'

9.text: They said, 'Man, get outta here! Who you think you are, judging us?' Then they moved in on Lot, ready to break down the door.

10.text: But the angels pulled Lot back inside and slammed the door shut.

11.text: Then they hit the men outside with blindness—young and old—so they couldn't even find the door.

12.text: The angels told Lot, 'You got people here? Sons, daughters, family? Get them outta here.'

13.text: 'The Most High sent us to destroy this place, 'cause the sin is too loud.'

14.text: Lot ran to tell his future sons-in-law, 'Y'all gotta get up and go! The Most High about to shut this city down!' But they thought he was playing.

15.text: At dawn, the angels told Lot, 'Hurry! Take your wife and daughters, or y'all gon' die too!'

16.text: But Lot hesitated, so the angels grabbed him, his wife, and his daughters and dragged them out.

17.text: One angel said, 'Run for your lives! Don't look back! Head to the mountains, or you'll be wiped out!'

18.text: Lot said, 'I can't make it to the mountains—I'll die out there!'

19.text: 'That little town over there—let me go there instead.'

20.text: The angel said, 'Fine, go there. But hurry—I can't destroy the city 'til you safe.'

21.text: Lot made it to Zoar right before the sun came up.

22.text: Then The Most High rained down fire and burning sulfur on Sodom and Gomorrah.

23.text: He wiped out everything—everybody, the land, the plants—everything.

24.text: But Lot's wife looked back—and she turned into a pillar of salt.

25.text: Early in the morning, Abraham went to the place where he had stood before The Most High.

26.text: He looked toward Sodom and Gomorrah and saw thick smoke rising like from a furnace.

27.text: But The Most High remembered Abraham and saved Lot from the destruction.

28.text: Lot was scared to stay in Zoar, so he moved to the mountains with his daughters.

29.text: One day, the older daughter said to the younger, 'Ain't no men left here. How we gon' keep our family line going?'

30.text: 'Let's get our father drunk and sleep with him so we can have kids.'

31.text: That night, they got Lot drunk, and the older daughter slept with him.

32.text: He was so out of it, he didn't even realize what happened.

33.text: The next night, they did the same thing, and the younger daughter slept with him.

34.text: Again, Lot didn't even realize it.

35.text: Both daughters got pregnant by their father.

36.text: The older daughter had a son named Moab—his descendants became the Moabites.

37.text: The younger daughter had a son named Ben-Ammi—his descendants became the Ammonites.

38.text: And that's where the Moabites and Ammonites came from.

1.text: Abraham moved to the Negev and stayed in Gerar.

2.text: He told folks Sarah was his sister (again), so King Abimelech of Gerar took Sarah into his house.

3.text: But The Most High came to Abimelech in a dream and said, 'You as good as dead! That woman you took? She married.'

4.text: Abimelech hadn't touched her yet, so he said, 'Lord, You gon' destroy an innocent nation?'

5.text: 'Ain't he the one who said, 'She my sister'? She even said, 'He my brother.' I did this with a clear heart.'

6.text: The Most High said, 'I know you did this without knowing. That's why I kept you from sinning against Me.'

7.text: 'Now return the woman to her husband—he a prophet, and he gon' pray for you so you live. But if you don't, you and your people gon' die.'

8.text: Early the next morning, Abimelech called his servants and told them what happened. Everybody got shook.

9.text: Then he called Abraham and said, 'Bruh, what have you done?! What I ever do to you that you'd put this kind of sin on me and my kingdom?'

10.text: 'Why'd you lie to me like this?'

11.text: Abraham said, 'I thought y'all didn't fear The Most High, and you'd kill me just to take my wife.'

12.text: 'And technically, she my sister—we got the same father, but different mothers.'

13.text: 'So when The Most High told me to leave my home, I told her, 'Wherever we go, just say you my sister.''

14.text: So Abimelech gave Sarah back to Abraham and blessed him with sheep, cattle, and servants.

15.text: He said, 'My land is open—settle wherever you want.'

16.text: To Sarah, he said, 'I'm givin' your husband silver to show everybody you innocent in this.'

17.text: Abraham prayed for Abimelech, and The Most High healed Abimelech, his wife, and his female servants, so they could have kids again.

18.text: 'Cause The Most High had closed every womb in Abimelech's house because of Sarah.

1.text: The Most High kept His word and did for Sarah exactly what He promised.

2.text: She got pregnant and had a son for Abraham in his old age, right on time, just like The Most High said.

3.text: Abraham named his son Isaac.

4.text: He circumcised Isaac when he was eight days old, just like The Most High commanded.

5.text: Abraham was 100 years old when Isaac was born.

6.text: Sarah said, 'The Most High made me laugh! Everybody who hears about this gon' laugh with me.'

7.text: 'Who would've thought I'd be nursing a baby at my age? And yet, here we are!'

8.text: Isaac grew, and on the day he was weaned, Abraham threw a big feast.

9.text: But Sarah saw Ishmael (Hagar's son) mocking Isaac.

10.text: So she told Abraham, 'Get rid of that woman and her son. He ain't about to share the inheritance with my boy.'

11.text: Abraham was hurt 'cause Ishmael was still his son.

12.text: But The Most High told him, 'Don't be upset. Do what Sarah says—Isaac is the son of the promise.'

13.text: 'But don't worry, I'ma still make Ishmael into a great nation.'

14.text: Early the next morning, Abraham gave Hagar food and water and sent her away. She wandered in the desert of Beersheba.

15.text: When the water was gone, she put Ishmael under a bush

16.text: Walked away, sayin', 'I can't watch my boy die.' Then she broke down crying.

17.text: But The Most High heard Ishmael crying, and an angel called out to Hagar, 'What's wrong? Don't be scared—The Most High got y'all.'

18.text: 'Get up, take your son by the hand—he gon' be a great nation.'

19.text: Then The Most High opened her eyes, and she saw a well of water. She gave Ishmael a drink.

20.text: The boy grew up in the wilderness, became an archer,

21.text: And lived in Paran, where his mama got him a wife from Egypt.

22.text: One day, Abimelech and Phicol (his army commander) told Abraham, 'God is clearly with you in everything.'

23.text: 'Swear to me right now you won't lie to me, my kids, or my descendants. Let's make a deal—we treat each other right.'

24.text: Abraham said, 'I swear.'

25.text: But Abraham brought up a well his men had dug, that Abimelech's men had taken.

26.text: Abimelech said, 'I ain't know nothin' about that 'til now.'

27.text: So Abraham gave Abimelech sheep and cattle, and they made a treaty.

28.text: Abraham also set seven lambs aside.

29.text: Abimelech asked, 'What's with these seven lambs?'

30.text: Abraham said, 'Take these as proof that I dug this well.'

31.text: So they called the place Beersheba (Well of the Oath).

32.text: After the treaty, Abimelech and Phicol left and went back to Philistine territory.

33.text: Abraham planted a tamarisk tree in Beersheba and called on The Most High—El Olam (Everlasting God).

34.text: And he lived in Philistine territory for a long time.

1.text: Some time later, The Most High tested Abraham. He called out, 'Abraham!' And Abraham said, 'I'm here.'

2.text: The Most High said, 'Take your son, your only son Isaac, the one you love, and go to Moriah. Sacrifice him as a burnt offering on a mountain I'll show you.'

3.text: Early the next morning, Abraham got up, saddled his donkey, and took two servants and Isaac with him. He chopped wood for the offering and set out for the place The Most High told him about.

4.text: On the third day, he looked up and saw the place in the distance.

5.text: He told his servants, 'Y'all stay here with the donkey. Me and the boy gon' go worship, then we'll be back.'

6.text: Abraham had Isaac carry the wood while he carried the fire and the knife. As they walked,

7.text: Isaac said, 'Father?' Abraham said, 'I'm here, son.' Isaac asked, 'We got the fire and the wood, but where the lamb for the offering?'

8.text: Abraham said, 'The Most High gon' provide the lamb, my son.' And they kept walking.

9.text: When they got to the place, Abraham built the altar, laid the wood, tied up Isaac, and put him on the altar.

10.text: He reached for the knife to kill his son—

11.text: But the angel of The Most High called out, 'Abraham! Abraham!' He said, 'I'm here!'

12.text: The angel said, 'Don't lay a hand on the boy! Now I know you fear The Most High, 'cause you ain't even hold back your son from Me.'

13.text: Abraham looked up and saw a ram caught in a bush by its horns. He took the ram and sacrificed it instead of his son.

14.text: He called the place Yahweh-Yireh (The Lord Will Provide). That's why folks still say, 'On the mountain of The Most High, it will be provided.'

15.text: The angel of The Most High called to Abraham a second time.

16.text: 'I swear by Myself, 'cause there's no one higher, that because you obeyed Me—'

17.text: 'I'ma bless you real good. Your descendants gon' be like the stars in the sky and the sand on the seashore. They gon' take over their enemies' gates.'

18.text: 'Through your family, all nations on earth gon' be blessed, 'cause you obeyed Me.'

19.text: Then Abraham went back to his servants, and they returned to Beersheba.

20.text: Some time later, Abraham got word that his brother Nahor's wife Milcah had sons.

21.text: Their names: Uz, Buz, Kemuel (who fathered Aram),

22.text: Kesed, Hazo, Pildash, Jidlaph, and Bethuel.

23.text: Bethuel became the father of Rebekah.

24.text: Nahor also had four more sons through his concubine Reumah: Tebah, Gaham, Tahash, and Maakah.

1.text: Sarah lived 127 years and passed away in Hebron, Canaan.

2.text: Abraham mourned and cried for her.

3.text: After mourning, he spoke to the Hittites,

4.text: 'I'm a foreigner here. Let me buy some land so I can bury my wife properly.'

5.text: The Hittites said, 'Sir, you're an important man—bury her in any of our tombs. Nobody gon' stop you.'

6.text: Abraham stood up, bowed, and said,

7.text: 'If y'all really want to help me, talk to Ephron son of Zohar for me.'

8.text: 'Tell him I want to buy the cave of Machpelah at full price, so it's legally mine.'

9.text: Ephron was sitting among the Hittites and heard Abraham. He said,

10.text: 'Sir, listen, I'll give you the land and the cave—free of charge.'

11.text: But Abraham insisted, 'Nah, let me pay full price, so it's officially mine.'

12.text: Ephron said, 'Aight, the land worth 400 silver shekels, but what's that between us? Go ahead and bury your wife.'

13.text: Abraham agreed, weighed out 400 shekels of silver, and bought the land.

14.text: The field, the cave, and the trees on it became Abraham's property in front of witnesses.

15.text: After that, he buried Sarah in the cave of Machpelah, near Hebron.

16.text: The land was now legally his as a permanent burial site.

17.text: The Hittites officially recognized Abraham's purchase of the land.

18.text: Abraham secured a resting place for his family in Canaan.

19.text: Sarah's grave became a sacred site for Abraham's descendants.

20.text: And that's how Abraham secured land in the land The Most High promised him.

1.text: Abraham was gettin' up there in age, and The Most High had blessed him in every way.

2.text: One day, Abraham told his main servant, the one in charge of everything he owned, 'Put your hand under my thigh.'

3.text: 'Swear to me by The Most High, the God of heaven and earth, that you won't let my son marry one of these local Canaanite women.'

4.text: 'Instead, go back to my homeland, to my people, and find a wife for Isaac.'

5.text: The servant asked, 'What if the woman don't wanna come back with me? Should I take Isaac there instead?'

6.text: 'No!' Abraham said. 'Make sure you never take my son back there.'

7.text: 'The Most High, who took me from my father's house and promised me this land, gon' send His angel ahead of you to help you find a wife for my son.'

8.text: 'But if she don't wanna come, you free from this oath. Just don't take my son back there.'

9.text: So the servant put his hand under Abraham's thigh and swore to do as he asked.

10.text: Then the servant packed up ten camels with all kinds of expensive gifts from Abraham and set out for Aram-Naharaim, Nahor's town.

11.text: He stopped outside the town near a well, where the women came to draw water in the evening.

12.text: He prayed, 'Lord, God of my master Abraham, please make this trip successful and show kindness to my master.'

13.text: 'I'm standing here by this well, and the young women of the town are coming out for water.'

14.text: 'Let the one who offers me water AND my camels be the one You chose for Isaac. That's how I'll know You got my master covered.'

15.text: Before he even finished praying, Rebekah showed up, carrying a water jar on her shoulder.

16.text: She was fine as ever, a virgin, and ready for marriage. She went down to the spring, filled her jar, and came back up.

17.text: The servant ran over to her and said, 'Excuse me, miss—can I get a sip of water from your jar?'

18.text: She said, 'Of course! Drink up, my lord.' Then she quickly lowered her jar and gave him water.

19.text: After he drank, she said, 'I'ma get water for your camels too—until they ain't thirsty no more.'

20.text: So she ran back and forth to the well, pulling water for all his camels.

21.text: The servant just stood there in silence, watching to see if The Most High had really made his trip successful.

22.text: After the camels finished drinking, he pulled out a gold nose ring and two big gold bracelets for her wrists.

23.text: Then he asked, 'Who's your daddy? And do y'all got space for me to stay the night?'

24.text: She said, 'I'm Bethuel's daughter—Nahor and Milcah's granddaughter.'

25.text: 'And yeah, we got plenty of room, plus feed for the camels.'

26.text: The servant bowed low and worshiped The Most High.

27.text: 'Thank You, Lord, God of my master Abraham! You been real with him and led me straight to his family.'

28.text: Rebekah ran home and told her family everything.

29.text: Her brother Laban saw the jewelry and ran out to meet the servant at the spring.

30.text: He had heard everything she said and saw the nose ring and bracelets.

31.text: Laban said, 'Come in, my guy! You blessed by The Lord! Why you still out here? We got a place ready for you and your camels.'

32.text: So the servant went inside. Laban unloaded the camels, fed them, and brought water to wash his feet.

33.text: Then they brought out food, but the servant said, 'I can't eat 'til I tell y'all why I'm here.' Laban said, 'Aight, go ahead.'

34.text: He said, 'I'm Abraham's servant.'

35.text: 'The Lord done blessed my master like crazy—he got money, livestock, silver, gold, servants, camels, and donkeys.'

36.text: 'And Sarah, his wife, had a son in her old age—Isaac. And my master gave him everything he got.'

37.text: 'My master made me swear that I wouldn't let Isaac marry a Canaanite woman.'

38.text: 'He told me to come here to his family and find Isaac a wife.'

39.text: 'I asked him, "What if she won't come back with me?"'

40.text: 'And he said, "The Lord will send His angel ahead of you and make your trip successful."'

41.text: 'If she won't come, I'm free from my oath.'

42.text: 'So today, I prayed at the well, asking The Most High to show me the right woman.'

43.text: 'And before I even finished praying, Rebekah showed up!'

44.text: 'She did exactly what I prayed for—offered me water and watered my camels too.'

45.text: 'So I asked her who her family was, and she said she was from Abraham's family.'

46.text: 'That's when I put the ring on her nose and the bracelets on her wrists.'

47.text: 'Then I bowed down and worshiped The Lord, knowing He led me straight to my master's family.'

48.text: Then he said, 'So tell me now—y'all gon' let Rebekah come with me or nah?'

49.text: Laban and Bethuel answered, 'This is from The Most High. We can't argue with that.'

50.text: 'Here's Rebekah—take her. Let her be Isaac's wife, just like The Lord planned.'

51.text: When the servant heard this, he bowed down and worshiped The Lord again.

52.text: Then he brought out silver, gold, and fine clothes and gave them to Rebekah. He also gave gifts to her family.

53.text: They ate and stayed the night.

54.text: The next morning, the servant said, 'Aight, send me back to my master.'

55.text: But her family said, 'Let her stay ten more days.'

56.text: He said, 'Nah, don't delay me—The Lord made my trip successful. Let me go.'

57.text: They called Rebekah and asked, 'You cool with going now?'

58.text: She said, 'Yeah, I'll go.'

59.text: So they blessed Rebekah and sent her off with the servant.

60.text: They prayed, 'May you be the mother of millions! May your descendants conquer their enemies!'

61.text: Rebekah and her servant girls hopped on camels and left with Abraham's servant.

62.text: Meanwhile, Isaac was out in the fields, thinkin' and prayin'.

63.text: He looked up and saw camels coming.

64.text: When Rebekah saw Isaac, she got down from her camel.

65.text: She asked the servant, 'Who's that man?' He said, 'That's my master.'

66.text: So she covered her face with a veil.

67.text: Isaac brought her into his mother Sarah's tent, married her, and loved her deeply. And she brought him comfort after his mother's passing.

1.text: Abraham married another wife, and her name was Keturah.

2.text: She gave birth to Zimran, Jokshan, Medan, Midian, Ishbak, and Shuah.

3.text: Jokshan's sons were Sheba and Dedan. Dedan's descendants were the Asshurites, Letushites, and Leummites.

4.text: Midian's sons were Ephah, Epher, Hanoch, Abida, and Eldaah. These were all Abraham's kids through Keturah.

5.text: Abraham gave everything he owned to Isaac.

6.text: But before he passed, he gave gifts to his other sons and sent them off east, far away from Isaac.

7.text: Abraham lived 175 years.

8.text: He died at a good old age, full of years, and joined his ancestors in death.

9.text: His sons Isaac and Ishmael buried him in the cave of Machpelah, near Mamre, in the field of Ephron son of Zohar the Hittite.

10.text: This was the same field Abraham bought from the Hittites, where he had buried Sarah.

11.text: After Abraham's death, The Most High blessed Isaac, and he settled near Beer-lahai-roi in the Negev.

12.text: This is the family line of Ishmael, Abraham's son through Hagar, Sarah's Egyptian servant.

13.text: Ishmael's sons, listed by name, were Nebaioth (the oldest), Kedar, Adbeel, Mibsam,

14.text: Mishma, Dumah, Massa,

15.text: Hadad, Tema, Jetur, Naphish, and Kedemah.

16.text: These twelve sons became the leaders of twelve tribes, named after them, based on where they settled.

17.text: Ishmael lived 137 years, then died and joined his ancestors.

18.text: His descendants lived from Havilah to Shur, near Egypt, in the direction of Asshur. They stayed beefin' with their relatives.

19.text: This is the story of Isaac, son of Abraham.

20.text: When Isaac was 40 years old, he married Rebekah, daughter of Bethuel the Aramean and sister of Laban the Aramean from Paddan-aram.

21.text: Rebekah couldn't have kids, so Isaac prayed to The Most High, and The Most High answered—Rebekah got pregnant with twins.

22.text: But the twins were fightin' inside her, so she asked, 'Lord, what's goin' on in my womb?'

23.text: The Lord said, 'You got two nations inside you. They gon' be rivals from the jump. One will be stronger than the other, and the older gon' serve the younger.'

24.text: When it was time to give birth, she had twins, just like The Most High said.

25.text: The first baby came out red and covered in thick hair like a fur coat—so they named him Esau.

26.text: His brother came out grabbing Esau's heel, so they named him Jacob. Isaac was 60 years old when the twins were born.

27.text: As they grew up, Esau became a skilled hunter, always outside, while Jacob stayed home and was more quiet.

28.text: Isaac loved Esau 'cause he enjoyed the wild game he brought home, but Rebekah loved Jacob.

29.text: One day, Jacob was cooking some stew, and Esau came home from the fields starving.

30.text: Esau said, 'Man, I'm bout to pass out. Lemme get some of that red stew.' That's how he got the name Edom (which means 'red').

31.text: Jacob said, 'Aight, but sell me your birthright first.'

32.text: Esau said, 'Man, I'm starving! What good is my birthright if I'm dead?'

33.text: Jacob said, 'Swear on it.' So Esau swore and sold his firstborn rights to Jacob.

34.text: Then Jacob gave him bread and lentil stew. Esau ate, drank, and left—he didn't care about his birthright at all.

1.text: Another famine hit the land, just like in Abraham's time. So Isaac moved to Gerar, where King Abimelech of the Philistines ruled.

2.text: The Most High appeared to Isaac and said, 'Don't go to Egypt. Stay here in the land I tell you.'

3.text: 'Live here, and I'ma bless you. I'ma give you and your descendants all this land, just like I promised Abraham.'

4.text: 'Your descendants gon' be as many as the stars, and through them, all the nations of the earth will be blessed.'

5.text: 'I'ma do this 'cause Abraham listened to Me and followed My commands.'

6.text: So Isaac stayed in Gerar.

7.text: The men in town saw Rebekah was fine and asked about her. Isaac lied, sayin' 'She's my sister' 'cause he was scared they'd kill him for her.

8.text: Some time later, King Abimelech looked out his window and saw Isaac all up on Rebekah.

9.text: Abimelech called for Isaac and said, 'Bruh, that's your wife! Why'd you say she's your sister?'

10.text: Isaac said, 'I thought y'all would kill me over her.'

11.text: So Abimelech warned everybody, 'Whoever touches this man or his wife gon' die.'

12.text: Isaac planted crops that year, and The Most High blessed him—he got back a hundred times what he planted.

13.text: He became rich, then richer, then VERY wealthy.

14.text: He had flocks, herds, and servants, but the Philistines started hatin' on him.

15.text: They blocked up all the wells Abraham's servants had dug.

16.text: Abimelech told him, 'You too powerful—leave.'

17.text: So Isaac moved to the valley of Gerar and camped there.

18.text: He re-dug his father's wells that the Philistines had blocked up.

19.text: His servants found fresh water.

20.text: But the Philistine herdsmen argued over it. Isaac named the well Esek (Dispute).

21.text: They dug another well—same drama. He called it Sitnah (Opposition).

22.text: Finally, they dug a third well, and nobody argued. So he named it Rehoboth (Room Enough) and said, 'Now The Most High has made space for us.'

23.text: Isaac moved to Beersheba.

24.text: And The Most High appeared again, saying, 'Don't be scared—I'm with you. I'ma bless you and multiply your descendants 'cause of Abraham.'

25.text: So Isaac built an altar, worshiped The Most High, and dug another well.

26.text: King Abimelech, Phicol (his army commander), and Ahuzzath came to Isaac.

27.text: Isaac asked, 'Why y'all here? You sent me away.'

28.text: They said, 'We know The Most High is with you. Let's make peace.'

29.text: 'Promise you won't harm us, since we didn't harm you.'

30.text: So Isaac made a feast, and they ate & drank together.

31.text: The next morning, they made a treaty and parted peacefully.

32.text: That same day, Isaac's servants said, 'We found water!' He named the well Shibah.

33.text: That's why the city was called Beersheba.

34.text: When Esau was 40, he married two Hittite women.

35.text: And they stressed Isaac & Rebekah OUT.

1.text: Isaac was gettin' old and losin' his eyesight, so he called for Esau, his older son. 'My son,' he said.

2.text: Esau answered, 'Yeah, Father?'

3.text: Isaac said, 'I'm old now, and I don't know when I'ma die.'

4.text: 'Go out, hunt some wild game for me, and cook my favorite meal. Then I'ma eat it and give you the blessing that belongs to my firstborn before I die.'

5.text: But Rebekah overheard what Isaac told Esau. After Esau left,

6.text: She told Jacob, 'Listen, I just heard your father tell Esau—'

7.text: 'Go hunt, cook for me, and I'ma bless you before I die.'

8.text: 'Now listen, son, and do exactly what I say.'

9.text: 'Go get me two young goats from the flock. I'ma cook up your father's favorite meal.'

10.text: 'Then you gon' take it to him so he can eat and bless you instead.'

11.text: Jacob said, 'But Ma, Esau's hairy, and my skin smooth.'

12.text: 'If my father touches me, he gon' know I'm playin' him. Then he gon' curse me instead of bless me!'

13.text: But Rebekah said, 'Let the curse fall on me, baby. Just do what I said.'

14.text: So Jacob went, got the goats, and Rebekah cooked up the meal.

15.text: Then she took Esau's best clothes and gave them to Jacob.

16.text: She covered his arms and his smooth neck with goat skin so he'd feel hairy.

17.text: Then she gave Jacob the meal and some fresh bread.

18.text: Jacob went to his father, 'Hey Pops.' Isaac said, 'Who is it? Esau or Jacob?'

19.text: Jacob lied, 'It's me, Esau, your firstborn. I did what you asked. Sit up and eat, so you can bless me.'

20.text: Isaac asked, 'How you find it so fast, son?'

21.text: Jacob said, 'The Lord put it in my path!'

22.text: Isaac said, 'Come closer so I can touch you and make sure you really Esau.'

23.text: So Jacob went closer, and Isaac touched him and said, 'The voice is Jacob's, but the hands are Esau's.'

24.text: But Isaac was fooled 'cause Jacob's arms felt like Esau's. So he blessed him.

25.text: 'Are you really Esau?' Isaac asked. 'Yes, I am.'

26.text: Isaac said, 'Bring me the food so I can eat and bless you.' So Jacob fed him.

27.text: Then Isaac said, 'Come closer and kiss me, son.'

28.text: When Jacob leaned in, Isaac smelled Esau's clothes and was convinced.

29.text: Then he blessed him, saying, 'The smell of my son is like the smell of the fields blessed by The Lord.'

30.text: 'May The Most High give you rain, good harvests, and plenty of food.'

31.text: 'May people serve you and nations bow to you.'

32.text: 'Be the master over your brothers, and may they bow to you.'

33.text: 'Whoever curses you gon' be cursed, and whoever blesses you gon' be blessed.'

34.text: As soon as Isaac finished blessing Jacob and Jacob had left, Esau came back from his hunt.

35.text: He cooked up a meal and brought it to Isaac. 'Here, Pops, eat so you can bless me!'

36.text: Isaac asked, 'Wait… who are you?'

37.text: Esau said, 'It's me, your firstborn, Esau.'

38.text: Isaac started shaking. 'Then who just brought me food?! I already ate and blessed him. AND THAT BLESSING STANDS.'

39.text: Esau broke down crying. 'Father, bless me too!'

40.text: But Isaac said, 'Your brother tricked me. He took your blessing.'

41.text: Esau said, 'No wonder his name is Jacob! He cheated me twice—first my birthright, now my blessing. Ain't you got nothing left for me?'

42.text: Isaac said, 'I already made him your master. I gave him everything.'

43.text: Esau begged, 'Please, Father, bless me too!' Then he started crying hard.

44.text: Isaac told him, 'You gon' live away from the best lands.'

45.text: 'You gon' live by your sword, serving your brother. But one day, you gon' break free.'

46.text: From that moment on, Esau hated Jacob 'cause of the blessing. He told himself, 'When Pops dies, I'ma kill Jacob.'

1.text: So Isaac called Jacob, blessed him, and said, 'Don't marry none of these Canaanite women.'

2.text: 'Go to Paddan-aram, to your grandfather Bethuel's house, and marry one of your uncle Laban's daughters.'

3.text: 'May The Most High bless you, give you many kids, and make your descendants into many nations.'

4.text: 'May He pass on to you the blessings He gave Abraham—so you can own this land where you're living as a foreigner.'

5.text: Then Isaac sent Jacob away, and he headed for Paddan-aram to stay with Uncle Laban, his mother's brother.

6.text: Meanwhile, Esau realized that Isaac had blessed Jacob and sent him away to find a wife.

7.text: He also knew that Jacob obeyed his parents and went to Paddan-aram.

8.text: Esau could tell Isaac wasn't feelin' these Canaanite women.

9.text: So he tried to fix things—he went to his uncle Ishmael's family and married Mahalath, Ishmael's daughter, in addition to the wives he already had.

10.text: Meanwhile, Jacob left Beersheba and headed toward Haran.

11.text: At sundown, he set up camp for the night. He found a stone to rest his head on and laid down to sleep.

12.text: In his sleep, he had a dream of a staircase reaching up to heaven. Angels were going up and down on it.

13.text: At the top stood The Most High, who said, 'I am The Lord, the God of your grandfather Abraham and your father Isaac.'

14.text: 'I'm giving this land to you and your descendants. They gon' be as many as the dust of the earth.'

15.text: 'I'm with you wherever you go, and I'ma bring you back here. I won't leave you.'

16.text: Jacob woke up shook and said, 'This place is holy—I ain't even realize it.'

17.text: He was shaken and said, 'This is The Most High's house! This the gate of heaven.'

18.text: The next morning, he took the stone he used as a pillow and set it up as a memorial pillar.

19.text: He called the place Bethel (House of God), though it used to be called Luz.

20.text: Then Jacob made a vow: 'If The Most High really gon' be with me, protect me, and provide for me—'

21.text: 'And if He brings me back home safely—then The Most High will be my God.'

22.text: 'And this stone gon' be His house, and I'ma give Him a tenth of everything I get.'

1.text: Jacob kept it moving and finally made it to the land of the east.

2.text: He saw a well in the distance with three flocks of sheep lying nearby. A huge stone covered the well.

3.text: The rule was that all the flocks had to get there first before the stone was moved and the animals got water.

4.text: Jacob walked up to the shepherds and said, 'Yo, where y'all from?'

5.text: They said, 'We from Haran.'

6.text: Jacob asked, 'Y'all know Laban, Nahor's grandson?' They said, 'Yeah, we know him.'

7.text: 'Is he good?' Jacob asked. 'Yeah, he's good. And look, here comes his daughter Rachel with the flock.'

8.text: Jacob said, 'Why don't y'all water the sheep now and let 'em go graze?'

9.text: They said, 'We can't 'til all the flocks get here and the stone gets moved.'

10.text: While they were talkin', Rachel pulled up with her father's sheep, 'cause she was a shepherd.

11.text: When Jacob saw her, he moved the stone himself and watered Laban's flock.

12.text: Then Jacob kissed Rachel and started crying—he told her who he was, her cousin, Rebekah's son.

13.text: Rachel ran home to tell her father, Laban.

14.text: When Laban heard the news, he ran to meet Jacob, hugged him, and brought him home. After Jacob told him everything, Laban said, 'You really my blood for real!'

15.text: After a month, Laban told Jacob, 'You shouldn't work for me for free just 'cause we family. Name your wages.'

16.text: Now Laban had two daughters—the older one, Leah, and the younger one, Rachel.

17.text: Leah's eyes were kinda weak, but Rachel was fine with a nice figure.

18.text: Since Jacob was in love with Rachel, he told Laban, 'I'ma work for you seven years if you let me marry Rachel.'

19.text: Laban said, 'Bet. Better you marry her than someone else.'

20.text: So Jacob worked seven years for Rachel, but his love was so strong it felt like just a few days.

21.text: Finally, Jacob said, 'Aight, I worked my time. Let me marry Rachel.'

22.text: Laban threw a big wedding feast,

23.text: But that night, when it was dark, he sent Leah instead of Rachel! Jacob slept with her without knowing.

24.text: Laban also gave Leah a servant, Zilpah, as her maid.

25.text: In the morning, Jacob realized it was Leah! He snapped at Laban, 'Bruh, what is this?! I worked for Rachel! Why'd you play me?'

26.text: Laban said, 'Man, we don't do the younger one first around here.'

27.text: 'But finish this wedding week, and I'll give you Rachel too—just work another seven years.'

28.text: So Jacob agreed, and a week later, Laban gave him Rachel as a second wife.

29.text: Laban also gave Rachel a servant, Bilhah, as her maid.

30.text: So Jacob slept with Rachel too, but he loved her more than Leah. He worked another seven years for Laban.

31.text: When The Most High saw Leah wasn't loved, He let her have kids, but Rachel couldn't get pregnant.

32.text: Leah had a son and named him Reuben, saying, 'The Lord saw my struggle—now my husband will love me.'

33.text: Then she had another son, Simeon, saying, 'The Lord heard I was unloved, so He gave me another son.'

34.text: Then she had a third son, Levi, saying, 'Maybe now my husband will feel something for me.'

35.text: Then she had a fourth son, Judah, saying, 'Now I'ma praise The Most High!' Then she stopped having kids.

1.text: When Rachel saw that she wasn't having no kids for Jacob, she got jealous of her sister. She begged Jacob, 'Give me kids, or I'ma just die!'

2.text: Jacob got mad and said, 'Look, I ain't God! He the one that kept you from having kids, not me.'

3.text: So Rachel said, 'Take my maid, Bilhah, and sleep with her. She gon' have kids for me, and that way I can have a family too.'
