4.text: Rachel gave her servant, Bilhah, to Jacob as a wife, and he slept with her.

5.text: Bilhah got pregnant and gave birth to a son for Jacob.

6.text: Rachel named him Dan and said, 'God looked out for me! He heard my prayer and gave me a son.'

7.text: Then Bilhah got pregnant again and had another son for Jacob.

8.text: Rachel named him Naphtali and said, 'I been struggling with my sister, but I'm winning now!'

9.text: Meanwhile, Leah saw she wasn't having no more kids, so she gave her maid, Zilpah, to Jacob as a wife.

10.text: Soon, Zilpah had a son for Jacob.

11.text: Leah named him Gad and said, 'Oh, I'm blessed for real now!'

12.text: Then Zilpah had another son.

13.text: Leah named him Asher and said, 'Now I got real joy! The other women gon' be happy for me.'

14.text: One day, during the wheat harvest, Reuben found some mandrakes in a field and brought them to his mama, Leah. Rachel begged Leah, 'Please, let me get some of your son's mandrakes.'

15.text: Leah was mad and said, 'Wasn't it enough that you stole my husband? Now you want my son's mandrakes too?' Rachel said, 'Fine, you can have Jacob tonight if you give me some of the mandrakes.'

16.text: That night, when Jacob was coming in from the fields, Leah ran out to meet him and said, 'You sleeping with me tonight! I done paid for you with my son's mandrakes.' So Jacob slept with Leah.

17.text: God heard Leah's prayers, and she got pregnant again and had a fifth son for Jacob.

18.text: She named him Issachar and said, 'God paid me back for giving my maid to my husband.'

19.text: Then Leah got pregnant again and had a sixth son for Jacob.

20.text: She named him Zebulun and said, 'God blessed me with a good reward. Now my husband finally gon' respect me, 'cause I gave him six sons.'

21.text: Later, Leah had a daughter and named her Dinah.

22.text: Then God finally looked out for Rachel and answered her prayers. He let her have kids.

23.text: She got pregnant and had a son. She said, 'God took away my shame.'

24.text: She named him Joseph and said, 'May the Lord give me another son too!'

25.text: Right after Rachel gave birth to Joseph, Jacob went to Laban and said, 'Let me go home to my country.'

26.text: Let me take my wives and my kids with me, 'cause I earned them by working for you. You know how hard I been grinding for you.

27.text: But Laban said, 'Please, listen to me. I been blessed 'cause the Lord got favor on you.'

28.text: 'Tell me what you want for your wages. Whatever it is, I'll pay it.'

29.text: Jacob said, 'You know how hard I worked for you, and how your flocks and herds grew while I was here.'

30.text: 'Before I got here, you didn't have much. But now? You rich, and the Lord blessed you because of me. But what about me now? When I'ma start providing for my own family?'

31.text: Laban asked again, 'So what you want?' Jacob said, 'Don't give me nothing. Just do this one thing, and I'll keep watching over your flock.'

32.text: 'Let me go through your flock today and pull out all the speckled, spotted, and black sheep and goats. That's all I'll take as my wages.'

33.text: 'So in the future, when you check, you'll know I been honest. If you find anything in my flock that ain't speckled, spotted, or black, you'll know I stole it.'

34.text: Laban said, 'Alright, sounds good. Let's do it.'

35.text: But that same day, Laban went behind Jacob's back and took out all the streaked, spotted, and speckled goats and black sheep. He gave them to his own sons.

36.text: Then he put a three-day journey between his sons' flock and Jacob's flock. Meanwhile, Jacob kept taking care of the rest of Laban's flock.

37.text: Jacob went and grabbed some fresh branches from poplar, almond, and plane trees. Then he peeled strips of bark off them, making white streaks on the wood.

38.text: He took those peeled branches and put them in the watering troughs where the animals drank. That's where they mated.

39.text: And sure enough, when the animals mated near those branches, they had streaked, speckled, and spotted babies.

40.text: Jacob separated his animals from Laban's flock. Whenever his animals were mating, he made sure they didn't mix with Laban's.

41.text: Whenever the stronger females were ready to mate, Jacob put the branches in the water in front of them.

42.text: But when the weaker animals were mating, he didn't use the branches—so the weak ones ended up belonging to Laban and the strong ones were Jacob's.

43.text: Jacob got crazy rich off this. He had a huge flock, plus a bunch of servants, camels, and donkeys.

1.text: Jacob started hearing Laban's sons talkin' mess, sayin', 'Man, Jacob done took all our father's wealth! He rich 'cause of him.'

2.text: Then Jacob noticed Laban wasn't actin' the same toward him no more.

3.text: Then The Most High told Jacob, 'Time to go back home—to your father's land. Don't worry, I'm with you.'

4.text: So Jacob called Rachel and Leah out to the field where he was watching the flock.

5.text: He told them, 'Look, I know your father ain't been treating me the same. But The Most High been with me.'

6.text: 'Y'all know how hard I worked for him.'

7.text: 'But he been playin' me—switchin' my wages ten times. But The Most High ain't let him mess me up.'

8.text: 'If he said, The speckled ones yours, then boom—all the animals came out speckled. If he said, Nah, the striped ones yours, then boom—all of 'em striped.'

9.text: 'Basically, The Most High flipped the script and gave me everything.'

10.text: 'One time, during mating season, I had a dream and saw only the speckled, streaked, and spotted animals mating.'

11.text: 'Then The Most High's angel spoke to me in the dream, Jacob!' I said, 'I'm here.'

12.text: 'The angel said, Look, I see how Laban been doin' you dirty. That's why I made sure the animals that belong to you kept multiplying.'

13.text: 'I'm The Most High, the One who showed up to you back in Bethel, where you made that vow. It's time to bounce—go back to your homeland.'

14.text: Rachel and Leah said, 'That's fine with us.'

15.text: 'We ain't got no inheritance from our father anyway.'

16.text: 'Matter fact, he treated us like strangers and spent all the money you gave him.'

17.text: 'Everything The Most High took from our father belongs to us. So, do whatever God told you.'

18.text: So Jacob packed up everything—his wives, kids, and all his belongings—and started heading back to Canaan.

19.text: While Laban was away shearing sheep, Rachel stole her father's household idols.

20.text: Jacob outplayed Laban by sneaking off without telling him.

21.text: They crossed the Euphrates River and headed toward the hills of Gilead.

22.text: Three days later, Laban found out Jacob was gone.

23.text: He grabbed some relatives and chased Jacob for seven days, finally catching up to him in Gilead.

24.text: But that night, The Most High appeared to Laban in a dream and said, 'Listen up—don't say nothin' good or bad to Jacob.'

25.text: Laban caught up with Jacob's camp and set up near him.

26.text: Laban said, 'Bruh, why you do me like this? Why you drag my daughters off like they prisoners?'

27.text: 'Why you sneak off? You coulda told me! We coulda had a whole send-off party with music and dancing!'

28.text: 'You ain't even let me kiss my daughters and grandkids goodbye. That was messed up.'

29.text: 'I could do you dirty right now, but The Most High showed up last night and told me to back off.'

30.text: 'I get it, you wanted to go home. But why you steal my idols?!'

31.text: 'I left 'cause I was scared you was gon' take your daughters back by force.'

32.text: 'But as for your gods—if you find 'em with anybody here, they die. Search the camp, and if you find anything of yours, take it.' (Jacob ain't know Rachel stole them.)

33.text: Laban searched Jacob's tent, Leah's tent, and the servant wives' tents. Nothing. Then he went to Rachel's tent.

34.text: Rachel had hidden the idols inside her camel's saddle and was sitting on it.

35.text: When Laban searched, she said, 'Sorry, Daddy, I can't stand up—I'm on my period.' So he didn't find anything.

36.text: Jacob got heated and said, 'What crime did I commit for you to chase me like a thief?'

37.text: 'You searched everything I own—find anything that's yours? Show it in front of everybody!'

38.text: 'I been workin' for you for 20 years—your sheep and goats never miscarried.'

39.text: 'If one got killed, I ain't bring you the carcass. I covered the loss myself.'

40.text: 'I worked in the burning sun and freezing cold. I had sleepless nights.'

41.text: 'I worked for you 14 years for your daughters, 6 years for your flock, and you switched my wages 10 times!'

42.text: 'If The Most High wasn't on my side, you woulda sent me away with nothing. But God saw how you been treating me, and that's why He checked you last night.'

43.text: Laban said, 'Everything here—my daughters, my grandkids, my flocks—used to be mine. But what can I do now?'

44.text: 'Let's make a deal. Let's set up a witness between us.'

45.text: Jacob grabbed a big stone and set it up as a marker.

46.text: Then he told his family, 'Y'all bring some stones.' So they stacked them up in a pile and ate a meal there.

47.text: Laban called it Jegar-sahadutha (Aramaic for 'Witness Pile'). Jacob called it Galeed (Hebrew for 'Witness Pile').

48.text: Laban said, 'This pile gon' remind us of our deal.' That's why it was called Galeed.

49.text: It was also called Mizpah (Watchtower), 'cause Laban said, 'May The Most High watch over us when we apart.'

50.text: 'If you mistreat my daughters or take other wives, The Most High will see—even if I don't.'

51.text: 'See this pile of stones? This monument? They stand between us as a witness.'

52.text: 'I won't pass this to harm you, and you don't pass it to harm me.'

53.text: 'I call on the God of Abraham and Nahor to be our judge.'

54.text: So Jacob took an oath, offered a sacrifice, and invited everyone to a covenant meal. They all ate and spent the night there.

55.text: The next morning, Laban kissed his daughters and grandkids, blessed them, then left and went home.

1.text: As Jacob kept moving, The Most High's angels pulled up on him.

2.text: When Jacob saw them, he said, 'Oh yeah, this God's camp for real.' So he named the place Mahanaim.

3.text: Then Jacob sent messengers ahead to Esau, who was living in Seir, in Edom.

4.text: He told them, 'When you see my brother Esau, say this—'

5.text: 'Humble greetings from your servant Jacob. I been staying with Uncle Laban all this time, and now I got cattle, donkeys, sheep, and servants. I'm sending this message to you, hoping you cool with me.'

6.text: The messengers came back and said, 'We saw Esau… and he comin' to meet you—with 400 men.'

7.text: Jacob got shook. He split his people, flocks, and herds into two groups.

8.text: He thought, 'If Esau attacks one group, maybe the other can escape.'

9.text: Then Jacob prayed, 'Lord, God of Abraham and Isaac—you told me to go back home, and You'd be with me.'

10.text: 'I don't deserve the love and faithfulness You've shown me. When I left, I had nothing but a walking stick. Now I got two whole camps!'

11.text: 'Lord, please protect me from Esau. I know he's mad and might try to kill me, my wives, and my kids.'

12.text: 'But You promised me You'd bless me and give me so many descendants they can't even be counted.'

13.text: Jacob stayed the night there and prepared gifts from his possessions for Esau.

14.text: He picked 200 female goats, 20 male goats, 200 ewes, and 20 rams.

15.text: He added 30 camels and their babies, 40 cows, 10 bulls, 20 female donkeys, and 10 male donkeys.

16.text: He split them into herds and assigned each to different servants. 'Go ahead of me with the animals, but keep space between the herds.'

17.text: He told the first servant, 'When Esau asks, "Who sent this?" tell him—'

18.text: 'These belong to your servant Jacob. They're a gift for you, my lord Esau. Jacob is behind us.'

19.text: He gave the same instructions to the second and third servants and all the others with the herds.

20.text: Jacob thought, 'I'ma send these gifts ahead to soften him up. Maybe when I see him, he won't try to kill me.'

21.text: So the gifts went ahead, but Jacob stayed in camp for the night.

22.text: That night, Jacob got up, took his wives, kids, and everything he owned, and crossed the Jabbok River.

23.text: After getting them across, he was left alone.

24.text: Suddenly, a man showed up and started wrestling with him until daybreak.

25.text: When the man saw he couldn't overpower Jacob, he touched Jacob's hip and threw it out of place.

26.text: Then the man said, 'Let me go—it's almost sunrise.'

27.text: But Jacob said, 'I ain't letting go 'til you bless me.'

28.text: The man said, 'What's your name?' Jacob answered, 'Jacob.'

29.text: The man said, 'Not anymore. From now on, your name is Israel, because you fought with God and men—and you won.'

30.text: Then Jacob said, 'Tell me your name.' But the man said, 'Why you need to know my name?' Then he blessed Jacob right there.

31.text: Jacob named the place Peniel (which means 'Face of God'), saying, 'I saw God face to face—and I'm still alive.'

32.text: As Jacob walked away, he was limping 'cause of his hip. That's why, even today, Israelites don't eat the tendon near the hip socket.

1.text: Jacob looked up and saw Esau coming with 400 men.

2.text: He split his family—servants & their kids first, Leah & her kids next, and Rachel & Joseph last.

3.text: Then Jacob walked ahead of them, bowing to the ground seven times as he approached Esau.

4.text: But Esau ran up and hugged him! They both cried.

5.text: Esau looked up and saw Jacob's family. He asked, 'Who all these folks with you?'

6.text: Jacob said, 'These are the children The Most High blessed me with.'

7.text: The wives and children all bowed to Esau.

8.text: Esau asked, 'What's with all the animals you sent ahead?'

9.text: Jacob said, 'A gift for you, my lord.'

10.text: Esau said, 'Bruh, I got enough—keep your stuff.'

11.text: But Jacob insisted, 'Please take them. Seeing your face smiling at me is like seeing The Most High's favor.'

12.text: So Esau accepted the gifts.

13.text: Esau said, 'Come on, let's travel together.'

14.text: Jacob said, 'My people and animals move slow. You go ahead—I'll meet you in Seir.'

15.text: Esau said, 'At least let me leave some of my men with you.'

16.text: Jacob said, 'No need, my lord.' So Esau went back to Seir.

17.text: But Jacob went to Succoth, built himself a house, and made shelters for his livestock.

18.text: Later, Jacob arrived in Shechem (Canaan).

19.text: He bought land there for 100 silver pieces from the sons of Hamor.

20.text: Then he built an altar and named it El-Elohe-Israel (The Most High, God of Israel).

1.text: One day, Dinah, Jacob and Leah's daughter, went out to see the other young women in the area.

2.text: But Shechem, the prince of the land, saw her, snatched her up, and raped her.

3.text: But then he got obsessed with her, started sweet-talking her, and wanted to be with her.

4.text: So he told his father, Hamor, 'Get me this girl—I wanna marry her.'

5.text: When Jacob heard what happened to Dinah, he didn't say anything at first 'cause his sons were still out in the fields.

6.text: Then Hamor came to talk with Jacob about the situation.

7.text: But as soon as Jacob's sons heard about it, they came running in hot. They were furious because Shechem disrespected their sister like that.

8.text: Hamor said, 'My son Shechem really loves your daughter. Please let him marry her.'

9.text: 'Matter fact, let's do a whole trade-off—y'all give us your daughters, and we'll give you ours.'

10.text: 'Y'all can stay here, trade with us, and buy land. Make yourselves at home.'

11.text: Then Shechem said directly to Jacob and his sons, 'Please, I really wanna marry her. Name your price—I'll pay anything.'

12.text: 'Whatever dowry you want, I'll give it—just let me have her.'

13.text: Since Shechem had violated their sister, Jacob's sons came up with a slick plan.

14.text: They said, 'We can't let our sister marry a man who ain't circumcised—that would be a disgrace.'

15.text: 'But here's the deal—if every man in your town gets circumcised like we are, then we good.'

16.text: 'We'll give you our daughters, and we'll take yours. We'll settle here and be one people.'

17.text: 'But if y'all don't get circumcised, we takin' Dinah and we out.'

18.text: Hamor and Shechem agreed immediately.

19.text: Shechem didn't waste any time 'cause he really wanted Dinah. He was also highly respected in his family.

20.text: So he and his father went to the town gates to talk to the men.

21.text: They said, 'Look, these folks cool with us. Let them settle here, trade, and own land.'

22.text: 'But they'll only agree to stay if all our men get circumcised like them.'

23.text: 'If we do this, all their wealth—livestock, property—will eventually be ours. Let's agree to it.'

24.text: So all the men in the town council agreed and got circumcised.

25.text: Three days later, when all the men were still in pain from the circumcision, Simeon and Levi (Dinah's brothers) pulled up with swords and slaughtered every male in town.

26.text: They killed Hamor and Shechem, took Dinah back, and left.

27.text: Then the rest of Jacob's sons came in, saw the bodies, and looted the town since their sister had been violated.

28.text: They took all the livestock—sheep, goats, donkeys—everything.

29.text: They raided the houses, took all the valuables, and even took the women and children as captives.

30.text: Jacob told Simeon and Levi, 'Y'all done messed us up! Now all the Canaanites and Perizzites gon' come for us. We too small to fight them—if they team up, we done for.'

31.text: But they snapped back, 'So we supposed to let them treat our sister like a prostitute?!'

1.text: The Most High told Jacob, 'Go to Bethel and build an altar where I appeared to you.'

2.text: Jacob told his people, 'Y'all gotta get rid of these foreign gods, clean yourselves up, and put on fresh clothes.'

3.text: 'We goin' to Bethel, where The Most High helped me when I was in trouble.'

4.text: They gave Jacob all the idols and earrings they had, and he buried them under an oak tree near Shechem.

5.text: Then they traveled on, and The Most High made the nearby cities too scared to attack them.

6.text: Jacob reached Bethel in Canaan.

7.text: He built an altar and named the place El-Bethel ('God of Bethel').

8.text: Rebekah's nurse, Deborah, passed away and was buried under an oak tree near Bethel.

9.text: The Most High appeared to Jacob again and blessed him.

10.text: 'Your name is Jacob, but now it's Israel.'

11.text: 'I am The Most High Almighty—be fruitful and multiply. A nation and kings gon' come from you.'

12.text: 'The land I gave to Abraham and Isaac? It's yours too.'

13.text: Then The Most High left him.

14.text: Jacob set up a stone pillar where The Most High spoke to him, poured out an offering, and worshiped.

15.text: He named the place Bethel.

16.text: As they left Bethel, Rachel went into hard labor.

17.text: The midwife said, 'Don't worry, you having a son.'

18.text: But Rachel was dying, so she named him Ben-Oni (Son of My Sorrow). But Jacob renamed him Benjamin (Son of My Right Hand).

19.text: Rachel died and was buried near Bethlehem.

20.text: Jacob set up a pillar on her grave.

21.text: Israel (Jacob) moved on and camped past Migdal-Eder.

22.text: But Reuben slept with Bilhah, Rachel's servant—and Jacob found out.

23.text: Jacob had 12 sons:

24.text: Leah's sons: Reuben, Simeon, Levi, Judah, Issachar, Zebulun.

25.text: Rachel's sons: Joseph, Benjamin.

26.text: Bilhah's sons: Dan, Naphtali.

27.text: Zilpah's sons: Gad, Asher.

28.text: Jacob went home to his father Isaac in Hebron.

29.text: Isaac lived 180 years before he passed away.

30.text: His sons, Esau & Jacob, buried him.

1.text: This right here is the family history of Esau (also called Edom).

2.text: Esau married two Canaanite women: Adah, daughter of Elon the Hittite; Oholibamah, daughter of Anah, granddaughter of Zibeon the Hivite.

3.text: And he also married Basemath, his cousin, daughter of Ishmael and sister of Nebaioth.

4.text: Adah had a son named Eliphaz. Basemath had a son named Reuel.

5.text: Oholibamah had three sons: Jeush, Jalam, and Korah. All these sons were born while Esau was still living in Canaan.

6.text: Esau packed up everything—his wives, kids, servants, cattle, and all his wealth—and moved away from Jacob.

7.text: The land couldn't support both of them 'cause they had too much livestock.

8.text: So Esau (Edom) moved to the hill country of Seir.

9.text: This is the family history of Esau's descendants (the Edomites), who lived in Seir.

10.text: Esau's sons: Eliphaz (by Adah), Reuel (by Basemath).

11.text: Eliphaz's sons: Teman, Omar, Zepho, Gatam, and Kenaz.

12.text: Eliphaz also had a son named Amalek (his mother was Timna, his concubine).

13.text: Reuel's sons: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, and Mizzah.

14.text: Oholibamah's sons were Jeush, Jalam, and Korah.

15.text: These are the clan leaders from Esau's sons.

16.text: From Eliphaz's line (Esau's oldest): Teman, Omar, Zepho, Kenaz, Korah, Gatam, Amalek.

17.text: From Reuel's line: Nahath, Zerah, Shammah, Mizzah.

18.text: From Oholibamah's line: Jeush, Jalam, Korah.

19.text: These were the clans that came from Esau (Edom), identified by their leaders.

20.text: These are the names of the tribes that descended from Seir the Horite. They lived in the land of Edom: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah.

21.text: Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan. These were the Horite clan leaders, the descendants of Seir, who lived in the land of Edom.

22.text: The descendants of Lotan were Hori and Hemam. Lotan's sister was named Timna.

23.text: The descendants of Shobal were Alvan, Manahath, Ebal, Shepho, and Onam.

24.text: The descendants of Zibeon were Aiah and Anah. (This is the Anah who discovered the hot springs in the wilderness while he was grazing his father's donkeys.)

25.text: The descendants of Anah were his son, Dishon, and his daughter, Oholibamah.

26.text: The descendants of Dishon were Hemdan, Eshban, Ithran, and Keran.

27.text: The descendants of Ezer were Bilhan, Zaavan, and Akan.

28.text: The descendants of Dishan were Uz and Aran.

29.text: So these were the leaders of the Horite clans: Lotan, Shobal, Zibeon, Anah, Dishon, Ezer, and Dishan.

30.text: The Horite clans are named after their clan leaders, who lived in the land of Seir.

31.text: These are the kings who ruled in the land of Edom before any king ruled over the Israelites.

32.text: Bela son of Beor ruled in Edom from his city of Dinhabah.

33.text: When Bela died, Jobab son of Zerah from Bozrah became king in his place.

34.text: When Jobab died, Husham from the land of the Temanites became king in his place.

35.text: When Husham died, Hadad son of Bedad became king in his place and ruled from the city of Avith. He was the one who defeated the Midianites in the land of Moab.

36.text: When Hadad died, Samlah from the city of Masrekah became king in his place.

37.text: When Samlah died, Shaul from the city of Rehoboth-on-the-River became king in his place.

38.text: When Shaul died, Baal-hanan son of Acbor became king in his place.

39.text: When Baal-hanan son of Acbor died, Hadad became king in his place and ruled from the city of Pau. His wife was Mehetabel, the daughter of Matred and granddaughter of Me-zahab.

40.text: These are the names of the leaders of the clans descended from Esau, who lived in the places named for them: Timna, Alvah, Jetheth,

41.text: Oholibamah, Elah, Pinon, Kenaz, Teman, Mibzar,

42.text: Magdiel, and Iram. These are the leaders of the clans of Edom, listed according to their settlements in the land they occupied.

43.text: They all descended from Esau, the ancestor of the Edomites.

1.text: Jacob settled back in Canaan, the land where his father had lived as a foreigner.

2.text: This is the story of Jacob's family. When Joseph was 17, he worked out in the fields with his half-brothers, the sons of Bilhah and Zilpah. But Joseph was a snitch—he kept telling his dad about the shady stuff his brothers were doing.

3.text: Now, Jacob loved Joseph more than all his other kids 'cause Joseph was born to him in his old age. He even made Joseph a fresh custom robe just for him.

4.text: But when his brothers saw that their dad treated Joseph better, they started hating on him hard. They couldn't even fake being nice to him.

5.text: One night, Joseph had a dream and told his brothers about it. They hated him even more after that.

6.text: He said, 'Y'all, check this out—I had a dream.'

7.text: 'We were out in the field tying up grain, and suddenly, my bundle stood up straight while all y'all bundles bowed down to mine!'

8.text: His brothers clapped back, 'Oh, so you think you gon' be king over us now? You really think you run this?' And they started hating on him even more 'cause of the dream.

9.text: Then Joseph had another dream and told his brothers, 'Listen, I had another one! This time, the sun, moon, and eleven stars bowed down to me!'

10.text: He even told his dad about it. But Jacob was like, 'Boy, what kind of dream is that? You mean to tell me, me, your mama, and your brothers all gon' bow down to you?'

11.text: His brothers were mad jealous, but his dad kept thinking about what the dream might mean.

12.text: Some time later, Joseph's brothers took the flocks to graze near Shechem.

13.text: Jacob told Joseph, 'Yo, your brothers out there with the sheep. Get ready—I'm sending you to check on them.' Joseph said, 'I'm on it.'

14.text: 'Go see how they doing, then come back and report to me.' So Joseph left Hebron and traveled to Shechem.

15.text: When Joseph got there, a man saw him wandering around and asked, 'What you looking for?'

16.text: Joseph said, 'I'm looking for my brothers. You know where they at?'

17.text: The man said, 'Yeah, I heard them say they heading to Dothan.' So Joseph followed their trail and found them there.

18.text: When his brothers saw Joseph rolling up in the distance, they started plotting to kill him.

19.text: They said, 'Here come the dreamer.'

20.text: 'Let's kill him and throw him in a pit. We can say a wild animal got him. Then we'll see what happens to all them dreams of his.'

21.text: But Reuben heard the plan and tried to save Joseph. He said, 'Nah, let's not kill him.'

22.text: 'Don't spill his blood. Just throw him in this empty pit here in the wilderness.' (Reuben planned to come back later and rescue Joseph.)

23.text: So when Joseph finally got to them, they snatched off his fresh robe.

24.text: Then they threw him into an empty pit.

25.text: As they sat down to eat, they saw a caravan of Ishmaelite traders coming from Gilead with spices and goods heading to Egypt.

26.text: Judah spoke up, 'Ayo, what do we gain by killing our own brother? We'd just have to cover it up.'

27.text: 'Instead of killing him, let's sell him to these traders. He's still our flesh and blood.' The brothers agreed.

28.text: So when the Midianite traders rolled by, they pulled Joseph out of the pit and sold him for 20 pieces of silver. Then the traders took Joseph to Egypt.

29.text: Later, Reuben came back to the pit and saw that Joseph was gone. He tore his clothes in grief.

30.text: He ran to his brothers like, 'The boy is gone! What am I supposed to do now?'

31.text: Then the brothers killed a goat, dipped Joseph's robe in its blood,

32.text: And sent the robe back to Jacob with a message: 'Look what we found. Ain't this Joseph's robe?'

33.text: Jacob recognized it immediately. He said, 'Yep, that's my son's robe. Some wild animal must've killed him. Joseph been torn to pieces!'

34.text: Jacob tore his clothes, put on sackcloth, and mourned for a long time.

35.text: His whole family tried to comfort him, but Jacob refused. He said, 'I'm taking this grief to my grave.' And he kept weeping.

36.text: Meanwhile, the Midianite traders sold Joseph in Egypt to Potiphar, one of Pharaoh's officers, captain of the palace guard.

1.text: Around this time, Judah left home and went to stay with a man named Hirah in Adullam.

2.text: While he was there, he met a Canaanite woman, daughter of Shua, and married her.

3.text: She got pregnant and had a son named Er.

4.text: Then she had another son named Onan.

5.text: And after that, she had a third son named Shelah. They were living in Kezib when he was born.

6.text: As time passed, Judah arranged a wife for Er. Her name was Tamar.

7.text: But Er was wicked in The Most High's sight, so God took his life.

8.text: Then Judah told Onan, 'Go marry your brother's widow. You gotta have a kid with her so your brother's bloodline can continue.'

9.text: But Onan knew the kid wouldn't be his, so whenever he slept with Tamar, he pulled out and spilled his seed on the ground.

10.text: But The Most High wasn't feeling that, so He took Onan's life too.

11.text: Then Judah told Tamar, 'Go back home to your parents and stay a widow until Shelah gets old enough to marry you.' (But Judah was capping—he was scared Shelah might die too, just like his brothers.)

12.text: Some years later, Judah's wife died. After his mourning, he went up to Timnah with Hirah to check on his shepherds.

13.text: Someone told Tamar, 'Hey, your father-in-law is heading up to Timnah to check on his sheep.'

14.text: Tamar saw that Shelah had grown up, but Judah still hadn't arranged for her to marry him. So she took off her widow's clothes, covered her face with a veil, and sat down near Enaim (which was on the way to Timnah).

15.text: Judah saw her and thought she was a prostitute 'cause she had her face covered.

16.text: So he stopped and said, 'Ayo, let me be with you.' (He didn't realize it was his daughter-in-law.)

17.text: Tamar asked, 'What you gon' pay me?' Judah said, 'I'll send you a young goat from my flock.'

18.text: Tamar said, 'Cool, but I need a guarantee until you send it.' Judah asked, 'What kind of guarantee?' She said, 'Leave me your seal, your cord, and your walking stick.' So Judah gave them to her, slept with her, and she got pregnant.

19.text: Then she went back home, took off the veil, and put her widow clothes back on.

20.text: Later, Judah sent Hirah with the young goat to get his stuff back, but he couldn't find Tamar anywhere.

21.text: He asked around, 'Where's the shrine prostitute that was sitting near Enaim?' The men said, 'Ain't no shrine prostitute ever been here.'

22.text: So Hirah went back to Judah and said, 'I couldn't find her. The locals say there's never been a shrine prostitute there.'

23.text: Judah said, 'Aight, let her keep the stuff. I tried to send her the goat, but we can't have people clowning us for this.'

24.text: Three months later, somebody told Judah, 'Tamar been out here wildin'—she pregnant from messing around.' Judah snapped, 'Drag her out and burn her!'

25.text: As they were bringing Tamar out, she sent a message to Judah: 'The man who owns these things got me pregnant. Look close—whose seal, cord, and walking stick are these?'

26.text: Judah recognized them immediately and said, 'She more righteous than me, 'cause I ain't keep my promise to give her Shelah.' Judah never slept with her again.

27.text: When Tamar was ready to give birth, she found out she was having twins.

28.text: During labor, one baby stuck his hand out, so the midwife tied a scarlet string around it, saying, 'This one came first!'

29.text: But then he pulled his hand back, and his brother popped out first. The midwife was like, 'What?! How you break out first?' So they named him Perez ('Breakthrough').

30.text: Then his brother came out, still wearing the scarlet string, and they named him Zerah.

1.text: When Joseph was taken to Egypt by the Ishmaelite traders, Potiphar, an Egyptian officer and Pharaoh's head of security, bought him as a slave.

2.text: But The Most High was with Joseph, so he was thriving in everything he did while serving Potiphar.

3.text: Potiphar noticed that Joseph was different—everything this man touched turned to gold.

4.text: So Potiphar made Joseph his personal attendant, putting him in charge of his whole household and all his property.

5.text: From the day Joseph took over, The Most High blessed Potiphar's house for Joseph's sake. Everything in Potiphar's crib ran smooth—his crops, his flocks, all of it.

6.text: So Potiphar put everything in Joseph's hands, not worrying about anything except what he wanted to eat. Now, Joseph was fine—handsome and well-built.

7.text: And before long, Potiphar's wife started thirsting after Joseph. She straight-up said, 'Come sleep with me.'

8.text: But Joseph shut that down quick. He said, 'Nah, look—my master trusts me with everything in this house.'

9.text: 'I got more authority than anybody here, and he ain't held nothing back from me—except you, 'cause you his wife. How could I do something this grimy? That'd be a straight-up sin against God.'

10.text: But she wasn't letting up—day after day, she kept pressuring him. But Joseph kept dodging her and staying out of her way.

11.text: One day, none of the other servants were around while Joseph was working inside.

12.text: She grabbed him by his cloak and demanded, 'Come on, sleep with me!' But Joseph yanked away and ran out, leaving his cloak in her hands.

13.text: When she saw she was holding his cloak and he had dipped,

14.text: She started screaming for the other servants, saying, 'Look! That Hebrew slave my husband brought here tried to take advantage of me!'

15.text: 'But when I screamed, he ran and left his cloak behind!'

16.text: She kept the cloak as 'evidence' until Potiphar came home.

17.text: Then she spun the same lie to her husband: 'That Hebrew slave you brought here tried to mess with me.'

18.text: 'But when I screamed, he ran outside and left his cloak!'

19.text: Potiphar was heated when he heard the story.

20.text: So he had Joseph thrown into prison, the same place where Pharaoh's prisoners were kept.

21.text: But even in prison, The Most High was with Joseph and showed him favor, making the prison warden take a liking to him.

22.text: Before long, the warden put Joseph in charge of all the other prisoners and everything that happened in the prison.

23.text: The warden had zero worries 'cause Joseph handled everything. The Most High was with Joseph, and everything he did was successful.

1.text: Some time later, Pharaoh's chief cup-bearer and chief baker messed up real bad and got on Pharaoh's bad side.

2.text: Pharaoh was heated and had both of them locked up.

3.text: They got thrown into the same prison where Joseph was, in the palace of the captain of the guard.

4.text: They stayed in prison for a while, and the captain put Joseph in charge of them.

5.text: One night, both the cup-bearer and the baker had dreams, and each one meant something different.

6.text: The next morning, Joseph saw them looking real stressed out.

7.text: He asked, 'What's up with y'all today? Why y'all looking so worried?'

8.text: They said, 'We both had dreams, but ain't nobody here to tell us what they mean.' Joseph said, 'Interpretations belong to The Most High. Go ahead and tell me your dreams.'

9.text: The cup-bearer spoke first: 'In my dream, I saw a grapevine in front of me.'

10.text: 'The vine had three branches. It started budding and blossoming, then—boom—full clusters of grapes popped up.'

11.text: 'I had Pharaoh's wine cup in my hand, so I grabbed the grapes, squeezed the juice into the cup, and handed it to Pharaoh.'

12.text: Joseph said, 'This is what your dream means: The three branches represent three days.'

13.text: 'In three days, Pharaoh gon' lift you up and put you back in your old job as his cup-bearer.'

14.text: 'And when that happens, do me a solid—mention me to Pharaoh so I can get outta here.'

15.text: 'I was kidnapped from my homeland, and now I'm locked up for something I ain't even do.'

16.text: When the chief baker saw that Joseph gave a good interpretation, he said, 'Aight, I had a dream too.'

17.text: 'In my dream, I had three baskets of white bread stacked on my head. The top basket had all kinds of baked goods for Pharaoh, but birds came and ate them up.'

18.text: Joseph said, 'This is what your dream means: The three baskets also represent three days.'

19.text: 'In three days, Pharaoh gon' lift you up too—but not in a good way. He gon' have you executed and hang your body on a pole. Then birds gon' eat your flesh.'

20.text: Three days later, it was Pharaoh's birthday, and he threw a huge banquet for all his officials.

21.text: He restored the cup-bearer to his old job, just like Joseph said.

22.text: But the chief baker? Yeah, Pharaoh executed him, just as Joseph predicted.

23.text: But the cup-bearer forgot all about Joseph—he ain't say nothing to Pharaoh.

1.text: Two years later, Pharaoh had a dream where he was standing by the Nile River.

2.text: He saw seven big, healthy cows come out the water and start grazing in the grass.

3.text: Then seven more cows came up after them, but these ones were scrawny and straight-up struggling.

4.text: Then the thin, ugly cows ate up the fat, healthy cows! At that point, Pharaoh woke up.

5.text: He fell asleep again and had another dream. This time, he saw seven full heads of grain growing on one stalk.

6.text: Then he saw seven more heads of grain, but these were thin and dried out from the east wind.

7.text: And the thin heads swallowed up the fat, healthy ones! Then Pharaoh woke up again and realized, 'Yo, that was a dream.'

8.text: In the morning, Pharaoh was real disturbed about the dreams. So he called all the magicians and wise men in Egypt, but nobody could tell him what the dreams meant.

9.text: Then the chief cup-bearer spoke up, saying, 'My bad, Pharaoh—I just remembered something I should've told you a long time ago.'

10.text: 'Remember when you got mad at me and the chief baker and threw us in prison?'

11.text: 'Both of us had dreams the same night, and each dream had a meaning.'

12.text: 'There was this young Hebrew dude in prison with us, a slave of the captain of the guard. We told him our dreams, and he broke it down for us.'

13.text: 'And just like he said, everything happened. I got my job back, and the baker got executed.'

14.text: Pharaoh sent for Joseph ASAP. They pulled him out of prison, let him shave, get dressed, and brought him to Pharaoh.

15.text: Pharaoh said, 'I had a dream, and nobody here can tell me what it means. But I heard you got a gift for interpreting dreams.'

16.text: Joseph said, 'I can't do it, but God can. He'll give you the meaning and peace of mind.'

17.text: So Pharaoh told Joseph his dream.

18.text: 'I was standing by the Nile when I saw seven fat, healthy cows come out and start grazing.'

19.text: 'Then I saw seven sick-looking cows—scrawny and ugly—come up behind them. I ain't never seen cows that rough-looking in all of Egypt.'

20.text: 'The thin, scrawny cows ate up the fat ones.'

21.text: 'But after eating them, they still looked just as skinny as before! Then I woke up.'

22.text: 'Then I had another dream: I saw seven heads of grain, full and beautiful, growing on a single stalk.'

23.text: 'Then seven more heads of grain appeared, but these were blighted, shriveled, and withered by the east wind.'

24.text: 'And the shriveled heads swallowed the seven healthy heads. I told my magicians, but none of them could explain it.'

25.text: Joseph said, 'Both dreams mean the same thing. God is telling you in advance what He's about to do.'

26.text: 'The seven fat cows and the seven full heads of grain both mean seven years of prosperity.'

27.text: 'The seven skinny cows and the seven dried-up heads of grain mean seven years of famine.'

28.text: 'It's gonna happen just like this, 'cause God is letting you know ahead of time.'

29.text: 'The next seven years gon' be real good in Egypt.'

30.text: 'But after that, seven years of famine so bad that people will forget the good years ever happened.'

31.text: 'It's gonna be so rough, the famine will wipe out every memory of the good times.'

32.text: 'Since you had two dreams about it, that means God has locked this in—it's happening for sure, and soon.'

33.text: 'Pharaoh, you need to find a wise and intelligent man to take charge of Egypt.'

34.text: 'You should appoint officers to collect one-fifth of all crops during the seven good years.'

35.text: 'Store it all in Pharaoh's warehouses so we got food ready.'

36.text: 'That way, when the famine hits, we won't starve, and Egypt won't collapse.'

37.text: Pharaoh and his officials loved Joseph's plan.

38.text: Pharaoh said, 'Can we find anyone else like this dude? He's clearly got the spirit of God in him.'

39.text: 'Since God gave you the meaning of these dreams, there's nobody as wise as you.'

40.text: 'You're now in charge of my court. Everybody in Egypt takes orders from you—only I rank higher.'

41.text: Pharaoh put Joseph in charge of the whole country.

42.text: He took off his royal ring and put it on Joseph's hand. He dressed him in fine linen and put a gold chain on him.

43.text: Joseph rode in the second-in-command chariot, and everywhere he went, people had to bow down.

44.text: Pharaoh told him, 'I'm still Pharaoh, but nobody moves in Egypt without your say-so.'

45.text: Pharaoh gave Joseph a new Egyptian name—Zaphenath-paneah—and a wife, Asenath, daughter of Potiphera, a priest of On.

46.text: Joseph was thirty when he started serving Pharaoh. He went throughout Egypt, checking on everything.

47.text: For seven years, Egypt had crazy good harvests.

48.text: Joseph collected food and stored it all in different cities.

49.text: There was so much grain, they stopped counting.

50.text: Before the famine, Joseph and Asenath had two sons.

51.text: Joseph named his first son Manasseh ('God made me forget my troubles and my father's house').

52.text: His second son was Ephraim ('God made me fruitful in this land of pain').

53.text: After the seven years of prosperity, the famine hit—just like Joseph said.

54.text: The famine was everywhere, but Egypt still had food.

55.text: People begged Pharaoh for food, and he told them, 'Go to Joseph. Do what he tells you.'

56.text: So Joseph opened the storehouses and sold grain to the Egyptians. The famine was severe.

57.text: People from all over the world came to buy grain from Joseph, 'cause the famine hit everywhere.

1.text: When Jacob heard there was grain in Egypt, he said to his sons, 'Why y'all just standing around looking at each other?'

2.text: 'I heard Egypt got food. Go down there and buy us some so we don't starve to death.'

3.text: So Joseph's ten older brothers went to Egypt to buy grain.

4.text: But Jacob wouldn't let Benjamin go, 'cause he was scared something might happen to him.

5.text: So the brothers headed to Egypt, along with a crowd of other folks trying to buy food, since the famine had hit Canaan too.

6.text: Since Joseph was governor over Egypt, all food sales had to go through him. So when his brothers arrived, they bowed down to him, faces to the ground.

7.text: Joseph recognized them immediately, but he acted like he didn't know them. He spoke to them harshly, saying, 'Where y'all from?'

8.text: Even though Joseph recognized them, they had no clue who he was.

9.text: Joseph remembered his dreams from way back and said, 'Y'all spies! Y'all came here to see how weak our land is.'

10.text: 'No, my lord!' they said. 'We just here to buy food.'

11.text: 'We all brothers—we honest men! We not spies.'

12.text: 'Nah,' Joseph insisted. 'Y'all came to scope out our land's weaknesses.'

13.text: 'Sir, there's twelve of us. We all brothers, sons of the same man in Canaan. Our youngest brother stayed home, and one of our brothers is no longer with us.'

14.text: Joseph said, 'Like I said—y'all spies.'

15.text: 'Here's how we gon' find out if y'all telling the truth. Swear on Pharaoh's life: Y'all ain't leaving Egypt till your youngest brother comes here.'

16.text: 'One of y'all go back and bring him. The rest of y'all staying here locked up. That'll prove if y'all telling the truth. If not, then I know y'all some spies.'

17.text: Then Joseph threw them all in jail for three days.

18.text: On the third day, Joseph said to them, 'I fear God, so here's the deal—y'all do this, and y'all live.'

19.text: 'If y'all really honest men, leave one of your brothers here in prison, and the rest of y'all take food back home for your starving families.'

20.text: 'But you must bring your youngest brother back to me. This will prove that you are telling the truth, and you will not die.' To this they agreed.

21.text: Speaking among themselves, they said, 'Clearly we are being punished because of what we did to Joseph long ago. We saw his anguish when he pleaded for his life, but we wouldn't listen. That's why we're in this trouble.'

22.text: 'Didn't I tell you not to sin against the boy?' Reuben asked. 'But you wouldn't listen. And now we have to answer for his blood!'

23.text: Of course, they didn't know that Joseph understood them, for he had been speaking to them through an interpreter.

24.text: Now he turned away from them and began to weep. When he regained his composure, he spoke to them again. Then he chose Simeon from among them and had him tied up right before their eyes.

25.text: Joseph then ordered his servants to fill the men's sacks with grain, but he also gave secret instructions to return each brother's payment at the top of his sack. He also gave them supplies for their journey home.

26.text: So the brothers loaded their donkeys with the grain and headed for home.

27.text: But when they stopped for the night and one of them opened his sack to get grain for his donkey, he found his money in the top of his sack.

28.text: 'Look!' he exclaimed to his brothers. 'My money has been returned; it's here in my sack!' Then their hearts sank. Trembling, they said to each other, 'What has God done to us?'

29.text: When the brothers came to their father, Jacob, in the land of Canaan, they told him everything that had happened to them.

30.text: 'The man who is governor of the land spoke very harshly to us,' they told him. 'He accused us of being spies scouting the land.'

31.text: 'But we said, 'We are honest men, not spies.'

32.text: 'We are twelve brothers, sons of one father. One brother is no longer with us, and the youngest is at home with our father in the land of Canaan.'

33.text: 'Then the man who is governor of the land told us, 'This is how I will find out if you are honest men. Leave one of your brothers here with me, and take grain for your starving families and go on home.'

34.text: 'But you must bring your youngest brother back to me. Then I will know you are honest men and not spies. Then I will give you back your brother, and you may trade freely in the land.'

35.text: As they emptied out their sacks, there in each man's sack was the bag of money he had paid for the grain! The brothers and their father were terrified when they saw the bags of money.

36.text: Jacob exclaimed, 'You are robbing me of my children! Joseph is gone! Simeon is gone! And now you want to take Benjamin, too. Everything is going against me!'

37.text: Then Reuben said to his father, 'You may kill my two sons if I don't bring Benjamin back to you. I'll be responsible for him, and I promise to bring him back.'

38.text: But Jacob replied, 'My son will not go down with you. His brother Joseph is dead, and he is all I have left. If anything should happen to him on your journey, you would send this grieving, white-haired man to his grave.'

1.text: The famine kept hitting Canaan real bad.

2.text: When the food they brought from Egypt started running out, Jacob told his sons, "Y'all gotta go back and get us some more food."

3.text: But Judah said, "That man was dead serious when he told us, 'Don't come back unless your brother is with you.'"

4.text: "If you send Benjamin with us, we'll go buy the food."

5.text: "But if you don't let him come, we ain't going either, 'cause the man straight up said, 'Y'all won't see me again unless your brother is with you.'"

6.text: Jacob sighed, "Why y'all always bringing me problems? Why did you even tell him y'all had another brother?"

7.text: They answered, "He kept asking questions about our family. He asked, 'Is your father still alive? Do y'all have another brother?' So we just answered him. How were we supposed to know he was gonna say, 'Bring your brother down here'?"

8.text: Then Judah told his father, "Look, send the boy with me, and we'll go. Otherwise, we all gon' die—not just us, but you and the kids too."

9.text: "I promise I'll bring him back safe. If I don't, you can hold me responsible forever."

10.text: "If we hadn't wasted all this time, we could've gone and come back twice by now."

11.text: So Jacob finally said, "Alright, if this gotta happen, then do this: Pack some of the best stuff from our land—some balm, honey, gum, resin, pistachios, and almonds."

12.text: "And take double the money, 'cause maybe that silver in your sacks last time was a mistake."

13.text: "Now take your brother and go back to the man."

14.text: "May God Almighty show y'all mercy so the man will let Simeon and Benjamin come back home. But if I gotta lose my sons, then so be it."

15.text: So the brothers packed their gifts, took double the money, and brought Benjamin. Then they went back to Egypt and stood before Joseph.

16.text: When Joseph saw Benjamin, he told his house manager, "Take these men to my house, set up a feast, and get everything ready—we eating together at noon."

17.text: The manager did what Joseph said and brought them to his house.

18.text: The brothers got real nervous when they saw where they were going. "Man, it's 'cause of that money that showed up in our sacks last time! He tryna trap us! He gon' take us as slaves and steal our donkeys too!"

19.text: When they got to the house, they went up to Joseph's house manager and spoke to him at the door.

20.text: "Sir, uh… we came down here before to buy food."

21.text: "But on our way back, we stopped for the night and opened our sacks, and we found all our money sitting right there at the top! We don't know how it got there, but we brought it back."

22.text: "We also brought extra money to buy more food. We promise we didn't steal nothing."

23.text: The house manager smiled and said, "Y'all relax. Don't be scared. Your God, the God of your father, must've put that money in your sacks. I know I got the payment y'all sent." Then he went and brought Simeon out to them.

24.text: The manager took them into Joseph's house, gave them water to wash their feet, and fed their donkeys.

25.text: The brothers got their gifts ready for Joseph since they were told they'd be eating with him at noon.

26.text: When Joseph came home, they gave him the gifts they brought and bowed low before him.

27.text: Joseph asked, "So how's your old man? The father y'all told me about—he still alive?"

28.text: They said, "Yes, sir. Our father is alive and well." Then they bowed low again.

29.text: Then Joseph saw Benjamin, his little brother from the same mother. "This your youngest brother? The one y'all told me about?" Joseph looked at him and said, "May God be gracious to you, my son."

30.text: Joseph had to hurry out the room, 'cause seeing Benjamin got him all in his feelings. He went into his private room and cried.

31.text: After washing his face, he pulled himself together and came back out. Then he said, "Alright, let's eat."

32.text: The waiters served Joseph at his own table, his brothers at another table, and the Egyptians who worked with him at a separate table—'cause Egyptians didn't mess with Hebrews like that.

33.text: Joseph had them seated in order from the oldest to the youngest, and the brothers looked at each other like, "How in the world does he know our birth order?"

34.text: Then Joseph sent food from his own table to theirs, but Benjamin got five times as much food as everybody else. So they ate, drank, and had a good time.

1.text: When his brothers were about to leave, Joseph told his house manager, "Fill their sacks with as much grain as they can carry, and put each man's money back in his sack."

2.text: "But in the youngest one's sack, put my personal silver cup right at the top, along with the money for his grain." So the manager did exactly what Joseph told him.

3.text: Early the next morning, the brothers loaded up their donkeys and hit the road.

4.text: But as soon as they got just outside the city, Joseph said to his house manager, "Go after them and stop them. When you catch up, ask them, 'Why y'all do me dirty after I treated you good?'"

5.text: "'Why would y'all steal my master's silver cup? That's the cup he uses to predict the future! Y'all really gonna do him like that?'"

6.text: So the house manager chased them down and said exactly what Joseph told him to say.

7.text: The brothers were shocked. "What are you even talking about?! We ain't steal nothing!"

8.text: "Didn't we bring back the money we found in our sacks from last time? Why would we steal silver or gold from your master's house?"

9.text: "Look, if you find his cup with any one of us, let that man die. And the rest of us? We'll all be your slaves."

10.text: The house manager said, "That's fair, but only the one who got the cup will be my slave. The rest of y'all can go free."

11.text: The brothers quickly got off their donkeys and opened their sacks.

12.text: The house manager searched through them one by one, from the oldest to the youngest. And when he got to Benjamin's sack—there was the cup!

13.text: The brothers tore their clothes in despair. Then they loaded up their donkeys and went back to the city.

14.text: When they got back, Joseph was still at the palace. Judah and his brothers fell to the ground before him.

15.text: Joseph looked at them and said, "What have y'all done? Don't y'all know a man like me can see things before they happen?"

16.text: Judah said, "My lord, what can we even say? How can we explain this? How can we prove we innocent? God is exposing our guilt. My lord, we all gon' stay and be your slaves—not just our brother who had the cup."

17.text: But Joseph said, "Nah, I'd never do that. Only the one who stole the cup will be my slave. The rest of y'all? Go back to your father in peace."

18.text: Then Judah stepped forward and said, "Please, my lord, let me say one thing to you. Don't be mad at me, even though you got power like Pharaoh himself."

19.text: "You asked us, 'Do y'all have a father or a brother?'"

20.text: "And we told you, 'Yes, we got an old father, and his youngest son is a child of his old age. His full brother is dead, so their father loves him more than anything.'"

21.text: "Then you told us, 'Bring him here so I can see him myself.'"

22.text: "But we told you, 'That boy can't leave his father, or his father will die.'"

23.text: "But you said, 'If your youngest brother don't come with y'all, you will never see me again.'"

24.text: "So we went home and told our father what you said."

25.text: "Then later, when he told us to come back and buy more food, we told him, 'We can't go unless Benjamin comes with us.'"

26.text: "We said, 'We'll never see the man's face unless Benjamin is with us.'"

27.text: "Then our father said, 'As you know, my wife only had two sons.'"

28.text: "'One of them went away and never came back. He must've been torn apart by some wild animal. I haven't seen him since.'"

29.text: "'Now if y'all take his little brother away and something happens to him, y'all gon' send this old man to his grave in sorrow.'"

30.text: "Now, my lord, I can't go back to my father without the boy. My father's life is tied up in the boy's life."

31.text: "If he sees that Benjamin ain't with us, he gon' die. And we? We gon' be responsible for breaking our father's heart."

32.text: "I promised my father I'd bring the boy back safe. I told him, 'If I don't, you can hold me responsible forever.'"

33.text: "So please, my lord, let me stay here as your slave instead of the boy. Let him go home with his brothers."

34.text: "I can't go home if the boy ain't with me. I can't stand to see the pain it would cause my father."

1.text: Joseph couldn't hold it in no more. With everybody else in the room, he shouted, "Everybody out! Leave me alone with my brothers!" So it was just him and them when he finally told them who he was.

2.text: Then he broke down crying—so loud that the Egyptians outside could hear him, and word spread all the way to Pharaoh's palace.

3.text: "I'm Joseph!" he said. "Is my father still alive?" But his brothers couldn't even speak. They were shook to realize Joseph was standing right in front of them.

4.text: "Come closer," he said. So they stepped up, and he told them again, "I'm Joseph, y'all brother—the one y'all sold into slavery in Egypt."

5.text: "But don't trip, and don't be mad at yourselves for selling me. God sent me ahead of y'all to save lives."

6.text: "This famine been wrecking the land for two years, and we still got five more to go—no planting, no harvesting."

7.text: "God put me in this position ahead of y'all to keep our family alive and make sure we survive."

8.text: "So really, it wasn't even y'all that sent me here—it was God! He made me Pharaoh's top adviser, manager of his whole palace, and governor of all Egypt."

9.text: "Now hurry back to my father and tell him: 'This is what your son Joseph says—God made me ruler over Egypt. Come down here quick!'"

10.text: "Y'all can live in Goshen so you'll be close to me—with all your children, grandchildren, flocks, herds, and everything you own."

11.text: "I'll take care of y'all there, 'cause we still got five more years of famine. Otherwise, y'all gon' starve—your whole household, your animals, everybody."

12.text: "Look! Y'all can see for yourselves, and so can my brother Benjamin—it's really me talking to y'all."

13.text: "Go tell my father about my position in Egypt. Tell him everything y'all saw, and bring him here quick!"

14.text: Then Joseph broke down again, hugging Benjamin, and Benjamin hugged him back.

15.text: Then Joseph kissed each one of his brothers, still crying. After that, they finally felt like they could talk to him freely.

16.text: Word got back to Pharaoh that Joseph's brothers had arrived, and Pharaoh and his officials were happy to hear it.

17.text: Pharaoh told Joseph, "Tell your brothers to do this: Load up your animals and hurry back to Canaan."

18.text: "Go get your father and all your families, and bring 'em here. I'll give y'all the best land in Egypt, and y'all gon' eat real good."

19.text: "Tell them to take wagons from Egypt to carry the kids and the wives, and bring your father here."

20.text: "Don't even worry about your stuff back home—the best of Egypt is yours now."

21.text: So Jacob's sons did what they were told. Joseph hooked them up with wagons, just like Pharaoh ordered, and gave them supplies for the trip.

22.text: He gave each of them new clothes, but for Benjamin, he gave five changes of clothes and 300 pieces of silver.

23.text: Joseph also sent ten male donkeys loaded with the best Egyptian goods and ten female donkeys carrying grain, bread, and supplies for the journey.

24.text: As his brothers were leaving, Joseph told them, "Now don't y'all be arguing on the way home!"

25.text: They left Egypt and went back to their father, Jacob, in Canaan.

26.text: "Joseph is still alive!" they told him. "And he's the governor of all Egypt!" Jacob was so shocked, he couldn't even believe what they were saying.

27.text: But when they told Jacob everything Joseph said, and he saw the wagons Joseph sent to carry him, his spirit came back to life.

28.text: Then Jacob said, "It must be true! My son Joseph is alive! I gotta go see him before I die."

1.text: So Jacob packed up all his stuff and set out for Egypt. When he got to Beersheba, he offered sacrifices to the God of his father, Isaac.

2.text: That night, God spoke to him in a vision. "Jacob! Jacob!" He called.

3.text: Jacob answered, "Here I am." Then God said, "I am God—the God of your father. Don't be scared to go down to Egypt, 'cause I'm gonna make your family a great nation there."

4.text: "I'll go with you to Egypt, and I'll bring you back again. And when you die, Joseph will be right there to close your eyes."

5.text: So Jacob left Beersheba, and his sons carried him, their kids, and their wives in the wagons Pharaoh provided.

6.text: They brought all their livestock and everything they owned from Canaan and moved to Egypt.

7.text: Jacob's whole family came with him—his sons, grandsons, daughters, granddaughters—everybody.

8.text: Here are the names of Jacob's descendants who went with him to Egypt:

9.text: Simeon's sons – Jemuel, Jamin, Ohad, Jakin, Zohar, and Shaul (his mother was a Canaanite woman).

10.text: Levi's sons – Gershon, Kohath, and Merari.

11.text: Judah's sons – Er, Onan, Shelah, Perez, and Zerah. (Er and Onan had already died in Canaan.) Perez's sons – Hezron and Hamul.

12.text: Issachar's sons – Tola, Puah, Jashub, and Shimron.

13.text: Zebulun's sons – Sered, Elon, and Jahleel.

14.text: These were the sons of Leah, born in Paddan-aram, plus their sister Dinah. Total descendants from Leah: 33.

15.text: Gad's sons – Zephon, Haggi, Shuni, Ezbon, Eri, Arodi, and Areli.

16.text: Asher's sons – Imnah, Ishvah, Ishvi, and Beriah. Their sister – Serah. Beriah's sons – Heber and Malkiel.

17.text: These were the sons of Zilpah, Leah's servant, given to her by her father, Laban. Total descendants from Zilpah: 16.

18.text: Joseph's sons (born in Egypt) – Manasseh and Ephraim. Their mother – Asenath, daughter of Potiphera (priest of On).

19.text: Benjamin's sons – Bela, Beker, Ashbel, Gera, Naaman, Ehi, Rosh, Muppim, Huppim, and Ard.

20.text: These were the sons of Rachel, Jacob's wife. Total descendants from Rachel: 14.

21.text: Dan's son – Hushim.

22.text: Naphtali's sons – Jahzeel, Guni, Jezer, and Shillem.

23.text: These were the sons of Bilhah, Rachel's servant, given to her by Laban. Total descendants from Bilhah: 7.

24.text: The total number of Jacob's direct descendants who went to Egypt (not counting his sons' wives) was 66.

25.text: Joseph had two sons in Egypt, bringing the full family count to 70 people.

26.text: As they got close to Egypt, Jacob sent Judah ahead to get directions to Goshen.

27.text: When they finally arrived, Joseph got his chariot ready and went to meet his father.

28.text: As soon as Joseph saw Jacob, he ran to him, hugged him tight, and cried for a long time.

29.text: Jacob finally said, "Now I'm ready to die, 'cause I've seen your face again and I know you're alive."

30.text: Joseph told his brothers and his father's family, "I'm gonna go tell Pharaoh that y'all have arrived."

31.text: "I'll tell him, 'My family has come from Canaan. They're shepherds and livestock keepers, and they brought all their flocks and everything they own.'"

32.text: "Now when Pharaoh calls y'all in and asks what y'all do for a living, tell him this…"

33.text: "'We, your servants, have raised livestock all our lives, just like our ancestors.'"

34.text: "That way, he'll let y'all settle in Goshen, 'cause Egyptians don't mess with shepherds like that."

1.text: Joseph went to Pharaoh and said, "My father and my brothers just got here from Canaan. They brought all their flocks, herds, and everything they own, and they settin' up in Goshen."

2.text: Joseph picked five of his brothers and brought them before Pharaoh.

3.text: Pharaoh asked them, "What do y'all do for a living?" They answered, "We your servants are shepherds, just like our ancestors."

4.text: "We here to stay for a while, 'cause back in Canaan, there ain't no pasture for our flocks. The famine real bad out there. Please, let us live in Goshen."

5.text: Pharaoh told Joseph, "Now that your father and brothers are here..."

6.text: "Let 'em pick any place they want in Egypt. Give 'em the best land—let 'em stay in Goshen. And if any of them got special skills, put 'em in charge of my livestock too."

7.text: Then Joseph brought Jacob in to meet Pharaoh, and Jacob blessed Pharaoh.

8.text: Pharaoh asked, "How old are you?"

9.text: Jacob said, "I've been on this earth 130 hard years. But my life been short compared to my ancestors."

10.text: Then Jacob blessed Pharaoh again before leaving his court.

11.text: Joseph gave his father and brothers the best land in Egypt—the region of Rameses—just like Pharaoh said.

12.text: Joseph made sure his father and his brothers had plenty of food, giving them what they needed for their whole families, even the little ones.

13.text: But the famine was so bad that all the food ran out. People were starving everywhere in Egypt and Canaan.

14.text: Joseph kept selling grain, and eventually, he collected all the money in Egypt and Canaan and put it in Pharaoh's treasury.

15.text: When the people ran out of money, the Egyptians came to Joseph, saying, "We broke! But please give us food, or we gon' die right here in front of you!"

16.text: Joseph said, "If y'all outta money, bring me your livestock, and I'll give you food in exchange."

17.text: So the people traded their horses, sheep, goats, cattle, and donkeys for food. Joseph made sure they had enough to last another year.

18.text: But when that year ended, they came back and said, "Look, we can't lie—our money's gone, our livestock is yours. We ain't got nothing left but our land and ourselves."

19.text: "Why should we die in front of you? Buy us and our land in exchange for food. Let us be Pharaoh's servants—just give us grain so we can live and so the land won't be abandoned."

20.text: So Joseph bought all the land in Egypt for Pharaoh. The famine was so severe that the people sold their fields, and soon Pharaoh owned all the land.

21.text: Then Joseph turned the people into workers across Egypt.

22.text: The only land he didn't buy was the land belonging to the priests. They got their food directly from Pharaoh, so they didn't have to sell their land.

23.text: Then Joseph told the people, "Look, today I bought y'all and your land for Pharaoh. But here's what I'm gonna do—I'll give y'all seeds to plant in the fields."

24.text: "When you harvest, one-fifth of your crop belongs to Pharaoh. The rest is yours to use as seed and food for y'all and your families."

25.text: They said, "You saved our lives! Thank you, my lord. We happy to be Pharaoh's servants."

26.text: So Joseph made it official—a law that Pharaoh would always get one-fifth of all crops grown in Egypt. (This law was still in effect generations later.)

27.text: Meanwhile, the Israelites settled in Goshen. They got land, they were fruitful, and their numbers grew fast.

28.text: Jacob lived in Egypt for 17 more years before his time came. In total, he lived 147 years.

29.text: When Jacob knew his time was almost up, he called Joseph and said, "Please, do me this favor—put your hand under my thigh and swear that you'll show me love and honor this last request: Don't bury me in Egypt."

30.text: "When I die, take me out of Egypt and bury me where my ancestors are." Joseph promised, "I'll do as you ask."

31.text: "Swear it," Jacob said. So Joseph gave his oath. Then Jacob bowed humbly at the head of his bed.

1.text: Some time after that, Joseph got word: "Your father ain't doin' too good—he fading fast." So Joseph went to visit him, bringing along his two sons, Manasseh and Ephraim.

2.text: When Jacob heard Joseph was coming, he gathered his strength and sat up in bed.

3.text: "God Almighty appeared to me back in Luz, in the land of Canaan, and He blessed me," Jacob said.

4.text: "He told me, 'I will make you fruitful and multiply you. Your descendants will become a whole nation, and I will give them this land of Canaan forever.'"

5.text: "Now listen, Joseph—I'm claiming your two boys, Ephraim and Manasseh, as my own. They gon' be mine just like Reuben and Simeon."

6.text: "But any more kids you have after them, those are yours. They'll inherit land under their brothers' names."

7.text: "Now, let me tell you something personal. When I was coming back from Paddan-aram, your mother Rachel died on the way in Canaan, not far from Ephrath (that's Bethlehem). I buried her right there by the road."

8.text: Then Jacob looked at the two boys and said, "Wait... are these your sons?"

9.text: "Yes, father," Joseph said. "These are the sons God gave me here in Egypt." Jacob said, "Bring 'em here, so I can bless 'em."

10.text: Jacob's eyesight was failing bad because of his age, so he could barely see. But when Joseph brought the boys closer, Jacob kissed them and hugged them.

11.text: Then Jacob said, "Man... I never thought I'd see your face again, Joseph, and now God done let me see your kids too!"

12.text: Joseph took his boys from Jacob's lap and bowed down with his face to the ground.

13.text: Then he positioned the boys for the blessing— He put Ephraim (the younger one) on Jacob's left side He put Manasseh (the firstborn) on Jacob's right side

14.text: But when Jacob reached out to bless them, he crossed his arms! He put his right hand on Ephraim's head (the younger one). He put his left hand on Manasseh's head (the firstborn).

15.text: Then Jacob blessed Joseph and said: "May the God my grandfather Abraham and my father Isaac walked with— The God who's been my Shepherd all my life till this very day,

16.text: The Angel who saved me from all harm— May He bless these boys. Let my name live on through them, And the names of Abraham and Isaac. May they grow and multiply all over the earth."

17.text: But when Joseph saw his father put his right hand on Ephraim (the younger one), he got upset. He grabbed his father's hand to move it to Manasseh instead.

18.text: "No, father! This one is the firstborn—put your right hand on his head."

19.text: But Jacob refused. "I know, my son, I know." Manasseh gon' be great, but his younger brother gon' be even greater. His descendants gon' become a whole nation."

20.text: So Jacob blessed the boys that day, saying: "When the people of Israel bless others, they gon' say, 'May God make you as great as Ephraim and Manasseh.'" In this way, Jacob put Ephraim ahead of Manasseh.

21.text: Then Jacob said to Joseph, "Look, my time is almost up. But God will be with you and bring you back to the land of our ancestors."

22.text: "And as for you, Joseph, I'm giving you a special extra portion of land—more than your brothers—land I took from the Amorites with my sword and bow."

1.text: Jacob called all his sons together and said, "Y'all gather around, 'cause I'm about to tell y'all what's gonna happen in the future."

2.text: "Listen up, sons of Jacob—pay attention to your father, Israel."

3.text: "Reuben, you my firstborn, my strength—the son of my prime years. You had rank, you had power."

4.text: "But you reckless, wild like a flood, and you ain't gon' be first no more. 'Cause you disrespected me—you slept with one of my wives. You messed up my house."

5.text: "Simeon and Levi? Y'all two are the same—violent and dangerous."

6.text: "I don't wanna be in on y'all schemes, I don't wanna be part of y'all plans. Y'all killed men in your rage and crippled animals just for fun."

7.text: "Y'all anger is cursed 'cause it's too fierce. Y'all wrath is cursed 'cause it's too cruel. I'ma scatter y'all among the descendants of Jacob—spread y'all out in Israel."

8.text: "Judah, your brothers gon' praise you. You gon' have your enemies by the neck. Your whole family gon' bow down to you."

9.text: "Judah, you a young lion, just finished eating. You lie down, chilling—who gon' dare wake you up?"

10.text: "The royal scepter won't leave Judah. The ruler's staff will stay with his descendants—until the real king, the one who all nations honor, comes."

11.text: "He gon' tie his donkey to a grapevine, wash his clothes in wine, and dip his robes in the blood of grapes."

12.text: "His eyes darker than wine, and his teeth whiter than milk."

13.text: "Zebulun gon' live by the seashore, a harbor for ships. His land gon' stretch all the way to Sidon."

14.text: "Issachar? That's a strong donkey, resting between two saddlepacks."

15.text: "He see how good the land is, how nice everything is. He gon' bend his back to carry the load and take up hard labor."

16.text: "Dan gon' govern his people like any other tribe of Israel."

17.text: "But he gon' be like a snake on the road, a venomous viper waiting on the path—biting the horse's hooves so the rider falls off."

18.text: "I trust in You for salvation, Lord!"

19.text: "Gad gon' get attacked by raiders, but he gon' fight back and get 'em when they retreat."

20.text: "Asher gon' eat good—dining on rich foods, cooking up meals fit for kings."

21.text: "Naphtali like a deer set free, running wild—bringing back beautiful words."

22.text: "Joseph like a wild donkey near a spring, standing tall up on a ridge."

23.text: "Haters came for him, shot arrows at him, attacked him left and right."

24.text: "But he stayed strong, held his bow tight—his arms steady 'cause the Mighty One of Jacob was with him, 'cause the Shepherd, the Rock of Israel, had his back."

25.text: "May the God of your father help you; may the Almighty bless you—blessings from heaven above, blessings from the deep waters below, blessings of the womb."

26.text: "May my blessing on you be bigger than the blessings of my ancestors—stretching to the highest hills. May all these blessings rest on Joseph, the true prince among his brothers."

27.text: "Benjamin a savage wolf—tearing up his enemies in the morning, splitting up his loot in the evening."

28.text: These are the 12 tribes of Israel. This was Jacob's last message to his sons—blessing each one the way they needed to be blessed.

29.text: Then Jacob gave them his final instructions: "I'm about to die. When I do, bury me with my ancestors."

30.text: "Put me in the cave in the field of Ephron the Hittite—the cave in the field of Machpelah, near Mamre in Canaan—the one Abraham bought for a permanent burial site."

31.text: "That's where Abraham and Sarah are buried, where Isaac and Rebekah are buried, and where I buried Leah."

32.text: "That's the land my grandfather Abraham bought from the Hittites."

33.text: When Jacob finished giving these instructions, he pulled his feet up in his bed, took his last breath, and joined his ancestors in death.

1.text: As soon as Jacob passed, Joseph threw himself over his father, crying and kissing him.

2.text: Then Joseph told the physicians who worked for him, "Y'all need to embalm my father's body." So they embalmed Jacob.

3.text: The embalming process took forty days, which was standard. The Egyptians mourned his death for seventy days.

4.text: When the mourning period was over, Joseph went to Pharaoh's officials and said, "Do me a favor—go to Pharaoh and tell him this…"

5.text: "Before my father died, he made me swear an oath. He told me, 'Listen, I'm about to die. Take my body back to Canaan and bury me in the tomb I prepared for myself.' So please let me go bury my father. I promise I'll come back right after."

6.text: Pharaoh agreed and said, "Go ahead and bury your father like you promised."

7.text: So Joseph went to bury his father, and all of Pharaoh's officials went with him—the high-ranking members of Pharaoh's court and all the top leaders in Egypt.

8.text: Joseph's entire household went, along with his brothers and their families. They left their little children, flocks, and herds back in Goshen.

9.text: A whole army of chariots and horsemen rolled out with them—it was a massive procession.

10.text: When they reached the threshing floor at Atad, near the Jordan River, they held a deep and serious memorial service. The mourning lasted seven days.

11.text: When the local Canaanites saw what was happening, they said, "This is some serious mourning from the Egyptians." So that place near the Jordan River was named Abel-Mizraim (which means 'Egyptian Mourning').

12.text: Jacob's sons did exactly what he told them to do.

13.text: They carried his body to Canaan and buried him in the cave in the field of Machpelah, near Mamre—the same burial site Abraham bought from Ephron the Hittite.

14.text: After the burial, Joseph and everyone who went with him returned to Egypt.

15.text: But now that their father was gone, Joseph's brothers got scared. They said to each other, "What if Joseph still mad at us? What if he finally gets revenge for what we did to him?"

16.text: So they sent him a message saying, "Before our father died, he told us to tell you this…"

17.text: "'Please forgive your brothers for all the wrong they did to you—for their sin and their cruelty.' So now, we, the servants of the God of your father, are begging you—please forgive us." When Joseph got the message, he broke down and cried.

18.text: Then his brothers came and fell to the ground before him. They said, "Look, we your slaves now!"

19.text: But Joseph told them, "Don't be scared. Do I look like God to you? I ain't the one who punishes."

20.text: "Y'all meant to hurt me, but God flipped it for good. He put me here so I could save many lives."

21.text: "So don't be afraid—I got you. I'll take care of you and your kids." Then he comforted them and spoke to them kindly.

22.text: Joseph and his brothers continued to live in Egypt, and Joseph lived to be 110 years old.

23.text: He lived long enough to see three generations of Ephraim's children and even got to hold the babies of Manasseh's son Makir.

24.text: Before he died, Joseph told his brothers, "I'm about to die, but listen—God ain't forgot about y'all. He gon' come help y'all and lead y'all outta here, back to the land He promised Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob."

25.text: Then Joseph made the Israelites swear an oath. He said, "When God comes to rescue y'all and take y'all home, y'all better take my bones with you."

26.text: So Joseph died at 110 years old. They embalmed him, and his body was placed in a coffin in Egypt.

1.text: This the heavy word the prophet Habakkuk saw comin'.

2.text: Lord, how long I gotta cry out before You hear me? I'm yellin' "Violence!" out here and You ain't savin' nobody.

3.text: Why You keep showin' me all this wickedness? Why You got me watchin' all this mess—robbery, drama, folks wildin' out everywhere?

4.text: The law got no power now, and justice? Man, it don't even show up. Wicked folks got the good folks surrounded, so wrong judgments keep comin' down.

5.text: Look around, all y'all—watch close. I'm 'bout to do somethin' so wild, y'all wouldn't believe it even if somebody told you.

6.text: I'm raisin' up the Chaldeans—yeah, them ruthless, quick-tempered folks. They movin' through lands that don't belong to 'em, takin' over like it's theirs.

7.text: They scary and dangerous—don't answer to nobody. They make they own rules and carry themselves like they gods.

8.text: Their horses faster than leopards, meaner than wolves at night. Them riders pullin' up from way out, movin' like eagles ready to eat.

9.text: They comin' straight for violence— they eyes sharp like that east wind, scoopin' folks up like sand in a bag.
