31.text: "Cry all you want, Philistine cities. Smoke comin' from the north. And when it hits? Ain't nobody gon' be missin' they mark."

32.text: What's the message for the world? That God Himself built Zion. And the poor, the outcasts, the overlooked? They safe in Him.

1.text: This the heavy word about Moab: In the dead of night, Ar done got wiped out—gone. Same night, Kir fell too—completely destroyed.

2.text: Moab's runnin' to their temples, cryin' at their altars. They up on Dibon's high places weepin'. They mournin' over Nebo, cryin' over Medeba. Everybody shaved bald, beards cut off—signs of straight-up grief.

3.text: Folks out in the streets rockin' sackcloth. They on rooftops, in the alleyways, Wailin' loud with bitter tears.

4.text: Heshbon and Elealeh join in—they screamin' so loud, folks hear it all the way in Jahaz. Even Moab's soldiers cryin' out now. Life feel too heavy for them to even carry.

5.text: "My heart hurt for Moab," Isaiah says. Their people runnin'—headed for Zoar like scared calves. On the road to Luhith, they goin' up cryin'. On the path to Horonaim, the cry of destruction echo loud.

6.text: Even the waters of Nimrim dried up. Grass dead. Land dead. Nothin' green left.

7.text: All they riches, all that stash they been holdin'? They packin' it up and takin' it with 'em—haulin' it to the Brook of the Willows.

8.text: The scream of Moab stretchin' out to every corner— Eglaim hearin' it, Beer Elim feelin' it.

9.text: Dimon's waters? Drenched in blood. But God said that ain't even the worst of it— He sendin' lions too. Whoever tryna escape Moab's fall? Them lions waitin'. Even the leftovers in the land ain't safe.

1.text: Send a lamb as tribute to Judah's king—from Sela in the wilderness all the way to Mount Zion.

2.text: Moab's daughters gon' be like birds flung from the nest—scared and scattered by the river crossings near Arnon.

3.text: "Yo, take advice, make it make sense. Be a safe shadow in the heat of the day. Hide the outcasts. Don't sell out the ones runnin' for their lives."

4.text: "Let My refugees stay with you, Moab. Be a safe zone from the destruction." 'Cause the oppressor? Done. Devastation? Wrappin' up. The destroyer? Already on his way out.

5.text: A new throne gon' be set up in mercy. Someone legit, sittin' in David's tent, ruling right—judging fair, movin' with speed and righteousness.

6.text: Yeah, we heard about Moab's ego—man got too much pride. Loud, arrogant, angry... But it's all talk. That stuff ain't holdin' up.

7.text: So Moab gon' cry for Moab. Everybody mournin'. Kir Hareseth's foundations? Cracked. The city feelin' that hit hard.

8.text: Heshbon's fields? Dried up. Sibmah's vineyard? Stripped bare. Foreign kings came in and crushed the best vines— They stretched all the way to Jazer, reached through the wilderness, even tryna stretch across the sea.

9.text: And I'm weepin' for Sibmah like Jazer did. Tears floodin' Heshbon and Elealeh. Why? 'Cause war just snatched their harvest. No more summer fruit. No joy in the fields.

10.text: Celebration's canceled. Ain't no music, no harvest songs, no stompin' grapes in the winepress. I personally hit the mute button on all that.

11.text: That's why my heart sound like a sad harp for Moab. Deep down, I feel it for Kir Heres.

12.text: Moab gon' be exhausted—cryin' on high places, runnin' to their idols. But all them prayers? Ain't gon' work. No answers comin'.

13.text: This ain't new. God already spoke this over Moab a while back.

14.text: But now He's stampin' it with a date: "In three years, like a contract with a hired worker, Moab's glory gon' be dust. All that population? Shrunk. All that pride? Gone. What's left? A weak, tiny remnant—barely hangin' on."

1.text: This the message against Damascus: "Look—Damascus gon' stop bein' a city. It's 'bout to be straight ruins."

2.text: Aroer's towns? Ghost towns now. Flocks just chillin' there, sleepin' peaceful. Ain't nobody around to bother 'em.

3.text: No more strongholds in Ephraim. Damascus lost its crown too. Syria gon' fade just like Israel did—temporary glory that didn't last," says the Lord of Heaven's Armies.

4.text: "In that day," God says, "Jacob's shine gon' dim. The fat of the land gon' dry up."

5.text: "It's gon' feel like harvesters cuttin' grain—only a few heads left. Like folks sweepin' the Valley of Rephaim for scraps."

6.text: "A few grapes still hangin'—like when you shake an olive tree and just two or three clingin' to the top branch. That's all that's left," says the Lord God of Israel.

7.text: But in that day, people gon' finally look up—to the One who made 'em. Eyes gon' lock on the Holy One of Israel.

8.text: They ain't gon' be worshipin' idols no more. No more statues, no handmade gods, no incense burnin' to blocks of wood.

9.text: All them cities they used to trust in? Abandoned like a dead tree limb. Left empty. No one comin' back.

10.text: "Why? 'Cause y'all forgot the God who saved y'all. Didn't even check in with the Rock that held you down. You out here plantin' foreign seeds, settin' up nice lil' gardens,

11.text: Tryin' to grow success overnight. But when harvest time hits? It's all rubble. Just pain and sorrow waitin' for you."

12.text: "Woe to all them loud nations—roarin' like ocean waves, Rushin' in deep like floodwaters."

13.text: "Yeah, they sound scary, but I'ma check 'em. God gon' speak, and they gon' scatter like dust on a windy mountain. They gon' roll away like tumbleweeds in a storm."

14.text: "Come evening? Trouble rollin' in. But by sunrise? It's all over. That's what happens to anybody who tried to rob us— That's their fate. That's what they get."

1.text: Woe to that land full of buzzing wings, Way out past the rivers of Ethiopia (Cush),

2.text: The one sendin' out slick ambassadors on papyrus boats, Sayin': "Go, messengers! Go holla at that tall, smooth-skinned nation, That people known for their strength since way back, A nation that been pressin' folks and claimin' territory— Land where rivers slice the land up."

3.text: Listen up, everybody on earth: When God raises His banner up on the mountains—you gon' see it. When He blow that trumpet—you gon' hear it.

4.text: The Lord told me: "I'm chillin'. Watchin' from above. Like the heat shimmerin' on a sunny day, Like morning dew sittin' quiet during harvest."

5.text: But before that harvest hits, Right when the bud lookin' good and the grapes start ripenin'— Snip! God pull out the pruning shears. He cuttin' off branches and takin' 'em down.

6.text: What's left? Birds of prey gon' feast all summer. Beasts of the wild gon' post up all winter. Bodies left in the open—no burial, no honor.

7.text: But hold up— In that time, a gift gon' come to the Lord of Armies. From that same tall, smooth-skinned people, From that same powerful nation that used to strike fear, From the land divided by rivers. And that gift? They bringin' it to Mount Zion, To where God's name stay lifted.

1.text: This the word against Egypt: Look, the Lord ridin' in on a fast cloud, Touchin' down in Egypt like, boom. All them Egyptian idols shakin'. The people's hearts? Meltin' inside they chest.

2.text: "I'ma have Egyptians turn on each other. Brother against brother. Neighbor against neighbor. City fightin' city. Kingdom beefin' with kingdom."

3.text: "Their whole spirit gon' collapse. I'ma shut down all their wisdom. They gon' run to idols, charmers, psychics, and witchcraft for answers."

4.text: "And then I'ma let a cruel master rule over them. A cold king gon' take charge," says the Lord of Heaven's Armies.

5.text: The sea gon' dry up. The river? Wasteland.

6.text: Streams turn nasty. Canals? Dry bones. Reeds and rushes? Dead.

7.text: The papyrus by the Nile? Gone. Crops by the river? Withered up and blown away.

8.text: Fishermen cryin'. Ain't no more hooks in the Nile, no nets workin'.

9.text: The folks who weave fine linens? Embarrassed. Industry shut down.

10.text: The foundation of the hustle—broken. Everybody tryna get a check? Hurtin' deep in they soul.

11.text: Them leaders in Zoan? Dumb. Pharaoh's "wise men"? Givin' foolish advice. Y'all really out here tellin' Pharaoh, "I'm wise. I'm royalty"? Please.

12.text: Where they at now? Tell us, if y'all so smart— What's God plannin' for Egypt?

13.text: Zoan's leaders? Played. Noph's crew? Fooled. These big-time officials led Egypt straight off the cliff.

14.text: God mixed a twisted spirit into the nation, Now they out here movin' like a drunk dude trippin' in his own throw up.

15.text: Ain't nobody workin'. Top or bottom, high or low, palm branch or reed—no jobs.

16.text: That day, Egypt gon' be shaky— Like scared little girls, flinchin' every time God lifts His hand.

17.text: Just hearin' "Judah" gon' make 'em nervous, 'Cause they know what God got planned.

18.text: On that day? Five cities in Egypt gon' speak Hebrew and rep the Lord of Armies. One of 'em gon' be called "The City of Destruction."

19.text: And in the middle of Egypt? An altar to God. At the border? A pillar for the Lord.

20.text: Both gon' be signs—a witness to the Lord in Egypt. When they cry out 'cause they gettin' pressed, God gon' send a Savior. A real one. A Mighty One. He gon' step in and save them.

21.text: That's when Egypt finally gon' know the Lord. They gon' offer Him sacrifice, make vows, and actually keep them.

22.text: God gon' strike them—but He also gon' heal them. They gon' turn back to Him, And He gon' respond with mercy and restoration.

23.text: In that day? A highway from Egypt to Assyria. Egyptians gon' travel to Assyria, Assyrians gon' pull up in Egypt, And they gon' serve God together.

24.text: On that day, it won't just be about Israel. It'll be Egypt, Assyria, and Israel—one squad, A blessing in the middle of the land.

25.text: God gon' bless all three like: "Egypt—My people. Assyria—My handiwork. Israel—My inheritance."

1.text: So in the year Tartan rolled up on Ashdod (Sargon, king of Assyria, sent him to handle business—and he took that city),

2.text: God told Isaiah, "Take off your sackcloth. Slide off your sandals." Isaiah did it—walked around barefoot and straight-up naked.

3.text: Then the Lord said, "Just like Isaiah walked around lookin' wild—naked and barefoot for three whole years as a sign—I'ma let y'all know what's comin' for Egypt and Ethiopia."

4.text: "The king of Assyria gon' snatch up Egyptians and Ethiopians—young and old—walkin' 'em out barefoot, stripped down, exposed. Backs out. Shame on full display."

5.text: The folks who were trustin' in Ethiopia's strength and Egypt's shine? They gon' be embarrassed. Shook.

6.text: And everybody in the region gon' be sayin', "Dang... we really thought they was gon' save us. Now we runnin' talkin' 'bout who gon' help us escape Assyria? If they got taken down like that—what hope we got?"

1.text: Message against the "Wilderness by the Sea": A storm's blowin' in from the desert—hot, wild, violent. Trouble comin' from a rough place.

2.text: This vision hittin' me hard. Betrayers stay betrayin'. Thieves stay robbin'. Elam—get ready. Media—tighten up and attack. God say He finna shut down Babylon's cries.

3.text: Man, this got me twisted up inside. My stomach hurt like labor pains. I was shook when I heard it. I froze when I saw it.

4.text: My heart racin', fear grippin' me. The night I thought would bring peace? Now it got me spooked.

5.text: Set the table, y'all. Post the guards. Feast if you want—but y'all better armor up. Anoint the shield—it's goin' down.

6.text: God told me: "Put a watchman on duty. Tell him to speak what he sees."

7.text: He saw it—a chariot pulled by horses. Donkeys. Camels. Troops movin' in. He watched close.

8.text: Then the watchman cried, "Yo! A lion! I been up on this tower day and night. Eyes open. And now—

9.text: Look, I see them ridin' in!" Then he said: "Babylon done fell. She fell for real. And all her fake gods? Smashed into the dirt."

10.text: My people, the ones threshed like grain— This is what I heard from the Lord of Heaven's Armies, And I'm tellin' it straight to you.

11.text: Message about Dumah (aka Edom): Somebody callin' me from Seir: "Watchman, what's good with the night? What's comin'?"

12.text: I said: "The morning comin', but night ain't over. You got questions? Ask. But you gon' have to come back again."

13.text: Message about Arabia: Y'all nomads from Dedan campin' out in the forest?

14.text: Tema's people—go bring water to the thirsty. Hand bread to them who been runnin'.

15.text: They runnin' from the sword, from war, From drawn bows and destruction.

16.text: The Lord told me: "In one year—just like a hired worker's contract— Kedar's glory gon' fade.

17.text: Them archers, them warriors? Most of 'em gone. God, the Lord of Israel, said it—and He don't miss."

1.text: Message to the Valley of Vision (aka Jerusalem): Why y'all actin' up on the rooftops? What's really goin' on?

2.text: This city loud, turnt up, actin' like it's a celebration— But your people ain't even dyin' in battle. They droppin' in shame.

3.text: Your leaders ran off together, But they got caught—archers got 'em. Folks in the city? Snatched and chained. Didn't matter how far they came from.

4.text: I said, "Man, don't even look at me. I'm cryin' for real. Don't try to comfort me— This is heartbreak for my people."

5.text: This right here a day of confusion, breakdown, and chaos, And it's comin' straight from the Lord God of Heaven's Armies. Walls fallin'. Screams echoin' off the mountains.

6.text: Elam rollin' deep with chariots and bows. Kir showin' up with shields ready.

7.text: The valleys? Full of war gear. Horsemen lined up at your gates.

8.text: God took away Judah's protection. And y'all? Instead of lookin' to Him, You ran to go dig through the royal armory.

9.text: Y'all saw how bad the city of David was hurt. Started collectin' water like it was gonna save you.

10.text: Counted your houses, Tore some down to build up your wall.

11.text: Built a water system between the walls to hold it down… But you ain't look back to the One who made it all. You ain't even acknowledge the One who set this up long ago.

12.text: God was callin' for tears, mourning, humility, People to humble themselves—sackcloth and all.

13.text: But instead? Y'all was out here throwin' parties: Slayin' oxen, grillin' sheep, drinkin' wine, talkin' 'bout: "Let's eat and drink, 'cause tomorrow we dead anyway."

14.text: And God whispered in my ear: "This sin right here? Ain't no forgiveness for it. Not in this life. Not before death." Says the Lord of Hosts.

15.text: The Lord said: "Go talk to Shebna, the dude over the palace. Tell him:

16.text: Who you think you are, carvin' out a fancy tomb for yourself? Like you royalty or somethin'?"

17.text: "Watch this— God gon' grab you up,

18.text: Twist you like a ball, And toss you far out the land. You gon' die out there. All them chariots you flexin'? They gon' be a disgrace to your people."

19.text: "You done. I'm takin' you out your seat, Pullin' you from power."

20.text: "That day, I'ma call Eliakim—son of Hilkiah.

21.text: He gettin' your robe, your belt, your role. I'm handin' him the keys. He gon' lead with heart—like a father to Judah and Jerusalem."

22.text: "I'ma put the key to David's house on his shoulder. If he open it? Can't nobody close it. If he close it? It's closed for real."

23.text: "He gon' be like a strong peg nailed in tight. A whole throne of honor for his fam."

24.text: "All the weight of his household— Every dish, every bowl— It's hangin' on him."

25.text: But even that peg— That strong one? One day it's comin' down. It gon' snap. The burden fall. Because the Lord said so.

1.text: "Cry out, Tarshish ships! Tyre been wiped out—no more houses, no more harbor. Word hit from Cyprus, and folks shook."

2.text: "Be quiet, y'all on the coast—especially you Sidon merchants, livin' off them seafarin' deals."

3.text: "Tyre was makin' bank off grain floatin' in from Egypt, off river harvests—she was everybody's go-to market."

4.text: "Sidon, hang your head. Even the sea speakin' now, sayin': 'I ain't raised no babies or built no future. I ain't birthin' no legacies.'"

5.text: "When Egypt hear the news? They gon' be in deep pain—can't believe Tyre took that L."

6.text: "Run on to Tarshish, coast folks! Start cryin'—your hub just collapsed."

7.text: "Y'all remember how lit Tyre used to be? That ancient city, movin' like royalty? Now she lookin' lost."

8.text: "Who flipped the script on Tyre? The one city where merchants moved like princes and ran the trade game with global respect?"

9.text: "God did. The Lord of Heaven's Armies. He brought down all that pride, all that global glory—turned it into shame."

10.text: "Tarshish, your land gon' be wide open—no more gates, no more might. Just floodin' out."

11.text: "God reached over the sea, shook up whole kingdoms. He gave the word: Canaan's strongholds gotta fall."

12.text: "And He said, 'Sidon, daughter tryna stay pretty while sufferin'? You ain't gon' celebrate no more. Go run to Cyprus—won't be no peace for you there either.'"

13.text: "Look at Babylon—land of the Chaldeans. They wasn't even a thing at first! Assyria built it up just for wild animals to take over later. They raised towers, palaces—then let it fall."

14.text: "Cry out again, ships of Tarshish—your stronghold? Wrecked."

15.text: "And listen, Tyre gon' be forgotten for seventy years—like one king's whole lifetime. But after them years up, she comin' back like the song say…"

16.text: "'Grab your harp, sis—walk the city like an old-school harlot. Play your tunes, sing loud, try to get folks to remember you again.'"

17.text: "After them seventy years, the Lord gon' let Tyre go back to hustlin'—tradin' with every kingdom out there, flirtin' with the whole world again."

18.text: "But this time, her money gon' be holy. She ain't stackin' it up for herself no more—it's all goin' to those who live before the Lord. They gon' eat good and stay fresh in fine clothes."

1.text: Look now—God 'bout to clear the whole earth out. He flippin' the land upside down and scatterin' everybody everywhere.

2.text: Don't matter who you are—priest or people, servant or master, employee or boss, buyer or seller, lender or borrower—ain't nobody exempt.

3.text: The whole land gon' be emptied out and looted. Why? 'Cause God said so. Period.

4.text: The earth mournin' and dryin' up. The world lookin' weak. Even the ones who thought they was on top feelin' it now.

5.text: Earth messed up 'cause of the folks in it—they broke God's rules, switched up the order, and disrespected the eternal covenant.

6.text: That's why the curse eatin' up the land, and folks feelin' the heat. Burned out. Only a few gon' be left standin'.

7.text: Ain't no more turnin' up—wine runnin' out, vines dyin', and happy folks out here groanin'.

8.text: The tambourines done gone quiet. The party noise done stopped. Ain't no more joy in them instruments.

9.text: Don't nobody even wanna sip no more—the liquor got a bitter aftertaste. Ain't no vibes.

10.text: The city confused and broke down. Houses boarded up—ain't nobody comin' in or out.

11.text: Folks out in the streets cryin' for wine, but joy gone. The whole land just heavy now.

12.text: City's a ghost town. Even the gate fallin' apart.

13.text: What's left of the people? They like the last olives clingin' to a tree or a couple grapes missed in the harvest. Just scraps.

14.text: But even in all this, a few gon' raise they voice and praise God from far away.

15.text: So go 'head and glorify the Lord in the early light—shout His name from the coastlines and across the seas.

16.text: From every corner of the earth, we hear it: "Glory to the righteous!" But me? I'm wrecked. Woe to me. These folks out here movin' foul—backstabbin' on a whole 'nother level.

17.text: Fear, traps, and pits waitin' on y'all, people of the earth. Ain't no escape.

18.text: You run from fear? You fall in a pit. Climb out that pit? Boom—you caught in a trap. Heaven openin' up, earth's foundation shakin' like it can't hold on.

19.text: The earth breakin' down bad. Split wide open. Shakin' like it's in a full-on meltdown.

20.text: It's wobblin' like a drunk, leanin' like a raggedy shack. All that sin weighin' it down—it's fallin' and ain't gettin' back up.

21.text: When that day hit, God comin' for the big shots—both heavenly and earthly. Ain't nobody safe.

22.text: They gon' be rounded up like inmates, locked down in the pit. After a while, the judgment still gon' hit.

23.text: Even the moon and sun gon' be embarrassed when God shows up in glory—reignin' from Zion, holdin' court in Jerusalem, lookin' majestic in front of His people.

1.text: Lord, You my God. I'ma lift You up, praise Your name, 'cause You been doin' big things. Everything You planned back then? Faithful and true, no cap.

2.text: You turned a whole city into rubble. That stronghold? Gone. That foreign palace? Ain't never comin' back.

3.text: That's why even strong nations gon' respect You. Big cities that used to act scary? They gon' fear You now.

4.text: You been a shelter for the broke and hurting. A safe spot in the storm. A cool shade in the heat. When the loud and wild ones tried it, You held it down like a strong wall.

5.text: You gon' shut them noisy oppressors up—like heat disappearing when a cloud rolls in. Their song? Fadin' out.

6.text: And right here on this mountain, the Lord gon' throw a feast for everybody. We talkin' rich food, real wine, no cheap stuff—choice cuts, full flavor, perfectly aged.

7.text: On this mountain, He takin' off the cover that been blockin' all the people. That heavy veil over the nations? Ripped away.

8.text: Death? He swallowin' it whole. Tears? Wiped from every face. Shame? Gone from His people—all across the earth. God done said it, and that's that.

9.text: In that day folks gon' say, "This right here is our God! We waited on Him, and He showed up! This the Lord! We waited, and now we rejoicin'—He saved us for real!"

10.text: God's hand gon' rest right here on this mountain. But Moab? He gon' stomp them down like straw gettin' trampled in a dirty pile.

11.text: They gon' reach out tryin' to swim through it, flailin' around—but He gon' drag that pride down. All them slick schemes they hands cooked up? Shut down.

12.text: That big ol' fortress wall? God knockin' it flat. Layin' it down in the dust—ain't gon' be nothin' left standin'.

1.text: On that day, Judah gon' be singin': "We got a strong city! God set up salvation like walls and defense all around us."

2.text: "Open up the gates—let the real ones in. The folks that stay true, that hold tight to God's ways."

3.text: You keep folks in perfect peace when they keep they mind on You—'cause they trust You for real.

4.text: Keep trustin' the Lord forever. In the Lord—Yah Himself—we got everlasting strength.

5.text: He brings down the high and mighty—the ones sittin' up in them lofty cities. He drop 'em to the ground, all the way to the dirt.

6.text: The poor and the lowly gon' step on what used to be high places. They walkin' on what used to walk on them.

7.text: God, You make the way straight for the ones who live right. You keep they steps steady and sure.

8.text: Lord, we been waitin' on You while You was movin' in judgment. Our soul just want Your name, Your presence, Your memory.

9.text: Even at night, I'm longin' for You. My spirit searchin' early. When You move in justice, the whole world gon' learn how to do right.

10.text: Even when You show the wicked grace, they still don't wanna act right. In a land full of righteousness, they still play dirty and ignore Your glory.

11.text: Lord, even when Your hand is lifted up, they act like they can't see it. But they gon' see eventually—shame gon' hit 'em hard. Jealousy gon' burn, and Your fire gon' finish what it started.

12.text: Lord, You the one who brings us peace. Every good thing we ever did—You was the one behind it.

13.text: God, other masters had us in chains before, but we only speak Your name now. You the only one we honor.

14.text: Them old rulers? Dead and gone. They not comin' back. You wiped them out and erased the memory of 'em.

15.text: You been growin the nation, Lord. You done made Your name big. You stretched the borders and showed out.

16.text: When times got hard, we came runnin' back to You. We poured our hearts out when You checked us.

17.text: We was like a woman in labor—cryin', strugglin', waitin' for the promise to come.

18.text: But all we gave birth to was wind. No breakthrough, no deliverance. The world stayed stuck, and we couldn't fix it.

19.text: But You said the dead gon' live. Our people who sleepin' in the dust gon' rise up. Wake up and sing, y'all—God's breath is like fresh dew, and the ground gon' give up the dead.

20.text: Come on, My people. Get inside, shut your doors, hide for a little while. Let God's anger pass through.

21.text: 'Cause the Lord steppin' out. He comin' to handle what's been done in secret. The earth gon' tell it all—every bit of blood spilled, every wrong that's been buried? It's all comin' to light.

1.text: When that day hit, the Lord gon' swing His heavy sword—sharp, strong, and mighty. He takin' down Leviathan, that slippery, twisty serpent. That sea monster? Yeah, God gon' finish it off.

2.text: On that day, somebody gon' start singin': "This right here is God's vineyard, red with new wine!"

3.text: The Lord say, "I'm the one who watches over her. I water her all the time. I don't let nobody mess with her—I'm on guard 24/7."

4.text: "Ain't no fury in Me. But if somebody try to throw thorns at Me, come at Me sideways? I'll burn it all down quick."

5.text: "But if they just grab hold of My strength, make peace with Me? Then we good. They can live in peace with Me."

6.text: God gon' help His people grow deep roots in Jacob. Israel gon' bloom, flourish, and spread fruit all over the world.

7.text: Did God hit Israel like He hit the nations that hit them? Nah. Did He wipe them out like He did the enemies? Nope.

8.text: God dealt with them gently, in doses. Like a strong wind He sent them away, but it wasn't to destroy—it was to correct.

9.text: That's how He gon' erase Jacob's guilt. That's the result of their sins gettin' removed: they gon' smash their altars to pieces—ain't no more idols standin' after that.

10.text: The cities that was once strong? Empty. Ain't nobody livin' there. Cows just chillin' where folks used to live, munchin' on the ruins.

11.text: The trees dried up, branches broken off. Women gatherin' 'em to burn. That's 'cause the people ain't got no sense. The One who made 'em ain't showin' 'em no mercy 'til they get it right.

12.text: But hold up—when that day come, the Lord gon' sweep the land like He threshin' wheat—from the Euphrates to the border of Egypt. And He gon' gather His people back, one by one.

13.text: A big ol' trumpet gon' sound off. Folks who was lost in Assyria, outcasts in Egypt—they gon' come back. They gon' show up in Jerusalem, worshippin' the Lord on His holy mountain.

1.text: Woe to y'all up in Ephraim, drunk off pride and liquor, rockin' that crown like you all that—y'all beauty fadin' fast like a flower on a hot day. Y'all sittin' high in them valleys, but y'all slippin'.

2.text: Look, the Lord ain't playin'. He got somebody strong comin'—like a hailstorm, a flood that don't quit. He finna slam y'all down with His own hand.

3.text: That proud crown the drunk folks in Ephraim rockin'? It's gon' be stomped on.

4.text: That glory they flexin'? Gon' fade like flowers. It's like a juicy grape picked too early—soon as somebody see it, they grab it and it's gone.

5.text: But when that day come, the Lord of Heaven's Armies gon' be the real crown of glory, shinin' for the leftovers, the faithful ones.

6.text: He gon' give justice to the judges, and power to the folks who stand strong at the gate, holdin' the line.

7.text: But even the priests and prophets drunk too. Wine got 'em twisted. They lost in the sauce, can't see straight, can't judge right.

8.text: The tables they sittin' at? Filthy. Vomit everywhere. Ain't a clean spot in sight.

9.text: And God's like, "Who I'ma teach? Babies fresh off milk? Toddlers just off the bottle?"

10.text: But they gotta learn slow—precept by precept, line by line, lil' here, lil' there.

11.text: So God gon' speak to 'em through foreign lips, other tongues, tryin' to get through to 'em.

12.text: He told 'em, "This the rest y'all need, this the peace I'm offerin'." But they ain't wanna listen.

13.text: So the Word hit 'em like this: Precept on precept, line on line, here a lil' there a lil'. But instead of growin', they trip and fall back. Now they trapped.

14.text: So hear this, y'all smug leaders in Jerusalem—the ones jokin' while runnin' the people into the ground:

15.text: Y'all think y'all got a deal with death? A pact with the grave? Y'all think y'all safe when disaster hits 'cause y'all hid behind lies and built bunkers of deception?

16.text: But the Lord God say, "Nah. I'm layin' a foundation in Zion—a tested stone, precious and solid. Whoever trusts in it ain't gon' panic."

17.text: God gon' measure with justice and righteousness. Lies? Gon' get swept away like floodwater. All that fake stuff? Exposed.

18.text: That contract y'all got with death? Void. That deal with the grave? Canceled. When the flood hits, y'all gettin' washed too.

19.text: Every time it sweeps by, it's takin' y'all. Mornin', night, over and over. Just hearin' 'bout it gon' give y'all chills.

20.text: The bed too short, y'all can't stretch out. The blanket too small, can't even cover up.

21.text: The Lord gon' rise up like He did at Perazim, wild like back in Gibeon. He comin' to do His strange, surprising work—judgment y'all ain't ready for.

22.text: So stop playin'! Don't keep mockin' or y'all chains gon' get tighter. I done heard from the Lord—destruction is comin' for the whole earth.

23.text: Now listen up—lean in and hear what I'm sayin'.

24.text: Does a farmer keep plowin' forever? Nah, he turns the soil, breaks it up, and then moves on.

25.text: When it's ready, he plants black cumin, cumin, wheat, barley, spelt—each in its own lane, all in order.

26.text: 'Cause God teaches him how to do it right. It's all divine wisdom.

27.text: You don't beat black cumin like you thresh wheat. It gets tapped with a stick. Cumin gets hit with a rod.

28.text: Bread flour gotta be ground down—but you don't crush it forever. Ain't no need to wreck the thing with wheels and horses.

29.text: This all comes from the Lord of Heaven's Armies. He's wise with His plans and flawless in how He guides.

1.text: Woe to Ariel—yeah, Ariel, the city where King David used to walk. Go 'head, keep countin' the years, keep havin' your lil' feasts.

2.text: But I'm gon' press you, Ariel. You gon' feel the weight. It's gon' get heavy with sorrow. But to Me? You still gon' be Ariel—My altar, My fire.

3.text: I'ma post up all around you, set up camp, dig in with trenches, build up walls—yeah, I'm comin' for you.

4.text: You gon' be brought low—real low. Talkin' from the dirt like whispers from the grave. Your voice gon' sound like you speakin' through dust.

5.text: And all them enemies comin' for you? Poof. Gone like fine powder in the wind. Them haters? Gon' blow away like ash. All that? Gon' shift in a second.

6.text: The Lord of Heaven's Armies gon' check y'all with thunder, earthquakes, loud noise, storms, hurricanes, and fire that don't quit.

7.text: All them nations tryin' to gang up on Ariel? They gon' vanish like a dream you can't remember.

8.text: It's gon' be like somebody dreamin' they eatin', but wake up still hungry. Or drinkin' in a dream, but wake up dry and thirsty. That's how all them nations gon' feel after tryin' to take Zion—empty and unsatisfied.

9.text: Y'all better stop and look. Be amazed—but y'all blind now. Y'all stumbling, not 'cause you drunk on wine, but 'cause your spirit off.

10.text: God done hit y'all with deep sleep. He shut the eyes of y'all prophets, put covers over the seers.

11.text: Now the whole vision like a sealed book. You hand it to someone who can read and say, "Hey, read this," but they like, "I can't—it's sealed."

12.text: Then you hand it to someone who can't read and say, "Read this," and they like, "I don't even know how."

13.text: So God say: "These folks talk like they close to Me, but their hearts? Way off. They honor Me with their mouths, but they just follow rules taught by people—not Me."

14.text: So I'ma shake things up again. Gon' do something wild—blow y'all minds. Them so-called wise men? Gon' lose their wisdom. All that knowledge? Vanish.

15.text: Woe to the ones tryin' to hide their moves from God, thinkin' they slick in the dark—like, "Ain't nobody seein' me. Ain't nobody knowin'."

16.text: Uh-uh, y'all flipped it all backwards. The clay don't tell the potter, "You ain't make me." The creation can't clown the Creator talkin' 'bout, "He don't know nothin'."

17.text: But don't trip—it ain't gon' be long. Lebanon gon' be like fertile fields again. Them fields gon' rise up like forests.

18.text: In that day, even the deaf gon' hear the words in the book. The blind gon' see light bustin' through their darkness.

19.text: The humble gon' have real joy in the Lord, and the poor gon' celebrate the Holy One of Israel.

20.text: The bullies? Done. The mockers? Canceled. And the folks always lookin' to catch somebody slippin'? They out.

21.text: The ones tryna trap people with their words, tryna get folks in trouble just for speakin' truth—God gon' deal with them too.

22.text: So the Lord who saved Abraham got a word for Jacob's fam: "Jacob ain't gotta be ashamed no more. Ain't gotta hide his face in shame."

23.text: When he sees his kids—My handiwork—he gon' honor My name. They gon' lift up the Holy One of Jacob and revere the God of Israel.

24.text: Even the ones who been lost in the sauce gon' catch some wisdom. The complainers? They finna learn for real.

1.text: "Woe to my hard-headed children," says the Lord. "Y'all makin' plans without checkin' in with Me. Y'all movin' in your own spirit, not Mine—stackin' sin on top of sin.

2.text: Runnin' off to Egypt lookin' for backup, without even askin' Me first. Trustin' Pharaoh like he got you covered. Believin' Egypt gon' keep you safe in the shadows.

3.text: But Pharaoh's 'strength'? That's gon' be your embarrassment. Egypt's protection? That's gon' be your downfall.

4.text: Look, his crew sittin' in Zoan, his messengers posted in Hanes—

5.text: And what good did they do you? Nada. Egypt ain't bring no help. Just shame and disappointment."

6.text: This the word on the wild south: trouble, danger, lions and serpents on the road. And here y'all go haulin' riches on donkeys, gold on camels—draggin' treasure to folks who can't do nothin' for you.

7.text: Egypt? Ain't worth it. Helpin' in vain. I call her "Rahab Who Just Sits There"—all bark, no bite.

8.text: God said, "Write it down. Put it on the record. Don't let 'em forget this."

9.text: "These folks rebellious—straight-up liars. They won't even listen when I speak.

10.text: They tell the prophets, 'Stop tellin' us the truth! We want smooth talk—tell us somethin' nice. Lie if you got to.'

11.text: 'Move out the way. Don't bring that Holy One of Israel talk to us no more.'"

12.text: So the Lord, the Holy One, says: "Since y'all reject My word and put your trust in oppression and crookedness,

13.text: You gon' fall like a cracked wall—one good shake, and boom—it all comes down, quick.

14.text: And when it falls, it's gon' shatter like a clay pot, no piece big enough to scoop a coal or dip out water."

15.text: The Lord God said: "Your salvation was always in returning to Me, in quiet rest and trust. That's where your strength was." But nah—you ain't want that.

16.text: Y'all said, "Nah, we ridin' out on horses!" Alright, then ride. But your enemies gon' be even faster.

17.text: A thousand of y'all gon' run from one enemy. Five folks chase y'all down till only one pole standin' on a hill, waivin' like a white flag.

18.text: But God? He waitin'. Waitin' to show y'all grace. He still gon' be exalted—still full of mercy. The Lord is fair. Blessed are the ones who just wait on Him.

19.text: Y'all gon' live in Zion again, and no more tears. He'll hear you when you cry—and answer.

20.text: Even when you go through hard times—eatin' the bread of pain and drinkin' struggle—your teachers won't be hidden no more. You gon' see clearly.

21.text: And you gon' hear a voice behind you sayin', "This the way. Walk in it," whether you turn left or right.

22.text: You gon' throw away your idols like trash—silver and gold images? Gone. You gon' be like, "Ugh! Get this mess outta here!"

23.text: Then God gon' send rain for your seeds. Your land gon' give you big harvests. Your cattle gon' eat good in wide pastures.

24.text: Even your work animals gon' get fancy feed—clean, sifted grain.

25.text: Streams gon' flow from every mountain on the day when the towers fall and the enemy gets crushed.

26.text: The moon gon' shine like the sun. The sun? Seven times brighter—like a full week of daylight in one. That's when God starts patchin' y'all up, healin' the wounds.

27.text: Look! The name of the Lord comin' from far off, burnin' with anger. His words heavy, His mouth full of fire,

28.text: His breath like a flood reachin' high—siftin' nations like flour, puttin' a bit in their mouths to steer 'em off course.

29.text: But you? You gon' have a praise song, like festival nights, like a joyful march to the mountain of God, with music in your soul.

30.text: God gon' speak LOUD. His arm comin' down with power—fire, storm, and hail. You gon' feel it.

31.text: Assyria? They gon' get beat just from hearin' His voice.

32.text: Every strike God land? It'll come with tambourines and harps playin'. A whole divine beatdown, but with rhythm.

33.text: That fire pit called Tophet? Already built—real deep and wide. Plenty of firewood. The Lord's breath gon' light it up like a blast of hot sulfur.

1.text: Woe to the ones runnin' down to Egypt for help. Trustin' in horses 'cause they deep, Relyin' on chariots 'cause they flashy, Thinkin' them riders strong enough to save them— But ain't even lookin' up to the Holy One of Israel. Ain't even tryna check in with the Lord.

2.text: But God? He ain't slow, He wise. He gon' bring the smoke, and His word ain't comin' back empty. He gon' stand up against the evildoers And the folks givin' them shady help.

3.text: Egypt? They just people—not God. Their horses? Made of flesh—not spirit. So when God stretch out His hand, Both the one helpin' and the one bein' helped? They both gon' fall. All of 'em goin' down together.

4.text: The Lord said, "When I pull up, it's gon' be like a lion standin' over its prey— Growlin' deep, unbothered. Let the shepherds make noise if they want to, I ain't moved. I ain't scared. I'm fightin' for Mount Zion. I'm fightin' for My people."

5.text: Just like birds swoopin' down to protect their nest, That's how the Lord gon' guard Jerusalem. He'll defend it, deliver it, and cover it— Won't let it fall.

6.text: Y'all need to turn back to the One y'all turned your back on— Y'all done did Him dirty for real.

7.text: But when that day hit, Everybody gon' toss them gold and silver idols like garbage. All that mess y'all made with your own hands? Gone.

8.text: Assyria gon' fall— Not by some regular man's sword, But by a sword they ain't ready for. They gon' run, Their soldiers gon' be forced to work like slaves.

9.text: Their leader? He gon' be shook, retreatin' to his fortress. His top men? Terrified of the banner—terrified of God's presence. The Lord speaks: "My fire burnin' in Zion, And My furnace stay lit in Jerusalem."

1.text: Look, a real King gon' step up and rule right, And His crew? They gon' lead with justice, not just titles.

2.text: That kind of man gon' be like shelter from the storm, Like water in a dry place, Like shade when the sun out here doin' the most— Peace in a wild world.

3.text: Folks gon' start seein' clearly, no more blind eyes. And ears? They actually gon' listen.

4.text: Even the reckless hearts gon' slow down and learn, And the ones who used to stutter? They gon' speak truth clear and bold.

5.text: You ain't gon' see fools gettin' called "generous" no more, And stingy folks won't be fakin' like they got good hearts.

6.text: 'Cause fools talk nonsense, They stay up to no good— Doin' dirty in the name of God, Letting the hungry stay hungry, And blockin' folks from gettin' even a sip.

7.text: The shady ones? Always plottin' on the poor, Lyin' just to keep them down, Even when the needy speak truth.

8.text: But the one with a real heart? He stay thinkin' up ways to bless others, And his blessings gon' keep him solid.

9.text: Y'all chillin' too hard— You women sittin' easy, listen up. Complacent daughters? This message for you too.

10.text: In just over a year, Y'all gon' feel that pressure— No grapes, no harvest, no good times.

11.text: Shake in your boots, you laid-back ladies. Take off the glam, throw on sackcloth, It's mourning season.

12.text: Folks gon' beat their chests in sorrow 'Cause the good fields dry up, Ain't no fruit on the vine.

13.text: The land? Gon' be filled with thorns and mess. Even the spots that used to be poppin'—quiet.

14.text: Mansions left empty, City vibes gone, It's just wild donkeys and sheep hangin' out now.

15.text: But hold up— When the Spirit comes down from on high, That desert gon' bloom. The dry field gon' turn lush, And the lush gon' grow like a forest.

16.text: Justice gon' set up camp in them dry places, And righteousness? It's gon' live out in the new growth.

17.text: When righteousness does its thing, It brings peace— Not just quiet, but that deep-down, ain't-worried kinda peace.

18.text: My people gon' live in real safety, Homes locked down with rest and calm vibes.

19.text: Even if the storm hits and takes down the forest, And the city takes a hit too— We gon' still be good.

20.text: Blessed are the ones sowin' seeds by every stream, Lettin' the ox and donkey roam free, 'Cause they ain't scared to keep it movin' and keep it flowin'.

1.text: Woe to you shady folks— You been robbin' folks, but ain't never been robbed yourself. You double-crossin' people, But soon as you stop? They gon' double-cross you right back.

2.text: Lord, come through for us. We been waitin' on You. Be our strength every morning, Our way out when trouble shows up.

3.text: When the chaos hit, folks gon' run scared. The moment You rise up? Nations gon' scatter like roaches when the lights cut on.

4.text: The stuff they stole? Gon' get picked clean— Like locusts sweepin' through a field.

5.text: God sittin' high and lifted— He posted up in heaven. Zion full of justice and right now 'cause of Him.

6.text: Wisdom and knowledge? That's your real security these days. Salvation your foundation. And fearin' the Lord? That's the real treasure.

7.text: Even the bravest out here cryin' in the streets. The peace-talkers got nothin' but tears.

8.text: Ain't nobody out on the roads. Travelin' man shut down. The agreements? Broken. Cities? Disrespected. People? Don't even matter no more.

9.text: The whole land lookin' dry and tired. Lebanon embarrassed, Sharon dry like desert. Bashan and Carmel done dropped all they fruit.

10.text: "Now it's My time," says the Lord. "I'ma stand up. I'ma show y'all who I really am."

11.text: Y'all been breathin' in lies and schemin'— You gon' birth nothin' but ashes. Yo own words? They gon' set you on fire.

12.text: Folks gon' burn up like lime in a fire pit. Like dry thorns—they gone.

13.text: Listen up! Y'all far away—hear what I did. Y'all close by—respect My power.

14.text: Even Zion's sinners shook now. The fake ones tremblin', askin': "Who can survive God's heat? Who can stand in this everlasting blaze?"

15.text: Only the ones walkin' right, Talkin' truth, Not takin' dirty money, Not listenin' to violence, Not watchin' evil.

16.text: That one? He safe— Gon' live high up in a strong fortress. He won't lack nothin'—bread steady, water sure.

17.text: You gon' see the King in all His beauty. And the land ahead? It's wide and full of promise.

18.text: Your heart gon' think back like, "Man, remember when we was scared? Where them tax men at? Where the enemy countin' our defenses?"

19.text: You won't see them wild people no more— No more confusing tongues, no more threats you don't even understand.

20.text: Look at Zion, God's city of feasts. Your eyes gon' see Jerusalem— Peaceful, steady, can't be moved. A tent that don't collapse, With ropes and stakes that don't snap.

21.text: That's where God gon' be our everything— A river too wide for enemy ships. No boats creepin' in. No sneak attacks.

22.text: 'Cause the Lord is our Judge. The Lord writes the laws. The Lord is our King. He the one who gon' save us.

23.text: The enemy ships? Can't even raise their sails. Their ropes loose, their gear busted. And all that treasure they tried to hold? Even the folks who was limpin' gon' snatch it up.

24.text: And the people livin' there? Ain't nobody talkin' 'bout "I'm sick" no more— 'Cause they sins forgiven. They good now.

1.text: Yo, all y'all nations—come close and listen. Everybody on earth, pay attention. This message ain't just for some—it's for the whole world.

2.text: God mad. Not just a little upset—He full-on furious with every nation out here. He ain't sparin' nobody. He already decided—they done for.

3.text: Bodies gon' be everywhere, tossed out. The stench? It's gon' be awful. Mountains soaked in blood—like the land itself cryin'.

4.text: Even the skies gon' break down. The stars gon' fall like old leaves off a vine, Or like figs droppin' off a tree in the wind.

5.text: God said, "My sword done been sharpened in heaven, Now it's comin' for Edom— Them folks I done marked for destruction."

6.text: That sword? It's drippin' with blood, Soaked with fat from the offerings— Lambs, goats, rams— 'Cause God holdin' court in Bozrah, And the whole land of Edom gon' be a slaughterhouse.

7.text: Even the wild bulls gon' fall with the regular ones. Blood gon' flood the land, And the dirt gon' be greasy with fat.

8.text: Why? 'Cause this the day God finally settin' the record straight. Zion's pain ain't been forgotten. This the year God get payback for all the hurt they took.

9.text: Edom gon' be cursed land now. Rivers turn to black tar, Dust turn to burning sulfur. The whole joint gon' be on fire.

10.text: And it won't stop. That fire gon' burn day and night— Smoke risin' forever. Nobody livin' there again. No foot traffic.

11.text: Only creatures like pelicans, porcupines, owls, and ravens Gon' call it home now. God usin' a blueprint of chaos And bricks of emptiness to rebuild it— A whole redesign of destruction.

12.text: Ain't no royalty gon' be left. The princes? Gone. The throne? Empty. They ain't got no shot at comin' back.

13.text: Thorns takin' over palaces. Brambles where mansions used to be. Jackals movin' in. Ostriches takin' walks through what used to be fortresses.

14.text: Wild animals linkin' up—jackals and desert beasts chillin'. Goats callin' out to each other. Even night creatures settlin' in like, "Yeah, this our spot now."

15.text: Snakes layin' eggs, nesting, hatchin', Keepin' their babies in the shadows. Even hawks gon' post up there—each one findin' her match.

16.text: Look it up in the Book. Ain't none of this gon' miss. Every piece gon' fall in place—just like God said. His Spirit already called the roll and gave 'em the land.

17.text: God divvied it up Himself. Measured it with His own hand. Now it's theirs—forever. That land? Gon' stay cursed and inhabited by beasts for all generations.

1.text: That dry land? Yeah, even the wilderness gon' be hype for what's comin'. The desert gon' rejoice like it just got a fresh rain. It's gon' bloom like roses outta concrete.

2.text: Flowers poppin' up everywhere, joy bustin' out with songs. Lebanon's glory, Carmel's beauty, Sharon's shine— All that splendor gon' be right there. They gon' see the glory of the Lord, How excellent our God really is.

3.text: Tell the ones whose hands weak, Whose knees be shakin': "Stand tall. Hold ya head up."

4.text: Say to the ones scared deep down, "Don't trip. Don't be afraid. God comin' for real this time— And He not just showin' up, He bringin' vengeance. He comin' to settle all accounts. He gon' save y'all."

5.text: Then the blind? They gon' see. The deaf? Ears wide open.

6.text: Folks who couldn't walk? They gon' leap like deer. And folks who ain't had no voice? They gon' sing loud. 'Cause water gon' bust out in dry places, Rivers showin' up where the desert used to rule.

7.text: Cracked ground turnin' into swimming holes. Thirsty land overflowin' with springs. The same spots jackals used to prowl? Now it's grass, reeds, and fresh life.

8.text: And there's gon' be a road runnin' through it— Called the Highway of Holiness. No mess allowed on this road—no foulness, no foolishness. Even if you ain't the smartest one walkin' it, You won't get lost.

9.text: Ain't no lions prowlin'. No wild beasts lurkin'. Only the ones God redeemed walk this road.

10.text: God's people—the ones He paid for—they comin' home. Marchin' to Zion with songs in their mouths And forever-joy on they heads. They gon' be full of gladness, And sorrow? Gone. Sighin'? Outta there. Just joy. Nothing but joy.

1.text: In the 14th year of King Hezekiah's reign, Sennacherib, king of Assyria, rolled up on all Judah's fortified cities and straight took 'em.

2.text: Then he sent his mouthpiece—the Rabshakeh—from Lachish to Jerusalem, with a whole squad behind him. They posted up at the aqueduct near the road to Fuller's Field.

3.text: Eliakim (Hilkiah's son), Shebna the secretary, and Joah (Asaph's boy, the historian) stepped out to meet him.

4.text: The Rabshakeh started poppin' off: "Tell Hezekiah this—straight from the so-called 'great king,' the king of Assyria: Why y'all so confident? Who gassed y'all up?"

5.text: "Y'all talkin' like y'all got strategy and muscle for war—but it's just talk. Who you even trustin' to make you think you can step to us?"

6.text: "Oh, you leanin' on Egypt? That weak stick? That cracked cane? If you put weight on that, it's just gon' stab through your hand. That's Pharaoh for you—he'll let down anybody who leans on him."

7.text: "Now if you tryna say, 'We trust in the Lord our God,' Ain't Hezekiah the same dude who tore down His altars and high places, And told y'all to only worship at this one altar in Jerusalem?"

8.text: "I'll even give y'all 2,000 horses right now… If y'all got enough men to even ride them. (Spoiler: You don't.)"

9.text: "If you can't even take one of our lowest-ranking soldiers, What makes you think Egypt gon' come save you with chariots and riders?"

10.text: "And let me tell you this: You think I came here without the Lord? Nah. He told me Himself— 'Go up against this land and wreck it.'"

11.text: Then Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah stepped in like, "Yo, speak in Aramaic. We understand you. Don't talk Hebrew in front of these people on the wall."

12.text: Rabshakeh was like, "Man, y'all think this message is just for y'all? Nah. The folks sittin' on that wall— They the ones who gon' suffer, Eatin' their own waste and drinkin' their own piss with y'all."

13.text: Then he yelled even louder, talkin' Hebrew now: "Listen up, Jerusalem! Hear the word of the great king of Assyria!"

14.text: "Don't let Hezekiah lie to y'all! He can't save you. Period."

15.text: "Don't let him gas you with that 'God gon' save us' talk. This city ain't safe."

16.text: "Here's what my king says: Make peace with me. Bring me a gift. Come out now, and you can eat off your own vines and fig trees, Drink from your own wells."

17.text: "That is… until I take y'all to a new place— Just like this one, but better: Grain, wine, bread, vineyards… A sweet setup."

18.text: "But don't let Hezekiah play y'all, sayin', 'The Lord gon' deliver us.' Ain't none of the gods of the other nations saved their lands from me."

19.text: "Where the gods of Hamath and Arpad at? What about Sepharvaim? Did any of them stop me from takin' Samaria?"

20.text: "If all them gods couldn't stop me, Why y'all think the Lord gon' deliver Jerusalem?"

21.text: But the folks didn't say nothin'. Not a word. King Hezekiah had made it clear: "Don't respond to him."

22.text: So Eliakim, Shebna, and Joah tore their clothes in grief, Went back to Hezekiah, And told him everything Rabshakeh said.

1.text: When King Hezekiah heard what was goin' down, he tore his clothes, threw on some sackcloth, and went straight to God's house.

2.text: He sent Eliakim (his house manager), Shebna (the scribe), and the elders of the priests—all wearin' sackcloth too—to go holla at the prophet Isaiah, son of Amoz.

3.text: They told Isaiah, "This day right here is full of pain, shame, and disrespect. It's like a woman tryna give birth but she too weak to push.

4.text: Maybe the Lord your God gon' hear the trash the Rabshakeh talked—the stuff the king of Assyria sent him to say against the livin' God—and God gon' check him for it. So please pray for the folks who still hangin' on."

5.text: Hezekiah's people gave Isaiah the message.

6.text: Isaiah replied, "Tell Hezekiah this: God said, 'Don't be shook by what you heard. Those dudes talkin' reckless? I heard 'em.

7.text: I'ma stir the king of Assyria's spirit, make him hear somethin' that'll send him runnin' back home—and when he gets there, he gon' get taken out with the sword.' "

8.text: The Rabshakeh dipped and found his king fightin' at Libnah, since he had left Lachish.

9.text: Word came that Tirhakah, the king of Ethiopia, was comin' to fight him. So Sennacherib sent another message to Hezekiah:

10.text: "Don't let your God play you, talkin' about 'Jerusalem won't fall into my hands.'

11.text: You heard what I did to everybody else—wiped 'em out! You think you different?

12.text: Their gods ain't save them: Gozan, Haran, Rezeph, Eden in Telassar—gone!

13.text: What happened to the kings of Hamath, Arpad, Sepharvaim, Hena, and Ivah? Exactly."

14.text: Hezekiah took that letter, read it, and went back to God's house. He laid it out right there in front of the Lord.

15.text: He prayed:

16.text: "Lord of Heaven's armies, God of Israel, chillin' between the cherubim—you God all by Yourself. Ain't no other. You made heaven and earth.

17.text: Please listen, Lord. Look at this! Hear what Sennacherib said—he tryin' You, the livin' God!

18.text: Yeah, he really did wipe out them other nations, no cap.

19.text: And he threw their gods in the fire—but that's 'cause they weren't really gods! Just man-made—wood and stone. So of course they ain't save nobody.

20.text: But Lord, we different. Please save us, so everybody out there will know—You alone are God."

21.text: Isaiah sent word back: "Because you prayed, Hezekiah, here's what the Lord says:

22.text: Zion—God's daughter—laughin' at that clown. Jerusalem just shook her head like, 'Boy, bye.'

23.text: Who you really think you was talkin' to? You raised your voice at God. You mocked the Holy One of Israel.

24.text: You bragged about your army, said you was gon' climb mountains, chop down Lebanon's best trees, take over forests and springs.

25.text: You said you drank up rivers and stomped through defenses like it was nothin'.

26.text: But hold up—I planned all that long ago. You just fulfillin' My will. You was supposed to knock over cities—I let that happen.

27.text: Their folks were weak anyway, like dry grass or rooftop weeds. They ain't stand a chance.

28.text: But I know where you stay. I know when you move. I know you mad.

29.text: And since your rage came up in My face, I'ma put My hook in your nose, My bridle in your mouth, and send you right back the way you came."

30.text: "Here's your sign: This year, y'all gon' eat whatever grows on its own. Next year too. But the third year? Plant, reap, and enjoy.

31.text: And the ones left in Judah? They gon' take root and grow strong again."

32.text: "Out of Jerusalem, a remnant gon' rise. Outta Zion, survivors will step forward. The Lord's passion gon' make it happen."

33.text: "So here's the deal about that Assyrian king: He not even gon' step foot in this city. He won't shoot no arrows, Won't hold no shields up, Won't build no siege ramps.

34.text: He leavin' the same way he came. He not comin' in here," says the Lord.

35.text: "I'ma protect this city, not for y'all— But for Me and My servant David."

36.text: That night, the angel of the Lord showed up and wiped out 185,000 Assyrian soldiers. When folks woke up? Bodies everywhere.

37.text: So Sennacherib bounced back to Nineveh, tail tucked.

38.text: But while he was worshipin' his fake god Nisroch, two of his own sons—Adrammelech and Sharezer—shanked him. They ran off to Ararat. Then his son Esarhaddon took the throne.

1.text: Around that time, King Hezekiah got real sick—like, deathbed sick. The prophet Isaiah, son of Amoz, came to him and said, "God said: Get your affairs in order. You ain't gon' make it."

2.text: Hezekiah turned his face to the wall and started prayin'.

3.text: He said, "Lord, please remember how I been walkin' with You for real—heart loyal, doin' right by You. Don't let it end like this." And the man broke down cryin', hard.

4.text: Then God spoke to Isaiah again,

5.text: "Go tell Hezekiah this: The Lord, the God of David your ancestor, heard your prayer. I saw them tears. I'm givin' you 15 more years.

6.text: And I'm not just savin' you—I'm gon' save this whole city from that Assyrian king. I got y'all covered."

7.text: "And to prove I'm serious, here's your sign:

8.text: I'ma make the sun move back 10 degrees on the sundial of Ahaz." And just like that, the sun backed it up ten degrees.

9.text: This is Hezekiah's own writing after God healed him:

10.text: "I said, In the middle of my life, I'm bout to die? I won't even get to live out my full years."

11.text: "I said, I won't get to see God While I'm alive on this earth. Won't get to see nobody no more, Won't be with the living."

12.text: "My life was snatched up Like somebody snatching down a tent. It's like I was a thread on a loom— Then God just cut it. From sunup to sundown, You was takin' me out."

13.text: "I laid there thinkin' all night, Like a lion tearin' up bones, You was breakin' me down, Lord."

14.text: "I was chirpin' like a bird, Mournin' like a dove, Eyes weak from lookin' up, Just cryin' out: 'Lord, I'm overwhelmed—please come through for me!'"

15.text: "What else could I even say? You told me what was gon' happen, And You did it. Now I'm tryna walk light— This shook me deep."

16.text: "But I learned somethin'— It's these hard things that teach us how to really live. You used this to save my life."

17.text: "Truth is, That pain brought me peace. You snatched me from the grave, And You threw my sins behind Your back."

18.text: "The grave can't thank You, Death don't worship You, Dead folks don't get to hope in Your promises."

19.text: "But the livin'? Oh, the livin' gon' praise You. That's what I'm doin right now. And I'ma make sure my kids know Your truth too."

20.text: "God came through for me, So we gon' sing with stringed instruments All our days in the house of the Lord!"

21.text: Isaiah had told them to press a fig poultice on Hezekiah's boil so he'd heal.

22.text: And Hezekiah had asked, "What sign will show me I'll be well enough to go back to the Lord's house?"

1.text: Around that time, Merodach-Baladan, son of Baladan and king of Babylon, heard Hezekiah was sick but bounced back. So he sent him letters and a gift.

2.text: Hezekiah was feelin' real good about that, so he went and showed off everything—his stash of silver, gold, spices, oils, his whole armory—all his treasures. Bruh showed them everything.

3.text: Then Isaiah the prophet came through like, "So what them men say to you? Where they from?" Hezekiah answered, "They came all the way from Babylon. Real far."

4.text: Isaiah followed up: "Aight, so what exactly did they see in your house?" Hezekiah was like, "Everything. I showed 'em the whole spot—didn't hide nothin'."

5.text: Then Isaiah hit him with a word from the Lord:

6.text: "Listen up. The time's comin' when everything in your house—all that your ancestors stacked up—gon' be taken to Babylon. Ain't nothin' gon' be left. That's the Lord talkin'."

7.text: "And even some of your sons, your descendants, gon' be taken too. They'll end up as eunuchs servin' in the king of Babylon's palace."

8.text: Hezekiah said, "Well… that word from the Lord is good." (He was thinkin', "At least things gon' stay peaceful and cool while I'm still alive.")

1.text: "Tell My people to chill and be comforted," says God.

2.text: "Let Jerusalem know it's over now. The war done. Her mess been forgiven. She took the hit—double for all that sin. But it's settled."

3.text: A voice cryin' out in the wilderness: "Get the road ready for the Lord! Make a path in this dry place—a highway for our God."

4.text: Every low place gon' rise up. Every mountain and hill gon' get brought down. Crooked roads straightened, rough paths smoothed out.

5.text: God's glory about to show out, and everybody gon' see it together—'cause the Lord Himself said it.

6.text: A voice said, "Cry out!" I asked, "What I'm supposed to say?" "All people? They like grass. Their beauty? Just like flowers in a field."

7.text: "Grass fades, flowers droop, when God breathes on 'em. Yep, people are just like that grass."

8.text: "Grass withers. Flowers fade. But God's Word? That thing stands forever."

9.text: Zion, you got good news—go shout it from the hills! Jerusalem, raise your voice! Don't be scared—yell it loud: "Check out your God!"

10.text: Look, the Lord is comin' strong, flexin' His power. He got His reward with Him, and His work right in front.

11.text: Like a shepherd, He gon' feed His people. He gon' scoop the babies up in His arms, holdin' them close, and gently guide the mamas with little ones.

12.text: Who you know that can cup the oceans in His palm? Who can stretch out the skies like He do? Weigh dust? Stack up mountains on a scale?

13.text: Who been God's advisor? Who gave Him game?

14.text: Who taught Him justice, knowledge, or understanding? Nobody.

15.text: The nations? Just a drop in the bucket. Some little specks on a scale. He lifts islands like they nothin'.

16.text: Even all of Lebanon's trees wouldn't make enough firewood for an offering worthy of Him.

17.text: To God, nations ain't even a blip. Less than nothin'. Straight-up empty.

18.text: So who you gon' compare to God? What could even come close?

19.text: Somebody tries to make a statue—gold-plated, silver-chained, real fancy.

20.text: And if you broke? You just pick a solid tree and find a skilled worker to carve you something that won't fall over.

21.text: Don't you know? Ain't you heard? Ain't this been known since day one? Since the foundation of the world?

22.text: God sits above the circle of the earth—folks look like grasshoppers from up there. He stretches out the skies like a curtain, like He settin' up a tent to live in.

23.text: He shuts down rulers like it's nothin'. Judges? Powerless before Him.

24.text: Before they even get rooted good, He breathes on 'em—they wither. Whirlwind snatchin' them up like dry weeds.

25.text: "Who y'all gon' compare Me to? Who stands on My level?" says the Holy One.

26.text: Look up! See all them stars? He made 'em. Calls 'em by name. Not one missing—'cause He that strong.

27.text: Why you trippin', Jacob? Why you think God forgot about you? Why you actin' like He ain't listenin' to your struggle?

28.text: You ain't heard? God ain't new to this—He the everlasting Creator. He don't get tired. He don't doze off. And His wisdom? Unsearchable.

29.text: He gives power to the ones who ain't got it. Strength to the ones runnin' on E.

30.text: Even the young folk gon' get tired, pass out, and fall behind.

31.text: But if you wait on the Lord? Oh, you get your strength back. You gon' soar like eagles, run and not pass out, walk and not fall behind.

1.text: "Aight y'all coastlands—be quiet and pay attention! Let folks get they strength up, step forward, and speak. Let's come face-to-face and settle this."

2.text: "Who raised up that one from the East? Called him with righteousness at his heels? Who handed nations over to him, made him boss up over kings? Who turned his enemies into dust under his sword, and dry weeds under his bow?"

3.text: "He chased 'em down, safe and smooth, takin' a road he ain't even been on before."

4.text: "Who been doin' all this from way back? Who been callin' generations like roll call?" "It's Me—the Lord! I'm the first, and I'm still here with the last."

5.text: The islands saw what went down and got shook. Folks from far off got scared, but came closer anyway.

6.text: Everybody hypin' each other up: 'Yo, stay strong, bruh!'

7.text: The metalworker boostin' the goldsmith. The hammer guy gassin' up the one who strikes the anvil, like, "It's ready now!" Then they nail it down so it don't fall over.

8.text: "But you, Israel? You My servant. Jacob, I chose you. You from Abraham—My homeboy."

9.text: "I pulled you from the ends of the earth, called you out from far away, and said: 'You Mine. I picked you. I ain't tossin' you away.'"

10.text: "So don't be scared—I'm with you. Don't trip—I'm your God. I'm gon' hold you up, strengthen you, help you out, and keep you steady with My righteous right hand."

11.text: "Anybody mad at you? Watch—shame and embarrassment. They gon' vanish like they never was. All your enemies? Gone."

12.text: "You gon' look around like, 'Where they at?' But you ain't findin' 'em. They disappeared like smoke in the wind."

13.text: "I'm the Lord, your God, holdin' your hand tight, tellin' you: 'Don't be scared. I got you.'"

14.text: "Don't fear, lil Jacob. Yeah, you feelin' like a worm out here. But I got you," says the Lord—"Your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel."

15.text: "I'm about to turn you into a brand-new threshing sledge—sharp and ready. You gon' crush mountains and stomp down hills like it's nothin'."

16.text: "You gon' throw all that junk in the air, and the wind gon' sweep it up. Whirlwinds gon' blow it away. Then you gon' rejoice in Me and give Me glory."

17.text: "Poor folks out here thirsty, mouths dry as dust—but I hear 'em. I ain't forgot. I'm the God of Israel. I got 'em."

18.text: "I'll bust rivers open on high hills, make fountains pop up in dry valleys. Turn deserts into pools, cracked ground into streams."

19.text: "I'm plantin' cedars, acacia, myrtle, olive trees—cypress, pine, boxwood too—all up in that dry land."

20.text: "So when folks see it, they gon' know—this ain't nature, this ain't luck—this was God. The Holy One of Israel did this."

21.text: "Go on then—bring your receipts," says the Lord. "Present your strongest case," says the King of Jacob.

22.text: "Show us what's comin'. Tell us the past too, break it down. Help us understand how it all ends. Speak on it."

23.text: "Tell us what's next. Show us you really gods. Do something! Good or bad, just make some noise so we know y'all exist."

24.text: "Y'all ain't nothin'. Your work? Trash. Anyone who picks you? Straight up bogus."

25.text: "I raised one up from the north—he comin'. From the east, callin' on My name. He gon' stomp on rulers like soft clay under a potter's foot."

26.text: "Anybody call this from the jump? Nah. Anybody speak on this before it happened? Nope. Y'all heard nothin'."

27.text: "I was the first to say to Zion, 'Look, they comin'!' And I sent good news to Jerusalem."

28.text: "I looked around, couldn't find nobody. No man. No counselor. No one could give Me answers."

29.text: "They all worthless. Their work is a joke. Their idols? Wind and straight-up confusion."

1.text: "Look here—My Servant, the One I hold down. My chosen one, the One I'm proud of. I done put My Spirit on Him. He gon' bring justice to the nations, even outside y'all little circle."

2.text: "He ain't gon' be loud in the streets, ain't tryna be seen or heard shoutin' everywhere."

3.text: "If somebody barely hangin' on, He ain't gon' break 'em. If their fire almost out, He ain't gon' snuff it. He gon' make sure justice stands for real."

4.text: "He ain't quitting, and He ain't gettin' discouraged till justice runs deep in this whole earth. Even the islands out there waitin' on His Word."

5.text: God, the One who made the heavens and stretched 'em like a sheet, the One who laid out the earth and gave folks breath and spirit, He said this:

6.text: "I called You with righteousness. I'm holdin' Your hand. I'm keepin' You, and I'm givin' You to the people as a promise, a light to the nations."

7.text: "You gon' open blind eyes, free folks locked up, and pull folks outta dark places and prison cells."

8.text: "I'm the Lord. That's My name. I ain't sharin' My glory with no one, and definitely not with no fake statues."

9.text: "Look, the old things already happened. I'm speakin' new things now. I'm tellin' y'all before they pop off."

10.text: Y'all better sing a new song to the Lord! All y'all from sea to sea, from coast to coast—lift that praise up!

11.text: Wilderness towns, folks from Kedar, folks chillin' in Sela—y'all too, shout from the mountain tops!

12.text: Let everybody give God His glory and let His name ring out across every coastline.

13.text: God movin' like a warrior now. His energy stirred up like a dude ready for battle. He shoutin' loud, not holdin' back—He takin' the W against all enemies.

14.text: "I been quiet for a long time—held My peace. But now? I'ma let it out like a woman in labor—pantin', gaspin'. It's go time."

15.text: "I'ma knock down mountains, dry up rivers, scorch the hills—strip it all bare. No green left."

16.text: "I'ma guide the blind down paths they ain't even know. Turn darkness into light for 'em. Make crooked roads smooth. I ain't leavin' 'em behind. I'm doin' this for real."

17.text: "But the folks worshippin' statues? They gon' be embarrassed—real bad. Talkin' bout 'These our gods.' Pssh. Shame."

18.text: "Yo—deaf folks, listen up. Blind folks, open ya eyes."

19.text: "Who more blind than My own servant? Who more deaf than My messenger? Who missin' it like the one I sent?"

20.text: "They lookin' at everything but not seein'. Listenin' but not hearin'. Useless!"

21.text: The Lord wanted to show off righteousness. That's why He made the Law big and important.

22.text: But these folks? Robbed, jacked, locked up in spiritual jail cells. Ain't nobody comin' to get 'em. Ain't nobody sayin' 'Run that back!' or 'Free them!'

23.text: "Anybody gon' actually listen? Anybody hear what's comin'?"

24.text: "Y'all wonderin' who let Israel get robbed? Who let Jacob get snatched up? It was Me—the Lord. Why? 'Cause they kept breakin' My commandments and refused to walk in My ways."

25.text: "So I let My anger fall. Let 'em feel the heat from war. They got burned up all around and still didn't get it. Didn't even take it to heart."

1.text: But now, the Lord—the One who made you, Jacob, who formed you, Israel—He say: "Don't be scared. I done paid for you. I called you out by name. You belong to Me."

2.text: "When you walk through deep water, I'm gon' be right there. When the river rise up, it won't drown you. When the fire comes, you ain't gon' get burned. Not even touched."

3.text: "I'm the Lord your God. The Holy One. Your Savior. I gave up Egypt, Ethiopia, and Seba just to get you back."

4.text: "You real precious to Me. I value you. I love you. I'll trade lives just to keep you safe."

5.text: "Don't be afraid—I'm with you. I'll bring your people from every direction—east, west, north, and south."

6.text: "I'll tell the north: 'Let 'em go!' And the south: 'Don't hold 'em back!' Bring My sons and daughters home, no matter how far they been scattered."

7.text: "Everybody called by My name, made by Me for My glory—I made them, formed them, shaped them. They Mine."

8.text: Bring out the blind—even if they got eyes. Bring out the deaf—even if they got ears.

9.text: Gather all the nations together. Let the people show what they know. Can anybody explain what's been goin' on? Let 'em testify—prove it's truth.

10.text: "Y'all are My witnesses," says the Lord, "and My chosen servant. I picked you so you could know Me, trust Me, understand I'm the One. Ain't no God before Me. Ain't gon' be none after."

11.text: "I, yes Me, I'm the Lord. And there ain't no other savior but Me."

12.text: "I told y'all what was comin'. I saved you. I spoke truth. Wasn't no foreign god doin' that. That's why y'all My witnesses—I'm God."

13.text: "Even before time was a thing—I been Me. Ain't nobody takin' nothin' out My hand. When I move, can't nobody undo it."

14.text: The Lord, your Redeemer, the Holy One of Israel says: "I'ma shut Babylon down for y'all. I'ma make them run scared—those proud Chaldeans cruisin' in they ships."

15.text: "I'm the Lord, your Holy One, the Creator of Israel, your King."

16.text: I'm the One who made a way through the sea, Split the deep waters wide open.

17.text: I pulled down the chariots, the horses, the whole army. They laid down, ain't gettin' back up. Snuffed out like a candle in the wind.

18.text: "Stop dwellin' on what happened before. Quit livin' in the past."

19.text: "I'm doin' something new—can't you see it? I'm makin' a way in the wilderness, puttin' rivers where the desert been dry."

20.text: "Even the wild animals gon' praise Me—jackals, ostriches—'cause I'm givin' water in dry places, refreshin' My chosen people."

21.text: "This people? I made them for Me. And they gon' praise My name."

22.text: "But you, Jacob? You ain't been callin' on Me. You tired of Me, Israel."

23.text: "You ain't brought no offerings, no sacrifices. I ain't even ask for all that pressure."

24.text: "You ain't even bring Me no sweet incense. But you did bring Me all your sins. Heavy. You wearin' Me out."

25.text: "Still—I'm the One who wipes your sins away. Not 'cause you earned it, but 'cause I said so. I ain't gon' bring 'em back up either."

26.text: "Go ahead. Remind Me if you want. Bring your argument. Try and prove yourself."

27.text: "Your ancestors messed up. Even the ones supposed to speak for you been outta line."

28.text: "So I let your leaders fall, let the temple folks get cursed. Jacob been exposed. Israel been clowned."

1.text: Now listen up, Jacob—My servant. Israel—My chosen one.

2.text: This what the Lord say, the One who made you, formed you since you was in the womb, the One who got your back: "Don't be scared, Jacob My servant. Jeshurun, I picked you."

3.text: "I'ma pour water on the ones who thirsty. I'ma flood the dry land. I'ma pour out My Spirit on your kids, and bless all your babies."

4.text: "They gon' grow up like willows by the water, flourishing, thriving."

5.text: One gon' say, 'I belong to the Lord.' Another gon' call himself a child of Jacob. Somebody else gon' tattoo 'Property of the Lord' on they hand and rep Israel by name.

6.text: This what the Lord, Israel's King and Redeemer, the Lord of armies, gotta say: "I'm the First and the Last. Ain't nobody else God but Me."

7.text: "Who else can speak on the future like I do? If they real with it, let them say what's comin'. Let them line it up like I did from the jump."

8.text: "Don't be scared. I already told y'all what's up. Y'all My witnesses. Is there another God? Nah. Ain't no other Rock. I ain't heard of one."

9.text: Folks who make idols? All of 'em useless. What they value won't do nothin' for 'em. They witness their own mess. They blind and clueless.

10.text: Who in they right mind makes a god that don't even help them?

11.text: Even the crew around them gon' be embarrassed. These dudes just human. Let 'em all gather—they still gon' be shook and ashamed.

12.text: The blacksmith sweatin' in the fire, hammerin' with tired arms. But he get weak, don't eat, and pass out.

13.text: The woodworker drawin' lines, using chalk and rulers, carving it to look like a man. All that just to sit in the house like decor.

14.text: He cuts down trees—cedar, cypress, oak. He plants pine trees, waits for rain, then—

15.text: —uses the wood to warm up, bake bread… and also carves an idol to worship. Same wood. He bowin' down to it.

16.text: One half goes in the fire to roast meat, and he say, "Mmm, I'm full and warm."

17.text: Other half? He turn it into a god. Falls down to it like, "Save me, you my god now."

18.text: They don't even realize they lost. God let 'em stay blind. They can't see or understand.

19.text: Ain't nobody stoppin' to think: "Yo, I used this wood to cook dinner… now I'm worshipin' the leftovers?"

20.text: That man's just eatin' ashes—straight delusional. He too far gone to even ask, "Yo, is this a lie in my hand?"

21.text: "Remember this, Jacob. Israel—you My servant. I made you. You belong to Me. I ain't forgot you."

22.text: "I erased your mess-ups like clouds disappear. I wiped out your sin like morning mist. Come back to Me—I already paid the price."

23.text: Sing, heavens! Shout, earth! Let the mountains get loud! Trees, clap your hands! The Lord redeemed Jacob and flexed His glory through Israel.

24.text: This what the Lord say—your Redeemer, the One who formed you since the womb: "I'm the One who made everything. I spread out the sky, stretched out the earth—all by Myself."

25.text: "I shut down fake prophets. I drive fortune-tellers crazy. I flip the script on the 'wise' and make their wisdom dumb."

26.text: "But when My servants speak, I back it up. When My messengers move, I make it happen. I told Jerusalem: 'You gon' be lived in again.' I told Judah: 'Your cities gon' be rebuilt. The ruins? I'ma lift 'em.'"

27.text: "I told the sea, 'Dry up.' And it dried."

28.text: "And I got Cyrus lined up. He My shepherd. He gon' do what I want—sayin' to Jerusalem, 'You gon' be rebuilt,' and to the Temple, 'Your foundation gon' be laid.'"

1.text: This what the Lord say to His chosen one, Cyrus—the one He holdin' by the right hand: "I'ma help you take down nations, loosen kings' belts, and open doors no man can shut."

2.text: "I'ma walk in front of you and clear the path, flatten the bumps, bust open bronze gates, and cut through iron bars."

3.text: "I'ma give you treasure from the shadows, riches folks ain't even know was hid, so you know it's Me—the Lord—callin' your name, the God of Israel."

4.text: "For the sake of Jacob My servant, and Israel who I picked, I'm callin' you by name, even though you don't know Me like that."

5.text: "I'm the Lord, ain't no one else. Ain't no God besides Me. I'm the one dressin' you for the fight, even though you ain't never called on Me."

6.text: "So folks all over—east to west—know ain't nobody else but Me. I'm the Lord. That's it. Period."

7.text: "I make light. I create dark. I bring peace. I stir up trouble. I'm the Lord—I do all that."

8.text: "Heavens, open up and let justice rain down! Let the skies pour out what's right. Let the earth open up and grow salvation, let righteousness sprout up side by side. I, the Lord, planted it."

9.text: Woe to the one tryna argue with the One who made 'em. Like clay tryna clap back at the potter. "Yo, what you makin'?" Or sayin', "You ain't got no hands."
