18.text: "You show love for thousands, but hold folks accountable across generations. You're great and mighty—Lord of armies is Your name."

19.text: "You wise, You move strong. You watch everything folks do, and You bless or correct based on how they livin'."

20.text: "You showed signs in Egypt, and You still do the same today in Israel and beyond. Your name stays famous."

21.text: "You brought Your people outta Egypt with power and fear and signs."

22.text: "You gave 'em this land You promised—the one flowin' with milk and honey."

23.text: "They moved in… but ain't do right. They ain't obey You. So now, everything You said would happen, done happened."

24.text: "Look at it—they buildin' siege ramps outside! This city already handed over to Babylon—famine, war, disease… just like You said."

25.text: "But then You tell me, 'Buy a field. Get witnesses.' Even while the city's fallin'?"

26.text: Then the Lord answered me:

27.text: "I'm the God of all people. Ain't nothin' too hard for Me."

28.text: "This city? I'ma give it to the Babylonians and Nebuchadnezzar. He gon' take it."

29.text: "The Babylonians gon' set fire to it. Burn it down. The houses where they burned incense to Baal and poured drinks for fake gods—yeah, them."

30.text: "Israel and Judah been wildin' since day one. They just stay tryna make Me mad."

31.text: "This city been a thorn in My side since the day they laid the first brick. I'm done watchin' it."

32.text: "From kings to prophets, priests to people, the whole squad in Judah and Jerusalem got blood on their hands."

33.text: "I tried to teach them. Got up early, gave 'em lessons—but they ain't listen."

34.text: "They brought their dirty idols into My house and disrespected it."

35.text: "They built altars to Baal and burned their sons and daughters in fire to Molech. That ain't ever crossed My mind. That's why Judah spiralin'."

36.text: "But now, hear this about the city y'all say is doomed to Babylon, sword, famine, and plague—"

37.text: "I'ma bring y'all back from every country I scattered y'all to in My anger. Y'all gon' live here safe again."

38.text: "Y'all gon' be My people, and I'ma be your God."

39.text: "I'ma give y'all one heart and one purpose—to fear Me forever. You and your kids gon' benefit from it."

40.text: "I'ma make an unbreakable promise: I won't stop doin' good for y'all. I'ma put reverence for Me deep in your hearts so y'all don't stray."

41.text: "I'ma be glad to bless y'all. I'ma plant y'all back in this land—with all My heart and soul."

42.text: "Just like I brought disaster, I'ma bring the good I promised."

43.text: "Fields gon' be bought again in this land y'all think is abandoned and cursed."

44.text: "Folks gon' buy land, sign papers, seal 'em, call witnesses—from Benjamin to Jerusalem, to the hills, lowlands, and down South. I'ma bring My people home."

1.text: While Jeremiah was still locked up in the prison yard, the Lord spoke to him again.

2.text: "This is what the Lord says—the One who made the world, who built it up solid. Yeah, the Lord is His name."

3.text: "Call Me. I'll answer. I'll show you stuff you ain't even imagined—big things, deep things you ain't never known."

4.text: "I'm talkin' about the homes in this city and the royal houses that been torn down to block the Babylonian siege ramps."

5.text: "Folks tried to fight, but all that happened was bodies fillin' the streets. I let it happen 'cause of all they wickedness—I had to turn My face from this city."

6.text: "But I ain't gon' leave it broken. I'ma bring healing. I'ma pour out peace and truth like rain."

7.text: "I'ma bring Judah and Israel's people back home. Rebuild everything like it used to be."

8.text: "I'ma wash away all the grime from they sins. Forgive everything they did wrong—every slip-up, every rebellion."

9.text: "Then this city? It's gon' be My joy, My pride, My testimony. The nations gon' see what I do and be shook—in awe of how I bless and prosper My people."

10.text: "You said this place was empty—no people, no animals, no life. But listen—"

11.text: "Laughter gon' return. Joy gon' echo again. Weddings gon' pop off. People gon' shout: 'Praise the Lord of Heaven's Armies, 'Cause He good, and His mercy never runs out!' And they gon' bring praise offerings to My house again, 'cause I'ma bring 'em back just like before."

12.text: "In these abandoned cities, folks gon' live again. Shepherds gon' chill with their flocks in peace."

13.text: "From the mountains to the valleys, from Benjamin to Jerusalem, sheep gon' be counted again by the hands of their keepers. I said it, and I meant it."

14.text: "Look, the days comin'," says the Lord, "when I'ma come through on every good promise I made to Israel and Judah."

15.text: "In that day, I'ma raise up a Branch from David's line. He gon' rule right, move just, and keep order in the land."

16.text: "Judah gon' be saved. Jerusalem gon' live safe. And folks gon' call her: 'The Lord Our Righteousness.'"

17.text: "David's line ain't never gon' be empty—there'll always be someone fit to sit on that throne."

18.text: "And the priests, the Levites? Always gon' be someone offering up sacrifices, grain offerings, and worship nonstop."

19.text: The Lord gave Jeremiah another word:

20.text: "If you can cancel daylight and nightfall,

21.text: Then maybe—just maybe—My covenant with David and My priests could be broken. But guess what? You can't."

22.text: "Just like you can't count the stars or the grains of sand, that's how big I'ma grow David's legacy and the tribe of Levi that ministers to Me."

23.text: Then the Lord said again:

24.text: "Ain't you heard what folks been sayin'? 'God done gave up on Israel and Judah.' They treat My people like they ain't worth nothin' anymore."

25.text: "But I'm the One who set day and night, sky and earth."

26.text: "And I ain't throwin' away Jacob's people or David's descendants. I still got rulers lined up to lead Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob's seed. I'ma bring 'em back and show mercy."

1.text: The Lord dropped a word on Jeremiah when King Nebuchadnezzar and every army under his rule was battlin' against Jerusalem and all the surrounding cities.

2.text: "Go tell King Zedekiah this," says the Lord God of Israel: "I'ma hand this whole city over to Babylon's king. He gon' set it on fire."

3.text: "You ain't escaping, Zedekiah. You gon' get caught. And when you do, you gon' see the Babylonian king eye to eye, face to face. And after that—you headed straight to Babylon."

4.text: "But listen close, Zedekiah," says the Lord. "You ain't gon' die by the sword."

5.text: "You gon' die in peace, like your ancestors did—back when they burned incense and held funerals sayin', 'Alas, king!' That's the word I spoke. Ain't no change to it."

6.text: So Jeremiah told Zedekiah everything the Lord said, right there in Jerusalem.

7.text: This was while the Babylonian army was still fightin' Jerusalem, Lachish, and Azekah—'cause those were the only cities left still holding on.

8.text: Then the Lord gave Jeremiah another word after Zedekiah had made a covenant with the people in Jerusalem to declare freedom.

9.text: The deal was: every Hebrew man or woman in slavery had to be set free. Nobody was supposed to keep their own people in bondage no more.

10.text: And at first? Everybody—leaders and all—followed through. They let their slaves go like they promised.

11.text: But later on, they switched up. Took back the men and women they freed and made 'em slaves again. Cold-blooded.

12.text: So the Lord hit Jeremiah with a word:

13.text: "I made a covenant with y'all ancestors when I brought 'em up outta Egypt, outta that house of slavery."

14.text: "I told them, after seven years, you supposed to free any fellow Hebrew who worked for you. Six years of service, then let 'em walk. But your folks ain't listen."

15.text: "Y'all just recently did the right thing—declared liberty and made a covenant in My house, the one with My name on it."

16.text: "Then you had the nerve to double back, disrespect My name, and drag those freed folks back into chains. You treated 'em like property all over again."

17.text: "So here's what I'ma do," says the Lord. "Since y'all ain't proclaim liberty for your people, I'ma proclaim liberty for y'all—to the sword, to disease, to famine. Y'all 'bout to be free… to suffer."

18.text: "And all y'all who broke this covenant—remember how y'all sliced that calf in two and walked between the pieces like y'all was serious?"

19.text: "Every prince, priest, and big shot that walked through that symbolic ceremony?"

20.text: "I'm handing all of them over to their enemies. They bodies gon' be laid out for vultures and wild beasts to feast on."

21.text: "Zedekiah and his crew? They not off the hook either. I'ma let their enemies get them too. Babylon's army might've backed off for a second, but they comin' back."

22.text: "Matter fact, I'm calling them back Myself," says the Lord. "They gon' burn this city down and turn Judah into a ghost town—ain't nobody gon' be left."

1.text: God sent Jeremiah a word during Jehoiakim's reign, son of Josiah, king of Judah.

2.text: "Go holler at the Rechabite family. Bring 'em to the Temple, into one of them side rooms, and offer 'em some wine."

3.text: So I grabbed Jaazaniah—he's Jeremiah's son (not me, another Jeremiah)—his brothers, sons, and the whole Rechabite clan.

4.text: I brought them into God's house, into the room of Hanan (son of Igdaliah, man of God), right by the chamber of the princes, above the room of Maaseiah the doorkeeper.

5.text: I laid out some bowls and cups of wine in front of the Rechabite crew and said, "Go 'head, drink up."

6.text: But they said, "Nah. We don't drink wine. Jonadab son of Rechab—our ancestor—told us not to. He said: 'Y'all and your kids? Never touch wine.'"

7.text: "'Don't build houses. Don't plant no crops or vineyards. Live in tents only—so y'all can survive and stay long in this land you just passing through.'"

8.text: "We been holding it down just like Jonadab said. No wine for us, our wives, our sons, or our daughters."

9.text: "No houses, no vineyards, no land. None of that."

10.text: "We stay in tents, just like we were told. Been stickin' to it since day one."

11.text: "Only reason we in Jerusalem now? Babylon rolled up with their army, and we had to dip for safety. That's why we here."

12.text: Then the Lord hit Jeremiah with another word:

13.text: "Go tell the people of Judah and the folks in Jerusalem—'Y'all still ain't tryna learn obedience, huh?'"

14.text: "Look at the Rechabites. They keepin' Jonadab's command like it's law. No wine, ever. And Me? I been talkin' to y'all over and over—and you still don't listen."

15.text: "I sent prophets early in the morning tellin' y'all, 'Turn from your wild ways. Fix your life. Quit chasing other gods.' I told y'all if you did that, you could stay in this land. But you ain't wanna hear Me."

16.text: "Jonadab's people followed one man. My people won't even follow Me—their God."

17.text: "So here's what I'ma do," says the Lord: "Judah and everybody in Jerusalem 'bout to get the judgment I been warning them about. I called—they ain't pick up. I spoke—they ain't answer."

18.text: Then Jeremiah turned to the Rechabite family and said, "This what the Lord of Heaven's Armies, the God of Israel, says: 'Because y'all kept Jonadab's commands to the letter and lived exactly how he told y'all to…'"

19.text: "'Jonadab will never lack a descendant standin' before Me. Forever.'"

1.text: In the fourth year of Jehoiakim (son of Josiah, king of Judah), God spoke to Jeremiah again.

2.text: "Grab a scroll. Write down everything I told you—about Israel, Judah, and all the other nations—from back in Josiah's day 'til now."

3.text: "Maybe if Judah hears all the mess I got lined up, they'll stop wildin'. And if they turn back, I'll forgive 'em."

4.text: So Jeremiah called up Baruch, son of Neriah. Baruch wrote down all God's words as Jeremiah said them.

5.text: Then Jeremiah told Baruch, "I can't step foot in the Temple—I'm locked down.

6.text: You gotta go. Take that scroll and read out loud what God said—on the day everybody fasting. Let all Judah hear it."

7.text: "Maybe, just maybe, they'll pray and turn from their ways. God's wrath ain't no joke."

8.text: Baruch did exactly what Jeremiah said. He read the scroll in God's house.

9.text: Fast forward to the fifth year of Jehoiakim, ninth month—they called a fast in Jerusalem. Folks from all over Judah came.

10.text: Baruch stood in the chamber of Gemariah (son of Shaphan) at the New Gate of God's house and read Jeremiah's words to the crowd.

11.text: Michaiah (son of Gemariah) heard all that and ran to the palace.

12.text: He pulled up in the scribe's office where all the top officials were—Elishama, Delaiah, Elnathan, Gemariah, Zedekiah, and the rest.

13.text: Michaiah said, "Y'all… Baruch just read some heavy stuff from Jeremiah in the Temple!"

14.text: The officials sent Jehudi to fetch Baruch. "Bring that scroll and come through." Baruch came, scroll in hand.

15.text: They said, "Sit down and read it for us." Baruch did just that.

16.text: When they heard everything, they looked around shook like, "Yo, we gotta tell the king."

17.text: They asked Baruch, "How you get all this down?"

18.text: Baruch said, "Jeremiah spoke it word for word—I just wrote it down."

19.text: The officials said, "Y'all better lay low. You and Jeremiah—disappear. Don't tell nobody where y'all at."

20.text: They went to the king but left the scroll stashed in Elishama's chamber. Told the king everything that was in it.

21.text: The king sent Jehudi to get the scroll. Jehudi brought it and read it to the king and his crew.

22.text: It was winter. The king was chillin' in his winter spot with a fire going.

23.text: As Jehudi read 3–4 columns, the king grabbed a knife, sliced the scroll, and tossed the pieces in the fire—burned the whole thing.

24.text: Nobody flinched. Not the king, not his crew. No one tore their clothes in fear.

25.text: Elnathan, Delaiah, and Gemariah tried to stop him—"Please don't burn it!" But he ignored 'em.

26.text: Then the king ordered some men to arrest Baruch and Jeremiah—but God hid them.

27.text: After the scroll got burned, God came back to Jeremiah.

28.text: "Get another scroll. Rewrite every word from the first one that Jehoiakim torched."

29.text: "And tell Jehoiakim this: You burned God's scroll, huh? Mad 'cause I said Babylon's coming to destroy this place?

30.text: Well guess what—no heir of yours will sit on David's throne. Your body gon' be thrown out like trash—burned by day, frozen by night.

31.text: You, your family, your servants—y'all getting punished. Everything I warned about? It's still coming, 'cause y'all ain't listen."

32.text: So Jeremiah took a fresh scroll and gave it to Baruch again. Baruch wrote every word down—and then some. Extra verses got added too.

1.text: Zedekiah, son of Josiah, ended up on the throne after King Nebuchadnezzar made him ruler instead of Coniah, Jehoiakim's boy.

2.text: But Zedekiah, his crew, and the people? They wasn't tryna hear God's word through Jeremiah—ignored it all.

3.text: Still, Zedekiah sent Jehucal and the priest Zephaniah to Jeremiah like, "Yo, pray to the Lord our God for us."

4.text: (At that time, Jeremiah was still free to walk around—he hadn't been locked up yet.)

5.text: Egypt's army rolled up, so the Babylonian army that was pressin' Jerusalem backed off when they heard Pharaoh's squad was coming.

6.text: Then God gave Jeremiah another word:

7.text: "Tell Zedekiah this: That Egyptian army you depending on? They gon' bounce. They headed back home."

8.text: "But Babylon? Oh, they comin' back. They gon' fight, take this city, and burn it to the ground."

9.text: "Don't get it twisted thinking they gone for good. They not. Don't lie to yourselves."

10.text: "Even if y'all beat the whole Babylonian army and only left some wounded soldiers, even they would get up and finish the job. This city still gettin' torched."

11.text: When the Babylonian troops backed off because of Egypt,

12.text: Jeremiah tried to dip outta Jerusalem, headin' to Benjamin to handle some personal business.

13.text: But when he got to the Benjamin Gate, a guard named Irijah (son of Shelemiah, son of Hananiah) stopped him. Irijah said, "You tryna defect to the Babylonians, ain't you?"

14.text: Jeremiah was like, "Man, that's a lie! I ain't goin' nowhere with them!" But Irijah wasn't tryna hear it—he snatched Jeremiah and took him to the officials.

15.text: The officials got heated. They beat him down and locked him up in the house of Jonathan the scribe, which had been turned into a jail.

16.text: They threw Jeremiah in a dungeon, deep in the cells. He was stuck down there for a long time.

17.text: Eventually, Zedekiah secretly had him brought out and asked him on the low, "Did God say anything new?" Jeremiah replied, "Yep. You gon' be handed over to Babylon's king."

18.text: Then he asked, "What did I even do to you or your people that got me thrown in jail?"

19.text: "Where them prophets at now—the ones who said the king of Babylon wouldn't show up? Where they at?"

20.text: "Please, Your Majesty—don't send me back to Jonathan's house. If I go back, I'ma die there."

21.text: So Zedekiah ordered that Jeremiah be moved to the prison yard instead. He also made sure Jeremiah got a slice of bread every day from the Bakers' Street—until the city ran outta bread.

22.text: And just like that, Jeremiah stayed posted up in the prison courtyard.

1.text: Shephatiah, Gedaliah, Jucal, and Pashhur heard what Jeremiah been tellin' everybody.

2.text: He said, "Look, this what the Lord say: If you stay in this city, you gon' die—by sword, hunger, or disease. But if you give yourself up to the Babylonians, you'll live. You might not have much, but at least you'll still be breathing."

3.text: "This city," he said, "for sure gon' fall into the hands of the king of Babylon's army. They comin', and they takin' it."

4.text: The officials ain't like that. They went to the king and said, "Man, you gotta kill this dude. He makin' our soldiers scared, tellin' everybody to give up. He ain't for us—he workin' against us."

5.text: Zedekiah said, "Y'all do what y'all want. I can't stop you anyway."

6.text: So they took Jeremiah and threw him in a dungeon—the one belongin' to Malchiah, the king's son. It was deep, and they lowered him down with ropes. No water down there, just thick mud. Jeremiah sank in it.

7.text: Now Ebed-Melech, a brother from Ethiopia who was a servant in the palace, heard what they did to Jeremiah. The king was chillin' at the Gate of Benjamin.

8.text: Ebed-Melech left the palace, went to the king and said,

9.text: "My king, them men done did Jeremiah dirty. They threw him in a hole where he gon' die of hunger. Ain't even no bread left in the city."

10.text: The king told Ebed-Melech, "Take thirty men and go get Jeremiah outta there before he dies."

11.text: Ebed-Melech took the men and went to the storage room under the palace. He grabbed some old clothes and rags, tied 'em to ropes, and lowered them down to Jeremiah.

12.text: He told him, "Put these rags under your arms so the ropes don't cut you." Jeremiah did what he said.

13.text: Then they pulled him up out the mud. Jeremiah stayed in the prison courtyard after that.

14.text: Later, King Zedekiah secretly sent for Jeremiah at the third entrance of the Lord's house. He said, "I need to ask you something—don't hold nothin' back."

15.text: Jeremiah said, "If I tell you the truth, you gon' kill me. And even if I give advice, you ain't gon' listen."

16.text: Zedekiah swore on the low, "As sure as God lives, I won't kill you or let them touch you."

17.text: Jeremiah said, "Alright then. The Lord, God of Heaven's Armies, say: If you surrender to Babylon's commanders, you'll live. The city won't get burned, and your family will be safe."

18.text: "But if you don't surrender, this city gon' fall. Babylon gon' set it on fire, and you won't escape."

19.text: Zedekiah said, "But what if the Jews who already surrendered tell on me and the Babylonians hurt me?"

20.text: Jeremiah said, "They not gon' touch you. Please, do what the Lord say—it'll go well for you. You'll live."

21.text: "But if you don't, here's what God showed me:

22.text: All the women left in your palace gon' be handed over to the Babylonian commanders. And they gon' mock you, sayin': 'Your friends lied to you, They got you caught up. Now you stuck in the mud, And they dipped on you.'"

23.text: "Then they gon' take your wives and kids. You ain't gon' escape. The king of Babylon gon' get you. And you the reason this city gon' burn."

24.text: Zedekiah told Jeremiah, "Don't tell nobody we had this talk, and you'll be safe."

25.text: "But if the officials find out and press you—'What did y'all talk about? Don't lie or we'll kill you'—

26.text: just tell them, 'I begged the king not to send me back to Jonathan's house, 'cause I ain't tryna die there.'"

27.text: Sure enough, the officials came and questioned Jeremiah. He told 'em what the king said to say. They left him alone, 'cause nobody had heard the conversation.

28.text: So Jeremiah stayed in the prison yard till the day Jerusalem got taken. And he was still there when it all went down.

1.text: In the ninth year of King Zedekiah's reign, tenth month, Nebuchadnezzar and his whole Babylonian army rolled up on Jerusalem and locked it down.

2.text: By the eleventh year, fourth month, ninth day—boom, they broke through the city walls.

3.text: Then Babylon's top brass came rollin' in and posted up at the Middle Gate—Nergal-Sharezer, Samgar-Nebo, Sarsechim (aka Rabsaris), and Nergal-Sarezer (aka Rabmag), plus the rest of the squad.

4.text: Zedekiah and his soldiers saw what was goin' down and tried to sneak out at night through the king's garden gate, between two walls. They hit the plains, thinkin' they was slick.

5.text: But the Babylonian army chased 'em down and caught Zedekiah in the Jericho flatlands. They snatched him up and took him to Nebuchadnezzar at Riblah. Judgment day.

6.text: The king of Babylon made Zedekiah watch his own sons get killed right in front of him—along with all the nobles of Judah.

7.text: Then he gouged out Zedekiah's eyes and chained him up with bronze shackles. Off to Babylon he went.

8.text: After that, the Babylonians torched the king's house and the houses of the people. Tore down Jerusalem's walls like they was knockin' over dominoes.

9.text: Captain Nebuzaradan took what was left—anyone still in the city or who had defected—and hauled them off to Babylon.

10.text: But he left behind the poor folks, the ones who ain't had nothin'. He gave them vineyards and fields to work with.

11.text: Meanwhile, Nebuchadnezzar gave Captain Nebuzaradan special orders about Jeremiah:

12.text: "Take care of him. Don't lay a finger on him unless he tells you to. Do whatever he says."

13.text: So Nebuzaradan, along with Nebushasban (Rabsaris), Nergal-Sharezer (Rabmag), and the rest of the Babylonian bosses,

14.text: pulled Jeremiah up out the prison yard and handed him off to Gedaliah, son of Ahikam, grandson of Shaphan. Jeremiah got to go back home and live among the people.

15.text: But while Jeremiah was still locked up, the Lord had already dropped another word on him:

16.text: "Go find Ebed-Melech the Ethiopian and tell him this is what the Lord of Heaven's Armies says:

17.text: 'I'm gon' do what I said to this city—judgment is comin', not blessings. You gon' see it go down.

18.text: But don't worry, I got you. You ain't gon' fall into the hands of the folks you scared of. I'm gon' keep you safe. You won't die by the sword. You gon' live, because you put your trust in Me,' says the Lord."

1.text: This what the Lord told Jeremiah after Nebuzaradan, captain of the guard, let him go free from Ramah. Jeremiah had been shackled up with the other folks gettin' deported from Jerusalem and Judah to Babylon.

2.text: The captain pulled Jeremiah aside and said, "Your God already called judgment on this place.

3.text: And look—He done exactly what He said He would. Y'all brought this on yourselves, not listenin' to Him and doin' y'all own thing."

4.text: "Now I'ma let you go. You ain't chained up no more. If you wanna come with me to Babylon, I got you—I'll take care of you. But if you'd rather stay here, that's fine too. The whole land's open to you—go wherever feels right."

5.text: While Jeremiah was still thinkin' it over, Nebuzaradan said, "You could go stay with Gedaliah, Ahikam's son, the one Babylon made governor over the cities of Judah. Or go wherever—your choice." Then he gave Jeremiah some food, a lil' gift, and let him bounce.

6.text: So Jeremiah went to stay with Gedaliah in Mizpah, living among the people who had been left behind in the land.

7.text: Out in the fields, the army captains who were still layin' low heard that Babylon had put Gedaliah in charge and trusted him with the folks left behind—the poor, the women, the kids, everybody who wasn't taken.

8.text: Then these leaders rolled up to Mizpah to see Gedaliah: Ishmael son of Nethaniah, Johanan and Jonathan (sons of Kareah), Seraiah son of Tanhumeth, sons of Ephai from Netophah, and Jezaniah from Maacah—with all their people.

9.text: Gedaliah told 'em straight: "Look, don't be scared to serve the Babylonians. Just live here, serve the king, and you'll be good."

10.text: "I'ma hold it down here in Mizpah, talk to Babylon's reps when they come. Y'all gather up the wine, oil, and summer fruits, store it up, and settle in the towns you've taken back."

11.text: When word got out to all the Jews who'd scattered—those in Moab, Ammon, Edom, and beyond—that a remnant was still standing in Judah and Gedaliah was in charge,

12.text: They came back. All of 'em. Returned to Judah, linked up with Gedaliah at Mizpah, and started harvestin' fruit and wine in abundance.

13.text: But then Johanan (son of Kareah) and the other field captains came to Gedaliah with some news.

14.text: "You heard what Baalis, king of the Ammonites, plotting? He sent Ishmael to kill you!" But Gedaliah didn't believe a word of it.

15.text: Then Johanan pulled him to the side and said, "Let me handle Ishmael. I'll take him out quietly—nobody will even know. 'Cause if he kills you, everything gon' fall apart. The people gon' scatter, and what's left of Judah gon' be done."

16.text: But Gedaliah told Johanan, "Nah, don't do it. You got the wrong idea about Ishmael."

1.text: In the seventh month, Ishmael—son of Nethaniah, grandson of Elishama, from royal blood and one of the king's former officers—pulled up to Mizpah with ten dudes. They sat down and broke bread with Gedaliah, son of Ahikam.

2.text: But while they was eatin', Ishmael and his ten men turned on Gedaliah and stabbed him dead. That's the same Gedaliah Babylon put in charge of the land.

3.text: Then Ishmael took out all the Jews that were with Gedaliah at Mizpah, and even the Babylonian soldiers that were stationed there. Straight massacre.

4.text: Two days after the hit, word still hadn't got out yet.

5.text: That's when a group of 80 men rolled in from Shechem, Shiloh, and Samaria. They was mournin', tore clothes and shaved faces, and brought incense and offerings, headed to the house of the Lord.

6.text: Ishmael walked out of Mizpah to meet 'em, fake-cryin' like he was grievin'. Told 'em, "Come on, y'all. Gedaliah wanna see y'all."

7.text: But once they stepped inside the city walls, Ishmael and his crew ambushed them too—killed 'em and dumped their bodies in a big pit.

8.text: Ten of the men begged for their lives, sayin', "We got wheat, oil, honey, barley hidden in the field—don't kill us." So Ishmael let them live.

9.text: The pit he used to toss the dead bodies? That was the same trench King Asa had built back in the day to protect against Baasha, king of Israel. Ishmael filled it with corpses.

10.text: Then Ishmael snatched up the rest of the folks at Mizpah—king's daughters and everybody else Nebuzaradan left under Gedaliah's care. He took them hostage and started headin' toward Ammon territory.

11.text: But Johanan (son of Kareah) and all his boys in the field heard what went down.

12.text: They grabbed their squad and went to confront Ishmael. They found him at the big pool in Gibeon.

13.text: When the people Ishmael had kidnapped saw Johanan and his soldiers, they got hype—relieved.

14.text: So all the folks Ishmael had taken turned back and ran to Johanan's side.

15.text: But Ishmael and eight of his men dipped. Slid off to Ammon before Johanan could catch 'em.

16.text: Then Johanan and the army leaders scooped up everybody Ishmael had stolen away from Mizpah—warriors, women, kids, eunuchs—all of 'em. They brought 'em back from Gibeon.

17.text: They stopped at a place called Chimham, near Bethlehem, on the way toward Egypt.

18.text: Why? 'Cause they was shook of the Babylonians. Ishmael's assassination of Gedaliah had them thinkin' Babylon was comin' for everybody next.

1.text: Then all the squad leaders—Johanan (son of Kareah), Jezaniah (son of Hoshaiah)—and everybody else, rich and poor alike, pulled up to Jeremiah.

2.text: They said, "Jeremiah, please talk to the Lord your God for us. We just a small crew now, barely hangin' on, as you can see.

3.text: Ask Him what we should do and where we should go next—'cause we lost out here."

4.text: Jeremiah said, "Bet. I hear you. I'ma take your request to God just like you said. And whatever He tells me, I'ma tell you—word for word. I'm not holdin' nothin' back."

5.text: They said, "Let the Lord be our witness—we swear, we gon' do whatever He says, no matter what.

6.text: Whether we like it or not, we gon' obey so we can finally catch a break."

7.text: Ten days later, God gave Jeremiah the word.

8.text: So Jeremiah called Johanan, all the military heads, and everybody else from the hood to the higher-ups.

9.text: He said, "Aight, here's what the Lord, God of Israel, said—since y'all asked:

10.text: 'If y'all stay put in this land, I'll build you up. I'm not tryna tear you down. I'll plant you and not yank you up. I'm coolin' on the judgment I brought.'

11.text: Don't be scared of the king of Babylon, even though you shook right now. I got you. I'll protect you. I'll bring you outta this.

12.text: I'll even soften his heart, so he'll let y'all live in peace in your own land."

13.text: "But," Jeremiah added, "if y'all say, 'Nah, we not stayin' here,' and ignore what God's sayin'—

14.text: If y'all tryna bounce to Egypt talkin' bout, 'We ain't tryna hear no trumpets, see no war, or starve no more'—

15.text: Then listen up, remnant of Judah! This is what the Lord says:

16.text: 'If y'all head to Egypt, that same sword you runnin' from? It's gon' find you there. That famine you tryna dodge? It's gon' be waitin' on you. And you gon' die there.'

17.text: Everybody who runs to Egypt thinkin' it's safe? Y'all gon' die—by war, by hunger, or by sickness. Ain't nobody makin' it out.

18.text: God said, 'Just like I poured out my wrath on Jerusalem, I'll do the same to y'all if you go down to Egypt. People gon' use your name as a curse, sayin' "Don't be like them." You'll become a walking cautionary tale. And you ain't ever comin' back here.'

19.text: So yeah—God said, "Don't go to Egypt." I'm tellin' you straight up today.

20.text: Y'all were fake from the jump. You said, "Pray for us, Jeremiah, we'll do whatever God says," but your hearts were lyin'.

21.text: I came back, gave y'all the exact message—and you still ain't listen.

22.text: So now you need to know: if y'all go where your hearts already settin' out to go, you gon' die by sword, famine, and disease—right there in the land you was tryna run to for safety.

1.text: After Jeremiah finished sayin' everything God told him to say—no edits, no extras—

2.text: Azariah (son of Hoshaiah), Johanan (son of Kareah), and a bunch of proud, hard-headed men stepped up and said, "You lyin', Jeremiah. God ain't tell you to say, 'Don't go to Egypt.'"

3.text: "Baruch put you up to this! He tryna get us snatched up by the Babylonians—either killed or deported."

4.text: So Johanan, all the military leaders, and everybody else flat-out refused to listen to God's word. They decided to ignore the command to stay in Judah.

5.text: Johanan and the whole crew scooped up all the survivors—men, women, kids, even the king's daughters. Everybody who had been left behind with Gedaliah. And yep, they dragged Jeremiah and Baruch too.

6.text: And they all bounced to Egypt. They went anyway. Got as far as Tahpanhes. Direct disobedience.

7.text: Then God spoke to Jeremiah again—right there in Egypt.

8.text: "Grab some big stones," God said, "and bury them in the clay courtyard right at the front of Pharaoh's palace in Tahpanhes. Make sure the folks from Judah see you do it."

9.text: Then say this: 'This what the Lord of Heaven's Armies, the God of Israel, says—

10.text: "I'm sendin' Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon—my servant—and he gon' set his throne right here on top of these very stones you see buried. He gon' stretch his royal tent over this spot."

11.text: "When he comes? Egypt gettin' the smoke. Some gon' die, some gon' get taken, some gon' fall by the sword. Everybody's number gettin' called.

12.text: He gon' light Egypt's fake gods and temples up. Burn 'em down and drag the rest away. He gon' walk through Egypt like it's his—like a shepherd throwin' on a cloak.

13.text: Even their so-called holy spots at Beth Shemesh? Broken down. All their idol houses? Burned to ash."

1.text: This the word that came to Jeremiah 'bout all them Jews livin' in Egypt—in places like Migdol, Tahpanhes, Noph, and Pathros.

2.text: The Lord Almighty, the God of Israel, said: "Y'all saw what I did to Jerusalem and all Judah's cities. Look at 'em now—ghost towns.

3.text: That's 'cause they was actin' wild—burnin' incense, worshipin' gods they ain't know nothin' about. Not them, not their daddies, not even you.

4.text: I kept sendin' my prophets, early in the morning, sayin', 'Stop doin' that nasty mess I hate!'

5.text: But y'all ain't listen. Ain't nobody tryna turn from they ways.

6.text: So My anger burned hot, and I wiped Judah and Jerusalem out. Just look around—ruins and rubble."

7.text: "So now," God said, "why y'all out here destroyin' your own selves? Why you tryin' to kill off every man, woman, and child from Judah?

8.text: Y'all still burnin' incense to false gods in Egypt, like I ain't gon' respond? You doin' this to your own downfall—makin' yourself a global joke.

9.text: You forgot how messy your ancestors were? How wild the kings and queens acted? Even y'all wives? You doin' the same exact foolishness.

10.text: And y'all still proud. No humility, no fear of Me. You straight-up refused to follow My law or walk how I told your people to walk."

11.text: "So listen up," says the Lord of Heaven's Armies, "I'm comin' for y'all—Judah ain't gettin' off easy.

12.text: That leftover crew that ran to Egypt? They all gon' get it—sword, famine, disease. From the big names to the nobodies, they all gon' fall.

13.text: Just like I did Jerusalem, I'm doin' Egypt the same way.

14.text: Ain't nobody from Judah who ran to Egypt gon' make it back. They might wanna go home, but it's not happenin'. Only a few gon' escape."

15.text: Then the men who knew their wives was out here burnin' incense, and all them women too—a whole crowd of 'em—said to Jeremiah,

16.text: "We ain't tryna hear what you talkin' 'bout in the name of the Lord.

17.text: We gon' do what we said we'd do: burn incense and pour drinks for the Queen of Heaven. We been doin' that forever—us, our folks, even the kings and leaders in Judah. And back then, we had food, peace, and good times.

18.text: Ever since we stopped, it's been nothing but famine and death."

19.text: The women jumped in like, "And when we made those cakes and poured out them drinks to the Queen of Heaven, we ain't do it behind our husbands' backs—they was in on it too!"

20.text: Jeremiah looked at all of 'em—men, women, the whole crew—and said,

21.text: "Y'all really think God forgot how y'all used to act in Judah? That He ain't notice all that incense y'all been burnin'?

22.text: He got tired of your mess. That's why Judah got torched and left empty.

23.text: Y'all ain't listen, y'all sinned hard, and y'all ignored God's law. That's why this disaster hit y'all like it did."

24.text: Then Jeremiah said, "Listen here, all of Judah in Egypt—especially y'all women:

25.text: The Lord said, 'Y'all made your vows to the Queen of Heaven, and you been keepin' them. Well guess what? Go ahead and do it, keep goin'.

26.text: But know this—by My own name, I'm sayin' no one from Judah in Egypt gon' say My name again. Not a soul.

27.text: I ain't watchin' over y'all for good—I'm watchin' to bring judgment. Y'all gon' die out here from war and hunger, till it's barely anybody left.

28.text: A small few might survive and make it back to Judah, but then everybody gon' know whose words stand—Mine or theirs.

29.text: And here's the sign I'm givin' y'all, so you know I ain't playin':

30.text: Pharaoh Hophra, the king of Egypt, gon' get handed over to his enemies, just like Zedekiah got handed over to Nebuchadnezzar. Same story, same end.' "

1.text: This the message Jeremiah gave to Baruch—Neriah's son—when Baruch was writin' down all the stuff Jeremiah had said, back in year four of Jehoiakim's reign.

2.text: The Lord, God of Israel, told Jeremiah to say this to Baruch:

3.text: "You out here sayin', 'Woe is me! God just keep stackin' grief on top of pain. I'm worn out from all this cryin'. I can't even rest.'"

4.text: "Well, here's what you tell him: 'God said, "Look, I'm tearin' down what I built up. I'm yankin' up what I planted. I'm wreckin' this whole land."'"

5.text: "And you, Baruch? You think this the time to chase dreams and go big? Nah. Don't be out here lookin' for greatness—not in times like this. Trouble comin' for everybody," says the Lord. "But you? I'ma let you keep your life, no matter where you end up. That's gon' be your blessing."

1.text: This the word the Lord gave Jeremiah 'bout all the other nations.

2.text: Startin' with Egypt—about Pharaoh Necho's army at Carchemish near the Euphrates. That's when Nebuchadnezzar, king of Babylon, beat them down in the fourth year of King Jehoiakim's reign.

3.text: "Grab y'all shields! Get ready to throw down!"

4.text: "Y'all better strap them horses up! Mount up! Helmets on, spears sharp, armor tight!"

5.text: "But what's this? They shook! They runnin' scared! The mighty warriors fallin' back. Ain't nobody tryin' to look back. Fear got 'em all twisted," says the Lord.

6.text: "Don't matter if you fast or strong—you not gettin' away. They all gon' trip up and fall right there by the Euphrates."

7.text: "Who this swellin' up like a flood, rollin' through like they own everything?"

8.text: "That's Egypt—comin' in loud, talkin' 'bout, 'We takin' over, destroyin' the land and the people!'"

9.text: "Come on then, horses! Rage, chariots! Ethiopians, Libyans with shields, Lydians with bows—pull up!"

10.text: "'Cause this the Lord's day—God of Heaven's Armies. He settin' the record straight. Vengeance time. That sword gon' eat, gon' drink blood. The Lord sacrificin' enemies by the Euphrates in the north."

11.text: "Go ahead, Egypt, head to Gilead, try that healing balm. But it's useless—ain't no cure for what's comin'."

12.text: "The whole world gon' hear how you got embarrassed. Your screams gon' echo everywhere. Soldiers trippin' over each other. Ain't nobody standin'."

13.text: The Lord gave Jeremiah another word—about Babylon comin' to smack down Egypt.

14.text: "Spread the word in Egypt, Migdol, Noph, and Tahpanhes: 'Get ready! The sword's out here devourin' folks!'"

15.text: "Where y'all mighty men now? Swept away. Couldn't stand, 'cause the Lord pushed 'em down."

16.text: "They fallin' like dominoes, tellin' each other, 'Let's run back home, this too much!'"

17.text: "They shoutin', 'Pharaoh just noise now. His time ran out.'"

18.text: The King, the Lord of Heaven's Armies, says, "As sure as Tabor's a mountain and Carmel by the sea—I'm bringin' that judgment."

19.text: "Daughter of Egypt, pack yo' bags. Y'all goin' into captivity. Noph gon' be empty—ghost town."

20.text: "Egypt cute like a young cow, but destruction comin' up from the north."

21.text: "Even her mercenaries—lookin' all strong—gon' run off. They shook 'cause their day done come. Time's up."

22.text: "Egypt gon' hiss like a snake tryna slide away. But Babylon comin' with axes like lumberjacks—choppin' down everything."

23.text: "'They gon' clear her forest,' says the Lord, 'even though it's thick and wild. Too many enemies to count—like a swarm of locusts.'"

24.text: "Egypt gon' be ashamed. She gettin' handed over to folks from up north."

25.text: The Lord of Heaven's Armies, Israel's God, says: "I'ma deal with Amon from No, Pharaoh, and all Egypt—their gods, kings, and everybody who trusted them."

26.text: "I'ma hand 'em over to Nebuchadnezzar and his crew. But later on, Egypt gon' be like it used to be," says the Lord.

27.text: "But don't be scared, My servant Jacob. Don't trip, Israel. I'ma bring y'all back. I'll rescue your kids from where they been dragged off. Y'all gon' rest and chill. Ain't nobody gon' scare y'all no more."

28.text: "I got you," says the Lord. "I'm takin' care of all them other nations that scattered y'all—but you? I ain't gon' wipe you out. I'ma check you, correct you, 'cause I ain't lettin' you slide either."

1.text: This the word the Lord dropped on Jeremiah 'bout the Philistines—before Pharaoh rolled up on Gaza.

2.text: The Lord said: "Look, a wave comin' from the north—like a flood breakin' loose. It's gon' wash over the whole land, the cities, the people— Ain't nobody safe. Folks gon' be cryin' out, Everybody screamin' and wailin'."

3.text: "You gon' hear them war horses stomp the ground, Them chariots flyin' by, Wheels rattlin' so loud— Dads gon' be so shook they won't even look back for their own kids. They too scared to move."

4.text: "It's that day—the one where all the Philistines get wiped out. Even Tyre and Sidon ain't gon' have no one left to back 'em. The Lord comin' to snatch everything from Philistia, Even what's left from Caphtor—gone."

5.text: "Gaza out here mournin'—head bald like they lost everything. Ashkelon got cut off. The whole valley quiet. Y'all still tryna hurt yourselves? How long y'all gon' do that?"

6.text: "Yo, sword of the Lord—when you gon' chill? Can't you just go back in the sheath? Rest, be still, stop all this?"

7.text: "But how can it stop? The Lord ain't finished. He got business in Ashkelon and on the coast. That sword got orders—it's still on assignment."

1.text: This what the Lord of Heaven's Armies, Israel's God, said 'bout Moab: "Woe to Nebo—city got ran through. Kirjathaim embarrassed, done got taken. That fortress everybody bragged on? Shook and ashamed."

2.text: "Moab don't get no praise no more. Over in Heshbon, folks plannin' her downfall: 'Let's erase Moab off the map.' Even Madmen gon' get chopped down. The sword on y'all necks."

3.text: "You gon' hear cries outta Horonaim: 'They wreckin' us! Everything gone!'"

4.text: "Moab destroyed. Even the lil' kids cryin'. The whole land got a sound of mourning."

5.text: "Folks climbin' Luhith Hill cryin' the whole way up. On the way down Horonaim? Screams 'cause the enemy right behind 'em."

6.text: "Y'all better run! Save yourselves! Be like a tumbleweed in the desert—light and gone."

7.text: "You was leanin' on your stuff—your riches, your grind. But now you 'bout to get snatched. Your god Chemosh? He headed to captivity too—priests, princes, all of 'em."

8.text: "Every city gon' get hit. Ain't nobody safe. The valley gon' fall. The flatlands? Toast. The Lord already said it."

9.text: "Give Moab some wings. She gon' need 'em to get outta here. All them cities? About to be ghost towns."

10.text: "Cursed is the one who half-step for God. Cursed if you hold back when it's time to swing that sword."

11.text: "Moab been chillin' since forever. Ain't never been shaken up. Ain't been poured out like wine. Ain't been exiled. So he still smell the same. Still taste the same."

12.text: "But days comin'," says the Lord, "I'ma send folks to pour Moab out, shatter them jars. He gon' be flipped upside down, drained dry."

13.text: "Moab gon' be embarrassed by Chemosh, Just like Israel got shamed for trustin' in Bethel."

14.text: "Y'all out here sayin', 'We strong, we warriors.' Really?"

15.text: "Moab been stripped. City by city fallin'. Your best fighters? Dead." Says the King—the Lord of Armies.

16.text: "Moab's disaster comin' quick. His downfall ain't far off."

17.text: "Cry for him, y'all that nearby. All who knew his name—say this: 'Dang, the power stick snapped. That royal rod just broke.'"

18.text: "Daughter of Dibon, come off that high horse. Sit down in thirst—'cause Moab's enemy done showed up. Strongholds? Gone."

19.text: "Folks in Aroer, Post up by the road, ask folks runnin' past: 'What happened?!'"

20.text: "Moab embarrassed. Wrecked. Cry loud. Spread the word in Arnon—Moab been looted."

21.text: "Judgment slid across the whole plains— Holon, Jahzah, Mephaath,"

22.text: "Dibon, Nebo, Beth Diblathaim,"

23.text: "Kirjathaim, Beth Gamul, Beth Meon,"

24.text: "Kerioth, Bozrah— Every city in Moab, near and far—ALL of 'em."

25.text: "Moab's horn snapped off. His arm? Broken." Says the Lord.

26.text: "Get him drunk, 'cause he got too full of himself. Now he gon' drown in his own vomit— Folks gon' clown him."

27.text: "Didn't you laugh at Israel? Actin' like he was some petty thief? Every time you brought him up, y'all rolled your eyes. Guess what? That energy comin' back."

28.text: "Y'all in Moab—run to the caves. Leave them cities behind. Be like doves that nest on cliff walls."

29.text: "We done heard how arrogant Moab is. Puffed up, proud, feelin' himself too much."

30.text: "Yeah, I know his temper," says the Lord, "But it don't mean nothin'. His talk ain't changed a thing."

31.text: "So I'ma weep for Moab, Cry for his people. Even them men in Kir Heres gon' get tears."

32.text: "Vine of Sibmah, I'm cryin' for you— Like Jazer cried for hers. Your vines stretched far, even to the sea. But the raiders came—no more harvest, no more wine."

33.text: "Ain't no joy left in Moab. Fields empty. Wine presses quiet. Ain't nobody shoutin' while pressin' grapes anymore."

34.text: "Heshbon and Elealeh all the way down to Jahaz cryin' out. Even Zoar and Horonaim groanin' like a young cow. Nimrim's water? Dried up."

35.text: "I'ma shut down the whole idol game in Moab," says the Lord. "No more sacrifices on them hills. No more incense to fake gods."

36.text: "My heart wailin' like flutes for Moab. For the people of Kir Heres too. All that wealth they stacked? Gone."

37.text: "Everybody bald-headed. Beards shaved off. Cuts on they hands. Sackcloth around the waist."

38.text: "Mourning everywhere—in the streets, on the roofs. Why? 'Cause I smashed Moab like a pot nobody wanted." Says the Lord.

39.text: "They all gon' cry out: 'Look at her now! Moab, ashamed, runnin' away.' Everybody watchin' gon' be shook and laughin'."

40.text: "The Lord says: Somebody gon' swoop in like an eagle, Wings stretched over Moab."

41.text: "Kerioth snatched up, Fortresses fallin' fast. The soldiers? Heart racin' like a woman in labor."

42.text: "Moab gon' be wiped out as a nation— 'Cause they got too big for their britches, Thought they could flex on God."

43.text: "Fear, trap, and snare waitin' for you, Moab," says the Lord.

44.text: "If you dodge one, the next gon' catch you. This your year to get got."

45.text: "Folks runnin' to Heshbon tryna hide, But fire comin' outta there too. That blaze gon' burn Moab's crown. Chemosh's folks? Cooked."

46.text: "Moab, it's a wrap. Your god Chemosh ain't save nobody. Your sons? Gone. Your daughters? Captives."

47.text: "But don't get it twisted," says the Lord, "I'ma bring Moab back in the end. They gon' get a second chance— Way down the line."

1.text: This what the Lord said 'bout the people of Ammon: "Israel ain't got no kids? No heirs? Then how Milcom out here takin' over Gad's land and settlin' in their cities?"

2.text: "Watch this," says the Lord. "I'ma sound the war horn in Rabbah, Ammon's capital. City gon' be left in rubble, villages up in flames. And guess what? Israel takin' they land back."

3.text: "Cry out, Heshbon, 'cause Ai been looted! Y'all daughters of Rabbah, throw on sackcloth, Run wild near the city walls in grief. Milcom 'bout to be snatched up too—him and his priests and his princes."

4.text: "Y'all was braggin' on your valleys, Talkin' slick like nobody could touch you. Trustin' your riches like they couldn't be stripped."

5.text: "Well, I'ma put fear in your chest," says the Lord God of Armies. "Everybody gon' scatter in a panic. Ain't nobody comin' back to collect y'all either."

6.text: "But down the road, I'ma bring Ammon's people back," says the Lord.

7.text: To Edom, the Lord said: "What happened to y'all wisdom down in Teman? Y'all used to be smart. Y'all lost it?"

8.text: "Dedan, run. Get low, hide deep. Esau got judgment comin'. It's his time."

9.text: "If grape-pickers pulled up, they'd leave a few grapes. If robbers broke in, they'd only take what they needed. But I ain't leavin' nothin' behind."

10.text: "Esau—I done exposed him. Ain't nowhere to hide. His fam and friends? Stripped down too. Ain't nobody left."

11.text: "But leave them orphans with Me—I got them. And tell the widows to lean on Me."

12.text: "Even folks who ain't supposed to suffer been sippin' the judgment cup. You really think you gon' slide by? Nah. You gon' drink it too."

13.text: "I swear," says the Lord, "Bozrah gon' be a wasteland—forever cursed. All them cities? Wiped."

14.text: "I heard a message— Nations bein' summoned. 'Pull up. Time to ride on Edom.'"

15.text: "I'ma shrink you down, Edom. Everybody gon' look down on you."

16.text: "Your pride lied to you. You thought you was safe tucked up in the rocks. You flew high like an eagle, But I'ma bring you down." Says the Lord.

17.text: "People gon' walk past Edom shocked— Shakin' they heads at the destruction."

18.text: "It's gon' be like Sodom and Gomorrah— Ain't nobody gon' live there again."

19.text: "I'ma come in like a lion out the Jordan bush. Chase the folks out quick. Ain't nobody strong enough to stand against Me. You got a shepherd better than Me? Didn't think so."

20.text: "So hear what I planned for Edom, What I got lined up for Teman. Even the weakest among y'all gon' drag the rest out. Whole neighborhoods—done."

21.text: "The earth gon' shake when y'all fall. The screams? Gon' reach all the way to the Red Sea."

22.text: "I'ma swoop in like an eagle over Bozrah. Edom's warriors gon' feel like women in labor—screamin' and shook."

23.text: The Lord says: "Hamath and Arpad—embarrassed and scared. Bad news got the sea stirred up—no peace."

24.text: "Damascus weak now. Tryna run but fear got her stuck. She hurtin' like a woman givin' birth."

25.text: "Why that proud city ain't deserted yet? The one I used to delight in?"

26.text: "But them young men gon' die in the streets. Every soldier gon' fall," says the Lord of Armies.

27.text: "And I'ma light up Damascus' walls. Them royal palaces of Ben-Hadad? Burnt."

28.text: God had a word about Kedar and the Hazor kingdoms—Babylon gon' wreck them: "Rise up and attack Kedar. Wipe out them Eastern nomads."

29.text: "Take their tents, flocks, curtains, pots, camels—everything. And they gon' scream, 'Fear all around!'"

30.text: "Hazor folks, run far! Hide deep," says the Lord. "Nebuchadnezzar got y'all name circled—he plottin' on you."

31.text: "Get up and attack that rich nation that thinks they safe," says the Lord. "They ain't got no gates, no bars, no allies. They chillin' solo."

32.text: "Well, I'ma take their camels and cattle as prizes. And scatter them folks to the wind. Hazor gettin' hit from all sides."

33.text: "Hazor gon' be left for jackals—empty forever. Ain't nobody livin' there again."

34.text: When King Zedekiah started his rule, the Lord gave Jeremiah this word about Elam:

35.text: "I'ma break Elam's bow—yeah, their strongest weapon."

36.text: "I'ma send winds from all directions, Blow Elam out to every nation. They gon' be scattered worldwide."

37.text: "They gon' be shook in front of every enemy. I'ma pour out My wrath. The sword comin' for 'em till they done."

38.text: "I'ma set up My throne in Elam— Wipe out their kings and rulers."

39.text: "But later on," says the Lord, "I'ma bring their people back from captivity."

1.text: This the word the Lord dropped on Babylon, comin' through the prophet Jeremiah.

2.text: Go tell everybody, let it be known! Set up a sign, don't keep this secret: "Babylon done fell! Bel embarrassed. Merodach broke to pieces. All them idols lookin' dumb now. Their statues? Shattered."

3.text: A nation from the north comin' for her, Gon' turn her land into a ghost town. Ain't gon' be no folks, no animals— Everybody evacuatin'.

4.text: "In them days," says the Lord, "My folks—Israel and Judah both— Gon' come cryin', seekin' Me with all they heart.

5.text: They gon' be askin' for directions to Zion, Facin' that way sayin', 'Let's get back to the Lord. Let's lock in with Him for good— A deal we won't forget.'"

6.text: My people out here lost like stray sheep. They shepherds led 'em wrong, Got 'em wanderin' from hill to hill, Now they don't even remember where home is.

7.text: Everybody who caught 'em took a bite, And didn't feel bad about it. They was like, "They sinned anyway, Turned they back on the Lord, The one who held 'em down."

8.text: Y'all better dip outta Babylon! Slide outta Chaldean territory. Run like rams leadin' the herd.

9.text: I'm bringin' a squad of nations from the north, And they gon' pull up hard on Babylon. She gettin' surrounded and captured. Arrows gon' fly straight— Ain't none missin'.

10.text: Chaldea gon' be ripe for the takin'. Anybody who snatches from her Gon' be walkin' away full, says the Lord.

11.text: Y'all got hype 'cause y'all wrecked My people, Y'all acted like y'all was on top. Like a cow in the field feelin' herself, Bellowin' like big bulls.

12.text: Well, guess what? Your mama gon' be ashamed. The one who birthed you gon' be disgraced. Y'all gon' be like nobodies— Left in the dust, dried up and forgotten.

13.text: Babylon caught God's anger, Ain't nobody livin' there no more. Whole place gon' be wrecked, Folks gon' pass by and be like, "Dang."

14.text: Line up against her from every side, All y'all bow shooters—let 'em fly. Don't hold back nothin'. She messed with the Lord.

15.text: Yell all around her! She's surrenderin'. Foundations gone. Walls down. This the Lord's revenge. Do her like she did y'all.

16.text: Cut off the farmers, The ones swingin' sickles. Everybody runnin' scared from the sword. Folk headin' back to their people, Dippin' back to their homelands.

17.text: Israel out here like scattered sheep. Lions tore into 'em. First Assyria ate 'em up, Now Babylon got what's left.

18.text: So this what the Lord, God of Israel, say: I'm comin' for the king of Babylon Just like I came for Assyria's king.

19.text: But I'ma bring Israel back home, They gon' eat in Carmel and Bashan. They gon' be full and satisfied Up on Mount Ephraim and Gilead.

20.text: "In them days," says the Lord, "You gon' look for Israel's sin—ain't none. Try find Judah's wrongs—they gone. I forgave the ones I saved."

21.text: Go up and smash Merathaim, Tear down Pekod's folks. Wipe 'em out, no mercy. Do everything I told you.

22.text: You hear that? That's war in the air—pure chaos.

23.text: Babylon, the hammer of the world, Broke in pieces! Now she just ruins In the middle of everybody.

24.text: I set you up, Babylon. You didn't even know it. Now you caught— 'Cause you went against Me.

25.text: God opened His armory, Brought out the tools of His anger. Time to handle His business In the land of the Chaldeans.

26.text: Come from all sides, Tear into her storehouses. Pile her up like trash heaps. Wipe her off the map.

27.text: Kill her strong ones. Let 'em fall like slaughtered cattle. This the day—payback time.

28.text: You hear them voices runnin' from Babylon? They made it to Zion shoutin': "God takin' vengeance, For His house, His temple!"

29.text: Gather the archers! Post up all around her. Don't let nobody out. Hit her back—measure for measure. She got too proud, Went toe to toe with the Holy One.

30.text: So her young men gon' drop in the streets. All her soldiers? Wiped out that day.

31.text: Look here, Miss Big Shot, I'm comin' for you, says the Lord. Your time's up.

32.text: Pride bout to trip and fall. Ain't nobody helpin' you up. Fire gon' eat up your cities And everything nearby.

33.text: Israel and Judah been oppressed— Snatched up and not released. Their captors ain't lettin' go.

34.text: But their Redeemer? He strong! His name the Lord of Heaven's Armies. He fightin' for 'em hard, Gon' give rest to the land And shake Babylon's peace.

35.text: A sword for the Chaldeans! For Babylon's folks, For her rulers and her wise men.

36.text: A sword for the fortune tellers— They lookin' dumb now. A sword for her mighty ones— They shakin' in fear.

37.text: A sword for her horses and chariots, For all them foreigners in her mix— They gon' fold like scared women. A sword for her treasures— Gettin' looted.

38.text: A drought comin' for her waters— All dried up. Too many fake gods, And folks losin' their minds over 'em.

39.text: So now it's just wild animals and hyenas, Even ostriches movin' in. Ain't nobody livin' there ever again.

40.text: Just like Sodom and Gomorrah Got wiped out with their folks, Ain't nobody settin' up shop in Babylon again.

41.text: Look, a crew comin' from the north, Big squad with kings and power, Rollin' from the far corners of the earth.

42.text: They armed up with bows and spears, Cruel, no mercy. They loud like waves crashin', Ridin' out deep— All aimed at Babylon.

43.text: King of Babylon heard the news, Hands shakin', heart racin', Scared like a woman givin' birth.

44.text: He comin' like a lion from the Jordan, Stormin' into the stronghold. I'ma run them out quick. Ain't nobody steppin' to Me. Who can check Me? Who bold enough to try?

45.text: So hear the Lord's game plan, His whole strategy against Babylon. Even the weakest gon' help take her down. Her land gon' be left empty with her.

46.text: When Babylon falls, The earth gon' tremble. Everybody gon' hear the cry worldwide.

1.text: The Lord said, 'Look, I'm sendin' a wild wind to tear Babylon up and hit all them folks over there in Leb Kamai.'

2.text: I'm sendin' folks to shake Babylon down—gon' strip her clean. When that judgment day hit, they gon' surround her from all sides.

3.text: Tell the archers: get ready. Don't hold back—wipe out her soldiers. Don't spare the young ones. Erase the whole army.

4.text: Them Chaldean streets gon' be full of bodies—folk laid out in the middle of the block.

5.text: God ain't left Israel or Judah hangin'. Even though they messed up big time, the Holy One still got 'em.

6.text: Run, y'all! Get up outta Babylon while you can. Don't get caught up in her mess. This God's moment of payback, and He don't miss.

7.text: Babylon was like a gold cup in God's hand—had the whole world drunk off her foolishness. Now everybody actin' wild.

8.text: Outta nowhere, Babylon done crashed. Cry for her, if you want. Try and heal her with some balm—but it might be too late.

9.text: We tried to fix Babylon, but she ain't wanna change. Let's bounce—go back home. Her judgment reach all the way to the sky.

10.text: The Lord showed up for us. Let's go back to Zion and tell everybody what God done did!

11.text: Sharpen them arrows. Grab your shields. God stirred up the Medes kings to destroy Babylon 'cause they disrespected His temple.

12.text: Put the flag up on Babylon's wall. Guard up. Watchmen posted. Trap set. God already planned this—now He makin' it happen.

13.text: You sittin' pretty by all them waters, with all that money—but your time up. You've been greedy too long.

14.text: God said, 'I swear, I'm gon' fill your city with men like locusts, and they gon' holler war cries all over you.'

15.text: God made the earth with His power, built the world with His wisdom, and stretched out the sky with His mind.

16.text: When He speaks, the heavens rumble. He pulls steam up from the earth, makes the lightning flash, and wind blow out His stash.

17.text: Folks be lookin' dumb—think they smart, but they ain't. Every smith embarrassed 'cause them fake gods they made ain't real.

18.text: Them idols? Worthless. Straight up nonsense. When God's judgment hits, they get wiped out too.

19.text: But our God? He ain't like that. He made everything. Israel belongs to Him. He go by 'The Lord of Heaven's Armies.'

20.text: God said, 'You my battle axe. I use you to wreck nations and tear up kingdoms.'

21.text: 'You break horses and riders, chariots and drivers.'

22.text: 'You smash men and women, old folks and kids, young men and girls.'

23.text: 'You wreck shepherds and their sheep, farmers and oxen, governors and rulers.'

24.text: God said, 'I'ma pay Babylon and everybody in Chaldea back for everything they did to Zion—y'all gon' see it.'

25.text: 'Babylon, you that big destroyin' mountain? I'm comin' for you,' says the Lord. 'I'ma throw you down and burn you up.'

26.text: 'Ain't nobody gon' use you to build nothin'. You gon' be empty and ruined forever.'

27.text: Raise the flag, sound the trumpet, gather the nations—Ararat, Minni, Ashkenaz. Call a commander. Send them horses like a swarm.

28.text: Get the armies ready—Medes and their kings, rulers, and whole territories.

29.text: The whole land gon' shake when God's will hits Babylon. Ain't nobody gon' be livin' there no more.

30.text: Babylon's strong soldiers gave up. They just sittin' in they spots—scared, weak, burnt out. Gates busted. Homes gone.

31.text: Runners passin' messages back and forth to the king—'Yo, the city surrounded!'

32.text: 'They blocked the exits, burnt the reeds, and the soldiers shook.'

33.text: God said, 'Babylon's like wheat on the threshin' floor—it's time to crush her. Her harvest day is comin'.'

34.text: 'Nebuchadnezzar swallowed us whole, chewed us up, spit us out like nothin'. Treated us like a snack.'

35.text: Zion says, 'Let Babylon pay for the pain they caused. Jerusalem say, 'Put our blood on their heads.'

36.text: God said, 'I got you—I'ma fight for you and get justice. I'ma dry up Babylon's sea and springs.'

37.text: 'Babylon gon' be a heap of rubble, a home for wild dogs. Folks gon' see her and hiss. Ain't nobody gon' live there.'

38.text: 'They used to roar like lions—now they ain't got nothin' left.'

39.text: 'I'ma give 'em a big feast, get 'em drunk, let 'em party—and then they gon' fall into a sleep they'll never wake up from.'

40.text: 'I'ma drag 'em down like lambs to the slaughter—like rams and goats headed to die.'

41.text: 'How the mighty Babylon fallin'! The city that folks praised is now nothin' but rubble.'

42.text: 'Like a sea flood, destruction drowned her. Waves covered everything.'

43.text: 'Her towns dried up, straight ghost towns. Ain't nobody walkin' through.'

44.text: 'I'm takin' down Bel, their fake god. Gonna spit out all he stole. Ain't no nations bowin' to him no more. Babylon's wall? Gone.'

45.text: God say, 'My people, get outta there! Save yourselves from the heat of My wrath!'

46.text: Don't be scared by all the rumors. First year it's one thing, then another rumor comes. War gon' break out—rulers fightin' each other.

47.text: God says, 'It's almost time—I'm takin' down every idol in Babylon. The land gon' be ashamed, and bodies gon' be everywhere.'

48.text: 'Heaven and earth gon' celebrate when Babylon fall—her enemies comin' from the north,' says the Lord.

49.text: Just like she made Israel bleed, now the whole world gon' watch Babylon bleed out too.

50.text: If you made it out alive, don't look back! Remember God and keep Jerusalem in your heart.

51.text: We embarrassed. Folks clownin' us 'cause outsiders walked all up in God's temple.

52.text: But God said, 'The day comin'—I'ma wreck them idols, and people gon' be groanin' all across the land.'

53.text: Even if Babylon climb to the sky, or fortify her towers, I'ma send robbers to snatch her up, says the Lord.

54.text: You hear that? That cry from Babylon? That's the sound of her fallin'.

55.text: The Lord shut down her loud mouth. She used to roar, now she drownin' in her own mess.

56.text: The thief comin'—her strong men caught, bows broken. God don't play. He repays for real.

57.text: He said, 'I'ma get her leaders, smart ones, soldiers—everybody—drunk. They gon' sleep and never wake up.'

58.text: God said, 'Them big Babylon walls? Cracked. Gates? Burned. Y'all workin' hard for nothin'—that fire gon' eat it all up.'

59.text: This what Jeremiah told Seraiah, son of Neriah, when he went to Babylon with King Zedekiah in his fourth year. Seraiah was the travel planner.

60.text: Jeremiah wrote all the bad stuff comin' for Babylon in a book—all of it.

61.text: He told Seraiah, 'When you get there and see the city, read this out loud.'

62.text: Then say, 'Lord, You said this city gon' be wiped out. No people, no animals—just empty forever.'

63.text: 'And when you finish readin', tie that scroll to a rock and toss it in the Euphrates.'

64.text: 'Then say, "Babylon gon' sink like this and never get back up from all the destruction God bringin'."' That's it—that's all Jeremiah had to say.

1.text: Zedekiah was twenty-one when he became king, and he ruled in Jerusalem for eleven years. His mama was Hamutal, daughter of Jeremiah from Libnah.

2.text: He did evil in the Lord's sight—just like Jehoiakim had done.

3.text: It all went down 'cause the Lord was done with Jerusalem and Judah. He let it all fall apart, pushed them out His presence. Zedekiah? He thought he was slick and rebelled against Babylon's king.

4.text: In Zedekiah's ninth year, tenth month, tenth day—Nebuchadnezzar and his whole army showed up at Jerusalem. They surrounded the city and built a wall to trap it in.

5.text: The siege dragged on 'til Zedekiah's eleventh year.

6.text: By the fourth month, ninth day, the famine hit hard—ain't no food left for anybody.

7.text: That's when the wall finally broke. The soldiers ran out at night through a gate by the king's garden. Chaldeans were everywhere, but they tried to escape across the plain.

8.text: But Babylon's army chased Zedekiah down and caught him near Jericho. His soldiers? Gone. Scattered.

9.text: They grabbed the king, brought him to Nebuchadnezzar at Riblah in Hamath, and that's where he got judged.

10.text: They made Zedekiah watch his sons get killed. Then they executed all Judah's leaders at Riblah too.

11.text: After that, they gouged out Zedekiah's eyes, chained him in bronze, and dragged him off to Babylon. He stayed locked up 'til the day he died.

12.text: In the fifth month, tenth day—nineteenth year of Nebuchadnezzar's reign—Nebuzaradan, the captain of the guard, rolled up on Jerusalem.

13.text: He set fire to the Lord's temple, the king's house, and every important house in the city. Burned it all down.

14.text: His whole crew tore down the walls surrounding Jerusalem.

15.text: Then Nebuzaradan took more folks captive: the rest of the poor, the ones who had switched sides, and all the skilled workers.

16.text: But he left a few poor folks behind to take care of the vineyards and farms.

17.text: The bronze pillars, the water basin, and the carts in God's house—they broke all that down and took the bronze back to Babylon.

18.text: They snatched up the pots, shovels, trimmers, bowls, spoons—all the bronze gear the priests used.

19.text: Also grabbed the gold and silver: basins, firepans, bowls, pots, lampstands, spoons, cups—everything of value.

20.text: Those two bronze pillars, that huge basin, the twelve bulls under it, and the carts Solomon made? Too much bronze to even measure.

21.text: One of those pillars was 27 feet tall, 18 feet around, 3 inches thick—hollow inside.

22.text: It had a 7½-foot-high bronze cap with netting and pomegranates all around it. The other pillar had the same.

23.text: Ninety-six pomegranates on the sides, one hundred total in the decoration.

24.text: Nebuzaradan arrested Seraiah the high priest, Zephaniah the second priest, and three doorkeepers.

25.text: He also took a military officer, seven of the king's close advisors, the army's top scribe who recruited troops, and sixty regular men still in the city.

26.text: He brought them all to the king of Babylon at Riblah.

27.text: The king had them executed right there in Hamath. That's how Judah got carried off into exile.

28.text: Here's who got taken: In year seven—3,023 Jews.

29.text: In year eighteen—832 more from Jerusalem.

30.text: In year twenty-three—745 more under Nebuzaradan. All together: 4,600 people.

31.text: Now check this—37 years into Jehoiachin's exile, twelfth month, 25th day, Evil-Merodach became king in Babylon. He decided to show Jehoiachin some love and pulled him out of prison.

32.text: He spoke real nice to him and gave him better status than the other captured kings in Babylon.

33.text: Jehoiachin took off the prison clothes, ate at the king's table regularly, and lived that royal life from then on.

34.text: And every single day, he got his food portion from the king—faithfully, until the day he died.

1.text: There was this man named Job, livin' in the land of Uz. Real solid dude—blameless, straight-up, feared God, and stayed far from evil.

2.text: He had seven sons and three daughters.

3.text: Bruh was loaded. He owned seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred pairs of oxen, five hundred female donkeys, and had mad workers. He was that guy out East—nobody had it like Job.

4.text: His sons used to throw feasts on their own scheduled days, and they'd invite their three sisters to come eat and drink with 'em.

5.text: After the party days wrapped up, Job would get up early, pray over his kids, and offer burnt sacrifices for all of 'em. He was like, 'Just in case one of them messed up or disrespected God in their hearts.' He did that every time—dude was committed.

6.text: One day, the heavenly crew came to check in with the Lord, and Satan slid in too.

7.text: The Lord said, 'Where you been?' Satan said, 'You know me—I've been out here roaming, walkin' all over the earth.'

8.text: Then God hit him with, 'So you peeped my guy Job, huh? Ain't nobody like him—solid, upright, fears Me, and don't mess with evil.'

9.text: Satan said, 'But Job ain't just loyal for nothin', though.'

10.text: 'You done put a whole fence around him, his family, and everything he own. He blessed because You blessed him. His bag is up cause of You.'

11.text: 'But let You touch his stuff, take it all away—watch him curse You to Your face.'

12.text: God said, 'Bet. You can do what you want with everything he got, just don't lay a hand on him.' So Satan dipped out from God's presence.

13.text: One day, Job's kids was all chillin', eatin' and drinking at the oldest brother's house.

14.text: Then a messenger came runnin' to Job like, 'The oxen were out workin' the field, and the donkeys nearby,'

15.text: 'When the Sabeans rolled up, took all the animals, and killed the workers. I'm the only one who made it out to tell you!'

16.text: While he was still talkin', another one pulled up: 'Fire from the sky—God's fire—came down and burned up the sheep and all the servants. I'm the only one who got out to tell you!'

17.text: Before he could finish, another dude ran in: 'The Chaldeans came in three squads, jacked all your camels, and killed the crew. I'm the only one left to tell you!'

18.text: And while he was still talkin', another burst in: 'Your sons and daughters were eatin' and drinkin' at the oldest brother's place,'

19.text: 'When a wild wind came outta nowhere, hit all four corners of the house—it collapsed. Everybody gone. I'm the only one who survived to tell you.'

20.text: Then Job stood up, tore his robe, shaved his head, fell to the ground—and worshipped.

21.text: He said, 'I came in this world with nothin', and I'ma leave with nothin'. The Lord gave it, the Lord took it away. Blessed be the name of the Lord.'

22.text: Through all this? Job ain't sin. He didn't blame God for anything.

1.text: Another day came around when God's heavenly crew pulled up to check in, and guess who showed up again? Yep—Satan was right there in the mix.

2.text: The Lord said to him, 'Where you been?' Satan said, 'Just out here, you know—roamin' the earth, walkin' around, peepin' everything.'

3.text: Then God said, 'So what about my guy Job? Still holdin' it down. Ain't nobody like him—blameless, real one, fears Me, stays away from evil. And even after you had Me let you mess with him for no reason, he still ain't switch up. Still solid.'

4.text: Satan said, 'Man, skin for skin! A man'll give up anything to save his own life.'

5.text: 'But go ahead—touch his body, his bones, his flesh. Bet he'll curse You to Your face.'

6.text: God said, 'Alright then—he's in your hands. Just don't kill him.'

7.text: So Satan dipped out and hit Job with nasty, painful boils—head to toe, feet to scalp.

8.text: Job ended up sittin' in ashes, scratchin' himself with a broken piece of pottery. That's all he had left.

9.text: Then his wife said, 'You still tryna keep your integrity? Just curse God and die already.'

10.text: Job said, 'Girl, you soundin' real foolish right now. Should we only take the good from God but not the bad too?' And even with all that pain, Job ain't say one sinful word.

11.text: When Job's three boys—Eliphaz from Teman, Bildad from Shuh, and Zophar from Naamah—heard about everything that happened, they pulled up from their own cities. They planned it out ahead of time to come sit with him, mourn with him, and try to comfort him.

12.text: When they got close and saw him from a distance, they didn't even recognize him. They broke down cryin', tore their robes, and threw dust in the air over their heads.

13.text: Then they just sat with him on the ground for seven days and seven nights. Didn't say a single word—'cause they could see the pain on him was too deep.

1.text: After all that, Job finally opened his mouth and cursed the day he was born.

2.text: He said,

3.text: 'Forget the day I came into this world, And the night somebody said, "It's a boy!"'

4.text: 'Let that day be straight-up darkness. Don't let God even look for it. Let the sun skip over it like it don't exist.'

5.text: 'Let darkness and death take claim on that day. Let a thick cloud smother it. Let it be shook by the terror of gloom.'

6.text: 'And that night? Let it get snatched by the shadows. Don't let it celebrate with the rest of the year. Leave it out the calendar like it never mattered.'

7.text: 'Let that night be dry—empty. No joy, no shouts, nothin'.'

8.text: 'Let the ones who curse days go in on it— The same folks who wake Leviathan up.'

9.text: 'Let its morning stars go dark. Let it hope for sunrise and get none. Let the daylight skip it like it's cursed.'

10.text: 'All 'cause it ain't block me from being born. It didn't keep me from all this pain I see now.'

11.text: 'Why didn't I just die when I was born? Why didn't I go out as soon as I came out the womb?'

12.text: 'Why was I even laid on somebody's knees? Why did they nurse me like I was supposed to grow up?'

13.text: 'If I had died, I'd be quiet by now. Sleepin'. At peace.'

14.text: 'I'd be laid out with kings and big-time leaders, The ones who built monuments that now sit in ruins.'

15.text: 'Or maybe with princes who stashed gold, And had silver piled up in their houses.'

16.text: 'Or maybe I should've been like a miscarriage, Like a baby who never saw the light of day.'

17.text: 'Where I'd be, the wicked ain't start nothin'. And the tired folks finally rest.'

18.text: 'Even the prisoners chill together. They don't hear no more yelling from oppressors.'

19.text: 'Everybody there—big or small. And the servant ain't got no boss no more.'

20.text: 'So why is light even given to people goin' through it? Why keep breathin' when your soul is bitter?'

21.text: 'Folks out here beggin' for death, Lookin' for it like it's treasure buried in the ground.'

22.text: 'And when they finally find a grave? They get hype, like they won the lottery.'

23.text: 'Why give life to somebody who can't see a way out? Somebody God done boxed in on every side?'

24.text: 'I'm cryin' before I can even eat. Groans be pourin' outta me like water.'

25.text: 'The thing I feared the most? It happened. The nightmare I tried to dodge? It pulled up on me.'

26.text: 'I ain't got no peace, no quiet, no break. Just pain—back to back to back.'

1.text: Then Eliphaz from Teman spoke up and said,

2.text: 'Bruh, if I say somethin', you gon' get mad? 'Cause honestly, I can't just sit here quiet.'

3.text: 'You the one who used to teach folks, Liftin' up the ones who was weak and worn down.'

4.text: 'Your words used to hold up folks who was about to fall, And you gave strength to shaky knees.'

5.text: 'But now that it's hittin' you? You out here overwhelmed and broken.'

6.text: 'Wasn't it your fear of God that gave you confidence? Wasn't it your integrity that kept you grounded?'

7.text: 'Let's think—who ever died for no reason, bein' innocent? When did the good folks ever get wiped out for nothin'?'

8.text: 'From what I've seen, If you plant mess, you gon' grow mess. If you spread drama, it's gon' come back around.'

9.text: 'God's breath alone can take folks out. His anger is like fire—it consumes.'

10.text: 'Lions may roar all tough, Young lions might show their teeth, But all of 'em can get their power snatched in a second.'

11.text: 'Old lions die if they can't find food. And the cubs? Scattered with no protection.'

12.text: 'Now let me tell you somethin' I heard on the low. It came to me in a whisper.'

13.text: 'In one of them eerie night visions— You know, when folks fall into deep sleep?'

14.text: 'A chill hit me. I started shakin'. My bones? Felt like they was about to crack.'

15.text: 'Then somethin'—a spirit—passed by my face. The hair on my body stood straight up.'

16.text: 'It stopped, but I couldn't make out what it was. There was this shadowy form, and silence. Then a voice broke through:'

17.text: "'Can a human be more righteous than God? Can anybody be purer than the One who made 'em?'"

18.text: "'If He don't even fully trust His own servants, And He's called out His angels when they slipped…'"

19.text: "'…Then how much more us—just dirt and bones, Livin' in bodies made of clay, easy to crush like bugs?'"

20.text: "'From sun-up to sundown, folks fall apart. They die off, and nobody even notices.'"

21.text: "'Even the strong ones fade. They die with no wisdom, no legacy.'"

1.text: 'Go 'head and cry out. See if anybody gon' answer. Which one of God's holy ones you think gon' pull up for you?'

2.text: 'Anger kills the fool, And jealousy? That'll take out the simple-minded quick.'
