3.text: 'Stand up and take it like a man. I got questions—you gon' answer Me.'

4.text: 'Where were you when I laid down the earth's foundation? Go 'head—explain it if you understand.'

5.text: 'Who decided how wide it should be? You know that too, huh? Who pulled the measuring line across it?'

6.text: 'What's holdin' it all up? Who dropped the cornerstone in place—'

7.text: 'Back when the morning stars were singin', And all heaven's crew was shoutin' for joy?'

8.text: 'Who shut up the sea behind doors When it broke loose like it was bein' born?'

9.text: 'When I wrapped it in clouds like a blanket, And made thick darkness its baby clothes?'

10.text: 'I gave it limits, laid down borders, Set up bars and locked gates.'

11.text: 'And I said, "You can come this far—no further. Your waves stop right here."'

12.text: 'Since you been alive, have you told the morning when to show up? Made the dawn know its place?'

13.text: 'So it could grab the earth by the edges And shake the wicked out like dust from a rug?'

14.text: 'It rolls out like clay under a stamp, And shines like a fresh robe.'

15.text: 'The wicked don't get that light. Their power gets snapped like a twig.'

16.text: 'You ever walk through the ocean floor? Explored the deepest parts of the sea?'

17.text: 'You ever seen the gates of death? Peeked inside the shadow of death's doorway?'

18.text: 'You really understand how wide this earth is? Tell Me, if you know all this.'

19.text: 'Where does the light live? Where darkness post up at?'

20.text: 'You know how to take it to its zone? Lead it back home like GPS?'

21.text: 'You know, right? You was born back then, You been around a long time, huh?'

22.text: 'You ever been inside the snow vault? Or seen where I store the hail—'

23.text: 'The same hail I keep ready for war, For the day trouble comes?'

24.text: 'What's the route light takes? Or the path the east wind travels across the land?'

25.text: 'Who carves out paths for floodwaters? Or directs lightning like it's on a mission?'

26.text: 'Who makes it rain where no one lives? Pourin' down on empty land?'

27.text: 'Just to bring life to dead ground, So grass can grow again?'

28.text: 'Rain got a daddy? Who fathered the drops of dew?'

29.text: 'Who gave birth to the ice? Who delivers heaven's frost?'

30.text: 'Water turns hard like rock, And the deep freezes over like glass.'

31.text: 'Can you lock together the Pleiades stars, Or unbuckle Orion's belt?'

32.text: 'Can you lead out the constellations at the right time, Or guide the Big Dipper and her cubs?'

33.text: 'You know the laws of the universe? Can you make them rule the earth?'

34.text: 'Can you call up the clouds And get rained on just like that?'

35.text: 'Can you send out lightning and have it check in with you like, "Here we are"?'

36.text: 'Who gave humans wisdom? Who put understanding in the mind and heart?'

37.text: 'Who can count the clouds with wisdom? Who tips over the water jars of heaven—'

38.text: 'When the dirt clumps up, And the ground locks up like cement?'

39.text: 'Can you hunt food for the lion, Or feed the young ones when they hungry?'

40.text: 'When they hidin' in the cut, Layin' low waitin' to pounce?'

41.text: 'Who gives the raven its food, When the babies cry out to God, Wanderin' around lookin' for somethin' to eat?'

1.text: 'You know when the wild mountain goats have their babies? Can you mark the moment the deer goes into labor?'

2.text: 'You know how long they carry before birth? You got their due dates on your calendar?'

3.text: 'They crouch down, push through the pain, And bring their babies into the world.'

4.text: 'Those babies grow up strong, eatin' off the land, Then they dip—and they ain't comin' back.'

5.text: 'Who gave the wild donkey its freedom? Who untied the ropes from the wild ass?'

6.text: 'I made the wilderness his crib, The desert his home address.'

7.text: 'He don't care about no city noise, He ain't listenin' to no boss yellin' orders.'

8.text: 'He roams the mountains for food, Lookin' for green wherever he can find it.'

9.text: 'You think the wild ox gon' work for you? Gon' lay down in your barn like a pet?'

10.text: 'Can you tie him up and make him plow your field? You think he gon' follow your lead down in the valley?'

11.text: 'Just 'cause he's strong—you gon' trust him? You really about to leave your grind in his hooves?'

12.text: 'You think he bringin' the harvest back to you, Piling grain on your threshing floor like a worker?'

13.text: 'The ostrich flaps her wings with pride, But they ain't shaped like the stork's.'

14.text: 'She just drops her eggs in the dust, Leaves them out where they could get stepped on.'

15.text: 'She forgets a foot might crush 'em, Or wild animals might come and break 'em.'

16.text: 'She treats her babies like they ain't even hers. She worked for nothin' and don't even care.'

17.text: 'Why? 'Cause I didn't give her wisdom. She ain't got no understanding.'

18.text: 'But when she runs? She lifts off, And clowns the horse and its rider like she runnin' track.'

19.text: 'You the one that gave the horse its strength? You the one who wrapped his neck in thunder?'

20.text: 'You make him jump like a locust, Snortin' so loud it shakes folks up?'

21.text: 'He stompin' the ground, hyped on his power, Rushin' straight into battle without hesitation.'

22.text: 'He laughs at fear—won't flinch, Ain't turnin' around from no sword.'

23.text: 'The quiver rattles, spears and javelins flash, But he's still movin' forward.'

24.text: 'He eats up the ground with his rage, And won't stop even when the trumpet blasts.'

25.text: 'As soon as he hears that trumpet, he like, "Let's go!" He smellin' battle from miles out— He hears the captains shout and knows what time it is.'

26.text: 'Does the hawk fly south 'cause of your wisdom? He spread his wings because you told him to?'

27.text: 'Does the eagle rise up at your command? Make his home way up high?'

28.text: 'He live on the rocks, Builds his spot in the cliffs and strongholds.'

29.text: 'From up there, he watching everything. He peepin' prey from miles away.'

30.text: 'His young ones drink blood like water. And wherever the dead are? That's where he be.'

1.text: Then the Lord kept speakin' to Job and said,

2.text: 'You really tryna check the Almighty? You the one correctin' Me now? If you bold enough to call Me out, go 'head—say somethin'.'

3.text: Then Job answered the Lord and said,

4.text: 'I got nothin'. I'm ashamed. What could I possibly say to You now?'

5.text: 'I already spoke once—I ain't sayin' no more. Said it twice, but I'm done. I'm quiet now.'

6.text: Then the Lord answered Job from the whirlwind and said,

7.text: 'Brace yourself like a man— You gon' answer Me this time.'

8.text: 'You really tryna cancel My judgment Just to make yourself look righteous?'

9.text: 'You got arms like Me? Can you thunder with a voice that shakes the sky?'

10.text: 'Then go ahead—dress yourself in glory. Throw on majesty like it's your outfit.'

11.text: 'Pour out all your anger on the proud. Humble 'em—bring 'em down.'

12.text: 'Take down every arrogant one you see. Make 'em bow right where they stand.'

13.text: 'Bury 'em in the dust. Lock 'em up in the dark where nobody sees 'em.'

14.text: 'If you can do all that, I'll admit you can save yourself.'

15.text: 'Now look at Behemoth—yeah, I made him same time I made you. He eats grass like an ox, but don't get it twisted.'

16.text: 'His strength sittin' heavy in his hips, His power stacked in them core muscles.'

17.text: 'He swings his tail like a cedar tree— His thighs? Built like rope-wrapped steel.'

18.text: 'His bones? Like bronze beams. His ribs? Iron bars.'

19.text: 'He top-tier—firstborn of My creations. Only I got the sword sharp enough for him.'

20.text: 'He chill in the mountains where the wild beasts play, And the hills feed him daily.'

21.text: 'He lays low under the lotus trees, Hidden deep in the marsh and the reeds.'

22.text: 'The trees shade him, And willows hang around him by the stream.'

23.text: 'The river could rage heavy, But he don't flinch. Even if the Jordan floods straight into his face—he cool.'

24.text: 'Try to trap him. Go ahead— Stick a hook in his nose if you bad. But you not. So sit back.'

1.text: 'Can you catch Leviathan with a fish hook? Can you tie his tongue with a string?'

2.text: 'You think you gon' run a rope through his nose, Or stab his jaw with a hook?'

3.text: 'You think he gon' beg you for mercy? Talk sweet to get free?'

4.text: 'You gon' sign a contract with him? Make him your pet for life?'

5.text: 'You tryna play with him like he a pet bird? Put him on a leash for your girls to giggle at?'

6.text: 'You and your homies throwin' a feast off him? Y'all splittin' Leviathan meat at the market?'

7.text: 'You think you can stab through his hide with harpoons, Or crack his skull with a spear?'

8.text: 'Go ahead—touch him. But you better remember that fight, 'Cause you won't want no rematch.'

9.text: 'Ain't no point in even hopin' to beat him— Just lookin' at him makes people freeze.'

10.text: 'Ain't nobody wild enough to challenge him— So tell me: who you think got the guts to stand against Me?'

11.text: 'Who gave Me anything first? Who put Me in debt? Everything under heaven belongs to Me.'

12.text: 'I ain't holdin' back—I'm about to break down this beast: His power, his build, his glory.'

13.text: 'Who can rip off his armor? Who can get close enough to control him?'

14.text: 'You ever looked him in the face? His mouth full of teeth like a nightmare.'

15.text: 'His back is covered in scales so tight, It's like they sealed up with iron.'

16.text: 'Each one locked to the next, Not even air can squeeze between them.'

17.text: 'They so tight they move like one. No separating 'em—solid unity.'

18.text: 'When he sneezes? It's like lightning. His eyes flash like sunrise.'

19.text: 'Fire sparks shoot out his mouth. Burnin' light comin' from deep within.'

20.text: 'Smoke pours from his nose Like a kettle on fire or reeds burnin' up.'

21.text: 'His breath could light a grill. A flame shoot out like a blowtorch.'

22.text: 'His neck drips strength, And just standin' near him brings fear.'

23.text: 'His body's layered up—thick, tight, Ain't nothin' soft about him.'

24.text: 'His heart? Like stone. Hard like a grindstone—cold and unmovable.'

25.text: 'When he rises up, even the brave lose it. They panic when he moves.'

26.text: 'Swing a sword? It bounces off. Spears, arrows, javelins—worthless.'

27.text: 'He treats iron like straw, Bronze like rotten wood.'

28.text: 'Arrows don't faze him. Sling stones? They might as well be dust.'

29.text: 'Darts are like grass to him. Javelins? He laughs at those.'

30.text: 'His belly scrapes the mud like blades. Leaves sharp tracks wherever he walks.'

31.text: 'He makes the ocean bubble like a boiling pot. Turns the sea into somethin' thick like lotion.'

32.text: 'He leaves a trail of white foam so shiny It looks like the sea got silver hair.'

33.text: 'Ain't nobody on earth like him. He was built without fear—none.'

34.text: 'He looks down on everything proud. He the king of the beasts—every creature full of pride answers to him.'

1.text: Then Job replied to the Lord and said,

2.text: 'Lord, I know now—you can do anything. Ain't no plan of Yours that can be stopped.'

3.text: 'You asked me, "Who out here talkin' reckless without knowledge?" That was me. I spoke on things way above my level— Too deep, too wonderful, I just didn't know.'

4.text: 'You told me, "Listen up—I'ma ask the questions, and you gon' answer." So here I am.'

5.text: 'I used to only know about You from what I heard, But now? I see You for myself.'

6.text: 'And I hate how I acted. I repent—sittin' in dust and ashes, humble before You.'

7.text: After the Lord finished speakin' to Job, He turned to Eliphaz the Temanite and said, 'I'm mad at you and your two homeboys. Y'all ain't talk about Me right— But My servant Job did.'

8.text: 'So here's what you do: take seven bulls and seven rams, Go to My servant Job, and offer a burnt offering. And Job gon' pray for y'all. I'll hear him—so I don't treat you like the fools you been actin' like. 'Cause you ain't speak truth about Me like Job did.'

9.text: So Eliphaz, Bildad, and Zophar went and did what the Lord told 'em, And the Lord accepted Job's prayer.

10.text: And when Job prayed for his friends, The Lord flipped the script and restored everything he lost— In fact, He doubled it.

11.text: Then all his people—his brothers, sisters, and old friends— Pulled up and had a meal with him at his house. They comforted him for all the pain the Lord had allowed. And each one brought him some silver and a gold ring.

12.text: God blessed Job's latter days even more than his beginning. He ended up with 14,000 sheep, 6,000 camels, 1,000 yoke of oxen, And 1,000 female donkeys.

13.text: He had seven sons and three daughters again.

14.text: He named the first daughter Jemimah, The second Keziah, And the third Keren-Happuch.

15.text: And across the whole land, There wasn't a woman alive as fine as Job's daughters. And he gave them an inheritance right along with their brothers.

16.text: After all this, Job lived another 140 years. He saw his kids, grandkids, great-grands—four generations deep.

17.text: Then Job passed away, Old, full of years, full of life, full of peace.

1.text: This right here the word from the Lord that came to Joel, son of Pethuel.

2.text: Listen up, elders. And everybody else in the land—y'all need to hear this. Ain't nothin' like this ever happened in your lifetime? Or even your daddy's lifetime?

3.text: You better tell your kids about this, and make sure they tell their kids, and they pass it down again. This ain't somethin' to forget.

4.text: Whatever the chew-up locust ain't eat, the swarmin' ones did. Whatever the swarmin' ones missed, the crawlin' ones came for. And whatever they didn't get, the destroyin' ones cleaned up. Whole thing got wiped out, wave after wave.

5.text: Wake up, all y'all who stay drunk. Cry, all you wine sippers. That new wine y'all love? Gone. Ain't touchin' your lips no more.

6.text: A whole nation rolled up on My land—deep and ruthless. They got teeth like lions and jaws like beasts. They came to devour.

7.text: They done tore up My vineyard, crushed My fig trees. Stripped 'em bare, snapped off the branches, left nothin' but pale stubs.

8.text: Mourn like a young woman cryin' in her wedding dress 'cause her man gone too soon.

9.text: Ain't no grain offerings, no wine offerings at the temple no more. The priests, the ones who serve the Lord? Mournin'.

10.text: The fields? Ruined. The land itself mournin'. Grain? Wrecked. Wine? Dried up. Oil? Gone.

11.text: Y'all farmers better hang your heads. You vine workers? Wail. Ain't no wheat, ain't no barley. The harvest? Dead.

12.text: Vines shriveled. Fig trees dried up. Pomegranates, palms, apples—everything withered. Even joy done dried up from folks' hearts.

13.text: Priests, y'all better put on sackcloth and cry out. Stay up all night in mourning clothes, y'all who serve at God's altar. Ain't no offerings comin'. God's house sittin' empty.

14.text: Call a fast. Call a holy meeting. Get the elders, get everybody in the land. Bring 'em to the house of the Lord your God and cry out to Him.

15.text: Man, it's about to go down. The day of the Lord is right at the doorstep. And when it hits? It's gon' feel like the Almighty Himself came to tear it up.

16.text: Ain't food already cut off right in front of us? Ain't joy and celebration gone from God's house?

17.text: Seeds dried up under dirt clumps. Grain storage? Wrecked. Barns? Broken. Crops? Withered and gone.

18.text: The animals moanin' too. Cows wanderin' with no grass to eat. Even the sheep strugglin'. Starvin'.

19.text: Lord, I'm cryin' out to You. Fire burned the open land. Flames tore through every tree.

20.text: Even the wild animals lookin' to You, Lord. The rivers dried up, and flames swallowed the fields. Ain't nothin' left but ash and silence.

1.text: Blow that trumpet in Zion, y'all. Sound the alarm on God's holy hill. Everybody in the land—tremble. The Lord's day is comin'… and it's right around the corner.

2.text: It's gon' be a day full of darkness and thick clouds, like when the morning fog covers the mountains. A crew is comin'—big and strong—ain't never been none like it before, and there won't be nothin' like it again, not for generations.

3.text: In front of 'em, it's fire—burnin' everything. Behind 'em, flames—ain't nothin' left untouched. What used to look like Eden? Gon' be a wasteland by the time they done. Ain't nothin' escapin' this wave.

4.text: They look like horses. Run like warhorses too.

5.text: The sound they make? Like chariots crashin' across mountaintops. Like a wildfire tearin' through dry grass. Like a battle line movin' with purpose.

6.text: When folks see 'em, they panic. Faces go pale. Hearts drop.

7.text: They move like elite soldiers—climb walls like trained fighters. Each one stay in formation, no one outta line.

8.text: They don't bump into each other. They stay locked in their lane. Even when weapons fly, they still keep movin'. Ain't nothin' stoppin' 'em.

9.text: They run through the city, scale the walls, bust up in houses, crawl in through windows like thieves in the night.

10.text: The earth shakes underneath them. The skies start trembling. The sun and moon go dark, and the stars lose they shine.

11.text: The Lord's voice go before His army. His squad? Massive. The One carryin' out His Word? Unstoppable. The day of the Lord is huge… and terrifying. Who can handle it?

12.text: But even now, God sayin': "Turn to Me with your whole heart—fastin', cryin', mournin'."

13.text: Don't just rip your clothes—tear your heart open. Come back to the Lord your God. He's gracious. He's full of mercy. Slow to pop off, full of love. He might change His mind and hold back the judgment.

14.text: Who knows? He might leave behind a blessing— enough to give a grain offering and a drink offering to the Lord again.

15.text: Blow that trumpet in Zion again! Call a fast. Bring the whole squad together.

16.text: Get everybody—old folks, babies, toddlers. Tell the bride and groom to pause the honeymoon—this urgent.

17.text: Let the priests weep right between the porch and the altar. Let 'em beg: "Spare Your people, Lord! Don't let the world clown us. Don't let other nations say, 'Where yo God at now?'"

18.text: Then the Lord gon' get fired up for His land. He gon' feel that deep compassion for His people.

19.text: He gon' respond: "Look—I'm sendin' y'all grain, new wine, and oil again. Y'all gon' eat good, and I ain't lettin' nobody mock you no more."

20.text: That northern army? God gon' push 'em way out—into the desert. Their front gon' hit the eastern sea, their back fall in the western sea. And the stank from their bodies? It's gon' be strong 'cause they did some grimy things.

21.text: Don't be scared, land. Be glad and shout for joy— God done did somethin' amazing!

22.text: Don't trip, animals. The grass comin' back. The trees droppin' fruit again. The fig and vine got power again.

23.text: Y'all kids of Zion, start smilin' again. Rejoice in the Lord your God! He's sendin' that early rain again, just like He promised. And He got that later rain on the way too—all in the same season.

24.text: The threshin' floor? Gon' be packed with wheat. The wine vats? Overflowin' with wine and oil.

25.text: God said: "I'mma give back what the locusts stole from you— every wave: chewin', crawlin', swarmin', destroyin'. All that mess I let roll through? I'm restorin' it."

26.text: Y'all gon' eat good again. Full and satisfied. And y'all gon' praise the name of the Lord who did all this. And My people? They will never be ashamed again.

27.text: Then y'all gon' know—for real—that I'm right here in the middle of y'all. I'm the Lord your God, ain't no other. And again… My people will never be put to shame.

28.text: And after all that, God said: "I'ma pour out My Spirit on everybody. Sons and daughters gon' prophesy. Old men gon' dream dreams. Young men gon' see visions.

29.text: Even My servants—men and women both— gon' get that same Spirit."

30.text: "I'ma show wonders in the sky and on the earth— blood, fire, pillars of smoke.

31.text: The sun gon' turn dark, the moon gon' look like blood, right before the great and powerful day of the Lord shows up.

32.text: But listen—anybody who calls on the name of the Lord? They gon' be saved. Up on Mount Zion and in Jerusalem, there's still gon' be deliverance— just like God said. Among the leftovers, the ones He called out by name… they gon' make it."

1.text: Look, when that time comes— when I bring My people back home, the ones from Judah and Jerusalem,

2.text: I'ma call all the nations together and bring them down to the Valley of Jehoshaphat. That's where I'm settin' the record straight— judging them for what they did to My people, My inheritance, Israel. They scattered 'em all over and tried to split up My land like it was theirs.

3.text: They was gamblin' with My people— trade a boy for a prostitute, sell a girl just to get some wine to sip. Cold-hearted.

4.text: Yo, Tyre and Sidon, and all y'all from the Philistine coast— what y'all think y'all doin' messin' with Me? You think you gon' clap back at Me for something? If that's your plan, just know—I'ma hit back quick, and it's gon' fall hard on your own heads.

5.text: You stole My silver, My gold, took what was sacred and tossed it in your fake temples.

6.text: And you sold off My people—Judah and Jerusalem folk— shipped 'em off to Greece, just to wipe 'em off the map.

7.text: But check this: I'ma bring them back from where y'all sold 'em to. And I'ma bring that payback right back on you.

8.text: Your sons and daughters? I'ma hand 'em over to the people of Judah, and they gon' sell 'em off to the Sabeans, far away. The Lord done spoke on it.

9.text: Go ahead and announce this to the whole world: "Gear up! It's war time!" Wake up your soldiers. Get everybody who can fight—pull up.

10.text: Turn your farm tools into weapons. Grab them plowshares and turn 'em into swords. Take them pruning hooks and turn 'em into spears. Even the weak ones gotta say, "I'm strong now!"

11.text: Gather up, all you nations. Come stand in this place. Lord, send down Your mighty ones!

12.text: Let the nations rise up and meet Me in the Valley of Jehoshaphat. That's where I'ma judge all them enemies surrounding My people.

13.text: Swing the sickle—the harvest is ready. Step on down into the winepress. It's overflowin' with wickedness. It's time.

14.text: Crowds on top of crowds in the valley of decision. The day of the Lord is close—real close—in that place of reckoning.

15.text: The sun and moon gon' go dark. The stars gon' fade out too.

16.text: But the Lord? He gon' roar loud from Zion. His voice from Jerusalem gon' shake the skies and the ground. But His people? He gon' be their shelter. He gon' be the strength for all His children.

17.text: You gon' know I'm the Lord your God, livin' right in Zion, My holy mountain. Jerusalem gon' be holy again. Ain't no foreigners messin' it up no more.

18.text: When that day hits, the mountains gon' drip with wine, the hills gon' flow with milk, and streams gon' overflow through Judah. A fresh fountain gon' spring up from the Lord's house and bless the whole Valley of Acacias.

19.text: Egypt gon' be nothin' but ruins. Edom gon' be a dry, dead place. Why? 'Cause they brought violence to Judah, sheddin' innocent blood in God's land.

20.text: But Judah? Judah gon' last forever. Jerusalem gon' stand strong for every generation.

21.text: And I'ma clear My people of all the bloodshed. I held it for a time, but now? I'm cleanin' it up. I'm livin' in Zion.

1.text: The Lord came to Jonah, son of Amittai, and was like,

2.text: "Get up and go to Nineveh—that big ol' city—and tell them folks they wildin'. Their mess done reached Me."

3.text: But what Jonah do? He said, "Nah, I'm good." Tried to dip out on God—ran the opposite way to Tarshish. He went down to Joppa, found a ship headin' that way, paid his lil' fare, and hopped on board. Thought he could duck God like that.

4.text: But God ain't playin'. He sent a violent storm on that water. Wind whippin'. Waves crashin'. That ship was about to snap in two.

5.text: The sailors? Terrified. Screamin' out to every god they knew. Start throwin' stuff off the boat just to keep it afloat. And where was Jonah? Knocked out. Sleepin' like he ain't got a care in the world—in the bottom of the ship.

6.text: The captain came down like, "Yo! How you sleepin' through this? Get up! Say somethin' to your God! We tryna live out here!"

7.text: The crew said, "Let's cast lots. Somebody's bringin' this bad luck." They cast lots and boom—it's Jonah.

8.text: They pressed him: "Bruh, what did you do?! Who are you?! Where you from?! What's your job?! What kinda trouble are you bringin' us?!"

9.text: Jonah said, "I'm Hebrew. I serve the Lord—the God that made the sea and the land."

10.text: The men got extra scared now. "You ran from that God?! Are you serious right now?!"

11.text: They like, "What we gotta do to make this sea chill out?"

12.text: Jonah said, "Throw me overboard. The storm's my fault. If I go, the sea'll calm down."

13.text: But the crew was tryna spare him. They rowed with everything they had, tryin' to get back to land. Didn't work. That storm just got louder.

14.text: So they prayed, "Lord, don't let us die 'cause of him. Don't blame us for this—we just doin' what we gotta do."

15.text: Then they picked Jonah up... And tossed him into the sea. Immediately—calm. Like the storm clocked out.

16.text: Them men were shook and amazed. They gave sacrifices to the Lord right then and there and made vows. God got their respect real quick.

17.text: Meanwhile, God already had a giant fish lined up. Soon as Jonah hit the water—chomp. That fish swallowed him whole. And Jonah sat in that fish belly for three whole days and three whole nights.

1.text: From inside that big ol' fish, Jonah finally came to his senses. He prayed to the Lord his God.

2.text: He said: "I cried out to the Lord 'cause I was goin' through it— And guess what? He still answered me. From the depths of hell itself, I called on You, And You heard me loud and clear.

3.text: "You the one who threw me out here, deep in the sea, Right in the middle where the waves crash heavy. All Your waters—just rollin' over me.

4.text: "I thought You had cut me off for good. But I kept my eyes on You. Still turned toward Your holy place, hopin' You'd see me.

5.text: "I was drownin'—like, soul-level drownin'. The deep wrapped me up tight. Seaweed was clingin' to my head like a crown of regret.

6.text: "I sank way down—like, to the roots of the mountains type deep. Felt like the earth shut the door behind me. But You, Lord my God, You brought me back up from all that darkness.

7.text: "When I had nothin' left, when my soul was weak and done, I remembered You, Lord. My prayer made it to You—straight into Your heavenly home.

8.text: "Folks who chase after fake gods? They turn their back on real mercy.

9.text: "But me? I'ma thank You for real. I'ma keep my word this time. 'Cause salvation only come from the Lord. Period."

10.text: Then God gave the fish the signal— And that fish spit Jonah out on dry land like, "I'm done with him."

1.text: God wasn't done with Jonah. He pulled up on him again, like, "Alright, let's try this one more time..."

2.text: "Get up. Go to Nineveh—that big ol' city—and this time, say exactly what I tell you to say."

3.text: So Jonah got up and actually did what God said this time. He made his way to Nineveh, a massive city—it would take three days just to walk across it.

4.text: On day one, Jonah started shoutin' in the streets: "In forty days, Nineveh gon' get wrecked!" That was the whole sermon. No mic. No slides. Just heat.

5.text: The folks in Nineveh actually listened. They believed what God said, called a fast, and put on sackcloth—from the bougie to the broke.

6.text: Word got to the king. He got off his throne, took off his royal fit, put on sackcloth, and sat down in ashes.

7.text: Then the king dropped a decree: "Don't let nobody eat—not even the animals. Cows, goats, folks—everybody fasting. Put sackcloth on the pets too! Cry out to God with all you got. Stop the wild behavior. Drop the violence. Fix it now."

8.text: "Everybody turn from your evil ways and the violence y'all been doin'. Get right!"

9.text: "Who knows? Maybe God will ease up. Maybe He won't go off on us like we deserve."

10.text: And guess what? God saw it. He saw how they changed up—for real. So He hit pause on the punishment. Didn't go through with the destruction He said was coming.

1.text: But Jonah? Man, he was heated. God showin' mercy had him mad for real.

2.text: He prayed, but it was more like a rant: "See Lord, this what I was talkin' 'bout back when I was still at home! This why I tried to dip to Tarshish in the first place. 'Cause I know You— You merciful. You patient. You full of love. You stay givin' folks a second chance. You always pull back when You could go off."

3.text: "So just go 'head and take me out, Lord. I'd rather die than watch this play out like I knew it would."

4.text: And the Lord was like, "So you mad… and you think that's okay?"

5.text: Jonah left the city, sat out east, and made himself a little spot— posted up in the shade, just waiting to see if Nineveh would still get clapped. (He was still hoping for fireworks.)

6.text: So God, being God, grew a big leafy plant right over Jonah. It gave him some good shade and cooled him down. Jonah was so happy about that plant. Had him feelin' blessed again.

7.text: But the next morning? God sent a worm. That worm ate that plant up. Gone.

8.text: Then God turned up the heat—literally. A hot east wind came through, and the sun was beatin' Jonah's head. He was weak, sweatin', miserable. He said, "Man, I'd rather die than live like this."

9.text: Then God asked again, "So you mad about the plant now?" Jonah said, "YES. Mad enough to die!"

10.text: And God hit him with a lesson: "You out here pressed over a plant. You ain't plant it, you ain't water it— it showed up in a night and disappeared just as quick.

11.text: And you mad over that, but I'm not supposed to care about Nineveh? A whole city with over 120,000 people who don't know up from down— plus all the animals?"

1.text: After Moses, the Lord's servant, passed away, the Lord spoke to Joshua, son of Nun, who had been Moses' right-hand man.

2.text: He said, 'Moses, my servant, gone now. It's your time. Get up, cross this Jordan River, you and all these people, and step into the land I'm giving y'all—the Israelites.'

3.text: 'Everywhere y'all step, I already gave it to you, just like I promised Moses.'

4.text: 'From the desert to Lebanon, from the big Euphrates River—where all them Hittites live—all the way to the Great Sea in the west, that's all your territory now.'

5.text: 'Ain't nobody gon' be able to step to you your whole life. Just like I was with Moses, I'm gon' be with you. I ain't never gon' leave you or turn my back on you.'

6.text: 'Be strong, hold your head high, and walk with courage. You gon' be the one to divide this land up for the people, just like I promised their ancestors.'

7.text: 'But for real, be strong and super courageous. Make sure you do everything in the law Moses gave you. Don't veer off—left or right—so you can move wisely wherever you go.'

8.text: 'Keep this book of the law on your mind, talk about it, think on it day and night. Live by what's in it, and you gon' be prosperous and successful in all you do.'

9.text: 'Ain't I told you already? Be strong, be brave. Don't be shook or stressed, cause the Lord your God is rolling with you wherever you go.'

10.text: Then Joshua told the officers of the people,

11.text: 'Go through the camp and tell everybody, 'Get your stuff ready, cause in three days, we crossing this Jordan to take the land the Lord your God is giving us to own.''

12.text: Then Joshua hollered at the Reubenites, the Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh,

13.text: 'Y'all remember what Moses, the Lord's servant, told you: 'The Lord your God is giving you rest and this land.''

14.text: 'Your wives, kids, and livestock can stay in the land Moses gave y'all on this side of the Jordan, but all y'all mighty warriors gotta strap up and go help your brothers claim their land.'

15.text: 'Once the Lord gives them rest like He gave y'all, and they got their land, then y'all can come back and settle in the land Moses gave you on this side of the Jordan, east of the sunrise.'

16.text: The people told Joshua, 'We got you. Whatever you tell us, we'll do. Wherever you send us, we'll go.'

17.text: 'Just like we listened to Moses, we listening to you. Only thing we ask is that the Lord your God stay with you like He was with Moses.'

18.text: 'Anybody who acts up and don't listen to your orders, or goes against what you say, they gotta go. But for real, Joshua, be strong and stay courageous.'

1.text: Then Joshua, son of Nun, sent out two men from Acacia Grove on the low, tellin' them, 'Go scope out the land, especially Jericho.' So they went and ended up at the house of a woman named Rahab, who was known to host folks, and they stayed there.

2.text: But word got to the king of Jericho, 'Yo, some Israelite men came in here tonight to check out the land and see what's up.'

3.text: So the king sent messengers to Rahab, sayin', 'Bring out the men that came to your house. We know they in here trying to spy on the whole country.'

4.text: But Rahab had already hidden them, so she told the king's men, 'Yeah, they was here, but I ain't know where they was from.'

5.text: 'Right when the gate was closin' at night, they dipped. I don't know where they went, but if y'all hurry, you might still catch them.'

6.text: (But for real, she had already took them up to the roof and hid them under some stalks of flax she had stacked up.)

7.text: So the king's men took off down the road toward the Jordan, looking for them. As soon as they left, they shut the city gate behind them.

8.text: Later that night, before the men went to sleep, Rahab went up to the roof to talk to them.

9.text: She told them, 'Look, I already know the Lord done gave y'all this land. Everybody round here scared stiff because of y'all.'

10.text: 'We heard how the Lord dried up the Red Sea when y'all came out of Egypt. And how y'all took down them two Amorite kings on the other side of the Jordan—Sihon and Og—y'all wiped them out completely.'

11.text: 'As soon as we heard all that, our hearts dropped. Ain't nobody got no courage left to fight y'all, cause the Lord your God? He the real one, running heaven and earth.'

12.text: 'So I'm asking y'all, since I showed y'all love, swear to me in the Lord's name that y'all gon' do the same for my family. Give me a sign that you for real.'

13.text: 'Promise me y'all gon' spare my father, my mama, my brothers, my sisters, and everything they got. Don't let us die when y'all take over.'

14.text: The men told her, 'Bet. If you keep quiet about what we doing, we got you. When the Lord hands this place over to us, we gon' make sure you and yours are straight.'

15.text: Then Rahab let them down through her window with a rope, cause her house was built into the city wall.

16.text: She told them, 'Y'all gotta hit the mountains quick so y'all don't run into the king's men. Lay low for three days till they give up and come back, then y'all can go on your way.'

17.text: The men told her, 'Aight, but here's the deal—we only gotta keep this promise if you follow these instructions.'

18.text: 'When we come back to take the land, you need to tie this red cord in the same window you let us down through. Also, make sure your whole family—your folks, your siblings, everybody—is inside your house.'

19.text: 'If anybody steps outside that door into the streets, that's on them. But if somebody come in your house and lay hands on your people, that's on us.'

20.text: 'But if you snitch on us, this deal is off, and we ain't gotta keep our word.'

21.text: Rahab said, 'Aight, bet. I'll do exactly what y'all said.' Then she let them go, and as soon as they left, she tied the red cord in the window.

22.text: The spies took off to the mountains and hid out for three days. The king's men was out there searching everywhere but couldn't find them.

23.text: After that, the two men came down from the mountains, crossed back over the Jordan, and went straight to Joshua. They told him everything that happened.

24.text: They told Joshua, 'Yo, the Lord really put this land in our hands. Everybody over there scared to death cause of us.'

1.text: Early the next morning, Joshua got up, and they left Acacia Grove, heading toward the Jordan River. Him and all the Israelites camped there for the night before crossing over.

2.text: After three days, the leaders started moving through the camp,

3.text: Telling the people, 'When y'all see the priests, the Levites, carrying the ark of the covenant of the Lord, that's your signal—it's time to move. Follow it.'

4.text: 'But keep a good distance—about two thousand cubits away—don't get too close. That way, y'all can see where you supposed to go, cause this ain't a path y'all been down before.'

5.text: Then Joshua told the people, 'Y'all need to get right and prepare yourselves, cause tomorrow the Lord gon' do some crazy wonders among us.'

6.text: Then Joshua told the priests, 'Pick up the ark of the covenant and lead the way across the Jordan.' So they picked it up and went ahead of the people.

7.text: Then the Lord spoke to Joshua, 'Today is the day I start putting you on the map in front of all Israel, so they know for sure that just like I was with Moses, I'm with you too.'

8.text: 'Tell the priests carrying the ark, 'When y'all get to the Jordan's edge, stand still in the water.''

9.text: So Joshua told the Israelites, 'Aight, come close and listen to what the Lord your God gotta say.'

10.text: Joshua said, 'This how y'all gon' know that the living God is right here with us and gon' clear out all these folks before us—the Canaanites, Hittites, Hivites, Perizzites, Girgashites, Amorites, and Jebusites.'

11.text: 'Look, the ark of the covenant of the Lord of all the earth is going ahead of y'all into the Jordan.'

12.text: 'So pick one man from each tribe of Israel—twelve in total.'

13.text: 'And here's what's gon' happen: the moment the priests carrying the ark step into the Jordan, the water gon' stop flowing. The river gon' stack up like a wall.'

14.text: So when the people packed up to cross the Jordan, the priests carrying the ark of the covenant led the way.

15.text: Now, the Jordan River was overflowing cause it was harvest season. But as soon as the priests' feet hit the edge of the water,

16.text: The water coming down from upstream stopped, piling up way far back at a town called Adam, near Zaretan. Meanwhile, the water flowing down to the Dead Sea completely dried up, so the people could cross the river right in front of Jericho.

17.text: The priests holding the ark of the covenant stood firm in the middle of the river on dry ground while all Israel walked across. Every last one of them got to the other side safe before the priests moved.

1.text: After everybody made it across the Jordan, the Lord spoke to Joshua, sayin':

2.text: 'Pick twelve men from the people—one from each tribe.'

3.text: 'Tell 'em to grab twelve stones from right where the priests are standin' in the middle of the Jordan. Y'all gon' carry 'em with you and set 'em down where y'all camping tonight.'

4.text: So Joshua called up the twelve men he had chosen from the Israelites—one from each tribe.

5.text: He told them, 'Go back to where the ark of the Lord is in the middle of the Jordan. Each of y'all grab a stone and put it on your shoulder, one for each tribe of Israel.'

6.text: 'This gon' be a sign for y'all. One day, when your kids ask, 'What's up with these stones?''

7.text: 'Tell 'em how the Lord stopped the Jordan River when the ark of the covenant crossed through. These stones are gon' be a reminder forever of what God did for us.'

8.text: So the Israelites did exactly what Joshua told them. They took twelve stones from the Jordan, just like the Lord had told Joshua, and carried 'em to the camp, setting 'em down there.

9.text: Joshua also set up twelve stones in the middle of the Jordan, right where the priests holding the ark had stood. And they still there to this day.

10.text: The priests stood in the middle of the Jordan until everything was done—just like the Lord had told Joshua, just like Moses had said. The people didn't waste no time; they hurried and crossed over.

11.text: After everybody was across, the priests carrying the ark of the Lord came out too, in front of all the people.

12.text: The warriors from Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh's tribe crossed over armed and ready, just like Moses had told them to do.

13.text: About forty thousand soldiers marched across, ready for battle, heading to the plains of Jericho.

14.text: That day, the Lord put Joshua on a whole new level in front of all Israel. From then on, they respected him just like they did Moses, all the days of his life.

15.text: Then the Lord told Joshua,

16.text: 'Tell the priests carrying the ark of the covenant to come up out of the Jordan.'

17.text: So Joshua gave the order, 'Come up out of the river!'

18.text: And as soon as the priests' feet hit dry ground, the water rushed back to where it was before, overflowing the banks like usual.

19.text: The people crossed the Jordan on the tenth day of the first month, then set up camp at Gilgal, east of Jericho.

20.text: Joshua took those twelve stones they pulled from the Jordan and set 'em up in Gilgal.

21.text: Then he told the Israelites, 'One day, when your kids ask, 'What these stones mean?''

22.text: 'Tell 'em, 'This is where Israel crossed the Jordan on dry land.''

23.text: 'Cause the Lord your God dried up the river for y'all to cross, just like He did with the Red Sea when we was coming out of Egypt.'

24.text: 'He did this so the whole world would know how powerful the Lord is, and so y'all would always respect and honor Him.'

1.text: When all the kings of the Amorites on the west side of the Jordan and all the Canaanite kings near the sea heard how the Lord dried up the Jordan River for the Israelites to cross, they got shook. Their courage was gone, and they ain't have no fight left in them.

2.text: Then the Lord told Joshua, 'Get you some flint knives and circumcise the Israelite men again.'

3.text: So Joshua made the knives and circumcised the men at the place they later called 'Hill of the Foreskins.'

4.text: Now here's why Joshua had to do this: All the men who left Egypt, the ones who were old enough to fight, had died in the wilderness during the journey.

5.text: All those who came out of Egypt had already been circumcised, but the ones born in the wilderness hadn't been.

6.text: The Israelites wandered forty years in the desert till all the old heads who left Egypt had died off cause they ain't listen to the Lord. The Lord had told them they wouldn't see the promised land—the land flowing with milk and honey—cause they ain't obey.

7.text: So now, their sons, the next generation, had to be circumcised cause nobody had done it while they were traveling.

8.text: After Joshua finished circumcising all the men, they stayed in the camp till they healed up.

9.text: Then the Lord told Joshua, 'Today, I've rolled away the shame of Egypt from y'all.' That's why that place is called Gilgal to this day.

10.text: While camped in Gilgal, the Israelites kept the Passover on the fourteenth day of the month, in the evening, on the plains of Jericho.

11.text: The day after Passover, they finally ate the food from the land—some unleavened bread and roasted grain, straight from the fields.

12.text: That same day, the manna stopped falling. From then on, they ate off the land of Canaan, no more manna from heaven.

13.text: One day, while Joshua was near Jericho, he looked up and saw a man standing in front of him with a sword drawn. Joshua walked up to him and said, 'You with us or against us?'

14.text: The man answered, 'Nah, I'm neither. I'm the Commander of the Lord's army, and I just got here.'

15.text: Then Joshua fell on his face, worshipped, and asked, 'What's the word from the Lord for me, His servant?'

16.text: The Commander of the Lord's army told him, 'Take off your sandals, cause where you standing is holy ground.' And Joshua did exactly that.

1.text: Jericho was on full lockdown cause of the Israelites—nobody was coming in or going out.

2.text: Then the Lord told Joshua, 'Look, I already gave you Jericho, its king, and all its warriors.'

3.text: 'Here's what y'all gon' do: All the soldiers march around the city once a day for six days.'

4.text: 'Seven priests gon' carry seven rams' horn trumpets ahead of the ark. But on the seventh day, y'all gon' march around the city seven times, and the priests gon' blow the trumpets.'

5.text: 'When y'all hear that long blast from the rams' horns, that's when everybody gon' shout loud! The walls gon' fall flat, and everybody can charge straight in.'

6.text: So Joshua called up the priests and told them, 'Pick up the ark of the covenant. Seven priests gon' carry seven trumpets and walk ahead of it.'

7.text: Then he told the people, 'Move out! March around the city. The armed men go first, leading the way for the ark of the Lord.'

8.text: So just like Joshua said, the seven priests with the trumpets started marching, blowing their horns, while the ark of the covenant followed behind.

9.text: The armed men went ahead of the priests blowing the trumpets, and the rear guard followed behind the ark. The trumpets stayed blasting the whole time.

10.text: Joshua told the people, 'Stay quiet—don't shout, don't talk, not a word until the day I tell y'all to shout. Then let it out loud!'

11.text: So the ark of the Lord went around the city once, then they all went back to camp and spent the night there.

12.text: Early the next morning, Joshua got up, and the priests picked up the ark of the Lord again.

13.text: The seven priests carrying the trumpets went ahead, blowing them non-stop, while the armed men marched in front and the rear guard followed the ark.

14.text: On the second day, they marched around the city once again, then went back to camp. They did this for six days.

15.text: On the seventh day, they got up at dawn and marched around the city seven times, just like before. This was the only day they did seven laps.

16.text: On the seventh lap, the priests blew their trumpets, and Joshua told the people, 'Shout! Cause the Lord done gave you this city!'

17.text: 'The whole city is set to be destroyed by the Lord, except Rahab and her family cause she hid our spies.'

18.text: 'Don't mess with none of the cursed stuff in the city, or you gon' bring trouble on all of Israel.'

19.text: 'All the silver, gold, bronze, and iron belong to the Lord's treasury—don't take none of it for yourself.'

20.text: When the priests blew the trumpets, the people shouted loud! As soon as they did, the walls of Jericho fell flat. Everybody rushed in and took the city.

21.text: They wiped out everything—men, women, kids, even the animals—nobody was spared.

22.text: Then Joshua told the two spies, 'Go to Rahab's house and bring her and her family out, just like we promised her.'

23.text: So the young men went in and brought out Rahab, her family, and everything she owned. They kept them safe outside the Israelite camp.

24.text: Then the Israelites burned down the whole city and everything in it. The only things they kept were the silver, gold, bronze, and iron, which went into the Lord's treasury.

25.text: But Rahab and her whole family got spared. She stayed living with the Israelites ever since, cause she hid the spies Joshua had sent to Jericho.

26.text: Then Joshua made a declaration: 'Anybody who tries to rebuild Jericho is cursed! They gon' lose their firstborn when they lay the foundation, and their youngest when they set up the gates.'

27.text: The Lord was with Joshua, and word about him spread everywhere across the land.

1.text: But Israel messed up—somebody took stuff they wasn't supposed to. Achan, son of Carmi, grandson of Zabdi, great-grandson of Zerah from the tribe of Judah, took some of the banned goods. And the Lord was heated at Israel for it.

2.text: Joshua sent some men from Jericho to Ai, near Beth Aven, east of Bethel, and told them, 'Go check out the land.' So they went and spied on Ai.

3.text: When they came back, they told Joshua, 'Ain't no need for everybody to go fight—just send two or three thousand men. Ai ain't got that many people; no need to wear everybody out.'

4.text: So about three thousand men went up, but they got whooped and had to retreat.

5.text: Ai's men chased them down from the city gate all the way to Shebarim, cutting down about thirty-six of them. The Israelites' courage vanished—they was shook.

6.text: Joshua tore his clothes, fell facedown in front of the ark of the Lord, and stayed there till evening. The elders of Israel did the same, throwing dust on their heads.

7.text: Joshua said, 'Lord God, why You even bring us over the Jordan if we just gon' get handed over to the Amorites and wiped out? We shoulda just stayed on the other side!'

8.text: 'Lord, what am I supposed to say now that Israel ran from their enemies?'

9.text: 'If the Canaanites and the rest hear about this, they gon' come for us, wipe us out, and then what's gon' happen to Your great name?'

10.text: The Lord told Joshua, 'Get up! Why you on the ground like that?'

11.text: 'Israel messed up bad—they broke My covenant. Somebody stole from what was set apart, lied about it, and hid it in their stuff.'

12.text: 'That's why Israel lost—they got cursed things among them. I ain't ridin' with y'all no more unless you clean house and get rid of it.'

13.text: 'Get up and tell the people: 'Get right for tomorrow, cause the Lord says there's something cursed in the camp. Y'all ain't gon' win another fight till it's gone.''

14.text: 'Tomorrow morning, all the tribes gon' come forward one by one, then the Lord gon' call out the guilty tribe. Then the families gon' step forward, then households, then man by man till the one who did this is found.'

15.text: 'Whoever got the cursed stuff gon' be burned up with everything they own, cause they disrespected the Lord and did Israel dirty.'

16.text: So Joshua got up early and had Israel come tribe by tribe. The Lord picked Judah.

17.text: Then He picked the clan of the Zarhites, then from them, He chose Zabdi's family.

18.text: Then one by one, He narrowed it down till Achan—son of Carmi, grandson of Zabdi, from Judah—was caught.

19.text: Joshua told Achan, 'Son, don't play with me. Give God His glory, come clean, and tell me what you did. Don't hide it.'

20.text: Achan answered, 'I ain't gon' lie—I messed up. I sinned against the Lord.'

21.text: 'I saw this fresh Babylonian robe, two hundred shekels of silver, and a gold bar worth fifty shekels. I wanted 'em bad, so I took 'em. They buried in my tent, with the silver underneath.'

22.text: Joshua sent some men to check, and sure enough, the stash was buried in Achan's tent with the silver underneath.

23.text: They grabbed the stolen goods, brought them back to Joshua and all Israel, and laid it out before the Lord.

24.text: Then Joshua and all Israel took Achan, the silver, the robe, the gold, his sons, his daughters, his cattle, donkeys, sheep, his tent, and everything he had, and dragged them to the Valley of Achor.

25.text: Joshua said, 'Why you bring trouble on us? Now the Lord bringin' trouble on you!' Then all Israel stoned them, then burned them up.

26.text: They piled a huge heap of stones over him, which is still there today. After that, the Lord's anger cooled down. That's why that place is called the Valley of Achor to this day.

1.text: Then the Lord told Joshua, 'Don't be scared or discouraged. Take all your warriors and go hit Ai. I already gave you the king, the people, the city, and the land.'

2.text: 'You gon' do Ai the same way y'all did Jericho and its king, but this time, y'all can keep the goods and livestock for yourselves. Set up an ambush behind the city.'

3.text: So Joshua and his army got ready to go against Ai. He picked thirty thousand strong warriors and sent them out at night.

4.text: He told them, 'Y'all gon' hide behind the city, not too far, and be ready.'

5.text: 'Me and the rest gon' roll up on the city. When they see us, they gon' chase us, thinking we running away like last time.'

6.text: 'They gon' leave the city wide open, thinking they got us. That's when we dip, acting like we scared.'

7.text: 'Then y'all gon' rush in, take the city, cause the Lord already handed it to us.'

8.text: 'Once y'all take it, burn it down. This is what the Lord told us to do.'

9.text: Joshua sent them out, and they went to hide between Bethel and Ai, on the west side of the city, while he stayed with the rest of the people overnight.

10.text: Early in the morning, Joshua got everybody ready, and him and the elders led them up to Ai.

11.text: The whole army moved in, camping north of Ai, with a valley between them and the city.

12.text: Then Joshua had another five thousand men hide between Bethel and Ai, west of the city.

13.text: With the army set up on both sides, Joshua went into the valley that night.

14.text: When the king of Ai saw them, he rushed out early in the morning with all his people, ready to fight. But he ain't know there was an ambush waiting behind the city.

15.text: Joshua and his army faked like they was losing and started running toward the wilderness.

16.text: All the men of Ai got hyped, came out the city, and chased after them, leaving the whole city wide open.

17.text: Ain't a single man left inside Ai or Bethel—they was all chasing Israel, thinking they had the upper hand.

18.text: Then the Lord told Joshua, 'Point your spear at Ai, cause I'm giving it to you now.' So Joshua stretched out his spear toward the city.

19.text: As soon as he did, the ambush squad jumped up, ran into the city, took it over, and set it on fire.

20.text: When the men of Ai turned around, they saw their city up in smoke. They had nowhere to run, cause Israel had them surrounded.

21.text: Once Joshua and his men saw the ambush team had taken Ai and set it on fire, they turned back and attacked the men of Ai.

22.text: The Israelites trapped them on both sides and wiped them out—nobody escaped.

23.text: They caught the king of Ai alive and brought him to Joshua.

24.text: After Israel finished taking out all Ai's people in the field and the wilderness, they went back into the city and finished the job.

25.text: That day, twelve thousand people—every last person in Ai—got taken out.

26.text: Joshua kept holding his spear up till everybody in Ai was destroyed.

27.text: But Israel kept the livestock and the city's goods, just like the Lord told Joshua.

28.text: Then Joshua burned Ai to the ground and left it as ruins, a wasteland forever.

29.text: He had the king of Ai hanged on a tree till evening. When the sun set, Joshua had his body taken down, thrown at the city gate, and covered with a big pile of stones—still there to this day.

30.text: Then Joshua built an altar to the Lord, the God of Israel, on Mount Ebal.

31.text: He did it just like Moses had commanded, using whole stones that nobody had ever cut with iron tools. Then they offered burnt offerings and peace offerings to the Lord.

32.text: There, in front of the Israelites, Joshua wrote down the whole law of Moses on stones.

33.text: Then all of Israel—leaders, officials, judges, and even the foreigners among them—stood on both sides of the ark of the covenant. Half stood in front of Mount Gerizim, the other half in front of Mount Ebal, just like Moses had told them to do.

34.text: Then Joshua read every word of the law, the blessings and the curses, exactly as it was written in the Book of the Law.

35.text: Not a single word Moses had commanded was left out—Joshua read it all to the whole assembly, including the women, kids, and foreigners living with them.

1.text: When all the kings west of the Jordan—up in the hills, in the valleys, and along the coast near Lebanon—heard what went down, including the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites,

2.text: They all teamed up, ready to go to war against Joshua and Israel.

3.text: But when the people of Gibeon heard what Joshua did to Jericho and Ai,

4.text: They got slick with it—they planned a scheme and acted like they was ambassadors. They loaded up old sacks on their donkeys, brought busted wineskins that had been patched up,

5.text: Wore raggedy sandals, dusty clothes, and brought dried-up, moldy bread like they been traveling for months.

6.text: They pulled up to Joshua at Gilgal and told him and the Israelites, 'We from a faraway land—let's make a deal, a covenant.'

7.text: But the Israelites was suspicious, saying, 'How we know y'all ain't just some locals tryna finesse us? We ain't supposed to make no covenant with folks living around here.'

8.text: The Gibeonites told Joshua, 'We your servants.' But Joshua wasn't buying it yet. He asked, 'Who are y'all, and where y'all really from?'

9.text: They said, 'We came from way far off cause we heard about the Lord your God—how He been handling business, what He did in Egypt,'

10.text: 'And how He took out Sihon, king of Heshbon, and Og, king of Bashan, over in Ashtaroth.'

11.text: 'So our leaders told us, 'Pack up, take some supplies, and go meet them. Tell them we your servants—make a deal with them.''

12.text: 'Look at this bread—it was fresh when we left, now it's all dried up and nasty.'

13.text: 'These wineskins? Brand new when we filled 'em, now they torn up. Our clothes and sandals? Straight up falling apart from all this traveling.'

14.text: The Israelites checked out their supplies, but they ain't bother to ask God what to do.

15.text: So Joshua made peace with them, set up a covenant letting them live, and the Israelite leaders swore on it.

16.text: But three days later, Israel found out the truth—the Gibeonites wasn't from no faraway land, they was neighbors, living right there.

17.text: So Israel went to check out their cities—Gibeon, Chephirah, Beeroth, and Kirjath Jearim—on the third day.

18.text: But they couldn't attack them, cause the leaders had already sworn an oath to them in the Lord's name. The whole community started complaining to the leaders about it.

19.text: The leaders told the people, 'We swore in the Lord's name—we can't go back on it now.'

20.text: 'Here's what we gon' do—we let them live, cause if we break our oath, we gon' bring down the Lord's wrath on us.'

21.text: 'But they gotta work for us now—they gon' be cutting wood and carrying water for the whole community, just like we promised.'

22.text: Then Joshua called the Gibeonites and said, 'Why y'all lie to us? Saying you from far away when you right next door?'

23.text: 'Now y'all cursed—you and your people gon' be stuck as servants, cutting wood and hauling water for the house of my God forever.'

24.text: The Gibeonites replied, 'We knew for sure that the Lord your God told Moses to give y'all this land and wipe everybody out. We was scared for our lives, so we did what we had to do.'

25.text: 'Now we in your hands—do whatever you think is right to us.'

26.text: So Joshua let them live and made sure Israel didn't kill them.

27.text: But from that day forward, the Gibeonites became the permanent woodcutters and water carriers for Israel and the altar of the Lord, just like Joshua said. And they still doing that to this day.

1.text: Adoni-Zedek, king of Jerusalem, heard how Joshua took Ai and wiped it out—just like he did Jericho and its king—and how Gibeon had made peace with Israel and was now rollin' with them.

2.text: This had him shook, cause Gibeon was a big city, like one of the royal towns, even bigger than Ai, and its men were some real warriors.

3.text: So Adoni-Zedek sent word to Hoham, king of Hebron, Piram, king of Jarmuth, Japhia, king of Lachish, and Debir, king of Eglon, saying,

4.text: 'Come help me out! We gotta hit Gibeon, cause they switched sides and joined Joshua and Israel.'

5.text: So the five Amorite kings—the kings of Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon—linked up, brought their armies, and camped outside Gibeon, ready for war.

6.text: The Gibeonites sent word to Joshua at Gilgal, saying, 'Yo, don't leave us hanging! Come quick, help us out! All these Amorite kings from the hills teamed up against us!'

7.text: So Joshua and his whole army, including his best warriors, rolled out from Gilgal.

8.text: The Lord told Joshua, 'Don't be scared of them—I already gave 'em to you. Not a single one of them gon' stand against you.'

9.text: Joshua and his army marched all night from Gilgal and pulled up on them unexpectedly.

10.text: The Lord threw the enemy into total confusion. Israel put in work, killing them all over Gibeon, chasing them down the road toward Beth Horon, and striking them down all the way to Azekah and Makkedah.

11.text: While they was running away, the Lord started throwing down giant hailstones from the sky all the way to Azekah. More of them died from the hail than from Israel's swords.

12.text: That day, when the Lord handed the Amorites over to Israel, Joshua called on the Lord in front of everybody and said: 'Sun, stop right over Gibeon! Moon, stay put in the Valley of Aijalon!'

13.text: And the sun stopped, and the moon stood still until Israel got their payback on their enemies. Ain't this written in the Book of Jasher? The sun stayed in place in the sky and didn't go down for nearly a whole day.

14.text: Ain't never been another day like that before or after, where the Lord actually listened to a man like that—cause the Lord Himself was out there fighting for Israel.

15.text: Then Joshua and his army headed back to their camp at Gilgal.

16.text: Meanwhile, them five kings ran off and hid in a cave at Makkedah.

17.text: Somebody told Joshua, 'We found them kings hiding in a cave at Makkedah.'

18.text: Joshua said, 'Roll some big stones over the cave entrance and post guards there.'

19.text: 'But don't just stand around—chase down their troops, attack their rear guard, and don't let them make it back to their cities, cause the Lord already handed them over to us.'

20.text: So Joshua and the Israelites kept wiping them out until barely any of them were left. The few who got away made it into fortified cities.

21.text: When the Israelites came back to camp at Makkedah, everybody was safe—nobody even dared to talk trash against them.

22.text: Then Joshua said, 'Open up that cave and bring those five kings out here.'

23.text: So they pulled out the five kings—the ones from Jerusalem, Hebron, Jarmuth, Lachish, and Eglon.

24.text: Joshua called his army captains and told them, 'Come here and put your foot on these kings' necks.' So they stepped up and did it.

25.text: Then Joshua told them, 'Don't be scared or weak—be strong and stand tall. This what the Lord gon' do to every enemy you fight.'

26.text: Then Joshua killed them and had them hanged on five trees, where they stayed till evening.

27.text: At sunset, Joshua ordered their bodies to be taken down, thrown into the cave they hid in, and sealed it with big rocks. That spot still like that to this day.

28.text: That same day, Joshua took Makkedah, killed the king and everybody in it—didn't leave nobody alive. He did Makkedah's king just like he did Jericho's.

29.text: Then Joshua and the Israelites rolled out to Libnah and went to war.

30.text: The Lord gave Libnah into Israel's hands—they took out the king, killed everyone in the city, and left no survivors, just like Jericho.

31.text: From Libnah, Joshua led the army to Lachish, set up camp, and attacked.

32.text: The Lord gave Lachish over to Israel on the second day, and they wiped out the whole city, just like Libnah.

33.text: When Horam, king of Gezer, came to help Lachish, Joshua and his army took him out too—nobody was left alive.

34.text: Then they moved to Eglon, set up camp, and went to war.

35.text: That same day, they took the city, wiped out everybody in it, and left no survivors—just like they did to Lachish.

36.text: From Eglon, Joshua and the Israelites went up to Hebron and attacked.

37.text: They took it, killed the king, and wiped out every single person—no survivors, just like they did to Eglon.

38.text: Then Joshua led the army to Debir and attacked.

39.text: They took the city, its king, and all the surrounding towns, killing everybody in it. No survivors. Joshua handled Debir just like he did Hebron, Libnah, and Jericho.

40.text: Joshua conquered the whole region—the mountains, the desert, the lowlands, the slopes—took out every king, left no survivors, wiping out everything that breathed, just like the Lord commanded.

41.text: He took them down from Kadesh Barnea all the way to Gaza, covering Goshen to Gibeon.

42.text: Joshua took down all these kings and their lands in one go, cause the Lord Himself was fighting for Israel.

43.text: Then Joshua and the whole army headed back to their camp at Gilgal.

1.text: When Jabin, king of Hazor, heard about all this, he sent word to Jobab, king of Madon, and to the kings of Shimron and Achshaph,

2.text: And to all the kings up north—in the mountains, the plains near Chinneroth, the lowlands, and the high places near Dor in the west,

3.text: To the Canaanites in the east and west, the Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, and Jebusites in the mountains, and the Hivites down near Mount Hermon in Mizpah.

4.text: All these kings gathered their armies—a massive crowd, as many as the sand on the shore. They had a crazy amount of horses and chariots.

5.text: They all linked up and camped at the waters of Merom, ready to go to war against Israel.

6.text: But the Lord told Joshua, 'Don't even trip about them. By this time tomorrow, I'm handing them all over to Israel—dead. You gon' hamstring their horses and burn up their chariots.'

7.text: So Joshua and his whole army pulled up on them at the waters of Merom, caught them slipping, and attacked.

8.text: The Lord gave Israel the victory—they chased them all the way to Greater Sidon, to the Brook Misrephoth, and to Mizpah Valley in the east, striking them down until nobody was left.

9.text: Just like the Lord told him, Joshua took out their horses' legs and set their chariots on fire.

10.text: Then Joshua turned back and took Hazor, killed its king, cause Hazor used to be the head of all these kingdoms.

11.text: They took out everybody in the city—every last one, no survivors. Then they burned Hazor to the ground.

12.text: Joshua went through all the cities of these kings, took them out, and wiped them out, just like Moses had commanded.

13.text: But Israel didn't burn down any other cities except Hazor.

14.text: They took all the wealth and livestock for themselves, but they killed every person, leaving no one alive.

15.text: Joshua did everything just like the Lord commanded Moses. He followed every instruction, leaving nothing undone.

16.text: So Joshua took all the land—the mountains, the southlands, Goshen, the lowlands, and the Jordan Valley. He conquered the mountains of Israel and their surrounding lands,

17.text: From Mount Halak near Seir all the way to Baal Gad in Lebanon Valley below Mount Hermon. He captured all their kings, took them out, and executed them.

18.text: Joshua was at war with these kings for a long time.

19.text: Not a single city made peace with Israel, except the Hivites from Gibeon. Everybody else had to get handled in battle.

20.text: The Lord made sure their hearts stayed hardened so they would fight Israel and get wiped out. He didn't let them get mercy—just like He told Moses.

21.text: At that time, Joshua also went after the Anakim—the giants in the mountains—from Hebron, Debir, Anab, and all over Judah and Israel. He wiped them out and tore down their cities.

22.text: None of the Anakim were left in Israel, except for a few in Gaza, Gath, and Ashdod.

23.text: So Joshua took the whole land, just like the Lord told Moses. Then he divided it among Israel's tribes as their inheritance. And finally, the land had peace—no more war.

1.text: These the kings Israel took down before they even crossed the Jordan—on the east side, from the River Arnon to Mount Hermon, covering all the eastern Jordan valley.

2.text: First was Sihon, king of the Amorites, who ruled from Heshbon. He controlled half of Gilead, from Aroer on the Arnon River all the way to the Jabbok River, which was the border of the Ammonites.

3.text: He also controlled the eastern Jordan valley, stretching from the Sea of Chinneroth to the Salt Sea, including the road to Beth Jeshimoth and the land south of Pisgah.

4.text: Then there was Og, king of Bashan, one of the last of the giants. He ruled from Ashtaroth and Edrei,

5.text: Covering Mount Hermon, Salcah, all of Bashan, up to the borders of the Geshurites and Maachathites, and half of Gilead, right up to Sihon's territory.

6.text: Moses, the Lord's servant, and Israel took them out, then gave their land to the Reubenites, the Gadites, and half of Manasseh's tribe as their share.

7.text: Now these the kings that Joshua and Israel took down after crossing the Jordan—on the west side, from Baal Gad in Lebanon Valley all the way to Mount Halak near Seir. Joshua split up this land among the tribes.

8.text: This land covered mountains, valleys, plains, slopes, deserts, and the southern region—taking out the Hittites, Amorites, Canaanites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.

9.text: The king of Jericho—one.

10.text: The king of Ai (next to Bethel)—one.

11.text: The king of Jerusalem—one.

12.text: The king of Hebron—one.

13.text: The king of Jarmuth—one.

14.text: The king of Lachish—one.

15.text: The king of Eglon—one.

16.text: The king of Gezer—one.

17.text: The king of Debir—one.

18.text: The king of Geder—one.

19.text: The king of Hormah—one.

20.text: The king of Arad—one.

21.text: The king of Libnah—one.

22.text: The king of Adullam—one.

23.text: The king of Makkedah—one.

24.text: The king of Bethel—one.

25.text: The king of Tappuah—one.

26.text: The king of Hepher—one.

27.text: The king of Aphek—one.

28.text: The king of Lasharon—one.

29.text: The king of Madon—one.

30.text: The king of Hazor—one.

31.text: The king of Shimron Meron—one.

32.text: The king of Achshaph—one.

33.text: The king of Taanach—one.

34.text: The king of Megiddo—one.

35.text: The king of Kedesh—one.

36.text: The king of Jokneam in Carmel—one.

37.text: The king of Dor (in the heights of Dor)—one.

38.text: The king of the people of Gilgal—one.

39.text: The king of Tirzah—one.

40.text: All together, Joshua and Israel took down 31 kings.

1.text: By this time, Joshua was getting old. The Lord told him, 'You up in age now, but there's still a lot of land left to take over.'

2.text: 'Here's what's left: all the land of the Philistines and the Geshurites,'

3.text: 'From Sihor, east of Egypt, up to Ekron in the north (which is counted as Canaanite land). This includes the five Philistine rulers—the ones over Gaza, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath, and Ekron—plus the Avites.'

4.text: 'From the south, all the land of the Canaanites, and Mearah that belongs to the Sidonians, reaching to Aphek and the Amorite border.'

5.text: 'The land of the Gebalites and all of Lebanon, from Baal Gad under Mount Hermon to Hamath's entrance.'

6.text: 'Everybody in the mountains from Lebanon to the Brook Misrephoth, and all the Sidonians—I'll clear them out Myself. But you need to divide this land up for Israel, just like I commanded.'

7.text: 'Now go ahead and split it up as an inheritance for the nine tribes and the half-tribe of Manasseh.'

8.text: The Reubenites and Gadites, along with the other half of Manasseh's tribe, already got their land on the east side of the Jordan—just like Moses, the Lord's servant, gave them.

9.text: From Aroer on the Arnon River, including the town in the middle of the valley, plus all the flatlands of Medeba as far as Dibon,

10.text: All the cities ruled by Sihon, king of the Amorites, who had Heshbon, stretching to the Ammonite border,

11.text: Gilead, the land of the Geshurites and Maachathites, Mount Hermon, and all of Bashan reaching to Salcah.

12.text: This included all of Og's kingdom in Bashan—he was one of the last giants. He ruled in Ashtaroth and Edrei. But Moses took him out and claimed the land.

13.text: But Israel didn't clear out the Geshurites or Maachathites completely, so they still living among them to this day.

14.text: Only the Levites ain't get no land—cause the Lord's sacrifices were their inheritance, just like He said.

15.text: Moses gave the tribe of Reuben their land, divided by their families.

16.text: Their territory stretched from Aroer on the Arnon River, including the town in the valley and all the plains by Medeba,

17.text: Heshbon and all the cities in the flatlands—Dibon, Bamoth Baal, Beth Baal Meon,

18.text: Jahaza, Kedemoth, Mephaath,

19.text: Kirjathaim, Sibmah, Zereth Shahar in the valley hills,

20.text: Beth Peor, Pisgah's slopes, and Beth Jeshimoth,

21.text: All the cities in the plains, plus the whole kingdom of Sihon, king of the Amorites, who ruled from Heshbon. Moses took him down along with the Midianite leaders—Evi, Rekem, Zur, Hur, and Reba—who were Sihon's officials.

22.text: Israel also took out Balaam, son of Beor—the sorcerer—when they handled Sihon's people.

23.text: Reuben's land stretched to the Jordan River. This was their inheritance—the cities and their surrounding villages.

24.text: Moses gave land to the tribe of Gad, divided by their families.

25.text: Their territory included Jazer, all the cities of Gilead, and half the Ammonite land up to Aroer, near Rabbah.

26.text: From Heshbon to Ramath Mizpah and Betonim, and from Mahanaim to Debir's border,

27.text: In the Jordan Valley—Beth Haram, Beth Nimrah, Succoth, and Zaphon, plus the rest of Sihon's kingdom from Heshbon. The Jordan River marked their border up to the edge of the Sea of Chinnereth, on the east side of the Jordan.

28.text: This was Gad's inheritance—the cities and villages that came with it.

29.text: Moses also gave land to half the tribe of Manasseh, divided by their families.

30.text: Their land stretched from Mahanaim, covering all of Bashan and the whole kingdom of Og, including all sixty towns of Jair in Bashan.

31.text: It also included half of Gilead, plus Ashtaroth and Edrei—two major cities in Og's kingdom. This was for the descendants of Machir, son of Manasseh, split among his people.

32.text: These were the lands Moses gave out east of the Jordan, in the plains of Moab near Jericho.

33.text: But the Levites ain't get no land—cause the Lord God of Israel Himself was their inheritance, just like He said.

1.text: These the lands Israel inherited in Canaan, divided up by Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the leaders of the tribes.

2.text: The land was handed out by casting lots, just like the Lord told Moses to do, for the nine and a half tribes.

3.text: Moses already gave land to the other two and a half tribes on the east side of the Jordan, but the Levites ain't get no land among them.

4.text: Since Joseph's descendants were split into two tribes—Manasseh and Ephraim—they still got their share. The Levites only got cities to live in, along with fields for their animals and crops.

5.text: Israel did just like the Lord told Moses, and they divided up the land.

6.text: Then the people of Judah came to Joshua at Gilgal, and Caleb, son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite, said, 'You remember what the Lord told Moses, the man of God, about me and you back in Kadesh Barnea?'

7.text: 'I was 40 years old when Moses sent me from Kadesh Barnea to spy on the land. I came back and gave him my honest take on it.'

8.text: 'But the other spies? They had everybody scared. Meanwhile, I stayed faithful to the Lord my God.'

9.text: 'So Moses made a promise that day: 'The land you walked on is yours forever, for you and your kids, cause you stayed faithful to the Lord.''

10.text: 'Now look—the Lord kept me alive just like He said, all these 45 years while Israel was out here wandering in the wilderness. Now I'm 85 years old.'

11.text: 'And I still got it. I'm just as strong now as I was when Moses sent me out—still got the strength to fight and handle business.'

12.text: 'So go 'head and give me that mountain the Lord promised back then. You know them Anakim giants live there, and their cities got big, strong walls. But with the Lord on my side, I'ma drive them out, just like He said.'

13.text: Joshua blessed Caleb and gave him Hebron as his inheritance.

14.text: So from that day on, Hebron belonged to Caleb, son of Jephunneh the Kenizzite, cause he stayed true to the Lord God of Israel.

15.text: Hebron used to be called Kirjath Arba, named after Arba, the greatest of the Anakim giants. After that, the land finally had peace from war.

1.text: This the land given to the tribe of Judah, divided up by their families. Their southern border stretched to Edom at the Wilderness of Zin.

2.text: The southern border started at the shore of the Salt Sea, from the bay facing south.

3.text: Then it ran south past Akrabbim, through Zin, went up the south side of Kadesh Barnea, passed through Hezron, went up to Adar, and curved around to Karkaa.

4.text: From there, it stretched toward Azmon, followed the Brook of Egypt, and ended at the Mediterranean Sea. That was their southern border.

5.text: Their eastern border was just the Salt Sea, all the way up to the mouth of the Jordan River.

6.text: The northern border started at the bay of the Salt Sea at the Jordan's mouth, ran up to Beth Hoglah, passed north of Beth Arabah, and went up to the stone of Bohan, son of Reuben.

7.text: Then it ran up to Debir from the Valley of Achor, turned north toward Gilgal (before the Ascent of Adummim), then went toward the waters of En Shemesh and ended at En Rogel.

8.text: Then it climbed through the Valley of the Son of Hinnom, running past the south side of Jebusite city (which is Jerusalem). It continued to the top of the mountain overlooking Hinnom Valley from the west, at the north end of Rephaim Valley.

9.text: From there, it curved to the spring at Nephtoah, went to the cities on Mount Ephron, and circled around Baalah (Kirjath Jearim).

10.text: Then it turned west from Baalah to Mount Seir, ran past the north side of Mount Jearim (Chesalon), went down to Beth Shemesh, and passed Timnah.

11.text: Then it ran north past Ekron, curved around to Shicron, passed Mount Baalah, stretched to Jabneel, and ended at the Mediterranean Sea.

12.text: The western border was just the coastline of the Mediterranean. That was Judah's territory, divided up by their families.
