13.text: Joshua gave Caleb, son of Jephunneh, a special share in Judah's land, just like the Lord commanded. He got Kirjath Arba (which is Hebron), named after Arba, the father of the Anakites.

14.text: Caleb pulled up and drove out the three Anakite brothers living there—Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai.

15.text: Then he marched on to Debir, which used to be called Kirjath Sepher.

16.text: Caleb said, 'Whoever takes this city can have my daughter Achsah as his wife.'

17.text: So Othniel, son of Kenaz (Caleb's younger brother), took the city, and Caleb gave him his daughter Achsah as a wife.

18.text: When she got married, she told Othniel to ask her father for some land. She hopped off her donkey, and Caleb asked, 'What you need?'

19.text: She said, 'Since you gave me land in the South, bless me with some springs of water too.' So Caleb gave her both the upper and lower springs.

20.text: This was the inheritance of the tribe of Judah, divided by their families.

21.text: The cities near the southern border, by Edom, were: Kabzeel, Eder, Jagur,

22.text: Kinah, Dimonah, Adadah,

23.text: Kedesh, Hazor, Ithnan,

24.text: Ziph, Telem, Bealoth,

25.text: Hazor, Hadattah, Kerioth, Hezron (also called Hazor),

26.text: Amam, Shema, Moladah,

27.text: Hazar Gaddah, Heshmon, Beth Pelet,

28.text: Hazar Shual, Beersheba, Bizjothjah,

29.text: Baalah, Ijim, Ezem,

30.text: Eltolad, Chesil,

31.text: Ziklag, Madmannah, Sansannah,

32.text: Lebaoth, Shilhim, Ain, and Rimmon. Altogether, that's 29 cities with their villages.

33.text: In the lowlands: Eshtaol, Zorah, Ashnah,

34.text: Zanoah, En Gannim, Tappuah, Enam,

35.text: Jarmuth, Adullam, Socoh, Azekah,

36.text: Sharaim, Adithaim, Gederah, and Gederothaim. Fourteen cities with their villages.

37.text: Zenan, Hadashah, Migdal Gad,

38.text: Dilean, Mizpah, Joktheel,

39.text: Lachish, Bozkath, Eglon,

40.text: Cabbon, Lahmas, Kithlish,

41.text: Gederoth, Beth Dagon, Naamah, and Makkedah. Sixteen cities with their villages.

42.text: Libnah, Ether, Ashan,

43.text: Jiphtah, Ashnah, Nezib,

44.text: Keilah, Achzib, and Mareshah. Nine cities with their villages.

45.text: Ekron, with all its surrounding towns and villages.

46.text: From Ekron to the sea, everything near Ashdod, including its villages.

47.text: Ashdod with its towns and villages, and Gaza with its towns and villages—all the way to the Brook of Egypt and the Mediterranean coastline.

48.text: In the hill country: Shamir, Jattir, Socoh,

49.text: Dannah, Kirjath Sannah (which is Debir),

50.text: Anab, Eshtemoh, Anim,

51.text: Goshen, Holon, and Giloh. Eleven cities with their villages.

52.text: Arab, Dumah, Eshean,

53.text: Janum, Beth Tappuah, Aphekah,

54.text: Humtah, Kirjath Arba (which is Hebron), and Zior. Nine cities with their villages.

55.text: Maon, Carmel, Ziph, Juttah,

56.text: Jezreel, Jokdeam, Zanoah,

57.text: Kain, Gibeah, and Timnah. Ten cities with their villages.

58.text: Halhul, Beth Zur, Gedor,

59.text: Maarath, Beth Anoth, and Eltekon. Six cities with their villages.

60.text: Kirjath Baal (which is Kirjath Jearim) and Rabbah. Two cities with their villages.

61.text: In the desert region: Beth Arabah, Middin, Secacah,

62.text: Nibshan, the City of Salt, and En Gedi. Six cities with their villages.

63.text: But when it came to the Jebusites living in Jerusalem, Judah couldn't drive them out completely. So to this day, the Jebusites still live among the people of Judah in Jerusalem.

1.text: The land given to Joseph's descendants started from the Jordan River, near Jericho, stretching east to the waters of Jericho, then up through the mountains to Bethel.

2.text: From Bethel, it went to Luz, then to the border of the Archites at Ataroth.

3.text: From there, it went west, past the land of the Japhletites, down to Lower Beth Horon, then to Gezer, and finally ended at the sea.

4.text: So the two tribes from Joseph's line—Manasseh and Ephraim—got their inheritance.

5.text: Ephraim's land, divided by family, had its eastern border start at Ataroth Addar, stretching to Upper Beth Horon.

6.text: From there, the border went north of Michmethath, then curved east toward Taanath Shiloh, passing by Janohah on the east.

7.text: Then it dropped down from Janohah to Ataroth and Naarah, reached Jericho, and ended at the Jordan River.

8.text: The border went from Tappuah west to the Brook Kanah, finally ending at the sea. This was the land given to the Ephraimites, divided by their families.

9.text: Even though the Ephraimites had their own cities, some of their towns were mixed into Manasseh's land, all with their own villages.

10.text: But they ain't drive out the Canaanites living in Gezer. So the Canaanites still live among the Ephraimites to this day, working for them as forced laborers.

1.text: The tribe of Manasseh got their land too, since Manasseh was Joseph's firstborn. His firstborn son, Machir, who was the father of Gilead, was a warrior—so he got Gilead and Bashan.

2.text: The rest of Manasseh's people got their share too, based on their families: the clans of Abiezer, Helek, Asriel, Shechem, Hepher, and Shemida. All these were the sons of Manasseh, Joseph's son.

3.text: But there was this one dude, Zelophehad—son of Hepher, grandson of Gilead, great-grandson of Machir, and part of Manasseh's tribe—who ain't have no sons, just daughters. His daughters' names were Mahlah, Noah, Hoglah, Milcah, and Tirzah.

4.text: They pulled up to Eleazar the priest, Joshua, and the leaders and said, 'The Lord told Moses to give us a share of the land just like our brothers got.' So, following the Lord's command, Joshua gave them land among their uncles.

5.text: Manasseh ended up with ten portions of land, plus Gilead and Bashan on the other side of the Jordan.

6.text: This happened because Manasseh's daughters got an inheritance just like the sons, and the rest of the sons got Gilead.

7.text: Manasseh's land stretched from Asher to Michmethath, east of Shechem, and then south to the people of En Tappuah.

8.text: Manasseh owned the land of Tappuah, but the actual city of Tappuah, sitting on Manasseh's border, belonged to the Ephraimites.

9.text: The border ran down to the Brook Kanah. Some of Ephraim's cities were actually inside Manasseh's territory. Manasseh's land ran north of the brook and ended at the sea.

10.text: Ephraim's land was to the south, Manasseh's to the north, and the sea was their western border. Manasseh's land also touched Asher's land up north and Issachar's land to the east.

11.text: Inside Issachar and Asher's territories, Manasseh had control over Beth Shean and its towns, Ibleam and its towns, Dor and its towns, En Dor and its towns, Taanach and its towns, and Megiddo and its towns—all hilly regions.

12.text: But Manasseh's people couldn't kick out the Canaanites from those cities. The Canaanites were too determined to stay.

13.text: Later on, when Israel got stronger, they put the Canaanites to forced labor, but they still didn't completely drive them out.

14.text: The descendants of Joseph came to Joshua and said, 'Why you only gave us one piece of land? We a big tribe! The Lord done blessed us, and we growing fast!'

15.text: Joshua told them, 'If y'all really that big, go clear out some land for yourselves in the forest country where the Perizzites and the giants live. Since the mountains of Ephraim ain't enough for you, expand out.'

16.text: But the people of Joseph said, 'That mountain land still ain't enough for us, plus the Canaanites in the valley got iron chariots! The ones in Beth Shean and the Valley of Jezreel? They too strong for us!'

17.text: Joshua told the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh, 'Listen, y'all a strong and powerful people. Y'all ain't just getting one share of land.'

18.text: 'That whole mountain country gon' be yours. Yeah, it's got forests now, but chop 'em down and take that land. You gon' push out the Canaanites, even if they got iron chariots and look strong.'

1.text: All the Israelites gathered at Shiloh and set up the meeting tent there. The land was now under their control.

2.text: But seven tribes still ain't got their share of land yet.

3.text: So Joshua asked them, 'How long y'all gon' sit around instead of claiming the land the Lord already gave you?'

4.text: 'Pick three men from each tribe, and I'll send them to go survey the land. They'll check it out, write everything down, and bring it back to me.'

5.text: 'They gon' divide it into seven sections. Judah gon' keep their land in the south, and Joseph's tribe gon' keep their land in the north.'

6.text: 'Y'all survey the land in seven parts and bring it back to me so we can cast lots before the Lord to divide it up fairly.'

7.text: 'The Levites ain't getting no land cause they got the Lord's priesthood instead. And Gad, Reuben, and half of Manasseh already got their land east of the Jordan, which Moses gave them.'

8.text: So the men got up and left to go survey the land. Joshua told them, 'Go walk through the land, write everything down, then come back so I can cast lots for y'all here in Shiloh before the Lord.'

9.text: The men went, mapped out the land in seven sections, wrote it all down in a book, and brought it back to Joshua at the camp in Shiloh.

10.text: Then Joshua cast lots in Shiloh before the Lord, dividing up the land among Israel based on their groups.

11.text: Benjamin's land was assigned by lot, and it ended up between the land of Judah and Joseph's descendants.

12.text: The northern border started at the Jordan River, stretched past Jericho on the north side, and ran west into the mountains, ending at the Wilderness of Beth Aven.

13.text: Then it went over to Luz (which is Bethel), headed south, then ran down to Ataroth Addar, near the hill by Lower Beth Horon.

14.text: Then the border turned west to the south side, running past the hill near Beth Horon and ending at Kirjath Baal (Kirjath Jearim), a city of Judah. That was the western border.

15.text: The southern border started at Kirjath Jearim, stretched west, and reached the spring of Nephtoah.

16.text: Then it went down the mountain at the edge of the Valley of Hinnom, which is north of the Rephaim Valley. It continued down to the Valley of Hinnom, near the Jebusite city (Jerusalem), and ran down to En Rogel.

17.text: From there, it turned north to En Shemesh, stretched to Geliloth (before the Ascent of Adummim), and went down to the stone of Bohan, son of Reuben.

18.text: Then it passed along the north side of Arabah and went down into Arabah.

19.text: The border kept going past the north side of Beth Hoglah and ended at the north bay of the Salt Sea, where the Jordan meets it in the south. That was the southern border.

20.text: The eastern border was the Jordan River. That's the land Benjamin got, with its boundaries mapped out for their families.

21.text: Benjamin's tribe got these cities: Jericho, Beth Hoglah, Emek Keziz,

22.text: Beth Arabah, Zemaraim, Bethel,

23.text: Avim, Parah, Ophrah,

24.text: Chephar Haammoni, Ophni, and Gaba—twelve cities with their villages.

25.text: Also: Gibeon, Ramah, Beeroth,

26.text: Mizpah, Chephirah, Mozah,

27.text: Rekem, Irpeel, Taralah,

28.text: Zelah, Eleph, Jebus (which is Jerusalem), Gibeath, and Kirjath—fourteen cities with their villages. This was the land given to Benjamin's tribe, split among their families.

1.text: The second lot went to Simeon's tribe, divided by their families. Their land was inside Judah's territory.

2.text: They got Beersheba (also called Sheba), Moladah,

3.text: Hazar Shual, Balah, Ezem,

4.text: Eltolad, Bethul, Hormah,

5.text: Ziklag, Beth Marcaboth, Hazar Susah,

6.text: Beth Lebaoth, and Sharuhen—13 cities with their villages.

7.text: They also got Ain, Rimmon, Ether, and Ashan—four cities with their villages.

8.text: Plus all the villages around these cities, reaching as far as Baalath Beer (also known as Ramah of the South). This was Simeon's inheritance, split up by families.

9.text: Simeon's land was inside Judah's because Judah had too much land, so Simeon got a piece of it.

10.text: The third lot went to Zebulun's tribe, divided by families. Their land stretched to Sarid.

11.text: Their border went west to Maralah, reached Dabbasheth, and followed the stream east of Jokneam.

12.text: From Sarid, it went east toward Chisloth Tabor, passed Daberath, and bypassed Japhia.

13.text: Then it ran east past Gath Hepher toward Eth Kazin and stretched to Rimmon, right by Neah.

14.text: Then it wrapped around the north side of Hannathon and ended at the Valley of Jiphthah El.

15.text: Their land included Kattath, Nahallal, Shimron, Idalah, and Bethlehem—12 cities with their villages.

16.text: That was Zebulun's inheritance, divided by families, including these cities and villages.

17.text: The fourth lot went to Issachar's tribe, divided by families.

18.text: Their land included Jezreel, Chesulloth, Shunem,

19.text: Haphraim, Shion, Anaharath,

20.text: Rabbith, Kishion, Abez,

21.text: Remeth, En Gannim, En Haddah, and Beth Pazzez.

22.text: The border stretched to Tabor, Shahazimah, and Beth Shemesh, ending at the Jordan. They got 16 cities with their villages.

23.text: That was Issachar's inheritance, divided by families, including these cities and villages.

24.text: The fifth lot went to Asher's tribe, divided by families.

25.text: Their land included Helkath, Hali, Beten, Achshaph,

26.text: Alammelech, Amad, and Mishal. It stretched west to Mount Carmel and the Brook Shihor Libnath.

27.text: It turned east toward Beth Dagon, reached Zebulun and the Valley of Jiphthah El, then went north past Beth Emek and Neiel, skirting Cabul on the left.

28.text: It included Ebron, Rehob, Hammon, and Kanah, reaching all the way to Greater Sidon.

29.text: Then it turned to Ramah and the fortified city of Tyre, before heading to Hosah and ending at the sea, near Achzib.

30.text: They also got Ummah, Aphek, and Rehob—22 cities with their villages.

31.text: That was Asher's inheritance, divided by families, including these cities and villages.

32.text: The sixth lot went to Naphtali's tribe, divided by families.

33.text: Their border started at Heleph, stretching past the terebinth tree at Zaanannim, through Adami Nekeb and Jabneel, reaching as far as Lakkum, where it ended at the Jordan.

34.text: From there, it extended west to Aznoth Tabor, then went toward Hukkok. It bordered Zebulun in the south, Asher in the west, and Judah at the Jordan in the east.

35.text: Their fortified cities were Ziddim, Zer, Hammath, Rakkath, and Chinnereth,

36.text: Adamah, Ramah, Hazor,

37.text: Kedesh, Edrei, En Hazor,

38.text: Iron, Migdal El, Horem, Beth Anath, and Beth Shemesh—19 cities with their villages.

39.text: That was Naphtali's inheritance, divided by families, including these cities and villages.

40.text: The seventh lot went to Dan's tribe, divided by families.

41.text: Their land included Zorah, Eshtaol, Ir Shemesh,

42.text: Shaalabbin, Aijalon, Jethlah,

43.text: Elon, Timnah, Ekron,

44.text: Eltekeh, Gibbethon, Baalath,

45.text: Jehud, Bene Berak, Gath Rimmon,

46.text: Me Jarkon, Rakkon, and the area near Joppa.

47.text: But Dan's people weren't satisfied with their land, so they went and fought against Leshem. They conquered it, wiped it out with the sword, took it over, and lived there. They renamed it Dan, after their ancestor.

48.text: That was Dan's inheritance, divided by families, including these cities and villages.

49.text: Once all the land had been divided up, the Israelites gave Joshua son of Nun his own share.

50.text: Following the Lord's command, they gave him the city he asked for—Timnath Serah in the mountains of Ephraim. He built up the city and lived there.

51.text: Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the tribal leaders divided up the land in Shiloh, at the entrance of the meeting tent, before the Lord. And that's how they finished dividing up the land.

1.text: Then the Lord spoke to Joshua, saying,

2.text: 'Tell the Israelites: Set up some cities of refuge, just like I told Moses.'

3.text: 'These cities gon' be safe spots for anybody who accidentally kills someone without meaning to. They can run there and be protected from anyone trying to get revenge.'

4.text: 'When they reach one of these cities, they gotta stand at the city gate and explain what happened to the elders. If it checks out, they'll let them in and give them a place to stay.'

5.text: 'If the person's being chased by someone looking for payback, the city can't hand them over—cause the killing wasn't on purpose, and there was no bad blood before it happened.'

6.text: 'They gotta stay in the city until they have a proper trial in front of the community. And they gotta stay there until the high priest of that time passes away. Then, they can go back home to their own city and house.'

7.text: So they set up these cities as refuges: Kedesh in Galilee, in Naphtali's mountains; Shechem in Ephraim's mountains; Kirjath Arba (which is Hebron) in Judah's mountains.

8.text: On the east side of the Jordan, near Jericho, they set up: Bezer in the wilderness, on the plains of Reuben's territory; Ramoth in Gilead, in Gad's territory; Golan in Bashan, in Manasseh's territory.

9.text: These cities were for all of Israel and any foreigners living with them—anyone who accidentally killed someone could flee there and stay safe until they had a fair trial, instead of being taken out by someone looking for revenge.

1.text: The leaders of the Levites came up to Eleazar the priest, Joshua son of Nun, and the heads of Israel's tribes.

2.text: They told them at Shiloh in Canaan, 'The Lord told Moses to give us cities to live in, plus land for our livestock.'

3.text: So, at the Lord's command, Israel gave the Levites cities and pastureland from their own shares.

4.text: The first lot went to the Kohathites. The descendants of Aaron (who were Levites and priests) got 13 cities from Judah, Simeon, and Benjamin's land.

5.text: The rest of Kohath's people got 10 cities from Ephraim, Dan, and half of Manasseh's land.

6.text: The Gershonites got 13 cities from Issachar, Asher, Naphtali, and the other half of Manasseh's land in Bashan.

7.text: The Merarites got 12 cities from Reuben, Gad, and Zebulun's land.

8.text: Israel gave the Levites these cities and lands by casting lots, just like the Lord told Moses.

9.text: From Judah and Simeon's land, these cities were set aside for the Levites,

10.text: They went to Aaron's descendants, who were part of the Kohathite clan, since their lot came first.

11.text: They got Kirjath Arba (also called Hebron), in Judah's mountains. (Arba was the ancestor of the Anakites.) They also got all the pastureland around it,

12.text: But the fields and villages around Hebron were given to Caleb, son of Jephunneh, as his share.

13.text: The Levites got: Hebron (a city of refuge) and Libnah

14.text: Jattir and Eshtemoa

15.text: Holon and Debir

16.text: Ain, Juttah, and Beth Shemesh. That's 9 cities from Judah and Simeon's land.

17.text: From Benjamin's land, they got: Gibeon and Geba

18.text: Anathoth and Almon. That's 4 cities in Benjamin.

19.text: In total, Aaron's descendants got 13 cities with their pasturelands.

20.text: Kohath's other Levite families got their share from Ephraim's land.

21.text: They received: Shechem (a city of refuge) and Gezer

22.text: Kibzaim and Beth Horon. That's 4 cities from Ephraim.

23.text: From Dan, they got: Eltekeh and Gibbethon

24.text: Aijalon and Gath Rimmon. That's 4 cities from Dan.

25.text: From half of Manasseh, they got: Tanach and Gath Rimmon. That's 2 cities from Manasseh.

26.text: In total, Kohath's remaining families got 10 cities with their pasturelands.

27.text: Gershon's Levites got land from the other half of Manasseh.

28.text: From Manasseh, they got: Golan in Bashan (a city of refuge) and Be Eshterah. That's 2 cities from Manasseh.

29.text: From Issachar, they got: Kishion and Daberath

30.text: Jarmuth and En Gannim. That's 4 cities from Issachar.

31.text: From Asher, they got: Mishal and Abdon

32.text: Helkath and Rehob. That's 4 cities from Asher.

33.text: From Naphtali, they got: Kedesh in Galilee (a city of refuge), Hammoth Dor, and Kartan. That's 3 cities from Naphtali.

34.text: In total, Gershon's Levites got 13 cities with their pasturelands.

35.text: Merari's Levites got their share from Zebulun's land.

36.text: From Zebulun, they got: Jokneam and Kartah

37.text: Dimnah and Nahalal. That's 4 cities from Zebulun.

38.text: From Reuben, they got: Bezer and Jahaz

39.text: Kedemoth and Mephaath. That's 4 cities from Reuben.

40.text: From Gad, they got: Ramoth in Gilead (a city of refuge) and Mahanaim

41.text: Heshbon and Jazer. That's 4 cities from Gad.

42.text: In total, Merari's Levites got 12 cities with their pasturelands.

43.text: In total, the Levites received 48 cities across Israel, with their pasturelands.

44.text: Each city had land surrounding it, just like the Lord commanded.

45.text: The Lord gave Israel all the land He promised to their ancestors. They took it and lived there.

46.text: The Lord gave them peace on all sides, just like He promised. None of their enemies could stand against them—God put them all in Israel's hands.

47.text: Not a single promise the Lord made to Israel failed. Everything came true.

1.text: Then Joshua called up the Reubenites, Gadites, and half the tribe of Manasseh.

2.text: He told them, 'Y'all did everything Moses told you to do, and you listened to me every step of the way.'

3.text: 'For all this time, you ain't abandoned your brothers. You held it down and kept the Lord's command.'

4.text: 'Now the Lord has given peace to your people, just like He promised. So go on, head back to your tents, back to your land—the land Moses gave y'all on the other side of the Jordan.'

5.text: 'But listen, make sure you stay faithful. Follow the Lord's commands, love Him, walk in His ways, hold on tight to Him, and serve Him with all your heart and soul.'

6.text: Then Joshua blessed them and sent them home, and they went back to their tents.

7.text: Half of Manasseh's tribe got land in Bashan, while the other half got land west of the Jordan. Before they left, Joshua gave them a blessing too.

8.text: He told them, 'Go home with all these riches—livestock, silver, gold, bronze, iron, and clothes. And make sure you share the loot with your brothers.'

9.text: So Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh's tribe left Israel's camp at Shiloh in Canaan and went back home to Gilead, the land they got from the Lord through Moses.

10.text: When they got to the Jordan, the eastern tribes built a huge altar by the river.

11.text: But when the rest of Israel heard about it, folks started talking: 'Yo, did y'all hear? Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh just built an altar on our side of the Jordan!'

12.text: The whole congregation got heated and gathered at Shiloh, ready to go to war against them.

13.text: Israel sent Phinehas, son of Eleazar the priest, to Gilead to talk to the eastern tribes.

14.text: They also sent ten tribal leaders, one from each tribe, all heads of their families in Israel.

15.text: They met with Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh in Gilead and told them,

16.text: 'What is this nonsense y'all just pulled? Why you rebelling against the Lord by building your own altar?'

17.text: 'Didn't we just recover from that mess at Peor? We still feeling the consequences of that sin!'

18.text: 'Now y'all wanna turn from the Lord again? You do this today, and tomorrow God's wrath gon' fall on all of us!'

19.text: 'Look, if your land ain't good enough, just move over to the Lord's land where the tabernacle is! But don't go making another altar and rebelling against God—and don't drag us into it!'

20.text: 'Y'all remember what happened to Achan, right? He sinned, and the whole nation suffered. This ain't just about you!'

21.text: Reuben, Gad, and half of Manasseh answered Israel's leaders and said,

22.text: 'The Lord God of gods, the Lord God of gods—He knows the truth. And Israel, y'all need to know it too. If we rebelled against God, then let Him deal with us right now.'

23.text: 'If we built this altar to go against the Lord, offer sacrifices, or start some mess—then may God punish us.'

24.text: 'But that ain't why we did it. We built it because we were worried about the future.'

25.text: 'We thought, What if later on, y'all start telling our kids: "Y'all ain't got no part in the Lord!"?'

26.text: 'So we built this altar not for sacrifices, but as a reminder to future generations.'

27.text: 'It's proof that we serve the Lord just like y'all do—that we bring offerings and sacrifices to the Lord, so nobody can ever say, "Y'all don't belong to God."'

28.text: 'If anybody ever tries to challenge us in the future, we'll just point to this altar and say, "This right here is proof that we follow the same Lord."'

29.text: 'Far be it from us to turn against the Lord! We ain't trying to make a separate altar for burnt offerings or sacrifices—there's only one altar, the Lord's altar, in front of the tabernacle.'

30.text: When Phinehas and the leaders heard their explanation, they relaxed. They saw it was all good.

31.text: Phinehas told them, 'Aight, now we see the Lord is still with us, cause y'all ain't committed no sin. Y'all just made sure Israel won't have beef down the road. That's a real win.'

32.text: So Phinehas and the leaders went back to Israel's camp in Canaan and gave their report.

33.text: Everybody in Israel was cool with it. They praised God and dropped all plans for war against Reuben, Gad, and Manasseh.

34.text: Reuben and Gad named the altar "Witness," saying, 'It stands as proof between us that the Lord is God.'

1.text: A long time passed after the Lord had given Israel peace from all their enemies. By then, Joshua was old and up in age.

2.text: So Joshua called all of Israel together—the elders, leaders, judges, and officers—and said to them:

3.text: 'Y'all saw with your own eyes what the Lord did to all these nations for you. It was the Lord fighting for you the whole time.'

4.text: 'I already divided up the remaining nations as your inheritance—from the Jordan to the Great Sea in the west, including the lands we took from defeated nations.'

5.text: 'And the Lord Himself gon' push the rest of them out. He gon' clear the way for y'all just like He promised.'

6.text: 'So be strong and make sure you follow everything written in the Book of the Law of Moses. Don't go left or right—stay on track!'

7.text: 'Don't start mixing with these nations still around you. Don't even mention their gods, don't swear by them, don't worship them, and don't bow down to them.'

8.text: 'Instead, stick tight to the Lord, just like you been doing till now.'

9.text: 'The Lord already drove out powerful nations before you, and nobody has been able to stand against you.'

10.text: 'One of y'all can chase a thousand, cause it's the Lord who fights for you—just like He promised.'

11.text: 'So stay on guard and make sure you love the Lord with everything you got.'

12.text: 'But if y'all turn back and start mixing with these nations, marrying them, and making alliances with them…'

13.text: 'Just know: The Lord ain't gon' push them out for you anymore. Instead, they gon' become traps, whips to your back, and thorns in your eyes—until y'all are completely wiped out from this land the Lord gave you.'

14.text: 'Look, today I'm about to leave this world like everybody else does. But y'all know deep down that every single promise the Lord made to you came true. Not one of them failed.'

15.text: 'But listen, just like the Lord kept His good promises, He gon' keep His warnings too. If y'all turn against Him, trouble is coming. Y'all will be destroyed from this good land He gave you.'

16.text: 'If you break the Lord's covenant and start serving other gods, bowing down to them, His anger gon' burn against you. And trust me, y'all gon' lose this land real quick.'

1.text: Joshua gathered all the tribes of Israel at Shechem. He called for the elders, leaders, judges, and officers, and they all stood before God.

2.text: Joshua told them, 'This what the Lord God of Israel says: 'Back in the day, your ancestors—including Terah, Abraham's and Nahor's daddy—lived on the other side of the river, and they worshiped other gods.'

3.text: 'But I took Abraham from across the river, led him all through Canaan, made his family big, and gave him Isaac.'

4.text: 'Then I gave Isaac two sons: Jacob and Esau. I gave Esau the mountains of Seir to live in, but Jacob and his people ended up in Egypt.'

5.text: 'Then I sent Moses and Aaron and brought plagues on Egypt. After that, I pulled y'all out.'

6.text: 'When I brought your ancestors out of Egypt, they got chased down by Pharaoh's army with chariots and horsemen at the Red Sea.'

7.text: 'Y'all called out to Me, so I put darkness between y'all and the Egyptians, then drowned them in the sea. Y'all saw it with your own eyes. Then y'all wandered in the wilderness for a long time.'

8.text: 'I brought y'all into the land of the Amorites, and they fought against you. But I handed them over, so y'all could take their land. I wiped them out for y'all.'

9.text: 'Then Balak, king of Moab, tried to come for y'all. He sent for Balaam to curse you,'

10.text: 'But I didn't let Balaam curse you. Instead, he kept blessing y'all, and I saved you from him.'

11.text: 'Then y'all crossed the Jordan and came to Jericho. The people of Jericho fought against you—the Amorites, Perizzites, Canaanites, Hittites, Girgashites, Hivites, and Jebusites—but I gave you the victory.'

12.text: 'I sent hornets ahead to chase them out—y'all ain't even need swords or bows for that.'

13.text: 'I gave y'all land you didn't work for, cities you didn't build, and vineyards and olive groves you didn't plant—and now y'all living off it.'

14.text: 'So now, fear the Lord and serve Him for real. Get rid of those fake gods your ancestors worshiped in Egypt and beyond the river. Serve the Lord!'

15.text: 'But if y'all don't wanna serve Him, then choose today who you gon' serve—the gods your ancestors had across the river, or the gods of the Amorites in this land. But as for me and my house, we serving the Lord!'

16.text: The people answered, 'Nah, we could never turn away from the Lord to serve other gods!'

17.text: 'The Lord is the one who brought us and our ancestors out of Egypt, out of slavery. He did miracles right in front of us, protected us on our journey, and kept us safe from our enemies.'

18.text: 'The Lord drove out all the people in this land before us, including the Amorites. We gon' serve the Lord too, cause He's our God!'

19.text: Joshua told them, 'Y'all can't serve the Lord like that, cause He's holy and jealous. He ain't gon' overlook y'all sins.'

20.text: 'If y'all turn away and start serving other gods, He gon' come for y'all. Just like He blessed you, He can take you out.'

21.text: But the people insisted, 'No! We gon' serve the Lord!'

22.text: Joshua said, 'Alright then, y'all are witnesses against yourselves that you chose to serve the Lord.'

23.text: 'Then get rid of those fake gods and give your full heart to the Lord God of Israel.'

24.text: The people replied, 'We gon' serve the Lord and listen to Him!'

25.text: So Joshua made a covenant with the people that day and set up rules in Shechem.

26.text: Then he wrote everything down in the Book of the Law of God. He also took a big stone and set it up under the oak tree by the Lord's sanctuary.

27.text: Joshua told the people, 'Look, this stone gon' be a witness against us. It heard everything the Lord said to us today. So don't play yourself and turn against Him.'

28.text: Then Joshua sent everybody back home to their own land.

29.text: After all this, Joshua son of Nun, the Lord's servant, died at 110 years old.

30.text: They buried him in his land at Timnath Serah, up in the mountains of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.

31.text: Israel stayed faithful to the Lord as long as Joshua lived, and even after that, as long as the elders who knew about the Lord's miracles were still alive.

32.text: They also buried Joseph's bones at Shechem—the ones the Israelites brought from Egypt. They buried them on land that Jacob bought from Hamor's sons for 100 pieces of silver. That land became Joseph's descendants' inheritance.

33.text: Eleazar, son of Aaron, also died. They buried him in a hill that belonged to his son Phinehas, up in the mountains of Ephraim.

1.text: After Joshua passed, the Israelites went to God and asked, 'Aight Lord, who goin' up first to fight these Canaanites for us?'

2.text: And the Lord said, 'Judah got this. I already put the land in his hands.'

3.text: So Judah hit up his bro Simeon like, 'Yo, roll with me to my spot so we can take down these Canaanites. If you got me, I got you when it's your turn.' And Simeon was down.

4.text: Judah stepped up, and the Lord let them wreck shop on the Canaanites and the Perizzites—took out 10,000 men in Bezek.

5.text: That's where they found Adoni-Bezek, went toe-to-toe with him, and straight-up crushed the Canaanites and Perizzites.

6.text: Adoni-Bezek tried to dip, but they caught him and cut off his thumbs and big toes.

7.text: Adoni-Bezek was like, 'Man, 70 kings had to scrape for food under my table 'cause I did 'em dirty like this. Now God done hit me back the same way.' Then they took him to Jerusalem, and that's where he died.

8.text: Judah's squad went in on Jerusalem, took it over, hit it with the sword, and set the whole city on fire.

9.text: After that, Judah's folks went after more Canaanites—ones in the mountains, down south, and in the lowlands.

10.text: Then they came for the Canaanites in Hebron, back when it was called Kirjath Arba. They handled Sheshai, Ahiman, and Talmai.

11.text: Next, they pulled up on the people in Debir, which used to be called Kirjath Sepher.

12.text: Caleb put it out there, 'Whoever takes down Kirjath Sepher, I'ma give 'em my daughter Achsah as a wife.'

13.text: Othniel, Kenaz's son and Caleb's younger bro, went ahead and did it, so Caleb gave him Achsah.

14.text: When Achsah got with Othniel, she told him, 'Ask my pops for some land.' She pulled up on Caleb, hopped off her donkey, and he was like, 'What's up?'

15.text: She said, 'Bless me real quick—since you already gave me dry land, hook me up with some water too.' And Caleb gave her the upper and lower springs.

16.text: The Kenites, Moses' in-laws, left Jericho with Judah's people and settled in the wilderness of Judah, down south near Arad.

17.text: Then Judah and Simeon linked up again, ran up on Zephath, and completely wiped it out. That's why they renamed the place Hormah.

18.text: Judah also took over Gaza, Ashkelon, and Ekron, plus all their surrounding land.

19.text: The Lord was with Judah, and they pushed back the mountain folks. But they couldn't handle the people in the lowlands 'cause they had iron chariots.

20.text: Like Moses said, they gave Hebron to Caleb, and he kicked out the three sons of Anak.

21.text: But the tribe of Benjamin didn't drive out the Jebusites in Jerusalem, so they still there living with Benjamin's people to this day.

22.text: The house of Joseph went up against Bethel, and the Lord was rocking with them.

23.text: They sent some men to spy on Bethel, which used to be called Luz.

24.text: The spies saw a man leaving the city and told him, 'Yo, show us a way in, and we'll look out for you.'

25.text: Dude showed them the entrance, and they took over the city, wiping it out with swords—but they let him and his fam go.

26.text: That man dipped to the land of the Hittites, built a new city, and called it Luz, and that's what it's still called.

27.text: But Manasseh didn't clear out the folks in Beth Shean, Taanach, Dor, Ibleam, or Megiddo—the Canaanites held their ground.

28.text: When Israel got stronger, they made the Canaanites pay taxes, but they never fully kicked them out.

29.text: Ephraim didn't get rid of the Canaanites in Gezer either, so they stayed living among them.

30.text: Same with Zebulun—Kitron and Nahalol still had Canaanites in them, and they just put them under taxes.

31.text: Asher didn't drive out the people from Acco, Sidon, Ahlab, Achzib, Helbah, Aphik, or Rehob.

32.text: So instead of the Canaanites moving out, Asher's people just lived among them.

33.text: Naphtali did the same with the folks in Beth Shemesh and Beth Anath. They didn't take over completely, just taxed them.

34.text: Meanwhile, the Amorites straight up pushed the tribe of Dan into the mountains and wouldn't let them come down into the valley.

35.text: The Amorites held strong in Mount Heres, Aijalon, and Shaalbim. But when Joseph's house got stronger, they put them under tribute too.

36.text: The border of the Amorites ran from the Ascent of Akrabbim, from Sela and upward.

1.text: Then the Angel of the Lord pulled up from Gilgal to Bochim and said, 'Look, I brought y'all outta Egypt, set y'all up in the land I promised your ancestors, and told y'all straight up—I ain't never breaking my covenant with you.'

2.text: 'I told y'all not to be making no deals with these folks in this land. Tear down their altars, don't mix with 'em. But what y'all do? Y'all ain't listen. Why you gotta do me like this?'

3.text: 'So now, since y'all ain't listen, I ain't clearing these folks out for you. They gon' stay right here, be a thorn in your side, and their gods gon' trap you up.'

4.text: When the Angel of the Lord finished speaking to all Israel, the people broke down crying, loud as ever.

5.text: They called that spot Bochim, which means 'weeping,' and they sacrificed to the Lord right there.

6.text: After Joshua let everybody go, the Israelites went back to claim their land and settle in.

7.text: The people kept serving the Lord as long as Joshua was alive, and even while the elders that came up with him were still around—those who had seen with their own eyes all the great things the Lord did for Israel.

8.text: Then Joshua, son of Nun, the Lord's servant, died at 110 years old.

9.text: They buried him in his land at Timnath Heres, up in the mountains of Ephraim, north of Mount Gaash.

10.text: And after that whole generation was gone, a new generation came up who ain't know the Lord or all the stuff He did for Israel.

11.text: Then the Israelites started acting up—doing evil in the Lord's sight and serving these weak little Baal gods.

12.text: They straight up abandoned the God of their ancestors, the one who freed them from Egypt, and started chasing after these fake gods from the nations around 'em. Bowing down to 'em, worshipping 'em—making the Lord real mad.

13.text: They turned their backs on the Lord and started serving Baal and Ashtoreth, getting caught up in all that idol mess.

14.text: So the Lord got heated. He let raiders come through, take their stuff, and handed them over to their enemies. They couldn't even stand up against them.

15.text: Everywhere they went, the Lord's hand was against them. Just like He warned 'em, they were catching nothing but L's and ended up real miserable.

16.text: But even then, the Lord had mercy and raised up judges to help rescue them from the folks that was doing 'em dirty.

17.text: But nope, they ain't wanna listen to the judges either. Instead, they ran after these other gods, bowing down and wildin' out. They turned away from how their ancestors lived, ignoring God's commandments like it was nothing.

18.text: But every time the Lord put a judge in place, He was with them. As long as the judge was alive, He made sure Israel was good. He had compassion on them 'cause He heard their cries from all the trouble they was in.

19.text: But the second that judge died? They went right back to acting worse than before. Chasing after these false gods, bowing down, being hardheaded, and refusing to change their ways.

20.text: So the Lord got fed up and said, 'Since y'all keep breaking my covenant and ignoring my commands…'

21.text: 'I'm done clearing out these nations for y'all. The ones Joshua ain't get rid of before he died? They staying right here.'

22.text: 'Let's see if Israel will actually stick to my ways and live how their ancestors did, or if they gon' keep messing up.'

23.text: So the Lord left those nations where they were. He didn't clear 'em out right away, and He ain't give them over to Joshua neither.

1.text: These the nations the Lord left behind to test Israel—to see what the new generation, who ain't been in those Canaan battles, was really about.

2.text: (He did this to teach the next generation how to fight since they ain't have no war experience before.)

3.text: These were the ones left: five rulers of the Philistines, all the Canaanites, the Sidonians, and the Hivites living up in Mount Lebanon, from Mount Baal Hermon to the entrance of Hamath.

4.text: God left them there to see if Israel would actually follow His commandments like He told their ancestors through Moses.

5.text: But instead of driving them out, Israel started living among the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Hivites, and Jebusites.

6.text: They started intermarrying—giving their daughters to these folks and taking their daughters as wives. Next thing you know, they out here serving their gods.

7.text: Israel started acting up again, doing evil in the Lord's sight. They straight up forgot about the Lord and started worshipping Baal and Asherah.

8.text: So God got fed up and handed them over to Cushan-Rishathaim, king of Mesopotamia. Israel ended up serving him for eight years.

9.text: Then Israel cried out to the Lord, and He raised up a deliverer for them—Othniel, the son of Kenaz, Caleb's younger brother.

10.text: The Spirit of the Lord came on Othniel, and he became Israel's judge. He led them into battle, and the Lord helped him take down Cushan-Rishathaim, giving him the W.

11.text: And just like that, the land had peace for 40 years. Then Othniel died.

12.text: But as soon as Othniel was gone, Israel started wildin' again, doing evil in the Lord's sight. So the Lord let Eglon, king of Moab, rise up against them because of their sins.

13.text: Eglon linked up with the Ammonites and Amalekites, came through, put Israel in a chokehold, and took over the City of Palms.

14.text: Israel was stuck serving Eglon, king of Moab, for eighteen years.

15.text: But when they finally cried out to the Lord, He raised up a deliverer—Ehud, the son of Gera from the tribe of Benjamin, a left-handed warrior. Israel sent him to bring tribute money to King Eglon.

16.text: Ehud had a plan, though. He made himself a double-edged dagger, about a foot and a half long, and strapped it under his clothes on his right thigh.

17.text: He brought the tribute to Eglon, who, by the way, was a very heavy man.

18.text: After dropping off the tribute, Ehud sent the other guys who helped carry it back home.

19.text: Then he doubled back from the stone idols at Gilgal and told Eglon, 'Yo, King, I got a secret message for you.' Eglon was intrigued and told his attendants to leave.

20.text: Ehud came up close while Eglon was chilling in his private upstairs room. Then Ehud said, 'I got a message straight from God for you.' Eglon stood up from his seat.

21.text: That's when Ehud, quick as ever, pulled his dagger from his right thigh with his left hand and drove it straight into Eglon's belly.

22.text: The whole dagger went in deep, handle and all, and the fat closed over it. Ehud ain't even pull the blade out—Eglon's guts spilled everywhere.

23.text: Ehud dipped out through the porch, locked the doors behind him, and got away.

24.text: After he left, Eglon's servants came by and saw the doors locked. They figured, 'Oh, he probably just using the bathroom in there.'

25.text: They waited. And waited. Until they got embarrassed 'cause he was taking way too long. Finally, they grabbed the key, unlocked the doors, and—boom—found their king dead on the floor.

26.text: Meanwhile, Ehud had already escaped, passed the stone images, and made it to Seirah.

27.text: As soon as he got there, he blew the trumpet in the mountains of Ephraim, rallying the Israelites to rise up.

28.text: He told them, 'Let's go! The Lord done handed the Moabites over to us!' So they followed him, took control of the Jordan crossings, and let nobody escape.

29.text: They wiped out 10,000 Moabite warriors that day—all strong, capable fighters. Not a single one got away.

30.text: And just like that, Moab was humbled under Israel's rule. The land stayed peaceful for 80 years.

31.text: After Ehud, there was Shamgar, the son of Anath. This man took an ox goad (basically a long stick) and used it to kill 600 Philistines by himself. And just like that, he saved Israel.

1.text: After Ehud died, Israel started acting up again, doing evil in the Lord's sight.

2.text: So the Lord let them get taken over by Jabin, king of Canaan, who ruled from Hazor. His top general was Sisera, who lived in Harosheth Hagoyim.

3.text: Israel cried out to God 'cause Jabin had 900 iron chariots and had been oppressing them hard for 20 years.

4.text: Now at that time, Deborah, a prophetess and wife of Lapidoth, was judging Israel.

5.text: She would sit under the Palm of Deborah between Ramah and Bethel in the hill country of Ephraim, and the Israelites came to her to settle their disputes.

6.text: One day she sent for Barak, son of Abinoam from Kedesh in Naphtali, and told him, 'Didn't the Lord tell you to get your troops together? Go post up at Mount Tabor with 10,000 men from Naphtali and Zebulun.'

7.text: 'Sisera, Jabin's general, gon' roll up on y'all by the Kishon River with his army and chariots. But don't trip—God already set it up for you to win.'

8.text: Barak said, 'I'll go… but only if you go with me!'

9.text: Deborah was like, 'Bet, I'll go. But just so you know, you ain't getting no credit for this victory—God gon' hand Sisera over to a woman.' So Deborah rolled with Barak to Kedesh.

10.text: Barak called up the tribes of Zebulun and Naphtali, and 10,000 men followed him. Deborah was right there with him.

11.text: Meanwhile, Heber the Kenite, from Moses' in-law's family, had split off from his people and set up camp near the oak tree at Zaanaim, close to Kedesh.

12.text: Sisera got the word that Barak was up at Mount Tabor.

13.text: So he rounded up all 900 iron chariots and his whole army and headed to the Kishon River, ready for war.

14.text: Then Deborah told Barak, 'Aight, time to move! Today's the day the Lord is handing Sisera over to you. You already know He went ahead of you!'

15.text: So Barak charged down from Mount Tabor with his 10,000 men, and the Lord threw Sisera's army into chaos. Barak's squad ran through them with the sword, and Sisera had to jump out his chariot and take off on foot.

16.text: Barak and his men chased the enemy all the way back to Harosheth Hagoyim. By the time it was over, every single one of Sisera's soldiers was dead.

17.text: Sisera, meanwhile, ran off to the tent of Jael, wife of Heber the Kenite. Since Heber's people had a peace treaty with Jabin, Sisera thought he was safe.

18.text: Jael stepped out to meet him and said, 'Come in, my lord, don't be scared.' So he went in, and she covered him up with a blanket.

19.text: He told her, 'Please, I'm mad thirsty—gimme some water.' But instead of water, she gave him some milk, then tucked him in real good.

20.text: Then Sisera said, 'Stand at the tent door, and if anybody asks if I'm in here, tell 'em no.'

21.text: But while he was knocked out, Jael grabbed a tent peg and a hammer, crept up on him, and drove that peg straight through his skull into the ground. Dude ain't even wake up—he was gone.

22.text: When Barak came looking for Sisera, Jael stepped out and said, 'I got who you looking for.' He stepped inside and saw Sisera laid out, dead, with a tent peg through his head.

23.text: And just like that, God humbled Jabin, the king of Canaan, right in front of Israel.

24.text: From that day forward, Israel kept pressing harder and harder against Jabin until they completely wiped him out.

1.text: On that day, Deborah and Barak, son of Abinoam, sang this song:

2.text: 'When the leaders step up, and the people willingly follow, bless the Lord!'

3.text: 'Listen up, kings! Pay attention, rulers! I'ma sing to the Lord, I'ma praise the Lord, the God of Israel!'

4.text: 'Lord, when You stepped out from Seir, when You marched from Edom's fields, the earth shook, the heavens opened up, and the clouds let loose rain.'

5.text: 'The mountains trembled before You, Lord, yes, even Mount Sinai before the God of Israel!'

6.text: 'Back in the days of Shamgar, son of Anath, and in Jael's time, the highways were empty—travelers had to take the backroads just to be safe.'

7.text: 'Village life straight-up stopped in Israel, until I, Deborah, stood up, stood up like a mother to Israel.'

8.text: 'They went and chose new gods, and what happened? War came right to their gates. But not a single shield or spear was seen among forty thousand in Israel.'

9.text: 'My heart is with the leaders of Israel, the ones who stepped up and stood with the people. Bless the Lord!'

10.text: 'Y'all who ride on white donkeys, y'all who wear fine clothes and sit in judgment—speak on this!'

11.text: 'By the wells, far from the battle cries, they gon' tell the stories of the Lord's victories, how He saved His people. Then the Lord's people will come down to the gates!'

12.text: 'Wake up, wake up, Deborah! Wake up, wake up and sing! Get up, Barak! Lead your captives away, son of Abinoam!'

13.text: 'Then the survivors of Israel rose up, and the Lord sent them against the mighty.'

14.text: 'From Ephraim came warriors, tracing back to Amalek. Benjamin's people followed close behind. From Machir came leaders, from Zebulun, those who carry the commander's staff.'

15.text: 'The princes of Issachar were with Deborah; they rode with Barak, charging into the valley. But Reuben? Man, y'all hesitated!'

16.text: 'Why y'all still chillin' by the sheep pens, listening to the shepherds play their flutes? Reuben was over there debating when the fight was already on!'

17.text: 'Gilead stayed put on the other side of the Jordan. And Dan? Still out at sea. Asher was relaxing on the coast, posted up by the shores.'

18.text: 'But Zebulun? Naphtali? They put their lives on the line in the heat of battle.'

19.text: 'The kings of Canaan pulled up, fought hard at Taanach, by Megiddo's waters. But guess what? They ain't win nothing—not even silver for their trouble!'

20.text: 'Even the stars up in the sky fought against Sisera, working against him from the heavens!'

21.text: 'The Kishon River swept them away—that old, mighty river, Kishon. March on, my soul, with strength!'

22.text: 'Then the enemy's horses were galloping, their mighty steeds pounding the ground in retreat.'

23.text: 'Curse Meroz!' said the angel of the Lord. 'Curse the people there bad, 'cause they ain't come help the Lord fight the strong ones!'

24.text: 'Most blessed among women is Jael, the wife of Heber the Kenite—blessed among all the tent-dwelling women!'

25.text: 'Sisera asked her for water, but she gave him milk. She brought it in a royal cup, playing the part so smooth.'

26.text: 'Then she grabbed that tent peg with one hand, the workman's hammer in the other. She crushed his skull, smashed his temple, drove that peg straight through!'

27.text: 'At her feet, he sank down. He fell. He lay still. At her feet, he sank, he fell. Right where he dropped, that's where he died.'

28.text: 'Meanwhile, Sisera's mama was looking out the window, crying through the curtains: 'Why is his chariot taking so long? Why don't I hear his horses coming?''

29.text: 'Her ladies tried to reassure her, and even she told herself: '

30.text: 'Oh, they must be dividing the spoils! Each soldier getting a woman or two. Sisera getting embroidered cloth, fancy dyed garments, rich robes for the victor!'

31.text: 'But Lord, let all Your enemies perish like that! And let those who love You shine bright like the sun at full strength!'

32.text: And just like that, the land had peace for forty years.

1.text: Once again, Israel started acting up, doing evil in the Lord's sight. So the Lord let the Midianites run them for seven years.

2.text: Midian had them so shook that the Israelites started hiding out in caves, mountains, and strongholds just to stay safe.

3.text: Every time Israel planted crops, the Midianites, Amalekites, and other eastern tribes would roll up on them.

4.text: They'd camp out, wreck the fields all the way to Gaza, and leave Israel with nothing—no food, no sheep, no oxen, no donkeys.

5.text: Midian and their crew came in like locusts, deep with camels and everything. It was so many of them, they basically overran the land just to destroy it.

6.text: Israel was struggling hard because of Midian, so they finally cried out to the Lord for help.

7.text: When Israel called out to God about Midian, He sent a prophet to check them.

8.text: The prophet told them, 'This what the Lord, the God of Israel, says: I brought y'all up out of Egypt, out of slavery.'

9.text: 'I saved y'all from the Egyptians and everybody else who was messing with you. I drove them out and gave y'all their land.'

10.text: 'I told y'all, "I am the Lord your God. Don't be out here fearing these Amorite gods in whose land you living now." But what did y'all do? You ain't listen.'

11.text: One day, the Angel of the Lord pulled up and sat under the terebinth tree in Ophrah, where Joash the Abiezrite lived. His son Gideon was hiding in a winepress, trying to thresh wheat so the Midianites wouldn't catch him.

12.text: Then the Angel of the Lord appeared to him and said, 'The Lord is with you, mighty warrior!'

13.text: Gideon was like, 'Man, if the Lord is really with us, then why is all this happening? Where are all the miracles our ancestors told us about—how He brought them out of Egypt? Right now, it just feel like He left us hanging, handing us over to Midian.'

14.text: The Lord looked at him and said, 'Go with the strength you got and save Israel from the Midianites. Didn't I send you?'

15.text: But Gideon was like, 'Lord, how am I supposed to save Israel? My family is the weakest in Manasseh, and I'm the least important in my whole house!'

16.text: The Lord said, 'I'll be with you. And trust me, you gon' take Midian down like they just one man.'

17.text: Gideon said, 'Alright then, if I really got favor with You, prove it—give me a sign that it's really You talking to me.'

18.text: 'Hold on right here till I come back with an offering.' And the Lord was like, 'Aight, I'll wait.'

19.text: Gideon ran inside, prepped a young goat and some unleavened bread with an ephah of flour. He put the meat in a basket, the broth in a pot, and brought it back under the tree.

20.text: The Angel of God said, 'Put the meat and bread on this rock and pour out the broth.' So Gideon did it.

21.text: Then the Angel of the Lord touched the food with His staff—BOOM—fire shot up from the rock and burned it all up. And just like that, the Angel disappeared.

22.text: That's when Gideon realized, 'Oh snap! That was really the Angel of the Lord!' He panicked and said, 'Lord God, I done seen the Angel of the Lord face to face!'

23.text: But the Lord said, 'Calm down. Peace be with you. You ain't gon' die.'

24.text: So Gideon built an altar there and called it The Lord is Peace. And that altar still standing in Ophrah of the Abiezrites.

25.text: That night, the Lord told Gideon, 'Take your daddy's bull, the second one that's seven years old. Tear down your father's altar to Baal, and cut down the Asherah pole next to it.'

26.text: 'Then build an altar to the Lord your God on top of this rock in the right way. Use the wood from the Asherah pole to burn the bull as a sacrifice.'

27.text: Gideon grabbed ten of his servants and did what the Lord said. But he was too scared of his family and the city folks to do it in broad daylight, so he did it at night.

28.text: Next morning, the town woke up and saw Baal's altar destroyed, the Asherah pole chopped down, and the bull burning on a new altar.

29.text: They started asking around, 'Who did this?' After some investigation, they found out it was Gideon, son of Joash.

30.text: The men of the city went to Joash and said, 'Bring your son out here! He gotta die for tearing down Baal's altar and cutting down that Asherah pole!'

31.text: But Joash clapped back, 'Y'all really out here fighting for Baal? Y'all need to save him? If Baal is really a god, let him handle his own business! If anybody wanna fight for Baal, they better be dead by morning!'

32.text: That day, they started calling Gideon Jerubbaal, meaning 'Let Baal handle him,' since he tore down Baal's altar.

33.text: Not long after, the Midianites, Amalekites, and the other eastern people grouped up, crossed over, and set up camp in the Valley of Jezreel.

34.text: Then the Spirit of the Lord took over Gideon. He blew the trumpet, calling his clan, the Abiezrites, to follow him.

35.text: He also sent messengers to the tribes of Manasseh, Asher, Zebulun, and Naphtali, and they all came to join him.

36.text: Gideon said to God, 'If You really gonna use me to save Israel like You said…'

37.text: 'I'ma put this fleece of wool out on the ground. If in the morning the fleece is wet but the ground is dry, then I'll know You really got me on this.'

38.text: And sure enough, the next morning, Gideon wrung out a bowlful of water from the fleece while the ground stayed dry.

39.text: But Gideon wasn't done. 'Lord, don't be mad at me, but let me check one more time. This time, let the fleece stay dry, but the ground be covered in dew.'

40.text: That night, God did exactly that—fleece was bone dry, but the whole ground was soaked.

1.text: Early in the morning, Jerubbaal (a.k.a. Gideon) and his crew camped near the well of Harod. Meanwhile, the Midianites were posted up north of them in the valley by the hill of Moreh.

2.text: Then the Lord told Gideon, 'Bruh, you got too many people with you. If y'all win like this, Israel gon' start acting like they did it all on their own and not give Me the credit.'

3.text: 'So go tell 'em: If anybody scared, they can go home right now.' And just like that, 22,000 of them dipped. Only 10,000 stayed.

4.text: But the Lord said, 'Still too many. Take them down to the water—I'ma test them for you there. I'll tell you who stays and who goes.'

5.text: So Gideon brought them to the water, and the Lord said, 'Separate the ones who scoop water with their hands and lap it up like a dog from the ones who kneel to drink.'

6.text: Only 300 men drank from their hands. The rest kneeled to drink straight from the stream.

7.text: Then the Lord said, 'Aight, these 300 right here? They the ones. I'ma hand Midian over to you through them. Send everybody else home.'

8.text: So the 300 stayed, taking supplies and trumpets, while the rest went home. Meanwhile, the Midianites were still camped out below in the valley.

9.text: That same night, the Lord told Gideon, 'Get up, go attack the camp—I already gave them to you.'

10.text: 'But if you nervous, take your boy Purah and go eavesdrop on them first.'

11.text: 'Listen to what they saying, and I promise it'll hype you up for battle.' So Gideon and Purah snuck down near the enemy's outpost.

12.text: Midianites, Amalekites, and all the eastern people were deep in that valley, as thick as locusts. Their camels alone were countless, like the sand on the seashore.

13.text: As Gideon got closer, he heard one soldier telling his homie a dream: 'Man, I had this wild dream—a barley loaf rolled into our camp, hit a tent, flipped it over, and the whole thing collapsed!'

14.text: His friend was like, 'Oh snap, that's gotta mean Gideon, son of Joash, is about to take us down. God already gave Midian to him!'

15.text: When Gideon heard that, he bowed in worship. Then he ran back to camp and said, 'Get up! The Lord already handed Midian over to us!'

16.text: Gideon split his 300 men into three groups. He gave each of them a trumpet, an empty jar, and a torch hidden inside the jar.

17.text: He told them, 'Watch me. Do exactly what I do. When we get to the edge of the camp, follow my lead.'

18.text: 'When I blow my trumpet, all of y'all blow yours too and shout, "The sword of the Lord and of Gideon!"'

19.text: So Gideon and 100 of his men rolled up to the enemy camp just as the night guards were changing shifts.

20.text: All three groups blew their trumpets, smashed their jars, grabbed their torches, and yelled, 'The sword of the Lord and of Gideon!'

21.text: Nobody moved—just stood their ground while the enemy camp went into full panic mode, running around screaming.

22.text: Then when the 300 blew their trumpets, the Lord made the enemy turn on each other with their own swords. They started fighting themselves and ran toward Beth Acacia, Zererah, and as far as the border of Abel Meholah near Tabbath.

23.text: Meanwhile, men from Naphtali, Asher, and Manasseh gathered up and chased Midian down.

24.text: Gideon sent messengers to the Ephraimites, telling them, 'Come through and cut off the Midianites at the Jordan and Beth Barah!'

25.text: So the men of Ephraim caught up, blocked them off, and captured Midian's two princes, Oreb and Zeeb. They killed Oreb at the Rock of Oreb, and Zeeb at the Winepress of Zeeb. And just to make sure Gideon knew, they brought him the heads of Oreb and Zeeb across the Jordan.

1.text: Then the men of Ephraim came at Gideon like, 'Bruh, why you ain't call us when you went to fight Midian? You just left us out like that?' They was heated.

2.text: Gideon hit 'em back like, 'Chill, y'all did more than me! Ain't Ephraim's leftovers better than all of Abiezer's best?'

3.text: 'Y'all the ones who took down Oreb and Zeeb, the Midianite princes. What I did don't even compare to that!' And just like that, they calmed down.

4.text: Gideon and his 300 men crossed the Jordan, exhausted but still chasing Midian.

5.text: They got to Succoth, and Gideon was like, 'Yo, can y'all give my people some bread? We tired, but we still hunting Zebah and Zalmunna, Midian's kings.'

6.text: The leaders of Succoth were like, 'You ain't caught 'em yet, so why should we help?'

7.text: Gideon snapped back, 'Aight bet—when I do catch 'em, I'ma come back and tear y'all up with desert thorns and briers!'

8.text: Then he went to Penuel and asked the same thing, but they disrespected him too.

9.text: So he told them, 'When I come back in peace, I'ma tear this whole tower down!'

10.text: Meanwhile, Zebah and Zalmunna were chillin' in Karkor with about 15,000 men—only ones left from an army that started at 120,000.

11.text: Gideon pulled up through a back route, sneaking up from the east, past Nobah and Jogbehah. The enemy wasn't even ready for it.

12.text: Zebah and Zalmunna tried to run, but Gideon chased 'em down, captured them, and wrecked the rest of their army.

13.text: After the battle, Gideon came back through the Ascent of Heres.

14.text: He caught a young man from Succoth, made him write down the names of their 77 leaders.

15.text: Then he rolled up to Succoth and said, 'Remember when y'all clowned me, saying I ain't caught Zebah and Zalmunna? Well, here they go!'

16.text: Then he grabbed the city elders, got some thorns and briers, and taught them a painful lesson.

17.text: Then he went to Penuel, tore down their tower like he promised, and killed the men of the city.

18.text: Then he asked Zebah and Zalmunna, 'The men y'all killed at Tabor, what did they look like?'

19.text: They said, 'Man, they looked like you—like sons of a king.'

20.text: Gideon was like, 'Yeah, 'cause they was my brothers. If y'all had spared them, I wouldn't be killing you now.' Then he told his son Jether, 'Go ahead, take 'em out!'

21.text: But Jether hesitated—he was young and too scared to do it. So Zebah and Zalmunna said, 'Man, if you really bout it, do it yourself!' So Gideon handled it and took the royal ornaments off their camels' necks.

22.text: After all that, Israel came to Gideon like, 'You the man! Rule over us—you, your son, and your grandson. You saved us from Midian!'

23.text: But Gideon was like, 'Nah, I ain't ruling over y'all, and neither will my son. The Lord is your ruler.'

24.text: 'But I do got one request—everybody drop one gold earring from the loot y'all took.' (The Midianites wore gold earrings 'cause they were Ishmaelites.)

25.text: They said, 'Bet, we got you!' and spread out a cloth, throwing in their gold earrings.

26.text: Altogether, Gideon got 1,700 shekels of gold—not counting the royal chains, pendants, and purple robes from Midian's kings, plus the gold chains from their camels.

27.text: Gideon took all that gold and made an ephod, setting it up in his hometown, Ophrah. But Israel started worshipping it, and it became a trap for Gideon and his fam.

28.text: Still, Midian got humbled. They never rose up again, and Israel had peace for 40 years while Gideon was alive.

29.text: After all that, Gideon (Jerubbaal) went back home.

30.text: Bruh had 70 sons—dude had a lot of wives.

31.text: He even had a side chick in Shechem who gave him a son named Abimelech.

32.text: Eventually, Gideon died of old age and was buried in his father Joash's tomb in Ophrah.

33.text: But the second Gideon was gone, Israel started acting up again—going right back to worshipping Baal and making Baal-Berith their god.

34.text: They straight up forgot about the Lord, the One who saved them from all their enemies.

35.text: And they ain't even show love to Gideon's family, despite all the good he did for them.

1.text: Abimelech, Gideon's son, rolled up to Shechem, went to his uncles and his mama's family, and said,

2.text: 'Y'all gotta decide—what's better? Having all seventy of Gideon's sons ruling over you, or just one? And don't forget, I'm your own flesh and blood!'

3.text: His uncles spread the word, hyping him up to the men of Shechem, and they were like, 'Yeah, he our brother. Let's roll with him.'

4.text: So they gave him seventy shekels of silver from Baal-Berith's temple, and he used that money to hire a crew of wild, reckless dudes to follow him.

5.text: Then he went to his daddy's house in Ophrah and killed all seventy of his brothers on one stone. But the youngest, Jotham, managed to hide and escape.

6.text: The men of Shechem and Beth Millo got together and crowned Abimelech king by the big tree near the pillar in Shechem.

7.text: When Jotham heard what happened, he climbed up Mount Gerizim and yelled, 'Listen up, men of Shechem! If y'all hear me, maybe God will hear y'all too!'

8.text: 'One day, the trees wanted a king. They went to the olive tree and said, "Rule over us!"'

9.text: 'But the olive tree said, "Why would I stop making oil that honors God and people just to wave around over some trees?"'

10.text: 'Then they went to the fig tree, saying, "Come be our king!"'

11.text: 'But the fig tree said, "Why would I stop making sweet fruit just to rule over y'all?"'

12.text: 'Next, they asked the grapevine, "Come be our king!"'

13.text: 'The vine said, "Why would I stop making wine that brings joy to God and people just to wave over y'all?"'

14.text: 'Finally, they went to the bramble bush and said, "You come and rule over us!"'

15.text: 'The bramble said, "If y'all really want me as king, then come sit in my shade. But if not, may fire come from me and burn down the mighty cedars of Lebanon!"'

16.text: 'So if y'all really did right by Gideon's family when y'all made Abimelech king, then cool, enjoy him.'

17.text: 'But don't forget—my father fought for y'all, risked his life, and saved y'all from Midian.'

18.text: 'And this how y'all repay him? Killing his seventy sons and putting this dude, the son of a servant woman, in charge just 'cause he's your kin?'

19.text: 'If y'all did right by Gideon, cool. But if not, may fire come from Abimelech and burn y'all up, and may fire come from y'all and burn him up!'

20.text: 'Y'all gon' destroy each other!'

21.text: Then Jotham took off running, dipped to Beer, and stayed low 'cause he knew Abimelech was coming for him.

22.text: Abimelech ruled over Israel for three years.

23.text: But then, God sent bad blood between Abimelech and the men of Shechem, and they turned on him.

24.text: This was God paying them back for what they did to Gideon's seventy sons. Both Abimelech and the Shechemites had blood on their hands.

25.text: Shechem's people started setting up ambushes in the hills, robbing everybody passing through. Somebody told Abimelech what was going on.

26.text: Then a dude named Gaal, son of Ebed, rolled into Shechem with his brothers, and the people started rocking with him instead.

27.text: They went to their vineyards, crushed grapes, made wine, got lit, and started talking crazy about Abimelech at their false god's temple.

28.text: Gaal started popping off: 'Who is Abimelech, and why should we serve him? Ain't he just Gideon's son? And ain't Zebul just his officer? We should be serving the real leaders of Shechem's past!'

29.text: 'Man, if I was in charge, I'd handle Abimelech real quick!' Then he said, 'Come on, Abimelech! Bring your army and let's settle this!'

30.text: Zebul, the city's governor, heard Gaal running his mouth and got mad.

31.text: He secretly sent messengers to Abimelech, saying, 'Yo, Gaal and his people are hyping the city against you!'

32.text: 'You better move tonight, take your soldiers, and ambush the city.'

33.text: 'At sunrise, rush in and handle business when Gaal and his people step out.'

34.text: So Abimelech and his troops set up at night, lying in wait in four groups outside Shechem.

35.text: Early in the morning, Gaal walked to the city gates, and Abimelech's troops popped up out of nowhere.

36.text: Gaal saw them and told Zebul, 'Yo, look! People coming down from the mountains!'

37.text: Gaal looked again: 'Nah, I'm telling you, people are coming down from the middle of the land! And another squad is rolling up from the Diviner's Tree!'

38.text: Zebul hit him back: 'Where's all that big talk now? You was talking reckless about Abimelech—now go fight him!'

39.text: So Gaal led Shechem's men out to fight Abimelech.

40.text: Abimelech chased him down, and Gaal's men got wrecked all the way back to the city gates.

41.text: Abimelech stayed at Arumah while Zebul kicked Gaal and his brothers out of Shechem.

42.text: Next day, Shechem's people went out to the fields, and somebody told Abimelech.

43.text: He set another ambush, split his men into three groups, and attacked when they came out.

44.text: Abimelech and his squad stormed the city gates while the other two squads hit everyone still in the fields.

45.text: He fought Shechem all day, took the city, killed everyone inside, tore it down, and scattered salt all over it.

46.text: When the people in Shechem's tower heard what happened, they ran to the temple of their false god, Berith.

47.text: But Abimelech found out they were hiding there.

48.text: He and his troops went to Mount Zalmon. Abimelech chopped a tree branch, put it on his shoulder, and said, 'Y'all see what I just did? Do the same thing!'

49.text: So everybody grabbed branches, stacked them around the temple, and set it on fire. About a thousand men and women burned alive.

50.text: Then Abimelech went to Thebez, took over the city.

51.text: But the people ran into a strong tower, locked themselves in, and climbed to the roof.

52.text: Abimelech rushed the tower and was about to set it on fire.

53.text: But a random woman dropped a millstone on his head and cracked his skull!

54.text: Abimelech, not wanting to die by a woman's hand, told his armor-bearer, 'Run me through with your sword! I can't go out like this!' So the young man killed him.

55.text: When the Israelites saw Abimelech was dead, they all went home.

56.text: That's how God paid back Abimelech for killing his seventy brothers.

57.text: And all the evil Shechem did came back on them too. Everything played out just like Jotham said.

1.text: After Abimelech, a man named Tola, son of Puah, grandson of Dodo, from the tribe of Issachar, stepped up to save Israel. He lived in Shamir, up in the hills of Ephraim.

2.text: Tola judged Israel for 23 years. Then he died and was buried in Shamir.

3.text: After Tola, a man named Jair, a Gileadite, became judge over Israel. He led for 22 years.

4.text: Jair had thirty sons, and they was out here riding thirty donkeys. Each one of them had their own town, which they called 'Havoth Jair'—the Villages of Jair. That name still sticks to this day in Gilead.

5.text: Then Jair died and was buried in Camon.

6.text: But, like clockwork, Israel started wildin' again—doing evil in the Lord's sight. They was out here serving every god they could find: Baal, Ashtoreth, the gods of Syria, Sidon, Moab, Ammon, and the Philistines. Straight up forgot about the Lord.

7.text: So the Lord got fed up and let the Philistines and the Ammonites run all over them.

8.text: For 18 years, these enemies harassed and oppressed Israel, especially the folks living in Gilead, the land of the Amorites.

9.text: Then the Ammonites got even bolder and crossed the Jordan, bringing the fight to Judah, Benjamin, and Ephraim. Israel was struggling heavy.

10.text: Finally, Israel cried out to the Lord, saying, 'We messed up, Lord! We abandoned You and started serving these fake gods!'

11.text: But the Lord hit them back with, 'Didn't I save y'all before? I pulled y'all out of Egypt, rescued you from the Amorites, the Ammonites, and the Philistines.'

12.text: 'I saved y'all from the Sidonians, the Amalekites, and the Maonites when they oppressed you. Every time y'all cried out, I came through.'

13.text: 'But y'all keep ditching Me for these other gods. So nah, I ain't saving y'all no more.'

14.text: 'Matter fact, go cry to them gods y'all love so much. Let's see if they pull up for you when you in trouble.'

15.text: But Israel pleaded, 'Lord, we messed up! Do whatever You gotta do to us, but please, just save us today!'

16.text: So they threw out all their fake gods and started serving the Lord again. And God—seeing how much they was suffering—couldn't ignore their misery no more.

17.text: Meanwhile, the Ammonites gathered their army and camped in Gilead. Israel's people came together too, setting up camp in Mizpah.

18.text: Then the leaders of Gilead started talking: 'Who gon' be the one to lead us against the Ammonites? Whoever steps up first gon' be the ruler over all of Gilead.'

1.text: Jephthah, the Gileadite, was a straight-up warrior, but his mom was a prostitute. His father, Gilead, had him outside of marriage.

2.text: When Gilead's legit sons grew up, they told Jephthah, 'Bruh, you ain't getting nothing from this family. You the son of another woman—get out.'

3.text: So Jephthah left and went to live in the land of Tob. While he was there, a bunch of reckless dudes linked up with him, and they started rolling together like a gang.

4.text: Some time passed, and the Ammonites started beefing with Israel again.

5.text: When war broke out, the elders of Gilead went looking for Jephthah in Tob.

6.text: They said, 'Come be our commander so we can fight the Ammonites!'

7.text: But Jephthah was like, 'Oh now y'all need me? Ain't y'all the same ones that kicked me out my daddy's house? Now y'all in trouble and suddenly I'm important?'

8.text: The elders were like, 'Yeah… that's why we came back to you. Lead us in battle, and you can be the head over all of Gilead.'

9.text: Jephthah said, 'So if I come back, lead the fight, and God gives me the victory, y'all really gon' make me the ruler?'

10.text: They swore on it, saying, 'The Lord is our witness—we'll do exactly what we said.'

11.text: So Jephthah went with them, and the people made him their leader. Then Jephthah made it official before the Lord in Mizpah.

12.text: Jephthah sent messengers to the king of Ammon, asking, 'Yo, why you pulling up on my land trying to fight me?'

13.text: The Ammonite king responded, 'Y'all took our land when you came from Egypt—from the Arnon to the Jabbok and over to the Jordan. Give it back peacefully, and we won't have a problem.'

14.text: Jephthah sent another message, saying,

15.text: 'Israel never took Moab's land or Ammon's land.'

16.text: 'When Israel left Egypt, they wandered the wilderness, passed through the Red Sea, and came to Kadesh.'

17.text: 'They asked Edom's king, "Can we pass through your land?" but he said no. They asked Moab's king, same thing—no entry. So they had to stay put in Kadesh.'

18.text: 'Then they went around Edom and Moab and camped near the Arnon River, but never crossed into Moab's land.'

19.text: 'Then they asked Sihon, king of the Amorites, "Let us pass through your land to get where we going."'

20.text: 'But Sihon wasn't having it. Instead, he came at Israel with his whole army, ready to fight.'

21.text: 'But the Lord handed Sihon and his people over to Israel, and we took all their land.'

22.text: 'From the Arnon to the Jabbok, from the wilderness to the Jordan—it all became ours.'

23.text: 'So if God took this land from the Amorites and gave it to us, why should we give it to you?'

24.text: 'Y'all keep what your god Chemosh gives you, and we gon' keep what our God gives us.'

25.text: 'Are you better than Balak, Moab's king? He never picked a fight with Israel.'

26.text: 'Israel been living in Heshbon, Aroer, and along the Arnon for 300 years—why y'all just now trying to claim it?'

27.text: 'I ain't the one in the wrong. You are. So let the Lord judge between us today!'

28.text: But the Ammonite king ignored Jephthah's message.

29.text: Then the Spirit of the Lord came on Jephthah. He traveled through Gilead and Manasseh, then passed through Mizpah on his way to fight Ammon.

30.text: Before the battle, Jephthah made a vow to the Lord: 'If You let me win, Lord…'

31.text: 'Whatever comes out my house first when I get back, I'ma give it to You as a burnt offering.'

32.text: Jephthah led his army against the Ammonites, and the Lord gave him the victory.

33.text: He wiped them out from Aroer to Minnith—twenty cities—reaching Abel Keramim. It was a brutal defeat, and Ammon fell under Israel.

34.text: But when Jephthah came home to Mizpah, his only child—his daughter—ran out to greet him with tambourines, dancing.

35.text: When he saw her, he tore his clothes and cried out, 'Nooo! My daughter! You just broke me down! I made a vow to the Lord, and I can't take it back!'

36.text: She told him, 'Daddy, if you made a vow to the Lord, you gotta keep it—since He gave you the victory over your enemies.'

37.text: 'But let me have two months to go into the mountains with my friends and mourn the fact that I'll never have a husband or kids.'

38.text: Jephthah agreed. 'Go ahead.' So she and her friends spent two months mourning in the mountains.

39.text: After that, she came back, and Jephthah fulfilled his vow. She never married or had children.

40.text: From then on, the daughters of Israel set aside four days each year to remember Jephthah's daughter.

1.text: The men of Ephraim got together, crossed over to Zaphon, and came at Jephthah like, 'Bruh, why you go fight Ammon without us? You ain't call us? We 'bout to burn your house down with you in it!'
