2.text: Jephthah clapped back, 'Look, me and my people was struggling against Ammon. I did call y'all, but y'all ain't come help.'

3.text: 'So when I saw y'all wasn't coming, I risked my own life, went to fight Ammon, and the Lord gave me the W. So why y'all pulling up on me now?'

4.text: Then Jephthah and his Gileadite soldiers went to war against Ephraim and beat them, 'cause Ephraim was talking reckless, saying, 'Y'all Gileadites are just Ephraimite runaways—y'all ain't real.'

5.text: After the battle, the Gileadites took control of the Jordan River crossings. Anytime an Ephraimite tried to escape and said, 'Let me cross over,' the Gileadites would ask, 'You an Ephraimite?'

6.text: If the person said no, they'd make him say, 'Shibboleth.' If he couldn't pronounce it right and said, 'Sibboleth,' they knew he was lying and would take him out right there. 42,000 Ephraimites died that day.

7.text: Jephthah judged Israel for six years. Then he died and was buried somewhere in Gilead.

8.text: After Jephthah, Ibzan from Bethlehem took over as judge.

9.text: This dude had thirty sons, gave away thirty daughters in marriage, and brought in thirty daughters for his sons. He judged Israel for seven years.

10.text: Then Ibzan died and was buried in Bethlehem.

11.text: Next up was Elon from the tribe of Zebulun. He judged Israel for ten years.

12.text: Then Elon died and was buried in Aijalon, in the land of Zebulun.

13.text: After him came Abdon, son of Hillel, from Pirathon.

14.text: He had forty sons and thirty grandsons, and all of them rode around on seventy donkeys. He judged Israel for eight years.

15.text: Then Abdon died and was buried in Pirathon, in Ephraim, in the hill country where the Amalekites used to be.

1.text: Once again, Israel started acting up, doing evil in the Lord's sight. So the Lord let the Philistines run them for forty years.

2.text: There was this man from Zorah, from the tribe of Dan, named Manoah. His wife couldn't have kids.

3.text: Then the Angel of the Lord pulled up and told her, 'Look, I know you ain't been able to have kids, but you 'bout to have a son.'

4.text: 'So listen up—don't drink no wine, don't touch strong drinks, and don't eat anything unclean.'

5.text: 'This baby gon' be special. No razor should ever touch his head, 'cause he's gonna be dedicated to God as a Nazirite from birth. And he's the one that's gonna start rescuing Israel from the Philistines.'

6.text: The woman ran and told her husband, 'A Man of God came to me! He looked like an angel—real powerful. I ain't ask where He came from, and He ain't tell me His name.'

7.text: 'But He told me, "You gon' have a son. Don't drink wine, don't eat nothing unclean, 'cause this child is dedicated to God from the womb until he dies."'

8.text: Then Manoah prayed, 'Lord, please send that Man of God back so we can know exactly how to raise this child.'

9.text: God heard him, and the Angel of the Lord showed up again while his wife was out in the field. But Manoah wasn't with her.

10.text: She ran back, found her husband, and said, 'He's back! The Man who talked to me the other day just appeared again!'

11.text: Manoah followed her, came up to the Man, and asked, 'Are you the one who spoke to my wife?' And He said, 'I am.'

12.text: Manoah said, 'Alright then, let everything You said happen! But tell us—how we supposed to raise this boy? What's his purpose?'

13.text: The Angel of the Lord said, 'She gotta follow everything I told her.'

14.text: 'No wine, no strong drinks, nothing unclean—she gotta stick to all My instructions.'

15.text: Then Manoah said, 'Please, stay for a while. Let us prepare a young goat for You.'

16.text: But the Angel of the Lord said, 'Even if I stay, I ain't eating your food. But if you want to make an offering, give it to the Lord.' (Manoah still ain't realize this was the Angel of the Lord.)

17.text: Then Manoah asked, 'What's Your name? That way, when everything You said comes true, we can honor You.'

18.text: But the Angel of the Lord said, 'Why you asking My name? It's beyond understanding—it's wonderful.'

19.text: So Manoah took a young goat and a grain offering, sacrificed it on a rock to the Lord. And while they were watching, something amazing happened.

20.text: As the flames rose up to heaven, the Angel of the Lord went up in the fire! When Manoah and his wife saw it, they fell flat on their faces.

21.text: After that, the Angel of the Lord disappeared. That's when Manoah realized, 'Oh snap, that was the Angel of the Lord for real!'

22.text: Then he freaked out, telling his wife, 'We 'bout to die! We just saw God!'

23.text: But his wife was calm and said, 'If the Lord wanted us dead, He wouldn't have accepted our offering. He wouldn't have shown us all this or told us what's about to happen.'

24.text: Then she gave birth to a son and named him Samson. The boy grew up, and the Lord blessed him.

25.text: And the Spirit of the Lord started working in him while he was at Mahaneh Dan, between Zorah and Eshtaol.

1.text: One day, Samson went down to Timnah and saw a Philistine woman that caught his eye.

2.text: He came back home and told his parents, 'I saw this fine woman in Timnah—one of the Philistine girls. Go ahead and set that up for me as my wife.'

3.text: His parents were like, 'Hold up, ain't there no woman from our own people you can marry? Why you gotta go after one of these uncircumcised Philistines?' But Samson was like, 'Nah, she the one I want. Go get her for me.'

4.text: What his parents ain't know was that the Lord was behind this, setting things up to bring trouble to the Philistines—since they were still running Israel at the time.

5.text: So Samson and his folks headed down to Timnah. Along the way, near the vineyards, a young lion jumped out at him, roaring.

6.text: But the Spirit of the Lord hit Samson with crazy strength, and he tore that lion apart with his bare hands—like it was nothing! He ain't even have a weapon. But he ain't tell his parents what happened.

7.text: After that, he went to talk with the Philistine woman, and yeah—he was feeling her heavy.

8.text: Later on, when he came back to get her, he decided to check out the lion's carcass. And what did he see? A whole beehive inside, with honey dripping.

9.text: He scooped some up and ate it on the way. When he got to his parents, he gave them some too, but he ain't tell them where it came from.

10.text: His father went ahead and arranged the marriage. Samson threw a feast, like young men usually did in those days.

11.text: When the Philistines saw Samson, they brought thirty men to hang with him—basically like wedding guests.

12.text: Then Samson told them, 'Aight, let's make this fun. I got a riddle for y'all. If you can solve it in the seven days of the feast, I'll give y'all thirty linen garments and thirty fresh outfits.'

13.text: 'But if y'all can't solve it, y'all gotta give me thirty linen garments and thirty changes of clothes.' They were like, 'Aight, bet. Hit us with the riddle.'

14.text: So Samson said, 'Out of the eater came something to eat, And out of the strong came something sweet.' But for three days, they was stuck—they had no clue what the answer was.

15.text: By the seventh day, they was getting mad. So they went to Samson's wife and told her, 'You better get your husband to tell you the answer, or we burning you and your daddy's house down! You brought us here just to rob us?'

16.text: So Samson's wife started crying on him, saying, 'You don't love me! You hate me! You made this riddle for my people, but you ain't even tell me the answer!' But Samson was like, 'Girl, I ain't even tell my parents! Why would I tell you?'

17.text: But she kept crying. The whole feast, she was pressing him. By the seventh day, he gave in and told her. And of course, she ran straight to her people with the answer.

18.text: So before the sun went down, the Philistine men came to Samson and said, 'What is sweeter than honey? And what is stronger than a lion?' And Samson was heated. He snapped back, 'If y'all ain't been messing with my wife, Y'all wouldn't have solved my riddle!'

19.text: The Spirit of the Lord came on Samson again, and he went down to Ashkelon, killed thirty Philistine men, took their clothes, and gave them to the men who solved the riddle. But he was still mad, so he stormed off back to his father's house.

20.text: And while he was gone, Samson's wife was given to his best man instead!

1.text: Sometime later, during the wheat harvest, Samson pulled up to see his wife, bringing a young goat as a gift. He was like, 'Aight, let me go see my wife in her room.' But her dad blocked the door.

2.text: Her father said, 'Look, I really thought you was done with her, so I gave her to your boy. But hey, ain't her younger sister even finer? Take her instead.'

3.text: Samson was heated. He said, 'Aight, this time, when I get back at the Philistines, y'all can't blame me!'

4.text: So Samson caught 300 foxes, tied them together in pairs by their tails, and strapped torches between them.

5.text: Then he lit the torches and let the foxes loose in the Philistine fields, burning up all their grain, vineyards, and olive groves.

6.text: The Philistines were like, 'Who did this?!' And somebody told them, 'It was Samson, that Timnite's son-in-law, 'cause his father-in-law gave his wife to another dude.' So the Philistines came through and burned both Samson's wife and her father alive.

7.text: Samson snapped, 'Oh, y'all wanna play like that? Aight, bet—I will get my revenge, and after that, I'm done.'

8.text: Then he ran through them, wrecking everybody, taking them down left and right. After that, he dipped to a cave in the rock of Etam.

9.text: The Philistines rolled up, set up camp in Judah, and prepared to take over Lehi.

10.text: The men of Judah asked, 'Yo, why y'all here?' The Philistines said, 'We came to arrest Samson and do to him what he did to us.'

11.text: So 3,000 men from Judah went to Samson's hideout in the cave and said, 'Bruh, you know the Philistines run this place! Why you bringing trouble on us?!' Samson said, 'Man, I just did to them what they did to me.'

12.text: They told him, 'Look, we gotta turn you in to them.' Samson said, 'Fine, but swear to me that y'all won't kill me yourselves.'

13.text: They promised, 'Nah, we just tying you up and handing you over—we ain't gon' kill you.' So they tied him up with two fresh ropes and led him out.

14.text: As soon as they brought Samson to Lehi, the Philistines saw him and started shouting like they already won. But the Spirit of the Lord hit Samson with power—the ropes around his arms snapped like burnt thread, and his hands broke free like nothing.

15.text: He looked around, grabbed a fresh donkey's jawbone, and went crazy—took out a thousand men with it.

16.text: Then Samson said, 'With a donkey's jawbone, I stacked 'em in heaps, With a donkey's jawbone, I just took out a thousand men!'

17.text: After he finished, he tossed the jawbone and called that spot Ramath Lehi (which means 'Jawbone Hill').

18.text: After all that, Samson was mad thirsty, so he prayed, 'Lord, You just gave me this big victory, and now I'm 'bout to die of thirst and get caught by these uncircumcised dudes?'

19.text: So God made water flow from a hollow place in Lehi. Samson drank, got his strength back, and felt revived. That place was called En Hakkore ('Spring of the Caller'), and the name stuck.

20.text: And Samson judged Israel for twenty years while the Philistines were still in charge.

1.text: Samson went down to Gaza, saw a prostitute, and spent the night with her.

2.text: When the people of Gaza found out, they were like, 'Oh, Samson in town? Bet. We gon' wait for him all night, and when the morning comes, we gon' kill him.'

3.text: But Samson laid low until midnight. Then he got up, grabbed the city gate doors—posts, bars, and all—ripped them out the ground, threw them on his shoulders, and carried them all the way to the top of a hill near Hebron.

4.text: Sometime later, Samson fell for a woman in the Valley of Sorek named Delilah.

5.text: The Philistine leaders came to her and said, 'Find out what makes him so strong and how we can take him down. We wanna tie him up and make him suffer. Each of us will give you 1,100 pieces of silver if you do it.'

6.text: So Delilah started working on him, saying, 'Baby, tell me the secret to your strength. How can someone tie you up and make you weak?'

7.text: Samson played with her and said, 'If they tie me up with seven fresh bowstrings that haven't dried, I'll be weak like any other man.'

8.text: So the Philistine leaders brought her the bowstrings, and she tied him up.

9.text: Then she had men hiding in the room, and she called out, 'Samson! The Philistines are here!' But he snapped those bowstrings like they was nothing, and they still ain't know his secret.

10.text: Delilah got mad and said, 'You lied to me! Tell me the real way to tie you up.'

11.text: Samson said, 'If they tie me with brand-new ropes that ain't never been used, then I'll be weak like anybody else.'

12.text: So Delilah tied him up with new ropes and called out, 'Samson! The Philistines are here!' But he broke the ropes like thread.

13.text: Delilah was real fed up now: 'You keep playing with me, Samson! Tell me the truth!' So Samson said, 'Alright, alright. If you weave the seven braids of my hair into a loom, I'll be weak.'

14.text: So she did it, pinned it down, and shouted, 'Samson! The Philistines are here!' But he woke up, pulled the pin out, and broke free again.

15.text: Delilah hit him with, 'How you gon' say you love me, but you keep lying?'

16.text: She kept nagging him day after day until he was fed up with her pressing him.

17.text: So he finally broke and told her everything: 'I've been dedicated to God since birth as a Nazirite. If my head ever gets shaved, I'll lose my strength and be weak like any other man.'

18.text: Delilah knew this time was real. She called the Philistine leaders and said, 'Come on, this time he told me everything!' And they came back with the silver in their hands.

19.text: She made him fall asleep on her lap, then called a man to shave off his seven braids. Then she started messing with him, and his strength was gone.

20.text: She yelled, 'Samson! The Philistines are here!' He woke up thinking, 'I'ma break free like before.' But he ain't know the Lord had left him.

21.text: The Philistines grabbed him, gouged out his eyes, dragged him to Gaza, and put him in prison, making him grind grain like a slave.

22.text: But while he was locked up, his hair started growing back…

23.text: One day, the Philistine rulers threw a big party to worship their god, Dagon. They were hyped, saying, 'Our god gave us victory over Samson!'

24.text: The people celebrated, saying, 'Samson, the one who wrecked our land and killed our people, is finally in our hands!'

25.text: When they got drunk, they said, 'Bring out Samson so he can entertain us!' So they pulled him out the prison and put him on display.

26.text: Samson said to the boy guiding him, 'Take me to the pillars holding up the temple so I can lean on them.'

27.text: The temple was packed—3,000 men and women, including all the Philistine rulers, were watching from the roof.

28.text: Samson prayed, 'Lord God, remember me. Please, just one more time—give me the strength to get revenge for my two eyes!'

29.text: He grabbed the two central pillars holding up the temple, put one hand on each, and braced himself.

30.text: Then he said, 'Let me die with these Philistines!' And he pushed with all his might. The whole temple came crashing down, killing everyone inside—including Samson. In that moment, he killed more Philistines in death than he ever did in life.

31.text: Later, his brothers and family came, took his body, and buried him between Zorah and Eshtaol, in his father Manoah's tomb. He had led Israel for twenty years.

1.text: There was this man named Micah, living up in the mountains of Ephraim.

2.text: One day, he told his mom, 'Remember them eleven hundred pieces of silver that got stolen from you? The ones you put a curse on—yeah, I took them.' But his mom ain't even mad. She said, 'May the Lord bless you, my son!'

3.text: So after he gave the money back, she said, 'I had dedicated this silver to the Lord for you—so we could make a carved idol and a molded statue. Now, I'm giving it back to you to make it happen.'

4.text: So Micah returned the money, and his mom took two hundred shekels, gave them to a silversmith, and had him make an idol. They put it in Micah's house.

5.text: Micah even built a little shrine, made an ephod (a priestly vest), and set up some household gods. Then he ordained one of his own sons to be his priest.

6.text: Back then, Israel ain't have no king—everybody was just doing whatever they thought was right.

7.text: Now there was a young Levite from Bethlehem in Judah, looking for a place to stay.

8.text: He left Bethlehem, just trying to find a spot where he could settle down. While traveling, he came to Micah's house in the mountains of Ephraim.

9.text: Micah asked him, 'Where you from?' And the young man said, 'I'm a Levite from Bethlehem, just out here looking for a place to stay.'

10.text: Micah said, 'Aight, stay with me. Be my priest and my spiritual leader. I'll hook you up with ten pieces of silver a year, a fresh set of clothes, and everything you need.'

11.text: The Levite agreed, moved in, and became like a son to Micah.

12.text: Micah then ordained him as his personal priest, and the Levite stayed in Micah's house.

13.text: Micah was hyped. He said, 'Now I know the Lord gon' bless me—I got a legit Levite as my priest!'

1.text: Back in those days, Israel ain't have no king, and the tribe of Dan was still out here looking for land to claim for themselves.

2.text: So the Danites sent five strong men from Zorah and Eshtaol to scout out a new spot. They told them, 'Go check out the land and report back.' As they traveled, they stopped at Micah's house in the mountains of Ephraim and stayed the night.

3.text: While they were there, they overheard the Levite priest talking and recognized his accent. So they asked, 'Yo, who brought you here? What you doing in this place?'

4.text: He told them, 'Oh, Micah hired me. I'm his personal priest now.'

5.text: So the men said, 'Aight, can you ask God if this trip gon' be a success?'

6.text: The priest told them, 'Yeah, y'all good. The Lord got you on this journey.'

7.text: So the five men went on to Laish. They saw that the people there were chill—living peaceful, like the Sidonians, without no rulers pressing them. Plus, they ain't have any strong allies to back them up.

8.text: When the spies got back to Zorah and Eshtaol, their people asked, 'So what's the word?'

9.text: They said, 'Man, we gotta move! This land is real nice. Why y'all just sitting here? Let's go take it!'

10.text: 'The people there ain't got no defenses, and the land is stacked with everything we could want. God already gave it to us!'

11.text: So 600 armed men from the tribe of Dan left from Zorah and Eshtaol, ready for war.

12.text: On the way, they camped at Kirjath Jearim in Judah, and that spot became known as Mahaneh Dan (which means 'Camp of Dan').

13.text: Then they continued through the mountains of Ephraim and stopped at Micah's house.

14.text: The five spies told the rest of the group, 'Yo, y'all know Micah got an ephod, household idols, a carved image, and a molded statue, right? We need to do something about that.'

15.text: So they rolled up to Micah's house and greeted the young Levite priest.

16.text: Meanwhile, the 600 armed Danites were posted up at the entrance of the gate.

17.text: The five spies went inside and straight-up stole the carved idol, ephod, household gods, and molded image, while the priest stood outside with the warriors.

18.text: When the priest saw them taking everything, he asked, 'Bruh, what y'all doing?'

19.text: They told him, 'Look, be quiet and come with us. You wanna be a priest for one man, or you wanna be a priest for an entire tribe of Israel? Think about it—this is an upgrade!'

20.text: The priest thought about it, and he was real happy. He grabbed the idols and joined them.

21.text: Then the Danites took off, putting their families, livestock, and goods up front.

22.text: After they got some distance, Micah and some of his neighbors caught up to the Danites.

23.text: They shouted at them, and the Danites turned around, saying, 'Why you pressing us? What's the problem?'

24.text: Micah said, 'Y'all stole my gods and my priest, and now you asking me what the problem is? Bruh, y'all took everything from me!'

25.text: The Danites responded, 'Look, keep your voice down before one of these hotheads gets mad and you end up dead—your whole household too.'

26.text: Micah saw they had him outnumbered, so he just turned around and went home.

27.text: The Danites took Micah's idols and priest, went to Laish, and attacked. They wiped out the peaceful people there with the sword and burned the whole city down.

28.text: Nobody came to save them, 'cause they was too far from Sidon and had no alliances. After that, the Danites rebuilt the city and moved in.

29.text: They renamed the city Dan, after their ancestor. But before that, it was called Laish.

30.text: Then the Danites set up Micah's idol and made Jonathan, the son of Gershom (Moses' grandson), and his sons the tribe's priests. They stayed in that role until Israel got taken into captivity.

31.text: So the Danites kept Micah's idol with them the whole time, even though the true house of God was in Shiloh.

1.text: Back in those days, Israel ain't have no king. There was this Levite living up in the remote mountains of Ephraim, and he had a concubine from Bethlehem in Judah.

2.text: But she wasn't loyal—she stepped out on him, then ran off to her daddy's house in Bethlehem, staying there for four months.

3.text: After a while, her husband decided to go get her. He wanted to talk to her nice and bring her back. He pulled up with his servant and two donkeys. When she saw him, she took him into her father's house. Her father was happy to meet him.

4.text: Her dad convinced him to stay for three days, so they ate, drank, and kicked it.

5.text: On the fourth day, the Levite got up early to leave, but his father-in-law said, 'Hold up, eat something first, get your strength up, then y'all can go.'

6.text: So they sat down, ate, and drank together. Then her dad was like, 'You should stay another night, have a good time.'

7.text: When the Levite got up to leave, his father-in-law insisted he stay again. So he stayed another night.

8.text: Next morning, he got up early to leave, but her dad said, 'Come on, eat first, take your time.' So they ended up chilling till the afternoon, eating and drinking again.

9.text: When the Levite got up again to leave with his concubine and servant, her father said, 'Look, it's getting late. Just stay one more night and leave early tomorrow.'

10.text: But the Levite was done waiting. He took his concubine and left, making it as far as Jebus (which is Jerusalem). His two donkeys were saddled, and they kept it moving.

11.text: As the sun was going down, his servant said, 'Master, let's stop here in Jebus and stay the night.'

12.text: But the Levite said, 'Nah, we ain't staying in no foreign city with people who ain't Israelites. We'll go to Gibeah.'

13.text: 'Matter of fact, let's try to make it to Gibeah or Ramah before we stop for the night.'

14.text: They kept walking, but the sun went down when they reached Gibeah, which was in the land of Benjamin.

15.text: So they stopped there, but nobody in town offered them a place to stay, so they just sat in the city square.

16.text: Then, an old man came in from working in the fields. He was from Ephraim but lived in Gibeah, unlike the Benjamites who ran the place.

17.text: He saw the travelers and asked, 'Where y'all coming from? Where y'all headed?'

18.text: The Levite answered, 'We're coming from Bethlehem, heading back to my home in Ephraim. But nobody here is offering us a place to stay.'

19.text: 'We got food, wine, straw for our donkeys—everything we need. We just need a place to rest.'

20.text: The old man said, 'Y'all good. I got you. Just don't sleep in the square.'

21.text: So he took them to his house, fed their donkeys, and they washed up, ate, and drank.

22.text: While they were relaxing, some wicked men from the city came and surrounded the house. They started banging on the door and shouted to the old man, 'Bring out that traveler! We wanna know him!'

23.text: The old man stepped outside and said, 'Nah, my brothers! Don't do this evil thing. This man is a guest in my house—don't bring this shame on us!'

24.text: 'Look, take my daughter, she's a virgin, and take his concubine—do whatever you want to them, but don't do this wickedness to this man!'

25.text: But the men weren't trying to hear it. So the Levite grabbed his concubine and threw her outside to them. They assaulted her all night, abusing her until the morning. At sunrise, they finally let her go.

26.text: As the sun rose, she barely made it back to the house, collapsed at the door, and laid there with her hands stretched toward the threshold.

27.text: Her master got up in the morning, opened the door to leave, and saw her lying there. He said, 'Get up, let's go.' But she ain't answer.

28.text: So he picked her up, put her on his donkey, and took her home.

29.text: When he got home, he grabbed a knife, took his concubine's body, and cut her into twelve pieces. Then he sent one piece to each tribe of Israel.

30.text: Everybody who saw it was shook. They said, 'Ain't nothing like this ever happened in Israel—not since we left Egypt! We gotta talk about this. We need to figure out what to do!'

1.text: All the Israelites, from Dan to Beersheba and even Gilead, came together like one squad before the Lord at Mizpah.

2.text: The leaders from every tribe showed up, and 400,000 soldiers ready for battle stood together.

3.text: Meanwhile, the tribe of Benjamin got word that Israel was gathering at Mizpah.

4.text: The Levite—the one whose concubine was murdered—stood up and said, 'Me and my concubine went to Gibeah in Benjamin to spend the night.'

5.text: 'But the men of Gibeah surrounded the house, ready to kill me, and instead, they assaulted my concubine until she died.'

6.text: 'So I cut up her body and sent the pieces all over Israel, because this was an evil crime against our people!'

7.text: 'Now y'all tell me—what are we gonna do about it?'

8.text: Everybody agreed: 'We ain't going home till we handle this.'

9.text: 'Here's the plan: We're taking Gibeah down. We'll divide our forces and make sure justice gets served.'

10.text: 'We'll send out ten percent of our men to gather supplies so that when we move on Gibeah, we'll be ready to make them pay for this wickedness.'

11.text: So all of Israel stood together, ready to wipe Gibeah off the map.

12.text: The tribes of Israel sent messengers to the Benjamites, saying, 'What's up with this wickedness happening in Gibeah?'

13.text: 'Hand over the ones who did this so we can put them to death and remove this evil from Israel!' But Benjamin refused to listen to their own kin.

14.text: Instead of handling the guilty men, the Benjamites gathered their own army from different cities and got ready to fight Israel.

15.text: They had 26,000 soldiers, plus 700 elite fighters from Gibeah.

16.text: These 700 men were left-handed sharpshooters who could sling a stone and hit a target without missing.

17.text: Meanwhile, the Israelites had 400,000 trained soldiers.

18.text: Before going into battle, Israel went to the house of God and asked, 'Lord, who should go up first against Benjamin?' The Lord said, 'Judah first!'

19.text: So Israel camped near Gibeah and got ready.

20.text: When the fight started, Israel lined up against Benjamin.

21.text: But the Benjamites came out swinging, and that day, they killed 22,000 Israelites.

22.text: Israel's men regrouped and got back in position, refusing to give up.

23.text: They went back to the Lord, weeping and asking, 'Should we fight our brothers again?' The Lord said, 'Yes, go back to battle.'

24.text: So they fought again the next day.

25.text: But this time, Benjamin struck down another 18,000 Israelite soldiers.

26.text: After losing twice, all of Israel went before the Lord, crying, fasting, and offering sacrifices.

27.text: At that time, the Ark of the Covenant was still in Israel, and Phinehas, the grandson of Aaron, was the high priest.

28.text: Israel asked again, 'Lord, should we keep fighting or stop?' And the Lord said, 'Go again. Tomorrow, I'll hand them over to you.'

29.text: This time, Israel set up an ambush around Gibeah.

30.text: On the third day, Israel attacked just like before, lining up for battle.

31.text: The Benjamites thought they had the upper hand again, so they rushed out, striking down some Israelites on the highways and in the fields.

32.text: They thought, 'We got 'em just like before!' But Israel was setting a trap.

33.text: Israel's soldiers pulled back, drawing the Benjamites away from the city. Then the hidden ambush unit rushed in and attacked Gibeah.

34.text: The battle got real intense, and Benjamin didn't even realize disaster was coming for them.

35.text: This time, the Lord handed Benjamin over to Israel. They wiped out 25,100 Benjamite soldiers.

36.text: The Benjamites saw they were losing and tried to retreat.

37.text: Meanwhile, the Israelite ambush team stormed Gibeah, slaughtered the city, and burned it down.

38.text: They had set a signal—once a huge smoke cloud rose from the city, the Israelite army would know the ambush was complete.

39.text: At first, the Benjamites thought they were winning, taking down some Israelites. But when they looked back and saw the smoke rising, they panicked.

40.text: That's when they knew—it was over.

41.text: The Israelites turned back and attacked full force. The Benjamites realized disaster had hit.

42.text: They tried to run toward the wilderness, but Israel chased them down, cutting them down wherever they ran.

43.text: They surrounded them, trapping them in a deadly battle that spread east toward Gibeah.

44.text: By the time it was over, 18,000 Benjamite warriors were dead.

45.text: The survivors ran for their lives toward the wilderness at Rimmon Rock, but Israel kept chasing. They cut down another 5,000 on the highways, then another 2,000 at Gidom.

46.text: In total, 25,000 Benjamites died that day—elite warriors who fought to the end.

47.text: Only 600 Benjamites made it out alive, escaping to Rimmon Rock, where they hid for four months.

48.text: Meanwhile, Israel went through all the Benjamite towns, destroying everything—men, livestock, and cities. They set fire to everything they found.

1.text: The men of Israel had made a serious oath at Mizpah, saying, 'Ain't none of us giving our daughters to Benjamin as wives.'

2.text: Then the people came to the house of God and stayed there till evening, crying out loud and weeping hard.

3.text: They said, 'Lord, how did it come to this? How did we end up losing a whole tribe of Israel today?'

4.text: The next morning, they got up early, built an altar, and offered burnt offerings and peace offerings to God.

5.text: Then they asked, 'Who from Israel ain't show up when we gathered at Mizpah? 'Cause we swore that anybody who ain't show up should be put to death.'

6.text: The Israelites were grieving hard for Benjamin, saying, 'One of our own tribes is about to disappear—what we supposed to do?'

7.text: 'How we gon' find wives for the few that's left, since we already swore not to give them our daughters?'

8.text: Then they asked, 'Wait, which tribe ain't come to Mizpah?' Turns out, nobody from Jabesh Gilead had shown up.

9.text: When they did a headcount, they realized not one single person from Jabesh Gilead had come to the gathering.

10.text: So Israel sent 12,000 of their best warriors and told them, 'Go to Jabesh Gilead and wipe 'em out—kill all the men and every woman who's already been with a man.'

11.text: 'Take out every male and every married woman.'

12.text: They ended up finding 400 young virgins who hadn't been with a man. They brought them back to the camp at Shiloh in Canaan.

13.text: Then the whole congregation sent messengers to the surviving Benjamites hiding at Rimmon Rock, letting them know they could come back in peace.

14.text: So Benjamin returned, and Israel gave them the women they had taken from Jabesh Gilead. But it still wasn't enough.

15.text: The people were hurting, 'cause they knew the Lord had allowed this tribe to be nearly wiped out.

16.text: The elders asked, 'What we gon' do for the rest of these men? They need wives, and all the women of Benjamin are gone.'

17.text: 'We gotta make sure Benjamin don't disappear completely—every tribe needs an inheritance.'

18.text: 'But we can't give them our daughters, 'cause we swore an oath against that.'

19.text: Then somebody had an idea: 'Wait a minute—there's that yearly festival of the Lord in Shiloh. The one north of Bethel, near the road that leads to Shechem.'

20.text: So they told the remaining Benjamites, 'Here's what y'all gon' do: Hide out in the vineyards near Shiloh.'

21.text: 'When the young women come out to dance for the festival, jump out, grab a wife, and take her back to Benjamin!'

22.text: 'And when their fathers and brothers complain, we'll tell them, "Look, just let it slide. Y'all ain't really 'give' them to Benjamin, so technically, you ain't breaking your oath."'

23.text: So the Benjamites did exactly that—when the young women of Shiloh came out dancing, they grabbed enough wives for themselves, then went back home to rebuild their cities.

24.text: After that, everybody went back to their own tribes and homes, returning to their land and inheritance.

25.text: Back in those days, Israel ain't have no king—everybody just did whatever they thought was right.

1.text: Look at her now—Jerusalem sittin' all alone, like a widow. Used to be full of folks, now she empty. She was that girl, a queen in the game. Now? Just another servant.

2.text: She cryin' all night long, tears runnin' down her cheeks. Used to have lovers, now ain't nobody comin' to wipe her face. Her so-called friends? Snakes. Turned on her quick.

3.text: Judah got dragged off, heavy and hurt. No rest, no peace. She livin' in strange lands now, and her enemies stay on her neck.

4.text: The roads to Zion? Quiet. Ain't nobody comin' to celebrate no more. The gates? Dead silent. Priests sighin', young girls broken. The whole city deep in bitterness.

5.text: Her enemies walkin' around like they run the place. Why? 'Cause the Lord let it happen—too many sins stacked up. Her kids? Snatched away by the enemy.

6.text: Zion's glow is gone. Her leaders out here movin' like starving deer—tired, weak, and runnin' scared.

7.text: Now that she's sufferin', she rememberin' the good ol' days—when she had joy, peace, all that. But when her people fell, ain't nobody came to help. The enemies laughed at her downfall.

8.text: Jerusalem messed up bad, and now she look a mess. Folks who used to respect her now turn their nose up. They seen her shame—now she just sighs and hides her face.

9.text: She ain't even think about where her choices would lead. Now her fall hit hard—no one there to catch her. She cryin' out, "Lord, look at me. I'm sufferin'. The enemy out here flexin'!"

10.text: The enemy done reached into her treasure chest, takin' all her goods. She even saw outsiders walk through the temple—folks You said ain't even supposed to step in there.

11.text: Her people hungry, tryna trade whatever they got for some bread. She pleadin', "Look, Lord. See what's happenin' to me. I'm bein' played and disrespected."

12.text: "Y'all just gon' walk by like this ain't nothin'? Stop and look—ever seen pain like this? The Lord came down hard on me. His anger hit different."

13.text: "He sent fire straight to my bones. Set me up like a trap. Now I'm stuck, drained, barely holdin' on."

14.text: "My sins? Heavy like a yoke on my neck. He wove 'em together, pressed 'em on me. My strength gone. He handed me over to folks I couldn't even fight off."

15.text: "He crushed all my warriors. Called a whole meeting just to stomp out my young men. God stepped on the daughter of Judah like grapes in a winepress."

16.text: "That's why I'm cryin'. Tears steady fallin'. The one who used to bring me comfort—gone. My children abandoned, 'cause the enemy won."

17.text: Zion stretchin' out her hands, beggin' for help—but nobody listenin'. God made sure her neighbors turned on her. Now Jerusalem gettin' treated like she unclean.

18.text: "God was right. I went against His Word. Y'all better listen—I'm hurtin'. My daughters, my sons? Gone. Caught up in captivity."

19.text: "I tried to call the ones I loved, but they ghosted me. Even the priests and elders died lookin' for food—just tryna survive."

20.text: "Lord, you see me. I'm stressed for real. Heart all twisted up. I know I rebelled, but outside got swords and inside feel like death."

21.text: "Folks hear me cryin', but nobody show up. My enemies? They smilin' like they won somethin'. But You did this, Lord. Bring that same energy to them."

22.text: "Let all they mess get put on blast, just like mine. Hit them with what You hit me with, 'cause I got a whole lotta sorrow and my heart barely hangin' on."

1.text: The Lord done covered Zion in a storm cloud of anger. He threw down Israel's glory from heaven to the dirt—like it was nothin'. Didn't even spare His own footstool when He got mad.

2.text: God ain't hold back—He wiped out every home in Jacob. Tore down Judah's strongholds in pure rage. He threw the kingdom down like trash and dragged the royal crew through the mud.

3.text: In His fury, He snatched away Israel's strength. Pulled back His right hand like, "Y'all on your own now." Then He lit up Jacob like wildfire—burned everything in sight.

4.text: He stood like He was the enemy. Bow drawn, hand steady. Took out the ones He used to love. Dropped that heat on Zion like a bomb.

5.text: Yeah, the Lord came through like an enemy for real. Knocked down Israel's whole setup. Palaces? Gone. Forts? Gone. Now it's just tears and heartbreak in Judah.

6.text: He bulldozed His own house like it was a backyard garden. Shut down the festivals, canceled the Sabbath. God ain't even check for the king or priest no more—He was done.

7.text: He turned His back on the altar, bounced on the sanctuary. Let the enemy break through the palace gates. They in there now, wildin' out in the temple like it's a block party.

8.text: God already had it planned—to destroy Zion's wall. He pulled out the measuring line like a contractor, but it was for demolition. Walls and defenses cried out like they knew they was next.

9.text: Her gates? Gone. Sunk straight into the dirt. The bars snapped off. Ain't no king, no princes—everybody scattered. God ain't speakin' through the prophets either. Silence.

10.text: The elders just sittin' on the ground in silence, tossin' dust on their heads, wrapped in sackcloth. The young girls got their heads down too—grief heavy in the air.

11.text: My eyes tired from cryin', my stomach turnin'. I'm sick over what happened to my people. Little kids out here faintin' in the streets like they got no chance.

12.text: They beggin' their mamas, "Where the food at? Where the drink?" But they passin' out in the streets, fallin' like wounded soldiers. Dying in their mama's arms.

13.text: What can I even say to you, Jerusalem? What example fits what you goin' through? Your hurt is wide like the ocean—who got the remedy for that?

14.text: Your so-called prophets been lyin'. Told you what you wanted to hear. Never checked you, never called out your mess. Just fed you fairy tales and delusions.

15.text: Folks walkin' by lookin' at you sideways, clappin' sarcastically. "This the 'joy of the whole earth'? This the 'perfect city'?" They laughin' now.

16.text: Your enemies got their mouths wide open, hatin' out loud. Grittin' teeth, talkin' slick: "We got her. This the day we been waitin' for."

17.text: The Lord followed through on what He said He'd do. He didn't flinch. Tore the place down without pity. Let your enemies have the last laugh. Lifted them up while you hit rock bottom.

18.text: Zion's people cried out to the Lord like, "Let the tears fall nonstop, day and night. Don't hold back. Don't rest."

19.text: "Get up. Cry through the night. Pour your heart out in front of God. Lift your hands and beg for your kids—starvin' and droppin' in every street corner."

20.text: "Lord, look! Look what's happenin'! Is this what You meant to do? Mothers eatin' their babies? Priests and prophets bein' killed in Your house?"

21.text: "The streets full of bodies—young and old. Girls and boys dead from the sword. You did this in Your anger, God. You didn't hold back."

22.text: "You called disaster like You was callin' folks to a party. But there was no escape. The ones I raised, the ones I loved? My enemies wiped 'em out."

1.text: I'm that man who seen pain up close—beat down by God's heavy hand.

2.text: He led me straight into darkness. Ain't no light, just shadows.

3.text: Day after day, He kept swingin' on me. Felt like I couldn't catch a break.

4.text: My body feel old. Skin cracked, bones hurtin'. He wore me out.

5.text: Surrounded me with bitterness, locked me in misery.

6.text: He sat me down in the dark, like I been dead and buried.

7.text: Built walls around me—I couldn't leave. Put chains on my soul.

8.text: I screamed, I begged—but He ain't pick up. My prayers ain't goin' nowhere.

9.text: Every path I tried? Blocked. Twisted. Like He made the road hard on purpose.

10.text: He came at me like a bear in the cut, or a lion ready to pounce.

11.text: Snatched me off my path, tore me apart. Left me feelin' empty.

12.text: He pulled His bow, aimed right at me—like I was the target.

13.text: His arrows hit deep. Pierced through me like He was settin' a message.

14.text: Now folks laugh at me. I'm the joke, the meme, the group chat topic.

15.text: He filled me with bitterness—made me drink pain like it was my medicine.

16.text: Broke my teeth on gravel. Rubbed my face in ashes.

17.text: Peace? Don't even know her no more. Joy? Can't remember the last time.

18.text: I said to myself, "It's over. My strength and my hope died today."

19.text: Lord, remember how bad it's been. That bitterness, that sorrow—it stay in my chest.

20.text: My soul still feelin' it. I stay sunk low.

21.text: But I gotta pull somethin' up out my memory—this one thing keeps me hangin' on:

22.text: We ain't been wiped out completely 'cause God still got mercy. His love don't run dry.

23.text: New mercies show up every single morning. Your faithfulness? Solid.

24.text: Deep in my soul I say, "God is all I got, so I'ma keep hopin' in Him."

25.text: The Lord good to them who wait on Him, who chase after Him with their whole heart.

26.text: It's a blessing to wait quiet, even when it's hard—trustin' God gon' come through.

27.text: Better to carry some weight while you young—learn the lesson early.

28.text: Sit in that silence. Don't complain. If God handed it to you, there's a reason.

29.text: Put your face in the dirt—humble yourself. You might still find some hope down there.

30.text: If you get slapped, take it. If folks talk down on you, endure it. God seein' all of it.

31.text: The Lord ain't gon' leave you forever.

32.text: He might let you hurt for a season, but His compassion still deep. Real deep.

33.text: God don't enjoy watchin' us suffer. That ain't His heart.

34.text: He ain't about crushin' folks for no reason, or abusin' power over prisoners.

35.text: He don't like it when people block justice, or cheat somebody outta their rights.

36.text: Tryin' to twist someone's case? That ain't it. God ain't with that.

37.text: Who can make somethin' happen if God ain't co-signed it?

38.text: Ain't it both good and bad that come from the Most High's mouth?

39.text: So why you mad at life when you the one that messed up? Own your sins.

40.text: Let's check ourselves. Let's turn back to God while we still got time.

41.text: Lift our hearts and hands to the One in heaven. No shame in surrender.

42.text: We rebelled. We crossed the line. And You ain't let it slide.

43.text: You chased us down with Your anger. Cut us off. No mercy that time.

44.text: You blocked us off with a thick cloud. Prayers couldn't even get through.

45.text: Now the nations look at us like trash—refuse. Dirt under their feet.

46.text: Our enemies talk wild. Mouths open wide.

47.text: Fear everywhere. Traps everywhere. All we see is destruction.

48.text: My eyes stay leakin', cryin' rivers for my people.

49.text: I can't stop. The tears don't pause.

50.text: Not till God looks down from heaven and sees what's goin' on.

51.text: What I see hurt my soul. Especially what's happened to my sisters in the city.

52.text: My enemies hunted me like I was a bird, for nothin'.

53.text: Threw me in a pit. Tried to bury me alive. Tossed rocks on top.

54.text: Water closed in over me. I said, "This it. I'm done."

55.text: But I called on Your name, Lord—from the bottom. From the pit.

56.text: You heard me cryin'. You ain't shut Your ears.

57.text: When I called, You came close. You said, "Don't be scared."

58.text: Lord, You fought for me. You saved my life.

59.text: You seen what they did to me. You know how they wronged me. Handle it.

60.text: You saw all the shade, all the schemes they ran.

61.text: You heard their slick talk, Lord. You peeped the whispers and the hate.

62.text: The way they talked, the things they plotted—it was constant.

63.text: They mock me when I sit, when I stand. I'm their lil' joke now.

64.text: Lord, pay 'em back for all they done. Let them reap what they sowed.

65.text: Give 'em a heart that can't see the truth. Let Your judgment rest on 'em.

66.text: In Your anger, chase 'em down. Wipe 'em out from under heaven.

1.text: Look at that—gold gone dull. The fine stuff? Tarnished. The stones from God's house? Scattered like trash on the corners.

2.text: Zion's sons used to shine like pure gold. Now folks treat 'em like clay pots—cheap and cracked, like they ain't nothin' special.

3.text: Even wild jackals nurse their babies. But our people? Cold. Actin' heartless like ostriches in the desert—don't even care for they own.

4.text: Babies out here dry-mouthed, tongue stuck to the roof from thirst. Kids cryin' for food, but nobody breakin' bread for them.

5.text: Folks who used to eat luxury meals? Now they sittin' on sidewalks lookin' lost. Ones raised in velvet robes? Huggin' piles of ash.

6.text: Zion's punishment hit harder than Sodom's. At least Sodom got wiped quick. No one was left to even reach for help.

7.text: Her Nazirites used to glow—skin bright like snow and milk, cheeks red like rubies, faces like sapphires.

8.text: Now they look like soot—ashy, unrecognizable. Skin stuck to bones, bodies dried up like brittle wood.

9.text: Better to die by the sword than waste away from hunger. At least that's fast. Hunger makes you slowly disappear.

10.text: Women once full of love got pushed so far, they cooked their own kids just to survive. That's how deep the destruction hit.

11.text: The Lord ain't hold back. His anger came down like wildfire. Burned through Zion to the foundation.

12.text: The kings of the world ain't believe it. Nobody thought enemies could walk through Jerusalem's gates—but they did.

13.text: And why? 'Cause the prophets were dirty. The priests were wildin'. They spilled innocent blood and led the people wrong.

14.text: Now they out here wanderin' blind, blood on them, lookin' unclean. Folks don't even wanna touch their clothes.

15.text: People shout, "Back up! Don't come near! You unclean!" They ran, they hid—but even the other nations said, "Y'all can't stay here."

16.text: God turned His face away. He wasn't tryna hear it. The people lost respect for the priests, didn't care about the elders.

17.text: We kept watchin' the horizon, hopin' for help. Waited on nations that never came through. Just empty promises.

18.text: They followed our every move. Streets weren't safe. We knew the end was near. Time was up.

19.text: Our enemies chased us like eagles—fast, fierce. Got us on the mountains, stalked us in the wilderness.

20.text: The one we thought was our lifeline, the anointed one, even he got caught. We said, "We'll live safe under his protection"—but that shadow vanished too.

21.text: Go ahead and laugh now, Edom. You next. That cup of judgment? You gon' drink it too. And you gon' be exposed—stripped bare.

22.text: But Zion, your time of payin' is just about done. No more exile. But Edom? Oh, He still got somethin' for you. Your dirt gon' get aired out.

1.text: Lord, please remember what happened to us. Look at the shame we carry—see us for real.

2.text: Everything that was ours—our land, our homes—got taken over by outsiders. Strangers livin' in our inheritance.

3.text: We like orphans now. No protection. Our mamas feel like widows—left alone.

4.text: We gotta pay just to get water to drink. Even firewood cost us somethin'.

5.text: We can't catch a break. They stay on our backs. We work hard, but we don't get no rest.

6.text: We been out here beggin' Egypt and Assyria just to put some bread on the table.

7.text: Our fathers messed up and now they gone. But we the ones payin' the price.

8.text: Servants runnin' things now. And ain't nobody showin' up to rescue us.

9.text: We gotta risk our lives just to find food. The wilderness got swords waitin' on us.

10.text: Our skin feel like it's burnin' up—hot like an oven. Famine fever got us weak.

11.text: Our women been violated in Zion. Our daughters in Judah ain't safe no more.

12.text: The princes got hanged by their hands. Elders? Ain't nobody respectin' them.

13.text: The young men workin' like slaves at the grindstone. Little boys bucklin' under wood loads.

14.text: The elders don't even sit at the gate no more. The young ones? The music done stopped.

15.text: Ain't no joy in our hearts. The party's over. Our dance done turned into a funeral.

16.text: The crown done fell off our head. We lost our shine. All 'cause we sinned. This pain? We earned it.

17.text: Our hearts heavy because of all this. Our eyes stay cloudy with tears.

18.text: Mount Zion, once so holy, now deserted—foxes just runnin' around like they own it.

19.text: But You, Lord, You still on the throne. Always have been. Always will be.

20.text: So why You feel so far off? Like You forgot about us? Why You lettin' it drag on like this?

21.text: Turn us back to You, Lord. We ready. We want to be restored. Bring us back to how it used to be.

22.text: Unless… You done really turned Your back. Unless Your anger still burnin'. But Lord… don't leave us like this.

1.text: The Lord called Moses from the Tabernacle and told him,

2.text: "Aight, tell the people of Israel this—when y'all bring an animal as an offering to Me, it gotta come from your herd of cattle, or your flock of sheep and goats.

3.text: If you bringing a bull for a burnt offering, it gotta be a male with no defects. Bring it to the entrance of the Tabernacle, so the Lord can accept you.

4.text: Put your hand on the animal's head, and the Lord will take it as a stand-in for you—it's gonna purify you and make you right with Him.

5.text: Then y'all gotta slaughter the young bull in the Lord's presence, and Aaron's sons—the priests—will take the blood and splash it on all sides of the altar at the Tabernacle entrance.

6.text: After that, skin the animal and cut it up.

7.text: The sons of Aaron will set up a fire on the altar,

8.text: and they'll lay the pieces—including the head and the fat—on the burning wood.

9.text: But before that, the internal organs and the legs gotta be washed with water. Then the priest will burn the whole thing on the altar as a burnt offering. It's a special gift, something that smells real good to the Lord.

10.text: If you bringing a sheep or a goat for a burnt offering, it gotta be a male with no defects.

11.text: Slaughter it on the north side of the altar, right in front of the Lord, and Aaron's sons will splash its blood on all sides of the altar.

12.text: Then cut it into pieces, and the priests will arrange the parts—including the head and fat—on the burning wood.

13.text: The insides and legs gotta be washed first, and then the priest will burn the whole thing as a burnt offering. It's a special gift, and it's a pleasing smell to the Lord.

14.text: If you bringing a bird as a burnt offering, make sure it's either a turtledove or a young pigeon.

15.text: The priest will take it to the altar, wring its head off, and burn it there. But first, he gotta drain the blood on the side of the altar.

16.text: Then he'll take out the bird's crop and feathers and toss them in the ashes on the east side of the altar.

17.text: Finally, he'll grab the bird by its wings and tear it open—but not all the way apart—and then burn it on the altar's wood fire. Just like the other offerings, it's a special gift, a pleasing aroma to the Lord.

1.text: If you bring a grain offering to the Lord, it gotta be the finest flour. Pour olive oil on it and sprinkle some frankincense on top.

2.text: Then take it to Aaron's sons, the priests. One of them will grab a handful of that flour, mix it with the oil and all the frankincense, and burn it on the altar. This offering is a special gift, and the smell pleases the Lord.

3.text: The rest of the grain offering goes to Aaron and his sons. This part of the offering is real holy—one of the special gifts set apart for the Lord.

4.text: If you baking your grain offering in an oven, it gotta be made from the finest flour, no yeast allowed. You can bring it as thin cakes mixed with olive oil or wafers brushed with oil.

5.text: If you cooking your grain offering on a griddle, it still gotta be made with the finest flour and olive oil, but no yeast.

6.text: Break it into pieces and pour some olive oil on it. That's your grain offering.

7.text: If your grain offering is made in a pan, same rule—use the finest flour and olive oil.

8.text: No matter how you make your grain offering, bring it to the priest, and he'll take it to the altar.

9.text: The priest will grab a handful from it and burn that portion on the altar as a special gift. The smell gonna be real pleasing to the Lord.

10.text: The rest of the grain offering belongs to Aaron and his sons as their food. It's a most holy part of the special gifts offered to the Lord.

11.text: Don't use no yeast when making any grain offering to the Lord. And don't be adding honey either, cause neither of them can be burned as an offering to the Lord.

12.text: If you bringing a first-fruits offering from your harvest, you can use yeast and honey, but you can't put that on the altar as a burnt offering that's supposed to smell good to the Lord.

13.text: Make sure you season all your grain offerings with salt, cause that salt is a reminder of God's eternal covenant. Don't ever forget to add salt to your offerings.

14.text: If you bringing a grain offering from the first part of your harvest, bring fresh grain that's been roasted and coarsely crushed.

15.text: Pour some olive oil on it and sprinkle some frankincense over it.

16.text: The priest will take a handful of that grain mixed with oil, along with all the frankincense, and burn it on the altar as a special gift to the Lord.

1.text: If you bringing an animal from the herd as a peace offering to the Lord, it can be a male or a female, but it gotta be without any defects.

2.text: Put your hand on the animal's head and slaughter it at the entrance of the Tabernacle. Then Aaron's sons, the priests, gonna take the blood and splash it on all sides of the altar.

3.text: The priest gotta take some of this peace offering as a special gift to the Lord. That includes all the fat around the internal organs,

4.text: The two kidneys, the fat around them near the loins, and the long lobe of the liver—these gotta be removed with the kidneys.

5.text: Aaron's sons will burn these parts on top of the burnt offering, over the wood burning on the altar. This offering is a special gift, and the Lord gonna love the smell.

6.text: If you bringing an animal from the flock as a peace offering to the Lord, it can be a male or a female, but it gotta be without defects.

7.text: If you offering a sheep, bring it before the Lord,

8.text: Put your hand on its head and slaughter it in front of the Tabernacle. Aaron's sons will then splash its blood on all sides of the altar.

9.text: The priest gotta take the fat of this peace offering as a special gift to the Lord. That includes the fat of the broad tail cut off near the backbone, all the fat around the internal organs,

10.text: The two kidneys, the fat around them near the loins, and the long lobe of the liver—these must be removed with the kidneys.

11.text: The priest will burn them on the altar as a special gift of food to the Lord.

12.text: If you bringing a goat as a peace offering, bring it before the Lord,

13.text: Put your hand on its head and slaughter it in front of the Tabernacle. Aaron's sons will then splash its blood on all sides of the altar.

14.text: The priest gotta take some of this offering as a special gift to the Lord. That includes all the fat around the internal organs,

15.text: The two kidneys, the fat around them near the loins, and the long lobe of the liver—these gotta be removed with the kidneys.

16.text: The priest will burn them on the altar as a special gift of food, a smell the Lord gonna love. All the fat belongs to the Lord.

17.text: Y'all must never eat no fat or blood. This rule stays forever, for every generation, no matter where y'all live.

1.text: Then the Lord told Moses,

2.text: Go tell the people of Israel how to handle things when somebody sins on accident, breaking one of the Lord's commands without knowing.

3.text: If the high priest messes up and brings guilt on the whole community, he gotta bring a young bull with no defects as a sin offering for what he did.

4.text: He gotta bring that bull to the entrance of the Tabernacle, put his hand on its head, and kill it right there before the Lord.

5.text: Then the high priest will take some of the bull's blood inside the Tabernacle,

6.text: Dip his finger in the blood, and sprinkle it seven times in front of the inner curtain in the sanctuary.

7.text: After that, he'll put some of the blood on the horns of the incense altar inside the Tabernacle, in the Lord's presence. The rest of the blood? He gonna pour that out at the base of the burnt offering altar at the entrance of the Tabernacle.

8.text: Then he gotta take all the fat from the bull as part of the sin offering—

9.text: That means the fat around the internal organs, the two kidneys, the fat around the loins, and the long lobe of the liver.

10.text: He gotta remove them just like he would for a peace offering and burn them on the burnt offering altar.

11.text: But the rest of the bull—the hide, the meat, the head, legs, internal organs, and even the dung—

12.text: He gotta take all of that outside the camp to the special clean place where the ashes get dumped. He will burn it there on a wood fire at the ash heap.

13.text: If the whole Israelite community messes up and breaks one of the Lord's commands without knowing, they still guilty.

14.text: When they realize what they did, they gotta bring a young bull as a sin offering and present it in front of the Tabernacle.

15.text: The community elders will put their hands on the bull's head and kill it before the Lord.

16.text: Then the high priest will take some of the bull's blood inside the Tabernacle,

17.text: Dip his finger in it, and sprinkle it seven times in front of the inner curtain.

18.text: He will then put some of the blood on the horns of the incense altar inside the Tabernacle, and pour the rest of the blood out at the base of the burnt offering altar at the entrance.

19.text: Then he gotta take all the fat off and burn it on the altar,

20.text: Just like he did for the high priest's sin offering. That's how the priest makes things right for the people, and they will be forgiven.

21.text: Then he gotta take the rest of the bull outside the camp and burn it, just like the high priest's sin offering. This is for the whole congregation's sin.

22.text: If one of Israel's leaders messes up and breaks a command without realizing, he still guilty.

23.text: When he finds out what he did, he gotta bring a male goat with no defects as his sin offering.

24.text: He'll put his hand on the goat's head and kill it at the same place as the burnt offerings, before the Lord.

25.text: Then the priest will dip his finger in the blood and put it on the horns of the burnt offering altar. The rest of the blood? He will pour it out at the base of the altar.

26.text: Then he will burn all the fat on the altar just like he would for a peace offering. That's how the priest makes things right for the leader, and he will be forgiven.

27.text: If any regular person sins by breaking one of the Lord's commands without knowing, they still guilty.

28.text: When they find out what they did, they gotta bring a female goat with no defects as a sin offering.

29.text: They'll put their hand on the goat's head and kill it where the burnt offerings are slaughtered.

30.text: Then the priest will dip his finger in the blood and put it on the horns of the burnt offering altar. The rest of the blood? He will pour it out at the base of the altar.

31.text: Then he will take all the fat off, just like with a peace offering, and burn it on the altar. The smell gonna be pleasing to the Lord. That's how the priest makes things right for the person, and they will be forgiven.

32.text: If they bring a sheep as their sin offering, it gotta be a female with no defects.

33.text: They'll put their hand on its head and kill it at the place where burnt offerings get slaughtered.

34.text: Then the priest will dip his finger in the blood and put it on the horns of the burnt offering altar. The rest of the blood? He will pour it out at the base of the altar.

35.text: Then he gotta remove all the fat, just like he would with a peace offering, and burn it on top of the special gifts presented to the Lord. That's how the priest makes things right for them, and they will be forgiven.

1.text: If you get called to testify about something you seen or know about, and you refuse to speak up, that's a sin. You gonna be held accountable for that.

2.text: If you accidentally touch something that's unclean—like a dead animal that ain't supposed to be eaten—once you realize what you did, you gotta admit you made yourself unclean.

3.text: Same thing if you touch something that makes a person unclean. When you realize it, you gotta acknowledge your guilt.

4.text: If you make a reckless vow—whether it's to do something good or bad—and later realize it was foolish, you gotta admit your guilt.

5.text: Whenever you become aware of your sin in any of these ways, you gotta confess what you did.

6.text: Then you gotta bring a female sheep or goat from your flock as a sin offering. The priest will use it to purify you and make things right with the Lord.

7.text: If you can't afford a sheep, you can bring two turtledoves or two young pigeons instead—one for a sin offering, the other for a burnt offering.

8.text: Take them to the priest. He will offer the first bird for the sin offering by wringing its neck, but he won't pull the head off completely.

9.text: He'll sprinkle some of the blood against the sides of the altar and drain the rest at the base. That's the sin offering.

10.text: Then he will prepare the second bird as a burnt offering, following the usual rules. This way, the priest will purify you, making things right with the Lord, and you will be forgiven.

11.text: If you can't afford two birds, you can bring about two quarts of fine flour as your sin offering. But don't mix it with oil or put frankincense on it, cause it's a sin offering.

12.text: Take the flour to the priest. He will take a handful and burn it on the altar on top of the special gifts for the Lord. This is the sin offering.

13.text: Through this process, the priest will purify you from any of these sins, making things right with the Lord, and you will be forgiven. The rest of the flour belongs to the priest, just like the grain offering.

14.text: Then the Lord told Moses,

15.text: If you accidentally mess up and disrespect something sacred that belongs to the Lord, you gotta bring a guilt offering. That means bringing a ram with no defects—or buying one of equal value with silver, using the sanctuary shekel for measurement.

16.text: You also gotta pay back what you messed up, plus an extra 20 percent. When you give it to the priest, he will purify you by sacrificing the ram as a guilt offering, making things right with the Lord. Then you'll be forgiven.

17.text: If you break one of the Lord's commands, even if you didn't know you messed up, you're still guilty and gotta face the consequences.

18.text: For a guilt offering, you gotta bring a ram with no defects, or buy one of equal value. The priest will use it to purify you from your unintentional sin, making things right with the Lord, and you'll be forgiven.

19.text: This is a guilt offering, cause you been guilty of an offense against the Lord.

1.text: Then the Lord told Moses,

2.text: If somebody sins against their neighbor, they also being unfaithful to the Lord. That means if they cheat somebody in a deal, steal, or commit fraud,

3.text: Or if they find lost property and lie about it, or swear to tell the truth but still lie, or do anything shady like that—

4.text: If they guilty of any of these things, they gotta pay back what they stole, took by fraud, kept from somebody, or lied about.

5.text: They gotta return the full amount plus an extra 20 percent to the person they wronged. And on that same day, they gotta bring a guilt offering.

6.text: For their guilt offering, they gotta bring a ram with no defects to the priest, or buy one of equal value.

7.text: Then the priest will purify them before the Lord, making things right, and they'll be forgiven for whatever sin they committed.

8.text: Then the Lord told Moses,

9.text: Tell Aaron and his sons these instructions about burnt offerings. The burnt offering gotta stay on the altar all night until morning, and the fire must keep burning the whole time.

10.text: In the morning, the priest on duty will put on his linen clothes and undergarments, then clean out the ashes from the burnt offering and put them beside the altar.

11.text: Then he'll change back into his regular clothes and take the ashes outside the camp to a place that's clean.

12.text: Meanwhile, the fire on the altar must never go out. Every morning, the priest will add fresh wood, arrange the burnt offering, and burn the fat from the peace offerings.

13.text: That fire gotta stay burning on the altar—it must never go out.

14.text: These the instructions for the grain offering. Aaron's sons gotta present it before the Lord, in front of the altar.

15.text: The priest on duty will grab a handful of the best flour, mix it with olive oil, and add all the frankincense. Then he'll burn this portion on the altar, and the smell will please the Lord.

16.text: Aaron and his sons can eat the rest of the flour, but it gotta be baked without yeast and eaten in a holy place inside the Tabernacle courtyard.

17.text: It must never be made with yeast, cause this is their portion of the Lord's special gifts, just like the sin offering and the guilt offering—it's most holy.

18.text: Any male descendant of Aaron can eat from these sacred offerings. This is their permanent right, passed down through generations. Anybody who touches these offerings will become holy.

19.text: Then the Lord told Moses,

20.text: On the day Aaron and his sons get anointed, they gotta bring a grain offering of two quarts of fine flour—half in the morning, half in the evening.

21.text: It gotta be mixed with olive oil and cooked on a griddle. Then it must be sliced up and presented as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.

22.text: Every high priest after Aaron must prepare this same offering. It belongs to the Lord and must be completely burned up.

23.text: Every grain offering from a priest must be burned entirely—none of it can be eaten.

24.text: Then the Lord told Moses,

25.text: Tell Aaron and his sons: The sin offering is most holy, and it must be slaughtered in the Lord's presence at the same place where burnt offerings are killed.

26.text: The priest who offers the sacrifice must eat his portion in a sacred place inside the Tabernacle courtyard.

27.text: Anything or anyone that touches this sacrificial meat will become holy. If any of its blood splashes on somebody's clothes, they gotta wash that garment in a sacred place.

28.text: If the meat is boiled in a clay pot, that pot must be broken afterward. If it's cooked in a bronze pot, it gotta be scrubbed and rinsed with water.

29.text: Any male from a priest's family can eat this offering, cause it's most holy.

30.text: But if the blood from the sin offering is brought inside the Tabernacle for purification, then that offering can't be eaten—it gotta be completely burned with fire.

1.text: These the rules for the guilt offering. It's most holy.

2.text: The animal used for the guilt offering gotta be slaughtered in the same place as the burnt offerings, and its blood gotta be splattered on all sides of the altar.

3.text: The priest will take all the fat and burn it on the altar—this includes the fat from the broad tail and the fat around the internal organs.

4.text: The two kidneys, the fat near the loins, and the long lobe of the liver all gotta be removed with the kidneys.

5.text: The priests will burn these parts on the altar as a special gift to the Lord. This is the guilt offering.

6.text: Any male from a priest's family can eat the meat, but it gotta be eaten in a sacred place, cause it's most holy.

7.text: The same rules apply for both the guilt offering and the sin offering—both belong to the priest who offers them to purify someone before the Lord.

8.text: If it's a burnt offering, the priest who sacrifices it gets to keep the hide of the animal.

9.text: Any grain offering that's baked in an oven, cooked in a pan, or on a griddle belongs to the priest who presented it.

10.text: All other grain offerings, whether dry or mixed with olive oil, gotta be shared equally among Aaron's descendants—the priests.

11.text: These the rules for the different kinds of peace offerings people can bring to the Lord.

12.text: If it's a thanksgiving offering, it gotta come with bread made without yeast—thin cakes mixed with olive oil, wafers spread with oil, and cakes made with choice flour and olive oil.

13.text: This peace offering also gotta come with loaves of bread made with yeast.

14.text: One of each type of bread must be presented as a special gift to the Lord, and it will belong to the priest who splatters the blood of the peace offering on the altar.

15.text: The meat from this thanksgiving peace offering must be eaten on the same day. None of it can be saved for the next morning.

16.text: If the offering is for a vow or just a voluntary offering, the meat must be eaten the same day, but leftovers can be eaten the next day.

17.text: But any meat left until the third day gotta be completely burned up.

18.text: If anybody eats from the peace offering on the third day, it won't be accepted, and they won't get credit for the offering. By that time, the meat is contaminated, and if they eat it, they'll be punished for their sin.

19.text: If the meat touches anything unclean, it can't be eaten—it must be burned up. But if it's still clean, only people who are ceremonially clean can eat it.

20.text: If anybody who is unclean eats the peace offering meat, they gonna be cut off from the community.

21.text: If somebody touches anything unclean—whether it's a dead body, an unclean animal, or something nasty—and then eats from the peace offering, they gonna be cut off from the community.

22.text: Then the Lord told Moses,

23.text: Tell the Israelites never to eat the fat from cattle, sheep, or goats.

24.text: If an animal dies on its own or gets torn up by wild animals, its fat can be used for other purposes, but it can't be eaten.

25.text: Anybody who eats fat from an animal that was offered to the Lord as a gift will be cut off from the community.

26.text: No matter where y'all live, never eat the blood of any bird or animal.

27.text: Anybody who eats blood will be cut off from the community.

28.text: Then the Lord told Moses,

29.text: Tell the Israelites: When y'all bring a peace offering to the Lord, part of it gotta be set aside as a special gift.

30.text: You gotta bring the fat of the animal, along with the breast, and lift it up as a special offering to the Lord.

31.text: The priest will burn the fat on the altar, but the breast belongs to Aaron and his sons.

32.text: The right thigh of the peace offering must be given to the priest as a special gift.

33.text: The right thigh always belongs to the priest who offers the blood and fat of the peace offering.

34.text: The Lord said: I have set aside the breast of the special offering and the right thigh of the sacred offering for the priests. This is their permanent portion from the peace offerings brought by the Israelites.

35.text: This is their rightful share—the special gifts that belong to Aaron and his descendants from the time they were chosen to serve as priests.

36.text: On the day they were anointed, the Lord commanded that these portions belong to the priests forever—from generation to generation.

37.text: These are the official instructions for the burnt offering, grain offering, sin offering, guilt offering, ordination offering, and peace offering.

38.text: The Lord gave all these instructions to Moses on Mount Sinai when He commanded the Israelites to bring their offerings in the wilderness.

1.text: Then the Lord told Moses,

2.text: Bring Aaron and his sons, their special robes, the anointing oil, the bull for the sin offering, the two rams, and the basket of bread made without yeast.

3.text: Then call the whole community of Israel together at the entrance of the Tabernacle.

4.text: So Moses did what the Lord said, and the whole community gathered at the Tabernacle entrance.

5.text: Then Moses told them, 'This is what the Lord commanded us to do!'

6.text: Moses then brought Aaron and his sons forward and washed them with water.

7.text: He put the tunic on Aaron, tied the sash around his waist, dressed him in the robe, put the ephod on him, and fastened it with its decorative sash.

8.text: Then Moses put the chestpiece on Aaron and placed the Urim and Thummim inside it.

9.text: He set the turban on Aaron's head and attached the gold medallion—the badge of holiness—to the front of the turban, just like the Lord commanded.

10.text: Then Moses took the anointing oil and anointed the Tabernacle and everything in it, making them holy.

11.text: He sprinkled the oil on the altar seven times, anointing it, all its tools, the washbasin, and its stand to make them holy.

12.text: Then he poured some of the anointing oil on Aaron's head, anointing him to set him apart for his work.

13.text: Next, Moses brought Aaron's sons forward. He dressed them in their tunics, tied their sashes around them, and put special head coverings on them, just as the Lord commanded.

14.text: Then Moses brought out the bull for the sin offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.

15.text: Moses killed the bull and took some of the blood, putting it on the four horns of the altar with his finger to purify it. Then he poured out the rest of the blood at the base of the altar to make it holy.

16.text: Moses then took all the fat around the internal organs, the long lobe of the liver, and the two kidneys with their fat, and burned them on the altar.

17.text: But the rest of the bull—including its hide, meat, and dung—was burned outside the camp, just like the Lord commanded.

18.text: Then Moses brought out the ram for the burnt offering, and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.

19.text: Moses slaughtered the ram and splattered its blood on all sides of the altar.

20.text: Then he cut the ram into pieces and burned the head, the pieces, and the fat on the altar.

21.text: After washing the internal organs and legs with water, Moses burned the whole ram on the altar. It was a burnt offering, a pleasing smell, a special gift to the Lord, just as He commanded.

22.text: Then Moses brought out the second ram—the ordination ram—and Aaron and his sons laid their hands on its head.

23.text: Moses slaughtered it, then took some of its blood and put it on Aaron's right ear, right thumb, and right big toe.

24.text: Then Moses did the same for Aaron's sons, putting the blood on their right ears, right thumbs, and right big toes. Then he splattered the rest of the blood on all sides of the altar.

25.text: Then Moses took the fat from the broad tail, the fat around the internal organs, the long lobe of the liver, the two kidneys with their fat, and the right thigh.

26.text: On top of that, he placed a thin cake of bread made without yeast, a cake of bread mixed with olive oil, and a wafer spread with oil—all taken from the special basket in the Lord's presence.

27.text: He put all these in Aaron and his sons' hands and lifted them up as a special offering to the Lord.

28.text: Then Moses took all the offerings back and burned them on the altar, on top of the burnt offering. This was the ordination offering, a pleasing smell and a special gift to the Lord.

29.text: Then Moses took the breast of the ram and lifted it up as a special offering. That was his portion of the ordination offering, just like the Lord commanded.

30.text: Then Moses took some of the anointing oil and some of the blood from the altar and sprinkled them on Aaron and his sons, along with their robes. This made them and their garments holy.

31.text: Then Moses told Aaron and his sons, 'Boil the rest of the meat at the Tabernacle entrance and eat it there, along with the bread from the ordination basket, just like the Lord commanded.'

32.text: If there's any leftover meat or bread, it must be completely burned up.

33.text: You can't leave the Tabernacle entrance for seven days—this is how long the ordination ceremony lasts.

34.text: Everything we did today was commanded by the Lord to purify you and make you right with Him.

35.text: Now, y'all gotta stay at the entrance of the Tabernacle day and night for seven days and do everything the Lord requires. If y'all don't follow through, you will die—that's the Lord's command.

36.text: So Aaron and his sons did everything the Lord commanded through Moses.

1.text: After the ordination ceremony, on the eighth day, Moses called Aaron, his sons, and the elders of Israel together.
