2.text: Moses told Aaron, 'Go get a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering. Both gotta be flawless. Present them to the Lord.'

3.text: Then tell the Israelites, 'Bring a male goat for a sin offering. Also, bring a calf and a lamb, both a year old and without defects, for a burnt offering.'

4.text: Bring a bull and a ram for a peace offering, along with some flour mixed with olive oil for a grain offering. Present all this to the Lord, cause He gon' show up today.'

5.text: So the people brought everything to the entrance of the Tabernacle, just like Moses commanded. Then the whole community came forward and stood before the Lord.

6.text: Moses told them, 'This is what the Lord said to do, so His glory can show up among y'all.'

7.text: Then Moses told Aaron, 'Go up to the altar and sacrifice your sin offering and burnt offering to purify yourself and the people. Then offer the people's sacrifices so they can be made right with the Lord, just like He commanded.'

8.text: So Aaron stepped up to the altar and killed the calf for his own sin offering.

9.text: His sons brought him the blood, and he dipped his finger in it and put it on the horns of the altar. Then he poured the rest of the blood at the base of the altar.

10.text: Aaron burned the fat, kidneys, and the long lobe of the liver from the sin offering on the altar, just like the Lord told Moses.

11.text: But the rest of the bull—its meat and hide—he burned outside the camp.

12.text: Then Aaron killed the animal for the burnt offering. His sons brought him the blood, and he splattered it on all sides of the altar.

13.text: Then they handed him each piece of the burnt offering, including the head, and Aaron burned them on the altar.

14.text: He washed the internal organs and the legs, then burned them on the altar along with the rest of the burnt offering.

15.text: Next, Aaron presented the people's offerings. He killed the goat for their sin offering, just like he did for his own.

16.text: Then he presented the burnt offering and sacrificed it just like the Lord commanded.

17.text: He also presented the grain offering, burning a handful of the flour mixture on the altar, along with the usual morning burnt offering.

18.text: Then Aaron killed the bull and ram for the people's peace offering. His sons brought him the blood, and he splattered it on all sides of the altar.

19.text: Then he took the fat of the bull and ram—the broad tail, the fat around the internal organs, the kidneys, and the long lobes of the livers.

20.text: He placed the fat on top of the breasts of the animals and burned them on the altar.

21.text: Aaron then lifted up the breasts and right thighs as a special offering to the Lord, just like Moses commanded.

22.text: After that, Aaron raised his hands toward the people and blessed them. Then, after offering the sin offering, the burnt offering, and the peace offering, he stepped down from the altar.

23.text: Moses and Aaron then went inside the Tabernacle. When they came back out, they blessed the people again, and the glory of the Lord appeared to the whole community.

24.text: Suddenly, fire blazed out from the Lord's presence and burned up the burnt offering and the fat on the altar. When the people saw it, they shouted for joy and fell face down on the ground.

1.text: Aaron's sons, Nadab and Abihu, grabbed their incense burners, put hot coals in them, and sprinkled incense over the top. But they disobeyed the Lord by burning the wrong kind of fire—something He ain't never told them to do.

2.text: So fire shot out from the Lord's presence and burned them up right there, and they died before the Lord.

3.text: Then Moses told Aaron, 'This what the Lord meant when He said: I will show My holiness through those close to Me. I will let My glory be known to all the people.' Aaron ain't say a word.

4.text: Then Moses called for Mishael and Elzaphan, Aaron's cousins (the sons of Uzziel, Aaron's uncle). He told them, 'Come get your kinfolk and take them outside the camp.'

5.text: So they came forward, picked up the bodies by their clothes, and carried them out the camp, just like Moses told them.

6.text: Then Moses told Aaron and his sons, Eleazar and Ithamar, 'Don't show y'all mourning by messing up your hair or tearing your clothes. If you do, you'll die, and God's anger gonna hit the whole community. But the rest of the Israelites—your family—they can mourn for Nadab and Abihu and how the Lord struck them down.'

7.text: 'But y'all can't leave the entrance of the Tabernacle or you'll die, cause you been anointed with the Lord's oil.' So they did what Moses said.

8.text: Then the Lord spoke directly to Aaron,

9.text: 'You and your descendants must never drink wine or alcohol before coming into the Tabernacle. If y'all do, you'll die. This rule is permanent and applies to every generation.'

10.text: 'You gotta be able to tell the difference between what's holy and what's regular, between what's clean and what's unclean.'

11.text: 'And you gotta teach the Israelites all the Lord's commands that He gave through Moses.'

12.text: Then Moses told Aaron and his remaining sons, Eleazar and Ithamar, 'Take what's left of the grain offering, after the portion given to the Lord, and eat it beside the altar. It can't have yeast, cause it's most holy.'

13.text: 'You gotta eat it in a sacred place, cause it's y'all's share of the special gifts given to the Lord. That's what God commanded.'

14.text: 'But the breast and thigh that were lifted as a special offering? Y'all can eat them anywhere that's ceremonially clean. These parts are for y'all and y'all descendants as part of the peace offerings given by Israel.'

15.text: 'You gotta lift up the thigh and breast as a special offering to the Lord, along with the fat. These parts belong to y'all forever, just like the Lord commanded.'

16.text: Then Moses started looking for the goat that was offered as a sin offering. When he realized they burned it up, he got mad at Eleazar and Ithamar, Aaron's remaining sons.

17.text: 'Why ain't y'all eat the sin offering in the sacred area?' he demanded. 'That offering is holy! The Lord gave it to y'all to remove the people's guilt and purify them, making them right with Him.'

18.text: 'Since its blood wasn't brought inside the Holy Place, y'all should've eaten the meat in the sacred area, like I told y'all to!'

19.text: But Aaron told Moses, 'Look, today my sons gave their sin offering and burnt offering to the Lord. But then this tragedy happened to me. If I had eaten the people's sin offering today, do you really think the Lord would've been pleased?'

20.text: When Moses heard that, he let it go.

1.text: Then the Lord told Moses and Aaron,

2.text: 'Tell the people of Israel: These are the animals y'all can eat from all the land animals.'

3.text: 'You can eat any animal that has completely split hooves and chews the cud.'

4.text: 'But y'all can't eat these animals, cause they either chew the cud or have split hooves, but not both. The camel chews the cud but don't have split hooves, so it's unclean for y'all.'

5.text: 'The hyrax chews the cud but don't have split hooves, so it's unclean for y'all.'

6.text: 'The hare chews the cud but don't have split hooves, so it's unclean.'

7.text: 'The pig got split hooves, but it don't chew the cud, so it's unclean.'

8.text: 'Y'all can't eat these animals or even touch their dead bodies—they unclean for y'all.'

9.text: 'Y'all can eat anything that comes from the water if it has fins and scales, whether it's from the sea or a river.'

10.text: 'But y'all must never eat creatures from the water that don't have both fins and scales. They nasty to y'all.'

11.text: 'They will always be nasty to y'all. Don't eat their meat or touch their dead bodies.'

12.text: 'If it don't have fins and scales, it's nasty to y'all.'

13.text: 'These are the birds y'all can't eat—they nasty: griffon vulture, bearded vulture, black vulture,'

14.text: 'Kite, falcons of all kinds,'

15.text: 'Ravens of all kinds,'

16.text: 'Eagle owl, short-eared owl, seagull, hawks of all kinds,'

17.text: 'Little owl, cormorant, great owl,'

18.text: 'Barn owl, desert owl, Egyptian vulture,'

19.text: 'Stork, herons of all kinds, hoopoe, and bats.'

20.text: 'Don't eat any winged insects that walk on the ground—they nasty to y'all.'

21.text: 'But y'all can eat winged insects that got jointed legs to help them jump.'

22.text: 'Y'all can eat locusts, bald locusts, crickets, and grasshoppers.'

23.text: 'But all other insects that walk on the ground are nasty.'

24.text: 'These creatures will make y'all ceremonially unclean. If you touch their dead bodies, you unclean until evening.'

25.text: 'If you pick up their carcasses, you gotta wash your clothes, and you unclean till evening.'

26.text: 'Any animal with split hooves that ain't evenly divided, or that don't chew cud, is unclean for y'all. Touch it, and you unclean.'

27.text: 'Any four-legged animal with paws is unclean. If you touch its dead body, you unclean till evening.'

28.text: 'If you pick up its carcass, you gotta wash your clothes and you unclean till evening. These animals are unclean for y'all.'

29.text: 'These small creatures that scurry around are unclean: mole rat, rat, and all lizards,'

30.text: 'Gecko, monitor lizard, common lizard, sand lizard, and chameleon.'

31.text: 'All these little animals are unclean. If you touch one of them dead, you unclean till evening.'

32.text: 'If one of them dies and falls on something, that thing is unclean—whether it's wood, cloth, leather, or burlap. You gotta dip it in water, and it stays unclean till evening. Then it's clean again.'

33.text: 'If one of these animals falls into a clay pot, everything inside is unclean, and the pot must be smashed.'

34.text: 'If the water from that pot spills on food, that food is unclean. If you drinking from that pot, the drink is unclean.'

35.text: 'If the dead body of one of these animals falls on something, it's unclean—whether it's an oven or a stove, it gotta be destroyed cause it's contaminated.'

36.text: 'But if it falls into a spring or well, the water is still clean. But if somebody touches the dead body, they unclean.'

37.text: 'If the dead body lands on dry seed grain, the grain is still clean.'

38.text: 'But if the seed is wet when the dead body lands on it, the seed is unclean.'

39.text: 'If an animal y'all can eat dies and you touch its dead body, you unclean till evening.'

40.text: 'If you eat the meat or carry its carcass, you gotta wash your clothes and stay unclean till evening.'

41.text: 'All small animals that scurry on the ground nasty to y'all. Don't eat them.'

42.text: 'That includes animals that crawl on their bellies, walk on four legs, or got too many legs to count—don't eat none of them.'

43.text: 'Don't make y'all selves unclean by touching them or eating them.'

44.text: 'Cause I am the Lord your God, and y'all gotta set yourselves apart and be holy, cause I am holy. So don't defile y'all selves with these creatures.'

45.text: 'I'm the one who brought y'all outta Egypt so I could be your God. That's why y'all gotta be holy—cause I'm holy.'

46.text: 'These are the official rules about land animals, birds, marine creatures, and ground animals.'

47.text: 'These rules let y'all know what's clean and unclean, and what animals can and can't be eaten.'

1.text: Then the Lord told Moses,

2.text: 'Tell the people of Israel: If a woman gets pregnant and has a son, she gonna be ceremonially unclean for seven days, just like when she on her period.'

3.text: 'On the eighth day, the baby boy gotta be circumcised.'

4.text: 'Then she gotta wait thirty-three days to be purified from the bleeding of childbirth. During this time, she can't touch anything holy or enter the sanctuary till her purification time is over.'

5.text: 'If she has a daughter, she will be unclean for two weeks, just like during her period. Then she gotta wait sixty-six days to be purified from childbirth.'

6.text: 'When her purification time is completed—whether she had a son or a daughter—she gotta bring a one-year-old lamb for a burnt offering and a young pigeon or turtledove for a purification offering.'

7.text: 'She gotta take these offerings to the priest at the entrance of the Tabernacle. The priest will present them before the Lord to purify her. After that, she will be clean again from the bleeding of childbirth.'

8.text: 'These are the rules for a woman after giving birth to a son or daughter.'

1.text: The Lord pulled up on Moses and Aaron and said,

2.text: "If somebody got a bump, a scab, or a light spot on their skin that look like it could be something serious, they need to go see Aaron the priest or one of his sons.

3.text: The priest gotta check them out—if the hair in that spot turned white and it look deep, like it's sitting under the skin, that's leprosy. The priest gotta call it like it is—unclean.

4.text: But if the spot ain't deep and the hair ain't turned white, then the priest gotta put them in quarantine for seven days.

5.text: On the seventh day, the priest gotta check again. If the spot ain't changed or spread, then he gotta isolate them for another seven days.

6.text: After another seven days, if the spot faded and ain't spread, the priest can clear them—it's just a scab. They gotta wash their clothes and they good.

7.text: But if that scab start spreading after the priest already checked them, they gotta go back.

8.text: If the priest sees it spreading for real, he gotta call it—unclean. That's leprosy.

9.text: If somebody got full-on leprosy, they gotta be brought to the priest.

10.text: The priest gotta check for swelling, white hair, and raw flesh inside the sore.

11.text: If all that's there, that's an old case of leprosy. Ain't no need to quarantine, they just straight-up unclean.

12.text: But if the leprosy done spread everywhere, from head to toe,

13.text: And it's all turned white, then the priest gotta check them and say, "You clean."

14.text: But if some raw flesh shows up, they unclean again.

15.text: If the priest sees that raw flesh, they gotta call it unclean, 'cause that means it's active.

16.text: If the raw flesh goes away and turns white, they gotta go back to the priest.

17.text: The priest gotta check them again—if it's all white now, they clean.

18.text: If somebody had a boil that healed up,

19.text: But then a white or reddish-white bump pops up where the boil was, they gotta see the priest.

20.text: If the priest sees white hair in it and it looks deep, he gotta call it unclean—it's a leprous sore from that boil.

21.text: But if the hair ain't white and it don't look deep, just a little faded, the priest gotta quarantine them for seven days.

22.text: If it spreads, they unclean.

23.text: But if it stays put, it's just a scar—they clean.

24.text: If somebody got burned and a reddish-white or white sore shows up in the burn,

25.text: The priest gotta check it out. If the hair in it turned white and it looks deep, that's leprosy from the burn. They unclean.

26.text: But if the hair ain't white and it ain't deep, just faded, they gotta be quarantined for seven days.

27.text: If it spreads, they unclean.

28.text: But if it stays put and don't spread, it's just a burn scar—they clean.

29.text: If somebody got a sore on their head or beard,

30.text: The priest gotta check if it's deep and got thin yellow hair in it. If so, that's a serious scalp disease—they unclean.

31.text: If it ain't deep and no yellow hair, quarantine them for seven days.

32.text: After seven days, if it ain't spread and no yellow hair grew,

33.text: They gotta shave everything but the sore, then stay quarantined another seven days.

34.text: If after that it still ain't spread and don't look deep, they clean—just gotta wash their clothes.

35.text: But if it spreads after they been cleared,

36.text: They unclean, no need to check for yellow hair.

37.text: If the sore stops spreading and black hair grows back, then they good.

38.text: If somebody got white spots on their skin,

39.text: The priest gotta check. If they just dull white patches, that's just a harmless skin condition—they clean.

40.text: If a man loses his hair and goes bald, he still clean.

41.text: If he just losing hair from the front, he still clean.

42.text: But if a reddish-white sore shows up on his bald head,

43.text: The priest gotta check—if it looks like leprosy,

44.text: Then that man got leprosy and he unclean. The priest gotta say it straight.

45.text: Anybody who got leprosy gotta wear torn clothes, let their hair stay wild, cover their mouth, and yell "Unclean! Unclean!"

46.text: As long as they got it, they unclean. They gotta live outside the camp, away from everybody else.

47.text: If a piece of clothing—whether wool, linen,

48.text: Or anything made from leather—

49.text: Starts getting weird greenish or reddish spots,

50.text: The priest gotta check it and quarantine it for seven days.

51.text: If the spots spread after seven days, it's unclean—active disease in the fabric.

52.text: That garment gotta be burned.

53.text: But if the spots ain't spread,

54.text: The priest gotta tell them to wash it, then isolate it another seven days.

55.text: If the stain don't fade after washing, it's still unclean—it gotta be burned.

56.text: But if it fades, they can cut the stained part out.

57.text: If the stain comes back, burn the whole thing.

58.text: If after another wash, the stain don't return, it's clean.

59.text: This is the rule for checking clothes to see if they clean or unclean.

1.text: Then the Lord told Moses,

2.text: 'These are the rules for somebody trying to get ceremonially clean after a skin disease. Once they healed, they gotta go to the priest.'

3.text: 'The priest will check them outside the camp. If he sees they healed, he will do a purification ceremony.'

4.text: 'For the ceremony, he needs two clean birds, a cedar stick, some scarlet yarn, and a hyssop branch.'

5.text: 'One bird gotta be killed over a clay pot filled with fresh water.'

6.text: 'Then the priest will take the live bird, the cedar stick, the scarlet yarn, and the hyssop branch and dip them into the blood of the bird that was killed.'

7.text: 'Then he'll sprinkle the blood seven times on the person being purified. After that, he'll set the live bird free in the open field.'

8.text: 'The person getting clean gotta wash their clothes, shave all their hair, and take a bath. Then they can return to camp, but they gotta stay outside their tent for seven days.'

9.text: 'On the seventh day, they gotta shave everything again—their head, beard, eyebrows—then wash their clothes and bathe again. After that, they clean.'

10.text: 'On the eighth day, they gotta bring: Two male lambs, One female lamb (a year old), A grain offering (six quarts of flour with olive oil), A cup of olive oil'

11.text: 'The priest will present them before the Lord at the Tabernacle entrance.'

12.text: 'Then he'll take one male lamb and the olive oil and offer them as a guilt offering, lifting them up as a special gift to the Lord.'

13.text: 'He will kill the lamb in the sacred area where sin and burnt offerings are made. Just like the sin offering, the guilt offering belongs to the priest—it's most holy.'

14.text: 'The priest will take some of the blood and put it on: The right earlobe, The right thumb, The right big toe of the person being purified.'

15.text: 'Then the priest will pour olive oil into his left hand.'

16.text: 'He'll dip his right finger in the oil and sprinkle it seven times before the Lord.'

17.text: 'Then he'll take some of the oil and put it on top of the blood that's on the person's right ear, right thumb, and right big toe.'

18.text: 'The rest of the oil in his hand will be put on the person's head to complete the purification before the Lord.'

19.text: 'Next, the priest will offer the sin offering to purify them. After that, he'll slaughter the burnt offering.'

20.text: 'The priest will burn the burnt offering and grain offering on the altar. After all that, the person will be fully clean.'

21.text: 'If somebody can't afford all that, they can bring: One male lamb for the guilt offering, Two quarts of flour with olive oil for the grain offering, A cup of olive oil'

22.text: 'And instead of three lambs, they can bring two turtledoves or two pigeons—one for a sin offering and one for a burnt offering.'

23.text: 'On the eighth day, they must take these offerings to the priest at the Tabernacle entrance.'

24.text: 'The priest will take the guilt offering lamb and the olive oil and lift them up as a special offering to the Lord.'

25.text: 'Then he'll kill the lamb and take some blood and put it on: The right earlobe, The right thumb, The right big toe of the person being purified.'

26.text: 'Then the priest will pour olive oil into his left hand.'

27.text: 'He'll dip his right finger in the oil and sprinkle it seven times before the Lord.'

28.text: 'Then he'll put some of the oil on top of the blood on the right ear, right thumb, and right big toe.'

29.text: 'The rest of the oil goes on the person's head to complete the purification.'

30.text: 'Then the priest will sacrifice the two birds—one for a sin offering and one for a burnt offering—along with the grain offering.'

31.text: 'That's how the priest makes them clean before the Lord.'

32.text: 'These are the rules for people who had a skin disease but can't afford the full offering.'

33.text: Then the Lord told Moses and Aaron,

34.text: 'When y'all get to Canaan, the land I'm giving y'all, I might allow mildew to show up in some houses.'

35.text: 'If a homeowner sees mildew, they gotta go to the priest and say, "It looks like my house got mildew."'

36.text: 'Before checking it out, the priest will tell them to empty the house so nothing inside gets pronounced unclean.'

37.text: 'Then the priest will inspect the house. If the mildew got green or red streaks and goes deeper than the surface,'

38.text: 'The priest will step outside and quarantine the house for seven days.'

39.text: 'On the seventh day, he'll check again. If the mildew spread,'

40.text: 'He'll order the infected stones to be removed and taken outside the town to an unclean place.'

41.text: 'The rest of the house must be scraped clean, and the debris dumped in the unclean place.'

42.text: 'Then new stones must replace the old ones, and the house must be replastered.'

43.text: 'But if mildew comes back after all that,'

44.text: 'The priest must inspect again. If it's still spreading, the house is unclean.'

45.text: 'That house must be torn down—all the stones, wood, and plaster must be taken outside the town to the unclean place.'

46.text: 'Anybody who enters the house while it's quarantined is unclean till evening.'

47.text: 'Anybody who sleeps or eats in that house gotta wash their clothes.'

48.text: 'If the mildew ain't come back after the house was fixed up, the priest will declare it clean.'

49.text: 'To purify a house, the priest needs: Two birds, A cedar stick, Scarlet yarn, A hyssop branch'

50.text: 'One bird will be killed over a clay pot with fresh water.'

51.text: 'Then the priest will dip the live bird, cedar stick, scarlet yarn, and hyssop branch in the blood and water and sprinkle the house seven times.'

52.text: 'That's how the house gets purified.'

53.text: 'Then the live bird is set free in the open fields, and the house will be ceremonially clean.'

54.text: 'These are the rules for dealing with skin diseases, sores,'

55.text: 'Mildew in clothes and houses,'

56.text: 'And any kind of rash or skin swelling.'

57.text: 'This is how to tell what's clean and unclean.'

1.text: Then the Lord told Moses and Aaron,

2.text: "Tell the people of Israel: If a man got a bodily discharge, he is ceremonially unclean."

3.text: "Whether the discharge keeps going or stops, he still unclean."

4.text: "Any bed he lies on and anything he sits on is unclean."

5.text: "If you touch his bed, you gotta wash your clothes, bathe in water, and you unclean till evening."

6.text: "If you sit where he sat, same thing—wash your clothes, bathe, and stay unclean till evening."

7.text: "If you touch him, you gotta wash your clothes, bathe, and stay unclean till evening."

8.text: "If he spits on you, you gotta wash your clothes, bathe, and stay unclean till evening."

9.text: "Any saddle blanket he rides on is unclean."

10.text: "If you touch anything that was under him, you unclean till evening. Wash your clothes and bathe."

11.text: "If he touches you without washing his hands first, you gotta wash your clothes, bathe, and stay unclean till evening."

12.text: "If he touches a clay pot, it gotta be smashed. If it's a wooden object, it must be rinsed with water."

13.text: "Once his discharge stops, he gotta wait seven days to be fully clean. Then he gotta wash his clothes, bathe in fresh water, and then he clean."

14.text: "On the eighth day, he must bring two turtledoves or two pigeons to the Tabernacle and give them to the priest."

15.text: "The priest will sacrifice one bird as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering to purify him before the Lord."

16.text: "If a man has an emission of semen, he gotta bathe his whole body in water and stay unclean till evening."

17.text: "Any clothes or leather that got semen on it must be washed, and they unclean till evening."

18.text: "If a man and woman have sex, both of them gotta bathe and stay unclean till evening."

19.text: "If a woman on her period, she unclean for seven days. Anybody who touches her is unclean till evening."

20.text: "Anything she lies on or sits on is unclean."

21.text: "If you touch her bed, you gotta wash your clothes, bathe, and stay unclean till evening."

22.text: "If you touch anything she sat on, same thing—wash your clothes, bathe, and stay unclean till evening."

23.text: "If you even touch her bed or anything she sat on, you unclean till evening."

24.text: "If a man has sex with her while she bleeding, he is unclean for seven days, and any bed he lies on is also unclean."

25.text: "If a woman has bleeding that lasts longer than her period, or comes at the wrong time, she is unclean as long as the blood keeps flowing."

26.text: "Anything she lies on or sits on is unclean, just like during her regular period."

27.text: "If you touch her bed or anything she sat on, you gotta wash your clothes, bathe, and stay unclean till evening."

28.text: "Once her bleeding stops, she must wait seven days, then she is clean."

29.text: "On the eighth day, she must bring two turtledoves or two pigeons to the priest at the Tabernacle entrance."

30.text: "The priest will sacrifice one as a sin offering and the other as a burnt offering to purify her before the Lord."

31.text: "This is how y'all keep the people of Israel from becoming unclean and defiling My Tabernacle. If they don't follow these rules, they could die."

32.text: "These are the instructions for handling anybody with a bodily discharge—including men who have semen emissions"

33.text: "Women on their periods, people with other discharges, and men who have sex with women during their period."

1.text: The Lord spoke to Moses after Aaron's two sons died for offering the wrong kind of fire before Him.

2.text: The Lord told Moses, 'Warn Aaron not to enter the Most Holy Place whenever he wants. If he does, he'll die. That's where the Ark's cover—the place of atonement—is, and I Myself am there in the cloud above it.'

3.text: 'When Aaron enters the sanctuary, he must bring a young bull for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering.'

4.text: 'He gotta put on his linen tunic, linen undergarments, linen sash, and linen turban—these are sacred garments. But before he puts them on, he must bathe in water.'

5.text: 'Aaron must take from Israel's community two male goats for a sin offering and a ram for a burnt offering.'

6.text: 'Aaron must sacrifice his own bull to make atonement for himself and his family.'

7.text: 'Then, he must take the two male goats and present them before the Lord at the Tabernacle entrance.'

8.text: 'He must cast lots to decide which goat is for the Lord and which will be sent into the wilderness of Azazel.'

9.text: 'The goat chosen for the Lord will be offered as a sin offering.'

10.text: 'The scapegoat will be kept alive, then sent into the wilderness to carry away the people's sins.'

11.text: 'Aaron must offer his own bull as a sin offering for himself and his family.'

12.text: 'Then, he will take a censer filled with burning coals from the altar and two handfuls of fragrant incense and bring them behind the inner curtain.'

13.text: 'He must put the incense on the burning coals so the cloud of incense covers the Ark's atonement cover—otherwise, he will die.'

14.text: 'Then, he must take some of the bull's blood and sprinkle it seven times on the Ark's atonement cover.'

15.text: 'Next, Aaron must kill the first goat as a sin offering for the people and bring its blood behind the inner curtain.'

16.text: 'By doing this, he will purify the Most Holy Place and the whole Tabernacle from the sins of Israel.'

17.text: 'Nobody else is allowed inside the Tabernacle while Aaron does this purification. He must atone for himself, his family, and all the Israelites.'

18.text: 'Then Aaron must go to the altar and purify it with the blood of the bull and the goat.'

19.text: 'He must sprinkle the blood on the altar seven times to cleanse it from Israel's sins.'

20.text: 'When Aaron is done purifying the Most Holy Place, the Tabernacle, and the altar, he must bring forward the live goat.'

21.text: 'He will lay both hands on the goat's head and confess all of Israel's sins, wickedness, and rebellion over it—transferring their sins onto the goat.'

22.text: 'Then, a chosen man will lead the goat into the wilderness. As it goes, it will carry all of Israel's sins into a desolate land.'

23.text: 'After that, Aaron must go back into the Tabernacle, take off his linen garments, and leave them there.'

24.text: 'Then he must bathe in a sacred place, put on his regular clothes, and go out to sacrifice the burnt offering for himself and the people.'

25.text: 'He must burn all the fat of the sin offering on the altar.'

26.text: 'The man who led the scapegoat into the wilderness must wash his clothes, bathe, and then he can return to camp.'

27.text: 'The bull and the goat that were used for the sin offering must be taken outside the camp and burned completely—including their hides, organs, and dung.'

28.text: 'The person who burns them must wash their clothes, bathe, and then return to camp.'

29.text: 'On the tenth day of the seventh month, everyone must deny themselves (fast) and do no work—this applies to Israelites and foreigners alike. This is a permanent law.'

30.text: 'On this day, the priest will perform the atonement ceremony to purify y'all before the Lord and cleanse y'all from all your sins.'

31.text: 'It will be a Sabbath day of complete rest, and y'all must humble yourselves. This is a permanent law.'

32.text: 'Every year, the priest who is anointed and ordained to replace Aaron must carry out this atonement ritual. He must wear the holy linen garments.'

33.text: 'He must purify the Most Holy Place, the Tabernacle, the altar, the priests, and all the people of Israel.'

34.text: 'This must be done once every year to purify Israel from their sins and make them right with the Lord.'

35.text: Moses did everything exactly as the Lord commanded.

1.text: Then the Lord told Moses,

2.text: 'Tell Aaron, his sons, and all the people of Israel what I'm commanding.'

3.text: 'If any Israelite sacrifices a bull, lamb, or goat anywhere inside or outside the camp,'

4.text: 'Instead of bringing it to the Tabernacle entrance to offer it to the Lord, that person is as guilty as a murderer. They have shed blood and will be cut off from the community.'

5.text: 'This law is to stop folks from sacrificing animals out in the open fields and to make sure they bring them to the priest at the Tabernacle.'

6.text: 'Then the priest will splatter the blood against the altar at the Tabernacle entrance and burn the fat as a pleasing aroma to the Lord.'

7.text: 'The people must stop sacrificing to goat idols—that's unfaithful to the Lord. This rule stays forever, for every generation.'

8.text: 'Tell them this too: If any Israelite or foreigner brings a burnt offering or sacrifice,'

9.text: 'But don't bring it to the Tabernacle entrance to offer it to the Lord, that person will be cut off from the community.'

10.text: 'If any Israelite or foreigner eats or drinks blood in any form, I will turn against them and cut them off from the community.'

11.text: 'Cause the life of the body is in the blood. I gave y'all blood to use on the altar to purify you and make you right with Me. Blood is given in exchange for a life, and that's how purification works.'

12.text: 'That's why I told Israel: Never eat or drink blood—this goes for y'all and any foreigners among you.'

13.text: 'If an Israelite or foreigner goes hunting and kills an approved animal or bird for food, they must drain its blood and cover it with dirt.'

14.text: 'Cause life is in the blood—that's why y'all must never eat or drink blood. If anybody does, they will be cut off from the community.'

15.text: 'If any Israelite or foreigner eats meat from an animal that died naturally or was torn up by wild animals, they gotta wash their clothes and bathe in water. They unclean till evening, then they clean.'

16.text: 'But if they don't wash their clothes or bathe, they gonna be punished for their sin.'

1.text: Then the Lord told Moses,

2.text: 'Tell the people of Israel: I am the Lord your God.'

3.text: 'Don't act like the people in Egypt, where y'all used to live, or like the people in Canaan, where I'm taking y'all. Don't copy their lifestyle.'

4.text: 'Follow My rules and be careful to obey My laws, cause I am the Lord your God.'

5.text: 'If y'all follow My laws and decrees, y'all will find life through them. I am the Lord.'

6.text: 'Y'all must never have sex with a close relative. I am the Lord.'

7.text: 'Don't violate your father by sleeping with your mother. She is your mother—don't do it.'

8.text: 'Don't have sex with any of your father's wives, cause that's violating your father.'

9.text: 'Don't have sex with your sister or half-sister—whether she's your dad's daughter or your mom's daughter, whether she grew up in your house or not.'

10.text: 'Don't have sex with your granddaughter, whether she comes from your son or your daughter—that's violating yourself.'

11.text: 'Don't have sex with your stepsister (your father's wife's daughter)—she is still your sister.'

12.text: 'Don't have sex with your father's sister (your aunt)—she's close family.'

13.text: 'Don't have sex with your mother's sister (your aunt)—she's close family.'

14.text: 'Don't violate your uncle by sleeping with his wife—she is your aunt.'

15.text: 'Don't have sex with your daughter-in-law—she is your son's wife, and you shouldn't touch her.'

16.text: 'Don't have sex with your brother's wife—that's violating your brother.'

17.text: 'Don't sleep with both a woman and her daughter. And don't sleep with her granddaughter, whether from her son or daughter—that's wicked.'

18.text: 'While your wife is still alive, don't marry her sister and have sex with her—cause that would cause rivalry.'

19.text: 'Don't have sex with a woman while she's on her period—that makes you unclean.'

20.text: 'Don't sleep with your neighbor's wife—that makes you impure.'

21.text: 'Don't sacrifice any of your children to Molech, cause that brings shame on My name. I am the Lord.'

22.text: 'Don't practice homosexuality, having sex with another man like you would with a woman. It's a detestable sin.'

23.text: 'A man must not have sex with an animal, and a woman must never offer herself to an animal for sex. That's perverse.'

24.text: 'Don't defile y'all selves in these ways, cause the people I'm driving out ahead of you have already corrupted themselves doing this.'

25.text: 'The whole land is polluted, so I'm punishing the folks who live there—the land itself is gonna vomit them out.'

26.text: 'Y'all must follow all My laws. Don't commit any of these detestable sins—this applies to both Israelites and foreigners living with y'all.'

27.text: 'The folks in this land have already done all this nasty stuff, and that's how the land got defiled.'

28.text: 'If y'all do the same, the land will vomit y'all out just like it's doing to the people before you.'

29.text: 'Anybody who commits these detestable sins will be cut off from the community.'

30.text: 'So follow My instructions and don't defile y'all selves with these nasty practices. The folks before y'all did them, and they ruined the land.' I am the Lord your God.

1.text: Then the Lord told Moses,

2.text: 'Tell the whole community of Israel: Y'all must be holy, cause I, the Lord your God, am holy.'

3.text: 'Respect your mother and father, and always observe My Sabbath days. I am the Lord your God.'

4.text: 'Don't put your trust in idols or make metal images of fake gods. I am the Lord your God.'

5.text: 'When y'all offer a peace offering, do it properly so the Lord accepts it.'

6.text: 'Eat the sacrifice on the same day or the next day. If there's any left on the third day, burn it up completely.'

7.text: 'If anybody eats it on the third day, it's contaminated, and I won't accept it.'

8.text: 'Whoever eats it will be punished for disrespecting what is holy—they will be cut off from the community.'

9.text: 'When y'all harvest your crops, don't collect every last bit—leave the edges of the fields alone. Don't pick up what falls to the ground.'

10.text: 'Same with your grapevines—don't strip them bare, and don't pick up fallen grapes. Leave them for the poor and foreigners. I am the Lord your God.'

11.text: 'Don't steal. Don't lie. Don't cheat each other.'

12.text: 'Don't swear falsely using My name—that disrespects Me. I am the Lord.'

13.text: 'Don't scam or rob your neighbor. Don't hold back your worker's pay until the next day—pay them on time.'

14.text: 'Don't disrespect the deaf or trip up the blind—fear your God. I am the Lord.'

15.text: 'Don't twist justice—don't favor the poor, and don't give the rich and powerful a pass. Always judge fairly.'

16.text: 'Don't spread gossip or slander among your people. Don't stand back and watch when your neighbor's life is in danger. I am the Lord.'

17.text: 'Don't hold hatred in your heart for your family. If somebody does wrong, confront them directly, so you don't share in their guilt.'

18.text: 'Don't seek revenge or hold grudges against your people. Love your neighbor as yourself. I am the Lord.'

19.text: 'Obey all My decrees: Don't mate different animals together. Don't plant two kinds of seed in the same field. Don't wear clothes woven from two different materials.'

20.text: 'If a man sleeps with a slave girl promised to another man, but she ain't free yet, he must pay her owner compensation. But since she ain't free, they won't be put to death.'

21.text: 'The man must bring a ram for a guilt offering to the Tabernacle.'

22.text: 'The priest will purify him before the Lord, and he will be forgiven.'

23.text: 'When y'all plant fruit trees in the land, don't eat from them for three years—the fruit is off-limits.'

24.text: 'In the fourth year, dedicate all the fruit to the Lord in a praise offering.'

25.text: 'In the fifth year, y'all can eat from it. This will make your harvest increase. I am the Lord your God.'

26.text: 'Don't eat meat with the blood still in it. Don't practice fortune-telling or witchcraft.'

27.text: 'Don't trim off the hair on your temples or shave the edges of your beard.'

28.text: 'Don't cut yourselves for the dead, and don't tattoo your body. I am the Lord.'

29.text: 'Don't turn your daughter into a prostitute, or the whole land will be full of wickedness.'

30.text: 'Keep My Sabbath days holy and show respect for My sanctuary. I am the Lord.'

31.text: 'Don't go to mediums or spiritists—don't defile yourselves with them. I am the Lord your God.'

32.text: 'Stand up and show respect for the elderly. Fear your God. I am the Lord.'

33.text: 'Don't mistreat foreigners living in your land.'

34.text: 'Treat them like one of your own. Love them as yourself, cause y'all were once foreigners in Egypt. I am the Lord your God.'

35.text: 'Don't cheat people with dishonest scales or measurements.'

36.text: 'Your weights, scales, and measuring cups must be accurate. I am the Lord your God, who brought you out of Egypt.'

37.text: 'Follow all My decrees and obey them carefully. I am the Lord.'

1.text: Then the Lord told Moses,

2.text: 'Tell the people of Israel: These rules apply to both Israelites and foreigners living among y'all.'

3.text: 'If anybody sacrifices their child to Molech, they must be put to death—the whole community must stone them.'

4.text: 'If the community ignores someone sacrificing their child to Molech and refuses to execute them,'

5.text: 'Then I Myself will turn against them and their whole family and cut them off from the community—cause they committed spiritual prostitution by worshiping Molech.'

6.text: 'I will also turn against anyone who seeks out mediums or spiritists to consult the dead—they will be cut off from the community.'

7.text: 'Set y'all selves apart and be holy, cause I am the Lord your God.'

8.text: 'Keep all My laws and actually do what I say, cause I am the Lord who makes you holy.'

9.text: 'Anybody who dishonors their parents must be put to death—that's a capital offense.'

10.text: 'If a man commits adultery with his neighbor's wife, both the man and the woman must be put to death.'

11.text: 'If a man sleeps with one of his father's wives, both him and the woman must be put to death. That's violating his father.'

12.text: 'If a man has sex with his daughter-in-law, they must be put to death. That's a perverse act.'

13.text: 'If a man sleeps with another man like he would with a woman, both of them have committed a detestable sin—they must be put to death.'

14.text: 'If a man marries both a woman and her mother, that's wicked. He and both women must be burned to death to wipe out that sin from among y'all.'

15.text: 'If a man has sex with an animal, he must be put to death, and the animal must be killed too.'

16.text: 'If a woman offers herself to an animal for sex, both her and the animal must be put to death.'

17.text: 'If a man marries his sister or half-sister and sleeps with her, that's shameful. They must be cut off from the community.'

18.text: 'If a man has sex with a woman while she on her period, both of them must be cut off from the community, cause they exposed her blood flow.'

19.text: 'Don't have sex with your aunt (either your mom's or dad's sister)—that's dishonoring a close relative. Both will be punished.'

20.text: 'If a man sleeps with his uncle's wife, he violated his uncle. Both will be punished, and they will die childless.'

21.text: 'If a man marries his brother's wife, that's impurity—he violated his brother. They will remain childless.'

22.text: 'Y'all must keep all My laws and actually live by them. Otherwise, the land I'm bringing y'all into will vomit you out.'

23.text: 'Don't live like the Canaanites—I'm kicking them out because they did all these shameful things.'

24.text: 'But I promised y'all: "You will possess this land, cause I'm giving it to you." It's a land flowing with milk and honey. I am the Lord your God, and I set y'all apart.'

25.text: 'So y'all must learn to tell the difference between clean and unclean animals. Don't defile yourselves by eating the unclean ones—I have already marked them as unclean for y'all.'

26.text: 'Be holy, cause I am holy. I set y'all apart from other nations so y'all can be My people.'

27.text: 'If any man or woman acts as a medium or consults spirits, they must be put to death by stoning. They are guilty of a capital offense.'

1.text: Then the Lord told Moses,

2.text: 'Tell the priests—the descendants of Aaron—these instructions: A priest can't make himself unclean by touching a dead body, except for his closest relatives.'

3.text: 'The only exceptions are his mother, father, son, daughter, brother, or his unmarried sister who depends on him cause she has no husband.'

4.text: 'But he can't make himself unclean for someone related only by marriage.'

5.text: 'Priests can't shave their heads, trim their beards, or cut their bodies.'

6.text: 'They must be set apart as holy and never bring shame on My name. They must stay holy cause they present the special gifts to Me—their God.'

7.text: 'A priest can't marry a woman who has been a prostitute or one who is divorced, cause they are set apart as holy.'

8.text: 'Treat them as holy cause they offer food to your God. Respect them cause I am the Lord, and I make y'all holy.'

9.text: 'If a priest's daughter becomes a prostitute, she dishonors her father's holiness—she must be burned to death.'

10.text: 'The High Priest is the top priest. He got anointing oil poured on him and wears the priestly garments. He can't leave his hair uncombed or tear his clothes.'

11.text: 'He can't go near a dead body or make himself unclean—not even for his mother or father.'

12.text: 'He must not defile the sanctuary of God by leaving to tend to the dead—he's been made holy by My anointing oil. I am the Lord.'

13.text: 'The High Priest must only marry a virgin.'

14.text: 'He can't marry a widow, a divorced woman, or a woman who was a prostitute. He must marry a virgin from his own people.'

15.text: 'That way, he won't dishonor his family line. I am the Lord who makes him holy.'

16.text: Then the Lord told Moses,

17.text: 'Tell Aaron: None of his descendants who got a physical defect can offer food to God at the altar.'

18.text: 'If they got any defect, they can't serve—whether they are blind, lame, disfigured, or deformed.'

19.text: 'If they got a broken foot or arm,'

20.text: 'Or if they are hunchbacked, dwarfed, have a defective eye, sores, scabs, or damaged testicles—they can't serve.'

21.text: 'No descendant of Aaron with a defect can come near the altar to offer food to God—they can't serve because of their condition.'

22.text: 'However, they can eat from the food offered to God, including the holy offerings and most holy offerings.'

23.text: 'But they can't enter the room behind the inner curtain or go near the altar cause that would dishonor My holy places. I am the Lord who makes them holy.'

24.text: So Moses told Aaron, his sons, and all of Israel these rules.

1.text: Then the Lord told Moses,

2.text: 'Tell Aaron and his sons to be careful with the sacred gifts that the Israelites offer to Me, so they don't disrespect My holy name. I am the Lord.'

3.text: 'From now on, if any priest is unclean and tries to handle the sacred offerings, he will be cut off from My presence. I am the Lord.'

4.text: 'If a priest has a skin disease or a discharge, he can't eat from the sacred offerings until he is clean.'

5.text: 'He also becomes unclean if he touches a dead body, has an emission of semen, touches an unclean animal, or touches someone else who is unclean.'

6.text: 'If a priest gets defiled like this, he will be unclean until evening. He can't eat from the sacred offerings until he bathes himself in water.'

7.text: 'Once the sun sets, he's clean again and can eat from the sacred offerings, cause that's his food.'

8.text: 'But he can't eat an animal that died on its own or was killed by wild animals—that would make him unclean. I am the Lord.'

9.text: 'The priests must follow My instructions carefully—if they don't, they will be punished and die for violating My rules. I am the Lord who makes them holy.'

10.text: 'Nobody outside a priest's family can eat the sacred offerings—not guests, not hired workers.'

11.text: 'But if a priest buys a slave, that slave can eat from the sacred offerings. If his slaves have kids, they can eat too.'

12.text: 'If a priest's daughter marries someone outside the priestly family, she can't eat the sacred offerings anymore.'

13.text: 'But if she becomes a widow or gets divorced and has no kids, and she moves back to her father's house, she can eat from his food again—but nobody else can.'

14.text: 'If somebody eats the sacred offerings by accident, they must pay the priest back for what they ate, plus an extra 20%.'

15.text: 'The priests must not let the Israelites dishonor the sacred offerings by letting unauthorized people eat them.'

16.text: 'If that happens, those people will carry guilt and must pay for their mistake. I am the Lord who makes them holy.'

17.text: Then the Lord told Moses,

18.text: 'Tell Aaron, his sons, and all the Israelites: If y'all bring a burnt offering to the Lord, whether it's to fulfill a vow or just a voluntary offering,'

19.text: 'It will only be accepted if it's a male animal with no defects—it can be a bull, a ram, or a goat.'

20.text: 'If it has any defect, don't bring it—the Lord won't accept it.'

21.text: 'If you bring a peace offering, it must be a perfect animal—no defects at all.'

22.text: 'Don't offer an animal that's blind, crippled, injured, has warts, skin sores, or scabs—these are not acceptable gifts.'

23.text: 'If a bull or lamb has one leg longer than the other, you can offer it as a voluntary offering but not to fulfill a vow.'

24.text: 'If an animal has damaged testicles or was castrated, don't offer it to the Lord—y'all must never do that.'

25.text: 'And don't take an animal from a foreigner and offer it to God—it won't be accepted cause it's mutilated or defective.'

26.text: Then the Lord told Moses,

27.text: 'When a calf, lamb, or goat is born, let it stay with its mother for seven days. After the eighth day, it's acceptable as an offering.'

28.text: 'But don't slaughter a mother animal and her baby on the same day.'

29.text: 'When you bring a thanksgiving offering, do it properly so God will accept it.'

30.text: 'Eat the whole sacrifice on the day you offer it—don't save any for the next morning. I am the Lord.'

31.text: 'Y'all must faithfully follow My commands and put them into practice—I am the Lord.'

32.text: 'Don't bring shame on My holy name—I will display My holiness among y'all. I am the Lord who makes you holy.'

33.text: 'I am the one who rescued y'all from Egypt so I could be your God. I am the Lord.'

1.text: Then the Lord told Moses,

2.text: 'Tell the people of Israel: These are My appointed festivals, official holy days where y'all must come together.'

3.text: 'For six days y'all can do your work, but the seventh day is a Sabbath of complete rest—a day for holy assembly.'

4.text: 'It don't matter where y'all live, this is the Lord's Sabbath, and it must be observed.'

5.text: 'The Lord's Passover begins at sundown on the fourteenth day of the first month.'

6.text: 'The next day, on the fifteenth day, y'all must start celebrating the Festival of Unleavened Bread. This festival lasts seven days, and y'all can only eat bread without yeast.'

7.text: 'On the first day, stop working and hold a holy assembly.'

8.text: 'For seven days, bring special offerings to the Lord. On the seventh day, stop working again and hold another holy assembly.'

9.text: Then the Lord told Moses,

10.text: 'Tell the Israelites: When y'all enter the land I'm giving you and harvest your first crops, bring a bundle of grain from the first cutting to the priest.'

11.text: 'On the day after the Sabbath, the priest will lift it up before the Lord so it may be accepted on y'all's behalf.'

12.text: 'On that same day, y'all must sacrifice a one-year-old male lamb with no defects as a burnt offering.'

13.text: 'With it, y'all must present a grain offering (four quarts of fine flour mixed with olive oil) and a liquid offering (one quart of wine).'

14.text: 'Until y'all bring this offering, don't eat any bread, roasted grain, or fresh kernels. This is a permanent law.'

15.text: 'From the day after the Sabbath—the day y'all bring the bundle of grain—count off seven full weeks.'

16.text: 'The day after the seventh Sabbath (50 days later), bring a new grain offering to the Lord.'

17.text: 'From wherever y'all live, bring two loaves of bread to lift up before the Lord as a special offering. They must be made with yeast from the first of your crops.'

18.text: 'Along with the bread, present: Seven one-year-old male lambs with no defects, One young bull, Two rams. These will be burnt offerings, along with the grain and liquid offerings—a pleasing aroma to the Lord.'

19.text: 'Also, offer one male goat as a sin offering and two one-year-old lambs as a peace offering.'

20.text: 'The priest will lift up the two lambs and bread as a special offering before the Lord—these offerings belong to the priests.'

21.text: 'That same day will be proclaimed a holy day, and y'all must stop working. This is a permanent law.'

22.text: 'When y'all harvest the crops, leave the edges of your fields for the poor and foreigners. I am the Lord your God.'

23.text: Then the Lord told Moses,

24.text: 'On the first day of the seventh month, observe a holy day of complete rest—a day of loud trumpet blasts.'

25.text: 'Don't do any work. Instead, bring special offerings to the Lord.'

26.text: Then the Lord told Moses,

27.text: 'On the tenth day of the seventh month, celebrate the Day of Atonement—a day for a holy assembly and self-denial.'

28.text: 'Do no work that day, cause it's the day when you get purified before the Lord.'

29.text: 'Anybody who doesn't deny themselves will be cut off from the community.'

30.text: 'Anybody who works on that day will be destroyed.'

31.text: 'No work at all—this is a permanent law.'

32.text: 'It's a Sabbath day of rest, starting at sundown on the ninth day and lasting until sundown on the tenth day.'

33.text: Then the Lord told Moses,

34.text: 'On the fifteenth day of the seventh month, celebrate the Festival of Shelters—it lasts seven days.'

35.text: 'On the first day, hold a holy assembly—stop working.'

36.text: 'For seven days, bring special offerings to the Lord. On the eighth day, hold another holy assembly—this will be a solemn occasion where y'all bring special offerings.'

37.text: 'These are the Lord's appointed festivals—y'all must celebrate them each year as holy days by presenting burnt offerings, grain offerings, sacrifices, and liquid offerings.'

38.text: 'These festivals must be observed in addition to: The regular Sabbaths, Your personal gifts, Your vow offerings, Your voluntary offerings to the Lord.'

39.text: 'After y'all finish the harvest, celebrate the Festival of Shelters starting on the fifteenth day of the seventh month.'

40.text: 'On the first day, gather branches from magnificent trees—palm fronds, leafy branches, and willows—and celebrate with joy before the Lord for seven days.'

41.text: 'Y'all must celebrate this festival every year—this is a permanent law.'

42.text: 'For seven days, y'all must live in temporary shelters.'

43.text: 'This will remind each generation that I made your ancestors live in shelters when I brought them out of Egypt. I am the Lord your God.'

44.text: So Moses told the Israelites all the instructions about the Lord's festivals.

1.text: Then the Lord told Moses,

2.text: 'Tell the people of Israel to bring you pure olive oil for the lamps, so they stay lit all the time.'

3.text: 'This lampstand stands in the Tabernacle, in front of the inner curtain that hides the Ark of the Covenant. Aaron must keep the lamps burning before the Lord all night.'

4.text: 'This is a permanent law y'all must follow for every generation.'

5.text: 'Bake twelve flat loaves of bread using four quarts of flour per loaf.'

6.text: 'Place them on the pure gold table before the Lord in two stacks of six.'

7.text: 'Put pure frankincense near each stack as a representative offering, a special gift to the Lord.'

8.text: 'Every Sabbath day, this bread must be laid out as a gift from the Israelites—it's part of the eternal covenant.'

9.text: 'The loaves belong to Aaron and his descendants. They gotta eat them in a sacred place cause they are most holy. This is a permanent right for the priests.'

10.text: One day, a man with an Israelite mother and an Egyptian father got into a fight with an Israelite man.

11.text: During the fight, he blasphemed the Lord's Name and cursed. So they brought him to Moses for judgment.

12.text: His mother was Shelomith, daughter of Dibri, from the tribe of Dan.

13.text: They held the man in custody until the Lord told them what to do.

14.text: Then the Lord told Moses: 'Take the blasphemer outside the camp. Everybody who heard him curse must lay their hands on his head. Then the whole community must stone him to death.'

15.text: 'Tell the people of Israel: Anybody who curses their God will be punished.'

16.text: 'Anybody who blasphemes the Lord's Name must be stoned to death by the entire community. Whether they Israelite or foreigner, they must be put to death.'

17.text: 'If somebody kills another person, they must be put to death.'

18.text: 'If somebody kills another person's animal, they must repay it in full—a live animal for the one they killed.'

19.text: 'If somebody injures another person, they must be dealt with the same way.'

20.text: 'A fracture for a fracture, an eye for an eye, a tooth for a tooth—whatever harm they caused must be paid back in kind.'

21.text: 'Whoever kills an animal must pay for it, but whoever kills a person must be put to death.'

22.text: 'This law applies to both Israelites and foreigners living among y'all. I am the Lord your God.'

23.text: After Moses gave these instructions, the Israelites took the blasphemer outside the camp and stoned him to death, just as the Lord commanded.

1.text: While Moses was on Mount Sinai, the Lord told him,

2.text: 'Tell the people of Israel: When y'all enter the land I'm giving you, the land itself must observe a Sabbath rest every seventh year.'

3.text: 'For six years, y'all can plant, prune, and harvest. But in the seventh year, the land gotta have a complete rest.'

4.text: 'This Sabbath year is for the Lord—don't plant fields or prune vineyards.'

5.text: 'Don't store up crops that grow on their own or gather grapes from unpruned vines—the land gotta rest.'

6.text: 'But y'all can eat whatever the land produces on its own—this applies to y'all, y'all's servants, workers, and foreigners living among you.'

7.text: 'Even the livestock and wild animals can eat what grows naturally.'

8.text: 'Count off seven Sabbath years—that's 49 years total.'

9.text: 'Then, on the Day of Atonement in the 50th year, blow the ram's horn loud throughout the land.'

10.text: 'Set this year apart as holy—proclaim freedom for everybody. This is the Year of Jubilee—everybody returns to their family land and clans.'

11.text: 'In this 50th year, don't plant or store away crops—let the land rest. Eat what grows naturally.'

12.text: 'It's a holy year, so keep it sacred and only eat what grows by itself.'

13.text: 'In the Year of Jubilee, everyone gets to return to their ancestral land.'

14.text: 'If y'all buy or sell property, don't cheat each other.'

15.text: 'The price must be based on the number of years until the next Jubilee—since you're really buying harvests, not land.'

16.text: 'More years till Jubilee? Higher price. Fewer years? Lower price.'

17.text: 'Show respect for God—don't take advantage of each other. I am the Lord your God.'

18.text: 'If y'all follow My laws, the land will be blessed, and y'all will live securely.'

19.text: 'The land will produce plenty, and y'all will have more than enough to eat.'

20.text: 'But y'all might ask: "What do we eat during the seventh year if we can't plant or harvest?"'

21.text: 'Don't worry—I'll bless y'all in the sixth year so the land produces enough for three years!'

22.text: 'Even in the eighth year, y'all will still be eating from the sixth-year harvest until the new crops are ready in year nine.'

23.text: 'Y'all can't sell the land permanently, cause the land belongs to Me. Y'all just living there as tenants.'

24.text: 'Whenever land is sold, the seller must have the right to buy it back.'

25.text: 'If an Israelite falls into poverty and sells family land, a close relative should buy it back for them.'

26.text: 'If there's no relative to buy it back, but the seller makes enough money, they can redeem it themselves.'

27.text: 'The price should be adjusted based on the years left until Jubilee—then the original owner can return.'

28.text: 'But if they can't buy it back, the land stays with the new owner until the Year of Jubilee, when it must be returned to the original family.'

29.text: 'If somebody sells a house inside a walled city, they got one year to buy it back.'

30.text: 'If they don't redeem it in a year, the sale can't be undone—the house is permanent property.'

31.text: 'But houses in villages (without walls) follow the same rules as farmland—they can be bought back at any time and must be returned at Jubilee.'

32.text: 'The Levites can always buy back their property in their towns.'

33.text: 'Any land sold by the Levites must be returned in Jubilee, cause that's their only inheritance.'

34.text: 'But Levite pastureland can't be sold—it's theirs forever.'

35.text: 'If an Israelite falls into poverty, help them as if they were family—let them stay with you.'

36.text: 'Don't charge them interest or make a profit off them. Fear God and take care of them.'

37.text: 'Don't charge interest on money or profit off food you lend them.'

38.text: 'I am the Lord, who brought y'all outta Egypt and gave you this land.'

39.text: 'If an Israelite falls into poverty and sells himself to you, don't treat him like a slave.'

40.text: 'Treat him like a hired worker or temporary resident—he will serve until the Year of Jubilee.'

41.text: 'Then he and his children will be free to return to their family land.'

42.text: 'The people of Israel belong to Me—I brought them outta Egypt, so they must never be sold as slaves.'

43.text: 'Fear God, and don't treat them harshly.'

44.text: 'Y'all can buy slaves from the nations around you.'

45.text: 'Y'all can also buy children of foreigners living among you—they can become property.'

46.text: 'Y'all can pass them down to your children as an inheritance. But don't treat fellow Israelites this way.'

47.text: 'If an Israelite becomes poor and sells himself to a rich foreigner, he can be bought back.'

48.text: 'He can be redeemed by his brother, uncle, cousin, or any close relative.'

49.text: 'He can also redeem himself if he makes enough money.'

50.text: 'The price must be calculated based on how many years are left until Jubilee—just like hiring a worker.'

51.text: 'If many years remain, the cost is high. If only a few years remain, the price is lower.'

52.text: 'It must be a fair price based on how long he served.'

53.text: 'The foreign owner must treat him fairly—don't allow harsh treatment.'

54.text: 'If he hasn't been redeemed by the time Jubilee arrives, he and his children must be set free.'

55.text: 'Cause Israel belongs to Me—y'all are My servants, and I brought y'all outta Egypt. I am the Lord your God.'

1.text: "Y'all bet not be out here making idols for yourselves. No statues, no sacred pillars, no engraved stones to bow down to. I'm the Lord, your God—don't play with Me."

2.text: "Keep My Sabbaths holy and show respect to My sanctuary, 'cause I'm the Lord."

3.text: "If y'all live by My rules, keep My commandments, and actually do what I told you,"

4.text: "I'mma make sure y'all get rain when y'all need it. The land gon' give y'all good crops, and the trees gon' stay producing fruit."

5.text: "Y'all gon' have so much grain, you still gon' be gathering it up when it's time for grapes. And when the grape harvest come, y'all still gon' be eating off the last batch. Ain't nobody out here starving—you'll have more than enough."

6.text: "I'ma bring peace to the land. You gon' be able to lay down at night without worry. No wild animals, no war coming through your streets."

7.text: "Your enemies? They ain't got a chance—y'all gon' be chasing them off. They gon' be dropping left and right."

8.text: "Just five of y'all can run off a hundred of them, and a hundred of y'all gon' send ten thousand packing. They gon' fall by the sword."

9.text: "I'ma bless y'all, make sure y'all grow, and keep My promise strong with y'all."

10.text: "You gon' have so much food from the last harvest, you gotta clear it out to make room for the new one."

11.text: "I'ma live with y'all—My Spirit ain't gon' leave you."

12.text: "I'ma walk among y'all, be your God, and y'all gon' be My people."

13.text: "Remember, I'm the same God that broke y'all outta Egypt, got y'all free from being slaves, and lifted that weight off your backs so you could stand up straight."

14.text: "But if y'all don't listen to Me, if y'all ignore My commandments,"

15.text: "If y'all act like My laws don't matter, disrespect what I said, and straight-up break My covenant,"

16.text: "Then here's what I'ma do: I'ma hit y'all with terror, diseases, and fevers that'll break you down and leave you weak. Y'all gon' plant crops, but your enemies gon' eat 'em instead of you."

17.text: "I'ma turn My back on you, let your enemies take y'all down. The folks who hate you gon' be running things. Y'all gon' be scared for no reason, running when nobody even chasing you."

18.text: "If y'all still don't listen after that, I'ma turn it up—punish y'all seven times worse."

19.text: "I'ma crush that fake confidence y'all got. The sky? Hard as iron. The ground? Dry as bronze."

20.text: "Y'all gon' put in all this work, but the land ain't gon' produce nothing. The trees? No fruit."

21.text: "If y'all keep acting up and still won't listen, I'ma send seven times the plagues based on your sins."

22.text: "I'ma let wild animals loose on y'all. They gon' take your kids, kill your livestock, and leave your roads empty."

23.text: "If after all that, y'all still don't turn back to Me,"

24.text: "Then I'ma turn against you too and punish you seven times harder."

25.text: "I'ma let war break out, since y'all breaking the covenant. When y'all hide in your cities, I'ma send plagues in there. And your enemies? They gon' own you."

26.text: "I'ma cut off your food supply. Ten women gon' be cooking in one oven, and y'all still won't have enough to eat."

27.text: "If after all this, y'all still ain't listening and keep going against Me,"

28.text: "I'ma come at you with fury and personally make sure your punishment is seven times worse."

29.text: "It's gon' get so bad, y'all gon' be eating your own kids."

30.text: "All them fake altars y'all got? Gone. The places where y'all worshipped other gods? Destroyed. Y'all bodies gon' be laid out next to them worthless idols. And I? Ain't messin' with y'all no more."

31.text: "Your cities? Empty. Your holy places? Wrecked. Your sacrifices? I don't want 'em."

32.text: "I'ma leave your land in ruins, so bad that even your enemies gon' be shocked."

33.text: "I'ma scatter y'all everywhere, with war following you. Your homeland? Abandoned. Your cities? Ruined."

34.text: "The land finally gon' get its Sabbath rest since y'all never let it."

35.text: "It'll be empty long enough to make up for all the times y'all ignored Me."

36.text: "Those who survive? They gon' be so scared in their enemy's land that even the sound of a rustling leaf gon' have them running."

37.text: "They gon' be tripping over each other, falling down like somebody chasing them—but ain't nobody there."

38.text: "They gon' die in enemy land,"

39.text: "Waste away 'cause of their own sins, and the sins of their fathers."

40.text: "But if they wake up, admit what they did, confess their sins and the sins of their ancestors,"

41.text: "If they stop acting prideful, humble themselves, and take responsibility,"

42.text: "Then I'ma remember the promise I made to Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham. I'ma remember the land too."

43.text: "Even though the land got left behind and finally got to rest, Even though they got what they deserved for disrespecting My rules, I ain't gon' forget them."

44.text: "Even when they stuck in their enemies' land, I won't wipe them out completely or break My promise. 'Cause I'm the Lord, their God."

45.text: "I'ma remember the deal I made with their ancestors—the same ones I brought outta Egypt in front of the whole world. 'Cause I'm the Lord."

46.text: "These the rules, laws, and commands that the Lord laid down for Israel on Mount Sinai through Moses."

1.text: Then the Lord told Moses,

2.text: 'Tell the Israelites: If anybody makes a special vow to dedicate someone to the Lord by paying their value, here's how to do it:'

3.text: 'A man between 20 and 60 years old is valued at 50 shekels of silver (measured by the sanctuary shekel).'

4.text: 'A woman in that age range is valued at 30 shekels of silver.'

5.text: 'A boy between 5 and 20 years old is valued at 20 shekels; a girl of that age is valued at 10 shekels.'

6.text: 'A baby boy between 1 month and 5 years old is valued at 5 shekels; a baby girl is valued at 3 shekels.'

7.text: 'A man older than 60 is valued at 15 shekels; a woman at 10 shekels.'

8.text: 'If somebody can't afford to pay the full amount, they must take the person to the priest, and he will set a price based on what they can afford.'

9.text: 'If your vow involves giving an animal that's acceptable as an offering, that gift is holy.'

10.text: 'You can't swap it out for another animal—good for bad or bad for good. But if you try, then both animals will be considered holy.'

11.text: 'If your vow involves an unclean animal (one that can't be sacrificed), bring it to the priest.'

12.text: 'The priest will set a value, and his decision is final—whether high or low.'

13.text: 'If you want to buy the animal back, you must pay the priest's price plus 20%.'

14.text: 'If somebody dedicates a house to the Lord, the priest will assess its value—whether high or low. His decision is final.'

15.text: 'If the person wants to buy it back, they must pay the full value plus 20%.'

16.text: 'If somebody dedicates land, its value will be based on how much seed is needed to plant it—50 shekels per five bushels of barley seed.'

17.text: 'If the land is dedicated during the Year of Jubilee, the full price applies.'

18.text: 'If it's dedicated after the Year of Jubilee, the priest will adjust the price based on how many years are left until the next Jubilee.'

19.text: 'If the person wants to buy it back, they must pay the full price plus 20%.'

20.text: 'If they don't buy it back and it gets sold to someone else, it can't be bought back anymore.'

21.text: 'At Jubilee, the field will become holy and set apart for the Lord. It will belong to the priests.'

22.text: 'If someone dedicates land they bought (not family land), the priest will set a price based on the years left until Jubilee.'

23.text: 'That price must be given as a sacred donation to the Lord.'

24.text: 'In the Year of Jubilee, the land must return to its original owner.'

25.text: 'All values must be measured by the sanctuary shekel (20 gerahs).'

26.text: 'You can't dedicate firstborn animals to the Lord, cause they already belong to Him.'

27.text: 'But if it's a ceremonially unclean firstborn animal, you can buy it back for its assessed value plus 20%. If you don't, the priest will sell it.'

28.text: 'Anything permanently dedicated to the Lord—whether a person, animal, or land—can't be sold or bought back. It's holy and belongs to the Lord.'

29.text: 'People set apart for destruction must be put to death—they can't be bought back.'

30.text: 'One-tenth of all grain and fruit belongs to the Lord—it is holy.'

31.text: 'If you want to buy back your tithe, you must pay the full value plus 20%.'

32.text: 'Every tenth animal from your herds and flocks must be set apart as holy to the Lord.'

33.text: 'You can't pick and choose which animals—you must count every tenth one.'

34.text: These are the commands the Lord gave Moses on Mount Sinai for the Israelites.

1.text: This the heavy word from the Lord to Israel, straight through His messenger Malachi.

2.text: "I been lovin' y'all," says the Lord. But y'all keep askin', 'How You love us tho?' Wasn't Esau Jacob's brother?" God says. "Yeah, but I chose Jacob. I rocked with him.

3.text: But Esau? Nah. I turned my back on him. I let his whole territory fall apart—his mountains now home to wild jackals.

4.text: And even when Edom tryna clap back like, 'We broke now, but we comin' back—we gon' rebuild all this,' God said, 'Let 'em try. I'll tear down whatever they put up. They gon' stay known as Wicked Territory—folk I stay mad at forever.'

5.text: You gon' see it with your own eyes. And you gon' say, 'God movin' even outside Israel. He big-big.'

6.text: "A son show his daddy some honor, right? And a worker respect his boss? Well if I'm your Father—where's My honor? If I'm your Master—why y'all don't respect Me?" That's what the Lord of Heaven's Armies says to y'all priests who keep disrespectin' His name. But y'all still askin', 'How we disrespected You tho?'

7.text: Y'all bringin' raggedy, defiled food to My altar. But you still ask, 'Wait, what did we do wrong?' You talkin' 'bout My table like it ain't nothin. Like I'm just some regular.

8.text: You bring blind animals as sacrifices. You think that's okay? Lame ones, sick ones too—y'all serious? Try givin' that to your governor and see if he smile at you. See if he take that mess.

9.text: Now you wanna ask Me for favor? You want Me to bless y'all while you disrespectin' Me with these weak offerings? You think I'm takin' that in good faith? For real?"

10.text: "I wish somebody would just shut the temple doors already. Stop wastin' fire on My altar if it ain't comin' from the heart. I'm not feelin' y'all fake worship," says the Lord of Hosts. "I'm not acceptin' nothin from your hands."

11.text: "Let Me make it clear— From sun-up to sun-down, My name gon' be lifted up among the nations. People all over gon' offer Me real incense, real worship, real honor. My name ain't just holy in Israel—it's holy everywhere."

12.text: "But y'all over here treatin' My table like it's trash. Y'all talkin' 'bout the food like it's beneath you.

13.text: You rollin' your eyes like it's a burden to even serve. You act like bringin' Me an offering is too much work. And then you got the nerve to bring Me stolen stuff? Or them busted, sick animals? You think I'ma bless that? You serious?"

14.text: "Cursed is the one who got a good offering in his stash, Makes a promise to give it to Me, Then turns around and gives Me the busted one instead. Don't play Me like that. I'm a Great King," says the Lord of Hosts. "My name deserves reverence—even the nations fear Me."

1.text: "Aight now, this one right here? This commandment for y'all priests."

2.text: "If y'all don't listen up, And if y'all don't take Me serious and give Me the glory I deserve," Says the Lord of Heaven's Armies, "I'ma curse what was supposed to bless y'all. Matter fact, it's already cursed—'cause y'all hearts ain't in it."

3.text: "Watch this—I'ma check your descendants, And straight up smear dung on y'all faces— Yeah, the same mess from them so-called holy festivals. And y'all gon' get dragged out with it."

4.text: "Then maybe y'all'll realize I meant what I said. I gave this word so My covenant with Levi would stay solid," Says the Lord of Hosts.

5.text: "That covenant was about life and peace, And I gave it to him so he'd respect Me. And he did. He feared Me for real. He honored My name."

6.text: "He spoke truth. He ain't twist nothin'. He walked close with Me, stayed fair, And turned a bunch of folks away from sin."

7.text: "See, a priest's mouth supposed to keep wisdom ready. People should be able to come to y'all for God's law. You the messenger—I trusted you with My word."

8.text: "But you? You swerved off the path. You out here makin' people trip over the Word. You broke the Levi covenant," Says the Lord of Hosts.

9.text: "So guess what? I made you look foolish in front of everybody. You ain't follow My ways, And you pick and choose who gets justice."

10.text: Ain't we all got the same Father? Ain't the same God make all of us? So why we doin' each other dirty, And actin' like we forgot our ancestors' covenant?

11.text: Judah wildin'. Israel and Jerusalem too—straight up disrespect. They out here messin' up what God said was holy. Judah married some foreign-god worshipper, And God ain't havin' it.

12.text: May the Lord cut off anybody in Jacob's crew Who does that mess— Even if they wide awake and still bringin' offerings like it's cool.

13.text: And here's the second thing y'all do: Y'all cryin' and weepin' at the altar, Tears everywhere, but God not listenin'. He not takin' them offerings no more, Not with love. Not with favor.

14.text: And you ask, "But why tho?" 'Cause the Lord saw what you did. You played dirty with the wife of your youth— The one you made a covenant with. She was your partner, man. Your rib.

15.text: Didn't God make y'all one? He gave y'all His Spirit so y'all could produce godly kids. That's why He joined y'all like that. So take care of your spirit— And don't go cheatin' on the one you started with.

16.text: "I, the Lord God of Israel, hate divorce. It stains your robe with violence," Says the Lord of Hosts. "So guard your spirit, And stop movin' grimy."

17.text: Y'all makin' God tired with all this talk. And still you say, "What we say that wore Him out?" It's when y'all start sayin' stuff like: "Evil people blessed. God must be cool with 'em." Or, "Where God at? Where the justice?"

1.text: Look, I'm sendin' My messenger ahead of Me— He gon' clear the path. And the Lord y'all been lookin' for? Yeah, He comin' to His temple. The Messenger of the covenant—the One y'all claim to be hype about? He on His way," says the Lord of Heaven's Armies.

2.text: But let's be real—who can handle it when He shows up? Who gon' still be standin' when He steps in? He comin' like fire in a furnace, Like bleach on dirty clothes.

3.text: He gon' sit down like a silversmith, Refinin' and purifyin' the Levites— Burnin' off the grime like gold and silver So they can bring offerings that actually mean somethin'.

4.text: Then the gifts from Judah and Jerusalem Gon' be somethin' God can smile on again— Just like back in the good ol' days.

5.text: And I ain't just showin' up to chill— I'm comin' with judgment. I'ma be quick to testify Against the sorcerers, the cheaters, The liars, the ones robbin' workers, widows, and orphans, And the ones who treat strangers like trash— All 'cause they don't fear Me," says the Lord of Hosts.

6.text: "I'm the Lord—I don't change. That's the only reason y'all ain't been wiped out, Sons of Jacob.

7.text: Since your great-great-granddaddies' day, Y'all been wildin'— Turnin' away from My rules, Not keepin' what I said. Come back to Me, and I'll come back to you," Says the Lord of Hosts. But y'all over here talkin' 'bout, "How we supposed to come back?"

8.text: Can a human rob God? Well guess what? Y'all robbin' Me. And still y'all ask, "How we robbin' You?" Through tithes and offerings. That's how.

9.text: Y'all under a curse— The whole nation—'cause you been stealin' from Me.
