10.text: Bring the full tithe into the storehouse, So there's food in My house. Test Me on this one," Says the Lord of Hosts. "See if I don't crack open the windows of heaven And pour out blessings you ain't even got room for.

11.text: I'll shut down the devourer for y'all. He won't be eatin' up your crops, Or stoppin' your vines from producin'," Says the Lord of Hosts.

12.text: "Everybody gon' call y'all blessed, 'Cause your land gon' be that beautiful," Says the Lord of Hosts.

13.text: "But y'all been talkin' slick about Me," Says the Lord. And y'all still got the nerve to ask, "What we say that was wrong?"

14.text: You said, "Ain't no point servin' God. What we get outta keepin' His commandments? All this mournin' and repentant stuff ain't payin' off."

15.text: "Now we call the proud 'blessed,' The ones actin' foul get promoted, And the ones testin' God ain't even gettin' checked."

16.text: But then the ones who actually feared God Started talkin' to each other. And God leaned in—He heard every word. So He had a book of remembrance written— For the folks who fear Him And keep His name close to heart.

17.text: "They Mine," says the Lord of Hosts. "On the day I show out, They gon' be like My jewels— I'ma spare them like a father who spares his faithful son."

18.text: Then you'll finally see the difference— Between the righteous and the wicked, Between the one who serves God And the one who don't even try.

1.text: Look, the day is comin'— Hot like a furnace. All the proud folk and the ones wildin'? They gon' burn up like dry grass. That day gon' blaze through 'em," Says the Lord of Heaven's Armies, "Leavin' nothin' behind—not even roots or branches.

2.text: But for the ones who respect My name? The Sun of Righteousness gon' rise— He bringin' healin' in His wings. Y'all gon' run out like calves fresh out the pen— Fed, full, and free.

3.text: You gon' stomp down the wicked— They gon' be dust under your feet On the day I step in," Says the Lord of Hosts.

4.text: Don't forget the Law of Moses, My servant— The same commandments I gave him at Mount Horeb For all y'all in Israel. Hold on to them statutes and judgments.

5.text: I'm sendin' Elijah the prophet to y'all Before the great and heavy day of the Lord shows up.

6.text: He gon' flip hearts— Fathers turnin' back to their kids, And kids back to their fathers— So I don't have to come through And strike the earth with a curse.

1.text: This the message the Lord gave to Micah from Moresheth, back when Jotham, Ahaz, and Hezekiah were kings in Judah. It was about Samaria and Jerusalem.

2.text: Listen up, y'all—all people, everywhere! Earth, you too! God about to testify against y'all, comin' straight from His holy spot.

3.text: Look, the Lord steppin' out His place. He comin' down, walkin' on the high places like He runnin' the whole thing.

4.text: Mountains gon' melt like candle wax, valleys gon' crack open and slide like water rollin' off a steep hill.

5.text: All this 'cause Jacob (aka Israel) wildin' out. Their sins got outta control. What's the root of Jacob's mess? Ain't it Samaria? And them "high places" in Judah? Ain't that Jerusalem?

6.text: So Samaria? Gon' be turned into straight rubble. Folks gon' be plantin' vineyards where cities used to be. God gon' throw them stones downhill and rip up the whole foundation.

7.text: All them little idol statues? Smashed. All the money they made hustlin'? Burned up. Them idols gon' be left lookin' sad and broke. She got it actin' like a harlot, and it's gon' go back to that same dirty cycle.

8.text: I'ma cry out loud for real. I'ma be out here barefoot, butt naked, howlin' like a wild dog, mournin' like an ostrich. That pain deep.

9.text: 'Cause the wounds? Too deep to fix. This thing done hit Judah now—right up to the gate of my own people. It's knockin' on Jerusalem's door.

10.text: Don't even speak on it in Gath. Don't cry out there. But in Beth Aphrah, roll in the dirt—show that grief.

11.text: Shaphir folks, y'all gon' walk out in shame, bare. Zaanan folks too scared to even step outside. Beth Ezel cryin', and you ain't got nowhere safe to stand.

12.text: The people of Maroth waitin' for good news, but what's comin' is straight disaster from the Lord, right to Jerusalem's gate.

13.text: Lachish, y'all better get that chariot ready—y'all was the first ones to pass them sinful vibes down to Zion. Israel's wrongdoings showed up right there with you.

14.text: So now you gotta send farewell gifts to Moresheth Gath. And Achzib? That city gon' play the kings—nothin' but false hope.

15.text: But listen, Mareshah—you got somebody comin' for your spot. Israel's glory gon' be forced to hide out in Adullam.

16.text: Go on and shave your head, mourn hard for your babies. Make yourself bald like an eagle, 'cause your kids about to be snatched up into captivity.

1.text: Woe to them folks who be sittin' up in bed plottin' evil—layin' out wrong like it's a business plan. Soon as the sun come up, they out there doin' dirt, just 'cause they can.

2.text: They greedy for folks' land and straight up snatch it. Same with houses—they take what ain't theirs. They rob a man of his home and his whole legacy.

3.text: So the Lord said, "Bet. I got somethin' cooked up for y'all too—a disaster you can't duck. Y'all won't be able to hold your heads high no more. This ain't the time to act big."

4.text: That day gon' hit hard. Folks gon' be singin' sad songs 'bout y'all, talkin' 'bout: 'We done lost everything. God switched up our blessing and gave it away to folks that don't even rock with us.'

5.text: Ain't gon' be nobody left to split up land for you when it's time to divvy up God's promise. You out.

6.text: Y'all out here tellin' prophets, "Stop talkin', hush up." So cool—God gon' stop speakin' to you. Y'all won't be hearin' no good word back.

7.text: Oh house of Jacob, y'all really think God don't move like He used to? You think He switched up? Nah, His words still bless those who live right.

8.text: But lately, y'all actin' like ops to your own people. Runnin' up on folks who trusted you—strippin' the clothes off their backs like war just ended.

9.text: Y'all kickin' women out their homes, robbin' children of their future, snatchin' away My glory like it don't mean nothin'.

10.text: So get up and go. This land ain't gon' be your peace anymore. It's tainted. And it's gon' chew you up and spit you out.

11.text: Some slick-tongued dude can come up talkin' nonsense like, "Lemme give y'all a prophecy 'bout wine and good times," and that's the kinda voice y'all love to hear. For real?

12.text: But look—I still got y'all. I'ma bring My people back together, every last one that's left. Like sheep gathered up safe, packed close in the field—so many it's gon' be loud.

13.text: The one breakin' through gon' lead y'all out. Y'all gon' pass through that gate and walk free. Your King gon' walk ahead of you. And the Lord? He at the front of the line.

1.text: Then I said, "Ayo, listen up—y'all leaders of Jacob, y'all big dogs in Israel. Ain't it your job to know what justice look like?"

2.text: But nah, y'all hate what's good and love what's evil. Y'all be skinning My people alive—strippin' 'em bare like they ain't even human.

3.text: Y'all eatin' folk up—breakin' their bones, tearin' up their bodies like meat in a stew pot. You treatin' folks like food, not family.

4.text: But best believe, a time comin' where y'all gon' cry out to Me—but I ain't listenin'. I'm gon' hide My face, 'cause y'all been movin' foul.

5.text: Now here's what the Lord got to say 'bout them fake prophets out here: y'all got My people twisted. You singin' lullabies about peace when your belly full, but as soon as somebody ain't feedin' you, it's smoke and war.

6.text: So guess what? Ain't gon' be no more visions. Dark times comin'. No dreams, no prophecies. Sun goin' down on all y'all so-called prophets.

7.text: All them "seers" gon' be lookin' real foolish. The fortune-tellers gon' be embarrassed too. They gon' cover their mouths 'cause God ain't speakin' to none of them.

8.text: But me? I'm powered up with the Spirit of the Lord. I got strength, justice, and boldness to call y'all out—Jacob, Israel, all y'all—on y'all mess.

9.text: Now hear this, you crooked leaders of Jacob and Israel—y'all hate justice, twistin' everything to fit your own agenda.

10.text: You build Zion off bloodshed. Y'all stackin' bricks with people's pain. Jerusalem built off straight-up wrongdoing.

11.text: The judges only judge if the check clear. Priests won't teach unless you cashin' 'em out. Prophets out here sellin' prophecies for a price. Yet they still talkin' like, "God got us. We good. Can't nothin' happen to us."

12.text: But 'cause of y'all, Zion gon' get plowed like farmland. Jerusalem? A pile of rubble. And that temple mount? It's gon' look like a raggedy forest hill. No glory, just dust.

1.text: One day, in the days up ahead, the Lord's crib—the mountain where His house sit—is gon' be set up high, way above all the other hills. And folks from everywhere gon' be flockin' to it.

2.text: Whole nations gon' be sayin', "Come on, let's roll up to the Lord's mountain, to the house of Jacob's God. He gon' teach us how to live right, and we gon' walk that path He show us." 'Cause outta Zion gon' come the law, and the Lord's word straight outta Jerusalem.

3.text: He gon' settle disputes between folks, check even the strongest nations from far off. Swords? They gon' be turned into plows. Spears? Turned into garden tools. Ain't gon' be no more war training. Ain't nobody pickin' up arms no more.

4.text: Folks gon' be chillin' under they own vine and fig tree—peaceful, unbothered. Ain't nobody out here scaring folks. The Lord Himself said it, and that's on everything.

5.text: Other folks might walk in the name of they little gods, but as for us? We walkin' in the name of the Lord our God, forever and ever.

6.text: The Lord say, "When that time come, I'ma gather up the ones who been limpin', left out, pushed aside—the ones I had to break down."

7.text: "I'ma take the lame ones and make 'em My people. The ones the world threw away? I'ma turn 'em into a whole strong nation. I'ma rule over them from Mount Zion—forever."

8.text: And you, Tower of the Flock—Zion's stronghold—yo time comin'. Everything you lost, gon' be given back. Royalty gon' rise again in Jerusalem.

9.text: So why you cryin' now? Ain't there a king in you? Where your advisor at? You sound like a woman goin' through labor pains.

10.text: Cry out, push through, daughter of Zion. You about to give birth to something new. But first, you gon' leave the city, live in the field, and end up in Babylon. But it's there—right there—I'ma come through and save you. I'ma get you outta enemy hands.

11.text: Yeah, nations all around got they eyes on you. They talkin' wild like, "Let her fall. Let us feast on her downfall."

12.text: But they don't even know God's plan. They ain't peeped how He move. He stackin' all them folks together like wheat, just waitin' to thresh.

13.text: "Get up, daughter of Zion! Time to stomp. I'm makin' your horns like iron, your hooves like bronze. You gon' crush these nations. All that they gain? All that wealth? That's comin' to Me. It's all gon' be holy—belongin' to the Lord of the whole earth."

1.text: Aight now, gather up, daughter of troops—y'all battlin' out here. The enemy settin' up shop, surroundin' us. They gon' smack Israel's judge in the face with a stick.

2.text: But you, Bethlehem Ephrathah—You might seem small compared to all Judah's cities, But outta you gon' come somebody big for Me—The One who gon' rule over Israel. He been around since way back—eternity-type back.

3.text: So God gon' let things play out for a while, Till the one in labor give birth. Then the rest of His people—His fam—gon' come back home to Israel.

4.text: He gon' stand strong, take care of His people like a real Shepherd, Powered up by the Lord, movin' in His name. His folks gon' live in peace, 'Cause His name gon' stretch worldwide.

5.text: And this King? Yeah—He gon' be our peace. When the Assyrians roll up on us, When they step in our homes—We gon' raise up seven shepherds, shoot, maybe even eight leaders ready to handle business.

6.text: They gon' wreck Assyria with the sword, Even the land of Nimrod at the gates. He gon' save us from the Assyrian threat When they try to cross into our space.

7.text: The leftover crew from Jacob? They gon' be out here among the nations like morning dew—Like soft showers on the grass, Ain't waitin' on nobody, Ain't need no permission.

8.text: That remnant of Jacob? They gon' be like a lion in the middle of the wild—Like a young lion rollin' through a flock of sheep. When they come through? It's a wrap—stompin' and tearin' through. Ain't nobody savin' nothin'.

9.text: Your hand gon' be lifted high against all your enemies, And every single one of 'em? Gone.

10.text: The Lord say, "When that day hit, I'm gettin' rid of all y'all's horses and chariots—no more military flexin'.

11.text: Cities? Knocked down. Strongholds? Gone.

12.text: I'ma shut down all that magic, Ain't gon' be no fortune tellers left.

13.text: Y'all idols? I'ma break every last one. No more bowin' to stuff you built with your own hands.

14.text: Them wooden gods? Ripped out. Cities? Flattened.

15.text: I'm comin' with heat—real vengeance—On all them nations that ain't listen."

1.text: Aight now, listen up to what the Lord sayin': "Get up—go make your case. Let the mountains hear you out, And let the hills tune in too.

2.text: Y'all mountains, y'all strong foundations of the earth, Hear the Lord out—He got a complaint against His people, And He takin' it up with Israel.

3.text: My people, what did I do to you? How I wearied you? Go 'head and speak on it—what's the charge?

4.text: Didn't I bring y'all up outta Egypt? Freed you from that slave house? Didn't I send Moses, Aaron, and Miriam to lead the way?

5.text: My people, remember what Balak, king of Moab, tried to pull? And how Balaam, Beor's son, had to answer him? From Shittim to Gilgal—I was showin' y'all how righteous I am."

6.text: So now…what I'm supposed to bring to the Lord? How I'm supposed to bow before the Most High? Burnt offerings? Year-old calves?

7.text: Will the Lord be impressed with thousands of rams? Ten thousand rivers of oil? Should I even offer up my firstborn for my sins? My own child for the wrong I done?

8.text: Naw. He already showed you what's good, fam. And what He want from you is simple: Do right. Love mercy. Walk humble with your God.

9.text: The Lord's voice boomin' through the city—And if you got any wisdom, you gon' pay attention: "Listen when the rod speaks—ask yourself who sent it.

10.text: Is wickedness still sittin' comfy in these houses? Folks still out here usin' short measures that ain't right?

11.text: You think I'm gon' act like that's pure? When you usin' crooked scales and got a bag full of lies?

12.text: Your rich folks violent, Your people stay lyin', And them tongues slick with deceit.

13.text: So yeah—I'ma strike y'all down. You gon' feel it. Gon' be sick and empty 'cause of your sin.

14.text: You'll eat, but never be full—Your hunger gon' linger. You'll try to hold on to what you got, But it won't save you. Even what you manage to keep? I'ma let the sword take that too.

15.text: You'll plant seeds, but you ain't gon' reap nothin'. You'll stomp olives, but not get no oil. Make wine, but not a sip to drink.

16.text: Y'all still followin' Omri's crooked rules, Still walkin' in Ahab's dirty footsteps. So guess what? I'ma leave y'all desolate. Folks gon' see you and hiss—You gon' carry the shame of My people."

1.text: Man…woe is me. I feel like somebody who out here tryna find summer fruit, Tryna pick them last grapes off the vine—Ain't nothin' good left, not even one ripe one for my soul to enjoy.

2.text: Ain't no real ones left on earth. Not a single upright soul in sight. Everybody out here tryna catch a body, They huntin' each other like wild animals in a trap.

3.text: Folks out here wildin' with both hands—real coordinated with the evil. The prince takin' bribes, The judge crooked too, And the big dogs just say what they want, Then they all link up to make it happen.

4.text: Even the "best" of them? They like thorns and barbed wire. The straightest ones still sharp enough to cut you. But the watchman's day—the one who sees what's comin'—Yeah, it's finally here. And now they all confused.

5.text: Don't even trust your homeboy. Don't put no faith in your ride-or-die. Keep your mouth shut—even 'round your boo thang layin' in your arms.

6.text: 'Cause sons turn on their daddies, Daughters pop off on their mamas, Daughters-in-law throw shade at their husbands' mamas, And the folks under your own roof? That's your biggest threat.

7.text: But me? I'ma keep my eyes on the Lord. I'ma wait on my God to come through with salvation. He gon' hear me when I call.

8.text: Don't you dare gloat over me, enemy. Yeah, I might fall…but I'ma get back up. I might be sittin' in the dark right now, But the Lord gon' be my light.

9.text: I messed up, and I'ma take this L. I'ma sit with the consequences 'til God steps in, Pleads my case, brings justice, And walks me back into the light. Then I'll see His righteousness clear as day.

10.text: The one who was tryna clown me, Talkin' slick like "Where your God at now?" Yeah, she gon' see. She gon' be filled with shame. I'ma see her get dragged like dirt in the streets.

11.text: In that day, when your walls goin' up, That decree gon' go global.

12.text: People gon' come to you from Assyria, From locked-down cities, from across rivers, From sea to sea, from mountain to mountain.

13.text: But the land gon' still look empty and tore up, All 'cause of the wild mess they did.

14.text: Lord, go 'head and shepherd Your folks—Your chosen ones. The ones who out here dwellin' quiet in the woods. Let 'em eat good in Bashan and Gilead, Like they used to back in the day.

15.text: Just like back when You brought us outta Egypt, Do it again—show us them wonders.

16.text: The nations gon' be stunned silent, All their so-called power? Embarrassed. They gon' cover their mouths, And they ears won't even work right from the shock.

17.text: They gon' eat dirt like snakes, Slither out they lil' holes lookin' scared. They gon' fear You, Lord—And be shook at how mighty You are.

18.text: Who you know that's like our God?! Forgivin' sins and lookin' past our mess. He don't stay mad forever—Nah, He actually enjoys showin' mercy.

19.text: He gon' come back with compassion, He gon' stomp out our sins. He throwin' all that mess into the sea, Deep where nobody can go fishin' for it.

20.text: You gon' stay true to Jacob, Show mercy to Abraham, Just like You promised our ancestors Back in the day.

1.text: This here the heavy word on Nineveh. Nahum from Elkosh saw it all in a vision.

2.text: God don't play when He jealous. The Lord don't miss when He pay folks back. Yeah, He mad for real — and He keep that smoke for His enemies.

3.text: The Lord got patience, but don't get it twisted — He powerful. He ain't lettin' the wicked slide. He move through the whirlwind and storm like He own 'em. Even the clouds? Just dust on His feet.

4.text: When He speak, the sea dry up. Rivers gone. Bashan and Carmel shrivel up. Lebanon? Lookin' dead and dusty.

5.text: Mountains shake in front of Him. Hills melt like butter. The earth straight-up tremble when He show up — everybody on it too.

6.text: Who can handle that kind of heat? Who gon' stand tall in that anger? His rage hit like wildfire, and rocks crumble when He mad.

7.text: But don't get it twisted — the Lord is good too. He like a safe place when life hit hard. He know who really trustin' Him.

8.text: But His enemies? He floodin' their spot. Gonna wipe it clean. Darkness gon' chase 'em down.

9.text: Y'all think y'all can plot on God? He gon' shut all that down — for good. That affliction? Ain't comin' back a second time.

10.text: Even if y'all tangled up and wild drunk, God gon' burn y'all up like dry brush in a fire.

11.text: Somebody from y'all crew out here schemin' against the Lord — plotting evil, runnin' they mouth.

12.text: But God said: "They might look safe. Might be plenty of 'em. But when I pass through, they gettin' chopped down. Yeah, I let you suffer for a minute, But that pain? I'm done with it."

13.text: "I'm breakin' that heavy chain off your neck. Snappin' them ropes. You free now."

14.text: God done spoke on this one: "Your name? Ain't nobody gonna remember it. I'ma smash your idols — carved or molded. Diggin' your grave myself, 'cause you foul."

15.text: Look! Somebody runnin' up in the hills, Bringing good news, shouting peace! Judah, go head and celebrate your feasts. Keep your vows. That wicked man? He ain't ever walkin' through here again. He gone. For good.

1.text: Look who pullin' up now — the one who scatters everything in sight. Better guard the gate, post up on the road, tighten up your crew, and get your strength up.

2.text: 'Cause the Lord about to bring Jacob back to glory — just like He did with Israel. Y'all tore up their vines and left 'em dry, but He fixin' to restore what y'all wrecked.

3.text: His warriors stay ready — shields shined up red, soldiers drippin' in scarlet. Them chariots lit up like fire, swords flashin' like it's go time.

4.text: Chariots tearin' through the city streets, runnin' wild in the open roads. They movin' like fireballs, lightnin' fast.

5.text: He tryin' to rally his top men — but they stumblin' all over the place. They rush to the wall, scramblin' to hold the line.

6.text: But the river gates bust wide open — palace crumblin', foundations gone.

7.text: It's already written: She gettin' dragged off into exile. Her ladies cryin' soft like doves, beatin' on their chests in sorrow.

8.text: Nineveh used to be calm like a pool of water. Now? Everybody runnin' for their lives. "Stop! Stop!" they yell — but ain't nobody stoppin'.

9.text: Snatch that silver! Grab all the gold! Treasure everywhere — more riches than they can count.

10.text: Now it's all gone. The place empty, destroyed, silent. Hearts droppin', knees bucklin', everybody shakin', faces pale as ghosts.

11.text: Where's that lion den now? The spot where the big cats used to roam free — lion, lioness, and cubs? Ain't nobody scared back then.

12.text: That lion used to kill what he wanted, feedin' his fam, stackin' up meat in his cave like trophies.

13.text: But now God said: "I'm comin' for you. Your chariots? Burned up. Your young soldiers? Gettin' cut down. Your prey? Gone. And your messengers? Ain't nobody gon' hear from them again."

1.text: Woe to that bloodstained city! Full of lies, full of theft — and the violence? Never quits.

2.text: You hear it? Whips crackin', wheels rattlin', horses poundin' the ground, chariots clankin' down the street.

3.text: Warriors ridin' in swords drawn, spears flashin' — Bodies everywhere. Dead piled high. Folks trippin' over corpses 'cause the streets so full of 'em.

4.text: And why? 'Cause this city was out here seducin' nations like a smooth-talkin' harlot — witchcraft in her hands, spells castin' families and countries into her trap.

5.text: "I'm comin' for you," says the Lord of Heaven's Armies. "I'ma snatch your skirt up over your head and let the world see you exposed. Everybody gon' see your shame.

6.text: I'ma throw filth on you, drag your name through the mud, and turn you into a spectacle.

7.text: Folks gon' run the other way like, 'Dang! Nineveh done for!' Ain't nobody cryin' over you. Ain't even no one to comfort you."

8.text: You thought you was better than No Amon? That city by the Nile? She had water for walls, rivers for defense.

9.text: Ethiopia and Egypt had her back, Put and Libya too — a whole army of allies. But guess what?

10.text: She still got snatched up, kids murdered in the streets, leaders rolled like dice for fun, and all her bosses got chained up.

11.text: Now it's your turn. You gon' get drunk and disappear, hidin' from your enemies, lookin' for shelter.

12.text: Your fortresses? They soft — like ripe figs just waitin' to fall into someone's mouth.

13.text: Your soldiers? Like scared women in the middle of war. Your gates? Wide open. Fire 'bout to burn all that down.

14.text: Go ahead — draw your water, stack them bricks, mold that clay, fortify the walls all you want…

15.text: But the fire still comin'. The sword still slicin'. The locusts still eatin'. Multiply like you some army of bugs — it won't save you.

16.text: You had merchants swarmin' like stars in the sky — but they flew off with all the loot when stuff got hot.

17.text: Your officials? Just grasshoppers. Campin' out when it's cold, but soon as the sun pop out? Poof — they gone. Don't nobody even know where they went.

18.text: Yo, king of Assyria — your shepherds sleepin'. Your leaders gone. Your people scattered like sheep in the mountains. And ain't nobody comin' to find them.

19.text: Your wound? Yeah, that ain't healin'. Your pain run deep. Everybody who hears this story? Gon' be clappin'. 'Cause ain't nobody escaped the evil you spread for so long.

1.text: These the words of Nehemiah, Hachaliah's son. It all went down in the month of Chislev, in the twentieth year, while I was chillin' in the fortress city of Shushan.

2.text: My brother Hanani pulled up with some folks from Judah, so I asked 'em how the folks who made it through exile were doin', and what was up with Jerusalem.

3.text: They told me straight up: 'The folks left in the land after all that captivity? They strugglin', for real. Folks clownin' 'em, and the city wall is in shambles. Gates got torched—burned to the ground.'

4.text: When I heard all that, man—I just sat down and cried. I mourned for days, fastin' and prayin' to the God of heaven. That pain hit deep.

5.text: I said, 'Lord God of heaven, You mighty and awesome, always keepin' Your promises and showin' love to the ones who ride for You and keep Your commandments—'

6.text: Please, hear me out. Open Your ears and eyes to this prayer I'm bringin' You day and night for Your people Israel. I'm layin' it all out—the sins we done committed. Me, my family, all of us—we messed up.

7.text: We been actin' foul, real corrupt, and we ain't kept the laws, rules, or directions You gave Moses, Your servant.

8.text: But God, remember what You told Moses: 'If y'all wild out and get disloyal, I'll scatter y'all across the nations.'

9.text: 'But if y'all come back to Me, stay loyal, and follow what I said—I'll gather y'all up, no matter how far gone you are, and bring you back to the place I picked to carry My name.'

10.text: These Your people, Lord. The ones You bought back with Your strong hand and mighty power.

11.text: So please, Lord, listen to me and all Your servants who still fear You and call on Your name. Let me get some favor today. Let this man show me some grace.' (Side note: I was the king's cupbearer.)

1.text: So in the month of Nisan, during the twentieth year of King Artaxerxes, I was servin' him wine like usual. I gave it to the king—but this time, I wasn't even tryin' to hide how sad I looked. I'd never been down in front of him before.

2.text: The king peeped game and said, 'Yo, why your face look like that? You ain't sick—this gotta be some deep pain.' That shook me up. I was scared for real.

3.text: But I said, 'Long live the king! But how can I not be sad, when the city where my ancestors are buried is straight wrecked? The gates? Burned to ashes.'

4.text: Then the king asked me, 'So what you want?' I shot a quick prayer up to the God of heaven.

5.text: Then I told him, 'If it's all good with you, and you got favor on me, send me to Judah—to my people's city—so I can rebuild it.'

6.text: The king, with the queen sittin' right beside him, asked, 'How long you gon' be gone? When you comin' back?' I gave him a timeline, and he gave me the greenlight.

7.text: Then I added, 'If you cool with it, let me get some letters for the governors beyond the River, so they'll let me pass through on the way to Judah.'

8.text: 'Also, can I get a letter for Asaph, who runs your forest? I need timber to rebuild the temple gate fortress, the city wall, and a crib for myself.' The king said yes—God's favor was all over me.

9.text: So I went to the regional governors, handed them the letters. The king even sent army officers and cavalry with me—had me movin' official.

10.text: But when Sanballat the Horonite and Tobiah the Ammonite officer heard I was there to help Israel, they got real salty. They ain't like that at all.

11.text: When I got to Jerusalem, I laid low for three days.

12.text: One night, I got up and took a few folks with me. I ain't tell nobody what God put on my heart to do for Jerusalem. Didn't bring no extra animals either—just the one I was ridin'.

13.text: That night, we rolled out through the Valley Gate, past the Snake Spring and Dung Gate. I checked out the walls—all busted up. Gates still burnt.

14.text: Then I went toward the Fountain Gate and the King's Pool, but it got too tight—my ride couldn't even squeeze through.

15.text: So I went up through the valley, still scoping out the wall. Then I circled back and came back in through the Valley Gate.

16.text: Ain't nobody—priests, leaders, officials, or workers—knew where I went or what I was on. I hadn't said nothin' yet.

17.text: Then I finally told them, 'Y'all see what kind of mess we in. Jerusalem tore up, gates torched. Come on—let's rebuild this wall, so we ain't out here lookin' weak no more.'

18.text: I told 'em how God had been with me and what the king said. They got hype and said, 'Let's get up and build!' And they got straight to work.

19.text: But as soon as Sanballat, Tobiah, and Geshem the Arab heard about it, they clowned us. 'What y'all think y'all doin'? Y'all plannin' a rebellion or somethin'?'

20.text: I clapped back, 'The God of heaven got us. We gon' get up and build, 'cause this our business. Y'all? Y'all don't got no part, no claim, not even a memory in Jerusalem.'

1.text: Eliashib the high priest got up with his priest folks and started buildin' the Sheep Gate. They blessed it and put the doors on. They kept buildin' all the way to the Tower of the Hundred and even the Tower of Hananel—blessed that whole stretch too.

2.text: Right next to him, the crew from Jericho was workin'. Beside them, Zaccur, Imri's son, was doin' his part.

3.text: The sons of Hassenaah built the Fish Gate—they laid the beams, hung the doors, put the bolts and bars on tight.

4.text: Meremoth, son of Urijah, grandson of Koz, handled repairs next to them. Then came Meshullam, son of Berechiah, son of Meshezabel. Next to him, Zadok, son of Baana, got to work.

5.text: Then the Tekoite crew helped out—but their nobles ain't lift a finger. They thought they was too good for God's work.

6.text: Jehoiada, son of Paseah, and Meshullam, son of Besodeiah, fixed up the Old Gate. They set beams, hung doors, and locked it all in with bolts and bars.

7.text: Right next to them, Melatiah from Gibeon, Jadon from Meronoth, and the folks from Gibeon and Mizpah worked on the spot near the governor's house.

8.text: Uzziel, son of Harhaiah (he was a goldsmith), did repairs next to them. Right beside him, Hananiah the perfumer worked too. They reinforced the wall all the way to the Broad Wall.

9.text: Rephaiah, son of Hur and leader of half the Jerusalem district, patched up his part.

10.text: Jedaiah, son of Harumaph, worked on the section right in front of his house. Then Hattush, son of Hashabniah, jumped in too.

11.text: Malchijah (son of Harim) and Hashub (son of Pahath-Moab) tackled another section, plus the Tower of the Ovens.

12.text: Shallum, son of Hallohesh and leader of half of Jerusalem's district, worked too—with his daughters. Whole fam was puttin' in work.

13.text: Hanun and the crew from Zanoah fixed the Valley Gate. Built it up, put on doors, bolts, and bars. They even repaired 1,000 cubits of wall up to the Dung Gate.

14.text: Malchijah, son of Rechab and leader of Beth Haccerem, fixed the Dung Gate—built it and locked it down with bolts and bars.

15.text: Shallun, son of Col-Hozeh and leader in Mizpah, took care of the Fountain Gate. He built it, roofed it, locked it down, and also rebuilt the wall near the Pool of Shelah by the King's Garden—all the way to the steps from the City of David.

16.text: Nehemiah (not me, a different one—son of Azbuk), who led half the district of Beth Zur, fixed up the area by David's tombs, the man-made pool, and the House of the Mighty.

17.text: The Levites under Rehum (son of Bani) did repairs next. Then Hashabiah, leader of half the Keilah district, fixed up his zone.

18.text: Their folks under Bavai (son of Henadad) who led the other half of Keilah worked too.

19.text: Ezer, son of Jeshua and head man in Mizpah, handled repairs near the armory climb at the buttress.

20.text: Baruch, son of Zabbai, was mad focused—he worked carefully on another stretch, from the buttress to Eliashib the high priest's house.

21.text: Then Meremoth (son of Urijah, son of Koz) picked it back up, fixin' from Eliashib's door to the end of his crib.

22.text: The priests who lived out in the flatlands? They got busy too.

23.text: Benjamin and Hasshub worked right across from their house. Azariah (son of Maaseiah, son of Ananiah) patched up the wall by his own house.

24.text: Binnui (son of Henadad) did another stretch—from Azariah's house to the buttress and the corner.

25.text: Palal (son of Uzai) repaired by the buttress and the tower that sticks out from the king's upper house near the prison yard. Pedaiah (son of Parosh) was next up.

26.text: The temple servants stayin' in Ophel put in work all the way to the Water Gate and that big tower.

27.text: The Tekoites weren't done—they came back and worked another part, up to the wall of Ophel.

28.text: Beyond the Horse Gate, the priests handled repairs—each one fixin' what was in front of their own spot.

29.text: Zadok (son of Immer) did the section by his house. Shemaiah (son of Shechaniah), who watched the East Gate, was on duty there.

30.text: Then came Hananiah (son of Shelemiah) and Hanun (sixth son of Zalaph)—they fixed another section. Meshullam (son of Berechiah) worked by his place.

31.text: Malchijah, one of the goldsmiths, worked all the way to the temple servants' and merchants' area, up to the Miphkad Gate, and around to the upper room on the corner.

32.text: From that upper corner room to the Sheep Gate, the goldsmiths and merchants were tag-teaming repairs.

1.text: When Sanballat found out we was rebuildin' the wall, he lost it—dude was big mad. Started clownin' the Jews like it was a joke.

2.text: He stood up in front of his boys and the army of Samaria talkin' reckless: 'What these weak Jews think they doin'? They think they gon' rebuild by themselves? Gonna pray and it just magically finish in a day? They really tryna stack burnt-up bricks from trash heaps?'

3.text: Tobiah the Ammonite co-signed the shade: 'Man, even if a fox jumped on they wall, it'd crumble.'

4.text: So we prayed: 'Lord, hear us—we gettin' mocked out here. Flip it on them! Let them be the ones gettin' dragged off and humiliated.'

5.text: 'Don't let their mess-ups slide. Don't erase their sins, 'cause they dissin' You right in front of us while we tryna build.'

6.text: Still, we kept at it. We built that wall up halfway 'cause the people had they mind locked in—they was all in.

7.text: When Sanballat, Tobiah, the Arabs, Ammonites, and Ashdodites heard we really closin' the gaps in the wall, they got heated.

8.text: They started plottin' together to pull up on Jerusalem and start chaos.

9.text: But we stayed prayed up, and we had folks posted watchin' day and night—ready for whatever.

10.text: Judah started feelin' it though—they said, 'Man, we tired. There's too much junk and rubble everywhere. We can't keep this up.'

11.text: Our enemies was whisperin', 'They won't see us comin'. We gon' slide in, kill 'em off, and shut the whole project down.'

12.text: The Jews who stayed near 'em kept warnin' us—like ten times: 'No matter where y'all move, they plannin' to ambush you.'

13.text: So I set up folks in the cut—behind the lowest parts of the wall, where it was open. Had 'em grouped up by family, each one strapped with swords, spears, and bows.

14.text: I looked around, stepped up, and told the nobles, leaders, and everybody else: 'Don't be scared of them. Remember God—He mighty and awesome. Fight for your brothers, your sons, your daughters, your wives, and your homes!'

15.text: When our enemies found out we knew what was up—and God had already ruined their whole scheme—we all went back to work like normal.

16.text: From that point on, half the crew worked on construction, while the other half held it down with spears, shields, bows, and armor. The leaders stood behind the crew from Judah.

17.text: The folks buildin' and carryin' loads was on double-duty—workin' with one hand and holdin' a weapon with the other.

18.text: Every builder had their sword on their side while they worked. And the trumpet guy? He stayed right next to me.

19.text: I told the nobles, leaders, and everybody: 'Look, this job is big and we spread out across the wall.'

20.text: 'So when you hear that trumpet blow, run to that spot. God gon' fight for us right there.'

21.text: We kept grindin'. Half the crew held spears from the crack of dawn 'til the stars came out.

22.text: I also told the people: 'Everybody and your crew—stay the night in Jerusalem. You'll be our security squad at night, and work crew in the day.'

23.text: We ain't even change clothes—me, my people, the guards, nobody—unless we was washin' up. That's how locked in we were.

1.text: The people—and their wives too—started speakin' up loud. They was fed up with how their own Jewish brothers was treatin' them.

2.text: Some folks said, 'Look, we got big families—sons, daughters—we need grain just to eat and survive.'

3.text: Others said, 'We had to put up our fields, vineyards, and houses just to get food during this famine.'

4.text: Some said, 'We had to borrow money to pay the king's taxes on our land and vineyards.'

5.text: 'Now we just like everybody else, same flesh and blood, our kids just like theirs—but we out here sellin' our sons and daughters into slavery. Some of our daughters already gone. And we can't do nothin' to buy 'em back, 'cause our land and vineyards are already in somebody else's name.'

6.text: When I heard all that, I got hot. I was mad for real.

7.text: So after thinkin' it over hard, I called out the nobles and rulers. Told 'em straight up: 'Y'all out here taxin' your own people with interest. That ain't right.' Then I pulled everybody together for a big assembly to confront it.

8.text: I said to them, 'We been doin' what we can to buy back our Jewish people who got sold off to other nations. And now y'all turnin' around and sellin' your own folks again? What we supposed to do—buy 'em back from you too?' They had nothin' to say. Just silence.

9.text: Then I kept goin': 'This ain't it. Y'all know better. Ain't y'all scared of God? The way the nations watchin' us and talkin' down? We gotta do better.'

10.text: 'Me, my folks, and my crew—we been lendin' money and grain too. But we not taxin' interest. Let's dead this greedy mess now.'

11.text: 'Give them back everything today—their fields, vineyards, olive trees, houses, and that interest y'all been chargin'—money, grain, wine, oil, all of it.'

12.text: They said, 'We got you. We'll give it all back. Won't ask for nothin' else. We'll do exactly what you said.' So I called the priests and made them swear they'd follow through on that promise.

13.text: Then I shook out my clothes and said, 'Let God shake out anybody who don't keep this promise. Let 'em lose their stuff and be emptied out like these folds.' Everybody said, 'Amen!' and gave God praise. And they did what they said they would.

14.text: Also, ever since I was made governor in Judah—from year twenty to thirty-two of King Artaxerxes, twelve years total—I never took the governor's food allowance. Neither did my brothers.

15.text: The ones who came before me? They put heavy pressure on the people—takin' bread, wine, and forty silver coins on top of that. Even their staff was wildin' with power. But I ain't move like that—'cause I feared God.

16.text: I stayed focused on buildin' the wall. Didn't buy up no land for myself. And all my crew stayed on the job with me.

17.text: I fed 150 Jewish folks and leaders at my table, plus folks who came through from the surrounding nations.

18.text: Each day we was servin' one ox, six top-tier sheep, and birds too. Every ten days we had all kinds of wine in heavy supply. And still—I didn't take the governor's share. I knew the people were already carryin' too much.

19.text: 'Lord, remember me for good—for everything I done for these people.'

1.text: So check it—when Sanballat, Tobiah, Geshem the Arab, and all our haters heard that the wall was finished with no more gaps (except I hadn't put the doors on the gates yet), they got bold.

2.text: Sanballat and Geshem sent a message like, 'Yo, come meet us down in one of them villages on the plain of Ono.' But I already knew—they was plottin'. Tryna do me dirty.

3.text: I sent a message back like, 'I'm doin' important work—I ain't got time to come down there. Why should I stop buildin' just to meet y'all?'

4.text: They hit me with the same invite four times. I hit 'em back with the same energy. 'Nope.'

5.text: Then on the fifth time, Sanballat sent his boy with an open letter—tryna stir up drama.

6.text: The letter said: 'Everybody talkin'. Word is, you and the Jews tryna rebel. Geshem said y'all rebuildin' the wall 'cause you tryna make yourself king.'

7.text: 'Supposedly, you even got prophets lined up to announce you as king in Judah. And if the king hears this? It's gon' be smoke. So let's talk before it gets outta hand.'

8.text: I clapped back: 'None of that is true. You makin' this mess up outta thin air.'

9.text: They just wanted to shake us up—hopin' we'd get scared and fall off the job. But I prayed, 'God, keep my hands strong.'

10.text: Later I went to Shemaiah's house—he was on some undercover informant type stuff. He said, 'Let's hide in the temple, behind locked doors. They comin' for you tonight—they gon' try to kill you.'

11.text: I was like, 'Ain't no way I'm runnin'. You think I'm gon' hide in the temple just to save myself? I ain't goin'.'

12.text: That's when I realized—God didn't send him. Dude was paid off by Tobiah and Sanballat to fake a prophecy.

13.text: They wanted me to act scared, slip up, and sin—so they'd have dirt on me to drag my name through the mud.

14.text: God, remember Tobiah and Sanballat for what they pulled. And don't forget about Noadiah the prophetess and all the other folks who tried to scare me.

15.text: We finished that wall on the twenty-fifth of Elul. Took us fifty-two days.

16.text: When all our enemies heard and saw what we pulled off, they got shook. They knew—this wasn't just us. God made this happen.

17.text: But even then, some of Judah's elite was sendin' letters to Tobiah, and he was writin' them back.

18.text: A bunch of folks in Judah were tight with him—he was married into Shechaniah's family, and his son married Meshullam's daughter. So he had connections.

19.text: They kept tryin' to gas him up to me, like, 'Tobiah really ain't that bad.' Meanwhile, they ran back and told him everything I said. And he kept sendin' letters tryna shake me up.

1.text: Once we had that wall all the way up and the doors locked in, I set up the gatekeepers, singers, and Levites to hold it down.

2.text: I put my brother Hanani in charge of the city, along with Hananiah who ran the citadel. Dude was solid—loyal and feared God more than most.

3.text: I told them, 'Don't open them gates till the sun is high in the sky. And even then, keep guards on watch while you close and bar the doors. Set up guards from the folks in town—some watchin' by post, some watchin' outside their own front door.'

4.text: The city was big and had space, but barely anybody lived there. Most houses still weren't rebuilt yet.

5.text: Then God put it on my heart to round up the nobles, leaders, and regular folks to register them by family lines. I found a scroll with the names of those who came back during the first wave, and here's what it said:

6.text: These the people who returned to their cities in Judah after Babylon's King Nebuchadnezzar had taken 'em into captivity.

7.text: They rolled in with Zerubbabel—Jeshua, Nehemiah, Azariah, Raamiah, Nahamani, Mordecai, Bilshan, Mispereth, Bigvai, Nehum, and Baanah.

8.text: Parosh's crew—2,172.

9.text: Shephatiah's line—372.

10.text: Arah's fam—652.

11.text: The sons of Pahath-Moab (from Jeshua and Joab's line)—2,818.

12.text: Elam's squad—1,254.

13.text: Zattu's people—845.

14.text: Zaccai's crew—760.

15.text: Binnui's fam—648.

16.text: Bebai's line—628.

17.text: Azgad's people—2,322.

18.text: Adonikam's descendants—667.

19.text: Bigvai's group—2,067.

20.text: Adin's folks—655.

21.text: Ater (from Hezekiah's line)—98.

22.text: Hashum's family—328.

23.text: Bezai's people—324.

24.text: Hariph's crew—112.

25.text: Gibeon's sons—95.

26.text: Bethlehem and Netophah folks—188.

27.text: Anathoth's people—128.

28.text: Beth Azmaveth's crew—42.

29.text: Kirjath Jearim, Chephirah, and Beeroth together—743.

30.text: Ramah and Geba—621.

31.text: Michmas men—122.

32.text: Bethel and Ai together—123.

33.text: The other Nebo group—52.

34.text: The other Elam line—1,254.

35.text: Harim's crew—320.

36.text: The folks from Jericho—345 deep.

37.text: Lod, Hadid, and Ono's crew—721.

38.text: Senaah's squad—3,930. That was a whole crowd!

39.text: Jedaiah's family line (from Jeshua's house)—973 priests.

40.text: Immer's line—1,052.

41.text: Pashhur's folks—1,247.

42.text: Harim's line—1,017.

43.text: Jeshua and Kadmiel's line (from Hodevah's side)—74 Levites.

44.text: Asaph's crew—the singers—148.

45.text: Gatekeepers held it down: Shallum's fam, Ater's fam, Talmon's fam, Akkub's fam, Hatita's fam, and Shobai's fam—138 total.

46.text: The Nethinim crew showed up too. Ziha, Hasupha, Tabbaoth,

47.text: Keros, Sia, Padon,

48.text: Lebana, Hagaba, Salmai,

49.text: Hanan, Giddel, Gahar,

50.text: Reaiah, Rezin, Nekoda,

51.text: Gazzam, Uzza, Paseah,

52.text: Besai, Meunim, Nephishesim,

53.text: Bakbuk, Hakupha, Harhur,

54.text: Bazlith, Mehida, Harsha,

55.text: Barkos, Sisera, Tamah,

56.text: Neziah, and Hatipha.

57.text: These folks came from Solomon's servant lines: Sotai, Sophereth, Perida,

58.text: Jaala, Darkon, Giddel,

59.text: Shephatiah, Hattil, Pochereth of Zebaim, and Amon.

60.text: All together—Nethinim and Solomon's servant descendants—392.

61.text: Some came from Tel Melah, Tel Harsha, Cherub, Addon, and Immer, but couldn't prove their family line or if they were really from Israel.

62.text: Delaiah, Tobiah, and Nekoda's folks—642 total.

63.text: Even some priest families couldn't trace their roots: Habaiah, Koz, and Barzillai (who had married into Barzillai the Gileadite's family and took that last name).

64.text: They tried to get counted in the priest list, but they didn't make the cut. So they were shut out—couldn't serve as priests.

65.text: The governor told 'em not to eat any of the holy food till a priest could check things out with the Urim and Thummim (God's decision tools).

67.text: Plus 7,337 male and female servants. They had 245 singers—men and women.

69.text: Camels? 435. Donkeys? 6,720. That's a whole lotta hooves.

70.text: Some of the heads of families gave to support the temple work. The governor dropped 1,000 gold coins, 50 basins, and 530 sets of priest gear.

71.text: Other family leaders gave 20,000 gold coins and 2,200 silver minas.

72.text: The rest of the people gave another 20,000 gold coins, 2,000 silver minas, and 67 priest outfits.

73.text: So the priests, Levites, gatekeepers, singers, some regular folks, the Nethinim, and all the Israelites moved into their own cities. And when the seventh month came, everybody was settled in their spots.

1.text: Everybody pulled up to the Water Gate plaza like one big family. They asked Ezra the scribe to bring out the Book of the Law that God gave Moses for Israel.

2.text: So Ezra, the priest, stepped up with the book and read it out loud to the whole crowd—men, women, and anybody old enough to understand. It was the first day of the seventh month.

3.text: Ezra read from the Law in front of the Water Gate plaza, from sun up to noon. The people was locked in—listening close, tuned in to every word.

4.text: Ezra stood on a wooden platform they built just for this. On his right stood Mattithiah, Shema, Anaiah, Urijah, Hilkiah, and Maaseiah. On his left: Pedaiah, Mishael, Malchijah, Hashum, Hashbadana, Zechariah, and Meshullam.

5.text: Ezra opened the book so everybody could see. Since he was posted up above the crowd, when he cracked that book open, the whole crowd stood up.

6.text: Ezra blessed the Lord, the great God, and everybody shouted, 'Amen! Amen!' with their hands lifted. Then they bowed down, faces to the ground, worshipin' the Lord.

7.text: Jeshua, Bani, Sherebiah, Jamin, Akkub, Shabbethai, Hodijah, Maaseiah, Kelita, Azariah, Jozabad, Hanan, Pelaiah, and the Levites were out there helpin' folks understand what the Word meant. Everybody stayed in place.

8.text: They read the Law clearly, verse by verse, breaking it down so the people could really get it. They made it plain.

9.text: Then Nehemiah the governor, Ezra the priest and scribe, and the Levites told the people, 'Today is holy to the Lord. Don't cry, don't be sad.' Because everybody started weepin' when they heard the Law being read.

10.text: Ezra said, 'Go on now—eat good, drink somethin' sweet, and make sure to share with folks who ain't got nothin' ready. Today is holy. Don't be down, 'cause the joy of the Lord is where your strength comes from.'

11.text: The Levites calmed everybody down like, 'It's all right. Be still. This day is sacred. Don't let sadness take over.'

12.text: So the people left, feelin' lifted—eatin', drinkin', sharin', and celebratin', 'cause now they understood what had just been spoken to them.

13.text: On day two, all the heads of households, plus the priests and Levites, came back to Ezra to dig deeper into the Word.

14.text: They found in the Law that God gave Moses that the people were supposed to live in booths—little shelters—during the feast in the seventh month.

15.text: They were supposed to spread the word in every town and in Jerusalem: 'Go up the mountain and grab olive branches, wild olive branches, myrtle, palm, and leafy trees to build your booths—just like it says in the Law.'

16.text: So the people went and got what they needed and made the booths—on rooftops, in courtyards, in God's temple courts, and all up in the Water Gate and Ephraim Gate squares.

17.text: Everybody who had come back from exile built booths and chilled under 'em. They hadn't celebrated like this since Joshua's time. And the joy? Man, it was next level.

18.text: Ezra kept reading from the Book of the Law every day—first day to the last. They celebrated the feast for seven days, and on the eighth day, they had a sacred gathering, just like the Law said.

1.text: On the 24th day of the month, all the Israelites gathered again—but this time, they came fasting, rockin' sackcloth, and had dust on their heads. They came humble.

2.text: The ones with Israelite blood stepped aside from the foreigners. They stood up and confessed their sins—and the mess their ancestors had gotten into too.

3.text: They stood where they were and read from God's Law for a fourth of the day. Then for another fourth, they confessed and worshipped the Lord their God.

4.text: Jeshua, Bani, Kadmiel, Shebaniah, Bunni, Sherebiah, Bani, and Chenani stood up on the Levite stairs and cried out loud to God with passion.

5.text: Then the Levites—Jeshua, Kadmiel, Bani, Hashabniah, Sherebiah, Hodijah, Shebaniah, and Pethahiah—said: 'Everybody stand up and bless the Lord your God forever and ever!'

6.text: 'You alone, Lord, are God. You made the heavens—even the highest heavens with all their angels, the earth and everything on it, the oceans and everything in them. You keep it all going. Heaven's army worships You.'

7.text: 'You chose Abram and brought him out of Ur in Babylon territory, then changed his name to Abraham.'

8.text: 'You saw his heart was true to You, so You made a covenant with him—to give his descendants the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Perizzites, Jebusites, and Girgashites. And You kept Your word—'cause You righteous like that.'

9.text: 'You saw our people suffer in Egypt. You heard them cryin' at the Red Sea.'

10.text: 'You flexed with signs and wonders on Pharaoh, his crew, and all Egypt, 'cause You knew how foul they were treatin' Your people. You made a name for Yourself that's still known today.'

11.text: 'You split the sea so our folks could walk through on dry land. But You threw the Egyptians in after 'em—sank 'em like stones in deep water.'

12.text: 'By day, You led them with a cloud. At night, fire lit the way. You never left 'em lost.'

13.text: 'You came down on Mount Sinai and spoke from heaven. You gave 'em laws that were right, rules that were true, and commands that were just.'

14.text: 'You taught 'em about Your holy Sabbath and handed down commandments through Moses, Your servant.'

15.text: 'You fed them with bread from heaven when they were hungry and gave them water from a rock when they were thirsty. You told 'em to go take the land You promised them.'

16.text: 'But our ancestors got proud and hard-headed. They ignored what You said.'

17.text: 'They straight up refused to obey. Forgot about the miracles You did for them. Got rebellious. Picked a new leader to take them back to slavery.'

18.text: 'They even made a fake calf and said, "This is our god who brought us out of Egypt." Wild disrespect.'

19.text: 'But even then, You didn't dip on them. You kept guiding them with the cloud by day and fire by night—still showin' love.'

20.text: 'You gave them Your Spirit to teach them. Kept feedin' them manna. Gave 'em water when they were thirsty.'

21.text: 'You took care of them for 40 years in the wilderness. They had everything they needed. Their clothes didn't rip. Their feet ain't even swell up.'

22.text: 'You handed them kingdoms and nations, even broke up the lands so they could settle in them. They got Sihon's territory and Og's land too.'

23.text: 'You made their families grow like stars in the sky. Then brought them into the land You'd promised to their ancestors.'

24.text: 'They took over the land. You gave 'em the Canaanites, the kings, and all the locals—put it all in their hands.'

25.text: 'They moved into strong cities and lived off the good life—houses stocked with everything, wells already dug, vineyards, olive trees, and more fruit than they could eat. They ate good, got full, and lived it up off Your kindness.'

26.text: 'But then they rebelled again. Disrespected You, tossed Your law behind their backs. They even killed the prophets who warned them to turn back. Just kept doin' the most.'

27.text: 'So You let their enemies catch 'em slippin'. But every time they cried out to You, You came through. Sent rescuers to save them—over and over.'

28.text: 'But once things calmed down? They wilded out again. So You let the enemies come back. But again, when they cried out, You came through. Mercy after mercy.'

29.text: 'You kept warnin' them to come back to Your law. But they acted proud, refused to listen. Broke the rules that could've given them life. Shrugged off Your word, stiff-necked, wouldn't hear it.'

30.text: 'You were patient with them for years. Kept speakin' through prophets by Your Spirit. Still, they ain't listen. So You gave 'em up to other nations.'

31.text: 'Even then, You didn't completely wipe 'em out. You still had mercy. You're a God full of grace.'

32.text: 'So now, God—great, mighty, and awesome—the one who always keeps His word—don't overlook what we've been through. From Assyria 'til now, our kings, our leaders, priests, prophets, ancestors—everybody's gone through it.'

33.text: 'But You were fair. Everything that's happened to us? We deserved it. You stayed faithful—we didn't.'

34.text: 'Our kings, leaders, priests, and ancestors all ignored Your law. They wouldn't listen to Your commandments, even though You warned them.'

35.text: 'Even when they lived in a land full of blessings, in comfort, with everything they needed, they still wouldn't serve You. They stayed in their mess.'

36.text: 'Look at us now—we servants on our own land. The same land You gave our ancestors to enjoy.'

37.text: 'It's producing crops, but it's goin' to the kings You let rule over us—'cause of our sins. They run our bodies and our animals however they want. We strugglin' out here.'

38.text: 'So we makin' a fresh covenant—puttin' it in writing. And our leaders, Levites, and priests are signin' it to show we for real.'

1.text: These the folks who put their stamp on the covenant: Nehemiah the governor, son of Hacaliah, and Zedekiah.

2.text: Seraiah, Azariah, Jeremiah.

3.text: Pashhur, Amariah, Malchijah.

4.text: Hattush, Shebaniah, Malluch.

5.text: Harim, Meremoth, Obadiah.

6.text: Daniel, Ginnethon, Baruch.

7.text: Meshullam, Abijah, Mijamin.

8.text: Maaziah, Bilgai, and Shemaiah—these were the priests.

9.text: The Levites: Jeshua son of Azaniah, Binnui (from Henadad's family), and Kadmiel.

10.text: Their folks: Shebaniah, Hodijah, Kelita, Pelaiah, Hanan.

11.text: Micha, Rehob, Hashabiah.

12.text: Zaccur, Sherebiah, Shebaniah.

13.text: Hodijah, Bani, and Beninu.

14.text: The leaders of the people: Parosh, Pahath-Moab, Elam, Zattu, Bani.

15.text: Bunni, Azgad, Bebai.

16.text: Adonijah, Bigvai, Adin.

17.text: Ater, Hezekiah, Azzur.

18.text: Hodijah, Hashum, Bezai.

19.text: Hariph, Anathoth, Nebai.

20.text: Magpiash, Meshullam, Hezir.

21.text: Meshezabel, Zadok, Jaddua.

22.text: Pelatiah, Hanan, Anaiah.

23.text: Hoshea, Hananiah, Hasshub.

24.text: Hallohesh, Pilha, Shobek.

25.text: Rehum, Hashabnah, Maaseiah.

26.text: Ahijah, Hanan, Anan.

27.text: Malluch, Harim, and Baanah.

28.text: Everybody else—the priests, Levites, gatekeepers, singers, temple servants, and all who separated themselves from the surrounding people to follow God's Law—along with their wives, sons, and daughters (everyone who understood what was goin' on)—

29.text: They all made a promise with an oath, sayin' they'd follow God's Law, which He gave through Moses His servant, and they'd live by all the commands, rules, and regulations of the Lord.

30.text: We won't give our daughters to marry folks from outside the faith, and we won't let our sons marry their daughters either.

31.text: If folks from the land come sellin' goods on the Sabbath or any holy day, we ain't buyin'. And every seventh year, we'll let the land rest and cancel all debts.

32.text: We made a rule to chip in a third of a shekel each year for the upkeep of God's house.

33.text: That money goes to the bread offerings, the daily grain and burnt offerings, Sabbath sacrifices, New Moon rituals, festival supplies, holy things, sin offerings for the nation, and all the work done in God's house.

34.text: We rolled dice among the priests, Levites, and the people to decide when each family would bring wood for the altar of God every year, just like the Law said.

35.text: We promised to bring the first of our crops and the first of every tree's fruit to the house of the Lord every year.

36.text: We'll also bring our oldest sons and the firstborn of our livestock—just like the Law says—to God's house, to the priests who serve there.

37.text: We'll bring the first batch of our dough, our offerings, the fruit from every kind of tree, our new wine and oil, to the priests and to the storerooms at God's house. And we'll bring our tithes to the Levites, since they're the ones assigned to receive them in every town where we farm.

38.text: And when the Levites collect the tithes, a priest from Aaron's family will be there too. Then the Levites will take a tenth of that tithe up to the temple storerooms.

39.text: Us Israelites, along with the Levites, will bring offerings of grain, wine, and oil to the storage rooms, where the temple gear is kept—and where the priests, gatekeepers, and singers stay. We not gon' neglect God's house. Period.

1.text: The leaders of the people were already livin' in Jerusalem. But the rest of the people cast lots to pick one outta every ten to move into the holy city, Jerusalem. The other nine stayed in their own towns.

2.text: The people gave props to the ones who volunteered to live in Jerusalem on their own.

3.text: These the heads of the province who lived in Jerusalem. (Meanwhile, the rest of Israel—priests, Levites, temple servants, and descendants of Solomon's workers—lived in their hometowns throughout Judah.)

4.text: In Jerusalem lived some folks from the tribes of Judah and Benjamin. From Judah's side: Athaiah, son of Uzziah, son of Zechariah, son of Amariah, son of Shephatiah, son of Mahalalel—he was from the Perez line.

5.text: Also Maaseiah, son of Baruch, son of Col-Hozeh, son of Hazaiah, son of Adaiah, son of Joiarib, son of Zechariah, son of Shiloni.

6.text: There were 468 soldiers from the Perez clan livin' in Jerusalem. All of 'em strong.

7.text: From Benjamin's family: Sallu, son of Meshullam, son of Joed, son of Pedaiah, son of Kolaiah, son of Maaseiah, son of Ithiel, son of Jeshaiah.

8.text: Gabbai and Sallai came after him. They had 928 men in total.

9.text: Joel son of Zichri was their leader, and Judah son of Senuah was second-in-command for the city.

10.text: Among the priests were Jedaiah son of Joiarib, and Jachin.

11.text: Seraiah, son of Hilkiah, son of Meshullam, son of Zadok, son of Meraioth, son of Ahitub, was in charge of God's house.

12.text: Their crew—who worked in God's house—was 822 people strong. Also there was Adaiah, son of Jeroham, son of Pelaliah, son of Amzi, son of Zechariah, son of Pashhur, son of Malchijah.

13.text: And his people, the family heads, were 242 men. Also Amashai, son of Azarel, son of Ahzai, son of Meshillemoth, son of Immer.

14.text: And his crew—128 tough men. Zabdiel, son of one of the greats, was their leader.

15.text: From the Levites: Shemaiah, son of Hasshub, son of Azrikam, son of Hashabiah, son of Bunni.

16.text: Shabbethai and Jozabad, who were some of the Levite chiefs, handled business outside God's temple.

17.text: Mattaniah, son of Micha, son of Zabdi, son of Asaph, was the worship leader who kicked things off with thanksgiving and prayer. Bakbukiah was second-in-command. Abda, son of Shammua, son of Galal, son of Jeduthun, was also with them.

18.text: Altogether, 284 Levites were livin' in the holy city.

19.text: The gatekeepers were Akkub, Talmon, and their brothers—172 men standin' watch at the gates.

20.text: The rest of Israel—the priests and Levites—lived throughout Judah in the towns they inherited.

21.text: The temple servants lived in Ophel. Ziha and Gishpa were the ones over them.

22.text: Uzzi, son of Bani, son of Hashabiah, son of Mattaniah, son of Micha, from Asaph's line, was in charge of the Levites in Jerusalem. He handled the singers who ran worship at God's house.

23.text: The king had made it law that the singers got their share of food each day. That was their setup.

24.text: Pethahiah, son of Meshezabel, from Zerah's line (Judah's son), was the king's right-hand man for anything dealin' with the people.

25.text: In the villages and farmlands: some of Judah's people lived in Kirjath Arba and the villages around it, Dibon and its villages, and Jekabzeel and its villages.

26.text: Also in Jeshua, Moladah, and Beth Pelet.

27.text: In Hazar Shual, Beersheba, and the nearby towns.

28.text: In Ziklag, Meconah, and their surrounding villages.

29.text: In En Rimmon, Zorah, and Jarmuth.

30.text: In Zanoah, Adullam, and nearby villages, as well as in Lachish and its fields, and in Azekah and its villages. Basically, they spread out from Beersheba up to the Valley of Hinnom.

31.text: Some folks from Benjamin lived in Geba, Michmash, Aija, and Bethel with its villages.

32.text: Also in Anathoth, Nob, and Ananiah.

33.text: In Hazor, Ramah, and Gittaim.

34.text: In Hadid, Zeboim, and Neballat.

35.text: In Lod, Ono, and the Valley of the Craftsmen.

36.text: Some of the Levite groups from Judah were livin' in Benjamin's territory.

1.text: These the priests and Levites that came up with Zerubbabel son of Shealtiel, and Jeshua: Seraiah, Jeremiah, Ezra.

2.text: Amariah, Malluch, Hattush.

3.text: Shechaniah, Rehum, Meremoth.

4.text: Iddo, Ginnethoi, Abijah.

5.text: Mijamin, Maadiah, Bilgah.

6.text: Shemaiah, Joiarib, Jedaiah.

7.text: Sallu, Amok, Hilkiah, and Jedaiah. These were the heads of the priests and their brothers during Jeshua's time.

8.text: The Levites were: Jeshua, Binnui, Kadmiel, Sherebiah, Judah, and Mattaniah—he led the praise songs with his crew.

9.text: Bakbukiah and Unni, their brothers, stood across from them in rotation.

10.text: Jeshua had Joiakim, Joiakim had Eliashib, Eliashib had Joiada.

11.text: Joiada had Jonathan, and Jonathan had Jaddua.

12.text: In Joiakim's time, the priest family heads were: for Seraiah—Meraiah; for Jeremiah—Hananiah.

13.text: For Ezra—Meshullam; for Amariah—Jehohanan.

14.text: For Melichu—Jonathan; for Shebaniah—Joseph.

15.text: For Harim—Adna; for Meraioth—Helkai.

16.text: For Iddo—Zechariah; for Ginnethon—Meshullam.

17.text: For Abijah—Zichri. For Minjamin and Moadiah—Piltai.

18.text: For Bilgah—Shammua; for Shemaiah—Jehonathan.

19.text: For Joiarib—Mattenai; for Jedaiah—Uzzi.

20.text: For Sallai—Kallai; for Amok—Eber.

21.text: For Hilkiah—Hashabiah; for Jedaiah—Nethanel.

22.text: During King Darius of Persia's reign, they kept records of the Levites and priest family heads in Eliashib, Joiada, Johanan, and Jaddua's time.

23.text: The family heads from the Levites, up through Johanan son of Eliashib, were recorded in the history books.

24.text: The top Levites were: Hashabiah, Sherebiah, and Jeshua son of Kadmiel. Their families stood across from them, doing praise and thanksgiving, group by group, just like David told 'em.

25.text: Mattaniah, Bakbukiah, Obadiah, Meshullam, Talmon, and Akkub were the gatekeepers guardin' the storage rooms by the gates.

26.text: All these folks were alive in the time of Joiakim son of Jeshua, son of Jozadak, and also in Nehemiah the governor and Ezra the priest-scribe's days.

27.text: When it came time to dedicate the wall of Jerusalem, they went and gathered all the Levites from wherever they were to bring 'em to the city for the celebration—with joy, praise, music, cymbals, strings, and harps.

28.text: The singers showed up too, from the villages around Jerusalem, especially the Netophathite towns.

29.text: They came from Gilgal, and the fields around Geba and Azmaveth—'cause the singers had built their own villages near the city.

30.text: Then the priests and Levites purified themselves, the people, the gates, and the wall.

31.text: I had the leaders of Judah climb up on the wall. I put together two big choirs to lead the thanksgiving. One went to the right, toward the Dung Gate.

32.text: Following them were Hoshaiah and half of Judah's leaders.

33.text: Then came Azariah, Ezra, Meshullam.

34.text: Judah, Benjamin, Shemaiah, Jeremiah.

35.text: And some of the priests' sons with trumpets—Zechariah, son of Jonathan, son of Shemaiah, son of Mattaniah, son of Michaiah, son of Zaccur, son of Asaph.

36.text: His people were Shemaiah, Azarel, Milalai, Gilalai, Maai, Nethanel, Judah, and Hanani—all with instruments from David's time. Ezra the scribe was leadin' the way.

37.text: They passed the Fountain Gate, climbed the stairs of David's City, went up the wall near David's palace, and kept goin' to the Water Gate on the east side.

38.text: The other choir went the opposite way, and I followed them with half the people. We walked on top of the wall past the Oven Tower, to the Broad Wall.

39.text: Then above the Gate of Ephraim, past the Old Gate, Fish Gate, the Tower of Hananel, the Tower of the Hundred, and on to the Sheep Gate. We stopped at the Prison Gate.

40.text: So both choirs stood inside God's house. Me and half the officials were there too.

41.text: The priests were Eliakim, Maaseiah, Minjamin, Michaiah, Elioenai, Zechariah, and Hananiah—with trumpets.

42.text: Also Maaseiah, Shemaiah, Eleazar, Uzzi, Jehohanan, Malchijah, Elam, and Ezer. The singers sang loud, and Jezrahiah was runnin' the choir.

43.text: That day, they gave big offerings and celebrated hard. God had filled their hearts with joy. Even the women and kids were turnin' up. You could hear the joy of Jerusalem from way far off.

44.text: At that time, folks were put in charge of the storerooms for the offerings, firstfruits, and tithes. They gathered all the portions from the fields to give to the priests and Levites—'cause Judah was hyped about the ones servin' in God's house.

45.text: The singers and gatekeepers kept doin' what God asked, and made sure everything stayed purified—just like David and Solomon had set up.

46.text: Back in the day of David and Asaph, they had music leaders and songs of praise and thanksgiving for God.

47.text: In Zerubbabel and Nehemiah's time, all Israel gave what was due to the singers and gatekeepers every day. They also set apart holy things for the Levites, and the Levites passed it on to the sons of Aaron.

1.text: That day, they read the Book of Moses out loud for everybody to hear. They found out it said no Ammonite or Moabite was ever supposed to be part of God's people.

2.text: 'Cause back when Israel needed help, those folks ain't bring no bread or water—instead, they hired Balaam to throw curses. But God flipped that curse into a blessing.

3.text: So when they heard what the Law said, they cut off ties with all the folks who weren't part of Israel.

4.text: Before all that, Eliashib the priest—who was in charge of the temple storerooms—was tight with Tobiah.

5.text: He let Tobiah move into a big room that used to hold grain offerings, incense, temple tools, and the tithes for the Levites, singers, and gatekeepers—plus the offerings for the priests.

6.text: I wasn't in Jerusalem when that happened. I had gone back to the king in the 32nd year of King Artaxerxes of Babylon. Later on, I asked for permission to return.

7.text: When I got back to Jerusalem, I saw what Eliashib had done for Tobiah—lettin' him live inside God's temple courts. I was heated.

8.text: I was sick over it, so I tossed all of Tobiah's furniture out that room. Everything.

9.text: Then I told 'em to deep-clean the rooms, and I put all the temple goods and grain offerings and incense back where they belonged.

10.text: I also found out the Levites hadn't been gettin' their share, so the singers and Levites had left and gone back to workin' their fields.

11.text: I went off on the officials and said, 'Why y'all lettin' God's house fall off like this?' Then I brought the Levites and singers back and put them in place.

12.text: Then all Judah brought in their tithes—grain, wine, and oil—and put it in the storehouse.

13.text: I put Shelemiah the priest, Zadok the scribe, and Pedaiah the Levite in charge of the storehouse. Hanan son of Zaccur, son of Mattaniah, was right there with them. These men had good reputations. Their job was to hand everything out right.

14.text: God, remember me for this. Don't erase the good I did for Your temple and everything that goes on in it.

15.text: In those days, I saw folks in Judah workin' the wine press on the Sabbath. They was bringin' in grain, loadin' donkeys with wine, grapes, figs, and all kinds of stuff—and sellin' it on the Sabbath in Jerusalem. I had to step in and check them.

16.text: Some men from Tyre lived in the city too. They brought fish and all kinds of goods and sold them to Judah on the Sabbath—even in Jerusalem.

17.text: I called out the nobles of Judah and said, 'What y'all doin' breakin' the Sabbath like this? This ain't right.'

18.text: 'Didn't our ancestors mess up just like this? And didn't God bring all this drama on us and this city because of that? Now y'all addin' more fuel to the fire by disrespectin' the Sabbath again.'

19.text: So when the sun started settin' before Sabbath, I ordered the city gates shut—and told 'em don't open till Sabbath's over. I posted guards at the gates to stop anything from comin' in.

20.text: Some of the merchants still tried to camp out outside the wall once or twice.

21.text: But I warned 'em: 'Why y'all hangin' around the wall? Do it again, and I'ma lay hands on you.' After that, they ain't try that no more.

22.text: I told the Levites to cleanse themselves and guard the gates so the Sabbath would stay holy. God, remember me for this too, and show me mercy like only You can.

23.text: Around that same time, I saw some Jews had married women from Ashdod, Ammon, and Moab.

24.text: Half their kids couldn't even speak our language—they was speakin' Ashdod or one of them other foreign tongues.

25.text: I got in their faces, cursed 'em out, smacked some, even pulled hair. Then I made 'em swear to God: 'Don't let your daughters marry their sons, and don't take their daughters for your sons—or for yourselves.'

26.text: 'Didn't Solomon mess up this exact same way? And he was the king of all kings back in the day—loved by God, ruler over all Israel. But foreign women made even him fall.'

27.text: 'So now we supposed to ignore y'all doin' the same evil—betrayin' our God by marryin' these outsiders?'

28.text: One of Joiada's sons—he was Eliashib the high priest's grandson—had married Sanballat the Horonite's daughter. I kicked him out, no hesitation.

29.text: God, remember them for disrespectin' the priesthood and breakin' the sacred promise to the Levites and priests.

30.text: So I cleaned house. Got rid of anything foreign. I set the priests and Levites up with their duties—made sure they were doin' their jobs.

31.text: I also made sure the wood offerings and firstfruits were brought in on time. God, remember me for good.

1.text: The Lord pulled up on Moses while they was out in the wilderness of Sinai, inside the meeting tent. This was the first day of the second month, two years after they bounced up outta Egypt. He said,

2.text: 'Go 'head and count up everybody in Israel. Do it by family, by their daddy's people, name by name, every dude one by one.

3.text: If they twenty or older and can fight, count 'em. You and Aaron gotta list 'em out by their squads.

4.text: And every tribe gotta send a man, the leader of his family, to help y'all with the count.

5.text: Here go the names of the ones rolling with you: from Reuben, Elizur, son of Shedeur;

6.text: From Simeon, Shelumiel, son of Zurishaddai;

7.text: From Judah, Nahshon, son of Amminadab;

8.text: From Issachar, Nethanel, son of Zuar;

9.text: From Zebulun, Eliab, son of Helon;

10.text: From Joseph's people: from Ephraim, Elishama, son of Ammihud; from Manasseh, Gamaliel, son of Pedahzur;

11.text: From Benjamin, Abidan, son of Gideoni;

12.text: From Dan, Ahiezer, son of Ammishaddai;

13.text: From Asher, Pagiel, son of Ocran;

14.text: From Gad, Eliasaph, son of Deuel;

15.text: From Naphtali, Ahira, son of Enan.

16.text: These the main dudes, the head honchos of their family tribes. The top dogs over all the squads of Israel.

17.text: Moses and Aaron took these men, the ones called out by name,

18.text: And on the first day of the second month, they got all the people together. They ran through everybody's family history, going by their daddy's side, and listed out everybody name by name, twenty and up.

19.text: Just like the Lord told Moses, he counted them up in the wilderness of Sinai.

20.text: From Reuben, the firstborn of Israel: all the men twenty and up, able to fight, counted by their family and daddy's house—

21.text: The total for Reuben's squad: 46,500.

22.text: From Simeon, every dude twenty and up, ready for battle, counted by family—

23.text: Simeon's total: 59,300.

24.text: From Gad, all the men twenty and up, ready to fight, counted by their family—

25.text: Gad's total: 45,650.

26.text: From Judah, every man twenty and up, war-ready, counted by family—

27.text: Judah's total: 74,600.

28.text: From Issachar, all the men twenty and up, ready to ride—

29.text: Issachar's total: 54,400.

30.text: From Zebulun, every man twenty and up, suited up for war—

31.text: Zebulun's total: 57,400.

32.text: From Joseph's people, the Ephraim squad: every dude twenty and up, ready for battle—

33.text: Ephraim's total: 40,500.

34.text: From Manasseh, every man twenty and up, prepped for war—

35.text: Manasseh's total: 32,200.

36.text: From Benjamin, every dude twenty and up, down for the fight—

37.text: Benjamin's total: 35,400.

38.text: From Dan, all the men twenty and up, counted by family—

39.text: Dan's total: 62,700.

40.text: From Asher, all the men twenty and up, war-ready—

41.text: Asher's total: 41,500.

42.text: From Naphtali, every man twenty and up, suited up—

43.text: Naphtali's total: 53,400.

44.text: These the ones that got counted, the ones Moses and Aaron wrote down, plus the twelve leaders of Israel, one from each tribe.

45.text: So, after counting all the men twenty and up, ready to fight, by their family—

46.text: The grand total came up to 603,550.

47.text: But the Levites? They ain't get counted with the rest of 'em.

48.text: The Lord told Moses,

49.text: 'Don't count the tribe of Levi or put them in the mix with the rest of Israel.'

50.text: 'Instead, put them in charge of the tabernacle of the Testimony. They gon' handle all its stuff, move it when needed, and set it up when y'all stop. Ain't nobody else supposed to come near it.'

51.text: 'When it's time to move, the Levites gon' pack it up. When it's time to camp, they gon' set it up. If anybody else try to step up, they getting put down.'

52.text: 'Everybody else in Israel gotta camp by their own squad, under their family's banner.'

53.text: 'But the Levites? They gotta camp around the tabernacle, keeping it safe so my anger don't hit Israel. They gotta watch over the tabernacle like it's their main job.'

54.text: And that's exactly what Israel did. Just like the Lord told Moses, they followed through.

1.text: Then the Lord spoke to Moses and Aaron and said,

2.text: 'Tell everybody in Israel they gotta set up camp under their family's banner, posted up by their squad's emblem. But they can't camp too close to the meeting tent.'

3.text: 'On the east side, where the sun comes up, Judah's crew gon' set up first, posted up by their squad. Nahshon, son of Amminadab, gon' be their leader.'

4.text: 'Judah's army got 74,600 men.'

5.text: 'Next to them, Issachar's tribe gon' set up camp. Their leader is Nethanel, son of Zuar.'

6.text: 'Issachar's army got 54,400 men.'

7.text: 'Then Zebulun's tribe gon' set up next. Their leader is Eliab, son of Helon.'

8.text: 'Zebulun's army got 57,400 men.'
