2.text: "So you can keep good sense and know when to speak with real understanding."

3.text: "That smooth talk from a wild woman? Sound like honey, drip like oil—too slick."

4.text: "But in the end? She bitter like poison and cut deep like a double-edged sword."

5.text: "She walkin' straight toward destruction—headin' down to the grave without even blinkin'."

6.text: "Don't try to figure her out—she unstable, unpredictable, and lost in her own mess."

7.text: "So now hear me, kids—don't ignore what I'm tellin' you."

8.text: "Stay far from her. Don't even walk past her front door."

9.text: "Or you'll hand your honor over to somebody else—and your best years to somebody who don't care about you."

10.text: "Strangers'll eat off your grind—and your money gon' end up in somebody else's hands."

11.text: "Then you gon' cry out at the end—when your body and soul been worn down."

12.text: "You'll be sayin': 'Man… why'd I hate correction so much? Why'd I ignore every warning?'"

13.text: "'I ain't listen to my teachers. I tuned out every voice that tried to guide me.'"

14.text: "'Now I'm out here on the edge—ruined in front of everybody.'"

15.text: "Drink from your own well—get your refreshment from what's yours, not somebody else's."

16.text: "Should your love be spillin' out in the streets? Wasted in places it don't belong?"

17.text: "Nah—keep that between you and yours. Don't invite no strangers into that space."

18.text: "Let your love life be blessed—rejoice in the wife you started with."

19.text: "Let her love satisfy you like no other—stay wrapped up in her affection, always."

20.text: "So tell me, son… why would you chase some other woman? Why end up in the arms of someone who don't care about your soul?"

21.text: "Every step a man takes? The Lord sees it all—He watching the whole path."

22.text: "The wicked get caught up in their own mess—tangled in the ropes of their own sin."

23.text: "Without instruction, he falls off. Lost in his foolishness, he wander far and don't come back."

1.text: "My son, if you put yourself on the line for somebody else—if you cosigned or promised money for a stranger…"

2.text: "Then you trapped by your own words. You talked yourself into a bind."

3.text: "Here's what you gotta do, my son—get yourself free. Go humble yourself. Talk it out. Beg if you have to."

4.text: "Don't wait, don't sleep on it. Don't let your eyes even close."

5.text: "Run like your life depend on it—like a deer runnin' from a hunter, like a bird tryin' to break out the trap."

6.text: "Look at the ant, lazybones. Watch how she moves and learn something."

7.text: "She ain't got no boss, no manager…"

8.text: "But she stacks her stuff in summer—and gathers food when harvest time hits."

9.text: "So how long you gon' lay there? When you gon' get up off that bed?"

10.text: "'Just a little more sleep… just a little more rest…' That's how it starts…"

11.text: "And then poverty gon' creep up on you like a thief—broke and unprepared like a man caught slippin' by a robber."

12.text: "A shady dude? Worthless and wicked—he talk sideways with a slick mouth."

13.text: "Always doin' the most—winkin', twitchin', throwin' signals with his hands and feet."

14.text: "He got evil in his heart and drama on his mind—always stirrin' up mess."

15.text: "That's why his downfall gon' be quick. When it hits, ain't no fixin' it."

16.text: "There's six things the Lord hates—seven that He can't stand:"

17.text: "1: Proud eyes. 2: A lying tongue. 3: Hands that shed innocent blood."

18.text: "4: A heart that keeps schemin' up evil. 5: Feet that stay rushin' into drama."

19.text: "6: A false witness tellin' lies. 7: And folks who keep stirrin' up trouble between people."

20.text: "My son, hold tight to your father's wisdom—and don't ignore your mama's teaching."

21.text: "Keep them lessons close—wrap 'em around your heart and your life."

22.text: "Wherever you go, they'll guide you. When you sleep, they'll guard you. When you wake up, they'll speak to you."

23.text: "These commands are like a lamp. The teaching? It's light. And correction? That's how you stay alive."

24.text: "They'll protect you from that slick-talking woman—flattery comin' out her mouth like sugar."

25.text: "Don't get caught lustin' after her looks—or seduced by how she bats her lashes."

26.text: "Messin' with a woman like that? She'll drain you dry. You'll be down bad—livin' off crumbs."

27.text: "Can a man hold fire in his lap and not burn his clothes?"

28.text: "Can you walk on hot coals and not scorch your feet?"

29.text: "Same goes for messin' with another man's wife—you gon' get burned. Ain't no innocence in that."

30.text: "Now if a man steals food 'cause he's starving, folks understand…"

31.text: "But he still gotta pay it back sevenfold—even if he gotta sell everything he owns."

32.text: "But if you commit adultery? That ain't just foolish—it's suicidal."

33.text: "You gon' get scars. Public shame. And people won't forget it."

34.text: "Her man? He ain't lettin' that go. His jealousy burn hot."

35.text: "You can't pay him off. Don't matter what you offer—he won't take it."

1.text: "My son, hold on to what I'm tellin' you—keep my words close."

2.text: "Do what I say and live. Treat my instruction like your most prized possession."

3.text: "Wrap 'em around your fingers—etch 'em deep into your heart."

4.text: "Call wisdom your sister—and treat understanding like your closest cousin."

5.text: "So they can keep you from that seductive woman—the one who reels you in with sweet words."

6.text: "So I'm lookin' out my window one day, watchin' from the blinds…"

7.text: "And I peeped a crew of young dudes. One of 'em stood out—real green. No sense."

8.text: "He was just walkin'… slidin' through the wrong side of the block. Right past her corner."

9.text: "It was late—sun gone, sky dark. Whole vibe felt off."

10.text: "Then here she come—dressed to get attention, with a plan in her heart."

11.text: "She loud. Don't listen to nobody. Always in the streets. Never sittin' still."

12.text: "One minute she outside, next she postin' up at the corner store. She everywhere."

13.text: "She ran up on him. Kissed him. Straight bold. Didn't even blink."

14.text: "She hit him with: 'I just made my peace offering. I did my little religious routine.'"

15.text: "'I came out here lookin for you. You the one I wanted. And I found you.'"

16.text: "'My bed lookin' good—Egyptian sheets, imported fabrics.'"

17.text: "'It smell like myrrh, aloe, cinnamon. Got it all laid out.'"

18.text: "'Let's make love all night. Let's wild out till sunrise.'"

19.text: "'Don't worry—my man outta town. Long trip. He gone with the bag.'"

20.text: "'He not comin' back till a set time, trust me.'"

21.text: "With all that smooth talk, she got him. The flattery? Pulled him in."

22.text: "And just like that… he followed her. Like an ox goin' straight to the slaughter. Like a fool gettin' locked up with no clue."

23.text: "Until it was too late. Like an arrow straight to his liver. Like a bird flyin' right into the trap—he ain't know it would cost him everything."

24.text: "Now listen here, my kids—don't brush this off. Hear me out."

25.text: "Don't let your heart lean toward her. Don't even start down her street."

26.text: "She done brought down a lot of folks. And don't get it twisted—they weren't weak. Strong men got folded too."

27.text: "Her house? Straight path to hell. That bed leads to the grave."

1.text: Don't you hear wisdom callin'? Don't you hear understanding liftin' up her voice?

2.text: She posted up on the highest hill—right where paths cross, where folks gotta choose direction.

3.text: She shoutin' at the city gates, right by the doors, sayin':

4.text: "I'm talkin' to y'all, men. My voice is for everybody."

5.text: "Simple ones, it's time to wise up. Fools, come get a heart that understands."

6.text: "Listen close—I'm speakin' facts. What come out my mouth? It's right and real."

7.text: "I don't speak lies. I can't stand wickedness—it ain't welcome on my tongue."

8.text: "Every word I say is righteous. Ain't nothin' twisted or shady in me."

9.text: "If you got understanding, you'll see it plain. If you got sense, you'll recognize what's right."

10.text: "Take my instruction over silver. Choose my knowledge instead of gold."

11.text: "Wisdom worth more than rubies—and there's nothin' you want that can touch her value."

12.text: "I'm wisdom. I roll with good judgment. I move with sense and sharp discretion."

13.text: "Fearin' the Lord means hatin' evil. That's why I hate pride, arrogance, and dirty talk."

14.text: "Real advice? That's mine. Solid wisdom? Me again. I am understanding—I bring strength."

15.text: "Kings rule by me. Leaders make just decisions 'cause of me."

16.text: "Princes, nobles, judges—all of 'em lead right when they follow me."

17.text: "I love the ones who love me back. And the ones who chase me hard? They gon' find me."

18.text: "I got riches and honor walkin' with me. But not the kind that fades—the kind that last."

19.text: "What I give? Better than gold. Sweeter than silver. Worth more than both."

20.text: "I walk in righteousness—I move through justice like it's home."

21.text: "And if you love me? I'll make sure you inherit good things. Your storehouses gon' stay full."

22.text: "The Lord brought me in first—before His works, back at the very beginning."

23.text: "I been here since forever. Before time. Before the earth was even a thought."

24.text: "Before the oceans showed up. Before any springs poured out."

25.text: "Before the mountains got settled. Before hills had a name—I was already here."

26.text: "Before He made the land, the fields, or even the dust that forms the earth."

27.text: "When He laid out the heavens, I was right there. When He traced the circle on the deep waters, I saw it all."

28.text: "When He pulled the clouds tight and told the deep 'stay in your place'…"

29.text: "When He drew the boundary for the sea so it wouldn't overflow… when He mapped out the earth's foundations—"

30.text: "I was beside Him. Like a master builder. I was His joy every day, and I rejoiced in everything He made."

31.text: "Especially mankind—I loved being with y'all. Still do."

32.text: "Now hear me, children—blessed are the ones who keep to my ways."

33.text: "Pay attention to correction. Be wise. Don't roll your eyes at instruction."

34.text: "The one who listens to me? Blessed. The one watching daily at my door? Double blessed."

35.text: "Whoever finds me? Finds life—and gets favor straight from the Lord."

36.text: "But if you reject me? You hurtin' yourself. If you hate me? You flirtin' with death."

1.text: Wisdom done built her house—solid, strong, with seven pillars holdin' it up.

2.text: She done cooked the food, seasoned it up right. Mixed her wine. Laid the table out.

3.text: She sent out her girls, posted up on every corner, shoutin' from the rooftops.

4.text: "Aye, you simple folk! Yeah, you! Come on in here!"

5.text: "Come eat what I made. Sip on what I poured. This table right here? It's real."

6.text: "Leave the foolishness behind—and live. Walk in the lane of understanding."

7.text: "Try to correct a clown? You gon' catch heat. Try to check the wicked? They'll turn it on you."

8.text: "Don't waste your time on a scoffer—they just gon' hate you. But check a wise one? They gon' love you for it."

9.text: "Give some game to a wise person—they just gon' get wiser. Teach the just, and they gon' keep growin'."

10.text: The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom. And knowin' the Holy One? That's real understanding.

11.text: "Roll with me, and your life gon' stretch long. Years get added when you walk with wisdom."

12.text: "If you choose wisdom, you blessin' yourself. But if you scoff? That's your burden to carry alone."

13.text: Now flip the script—Foolishness? She loud, messy, and empty-headed.

14.text: She sittin' on her porch too—at a high place, lookin' just like Wisdom from a distance.

15.text: She callin' out to the passersby—folks just tryin' to go about their business.

16.text: "Aye, simple one! Come in here!" she yells. "If you clueless, this the spot!"

17.text: "Stolen water taste better. Bread in secret? Hit different."

18.text: But they don't know... the dead already in that house. Her table lead straight to the grave. Her guests sittin' in hell.

1.text: A wise son? He make his daddy proud. A foolish son? That's heartache for his mama.

2.text: Dirty money don't last. But livin' right? That could save your life.

3.text: The Lord ain't lettin' the righteous go hungry. But He shuts down the cravings of the wicked.

4.text: Lazy hands stay broke. But hard workers? They stack.

5.text: A wise kid knows to grind in season. But sleepin' through opportunity? That's shameful.

6.text: Blessings rest on the righteous. But the wicked? Violence stay in they mouth.

7.text: Good people get remembered with love. But the wicked name gon' rot.

8.text: Wise folks take instruction. But big talkin' fools? They gon' fall hard.

9.text: Walk with integrity, and you walk safe. But crooked steps always get exposed.

10.text: Slick looks and shady eyes cause trouble. And loud-mouth fools? They still fall.

11.text: Righteous words give life. Wicked mouths? Full of violence.

12.text: Hate stirs up mess. But love? Love covers it all.

13.text: Wise words live on wise lips. But fools? They learn through pain.

14.text: The wise stack knowledge. Fools run they mouth toward destruction.

15.text: The rich think their money protects 'em. The poor? Often get crushed by lack.

16.text: What the righteous work for leads to life. But the wicked grind only feeds sin.

17.text: Listen to instruction—you walk the path of life. Reject correction? You lost.

18.text: Hiding hate makes you fake. Talkin' reckless makes you foolish.

19.text: Too much talk leads to sin. Real wisdom? Knowin' when to shut up.

20.text: A righteous tongue is pure silver. But a wicked heart? Worthless.

21.text: Righteous folks feed others with their words. But fools starve from lack of wisdom.

22.text: When God blesses you—it's real rich. And He don't add pain to it.

23.text: Fools treat evil like a game. But the wise? They walk with purpose.

24.text: What the wicked fear? It comes true. What the righteous hope for? It gets granted.

25.text: When chaos rolls through, the wicked vanish. But the righteous stand like a rock.

26.text: A lazy person? Like vinegar in your teeth or smoke in your eyes—just annoying.

27.text: Fear the Lord, live longer. Disrespect Him, and your time get cut short.

28.text: The righteous got joyful hope. But the wicked? Their dreams die off.

29.text: God's way? Strength to the upright. But wickedness gon' destroy itself.

30.text: The righteous ain't goin' nowhere. But the wicked? They don't last in the land.

31.text: The righteous speak wisdom naturally. But wicked words get cut out quick.

32.text: Righteous lips know what's right to say. But wicked mouths? Stay speakin' wrong.

1.text: God can't stand rigged scales—but He love when the weight is fair and square.

2.text: Pride gon' bring you shame. But the humble? They carry wisdom with 'em.

3.text: The honest let integrity lead them. The shady? Their own crookedness gon' wreck them.

4.text: Money can't save you in the day of judgment—but living right? That might.

5.text: Righteousness keeps your steps straight. But wicked folks trip over their own mess.

6.text: The upright get rescued by their righteousness. But the unfaithful get caught up in their own thirst.

7.text: When the wicked die, their dreams die with 'em. False hope ends with the casket.

8.text: The righteous get outta trouble. That same trouble? Falls on the wicked instead.

9.text: A fake friend will ruin you with his mouth. But the wise? They survive through truth.

10.text: When good people win, the whole city celebrates. When the wicked drop? Folks rejoice.

11.text: Good people bless the city. But wicked mouths? Tear the city down.

12.text: A fool disrespects his neighbor. A wise one? Knows when to stay quiet.

13.text: A messy person can't hold water. But the loyal? Know how to keep it discreet.

14.text: No guidance? People fall. But with good advisors? You safe.

15.text: Cosignin' for strangers? That's pain waitin' to happen. Hate that trap? You safe.

16.text: A kind woman earns respect. Ruthless men just stack cash—but that's all they get.

17.text: If you show mercy, you bless yourself. But if you cruel? You hurting your own soul.

18.text: The wicked work shady for fake rewards. But righteousness? That's solid return.

19.text: Livin' right leads to life. Chasin' evil? Gon' lead to death.

20.text: Crooked hearts? Disgusting to the Lord. But blameless folks? He take joy in 'em.

21.text: Even if the wicked link up deep, they still won't dodge punishment. But God gon' protect the righteous and their kids.

22.text: A fine woman with no wisdom? That's like a gold ring in a pig's nose.

23.text: The righteous only want what's good. But the wicked? All they got comin' is wrath.

24.text: Some folks give freely and end up with more. Others hoard too much and end up broke.

25.text: The one who blesses others? They gon' be blessed back. If you pour into others, you gon' get poured into too.

26.text: Folks curse the one who holds back the grain. But blessings fall on the one who shares it.

27.text: Chasin' good brings favor. But lookin' for trouble? Trouble gon' find you first.

28.text: If you trust in money, you gon' fall. But the righteous? They grow strong like a tree.

29.text: If you stir up chaos in your own home, you gon' inherit nothin' but wind. Fools gon' end up servin' the wise.

30.text: A righteous life is like a tree of life—and the one who wins souls? That's real wisdom.

31.text: If the righteous get checked here on earth, what you think gon' happen to the wicked and the wild?

1.text: If you love correction, you love knowledge. But if you hate bein' checked? You just actin' dumb.

2.text: A good man finds favor with the Lord. But if your heart's wicked? God ain't ridin' with you.

3.text: You can't build a strong life on shady ways. But the righteous? They rooted deep and unshakable.

4.text: A solid wife? She the crown of her man. But a messy one? That's rot in his bones.

5.text: Righteous folks think right. But wicked advice? Full of lies and schemes.

6.text: The wicked be plottin' murder with their words. But the upright? They speak life that protects.

7.text: The wicked get wiped out quick. But the righteous? Their house gon' stand.

8.text: Wisdom earns respect. But a twisted heart? People see through that.

9.text: Better to be lowkey with a little help, than act important and still be broke.

10.text: A good person treats even their animals with care. But even the 'kindness' of the wicked? Still cruel.

11.text: Work your land, and you'll eat good. But chase nonsense? That's a fool's move.

12.text: Wicked folks jealous of evil people's come-up. But the righteous? They grow fruit from the inside.

13.text: Lies trap the wicked. But the righteous know how to walk through trouble and keep it movin'.

14.text: Good talk brings good things. And hard work? You get paid what you earn.

15.text: Fools think they always right. The wise? They listen to advice.

16.text: A fool blow up quick. But a wise one keeps it cool and keeps it pushin'.

17.text: Truth tellers speak justice. But liars? Straight deceit.

18.text: Some folks talk reckless, like stabbin' with words. But wise speech? It heals.

19.text: Truth don't expire. But lies? They only last a minute.

20.text: Evil hearts stay schemin'. But peaceful people? They full of joy.

21.text: Trouble don't stick to the righteous. But the wicked? Always surrounded by mess.

22.text: God hates lying lips. But folks who keep it 100? He delights in them.

23.text: The wise don't flex what they know. But fools? Loud with empty talk.

24.text: The hard worker gon' end up in charge. The lazy one? They gon' be takin' orders.

25.text: Worry weighs the heart down. But the right word at the right time? That'll lift it up.

26.text: The righteous choose friends with care. But the wrong crowd'll lead you off track fast.

27.text: Lazy folk won't even cook what they caught. But the diligent? They treat effort like gold.

28.text: Righteousness leads to life—and that path? No death on it.

1.text: A wise son listens to his father's instruction. A hardheaded one? Don't hear nothin'.

2.text: A good man eats good off what he says. But unfaithful folks? They stay cravin' violence.

3.text: Guard your mouth, you protect your life. Run your mouth wild? You askin' for destruction.

4.text: Lazy people always want somethin' but never got nothin'. The diligent? They gon' eat well.

5.text: Righteous folks hate lies. Wicked folks? Nasty and shameful.

6.text: Livin' right protects the one walkin' straight. Sin? Gon' flip the sinner every time.

7.text: Some act rich but got nothin'. Others live lowkey and sittin' on real wealth.

8.text: Money might bail you out sometimes. But if you broke, ain't nobody askin' for a ransom.

9.text: Righteous people shine with joy. But the wicked? Their light gon' burn out.

10.text: Pride brings drama. But the wise take advice and move smart.

11.text: Money made quick and shady won't last. But stackin' slow and steady? That grows.

12.text: Waitin' too long for a dream hurts the heart. But when it finally happens? It's life-givin'.

13.text: Disrespect God's word? You playin' with destruction. But if you fear His commands, you'll be blessed.

14.text: Wise teaching is like a life fountain—it'll keep you from death traps.

15.text: Good sense earns you favor. But living dirty? That path stay hard.

16.text: Smart people move with knowledge. Fools? They show they whole hand—loud and proud.

17.text: A wicked messenger gon' end up in trouble. But a faithful one? Bring peace and healing.

18.text: Ignore correction? Expect poverty and shame. Take it seriously? That's how you earn respect.

19.text: When a dream comes true, it feels amazing. But fools hate leaving sin behind, so they never get there.

20.text: Kick it with wise folks? You gon' get wise. Chill with fools? You gon' crash.

21.text: Evil always chasin' down the sinner. But the righteous? They get paid back in good.

22.text: A good man leaves blessings for his grandkids. But sinners? Their wealth gon' end up in righteous hands.

23.text: The poor got food in their fields—but injustice lets it go to waste.

24.text: Don't discipline your child? That's not love. Real love corrects early and often.

25.text: The righteous eat and stay full. But the wicked? They always hungry, always lackin'.

1.text: A wise woman builds her home up strong. A foolish one? She tear it down with her own hands.

2.text: Walkin' upright shows you fear the Lord. But when you wild and crooked? That's disrespect.

3.text: A fool talk reckless with pride. But the wise? Their words protect 'em.

4.text: No ox means no mess, yeah—but also no harvest. Strength brings increase, even if it's a little messy.

5.text: A real one don't lie. A fake one? Lies come easy.

6.text: A scoffer stay searchin' but never gets it. But the wise? Knowledge come easy to them.

7.text: Don't waste your time around fools. If they ain't speakin' wisdom, move around.

8.text: The wise think ahead and understand their moves. Fools stay trippin' in their own lies.

9.text: Fools laugh at sin like it's cute. But the upright? They walk in favor.

10.text: Only your heart knows its own bitterness. And your joy? That ain't for strangers to fully understand.

11.text: The wicked house gon' fall. But even the upright's tent gon' thrive.

12.text: There's ways that look right at first… but the end of that road is death.

13.text: Even laughter can cover sorrow. And that party vibe? Sometimes it ends in pain.

14.text: A backslider gon' be full of himself. But a good man? He stays full from above.

15.text: The simple believe whatever they hear. The wise? They check the facts and move smart.

16.text: The wise stay alert and avoid evil. But a fool? He stay loud and overconfident.

17.text: A hothead gon' act stupid. And shady people? Nobody trust them.

18.text: The simple get stuck with foolishness. But the wise? They stay crowned with knowledge.

19.text: The wicked gon' bow one day. Even at the gates, they gotta respect the righteous.

20.text: The poor get ignored—even by neighbors. But the rich? Folks flock to them.

21.text: If you despise your neighbor, you in the wrong. But if you show mercy to the poor? You blessed.

22.text: Folks who plot evil? They lost. But mercy and truth follow those who plan good.

23.text: Hard work always pays. But too much talk and no action? That's a broke man's game.

24.text: Wisdom is wealth to the wise. But fools? They stuck in their foolishness.

25.text: A truthful witness saves lives. A liar? They just push lies deeper.

26.text: Fearin' the Lord gives confidence—and your kids gon' have a safe place too.

27.text: That fear of the Lord? It's a fountain of life—keepin' you outta the trap.

28.text: A ruler's honor is in a crowd of people. But no people? No power.

29.text: Patience shows you understand. But poppin' off too quick? That's just foolishness on display.

30.text: A peaceful heart keeps you healthy. But envy? That'll rot you from the inside.

31.text: Oppressin' the poor is disrespectin' God. But helpin' the needy? That's honorin' Him.

32.text: The wicked get caught in their own fall. But the righteous? Even in death, they got refuge.

33.text: Wisdom lives quiet in the heart of the wise. But a fool gon' put all his nonsense on blast.

34.text: Righteousness lifts up a nation. Sin? It brings shame to any people.

35.text: A wise servant gets the king's blessing. But one who brings shame? Gon' catch his wrath.

1.text: A soft answer cools folks down. But come in hot? You gon' stir up a fight.

2.text: Wise folks use their words right. But fools? They just let foolishness fly.

3.text: The Lord see everything. Ain't nothin' hid—He watchin' good and evil alike.

4.text: Kind words bring life like a tree. But twisted talk? That break the spirit.

5.text: A fool shrugs off his father's correction. But the wise take rebuke seriously.

6.text: A righteous home? Full of treasure. But wicked money stay bringing trouble.

7.text: Wise lips spread wisdom. But a fool's heart got nothin' to give.

8.text: God ain't impressed with the wicked's offerings. But a righteous prayer? He love that.

9.text: God can't stand wicked living. But He loves folks who chase after what's right.

10.text: Walkin' away from the right path brings pain. Hate correction? That path ends in death.

11.text: Hell wide open to God's eyes—so you know He sees what's in our hearts.

12.text: A scoffer hates correction. You won't catch them around wise people.

13.text: A joyful heart lights up the face. But deep sorrow crushes the spirit.

14.text: A wise person's heart stays hungry for knowledge. A fool? They snack on nonsense.

15.text: If you always see life as pain, that's all it'll feel like. But a joyful heart? It's like a feast every day.

16.text: Better to have a little with God than a whole lot with stress.

17.text: Better a plate of greens with love than steak with tension and hate.

18.text: A hot-tempered person keepin' up mess. But the calm one? They bring peace.

19.text: A lazy man's path is full of excuses. But the righteous? They stay on the move.

20.text: A wise child makes their father proud. A foolish one? Brings shame to their mama.

21.text: Fools laugh at foolishness. But wise folks walk right and don't play with their purpose.

22.text: No guidance? Your plans fall apart. But many wise voices? That's how you get things solid.

23.text: A good answer hits different—it brings joy. Say the right thing at the right time? That's gold.

24.text: The wise keep rising—headin' up toward life, and away from the pit.

25.text: God tears down the proud man's house. But He protects the widow's boundary line.

26.text: Evil thoughts disgust the Lord. But honest words? He finds joy in those.

27.text: Greedy folks bring drama to their own house. But people who reject bribes? They live.

28.text: The righteous think before they speak. The wicked? They just spit out harm.

29.text: The Lord don't hang near the wicked. But He lean in when the righteous pray.

30.text: A smile in the eyes lifts your heart. And good news? That's healing for the bones.

31.text: If you can handle correction, you'll stay around wise company.

32.text: If you hate instruction, you hurting yourself. But if you listen to rebuke, you grow.

33.text: Fearing the Lord teaches you wisdom. And if you want honor? You gotta walk through humility first.

1.text: We can make our plans—but what comes out our mouth? God still got the final word.

2.text: We think we good. We always think we right. But God? He see through the surface and check our motives.

3.text: Put your plans in God's hands, and He'll help your thoughts fall into place.

4.text: God made everything for a purpose—even the wicked for judgment day.

5.text: God hates pride in the heart. Folks can squad up all they want—if they movein' pride, they still gettin' dealt with.

6.text: Mercy and truth clean the slate. But fearin' the Lord? That's how you really walk away from evil.

7.text: When your life pleases the Lord? He can make your enemies chill too.

8.text: Better to be broke and righteous than rich with no justice in your hands.

9.text: We plan our path. But God still be guiding our steps.

10.text: Kings supposed to speak wisdom like it's law. Don't let your mouth mess up your judgment.

11.text: Fair scales and honest business? That's the Lord's standard. Every weight you measure with belongs to Him.

12.text: God detests wicked leaders. Righteousness is what makes a throne stable.

13.text: Leaders love honest talk. Truth-tellers earn real favor.

14.text: A king's anger is deadly—but a wise man knows how to calm that storm.

15.text: When the king smile on you? That's life. His favor feel like spring rain on dry land.

16.text: Wisdom worth way more than gold. Understanding? More valuable than silver.

17.text: The upright stay on a clean path. That's how you keep your soul safe.

18.text: Pride come right before the fall. Arrogance? That's the setup for the crash.

19.text: Better to be humble with the lowly than ballin' out with the proud.

20.text: Whoever listens to wisdom gon' find good. Trustin' God? That's where real joy is.

21.text: Wise hearts get called discerning. And sweet words help people learn better.

22.text: Understanding is like a fountain of life for the one who got it. But tryin' to correct a fool? That's a waste.

23.text: A wise heart shapes wise speech. What you learn pours out your mouth.

24.text: Kind words hit like honey—sweet for the soul, healing for the body.

25.text: Some paths feel right… but they end in death.

26.text: Hunger drives a worker. Sometimes your belly push you harder than your goals.

27.text: The wicked stir up drama—and they talk like they got fire on their tongue.

28.text: A shady person spreads strife. A whisperer? Breaks up close friends.

29.text: A violent man gasses his neighbor up to do wrong—and leads him straight into trouble.

30.text: He winkin' and schemin', twistin' his lips—plotting evil without sayin' a word.

31.text: Gray hair? That's a crown—as long as it come from walkin' with righteousness.

32.text: Slow to anger? That's stronger than a warrior. Rule your spirit? That's real power.

33.text: You can roll the dice—but God controls the outcome.

1.text: Better to eat dry bread in peace than to feast in a house full of drama.

2.text: A wise servant gon' outrank a shameful son—and might even get a cut of the inheritance.

3.text: Silver gets tested in fire. Gold in the flames. But the Lord? He tests the heart.

4.text: A wicked person eats up lies. A liar loves to listen to messy, spiteful talk.

5.text: Makin' fun of the poor? That's dissin' their Creator. Laughin' at folks' downfall? That ain't gon' end well for you.

6.text: Grandkids are a crown for old heads. And kids? They shine when they got a solid daddy.

7.text: Fancy words don't fit a fool. Just like lies ain't supposed to come out a leader's mouth.

8.text: A gift can feel like magic to the one givin' it—makes moves happen wherever it go.

9.text: If you cover somebody's mistake, you're protectin' love. But if you keep bringin' it up? You breakin' bonds.

10.text: A simple rebuke hits harder for a wise one than a hundred beatdowns on a fool.

11.text: Evil folks stay plottin'. That's why destruction keep knockin' on their door.

12.text: You better run into a mama bear robbed of her cubs than a full-blown fool in his foolishness.

13.text: Pay back good with evil? Don't expect peace to visit your house.

14.text: Startin' drama is like bustin' a pipe open. Walk away before it floods into a fight.

15.text: Sayin' the guilty innocent or the innocent guilty? God can't stand either one.

16.text: Why a fool holdin' the price of wisdom when he got no real interest in learnin'?

17.text: A real friend rides at all times. A brother shows up when the struggle hits.

18.text: Only someone who ain't thinkin' straight co-signs loans for a friend with no backup plan.

19.text: If you love breakin' rules, you probably love drama too. Tryin' to flex all big? That's a setup for a fall.

20.text: Twisted hearts don't find good things. And slick mouths? They fall into evil.

21.text: If you raise a scoffer, you raisin' sorrow. A fool for a child? That joy gon' be hard to come by.

22.text: A joyful heart is like good medicine. But a crushed spirit? That'll drain your bones dry.

23.text: Wicked folks take bribes in secret—just to mess up justice behind the scenes.

24.text: The wise keep their eyes on what matters. Fools? They lookin' way out there, never focused.

25.text: A foolish child? That's heartbreak for their daddy—and bitterness for the mama who raised 'em.

26.text: Punishing good people? That ain't right. Smackin' down leaders for standin' tall? Just as wrong.

27.text: A smart person speaks less. And a calm spirit? That's real understanding.

28.text: Even a fool look wise when he keep quiet. If he shuts up, folks might think he deep.

1.text: The one who isolates themself only cares about their own desires—they fight against all sound wisdom.

2.text: Fools don't want understanding—they just wanna hear themselves talk.

3.text: When wickedness rolls in, disrespect follows. And with shame comes straight-up mockery.

4.text: A wise person's words run deep like waters—flowing like a stream of wisdom.

5.text: Showin' favor to the wicked or denyin' justice to the righteous? Both wrong.

6.text: A fool's lips bring conflict, and their mouth? It's beggin' for a beatdown.

7.text: A fool's mouth is their own destruction—their lips are a trap for their soul.

8.text: Gossip tastes sweet going down—hits the deepest parts of your belly.

9.text: Being lazy in your work? That's the same as being straight-up destructive.

10.text: The Lord's name is a strong tower—the righteous run to it and stay safe.

11.text: The rich think their money is a fortified city—a high wall in their imagination.

12.text: Pride comes right before destruction. But humility? That's what leads to honor.

13.text: Answering before listening? That's foolishness and shame.

14.text: Your spirit can help you endure sickness. But a broken spirit? Who can bear that?

15.text: The heart that wants knowledge stays acquiring it. The wise ear keeps seeking it out.

16.text: A gift opens doors for you—can get you in rooms with important people.

17.text: The first to state their case sounds right—until somebody start cross-examining.

18.text: Drawing lots can settle disputes—even separate the powerful who beefing.

19.text: An offended friend is harder to win back than a fortified city. Arguments? Like bars on a castle.

20.text: Your words fill your belly—you eat what your mouth produces.

21.text: Life and death are in the power of the tongue—if you love talking, you'll eat its fruit.

22.text: Finding a good wife? That's finding something good—and receiving favor from the Lord.

23.text: The poor speak with pleas. But the rich? They answer rough.

24.text: Some friends just there to socialize. But a real one? Closer than family.

1.text: Better to be broke and walk with integrity than to be foul with your mouth and act a fool.

2.text: Movein' without knowledge? Dangerous. Rushin' into things? That's how you mess up.

3.text: A man wrecks his own life, then blames God for the mess he made.

4.text: Money attracts people quick. But let you go broke? Even your day ones dip.

5.text: Lyin' in court? You gon' get caught. Lying on folks? Ain't no way outta that.

6.text: People stay chasing favor from the rich and powerful. Gift givers? They never short on "friends."

7.text: Even your own family avoid you when you're poor. And friends? They ghost real fast.

8.text: If you get wisdom, you lovin' yourself. Keep good sense, and you'll find real blessings.

9.text: Lie again and again? You not escaping—your words gon' catch up to you.

10.text: Lavish livin' don't fit a fool. And servants tryin' to run royalty? That ain't it either.

11.text: A wise person keeps their cool. And real strength? Knowing when to let stuff slide.

12.text: A king's anger hit like a lion's roar. But his favor? Like morning dew—gentle and life-givin'.

13.text: A foolish child? A father's downfall. And a naggin' spouse? Like water drip-drip-drippin' nonstop.

14.text: You can inherit money and property from your folks. But a smart, solid wife? That's straight from God.

15.text: Lazy folks sleep all day—and end up hungry at night.

16.text: Keep God's commands, you protect your soul. But neglect your ways? That path leads to death.

17.text: When you give to the poor, you loanin' to the Lord. And He always pays back.

18.text: Discipline your kid while you still can. Don't wait till they too far gone.

19.text: A hothead gon' keep gettin' into trouble. You bail 'em out now? You gon' be back again.

20.text: Listen to advice. Learn from correction. That's how you grow wiser for later.

21.text: You can plan all you want—but it's God's purpose that really holds weight.

22.text: What people look for? Kindness. And a broke man with integrity beats a rich liar any day.

23.text: Fearin' the Lord brings life—and peace. You gon' sleep satisfied, unbothered by evil.

24.text: A lazy man won't even lift his food from the plate to his mouth. That's next-level triflin'.

25.text: Hit a mocker with discipline, and simple folks take notes. Correct the wise, and they grow sharper.

26.text: A son that disrespects his dad and runs his mama off? That's shame walkin'.

27.text: Stop listenin' to wisdom, and you'll start walkin' away from truth without even knowin' it.

28.text: A corrupt witness don't care about justice. Wicked folks? They eat sin up like it's dessert.

29.text: Judgment gon' hit mockers. And fools? Sometimes they only learn through pain.

1.text: Wine will clown you. Liquor'll have you ready to fight. If it runs you? You not movin' wise.

2.text: A king's anger? Like a lion's roar. Play with power, and you playin' with your own life.

3.text: Real strength? Walkin' away from mess. Fools always got time for beef.

4.text: Lazy folks won't grind when it's cold. But come harvest? They'll be beggin' and broke.

5.text: Deep thoughts sit in the heart—but wise folks know how to pull it out.

6.text: Everybody talk like they solid. But where the faithful ones at?

7.text: A righteous man walks with integrity. His kids eat the fruit of that legacy.

8.text: A just ruler don't let evil slide. One glance from him clears a whole room.

9.text: Who can really say, "I cleaned my heart, I'm sin-free"? Exactly. Nobody.

10.text: Two sets of weights? Two-faced dealings? God ain't pleased with shady business.

11.text: Even a kid shows you who they are by what they do, not what they say.

12.text: The ear that hears and the eye that sees? God made both—so use 'em well.

13.text: Love sleep too much, you gon' stay broke. Wake up and get to it—you'll have what you need.

14.text: "This ain't worth much," the buyer says. But soon as he leaves? He flexin' on the deal.

15.text: Gold and rubies are cool. But wise words? That's rare jewel status.

16.text: If somebody cosignin' for a stranger or flirtin' with danger, hold some collateral. Protect yourself.

17.text: Stealin' tastes sweet at first—but that aftertaste? Like gravel in your mouth.

18.text: Got plans? Get advice. If you about to go to war? Don't move without wise counsel.

19.text: Gossipers can't hold water. Flatterers be extra shady. Keep your circle clean.

20.text: Curse your mama or daddy? That light inside you? Snuffed out in the darkest way.

21.text: Fast money, fast inheritance—it don't last. It won't be blessed in the end.

22.text: Don't say, "I'll get even." Let the Lord handle it. He gon' make it right.

23.text: Shady business? Still abomination. God ain't cool with scams, big or small.

24.text: Our steps? Ordered by the Lord. So how we gon' act like we fully understand our path?

25.text: Call somethin' holy too quick, then regret it? That's a trap. Don't make promises you ain't prayed on.

26.text: A wise king clears out the wicked—he ain't afraid to press the threshing wheel if he got to.

27.text: Your spirit? That's God's flashlight—He uses it to search every corner of your heart.

28.text: A real leader is held up by mercy and truth. That lovingkindness? Keeps his throne steady.

29.text: Young folks shine with strength. Old folks? Their silver hair is their crown—earned wisdom.

30.text: Pain ain't always punishment. Sometimes the wounds go deep enough to clean out the soul.

1.text: The king's heart? It's in God's hands. He steers it like water—wherever He want.

2.text: Everybody think they right. But God ain't fooled—He weighin' hearts, not appearances.

3.text: God want justice and righteousness more than your fake sacrifices.

4.text: Arrogant eyes, a proud heart, and evil work? That's sin—plain and simple.

5.text: Careful plans from a hard worker lead to abundance. Rushed hustles? That's a shortcut to broke.

6.text: Fast money through lies? It fades fast. That kind of treasure comes with a death wish.

7.text: The wicked destroy themselves. Why? 'Cause they refuse to do what's right.

8.text: Guilty folks live crooked. But the pure? They walk straight and clear.

9.text: Better to chill in the attic by yourself than live in a big house with a combative woman.

10.text: The wicked crave evil—and they don't care who get hurt.

11.text: When a fool gets checked, even the simple learn. But the wise? All they need is a word.

12.text: God peeps the wicked's house. He knows what's up—and He gon' flip it.

13.text: If you ignore the poor when they cry out? Your cries gon' get ignored too.

14.text: Quiet gifts can calm anger. Backdoor bribes can cool serious heat—but that don't make it right.

15.text: The righteous love justice. But the wicked? They gon' catch destruction.

16.text: Drift too far from wisdom? You gon' end up sittin' with the dead.

17.text: If you chase pleasure too hard, you'll stay broke. Fancy drink and luxury? Won't make you rich.

18.text: The wicked gon' get what's comin'. Sometimes their downfall covers the cost for the righteous.

19.text: Better to be out in the wilderness than stuck in the house with a bitter, angry woman.

20.text: The wise keep wealth and resources stored up. Fools spend it all quick and got nothin' left.

21.text: Chase righteousness and mercy? You'll find life, real right-standing, and respect.

22.text: A wise person can break into a mighty city—and take down what they thought was unshakable.

23.text: Watch your mouth. Guard your words. That's how you keep yourself outta drama.

24.text: A loud, arrogant man? That's a straight-up scoffer—always movin' with pride.

25.text: The lazy one stay dreamin' and desirin'—but won't lift a hand to work.

26.text: All day long he wants stuff. But the righteous? They give freely, no hesitation.

27.text: A wicked man's offering? God hates it. And if his motives wrong too? Even worse.

28.text: A false witness gon' disappear. But the one who listens and speaks truth? That word gon' carry.

29.text: A wicked man stays stubborn. But the upright? They lock in and walk solid.

30.text: Ain't no wisdom, no strategy, no plan that can outsmart God.

31.text: You can prep your horse for battle all day—but victory? That comes from the Lord.

1.text: A good name hit harder than a fat bank account. Favor? Worth more than silver and gold.

2.text: Rich or broke—don't matter. God made all of us.

3.text: The wise peep danger and step back. The naive? They keep walkin' and get caught up.

4.text: Humility and reverence for God? That's where real riches, respect, and long life start.

5.text: Twisted paths full of traps and thorns. Guard your soul—you won't even be in the area.

6.text: Teach your kids the right way early, and even when they grown, they won't forget.

7.text: The rich call the shots. The borrower? Still on the clock—servin' debt.

8.text: Plant wickedness? You gon' harvest pain. Anger issues won't hold up forever.

9.text: Generous folks? They stay blessed—'cause they feed the hungry without a second thought.

10.text: Kick the mocker out, and the drama leave with him. Peace follows.

11.text: Love purity, speak kindness? Even kings gon' keep you close.

12.text: God watches over real knowledge—but He flips the script on liars.

13.text: Lazy folks stay scared: "A lion might be outside!" That's just an excuse to stay stuck.

14.text: A seductive mouth? Deep pit. If you ain't right with God, you'll fall right in.

15.text: Foolishness lives in kids by default. Correction pushes it out.

16.text: If you crush the poor to get rich or give to the rich to get in good? Poverty still gon' catch you.

17.text: Listen up. Lean into these wise words. Let 'em soak into your heart.

18.text: Hold 'em close. Keep 'em on your lips. These words taste good once they in you.

19.text: All this so you'll learn to trust God. I'm talkin' to you today.

20.text: Didn't I already bless you with solid counsel and wisdom that hits?

21.text: So you'd know what's true—and speak truth when somebody pulls up askin' for answers.

22.text: Don't rob folks just 'cause they poor. Don't press the vulnerable 'cause they ain't got backup.

23.text: God gon' step in for them. And if you rob 'em, He gon' flip that same energy on you.

24.text: Don't run with angry people. Don't ride with the hot-headed.

25.text: 'Cause you might pick up their mess—and set a trap for yourself.

26.text: Don't be the one co-signing debt. Don't shake hands on promises you can't cover.

27.text: If you can't pay, don't be surprised when your bed's repossessed.

28.text: Don't move the old boundary lines. Respect what your people established.

29.text: You see somebody great at what they do? That one gon' stand before kings—not fade out in the background.

1.text: If you sit at the table with somebody powerful, don't just eat—pay attention to what's in front of you.

2.text: If you greedy, better check yourself—like puttin' a knife to your own throat.

3.text: Don't get caught up cravin' fancy food. That plate come with motives.

4.text: Don't burn yourself out tryna get rich. Use your head—chill out.

5.text: Money ain't stable. It sprout wings and fly off like an eagle if you blink too long.

6.text: Don't eat with stingy folks. Don't crave nothin' they serve.

7.text: 'Cause the whole time they sayin' "Eat, drink," they not with you. Their heart somewhere else.

8.text: What you ate gon' come right back up. And all that nice convo? Wasted.

9.text: Don't drop wisdom in front of a fool—they not gon' respect it anyway.

10.text: Don't move old boundary lines. Don't take what belongs to the vulnerable.

11.text: 'Cause their Defender? God Himself. And He don't lose in court.

12.text: Lock in. Let your heart lean into instruction. Tune your ears to wisdom.

13.text: Don't skip discipline when it comes to your child. Correction won't kill them.

14.text: In fact, that correction might just save their soul.

15.text: My child, if your heart chooses wisdom, my whole soul gon' be glad.

16.text: When I hear you speakin' truth? That's joy deep down in my bones.

17.text: Don't let envy get in your heart for folks out here wildin'. Keep your fire for fearin' God.

18.text: 'Cause there's an afterlife—and your hope will be rewarded.

19.text: Listen up, my son. Be wise. Let your heart stay on track.

20.text: Don't run with heavy drinkers or folks who eat like they ain't got control.

21.text: Drunks and gluttons gon' end up broke and raggedy.

22.text: Listen to your father. Don't roll your eyes at your mama just 'cause she older.

23.text: Get truth—and don't sell it out. Same goes for wisdom, instruction, and understanding.

24.text: A father with a righteous child? That man gon' be full of joy.

25.text: So let your mama and daddy be proud of you—make the one who raised you smile.

26.text: My child, give me your heart. And watch how I live—pay attention.

27.text: A promiscuous woman? That's a deep trap. A seductress? Narrow and dangerous.

28.text: She always out here huntin'. Her body count addin' up—and not in a good way.

29.text: Who got drama? Who stay hurt? Who always got something to complain about? Who look like they been cryin' and swingin' all night?

30.text: The ones who stay at the bottle. The ones chasin' that next drink.

31.text: Don't get mesmerized by the wine—how it sparkle, swirl, look smooth in the glass…

32.text: 'Cause when it hits? It bites like a snake. That aftertaste stings like a viper.

33.text: You gon' start seein' wild stuff. Sayin' reckless things out your mouth.

34.text: You gon' feel like you lost at sea. Rockin' back and forth, outta touch with reality.

35.text: Talkin' like: "They hit me, but I ain't feel nothin'. I don't even remember. When I wake up, I need another drink…"

1.text: Don't waste energy wishin' you could be like evil people. Don't even hang with 'em.

2.text: Their mind stay on violence. Their mouth stay stirrin' up mess.

3.text: You build a solid life with wisdom. Understanding holds it all together.

4.text: Fill your space with knowledge, and your life gon' be rich and beautiful from the inside out.

5.text: A wise person ain't just smart—they strong. Knowledge upgrades your strength.

6.text: You need strategy to fight your battles. Stack wise voices around you—there's safety in that.

7.text: Fools can't reach high-level wisdom. At the gate (where decisions get made)? They quiet.

8.text: If you out here schemin' evil, people gon' call you exactly what you are: a plotter.

9.text: Even plannin' foolishness is sin. And a mocker? Folks can't stand him.

10.text: If you fold under pressure, your strength was never deep to begin with.

11.text: Speak up for those headed to destruction. Don't let folks walk into ruin without tryin' to help.

12.text: Don't play dumb like, "I ain't know." God sees hearts. He knows what's real. And He repays accordingly.

13.text: My child, eat honey—it's good. Sweet to your taste, just like wisdom to your soul.

14.text: Wisdom feels sweet when you get it. If you find it, you got a future. Your hope locked in.

15.text: Yo, wicked man—don't run up on the righteous. Don't rob their rest.

16.text: A righteous one might fall seven times, but they get back up. The wicked fall once and stay down.

17.text: Don't celebrate when your enemy loses. Don't smile when they fall.

18.text: God might see your pride and pull back His judgment—now you back to square one.

19.text: Don't stress over what the wicked got. Don't envy their lifestyle.

20.text: They got no future in it. Their light gon' go out.

21.text: Respect God. Respect leadership. And don't join folks who stay switchin' up.

22.text: 'Cause when their downfall hits, it's gon' come fast—and you don't wanna get caught in that blast.

23.text: Here's more wisdom for the real ones: Don't play favorites in court.

24.text: If you call the wicked "innocent," folks gon' curse you. Whole nations gon' hate that.

25.text: But if you check the wicked straight up? You'll get respect and blessing for it.

26.text: Speak truth with clarity—that's like a kiss of respect and trust.

27.text: Handle your business in the field first—set up your grind. Then build your house.

28.text: Don't lie in court just to hurt your neighbor. Don't twist truth with your words.

29.text: Don't say, "I'm just givin' them what they gave me." That's not how you win.

30.text: I walked past the field of a lazy man—the land of someone with no understanding.

31.text: It was wild. Thorns everywhere. Nettles takin' over. The wall broken down.

32.text: I looked at it. Took mental notes. That sight taught me something.

33.text: "Just a little more sleep, a little more rest," they say…

34.text: But poverty gon' sneak up like a robber—and lack gon' hit like a stickup.

1.text: These are more proverbs from Solomon—Hezekiah's people made sure they got written down.

2.text: God gets glory from keeping certain things hidden. But kings? They shine when they dig into truth.

3.text: The sky got height. The earth got depth. But a king's mind? That's a whole mystery.

4.text: Get the impurities out the silver, and it's ready for a real craftsman.

5.text: Remove the wicked from around a leader, and now his throne can actually be righteous.

6.text: Don't hype yourself up in front of powerful folks. Don't post up where the VIPs sit.

7.text: It's better for the king to say "Come up" than for them to tell you "Back down" in front of everybody.

8.text: Don't rush into court—'cause when your case backfires, you gon' be the one embarrassed.

9.text: Settle your business with the person directly. Don't be tellin' folks their secrets.

10.text: 'Cause if that gets out, your name gon' take a hit—and your reputation won't recover easy.

11.text: The right word, at the right time? Priceless. Like golden apples in silver settings.

12.text: A wise correction, given to someone who's open? That's fine jewelry right there.

13.text: A faithful messenger? Like a snow-cold drink during harvest season—refreshing and rare.

14.text: Someone who lies about being generous? All talk—no rain, just clouds and wind.

15.text: Patience can change a leader's mind. A gentle word? Can break through hard resistance.

16.text: Found some honey? Cool. But don't wild out—you eat too much, you'll throw up.

17.text: Don't be at your neighbor's house all the time. Too much of you? They gon' start avoiding you.

18.text: Lying on someone? That's like swingin' a bat, pullin' a knife, or shootin' arrows. It hits hard.

19.text: Countin' on someone unfaithful in a crisis? That's like chewin' with a busted tooth or steppin' on a bad ankle.

20.text: Singin' happy songs to someone who's heartbroken? Like snatching a coat in winter or mixin' vinegar with soda—just wrong timing.

21.text: If your enemy hungry? Feed 'em. If they thirsty? Give 'em water.

22.text: That kindness gon' humble them—and God gon' bless you for it.

23.text: North wind brings rain. Gossip brings side-eyes and tension.

24.text: Better to live on the roof than in the same house with a woman who stay arguing.

25.text: Good news from far away? That hit like cold water when you tired.

26.text: When a righteous person folds in front of the wicked? That's like dirty water from a spring—nasty and disappointing.

27.text: Too much honey ain't good. Same with chasin' your own glory—it don't sit right.

28.text: If you can't control yourself, you like a city with no walls—wide open to anything.

1.text: Snow in summer? Rain during harvest? That's how wrong it is to give a fool honor.

2.text: Just like birds fly and keep movin', a curse with no reason don't land nowhere.

3.text: Horses need whips, donkeys need bridles—and fools? Sometimes they just need correction.

4.text: Don't argue with a fool on his level—you'll end up lookin' just like him.

5.text: But sometimes, you do gotta check a fool—so he don't think he smart in his own mind.

6.text: Send a fool to deliver your message? You might as well cut off your own feet. It's self-sabotage.

7.text: A proverb in a fool's mouth? Like useless, limp legs—he don't know what he sayin'.

8.text: Giving honor to a fool? That's like tyin' a rock to a slingshot—you ain't hurtin' nobody but yourself.

9.text: A fool with a proverb? Like a drunk swingin' around thorns—somebody's gettin' hurt.

10.text: God made everybody. But fools and rebels? They still gon' get what's comin' to 'em.

11.text: A fool goin' back to his mess? That's like a dog eatin' his own vomit—disgusting and senseless.

12.text: Think you wise in your own eyes? A straight-up fool got more hope than you.

13.text: Lazy folks stay makin' up wild excuses: "There's a lion outside! I might die if I leave!"

14.text: They roll around in bed like a door on hinges—movin' but goin' nowhere.

15.text: They too lazy to even lift food from the plate to their mouth. Make it make sense.

16.text: Lazy folks swear they smarter than seven people with real answers.

17.text: Jumpin' in other people's beef? That's like grabbin' a dog by the ears—you gon' get bit.

18.text: Playin' around with lies and violence? That's like a crazy man throwin' fire and arrows.

19.text: Tell a lie, hurt your neighbor, then say "I was just playin'"? That ain't funny. That's toxic.

20.text: Without gossip, the fire dies out. No mess? No drama.

21.text: Just like wood fuels fire, messy folks keep arguments burnin'.

22.text: Gossip? Tastes juicy—but it sinks deep and messes up your insides.

23.text: Smooth talk comin' from a cold heart? That's fake silver on cheap clay.

24.text: Haters fake it with sweet talk—but they sittin' on lies deep inside.

25.text: Even when they sound nice, don't trust it—there's evil layered in that heart.

26.text: Their hate might be hidden for a minute—but it's gon' show up in public eventually.

27.text: Dig a ditch for somebody? You the one gon' fall in. Push a stone at someone? It's comin' back at you.

28.text: A liar got hate behind that tongue. A flatterer? Ruin stay close to their mouth.

1.text: Don't brag about tomorrow. You don't know what the day got planned for you.

2.text: Let somebody else hype you up—not your own mouth. Let a stranger sing your praises, not you.

3.text: A heavy stone or a bag of sand ain't nothin'—but a fool wildin' in anger? That's a whole burden.

4.text: Anger hits hard, rage runs wild—but jealousy? Whew. That's a storm you might not survive.

5.text: It's better to get called out with love than to have someone claim they care but never say nothin'.

6.text: Real friends might hurt your feelings—but they do it to help. An enemy's compliments? Fake and dangerous.

7.text: A full person pushes sweetness away. But the hungry? Even the bitter stuff tastes like a blessing.

8.text: A person who drifts too far from home? Like a bird lost from its nest.

9.text: Good cologne smells nice, but wise, heartfelt advice from a real friend? That's what truly refreshes you.

10.text: Don't ditch your day-one friends or your daddy's friends. And when life hits, don't just run to family far away. A good neighbor next door is more helpful in hard times.

11.text: Be wise, my child, and make me proud—so I can clap back when haters try to shame me.

12.text: The wise see trouble comin' and step aside. The naive? They keep walkin' into pain.

13.text: If somebody cosigns for a stranger or a flirt, hold somethin' for collateral. Protect yourself.

14.text: If you too loud complimentin' your friend early in the morning… it's gon' sound more like a curse than love. Chill.

15.text: A naggin', combative woman? Like water drippin' non-stop on a stormy day.

16.text: Tryin' to stop her is like tryna hold wind or grab oil with your bare hand—slippin' and impossible.

17.text: Iron sharpens iron—so one real friend sharpens another.

18.text: Take care of your fig tree, you'll eat good. Serve your people right, and honor gon' come.

19.text: Just like a mirror shows your face, your heart shows who you really are.

20.text: Hell and the grave never say "That's enough." Same way people stay cravin' more, never satisfied.

21.text: Fire tests silver, heat tests gold—and a man? He gets tested by how people speak on his name.

22.text: You can grind a fool down like grain… but that foolishness still ain't leavin' him.

23.text: Know what's goin' on with your flocks. Keep tabs on your resources.

24.text: Money don't last forever. Crowns don't always pass down clean through generations.

25.text: When the grass is cut and the fields harvested—get your business in order.

26.text: Your lambs gon' clothe you. Your goats gon' pay off some land.

27.text: You'll have enough goat's milk for meals—for you, your family, and the folks workin' with you.

1.text: The wicked stay paranoid—runnin' when nobody after 'em. But the righteous? They bold like lions.

2.text: When a land got too much sin, leaders keep switchin'. But one wise ruler can hold things steady.

3.text: A broke man oppressin' the poor? That's like a flood wreckin' the crops—no help, just damage.

4.text: Folks who throw away God's law hype up the wicked. But those who follow the Word push back.

5.text: Evil people don't get justice. But if you seek the Lord? You see it clear.

6.text: Better to be broke and honest than rich and twisted.

7.text: Keepin' God's law shows wisdom. But hangin' with wild, greedy folks? You embarrassin' your people.

8.text: Stackin' money off scams and high-interest loans? That wealth gon' end up with somebody who actually helps the poor.

9.text: If you ignore God's Word, your prayers hit the ceiling. He ain't hearin' that.

10.text: Trickin' good folks into sin? You fallin' into your own trap. But the ones who stay solid? They gon' eat good.

11.text: A rich man thinks he's wise. But a poor man with understanding sees straight through him.

12.text: When the righteous shine, everybody celebrate. But when wicked folks take over? People start hidin'.

13.text: Hide your sins? You won't prosper. But confess and let it go? You'll find mercy.

14.text: Blessed is the one who stays humble and alert. But hard hearts always crash.

15.text: A wicked ruler over the poor? Like a lion roarin' or a bear runnin'—pure danger.

16.text: A clueless leader gon' oppress folks. But one who ain't greedy? He'll last long.

17.text: A person with blood on their hands will stay on the run. Don't cover for 'em.

18.text: Walk straight, you'll be safe. But take a crooked path? You gon' fall—hard.

19.text: Work your land, and you'll stay fed. Chase fantasies? Starvation comin'.

20.text: Faithful folks stay blessed. But folks in a rush to get rich? Trouble's waitin'.

21.text: Don't play favorites—it backfires. Some folks sell out for crumbs.

22.text: Greedy eyes stay chasin' fast money—but don't realize they runnin' straight into poverty.

23.text: Checkin' somebody in love? They'll respect you more later than someone who just tryna flatter.

24.text: Robbin' your mama or daddy and actin' like it's nothin'? That's straight-up destruction energy.

25.text: Prideful hearts keep drama goin'. Trustin' God? That brings peace and prosperity.

26.text: If you only trust your own heart? You playin' yourself. Walkin' in wisdom? That's how you stay safe.

27.text: Give to the poor and you won't lack. But turn a blind eye? Curses gon' follow.

28.text: When the wicked rise up, folks go ghost. But when they fall off? Righteousness steps in.

1.text: Keep gettin' checked and still won't listen? You gon' crash hard—with no way back.

2.text: When righteous folks lead, the people celebrate. When the wicked in charge? Everybody groanin'.

3.text: If you love wisdom, you make your daddy proud. But if you stay out wildin'? You gon' lose everything.

4.text: A king who plays fair keeps the country strong. But bribes? That'll tear everything down.

5.text: Flatterin' your neighbor? That's just settin' a trap under their feet.

6.text: Sin ties evil folks up in knots. But the righteous? They stay singin' with joy.

7.text: A good person looks out for the poor. But wicked folks don't even get that kind of care.

8.text: Mockers stir up cities like they startin' fires. But wise ones know how to calm it down.

9.text: Arguin' with a fool? Whether he yellin' or jokin', you ain't gettin' peace.

10.text: Bloodthirsty people hate the blameless. But real ones protect the innocent.

11.text: A fool runs his mouth with all his emotions. A wise man? He holds that in.

12.text: If a leader listens to lies, everybody under him gon' get shady.

13.text: Poor or powerful, they both breathe 'cause God lit their eyes.

14.text: A king who stands up for the poor with truth? His rule gon' last.

15.text: Correction and discipline teach wisdom. But if you let a child raise himself? His mama gon' be ashamed.

16.text: When wicked folks multiply, sin multiplies. But the righteous? They gon' see their downfall.

17.text: Discipline your son—he'll give you peace. He'll bring joy to your soul.

18.text: When folks ain't got vision or guidance, they wild out. But if they follow God's law? They stay blessed.

19.text: Some folks don't change off words alone. They hear you, but won't move.

20.text: Quick to talk, no filter? A fool got a better shot than that man.

21.text: If you spoil your worker since childhood, don't be surprised when he act entitled like your son.

22.text: An angry man keep conflict goin'. A hothead stacks up sin like it's nothin'.

23.text: Pride'll drop you quick. But humility? That's what keeps you honored.

24.text: Helpin' a thief? You hurting yourself. You supposed to tell the truth, but you stay silent.

25.text: Worryin' about what people think will trap you. Trust God—that's where safety lives.

26.text: Everybody want favor from the powerful. But true justice? That come from the Lord.

27.text: Crooked folks make righteous people sick. But upright living? That offends the wicked too.

1.text: These the words of Agur, son of Jakeh. This what he said to Ithiel—and to Ucal too.

2.text: Real talk—I feel slower than most folks. I ain't got it all figured out.

3.text: I never got taught deep wisdom. I don't fully know the Holy One like I should.

4.text: Who went up to heaven and came back down? Who holds the wind in His hands? Who wrapped up the oceans like cloth? Who set the boundaries of the earth? What's His name? And His Son's name—you know it?

5.text: Every word from God? Flawless. He protect those who trust Him.

6.text: Don't add to His Word. He'll call you out—and make you look like a straight-up liar.

7.text: Lord, I only ask for two things. Please don't hold 'em back before I die:

8.text: Keep lies far from me. And don't give me too much or too little—just enough to live on.

9.text: If I got too much, I might forget You and act brand new. If I got too little, I might steal and disrespect Your name.

10.text: Don't snitch on a servant to his boss—he might curse you out, and you'll be in the wrong.

11.text: There's a whole generation that curses their daddy and won't bless their mama.

12.text: A generation thinkin' they clean, but still filthy.

13.text: Eyes full of pride. Chin up high. Actin' like they untouchable.

14.text: Teeth like blades, mouths like knives. They prey on the poor and chew up the needy.

15.text: The leech got two daughters: "Gimme" and "Gimme More." Three things never satisfied—nah, four always want more:

16.text: The grave, a barren womb, a dry earth that stay thirsty, and fire—fire never says, "That's enough."

17.text: If you mock your daddy or ignore your mama? Birds of the valley gon' pluck that eye clean.

18.text: Three things blow my mind—four that I just can't figure out:

19.text: An eagle flyin' through the sky, A snake slidin' over a rock, A ship sailin' through the sea, And a man wooing a woman.

20.text: The way of a cheating woman? She eat, wipes her mouth, and says, "I ain't do nothin' wrong."

21.text: Four things make the earth wanna snap:

22.text: A servant who suddenly runnin' the show, A fool sittin' back full and smug,

23.text: A bitter woman finally gettin' a ring, And a side chick takin' over the main spot.

24.text: Four little things on earth—but they wise for real:

25.text: Ants—small but stay preparin'.

26.text: Rock badgers—soft but live safe in the cliffs.

27.text: Locusts—no king, but they move in formation.

28.text: Spiders—you'll find 'em in palaces, creepin' up with skill.

29.text: Three things got that boss energy—four walk like royalty:

30.text: The lion—undefeated, fearless.

31.text: The stridin' war horse, The strong goat, And a king in command with his whole army behind him.

32.text: If you been actin' arrogant or plottin' mess? Put your hand over your mouth.

33.text: Just like churnin' milk makes butter, And punchin' a nose draws blood— Pushing anger always leads to drama.

1.text: These right here? King Lemuel speakin'—but it's what his mama put in him.

2.text: "What you doin', my son? My baby boy. The one I prayed for?"

3.text: "Don't give all your energy to wild women—or chase things that break down kings."

4.text: "Ain't no reason for a king to be out here gettin' drunk. Princes either. That ain't royal behavior."

5.text: "If y'all drink too much, you'll forget the law. And folks who need justice? They gon' get done dirty."

6.text: "Let the folks who lost all hope drink. Let the ones in deep pain sip to forget."

7.text: "They tryna numb the struggle. But you? You leadin'. That ain't for you."

8.text: "You? You speak for those who can't. Speak up for the ones they throw away."

9.text: "Open your mouth. Speak right. Stand up for the poor and the overlooked."

10.text: A real one? A virtuous woman? She rare—more valuable than rubies.

11.text: Her man trusts her deep. She got him, so he ain't worried about lack.

12.text: She got his back—good days, bad days, all the days.

13.text: She find what she need, and she don't mind workin' with her hands.

14.text: She's like them merchant ships—movin' smart, bringin' in what the house needs from wherever.

15.text: She up before the sun. Feedin' her people. Breakin' bread with her team too.

16.text: She got business vision. Buys land, flips profit, and plants something that grows.

17.text: She don't just work hard—she builds strength. Physically. Mentally. Spiritually.

18.text: She know her hustle is good. Her light don't go out just 'cause it's dark outside.

19.text: She got skills—turnin' raw materials into real results.

20.text: And her heart? Always open to the ones who don't have enough.

21.text: When it's cold? Her whole house warm. She stay prepared.

22.text: She dress fly too. Classy and creative—she wear royalty.

23.text: Her man well known—not just 'cause of him, but because she got his life together.

24.text: She got side hustles. Makes and sells her own goods. She feedin' the streets and the marketplace.

25.text: Strength and dignity? That's her outfit. And she ain't worried about the future—she laughs at it.

26.text: When she talks, wisdom flows. Her mouth stay wrapped in kindness.

27.text: She keeps her house in check. She don't sit around wastin' time.

28.text: Her kids give her her flowers while she alive. Her man stay singin' her praises.

29.text: "Other women cool... but you? You different. You on a whole 'nother level."

30.text: Charm? It's a vibe—but it can be fake. Beauty? It fades. But a woman who fears the Lord? She's the one who gets praised.

31.text: Let her eat the fruit of all she done. Let her work speak loud for her at the gates.

1.text: Blessed is the one who don't be takin' advice from shady folks, don't chill where sinners hang out, and don't post up with folks who stay mocking.

2.text: Instead, they be lovin' the Lord's Word—thinkin' on it day and night like it's they favorite song on repeat.

3.text: They like a tree planted by a stream—deep roots, strong trunk. Always got fruit in season, leaves don't shrivel, and everything they touch? It flourish.

4.text: But the wicked? Nah, they ain't built like that. They like dry husks—blown away by the wind, ain't got no foundation.

5.text: That's why they won't hold up in court when judgment hits, and they don't belong where the righteous folks gather.

6.text: The Lord sees and knows the way of the righteous—He walkin' with them. But the path of the wicked? That road lead straight to ruin.

1.text: Why the nations wildin'? Why folks out here plottin' stuff that ain't gon' work?

2.text: The kings of the world settin' theyselves up, the rulers all teamin' up—tryna come at the Lord and His Chosen One like they gon' do somethin'.

3.text: They say, 'Let's break free from all this! We done with their rules and control.'

4.text: But the One sittin' up in heaven? He just laughs. God lookin' at 'em like, 'Y'all really tried it.'

5.text: Then He gon' speak, and when He do—it's gon' be heat. His anger gon' shake 'em up real good.

6.text: He say, 'I already picked My King, and He posted up on Zion—My holy mountain.'

7.text: Lemme go 'head and repeat what God said: 'You my Son. Today, I made that official.'

8.text: 'Ask Me, and I'll hand You the nations. The whole earth Yours if You want it.'

9.text: 'You gon' break 'em down with an iron rod—like smashin' clay pots, no mercy.'

10.text: So look, kings—y'all better wise up. And judges? Y'all better listen close.

11.text: Serve the Lord with some real respect, and celebrate Him—but don't get too casual. Keep it humble.

12.text: Show love to the Son, or He might get heated—and when He do, it's a wrap. One spark of His anger and folks get wiped out. But if you trust Him? You blessed.

1.text: Lord, my enemies just keep multiplying! So many folks tryna come for me now.

2.text: Plenty of people out here sayin', 'He ain't got no help—God not messin' with him.'

3.text: But You, Lord? You my shield. You my honor. You the one that keep my head held high.

4.text: I cried out loud to You, Lord—and You heard me from Your holy mountain.

5.text: I laid down and went to sleep. I woke up still breathing—'cause You kept me safe through the night.

6.text: I ain't scared, not even if ten thousand folks surroundin' me on all sides.

7.text: Get up, Lord! Save me, my God! You been out here swingin'—You hit my enemies in the face and knocked out they teeth.

8.text: Rescue comes from You, Lord. Your blessing stay on Your people.

1.text: God of my right standing—hear me when I call! You came through for me when I was stressed. Have mercy, and listen to my prayer.

2.text: Y'all, how long you gon' try to shame me? How long you gon' chase empty things and fall for lies?

3.text: But know this—the Lord set apart the real ones for Himself. When I call on Him, He gon' hear me.

4.text: Go 'head and be mad—but don't sin. Lay in bed, think on it, and be still.

5.text: Bring God the right kind of offering—one that's honest. And trust Him for real.

6.text: Plenty folks out here askin', 'Who gon' come through with something good?' Lord, let Your face shine on us.

7.text: You done filled my heart with joy—more than they get when they pockets full and their wine flowing.

8.text: I'm gon' lay down and sleep in peace, 'cause You the only one, Lord, who keeps me safe.

1.text: Lord, listen to what I'm sayin'. Hear what's heavy on my heart.

2.text: Pay attention to my cry, my King and my God—'cause I'm talkin' to You.

3.text: Every morning, You gon' hear my voice. I lay my prayers before You early, and I wait, watchin'.

4.text: You not the kind of God that mess with wickedness—evil can't chill where You at.

5.text: The arrogant ain't got no space in Your presence. You not rockin' with folks who do dirty.

6.text: You takin' out the liars. You can't stand folks who love violence and play people.

7.text: But me? I'm comin' into Your house leanin' on Your mercy. I bow down in reverence, facin' Your holy place.

8.text: Lord, lead me right—'cause my enemies lurkin'. Show me the straight path.

9.text: Ain't nothin' true in their words. Deep down, they full of destruction. Their throats wide open like graves, and they slick with the talk.

10.text: Hold 'em accountable, God. Let 'em trip over their own schemes. Kick 'em out for all the wrong they do—'cause they went against You.

11.text: But everybody who trust You? Let 'em celebrate! Let 'em shout with joy, 'cause You coverin' them. Let the ones who love Your name turn up in joy.

12.text: Lord, You bless the righteous. You cover 'em in favor like a shield.

1.text: Lord, please don't check me outta anger. Don't discipline me when You heated.

2.text: Have mercy on me, Lord—I'm weak right now. Heal me, 'cause my body hurt deep.

3.text: My soul feel heavy too… But You, Lord—how long I gotta wait?

4.text: Come back for me, Lord. Pull me outta this. Save me, not 'cause I'm worthy, but 'cause You got mercy.

5.text: 'Cause once I'm gone, I can't praise You. Ain't no shoutin' You out from the grave.

6.text: I'm tired of cryin'. My bed soaked every night, tears floodin' my pillow.

7.text: My eyes done puffed up from all this grief—worn out from dealin' with these enemies.

8.text: Y'all who do evil? Fall back. The Lord heard my cryin'.

9.text: Yeah, the Lord heard my request. He gon' take my prayer in.

10.text: All my enemies? Let 'em be ashamed and shook. Let 'em retreat quick, embarrassed and broken.

1.text: Lord my God, I'm puttin' all my trust in You. Save me from the folks tryna hunt me down. Rescue me.

2.text: If You don't, they gon' tear me up like a lion—rippin' me apart, and nobody gon' be there to help.

3.text: Lord my God, if I really did something foul—if I got guilt on my hands—

4.text: If I paid back somebody's peace with drama, or stole from an enemy without reason—

5.text: Then go 'head, let the enemy catch me. Let him stomp me out, drag me down to the dirt, and bury my name.

6.text: But Lord, if that ain't me—get up! Rise in Your anger. Push back the rage of my enemies. Step in with the justice You already declared!

7.text: Let all the people gather 'round You. Come back and sit high above it all for their sake.

8.text: You judge everybody, Lord. So judge me based on how I've lived—on the integrity inside me.

9.text: Let the wicked mess come to an end, God. But lift up the ones tryin' to do right. You the kind of God that check hearts and motives.

10.text: You my defense, God. You save the ones who stay solid in their heart.

11.text: God don't play favorites—He a righteous judge. And He stay mad at wickedness every single day.

12.text: If folks don't turn from their mess, God gon' sharpen His sword. He already pullin' back His bow.

13.text: He gettin' ready with weapons that bring death. His arrows? They comin' in hot—on fire.

14.text: Wicked folks be pregnant with sin—they carry trouble and birth straight-up lies.

15.text: They dig pits for others, but end up fallin' in their own trap.

16.text: Everything they plotted gon' bounce back on 'em. The violence they dealt? It's comin' down on their own head.

17.text: But me? I'ma praise the Lord for His righteousness. I'ma sing to the name of the Lord Most High!

1.text: Lord, our Lord—Your name hit different across the whole earth. Your glory? It's higher than the heavens!
