1.text: Girl, you fine, for real. Like, breathtaking. Your eyes behind that veil? Dove-like—soft and deep. Your hair fall like a whole flock of goats cascading down Mount Gilead.

2.text: Your teeth? White like a bunch of sheep freshly sheared, comin' up clean from the river—each one got a twin, not a gap in sight.

3.text: Your lips got that red ribbon vibe—soft, sweet, speakin' life. Your mouth? Lovely. And your cheeks behind that veil look like a slice of pomegranate—blushin' and beautiful.

4.text: Your neck stand tall like the tower of David, strong, elegant, made to carry honor. Warriors' shields hang from it—you a queen built for battles won.

5.text: Your breasts like twin baby deer, grazin' gentle in a field of lilies—soft, tender, perfectly paired.

6.text: 'Til sunrise breaks and night disappears, I'ma make my way to your mountain of myrrh, and that hill of frankincense. (You know what I mean.)

7.text: Baby girl, you flawless. Ain't a blemish on you anywhere. You all beauty, no doubt.

8.text: Come with me, my bride. Step outta Lebanon with me. Let's climb to the peaks—Amana, Senir, Hermon. Come away from lion dens, from leopard mountains. Come safe with me.

9.text: You got my heart in a chokehold, girl. My queen, my love—One glance from your eyes, one jewel on your chain—and I'm done for.

10.text: Your love? Whew—it hit different. Better than the finest wine. And your scent? It beat every spice on earth.

11.text: When you kiss me? It drip like honeycomb. Milk and honey rest under your tongue. Even your clothes smell like fresh Lebanon air.

12.text: You a whole private garden, sis. Locked up, sacred. A spring no one touched. A sealed-up fountain. You protected and precious.

13.text: Inside you? A whole orchard—pomegranates, sweet fruits, henna blossoms, and spikenard flowin' heavy.

14.text: Spikenard, saffron, calamus, cinnamon—trees pourin' out frankincense, myrrh and aloe—every rich spice a king could ask for.

15.text: You a garden fountain, a fresh spring full of life, water runnin' wild from the mountains of Lebanon.

16.text: Wake up, north wind! Come on, south wind! Blow through my garden, let the fragrance flow. Let my man come in and taste what's his—Let him feast on all this fruit I've been growin'.

1.text: I pulled up in my garden, sis—you know that's mine. Snatched myrrh and spice, scooped up the honeycomb and the honey. Had my wine, poured my milk. To all my people: y'all better eat! Drink up—drink deep, beloveds!

2.text: I was sleepin', but my heart stayed up. Then I heard him knockin'. "My love, my dove, my girl—open up for me. I'm out here drippin' with night dew, my hair wet from waitin'."

3.text: "I done took off my robe—how I'm supposed to put it back on? I already washed my feet—ain't tryna mess 'em up again."

4.text: Then he reached through the latch on the door—And my heart? It jumped. That man got me open.

5.text: I got up quick to let him in. My hands were slick with myrrh, fingers drippin' sweet scent, Right on the lock.

6.text: I opened the door, but he was gone. I felt it deep—he spoke, and it shook me. I ran lookin', but couldn't find him. I called, but he didn't say nothin' back.

7.text: The city guards caught me slippin'. They hit me. Bruised me. Took my veil and left me exposed.

8.text: Y'all, daughters of Jerusalem—if you see my man, Tell him I'm love-sick for real. Like, head over heels.

9.text: Girl, what's so special about your man? Why you so pressed? What make him stand out from everybody else?

10.text: My man? He different. Light-skinned with a glow, deep reddish-brown too—He stand out in a crowd of ten thousand.

11.text: His head? Pure gold. His curls? Laid and black like a raven.

12.text: His eyes be soft like doves chillin' by the riverside—Washed clean, set just right.

13.text: His cheeks? Like gardens full of spice. His lips? Lilies, drippin' with myrrh. I could kiss 'em forever.

14.text: His hands? Solid gold, iced out. His body? Sculpted like ivory, detailed with jewels.

15.text: His legs? Strong like marble columns, Standin' on gold foundations. He carry himself like a cedar tree from Lebanon—noble.

16.text: His mouth? Sweet as honey. Yeah, he all that. That's my man, my friend, So don't ask me twice.

1.text: Girl, where yo' man at? You the baddest of us all—Where he turn off to? We'll help you look for him.

2.text: He out in his garden, Where the spices bloom. Feeding his sheep, Picking lilies like he always do.

3.text: I belong to my man, And he belongs to me. He stay in the lilies—right where I can find him.

4.text: My love, you lookin' like Tirzah—fine and regal. Like Jerusalem herself—majestic, unstoppable, like an army marchin' with flags flyin'.

5.text: Turn your eyes away, girl, You starin' me down too hard. Your gaze? Got me weak. And that hair? Fallin' like goats on a hill in Gilead.

6.text: Your teeth? Still like sheep fresh out the water—all lined up, every one got a twin. No gaps, no stragglers.

7.text: Your cheeks behind that veil? They glow like ripe pomegranate slices. Full of color, full of life.

8.text: Look, I could have sixty queens, eighty side pieces, and virgins without number—

9.text: But you? You my dove. You the one. Only daughter of your mama, Her favorite child. Even the other girls see you and call you blessed—Queens, concubines, all of 'em praise your name.

10.text: Who is she, shinin' like sunrise? Soft like the moonlight, Bright like the noon sun, Standin' strong like a whole army lined up?

11.text: I went out to the valley, Just to check the garden—See if the vines started growin', See if the pomegranates were bloomin'.

12.text: Next thing I know, My spirit lifted me like a royal chariot—Rollin' with my people, feelin' chosen.

13.text: Come back, come back, Shulamite girl! We just wanna see you. Come on back, let us look at you! What y'all lookin' at in me anyway? Is it like watchin' a sacred dance, Like two armies movin' as one?

1.text: Girl, your feet in them sandals? Whew—royalty. You walkin' like a queen. Your thighs curved like they was sculpted by a master. Straight art.

2.text: That belly? Smooth like a goblet, Always full—never lackin'. Your waist? Round and full like a wheat harvest, Surrounded in softness like lilies bloomin'.

3.text: And your breasts? Like two baby deer—Twins of a gazelle, restin' easy.

4.text: Your neck got that regal posture, Like an ivory tower standin' tall. Your eyes? Deep like the pools in Heshbon, Right near the city gate. That nose? Strong and centered—like the tower in Lebanon, Facing Damascus bold.

5.text: That head of yours? Sittin' proud like Mount Carmel. And your hair? Deep purple waves—got a king locked in with just one look.

6.text: You so fine, so pleasant—Everything about you bring joy. I could stare at you for days.

7.text: Your body tall and elegant, Like a palm tree reachin' high. And your breasts? Full like them palm clusters.

8.text: I said to myself, "I'm climbin' that tree. Gonna hold on tight to them branches." Let them curves be like sweet grape clusters, Let your breath smell like fresh-picked apples.

9.text: And your kisses? Whew—like sippin' the finest wine. That wine slide down smooth for my man, Soft on the lips, sweet in his dreams.

10.text: I belong to my love—And he want me just as much as I want him.

11.text: Come on, baby. Let's dip out to the countryside. Let's stay the night somewhere quiet, just you and me.

12.text: Let's wake up early, hit the vineyards, See if the vines startin' to bloom, If the grapes got blossoms, If them pomegranates burstin' open. That's where I'm givin' you all this love.

13.text: The mandrakes got the whole place smellin' right, And by our door? Every kind of fruit—old memories, new moments. I saved it all for you, my love.

1.text: I wish you was like my brother, Somebody I could kiss out in the open, No side eyes, no shame, just love.

2.text: I'd take you by the hand, Bring you into mama's house—The same place I learned how to care. I'd pour you a glass of spiced wine, Let you taste the sweetness of my love.

3.text: His left arm holdin' up my head, His right arm wrapped tight 'round me. That's how we rest.

4.text: I'm tellin' y'all again, daughters of Jerusalem—Don't wake love before it's ready. Let it rise when it wanna rise.

5.text: Who this woman comin' up from the wild, Leanin' on her man like home? I brought you up under that apple tree, Right where your mama birthed you into this world.

6.text: Put me like a tattoo on your heart, Lock me in like a bracelet on your arm. This love? It don't play. It's strong like death, Jealous like the grave, And hot like wildfire. Ain't nothin' lukewarm about it.

7.text: Ain't no flood that can drown it. Ain't no river that can wash it away. If a man tried to buy this love with everything he got? He'd get laughed out the room.

8.text: We got a little sister, She still young, no curves yet. What we gon' do when a man start lookin' at her?

9.text: If she solid like a wall, We'll crown her with silver. If she wide open like a door, We'll frame her in with cedar—lock her in tight.

10.text: Well, I am a wall. And these curves? Yeah, they towerin'. He looked at me and saw peace. Like, finally… this the one.

11.text: Solomon got a vineyard out in Baal Hamon, He leased it out, made folks pay for the fruit—A thousand silver coins just for what grows.

12.text: But my vineyard? That's mine. You, Solomon, can keep your thousands, Let the workers get their cut. But what I got? Priceless. I ain't for sale.

13.text: You out there in the gardens, Everybody listenin' for your voice—Let me be the one to hear it.

14.text: Come on, baby. Run to me like a gazelle, Fast and free, On the hills that smell like home.

1.text: It was the eighth month of the second year King Darius was in charge when God gave a word to Zechariah, son of Berekiah, grandson of Iddo—the prophet.

2.text: The Lord was big mad with y'all ancestors.

3.text: So go tell the folks this: "The Lord of Heaven's Armies said, 'Come back to Me, and I'ma come back to y'all.' That's a promise."

4.text: Don't be like your hardheaded ancestors. The old prophets already told them, "Turn from y'all dirty ways and evil doin'!" But they ain't listen. They ain't even pay God no mind.

5.text: Where your ancestors at now? They gone. And those prophets? They ain't here forever either.

6.text: But the words and commands I gave through my prophets? They came true. Hit your ancestors like a freight train. So eventually, the people was like, "God did what He said He was gon' do—judged us based on how we acted. We can't even argue."

7.text: On the twenty-fourth day of the eleventh month—Shebat—in Darius's second year, God gave Zechariah another word.

8.text: That night, I saw somethin' wild—a man ridin' a red horse chillin' in some myrtle trees down in a valley. Behind him? More horses: red, brown, and white.

9.text: I said, "Uh… what's this mean, my lord?" The angel talkin' to me said, "I got you. I'ma show you what this is about."

10.text: Then the man standin' in the myrtle trees spoke up: "These horses? They the ones God sent out to walk the earth and scope things out."

11.text: And the horses came back and said to the Angel of the Lord standin' there, "We been all over the earth. Everything calm and quiet out there."

12.text: Then the Angel of the Lord said, "Lord of Heaven's Armies, how long You gon' hold back Your mercy from Jerusalem and Judah? It's been seventy years since You showed 'em tough love."

13.text: God answered the angel with words that brought comfort and hope.

14.text: The angel told me, "Go tell the people this: The Lord of Heaven's Armies says, 'I'm real jealous for Jerusalem and Zion. That's My spot.

15.text: And I'm heated with these other nations that act all chill. I was just a lil' angry, but they went too far with how they treated My people.'"

16.text: So here's what the Lord says: 'I'm coming back to Jerusalem with mercy. My house gon' be built again, and I'ma send the surveyors out to measure the city.'

17.text: Then He said again, "Tell 'em this: 'My cities gon' be blessed again, overflowin' with good. I'ma comfort Zion one more time and choose Jerusalem all over again.'"

18.text: Then I looked up and saw four horns.

19.text: I asked the angel talkin' to me, "What's these mean?" He said, "These the horns that scattered Judah, Israel, and Jerusalem."

20.text: Then God showed me four craftsmen.

21.text: I asked, "What they here to do?" He said, "These horns scattered Judah so bad folks couldn't even hold their heads up. But these craftsmen? They comin' to shut all that down. They gon' strike fear in those nations, tear down the horns that came up against Judah, and stop them from spreading destruction."

1.text: I looked up and saw a man holdin' a measuring line in his hand.

2.text: I asked him, "Where you headed?" He said, "I'm bout to measure Jerusalem. Tryna see how wide and how long it is."

3.text: The angel that was talkin' with me started walkin' out, and then another angel came out to meet him.

4.text: That second angel said, "Run and go tell that young man this: 'Jerusalem gon' be a city with no walls, 'cause it's gon' be packed with people and animals everywhere.

5.text: And God say, 'I'm gon' be a wall of fire around her and My glory gon' be right in the middle of it.'"

6.text: "Get up, get up! Run from the north," says the Lord. "I done scattered y'all like the four winds across the sky."

7.text: "Zion, get outta Babylon! Run from that mess!"

8.text: The Lord of Heaven's Armies says this: "He sent Me to the nations that robbed y'all. And lemme tell you—anybody that messes with you? They pokin' God straight in the eye.

9.text: I'ma raise My hand against them, and they gon' get taken down. Their own servants gon' flip the script and take what they got. Then you'll know for real that the Lord of Hosts sent Me."

10.text: "Sing, Zion! Rejoice, daughter! 'Cause I'm comin'. I'm gon' move in and live right there with y'all," says the Lord.

11.text: "That day, a bunch of nations gon' turn to Me and be My people too. I'm gon' dwell in the middle of all y'all. And then you gon' know I was sent by the Lord of Heaven's Armies.

12.text: God gon' claim Judah again as His own in the Holy Land, and He gon' choose Jerusalem one more time."

13.text: "Everybody everywhere—shut it down. Be still. God just stood up from His holy throne, and He got somethin' to say."

1.text: Then I saw Joshua, the high priest, standin' in front of the Angel of the Lord. And Satan was right there on his side, tryna come for him.

2.text: But the Lord shut that down quick: "The Lord rebuke you, Satan! Yeah, the One who chose Jerusalem rebuke you! This man right here? He like a stick snatched straight outta the fire."

3.text: Joshua was standin' there wearin' filthy clothes—lookin' real unclean in front of the Angel.

4.text: Then the Angel spoke up and said to the ones standin' around, "Take them dirty clothes off him." And then He said to Joshua, "Look—I just took your sin off you. Now I'ma dress you in somethin' real nice."

5.text: I said, "Put a clean turban on his head too." So they gave him a fresh turban and dressed him up in new clothes, while the Angel of the Lord stood there watchin'.

6.text: Then the Angel of the Lord gave Joshua a serious word, sayin':

7.text: "This what the Lord of Heaven's Armies says: 'If you walk the way I tell you, And do what I command, You gon' be in charge of My house, Run My courts, And I'ma give you access to walk with these heavenly ones right here.'

8.text: So listen up, Joshua the high priest—you and your folks sittin' with you. Y'all a symbol of somethin' bigger. I'm about to bring My servant, the Branch.

9.text: Check this—there's a stone I put in front of Joshua. It got seven eyes on it. I'ma carve something deep on it," says the Lord of Hosts, "and I'ma wipe out all the sin in this land in one single day.

10.text: On that day," says the Lord of Heaven's Armies, "everybody gon' be chillin', sittin' under their own vine and fig tree, choppin' it up with their neighbors."

1.text: The angel that had been talkin' with me came back and woke me up—like somebody tryna shake a dude outta deep sleep.

2.text: He asked, "What you seein'?" I said, "I see a gold lampstand. It got a bowl on top, and seven lamps on it. Each lamp got seven pipes runnin' to it.

3.text: And next to it, there's two olive trees—one on the right side of the bowl, the other on the left."

4.text: So I asked the angel who was talkin' to me, "Umm… what all this mean, my lord?"

5.text: He said back, "You don't know what this is?" I said, "No sir, I really don't."

6.text: He said, "This right here? This the word of the Lord to Zerubbabel: 'It ain't gon' happen by strength, It ain't gon' happen by force—But only by My Spirit,' says the Lord of Heaven's Armies.

7.text: Who you think you are, big mountain? Before Zerubbabel, you gon' flatten out like a plain. He gon' set that final stone in place While everybody shoutin', 'Grace! Grace on it!'"

8.text: Then I got another word from the Lord:

9.text: "Zerubbabel laid down the first brick of this temple, And it's gon' be his hands that finish it too. Then y'all gon' know for sure That the Lord of Hosts sent Me."

10.text: "Don't sleep on the small beginnings. Them seven eyes been watchin'—they glad to see that plumb line in Zerubbabel's hand. Those eyes? They the eyes of the Lord, Lookin' all over the whole world."

11.text: Then I asked him, "Okay but… what's up with these two olive trees on both sides of the lampstand?"

12.text: I kept goin': "And them two olive branches—what's up with them drippin' oil into the gold pipes?"

13.text: The angel said again, "You still don't know what this is?" I said, "Nope. Still don't."

14.text: He said, "These are the two anointed ones—the ones standin' by the Lord of the whole earth."

1.text: Then I looked up again—and saw a scroll flyin' through the air.

2.text: The angel asked me, "What you seein'?" I said, "It's a scroll, flyin'. Look like it's twenty cubits long and ten cubits wide."

3.text: Then he told me, "This right here is the curse goin' out over the whole land. One side say every thief gettin' kicked out, and the other side say every liar who swears falsely gettin' kicked out too."

4.text: "I'ma send this curse out Myself," says the Lord of Heaven's Armies. "It's gon' fly straight into the house of every thief, And into the home of anybody lyin' in My name. It's gon' stay right there in they house Till it tears that place down—wood, stone, all of it."

5.text: Then the angel who was talkin' with me came up again and said, "Look up. You see that? Tell me what's goin' out now."

6.text: I asked, "What is that?" He said, "It's a basket." Then he said, "This basket represents how things look all over the earth right now."

7.text: Then the lid—made of heavy lead—was lifted up, and I saw a woman sittin' inside the basket.

8.text: He said, "That right there? That's Wickedness!" Then he straight shoved her back down in the basket and slammed the lid shut.

9.text: I looked up again—and now two women were comin' through the sky. They had wings like storks, and the wind was pushin' them forward. They lifted up the basket, floatin' it between earth and heaven.

10.text: So I asked the angel, "Where they takin' that basket?"

11.text: He said, "To the land of Shinar. They buildin' a house for it there. Once it's ready, that basket gon' sit right there on its own base."

1.text: Then I looked up again and saw four chariots rollin' out from between two mountains—and them mountains was made of bronze.

2.text: The first chariot had red horses,

3.text: the second one had black horses,

4.text: the third had white horses, and the fourth had dappled horses—big, strong, muscular ones.

5.text: I asked the angel talkin' to me, "What's all this mean, my lord?" He said, "These chariots? They represent four spirits of heaven, comin' out from where they stand in front of the Lord of all the earth.

6.text: The chariot with the black horses is headed to the north, the white ones goin' right behind 'em, and the dappled ones ridin' down south."

7.text: The strong horses was hype—ready to move out, eager to patrol the earth. And He said, "Aight then—go ahead, walk the earth." So they took off, movin' all over the world.

8.text: Then He called out to me and said, "You see them ones goin' north? They done gave My Spirit some peace up there."

9.text: Then the Lord gave me another word:

10.text: "Go get that gift from the folks who came back from exile—Heldai, Tobijah, and Jedaiah. They just got back from Babylon. Same day, pull up at Josiah son of Zephaniah's house.

11.text: Take that silver and gold they brought. Craft a royal crown—real fancy. Then place it on the head of Joshua, the high priest, son of Jehozadak.

12.text: Tell him this is what the Lord of Heaven's Armies says: 'Look, the Man named the BRANCH is comin'. He gon' sprout up from where He is And build the temple of the Lord.

13.text: Yep—He gon' build it alright. And He gon' carry the glory, Sit on a throne, And rule as both priest and king. And there'll be real peace between both roles—no conflict.'

14.text: That crown you made? It's gon' be kept in the Lord's temple as a reminder— Dedicated to Helem, Tobijah, Jedaiah, and Hen son of Zephaniah.

15.text: Even folks from far away gon' come help build God's temple. And when it all goes down, you'll know for sure The Lord of Heaven's Armies sent Me. But listen— This only happens if y'all obey the voice of the Lord your God."

1.text: In the fourth year of King Darius' reign, a word from the Lord came to Zechariah on the fourth day of the ninth month—Chislev.

2.text: The people sent Sherezer and Regem-Melech with a few others to the temple to pray before the Lord.

3.text: They also went to ask the priests at the temple of the Lord of Heaven's Armies—and the prophets too—"Yo, we been fastin' and cryin' every fifth month for years. Should we still keep doin' that?"

4.text: Then the Lord of Hosts gave me this word:

5.text: "Tell everybody in the land, and the priests too: When y'all was fastin' and mournin' in the fifth and seventh months all them seventy years—was you really doin' it for Me? For real?

6.text: And when y'all eat and drink, ain't y'all doin' that for yourselves too?

7.text: Shouldn't y'all have listened to the words the Lord already gave through the prophets back when Jerusalem and the towns around it was full and poppin'? Back when the Southland and the valley areas was alive?"

8.text: Then another word came from the Lord to Zechariah:

9.text: "This what the Lord of Hosts say: 'Do what's right. Treat people fair. Show love and compassion to your folks.

10.text: Don't be pressin' the widows, orphans, immigrants, or the poor. And don't be schemin' in your heart against your own brother.'

11.text: But they ain't wanna hear that. They shrugged it off and covered they ears, actin' like they ain't hear nothin'.

12.text: They hardened they hearts like stone—refusin' to hear the law and the messages I sent through My Spirit by the prophets. That's why My anger came down heavy.

13.text: So when I called out and they ignored Me, I flipped it—when they called out, I ain't listen," says the Lord of Hosts.

14.text: "I scattered them like a storm across nations they ain't never known. The land they left behind? Empty. Deserted. Ain't nobody passin' through there no more. They the reason that good land turned into a ghost town."

1.text: Then another word from the Lord of Heaven's Armies came to me.

2.text: "This what the Lord of Hosts says: I'm fired up for Zion—like, real passionate. I'm comin' with intense love and energy for her."

3.text: "This what the Lord says: I'm comin' back to Zion. I'ma live in the middle of Jerusalem again. People gon' call it the City of Truth. The mountain where I live? That's the Holy Mountain."

4.text: "Here's what the Lord of Hosts says: Old men and old women gon' be sittin' in the streets of Jerusalem again, Leanin' on they canes 'cause they lived long and strong.

5.text: And the streets gon' be filled with little kids Laughin' and playin' all over the city."

6.text: "The Lord of Hosts says this: It might sound too good to be true to the folks left alive right now, But you think it's too marvelous for Me? Nah."

7.text: "The Lord of Hosts says: I'm gon' save My people from the east and the west—don't matter where they scattered.

8.text: I'ma bring 'em back, and they gon' live in Jerusalem. They'll be My people, and I'll be their God, Holdin' it down with truth and righteousness."

9.text: "So here's the word, straight from the Lord of Hosts: Y'all who been listenin' to the prophets lately— The same ones who spoke when the temple foundation got laid— Y'all better stay strong.

10.text: Back in the day, there wasn't no money for folks, No work for animals, And no peace either—enemies everywhere. I let folks turn against each other.

11.text: But now? I ain't treatin' this leftover remnant like I did before," says the Lord of Hosts.

12.text: "Now the seeds y'all plant gon' grow, The vines gon' give sweet fruit, The ground gon' yield crops, The skies gon' send dew. I'ma hook y'all up—y'all gon' own all that again.

13.text: Look, y'all used to be the curse of the nations—folks looked down on Judah and Israel. But now I'ma save y'all, And y'all gon' be the blessing. So don't be scared—get your strength back."

14.text: "The Lord of Hosts says: Just like I was dead set on punishin' y'all ancestors when they made Me mad—and I ain't back down—

15.text: Now I'm just as locked in to bless Jerusalem and Judah. So again, don't be scared.

16.text: Here's what I need from y'all now: Tell the truth to your neighbor. Judge fair and right when you settle stuff. Bring peace into every decision.

17.text: Don't sit around plottin' evil on folks. And stop lovin' lies and fake oaths. I hate all that mess," says the Lord.

18.text: Then another word from the Lord of Hosts came through:

19.text: "This what the Lord says: All them fasts—the one in the fourth month, fifth, seventh, and tenth— They ain't gon' be sad days no more. They gon' be days of joy, celebration, and good vibes for Judah. So love truth and peace."

20.text: "The Lord of Hosts says: People from all kinds of cities gon' pull up.

21.text: Folks from one town gon' hit up another like, 'Let's go seek the Lord together. Let's pray in His presence.' And the other one gon' say, 'Bet—I'm comin' too.'

22.text: A whole bunch of people—nations with real strength— Gon' come to Jerusalem to seek the Lord and pray in His house."

23.text: "And in that day," says the Lord of Hosts, "Ten people from ten different languages gon' grab hold of one Jewish man's sleeve and say, 'We comin' with you—'cause we heard God is with y'all.'"

1.text: This the message from the Lord— A heavy word against Hadrach's land, With Damascus as the place it gon' hit. Everybody watchin' now—every tribe in Israel got their eyes on the Lord.

2.text: Same thing comin' for Hamath next door, Then Tyre and Sidon, even though they slick and think they smart.

3.text: Tyre tried to flex— Built up towers, stacked silver like it was dirt, Piled up gold like trash in the streets.

4.text: But God gon' toss her out. He gon' snatch her strength right out the sea, And she gon' get burned down in flames.

5.text: When Ashkelon see it, she gon' be shook. Gaza? Heartbroken. Ekron gon' be crushed— 'Cause the little hope she had left? Gone. The king in Gaza gon' be wiped out. Ashkelon gon' be empty and desolate.

6.text: Foreign folks gon' move into Ashdod. And I'ma cut off that pride the Philistines got.

7.text: I'ma snatch that bloody mess outta their mouths, And remove all them nasty, unclean things they keep doin'. But whoever's left? They gon' belong to God. They gon' roll with Judah like a clan leader. And Ekron? Gon' be like the Jebusites—folded in.

8.text: I'ma post up and guard My house— So no army can just roll through whenever they feel like it. No more oppressors creepin' in. I see everything now. I'm watchin' it all Myself.

9.text: Zion, go 'head and turn up! Jerusalem, shout loud! Your King is comin'— He righteous, bringin' salvation, Humble and ridin' on a donkey. Yeah, a young donkey—just a colt.

10.text: I'ma shut down all the war weapons— No more chariots in Ephraim, No more horses in Jerusalem. The battle bows? Gone. He gon' speak peace to all the nations. And His kingdom? From sea to sea, From the River all the way to the ends of the earth.

11.text: And you? Yeah, you— Because of the blood covenant I made with you, I'ma pull your people up out that dry pit. They ain't stuck no more.

12.text: Come back to safety, You prisoners of hope. Today I'm lettin' it be known— I'ma pay you back double for what you lost.

13.text: I got Judah locked and loaded— They My bow. Ephraim? That's My arrow. And I'm raisin' up Zion's sons to go head-to-head with Greece. Y'all gon' be like a mighty warrior's sword.

14.text: The Lord gon' show up on top, His arrow flashin' like lightning. He gon' blow the trumpet loud, Ridin' with whirlwind power outta the south.

15.text: The Lord of Heaven's Armies gon' protect 'em. They gon' stomp their enemies— Crush 'em like stones in a sling. They gon' drink and roar like they drunk, Full like bowls at the altar, Covered in the blood of victory.

16.text: On that day, their God gon' save 'em— His people, His flock. They gon' shine like jewels in a crown, Raised high like a banner across the land.

17.text: Look how good God is! Look how beautiful what He's doin'! The young men gon' flourish off grain, The young women off new wine— Full of life, full of joy.

1.text: When it's time for the latter rain— Y'all better ask the Lord for it. He the one who sends the storm clouds. He the one who gives the rain showers, And makes the fields grow green for everybody.

2.text: But the idols? They straight up lyin'. The fortune-tellers just makin' stuff up. Their dreams fake, their comfort weak. So the people out here wanderin' like lost sheep, Strugglin' 'cause they ain't got no real shepherd.

3.text: God said, "I'm heated with these so-called shepherds. And I'm comin' for them fake leaders. But I'ma show up for My people—My flock, Judah. I'ma make 'em strong, Like war horses ready to ride into battle for the King."

4.text: Outta Judah gon' come the cornerstone, The tent peg that holds everything down, The battle bow that wins the fight, And every ruler, all from one place.

5.text: They gon' be like warriors in the street— Trampling their enemies in the mud. They gon' fight and win 'cause the Lord ridin' with 'em. And them horsemen? They gon' be embarrassed.

6.text: "I'ma strengthen Judah, And I'ma save Joseph's crew too. I'ma bring 'em back 'cause I still got mercy. It'll be like they never even got cast out— 'Cause I'm their God, and I'm listenin' to 'em again.

7.text: Ephraim's people? Gon' be mighty. They hearts gon' turn up like they sippin' good wine. Even their kids gon' see it and get happy. They hearts gon' rejoice in the Lord."

8.text: "I'ma call out to 'em—whistle like I'm callin' My crew back. I done bought 'em back, and they gon' grow again, Just like they did back in the day.

9.text: I scattered them across nations, But even in them far-off lands, they still gon' remember Me. They gon' live—they and their kids— And one day, they comin' home."

10.text: "I'ma bring them outta Egypt, And gather 'em from Assyria. I'ma plant 'em back in Gilead and Lebanon— So many of 'em, it won't even be enough space to hold 'em.

11.text: I'ma pass through the stormy seas with 'em, Strike the waves down, Dry up every river that tried to drown 'em. Assyria's pride? Gone. Egypt's power? Dead."

12.text: "I'ma make My people strong in Me. They gon' move with purpose, Walkin' up and down in My name," Says the Lord.

1.text: Open up your doors, Lebanon— Fire 'bout to eat up all your cedar trees.

2.text: Cry out, cypress trees—'cause the big strong cedars done fell. The mighty forest is wrecked. Cry, oaks of Bashan— That whole thick forest been brought down low.

3.text: You hear that? The shepherds weepin'— 'Cause all their glory done crashed. You hear them lions roarin'? The pride of the Jordan land been ruined too.

4.text: This what the Lord my God said: "Go feed the flock that's been set up for slaughter.

5.text: The ones ownin' them sheep kill 'em without a second thought. Then turn around and say, 'Praise the Lord—I'm rich now!' And the so-called shepherds? They don't even care that the flock dyin'."

6.text: "I'm done showin' pity to the people in this land," says the Lord. "I'ma hand everybody over to they neighbors and they king. Folks gon' be destroyin' each other. I'm not stoppin' it."

7.text: So I went ahead and fed the flock marked for slaughter—especially the poor ones. I picked up two staffs: One I named Beauty, and the other Bonds. And I started shepherdin' the flock.

8.text: I fired three of them fake shepherds in one month. I couldn't stand 'em. And they hated me too.

9.text: Then I said, "I ain't feedin' y'all no more. The ones dyin'? Let 'em die. The ones fallin' off? Let 'em fall. The rest of y'all? Eat each other alive if you want."

10.text: Then I broke my staff called Beauty— That was Me breakin' the covenant I had with all the people.

11.text: And that day it was broken. The poor ones, the ones watchin' close? They knew—this was the word of the Lord.

12.text: Then I told 'em, "If y'all feel like payin' me, go ahead. If not, whatever." So they gave me thirty pieces of silver.

13.text: And the Lord said, "Throw that mess to the potter— The 'royal price' they thought I was worth." So I threw the thirty pieces into the temple of the Lord—for the potter.

14.text: Then I snapped my other staff, Bonds, in half— That was Me breakin' the unity between Judah and Israel.

15.text: Then the Lord told me, "Now grab the tools of a foolish shepherd.

16.text: I'm gon' let a shepherd rise up who don't care about the ones who strayed, Don't look for the young ones, Don't heal the ones hurt, Don't even feed the ones still standin'. He just gon' eat the fat sheep and tear 'em apart."

17.text: Woe to that fake shepherd who dipped out on the flock! His arm gon' get struck down, His right eye gon' go blind. That arm? Withered and useless. That eye? Completely dark.

1.text: This the heavy word from the Lord about Israel— The One who stretched out the heavens, Laid down the foundation of the earth, And formed the spirit inside humans—He said:

2.text: "Watch this—I'm gon' make Jerusalem like a cup that make all the nations around her drunk. When they try to come for Judah and lay siege on the city, They ain't gon' know what hit 'em.

3.text: On that day, Jerusalem gon' be like a stone too heavy to lift. Anybody try to move it? Gon' end up cut and broken. Even if the whole world squad up against her."

4.text: The Lord says, "When that day hits— I'ma confuse every horse and make the riders lose their minds. But My eyes gon' stay locked on Judah. I'ma strike the enemies' horses blind.

5.text: The leaders of Judah gon' say to themselves, 'Our strength comes from the folks in Jerusalem, From the Lord of Heaven's Armies—our God.'"

6.text: "On that day," God says, "I'ma make the leaders of Judah like fire in dry wood, Like a torch burning through bundles of straw. They gon' burn through the nations on both sides. But Jerusalem? She gon' still be standin', Safe and sound, right where she belong."

7.text: "I'ma save the country folks in Judah first, So the house of David and the folks in Jerusalem Don't try to act like they more important than the rest.

8.text: On that day, I'ma defend everybody in Jerusalem. Even the weakest person there gon' fight like David. And David's house? They gon' move like God Himself—like the Angel of the Lord leadin' the charge.

9.text: And I'ma be lookin' to destroy any nation that try to run up on Jerusalem."

10.text: "Then I'ma pour out My Spirit— The Spirit of grace and mercy— All over the house of David and the people of Jerusalem. They gon' look at Me—the One they pierced— And mourn like they lost their only son. They gon' cry like they just buried their firstborn."

11.text: "On that day, the whole city gon' be in deep mourning— Like that time they mourned at Hadad Rimmon in Megiddo.

12.text: Every family gon' be grievin' in their own space: The house of David and their wives, The house of Nathan and their wives,

13.text: The house of Levi and their wives, The house of Shimei and their wives—

14.text: All the rest of the families too—each one mournin' separate, husbands and wives apart."

1.text: "On that day, a fountain gon' open up For the house of David and all the folks in Jerusalem— To wash away all they sin and dirtiness."

2.text: "On that day," says the Lord of Heaven's Armies, "I'ma wipe out every idol's name from the land. Ain't nobody even gon' remember 'em no more. I'ma run out all the fake prophets And that nasty unclean spirit too."

3.text: If anybody still out here tryna prophesy lies, Even his mama and daddy gon' step up and say, 'You ain't gon' live—not while you speakin' lies in God's name.' They own parents gon' shut it down—stab him for lyin' like that.

4.text: On that day, them so-called prophets gon' be embarrassed. They gon' be ashamed of them visions they claimin'. They not gon' rock them prophet outfits no more— No more tryna act holy wearin' rough clothes just to fool folks.

5.text: Instead, they gon' say, "Nah, I'm just a farmer. Always been. Somebody taught me to raise cattle since I was a kid."

6.text: But somebody gon' ask him, "Then what's them scars on your arms?" And he'll say, "Oh, I got those at my home— From folks I used to call my friends."

7.text: "Wake up, sword— Go after My Shepherd, The Man who walks close with Me," Says the Lord of Hosts. "Strike the Shepherd, And the sheep gon' scatter. Then I'ma turn and deal with the rest—the little ones."

8.text: "In the whole land," says the Lord, "Two-thirds of the people? They not gon' make it. But one-third? I'ma let them live."

9.text: "That one-third? I'ma take 'em through the fire— Like silver gettin' refined, Like gold gettin' tested. They gon' call out to Me, And I'ma answer, 'These My people right here.' And they gon' say, 'The Lord is my God.'"

1.text: Look, the day of the Lord comin'— And everything y'all took gon' be divided right in front of you.

2.text: I'm bringin' all the nations together To go to war against Jerusalem. The city gon' get invaded, Houses broken into, Women violated. Half the city gon' get dragged off, But some of the people gon' remain—they won't be wiped out.

3.text: Then the Lord Himself gon' step in— And He gon' fight those nations Like He always do when it's time for battle.

4.text: On that day, His feet gon' land on the Mount of Olives— That's the mountain east of Jerusalem. And the mountain gon' split in two, From east to west, Creating a huge valley— Half the mountain movin' north, the other half south.

5.text: Y'all gon' run through that valley— All the way to Azal. Just like y'all ran from the earthquake Back when King Uzziah was runnin' Judah. But this time? The Lord gon' show up, And all His holy ones comin' with Him.

6.text: On that day, the light gon' be dim. The usual glow? It won't shine.

7.text: But it'll be one special day— Only the Lord knows it. It won't be daytime or nighttime— But when evening hits, boom—light.

8.text: And on that day, living water gon' flow outta Jerusalem— Half of it headin' east to the Dead Sea, Half west to the Mediterranean. It'll flow year-round—summer and winter.

9.text: The Lord gon' be King over the whole earth. On that day everybody gon' say: "The Lord is One. His name is One."

10.text: The whole land, from Geba to Rimmon south of Jerusalem, Gon' flatten out like a plain. But Jerusalem? She gon' rise up—lifted, rebuilt, and filled with people— From Benjamin's Gate to the First Gate, The Corner Gate to Hananel's Tower, Down to the king's winepress.

11.text: Folks gon' live there again. No more destruction. Jerusalem gon' be safe—finally.

12.text: But here's what's gon' happen to the ones who tried Jerusalem: Their flesh gon' rot off while they still standin'. Their eyes gon' melt in their sockets. Their tongues gon' rot right in they mouths.

13.text: On that day, the Lord gon' send a panic. Folks gon' turn on each other— Grabbing each other, swingin' on their own neighbors.

14.text: Even Judah gon' be fightin' inside Jerusalem. And all the wealth from the enemy nations? Gold, silver, and clothes—piled up high.

15.text: And that plague? It ain't just for the people. It gon' hit the horses, mules, camels, donkeys— Every animal in those camps gon' feel it too.

16.text: And everybody left from those nations that tried Jerusalem? Every year, they gon' have to pull up to worship the King— The Lord of Heaven's Armies— And celebrate the Feast of Tabernacles.

17.text: If they don't show up? No rain for them.

18.text: If Egypt try to skip out? No rain. They'll get hit with the same plague God promised to any nation That refuse to come celebrate the Feast.

19.text: That's the punishment for Egypt and everybody else Who act like they too good to worship the King.

20.text: On that day, even the bells on the horses gon' say: "HOLINESS TO THE LORD." Every pot in the Lord's house? Just as sacred as the altar bowls.

21.text: In fact, every pot in Judah and Jerusalem gon' be holy— Anybody bringin' a sacrifice can use one to cook in. And on that day? Ain't gon' be no Canaanite left in the house of the Lord.

1.text: This the message from the Lord that came to Zephaniah, son of Cushi, grandson of Gedaliah, great-grandson of Amariah, and great-great-grandson of Hezekiah, back when Josiah son of Amon was king in Judah.

2.text: The Lord said, "I'ma wipe everything off the face of the earth."

3.text: "People, animals, birds in the sky, fish in the sea—gone. I'ma clean house. Anybody wildin' out or doing wicked stuff? They gettin' cut off too."

4.text: "I'ma stretch My hand out over Judah and everybody living in Jerusalem. All that Baal worship? Dead. I'ma erase every last trace of those fake gods and the priests that reppin' them."

5.text: "That includes folks who worship the stars up on the roof, folks who swear by Me and Milcom like they can play both sides."

6.text: "And the ones who walked away from Me, who don't seek Me or even try to check in? Yeah, them too."

7.text: Shhh… be quiet in the presence of the Lord God. The day of the Lord comin' real soon. He already got the sacrifice set and invited the guests.

8.text: "And when that day hits, I'm comin' for the big dogs too—the royal fam, the officials, the rich folks stuntin' in them foreign fits."

9.text: "Same day, I'ma deal with folks who step over the threshold like they above it all, stackin' up violence and lies in their homes."

10.text: The Lord says, "That day, you gon' hear folks crying at the Fish Gate, wailing in the Second Quarter, and loud crashes echoin' from the hills."

11.text: Y'all in Maktesh? Mourn hard. All them merchants gon' be wiped out. Money handlers? Done for.

12.text: "That day, I'ma pull up with lamps and search every corner of Jerusalem. I'ma punish them chillin' in complacency, the ones sayin' in they heart, 'God ain't gon' do nothin'—not good or bad.'"

13.text: "But they gon' lose everything. All they goods? Gone. Houses? Empty. They gon' build, but never live in it. Plant vineyards, but never sip that wine."

14.text: The great day of the Lord? It's close. Real close. Coming fast. It's gon' be loud, bitter, and full of chaos. Even the strongest gon' cry.

15.text: That day gon' be all wrath, pain, destruction, darkness, and despair. A whole cloud of gloom hangin' over the land.

16.text: Trumpets blowin', alarms ringin'. Fortified cities and high towers? Under attack.

17.text: "I'ma make folks stumble like blind men, 'cause they been sinning heavy. Blood gon' spill like dust. Bodies thrown out like trash."

18.text: Don't think your silver or gold can save you. On the day of God's wrath, all of it gettin' burned up. The whole land gon' feel the heat of His jealousy. He cleanin' house, quick and final.

1.text: Y'all better get it together—yes, all of y'all, you hard-headed nation.

2.text: Do it before God's decree drop. Before the time pass like dust in the wind. Before the Lord's anger pull up on y'all. Don't wait 'til the Day of the Lord's wrath hit!

3.text: All y'all humble folks out here that still try to do right—seek the Lord. Chase righteousness. Walk in humility. Maybe, just maybe, He'll hide you when that judgment hits.

4.text: Gaza gon' be abandoned. Ashkelon left in ruins. Ashdod getting run out in broad daylight. And Ekron? Ripped up from the roots.

5.text: Woe to y'all living by the coast—y'all Cherethites! The Lord got smoke for you. Canaan, land of the Philistines? You gettin' wiped clean. No one gon' be left.

6.text: That whole coast finna be empty pastures now. Just grass, shepherds, and sheep pens.

7.text: The leftovers from Judah? They gon' move in. They gon' feed they flocks out there. They gon' sleep in Ashkelon like it's theirs—because the Lord gon' come through for them and bring His people back.

8.text: "I been heard what Moab and Ammon been sayin'. All that trash talk, the way they've been wildin' against My people, threatening borders like they runnin' things."

9.text: "So as sure as I live," says the Lord of Heaven's Armies, "Moab gon' end up like Sodom. Ammon? Just like Gomorrah. Overrun with weeds, full of salt pits, and nothin' but wasteland."

10.text: "And guess what? My people, the ones who still standing? They takin' all that over. They gon' own it."

11.text: They brought that on themselves with all that pride, runnin' they mouth against God's people and actin' brand new.

12.text: But the Lord gon' make it known—He ain't to be played with. He gon' snatch every fake god off the map. Folks all over the world, from every coast, they gon' bow to Him from wherever they at.

13.text: "And you too, Ethiopians? My sword comin' for y'all too."

14.text: He gon' stretch His hand up north, destroy Assyria, and turn Nineveh into a dried-up ghost town—lookin' like a desert.

15.text: Animals gon' chill there like it's a field. All kinds of creatures—birds, wild beasts, you name it. Birds squawkin' through the windows. Ruins at the doorstep. He gon' tear all that fine cedar down.

16.text: This that city that used to be loud and proud, sittin' back comfy like, "I'm that girl—ain't nobody touchin' me." But look at her now—nothing but ruins. Just a rest stop for stray animals. Folks gon' pass by and hiss, throwin' shade and side-eyes.

1.text: Woe to that city that don't listen, that's full of mess and always tryna hurt folks.

2.text: She don't listen to God's voice. Won't take no correction. Ain't even tryin' to trust the Lord or get close to Him.

3.text: Her leaders? Like lions, loud and always lookin' to devour. Her judges? Like wolves that leave nothin' behind—not even bones by the next morning.

4.text: Her prophets out here wildin', actin' reckless and fake. The priests done messed up the temple and broke God's law like it ain't nothin'.

5.text: But the Lord? He still righteous right there in the city. He don't do no wrong. Every morning He bring justice like clockwork. He don't miss. But the wicked? They don't even feel shame.

6.text: "I done tore down nations," God says. "Left their cities empty. Ain't nobody walkin' them streets. They ruined, straight deserted."

7.text: "I thought for sure y'all would finally respect Me after all that. Thought y'all would learn something so I wouldn't have to destroy your home. But nah—they woke up early just to keep doin' wrong."

8.text: "So wait on Me," says the Lord. "When I rise up to get what's Mine, I'm bringin' all nations together for judgment. I'm pourin' out My fierce anger. The whole earth gettin' dealt with."

9.text: "But after that, I'mma clean up the people's speech—make it pure—so everybody can call on My name and serve Me side by side."

10.text: "From way beyond Ethiopia, My people gon' come back and worship Me again. They bringin' Me offerings with love."

11.text: "On that day, you won't be ashamed for how you acted before. I'mma get rid of the proud ones who always actin' superior. You ain't gon' be stuntin' on My holy mountain no more."

12.text: "I'ma leave behind a humble, quiet people—folk who lean fully on the name of the Lord."

13.text: "That remnant? They won't lie. Won't do folks dirty. No slick talk. They gon' rest easy, feed they flocks, and sleep in peace—with no fear."

14.text: Sing loud, daughter Zion! Shout up, Israel! Be glad and go 'head and rejoice with everything you got!

15.text: The Lord done cleared your record. He kicked the enemy out. Your King—yeah, the Lord—He right there with you. No more disaster, period.

16.text: On that day, people gon' say to Jerusalem: "Don't trip! Don't be scared! Don't let your hands hang down in fear."

17.text: The Lord your God is with you, strong and mighty to save. He delights in you. He gon' calm you down with His love and sing over you with joy.

18.text: "I'ma gather all the ones who hurt from missing out on worship, the ones who been feelin' heavy 'cause of the shame they carry."

19.text: "At that time, I'mma handle everybody that did y'all dirty. I'll heal the hurt, bring back the ones who got pushed out, and give y'all a name and respect everywhere you used to get clowned."

20.text: "When I bring y'all back and gather y'all together again, I'mma make the whole world give y'all praise and honor. I'll restore everything right before your eyes," says the Lord.
